Preface
When do you use a dictionary? Is it when you don’t know which kanji
to use, or when you come across a noun or a verb you don’t know the
meaning of? For things like kanji and word meanings, a Japanese
language dictionary is very useful. If you want to know the difference
between words like うっかり and つい, a thesaurus will help. However, there
are times when no conventional dictionary will give you the answer you
are looking for. For example, you may want to know exactly what the
word せっかく means when it is used in the pattern せっかく…からには, as opposed
to the pattern せっかく…けれども. Or you may wonder what sort of thinking lies
behind the use of expressions like …にしてからが and …にしたところで, or about the
meaning that expressions like ...ともかぎらない, …わけではない, and …にちがいない add to
the sentences in which they are used. These questions are not dealt
with adequately in conventional dictionaries.
This dictionary is a handbook that looks at
grammar patterns in terms of their meaning, function, and usage in
relation to sentences or clauses. It also describes how these patterns
are used in different situations and contexts. When you want to look
up expressions that you can’t find in conventional dictionaries, or
gain information that isn’t available in those dictionaries, this
handbook will be a powerful resource.
This handbook contains 3,000 entries, including all of the grammar
patterns found in the Chuujookyuu Nihongo Kyookasho Bunkei
Sakuin (eds. Yuriko Sunakawa et al.) and Bumpoo-tekina Kinoogo
no Tagui, which is part of the test content specifications for Levels
1 and 2 of the Japanese Language Proficiency Test (Japan
Foundation/Association of International Education, Japan). It also
includes some grammar patterns gathered from newspapers, magazines,
novels, movie scripts, and other sources. It is a comprehensive
handbook that covers a variety of grammar patterns which Japanese
language learners at the intermediate level and above often find to be
challenging.
In this handbook we have tried to explain
grammar patterns in clear and concise Japanese, so that learners of
Japanese as a foreign or second language will find them easy to
understand. We have also done the following things.

content: Provided as many illustrative examples as

content.content: possible, in order for readers to be able to grasp how each pattern is
used.

content: Avoided using kanji other than Jooyoo

content.content: Kanji (Kanji for Common Use) and provided a pronunciation guide for kanji
used in examples.

content: Provided examples of “incorrect usage”

content.content: when appropriate, in order to illustrate common mistakes that learners
should take care to avoid.

content: Included as much information as possible

content.content: with respect to the structure of each pattern, situations in which it
is actually used, differences from similar expressions, and other
points useful for Japanese language learning.

content: Made a special effort to deal with

content.content: expressions typical of spoken language, such as っけ in なんて言ったっけ and
っこない in できっこない.

content: To facilitate easy look-up of words and

content.content: expressions, we have also provided three kinds of indexes: a Japanese
phonetic syllabary index (50-on index), a reverse order index,
and an index of meaning and function groups.
It has been eight years since the plan for this
handbook was conceived. Since it was written and edited by a team with
whimsical and diverse interests, it would not have been possible to
complete it without the support and encouragement of many people.
Special thanks go to Toshihiro Fukunishi of Kurosio Publishers, who
worked overtime and gave up his days off to ensure that this handbook
was published. We are also grateful to Yumiko Sando and Yoko Sato for
all of their help. Furthermore, we are indebted to Jiro Abe and the
others who collaborated with the editing, and we are also grateful to
many friends and colleagues for their feedback and advice.
We sincerely hope that this handbook will be a
useful resource for those who are learning Japanese as a foreign or
second language, for Japanese language teachers, and for others who
are interested in the use of Japanese.

Preface to the English Edition
A Handbook of Japanese Grammar Patterns is a dictionary that
was compiled for the use of teachers and students of Japanese as a
foreign or second language. Since publication of the original Japanese
edition, translations of the Handbook have been published in
Chinese, Vietnamese, Korean, and Thai, and many people in Asia have
been able to use it. However, publication of an English edition lagged
behind. Now that we have finished the long-overdue English edition, it
is our hope that many people in Europe, North America, and a wide
range of other places will be able to use it.
We are grateful to all of the translators who
put so much time and effort into translating a book of this length
into English. We are also greatly indebted to Mariko Ichikawa of
Kurosio Publishers, as well as to all of the other employees at
Kurosio, for their hard work throughout the editing process.
When this dictionary was originally compiled, we
tried to keep the grammatical explanations as clear and concise as
possible, and to include as many illustrative examples as possible. We
also tried to create examples that would be easy to understand, and
for which it would be easy to imagine the situation of use. In
addition, we tried to make individual grammar patterns and expressions
as easy to find as possible, by providing detailed headword listings
and multiple indexes. We sincerely hope that our endeavors will be of
benefit to teachers and learners of Japanese all over the world.
September 2015
Yuriko Sunakawa

Guide to the Handbook's structure and use
1.The key contents of this handbook are
structured in three tiers. The first tier is a headword and/or head
phrase, the second tier is a category heading that shows meaning or
function, and the third tier is a sub-heading for further
categorization. As shown in the example below, the second tier is
numbered using Arabic numerals (1, 2, 3), and the third tier is
ordered using letters of the alphabet (a, b, c).
2.Grammatical information is given in the
second and third tiers, using grammar symbols and notations. When
there are too many notations to be included in the tier heading, they
are given inside square brackets [ ].

3.Headwords are listed in the order of the
Japanese 50-on syllabary. Headings in the second and third
tiers are not necessarily in this order.
4.Stable compound expressions such as ていけない
and とする are treated as headwords. While conventional dictionaries
would list these entries under the headwords いけない and する, this
handbook describes their usage under headings that include the
particles. At the same time, this handbook also allows users to find
these expressions using the conventional route. In other words,
multiple look-up methods are possible.
5.A Japanese phonetic syllabary index (50-on
index), a reverse order index, and a list of meaning and function
groups are given at the end of this handbook. When the word you are
looking for is not easy to find, or when you want to find an
expression using the last word or particle that it contains, this
handbook will lead you there quickly.

ta-form of a verb
e.g.：書いた、読んだ、見た、来た、した
V-たろう
conjectural form of a verb in past tense
e.g.：書いたろう、読んだろう、見たろう、来たろう、したろう
V-ない
negative form of a verb
e.g.：書かない、読まない、見ない、来ない、しない
V-て
te-form of a verb
e.g.：書いて、読んで、見て、来て、して
V-ば
ba-form of a verb
e.g.：書けば、読めば、見れば、来れば、すれば
V-よう
intentional form of a verb
e.g.：書こう、読もう、見よう、来よう、しよう
V-れる
potential form of a verb
e.g.：書ける、読める、見られる、来られる、できる
V-られる
passive form of a verb
e.g.：書かれる、読まれる、見られる、来られる、される
V-させる
causative form of a verb
e.g.：書かせる、読ませる、見させる、来させる、させる
〈Other symbols〉
Means “or.”
e.g.：［N／Naになる］ means ［Nになる］ or ［Naになる］, and ［V-たあとに／で］
means ［V-たあとに］ or ［V-たあとで］.
Means “possible either with or without.”
e.g.：それゆえ（に）means that both それゆえand それゆえにare possible.
Indicates in what situation(s) the example may apply.
e.g.：《手紙》まずはご報告まで。
Indicates information about the grammar pattern.
e.g.：［あまりV-ない］
Indicates the meaning and/or function of the grammar
pattern.
e.g.：...みたいだ 〈supposition〉, V-てくれない（か） 〈request〉
Indicates an example given in the explanation of a grammar
pattern.
Indicates an incorrect usage example.
Indicates a correct usage example.
Means “refer to a different entry.”
subscript numbers
Used when there are two or more headwords with the same
form.
e.g.：
【のに1】
【のに2】
【あいだ】
1. Nのあいだa. Nのあいだ〈space〉

content: ステレオと本棚の間にテレビを置いた。

content.content: I placed the television between the stereo and the bookshelf.

content: 古本を買ったら、ページの間に1万円札がはさまっていた。

content.content: When I bought a secondhand book, I found a 10,000 yen bill between the pages.

content: 大阪までの間のどこかで駅弁を買って食べよう。

content.content: I’ll buy lunch (a lunch box) at a station somewhere before Osaka and eat it.
あいだ indicates a space between two places/things. When both things or places are indicated, NとNのあいだ is used, as in
b. Nのあいだ〈relationship〉

content: 最近二人の間はうまくいっていないようだ。

content.content: It seems that the relationship between the two hasn’t gone well recently.

content: そのホテルは安くて清潔なので、旅行者たちの間で人気がある。

content.content: Since the hotel is cheap and clean, it is popular among travelers.

content: 二つの事件の間にはなにか関係があるらしい。

content.content: It seems that there is some relationship between the two incidents.
In these cases, あいだ indicates “the relationship among several people or matters,” and it is used to express a state or an action or an event that happens in it.
2. あいだ〈time〉a. ...あいだ［Nのあいだ］［A-いあいだ］［V-ている／V-る　あいだ］

content: 彼は会議の間ずっといねむりをしていた。

content.content: He was dozing all through the meeting.

content: 彼女が戻ってくるまでの間、喫茶店で本を読むことにした。

content.content: I decided to read a book at the coffee shop until she returned.

content: 一生懸命泳いでいる間はいやなことも忘れてしまう。

content.content: I can forget about an unpleasant thing while swimming hard.

content: 子供が小さい間は、なかなか夫婦での外出ができなかった。

content.content: When my child was small, I could hardly ever go out with just my husband.

content: 友子は、大阪にいる間は元気だったが、東京に引っ越したとたんに体をこわしてしまった。

content.content: Tomoko was fine when she was in Osaka, but she fell sick just after she moved to Tokyo.

content: 私たちがお茶の用意をする間、彼らは緊張して一言もしゃべらずに座っていた。

content.content: While we prepared tea, they were sitting nervously without uttering a single word.

In these cases, あいだ indicates a period of time in which a state or an action continues, and the sentence that follows indicates a durative state or a parallel action during that period. When the predicate in the following sentence is an action verb, forms which mean duration, such as V-ている, V-つづける, are used.
（×）私が勉強している間、弟は遊んだ。
While I was studying, my younger brother played.
（○）私が勉強している間、弟は遊んでいた。
While I was studying, my younger brother was playing.
When describing the past, V-ていた／A-かった　あいだ are also used.
（例）彼はドイツに留学していた間、スウェーデン人の女の子と一緒に生活していたらしい。
I heard that he was living with a Swedish girl while studying in Germany.
b. ...あいだに［Nのあいだに］［Na なあいだに］［A-いあいだに］［V-ている／V-る   あいだに］

content: 留守の間にどろぼうが入った。

content.content: My house was broken into by a thief during my absence.

content: 4時から5時までの間に一度電話をください。

content.content: Please give me a call sometime between four and five o’clock.

content: 家族がみんな寝ている間に家を出ることにした。

content.content: I decided to leave home while everyone in my family was sleeping.

content: リサが日本にいる間に一緒に旅行したかったのだが、残念ながらできなかった。

content.content: I wanted to travel with Lisa while she was in Japan, but to my regret, I was not able to do so.

content: 私がてんぷらを揚げる間に、母はおひたしと酢の物と味噌汁まで作ってしまった。

content.content: While I was making tempura, my mother made boiled greens, a vinegared dish, and even miso soup.

content: あそこも日本人旅行者が少ない間に行っておかないと、きっとすぐに開発されて日本人だらけになるだろう。

content.content: We had better visit there while the number of Japanese travelers is small, otherwise it will surely be developed soon and be full of Japanese.

content: 祖母が元気な間にいろいろ話を聞いておこう。

content.content: I will ask my grandmother many things while she is still in good health.

...あいだに indicates a period of time in which a state/action continues, and a sentence that expresses an action or a situation within that time follows. The predicate of the following sentence is a verb, and forms that do not indicate duration, like ...する, ...しはじめる, ...になる, are used.
（×）授業の間にずっとおしゃべりをしていた。
I was chatting during the lesson.
（○）授業の間に3回質問をした。
I asked questions three times during the lesson.
To describe a past matter, ...たあいだに is also used. When the agents of the first and second clauses are different, as in

content: , it means the two persons acted in parallel at the same time.

content.content: 【あいまって】→
【とあいまって】
【あえて】
1. あえて

content: 私はあえてみなさんに規則の見直しを提案したいと思います。

content.content: I would dare to suggest we re-examine the regulations.

content: 誰も助けてくれないかもしれないが、それでもあえてこの計画は実行に移したいと思う。

content.content: Although nobody might help me, I still want to put this plan into action.

content: 恥を忍んであえてお聞きしますが、今のお話のポイントは何だったのでしょうか。

content.content: It’s embarrassing to ask you this, but what was the point of your speech just now?

content: 反感を買うのを承知であえて言いたいのは、彼らにこの仕事を任せるのはリスクが大きいということだ。

content.content: I know I will offend them, but I dare say that it is too risky to leave this work to them.

content: これができるのはあなたしかいないから、負担をかけることはわかっていても、あえてお願いしているのです。

content.content: I know it is a burden for you, but I dare to ask because only you can do this job.

When あえて is followed by a verb of utterance, like 言う, 提案する, お願いする, or verbs like やる, 実行する, it expresses “doing it would offend others or involve risks and difficulties, but I still want to do it, or must do it.” It is used to state a strong opinion or bring up an idea.
2. あえてV-ば

content: 反対されるのを承知であえて言えば、こんな計画は百害あって一利なしだ。

content.content: I know there may be objections, but if I dare say so, such a plan is harmful and really no good.

content: 少々言いにくいことなのですが、あえて言わせていただければ、お宅のお子さんは他の学校に変わられた方がいいのではないかと思うのですが。

content.content: It is slightly hard to say, but if I’m allowed to say so, I think your child had better move to another school.

content: この映画はあまりストーリー性がないのだが、あえて説明すれば、二組のカップルがあちらこちらを旅して回り、行く先々で事件が起こるというものだ。

content.content: This movie doesn’t have much of a story line, but if I had to explain it, I’d say it’s a story about two couples traveling here and there and troubles happen at every place they visit.

content: まだこのプロジェクトの方針は漠然としているのだが、あえて言うとすれば、環境破壊が進んでいる地域に対して、民間の援助によってそれを食い止めようというものだ。

content.content: The policy of this project is still vague, but if I try to explain it, it is to stop environmental destruction in areas that destruction is taking place, with the support of the private sector.

In these cases, when あえて is followed by a verb of utterance such as 言う, お話しする, or 説明する, it is used as a prefatory expression when one wants to say something in spite an objection or criticism being raised, or when one cannot find an appropriate way to say something.
3. あえて...ない

content: そのやり方にあえて反対はしないが、不満は残っている。

content.content: I don’t dare to object to that way of doing things, but I’m not satisfied with it.

content: 相手が偉い先生だからといって、あえてへりくだる必要もない。

content.content: It is not necessary to be overly modest, even if he is a great teacher.

content: 親に反対されてまで、あえて彼と結婚しようとは思わない。

content.content: I won’t dare to marry him, if it’s against my parents’ wishes.

content: みんなに嫌がられてまで、あえて自分の方針を押し通すこともないじゃないか。

content.content: Why do you have to push your policy through while putting people off?
When expressions like する必要もない, することもない, しようとは思わない follow, あえて expresses the meaning “others would object or be antagonized, so one doesn’t, or shouldn’t, do such a risky thing.”
【あがる】
1. R-あがる〈upward direction〉

content: 彼は立ち上がってあたりを見回した。

content.content: He stood up and looked around.

content: 妹は帰ってくるなり階段を一気にかけ上がって、自分の部屋に飛び込んだ。

content.content: As soon as my sister came home, she ran upstairs and jumped through the doorway into her room.

content: 彼女はライバルを押しのけて、スターの座にのしあがった。

content.content: She pushed her rivals away and rose to become a star.

content: 政治学の先生はひたいがはげ上がっている。

content.content: Our political science teacher has a receding hairline.

content: 冬休みにみんなで温泉に行こうという計画が持ち上がった。

content.content: We had a plan to go all together to a hot spring in winter vacation.

content: ツアーの申し込み人数が少なすぎるので、家族連れで参加できることにしたら、人数が倍以上にふくれ上がって旅行会社は困っている。

content.content: After initially receiving too few applications, the travel agency now has problems with twice as many applications as they expected, since they allowed people to apply for the tour with their families.

content: 彼女はボーイフレンドにプロポーズされてすっかり舞い上がっている。

content.content: She was proposed to by her boyfriend, so she is totally excited.

content: 自分がリーダーになればみんなついてくるに決まっているだって？　思い上がるのもいい加減にしろ。

content.content: Are you saying everyone will surely follow you if you become a leader? Stop being conceited.
When あがる is appended to a verb stem, it indicates an action/movement or a state that is going in an upward direction.

content: are figurative expressions with the meaning of “in an upward direction.”

content.content: 2. R-あがる〈extreme degree〉

content: 長い間雨が降らないので、湖も干上がってしまった。

content.content: Since it has not rained for a long time, the lake has dried up.

content: 店員は男にピストルを突きつけられてふるえ上がった。

content.content: The salesclerk was terrified when a pistol was pointed at him by a man.

content: ふだんほとんど叱らない先生をバカにしていた生徒は、タバコを吸っているのを見つかって大声でどなりつけられ、縮み上がっていた。

content.content: The student, who had made fun of the teacher that hardly ever scolds anyone, shrank away when he was found smoking and yelled at by that teacher.

content: その俳優は、たいして演技もうまくないのに周りの人たちにおだてられて、自分は誰よりも才能があるんだとのぼせ上がっている。

content.content: Even though his acting is not very good, that actor is overconfident and believes  that he is more talented than anyone else, due to flattering by people around him.
When あがる is joined to a verb stem, it expresses a situation that progresses to an extreme degree. It can be used with only a limited number of verbs.
3. R-あがる〈accomplishment〉

content: パンがおいしそうに焼きあがった。

content.content: The bread turned out delicious.

content: みんなの意見を取り入れて、とても満足のいく旅行プランができあがった。

content.content: By taking into account everyone’s opinions, a very satisfying tour plan was arranged.

content: スパゲッティがゆであがったら、すばやくソースにからめます。

content.content: When the spaghetti is finished cooking, put the sauce on it quickly.

content: 注文していた年賀状が刷りあがってきた。

content.content: The New Year’s cards that I ordered were printed.

In these cases, あがる is appended to a verb stem and expresses that an action is completed. It is usually appended to transitive verbs that involve making things, such as 編む, 練る, 刷る. The intransitive verb できる is an exception.
【あくまで】
1. あくまで（も）〈volition〉

content: 私はあくまでもこの方針を貫くつもりだ。

content.content: I will accomplish this policy.

content: 国連はあくまでも平和的な解決に向けて話し合いを続ける考えです。

content.content: The United Nations is going to continue negotiations to reach a peaceful settlement.

content: 彼はあくまでも知らぬ存ぜぬで押し通すつもりらしい。

content.content: He seems to persist in denying all knowledge of it.

content: 彼女があくまでいやだと言い張ったので、他の候補を探さなければならなくなった。

content.content: She kept saying that she didn’t want to do it, so we had to find another candidate.
When followed by verbs of volitional acts, あくまで expresses a strong resolution to do what one wants to do in spite of major difficulties or strong objections. It is a rather formal expression.
2. あくまで（も）〈claim〉

content: 私が今申し上げたことはあくまでも試案ですので、そのおつもりで。

content.content: What I said now is just a tentative plan, so please keep that in mind.

content: それはあくまでも理想論に過ぎず、実現は不可能なのではないか。

content.content: Because it is no more than an idealistic thought, isn’t it impossible to realize?

content: この家はあくまでも仮の住まいで、ここに永住するつもりはない。

content.content: This is only a temporary house, because I won’t reside here permanently.

content: 断っておくが、彼とはあくまでも仕事の上の仲間でしかなく、それ以上の個人的なつきあいはいっさいしていないのだ。

content.content: I must tell you that he is only my friend from work, so we don’t have any personal association beyond that.

In these cases, あくまで expresses a strong assertion/claim of one’s belief about a matter. It is often used to deny or revise a general expectation, or a judgment, belief, or expectation on the part of the listener.
3. あくまで（も）〈strong degree〉

content: 空はあくまでも青く澄み渡り、砂浜はどこまでも白く続いていた。

content.content: The sky is pure blue and very clear, and the white sandy beach stretches on forever.

content: どんなに疲れている時でも、彼はあくまでも優しかった。

content.content: No matter how tired he was, he was always very kind.

content: あくまで広い見渡すかぎりの菜の花畑の中に、真っ赤な服を着た女の子が一人立っていた。

content.content: A girl wearing a brick red dress was standing in the vast field of canola blossoms that stretched as far as the eye could see.
Expresses that the situation in question is “completely/thoroughly (something).” It is a literary expression.
【あげく】
1. ...あげく［Nのあげく］［V-たあげく］

content: さんざん悩んだあげく、彼には手紙で謝ることにした。

content.content: After worrying and worrying, I decided to apologize to him in a letter.

content: 考えに考えたあげく、この家を売ることに決めた。

content.content: After thorough consideration, I have decided to sell this house.

content: 弟は6年も大学に行って遊びほうけたあげくに、就職したくないと言い出した。

content.content: After fooling around for six years at university, then my younger brother said that he didn’t want to get a job.

content: それは、好きでもない上司の御機嫌を取ったり、家族に当たり散らしたりの大騒ぎをしたあげくの昇進であった。

content.content: It was a promotion that finally came about after the great fuss of currying favor with the boss he doesn’t like and taking out his anger on his family.

content: 姉は籍を入れないだの一緒に住まないだのと言って親と対立し、すったもんだのあげくにようやく結婚した。

content.content: My sister finally married, after much quarreling with our parents and indecision about things like registering her marriage and whether or not to live together.

Whenあげくis followed by an expression of some situation, it means that such a conclusion/solution/progress was reached after the previous state had continued long enough. In many cases, that continuous state is a mental burden or nuisance for the person. あげくに is also used, as in

content: , and あげくのN  is used before a noun, as in

content.content: 2. あげくのはてに（は）

content: 部長はますます機嫌が悪くなり、あげくの果てには関係ない社員にまでどなり散らすようになった。

content.content: The manager’s mood went from bad to worse, and to top it off, he even yelled at employees who had nothing to do with it.

content: 彼女は我慢に我慢を重ねたあげくの果てに、私のところに相談に来た。

content.content: After persevering and persevering, she finally came to me for advice.
This is used to describe a result that arises after a certain situation has continued for a long time and reached some sort of limit. Generally that result is not good.
【あげる】
1. R-あげる〈upward direction〉

content: 男は大きな岩を軽々と持ち上げた。

content.content: The man lifted a big rock effortlessly.

content: 先生に漫画の本を取り上げられた。

content.content: The teacher took away my comic book.

content: 彼女が髪をかき上げる仕草を見ているのが好きだ。

content.content: I like to see her combing her hair and pulling it back.

content: 彼女はあたりかまわず声をはり上げて泣きわめいた。

content.content: Disregarding those around her, she screamed and cried.

content: その土地は自治体が買い上げて大きな遊園地を作ることに決まった。

content.content: The local government decided to buy up that land and build a big amusement park.
あげる, when joined to a verb stem, means an action to make an object move upward. It is also used figuratively, in

content: and

content.content: 2. R-あげる〈accomplishment〉

content: 大事なお客さんが来るので、母は家中をぴかぴかにみがき上げた。

content.content: Because an important guest is coming, my mother cleaned up the whole house.

content: 彼は原稿用紙500枚の小説を一気に書き上げた。

content.content: He dashed off the whole novel of five hundred pages.

content: クリスマスまでに何とかセーターを編み上げてプレゼントしようと思っていたのに。

content.content: I thought I would somehow be able to finish knitting the sweater before Christmas and give it as a present.

content: 刑事は犯人をロープで身動きできないようにしばり上げた。

content.content: The detective tied up the criminal with a rope so he wasn’t able to move.

content: みんなで一晩中かかってまとめ上げたデータが何者かに盗まれた。

content.content: The data which we took all night to complete were stolen by someone.

content: この織物は草や木の根などを集めてきて染めた糸で丹念に織り上げたものだ。

content.content: This textile is woven very elaborately with yarn which was dyed with grass and tree roots.

content: 何年もかかって築き上げてきた信頼が、たった一度の過ちで崩れてしまった。

content.content: The confidence that was built up over many years has collapsed because of a single mistake.

When joined to a verb stem, あげる expresses the accomplishment or completion of an act. With verbs of creation, such as 書くor 編む, it means to complete. It includes a sense of the effort needed to accomplish the act.
3. R-てあげる→
【てあげる】
【あたかも】［あたかもN（であるか）の　ようだ］［あたかもN（であるか）の　ごとし］［あたかもVかの　ようだ］［あたかもVかの　ごとし］

content: その日はあたかも春のような陽気だった。

content.content: That day was just like spring weather.

content: 人生はあたかもはかなく消える夢のごときものである。

content.content: Life is just like a dream that comes to nothing.

content: 彼は、あたかも自分が会の中心人物であるかのように振る舞っていた。

content.content: He behaved in the meeting as if he were the leader.

content: 彼女はいつも、あたかも目の前にその光景が浮かび上がってくるかのような話し方で、人々を魅了する。

content.content: She always fascinates people, with her way of talking as if the scene will appear before one’s very eyes.

content: その人は、あたかもファッション雑誌からそのまま抜け出してきたかのような最新流行のファッションで全身を飾って、パーティーに現れた。

content.content: That person—dressed from head to foot in the latest fashion—appeared at the party looking like she had just stepped out of a fashion magazine.

content: 大火事がおさまると、街はあたかも空襲で焼き払われたかのごとく、ビルも家も跡形もなく燃え尽きてしまっていた。

content.content: After the big fire was under control, the city had been burned down as if in an air raid, with no trace of any buildings or houses left.

あたかも is used to explain a state by comparing it to another state, and it expresses that these states are very similar, although they are actually different. It is not used in casual spoken language, but in novels and other written language. まるで is used in spoken language, and ごとし, which conjugates as ごとき, ごとく, is literary language.
【あっての】［NあってのN］

content: 学生あっての大学だ。学生が来なければ、いくらカリキュラムが素晴らしくても意味がない。

content.content: A university needs students. If students don’t come, the university’s existence is meaningless, no matter how good a curriculum it has.

content: 私を見捨てないでください。あなたあっての私なんですから。

content.content: Please don’t leave me. I do not exist without you.

content: お客あっての商売なんだから、まずお客さんのニーズに応えなければならないだろう。

content.content: Business cannot be carried out without customers, so we have to meet the needs of customers first.
XあってのY expresses that Y can be realized because Y has X. It includes the meaning that Y is not realized if Y doesn’t have X. Nouns that refer to human beings are used for X.
【あと1】
1. あと〈space〉［Nのあと］［V-る／V-た　あと］

content: みんな私の後についてきてください。

content.content: Everyone, please follow me.

content: 彼が走っていく後を追いかけた。

content.content: He ran away, but I chased after him.

content: 観光客が去ったあとには、お菓子の袋や空きかんが散らばっていた。

content.content: After the tourists left, snack wrappers and empty cans were scattered all over.

content: チューリップを抜いたあとに見たこともない草が生えてきた。

content.content: After we pulled up the tulips, a kind of grass I had never seen began to sprout.
あとmeans something is spatially behind or after something.

content: means the place where something was pulled out, but it can also be interpreted as referring to〈time〉, as in Usage 2b. ...をあとにして, in the following example, is an idiom which means “leave for.”

content.content: （例）彼は、ふるさとの町を後にして、都会へ出ていった。
He left his hometown for the city.
2. あと〈time〉a. ...あと［Nのあと］［V-たあと］

content: 試験の後はいつも気分が落ち込む。

content.content: I am always depressed after examinations.

content: 今日は夕食の後、友達と花火をすることになっている。

content.content: I am going to set off fireworks with my friend after dinner today.

content: パーティーが終わったあとの部屋はとても散らかっていた。

content.content: The room was very messy after the party.

content: 彼はアルバイトをやめたあと、特にすることもなくて毎日ぶらぶらしている。

content.content: Since he left his part-time job, he is idling away every day.

content: 彼女は新しい上司についてひとしきり文句を言ったあとは、けろっとして何も不満がないかのように働いていた。

content.content: After she complained about the new boss for a while, she went back to normal, working like there is nothing to complain about.
In these cases, あとindicates that something has been finished or completed. The clause that follows describes the state at that time, or something that happens next.
b. ...あと　（で／に）［Nのあと　で／に］［V-たあと　で／に］

content: 田中さんにはお世話になったから、引っ越しの後で改めてお礼にうかがおう。

content.content: Since Tanaka-san kindly helped me, after moving I will visit and express my thanks to him.

content: 映画を見たあとでトルコ料理を食べに行きましょう。

content.content: Let’s go out for Turkish food after the movie.

content: 友達と旅行の約束をしてホテルも予約してしまったあとで、その日が実は出張だったことを思いだした。

content.content: After I promised to travel with my friend and reserved a hotel room, I remembered that I actually had to go on a business trip on that day.

content: 食事を済ませたあとに1時間ほど昼寝をした。

content.content: I took a nap for about an hour after finishing lunch.

content: みんなが帰ってしまったあとには、いつも寂しい気持ちにおそわれる。

content.content: After everybody goes home, I always feel lonely.

content: 詳しい釈明を聞いた後にも、やっぱりおかしいという疑念は残っていた。

content.content: Even after hearing a detailed explanation, I still had a suspicion that it was wrong.
Means “afterward.” It is used to describe a chronological sequence of events.
c. V-たあとから

content: 募集を締め切ったあとから応募したいと言ってこられても困る。

content.content: After the deadline for applications has passed, there is nothing we can do even if someone comes and asks.

content: 新製品の企画を提出したあとから、新しい企画は当分見合わせたいと上司に言われてがっかりした。

content.content: I was disappointed to hear that the boss would like to wait before considering a new project, after having submitted my plan for a new product.
This means “after a certain thing has taken place.” It is used to say that something else happens which contradicts the previous event.
【あと2】
1. あと

content: 料理はこのくらいあれば十分ですね。あと、飲み物はこれで足りますか。

content.content: This much food will be enough, right? And will these be enough drinks?

content: 以上でだいたい分かったと思いますが、あと、何か質問はありませんか。

content.content: I think you have understood more or less everything, but do you have any questions?

content: A:メンバーはこれだけですね。

content.content: These are all the members, right?
B:あ、あと、もしかしたら田中さんも来るかもしれないと言っていました。
Well, Tanaka-san said he might come, too.
あとis placed at the beginning of a sentence or clause. It is used when the speaker remembers something relevant to the matter at hand and adds a piece of information or an after thought.
2. あと+数量詞

content: その仕事を片づけるにはあと3日で十分です。

content.content: Three more days will be enough to finish that job.

content: あと二人そろえば野球チームが作れる。

content.content: We can make a baseball team with two more members.

content: あと10メートルでゴールインというところで、その選手は倒れてしまった。

content.content: The runner fell down ten meters before the finish line.

content: あと少しで終わりますので、待っていただけますか。

content.content: I will finish it in a moment, so could you please wait?

In these cases, あとindicates that a certain amount is added to the present number or quantity. It means that, by increasing the quantity by the amount indicated after あと, the conditions would be met for a certain event to take place. In other words, あと indicates the quantity that is needed to fulfill a certain condition, as shown in the following examples.
（例）卒業式まであと1週間だ。←あと1週間で卒業式だ。
It’s one week until the graduation ceremony. ←The graduation ceremony will be in one week.
（例）ビールはもうあと2本しかない。←あと2本でビールはなくなる。
There are only two bottles of beer left. ←The beer will be gone after just two more bottles.
（例）サラダがあと少し残っていますが、誰か食べませんか。←あと少しでサラダも終わりです。
There is a little more salad left—would anyone like to have it? ←The salad is nearly gone.
【あとから】

content: あとから文句を言われても困るので、何か言いたいことがある人は今のうちに出してください。

content.content: It’s troublesome for me to hear complaints after the fact, so if you have something to say, please tell me now.

content: 入学試験の合格通知が来たので喜んでいたら、あとからあれはまちがいだったという知らせがきて、がっくりした。

content.content: I was glad to get the entrance exam results, but later I was shocked to receive a note that it had been a mistake.

content: ツアーに参加したいという人があとからあとから出てきて、調整するのに困った。

content.content: People who wanted to join the tour kept coming one after another, so I had trouble coordinating everything.
This is used to express that a matter seems to have been settled, but then something else happens that is related to it or reverses the outcome.
【あとで】

content: あとでまた電話します。

content.content: I’ll call you again later.

content: あとで一緒に食事しませんか。

content.content: Shall we have a meal together later?

content: A:おかあさん、お人形の首がとれちゃった。直してよ。

content.content: Mom, the doll’s head came off. Fix it.
B:はいはい、あとでね。
Yes, dear, I’ll fix it later.
A:あとじゃなくて今。
Not later, now.
B:今忙しいんだから、ちょっと待ちなさい。
Just a minute. I’m busy now.
あとで indicates a point in time after an utterance. In some cases, it can be used to refuse to do something the speaker doesn’t want to do right then, as in
【あとは...だけ】

content: メンバーはほとんどそろって、あとは田中さんだけなのだが、なぜか予定の時刻を過ぎても現れる気配がない。

content.content: Almost all the members are here except for Tanaka-san, but for some reason these is no sign of him coming, even though it’s past the designated time.

content: 料理は全部できあがったし部屋も片づいたし、あとはみんなが来るのを待つばかりだ。

content.content: Dinner is ready and the room (house) is all tidied up, so the only thing I have to do now is wait for everyone to come.

content: コンサートのプログラムもとどこおりなく進み、あとは最後の難曲を残すのみとなった。

content.content: The concert program has gone smoothly so far, and the only thing left is one difficult piece.
Whenあと is followed by だけ, のみ, or ばかり, it indicates a condition to be met in order for a certain matter or event to be realized. It is used when most conditions have been met, but a few remain.
【あまり】あんまり can be used in spoken language for emphasis.
1. あまり／あんまり   ...ない［あまりNa ではない］［あまりA-くない］［あまりV-ない］

content: 今はあまりおなかがすいていないので、ケーキはいりません。

content.content: I am not very hungry, so I don’t need any cake.

content: 弟はあまり背が高くないので、女の子にもてない。

content.content: My younger brother is not so tall, so he is not popular with girls.

content: このごろあんまり映画を見ていない。

content.content: I haven’t seen very many movies recently.

content: けさはあまりごはんを食べなかった。

content.content: I didn’t have much for breakfast this morning.

content: 今日はあんまりお金がないので、CDを買うのは今度にしよう。

content.content: I don’t have enough money today, so I’ll buy a CD next time.
あまり is followed by a negative expression and indicates that the degree of something is not high. When used with a verb, it indicates that the frequency or quantity is not high.
2. あまり／あんまりa. あまりに（も）あんまり（にも）

content: あまりにおかしくて涙が出た。

content.content: It was so funny that tears came to my eyes.

content: ゆったりしたシャツは好きだが、これはあまりにも大きすぎる。

content.content: I like loose-fitting shirts, but this is too big for me.

content: ここのカレーはあまりにまずくて、とても食べられたものではない。

content.content: The curry in this shop is so bad that I just can’t eat it.

content: その人の申し出はあまりにも急な話だったので、すぐにOKするのはためらわれた。

content.content: This person’s offer came all of a sudden, so I hesitated to accept it immediately.

content: 彼があまりに僕の失敗を笑うから、だんだん腹が立ってきてなぐってしまった。

content.content: Because he laughed so much at my mistake, I gradually lost my temper and hit him.
あまり andあんまり are usually used with adjectives, but in some cases they are used with verbs, as in

content: . Both express that the degree of the adjective or verb is excessive. In many cases, あまり expresses a critical or negative feeling, and すぎる often follows it. There are also many cases in whichあまり is followed byて, ので, or から and indicates an inevitable matter caused by an extremely high degree, or a judgment or result that is drawn from it.

content.content: b. あまりのN   に／で

content: あまりの驚きに声も出なかった。

content.content: I was so surprised that I couldn’t say a word.

content: 海水浴に行ったが、あまりの人出でぐったり疲れてしまった。

content.content: I went bathing in the sea, but it was so crowded that I got exhausted.

content: あまりの問題の複雑さに、解決策を考える気力もわかない。

content.content: This problem is too complicated, so I have no motivation to seek a solution.

content: あまりの忙しさに、とうとう彼は体をこわして入院するはめになってしまった。

content.content: He was so busy that he finally got sick, ending up in the hospital.
With nouns that indicate a degree, あまりに expresses “because the degree is too high.” In the latter half of the sentence, an expression of an inevitable result follows.
（×）あまりの宿題に頭が痛くなった。
There was too much homework that I had a headache.
（○）あまりの宿題の多さに頭が痛くなった。
There was so much homework that I got a headache.
c. あまりに（も）...とあんまり（にも）...と

content: あまりボリュームを上げると隣の人が文句を言いに来るから気をつけてね。

content.content: Please be careful not to turn the volume up too loud; otherwise, the neighbors will come and complain about it.

content: あまりに安いとかえって心配だ。

content.content: I feel rather uneasy if it is too cheap.

content: 大きいバッグは便利だけど、あまりにも大きいと、中身をたくさん入れすぎて重くなって持ち歩くのがいやになるから、適当な大きさにした方がいいだろう。

content.content: A big bag is convenient, but if it’s too big, it’s easy to fill it too full and it’s a headache to carry, so it’s better to have a suitable size.
In these cases, あまり indicates an excessive degree of something, and the expression of an inevitable result follows in the latter half of the sentence.
d. ...あまり（に）［Nのあまり（に）］［V-るあまり（に）］

content: 母は悲しみのあまり、病の床に就いてしまった。

content.content: My mother has been sick in bed because of her great sorrow.

content: 彼は驚きのあまりに、手に持っていたカップを落としてしまった。

content.content: He was so surprised that he dropped the cup he had in his hand.

content: 忙しさのあまり、友達に電話をしなければならないのをすっかり忘れていた。

content.content: I was so busy that I completely forgot to call my friend.

content: 子供のことを心配するあまり、つい下宿に電話しては嫌がられてしまう。

content.content: I worry so much about my son that I’m always calling his boarding house, which annoys him.

content: 何とか逆転しようと焦るあまり、かえってミスをたくさん犯してしまった。

content.content: I was so impatient to turn the tables by any means possible that I ended up making even more errors than usual.

content: 彼女は彼のことを想うあまりに自分のことを犠牲にしてしまっている。

content.content: She is caring for him so much that she is sacrificing herself.
When あまりfollows a noun or verb that expresses an emotion or a state, it indicates an extreme degree. The latter half of the sentence describes an unfavorable result that then occurs.
3. 数量詞+あまり

content: その会の出席者は 100 名あまりだった。

content.content: More than one hundred people attended the meeting.

content: そこから5キロあまりの道のりを歩くだけの元気は残っていなかった。

content.content: I had no power left to walk the more than five kilometers from there.

content: 事故発生から2カ月あまりが経って、ようやく原因が突き止められた。

content.content: More than two months after the accident, the cause was finally identified.
Means “a little more than the number indicated by あまり." It is not used with exact numbers, but with round numbers. It is used in written language.
（×）ベーコンを 235 グラムあまり買った。
I bought a little more than 235 grams of bacon.
（○）ベーコンを 200 グラムあまり買った。
I bought a little more than 200 grams of bacon.
4. ...なんてあんまりだ→
【あんまり】3
【あらためる】［R-あらためる］

content: この文章の内容を子供向けに書き改めてくださいませんか。

content.content: Could you please rewrite this piece (essay) to make it for children?

content: その泥棒は自分のしたことを悔い改めて、まともな仕事についた。

content.content: The thief repented of his actions and found a decent job.
Follows a verb stem, but the range of verbs that can be used is limited. Means correcting the shortcoming(s) of someone/something and starting all over again.
【あるいは】Typical of written language. Also used in formal spoken language.
1. あるいはa. N（か）あるいはN

content: 黒あるいは青のペンで記入してください。

content.content: Please fill it in using a black or blue pen.

content: 欠席する場合には、口頭かあるいは書面で届け出ること。

content.content: If you are going to be absent, oral or written notification is required.

content: このクラブの施設は、会員あるいはその家族に限り、使用することができます。

content.content: Only members and/or their families can use the facilities of this club.

content: 応募は、25 歳以上、あるいは 20 歳以上で、職業をお持ちの方に限ります。

content.content: Applications are limited to those over 25 years of age or those in full-time employment aged 20 or more.

content: 被害者は、包丁あるいは登山ナイフのようなもので殺害されたらしい。

content.content: I heard that the victim was killed with something like a kitchen cleaver or a mountaineering knife.
Indicates “either X or Y.” It is often used when giving instructions to indicate “you can choose either X or Y, but choose only one of these,” as in

content: and
. It is also used for indicating a condition that implies “it’s all right if it conforms to either X or Y,” as in
and
. In the case of
, suitable answers include X, Y, or both. As shown in
, it is often used when “there are two possibilities (X or Y), so I don’t know which one to choose.”

content.content: XかY, XまたはY, XもしくはY are similar expressions. In everyday spoken language,  XかY is often used.
b. ...か、あるいは

content: 申し込み書類は、郵送するかあるいは事務所まで持参してください。

content.content: Please bring or send your application form to our office.

content: A:福岡へは、どうやって行ったらいいですかね。

content.content: How do I get to Fukuoka?
B:そうですね。新幹線で行くか、あるいは飛行機で行くか、でしょうね。
Well, either by shinkansen (bullet train), or by air.

content: 社会人大学院に入学するためには、定職に就いているか、あるいは 25 歳以上であることが条件である。

content.content: In order to enter graduate school for working adults, one must have regular employment or be over 25 years old.

content: 就職しようか、あるいは進学しようかと迷っている。

content.content: I am thinking about whether to find a job or continue on in school.

content: A:被害者は、犯人は知らない男だと言っています。

content.content: The victim says the culprit was unknown to him.
B:本当に知らないか、あるいは知らないふりをしているか、どちらかだな。
It must be one or the other—either he really doesn’t know who it was, or he’s pretending not to know.

content: 景気は数年で回復するのか、あるいは何十年もかかるのか、まったく予想できない。

content.content: No one can predict whether business conditions will look up in just a few years, or whether it will take decades.
XかあるいはY indicates “either X or Y.”

content: and
are examples in which either X or Y is acceptable (but only one is chosen). In
, it indicates “if it conforms to condition X or Y, either of them can be chosen,” and it is also acceptable if both are true.
, indicate “there are two possibilities (X and Y), but I don’t know which one to choose.”

content.content: 2. あるいは...かもしれない

content: このぶんでは、明日はあるいは雪かもしれない。

content.content: If the weather stays like this, it might snow tomorrow.

content: 彼の言うことは、あるいは本当かもしれない。

content.content: What he is saying might be true.

content: これで、手術は三度目だが、今回はあるいはだめかもしれない。

content.content: This is the third time for me to have surgery, but this operation might not succeed.

content: もう何年も国には帰っていない。両親でも生きていれば、あるいは帰りたいと思ったかもしれないが、知った人もほとんどいない今は、特になつかしいとも思わない。

content.content: I haven’t gone home for many years. If my parents were alive, I might want to go, but there’s hardly anyone I know these now, so I really don’t miss it so much.
In these cases, あるいはis used in the pattern あるいは...かもしれない and expresses the speaker’s supposition that something is possible. ひょっとすると andもしかすると are similar to あるいは...かもしれない.
あるいは can also be used with other suppositional expressions, such as あるいは...のだろう and あるいは...かもしれない.
3. あるいは...あるいは

content: 高校を卒業した学生たちは、あるいは進学し、あるいは就職し、それぞれの進路を歩み始める。

content.content: Students who have graduated from high school go off on their own ways, with some continuing on to college and some getting a job.

content: 美しかった街路樹も、あるいは横倒しになり、あるいは途中から二つに折れて、台風の威力のすさまじさを物語っている。

content.content: The beautiful trees lining the street have fallen over or been broken in two, attesting to the tremendous power of the typhoon.

content: 風の音は、あるいは泣くが如く、あるいは呻くが如く、高く低く、一晩中谷間に響いた。

content.content: The sound of the wind reverberated across the valley all through the night, sounding sometimes like crying and sometimes like groaning, at times high and at times low.
This is used to describe multiple situations.
In these cases, あるいはis used in the pattern あるいは...し、あるいは...し, as in

content: and
, where more than two actions or states are described in parallel and the meaning is something like “someone is..., and someone is....” In
, it means “sometimes it is..., and sometimes it is....” These are formal expressions used in written language, not in everyday spoken language.

content.content: 【あるまじき...だ】［NにあるまじきNだ］

content: 業者から金品を受け取るなど公務員にあるまじきことだ。

content.content: A public servant should not receive monetary gifts from a business.

content: 酒を飲んで車を運転するなど警察官にあるまじき行為だ。

content.content: His conduct of drinking and driving is unsuitable for a police officer.

content: 「胎児は人間じゃない」などとは、聖職者にあるまじき発言である。

content.content: A priest should never make statements like, “An unborn child is not a human.”

When あるまじきfollows a noun that refers to an occupation or a position, it means “... should not be done by such a person.” Nouns such as こと, 行為, 発言 or 態度 follow. This expression is used to criticize a person’s behavior as being inappropriate for his qualification/position/situation, which is indicated by Nに. This is a formal expression typical of written language.
【あれで】
1. あれで〈positive evaluation〉

content: あの人はいつもきついことばかり言っていますが、あれでなかなか優しいところもあるんですよ。

content.content: He always says harsh things, but actually he is quite a kind person.

content: 彼女、体は小さいけど、あれでけっこう体力はあるのよね。

content.content: Although she has a small build, she is quite strong physically.

content: あのレストランって、一見汚くてまずそうに見えるけど、あれでなかなかいけるんですよ。

content.content: At first glance, that restaurant looks dirty and not so appealing, but it actually is quite nice.

Used with words likeなかなか and けっこう, this expresses an evaluation of something in which there is an unexpected difference between its appearance and its true nature. The evaluation is expressed after あれで. This is used when praising the person or thing that is the topic of the sentence.
2. あれで〈surprise〉

content: あのコート、あれで4万なら安いものだ。

content.content: Forty thousand yen is very cheap for that coat.

content: え、彼女あれでスキー初めてなんですか。すごくうまいじゃないですか。

content.content: Is it really her first time to ski?  She is a very good skier.

content: 今日の食堂の定食、あれでよく改善したって言えるよね。まるで豚のえさだよ。

content.content: Today’s special at the cafeteria was food fit for pigs! How can they say that they’ve improved things?

content: あの映画、あれで（も）アカデミー賞授賞してるんですか。ちょっとひどすぎると思いませんか。

content.content: Did a movie like that win an Academy Award? Don’t you think that’s awful?
In these cases, あれで expresses slight surprise that a person or thing is in a certain state, has value, or can do something. This can be used for positive remarks, as in

content: and
, or for negative remarks, as in
and

content.content: 【あれでも】

content: あの人、患者の話を聞こうともしないで、あれでも医者なのですか。

content.content: That man doesn’t even try to listen to patients. Is he really a doctor?

content: あれでも彼は手伝っているつもりらしいが、かえってじゃまだ。

content.content: He seems to be trying to help me, but instead he’s getting in the way.

content: 子供ならあれでも楽しめるのだろうが、大人にはあんなバカげたゲームはとても耐えられない。

content.content: Although kids might enjoy such stuff, adults can’t stand such ridiculous games.

content: 彼女、あれでもスキー初めてなんですよ。それにしてはうまいでしょ。

content.content: Although you wouldn’t think so, this is the first time for her to ski. She is doing very well in spite of that, isn’t she?

あれでも is used to state the speaker’s opinion that the behavior of someone or the state of something, which is indicated by あれ and known to both the speaker and the listener, is not acceptable or out of the ordinary. It is often linked to the speaker’s criticism of the person or state, and it is often followed by a question or conjecture.
【あんまり】
1. あんまり...ない

content: このごろはあんまり映画を見ていない。

content.content: I haven’t seen a lot of movies recently.

content: 今日はあんまりお金がないのでCDを買うのは今度にしよう。

content.content: I don’t have enough money today, so I’ll buy a CD next time.
An emphatic way to say あまり. It is typical of spoken language.
【あまり】
2. あんまり

content: あんまりおかしくて涙が出た。

content.content: It was so funny that tears came to my eyes.

content: あんまり暑いと何も考えられなくなる。

content.content: I can’t think about anything when it is too hot.

content: 英語が下手だと馬鹿にされるが、あんまり上手だとかえって嫌がられる。ほどほどにできるのがいいようだ。

content.content: People make fun of you if your English is bad, but on the other hand, if it’s too good, then they don’t like you. It seems best if you are just somewhat fluent.
An emphatic way to say あまり. It is typical of spoken language.
【あまり】2a、
【あまり】2c
3. ...なんてあんまりだ

content: 誰も私のことを覚えていてくれなかったなんて、あんまりだ。

content.content: How upsetting that nobody remembered me!

content: A:君は明日から補欠だ。

content.content: You are a substitute player, starting tomorrow.
B:ええっ、監督、それはあんまりですよ。もう一度チャンスをいただけませんか。
What? That’s too much, coach. Please give me one more chance.

content: A:あの人、何をやらせてもミスが多いのよね。この間は大事な書類を電車に置き忘れるし。あの人が辞めてくれれば、もっと何でもスムーズにいくのに。

content.content: She makes so many mistakes in everything I have her do. Last time, she left some important documents on the train. If she quit her job, everything would go much smoother.
B:そういう言い方ってあんまりじゃない。彼女まだ経験も浅いんだし、その割には頑張ってるじゃない。
Isn’t that kind of harsh? She is still inexperienced, but she looks like she’s trying hard.

content: ある日突然解雇するなんて、あんまりと言えばあんまりだが、彼にもそうされるだけの理由があるのだ。

content.content: You could say it’s too much to fire him so suddenly, but there is reason enough for him to be fired.
In some cases, って, は, or とは can be used withあんまりだ instead of なんて. Refers to a preceding statement and expresses a strong protest with the sense of “That’s terrible.” あんまりといえばあんまりだ, in

content: , is an idiom.

content.content: 【いい】
1. いいa. いい〈praise〉

content: そのセーターいいですね。よく似合ってますよ。

content.content: That’s a nice sweater. It suits you very well.

content: A:彼女、新婚旅行ギリシャだって。

content.content: I heard she is going to Greece for her honeymoon.
B:へえ、いいなあ。
Really? That sounds nice.
This is used when one expresses praise or envy. Combines with ね or なあ.
b. いい〈refusal〉

content: A:もう一杯どうですか。

content.content: Would you like another cup of tea?
B:いえ、もういいです。
No, thank you.

content: A:ケーキがあるんだけど食べない？

content.content: Do you want some cake?
B:いや、今はいい。
Not now, thanks.
In these cases, いい is used to refuse an offer. It has the same meaning as けっこうです.
c. いい〈call someone’s attention to something〉

content: いいね、今言ったことは誰にもしゃべっちゃだめだよ。

content.content: Listen, you can’t tell anyone what I said just now.

content: いい、よく見ててね。ここを押すとスイッチが切れるから、それからコンセントを抜いてね。

content.content: OK now, look carefully—pressing here turns it off, and then pull the plug out. Got it?

content: いいか、よく聞け。これからは俺がこのグループのリーダーだ。

content.content: Listen up, everyone. I am the leader of this group from now on.

content: このグラフを見てください。いいですか。これは 2001 年までの世界の人口増加を表したものです。

content.content: Look at this graph, please. All right? This shows the increase in population in the world up to
Pronounced with a rising tone. Used to get the listener’s attention before giving an order or making a strong request, and to make sure that he/she is ready to listen.
d. いいから／いいよ

content: A:私があと3分早く着いていれば乗り遅れることもなかったのですが...。

content.content: If I had arrived just three minutes earlier, we wouldn’t have missed it.
B:もうそのことはいいから。それより今からどうしたらいいかを考えましょう。
Oh, that’s OK. Let’s think about what we should do now.

content: A:あ、タクシー1台来ました。どうぞ乗って下さい。次がいつ来るかもわかりませんし。

content.content: Here comes a taxi. Please take it. I’m not sure when another one will come.
B:いや、いいからどうぞ先に乗ってください。そちらの方が遠いんですから。
No, I’ll be all right, you go ahead. You have to go farther than I do.

content: A:ねえ、そんな道に入って行って大丈夫なの？　迷ったらどうするのよ。

content.content: Hey, is it all right to take such a road? What if we get lost?
B:いいからまかせとけって。こっちの方が近道なんだから。
It’s OK, just leave it to me. This is a shortcut.

content: A:あ、数字の入力はそのキーじゃなくてこっちだよ。

content.content: Wait, you should use this key to enter numbers, not that one.
B:いいから、黙っててよ。
Yes, yes, just shut up.

content: A:私がちゃんと財布を鞄の中にしまっておけば、とられたりはしなかったのよね。クレジットカードだって別のところに入れておくべきだった。ガイドブックにもそうしろって書いてあったし...。私が悪いのよ。

content.content: If I had put my wallet away in my bag, I wouldn’t have had it stolen. I should’ve kept my credit cards in another place. I remember the guidebook said to do that. This is my fault.
B:もういいよ。後悔したって始まらない。
It’s over and done with now. It’s a little late for regrets.
These express “You don’t have to say or think such a thing” about something the other person has said. They have the function of ending discussion and not letting the other person says anything more.

content: , and
are cases when the speaker wants to lighten up the situation, cheer up the other person, or say not to worry.
is a case when the speaker wants the other person to keep quiet because his/her concern is rather too much, and
means “There is no point in saying such a thing.” いいから means “You don’t have to worry about it; just keep quiet,” and it emphasizes putting a stop to the other person’s comments.
悪いことばかり覚えて、お前なんか、そのうち警察に捕まるがいいよ。

content.content: You learn only the bad things—someday the police ought to arrest you.

content: 悪い奴らはみんな悪魔にとりつかれて死んでしまうがいい。

content.content: All evil people should be possessed by a demon and die.
Expresses the speaker’s wish to bestow ill fortune on someone. Used to express criticism, to abuse, or to curse. An old-fashioned way of speaking.
【ていい】
【といい】
【いう】 The honorific form of いうis おっしゃる, and the humble form is 申す.
1. いう〈utterance〉a. ...という

content: みんなには行くと言ったが、やはり行きたくない。

content.content: I told everyone I was going, but I really don’t want to after all.

content: 道子さんは「すぐに行きます」と言いました。

content.content: Michiko said, “I’m coming soon.”

content: 道子さんはすぐに行くと言いました。

content.content: Michiko said that she would come in a moment.
いう is used when someone quotes another person. In quotations, it can be used for a direct quotation of someone’s words, as in

content: , and it can also be used for indirect quotations, as in
and

. In the case of an indirect quotation, the sentence should be in plain form. For asking about someone’s utterance, なんといいましたか or どういいましたか is used, and when a request or an order is quoted indirectly, ...ようにいう is used.

content.content: 【いう】1db. ...といっている

content: 山下さんはまだ決められないと言っている。

content.content: Yamashita-san is saying that he can’t decide yet.

content: みんな、それはめでたいことだと言っている。

content.content: Everyone is saying that it is a happy event.

content: A:この件について、当局はどう言っているのでしょうか。

content.content: What do the authorities say about this matter?
B:原因の分析がすむまで詳しいことは述べられないと言っています。
They say that they cannot explain in detail before they finish analyzing the cause.

content: 私は行きたくないと言っているのに、認めてもらえそうもない。

content.content: Although I’m saying that I don’t want to go, no one seems to take me at my word.

Indicates that a statement still holds true at the present time. It is generally used to quote something a third person has said. When the speaker quotes his/her own words, it is usually a situation where the speaker can’t get someone else to listen to him/her.
c. ...といわれている

content: この泉の水を飲めば若返ると言われている。

content.content: It is said that a person will grow younger by drinking from this spring.

content: この映画は日本映画史上の最高傑作だと言われている。

content.content: People say that this movie is the greatest masterpiece in the history of Japanese cinema.

content: 現在世界に数千万人の難民がいると言われている。

content.content: It is said there are currently tens of millions of refugees in the world.
Used for stating commonly known facts or opinions.
d. V-る／V-ない　ようにいう

content: ここへ来るように言われました。

content.content: I was told to come here.

content: 木村さんにすぐ本を返すように言って下さい。

content.content: Please tell Kimura-san to return the book immediately.

content: もっと静かにするように言いましょう。

content.content: Let’s tell them to be quieter.
Used when quoting a request or an order indirectly.
e. Nをいう

content: おじさんにお礼を言いなさい。

content.content: Say thank you to your uncle.

content: 友達にひどいことを言って嫌われてしまった。

content.content: My friend hates me now for saying something awful to her.
When combined with nouns or noun phrases like お礼, 嘘, or ひどいこと, this means “to say N.” Means to express something in words.
f. Nを...という

content: 彼はその子を妹だと言った。

content.content: He said the child was his younger sister.

content: 先生は私の意見を面白いと言ってくれた。

content.content: My teacher told me that my opinion was interesting.

content: あの人は私のことを馬鹿だと言った。

content.content: That person said that I was foolish.
Expresses an evaluation of or a relation to the person or thing represented by N. Used when quoting another person’s words.
2. ...という〈hearsay〉

content: 彼は卒業後郷里へ帰って母校の教師をしているという。

content.content: I heard that he returned to his hometown after his graduation and is working as a teacher at his old school.

content: その僧が去った後、その国は千年の間栄えたという。

content.content: It is said that the country prospered for a thousand years after the priest was gone.

content: アイルランドに蛇がいないのはセントパトリックが追い払ったからだという。

content.content: People say that the reason there are no snakes in Ireland is that St. Patrick drove them out.

content: この島の人々は黒潮に乗って南方から渡ってきたのだという。

content.content: They say that the people on this island came from the south by sailing along the Kuroshio Current.
Expresses hearsay or oral tradition. However, variants of というsuch as といった and といわないdo not convey the meaning of hearsay, but that of simple utterances. Usually written in hiragana.
3. ...という〈name〉a. NをNという

content: あの人は名前を白山武彦といいます。

content.content: That person’s name is Shirayama Takehiko.

content: あの船の名前は、なんといいますか。

content.content: What is the name of that ship?

content: 私は中山一と申します。どうぞよろしく。

content.content: My name is Nakayama Hajime. Nice to meet you.

content: A:これは日本語でなんといいますか。

content.content: What do you call this in Japanese?
B:扇子といいます。
This is called a sensu(fan).

content: A:すみませんが、お名前はなんとおっしゃいますか。

content.content: Excuse me, but may I ask your name?
B:山田和雄といいます。
My name is Yamada Kazuo.
XをYという or XはYというis used to indicate the name of X or what X is called. なんと in なんといいますか can become なんて in casual spoken language. いうcan be written as 言う, if a Chinese character is used. 申す, in

content: , is a humble expression for いう. おっしゃる, in
, is honorific language.

content.content: b. N（のこと）をNという

content: A:国連のことを英語ではなんといいますか。

content.content: How do you say kokuren in English?
B:United Nationsといいます。
It’s United Nations.

content: 中国語では「さようなら」を「再見」といいます。

content.content: Sayoonara is zài jiàn in Chinese.
N(のこと)をNという is used for restatement. とは or って can be used instead of のことを.
（例）国連って英語ではなんといいますか。
How do you say kokuren in English?
Used in spoken language. Cannot be used for explaining the meaning of words or giving a definition in cases other than a simple restatement.
（×）南風とは南から吹く風といいます。
Minami-kaze is called a wind blowing from the south.
（○）南風とは南から吹く風のことです。
Minami-kaze means a wind blowing from the south.
4. ...というN→
【という2】
5. ...というか→
【というか】
6. ...ということ→
【ということ】
7. ...というと→
【というと】
8. ...というのは→
【というのは】
9. ...というものだ→
【というものだ】
0. ...というより→
【というより】
1. ...といったらありはしない→
【といったらありはしない】、
【といったらありゃしない】
2. ...といったらない→
【といったらない】
3. ...にいわせれば→
【にいわせれば】
【いうまでもない】
1. ...はいうまでもない［Nはいうまでもない］［N　であるのはいうまでもない］［Na　であるのはいうまでもない］［Na　なのはいうまでもない］［A／V　 のはいうまでもない］

content: 全然学校に来なかった彼が卒業できなかったのは言うまでもない。

content.content: For someone like him who never came to school, it goes without saying that he could not graduate.

content: 単位が足りなければ卒業できないのは言うまでもないが、足りていても卒業論文を書かなければ卒業できない。

content.content: It goes without saying that one cannot graduate without enough credits, but even with enough credits, it’s impossible to graduate without writing a thesis.

content: 仕事につけば収入は増えるが自由時間は少なくなるというのは言うまでもないことだ。

content.content: Getting a job increases your income, but it goes without saying that your free time will decrease.

content: 上司にも気に入られ仕事の成績も伸ばしている彼の次期昇進の可能性は言うまでもない。

content.content: He is well-liked by his boss and has really grown the business, so I hardly need to tell you that there’s a very good chance he’ll be promoted in the next quarter.

content: A:彼女、今度パリに出張だそうですよ。彼女ならフランス語も完ぺきだし交渉もうまいし、適任ですよね。

content.content: I heard she is going to Paris on business. With her absolute command of French and skill in negotiating, that’s the perfect assignment for her, you know.
B:ええ、それはもう言うまでもないですよね。
Of course, that goes without saying.
Expresses that the matter at hand is common sense, something obvious, or widely recognized.
2. いうまでもないことだが

content: 言うまでもないことだが、ツアー旅行で勝手な行動をとって何か問題が起こっても、それはその人自身の責任だ。

content.content: Needless to say, it’s the person’s own responsibility if some trouble arises on a tour because he or she acted on his/her own.

content: 言うまでもないことですが、この計画はみなさんの御協力があって初めて成功するものです。

content.content: I hardly need to mention that this plan would never have succeeded without everyone's cooperation from the start.

content: 言うまでもないことだけど、結婚披露宴に白い服を着て行ってはいけないんだよ。

content.content: Sorry, but it’s just a given that you shouldn't go to a wedding reception wearing white.

Used at the beginning of a sentence, this means “although it is not necessary to say this because you already know it.” It is an idiomatic expression used to confirm something that should require no explanation.
3. いうまでもなく

content: 言うまでもなく、私たちをとりまく環境はどんどん汚染されてきている。

content.content: It is needless to say that our environment is getting more and more polluted.

content: 私などが言うまでもなく、彼の芸術的な才能はこれまでの画家には不可能だった新しいものを生み出している。

content.content: I hardly need to tell you that his artistic talent has produced novel works that would previously have been impossible for artists.

content: 日本は高齢化社会になりつつあるが、言うまでもなく国の対応は遅れており、国民は不満を感じている。

content.content: Japan is becoming an aged society, but as you might expect, the government’s countermeasures are lagging behind and citizens are feeling dissatisfied.

Used at the beginning of a sentence or clause, this means “although it is not necessary to say this because you already know it.” It is used before stating something obvious. It may be rephrased as 言うまでもないことだが when used at the beginning of a sentence.
【いか】
1. 数量詞+いか

content: なるべく4人以下でグループを作ってください。

content.content: If possible, please form a group of no more than four.

content: 500 グラム以下のパックは 50円引きです。

content.content: Packs containing 500 grams and under are 50 yen off.

content: 3000 円以下で何か記念品を買うとしたら、どんなものがあるでしょうか。

content.content: If we are to buy some sort of memento for under 3,000 yen, what kind of thing can we buy?
Indicates “the number/amount stated or fewer/less.”
2. Nいか

content: 中学生以下は入場無料です。

content.content: Admission is free for junior high school students and younger.

content: 中型以下の車ならこの道を通ることができる。

content.content: Any vehicle that is medium-sized or smaller can take this road.

content: B4サイズ以下のものでないとこの機械ではコピーできない。

content.content: Unless the paper size is B4 or smaller, you can’t make copies on this machine.
When いか follows a noun that is part of an order or sequence, or shows the degree of some attribute, it indicates something at or below the position or degree of N.
3. Nいかだ

content: おまえはゴキブリ以下だ。

content.content: You are lower than a cockroach.

content: そんなひどい仕打ちをするとは、あいつは人間以下だ。

content.content: To treat someone that cruelly makes him subhuman.

content: まったくあいつの頭ときたら小学生以下だ。

content.content: That guy hasn’t got the brains of a schoolchild!
Asserts that someone or something is lower than the person or thing represented by N. Used when one criticizes or slanders someone.
4. Nいか+数量詞

content: わが社では、社長以下約 300 人が全員一丸となって働いています。

content.content: In our company, everyone—including the president and about 300 employees—has joined forces to work together.

content: 山田キャプテン以下 38 名、全員そろいました。

content.content: Captain Yamada and 38 members—everyone is here.

content: その企業グループは、ABC社以下 12 社で構成されている。

content.content: This corporate group consists of ABC company and twelve other companies.

Used when describing a group that is led or represented by the person or thing referred to by the noun. When N is a person, a job title rather than an individual name is used. Used in written language and formal spoken language.
5. いか

content: 以下同文。

content.content: The rest of the text is the same as in the previous document.

content: 詳細は以下のとおりです。

content.content: The details are as follows.
Refers to the part following the present point in a written text or a speech. Usually used in written language.
【いかなる】Must be followed by a noun. Used in formal written language. In spoken language, どんな is often used instead of いかなる.
1. いかなるN（+助詞）も

content: 彼はいかなる困難にも負けないほど強い精神力の持ち主だった。

content.content: He possessed the strong mental fortitude to overcome any kind of difficulty.

content: いかなる罰則も暴走族の取り締まりには効を奏しなかった。

content.content: Even draconian penal regulations didn’t work well for a crackdown against motorcycle gangs.

content: この制御システムは、いかなる非常事態にも対応できるよう綿密に作られている。

content.content: This control system is precisely designed to deal with any emergency.

content: いかなる賞賛の言葉も彼女の前では嘘になってしまうほど、彼女はすばらしかった。

content.content: She was so wonderful that no words of praise could do her justice.
Means “the most extreme form of N.” Used to emphasize the certainty of the state or situation expressed by the predicate, by emphasizing N.
2. いかなるNでも

content: 絵画というのは、いかなる作品でもそこに作者独自の視点が反映されているものだ。

content.content: In pictures, the creator’s individual viewpoint is reflected in any piece of work.

content: いかなる状況であれ、自分の職務を離れるのは許されないことだ。

content.content: It is not permissible to abandon one’s duty, no matter what the situation.

content: それがいかなる方法であれ、それによって結果的に多くの人が助かるのならやってみるべきではなかろうか。

content.content: No matter what the method is, if it results in helping many people, shouldn’t it be tried?

content: いかなる意見であっても、出されたものは一応検討してみる必要があるだろう。

content.content: Whatever the opinions are, it seems necessary to at least consider each one offered.

In these cases, いかなる is used in the patterns いかなるNでも／Nであれ／Nであっても, which mean “if it is N, then no matter how extreme or unusual it is.” Prefaces the latter half of a sentence and thus emphasizes the assertion in this half.
3. いかなる...とも［いかなるNであろうとも］［いかなるN+助詞+V-ようとも］

content: いかなる状況になろうとも、断固として戦い抜く決意だ。

content.content: I made up my mind to fight it out no matter what became of the situation.

content: 彼なら、いかなる環境におかれようとも自らの道を歩んで行くことができるであろう。

content.content: With him, no matter what kind of environment he’s placed in, he’ll be able to make his own way.

content: いかなることがらが起きようとも、常に冷静に事態を判断する能力を身につけなければならない。

content.content: We have to acquire the ability to coolly judge the situation at all times, whatever may happen.

content: いかなる役割であろうとも、与えられれば誠意を尽くして精いっぱいやるのが私たちの努めだ。

content.content: No matter what our role may be, our duty is to do our very best with all sincerity in whatever we are given to do.
Means “no matter how difficult, extreme, or unusual something is.”
【いかに】Used in written language. In spoken language, どんなに is often used instead of いかに.
1. いかに...か

content: この町がいかに暮らしやすいかは、住んでいる人の表情からもうかがわれる。

content.content: You can tell from the inhabitants’ demeanor just how comfortable it is to live in this town.

content: この仕事がいかに精神的な苦労が多いかが、手伝ってみて初めて実感できた。

content.content: It was only when I started to help with the work that I could actually feel how mentally demanding it was.

content: あの人がいかにつきあいにくい人かおわかりいただけるだろうか。

content.content: Can you understand how difficult it is to get along with that person?

content: 愛する夫を飛行機事故で失って、彼女がいかにつらい思いをしているか、想像しただけで胸が痛くなる。

content.content: It makes my heart ache just to imagine how much she has been suffering since she lost her husband in an airplane accident.
Whenいかに is followed by an adjective, V-やすい, or V-にくい, it means “how much... it is.” It often includes the meaning of an extreme degree.
2. いかに...ても［いかにN／Na　　でも］［いかにA-くても］［いかにV-ても］

content: いかに工夫をこらしても、家族は私の料理には何の関心も示さない。

content.content: My family doesn’t show any interest in my cooking no matter how creative I try to be.

content: いかに精巧なコンピュータでも、しょせん機械はただの機械だ。

content.content: No matter how advanced a computer may be, in the end it is just a machine.

content: いかに歌が上手でも、人をひきつける魅力がなければ歌手にはなれない。

content.content: No matter how well you sing, you have to have the charm to attract people in order to be a professional singer.

content: いかに頭がよくても体が弱くてはこの仕事はつとまらない。

content.content: A person who is in poor health cannot do this work even if he or she is very intelligent.
Means どれほど...でも(no matter how...) and strongly emphasizes the statement that follows.
3. いかに...といっても

content: いかに彼が有能だと言っても、こんな難題を一人で処理することは不可能だろう。

content.content: Even if he is capable, it would be impossible to deal with such a difficult problem by himself.

content: いかに医療技術が進んだと言っても、治療して必ず快復するとは限らない。

content.content: No matter how much medical technology has progressed, not every patient recovers after treatment.

content: いかに彼女が多忙を極めていると言っても、電話1本をかける時間もないということはないだろう。

content.content: No matter how busy she is, that doesn’t mean she hasn’t got the time to make a single phone call.

Means “I recognize such-and-such as a fact, but still....” The second half of the sentence indicates a contradiction with the first half. Used to emphasize the intent of the second clause even after acknowledging the thing stated in the first.
4. いかに...とはいえ

content: いかに家賃が高いとはいえ、こんなに環境がいいのなら納得できるのではないか。

content.content: However high the rent is, wouldn’t you say the great surroundings mean that it’s to be expected?

content: いかに才能のある芸術家であるとはいえ、こんなに難解な作品ばかりでは一般の人には理解してはもらえないだろう。

content.content: However talented an artist he is, with only such esoteric works as these it must be hard for the general public to understand them.

content: いかに国全体が豊かになってきたとはいえ、まだまだ今の生活水準に満足していない人も多いのである。

content.content: However wealthy the whole nation is becoming, there are still many people who are not satisfied at all with their present standard of living.
Same as いかに...といっても. More of a literary expression.
5. いかに...ようと（も）［いかに修飾句+Nであろうと（も）］［いかにNa であろうと（も）］［いかにA-かろうと（も）］［いかにV-ようと（も）］

content: いかに便利な機械であろうと、それを使うことによって手で作る喜びが失われてしまうのだとしたら、使う意味はない。

content.content: However convenient this machine is, there is no sense in using it if it takes away the joy of creating something by hand.

content: いかに困難であろうと、やってみれば何らかの解決策は見えてくるはずだ。

content.content: No matter how daunting it is, if we give it a try some sort of solution is bound to appear.

content: いかにスポーツで体を鍛えようと、栄養のバランスが取れていなければ健康にはなれない。

content.content: No matter how fit he gets by playing sports, he won’t be healthy without maintaining a nutritionally balanced diet.

content: いかに環境保護に努めようと、ゴルフ場を作られてしまえば終わりだ。

content.content: No matter how hard we try to protect the environment, it will come to nothing if the golf course is built.

content: いかにみんなにほめられようと、しょせん素人の作品じゃないか。それにこんな値段つけるなんて信じられないよ。

content.content: No matter how much everyone praises it, it’s just the work of an amateur. I can’t believe it has been priced so high.

content: いかに仕事が苦しかろうとも決して文句を言わない。

content.content: No matter how demanding his work is, he never complains.
Means the same as いかに...ても, but is a rather literary expression.
【いかにも】
1. いかにも　...らしい／...そうだa. いかにもNらしい

content: 今日はいかにも秋らしい天気だ。

content.content: Today feels just like autumn weather.

content: 彼女はいつもいかにも教師らしい服装をしている。

content.content: She always dresses just like a teacher.

content: その家はいかにも旧家らしく、どっしりとした古めかしい作りだった。

content.content: That house was massive and ancient-looking, just as might be expected of a house belonging to an old, established family.
Expresses that “the typical nature or characteristics of N are well-displayed,” or “N is just as N should be.” いかにもemphasizes the meaning of らしい (like).
b. いかにも...そうだ［いかにもNa そうだ］［いかにもA-そうだ］

content: そのサンマはとれたてで、いかにもおいしそうだった。

content.content: The saury was freshly caught and looked really delicious.

content: その映画はストーリーを聞くといかにもおもしろそうなのだが、配役が気に入らないので見に行く気が起きない。

content.content: The story of that movie sounds quite interesting, but I don’t feel like going to see it because I don’t like the cast.

content: 新しい電子レンジはいろいろな機能がついていかにも便利そうだ。

content.content: With all their different functions, the new microwaves are the very picture of convenience.

content: サッカーの試合見物には母はいかにも行きたくなさそうな様子をしていたが、結局一番楽しんでいたのは母だった。

content.content: My mother looked like she wasn’t at all interested in going to watch the soccer game, but in the end she was the one who enjoyed it the most.
When いかにも is followed by the stem of an adjective plus そうだ, it means “as far as I can see, it seems very....” The meaning そうだ is emphasized because of いかにも.
2. いかにも

content: A:結局、この計画が成功するかしないかは、地域の住民の方々がどう反応するかにかかっているわけですね。

content.content: At the end of the day, whether this plan will succeed or not depends on how the local residents react, right?
B:いかにもその通りです。ですから、予測がつかないと言っているのですよ。
That’s just it. That’s why I’m saying we can’t predict the outcome.

content: A:この指輪は特別に作らせたものでございますか。

content.content: Is this the ring that you had specially made?
B:いかにも。宝石のデザインでは右に出るものはいないという優れた職人に頼んだものだ。
That’s right. I ordered it from an excellent craftsman who is second to none at designing jewelry.
Means “that’s true” or “that’s right” and is used to express agreement with the speaker. It is spoken language, but an old-fashioned expression. いかにもin

content: is an old way of speaking used by men, so women and young men seldom use this expression now.

content.content: 【いかん】
1. Nいかん

content: これが成功するかどうかはみんなの努力いかんだ。

content.content: Whether this will succeed or not depends on everyone’s effort.

content: 環境破壊を食い止めることは、私達一人一人の心掛けいかんだ。

content.content: Putting a stop to the destruction of the environment depends on the intentions of each and every one of us.

content: 政治改革の実現は、連立政権の結束いかんにかかっている。

content.content: The realization of political reform depends on the unity of the coalition government.
Means “whether a situation is realized or not depends on such-and-such a matter or state.” It is the same as ...しだいだ.
2. Nいかんで

content: 客の出足いかんでは1週間で上映を打ち切られる可能性もある。

content.content: Depending on the number of moviegoers, there’s a possibility that they’ll stop showing it in a week.

content: あの人いかんで予算は何とでもなる。

content.content: How much of a budget we get will depend on what that person has to say about it.

content: 参加するかどうかはその日の体調いかんで決めさせていただきます。

content.content: I shall decide whether or not to participate depending on how I feel on that day.
Means “depending on such-and-such a matter or state.” It is the same as ...しだいで.
【いがい】
1. ...いがい［Nいがい］［V-る／V-た　いがい］

content: 来週のパーティーには、山田さん以外みんな行くそうです。

content.content: I heard everyone is going to the party next week except Yamada-san.

content: これ以外で／にもっといい辞書はありませんか。

content.content: Do you have another dictionary better than this?

content: 温泉に行ってのんびりする以外にも、何かいい案があったら出してください。

content.content: Please give me any good ideas you have, other than relaxing at a hot spring.

content: 酔っぱらって転んで顔にけがをした以外は、今週は特に変わったこともなかった。

content.content: Besides falling down drunk and bruising my face, there was nothing out of the ordinary that happened this week.
Means “except” or “besides.”
2. ...いがいに...ない［Nいがいに...ない］［V-る／V-た　いがいに...ない］

content: 彼女以外にこの仕事を任せられる人はいない。

content.content: I can leave this work to no one but her.

content: 単語は、自分で努力して覚える以外に、習得の方法はない。

content.content: There is no way to acquire new words other than making the effort to memorize them on your own.

content: スーパーの店員に文句を言った以外には今日は誰とも一言も話さなかった。

content.content: Besides making a complaint to a clerk at the supermarket, I haven’t said a word to anyone today.
XいがいにYないmeans “only X is Y.” It is the same as ...のほかに...ない and ...しか...ない.
【いくら】
1. いくらa. いくら〈question〉

content: この本はいくらですか。

content.content: How much is this book?

content: 東京まで片道いくらですか。

content.content: How much is a one-way ticket to Tokyo?

content: この絵はいくらぐらいかなあ。

content.content: I wonder how much this picture is.
いくら expresses that a price is unknown. It is used for asking the price.
b. いくら〈indefinite〉

content: いくらなら案内してもらってもいいとこちらから先に提示した。

content.content: I told them beforehand how much I was prepared to pay for a guided tour.

content: フリーマーケットに出す品物は、それぞれいくらで売るということを決めてこの書類に金額を書き込んでください。

content.content: Please decide how much you want to charge for each item that you bring to the flea market, and fill in the amounts on this form.

content: いくら持ってきてくれという形で注文しないと、後でまた頼まなければならなくなったりするから、個数を確認してください。

content.content: If you don’t specify in your order how many items you want delivered, you may have to order more later on, so please confirm the number.
In these cases, いくら indicates an indefinite price or amount. It is used when one is not able to say or it is not necessary to say an exact amount.
2. いくらでも

content: ビールならまだいくらでもあるから、安心して飲んでください。

content.content: We still have plenty of beer, so please feel free to drink it.

content: これだけ暇ならいくらでも好きなことができる。

content.content: If I have this much free time, I can do whatever I’d like.

content: あの人の代わりならいくらでもいるから、やめられても全然困らない。

content.content: It’s no problem whatsoever for me if that person quits, because I can find any number of people to take his/her place.

content: いくらでもいたいだけここにいてくれてかまわないよ。

content.content: I don’t mind if you stay here as long as you want.
Expresses that something is unlimited and means “as much as one wishes.”
3. いくらも...ない

content: もうワインはいくらも残っていない。

content.content: There is not much wine left.

content: バスがでるまで時間はもういくらもない。

content.content: There is not much time left until the bus leaves.

content: 駅までは歩いていくらもかからなかった。

content.content: It didn’t take very much time to get to the station on foot.

content: 収入はいくらにもならないが、やることに意味がある。

content.content: Though I don’t get paid much for this, it is a worthwhile thing to do.
Expresses that the amount is very small.
4. いくら...てもa. いくらV-ても

content: いくら練習してもうまくならない。

content.content: I don’t get better however hard I practice.

content: いくら食べても太らない。

content.content: No matter how much I eat, I don’t put on weight.

content: 彼はいくら誘っても一度もパーティーに顔を出してくれない。

content.content: He never shows up at a party no matter how many times I invite him.

content: 私がいくら「お祝いにはバラの花束をあげよう」と言っても、誰も賛成してくれなかった。

content.content: No matter how many times I said we should give her a bouquet of roses to celebrate the occasion, no one would agree with me.
Means “no matter how many/how many times/how hard one does something.” Used for emphasizing degree or extent.
b. いくら...といっても［いくらNaだといっても］［いくらA-いといっても］

content: いくら給料がいいと言っても、残業がそんなに多いのでは就職するのはいやだ。

content.content: However high the salary is, I don’t want to take the job if there is that much overtime work.

content: いくら甘いものが好きだと言っても、一度におまんじゅうを3つは食べられない。

content.content: However much I like sweets, I can’t eat three manjuu(bean-jam buns) at a sitting.

content: いくらここの食べ物がまずいと言っても、生協食堂よりはましだろう。

content.content: However bad the food here is, it would be better than a co-op restaurant.
Means “I acknowledge that..., but still” and is used to emphasize an assertion that follows.
c. いくら...からといって（も）

content: いくら淋しいからと言って、夜中の3時に友達に電話するなんて非常識だ。

content.content: Even if he feels lonely, calling a friend at three o’clock in the morning shows a lack of common sense.

content: いくら体にいいからと言っても、毎日そればかり食べ続けていては病気になってしまう。

content.content: No matter how good it is for your health, you will get sick eating the same thing every day.

content: いくら新しいのを買うからと言っても、何も古いのをすぐに捨ててしまうことはないんじゃないか。

content.content: Even though you’re buying a new one, there isn’t any need to throw away the old one straight away, is there?
Takes the pattern いくらXからといって（も）Y and means “you might think that X leads to the conclusion Y, but that is strange.” Implies a slight criticism and is followed by an objection against Y. In

content: , for example, it is “not common sense” to do Y (calling a friend in the middle of the night) just because of X (being lonely).

content.content: d. いくら...からといっても

content: いくら才能がないからと言っても、10 年もピアノをやっていれば簡単な伴奏ぐらいはできるだろう。

content.content: Although you say that he has no talent at all, if he has been playing the piano for ten years, he should at least be able to play a simple accompaniment.

content: いくら不器用だからと言っても、それだけきれいにセーターが編めれば上出来だ。

content.content: However clumsy you may say you are, knitting that beautiful sweater shows you are pretty good after all.

content: いくら私が料理がうまいからと言っても、プロとは違うんだからそういうこったものは作れませんよ。

content.content: Even though I may be pretty good at cooking, I am not a professional, so I can’t make something as elaborate as that.
Similar to Usage 4c above, with the difference that Y is not explicit. Means something likes “even if X, what follows is (not Y) but Z” and expresses the speaker’s refutation of Y. In

content: , for example, the speaker is saying that even if X (“he has no talent for playing the piano”) is true, it doesn’t follow that “he can’t play the piano” (Y), but that “he should be able to play a simple accompaniment” (Z).

content.content: e. いくらなんでも

content: そういう言い方はいくらなんでもひどすぎるよ。

content.content: There’s no excuse for such a harsh statement.

content: いくらなんでも、その服はお母さんには派手すぎないか。
