content.content: Be that as it may, don’t you think that outfit is too flashy for our mother?

content: この料理はいくらなんでも辛すぎてとても食べられない。

content.content: I don’t care what you think, for me this food is so spicy that there’s no way I can eat it.
An adverbial idiom often used with ...すぎる. Expresses a feeling of criticism, as in “even if I take various circumstances into consideration, it’s still wrong/unusual/beyond common sense.”
5. いくらV-たところで

content: いくらがんばってみたところで結果的には同じことだ。

content.content: No matter how hard you try, you’ll get the same result.

content: いくら隠してみたところで、もうみんなにはばれているんだから仕方がないよ。

content.content: Even if you try to hide the fact, there’s nothing you can do since everyone already knows about it.

content: いくらいいドレスを買ったところで、どうせ着ていくところがないんだから無駄になるだけだ。

content.content: There’s no point in buying such a great dress, since you have no place to wear it.

content: いくら話し合ったところで、彼らは自分の意見を変える気はないんだから、話し合うだけ無駄だ。

content.content: No matter how many times we discuss it, it’s a waste of time because they have no intention of changing their opinion.

When いくらV-たところで is followed by phrases like同じだ, 仕方がない, or 無駄だ, it means “no matter how hard one tries to do something, the situation doesn’t change” or “it’s a waste to work so hard.” This is similar to いくら...ても in Usage 4a, but Usage 5 includes a feeling of resignation because the result of the action will be meaningless. This is used to give advice that “you should not do something because....”
【いけない】→
【てはいけない】→
【なくてはいけない】→
【なければ】2
【いご】
1. Nいご

content: あの事件以後、そこを訪れる人はほとんどいなくなった。

content.content: After that incident, almost no one visits that place.

content: 8時以後は外出禁止です。

content.content: Going out after eight o’clock is not allowed.
Means “after N,” when N indicates a point in time or an event.
2. いご

content: 以後私達はこの問題に関しては手を引きます。

content.content: From now on we are not going to touch anything connected with this problem.

content: 以後この話はなかったことにしてください。

content.content: From now on, please pretend we never had this talk.

content: 以後よろしく。

content.content: We’ll ask you to take over from here.
Means “from this time onward” or “from now on.”
【いささか】
1. いささか

content: 今回の試験は前回に比べていささか難解すぎたように思う。

content.content: I thought the exam this time was a bit too difficult compared to the last one.

content: みんなが自分勝手なことばかり言うので、いささか頭にきている。

content.content: I’m getting a little peeved at everyone only saying such self-centered things.

content: この部屋は事務所にするにはいささか狭すぎるのではないか。

content.content: I wonder if this room is a little too small for an office.
Means “a little” or “somewhat.” It can also be used as an indirect, euphemistic way to say かなり(considerably) or 相当(quite).
2. いささかも...ない

content: 今回の事件には私はいささかも関係ございません。

content.content: I have absolutely nothing to do with this incident.

content: 突然の知らせにも彼はいささかも動じなかった。

content.content: He was completely unfazed by the unexpected news.

content: 彼女は自分に反対する人に対してはいささかも容赦しないので、みんなから恐れられている。

content.content: She never forgives anyone who opposes her, so everyone is afraid of her.
Means “there is not... at all.”
【いざしらず】［Nはいざしらず］

content: 昔はいざしらず、今は会社を 10 も持つ大実業家だ。

content.content: I don’t know about his past, but now he is a business magnate who has ten companies.

content: 両親はいざしらず、我々は兄弟として妹の結婚を許すわけにはいかない。

content.content: I don’t know what our parents think, but as her brothers we can’t allow our sister’s marriage.

content: 幼稚園の子供ならいざしらず、大学生にもなって洗濯もできないとは驚いた。

content.content: I understand that a kindergarten child may not know how to do laundry, but I’m surprised that even a college student doesn’t know how.

content: 暇なときだったらいざしらず、こんなに忙しいときに客に長居されてはたまらない。

content.content: When I have lots of time I don’t mind, but I can’t stand to have long-term guests at such a busy time.

content: 国内旅行ならいざしらず、海外旅行に行くとなると、準備も大変だ。

content.content: Maybe not on a domestic trip, but if you are going on an overseas trip, there will be lots of preparation.

Following a noun plus は, なら, or だったら, いざしらず means “I don’t know/care about such-and-such, but....” Before and after いざしらず there are contrastive pairs, such as “the past and the present,” “a kindergarten child and a college student,” or “free time and busy time.” It is used to express that the matter in the latter half is superior in degree or importance to, or is a special case of, the matter in the first half. In the latter half, an expression of astonishment or something like “it’s a problem” often follows. The expression in

content: is an idiomatic way to say “different from the past.”

content.content: 【いじょう】
1. 数量詞+いじょう

content: 体重が 45 キロ以上なら献血できる。

content.content: If your weight is 45 kilograms or more, you can donate blood.

content: 65 才以上の人は入場料がただになる。

content.content: Admission is free for persons 65 and older.

content: 夏休みの間に食文化に関する本を3冊以上読んでレポートを書きなさい。

content.content: Your summer vacation homework is to read three or more books about food culture and then write a report.
This indicates a number equal to or greater than the figure cited.
2. いじょう　の／にa. ...いじょうのN［N／V　いじょうのN］

content: 自分の能力以上の仕事を与えられるのは悪いことではない。

content.content: It’s not a bad thing to be given a task which exceeds one’s ability.

content: その薬は期待以上の効果をもたらした。

content.content: This medicine was more effective than I’d expected.

content: 彼はみんなが期待している以上の働きをきっとしてくれる人だ。

content.content: He’s a person who will surely work even more than what everyone expects.

content: これ以上のことは今はお話しできません。

content.content: I cannot tell you any more at the moment.

content: 落ち込んでいる友達に対して、私には慰めの言葉をかける以上のことは何もしてあげられない。

content.content: I can do nothing more than give words of comfort to my depressed friend.

content: 新しく入ったアルバイトの学生は、命令された以上のことをやろうとしないのでほとんど役に立たない。

content.content: The new part-time worker, who is a student, doesn’t make any effort to do more than what he’s ordered to, so he’s hardly any use at all.
In these cases, いじょう expresses something which has a higher degree than the thing or action indicated by a noun or a verb.

content: are cases in which something exceeds the upper limit, while
are cases in which the something is the upper limit and is not exceeded.

content.content: b. ...いじょうに［N／V　 いじょうに］

content: あの人は噂以上におっちょこちょいだ。

content.content: That person is even more scatterbrained than I’d heard.

content: 試験の点は想像以上に悪かった。

content.content: The exam score was worse than I expected.

content: 彼女はタイの人なのに、日本人以上に日本の歴史について詳しい。

content.content: Although she is a Thai, she has more knowledge of Japanese history than  Japanese people do.

content: そのレストランはみんなが言う以上にサービスも味も申し分なかった。

content.content: The restaurant had service and food that was even better than what everyone had said.

content: 彼は思っていた以上に神経が細やかでよく気の付く人だった。

content.content: He was more sensitive and considerate than I had thought.

content: ほかの人が練習する以上にやっているつもりなのに、全然ピアノが上達しないのはどういうわけだろう。

content.content: I feel that I practice more than anyone else, so I can’t figure out why my piano playing hasn’t improved at all.
When いじょうに is attached to a noun or verb, it means “more than…” or “…is also quite a high degree, but this is even higher.”
3. これ／それ／あれ　いじょうa. これいじょう+修飾句+Nは...ない

content: これ以上わかりやすいテキストは、今のところない。

content.content: Right now there’s no other textbook that is easier to understand.

content: あれ以上くだらない映画もめったにない。

content.content: You’ll have to go a long way to see a sillier movie than that!

content: あの人以上に賢い人は日本中探してもいないだろう。

content.content: Even if you search high and low in Japan, there is probably no one smarter than that person.
In these cases, いじょう mainly follows これ, それ, or あれ, and it means that the thing referred to is of the highest (a very high) degree. It is the same as 一番...だ.
b. これいじょう...ば

content: これ以上水かさが増すと大変なことになる。

content.content: There will be trouble if the river rises higher than this.

content: これ以上雨が降らなければ、畑の作物は全滅するだろう。

content.content: If we have no more rain from now on, the harvest will be a total loss.

content: それ以上努力してもおそらく何の成果もあがらないと思うよ。

content.content: Even if you work harder, I don’t think there will be any better results.

content: あんな忙しい生活をこれ以上続けたら、きっと彼は体をこわしてしまうだろう。

content.content: He’ll surely damage his health if he continues leading such a busy life.

content: 明日の講演が今日の以上につまらないのなら、行くだけ時間の無駄だ。

content.content: It will be a waste of time to go if tomorrow’s lecture is more boring than today’s.

content: 今以上にいろいろ工夫して料理を作っても、誰もほめてくれなければつまらない。

content.content: Even if you come up with lots of new kinds of cooking, it’s no fun if no one praises you for it.

In addition to これいじょう, それいじょう and あれいじょう are also used, and と, たら, なら, and ても may be used in place of ば. These mean “if or even if a certain state has a higher degree than it has now.” They often include the meaning “even though there’s quite a high degree already.”
c. これいじょうV-て

content: それ以上頑張ってどうなると言うのだ。

content.content: What will become of you if you work harder than now?

content: 彼女、あんなに細いのに、あれ以上ダイエットしてどうするんだろう。

content.content: What does she mean by going on a stricter diet, as thin as she is already?

content: あなた、これ以上お金をためて、いったい何に使おうって言うのよ。

content.content: Tell me, if you save even more money, what are you going to use it for?

いじょうmainly joins to これ, それ, or あれ and means “to do more than the current state.” When it is followed by どうなるのか, どうするのか, 何をするのか, or 何になるのか, it often expresses “it’s useless to do ..., doing... won’t help.”
d. これいじょう...は+否定的表現

content: お互いこれ以上争うのはやめましょうよ。

content.content: Let’s stop this fight here.

content: もうこれ以上今のような忙しい生活には耐えられない。

content.content: I can’t take it if my life gets any busier than it is now.

content: さすが田中さんだ。ほかの人にはあれ以上の発明はちょっとできないだろう。

content.content: That’s exactly what I’d expect from Tanaka-san. It would have been impossible for other people to invent something better than that.

content: 雪もひどくなってきたし、もうこれ以上先へ進むのは危険だ。ここであきらめて下山しよう。

content.content: The snow has gotten even worse, and it’s dangerous to keep on going further. Let’s give up and head back down.

content: A:もっと安くなりませんか。

content.content: Can’t you make it any cheaper?
B:もうこれ以上は勘弁してくださいよ。これでももうほとんどうちの方はもうけがないくらいなんですから。
Please don’t push me any more.  We are hardly making any profit as it is already.
Whenいじょう is joined toこれ, それ, or あれ and is followed by a negative expression like できない, 難しい, 耐えられない, or やめよう, it means that the present state is the highest degree possible and cannot be exceeded.
4. Vいじょう（は）

content: 絶対にできると言ってしまった以上、どんな失敗も許されない。

content.content: Having stated that it can definitely be done, no one will allow any failure.

content: 全員一致で選ばれてクラブの部長になる以上、みんなの信頼を裏切るようなことだけはしたくない。

content.content: Now that I have been unanimously elected to be the head of the club, I don’t want to do anything to betray everyone’s confidence.

content: 大学をやめる以上、学歴に頼らないで生きていける力を自分で身につけなければならない。

content.content: Now that I am dropping out of university, I have to acquire the ability to get by on my own without relying on my academic record.

content: こういうことになってしまった以上、私が責任を取って辞めるしか解決策はないだろう。

content.content: Now that this kind of thing has happened, there is no other solution but for me to take responsibility and quit my job.

content: 私に通訳がちゃんとつとまるかどうかわかりませんが、お引き受けした以上は精一杯の努力はするつもりです。

content.content: I am not sure if I can do well as an interpreter, but I’ll do my best since I accepted the job.

With verbs that indicate an action involving responsibility or resolve, いじょう  expresses “given the circumstances that I have done/will do such-and-such.” In the latter half of the sentence, the speaker indicates his/her determination and intention to take responsibility by using expressions of resolution, warning, obligation, and so on.
5. いじょうa. いじょう（の）　+数量詞／N

content: 田中、木村、山本、吉田、以上の4人はあとで私のところに来なさい。

content.content: The following four persons are to come and see me later: Tanaka, Kimura, Yamamoto, and Yoshida.

content: 東京、大阪、京都、神戸、福岡、札幌、以上6つの都市が今回の調査対象となります。

content.content: Tokyo, Osaka, Kyoto, Kobe, Fukuoka, and Sapporo—these six cities are the survey targets this time.

content: 自分の長所、短所、自慢できること、今一番関心のあること、将来の夢、以上5点をはっきりさせて自己紹介文を書いてください。

content.content: Please write your self-introduction and include these five points: your strengths, your weaknesses, something you take pride in, the thing that most interests you now, and your future dreams.

content: 植物をむやみに採らないこと、火の後始末に気を付けること、トイレはきれいに使うこと、以上のことを必ず守ってキャンプしてください。

content.content: Please follow the rules for camping, which are not to pull up plants recklessly, to make sure all fires are carefully put out, and to keep the bathrooms clean when using them.

content: 発音はきれいか、言語表現は適切か、内容は興味を感じさせるか、訴えたいことははっきり伝わってくるか、以上のような点がスピーチの審査の時におもにポイントとなる。

content.content: Clear pronunciation, proper verbal expression, interesting content, and clear presentation—these are what generally count for the most points when judging a speech.
In these cases, いじょう is used when a series of items is listed and then summarized.
b. いじょう

content: 作業が終わり次第、必ず報告に来ること。以上。

content.content: Be sure to report to me as soon as you finish the work. That’s all.

content: 次の品物を記念品として贈呈します。置き時計一つ、木製本棚二つ、百科事典全 20 巻一式。以上です。

content.content: I will donate the following articles as memorabilia: one table clock, two wooden bookshelves, and a 20-volume set of encyclopedias. That’s all.
Means “that’s all I have to say” or “the end.” Often used for written documents such as official forms or lists.
【いずれ1】
1. いずれ

content: 進学と就職といずれの道を選ぶのがいいか、自分でも決めかねている。

content.content: I can’t decide which choice is better, furthering my education or finding a job.

content: 「はい」「いいえ」「どちらでもない」のいずれかに○をつけてください。

content.content: Please circle one: “Yes,” “No,” or “Neither.”
This is a way of saying どちら or どれ using a form more common in written language. It indicates one selection among two or more choices.
2. いずれにしても

content: 山田は仕事の都合で遅れるとは言っていたが、いずれにしても来ることにはなっている。

content.content: Yamada told me he would be late because of work, but he is going to be coming, at any rate.

content: 後遺症が出る可能性もあるが、いずれにしても回復に向かっていることだけは確かだ。

content.content: There is a chance of lingering complications, but all in all he is definitely recovering.

content: 彼が辞めるのがいいのかどうかはわからないが、いずれにしてもこのまま放っておくわけにはいかない。

content.content: I’m not sure whether he should resign, but anyhow we can’t just leave things as they are.

content: A:ここでついでにお昼ご飯食べましょうか。

content.content: Shall we have lunch here, as long as we’re here anyway?
B:そうですね。いずれにしても、どこかで食べておかなきゃならないんだし。
Yes, let’s. At any rate, we have to have lunch somewhere.

いずれにしても is placed at the beginning of a sentence or clause and expresses  “there are many possibilities to choose from, but anyway no matter which one you choose....” It is used to emphasize that the thing following いずれにしてもis something true or definite. It is used in both spoken and written language. いずれにしろ and いずれにせよ are more formal ways to say this. It can also be reworded as 何にしても.
3. いずれにしろ

content: やりたい仕事はいろいろあるが、いずれにしろこんな不況では希望する職にはつけそうもない。

content.content: There are lots of jobs I want to do, but having said that, I don’t think I will get one that I want in this recession.

content: ちょっと来客があったりするかもしれませんが、いずれにしろこの日なら時間が取れるので大丈夫です。

content.content: We might have a visitor or two in for a while, but even so I can make time for you on that day.

content: もっといい機種が出るまで待ってもいいけれど、いずれにしろいつかはパソコンを買わなければならないのなら、この機会に買ってしまったらどうか。

content.content: It’s OK to wait until a better model comes out, but if you have to buy a computer sooner or later, why don’t you take this opportunity to buy one?
いずれにしろ is a formal way to sayいずれにしても.
4. いずれにせよ

content: 今日はこの問題にはもう触れませんが、いずれにせよ今後も考えていかなければならないとは思っています。

content.content: I won’t talk about this problem anymore today, but at any rate, I am thinking  that it has to be considered in the future, too.

content: 今後誰にこのプロジェクトを任せるかは未定だが、いずれにせよ彼には降りてもらうことに決めた。

content.content: It hasn’t been decided who will be entrusted with this project, but at any rate, I’ve made up my mind to have him step down.
This is a formal way to sayいずれにしても.
5. いずれも

content: ここにございます宝石類は、いずれも最高級品でございます。

content.content: The jewelry here is all of the highest quality.

content: 今日の講演会のお話はいずれも大変興味深いものでした。

content.content: The lectures today were all very interesting.
This is a formal and polite way to sayどちらも or どれも.
【いずれ2】

content: いずれまた近いうちにおうかがいします。

content.content: I shall be visiting again in the near future.

content: 今はよくわからなくても、いずれ大人になればわかる時がくるだろう。

content.content: Even if you can’t understand it now, the time to understand will come when you grow up.

content: その事件については、いずれ警察の方から詳しい説明があることになっています。

content.content: The police will give us a detailed explanation about that incident in due time.

content: いずれこのあたりの山も開発が進んで、住宅地になってしまうだろう。

content.content: At some point the mountains around here will be developed into a residential area.

content: 円高もいずれ頭打ちになることは目に見えている。

content.content: It’s clear to see that the rise in the yen exchange rate will have to peak sometime.

Means at a point sometime in the future. This is used to say that, considering the present situation, the time for something to happen must eventually come, although it is not certain when. This is a somewhat formal expression typical of written language.
【いぜん1】

content: その問題はいぜん解決されないままになっている。

content.content: That problem remains unsolved.

content: 裁判ざたになっているにも関わらず、彼は依然自分は何も知らないと言い張っている。

content.content: In spite of being taken to court, he still keeps insisting that he doesn’t know anything at all.

content: ゴルフ場建設の工事は、依然として再開されていない。

content.content: The construction of the golf course has not resumed yet.
Expresses the state of a situation that hasn’t changed for a long period. Typical of written language. Same as 未だ(に). 依然として (still, as yet) is an idiom.
【いぜん2】
1. いぜん

content: 以前一度このホテルに泊まったことがある。

content.content: I have stayed at this hotel once before.

content: 彼女は以前の面影はまったくなく、やつれてしまっていた。

content.content: She looked haggard, a mere shadow of her former self.

content: 以前から一度あなたとはゆっくりお話ししたいと思っていました。

content.content: For a long time I have wanted a chance to talk with you.

content: 先生は以前にも増してお元気そうで、とても 70 才とは思えないほどだった。

content.content: The teacher appeared in even better health than before, so I could hardly believe he was seventy years old.
In these cases, いぜん means “long before now.” It is a more formal expression than 前 (before).
2. Nいぜん〈point in time〉

content: 彼は予定していたはずの3月 31 日以前に引っ越してしまったので、連絡がつかない。

content.content: He moved before the planned date of the 31st of March, so I can’t get in touch with him.

content: その地方では先週の大地震以前にも何度も小さな地震が起こっていた。

content.content: In that area, there have been small earthquakes many times before the big quake occurred last week.

content: 彼の 20 才以前の作品には他の画家の影響が強く見られる。

content.content: His works before the age of twenty appear to have been strongly influenced by other painters.

content: この間捕まった男は、それ以前にも何回も同じ手口で子供を誘拐していたらしい。

content.content: I heard that the man who was arrested the other day had previously used the same trick a number of times to kidnap children.
This indicates a point in time earlier than the time indicated by N.
3. V-るいぜん

content: 二人は結婚する以前から一緒に暮らしていた。

content.content: The two of them were living together before they got married.

content: 彼は映画監督になる以前は画家だったらしい。

content.content: I heard he was a painter before he became a movie director.

content: 家具を買う以前に、引っ越し先を決めなければ。

content.content: Before buying furniture, I should find a place to live first.

content: 新しい企画を始める以前に、今までのものをもう一度見直してみる必要もあるのではありませんか。

content.content: Don’t we need to re-examine the previous projects before starting a new one?
This means “before a certain event.” It is used to express the time relation between a sequence of events that occur over a long period of time.
（×）私はいつも寝る以前に日記を書く。
I always write in my diary before bed.
4. Nいぜん〈stage〉

content: そんなことは常識以前の問題だ。知らない方がおかしいのだ。

content.content: That’s a matter of common sense. It is strange not to know about it.

content: 挨拶がきちんとできるかどうかは、能力以前の話だ。いくら仕事ができても礼儀を知らないような人はお断りだ。

content.content: Whether or not someone can greet people properly precedes any discussion of ability. No matter how capable someone is, a person who has no manners isn’t needed here.

content: 受験者の動機や目的は面接以前の段階での調査項目だ。面接ではもっとほかのことを質問するべきだろう。

content.content: The examinees’ motivation and aims should have been asked before the interview stage. We should ask them about other things during the interview.

content: まずコンセントを差し込んでから電源を入れるという、使い方以前の常識さえないような人にこの機械を任せるわけにはいかない。

content.content: I cannot entrust this machine to a person who doesn’t even have the common sense to plug it in and turn it on.

Expresses that something hasn’t reached the stage indicated by the preceding noun. Implies that something/someone hasn’t reached the stage that would have been expected under normal circumstances. It is often used to criticize senseless or careless behavior.
【いたって】→
【にいたる】3
【いたっては】→
【にいたる】4
【いたっても】→
【にいたる】5
【いたり】［Nのいたり］

content: このたび我が社の長年の社会奉仕活動に対して地域文化賞をいただきましたことは誠に光栄のいたりに存じます。

content.content: We feel sincerely honored to have received the local culture prize for our company’s long years of community service.

content: このような後援会を開いてくださいまして、感激の至りです。

content.content: I am greatly impressed by the support group you organized for me.

content: お二人の晴れやかな門出をお祝いできて、ご同慶の至りです。

content.content: It is with the greatest happiness that I wish the two of you good luck at the start of your new life together.

With a limited number of nouns, いたり expresses the extremity or maximum extent of something. It is used in very formal greetings, in which it means “It is extremely....” It can also be used with the meaning of “as a result of something,” as below.
（例）彼があなたにずいぶん失礼なことを言ったようですが、若げのいたり（＝若さの結果としてのあやまち）と思って、ゆるしてやってください。
He seems to have said some very rude things to you, but please forgive him as it was all on account of his youthfulness.
【いたる】→
【にいたる】
【いちがいに...ない】

content: 有機野菜が安全だといちがいには言えない。

content.content: I cannot absolutely say that organic vegetables are safe.

content: 私の意見を一概にみんなに押しつけることはできない。

content.content: I can’t force my opinion indiscriminately on everyone.

content: 外国人労働者はどんどん受け入れればいいとは一概に主張できない。

content.content: I cannot insist, without due consideration, that we should accept more and more foreign workers.

content: 彼はまちがっていると一概に非難することもできないのではないだろうか。

content.content: We can’t criticize him wholesale for being wrong, can we?

content: 彼の案にも利点はあるのだから、そんなことはやっても無駄だと一概に決めつけることはできないだろう。

content.content: We can find advantages in his opinion, so we shouldn’t immediately jump to the conclusion that it’s a waste of time to do such a thing.

When いちがいに is followed by an expression denying or negating a possibility, such as できない or 言えない, it means “one cannot do something simply/without consideration for other things/at one’s convenience.” It implies that it is necessary to consider other conditions or situations.
【いちど】
1. いちど　Vと／V-たら

content: タイ料理は一度食べると病みつきになる。

content.content: Once you have tasted Thai food, you will get addicted to it.

content: あの森は一度迷い込んだらなかなか外に出られないらしい。

content.content: I heard that once you get lost in that forest, you can’t find your way out of it easily.

content: あの作家の小説は一度読み始めるとついつい最後まで一気に読んでしまう。

content.content: Once I start to read a book by that novelist, I read to the very end in a single sitting.

content: 一度いいワインの味を知ってしまうと、もう安物は飲めなくなる。

content.content: Once you get to know what a good wine tastes like, you can’t drink a cheap one anymore.
Means “once a person experiences something/is in a certain state, s/he cannot go back to the previous state.”
2. いちど　V-ば／V-たら

content: こんなところは一度来ればたくさんだ。

content.content: It’s enough to come to a place like this only once.

content: 一度こういう苦労を経験しておけばもう安心だ。何があっても耐えられる。

content.content: Once I have experienced such a hardship, I’ll have no worries. I can overcome whatever happens.

content: 一度やり方がわかれば、後は応用がきく。

content.content: Once you understand how to do it, then you can apply it.

Means “once I experience/understand something, that is sufficient/even if something similar happens, things will somehow turn out.” Implies “I don’t need to do it again.” When followed by the description of a continuing state, as in

content: , it can be replaced by いちどVと.

content.content: 【いっこうに】［いっこうに V-ない］

content: 30 分待ったが、彼はいっこうに現れない。

content.content: I’ve been waiting for thirty minutes, but there’s been absolutely no sign of him.

content: 薬を飲んでいるが、熱はいっこうに下がる気配がない。

content.content: I’m taking medicine, but it doesn’t seem like my temperature has gone down at all.

content: 毎日練習しているのに、いっこうに上手にならないのはどういうわけだろう。

content.content: I wonder how come I can’t improve even a little, in spite of the fact that I practice every day.

content: 何度も手紙を出しているのに、彼女はいっこうに返事をよこさない。

content.content: I’ve sent letters to her many times, but she hasn’t written a word back.

Means “not at all” and emphasizes the meaning of negation. Used in situations in which nothing seems to happen, in spite of the fact that a person continues doing something (in the expectation that something will happen). Conveys a feeling of irritation or suspicion about the situation at hand, and is a rather formal expression.
【いっさい】［いっさいない］［いっさい V-ない］

content: 計画の変更はいっさいない。

content.content: The plan will not never be changed under any circumstances.

content: そのような事実はいっさいございません。

content.content: I strongly deny such a “fact.”

content: なにか問題が起こっても、こちらはいっさい責任を持ちませんので、その点御了承ください。

content.content: Even if some problem occurs, we will not assume any responsibility whatsoever for it. I hope we have your understanding on this point.

content: 詳しいことについての説明はいっさいなされなかった。

content.content: There was no explanation at all concerning the details.

content: 彼は料理にはいっさい手をつけず、お酒ばかり飲んでいた。

content.content: He didn’t touch any food at all, he just drank alcohol.
Means “there is not...at all” and emphasizes the meaning of negation. This is the same as まったく...ない and 全然...ない. It is typical of written language.
【いっそ】
1. いっそ

content: こんなにつらい思いをするくらいなら、いっそ離婚してしまいたい。

content.content: I would rather get a divorce than endure unhappiness like this.

content: 彼に見放されるくらいなら、いっそ死んでしまった方がましだ。

content.content: I would rather die than be abandoned by him.

content: 今の職場はストレスがたまるばかりだし、いっそ思い切って転職してしまおうか。

content.content: It’s getting more and more stressful at my present workplace, so shall I take the plunge and change jobs?

content: そんなに住み心地が悪くて困っているのなら、いっそのこと引っ越したらどう。

content.content: Why don’t you move out, if you’re so miserable living in such an uncomfortable place?

content: ステレオは修理に出しても修理代がかさむし、もうこうなったら、いっそのこと新しいのに買いかえた方がいいかもしれない。

content.content: Even if I send my stereo in for repair, it will cost a lot, so now that it has come to this, perhaps I should just buy a new one.

Used with expressions of volition (…よう), demand (…たい), judgment (…べきだ), or persuasion (…たらどうか) at the end of the sentence. Expresses the feeling that one needs to make a great, daring change in order to solve a problem s/he has at that time.  いっそのこと, in

content: , is an idiomatic expression. Typical of spoken language, but slightly old-fashioned.

content.content: 2. よりいっそ（のこと）［N／V　よりいっそ（のこと）］

content: 休職よりいっそ転職を考えてみたらどうですか。

content.content: Why don’t you consider changing jobs rather than taking a leave of absence?

content: 彼に誘われるのを待っているより、いっそのこと自分から誘ってみたらいいんじゃないでしょうか。

content.content: Hadn’t you better invite him, rather than waiting for him to invite you?

content: このステレオはもう古いし、3万も出して直すよりいっそ買いかえた方がいいかもしれない。

content.content: This stereo is very old, so it might be better to buy a new one than to repair it for some thirty thousand yen.

content: 結果をあれこれ思い悩むより、いっそのこと行動に移してしまった方が気が楽になりますよ。

content.content: You’ll feel better if you take some action, rather than worrying about what the outcome might be.

XよりもいっそY expresses the feeling that, when facing a problem, one “gives up on X and dares to do Y.” Expressions of volition (…よう), demand (…たい), judgment (…べきだ), or persuasion (…たらどうか) are used at the end of the sentence.
【いったい】［いったい+疑問表現］

content: いったい彼は生きているのだろうか。

content.content: Is he even alive?

content: 祝日でもないのに、この人の多さはいったい何なのだ。

content.content: What in the world is this crowd, even though it’s not even a holiday?

content: いったい全体何が起こったのか、さっぱり見当がつかない。

content.content: What in heaven’s name happened? I have no idea at all.

content: いったいあいつは今ごろどこで何をしているのだろう。

content.content: Where in the world is he and what is he doing now?
いったい is used in interrogative expressions, and emphasizes the speaker’s feeling of bewilderment. いったい全体 is an even stronger expression.

いったらありはしない

content.content: 【いったらありはしない】→
【といったらありはしない】
【いったらない】→
【といったらない】
【いったん...と】

content: 彼女はおしゃべりな人で、いったん話し出すと止まらない。

content.content: She is a very talkative person; once she starts to talk, she never stops.

content: いったんテレビゲームを始めると2時間ぐらいはすぐに経ってしまう。

content.content: Once I start to play a video game, two hours or so pass very quickly.

content: いったんこの段階まで快復すれば、後はもう大丈夫だ。

content.content: Once you recover to this level, then you’ll be all right.

content: このお菓子はいったんふたを開けるとすぐに湿ってしまうので、早く食べなければならない。

content.content: These sweets get soggy right away once the lid is opened, so we have to eat them quickly.

content: いったんこんなゆとりのある生活に慣れてしまったら、もう前のような忙しい生活には戻れない。

content.content: Once you get used to a laid-back lifestyle like this, you can’t go back to the busy life you used to have.
たら and ば may also be used instead of と. Means that once changes take place, or things begin changing, it is not possible to return to the original state.
【いっぽう】
1. いっぽうa. V-る+いっぽう（で）

content: 自分の仕事をこなす一方で、部下のめんどうも見なければならない。

content.content: On the one hand I do my own work, but on the other I also have to take care of my subordinates.

content: 彼は全面的に協力すると言う一方、こちらが何か頼んでも忙しいからと言って断ってくる。

content.content: Even though he says he will cooperate fully with us, he refuses our requests, saying he is busy.

content: 彼女はお金に困っていると言う一方で、ずいぶん無駄遣いもしているらしい。

content.content: I heard that she says she is strapped for money, yet she seems to waste a lot of it.
いっぽう means “doing one thing in parallel with another” and is followed by an expression of the second activity.
b. いっぽうでは...たほうでは

content: この映画は、一方では今年最高との高い評価を受けていながら、他方ではひどい出来だと言われている。

content.content: This movie received some good reviews as the best of this year, but on the other hand, it was also said to be very badly made.

content: 彼は、一方では女性の社会進出は喜ぶべきことだと言い、他方では女子社員は早く結婚して退職した方がいいと言う。

content.content: He says, on the one hand, that it’s a good thing for women to take part in society, but on the other hand, he also says female employees should get married early and then quit working.

content: 彼女は、一方ではボランティア活動は大事だと言っているが、他方では何かと理由をつけて参加するのを避けている。

content.content: On the one hand she says volunteer activities are very important, but on the other hand, she always has excuses to avoid joining in.

content: 政治に対する関心は、一方では高まっているものの、他方では腐敗しきった政府に対する諦めのムードがまん延している。

content.content: On the one hand interest in politics is growing, but on the other hand, a mood of resignation is spreading with regard to the government, which is totally corrupt.
Describes two opposing matters in parallel. In many cases, いっぽうでは... is followed by a contradictory conjunction such as が, のに, ながら, or ものの.
c. いっぽう

content: 花子はみんなが帰ったあとも毎日残業していた。一方桃子は定時退社し、毎晩遊び回っていた。

content.content: Every day Hanako worked overtime after everyone left. On the other hand, Momoko left the office on time and went out gallivanting every night.

content: 日本では子供を生まない女性が増えている。一方アメリカでは、結婚しなくても子供はほしいという女性が増えている。

content.content: In Japan, the number of women who aren’t having children is increasing. In contrast, in America the number of women who want to have children without getting married is increasing.
Used at the beginning of a sentence or clause. その一方で can be used instead of いっぽう.
（例）土地の値下がりは現状を見ると絶望的だが、その一方で期待できる点もないわけではない。
With respect to the fall in land prices, the present situation appears hopeless, but at the same time, there are some encouraging signs.
2. V-るいっぽうだ

content: 事態は悪くなる一方だ。

content.content: The situation is getting worse and worse.

content: 父の病状は悪化する一方だった。

content.content: My father’s condition kept getting worse.

content: 仕事は忙しくなる一方で、このままだといつかは倒れてしまいそうだ。

content.content: Work is getting busier and busier, and at this rate I can see myself collapsing someday.

content: 最近、円は値上がりする一方だ。

content.content: Recently, the Japanese yen has been rising higher and higher.
Expresses a situation that is rapidly progressing in a certain direction and cannot be stopped. Often used about negative things.
【いつか】
1. いつか

content: 本を読んでいる間にいつか眠り込んでしまったようだ。

content.content: It seems like I dozed off at some point while I was reading a book.

content: いつか雨はやみ、雲の間から日が射していた。

content.content: Before I was aware of it, the rain had stopped and the sun was shining through the clouds.

content: 動物園はいつか人影もまばらになり、閉園のアナウンスが流れていた。

content.content: Before I noticed, there were hardly any people left in the zoo, and there was an announcement about closing time.
Means “before one knows/realizes it.” Often used in written language. いつのまにか is used often in spoken language, and いつしか is a literary expression.
2. いつかV-た

content: いつか見た映画の中にもこんな台詞があった。

content.content: I heard a dialogue like this in a movie I saw once.

content: 彼とはいつかどこかであったことがあるような気がする。

content.content: I feel like I’ve met him somewhere before.

content: この道は前にいつか通ったことがあったね。

content.content: I remember we took this road before.
Used in a sentence about a past event and indicates a point in the past that is indefinite  or cannot be determined exactly.
3. いつか（は）

content: あいつもいつかはきっと自分の間違いに気づくだろう。

content.content: He will surely realize his mistake one day.

content: がんばっていれば、いつかはだれかがこの努力を認めてくれるはずだ。

content.content: Someone will recognize all my effort one day, if I keep doing my best.

content: いつか一度でいいから世界中を放浪してみたい。

content.content: Someday, even just once, I want to try wandering around the world.

content: あの美術館へいつかは行こうと思いながら、全然行く暇がない。

content.content: I always think about going to that art museum someday, but I have no time at all.

When used in a sentence about a future event, いつか（は） indicates a point in the future that cannot be determined exactly. At the end of the sentence, ...するor ...するはずだ, するだろう, したい, or しよう may be used. いつか is frequently used with adverbs such as きっと (surely) and かならず (certainly).
4. いつかのN

content: いつかのセールスマンがまた来た。

content.content: That salesman from the other day came again.

content: 彼はいつかの交通事故の後遺症がいまだにあって苦しんでいるそうだ。

content.content: I heard he is still suffering from the after-effects of the traffic accident he was in before.

content: いつかの件はどうなりましたか。ほら、田村さんに仕事を頼んでみるって言っていたでしょ。

content.content: What happened to that thing from before? Remember, you said that you would ask Tamura-san to do the job.

content: いつかのあの人にもう一度会いたいなあ。

content.content: Someday I really want to meet that person once again.

Indicates a point in the past that cannot be determined exactly. Implies that something happened at that point, but what happened exactly depends on the context. For example, “the salesman from the other day” has many possible meanings, such as “he came / he talked with me / he called me” the other day.
【いつしか】

content: いつしかあたりは薄暗くなり、人影もまばらになっていた。

content.content: Before I knew it, it had become dark and I could hardly see anybody.

content: 山もいつしか紅葉に染まり、秋が深まっていた。

content.content: The next thing we knew, the trees on the mountains had turned color, and autumn was at its peak.

content: いつしか雨も止んで、空には虹がかかっていた。

content.content: The rain had stopped before I knew it, and a rainbow spanned the sky.

content: 去年まいた種がいつしか芽を出し、中にはつぼみをつけているものもあった。

content.content: The seeds I sowed last year had sprouted before I was aware of it, and some of them even had buds.
いつしか is an emphatic way to sayいつか and means “without realizing it, before one is aware.” It is written language and is often used in literary works.
【いつか】1
【いない】［数量詞+いない］

content: 10 人以内なら乗れます。

content.content: The passenger limit is ten persons.

content: おやつは 500 円以内で買いなさい。

content.content: Don’t spend more than 500 yen on snacks.

content: 10 分以内に戻ってくるので、待っていてください。

content.content: Please wait here, and I’ll be back in no more than ten minutes.

content: ここから2キロ以内でどこか広くて安いアパートはありませんか。

content.content: Are there any cheap and spacious apartments within two kilometers of here?
Means “within that range, including that number” or “that number is the upper limit and should not be exceeded.”
【いまごろ】
1. いまごろになって

content: 注文していた本が、今ごろになってやっと届いた。

content.content: It’s taken until now for that book I ordered to finally arrive.

content: 今ごろになってチケットを予約しようと思ってももう遅いよ。

content.content: It’s too late to book a ticket now.
Means “now,” but is used in situations in which the realization of a matter or the performance of an action is too late.
2. いまごろ　V-ても／V-たところで

content: 今ごろ佐藤さんに電話しても、もううちを出ているのではないだろうか。

content.content: Even if I call Sato-san now, I suppose he’ll have already left home.

content: 君ねえ、今ごろ来ても遅いよ。もう仕事はすんでしまったよ。

content.content: It’s too late to come now. The job is already finished.

content: 今ごろがんばってみたところで、もう結果は変わらないだろう。

content.content: However hard you try now, the result will not change.

content: 今ごろ行ってみたところで、もう食べ物も残っていないだろうし、行くのはよそう。

content.content: Even if we go now, there probably won’t be any food left or anything, so let’s not go.
Like いまごろになって, this means it’s too late or useless to take a particular action at the present time.
【いまさら】
1. いまさら

content: もうその問題は解決済みなのに、今さらどうしようというのですか。

content.content: This problem has already been resolved, so what else do you want to do about it now?

content: 今さら何が言いたいのだ。

content.content: After all that, what do you want to say now?

content: 今さら謝ってももう遅いよ。

content.content: It is too late to apologize to me now.

content: 結婚して何を今さらという感じだが、私は来月から料理学校に通うことにした。

content.content: It seems like it’s quite overdue, since I’m already married, but I’ve decided to go to cooking school starting next month.

Means “now; at this late hour.” Used when someone reintroduces a topic that has already been concluded or a problem that has already been resolved. Often used to criticize the person who tries to bring up the matter again or continue the debate. 何を今さら, in

content: , is an idiom which conveys the feeling that “the time to do such-and-such has already passed.”

content.content: 2. いまさらV-てもいまさらV-たところで

content: 今さら文句を言われてもどうしようもない。

content.content: I can’t do anything about it, even if someone complains now.

content: 今さら勉強しても、試験にはとうてい間に合わない。

content.content: I won’t get good results on my exams, even if I start studying now.

content: 今さらいやだと言ったところで、しなくてすむわけではない。

content.content: Even if you say you don’t want to do it, there’s no way to get out of it now.

content: 今さら隠してみたところで、もうみんな知っているんだから、この場できちんと婚約発表したらどうだ。

content.content: Even if you try to keep it a secret now, everyone already knows, so why don’t you announce your engagement properly here and now?
Means “it’s too late to do... now.” In many cases, it appears in combination with a negative expression and forms the pattern いまさら...ても...ない.
3. いまさらながら

content: 今さらながら彼の賢さには感心する。

content.content: I have renewed admiration for his intelligence.

content: 祖父が亡くなって1年たつが、今さらながらもっと長生きしてくれたらよかったのにと残念に思う。

content.content: It has been one year since my grandfather died, and now more than ever I feel regret that he didn’t live longer.

content: 先生は本当に親身になって心配してくださったんだなあと、今さらながらありがたく思う。

content.content: Now more than ever, I appreciate how my teacher was so warm and concerned about me.

content: あいつは本当にいつもへまばかりしていてどうしようもない奴だったが、今度の事件で今さらながらあいつの馬鹿さ加減にあきれている。

content.content: He’s always been a truly hopeless bungler, but after this incident, I am all the more appalled at the extent of his stupidity.
When いまさらながらis followed by an expression of emotion, such as ありがたい or 残念だ, it means that one’s feeling about something has been reinforced by a recent event.
4. いまさらのように

content: そういえば昔はここでよく友達と鬼ごっこをしたなあと、今さらのようになつかしく思った。

content.content: Come to think of it, I now remember fondly that I used to play tag with my friends here.

content: 昔の写真を見ると、当時の苦労が今さらのことのように思い出される。

content.content: Looking at the old pictures, I am now reminded of the hard times of those days.

content: 母はお前も地元で就職すればよかったのにと、今さらのように言う。

content.content: My mother still tells me that I should have found a job in my hometown.
When いまさらのように is followed by an expression like 思う, なつかしむ, or 言う, it means that a feeling about an old matter or something that was finished or forgotten has been brought back.
今さらのことのように is also used, as in
【いまだ】
1. いまだに

content: あの人いまだに病気で寝込んでるんだって。

content.content: I heard that person is still sick in bed.

content: その喫茶店は客もめっきり減ってしまったが、いまだにがんばって経営を続けている。

content.content: The number of customers who come to that coffee shop has sharply decreased, but it’s still hanging in there and staying in business.

content: 彼はいまだに大学のジャズ研究会に籍をおいて、活動を続けているそうだ。

content.content: I heard he is still continuing his activities as a member of the university jazz club, even now.

content: 祖父が亡くなって7年もたつというのに、いまだに祖父宛の年賀状が何通か届く。

content.content: We still receive a few New Year’s cards for my grandfather, although it’s been seven years since he died.
When いまだに is followed by an affirmative expression, it means that a state is continuing, although it should have changed. Typical of written language. Means the same as 今でも and まだ.
2. いまだ（に）V-ない

content: 行方不明の二人の消息は未だにつかめていない。

content.content: There is no news about the two missing persons yet.

content: 申し込んでから1ヶ月以上たつのに、未だに連絡が来ない。

content.content: It’s been more than one month since I applied, but I haven’t gotten any reply yet.

content: 今回の催しはもう日程まで決まっているのに、内容については未だ何の具体案も出されていない。

content.content: Even though the schedule for the next event has already been decided, there are no definite plans yet regarding the details.

content: 本来ならもうとっくに完成しているはずなのですが、工事は未だに中断されたままで、再開のめども立っていません。

content.content: According to the original schedule, it should have been completed long ago, but the construction is still on hold and there is no prospect of restarting it.

When いまだ is followed by a negative expression, it means that something hasn’t happened yet in reality, although it actually should have happened. Indicates a gap between expectation and reality, and emphasizes a more unexpected feeling than まだ. Has the feel of written language.
【いまでこそ】［いまでこそ　...N／...Na　だが］［いまでこそ　...A／...V　が］

content: 二人は今でこそ円満に暮らしているが、結婚当初は毎日喧嘩が絶えなかった。

content.content: The two of them live in harmony now, but they quarreled constantly at the beginning of their marriage.

content: 今でこそこの仕事に全力を尽くしているが、以前は何度やめようと思ったかしれない。

content.content: Now I’m doing my best at this job, but I can’t remember how many times I thought about leaving before.

content: いまでこそ留学も珍しくないが、お父さんが子供の頃は、留学など夢のまた夢だった。

content.content: It’s not uncommon to study abroad now, but when our father was a child, studying abroad was just a pipe dream.

content: 今でこそ何度も海外旅行をすることも当たり前になっているが、つい 10 年ほど前までは、一生に一度新婚旅行で行くのがやっとという感じだった。

content.content: Now it’s common to travel abroad any number of times, but until about ten years ago it was something you could do maybe once in a lifetime on a honeymoon trip.
Means “though everyone thinks it’s a matter of course nowadays.” Followed by an expression indicating that “the situation in the past was totally opposite to what it is now.”
【いまに】

content: あんなに働いていたら、あいつは今に過労で倒れるだろう。

content.content: He will collapse from overwork any day now if he keeps working like that.

content: 田中さんも今にすばらしい小説を書いてくれると信じています。

content.content: I believe Tanaka-san too will write a wonderful novel someday soon.

content: 見ていてごらんなさい。今にここの海も汚染されて魚も採れなくなりますよ。

content.content: You wait and see. Pretty soon the sea here will be polluted and we won’t be able to catch fish any more.

content: いたずらばかりしていると、今にひどい目に会うぞ。

content.content: If you keep getting into mischief, one day soon you’ll be in big trouble.

content: 今に見ていろ。きっと大物になってみせる。

content.content: You’ll see. I will become a big shot.

Means “one of these days.” Used when one conveys with confidence an expectation that something will happen in the near future. When it is directed at the listener, it expresses encouragement, advice, or a warning. The expression in

content: is an idiom used to express a challenge to someone.

content.content: 【いまにも】［いまにもV-そうだ］

content: 今にも雨が降りそうだ。

content.content: It looks like it’s going to rain any minute.

content: 彼女は今にも泣き出しそうな顔をしていた。

content.content: She looked like she was about to cry.

content: 「助けてくれ」と彼は今にも死にそうな声を出した。

content.content: He sounded like he was nearly dying when he groaned, “Help me.”

content: 嵐はますます激しくなり、小さな船は今にも沈みそうに波にもまれていた。

content.content: The storm was getting stronger, and small boats, tossed about by the waves, looked like they were about to sink.
Means that a certain situation looks like it’s going to be realized any minute. Used in situations that are quite urgent.
【いまや】

content: 彼女は今や押しも押されもせぬ花形スターだ。

content.content: She is now a popular star with an established reputation.

content: 今や時代は物より心である。

content.content: Now it is the age of the heart, not of material things.

content: 5年前はこのワープロも最新機種だったが、今やこんなのは無用の長物だ。

content.content: This word processor was the latest model five years ago, but now something like this is useless.

content: 昔は新婚旅行と言えばハワイだったが、今やトルコやエジプトも珍しくない。

content.content: In the old days, if you said “honeymoon” it meant a trip to Hawaii, but these days it’s not uncommon to go to Turkey or Egypt.
Means “at the present time.” Used to say that an old state or situation is over and done with, and the current state/situation is completely different and new.
【いらい】
1. いらいa. Nいらい

content: あれ以来彼女は姿を見せない。

content.content: She hasn’t shown up since then.

content: 先週以来ずっと会議続きで、くたくたに疲れきっている。

content.content: I’ m exhausted from the continuous meetings since last week.

content: 母は、去年の入院以来気弱になってしまった。

content.content: My mother has become shy and diffident since her time in the hospital last year.
When いらい follows a noun that indicates a certain point in time or an event, it means “the whole time from then until now.”
b. V-ていらい

content: 夏休みに風邪で寝込んで以来、どうも体の調子が悪い。

content.content: I haven’t felt well since I was in bed with a cold during summer vacation.

content: インドから帰ってきて以来、彼はまるで人が変わったようだ。

content.content: It’s as if he has become another person since he came back from India.

content: スポーツクラブに通うようになって以来、毎日の生活に張りが出てきた。

content.content: Since I began to go to the athletic club, I find everyday life is getting more enjoyable.

content: この家に引っ越して以来、毎日のようにいたずら電話がかかる。

content.content: Since I moved to this house, I have been getting crank calls almost every day.
Means “the whole time from when an event happened in the past to the present time.”  Not used for the recent past.
（×）弟は夕方うちに帰ってきて以来、部屋に閉じ込もったきりだ。
Since my brother came home this evening, he has shut himself up in his room.
（○）弟は先月イギリス出張から帰ってきて以来、忙しくて毎晩夜中まで帰ってこない。
Since my brother came back from his business trip to England last month, he has been too busy to come home until late at night.
c. V-ていらいはじめて

content: 引っ越してきて以来、初めて隣の人と言葉を交わした。

content.content: It was my first time to exchange words with my neighbor since I moved in.

content: 大学に入って以来、初めて図書館を利用した。

content.content: This was my first time to use the library since I started university.

content: この冬になって以来初めての寒波で、死者が6人も出た。

content.content: Six lives were lost in the first cold wave of this winter.
Expresses that something has occurred for the first time after quite a long time/since a certain point in the past.
2. Nは、...いらいだ［Nは、Nいらいだ］［Nは、V-ていらいだ］

content: お会いするのは、去年の9月以来ですね。

content.content: We haven’t met each other since last September.

content: 海外旅行はおととしトルコに行って以来だ。

content.content: I haven’t traveled abroad since I went to Turkey the year before last.

content: 数学の問題を解いたのは大学入試以来のことだから、もう何年ぶりになるだろうか。

content.content: I haven’t solved any math problems since my university entrance exam, so I wonder how many years it’s been.

content: 郷里に帰るのは、7年前に祖父の法事に出た時以来なので、町はかなり様子が変っていた。

content.content: I hadn’t returned to my hometown since I went to my grandfather’s memorial service seven years ago, so the town had changed a lot.
When いらいだ follows words that express a point in the past or a past event, it expresses that a long time has passed since.
【いわば】［いわばNのような］［いわばVような］

content: 彼女の家は石造りの洋館で、いわばドイツのお城のような造りだった。

content.content: Her house was a European-style building made of stone, in the style of a castle in Germany, as it were.

content: 多くの若者に慕われている彼は、いわば悩み多き人々を救済する神様だ。

content.content: He endears himself to many young people, as if he were a god who helps people with many worries.

content: そんな商売に手を出すなんて、いわばお金をどぶに捨てるようなものだ。

content.content: If you dabble in such a business, it will be just like throwing your money down the drain.

content: この小説は、いわば現代の源氏物語とでもいったような作品だ。

content.content: This novel is, in a manner of speaking, a modern-day The Tale of Genji.

content: コンピュータ・ネットワークは、いわば脳神経のように地球全土に張り巡らされていると言ってもいいだろう。

content.content: We can say that a computer network is, as it were, like a network of cranial nerves stretching out over the entire earth.

Means “so to speak” or “figuratively speaking.” Used to give a figurative example in order to explain something clearly. Combines with nouns and verbs which refer to well-known things and situations that can be easily imagined. Has the flavor of written language.

content: is a case in which ような is omitted, and
is a case in which ように is used and a predicate follows.

content.content: 【いわゆる】［いわゆるN］

content: これがいわゆるエスニック料理というものですか。

content.content: Is this what’s called ethnic cuisine?

content: 彼女はいわゆる普通のOLで、役職に就きたいなどとは考えたこともなかった。

content.content: She is a so-called “office lady,” an ordinary working woman, and she had never thought that she wanted to be promoted to a managerial position.

content: 彼も、いわゆるワールドミュージックのブームに乗って、世界的に売れるようになった歌手の一人だ。

content.content: He is one of the singers who became popular all over the world by getting on the so-called world music bandwagon.

content: A:うちの大学、最近またアメリカの大学と姉妹校になったんです。これで8校目ですよ。

content.content: Recently, my university became a sister school with another university in America. This is our eighth partner school.
B:ああ、いわゆる「大学の国際化」というやつですね。そういうのが国際化だと思っている人が、まだたくさんいるんですねえ。
Oh, yes, it’s what they call “the internationalization of universities.” There are still lots of people who regard things like that as internationalization.
Means “it is generally called....” Used to explain something clearly using everyday words. There are cases, as in

content: , in which it conveys that the expression or concept in question is unfavorable to the speaker.

content.content: 【うえ】
1. Nのうえで（は）

content: 暦の上ではもう春だというのに、まだまだ寒い日が続いている。

content.content: It is still cold, even though it is already spring according to the calendar.

content: データの上では視聴率は急上昇しているが、周りの人に聞いても誰もそんな番組は知らないと言う。

content.content: The data show that the ratings for this TV program are skyrocketing, but when I ask people I know about it, they say they’ve never heard of it.

content: その公園は地図の上では近くてすぐ行けそうに見えるが、実は坂がたくさんあってかなり行きにくい場所なのだ。

content.content: That park looks close and easy to get to on the map, but actually there are lots of hills, so it’s not a place you can get to easily.

content: 間取りは図面の上でしか確認できなかったが、すぐにそのマンションを借りることに決めた。

content.content: I decided immediately to rent this apartment, even though I was only able to check the layout by looking at the floor plan.
When うえで follows a noun that refers to something in written form, such as data or a map, it means “according to that information.”
2. V-るうえで

content: パソコンを買う上で注意しなければならないことは何ですか。

content.content: What do we have to be careful about when buying a computer?

content: このプロジェクトを進めていく上で障害となるのが、地元の住民の反対運動だ。

content.content: One obstacle to proceeding with this project is the opposition movement among local residents.

content: 女性が結婚相手を選ぶ上での重要なポイントとして、「三高」ということが言われていた。

content.content: It used to be said there were “three highs” (three important points) for women when choosing a marriage partner.

content: 留学生を実際にホームステイさせる上で、おそらく今までに予想もしなかった問題がいろいろ出てくるものと思われますので、そのための相談窓口を設けました。

content.content: When we actually place foreign students with homestay families, it’s possible that a variety of unforeseen problems may arise, so we’ve set up a counseling service to deal with them.
Means “in the case of/in the process of doing something.” Used to describe a problem or point to be aware of.
3. V-たうえで

content: では、担当の者と相談した上で、改めてご返事させていただきます。

content.content: Well then, after speaking to the person in charge, I’ll contact you again.

content: 一応ご両親にお話しなさった上で、ゆっくり考えていただいてけっこうです。

content.content: At any rate, after you’ve talked to your parents, you can take some time to think about it.

content: 金を貸してやると言ったのは、お前がちゃんと職についてまともな生活に戻った上でのことだ。働かないで遊んでばかりいるやつに金を貸すわけにはいかない。

content.content: When I said I’d lend you the money, I meant I'd give it to you if you found a regular job and went back to a proper lifestyle. I can’t lend money to a guy who doesn't work for a living and just fools around all the time.
Means “first do the action indicated by the verb.” Followed by an expression that means “do the next action, based on the result of the first.”
4. V-る／V-た　うえは

content: やると言ってしまったうえは、何がなんでもやらなければならない。

content.content: Since I said I’ll do it, I have to do it no matter what.

content: 留学を決心した上は、少々のことがあっても一人で乗り越えていけるだけの強さを養ってほしい。

content.content: Since you have decided to study abroad, I want you to develop the strength to overcome any little difficulties you may encounter, on your own.

content: みんなに期待されて出馬する上は、どんなことがあっても当選しなければならない。

content.content: When I run for election, as everyone expects, no matter what happens, I must get elected.

content: 他の仲間を押しのけてレギュラーメンバーになる上は、必ず得点してチームに貢献してみせる。

content.content: Now that I have pushed other members out of the way to become a regular, I am determined to make a contribution to the team by scoring points.

うえは follows words that express an act involving some kind of responsibility or resolution and means “because one does/did such-and-such an act.” Followed by an expression that means “based on that, one must take appropriate action.” Same as …からには and …以上は. A formal expression.
5. ...うえ（に）［Nであるうえに］［Na なうえに］［A／V　うえに］

content: 今年は冷夏である上に台風の被害も大きくて、野菜は異常な高値を記録している。

content.content: It’s been a cold summer, and in addition, there’s been a lot of damage from typhoons this year, so vegetable prices have been unusually high.

content: 彼女は、就職に失敗した上、つきあっていた人にもふられて、とても落ち込んでいた。

content.content: She was very depressed about failing to find a job, and on top of that, the person she was going out with broke up with her.

content: その選手は日本記録も更新した上に銀メダルももらって、自分でも信じられないという顔をしていた。

content.content: After he set a new Japanese record and, in addition, won a silver medal, the athlete looked like he himself could not believe it.

content: 彼は博士号を持っている上に教育経験も長い。周囲の信頼も厚く教師としては申し分のない人だ。

content.content: Along with a doctorate, he has a long career in teaching, too. He is also highly trusted by those around him, so he is perfect as a teacher.

content: その壁画は保存状態がいい上に図柄もこれまでにない大胆なもので、考古学者たちの注目の的となっている。

content.content: That mural is well-preserved, and besides, the pattern is bold and unlike any other found to date, so it has become the focus of archeologists’ attention.

content: 今年は冷夏であり、そのうえ台風の被害も大きくて、野菜は異常な高値を記録している。

content.content: It’s been a cold summer, and in addition, there’s been a lot of damage from typhoons this year, so vegetable prices have been unusually high.

content: このあたりは閑静なうえに、駅にも近く住環境としては申し分ない。

content.content: This is perfect area to live in, as it is quiet and close to the station.

うえ（に）indicates that a certain state or event coincides with or happens in addition to another state or event. When it is used after a noun, the noun takes the form Nである／だった／であった. そのうえ is used at the beginning of a sentence or a clause, as seen in
【うち】
1. うち〈limit〉a. Nのうち

content: この三曲のうちでどれが一番気に入りましたか。

content.content: Of these three songs, which one did you like best?

content: 三つのうちから好きなものを選びなさい。

content.content: Choose the one you like out of these three.

content: バッハとモーツァルトとベートーベンのうちで、一番人気があるのはやはりモーツァルトだそうだ。

content.content: I heard that, as might be expected, among Bach, Mozart, and Beethoven, the most popular composer is Mozart.

content: 昨日買ったCDのうち、2枚はインドネシアのポップスで、3枚はカリブの音楽だ。

content.content: Of the CDs I bought yesterday, two are Indonesian pop music and three  are Caribbean music.
Nのうち is used to delimit a range. It can be replaced by Nのなか, as in

content: , when someone is choosing something within that range. In some cases, N1とN2と...のうち is used to list a series of nouns, as in

content.content: b. ...うちにはいらない［Nのうちにはいらない］［A-いうちにはいらない］［Vうちにはいらない］

content: 通勤の行き帰りに駅まで歩くだけでは、運動するうちに入らない。

content.content: Just walking to the station on the way to and from the office is not exercise.

content: 5分やそこら漢字の練習をしたって、それではやったうちに入らない。

content.content: Doing kanji drills for five minutes or so doesn’t really count as practice.

content: ラーメンを作るのが得意だなんて、そんなの料理のうちに入らないよ。

content.content: You said you’re good at making raamen(Chinese noodles), but that doesn’t count as cooking.

content: 彼はきびしい教師だと評判だが、宿題を忘れた生徒を廊下に立たせるぐらいなら、特にきびしいうちには入らないと思う。

content.content: Everyone says he’s a strict teacher, but if all he does is make students who forgot their homework stand in the hallway, I don’t think that makes him so strict.
Means “such-and-such is not included in a certain range, cannot be regarded as belonging to a certain group because it is insufficient.”
2. うち〈time〉a. ...うちに［Nのうちに］［Na なうちに］［A-いうちに］

content: 朝のうちに宿題をすませよう。

content.content: Let’s finish our homework during the morning.

content: 朝のすずしいうちにジョギングに行った。

content.content: I went jogging in the morning while it was still cool.

content: ここ数日のうちには何とかします。

content.content: I’ll do something about it within the next few days.

content: ひまわりは留守のうちにかなり大きくなっていた。

content.content: The sunflowers grew very big while I was away.

content: 父親が元気なうちに、一度一緒に温泉にでも行こうと思う。

content.content: I think I’ll go to a hot spring with my father once while he is still in good health.

content: 電車が出るまでまだ少し時間があるから、今のうちに駅弁を買っておいたらどう？

content.content: Since we still have a little time before the train leaves, shall we buy some box lunches now?
うちに is used with expressions that indicate duration over an interval of time and means “while that state continues” or “within that period of time.” 今, in

content: , indicates not a point in time but “a length of time until a change takes place in the present situation.”

content.content: b. V-ている／V-る  うちに

content: 彼女は話しているうちに顔が真っ赤になった。

content.content: She turned red while she was speaking.

content: 手紙を書いているうちに、ふと彼が今日こっちに来ると言っていたことを思いだした。

content.content: As I was writing a letter, suddenly I remembered that he said he was coming here today.

content: 読み進むうちに次第に物語にのめり込んでいった。

content.content: I gradually became more and more absorbed in the story as I went on reading it.
Means “while one is …ing.” Followed by an expression indicating the occurrence of an event or a change. V-ている is used more than V-る, but the pattern V-るうちに is sometimes used.
c. V-ないうちに

content: 知らないうちに隣は引っ越していた。

content.content: My neighbor had moved away before I noticed.

content: あれから10分もしないうちにまたいたずら電話がかかってきた。

content.content: I received another crank call again within ten minutes after the first one.

content: 暗くならないうちに買い物に行ってこよう。

content.content: I’ll go shopping before it gets dark.

content: お母さんが帰ってこないうちに急いでプレゼントを隠した。

content.content: I hid the present quickly before my mother came home.
Means “while the state of something not having happened continues.” When the speaker knows that the state will change later on, as in

content: and
, V-る前に can be used instead.

content.content: d. V-るか V-ないうちに

content: 夕食に手をつけるかつけないうちに、ポケットベルで呼び出された。

content.content: Just as I had started to eat dinner, I was paged.

content: 朝まだ目がさめるかさめないうちに、友達が迎えにきた。

content.content: My friend came to pick me up in the morning when I was just waking up.

content: その手紙の最初の一行を読むか読まないうちに、もう何が書いてあるのかだいたい分かってしまった。

content.content: I already knew more or less what was written in the letter even before I’d finished reading the first line.
In this pattern, the same verb is repeated and the meaning is “when I’d started doing something but almost no time had yet elapsed.”
e. ...うちは［Nのうちは］［Na なうちは］［A-いうちは］［V-る／V-ている　うちは］［V-ない　うちは］

content: 明るいうちはこのあたりはにぎやかだが、夜になると人通りもなくなり、一人で歩くのは危ない。

content.content: It’s busy around here while it’s light, but after dark when there are few people on the street, it’s dangerous to walk around alone.

content: 記憶力が衰えないうちは、何とか新しい外国語も勉強できるだろう。

content.content: I’m sure I can learn a new foreign language somehow or other, before my memory starts to go.

content: 息子が大学生のうちは私も生きがいがあったが、就職して家から出て行ってしまってからは毎日がむなしい。

content.content: I had something to live for while my son was a university student, but after he left home to begin working, I have been feeling empty every day.

content: 父は働いているうちは若々しかったが、退職したとたんに老け込んでしまった。

content.content: My father was young and vibrant while he was working, but as soon as he retired, he suddenly aged.

content: 体が健康なうちは健康のありがたさに気づかないが、病気になってはじめてそれが分かる。

content.content: We don’t appreciate the value of our health while we still have it, it’s only after we get sick that we start to appreciate it.
Means “while a certain state continues without change.” Often used to compare this state with another that will arise (or has arisen) after the first one ends (or has ended).
f. ...うちが［Nのうちが］［Na なうちが］［A-いうちが］［V-る／V-ている　うちが］［V-てない　うちが］

content: 若いですねと言ってもらえるうちが花だ。

content.content: The best time in life is when people tell you how young you are.

content: 天体写真は雲が出ていないうちが勝負だ。

content.content: It’s crucial to take photographs of the night sky while there aren’t any clouds.

content: どんなに苦労が多くつらい毎日でも、生きているうちが幸せなのであって、死んでしまったら元も子もない。

content.content: No matter how hard and painful every day might be, to be alive is to be happy. If we die, that’s the end of everything.

content: いくら福祉施設が充実しても、やっぱり人生は体が丈夫なうちが楽しい。

content.content: No matter how much social welfare institutions improve, I think life is only enjoyable as long as we are in good health.

content: 人生、若いうちが花だ。

content.content: Youth is the best time of life.
When うちが is followed by words like 花だ, 勝負だ, いい, or 幸せだ, it means “the time that a certain state continues without change is good, valuable, or important.”
g. そのうち→
【そのうち】
【うる】［R-うる］

content: 彼が失敗するなんてありえない。

content.content: It’s impossible for him to fail.

content: それは彼女になしえた最大限の努力だったに違いない。

content.content: It must been the best effort that she could put forth.

content: その絵のすばらしさは、とても言葉で表しうるものではない。

content.content: It can’t be described in words how wonderful that picture is.

content: 確かに外国人労働者が増えればそういう問題も起こり得るだろう。

content.content: If the number of foreign workers increases, those kinds of problems might possibly occur, too.

content: 彼の自殺は誰もが予期し得なかったことだけに、そのショックは大きかった。

content.content: No one could have expected his suicide, so it was a great shock to us.

content: 彼の仕事ぶりには失望の念を禁じ得ない。

content.content: I cannot help being disappointed with his way of working.

うる joins to a verb stem. Both うる and える can be used in the dictionary form, but in the masu-form, negative form, and ta-form, only えます, えない, and えたare used. These expressions mean “one can do a certain action” or “it is possible that a certain situation will be realized.” In the negative, it means “one cannot do an action” or “it is impossible for a situation to be realized.” V-れる indicates potential, as in 書ける and 読める, and is only used with volitional verbs. うる, on the other hand, can also be used with non-volitional verbs, as in

content: and
. However, unlike V-れる, it cannot be used to express an ability.

content.content: （×）彼はフランス語が話しうる。
He is possible to speak French.
（○）彼はフランス語が話せる。
He can speak French.
Generally considered to be written language, but ありえない can also be used in daily conversation.
【える】

content: 21 世紀には人が月で生活することもありえるかもしれない。

content.content: It may be possible that people will live on the moon in the twenty-first century.

content: 私一人の力ではとてもなしえないことでした。

content.content: I could never have done it alone.
【うる】
【お...いたす】［おR-いたす］［ごNいたす］

content: お食事をお持ちいたしましょうか。

content.content: Shall I bring you your meal?

content: お名前をお呼びいたしますので、それまでここでお待ちください。

content.content: Please wait here until I call your name.

content: のちほどこちらから改めてご連絡いたします。

content.content: I will contact you again later.

content: それではレセプション会場の方へご案内いたします。

content.content: Allow me to take you to the reception hall.

content: 今回の件につきましては、皆様の納得の行くまでご説明いたしたいと存じます。

content.content: I would like to explain this matter to everyone’s satisfaction.
お...いたす is used with a verb stem or a noun of Chinese origin that indicates an act. When it is used with a noun of Chinese origin, it often takes the form ごNいたす, as in

content: , and
. This is a politer, more humble way to sayお...する. The masu-form is usually used.

content.content: 【お...いただく】［おR-いただく］［ごNいただく］

content: 今日は遠いところをわざわざお集まりいただきましてありがとうございます。

content.content: Thank you very much for coming all the way here today.

content: ここにお名前とご住所をお書きいただいて、あちらの窓口へお出しください。

content.content: Please fill in your name and address here, and take it to the teller’s window over there.

content: お忙しいのにご連絡いただき、まことに恐縮しております。

content.content: Thank you so much for contacting me even though you are so busy.

content: ご住職にご教示いただいた禅の心を、これからは生活の中で実践していきたいと思います。

content.content: What I have learned from the master about the spirit of Zen, I will put into practice from now on in my daily life.

content: 《案内状》先生にはぜひご出席いただきたく、お知らせ申し上げます。

content.content: 《in a written invitation to a teacher》This is to let you know about this event, with the sincere hope that you will be able to attend.

お...いただくis used with a verb stem or a noun of Chinese origin that indicates an act. Although it is a humble expression, like ていただく, it is more polite and formal than the latter. In the case of action nouns of Chinese origin, such as 連絡(する), 教示(する), and 出席(する) in

content: , and
, ごNいただくis usually used. However, in the case of 電話(する), お電話いただく is used.

content.content: 【お...ください】→
【お...くださる】
【お...くださる】［おR-くださる］［ごNくださる］

content: 今日お話しくださる先生は、東西大学の山川先生です。

content.content: The professor who will speak today is Yamakawa-sensei from Tozai University.

content: 今日ご講演くださる先生は、東西大学の山川先生です。

content.content: The professor who will give today’s lecture is Yamakawa-sensei from Tozai University.

content: お忙しいのにおいでくださって、本当にありがとうございます。

content.content: Thank you very much for coming, despite your busy schedule.

content: 大した料理ではございませんが、どうぞお召し上がりください。

content.content: It is not a grand feast, but please enjoy your meal.
お...くださる is used with a verb stem or a noun of Chinese origin that indicates an act. It is an honorific expression, like てくださる, but more polite and formal. For action nouns of Chinese origin, as in

content: , the pattern ごNくださるis often used, but in the case of 電話する, お電話くださる is used. お R-ください can be used for polite suggestions, as in

content.content: 【お...する】［おR-する］［ごNする］

content: 先生、お荷物をお持ちします。

content.content: Sir, I’ll bring your baggage.

content: 部長をお宅まで車でお送りした。

content.content: I took the department head home in my car.

content: ご注文の品をお届けしました。

content.content: We have delivered the goods you ordered.

content: お部屋へご案内しましょう。

content.content: I’ll show you to your room.

content: あとでこちらからご連絡します。

content.content: We will contact you later.
Used with either verb stems or nouns of Chinese origin that express an action. A humble expression that means “the speaker does something for someone.” With nouns of Chinese origin, as in

content: and
, usually the form ごNする is used. However, in the case of 電話する (to telephone), お電話する is used. Like
, the form おR-します can be used to offer to do something for someone. お...いたす is a more polite expression.

content.content: 【お...です】［おR-だ］［ごNだ］

content: 林先生は信州に別荘をお持ちだそうですよ。

content.content: I heard that Hayashi-sensei has a vacation home in Shinshu.

content: 今年の夏休みはどちらでお過ごしですか。

content.content: Where are you going to spend your summer vacation this year?

content: 昨日は大阪にお泊まりでしたか。

content.content: Did you stay in Osaka last night?

content: 《ファーストフードの店で》こちらでお召し上がりですか。

content.content: 《at a fast-food restaurant》Is this to stay?

content: 原田部長は明日からご旅行で2週間いらっしゃらないそうです。

content.content: I heard that Mr. Harada (the department head) will be away on a trip for two weeks starting tomorrow.

content: お宅のご主人は本社にご栄転だそうですね。

content.content: I’ve heard that your husband is going to be promoted to the head office.
Used with either verb stems or nouns of Chinese origin that express an action. When used with nouns of Chinese origin expressing an action, as in

content: and
, it usually takes the form ごNだ. It is an honorific expression, like お...になる, but the range of words that can be used with お...です is limited and this expression is more idiomatic.

content.content: 【お...なさい】→
【なさい】
【お...なさる】［おR-なさる］［ごNなさる］

content: あの先生がお話しなさったことは、多くの人たちにとって生きていく心の支えとなるだろう。

content.content: What the teacher said will be a real comfort to many people in their lives.

content: ケニアへはいつご出発なさるんですか。

content.content: When are you going to depart for Kenya?

content: 今度あなたがその方達とお食事なさるときにでも、一度ご一緒させていただけるとうれしいのですが。

content.content: I would be delighted if I could accompany you sometime when you have dinner with them again.

content: どうぞ、お食べなさい。

content.content: Please go ahead and eat. (Please help yourself.)

content: 明子、自己紹介なさい。

content.content: Akiko, introduce yourself.

Takes either verb stems or nouns of Chinese origin that express an action. An honorific expression, like おR-になる. When used with a verb stem in expressions like お話しなさる ((someone of higher status) speaks) or お食べなさる ((someone of higher status) eats), it sounds a little old-fashioned. When used with a Chinese-origin noun, as in

content: , it usually takes the form ごNなさる. When used with なさい (do something, imperative), as in
and
, it is a polite imperative. However, in this case it is not used when talking to a person of higher status.

content.content: 【お...になる】［おR-になる］［ごNになる］

content: 村田さんはもうお帰りになりました。

content.content: Murata-san has already gone home.

content: このさし絵は山本さんご自身がお描きになったそうです。

content.content: I heard that Yamamoto-san drew this illustration himself.

content: 今度大阪においでになる時には、ぜひうちにお泊まりになってください。

content.content: When you come to Osaka next time, please stay at my house.

content: どうぞ、おかけになってください。

content.content: Please take a seat.

content: 野村先生は 1972 年に京都大学をご卒業になりました。

content.content: Nomura-sensei graduated from Kyoto University in

content: ご家族の方は半額の会費ですべてのスポーツ施設をご利用になれます。

content.content: Family members can use all sports facilities at half the membership price.
Takes either verb stems or nouns of Chinese origin that express an action. An honorific expression. When used with nouns of Chinese origin, as in

content: and
, it usually takes the form ごNになる. However, the range of words with which it can be used is limited. When used with てください, as in
, it becomes a polite suggestion or recommendation.

content.content: 【お...ねがう】［おR-ねがう］［ごNねがう］

content: 明日うかがいたいと、山田さんにお伝え願えますか。

content.content: Could you tell Yamada-san that I’d like to visit him tomorrow?

content: 来月のシンポジウムにご出席願いたいのですが、ご都合はいかがでしょうか。

content.content: I’d like to ask you to attend the symposium next month. Do you think you might be available?

content: 何か一言お話し願うことになるかもしれませんので、そのときはよろしくお願いします。

content.content: I may have to ask you to say a few words later, so I would appreciate it if you could do so.

content: 係員の指示を守っていただけない場合は、ご退場願うこともあります。

content.content: If you do not follow the directions of the person in charge, you may be asked to leave.

content: ご起立願います。

content.content: Please stand up.
Combines with either verb stems or nouns of Chinese origin that express an action. Used to ask someone to do something. As in

content: and
, it often appears in request forms such as 願えますか (Can I ask...?) or 願いたいのですが (I would like to ask...). When used with nouns of Chinese origin, as in
and
, it usually takes the form ごNねがう. It is a formal expression.

content.content: 【おいそれと（は）...ない】［おいそれと（は）V-れない］

content: 子供を産んだばかりの母ネコにはおいそれとは近づけない。

content.content: We can’t easily get close to a mother cat that has just had kittens.

content: 君ならできるとおだてられても、あんな大役は責任も重いし、おいそれとは引き受けられない。

content.content: Even though you flatter me that I can do it, I can’t easily undertake such an important task with so much responsibility.

content: 当時は大変な不景気で、大学を出たからといっておいそれと就職できるような時代ではなかった。

content.content: Those were really hard times, so even if someone had graduated from a university, it was not easy to get a job.

content: お礼にと言ってお金を差し出されたが、何か下心がありそうなので、おいそれと受け取るわけにはいかなかった。

content.content: They offered me money to show their gratitude, but I couldn’t easily accept it, because they seemed to have some kind of ulterior motive.

Means that, for some reason, an action can’t be easily done. Used with sentence-final expressions such as the negative form of the potential V-れる and indicates that the action expressed by a verb is impossible. Sometimes おいそれと...する modifies nouns, such as 時代 in

content: . In that case, too, the noun is followed by a negative expression. V-るわけにはいかない, as in
, expresses impossibility.

content.content: 【おいて】

content: この研究分野の第1人者ということなら、加藤先生をおいてほかはないでしょう。

content.content: If we were to name the leading expert in this research field, it would be none other than Kato-sensei (Professor).

content: 何をおいても期日には間に合わせなければならない。

content.content: Above all else, I have to meet the deadline.
【をおいて】
【おうじて】→
【におうじて】
【おかげだ】→
【おかげで】［Nのおかげで］［Na　な／だった　おかげで］［Aおかげで］［V-たおかげで］

content: あなたのおかげで助かりました。

content.content: Thanks to you, I survived.

content: 祖父は生まれつき体が丈夫なおかげで、年をとっても医者の世話にならずにすんでいる。

content.content: Thanks to being born with a strong constitution, my grandfather can get by without a doctor’s care in spite of his old age.

content: あなたが来てくれたおかげで、楽しい会になりました。

content.content: Because you came, the party turned out to be a lot of fun.

content: A:お子さんのけがはどうですか。

content.content: How is your child’s injury?
B:おかげさまで、だいぶ良くなりました。
Thank you, it is almost healed.

content: まったく、君に頼んだおかげでかえってややこしいことになってしまったじゃないか。

content.content: Honestly, thanks to your help, things just ended up getting more complicated.

content: 今年は夏が涼しかったおかげで冷房はほとんど使わずにすんだ。

content.content: Because of the cool weather this summer, we hardly had to use the air conditioner at all.
Expresses a reason or cause for a positive outcome. In the case of a negative result, ...せいで is used.
（例）あなたのおかげで成功した。
I succeeded, thanks to you.
（例）あなたのせいで失敗した。
I failed because of you.
When another person’s action is referred to, the forms V-てくれたおかげで or V-てもらったおかげで are often used. おかげさまで in

content: is an idiomatic expression of appreciation. V-たおかげで is sometimes used with irony, as in

content.content: 【おきに】［数量詞+おきに］

content: 大学行きのバスは 10 分おきに出ている。

content.content: The buses to the university run every ten minutes.

content: この薬は2時間おきに飲んでください。

content.content: Please take this medicine every two hours.

content: この道路には 10 mおきにポプラが植えられている。

content.content: On this street, poplars have been planted at intervals of ten meters.

content: このあたりは高級住宅街で、2軒おきぐらいに外車を持っている家がある。

content.content: This area is an upscale residential district, and every third house or so has an imported car.

content: 映画館に入ると、座席は一つおきにしかあいていなかったので、友達とは離れて座ることになった。

content.content: When we got into the theater, every other seat was taken, so my friend and I ended up sitting separately.
Usually follows a word expressing time or distance and means “with that amount of time or space in between.” The words used with おき in

content: and
don’t express distance, but they do refer to things arranged in a line (houses
, seats
) and are interpreted to express distance. When おきに refers to a point in time or space, as in
, it can be replaced with ごとに. However, when おきに and ごとに are used to refer to the number one, they differ in meaning, as shown in the examples below.

content.content: （例）1年おきに大会が開かれる。（2年に1回）
The meeting is held every other year.  (= once every two years)
（例）1年ごとに大会が開かれる。（1年に1回）
The meeting is held every year.  (= once a year)
【おそらく】

content: おそらく彼はそのことを知っているだろう。

content.content: Probably he knows that.

content: 相手チームはおそらくこちらのことを何から何まで詳しく調べているだろう。

content.content: I suppose the opposing team will have researched us in detail.

content: 台風 12 号は、おそらく明日未明には紀伊半島南部に上陸するものと思われます。

content.content: Typhoon No.12 is expected to make landfall on the southern Kii Peninsula before dawn tomorrow.

content: おそらくは首相も今回の事件に関わっているにちがいない。

content.content: I’d say the prime minister also has to be involved in this affair.

Combined with sentence-final suppositional expressions such as ...だろう or ...にちがいない, おそらく expresses the speaker’s supposition. It is used when a supposition is highly certain. It is also used in the form おそらくは, as in

content: . It is a formal expression, and たぶんand きっと are used more often in casual conversation.

content.content: 【おそれがある】［Nのおそれがある］［V-るおそれがある］

content: 今夜から明日にかけて津波の恐れがあるので、厳重に注意してください。

content.content: From tonight until tomorrow, there is a possibility that a tsunami may occur, so please take all necessary precautions.

content: 再び噴火する恐れがあるため、警戒区域の住民に避難勧告が出された。

content.content: Since there is a risk that the volcano may erupt again, an advisory was issued for local inhabitants within the danger zone to evacuate.

content: 親鳥に気付かれる恐れがあることから、撮影チームはそれ以上巣に近づくことをあきらめた。

content.content: Because there was a possibility that the parent birds might notice them, the camera crew gave up approaching the nest any more closely.

content: ハリケーンの被害が拡大する恐れが出てきたため、大統領は各国に緊急援助を求める予定である。

content.content: Since there is a danger that the hurricane damage may become even more extensive, the president is planning to seek emergency assistance from each country.

Expresses the possibility that an undesirable event will happen. Similar expressions include 危険がある (there is a danger) and 不安がある (there is a fear). A formal expression often found in written language. Commonly used in television news, newspaper commentaries, and so on.
【おなじ】
1. ...とおなじ［Nとおなじ］［Vのとおなじ］

content: このステレオはうちのと同じだ。

content.content: This stereo is the same as ours.

content: この本はあの本と出版社が同じだ。

content.content: This book has the same publisher as that one.

content: この点で妥協することはすべてをあきらめるのと同じことだ。

content.content: Compromising on this point is tantamount to abandoning everything.

content: あの人が食べているのと同じものをください。

content.content: Please give me the same thing that person is eating.

content: ヒンディー語は英語と同じインド・ヨーロッパ語族の言語だ。

content.content: Hindi is an Indo-European language, just like English.
Means that two objects or things are equivalent.
2. おなじV-る　なら／のだったら

content: 同じ買うなら、少々高くても長持ちするものの方がいい。

content.content: If I am going to buy one, I want something that lasts for a long time, even if it is a little more expensive.

content: 久しぶりの旅行なんだから、同じ行くんだったら思い切って遠くに行きたいな。

content.content: This is my first trip in a while, so as long as I’m going, I want to take the plunge and travel somewhere really far away.

content: 同じお金をかけるのなら、食べてなくなるものでなく、いつまでも使えるものにかける方が意味があると思う。

content.content: If I’m going to spend the money, I think it makes more sense to spend it on something I can use for a long time rather than something to eat, which doesn’t last.

content: A:一緒にフランス語か何か習いに行かない？

content.content: Shall we take French classes or something together?
B:そうねえ、フランス語もいいけど、同じ習うんだったら人のやってないような言語の方がいいと思わない？
Well, sure, French would be fine, but if we’re going to study a language, don’t you think it would be better to study one that no one else does?
Means “as long as one is going to do a particular thing.” When there are many ways to do something, this pattern is used to state the best way. Similar to どうせなら and せっかくなら.
【おぼえはない】
1. V-られるおぼえはない

content: きみにそんなひどいことを言われる覚えはない。

content.content: I don’t remember doing anything that would make you say something so awful to me.

content: おまえになぐられる覚えはない。

content.content: I don’t remember doing anything to make you hit me.

content: あなたのように冷たい人に「冷淡だ」などと非難される覚えはありません。

content.content: There is no reason why I should be called “heartless” by such a cold person as yourself.
