Follows the passive form V-られる. Refers to an action of the person spoken to and means “I don’t remember doing anything that would make you take such an action.” A feeling of criticism is implied.
2. V-たおぼえはない

content: 彼があんなに怒るようなことを言った覚えはないんだけど。

content.content: I really don’t remember saying anything to make him so angry.

content: A:この間の1万円、早く返してもらえませんか。

content.content: About the 10,000 yen I lent you the other day... could you pay me back sometime soon?
B:何のことですか。私はあなたにお金を借りた覚えはありませんが、他の人と間違えているのではないですか。
What? I don’t remember borrowing money from you. Aren’t you confusing me with someone else?

content: こちらは山田にいじめられた覚えはないのだが、山田は「いじめて悪かった」と謝ってきた。

content.content: I don’t remember being bullied by Yamada, but Yamada apologized for bullying me.
Means the speaker has no recollection of an event or experience. Often used when the speaker is criticized and wants to justify him/herself.
【おまけに】

content: あたりはすっかり暗くなり、おまけに雨まで降ってきた。

content.content: It has gotten dark, and on top of that, it has started raining.

content: 友達の引っ越しを手伝いにいったら本人は風邪がひどくて重い荷物を運ばされ、おまけに掃除までやらされた。

content.content: When I went to help my friend move, he had a bad cold, so I was the one who ended up carrying all the heavy items and, what’s more, doing the cleaning afterwards.

content: きのう、おばさんに映画に連れていってもらって、おまけに夕食までごちそうになった。

content.content: Yesterday, my aunt took me to a movie and then even treated me to dinner.

content: 彼は背が高くて、ハンサムでユーモアがあって、おまけに金持ちときては、女性にもてるわけだ。

content.content: He is tall, handsome, has a sense of humor, and what’s more, he is well off. No wonder he is very popular with women.

content: 洋子はかわいいし、明るいし、おまけにやさしいから、だれにでも好かれる。

content.content: Yoko is cute, cheerful, and kind as well, so everyone likes her.
Indicates the addition of one more item or attribute to several others that are similar. A casual expression used in spoken language that means “besides, in addition to.” おまけに...まで in

content: , and
expresses an intensified degree.

content.content: 【おもう】
1. ...とおもうa. ...とおもう

content: 今日は雨が降ると思います。

content.content: I think it’ll rain today.

content: 山田先生は来ないと思う。

content.content: I think Yamada-sensei won’t come.

content: あの人のやり方はひどいと思います。

content.content: I think the way he does things is awful.

content: 彼の言ったことはうそだと思う。

content.content: I feel what he said was a lie.

content: 確か、机の上に置いたと思う。

content.content: I’m sure I put it on the desk.

content: あなたには幸せになってほしいと思うから、あえてこういうきつい忠告をするのです。

content.content: I want you to be happy, so that is why I am giving you such stern advice.

content: こんな忙しい会社にいつまでもいては過労死しかねないと思って、思いきって転職することにした。

content.content: I thought there was a real chance of dying from overwork if I stayed at such a busy company, so I took the plunge and changed jobs.

Follows a clause and indicates that the content of the clause is the speaker’s subjective judgment or personal opinion. When used in an interrogative sentence, its function is to ask for the listener’s personal judgment or opinion . When used in the dictionary form (と思う) or masu-form (と思います) as a declarative statement, the subject is always the speaker and never another person. For example, in

content: the person doing the thinking is 私 (I), not 山田先生 (Yamada-sensei). If the speaker wishes to say that the person doing the thinking is 山田さん, then use of the form 思っている is required, as in 山田さんは（田中さんが来ない）と思っている (Yamada-san thinks that (Tanaka-san will not come)). However, 思う can refer to a third person’s judgment when it is used in ta-form, as in the example below.

content.content: （例）山田さんは来ないと思った。
I thought Yamada-san wouldn’t come./Yamada-san thought (someone else) wouldn’t come.
In this case, the original sentence can be interpreted as either “I thought Yamada-san wouldn’t come” or “Yamada-san thought (someone else) wouldn’t come.”
b. ...とおもっている

content: 私は自分のしたことが正しいと思っている。

content.content: I think what I did was right.

content: イギリスに留学してよかったと思っている。

content.content: I feel that studying in the U.K. was very good for me.

content: 警察はあの男が犯人だと思っている。

content.content: The police think that man is the culprit.

content: その実力で合格できると思っているの。

content.content: Do you really think your ability can get you a passing grade?

Follows a clause and expresses an opinion, judgment, or belief on the part of the speaker or another person. The difference between 思っている and 思う (see Usage 1a above) is that 思う is interpreted to mean that the speaker’s judgment has been made on the spot, while 思っている implies that someone has held a certain opinion or belief from some point in the past until the present. Also, 思っている can express the opinion or judgment of another person, as in

content: and
, while 思うcannot.

content.content: c. ...とおもわれる

content: このままの状態では環境汚染は進む一方だと思われる。

content.content: There is reason to believe that if things are left as they are, environmental pollution will only get worse.

content: 私にはこのことが正しいとは思われません。

content.content: This doesn’t seem right to me.

Means “a certain judgment is formed spontaneously.” Used when stating an opinion objectively rather than arbitrarily, or for softening the impact of an assertion. Often used in academic papers, lectures, and other kinds of written language. と can be replaced by ように to form the expression ように思われる.
2. ...とはおもわなかった

content: まさか今日あの人が来るとは思わなかった。

content.content: I never thought that person would come today!

content: こんな街中にこんな静かな公園があるとは思わなかった。

content.content: I didn’t expect there to be such a quiet park like this right in the middle of downtown.

content: 独身寮の部屋は狭いとは聞いていたが、こんなに狭いとは思わなかった。

content.content: I’d heard that the rooms in the singles dormitory were small, but I never imagined they would be this small.

content: いつも反抗的なお前がそんなに素直に謝るとは思わなかったな。

content.content: I never thought that someone as contrary as you would apologize so sincerely.

content: A:引っ越し先のおとなりが田中さんだなんて思ってもみませんでしたよ。奇遇ですね。

content.content: I never imagined that I was moving in next to you, Tanaka-san. What a coincidence!
B:いや、ぼくも隣に越してくるのが君だとは思わなかったよ。
Well, I never thought you were the person moving in next door either!
Means that the speaker views a situation or event as completely unexpected. Usually implies a feeling of surprise.
3. R-たいとおもう

content: アメリカに留学したいと思います。

content.content: I want to go to the U.S. to study.

content: 結婚式には是非参加したいと思っております。

content.content: I’d very much like to attend your wedding ceremony.

content: 一流会社に就職したいと思っている。

content.content: I’d like to work for a top-ranked company.

content: では、ご一緒に乾杯をしたいと存じます。

content.content: I would now like to ask you all to join me in a toast.

思う is combined with ...たい, which expresses a wish or desire on the part of the speaker, to soften the directness of the ...たい expression and make the statement more polite. 存じます can be used instead of 思う／思います, as in

content: , to create an even politer expression. Sentence-final use of ...たい（です） gives an impression of childishness and is not appropriate in formal conversation among adults, in which case たい is usually followed by 思う or のだ.

content.content: 4. ...おもう［Na におもう］［A-くおもう］

content: 先生に指導していただけることになって、本当に幸せに思います。

content.content: I am very happy to have the opportunity to be instructed by you.

content: バスが全然来ないので、不思議に思って聞いてみたら、昨日からダイヤが変わったとのことだった。

content.content: I wondered why there were no buses coming, so I asked, and they said that the bus schedule had changed starting yesterday.

content: この度の突然のご逝去をまことに辛く悲しく思います。

content.content: I am deeply grieved to hear of his sudden death.

content: お会いできてうれしく思います。

content.content: It was very nice to have the chance to see you.

content: このような賞をいただくことができ、まことに光栄に存じます。

content.content: It is truly an honor to receive a prize such as this.
When 思うfollows the conjunctive form of i-adjectives and na-adjectives that express feelings or emotions, it expresses how the speaker feels. The pattern XをYに（Yく）おもう is also used, as in

content: and
. To ask about the listener’s impression, どう思う／思いますか are used, as in the example below.

content.content: （例）あの人についてどう思いますか。
What do you think of that person?
5. V-ようとおもう

content: 今日はゆっくり休もうと思う。

content.content: I’m going to take it easy and rest today.

content: この仕事をやめようと思っている。

content.content: I’m thinking of quitting this job.

content: A:夏休みはどうするつもりですか。

content.content: What are you planning to do this summer vacation?
B:ヨーロッパを旅行しようと思っています。
I’m going to tour Europe.

content: 将来、どんな仕事をしようと思っているんですか。

content.content: So what sort of work are you going to do in the future?

When combined with the intentional form of a verb, と思う expresses the speaker’s plans or intentions. In interrogative sentences, the function of this combination is to ask about the listener’s intentions. When と思う is used with the dictionary form, as in the following example, it indicates that the speaker’s plans are uncertain; this form cannot be used to express intention.
（例）私は来年アメリカに行くと思う。
I think I’ll go to the U.S. next year.
6. ...ようにおもう［N／Na　であるようにおもう］［A／V　ようにおもう］

content: 太田くんは内気なので、ウェイターの仕事は向いていないように思う。

content.content: Because Ota-kun is shy, I don’t think he is suited to be a waiter.

content: 住民の多くが反対していることを考えると、マンションの建築は見合わせた方がいいように思う。

content.content: Considering the fact that many local residents are opposed to it, I think it would be better to postpone construction of the condominiums.

content: この社員旅行のプランはちょっとゆとりがなさすぎるように思うのですが。こんなに短期間であちこち動き回っても疲れるだけではないでしょうか。

content.content: I think the plan for this company trip doesn’t include enough free time. Moving from one place to another in such a short time will only tire everyone out.

content: 《上司に》パソコンは一人に一台あった方が仕事の能率も上がるように思うのですが、購入するわけにはいきませんか。

content.content: 《to one’s boss》I think we would be able to work more efficiently if each person had his/her own computer. Couldn’t we buy more computers?

content: 国民一人一人の幸せを考えることは首相としての当然の義務であるように思われますが、首相はいかがお考えでしょうか。

content.content: It seems to me that considering the happiness of each and every citizen is a given duty of the prime minister. What do you, as prime minister, think about this?

Expresses a mild assertion of opinion. Often used when the speaker thinks there is a possibility that the listener has a different opinion, or when the speaker offers an opinion with which it is difficult for the listener to agree. When an even more euphemistic expression is desired, ように思われる is used.
7. N（のこと）をおもう

content: 親が子供を思う気持ちは何にも変えられない。

content.content: Nothing can replace the love parents have for their children.

content: いつもあなたのことを思っている。

content.content: I’m always thinking about you.

content: 試験のことを思うと心配で眠れない。

content.content: When I think about the exam, I get so worried that I can’t sleep.

content: 母の優しさを思うと気持ちが安らぐ。

content.content: My mind is at peace when I remember my mother’s gentleness.

When combined with a noun or a noun followed by のこと, 思う means that the speaker thinks or feels strongly about something. Depending on the meaning of the preceding noun, it can express a variety of cognitive processes, including imagination, retrospection, anxiety, reserve, and love.
8. Nを...とおもう［Nを　N／Na　だとおもう］［Nを　A／V　とおもう］

content: 最初は保子さんを男の子だと思った。

content.content: At first, I thought Yasuko-san was a boy.

content: 人々は私の考えを奇想天外だと思ったようだ。

content.content: People seemed to consider my idea to be bizarre.

content: みんな、彼の提案を実現不可能だと思って相手にしなかった。

content.content: Everyone thought his suggestion was unfeasible and wouldn’t go along with him.

content: 彼女の横顔を美しいと思った。

content.content: I thought her profile was beautiful.

content: みんなが彼のことを死んだと思っていた。

content.content: Everyone thought he had died.

content: 彼は自分のことを天才だと思っている。

content.content: He considers himself a genius.
Used to express one’s feeling, impression, or judgment concerning something. Sometimes Nが is used instead of Nを, as below:
（例）人々は私の考えが奇想天外だと思ったようだ。
People seemed to think my idea was bizarre.
Can also be used to indicate that someone has mistaken something or someone for something or someone else, as in
【おもえば】
1. おもえば

content: 思えば、学生時代はみんな純粋だった。

content.content: When I think about it now, back in our student days everyone was pure and innocent.

content: 思えば、あのころはよくあなたと徹夜で議論しましたねえ。

content.content: I remember how we used to stay up all night and argue in those days.

content: A:中島さん、あのころは毎日朝から晩までお酒飲んでましたよね。

content.content: Nakajima-san, back then you used to drink every day from morning till night, didn’t you?
B:ええ、思えば、よくもあのときアル中で死ななかったものですよね。もう体じゅうぼろぼろでしたからね。
Yeah, now that I think about it, it’s a miracle I didn’t die of alcoholism back then. I was a physical wreck.

content: 思えば、あのとき彼女に引き止められなければ、私はあの墜落した飛行機に乗って死んでいたのだ。彼女は命の恩人だ。

content.content: When I think back on it, if she hadn’t held me up, I would have gotten on that plane and died when it crashed. I owe her my life.
Used at the beginning of a sentence to describe, with a feeling of yearning or nostalgia, a recollection of the past.
2. いまからおもえば

content: 母は、私が下宿するのに猛反対したが、今から思えばその気持ちもわからなくもない。

content.content: My mother was dead set against my moving into a boarding house. Now that I think about it, I can understand something of what she felt.

content: あのときは彼の運営方針に反発したが、今から思えば彼がああいう方針をとったことも理解できる。

content.content: At the time I opposed his management policy, but now when I think about it, I can understand why he took that kind of approach.

content: 今から思えば、あのとき転職しておけばよかったとつくづく思います。当時は転職してもいい仕事ができるとは限らないと思ってしりごみしたのですけどね。

content.content: Now that I think about it, I really believe I should have changed jobs back then. At the time, though, I thought that even if I changed jobs there would be no guarantee of a good career, so I dragged my feet.

content: 今から思えば、あのとき結婚するのをやめてよかったと思う。婚約を破棄したときは、本当にこれでいいのかと思って、ものすごく不安だったが。

content.content: Now that I think about it, I’m glad I decided not to get married back then. Although when I broke off my engagement, I was really worried about whether or not I was doing the right thing.

Means that the speaker is reconsidering a past situation or event. Used when one’s knowledge or opinion has changed and one can now look at things differently. Expresses the notion that one can now understand someone else’s actions, even though it wasn’t possible in the past, or that one now thinks his/her own past behavior was a mistake, even though s/he used to think it was appropriate, or vice versa. Example

content: means “At the time, I couldn’t understand the reason why my mother was against it, but now I can,” and

means “At the time, I thought I shouldn’t change  jobs, but now I think if I had, I could have gotten a better one.” This expression often describes a contrast between the past and the present. 今から思うと can also be used.

content.content: 【おもったら】［N／Na　だとおもったら］［A／V　とおもったら］

content: 息子の姿が見えないと思ったら、押し入れの中で寝ていた。

content.content: I was wondering where my son could be, and there he was sleeping in the closet.

content: なんだか寒いと思ったら、窓が開いていたのか。

content.content: I was wondering why it was so chilly, but now I can see it’s because someone left the window open.

content: めがねがないないと思ったら、こんなところに置き忘れていたよ。

content.content: I was wondering why I couldn’t find my glasses, but now I see that I left them here, of all places!

content: 冷蔵庫においしそうなケーキがあると思ったら、お客さん用だった。

content.content: I was thinking that the cake in the refrigerator looked delicious, but it was for our guests.

content: 最近上田さんが学校に来ないと思っていたら、交通事故で入院しているらしい。

content.content: I was wondering why Ueda-san isn’t coming to school lately, and then I heard that she’s in the hospital because of a traffic accident.

content: 誰もいないのにうちに電気がついていると思ったら、弟が遊びに来て勝手に上がり込んでいたのだった。

content.content: I was wondering why the lights were on even though no one was home, but it turned out that my younger brother had dropped by for a visit and let himself in.

Placed after a clause and expresses an unsettled feeling about something for which the cause or reason is unknown. Followed by a statement of the cause, reason, or explanation, which also indicates that the matter has been satisfactorily resolved for the speaker. Example

content: means “I thought it was strange that my son wasn’t here, but I found him sleeping in the closet, so then I understood,” and

means “I was wondering why it was chilly, but then I noticed that the window had been left open, so I could understand the reason.” When an inexplicable situation continues over a period of time, と思っていたら can be used, as in

content.content: 【および】［NおよびN］

content: 会議終了後、名札およびアンケート用紙を回収します。

content.content: After the meeting is over, name tags and questionnaires will be collected.

content: この近辺ではとなりの児童公園および小学校の運動場が、災害が発生した場合の避難場所に指定されている。

content.content: In this neighborhood, the children’s park next door and the sports field at the elementary school have been designated as evacuation sites for when disaster strikes.

content: お祭りの前日および前前日は準備のため休業させていただきます。

content.content: This shop will be closed on the day before the festival as well as the day before that, in order to get ready.

content: 近隣住民から苦情のあったマンション内の騒音及びペットの問題が、次回の組合総会の議題となった。

content.content: The agenda for the next association meeting includes an item on complaints from the neighbors about noise in the apartment block and problems with pets.

content: 試験の日程及びレポートの提出期限については、追って掲示します。

content.content: The exam schedule and the submission deadline for papers will be posted at a later date.
Used to indicate a set or series of similar things. A written-language expression that means the same as NとN.
【おり】
1. おり（に）［Nのおり（に）］［V-る／V-た　おり（に）］

content: 前回の書類は今度の会議のおりにお渡しします。

content.content: I’ll give you the documents from the last meeting when I see you at the next meeting.

content: また何かのおりにでもお会いしましょう。

content.content: I hope to have the opportunity to see you again someday.

content: 今度お宅におうかがいするおりには、おいしいワインをお持ちします。

content.content: When I visit your home next time, I’ll bring some delicious wine.

content: 仕事で札幌に行ったおりに、足をのばして小樽に寄ってみた。

content.content: When I went to Sapporo on business, I also made a side trip to Otaru.

content: 高校時代の恩師にお会いしたおり、先生のお書きになった本を見せていただいた。

content.content: When I met a former teacher of mine from high school, he showed me a book he had written.
Means “time, occasion” or “opportunity.” Polite, formal expression.
2. おりからa. おりから［Aおりから］［V-るおりから］

content: 残暑の続くおりから、お体には十分お気をつけください。

content.content: Please mind your health as the summer heat continues.

content: 冷え込みの厳しいおりから、お風邪など召されませんように。

content.content: I hope you won’t catch a cold or anything in the harsh coldness of this season.

Means “time” or “season.” Used mainly in letters. The writer refers to an adverse weather condition (e.g. excessive heat or cold) using おり, and follows with an expression of concern for the health of the addressee.
b. おりからのN

content: 山は嵐のような天候になり、小さな山小屋は、おりからの風にあおられて簡単に吹き飛んでしまった。

content.content: The weather in the mountains turned stormy, and the little mountain hut was easily blown away by the ensuing winds.

content: 最近、ホームレスの人が増えているが、おりからの寒波で凍死した人もいるそうだ。

content.content: These days the number of homeless people is increasing, and apparently some even froze to death because of the recent cold snap.

content: もともと女子の就職状況は男子より悪かったが、今年はおりからの不況でますます女性には不利になっている。

content.content: Employment opportunities for women have always been less favorable than those for men, and this year the economic downturn is making this disadvantage even greater for women.

content: 海外旅行ブームがますます盛んになっているところへ、おりからの円高で、連休の海外旅行客は 40 万人を越えるそうだ。

content.content: Overseas travel has been getting more and more popular, and now, because of the strong yen rate, they say that more than 400,000 people will travel abroad over the holidays.

Means that something has happened at a certain time. Modifies nouns referring to bad weather, like 雨 (rain), 風 (wind), 嵐 (storm), and 寒さ(cold), or social conditions, like 不況 (economic downturn), 不景気 (recession), and 円高 (strong yen rate). Indicates that something has happened as a result of an ongoing situation. Used in written language.
1. ...か...か［NかN（か）］［Na かNa か］［AかAか］［VかVか］

content: 電車かバスで行くつもりだ。

content.content: I’m going to go by train or bus.

content: 水曜か金曜の夜なら都合がいいのですが。

content.content: Either Wednesday or Friday night would be convenient for me.

content: ネクタイはこれかそれかどっちがいいだろう。

content.content: Which tie is better, this one or that one?

content: 進学か就職かで悩んでいる。

content.content: I’m worried about whether I should continue my education or get a job.

content: その映画がおもしろいかおもしろくないかは見てみなければわからない。

content.content: I won’t know whether the movie is interesting or not unless I see it.

content: 二次会は、カラオケに行くかもう少し飲むか、どっちがいいでしょうか。

content.content: Which is better for the after-party, going to karaoke or having a few more drinks?

content: 夏休みは、香港か台湾かシンガポールに行きたい。

content.content: I want to go to Hong Kong or Taiwan or Singapore for the summer vacation.

content: 体が健康か不健康かは顔色で判断できることもある。

content.content: Sometimes we can judge whether or not a person is healthy from his/her facial color.
Expresses a choice between either X or Y. When X and Y are adjectives or verbs, かmay be used to pair the affirmative and negative forms, as in

content: above and the example below.

content.content: （例）行くか行かないか決めてください。
Please decide whether to go or not.
Also, sometimes more than two things are listed, as in
2. Nか+疑問詞+か

content: プレゼントはコーヒーカップか何かにしよう。

content.content: I’ll buy a coffee cup or something as a present.

content: その仕事は内田さんか誰かに頼むつもりだ。

content.content: I’m planning to ask Uchida-san or someone else to do that task.

content: 夏休みは、北欧かどこか、涼しいところに行きたい。

content.content: During summer vacation, I’d like to go someplace cool like Scandinavia (lit. Northern Europe).

content: また来週かいつかお電話しましょうか。

content.content: Shall I call you sometime, like next week or something?
In this pattern, か is used to give a prime example from a set of several possible choices.
3. ...か...かで［NかN（か）で］［Na かNa かで］［AかAかで］［VかVかで］

content: あの人の話は、たいてい自分の自慢話か仕事の愚痴かで、聞いているとうんざりする。

content.content: Most of what he says is either boasting about himself or complaining about his job, so I get sick and tired of listening to him.

content: あの人は毎晩飲み屋で飲んでいるかカラオケバーに行っているかで、電話してもほとんどつかまらない。

content.content: Every night she’s either drinking at a tavern or out at a karaoke bar, so I can hardly ever reach her by phone.

content: 最近の学生はアルバイトで忙しいかクラブ活動で疲れているかで、あまり家で勉強していないようだ。

content.content: It seems that students these days are either busy working part-time or tired from club activities, so they don’t study at home very much.

content: 家賃が安い家は交通が不便か部屋がきたないかで、どこか欠点があるような場合が多い。

content.content: Whether it’s inconvenient location or shabby rooms, low-rent houses often have some kind of drawback.

Indicates that something is either X or Y, both of which have negative evaluative meaning. Followed by the statement of some predicament or problem created as a result of X and/or Y. This pattern may also take the form XかYかしていて, as shown in the following example.
（例）彼はパーティーでもずっと飲むか食べるかしていて、全然他の人としゃべろうとしない。
Even at parties, he’s either eating or drinking the whole time and never makes any attempt to talk with other people.
4. ...かどうか［N／Na／A／V　かどうか］

content: あの人が来るかどうか知っていますか。

content.content: Do you know whether or not he’s going to come?

content: それが本物のパスポートかどうかはあやしい。

content.content: It is doubtful whether that passport is genuine.

content: その映画がおもしろいかどうかは見てみなければ分からない。

content.content: I won’t know whether the movie is interesting or not without seeing it.

content: このようなアドバイスが適切かどうかわかりませんが、お役に立てれば幸いです。

content.content: I don’t know whether this sort of advice is appropriate, but I’ll be happy if it helps you.
Means “does or does not” or “is or is not.” Used to change a yes/no question into the equivalent of a noun phrase, which is then embedded into another sentence. For example, in

content: , the phrase あの人が来るかどうか (whether or not he’s going to come), which is derived from the question あの人は来ますか (Is he going to come?), replaces それ (that) in the sentence あなたはそれを知っていますか (Do you know that?). かどうか is followed by predicates such as 知らない (not know), 分からない (not know), あやしい (is doubtful), 自信がない (not be sure), and 決める (decide).
行くか行かないか決めて下さい。

content.content: Please decide whether you’re going to go or not.

content: 面白いか面白くないか分からない。

content.content: I don’t know whether it’s interesting or not.
【か】1b. ...か...ない（か）［V-るかV-ない（か）］［V-たかV-ない（か）］

content: 去年彼女に会ったのは、たしかゴールデンウィークに入るか入らないかの頃だったと思います。

content.content: I’m fairly sure it was either just before or at the very beginning of Golden Week that I met her last year.

content: ベルが鳴り終わるか終わらないうちに、生徒達は外へ飛び出していった。

content.content: The students had run out of the room even before the bell stopped ringing.

content: 聞こえるか聞こえないかぐらいの程度だが、このレコードには変なノイズが入っている。

content.content: Even though they can barely be heard, there are strange noises on this record.

content: この銃は引き金に指が触れるか触れないかで弾が飛び出すので、慎重に扱う必要がある。

content.content: This gun needs to be handled carefully, because it can go off with just the faintest little touch of the trigger.

Uses the affirmative and negative forms of the same verb. Means that an action or event is so indefinite or at such a delicate stage that it is hard to tell whether or not it is actually happening. If the event took place in the past, the verb before かmay take the ta-form.  For example,

content: may be rephrased as 入ったか入らないか.

content.content: 6. 疑問詞...か

content: 彼がいつ亡くなったか知っていますか。

content.content: Do you know when he died?

content: パーティーに誰を招待したか忘れてしまった。

content.content: I forgot who I invited to the party.

content: 人生において重要なのは、何をやったかではなく、いかに生きたかということであろう。

content.content: The important thing in life is not what you have done, but how you have lived.

content: 人類の将来は、地球環境をいかに守っていくかにかかっていると言っても過言ではない。

content.content: It is not too much to say that the future of mankind depends on how we protect the global environment.
Used to change an interrogative sentence containing a question word (who, what, how, etc.) into the equivalent of a noun phrase; this phrase is then embedded into another sentence. For example, in

content: , the phrase 彼がいつ亡くなったか (when he died), derived from the sentence 彼はいつ亡くなりましたか (When did he die?), replaces それ (that) in the sentence あなたはそれを知っていますか (Do you know that?). The predicate preceding か takes the plain form.

content.content: 7. 疑問詞+かa. 疑問詞+か

content: 彼はどうも何かを隠しているらしい。

content.content: He seems to be hiding something.

content: 誰かに道を聞こう。

content.content: Let’s ask someone how to get there.

content: あの人にはいつか会ったことがある。

content.content: I’ve met that person before.

content: 郊外のどこかに安くて広い土地はないだろうか。

content.content: I wonder if there isn’t a large, inexpensive piece of land somewhere in the suburbs.

When か is attached to interrogatives such as なに (what), だれ (who), どこ (where) and いつ (when), it expresses something that is not clearly or concretely known, is not yet decided, or does not need to be mentioned.
b. 何+数量詞　+か／いくつか

content: ビールなら冷蔵庫に何本かある。

content.content: We have a few bottles of beer in the refrigerator, if that’s what you’re looking for.

content: 鉢植えをいくつか買ってきてベランダに置こう。

content.content: I’ll buy some potted plants and put them on the porch.

content: 男子学生を何人か呼んできて手伝ってもらえば、これくらいの荷物はすぐ運べる。

content.content: If I ask a few of the students to come and help me, a load of this size can be moved quickly.

content: いつかアフリカに何年か住んでみたい。それが私の夢だ。

content.content: Someday I’d like to live in Africa for a few years. That’s my dream.
When attached to an indefinite quantity such as 何本 (a few (bottles)) or いくつ (several), か means that although the exact quantity can’t be stated, it is not very much.

content: 彼女は自分も留学経験があるからか、留学生の悩みの相談によくのってあげている。

content.content: I’m not sure, but it might be because she herself has studied abroad that she often helps the international students with their problems.

content: 今日は風があるせいか、日差しが強いわりには涼しく感じられる。

content.content: I’m not sure if it’s because of the wind, but today it feels cool even with the bright sunshine.

content: 彼はそれを知っていたのか、私の話を聞いても特に驚いた様子はなかった。

content.content: It might be that he already knew about it, but he didn’t look surprised when he heard what I had to say.

content: 彼は家が本屋だからか、いろんな分野の本をよく読んでいるし、趣味で小説も書くらしい。

content.content: I’m not sure whether it’s because his family runs a bookstore, but he reads all sorts of books, and it also seems that he writes novels as a hobby.

Xからか、Y and other similar patterns are used to express a conjecture that the reason for Y might be X. The emphasis is placed on Y. The part of the sentence including か tends to take a form that expresses a reason, such as からか, せいか, ためか, のか. For example,

content: means “It feels cool today. This might be because of the wind.”

content.content: 【ことか】
0. ...どころか→
【どころ】
1. ...ばかりか→
【ばかりか】
【ものか】
【かい】
1. かいが　ある／ない［Nのかいが　ある／ない］［V-たかいが　ある／ない］

content: 努力したかい（が）あって、無事合格することができた。

content.content: As a result of all the effort I put in, I was able to pass the exam.

content: コンクールで優勝できるなんて、一日も休まず練習したかいがあったね。

content.content: The fact that we won the competition shows that practicing every single day was worth it.

content: 警官の懸命の説得のかいもなく、その男性は警官の顔をしばらくじっと見つめた後、屋上から飛び降りてしまったという。

content.content: All the policeman’s earnest persuasion was to no avail. They say the man stared at him for a while and then jumped off the roof.

content: 今になってまったく違う意見を主張されたのでは、せっかくみんなが歩み寄って意見を調整したかいがなくなるじゃないか。

content.content: If you’re going to assert a completely different opinion now, it will mean the trouble everyone took to make concessions and coordinate their opinions was really all for nothing.

Follows a verb or noun expressing an action and indicates that the action has been rewarded or the anticipated effect of the action has been achieved. When the negative form is used, it means that there was no reward despite the effort, or no result from the action.
2. R-がい

content: やりがいのある仕事を求めて転職する。

content.content: I want to find some work with a purpose, so I am changing jobs.

content: 仕事のほかに生きがいを見出せないような人生ではあまりにも寂しいではないか。

content.content: If you can’t find a reason to live other than your work, it is so sad, isn’t it.

content: もっと働きがいのある職場に移りたいと思うが、この不況では転職もなかなかむずかしそうだ。

content.content: I’d like to move to a workplace with a more rewarding job, but it seems pretty difficult to change jobs in this recession.

content: こんなに喜んでもらえるのだったら、料理のしがいがある。

content.content: If it makes you this happy, then cooking is worth it.

content: 一度失われた森林を元に戻すのは大変なことではあるが、そこに住む人たちの暮らしもかかっているだけに、苦労のしがいもあるというものだ。

content.content: It is hard to restore forestland once lost, but the people living there depend on it for their livelihoods, so it is well worth the trouble.

Attaches to a verb stem and means that an action has value or is effective or rewarding. It is used with only a limited range of verbs. When the action is difficult to accomplish or requires great effort, as in

content: and
, it indicates that the effort is worthwhile and meaningful.

content.content: 【かえって】

content: 親切で言ったつもりなのだが、かえって怒らせてしまったようだ。

content.content: I meant to say it out of kindness, but it made her angry instead.

content: 間に合うようにと思ってタクシーに乗ったのに、渋滞のせいでかえって遅くなってしまった。

content.content: Even though I took a cab so I would arrive in time, I ended up being late because of a traffic jam.

content: 昨日買ったカーテンは少し派手すぎたかなと思っていたが、かえって部屋が明るくなってよかった。

content.content: I was afraid that the curtains I bought yesterday were too loud, but I’m happy to say that they’ve made the room brighter.

content: A:お見舞いに来てくれたお礼に、川井さんにはお菓子でも持って行こうか。

content.content: Shall I bring a box of cookies or something to thank Kawai-san for visiting me when I was ill?
B:いや、そんなことをしたら、かえって向こうが気を遣うよ。
No, if you did that, it would just make her feel beholden.

content: A:この間はひどいことを言ってしまって、悪かった。

content.content: I’m sorry I said such an awful thing the other day.
B:いや、かえって良かったよ。あれから君の言葉を思い出してぼくもいろいろ反省したんだ。
No, it was actually good. After that, I thought over many things that you had said.
Used when a result is the opposite of one’s intention or expectation. Example

content: means “contrary to expectation, something said out of kindness to another person made him angry,” and
means “one would expect that bringing a box of cookies would make someone happy, but instead it would make her feel beholden.” Example

means “I thought I hurt the other person because I said such an awful thing, but it was actually a good chance for him to reflect on his conduct.” Indicates an outcome that is contrary to what one might expect in normal circumstances. It is therefore not likely to be used for unpredictable events.

content.content: （×）今日は雨が降ると思っていたが、かえっていい天気になった。
I thought it would rain today, but instead it was a beautiful day.
（○）今日は雨が降ると思っていたが、いい天気になった。
I thought it would rain today, but it turned out to be a beautiful day.
【かえる】［R-かえる］

content: 次の文を否定文に書きかえなさい。

content.content: Rewrite the next sentence as a negative statement.

content: 次の駅で急行に乗りかえましょう。

content.content: Why don’t we change to an express train at the next station?

content: 電球を新しいのと取りかえたら、部屋が見違えるように明るくなった。

content.content: When I replaced the light bulb, the room became so bright it was hardly recognizable.

content: もらってきた花を花びんに生けてあった花と入れかえて玄関に飾った。

content.content: I replaced the floral arrangement in the vase with the flowers I had been given and put them in the entrance.

content: 家を建てかえたので、ついでに家具も全部買いかえた。

content.content: Because we rebuilt our house, we also bought all new furniture.

content: 名札をジャケットからシャツに付けかえた。

content.content: I took my name tag off my shirt and put it on my jacket.

content: 彼はとても器用で、卓球をやっているとき、ラケットを左右に持ちかえながらプレイすることができる。

content.content: He is so skillful that he can keep changing his paddle from one hand to the other when he plays table tennis.
When かえる follows a verb stem, it expresses changing or exchanging something. Examples

content: , and
mean changing X to Y, and
and
mean exchanging X for Y. Example
and

mean moving the position of X from Y to Z. In addition to the examples above, 移しかえる (shift), 置きかえる (replace), 掛けかえる (put up a new (map)), 植えかえる (transplant) and 張りかえる (repaper/reupholster) are also used.

content.content: 【かぎり】
1. かぎりa. かぎりが　ある／ない

content: 資源には限りがある。無駄遣いしてはいけない。

content.content: Resources are limited. You must not waste them.

content: 限りある資源を大切にしよう。

content.content: We should value limited resources.

content: 宇宙の広がりには限りがないように思える。それが魅力だ。

content.content: The expanse of outer space seems to be without limits. That is its fascination.

content: 宇宙には限りない魅力がある。

content.content: Space holds an unlimited fascination.

content: パソコンには数限りない機種があるため、どれを選んだらいいのか、選択に困る。

content.content: There are countless types of computers, so it is hard to know which one to choose.
Expresses a limit or bound of time, space, degree, or amount. The forms in

content: and
are used to modify nouns and are idiomatic. 限りのある／ない can also be used. 数限りない in
is idiomatic and is used with countable nouns to indicate a large number. 数限りなく can also be used.

content.content: b. かぎりなくNにちかい

content: その着物は限りなく白に近い紫だった。

content.content: The color of that kimono was an extremely pale purple bordering on white.

content: その真珠のネックレスは限りなく本物に近い偽物で、見ただけでは偽物であることがわからない。

content.content: That fake pearl necklace is so realistic that you can’t tell it’s an imitation only by looking at it.

content: キムさんの日本語の発音は限りなく日本人に近いが、注意して聞くとやはり韓国語の影響が残っている。

content.content: Kim-san’s pronunciation is almost like that of a Japanese, but if you listen carefully, there’s still some influence of Korean.
Means something is almost exactly like the thing expressed by the noun.
2. ...かぎり〈limit, bounds〉a. Nかぎり

content: 彼女は今年限りで定年退職することになっている。

content.content: She’s scheduled to retire at the end of this year.

content: その演劇の公演は、今週限りで打ち切られる。

content.content: Performances of the play will be discontinued at the end of this week.

content: 勝負は1回限りだ。たとえ負けても文句は言うな。

content.content: There is only one chance to win or lose. Don’t complain even if you lose.

content: あの人はその場限りの思いつきの意見しか言わない人だ。

content.content: He is a person who always says whatever pops into his head, just to suit the occasion.

content: 今の話はこの場限りで忘れてください。

content.content: After you leave, please forget what we just spoke about here.
Attaches to nouns expressing time, frequency, or space and indicates a limit. In the case of space, only この場, その場, あの場 are used. Example

content: means “until the end of this year” and
means “on only that occasion.”

content.content: b. ...かぎり［Nのかぎり］［V-るかぎり］

content: 力の限り戦ったのだから負けても悔いはない。

content.content: I played as hard as I could, so I have no regrets about losing.

content: 選手たちは優勝をかけて命の限り戦ったが、惜しくも敗れてしまった。

content.content: The players gave it their all to win but unfortunately lost.

content: あの大統領は、権力の絶頂にあった頃ぜいたくの限りを尽くしていたそうだ。

content.content: I heard that the president indulged in a life of luxury at the peak of his power.

content: 難民たちは持てる限りの荷物を持って逃げてきた。

content.content: The refugees fled with as many bags as they could take away.

content: できる限りの努力はした。あとは結果を待つだけだ。

content.content: I gave it everything I had. Now all I can do is to wait for the result.

content: そこは見渡す限り（の）桜の花だった。

content.content: There were cherry blossoms as far as we could see.
Means “to the utmost limit” or “all.” 力の限り, 命の限り and ぜいたくの限り in

content: , all of which attach to nouns, are idiomatic expressions. 見渡す限り in
is an idiomatic expression which means the entire range of what one can see. When かぎり attaches to a verb, it often attaches to its potential form V-れる.

content.content: 3. かぎり〈limits〉a. V-る／V-ている／V-た　かぎり

content: 私の知る限り、彼は絶対そんなことをするような人ではない。

content.content: As far as I know, he is definitely not the kind of person to do such a thing.

content: 私が聞いている限りでは、全員時間どおりに到着するということだが。

content.content: As far as I know, everyone should be here on time.

content: 私の見た限りで「樹神」という姓の人は、電話帳に2軒しか載っていなかった。

content.content: As far as I can tell from the phone book, there are only two families with the surname of “Kotama.”

content: この植物は、私が今まで調べた限りでは、まだ日本では発見されていないようだ。

content.content: As far as I can tell from my research, this plant does not seem to have been found in Japan yet.

Attaches to verbs expressing awareness or perception, such as 見る (to see), 聞く (to listen) and 調べる (to research). Means evaluating something based on the range of one’s knowledge or experience. かぎりで and かぎりでは are also used.
b. V-る／V-ている  かぎり

content: この山小屋にいる限りは安全だろう。

content.content: As long as we are in this mountain hut, we should be safe.

content: プロである限り、その大会への出場資格はない。

content.content: Since you’re a professional, you don’t have the qualifications to enter the competition.

content: あいつが意地を張っている限りは、絶対にこっちも頭を下げないつもりだ。

content.content: So long as he continues to be stubborn, I have no intention of apologizing to him.

content: A:英会話なんか、ちょっと本気でやりさえすればすぐに上達するさ。

content.content: You know, for English conversation, if you just get a little serious about it, you can quickly improve.
B:おまえ、そんなこと言ってる限り、いつまでたってもうまくならないぞ。
So long as you keep on saying that, you won’t ever get any better.

Means “as long as that state continues.” Used to express a condition. Followed by an expression of the situation that will arise under that condition. Implies that if the condition changes, the situation might change too.
c. V-ないかぎり

content: 練習しない限り、上達もありえない。

content.content: Without practice, there’s no chance of improvement.

content: あいつが謝ってこない限り、こっちも折れるつもりはない。

content.content: Unless he apologizes to me, I won’t give in to him.

content: 絶対にやめようと自分で決心しない限り、いつまでたっても禁煙なんかできないだろう。

content.content: Unless you yourself pledge to quit smoking, you’ll never be able to do it.

content: 今の法律が変わらない限り、結婚したら夫婦はどちらか一方の姓を名乗らなければならない。

content.content: Until the present law changes, either the husband or wife will have to take the other’s surname when they get married.

Means “unless something happens.” Expresses a condition. Followed by an expression of the situation that will arise under that condition. Implies that if the condition changes, the situation might change too.
【かぎりに】→
【をかぎりに】
【かぎる】
1. ...にかぎる［Nにかぎる］［Na なのにかぎる］［Aのにかぎる］［V-るにかぎる］

content: 和菓子ならこの店にかぎる。

content.content: This is really the only shop for Japanese sweets.

content: 疲れた時は温泉に行くにかぎるね。

content.content: Going to a hot spring resort is the thing to do when you are tired, you know.

content: せっかくテレビを買いかえるのなら、画面がきれいなのにかぎる。

content.content: If you’re going to buy a new TV, then it has to be one with good picture quality.

content: ヨーロッパを旅行するなら電車にかぎるよ。安くて快適だしね。

content.content: Train is the only way to travel in Europe. It’s cheap and comfortable.

content: 家族みんなで楽しみたかったら、ディズニーランドに行くに限る。

content.content: If you want to have fun with your whole family, going to Disneyland is best.
Asserts that something is the best. Often preceded by a なら or たら clause.
2. Nにかぎったことではない

content: あの人が遅刻するのは今日にかぎったことではない。

content.content: Today is not the only day that he’s been late.

content: レポートのできが悪いのはこの学生にかぎったことではない。

content.content: It is not just this student whose reports are poorly written.

content: 日本の物価の高さはなにも食料品にかぎったことではない。

content.content: It is not only groceries that are expensive in Japan.

content: エンジンの故障が多いのはこの車種に限ったことではないらしく、同じメーカーの他の車種でも同じようなトラブルが起こっているということだ。

content.content: It is not only this model which has had all sorts of engine trouble; other models of this car manufacturer are also having the same sort of trouble.
Means that a problem is not limited to just one thing. Generally used with respect to negative matters and expresses that “this applies not only in this case but also in many others.”
3. ...とはかぎらない→
【とはかぎらない】
4. ...ともかぎらない→
【ともかぎらない】
【かくして】

content: かくして市民による革命が成し遂げられたのであった。

content.content: In this way, a citizens’ revolution was accomplished.

content: かくして長かった一党独裁の時代が終わりを告げたのである。

content.content: Thus, the long period of single-party political domination marked its end.

Placed after a stretch of written text, かくしてis used at the beginning of a sentence to express a conclusion or outcome derived from the previous text. このようにして and こうして have the same meaning. かくて is also used. Used in formal written language, in subjects such as history.
【かくて】→
【かくして】
【かけ】［R-かけ］

content: やりかけの仕事が残っていたので、会社に戻った。

content.content: I returned to the office because I had some unfinished work.

content: 彼女の部屋には編みかけのセーターが置いてあった。

content.content: In her room was a sweater she was knitting.

content: その本はまだ読みかけだったが、友達がどうしても貸してほしいと言うので貸したら、そのまま戻ってこなかった。

content.content: I was still reading that book, but I lent it to a friend who said he just had to have it and I never got it back.

content: 私は友達にもらった壊れかけのテレビを、もう5年も使っている。

content.content: For five years now I’ve been using a half-broken TV I got from a friend.

content: 食事を作ろうと思ったら、冷蔵庫の中には腐りかけの野菜しかなかった。

content.content: I was going to cook something, but all there was in the refrigerator were some vegetables starting to spoil.
Attaches to a verb stem and indicates that an action is in progress. Means either that someone has initiated an action that is still in progress, as seen in examples

content: , and
, or that an event has started and is still in progress, as in
and

content.content: 【かける】
1. R-かける〈exertion of influence〉

content: 電車の中で酔っぱらいに話しかけられるたびに、私は日本語がわからないふりをすることにしている。

content.content: Whenever drunks on the train try to talk to me, I act like I don’t understand any Japanese.

content: みんなに呼びかけて、いらなくなった衣類や食器などを持ってきてもらおう。

content.content: Let’s put a call out to people to have them bring clothes and dishes and other things they don’t need anymore.

content: その子は、人と目が合うたびにやさしく笑いかけるような、そんな、人を疑うということを知らないような子だったと言う。

content.content: They say that she would give a kind smile to people whenever their eyes met, and was the sort of child who wouldn’t know what it meant to doubt others.

content: リサイクル運動の市民グループを作りたいと思って、周りの友達に相談を持ちかけてみたが、みんな忙しいと言って話に乗ってこなかった。

content.content: I wanted to make a citizen’s recycling group so I brought up the topic with my close friends, but everyone said they were too busy and didn’t go along with my idea.
Attaches to a verb stem and expresses the effect an action has on others. 人に相談を持ちかける in

content: is an idiomatic expression, as are 問いかける (to ask someone), 語りかける(to talk to someone), and 誘いかける (to invite someone to do something).

content.content: 2. R-かける〈partway〉

content: 友達に大事な相談の手紙を書きかけたとき、玄関のベルが鳴った。

content.content: Just as I was about to write an important letter to a friend, the doorbell rang.

content: 「じゃあ」と言って受話器を置きかけて、しまったと思った。彼に用件を言い忘れていたことに気づいたのだ。

content.content: I said “Bye” and was about to put the receiver down when I realized my blunder—I had forgotten to tell him what I’d wanted to say.

content: その猫は飢えでほとんど死にかけていたが、世話をしたら奇跡的に命を取り戻した。

content.content: The cat was almost dead from starvation but, with my care, it miraculously revived.

content: 忙しい日々の中で忘れかけていた星空の美しさを、この島は思い出させてくれた。

content.content: This island has reminded me of the beauty of a starry sky, something which I had almost forgotten about in my busy daily life.

Attaches to a verb stem and means that an action has been initiated or an event is in progress but still has to be completed. Expresses either that an intentional action has been initiated but is still in progress, as in

content: and
, or that an unintentional event has started and is in progress, as in
and

content.content: 【かたがた】［Nかたがた］

content: 友達が風邪をひいたというので、お見舞いかたがた家を訪ねることにした。

content.content: My friend said he had caught a cold, so I decided to visit him at home to see how he was.

content: 散歩かたがたパン屋さんに行ってこよう。

content.content: I will stop by a bakery on my stroll.

content: 《手紙文》以上お礼かたがたお願いまで。

content.content: 《in a letter》I thought I would send you this brief note to thank you and also to take this opportunity to ask you another favor.

Attaches to a noun that describes an action; expresses that another action which is described after this noun takes place at the same time. The nouns with which かたがた can be used are limited in number and include お見舞い (a visit to someone who is ill/an expression of sympathy) and 散歩 (a walk/stroll).
【かたわら】
1. ...かたわら〈beside〉［Nのかたわら］［V-るかたわら］

content: 母が編み物をするかたわらで、女の子は折り紙をして遊んでいた。

content.content: The girl was playing with origami while her mother was knitting.

content: 楽しそうにおしゃべりしている田中くんのかたわらで、田川さんはしょんぼりうつむいていた。

content.content: Tagawa-san looked down with dejection all the while Tanaka-kun was chatting away cheerfully.
Attaches to a noun or a verb that expresses an action. Means “beside, alongside” and is often used in descriptions of scenes. A formal expression used in stories and the like.
2. ...かたわら〈secondary action〉［Nのかたわら］［V-るかたわら］

content: その教授は、自分の専門の研究をするかたわら、好きな作家の翻訳をすることを趣味としている。

content.content: That professor translates the works of his favorite authors, in addition to carrying out research in his field.

content: そのロック歌手は、演奏活動のかたわら、中高生向けの小説も書いているそうだ。

content.content: In addition to being a professional rock singer, they say he also writes novels for teenagers in his spare time.

content: その年老いた職人は、本職の家具作りのかたわら、孫のために簡単な木のおもちゃを作ってやるのが楽しみだった。

content.content: The elderly craftsman took pleasure in making simple wooden toys for his grandchildren, alongside his regular occupation making furniture.
Means “in one’s spare time, in addition to one’s usual activities/tasks.” A formal expression typical of written language.
【かつ】［N（であり）かつN］［Na かつ Na］［RかつV］

content: これで、福祉会館建設に関する議案を提出するのに必要かつ十分な条件が整った。

content.content: Now we have satisfied the conditions both necessary and sufficient to introduce a bill concerning the construction of a social welfare center.

content: 今回の大胆かつ巧妙な手口の犯行は犯人像を割り出す手がかりになるものと思われる。

content.content: It seems that this bold and clever modus operandi could be a clue to work out a profile of the culprit.

content: その知らせを聞いて一同皆驚きかつ喜び、中には涙を流す者さえいた。

content.content: When they heard the news, they were surprised and also delighted. Some among them even cried.

content: 我々は久しぶりの再会に、陽気に騒ぎかつ大いに飲み、時間のたつのも忘れた。

content.content: When we were reunited after a long separation, we partied hard and drank so much that we lost track of time.

content: 彼は私の親友であり、かつライバルでもある。

content.content: He is both my best friend and a rival.

Lists two states that are both true. Has the same meaning as そして (and also). Used in written language. In spoken language, the te-form is usually used, as in 必要で十分 (necessary and sufficient) or 騒いで飲む (partying and drinking).
【かつて】

content: このあたりは、かつては有名な米の産地だった。

content.content: This area was once famous for rice production.

content: 彼女はかつて新聞社の特派員として日本に滞在したことがあるそうだ。

content.content: I hear that she once resided in Japan as a correspondent for a newspaper company.

content: 今度この地方で地震が起こるとすれば、それはかつてないほどの規模のものになる恐れがある。

content.content: If an earthquake were to occur in this area now, it is likely to be on an unprecedented scale.

content: 久しぶりに会った彼は、相撲取りのように太っていて、かつての精悍なスポーツマンの面影はどこにもなかった。

content.content: When I met him after a long time, he was as fat as a sumo wrestler, without a trace of the fierce sportsman he had once been.

content: わが国が主食である米の生産を外国に頼るなどということは、未だかつてなかった。

content.content: Neither now nor in the past has our country ever depended on foreign nations for the production of rice, our staple food.
Means “before now, in the past.” Sometimes pronounced as かって. When used in the negative form, like かつてない in

content: and
, it means something has never happened before. かつてない and 未だかつて...ない are idiomatic expressions. Tends to be used in spoken language.

content.content: 【かというと】
1. ...かというと［N／Na　 （なの）かというと］［A／V　 （の）かというと］

content: 彼女はその仕事が気に入っているそうだ。しかし自分の時間を犠牲にしてでも打ち込んでいるかというと、そこまでは行かないらしい。

content.content: I hear she likes her job very much. Having said that, she doesn’t seem to like it enough to sacrifice her own free time for it.

content: 私はこの国に失望させられた。しかし、まったく見捨ててしまったのかというと、そうでもない。

content.content: I have been disappointed by this country. However, if you asked me whether or not I’ve abandoned it completely, I would say no.

content: 彼女はケーキ作りがとても上手なのだが、甘いものが好きなのかといえば、そうでもない。

content.content: She is very good at making cakes, but whether she likes sweet things or not is another matter.

content: 彼は入社して3ヶ月で会社を辞めてしまった。仕事や給料が不満だったのかというとそういうわけではなくて、もともと大学院に行きたかったので就職する気はなかったのだということだった。

content.content: He quit his job within three months. It wasn’t that he was dissatisfied with the work or the salary, but rather that he wanted to go to graduate school and really had no intention of starting a career in the first place.

When かというと is used with a negative expression in phrases such as Xかというとそうではない or Xかというとそうとは限らない, X is negated, even though X would have been the obvious outcome judging from the context of the preceding sentence. For example, in

content: , because “she likes her job so much,” one might expect that “she would devote herself to her job even at the expense of her personal time,” but in reality, this is not the case. かといえば is also used.

content.content: 2. 疑問詞+かというと

content: 私は彼がきらいだ。どうしてかというと、いつも人の悪口ばかり言っているからだ。

content.content: I don’t like him, and if you want to know why, it’s because he’s always badmouthing people.

content: 私は一度も海外に行ったことがない。どうしてかというと、飛行機に乗るのが恐いからだ。

content.content: I have never been abroad. The reason I haven’t is that I’m scared of flying.

content: 祖父がいつごろこの家を建てたかというと、戦争が終わってすぐの頃、食べるものも満足に手に入らないような苦労の時代だ。

content.content: To tell you about the time when my grandfather built this house—it was just after the war ended, and things were so bad that people couldn’t even get enough food.

content: 彼は入社して3ヶ月で一流企業を退職してしまった。やめて何をするかというと、インドへ行って仏教の修行をするらしい。

content.content: He’s left a leading company after three months. What he’ll do after quitting his job is to go to India and devote himself to Buddhist training.

content: 機械の苦手な私がどうやってパソコンに慣れたかというと、友達とパソコンでゲームをして遊んでいるうちに、だんだん恐くなくなってきたのだ。

content.content: If you want to know how someone as technically challenged as I am learned how to use a PC, it’s that I gradually got over my fear by playing computer games with friends.

content: A:なんで引っ越すの。今のアパート、家賃も安いし広いのに。

content.content: Why are you moving? The apartment you live in now is reasonable and roomy.
B:なんでかっていうとね、大家さんがうるさくて、友達を呼ぶと文句を言われるし、おまけに壊れたところも直してくれないのよね。
Well, to tell you the truth, the landlord is in my face all the time, complaining when I invite friends over, and—what’s more—he won’t repair anything that breaks down.
Attaches to a question with a question word in it and is used to indicate the point of the question. The answer to the question follows. When a reason is expressed, as in

content: , the sentence often ends with からだ, ためだ, or のだ. どうしてかというと and なぜかというと (both meaning “the reason being”) are idiomatic expressions. Used to explain something by asking oneself to come up with an answer. かといえば can also be used.

content: 急に空が暗くなったかと思うと、はげしい雨がふってきた。

content.content: Just as the sky grew dark, it started raining heavily.

content: やっと帰ってきたかと思ったら、また出かけるの？

content.content: You’ve just come back, and now you’re leaving again?

content: いつ寝ているのかと思うほどいそがしそうだ。

content.content: He looks so busy that I wonder when he ever sleeps.

content: 死ぬんじゃないかと思うほど苦しかった。

content.content: I was suffering so much that I thought I might die.

content: 葉がぜんぶ落ちた木があるかと思えば、まだたくさん残っている木もあった。

content.content: Some trees have lost all their leaves, while others still have many left.

content: 校庭のあちらではけんかをしている子供たちがいるかと思うと、こちらではじっと池の魚を観察している子もいる。

content.content: On that side of the schoolyard there were children tussling with each other, while on this side there were children intently watching fish in a pond.

content: 帰ってきたかと思ったら、また出かけていった。

content.content: He just got back, and now he has gone out somewhere again.

content: 何をやっているのかと思ったら、昼寝をしていたのか。

content.content: I was wondering what you were doing, and now I see you were napping, right?

【かな】

content: 山田さんは今日来るかな。

content.content: I wonder if Yamada-san will come today.

content: これ、おいしいのかな。

content.content: I wonder if this is tasty.

content: これ、もらって帰ってもいいのかな。

content.content: I wonder if I can take this home.

content: ちょっと手伝ってくれないかな。

content.content: I wonder if you would give me a hand?

content: 今度の旅行はどこへ行こうかな。

content.content: Where should I go on my next trip?

content: 最近なんでこんなに疲れやすいのかなあ。

content.content: I wonder why I get tired so easily these days.

かな is formed by attaching な to か, which is a marker indicating a question. かなis used at the end of a sentence and conveys the feeling of asking oneself a question. Although it expresses self-directed wondering or pondering, when uttered to another person it can be interpreted as an indirect request for assistance, permission, etc. Not combined with polite forms. A casual expression used in spoken language. The final sound な may be lengthened so it is pronounced as ...かなあ.
【かなにか】→
【なにか】3
【かならず】

content: 休むときはかならず連絡してください。

content.content: Be sure to contact us when you are going to be absent.

content: 宿題はかならずしなければならない。

content.content: You must always do your homework.

content: これからは、かならず朝ごはんを食べるようにしよう。

content.content: I will make sure I eat breakfast from now on.

content: ご招待ありがとうございます。かならずうかがいます。

content.content: Thank you for your invitation. I’ll most certainly visit you.

content: そうですか。かならず来てくださいよ。お待ちしていますから。かならずですよ。

content.content: Really? Please do come. I’ll be waiting for you. Don’t forget!
Means “without exception” or “surely.” Expresses a strong intention, as in

content: and
, a request, as in
and
, or an obligation, as in
. When used in the context of making promises, as in
and
, it can be replaced with きっと. It cannot be used in negative expressions.

content.content: （×）かならず行きません。
I won’t go without fail.
（○）ぜったい行きません。
I’ll definitely not go.
【かならずしも...ない】

content: 金持ちがかならずしもしあわせだとは限らない。

content.content: The rich are not necessarily happy.

content: 語学が得意だからといって、かならずしも就職に有利だとは限らない。

content.content: Being good at languages doesn’t always give you an advantage in finding employment.

content: 日本人は礼儀正しい人々だと言う人もいるようだが、実態は必ずしもそうではないとわたしは思っている。

content.content: Some people say the Japanese people are polite, but I don’t think that is always the case.

content: 政治家たちは国連は重要だと言う。しかし、必ずしも、常に尊重しなければならぬものだと思っているわけではない。

content.content: Politicians say that the United Nations is important. But they don’t necessarily think it has to be respected at all times.
Means that the logical relationship “if X, then invariably Y” does not always apply. For example,

content: means that the proposition 語学が得意なら就職に有利だ (being good at languages is advantageous for getting a job) is not always true. かならずしも is often used with わけではない and とはかぎらない. It has the flavor of written language.

content.content: 【かにみえる】→
【みえる】2f
【かねない】［R-かねない］

content: 風邪だからといってほうっておくと、大きい病気になりかねない。

content.content: If you just think it’s a cold and let it go, it may turn into a serious illness.

content: 君は、彼がそんなことをするはずがないと言っているそうだが、ぼくはあいつならやりかねないと思うけどね。

content.content: I hear you’re saying you’d never expect him to do such a thing, but I wouldn’t put it past him to do it.

content: 政府の今回の決定はいくつかの問題点をはらんでおり、近隣諸国の反発をまねきかねない。

content.content: This decision by the government entails some problems and may invite some resistance from neighboring countries.

content: 今回の土砂崩れは二次災害を引き起こしかねないものであり、対策を急がねばならない。

content.content: This landslide may lead to a secondary disaster, so countermeasures have to be taken quickly.
Means there is a possibility or a danger of something. Similar to かもしれない and ないとはいえない, but かねない can only be used for something the speaker evaluates negatively.
（×）私のこどものこの病気はなおりかねない。
This disease of my child’s may be cured.
（○）私のこどものこの病気はなおるかもしれない。
This disease of my child’s may be cured.
A formal expression often used in written language.
【かねる】［R-かねる］

content: そのご意見には賛成しかねます。

content.content: I am afraid I cannot agree with that opinion.

content: 残念ながら、そのご提案はお受けいたしかねます。

content.content: Regrettably, it is not possible for us to accept your proposal.

content: その中学生の死は、同級生のいじめにたえかねての自殺と見られている。

content.content: The death of that junior high school student appears to be a suicide triggered by the torments of his classmates, which he was no longer able to bear.

content: その人が、あまりにもこどもの心理を理解していないようなしかり方をするものだから、見かねて、つい口を出してしまったんだ。

content.content: I couldn’t bear to watch that person scold a child in a way that showed such a complete lack of understanding of children’s psyches, so I blurted out just how I felt.
Attaches to a verb stem and means “it is difficult or impossible to do something, even if one tries to.” 決めるに決めかねる and 見るに見かねて are idiomatic expressions. A formal expression used in written language.
【かのごとき】→
【ごとし】
【かのよう】→
【ようだ1】1b
【かもしれない】［N／Na／A／V　かもしれない］In spoken language, the form かもわからない can also be used. In informal conversation, かもね and かもよ may be used. かもしれぬ and かもしれず are formal expressions used in written language.
1. ...かもしれない

content: A:あの偉そうにしている人、ひょっとしてここの社長かもしれないね。

content.content: That person acting so high and mighty might just be the president of this company.
B:そうかもね。
That might be.

content: ここよりもあっちの方が静かかもしれない。行ってみようか。

content.content: It might be quieter over there than it is here. Shall we go?

content: 雨が降るかもしれないから、かさを持っていったほうがいいよ。

content.content: It might rain today, so you’d better take your umbrella.

content: A:来週のパーティー、行くの？

content.content: Are you going to the party next week?
B:まだ決めてないんだ。行くかもしれないし、行かないかもしれない。
I haven’t decided yet. I may go, or I may not go.

content: ノックをしても返事がない。彼はもう寝てしまったのかもしれない。

content.content: There was no response when I knocked on the door. He might have gone to sleep already.

content: 交渉相手が依然として強気の姿勢をくずさないということは、もしかすると何か強力な材料をもっているのかもしれない。

content.content: The fact that the other party continues to maintain a hard-line stance in negotiations may be because they have something very powerful to back their position....

content: 見合い話が壊れて、さぞがっかりしているだろうと心配していたが、それほど気にしている様子もない。当の本人は案外平気なのかもしれない。

content.content: I was worried about her being disappointed over the breakdown of the marriage negotiations, but she didn’t seem to mind it that much. She might be unexpectedly unconcerned about it.

content: ちょっと待って。今山田君が言ったそのアイデア、ちょっとおもしろいかもしれないよ。

content.content: Wait a second, the idea that Yamada-kun just mentioned could be interesting.

Expresses a supposition on the part of the speaker at the time of utterance. Means there is a possibility of something being the case. Compared to にちがいない and だろう, the degree of probability indicated by かもしれない is low, and there is a possibility it won’t happen. Sometimes used in the form のかもしれない, which consists of  かもしれない combined with のだ.
As in

content: , かもしれない may be used when the speaker wants to avoid an absolute declaration and soften his/her manner of expression. It may also be used by the speaker to preface an assertion, in expressions like 御存知かもしれませんが or 私が間違っているかもしれませんが.

content.content: In spoken language, かもしれない is used. In written language—including narrative passages in novels, in which different perspectives may be adopted freely—かもしれなかった can be used, as seen in the following example.
（例）このままでは、達彦自身の会社も危なくなるかもしれなかった。
At this rate, there was a possibility that Tatsuhiko’s own company would be in danger.
2. たしかに...かもしれないなるほど...かもしれない

content: A:この計画は危険すぎますよ。

content.content: This plan is too risky.
B:確かに、危険かもしれない。しかし、やってみるだけの価値はあると思う。
Certainly, it may be risky. However, it’s worth giving it a try.

content: A:今の時代、小さいころから受験勉強を始めなければ、いい大学には入れないんですよ。

content.content: In this day and age, it’s impossible to get into a good university unless you start preparing for the entrance exams when you’re very young.
B:なるほど君の言うとおりかもしれない。でも、いい大学に入れなくったって、いいじゃないか。
I see. That may well be the case, but would it really matter if we didn’t get into a good university?

content: 女性は強くなったといわれている。確かに、昔に比べれば女性も自由になったかもしれない。しかし、就職ひとつを例にとっても、真の男女平等と言うにはほど遠いのが日本の現状だ。

content.content: It is said that women have gotten stronger. It may be true that women have more freedom compared with the olden days, but if you look at employment as an example, the present situation in Japan is a long way from true gender equality.
Used by the speaker to state a differing opinion, after having first acknowledged the possibility that something the other person has said, or a general opinion, may be true.
3. ...ば／...たら　...かもしれないa. ...ば／...たら　V-るかもしれない

content: ここで代打がホームランでも打てば、形勢は逆転するかもしれない。

content.content: If the pinch hitter hits a home run here, the momentum of the game could be reversed.

content: もう少しがんばれば、志望校に合格できるかもしれない。

content.content: If I try a little harder, I may be able to pass the exam for the college I want to get into.
Indicates the speaker’s conjecture regarding what might happen next, based on the assumption of a certain condition.
b. ...ば／...たら　V-たかもしれない

content: あの時彼女を引き留めていたら、僕たちは別れずに済んだかもしれない。

content.content: If I had stopped her from leaving then, we might not have broken up.

content: もう少し早く手術をしていれば、あるいは助かったかもしれない。

content.content: Had he been operated on sooner, he might have been saved.

content: もし、あの時、救急車の到着があと5分遅かったら、私は今こうして生きていなかったかもしれない。

content.content: If the ambulance had arrived five minutes later than it did at that time, I might not be here alive.

This pattern is used to talk about something that has already happened and to express that, if the conditions had been different, the result could have been different. Used to express the speaker’s regret, or a sense of relief that a negative outcome was avoided.
【かもわからない】
1. ...かもわからない［N／Na／A／V　かもわからない］

content: 私は明日来られないかもわからない。

content.content: I’m not sure that I can come tomorrow.

content: きょうは山田さんも来るかもわからないから、日本酒も用意しておこう。

content.content: Yamada-san may come today, so I’ll get some sake ready, too.
Means almost the same as かもしれない but is not used as often.
2. ...か（も）わからない［N／Na　か（も）わからない］［A／V　か（も）わからない］

content: 先生の言っていることがわかりません。何について話しているかもわかりません。

content.content: I can’t understand what the teacher is saying. I can’t even understand what she is talking about.

content: 社長が今どこにいるのかもわからなくて、秘書がつとまると思っているのか。

content.content: You think you’re fit to be the company president’s secretary when you don’t even know where he is right now?

content: はたしてその計画をスタートさせることができるかどうかも分からないのに、成功した後のことをあれこれ言うのは早すぎる。

content.content: Here we aren’t even sure if we can put the plan into action or not, so it’s too soon to talk about doing this and that after it succeeds.

Follows an interrogative expression and means that someone doesn’t know or doesn’t understand the thing in the clause that ends with ...か, in addition to other things. In most cases, this pattern is used in situations where someone who should know something as a matter of course does not actually know it.
【かもしれない】
【から1】
1. Nからa. Nから

content: この町には、国じゅうからたくさんの人があつまってくる。

content.content: This town draws many people from all over the country.

content: あのクラスでは、試験の成績と出席率から成績が決められるそうだよ。

content.content: I hear that in that class, grades are determined from the test scores and attendance.

content: 窓からひざしがさしこんでいて、その部屋はとてもあたたかかった。

content.content: The room was very warm, with the sunshine streaming in from the windows.

content: 父からはこっぴどくしかられるし、母からはいやみを言われるし、さんざんな失敗だった。

content.content: I was severely scolded by my father and spoken to sarcastically by my mother, and it was a terrible failure.

content: 成績不振から解雇されたそのチームの監督はいまテレビの解説者をしている。

content.content: The manager of that team, who was dismissed because of a bad record, is now a commentator on television.

content: 日本は衆議院・参議院からなる二院制を取っている。

content.content: Japan has a bicameral system comprised of the House of Representatives and the House of Councilors.
Nから expresses the starting point, beginning, or origin of various actions and phenomena.
b. NからNまで

content: ここから目的地までは 10 キロほどあります。

content.content: It is about ten kilometers from here to our destination.

content: 10 日から 15 日まで休みます。

content.content: This store will be closed from the 10th through the 15th.

content: 子どもから大人まで楽しめる番組です。

content.content: Everyone—from children to adults—can enjoy this program.
When a starting point and endpoint are specified, から expresses a range of distance or time.
c. NからNにいたるまで

content: あの会社はヒラ社員から社長にいたるまで全員が制服を着ている。

content.content: In that company, everyone from the president down to ordinary employees wears a uniform.

content: この番組は、北海道から九州、沖縄に至るまで、全国ネットでお送りしています。

content.content: This program is broadcast nationwide, from Hokkaido all the way to Kyushu and Okinawa.

content: 当社は、設計・施工からアフターサービスに至るまで、みなさまの大切な住宅をお世話させていただきます。

content.content: Our company is pleased to take care of everything—from the design and construction down to the follow-up care necessary for your homes.

content: 一日の過ごし方から政治思想に至るまで、私があの思想家の影響を受けなかったものはない。

content.content: From the way I spend each day down to my political convictions, there is nothing in which I am not influenced by that thinker.
This pattern specifies a starting point and an endpoint and expresses that the range between them is large. Has the feel of written language.

content: この魚は、ヘビそっくりなところから、ウミヘビという名前をもつ。

content.content: The name of this fish is “sea snake,” because it looks just like a snake.

content: カボチャは、カンボジアからやってきたと言われているところからその名がついたそうだ。

content.content: I heard that the name kabocha (squash) is from Cambodia, where squash are said to have come from.

content: 車のバンパーから被害者の衣服の繊維が検出されたことから、その車の所有者にひき逃げの容疑がかかっている。

content.content: Because a fiber of the victim’s clothes was detected on the fender, the owner of the car is a suspect in a hit-and-run accident.

content: その人物が殺害されたことを記録した文書が全く存在しないところから、実はその人物は生き延びて大陸に渡ったのだという伝説が生まれたらしい。

content.content: From the absence of any documentation of his murder, the legend arose that he survived and crossed over to the continent.

content: 彼女は父親が中国人であるところから、中国人の知り合いも多い。

content.content: Because her father is Chinese, she has many Chinese friends.
こと／ところ　から expresses basis or origin. When the origin of a name is expressed, as in

content: and
, ところ is generally used more often. A formal expression used in written language.

【にしてからが】
9. 数量詞+からa. 数量詞+からのN

content: その説明会には 1000 人からの人々がつめかけたと言う。

content.content: They say that more than a thousand people crowded in for the explanatory meeting.

content: あの人は 3000 万からの借金をかかえているそうだ。

content.content: I hear he has a debt of more than thirty million yen.
Expresses “more than a certain amount,” with the implication that the amount is large. A rather formal expression.
b. 数量詞+からある／からする

content: その遺跡からは、 20 キロからある金塊が出土した。

content.content: A nugget of gold weighing twenty kilograms or more was excavated from those ruins.

content: 自動車産業は好調で 300 万からする車が飛ぶように売れている。

content.content: The automobile industry is doing well, and sales of cars priced at three million yen or more are skyrocketing.

content: その種の陶器は今では貴重で、小皿1枚が 10 万からしている。

content.content: That kind of pottery is now highly prized, and a small dish starts at about 100,000 yen.
Expresses that something is approximately a certain amount, or even more. Usually からある is used for weight, length, or size, and からする is used for price.
0. V-てから→
【てから】
【から2】［N／Na　だから］［A／V　から］

content: 今日は土曜日だから、銀行は休みですよ。

content.content: Because today is Saturday, the bank is closed.

content: それは私が持ちますから、あれを持って行っていただけますか。

content.content: I’ll carry that, so could I ask you to bring that one over there?

content: 星が出ているから、あしたもきっといい天気だろう。

content.content: Since the stars are out, the weather should be good tomorrow, too.

content: この辞書じゃよくわからないから先生に聞こう。

content.content: I don’t really understand what this dictionary says, so I’ll ask the teacher.
から attaches to both plain forms and polite forms. It is used to express the speaker’s reason for making a request, order, supposition, intention, or assertion. More subjective than ので.
2. ...から〈sentence-final usage〉

content: いつか、しかえししてやるからな。

content.content: I’ll get back at you someday!

content: おとなしく待ってろよ。おみやげ買ってきてやるからな。

content.content: Behave yourself while I’m away, and I’ll bring you a present.

content: A:たまご、買って来るの忘れちゃった。

content.content: I forgot to buy eggs.
B:いいから、いいから。それより、はやく手をあらいなさい。
Never mind, that’s all right. Just go and quickly wash your hands.

から is used at the end of a sentence and conveys a sense of warning or comforting. This is a usage that expresses various messages to the listener by implication, without explicit verbalization. The underlined parts in いつかしかえししてやるから、覚えてろ and いいから、早く手を洗いなさい are omitted or inverted. Used in spoken language.
3. ...からいい→
【からいい】
4. ...からこそ→
【からこそ】
5. ...からだa. ...のは...からだ

content: 試験に落ちたのは勉強しなかったからだ。

content.content: It was because I didn’t study that I failed the exam.

content: 今日こんなに波が高いのは台風が近づいているからだ。

content.content: The surf is high today because there’s a typhoon coming.

content: 君はまだ気がついていないのか。彼女が君につめたいのは、君がいつもからかうようなことを言うからだよ。

content.content: Haven’t you caught on yet that she’s cool to you because you’re always teasing her?
YのはXからだ is the reverse form of XからY, which expresses a reason. In this pattern, から cannot be replaced with ので.
（×）試験に落ちたのは勉強しなかったのでだ。
My not studying was why I failed the exam.
b. ...からだ

content: 試験に落ちたんだってね。勉強しなかったからだよ。

content.content: I heard that you failed the exam. It’s because you didn’t study.

content: A:今日は二日酔いだ。

content.content: I have a hangover today.
B:きのうあんなに飲んだからだよ。
That’s because you drank so much yesterday.
In this form, Yのは is omitted from the pattern YのはXからだ because it is clear from the context.

【から1】9b
【からいい】［N／Na　だからいい］［A／V　からいい］
1. ...からいいが

content: まだ時間はあるからいいが、今度からはもうちょっと早く来るようにしなさい。

content.content: It’s all right, because we have time. But you should come a little earlier next time.

content: ネギ、買ってくるの忘れたの？　まあ、少し残っているからいいけど。

content.content: Did you forget to buy leeks? Well, there are some left, so I guess it’s OK.

content: え？　今日も休むの？　まあ、あまり忙しくない時期だからいいけど。

content.content: What? You’re taking today off, too? Well, it’s not such busy time, so I guess it’s all right.
Takes the form からいいが or からいいけど and means “it is not a big problem, because of such-and-such.” Used in spoken language.
2. ...からいいようなものの

content: 大きな事故にならなかったからいいようなものの、これからはもっと慎重に運転しなさい。

content.content: It’s all right since it wasn’t a serious accident, but you should drive more carefully from now on.

content: だれも文句を言ってこないからいいようなものの、一つ間違えば大事故になっていたところだ。

content.content: Since no one complained about it, it’s all right, but it could have been a terrible accident.

content: 保険をかけてあるからいいようなものの、そうでなければ大変なことになっていたよ。

content.content: Thank goodness we took out insurance; otherwise, we could have been in serious trouble.

content: ちょうどタクシーが通りかかったからいいようなものの、あやうく遅刻するところだった。

content.content: It’s a good thing a taxi passed by just then—I wouldn’t have made it otherwise.

content: 大事に至らなかったからいいようなものの、今回の事故によって、政府の原子力政策は見直しをせまられそうだ。

content.content: It was fortunate that it didn’t lead to something serious, but this accident will force the Government to take a hard look at its nuclear energy policies.
Implies that the worst situation was avoided, but the outcome is still not favorable. Similar in meaning to からいいが／けど, but conveys a stronger feeling of criticism or rebuke.
【からいう】
1. Nからいうと

content: 私の立場から言うと、それはこまります。

content.content: Personally, I have a problem with that.

content: 先生の見方から言うと、私のやりかたはまちがっているのかもしれませんが、私はこれがいいんです。

content.content: From the teacher’s point of view, my way is incorrect, but I think this is how to do it.

content: あなたの考え方から言うと、私の主張していることなんかは急進的すぎるということになるんでしょうね。

content.content: According to your line of thinking, my claims might seem too radical.

content: 民主主義の原則から言えば、あのやり方は手続きの点で問題がある。

content.content: According to democratic principles, there are procedural problems with doing it that way.

Takes the forms Nからいうと／からいえば／からいったら and means “judging from a particular point of view.” Has the same meaning as からみると. Unlike からみると, however, Nからいうと and its variations cannot be attached directly to a noun that refers to a person.
（×）彼から言うと、それはまちがっているそうだ。
From him, it’s incorrect.
（○）彼の考え方から言うと、それはまちがっているそうだ。
From his point of view, it’s incorrect.
（○）彼から見ると、それはまちがっているそうだ。
As he sees it, it’s incorrect.
2. Nからいって

content: さっきの返事のしかたから言って、私はあの人にきらわれているようだ。

content.content: Judging from the way he just answered, he really seems to dislike me.

content: あの態度から言って、彼女は引き下がる気はまったくないようだ。

content.content: From her attitude, she doesn’t intend to back down at all.

content: あの口ぶりから言って、彼はもうその話を知っているようだな。

content.content: Judging from the way he talks, he seems to know about it already.

content: あの人の性格から言って、そんなことで納得するはずがないよ。

content.content: Judging from her character, she’d never go along with that.
Expresses the basis for a judgment. からして and からみて are also used.
【からいったら】→
【からいう】1
【からこそ】［N／Na　だからこそ］［A／V　からこそ］

content: これは運じゃない。努力したからこそ成功したんだ。

content.content: This wasn’t just luck. It’s because I made an effort that I succeeded.

content: A:君はぼくを正当に評価していない。

content.content: You’re not giving me a fair evaluation.
B:評価しているからこそ、もっとまじめにやれと言っているんだ。
It’s precisely because I think so much of you that I’m telling you to try even harder.

content: 愛が終わったから別れるのではなく、愛するからこそ別れるという場合もあるのだ。

content.content: There are times when a couple breaks up not because their love is gone but because they still do love each other.

content: 忙しくて自分の時間がないという人がいるが、私は忙しいからこそ時間を有効に使って自分のための時間を作っているのだ。

content.content: Some people say that they’re too busy and don’t have time for themselves, but it’s just because I am so busy that I make the best use of time and also make time for myself.

An expression that focuses on and emphasizes the reason or cause for something. Often used with のだ. Addition of こそ conveys the strong conviction of the speaker with respect to the reason expressed in the preceding phrase, so this pattern cannot be used to express a cause-effect relation objectively. のだis often used to end the sentence.
（×）今、東京は朝の9時だからこそ、ロンドンは夜中の 12 時だ。
Just because it’s nine o’clock in the morning in Tokyo, it’s midnight in London.
（○）今、東京は朝の9時だから、ロンドンは夜中の 12 時だ。
Now it’s nine o’clock in the morning in Tokyo, so it’s midnight in London.
【からしたら】→
【からする】1
【からして】
1. Nからして〈example〉

content: リーダーからしてやる気がないのだから、ほかの人たちがやるはずがない。

content.content: If the leader doesn’t have motivation, you can’t expect other people to do anything.

content: 課長からして事態を把握していないのだからヒラの社員によくわからないのも無理はない。

content.content: If the section chief doesn’t grasp the situation, it’s easy to guess that ordinary employees don’t understand what’s happening either.

content: ほら、その君の言い方からして、外国人に対する偏見が感じられるよ。

content.content: Look, even the way you talk makes me feel your prejudice against people from other countries.

content: 君はいろいろ言うが、まずこの問題には自分はまったく責任がないと信じ込んでいることからして私には理解しかねる。

content.content: You say many things about this, but, in the first place, I can’t understand why you believe that you don’t have any responsibility at all.

Used to present an extreme or typical example and expresses the feeling that “if something is so, then of course other things will also be so.” Often used in negative evaluations. にしてからが can also be used.
2. Nからして〈basis〉

content: あの言い方からして、私はあの人にきらわれているようだ。

content.content: From the way he spoke, he really seems to dislike me.

content: あの態度からして、彼女は引き下がる気はまったくないようだ。

content.content: From her attitude, she doesn’t intend to back down at all.

content: あの口ぶりからして、彼はもうその話を知っているようだな。

content.content: Judging from the way he talks, he already seems to know about what was said.

content: あの人の性格からして、そんなことで納得するはずがないよ。

content.content: Judging from her character, there’s no way she could be persuaded.
Expresses a basis from which to make a judgment. からすると, からみて, からいって are also used to express a similar meaning.
【からする】
1. Nからすると

content: あの言い方からすると、私はあの人にきらわれているようだ。

content.content: From the way he spoke, he really seems to dislike me.

content: あの態度からすると、彼女は引き下がる気はまったくないようだ。

content.content: From her attitude, she doesn’t intend to back down at all.

content: あの口ぶりからすると、彼はもうその話を知っているようだな。

content.content: Judging from the way he talks, he already seems to know what was said.

content: あの人の性格からすると、そんなことで納得するはずがないよ。

content.content: Judging from her character, there’s no way she could be persuaded.
Expresses the basis for making a judgment. からして, からみて and からいって are also used to express the same meaning.
2. 数量詞+からする→
【から1】9b
【からって】［N／Na　だからって］［A／V　からって］

content: 頭が痛いからって先に帰っちゃった。

content.content: She went home before we did, saying she had a headache.

content: 金持ちだからって何でも自由にできるというわけではない。

content.content: You can’t do anything you want, even if you are rich.
からって is an informal form of からといって.
【からといって】
【からでないと】→
【てから】2
【からでなければ】→
【てから】2
【からといって】［N／Na　だからといって］［A／V　からといって］
1. ...からといって

content: 用事があるからと言って、彼女は途中で帰った。

content.content: She said she had something to do and went home before it was over.

content: 電車の中でおなかがすくといけないからと言って、見送りに来た母は売店であれこれ買っている。

content.content: My mother, who had come to see me off, bought me one thing after another at the stall, saying it would never do to go hungry on the train.
Used to quote a reason that another person has given.
2. ...からといって+否定的表現

content: 手紙がしばらく来ないからといって、病気だとはかぎらないよ。

content.content: Even though we haven’t had a letter for a while, it doesn’t necessarily mean he is sick.

content: いくらおふくろだからといって、ぼくの日記を読むなんてゆるせない。

content.content: I can’t forgive her for reading my diary, even if she is my mother.
Expresses “for this reason alone.” Followed by a negative expression and means that “X, thus Y” doesn’t always apply.
【からには】［Vから（に）は］

content: 約束したからにはまもるべきだ。

content.content: If you make a promise, you should keep it.

content: 戦うからには、ぜったい勝つぞ。

content.content: Since I’m fighting, I’m in this to win.

content: この人を信じようと一度決めたからには、もう迷わないで最後まで味方になろう。

content.content: Since I’ve decided to believe him, I won’t waver in standing by him to the end.

content: こうなったからは、覚悟を決めて腰をすえて取り組むしかないだろう。

content.content: Since it’s come to this, all I can do is steel myself and get down to work on it.

Expresses the notion “since the situation is like that.” After からには, an expression like “persist in something to the end” follows. Used to express a request, order, intention, or something that one should do.
【からみたら】→
【からみる】1
【からみる】
1. Nからみると

content: イスラム教から見ると、それはおかしな考え方だ。

content.content: From an Islamic point of view, it is a strange way of thinking.

content: 先生から見ると、私のやりかたはまちがっているのかもしれませんが、私はこれがいいんです。

content.content: From the teacher’s point of view, my way of doing things might be incorrect, but for me it is right.

content: 私の立場から見ると、その見とおしは楽観的すぎると言わざるをえません。
