content.content: From my point of view, I can’t help saying that the forecast is too optimistic.

content: あなたのような人から見ると、私の主張していることなんかは急進的すぎるということになるんでしょうね。

content.content: From the stance of someone like you, what I am insisting on would probably be seen as too radical.

content: 子供たちから見ると、おとなはいったい何をやっているんだ、ということになるんだろうね。

content.content: The children are probably wondering what in the world the grown-ups are doing.

Used in the forms Nからみると／みれば／みたら and expresses judging something from a certain point of view. Has the same meaning as からというと, but can be directly attached to nouns expressing people, which makes it different from からというと.
2. Nからみて

content: あの言い方からみて、私はあの人にきらわれているようだ。

content.content: From the way he spoke, he really seems to dislike me.

content: あの態度から見て、彼女は引き下がる気はまったくないようだ。

content.content: Considering her attitude, she doesn’t seem to have any intention of withdrawing.

content: あの口ぶりから見て、彼はもうその話を知っているようだな。

content.content: Judging from the way he talks, he already seems to know what was said.

content: あの人の性格から見て、そんなことで納得するはずがない。

content.content: Judging from her character, there’s no way she could be persuaded.
Expresses the basis for making a judgment.
【かりそめにも】

content: かりそめにもそのような恐ろしいことを口にしてはならない。

content.content: Whatever happens, you shouldn’t say such an awful thing.

content: かりそめにも一城の主たる方が、こんなところにお泊まりになるはずがない。

content.content: I can’t imagine that the lord of a castle would ever have stayed in such a place.
An old-fashioned way of saying かりにも.
【かりにも】
【かりに】
1. かりに　...たら／...ば

content: かりに3億円の宝くじに当たったら、何をしますか。

content.content: If you were to win 300 million yen in the lottery, what would you do?

content: 仮に関東大震災と同程度の地震が今の東京に起こったら、東京はどうなってしまうだろうか。

content.content: If an earthquake of the same scale as the Great Kanto Earthquake happened in Tokyo now, what would happen to this city?

content: 仮に予定の時間までに私がもどってこない場合は、先に出発してください。

content.content: If I don’t come back by the appointed time, please go ahead and leave before me.

Used with a clause expressing a condition or situation, such as たら, ば, or 場合は, and expresses “a supposition that something has happened.” Has a similar meaning to もし（も）, but かりに implies a stronger feeling of supposing something while leaving the real situation aside. See Usage 1 of もし for further explanation about the differences between かりに and もし.
2. かりに　...とすれば／...としたら

content: かりに 100 人来るとしたら、この部屋には入りきらない。

content.content: Assuming that a hundred people come, they couldn’t all fit in this room.

content: 仮にあなたの話が本当だとすれば、彼は嘘をついていることになる。

content.content: If what you said is true, he would be telling a lie.

content: 仮に私の推測が正しいとすれば、あの二人はもうすぐ婚約するはずだ。

content.content: If my supposition is correct, they will soon be engaged.

content: 仮に時給千円とすれば、一日5時間働けば5千円もらえることになる。

content.content: If the pay is 1,000 yen per hour and if you work five hours a day, you will make 5,000 yen.
Used with とすれば, としたら, とする, and と呼ぶ and expresses “supposing something, then....” Used to describe what would happen if the speaker’s assumption about a certain thing or situation is realized.
Sometimes used without ば or たら, as in the following examples.
（例1）いまかりにXの値を 100 としよう。
Let’s give X a value of
（例2）かりにこの人をA子さんと呼んでおく。
We’ll call this person Ako-san for now.
Example 1 is often used in mathematics.
3. かりに　...ても／...としても

content: かりに参加希望者が定員に満たないような場合でも旅行は決行します。

content.content: Even if we don’t get enough applicants to fill all the openings, we will go ahead with the trip.

content: かりに予定の日までに私が帰って来ないようなことがあっても、心配しないで待っていてくれ。

content.content: Please wait for me and don’t worry even if I don’t come back by the expected day.

content: 仮にその話がうそだとしても、おもしろいじゃないか。

content.content: Even if that story is all a lie, don’t you think it’s interesting?

content: 仮に手術で命が助かったとしても、一生寝たきりの生活となるだろう。

content.content: He’ll be permanently bedridden, even if his life is saved by the operation.
With an adversative conditional clause such as ても／としても, this expresses “even if something has happened or is the case.”
【かりにも】An adverb which means “even if....” A rather formal expression used in written language. かりそめにも and かりにもせよ are also used.
1. かりにも+　禁止／否定の表現

content: かりにもこのことは人に言うな。

content.content: Whatever you do, don’t say this to other people.

content: かりにも人のものを盗んだりしてはいけない。

content.content: Whatever the situation, you shouldn’t steal someone else’s belongings.

content: 仮にもそのようなことは口にすべきではない。

content.content: Whatever happens, you shouldn’t say such a thing.

content: 仮にも死ぬなんてことは考えないでほしい。

content.content: I don’t even want you to think about suicide.

content: 仮にもあんな男と結婚したいとは思わない。

content.content: I wouldn’t dream of being married to such a man.
Used with a prohibition or a negative expression and expresses that “even just taking it as a supposition, one doesn’t or shouldn’t do such a thing.”
2. かりにも　...なら／...いじょうは

content: かりにも大学生なら、このくらいの漢字は読めるだろう。

content.content: Any university student worth his salt should be able to read at least these kanji.

content: かりにもチャンピオンである以上は、この試合で負けるわけにはいかない。

content.content: A champion worthy of the name shouldn’t lose this game.

content: 仮にも教師であるからには生徒に尊敬される人間でありたい。

content.content: Anyone who is a teacher ought to be respected by the students.

content: 仮にも学長という立場にある以上は、大学の経営についても関心を払うべきだ。

content.content: If someone is to be the president of a university, then he or she ought to pay attention to the university’s management.

content: 仮にも医者ともあろうものが患者を犠牲にして金もうけを行うとは信じがたいことだ。

content.content: It is unbelievable that someone who is supposed to be a doctor should sacrifice his patients to make money.

Used with a noun or clause which expresses an occupation or position, to describe something which should be done by the person in such a position. Used in sentence patterns such as Xなら／いじょうは／からには／ともあろうものがY, where Y expresses a judgment that is appropriate when X arises, or something which should be done by a person in that position. Xともあろうものが, in

content: , is used when X does something s/he shouldn’t do, and it means that X shouldn’t do it.

content.content: 【かれ】［A-かれA-かれ］

content: 遅かれ早かれ、山田さんも来るでしょう。

content.content: Sooner or later, Yamada-san will come, too.

content: 人は多かれ少なかれ、悩みをもっているものだ。

content.content: Be they many or few, everyone has worries.
Means “in both cases.” Two i-adjectives which have opposite meanings are used. Example

content: means “sometime sooner or later,” and
means “many or few.” Used as an idiomatic expression. よかれあしかれ is also used.

content.content: 【かろう】［N／Na　ではなかろう］［A-かろう］［A-く（は）なかろう］

content: その話は真実ではなかろう。

content.content: That is probably not true.

content: 親をなくしてはさぞや辛かろう。

content.content: He’s probably having a hard time after losing his one of his parents.

content: 少しは苦しむのもよかろう。

content.content: It is probably good for him to suffer a little.

content: 手術はさほどむずかしくはなかろうと存じます。

content.content: We believe the operation will probably not be that difficult.

Attaches to i-adjectives or ではな, which is the negative form of だ without い. Expresses supposition, and has almost the same meaning as だろう. The suppositional usage of V-よう corresponds to the form かろうfor verbs. A literary and old-fashioned expression used in written language or formal spoken language. In everyday spoken language, だろう is used.
【かろうじて】A formal, expression with the feel of written language. In everyday spoken language, どうにか and なんとか are often used. やっと and ようやく are similar expressions.
1. かろうじてV-た

content: 試験の開始時間に、かろうじて間に合った。

content.content: I barely arrived in time for the start of the exam.

content: 試験のできは良くなかったが、かろうじて合格できた。

content.content: I did badly on the exam but somehow managed to pass it.

content: 雨でタイヤがスリップした。危ないところだったが、かろうじて事故はまぬがれた。

content.content: My car skidded because of rain. It was really dangerous, and I just avoided having an accident.

content: 国連の介入で、かろうじて武力衝突は避けられた。

content.content: Because of the intervention of the United Nations, the use of arms was narrowly averted.

content: ひどい怪我だったが、かろうじて死なずにすんだ。

content.content: It was a terrible injury, and I narrowly escaped death.
Means “barely” or “narrowly managing to do something.” Used when a good result is achieved or the worst situation is avoided. Used in the forms かろうじて...をまぬがれた, かろうじて...せずにすんだ, and かろうじて...は避けられた.

やっと has the implication that a long time or great trouble is needed to achieve a result. On the other hand, with かろうじて a process is not always necessary, and the result is the important point. It is more formal than やっと and used in written language.
2. かろうじてV-ている

content: 毎日の生活は苦しいが、かろうじて借金はせずに済んでいる。

content.content: Everyday life is hard, and I just manage to get by without borrowing money.

content: 病人は機械の力を借りて、かろうじて生きている。

content.content: The patient is on life support, barely alive.

content: 現代人は、毎日のストレスに耐えて、かろうじてバランスを保っているに過ぎない。

content.content: People today are only just managing to endure the stress of everyday life and make ends meet.

content: 彼女も、かろうじて涙をこらえているようだった。

content.content: She also seemed to be fighting back tears.

Expresses “barely managing” or “accomplishing something with difficulty.” Used when conditions are bad, but the worst outcome is avoided and the present condition can be maintained with difficulty, as in

content: . Also used when the present condition is maintained by great effort or trouble, as in
. The meaning of
is that she is almost crying but refrains from it with effort.

content.content: 3. かろうじてV-るN

content: この道は、車二台がかろうじてすれ違える広さしかない。

content.content: This road is just wide enough to let two cars pass each other.

content: 列車の寝台というのは、人ひとりが、かろうじて横になれる大きさだ。

content.content: The berth in the train is barely big enough for a person to lie down.

content: その家は、僕にもかろうじて買えそうな値段だ。

content.content: The price of that house is at the limit of what I can afford.

content: 私の英語は、かろうじて日常会話ができる程度だ。

content.content: My English ability is barely enough for daily conversation.
With expressions of potentiality, as in

content: to
, かろうじて means “someone somehow manages to achieve something.” Used when something is difficult to do, but someone just barely can do it, with no margin to spare.

content.content: 【かわきりに】→
【をかわきりに】
【かわりに】［Nのかわりに］［Vかわりに］

content: わたしのかわりに山田さんが会議にでる予定です。

content.content: Instead of me, Yamada-san will attend the meeting.

content: ママは熱があるので、きょうはパパがかわりにむかえに行ってあげる。

content.content: Dad: Your mom has a fever, so today I’ll pick you up instead.

content: じゃあ、きょうはぼくが作るかわりに、あしたかぜがなおってたらきみが料理するんだぞ。

content.content: OK, I’ll cook today and then you can cook tomorrow, if you’re over your cold.

content: 今度転勤して来たこのまちはしずかでおちついているかわりに交通の便がややわるい。

content.content: While the town I was transferred to this time is quiet and calm, the public transportation is not so good.

content: 彼女のような生き方をしていたんでは、大きな失敗もしない代わりに、胸おどるような経験もないだろうね。

content.content: Living like she does means that there aren’t any big failures, but on the other hand, nothing thrilling happens, you know?
Expresses substitution of other people or things, as in

content: , and
. Also expresses that, while there is a good aspect to something, there is also a bad aspect, or vice versa, as in
and

content.content: 1. Nが

content: あの人が山本さんです。

content.content: That person is Yamamoto-san.

content: 隣のうちには猫が3匹いる。

content.content: There are three cats in the house next door.

content: あ、財布が落ちている。

content.content: Look, there’s a wallet on the floor.

content: この本は表紙がきれいですね。

content.content: This book has a beautiful cover, doesn’t it.

content: 私はジャズが好きです。

content.content: I like jazz.

content: 外交官になるには語学力が必要だ。

content.content: You need to be good at languages to be a diplomat.

content: 彼は 10 ヶ国語ができるらしい。

content.content: I heard that he can speak ten different languages.
Attaches to a noun and indicates that the noun is the subject of an action or state, as in

content: , and
, or that the noun is the object of a state, as in
, and
. When used in proverbs or idioms, it sometimes attaches to words other than nouns, as in 負けるが勝ち (Sometimes you have to lose to win).

content.content: 2. NがNだから

content: 親が親だから、子供があんなふうに生意気になるのだ。

content.content: With such parents, it’s no wonder the child is so bratty.

content: もう時間が時間だし、今から行ってもあのレストランは閉まってるかもしれないよ。

content.content: Considering what time it is now, the restaurant might be closed by the time we get there.

content: デパートをぶらぶら歩いていて、かわいいネックレスを見つけた。とても気に入ったのだが、なにしろ値段が値段だったので買うのはあきらめた。

content.content: I was wandering around the department store and found a pretty necklace. I really liked it, but with the price being what it was, I decided not to buy it.

content: A:再就職しようと思ったけど、なかなかむずかしいわ。

content.content: I thought I’d try to go back to work, but it’s really quite difficult to find a job.
B:そりゃ、年が年だもの。70すぎた人間なんか今どきどこも雇ってくれないわよ。
Well, it’s your age. These days no one wants to hire someone in his seventies.

The same noun is repeated and then followed by a word expressing a reason, such as だから, ので, し, だもの, or もので. In many cases, this pattern expresses a negative evaluation of the noun and is used to describe an inevitable result that arises from it. For example,

content: means the parents are too indulgent of their children,
means it is too late to go to the restaurant,
means the price is far too expensive, and
means that, in B’s opinion, A is too old to get another job.

content.content: 3. NがNだけに

content: ここの料理は、素材が素材だけに味も格別だ。

content.content: The food here is exceptionally tasty because of the ingredients.

content: この店は味は大したことはないが、場所が場所だけにたいていいつも満員だ。

content.content: The food at this restaurant isn’t particularly good, but its location means it’s almost always full.

content: この店はとても気に入っているのだが、場所が場所だけにそうしょっちゅうは来られないのが残念だ。

content.content: I really like this shop, but because it’s located where it is, unfortunately I can’t come very often.

content: その映画は戦時中の日本軍の侵略を扱ったもので、多くの評論家が絶賛している優れた作品だが、内容が内容だけに、一般的な娯楽映画と比べると興行成績は格段に悪かった。

content.content: The movie deals with the aggression of the Japanese army during the war. It is an excellent work that many critics have praised highly, but because of the subject matter, box office returns were markedly worse than those of ordinary movies made for entertainment.

content: 学長が収賄容疑で逮捕された。今までも小さな不祥事はあったが、マスコミには騒がれないよう注意してきた。しかし、今回はことがことだけに、マスコミの取材からは逃れられないだろう。

content.content: The president of the university was arrested on suspicion of bribery. There have been minor scandals before, but care was always taken to keep the media from making anything of them.  However, this time, with the situation being what it is, there will be no stopping the mass media from covering the story.

Repetition of the same noun indicates that a certain outcome is natural or inevitable, considering the characteristics of that noun. NがNだけに is followed by a description of the natural or inevitable outcome. The listener/reader does not know the exact nature of the noun’s characteristics until s/he reaches the description in the latter part of the sentence. For example, in

content: , the description 味も格別だ (exceptionally tasty) tells us the ingredients are good. However, in the sentence 素材が素材だけに大した料理はできやしない (Because the ingredients are what they are, the food can’t be very good), the interpretation is that the ingredients are bad.
means a place that is conveniently located and easy to get to. On the other hand,
means a place that is inconveniently located and hard to get to. ことがことだけに in
is an idiomatic expression. In this example, it means “because this situation is serious.”

content.content: 4. NがNなら...（が）

content: 時代が時代なら、この本も売れたかもしれないが、今の時代では人間の生き方を問うような本は若い人には読まれない。

content.content: If times were different, this book might have sold well, but in this day and age, young people don’t read books that raise questions about how to live.

content: 世が世ならあいつも出世できただろうに。

content.content: In another time and place, she probably would have been successful.

content: 俺も大学が大学ならもう少しましな仕事にもつけたのだろうが、この大学ではせいぜいこの会社ぐらいがいいところだ。

content.content: I suppose if I had graduated from a better university, I could have found a better job, but this is the best company anyone from a university like mine could hope to work for.

Repetition of the same noun indicates that the speaker is making the supposition “if the conditions were suitable....” NがNなら is accompanied by expressions such asだろうが, だろうに or かもしれないが, and a statement or description of the actual state of affairs then follows.

content: means “if it were a time when many people thought seriously about how to live,”
means “if people in society evaluated him correctly,” and

means “if I had graduated from a better university.” This pattern is used to hypothesize a situation that is better than reality; it means “if the situation were X, a good result like Y would follow.” Because the situation hypothesized is one that is actually impossible, a sense of pity, regret, or resignation is implied.

content.content: 5. NがNならNもNだ

content: この生徒はいつも教師に口答えばかりして困る。親もすぐ学校にどなりこんでくるし、まったく、親が親なら子も子だ。

content.content: This student always causes trouble to his teachers by answering back. His parents often come storming into the school with complaints, too. With such parents, it’s no wonder the children behave the way they do.

content: まったく、おじさんがおじさんなら、おばさんもおばさんだよ。おじさんが頑固なのはわかっているんだから、嘘でも「ごめんなさい」って言えば喧嘩なんかすぐにおさまるのに。

content.content: (to an aunt and uncle) Honestly, you two are both just as bad as each other. (to the aunt) You know he’s obstinate, so if you say “I’m sorry,” even if you don’t mean it, the quarrel will quickly be resolved.

The first noun (repeated in NがNなら) is different from the second noun (repeated in NもNだ), but the two nouns are related. The expression as a whole conveys a negative evaluation: both N’s are equally bad.

content: means that the parents and child are equally problematic, and
means that both the uncle and aunt are bad, because they are equally stubborn. Used to criticize both parties or elements.

content.content: 6. V-たがさいご→
【がさいご】
7. V-るがはやいか→
【はやいか】
【が2】［N／Na　だが］［A／V　が］
1. が〈adversative connective〉

content: 彼は学生だが、私は社会人だ。

content.content: He is a student, but I work.

content: 昨日は暑かったが、今日は急に涼しくなって風邪をひきそうだ。

content.content: Yesterday it was hot, but today it’s turned cold all of a sudden, and I feel like I’m going to catch a cold.

content: 今日の試合は、がんばったが負けてしまった。

content.content: We did our best in the game today, but we lost.

content: 種をまいたが、芽が一つも出なかった。

content.content: I planted some seeds, but not a single one sprouted.

Connects two situations or events in a relation of contrast. Used when the content of the first half of the sentence contrasts with that of the second half, or when what is said in the second half is the opposite of what is expected from the first half.
2. が〈introductory remark〉

content: 山田と申しますが、陽子さんいらっしゃいますか。

content.content: My name is Yamada. May I speak to Yoko-san, please?

content: 今日広田さんに会うんですが、何か伝えておくことはありますか。

content.content: I’ll see Hirota-san today. Is there anything I should tell her?

content: 先日お願いいたしました件ですが、引き受けていただくことはできませんでしょうか。

content.content: Regarding the request I made the other day, do you think it would it be possible for you to take it on?

content: 先月パソコンを買ったのですが、使い方がよくわからないので教えてほしいんですが。

content.content: I bought a computer last month, but I don’t really know how to use it, so could you teach me...?
Used to make a remark that prefaces a question, a request, an order, or some other speech act that exerts an influence on the addressee.
3. が〈hesitation〉

content: 《コピーしている人に》あのう、ちょっと1枚だけコピーしたいんですが。

content.content: 《to someone making copies》Umm, do you think I could make just one copy?

content: すみませんが、ちょっとお先に失礼させていただきたいんですが。

content.content: I’m sorry, but I would like to be excused a little bit early.

content: あのう、実は明日の会議に出られないんですが。

content.content: Well, actually, I can’t attend the meeting tomorrow.

content: この辞書に書いてること、間違っていると思うんですが。

content.content: I think what it says in this dictionary is actually incorrect.
Can be added to the end of a sentence to soften something that is hard to say or a request that is difficult to make.

【がかり】がかり is a word derived from the verb かかる. かかる may mean “take,” as in時間／お金がかかる (take time/money), “see/receive treatment,” as in 医者にかかる (see a doctor), “be affected,” as in 雨がかかる (get wet in the rain), “start,” as in仕事にかかる (get started with work), and so on.
1. 数量詞+がかり

content: グランドピアノを5人がかりでやっと運んだ。

content.content: It took five people to move the grand piano.

content: 3日がかりで作り上げた巨大な雪だるまは、翌日のポカポカ陽気ですぐに溶けてしまった。

content.content: The enormous snowman it had taken us three days to build melted away quickly in the warm sunshine of the following day.

content: 5年がかりの調査の結果、その湖の生態系は壊れかかっているということがわかった。

content.content: As a result of five long years of research, we found that the ecosystem of the lake was breaking down.

content: さすが横綱は体が大きくて力も強いので、高校生力士が3人がかりで向かっていってもまるで勝ち目はなかった。

content.content: The yokozuna (grand champion) was as big and strong as you might expect, so there was no chance for a win by any of the three high school wrestlers who faced off against him.

Attaches to words like 人, 日, or 時間 and expresses an action that requires many people or a lengthy time to be accomplished. Followed by an expression of the action that was difficult and required such effort.
2. Nがかり

content: 彼女は 30 才にもなって、親がかりで留学した。

content.content: She studied abroad totally financed by her parents, even though she was already thirty years old.

content: 男は「君はバラのように美しいね」などと、芝居がかりのせりふを吐いた。

content.content: The man melodramatically spewed out lines like “You are as beautiful as a rose.”
Means something like “depending on/being served by (one’s parents),” as in

content: , or “has the quality of (a theatrical performance),” as in

. There are no other examples but 親がかり for the first type of usage. For the second type, 神がかり (possessed; fanatic) is also used, but there are very few other nouns to which がかり can be attached. The second type is also used in the forms Nがかっている and Nがかった; in such cases, a wider range of words is used, like 青みがかった (with blue overtones) and 左がかった (left-leaning).

content.content: 3. R-がかり

content: 広場でトランペットの練習をしていると、通りがかりの人が何人も足を止めて聞いていった。

content.content: When I was practicing my trumpet in a public square, a number of passersby stopped to listen.

content: それは他の部署の企画だったが、担当者にいくらかアドバイスもしたので、行きがかり上しかたなく私も関わることになってしまった。

content.content: Though it was another department’s project, since I had given some advice to the person in charge, I ended up getting involved with it myself.
Example

content: means “happened to pass by.” 行きがかり上 in
means “because of the sequence of events or situation up to this time.”
and
are idiomatic expressions, and がかり cannot be attached to any other verbs.

content.content: 【がかる】［NがかったN］

content: 川井さんは青みがかった紫色のとてもきれいなワンピースを着ていた。

content.content: Kawai-san wore a beautiful purple dress with blue overtones.

content: その絵は背景が赤みがかった空色で、まるで夕暮れの空のようだ。

content.content: The background in that drawing is sky-blue tinged with red, and it looks very much like an evening sky.

content: 山本は考えることが左がかっている（＝左翼的だ）。

content.content: Yamamoto’s thinking is “left-leaning” (=somewhat leftist).

content: あいつの行動はどこか芝居がかっていて、こっけいだ。

content.content: That guy’s actions are like something out of a play—really comical.

content: その人は、村では神がかった存在として尊敬されおそれられている。

content.content: That person has something of the supernatural about her, so she’s both respected and feared in the village.
がかった follows a noun and indicates that something shares some of the attributes associated with that noun. The range of nouns with which it can be used is limited. The form がかっている is also used, as in
【がさいご】［V-たがさいご］

content: ここで会ったが最後、謝ってもらうまでは逃がしはしない。

content.content: Now that I’ve met you here, I won’t let you go until you apologize to me.

content: この計画を聞いたが最後、あなたもグループに加わってもらおう。

content.content: Now that you’ve heard about this project, we’ll have you join the group.

content: 学校内でタバコを吸っているのを見つかったが最後、停学は免れないだろう。

content.content: Now that they’ve been found smoking in school, they won’t be able to avoid suspension.

content: その茶碗は、一度手に取ったが最後、どうしても買わずにはいられなくなるほど手触りや重さ、色合いなどが私の好みに合っていた。

content.content: Once I had picked up the bowl I couldn’t help buying it, since its feel, weight, and color were so much to my liking.
Expresses that a certain event occurs as the consequence of someone’s action or a course of events indicated in the subsequent clause. Example

content: expresses a challenge, meaning “I met you here, so you shall apologize to me.” Example
has the imperative meaning “because you have heard about this project, you have to join the group.” Also used in general, in non-threatening, non-imperative sentences such as
and

content.content: 【がたい】［R-がたい］

content: 信じがたいことだが本当なのだ。

content.content: It’s hard to believe, but it’s true.

content: あいつの言うことは何の根拠もないし常識はずれで、とうてい理解しがたい。

content.content: What he says is groundless, absurd, and hardly comprehensible.

content: 日本が戦時中にアジア諸国で名もない人たちを理由もなく殺したことは、動かしがたい事実である。

content.content: It is an indisputable fact that, during the war, the Japanese Army killed ordinary people in Asian countries for no reason.

content: 彼は部下の女性に対するセクシャル・ハラスメントで告発されたにもかかわらず、まるで反省の色が見えないばかりか、あの女は無能だなどと言いふらしており、まったく許しがたい。

content.content: Though he was prosecuted by a female subordinate for sexual harassment, he not only shows no sign of remorse, he’s also spreading reports that she’s incompetent. That’s really unpardonable!

Attaches to a verb stem and means that an action is difficult or impossible to do. Combines with verbs of perception and awareness, as in 想像しがたい (hard to imagine), 認めがたい (hard to admit/accept), (考えを) 受け入れがたい (hard to accept other people’s (opinions/ideas)), 賛成しがたい (difficult to agree with). Also used with verbs of utterance, as in 言いがたい (hard to say) and 表しがたい (difficult to express). 動かしがたい事実 in

content: is an idiomatic expression that means something is undeniably true. Often used in written language.

content.content: 【がち】
1. Nがち

content: その作家は、ここ数年病気がちでなかなかまとまった仕事ができないと言っている。

content.content: The writer says she has been sickly in recent years and has found it hard to complete any work.

content: このところ、はっきりしない曇りがちの天気が続いているので、洗濯ものが干せなくて困る。

content.content: Because we’ve been having such unsettled, mostly cloudy weather these days, it’s a real problem not to be able to hang the wash out to dry.

content: どうしてあんなことをしたんだと問いつめると、彼女は伏し目がちに、どうしてもお金がほしかったのだと答えた。

content.content: When I demanded to know why she had done such a thing, she answered, with downcast eyes, that she had been desperate for money.

content: 「よかったらうちまで車で送ってもらえないでしょうか」と、彼女は遠慮がちにたずねた。

content.content: “Could you possibly take me home in your car?” she hesitantly asked me.

Attaches to a noun and expresses that something has the characteristics of that noun or tends to be in the state it implies. Used when the state implied by the noun is considered unusual or has a negative connotation. Thus the words with which がち can be combined are limited. Examples

content: and
are idiomatic expressions.

content.content: 2. R-がち

content: 寒い季節は家の中にこもりがちだが、たまには外にでて体を動かした方がいい。

content.content: We tend to stay inside in the cold season, but it’s better to go outside once in a while and get some exercise.

content: 彼女に電話すると、どうしても長話になりがちで、いつも父親に文句を言われる。

content.content: When I phone her, it tends to be a long call and my father complains to me about it.

content: 甘いものはついつい食べ過ぎてしまいがちなので、ダイエット中は気をつけましょう。

content.content: It’s so easy to end up eating too many sweets, so we have to be careful when we’re on a diet.

content: 惰性で仕事を続けていると、この仕事に飛び込んだ頃の若々しい情熱をつい忘れがちになる。

content.content: When we keep on working from sheer force of habit, we tend to forget the youthful zest we once had when we started the job.

content: 「『役不足』とは『その役を務めるには能力が不足している』という意味だ」という解釈は、ありがちな間違いだ。

content.content: Interpreting the expression yakubusoku as “lacking the ability to fulfil that role” is a common error.

Attaches to a verb and means that one tends to do something even when one doesn’t mean to. Describes an unfavorable action. Often used withどうしても (can’t help but do something), つい (involuntarily, unwittingly), うっかり(carelessly, without realizing), and てしまう (end up doing something). ありがちな in

content: means “something that happens frequently.”

content.content: 【がてら】［Nがてら］［R-がてら］

content: 買い物がてら、その辺をぶらぶらしない？

content.content: While we’re shopping, why don’t we take a stroll around the place?

content: 散歩がてら、パンを買いに行こう。

content.content: Let’s go buy some bread on our walk.

content: 引っ越してきてから2週間ほどの間、私は運動がてら近所の町を歩き回った。

content.content: In the two weeks since I moved here, I’ve walked around the neighborhood partly for exercise.

content: 彼は映画評論家なので、仕事がてらよくアジアの映画を見ることがあるそうだ。

content.content: He is a movie critic, so he often watches Asian movies as part of his work.

content: 京都においでの節は、お遊びがてらぜひ私どものところへもお立ち寄りください。

content.content: When you visit Kyoto, please do stop by at our house as well.

Attaches to a noun that expresses an action or a verb stem. Used in the form XがてらY and means “combining action X with another action Y.” Often used when doing X results in being able to do Y. XをかねてY and XかたがたY are also used to express the same meaning.
【がな】

content: 山田さんはまだ来ないの？　遅れずに来るように言っておいたんだがな。

content.content: Yamada-san hasn’t come yet? I told her not to be late!

content: 今度の試験も駄目だった。一生懸命勉強したつもりなんだがなあ。

content.content: I did badly on this test, too...and I was sure I had studied so hard for it.

content: あした運動会だろう？　雨が降らないといいがなあ。

content.content: Tomorrow is the sports day, right? I sure hope it doesn’t rain.

content: 彼らももう少し本気で仕事に取り組んでくれるようになるといいんだがなあ。

content.content: I wish they would get a little more serious about their work.

content: 田口君、今、暇？　ちょっと手伝ってくれるとありがたいんだがな。

content.content: Taguchi-kun, are you free right now? It’d be great if you could give me a hand for a second.

Consists of the contradictory conjunction が combined with the particle な. Used at the end of a sentence and indicates either bewilderment at the gap between one’s intention and the actual outcome, or a wish for something that has yet to occur. As in example

content: , it can be used to make a request. It cannot be attached to a sentence in polite form. It is a spoken language expression used by men when they are talking to themselves or to someone close. The final sound な is sometimes lengthened so it is pronounced as ...がなあ. A similar expression, ...けどな, is used by women.

content.content: 【がはやいか】［V-るがはやいか］

content: そのことばを聞くがはやいか、彼はその男になぐりかかった。

content.content: As soon as he heard the word, he started hitting the man.

content: その男はジョッキをつかむがはやいか一気に飲みほした。

content.content: The instant the man picked up the beer mug, he drank it empty in one gulp.

content: こどもは、学校から帰って来ると、玄関にカバンをおくが早いか、また飛び出していった。

content.content: After getting home from school, the child no sooner placed his bag in the entrance than he rushed out again.

content: その鳥は、ウサギをするどいツメでとらえるが早いか、あっと言う間に空にまい上がった。

content.content: As soon as the bird had caught the rabbit with its sharp claws, it immediately flew up into the sky.
Means Y happens almost simultaneously with X. Similar to やいなや and とたんに. Used in written language.
【がゆえ】→
【ゆえ】3
【がよかろう】→
【よかろう】
【がり】→
【がる】
【がる】［Na がる］［A-がる］［V-たがる］

content: 注射をいやがるこどもは多い。

content.content: Many children hate injections.

content: その子は自分と同じくらいの大きさの犬をかわいがっている。

content.content: The girl loves the dog, which is almost her size.

content: 妻の死をいつまでもかなしがってばかりはいられない。わたしには残されたこどもたちをそだてていく義務がある。

content.content: It is not good for me to do nothing but grieve over the death of my wife. I have a duty to bring up the children she left me.

content: こわがらなくてもいいのよ。この人はおかあさんのともだちなの。

content.content: You don’t need to be scared. She is a friend of my mother’s.

content: そのラーメン屋は朝8時から夜の2時までやっているうえに安くてうまいので、近所の学生たちに重宝がられていた。

content.content: That Chinese noodle soup shop is open from eight in the morning to two in the following morning, and what’s more, they serve cheap and tasty noodles, so it’s really prized by students in the neighborhood.

content: こどもがおもちゃをほしがって地べたにすわりこんで泣いていた。

content.content: The child wanted the toy and plopped down on the floor in tears.

content: 人の話を最後まで聞かずに口をはさみたがる人がときどきいる。

content.content: There are some people who love to butt in without listening to the end of a story.

Attaches to adjectives or stems of the V-たい form, which expresses desire. Means thinking, feeling, or acting a certain way. This pattern is used with verbs that describe a situation objectively, so it usually isn’t used in the first person, except in the narrative passages of a novel or in cases like

content: where one looks at oneself objectively. が in 本が読みたい and 車がほしい is changed toを, as in 本を読みたがる and 車をほしがる. In addition to the examples above, はずかしがる, さびしがる, なつかしがる, けむたがる, つよがる, いたがる and とくいがる are often used.

content.content: Variations such as たがり or あつがり, さむがり, さびしがり, はずかしがり and こわがり are nouns that refer to people who think, feel, or act in such-and-such a way.
【きく】→
【ときく】
【きっかけ】［Nをきっかけに（して）］

content: 彼女は卒業をきっかけに髪をきった。

content.content: She had her hair cut for her graduation.

content: 彼は、就職をきっかけにして、生活をかえた。

content.content: Getting a job was what changed his life.

content: 日本は朝鮮戦争をきっかけにして高度成長の時代にはいったと言われる。

content.content: It is said that the Korean War gave the impetus for Japan’s coming into a period of high economic growth.

content: こんなところで同じ高校の出身の方と出会うとは思いませんでした。これをきっかけに今後ともよろしくお願いいたします。

content.content: I didn’t imagine I would meet someone who went to the same high school here. I hope this will be the start of a good relationship for both of us.
Expresses “a chance, a basis for something, or an opportunity.”
【きっと】

content: 鈴木さんもきっと来るでしょう。

content.content: Surely Suzuki-san will come.

content: 雲が出てきた。今夜はきっと雨だろう。

content.content: It’s clouding over. It’s definitely going to rain tonight.

content: 彼女はきっとあのことを知っているにちがいない。

content.content: There’s no doubt that she has to know about it.

content: ご招待ありがとうございます。きっとうかがいます。

content.content: Thank you for your invitation. I shall certainly come.

content: そうですか。きっと来てくださいよ。お待ちしていますから。きっとですよ。

content.content: Will you? Please come, by all means. Remember, I’ll be waiting for you.
Means “surely” or “certainly.” Expresses the speaker’s supposition (which is more certain than たぶん), as in

content: , the strong will of the speaker, as in
, or a strong request addressed to the listener, as in
. When it has the function of promise, as in
and
, it can be replaced by かならず. In that case, a negative expression cannot be used.

content.content: （×）きっと行きません。
I surely will not go.
（×）きっと来ないでください。
Certainly never come here.
【きらいがある】［Nのきらいがある］［V-るきらいがある］

content: 彼はいい男だが、なんでもおおげさに言うきらいがある。

content.content: He is a good man, but he tends to exaggerate everything.

content: 最近の学生は自分で調べず、すぐ教師に頼るきらいがある。

content.content: Students today tend not to examine things for themselves but to depend on teachers too readily.

content: あの先生の講義はおもしろいのだが、いつの間にか自慢話に変わってしまうきらいがある。

content.content: That teacher’s lecture is interesting, but it tends to turn to boasting.

content: あの政治家は有能だが、やや独断専行のきらいがある。

content.content: That politician is competent, but he tends to be arbitrary.
Expresses that something has a certain tendency. Used for negative things. Has the feel of written language.
【きり】In spoken language, this often changes toっきり.
1. Nきり

content: ふたりきりで話しあった。

content.content: We discussed the matter just between the two of us.

content: のこったのは私ひとりきりだった。

content.content: I was the only one who stayed behind.

content: 見て。残ったお金はこれ（っ）きりよ。

content.content: Look. This is all the money that’s left.
Attaches to a noun and delimits a range, with the sense of “only that.” When used withこれ, それ, and あれ, these tend to become これっきり, それっきり, and あれっきり.
2. R-きり

content: 彼女は3人の子供の世話にかかりきり（で）、自分の時間もろくにない。

content.content: She has hardly any free time, because she spends every moment caring for her three children.

content: 熱を出した子供をつき（っ）きりで看病した。

content.content: I was constantly by my child’s side when he had a fever.
きり attaches to a verb stem and expresses doing only one thing all the time without doing anything else.
3. V-たきり...ない

content: 彼は卒業して日本を出ていったきり、もう5年も帰ってこない。

content.content: He hasn’t come back for five years since he graduated and left Japan.

content: あの方とは一度お会いしたきり（で）、その後、会っていません。

content.content: I met her only once and I haven’t seen her since.
Often used in the pattern たきり、...ない. Expresses that it is the last time something happened and it hasn’t happened since then. これっきり, それっきり, and あれっきり are also used .
（例）あの方とは一度お会いしましたが、それ（っ）きり会っていません。
I met her only once and I haven’t seen her since.
【きる】Attaches to a verb stem and adds various meanings to the action.
1. R-きる〈completion〉

content: お金を使いきってしまった。

content.content: I ran out of money.

content: 山道を登りきったところに小屋があった。

content.content: At the end of the mountain trail was a small hut.

content: 長編の冒険小説を1週間かけて読み切った。

content.content: I read an entire adventure novel in a week.
Expresses “doing something to the utmost.”
2. R-きる〈thoroughly〉

content: 無理な仕事をして疲れきってしまった。

content.content: I was exhausted from the excessive work load.

content: そんな分かりきったことをいつまで言っているんだ。

content.content: How long are you going to keep telling me such obvious things?

content: この絵はその情景を十分に描き切っているとは言えない。

content.content: I can’t say that this picture fully depicts the scene.

content: 彼女は絶対に自分が正しいと言い切った。

content.content: She insisted that she was absolutely correct.
Expresses doing something sufficiently or strongly.
3. R-きる〈severance〉

content: 大きな布を二つに断ち切った。

content.content: I cut a big cloth into two pieces.

content: 別れてからも彼女のことを思い切ることができない。

content.content: I can’t stop thinking about her even since we broke up.

content: 故郷にとどまりたいという思いを断ち切って出発した。

content.content: I gave up my intentions to remain in my hometown and set out.
Means “cutting.” Derived meanings include “discarding” and “giving up.”
4. R-きれない

content: それはいくら悔やんでも悔やみきれないことだった。

content.content: I can’t get over my regret.

content: その人との別れは、あきらめきれないつらい思い出として、今でも私の胸の奥底にある。

content.content: The memory of being unable to accept our breakup still pains me deep in my heart.
Expresses the notion that one “can’t do something completely” or “can’t do something enough.”
【きわまりない】［Na（なこと）きわまりない］［A-いこときわまりない］

content: その探検旅行は危険きわまりないものと言えた。

content.content: They say that the exploration of that region is highly dangerous.

content: その相手の電話の切り方は不愉快きわまりないものだった。

content.content: The other party’s way of hanging up was really unpleasant.

content: そのような行動は、この社会では無作法（なこと）きわまりないものとされている。

content.content: That sort of action is regarded as very rude in this society.

content: 丁重きわまりないごあいさつをいただき、まことに恐縮です。

content.content: I wish to thank you sincerely for your very courteous greeting.

content: そのけしきは美しいこときわまりないものだった。

content.content: The view was stupendously beautiful.

Expresses that something reaches its ultimate limit. Also takes the form きわまる, which has the same meaning, but this form can only be combined with na-adjectives, as in 無作法／丁重／不愉快きわまる. A formal expression used in written language. ことこのうえない may also be used.
【きわまる】→
【きわまりない】
【きわみ】［Nのきわみ］

content: このような盛大なる激励会を開いていただき、感激のきわみです。

content.content: I am deeply impressed by such a grand party on my behalf.

content: 彼が自殺してちょうど一か月たつ。あの日何か話しをしたそうな様子だったのに忙しくてそのままにしてしまった。いま思うと痛恨の極みだ。

content.content: One month has passed since he took his own life. It seemed that he wanted to say something on that day, but I was busy and didn’t do anything. When I think of it now, it pains me terribly.

content: 不慮の事故でわが子を失った母親は悲嘆の極みにあった。

content.content: The mother who lost her child in an accident was in the utter depths of grief.

content: 資産家の一人息子として、贅沢の極みを尽くしていた。

content.content: Being the only son of the millionaire, he lived a life of luxury.
Takes a limited number of nouns, such as 感激 and 痛恨. Expresses an extreme condition.
【きんじえない】→
【をきんじえない】
【ぎみ】［Nぎみ］［R-ぎみ］

content: ちょっとかぜぎみで、せきが出る。

content.content: I have a slight cold and cough.

content: 彼女はすこし緊張ぎみだった。

content.content: She was a little tense.

content: ここのところ、すこしつかれぎみで、仕事がはかどらない。

content.content: I’m a little tired these days and I can’t make progress with my work.

content: 現在の内閣の支持率は発足時よりやや下がり気味である。

content.content: The approval rate of the present cabinet is trending a little lower than when it took office.
Expresses a situation or tendency. Often used for negative things.
【くさい】
1. Nくさい〈smell〉

content: あれ？　ガスくさいよ！

content.content: What? I smell gas!

content: この部屋はなんだかカビくさい。

content.content: It’s musty in this room.

content: 昨日火事があったところは、焦げくさい臭いが充満していた。

content.content: The place where the fire broke out yesterday was filled with a charred, acrid smell.
Refers to the smell of something. Used for bad smells.
2. Nくさい〈appearance〉

content: インチキくさい商品だなあ。

content.content: These goods look fake.

content: 子供たちに信頼される教師になりたいのなら、そのインテリくさいしゃべり方を止めろ。

content.content: If you want to be a teacher trusted by children, you shouldn’t talk like such a high-and-mighty intellectual.

content: 彼女はバタ臭い顔立ちをしている。

content.content: She’s got the face of a foreigner!
Expresses that “something is very much like something else.” Used in a pejorative sense.
3. Na／A　くさい〈emphasis〉

content: あんた、いつまでそんな古くさいこと言っているつもり？

content.content: How long do you intend to keep telling me such outdated things?

content: そんな面倒くさいことは、だれか別の人に頼んでくれ。

content.content: Please ask someone else to do such a troublesome job.

content: 彼はけちくさいことばかり言うので、嫌われている。

content.content: People dislike him because he always says such narrow-minded things.
Attaches to adjectives with negative connotation and emphasizes their meaning.
【くせ】［Nのくせに］［Na なくせに］［A／V　くせに］

content: 彼は、自分ではできないくせに、いつも人のやり方にもんくを言う。

content.content: Though he can’t do it himself, he is always complaining about other people’s methods.

content: もんく言うんじゃないの。自分はできないくせに。

content.content: Don’t complain. You can’t even do it yourself!

content: あの選手は、体が大きいくせに、まったく力がない。

content.content: In spite of his size, that player has no strength at all.

content: こどものくせにおとなびたものの言い方をする子だな。

content.content: For just being a child, she sure talks like some adult!

content: 好きなくせに、嫌いだと言いはっている。

content.content: She says she doesn’t like it, even though she really does.

Used in the form XくせにY, where the situation Y, which is contrary to what would be expected from the content of X, continues. Y is often an expression of a negative evaluation. The form Y。Xくせに is also used, as in

content: . When the subjects of the two clauses are different, as in the next example, くせに cannot be used.

content.content: （×）犬は散歩に行きたがっているくせに、彼はつれて行ってやらなかった。
Despite his dog wanted to go for a walk, he didn’t take it.
（○）犬は散歩に行きたがっているのに、彼はつれて行ってやらなかった。
Though his dog wanted to go for a walk, he didn’t take it.
2. ...くせして

content: 彼は、自分ではできないくせして、いつも人のやり方についてああだこうだと言う。

content.content: Although he can’t do it himself, he is always telling other people how to do it.

content: 人のやり方にけちつけるんじゃないの。自分ではできないくせして。

content.content: Quit criticizing other people. I know you can’t even do it yourself!

content: この人、大きなからだのくせして、ほんとに力がないんだから。

content.content: Even though he’s big, he’s got almost no strength.

content: こどものくせしておとなびたものの言い方をする子だな。

content.content: For being just a child, she sure talks like some adult!

content: 好きなくせして、嫌いだと言いはっている。

content.content: He insists he doesn’t like it, even though he really does.
Similar in meaning to くせに, but くせして often gives a more familiar impression.
3. そのくせ

content: 彼女はもんくばかり言う。そのくせ自分ではなにもしない。

content.content: She’s always complaining. But she does nothing herself.

content: 彼女は自分ではなにもしない。そのくせ、もんくだけは言う。

content.content: She does nothing herself. But she always complains.

content: 彼女はよく山田君はバカだと言ってるでしょ。そのくせ、私がそうだ、そうだというと、こんどはおこるのよ。

content.content: You know she always says Yamada-kun is a fool. But then, when I say she’s right, she gets angry.

content: 日本人は他人には非常に冷淡な時がある、そのくせ身内に対しては異常なくらい仲間意識を持つという側面がある、とその研究者は言っている。

content.content: That researcher says that, while Japanese people can be extremely standoffish to strangers, they have a remarkably strong sense of bonds with their relatives.
Connects two separate sentences. Expresses the same meaning as くせに, but そのくせ can’t be used with prohibitive or imperative expressions, such as もんく言うんじゃないの in example

content: of ...くせに.

content.content: （×）自分では何もしないじゃない。そのくせもんく言うんじゃないの。
You do nothing. Don’t complain.
【ください】→
【てください】
【くださる】→
【てくださる】
【くらい】ぐらい is often used as well. ほど is a very similar expression, butくらい is more for spoken language.
1. 数量詞+くらい〈approximation〉

content: この道を5分くらい行くと、大きな川があります。

content.content: If you go along this road for about five minutes, there will be a big river.

content: 修理には一週間ぐらいかかります。

content.content: The repairs will take about one week.

content: これ、いくらだろう。 3000 円ぐらいかな。

content.content: How much is this? About 3,000 yen, I suppose?

content: その島はこの国の3倍くらいの面積がある。

content.content: That island is about three times as large as this country.

content: 店内のお客さまに、まいごのお子さまのご案内を申し上げます。青いシャツと黄色のズボンの、2才ぐらいのお子さまがまいごになっていらっしゃいます。

content.content: We would like to make a lost child announcement to the customers in this store. A child about two years old, wearing a blue shirt and yellow trousers, is lost.
Attaches to a quantifier and expresses that something is around a certain amount or level (approximate figure). When a time or date is being referred to, ...くらいに is used.
（○）3時ぐらいに来てください。
Please come at around three o’clock.
（×）3時ぐらい来てください。
Please come three o’clock around.

Also, as the following example shows, when くらい is combined with question words such as どれ／どの (which), いくら (how much), 何メートル／キログラム／時間 (how many meters/kilograms/hours), it can be used to ask the approximate quantity, and when it is combined with これ, それ, or あれ (this/that), it can be used to show the actual quantity, size, etc.
（例）A:テープを切ってくれない？
Could you cut the tape?
B:どれくらい？
About how long?
A:《指を広げて大きさを示しながら》これくらい。
《showing the size by spreading two fingers》About this long.
2. Nくらい〈comparison〉a. N（とおなじ）くらい

content: A:物価は日本と比べてどうですか。

content.content: How is the cost of living as compared to Japan?
B:あまり変わりませんよ。日本と同じくらいです。
Not so different. It’s about the same as in Japan.

content: A:田中君って、いくつぐらいだろう。

content.content: How old do you think Tanaka-kun is?
B:そうだね。うちの息子ぐらいじゃないかな。
Let me see. About as old as my son is, I guess.

content: こんどのアパートは前のと同じぐらい広くて、しかも日当たりがいい。

content.content: This next apartment is about as big as the last one, and what’s more, it gets lots of sunshine.
Used in the pattern XはY（とおなじ）くらい...だ, and means that X and Y are almost the same in terms of quantity, size, etc. ほど does not have this usage.
b. N（とおなじ）くらいのN

content: このボールは、ちょうどリンゴくらいの大きさだ。

content.content: This ball is just about as big as an apple.

content: ジルさんは、トムさんと同じぐらいの成績だ。

content.content: Jill’s grades are about the same as Tom’s.

content: これと同じぐらいの値段でもっといいのがありますよ。

content.content: We have another one that is better for a similar price.
Used in the pattern XはYくらいのNだ and means that X and Y are almost the same in terms of some quantifiable characteristic.
The N position is filled by a noun that indicates quantity or degree, such as 大きさ (size), 重さ (weight), 高さ (height), 温度 (temperature), or 量 (amount).
c. ...くらい...Nはない

content: タバコぐらいからだにわるいものはない。

content.content: Nothing is worse for the health than cigarettes.

content: 山田さんくらい自分でこつこつと勉強する学生は少ない。

content.content: Few students study on their own as hard as Yamada-san does.

content: この車くらい若者から年輩の人にまで人気のある車は他にない。

content.content: No other car is as popular as this one among people of all ages.

content: 国民に見はなされた政治家ぐらいみじめなものはない。

content.content: No one is as miserable as a politician who has been forsaken by the people.

content: いまの私にとって、まずしくて書物が自由に買えないことぐらいつらいことはない。

content.content: For me at this time, nothing is harder than having no money and not being able to buy any book I want.

...くらい indicates that the thing it is being used to qualify has the highest degree of something. Means “such-and-such is the most....” Sometimes expressions such as すくない (few) or めずらしい (uncommon) are used instead of ない, as in

content: . ...くらい...Nはない can be replaced by ...ほど...Nはない.

content.content: d. Vくらいなら

content: あいつに助けてもらうくらいなら、死んだほうがましだ。

content.content: I would rather die than get help from him.

content: あんな大学に行くくらいなら、就職するほうがよほどいい。

content.content: I would much rather get a job than go to a university like that.

content: 上から紙を貼って訂正するくらいなら、もう一度はじめから書き直したほうがいいと思うよ。

content.content: I think it would be better to rewrite it from the beginning, rather than paste a paper over it and make corrections.

content: 銀行で借りるくらいなら、私が貸してあげるのに。

content.content: If you have to borrow from the bank, of course I’ll lend it to you.

content: 君に迷惑をかけるくらいなら、僕が自分で行くよ。

content.content: If it’s going to be a bother for you, I’ll go myself.

Used in patterns such as XくらいならYのほうがましだ (I’d rather take Y if I had to take X), XくらいならYのほうがいい (Y is preferable to X), and XくらいならYする (If X, do Y instead). Means “Y is better than X,” with an extreme example given for Y. Used when the speaker feels very negatively about the thing indicated by ...くらい or when s/he thinks “X is not desirable and therefore Y is preferable.”
3. ...くらい〈degree〉a. ...くらい

content: その話を聞いて、息が止まりそうになるぐらい驚いた。

content.content: Listening to that story, I was so astonished that I lost my breath.

content: 顔も見たくないくらい嫌いだ。

content.content: I hate him so much that I don’t even want to see his face.

content: 佐藤さんぐらい英語ができるといいのにな。

content.content: I wish I were as good at English as Sato-san.

content: 一歩も歩けないくらい疲れていた。

content.content: I was so tired that I could not walk another step.

content: コートがほしい（と思う）くらい寒い日だった。

content.content: It was such a cold day that I (felt like) I wanted a coat.

content: A:ずいぶん大きな声で怒っていたね。

content.content: You shouted at him in quite a loud voice, didn’t you?
B:うん、あいつにはあれぐらい言ってやらないとわからないんだ。
Yeah, that guy never understands unless you talk to him like that.
Expresses the degree of an action or state, using a metaphor or a concrete example. Can usually be used in the same way as ほど, but くらい cannot be used when the degree of something is extreme.
（○）死ぬほど疲れた。
I am tired to death.
（×）死ぬぐらい疲れた。
I am tired around to death.
b. ...くらいだ

content: 君が困ることはないだろう。困るのは僕のほうだ。もう、泣きたいぐらいだよ。

content.content: You do not have a problem. It is me who has a problem. I could just about cry.

content: 疲れて一歩も歩けないくらいだった。

content.content: I was so tired that I could not walk another step.

content: 寒い日で、コートがほしいくらいだった。

content.content: It was such a cold day that I wished I had a coat.

content: 今のぼくのうれしさがわかるかい。そこらへんの人をみんな抱きしめたいくらいだよ。

content.content: Can you see how happy I am? So much so that I could hug everyone around me.

content: おぼえてる？　あの寒い夜ふたりでわけあって食べたラーメン。おいしくて、あたたかくて、世の中にこんなごちそうはないと思うくらいだったね。

content.content: Do you remember? The raamen the two of us shared on that cold night. It was delicious, and hot, and we thought that nothing in the world tasted better.
Used to explain the degree or extent of the thing stated previously, by giving a concrete example.
c. ...くらいだから

content: あの人は、会社をみっつも持ってるぐらいだから、金持ちなんだろう。

content.content: I would guess that person is rich, because she owns no fewer than three companies.

content: 彼はいつも本さえあればほかにはなにもいらないと言っているぐらいだから、きっと家の中は本だらけなんだろう。

content.content: Since he’s always saying he wants nothing except books, I would guess that his house is full of them.

content: あの温厚な山田さんが怒ったくらいだから、よほどのことだったのでしょう。

content.content: I guess it must really have been something, to make even the mild-tempered Yamada-san get angry.

content: 素人の作品でも、こんなにおもしろいくらいだから、プロが作ればもっとおもしろいものができるだろう。

content.content: If the work of an amateur is this interesting, then a professional should be able to make something even better.

Indicates the degree of a certain action or condition; used when the speaker is stating the basis for a judgment or supposition. Often followed by expressions that indicate supposition or conjecture, such as のだろう, にちがいない, and はずだ.
d. ...くらいの...しか...ない

content: 燃料が少なくなっているので、あと 10 キロくらい（の距離）しか走れない。

content.content: Since we’re running out of gas, we can only drive (a distance of) about ten more kilometers.

content: 10 年間も英語を習っているのに、挨拶くらいの会話しかできない。

content.content: Although I’ve been studying English for no less than ten years, I can only converse at the level of greetings.

content: 体が丈夫で、風邪で数日寝込んだことくらいしかない。

content.content: Since I have a strong constitution, I’ve never been sick in bed except for a few days with a cold.

content: 今忙しいので、ちょっとお茶を飲むくらいの時間しかありませんが、いいですか？

content.content: I’m busy right now, so I only have time for a quick cup of tea—is that all right?

content: 学費を払うために無理をしている息子をなんとか助けてやりたいのだが、失業中の私たちには、励ましの言葉をかけてやるくらいのことしかできない。

content.content: I wish I could find some way to help my son, who is really struggling to pay his school expenses, but since we’re unemployed now, all we can do is give him words of encouragement.

The pattern XくらいのYしか...ない gives X as an example of something with a small degree and shows that Y is not greater than X. Often followed by expressions that indicate impossibility, in which case the meaning is X以上のYは...できない (one cannot do Y to a greater extent than X).
4. ...くらい〈minimization〉

content: そんなことくらい子供でもわかる。

content.content: Even a child can understand something like that.

content: 山田さんは1キロメートルぐらいなら片手でも泳げるそうです。

content.content: They say that if it’s just a kilometer or so, Yamada-san can swim it using only one arm.

content: ちょっと足がだるいぐらい、ふろにはいればすぐになおるよ。

content.content: You can quickly cure a little tiredness in your legs by taking a bath.

content: すこし歩いたぐらいで疲れた疲れたって言うなよ。

content.content: Stop saying you’re tired just because you walked a little.

content: 1回や2回試験に落ちたくらいがなんだ。このおれなんて、これまで払った受験料だけで大学がひとつ買えるぐらいだぞ。

content.content: Failing exams once or twice is nothing. In my case, I could just about buy a university with all the entrance examination fees I’ve paid so far.

content: ビールぐらいしか用意できませんが、会議の後で一杯やりましょう。

content.content: We can only offer you beer, but let’s have a drink after the meeting is over.

content: あいさつくらいの簡単な日本語しか話せない。

content.content: I can only speak very basic Japanese, like greetings.

content: 指定された曜日にゴミを出さない人がいる。自分一人ぐらいかまわないだろうと軽く考えているのだろう。

content.content: There are people who do not put their garbage out on the specified days of the week. I guess they pass it off by thinking that just one person won't make a big difference.
Shows the feeling that something is viewed as unimportant or not making any difference.
Means “such a simple thing, such a trivial matter.” Often followed by expressions that mean “it doesn’t matter much” (大したことではない), “it’s easy” (容易である), or “there’s no problem” (問題はない).
5. ...くらい〈limit, restriction〉a. Nくらい

content: 子供じゃないんだから、自分のことぐらい自分で決めなさい。

content.content: You're not a child, so you need to make your own decisions.

content: A:もう、11 時ですよ。

content.content: It’s already eleven o’clock, you know.
B:いいじゃないか。日曜日ぐらい、ゆっくり寝かせてくれよ。
Well, so what? Let me sleep in at least on Sundays.

content: 帰りがおそくなるのなら、電話の一本ぐらいかけてくれてもいいじゃないか。

content.content: If you’re going to get home late, would it really be too much to ask you to give me a call?

content: あいさつぐらいしたらどうだ。

content.content: Can't you at least say hello?
The form ...くらい is used to give an extreme example and indicate that something is the bare minimum that is expected.
b. ...のは...ぐらいのものだ

content: 息子が電話をよこすのは、金に困った時ぐらいのものだ。

content.content: My son gives me a call only when he needs money.

content: 仕事が忙しくて、ゆっくりできるのは週末ぐらいのものだ。

content.content: Since I’m so busy with work, I can only relax on the weekends.

content: そんな高価な宝石が買えるのは、ごく一部の金持ちくらいのものだ。

content.content: Only a very few wealthy people can buy such an expensive jewel.

content: 社長に、あんなにずけずけものを言うのは君くらいのもんだよ。

content.content: You are about the only one who can speak so frankly to our president.
Used in the pattern XのはYくらいのものだ, this means that “X occurs only in the case of Y.”
【くらべる】→
【にくらべて】
【くれ】→
【てくれ】
【くれる】→
【てくれる】
【くわえて】［NくわえてN］

content: 規則正しい食事、適度な運動、くわえて近所の人達との日常的なつきあい、そういったものがこの村のお年寄りの長生きの秘訣と考えられる。

content.content: It is believed that the secret to the long lives of the elderly in this village lies in such things as regular eating habits and an appropriate amount of exercise, along with daily contact with their neighbors.

content: 慢性的な不作、加えて百年に一度という大災害で食糧不足はいっそう深刻になっている。

content.content: The food shortages have become even more serious due to the chronically poor harvests and, on top of that, a natural disaster such as happens only once every hundred years.

content: 地場産業の衰退、加えて児童の減少による小学校の廃校が、この地域の人口流出に拍車をかけているようだ。

content.content: The decline in local industries and, in addition, the closing down of elementary schools due to fewer pupils seem to be accelerating the exodus of the population from this region.
Expresses that something is added. Means “not only that” or “on top of that.” Tends to be used in written language. In formal written language, くわうるに is also used.
【けっか】［N のけっか］［V-たけっか］

content: 投票の結果、議長には山田さんが選出された。

content.content: The result of the vote was that Yamada-san was selected as the chairperson.

content: 調べた結果、私がまちがっていることがわかりました。

content.content: My investigations showed that I was in the wrong.

content: 3人でよく話し合った結果、その問題についてはもうすこし様子を見ようということになった。

content.content: After discussing it amongst the three of us, the decision was to let the issue lie for a bit longer and see what happens.

content: 国会審議の空転の結果、この法案がこの会期中に採決される見通しはなくなった。

content.content: As a result of the stalled Diet deliberations, there is no longer any prospect of this bill being adopted during the current session.

Although 結果 (result) is basically a noun, as in 調べた結果を教えてください(Please tell me the results of your investigation), it can be used as an expression to link cause and effect, as shown in the examples above. Combined with an expression that describes the cause, it means “for that reason” or “because of such-and-such.” Followed by a description of the resulting effect. Used more in written language.
【けっきょく】

content: バーゲンセールに行ったが、結局何も買わないで帰ってきた。

content.content: I went to a bargain sale, but I ended up coming home without buying anything.

content: 結局、世の中は万事金で決まるということだよ。

content.content: In the end, money decides everything in this world.

content: 挑戦者も善戦したが、結局は判定でチャンピオンが勝利をおさめた。

content.content: The challenger also fought well, but in the end the champion won the decision on points.

content: 結局のところ、あなたは何が言いたいのですか。

content.content: So at the end of the day, what do you want to say?
Used at the beginning or in the middle of a sentence when stating the final conclusion or result of something. As in

content: and

, it is sometimes used in the forms 結局は or 結局のところ. Often used to state a conclusion or result settled beyond the power of a person’s will, in spite of his/her efforts or expectations, and carries the slightly negative connotation of “that’s just the way things are (were).” Consequently, it is unnatural and difficult to use this expression when stating a positive result.

content.content: （×）猛勉強を続け、結局、彼は一流大学に合格した。
He kept studying very hard, and he ended up passing the entrance exam for a first-class university.
（○）猛勉強を続けたが、結局、彼は希望した大学に合格できなかった。
He kept studying very hard, but he ended up not passing the entrance exam for the university of his choice.
In

content: , 結局 is followed by an interrogative sentence and its function is to press the listener to draw a conclusion.

content.content: 【けっして...ない】

content: あなたのことはけっしてわすれません。

content.content: I will never forget you.

content: いいかい。知らない人においでとさそわれても、けっしてついて行ってはいけないよ。

content.content: Listen. Even if a stranger invites you to go with him, you must never follow him.

content: きみのために忠告しておく。人前でそんなばかなことは決して言うな。

content.content: I will give you a piece of advice. Never say such a foolish thing in front of others.

content: 気をわるくされたのならあやまります。失礼なことを言うつもりは決してなかったのです。

content.content: I apologize if I hurt your feelings. I never had the slightest intention of saying anything rude.
Often used with negative forms and expressions of prohibition. Emphasizes the meaning of negation or prohibition and/or shows a strong sense of intention or resolution.
【けど】
1. けど

content: A:この本は、恵子にやるつもりだ。

content.content: I’m planning to give this book to Keiko.
B:けど、それじゃ、良子がかわいそうよ。
But that doesn’t seem fair to Yoshiko.

content: このカメラ、貸してもいいよ。けど、ちゃんと扱ってくれよ。

content.content: I don’t mind lending you this camera. But please take good care of it.
This is an informal way to say けれど. Usually not used in polite-form conversations.
【けれど】

content: みんながあの映画はいいと言うけど、わたしにはちっともおもしろいと思えない。

content.content: Everyone says that movie is good, but I don’t think it’s interesting at all.

content: これは給料はよくないけど、やりがいのある仕事だ。

content.content: It doesn’t pay well, but it’s a worthwhile job.

content: A:これから、出かけるんだけど、一緒に行かない。

content.content: I’m about to go out—do you want to come with me?
B:うん、行く。
Yes, I do.

content: 役所は認めてくれませんけど、これは立派な託児所です。

content.content: Although the government office won’t give us its approval, this is a respectable day-care center.

content: すみません、電話が故障しているらしいんですけど。

content.content: Excuse me, but the telephone seems to be out of order.
An informal way of saying けれど. Sounds slightly feminine when used in polite-form sentences.
【けれど】
【けれど】
1. けれど

content: 2時間待った。けれど、彼は姿を現さなかった。

content.content: I waited for two hours. However, he did not show up.

content: パーティーではだれも知っている人がいなかった。けれど、みんな親切でとても楽しかった。

content.content: There was no one I knew at the party. However, everybody was nice and I had a really good time.

content: この作品で3等賞ぐらいとれるかなと期待していた。けれど、結果は思いがけなく1等賞だった。

content.content: I was hoping I might win third prize with this piece. But, to my surprise, the result was first prize.

Placed at the beginning of a sentence, けれど indicates that what comes next will develop in a way that differs from what might be expected from the preceding sentence(s). Compared with しかし, けれど is used more often in spoken language. However, it can be used in informal writing too.

content: 2時間待ったけれど、彼は姿を現さなかった。

content.content: I waited for two hours, but he did not show up.

content: あの人はきれいだけれど、意地悪だ。

content.content: That woman is beautiful but ill-natured.

content: 下手だけれど、ピアノを弾くのは楽しい。

content.content: I’m not good at it, but playing the piano is fun.

content: 野球もおもしろいけれどサッカーはもっとおもしろいと思う若い人が増えている。

content.content: More and more young people are starting to think that, although baseball is fun, soccer is even more fun.

content: 係長はもうすぐ帰ると思いますけれど、ここでお待ちになりますか。

content.content: I’m sure the subsection chief will be back soon...would you like to wait here?

Attaches to the end of a clause and signals that what comes next will develop in a way that is different from what might be anticipated from the statement in the preceding clause. It is an adversative expression, but not necessarily limited to adversative use. It can also be used to make a preliminary remark, as in

content: . Tends to be used in spoken language, but may also be used in informal writing.
いま母は留守なんですけれど。

content.content: My mother isn’t home right now....

content: 来週は外国出張で、いないんですけれど。

content.content: I’m afraid I have an overseas business trip next week, so I won’t be here....

content: 紅茶は切らしています。コーヒーならありますけれど。

content.content: We’ve run out of tea. We do have coffee, though....

content: ちょっとコピー機が動かないんですけれど。

content.content: Excuse me, but the copy machine isn’t working....

content: 書類が一枚足りないんですけれど。

content.content: A page of the document seems to be missing....

content: かあさん、友達が夏休みにうちへ泊まりに来たいって言ってるんだけれど。

content.content: Mom, a friend of mine says she wants to come and stay at our house during the summer break....

Placed at the end of a sentence, ...けれど creates the impression that the sentence is unfinished. Used to state an excuse, an explanation of circumstances, etc. in a soft and gentle manner. Also used to make indirect requests, as in

content: , and
. Can be attached to both polite and plain forms. When attached to polite forms, it makes the expression more feminine and polite. Spoken language.

content.content: 【けれども】
1. けれども

content: 2時間待った。けれども、一郎は姿を現さなかった。

content.content: I waited for two hours. However, Ichiro did not show up.

content: 彼は話すのが下手だ。けれども、彼の話し方には説得力がある。

content.content: He is not good at speaking. And yet, his speaking style is persuasive.
Same as けれど.
【けれど】
2. ...けれども

content: 結婚式の日取りはまだ決まっていないんですけれども、たぶん夏ごろになると思います。

content.content: The wedding date isn’t fixed yet, but I guess it will be sometime in summer.

content: あの人とは仲良く仕事をしたいと思っているんですけれども、なかなかうまく行きません。

content.content: I would like to have a good working relationship with that person, but it isn’t going very well.

content: このままずっとここにいたいけれども、いつか国へ帰らなければならない。

content.content: I would like to stay here forever, but I have to go back to my country at some point.

content: これは正式には発表されていないんですけれども、近いうちに大きな関心を呼ぶことになると思います。

content.content: This hasn’t been announced officially, but I think it will attract great interest in the near future.
Same as けれど. When placed after expressions in polite form, it can be used in official settings such as meetings.
【けれど】
【げ】［Na げ］［A-げ］［R-げ］

content: その人は退屈げに雑誌のページをめくっていた。

content.content: That person was leafing through the pages of a magazine in a bored manner.

content: 「そうですか」というその声には悲しげな響きがあった。

content.content: The voice saying “Soo desuka (is that so?)” was tinged with sadness.

content: 彼女の笑顔にはどこか寂しげなところがあった。

content.content: Her smiling face had something of a look of loneliness.

content: 彼のそのいわくありげな様子が私には気になった。

content.content: There was something deliberate in his manner that bothered me.

げ is combined with the stem of an i-adjective or verb to create a na-adjective with the meaning “to have a certain look or manner.” The examples above can be paraphrased using ...そう, as in 退屈そう and 悲しそう, but ...げ is more for written language. There are also idiomatic expressions such as the one shown in
【げんざい】

content: 彼が死んでしまった現在、もうそんなことを言っても意味がないよ。

content.content: Now that he’s dead, it’s meaningless to say such a thing.

content: 失敗の原因が明らかになった現在、われわれは何をすべきか。

content.content: Now that the cause of the failure has been clarified, what should we do?

content: あの改革案がいまだに大方の賛同を得られていない現在、新たな方策を考えておくことも重要なことではないか。

content.content: At this time, when that proposal for reform has not yet gained general support, isn’t it important to consider new measures?

content: 地球環境の保護が叫ばれている現在、クリーンエネルギーの夢を広げるその計画への期待は大きい。

content.content: Now, when people are clamoring for protection of the global environment, expectations regarding that plan to expand the dream of clean energy are great.

Originally a noun, as in 過去と現在 (past and present) and 現在の気温は 29 度だ (the current temperature is 29 degrees). When attached to the end of a clause, it becomes an expression to present the current situation and then state an assertion on the part of the speaker. A formal expression that tends to be used in written language.
【こしたことはない】→
【にこしたことはない】
【こそ】
1. Nこそ

content: A:よろしくお願いします。

content.content: Thank you for your help.
B:こちらこそよろしく。
The pleasure is all mine.

content: ことしこそ『源氏物語』を終わりまで読むぞ。

content.content: This year, I’m determined to read The Tale of Genji to the end!

content: いまでこそ、こうやって笑って話せるが、あの時はほんとうにどうしようかと思ったよ。

content.content: Now I can smile when I talk about it, but at that time I really didn’t know what to do.

content: そうか。彼はひきうけてくれたのか。それでこそわれわれが見こんだとおりの人物だ。

content.content: I see. He agreed to do it, did he. That means he’s exactly the person we expected him to be.

content: A:やはり私は文学部に進みたいと思います。

content.content: As you might have expected, I would like to get into the Department of Literature.
B:そうか。それこそ、亡くなったきみのお父さんものぞんでいたことだ。
I see. That’s exactly what your late father had hoped for.
Emphasizes a certain thing, giving it the meaning “it is this and nothing else.”
2. ...こそ　あれ／すれ［Nこそすれ］［Na でこそあれ］［R-こそすれ］

content: あなたのその言い方は、皮肉でこそあれ、けっしてユーモアとは言えない。

content.content: The way you say it, it sounds ironic but never humorous.

content: あなたをうらんでいるですって？　感謝（し）こそすれ、私があなたをうらむ理由があるわけがないでしょう。

content.content: I have a grudge against you? On the contrary, I should be thankful to you—there is absolutely no reason for me to have a grudge against you!

content: 政府のその決定は、両国間の新たな緊張の火種になりこそすれ、およそ賢明な選択とは言いがたいものである。

content.content: That decision by the government will only sow new seeds of tension between the two countries, and on the whole it is hard to say that it is a sensible choice.

This pattern takes the form Xこそあれ／Xこそすれ, Yではない and is used to assert that the fact is X and not, under any circumstances, Y. In order to emphasize strongly the assertion of not-Y, this usage also presents X, which contrasts Y. Used mostly in written language.

content: can be rephrased as 「火種にこそなれ」 (“become the cause of a conflict/dispute”).

content.content: 3. ...こそ...が［Nこそ...が］［Na でこそあるが］［R-こそするが］

content: この靴は、デザインこそ古いが、とても歩きやすい。

content.content: The design of these shoes is old, but they are very good for walking.

content: 書きこそしたが、彼のレポートはひどいものだった。

content.content: He did write up the paper, but it was an awful piece of work.

content: 彼はいちおう会長でこそあるが、実権はまったくない。

content.content: Although he has the title of president, he doesn’t hold any real power.

content: あの学生は宿題こそいつもきちんと提出するけれども、試験をしてみると何もわかっていないことがわかる。

content.content: Although that student always submits his assignments on time, when I give an exam it becomes clear that he understands nothing.

content: その作家は、ベストセラーこそないけれども、ある一群の読者たちにささえられて、一作一作着実に書いてきた。

content.content: Although that writer doesn’t have any bestsellers, she is supported by a certain group of readers and has steadily produced one book at a time.
By stating XはYこそAだが、Z, the speaker first acknowledges that, as for X, “Y is A” is true to a certain extent.  Then, states that there is a situation Z that contrasts “Y is A.”
4. ...からでこそ→
【それでこそ】
5. ...からこそ→
【からこそ】
6. ...だからこそ→
【だからこそ】
【てこそ】
【ばこそ】
【こと】
1. ...こと〈thing, matter〉［Nのこと］［Na なこと］［A／V　こと］

content: なにかおもしろいことないかなあ。

content.content: I wonder if there’s something interesting...?

content: 卒業したらやりたいと思っていることはありますか。

content.content: Is there something you hope to do after graduation?

content: 私がきのう言ったこと、おぼえてる？

content.content: Do you remember what I said yesterday?

content: 世の中には君の知らないことがまだまだたくさんあるんだよ。

content.content: There are still so many things in the world that you don’t know.

content: 本を読んで思ったこと、感じたことなどは、書名・著者名などといっしょにカードに書いておくとよい。

content.content: It’s good to make notes on cards about what you think or feel when you read a book, along with the title, name of the author, and so on.

content: なんでも好きなことをやってよい。

content.content: You can do whatever you want to do.
...こと attaches to a clause and is used to indicate a thought, statement, or piece of knowledge, without referring concretely to its content. For the difference between こと and もの, see Usage 1 of もの.
2. ...（という）こと〈fact〉

content: 山田さんが魚がきらいなことを知っていますか。

content.content: Do you know that Yamada-san doesn’t like fish?

content: 午後から会議だということをすっかりわすれていた。

content.content: I completely forgot that there was a meeting in the afternoon.

content: きみが将来アフリカに行きたいと思っている（という）ことは、もう彼女に話したのか。

content.content: Have you already told her that you want to go to Africa in the future?

content: 彼は死んでもうこの世にいない（という）ことが、まだわたしには信じられない気がする。

content.content: I still can’t believe that he is dead and no longer in this world.
ことis attached to a clause and used to indicate that the thing stated in the clause is a fact. In the case of na-adjectives, it takes the form 魚がきらいなこと, as in

content: , or 魚がきらいだということ.

content.content: 3. V-る／V-ない　こと〈imperative〉

content: 休むときは、かならず学校に連絡すること。

content.content: Be sure to contact the school when you are absent.

content: 期末レポートは、かならず縦書き 400 字づめ原稿用紙を使用すること（とする）。

content.content: The final term paper must be written vertically on 400-character manuscript paper.

content: 体育館には土足ではいらないこと。

content.content: Do not enter the gymnasium with your shoes on.

content: 教室を授業以外の目的で使用するときは、前もって申請をすること。

content.content: You must apply for permission in advance in order to use a classroom for non-class related purposes.

When used at the end of a sentence, こと expresses an imperative or a feeling on the part of the speaker that something should be done. Conveys rules or directions to be observed. Often used in writing. Can end in こととする, as in
4. ...こと〈admiration, wonder〉［Nだこと］［Na　だ／なこと］［A-いこと］［V-ていること］

content: まあ、かわいいあかちゃんだこと。

content.content: My, what a cute baby!

content: あら、すてきなお洋服だこと。おかあさんに買ってもらったの？

content.content: My, what a lovely outfit! Did your mother buy it for you?

content: あらあら、元気だこと。でも電車の中でさわいではいけませんよ。

content.content: Now, now—you've got lots of energy! But you can't roughhouse when we're on the train, you know.

content: え？　この子まだ2才なの？　まあ、大きいこと。

content.content: What? This child is only two? My, how big she is!

content: このネコ、見てよ。よくふとっていること。病気かしら。

content.content: Take a look at this cat. It's so fat. I wonder if it’s sick.
Attaches to expressions that indicate a state or characteristic of a person or thing. Conveys a sense of wonder, surprise, or admiration. When na-adjectives are used, as in

content: , な can be used instead of だ (in this case, 元気なこと). Spoken language. Feminine expression. Not used by either males or females who belong to the younger generation.

content.content: 5. NことN

content: 小泉八雲ことラフカディオ・ハーンはギリシャ生まれのイギリス人だ。

content.content: Lafcadio Hearn, known as Koizumi Yakumo, was an Englishman born in Greece.

content: これが、あの太陽王ことフランスのルイ 14 世が毎日使っていたワイングラスです。

content.content: This is the wine glass that the French King Louis XIV, known as the Sun King, used every day.

content: 漱石こと夏目金之助は 1867 年、東京に生まれた。

content.content: Natsume Kinnosuke, known as Soseki, was born in Tokyo in

こと is used in the pattern XことY, where X denotes the name a person is generally known by, a pen name, or a nickname, and Y denotes his/her real name or more official name. Means “X, in other words Y” and shows that X and Y are the same person. More common in written language.
6. Nのこと

content: 私のこと、すき？

content.content: Do you like me?

content: あなたのことは一生わすれない。

content.content: I will never forget you for the rest of my life.

content: 彼女のことはもうあきらめなさい。

content.content: It's time you gave up on her.

content: パーティのこと、もう山田さんに言った？

content.content: Did you already tell Yamada-san about the party?

content: 最近私は、どういうわけか、ふとしたひょうしに、ずいぶん前に死んだ祖母のことを考えていることが多い。

content.content: These days, I don’t know why, but I often find myself all of a sudden thinking about my grandmother, who passed away quite long ago.

Expresses something not as an independent entity but as an integrated whole that encompasses everything surrounding it, including circumstances, memories, voices, or even in some cases things like smell. Often used to indicate the object of verbs of perception, thought, emotion, or linguistic activity.
【ことうけあいだ】

content: こんどあの人のところに行くときは花を持って行くといい。よろこんでもらえること請け合いだよ。

content.content: Next time you visit that person, you should take some flowers. That will make her happy, I guarantee.

content: あんなやり方をしていたのでは、失敗することはうけあいだ。

content.content: With that way of doing things, failure is a certainty.

content: この計画に彼を参加させるには、成功したら手にはいるばく大な金のことを話せばいい。乗ってくることうけあいだ。

content.content: If you want to get him involved in this project, you should talk about all the money he stands to make if it succeeds. I promise you he'll come on board.
Attaches to a clause and is used to predict or guarantee a future event with certainty. は is sometimes inserted, as in

content: . A somewhat old-fashioned expression.

content.content: 【ことか】［疑問詞+Na なことか］［疑問詞+　A／V　ことか］

content: つまらない話を3時間も聞かされる身にもなってください。どれほど退屈なことか。

content.content: Put yourself in my place and imagine having to listen to that drivel for three hours. How boring it was!

content: 続けて二人も子供に死なれるなんて。どんなにつらいことか。

content.content: To think that they’ve lost two children, one right after the other. I can't imagine how painful it must be!

content: とうとう成功した。この日を何年待っていたことか。

content.content: We finally succeeded. We've waited so many years for this day!

content: それを直接本人に伝えてやってください。どんなに喜ぶことか。

content.content: Please tell that directly to the person in question. She’ll be thrilled!
Conveys a sense of deep emotion. Means the emotion is so intense that it is difficult to specify its degree or amount.
【ことがある】
1. V-たことが　ある／ない

content: A:京都へ行ったことがありますか。

content.content: Have you ever been to Kyoto?
B:いいえ、まだないんです。
No, not yet.

content: ああ、その本なら子供の頃読んだことがあります。

content.content: Oh, I read that book once when I was a child.

content: そんな話は聞いたこともないよ。

content.content: I’ve never heard such a story.

content: 高橋さんにはこれまでに2度お会いしたことがあります。

content.content: I’ve met Takahashi-san previously on two occasions.

content: 高橋さんにはまだお会いしたことがありませんが、お噂はよく聞いています。

content.content: I have not met Takahashi-san yet, but I have heard a lot about him.

content: このあたりは過去に何回か洪水に見舞われたことがある。

content.content: This area has been struck by flooding several times in the past.
Used to state whether or not a certain event has been experienced. Used mainly with verbs, but may also take the form N+だった, as shown in the examples below.
（例）あのホテルはできるだけ早く予約した方がいいよ。3ヶ月前に電話したのに満員だったことがあるんだ。
It’s best to make reservations at that hotel as early as possible. What happened to me once is that even though I called them three months in advance, they were already fully booked.
This pattern can also be used in the form V-なかったことがある, to state the experience of not having done something.
（例）財布を拾ったのに警察に届けなかったことがある。
Once I picked up a wallet on the street, but I didn’t take it to the police.
2. V-る／V-ない　ことがある

content: 子供たちは仲がいいのですが、たまに喧嘩をすることがあります。

content.content: The kids get along with each other, but they do squabble at times.

content: これだけ練習していても、時として失敗することがある。

content.content: Even though I practice this much, sometimes I do make mistakes.

content: 天気のいい日に子供と散歩することがあるぐらいで、ふだんはあまり運動しません。

content.content: On nice days I occasionally go for a walk with my children, but I usually don't get very much exercise.

content: A:最近、外で食事することはありますか。

content.content: Do you sometimes dine out these days?
B:最近はあまりないですねえ。
These days, not very often.

content: 長雨が続くと、害虫の被害を受けることがある。

content.content: When there’s a long spell of rainy weather, we sometimes get pest damage.

content: 彼は仕事が忙しくて、食事の時間をとれないこともあるそうだ。

content.content: I heard that sometimes he can’t find the time to eat because he’s too busy with work.

content: 乾期にはいると2ヶ月以上も雨が降らないことがある。

content.content: When the dry season starts, we sometimes have no rain for more than two months.
Indicates that a certain event happens sometimes or occasionally. Cannot be used regarding an event that happens frequently.
（×）このあたりはよく事故が起こることがある。
Accidents often occur sometimes around here.
（○）このあたりはよく事故が起こる。
Accidents often occur around here.
【ことができる】［V-ることができる］

content: アラビア語を話すことができますか。

content.content: Can you speak Arabic?

content: あの人は、ゆっくりなら 20 kmでも 30 kmでも泳ぐことができるそうだよ。

content.content: They say she can swim as far as twenty or thirty kilometers, if she goes slowly.

content: 残念ですが、ご要望におこたえすることはできません。

content.content: Unfortunately, I am unable to respond to your request.

content: その社会や階級の構成員を「再生産」するという観点から、「教育」というものをとらえ直してみることもできるだろう。

content.content: From the perspective of “reproducing” the members of that society or social class, I suppose it is possible to try to re-think the idea of “education.”
Expresses the existence/non-existence of an ability (

content: ) or possibility (

). Can be substituted with V-れる, which shows possibility, as in 話せる (can speak) and 泳げる (able to swim). However, there is a slight tendency for ことができる to be preferred in formal situations and formal written language, especially when expressing possibility.

content.content: 【ことこのうえない】［Na なことこのうえない］［A-いことこのうえない］

content: 丁重なことこの上ないごあいさつをいただき、恐縮しております。

content.content: We are truly overwhelmed at the warmth of the greeting you have given us.

content: その風景は、さびしいことこのうえ（も）ないものであった。

content.content: The landscape was lonely beyond description.

content: 有権者の存在を無視したような、その政治家たちの舞台裏での争いは、見ぐるしいことこの上ないものであった。

content.content: The infighting among those politicians behind the scenes—as if they were totally indifferent to the voting public—was disgraceful beyond description.
