Means “there is nothing more than such-and-such.” A formal expression used in written language. The examples above can be paraphrased, respectively, as このうえなく丁重なあいさつ (the most cordial of greetings), このうえなくさびしい (the loneliest possible), and このうえなく見ぐるしいもの (unspeakably disgraceful).
【ことだ】
1. V-る／V-ない　ことだ

content: 日本語がうまくなりたければもっと勉強することです。それいがいに方法はありません。

content.content: If you want to be better at Japanese, study harder. There is no other way.

content: かぜをはやくなおしたいんだったら、あたたかくしてゆっくり寝ることだ。

content.content: If you want to get over your cold quickly, stay warm and get lots of sleep.

content: まあ、ここは相手に花を持たせておくことだね。またチャンスもあるよ。

content.content: Well, here it’s better to let the other person have the credit for it. You’ll surely have another chance.

content: こどもにさわらせたくないというのなら、最初から手のとどく所におかないことだ。

content.content: If you don't want the children to touch it, put it somewhere out of reach right from the very beginning.
Used to state the best or most desirable thing under a certain condition. Functions indirectly to give a piece of advice or an order. Used in spoken language.
2. ...ことだ［Na なことだ］［A-いことだ］

content: 家族みんな健康で、けっこうなことだ。

content.content: I am pleased to see that everyone in the family is well.

content: いつまでもお若くて、うらやましいことです。

content.content: You always look so young; I envy you.

content: 夜はあぶないからって、あのお母さん、こどもを塾まで送り迎えしてるんだって。ごくろうなことだね。

content.content: Because she says it’s dangerous at night, that mom takes her children to cram school and then brings them home again. How troublesome for her!

content: 道路に飛び出した弟を止めようと追いかけていって車にはねられるなんて...。いたましいことだ。

content.content: She was hit by a car while chasing after and trying to stop her little brother, who had dashed into the street.... What a tragedy!
Shows surprise, awe, irony, deep emotion, etc. on the part of the speaker. Used with a limited range of adjectives.
3. ...ということ→
【ということ】
4. ...とは...のことだ→
【とは】
【ことだから】［Nのことだから］

content: 彼のことだからどうせ時間どおりにはこないだろう。

content.content: Given the way he is, he probably won’t come on time anyway.

content: あの人のことだから、わすれずに持ってきてくれると思うけどな。

content.content: I would say that, because he’s got it, he’ll probably remember to bring it.

content: 慎重な山田さんのことだから、そのへんのところまでちゃんと考えてあるとは思うけどね。

content.content: Since Yamada-san is so cautious, I would guess that she already has everything all thought out.

content: あの人のことだから、この計画が失敗しても自分だけは責任をのがれられるような手はうってあるんだろう。

content.content: You know how he is—I would guess that he’s already taken measures to ensure he can escape having to take any responsibility in case the plan fails.

Usually attached to a noun that denotes a person. Used when making some sort of judgment about a person that both the speaker and the listener know very well, based on that person’s character or behavioral patterns. In some cases, the characteristic or special feature  that forms the basis for the judgment about the person in question is specified in the context, such as 慎重な (cautious) in
【ことだし】［N／Na　であることだし］［Na なことだし］［A／V　ことだし］

content: 雨がふってきそうだから、きょうは散歩はやめておこうか。こどもたちもかぜをひいていることだし。

content.content: Since it looks like it’s going to rain, why don’t we put off going for a walk today? Besides, the children have colds.

content: おいしそうな料理もでてきたことですし、私のへたなごあいさつはこのへんで終わりにしたいと存じます。

content.content: With all this delicious food ready to eat, I will put an end here to my clumsy remarks.

content: 委員も大体そろったことだし、予定時間も過ぎているので、そろそろ委員会を始めてはいかがですか。

content.content: Since most of the committee members are present, and we are already a little behind schedule, how would it be if we started the meeting?

Attaches to a clause. This construction combines ことだ+し and is used when describing the conditions or circumstances that form the reason or basis for some kind of judgment, decision, or hope. ことですし, as in

content: , is a more polite form. Sometimes two reasons are stated, as in
, sometimes one reason is stated, as in
, and sometimes the reason is tacked on at the end as additional information, as in
. Although this is a spoken language expression, it is more formal than using only し.

content.content: 【ことだろう】［Na　な／である　ことだろう］［A／V　ことだろう］

content: 会っていないが、山田さんのこどもさんもさぞおおきくなったことだろう。

content.content: I haven’t seen them, but I suppose that Yamada-san’s children must have really grown up.

content: 市内でこんなにふっているのだから、山のほうではきっとひどい雪になっていることだろう。

content.content: Since it’s falling this hard in the city, there must be a terrible snowstorm in the mountains.

content: 《手紙》息子さん、大学合格とのこと。さぞかしお喜びのことでございましょう。

content.content: 《letter》We heard that your son passed his university entrance examination. You must be so very pleased.

content: この誘拐事件は人質の安全を考慮して今はふせられているが、公表されれば、まちがいなく社会に大きな衝撃をあたえることだろう。

content.content: This kidnapping case is presently being kept quiet out of consideration for the safety of the hostage, but once it’s made public, there’s no question it will cause a great shock to our society.

Attaches to a clause and indicates a conjecture. It is also possible just to say だろう; however, ことだろう is a more formal expression that is suited to written language and used to make empathetic conjectures about things that are not known in the here and now. When used with the adverb さぞ（かし） (how, surely), as in

content: , this expression conveys an even stronger emotional involvement.

content.content: 【ことで】［Nのことで］

content: さっきのお話のことで質問があるんですが。

content.content: I have a question about the thing you mentioned just now....

content: 先生、レポートのことで、ご相談したいことがあるんですが。

content.content: Sensei (Professor), there’s something I would like to talk to you about regarding the term paper....

content: 君がきのう出した企画書のことで、課長が話があるそうだよ。

content.content: Apparently the section chief wants to talk to you about the proposal you submitted yesterday.

Used with verbs that refer to the act of speaking, such as 質問する (ask a question), 相談する (consult), and 話す (talk (to)), and means ...について (about, regarding). Used to start a conversation by presenting a reason or background situation.
【こととおもう】［Nのこととおもう］［Na なこととおもう］［A／V　こととおもう］

content: 《手紙》「ごぶさたいたしておりますが、お元気でおすごしのことと思います。」

content.content: 《letter》“It has been some time since I last wrote, but I trust you are doing well.”

content: 《手紙》「このたびのおかあさまのご不幸、さぞお力落としのことと存じます。」

content.content: 《letter》“I can imagine how grieved you must be at this time over the loss of your mother.”

content: みなさんもずいぶん楽しみになさっていたことと思いますが、旅行の中止は私もたいへん残念です。

content.content: I am sure that you were all looking forward to this trip very much, and I am also quite disappointed that it has been canceled.

Attaches to a clause and is used to present a supposition about the addressee’s situation that includes a feeling of compassion or empathy. Often used with adverbs such as さぞ (how, very), さぞかし (how, indeed), and ずいぶん (considerably, extremely). Conveys more of a tone of formal written language than ...とおもう, and is frequently used in written letters. ...ことと存じます, as in

content: , is an even more formal and polite form of this expression.

content.content: 【こととて】［Nのこととて］［Vこととて］

content: 子供のやったこととて、大目に見てはいただけませんか。

content.content: Since it was a child who did it, couldn’t we ask you to overlook it?

content: なにぶんにも年寄りのこととて、そそうがあったらお許しください。

content.content: As I am getting on in years, please excuse me if I make mistakes.

content: 慣れぬこととて、失礼をいたしました。

content.content: I’m sorry for my discourtesy—I am not used to this.

content: 知らぬこととて、ご迷惑をおかけして申しわけございません。

content.content: I’m sorry to have put you to such trouble—I didn’t know.

Used to state the reason for an apology or a request for forgiveness. Followed in the latter half of the sentence by words that express the apology or ask for forgiveness. A somewhat old-fashioned expression. V-ぬ, as in

content: and
, is the written-language equivalent of V-ない.

content.content: 【ことなく】［V-ることなく］

content: ひどいゆきだったが、列車はおくれることなく京都についた。

content.content: Despite the heavy snow, the train arrived at Kyoto without delay.

content: われわれは、いつまでもかわることなくともだちだ。

content.content: We will always remain friends.

content: その子は、もうこちらをふりかえることもなく、両手を振り、胸を張って、峠の向こうに消えて行った。

content.content: Without turning around in our direction, the child disappeared over the mountain pass, arms swinging and head held high.
Also takes the form ...こともなく, as in

content: . Similar to ...ないで and ...ず(に), but ...ことなく is used in written language. In terms of meaning, as shown in the respective examples above, ...ことなく implies that although there is a possibility that something or someone will be late (おくれる), or change (かわる), or turn around (ふりかえる), this does not happen.

content.content: 【ことなしに】［V-ることなしに］

content: 努力することなしに成功はありえない。

content.content: Success is impossible without effort.

content: 誰しも他人を傷つけることなしには生きていけない。

content.content: No one can live without hurting others.

content: リスクを負うことなしに新しい道を切り開くことはできないだろう。

content.content: A new trail cannot be blazed without taking risks.

Followed by expressions that deny the possibility of something, in the pattern XすることなしにYできない. Means “without doing X, it’s impossible to do Y” (XをしなければYができない), or in other words, “if one intends to do Y, then doing X is unavoidable” (Yをしようと思ったら、Xをすることは避けられない). A formal expression.
【ことに】［Na なことに］［A-いことに］［V-たことに］

content: 残念なことに、私がたずねたときには、その人はもう引っ越したあとだった。

content.content: Unfortunately, when I visited, that person had already moved out.

content: おもしろいことに、私がいま教えている学生は、私がむかしお世話になった先生のこどもさんだ。

content.content: Interestingly, one of the students I’m teaching now is the child of a teacher who mentored me long ago.

content: おどろいたことに、彼女はもうその話を知っていた。

content.content: Surprisingly, she already knew that story.

content: あきれたことに、その役所は知事の選挙資金のために裏金をプールしていた。

content.content: It’s appalling, but that local government office was pooling money in a slush fund for the governor’s campaign expenses.
Attached to an adjective or verb of emotion and used to indicate in advance the feeling or attitude of the speaker regarding the situation s/he is about to describe. Has the tone of written language.
【ことにしている】［Vことにしている］

content: 私は毎日かならず日記をつけることにしている。

content.content: I make it a rule to write in my diary every day without fail.

content: 夜はコーヒーを飲まないことにしているんです。

content.content: I don’t drink coffee at night.

content: 彼の家族は、家事はすべて分担してやることにしているそうだ。

content.content: I hear that his family makes it a policy to divide up all the household tasks among themselves.

content: 運動不足解消のため、私はこどもと公園に行くとかならず鉄棒をやることにしている。

content.content: To deal with my lack of exercise, I make it a rule to exercise on the horizontal bar every time I go to the park with my children.

content: ずいぶん前から、不正をおこなった場合は失格ということにしています。

content.content: For a long time now, any case of misconduct has led to disqualification.

Indicates that something has been made into a habit or rule, based on a certain decision. Can be considered to mean that the result of the decision or resolution made in the act of ことにする is now a regular habit. Therefore, the form ことにしている is not used to refer to customs or manners in general.
（×）日本人は、はしを使ってご飯を食べることにしています。
Japanese people have decided to use chopsticks to eat rice.
（○）日本人は、はしを使ってご飯を食べます。
Japanese people use chopsticks to eat rice.
【ことにする】
1. ...ことにする〈decision〉［Vことにする］

content: あしたからジョギングすることにしよう。

content.content: Starting tomorrow, I am going to jog.

content: これからはあまりあまい物は食べないことにしよう。

content.content: From now on, I'm not going to eat so many sweets.

content: きょうはどこへも行かないで勉強することにしたよ。

content.content: I decided not to go anywhere and just study today.
Indicates a decision or resolution to perform an action in the future. When the form ことにした is used, as in

content: , it conveys the meaning that a decision or resolution has already been made. こととする has the same meaning as ことにする, but こととする is more formal and tends to be used in written language.

content.content: 2. ...ことにする〈treatment〉［N（だ）ということにする］［Na　だということにする］［V-た（という）ことにする］

content: その話は聞かなかった（という）ことにしましょう。

content.content: Let’s just say that we never heard that story.

content: その件は検討中（だ）ということにして、すこしなりゆきを見まもろう。

content.content: Let’s put that matter under consideration and see how things go for a while.

content: 敵の攻撃に対する防御の時間をかせぐために、大統領はすこぶる健康だということにしておくべきだ。

content.content: We’d better pretend that the president is in excellent health, in order to gain time to prepare a defense against attacks from the enemy.

content: 出張に行った（という）ことにして出張費を着服したり不正流用することを、俗に「カラ出張」と言う。

content.content: Pretending to have been on a business trip and pocketing or misappropriating the travel expenses is commonly known as a kara-shutchoo (phoney business trip).

Attached to a clause describing an action or state, this expression is used to pretend something is true when it isn’t, or to signal that someone will handle a situation in a certain way. When used with a noun, it takes the form N(だ)ということにする, as in

content: . With verbs, it follows the ta-form, as in
and
. In that case, use of という is optional. ...こととする, which has the same meaning, is more formal and used in written language. See Usage 1 of ことになる for a comparison with that expression.

content.content: 【ことになっている】［Nということになっている］［V-る　（という）ことになっている］［V-ない　（という）ことになっている］

content: やすむときは学校に連絡しなければならないことになっています。

content.content: There is a rule that you must contact the school when you are absent.

content: 乗車券をなくした場合は最長区間の料金をいただくことになっているんですが。

content.content: I'm afraid that, when you’ve lost your train ticket, we have to ask you to pay the fare for the maximum distance.

content: 規則では、不正をおこなった場合は失格ということになっている。

content.content: According to the regulations, when you commit an act of wrongdoing, you will be disqualified.

content: 駐車場内での盗難や事故については、駐車場側は関知しないことになっております。

content.content: The parking lot management takes no responsibility for theft or accidents that take place inside the parking lot.

content: パーティーに参加する人は、6時に駅で待ち合わせることになっている。

content.content: Those who are going to attend the party are supposed to meet at the station at six o’clock.

content: 夏休みのあいだ、畑の水やりは子供たちがすることになっている。

content.content: During summer vacation, it’s the children's job to water the garden.

Indicates a variety of rules that govern people’s activities, including their plans, agreements in daily life, laws and rules, and even customs. Can be considered to mean that the conclusion or result of ...ことになる continues to have an effect.
【ことになる】
1. ...ことになる〈decision〉［Nということになる］［V-る　（という）ことになる］［V-ない　（という）ことになる］

content: こんど大阪支社に行くことになりました。

content.content: It’s been decided that I am to go to the Osaka branch office.

content: ふたりでよく話し合った結果、やはり離婚するのが一番いいということになりました。

content.content: After a long discussion between the two of us, we came to the conclusion that, as we had suspected, divorce was the best solution.

content: よく話し合った結果、やはり離婚ということになりました。

content.content: After a long discussion, the decision, as expected, was to divorce.

content: 亡くなった山田さんは形式ばったことがきらいな人だったから、葬式などはしないことになりそうだな。

content.content: As the late Yamada-san was a person who disliked ceremony, it looks like that there won’t be a funeral or anything.

content: この問題は、細部については両政府の次官級協議にゆだねられることになった。

content.content: Regarding this issue, it was decided that the details were to be left to vice-minister level consultations between the two governments.

Means that some kind of decision or agreement was made concerning a future action, and a certain result will follow. In contrast to ...ことにする, which specifies who made the decision or resolution, ことになるconveys the meaning that the conclusion or result in question will be obtained naturally, unintentionally, and of its own accord. Often used in the ta-form ことになった, as in

content: , and
. こととなる, which has the same meaning, is a more formal expression used in written language.

content.content: 2. ...ことになる〈restatement〉［Nということになる］［V-る　（という）ことになる］［V-ない　（という）ことになる］

content: 4年も留学するの？　じゃあ、あの会社には就職しないことになるの？

content.content: You’re going to study abroad for four years? So, you’re not going to get a job at that company after all?

content: りえさんはわたしの母の妹のこどもだから、わたしとりえさんはいとこどうしということになる。

content.content: Rie-san is the child of my mother’s sister, so that makes Rie-san and me cousins.

content: これまで 10 年前と4年前に開いているので、これで日本での開催は3回目ということになる。

content.content: It was held here ten years ago and four years ago, so that makes this the third time for it to be held in Japan.
Used to paraphrase, to look at something from a different perspective, or to point out the true nature of something.
【ことには】
1. V-ることには

content: その子供たちの言うことには、彼らの両親はもう二日も帰ってきていないらしい。

content.content: From what the children say, it appears that their parents have not been home for two days already.

content: 学生たちの言うことには、ことしは就職が予想以上にきびしいらしい。

content.content: From what the students say, it sounds like job-hunting this year is much harder than they had imagined.

content: 先生のおっしゃることには、最近の学生は言われたことしかしないそうだ。

content.content: According to the professor, students these days do only what they’re told to do.

content: たぬきさんの言うことにゃ、きつねさんがかぜをひいたそうじゃ。

content.content: What Mr. Raccoon says is that Mr. Fox has caught a cold.
Often attached to 言う (say) or to the dictionary form of a similar verb. Specifies the person who made the utterance that is quoted or reported. In

content: , it means “those children are saying that their parents haven’t been home for a full two days.” A slightly old-fashioned expression that has the tone of written language; in particular, the form ことにゃ (as shown in
) is often used in folktales and the like.

content.content: 2. V-ないことには

content: 先生が来ないことにはクラスははじまらない。

content.content: The class cannot start if the teacher doesn’t come.

content: いい辞書を手にいれないことには外国語の勉強はうまくいかない。

content.content: Studying a foreign language will not go well if you don’t get a good dictionary.

content: あなたがこころよく見おくってくれないことには、私としても気持ちよく出発できないよ。

content.content: I won’t be able to feel good about leaving if you don’t come willingly to see me off.

content: とにかくこの予算案が国会で承認されないことには、景気回復のための次のてだてを講ずることは不可能だ。

content.content: Anyway, if this budget proposal is not approved by the Diet, it will be impossible to take the next measures to restore the economy.
Used in the pattern XないことにはYない and means that Y cannot be realized without realizing X. X is a necessary condition for the realization of Y. Can be paraphrased with なければ or なくては.
【ことは...が】［Na なことはNa だが］［AことはAが］［VことはVが］

content: 読んだことは読んだが、ぜんぜん分からなかった。

content.content: Though I did read it, I didn’t understand it at all.

content: あの映画、おもしろいことはおもしろいけど、もう一度金をはらって見たいとは思わないね。

content.content: I do agree that that movie is interesting, but I wouldn’t pay money to see it again.

content: おいしかったことはおいしかったけどね、でも高すぎるよ。

content.content: Yes, it was delicious, but it’s too expensive!

content: どうしてもやれと言うなら、いちおうやってみることは（やって）みるけど、うまく行かないと思うよ。

content.content: If you insist, I will at least give it a try, but I don’t think it will work.

content: A:ひさしぶり。元気だった？

content.content: Long time no see. How have you been?
B:元気なことは元気なんだけどねえ。なにかもうひとつ満たされない気分なんだなあ。
I am doing well, but even so.... I feel like something’s missing.
The same word is repeated. This pattern expresses concession. It is used when the speaker acknowledges something to a certain extent, but not vigorously or completely.
When a verb is used, as in

content: and

, it means that the speaker will perform (or has performed) the action but thinks that the result will not be (or was not) satisfactory. Often used with てみる. When a noun or an adjective is used with this pattern, as in
, and
, it means “although I do not deny such-and-such....” For example,
can be paraphrased as おもしろくない(という)わけではないが (it’s not that it isn’t interesting).

content.content: When this pattern is used to refer to past events, sometimes both words are changed to the ta-form, as in

content: , and sometimes only the second word is changed, as in the example below.

content.content: （例）読むことは読んだが、ぜんぜん分からなかった。
I did read it, but I didn’t understand it at all.
【ことはない】［V-ることはない］

content: 心配することはないよ。ぼくもてつだうからがんばろう。

content.content: There’s nothing to worry about. I’ll help you too, so let’s do it.

content: こまったことがあったらいつでも私に言ってね。ひとりでなやむことはないのよ。

content.content: Please let me know if you have any problems. There’s no need to agonize on your own.

content: そのことでは彼にも責任があるんだから、君だけが責任をとることはないよ。

content.content: He’s to blame for it too, so you really don’t have to take all the responsibility yourself.
Used with respect to a certain action, to say that there is no necessity for it or no need to do it. Often used to encourage someone or to give advice.
【ことはならない】［V ことはならない］

content: だめだ。あんな男と結婚することはならない。おまえはだまされているんだ。おとうさんはぜったいにゆるさない。

content.content: No. I won’t allow you to marry such a man. You have been deceived. I (your father) will never allow it.

content: 戦前は、天皇の写真でさえ顔を上げて見ることはならないとされていた。

content.content: Before the war, it was prohibited to look directly at even a picture of the Emperor.

content: こどものころ、本や新聞をまたぐことはならぬとよくおじいさんにしかられたものだ。

content.content: When I was a child, my grandfather often scolded me not to step over books or newspapers.
Has the meaning of prohibition, as in “you shouldn’t do....” Also takes the form ならぬ, as in

content: . An old-fashioned expression.

content.content: 【このたび】

content: この度はご結婚おめでとうございます。

content.content: Congratulations on the occasion of your marriage.

content: 《あいさつ》この度、転勤することになりました。

content.content: 《speech》It has been decided that I will be transferred.

content: この度、会長に選ばれました佐々木でございます。どうぞよろしくお願いいたします。

content.content: My name is Sasaki, and I have been selected as chairperson on this occasion. I greatly appreciate your support.
Means “(at) this time” and is a formal idiomatic expression.
【このぶんでは】→
【ぶん】3
【こむ】［R-こむ］

content: ここに名前を書きこんでください。

content.content: Please write your name in this (space).

content: かばんに本をつめこんで旅にでかけた。

content.content: He left on a trip, with books stuffed into his suitcase.

content: トラックに荷物を積みこむのを手伝った。

content.content: I helped to load the baggage into the truck.

content: その客は家にあがりこんで、もう5時間も帰らない。

content.content: It’s been five hours since that visitor came into the house, and he still isn’t leaving.

content: 日本の社会に溶け込むことと自分の文化を見うしなわないこととは両立するのだろうか。

content.content: Is it possible to integrate into Japanese society and, at the same time, not lose one’s own culture?

content: 人の部屋に勝手に入り込まないでくれ。

content.content: Please don’t come into my room uninvited.

content: 友達と話し込んでいたらいつのまにか朝になっていた。

content.content: I talked and talked with my friends, and then before I knew it, it was morning.

content: サルに芸を教え込むことと子供を教育することとの違いが分かっていない教師がいる。

content.content: Some teachers don’t understand the difference between training monkeys and educating children.

content: 部屋の片隅に座り込んで、じっと考え事をしている。

content.content: She is sitting down in a corner of the room, thinking intensely.
Used to make a transitive verb that means putting something into something else, as in

content: , an intransitive verb that means entering into something, as in
, or a verb that means “do something thoroughly/amply,” as in

content.content: 【これだと】

content: これだと、ちょっと困るんですけど。

content.content: With this, I would have a slight problem....

content: これだと、まだ解決には遠いようですね。

content.content: The way things are, it seems that we are still far from a solution.

content: これだと、人には薦められません。

content.content: The way this is, I can’t recommend it to others.

content: これだと、目的地に到着するまでまだ2～3時間かかりそうだ。

content.content: At this rate, it’s likely to take another two or three hours before we reach our destination.
Same as これでは.
【これでは】
【これでは】

content: これでは、生活していけません。

content.content: With only this, we cannot live.

content: これでは、問題の解決になっていない。

content.content: This doesn’t provide a solution to the problem.

content: 君の作文は誤字が多すぎる。これでは、試験にパスしないだろう。

content.content: Your compositions contain too many spelling mistakes. At this rate, I’m afraid you won’t pass the examination.

content: 高速道路の渋滞がひどい。これでは目的地に到着するまで、2～3時間はかかりそうだ。

content.content: There’s a terrible traffic jam on the expressway. At this rate, it’ll probably be two or three hours before we arrive at our destination.
Means “under these circumstances/conditions.” Often followed by an unfavorable judgment or prediction.
【ごし】
1. Nごし〈space〉

content: となりの人とへいごしにあいさつした。

content.content: I said “Hello” to my neighbor over the fence.

content: そのふるい映画には恋人どうしがガラスごしにキスをするシーンがあった。

content.content: In that old movie, there was a scene in which the lovers kissed each other through the window glass.

content: 窓越しに見える無数の星を見るのが好きだ。

content.content: I love to look at the infinite number of stars I can see through the window.
Means “through or over something.”
2. Nごし〈time〉

content: 3年ごしの話し合いで、やっと離婚した。

content.content: After three years of negotiations, they finally got divorced.

content: 私にとっては 10 年ごしの問題にやっとくぎりがつき、まとめたのが、この作品です。

content.content: For me, this work (of art) integrates and finally closes the chapter on ten long and difficult years.

content: 7年ごしの交渉がようやく実を結び、両国の間に平和条約が結ばれた。

content.content: The seven years of negotiation finally bore fruit, and a peace treaty was concluded between the two countries.
Usually takes the form ...年ごしのN. Means that an action or situation continued throughout a certain period of time.
【ごとし】A literary expression that is now used only in written language. ごとしis the form that is used at the end of a sentence, and the conjugated forms are ごときN and ごとくV.
1. ごとし［Nのごとし］［Nであるがごとし］

content: 光陰矢のごとし。

content.content: Time flies like an arrow.

content: 時間というものは、矢のごとくはやくすぎさっていくものだ。

content.content: Time passes by quickly, just as an arrow flies.

content: 山田ごときに負けるものか。

content.content: I’ll never lose to someone like Yamada.
Used to compare one thing to another, like ...のようだ. The form Nごとき is usually followed by a noun to create the pattern NごときN, but sometimes Nごとき is used by itself as a noun, as in

content: . This usage is limited to cases in which the meaning is accompanied by a negative evaluation. With the exception of proverbs and idioms, ようだ is now used more often than ごとし.

content.content: 2. ...かのごとし

content: 彼女はそのことを知っているはずなのに、まったく聞いたことがないかのごとき態度だった。

content.content: Though she should have known about it, she acted as if she had heard nothing at all.

content: そのふたりはまずしかったが、世界中が自分たちのものであるかのごとくしあわせであった。

content.content: Although the two of them were poor, they were as happy as if everything in the world belonged to them.

content: 「盗作する」とは、他人の作品を自分の作品であるかのごとく発表することである。

content.content: Toosaku-suru (plagiarize) means to publish or present someone else’s work as if it were your own.

content: あの政治家は、いつも優柔不断であるかのごとくふるまってはいるが、実はそうかんたんには真意を見せないタヌキである。

content.content: That politician always acts as if he can’t make a decision, but he is really a sly fox who doesn't readily reveal his true intentions.
This is used after a sentence, but in the case of nouns and na-adjectives, as in

content: and
, it follows である and not だ. Means that something is not actually so, but looks as if it is. Now かのようだ is used more often. In particular, the dictionary form かのごとし is almost never used nowadays.

content.content: 【ごとに】［Nごとに］［V-るごとに］

content: このめざまし時計は5分ごとに鳴る。

content.content: This alarm clock rings every five minutes.

content: こどもというものは、見るごとに大きくなっていくものだなあ。

content.content: Children get bigger every time we see them, don't they?

content: この季節は、よくひと雨ごとにあたたかくなるという。

content.content: In this season, it is often said that it gets warmer with each rainfall.

content: 彼は、会う人ごとに、こんど建てた家のことを自慢している。

content.content: He brags to every person he meets about the house he’s just built.
Used to express the meaning of “each and every time,” as in

content: , and
, as well as the notion of “each person or individual,” as in
. With verbs (see
), たびに is used more often, as in 見るたびに (every time I see (s.o./s.t.)). Also,
can be paraphrased as 人に会うたびに (every time he meets someone) or 会う人会う人に (every person he meets).

content.content: 【ごらん】

content: どうぞ、ご自由にごらんください。

content.content: Please, look around freely.

content: ごらん（なさい）、つばめがやってきた。

content.content: (Please) look, the swallows are here.

content: ひとりでやってごらん。ここで見ててあげるから。

content.content: Try and do it by yourself. I’ll be watching you from here.

content: こどもはいくらかな。駅員さんに聞いてきてごらん。

content.content: I wonder how much the fare is for children. Go and ask one of the station staff, will you?
Honorific expression for 見る (look, see). In some cases, as in

content: , it is used in the form ごらんください, which is an honorific form of 見てください (please look). In other cases, like
, it is used as an elegant way of saying 見なさい (look) (ごらん is the abbreviated form of ごらんなさい). It is also used in the form てごらん, as in
and
, which is an elegant way of saying てみなさい (try to do...). Even though
, and
are refined expressions, they still mean ...しなさい (do it) and are not used when talking to a higher-status person.

content.content: 【さあ】
1. さあ

content: さあ、いこう。

content.content: All right, let’s go.

content: さあ、いそいで、いそいで。

content.content: Come on, hurry up, hurry up.

content: さあ、がんばるぞ。

content.content: OK, I’ll do my best.

content: さあ、春だ。

content.content: Now, it is spring.

content: さあ、ごはんができたぞ。

content.content: Now dinner is ready.
Used to urge or invite the listener to do something.

content: is an example of someone encouraging him/herself. In cases like
and
, the functions seen in
, and

, such as urging, inviting, or encouraging someone to do something, are concealed. These examples can be paraphrased as さあ、春だ。がんばるぞ (Now, it is spring. I will work hard!) and さあ、ごはんができたぞ。食べよう／食べなさい (Now, dinner is ready. Let’s eat!/Start eating!). With the exception of the usage shown in
, さあ can also be used by itself when the meaning is clear from the situation.

content.content: 2. さあ

content: A:あの人、だれ？

content.content: Who is that person?
B:さあ（、知りません）。
Well... (I don’t know).

content: A:これから、どうする？

content.content: What are you going to do from now on?
B:さあ、どうしようかな。
Well, I’m not sure yet.
Used in response to a question or a situation when the speaker does not know the answer, as in

content: , or when the speaker has trouble making a judgment, as in
. さあ is used by itself, particularly with the meaning shown in
, only when the conversation is between people in a close relationship.

content.content: 【さい】［Nのさい（に）］［Vさい（に）］

content: お降りのさいは、お忘れ物のないよう、お気をつけください。

content.content: When getting off (the train), be sure not to leave anything behind.

content: 先日京都へ行った際、小学校のときの同級生をたずねた。

content.content: When I went to Kyoto the other day, I visited a classmate of mine from elementary school.

content: このさい、おもいきって家族みんなでスペインにひっこさない？

content.content: This is an opportunity, so why don’t we take the plunge and move to Spain all together as a family?

content: 国際会議を本県で開催される際には、次回はぜひとも我が市の施設をお使いくださるよう、市長としてお願い申し上げます。

content.content: When an international conference is held in this prefecture, I as mayor of this city beg that next time you use our city’s facilities.

Can often be paraphrased as とき. Differences between さい and とき include: (a) さい is more formal than とき, (b) さい has the additional meaning of opportunity, chance, or trigger, and (c) さい is less likely to be used with negative forms than とき. Also, it should be noted that このさい, as in

content: , is an idiomatic expression used when a decision is made by resolutely seizing an opportunity, and as such it cannot be paraphrased as とき.

content.content: 【さいご】→
【がさいご】
【さいちゅう】［Nのさいちゅう］［V-ているさいちゅう］

content: 大事な電話の最中に、急におなかが痛くなってきた。

content.content: In the middle of an important telephone call, I suddenly started to get a stomachache.

content: きのうの断水のとき私はちょうどシャワーの最中でした。

content.content: When the water got turned off yesterday, I was right in the middle of taking a shower.

content: 授業をしている最中に非常ベルが鳴りだした。

content.content: The alarm bell started to ring during the middle of class.

content: その件は私たちの方で今話し合っている最中だから、最終結論を出すのはもうちょっと待ってくれないか。

content.content: We are still discussing the matter among ourselves, so could you wait a little while longer before you make a final decision?
Means that a certain action or phenomenon is in progress at just that time. Often used in cases when something suddenly happens while the action etc. is in progress, as in
【さえ】
1. さえ［N（+助詞）さえ（も）］［疑問詞...かさえ（も）］

content: あのころは授業料どころか家賃さえはらえないほどまずしかった。

content.content: In those days we were so poor that we couldn’t even afford to pay the rent, let alone the tuition fees.

content: この本はわたしにはむずかしすぎます。何について書いてあるのかさえわかりません。

content.content: This book is too difficult for me. I don’t even understand what it is about.

content: そんなことは小学生でさえ知ってるよ。

content.content: Even elementary school children know things like that.

content: 本人にさえわからないものを、どうしてあの人にわかるはずがあるんだ。

content.content: Why would you expect her to understand it, when even the person in question doesn’t understand?

content: その小説はあまりにもおもしろくて、食事の時間さえもったいないと思ったほどだった。

content.content: That novel was so exciting that I felt like even time spent eating was a waste.

content: A:ぼくたち、いつ結婚するんだ。

content.content: When are we getting married?
B:なに言ってるの。するかどうかさえ、私はまだ決めてないのよ。
What are you talking about? I haven’t decided yet whether or not we should even get married.

Used to state that something assumed as a matter of course is not true, and to imply that other conditions are even less likely to be true. When attached to the grammatical subject, it often takes the form でさえ. Can be replaced by ...も.
2. ...さえ　...たら／...ば［Nさえ　...たら／...ば］［R-さえ　したら／すれば］［V-てさえ　...たら／...ば］［疑問詞...かさえ　...たら／...ば］

content: あなたさえそばにいてくだされば、ほかにはなにもいりません。

content.content: If you are close to me, I don’t need anything else.

content: あなたがそばにいてさえくだされば、ほかにはなにもいりません。

content.content: If only you are close to me, I don’t need anything else.

content: あなたがそばにいてくださりさえすれば、ほかにはなにもいりません。

content.content: As long as you are close to me, I don’t need anything else.

content: 今度の試験で何が出るのかさえわかったらなあ。

content.content: If only I could know what’s going to be on the exam this time....
Expresses the feeling that it is enough if a certain thing is realized, and that other things are trivial, unnecessary, or do not pose a problem.
3. ただでさえ→
【ただでさえ】
【さしあげる】→
【てさしあげる】
【さしつかえない】

content: さしつかえ（が）なければ、今夜ご自宅にお電話しますが...。

content.content: If it is not inconvenient, I would like to call you at home tonight....

content: これ、来週までお借りしてほんとうにさしつかえありませんか。

content.content: Are you sure that it is all right for me to keep this until next week?

content: わたしがおおくりしてさしつかえないのなら、山田先生はわたしの車でおつれしますが。

content.content: If it is all right for me to drive him, I would be happy to take Yamada-sensei in my car.
Means “no problem” or “no objection.” Also used in the form て(も)さしつかえない, as in

content: and
. It is possible to insert が in cases like
, but not in cases like
and

content.content: 【さすが】
1. さすが

content: これ、山田さんがつくったの？　うまいねえ。さすが（は）プロだねえ。

content.content: Did Yamada-san make this? Marvelous! Just what you’d expect from a pro.

content: さすが（は）山田さんだねえ。うまいねえ。

content.content: That’s just what I’d expect from Yamada-san. Marvelous!

content: これ山田さんがつくったの？　さすがだねえ。

content.content: Did Yamada-san make this? Only she could do it!

content: さすが（は）世界チャンピオン、その新人の対戦相手を問題にせずしりぞけた。

content.content: Being the world champion that he is, he defeated the rookie opponent without any difficulty.
Often appears at the beginning of a sentence. Can take the form さすが(は)Nだ, as in

content: , and
, or さすがだ, as in
. Used when a result is obtained that is consistent with the speaker’s knowledge or conventional wisdom. Similar to やはり, but さすが is only used to convey positive evaluation.

content.content: 2. さすがに

content: 沖縄でもさすがに冬の夜はさむいね。

content.content: It is cold at night in winter, even in Okinawa.

content: いつもはおちついている山田さんだが、はじめてテレビに出たときはさすがに緊張したそうだ。

content.content: I heard that even Yamada-san, who is usually imperturbable, got very nervous the first time he appeared on television.

content: 世界チャンピオンもさすがにかぜには勝てず、いいところなくやぶれた。

content.content: Even the world champion could not defeat the common cold, and she lost without doing anything remarkable.

content: 最近調子を落としている山田選手だが、このレベルの相手だとさすがにあぶなげなく勝った。

content.content: Even though Yamada-senshu (the athlete) has not been in the best condition lately, she won easily against this level of opponent.

content: ふだんはそうぞうしいこどもたちも今夜ばかりはさすがにお通夜のふんいきにのまれているようだ。

content.content: The children, who are usually very boisterous, seem to be overwhelmed tonight by the atmosphere of the wake.
Used when someone (or something) that is usually evaluated in a certain way is put into an extraordinary situation and shows a result or behavior that diverges from that evaluation. For instance, in

content: , it means that Okinawa, which in Japan is evaluated as being warm, is actually not so in the situation of winter nights. Used for both positive and negative evaluation.

content.content: 3. さすが（に）...だけあって［Nだけあって］［Na なだけあって］［A-いだけあって］［Vだけあって］

content: さすがプロだけあって、アマチュア選手を問題にせず勝った。

content.content: Being the pro that he is, he beat the amateur player without any problem.

content: さすがに熱心なだけあって、山田さんのテニスはたいしたもんだ。

content.content: Just as you might expect from her enthusiasm, Yamada-san’s tennis is extraordinary.

content: さすがからだが大きいだけあって、山田さんは力があるねえ。

content.content: As might be expected of a big person like him, Yamada-san has a lot of power, doesn’t he.

content: 山田さんは、さすがによく勉強しているだけあって、この前のテストでもいい成績だった。

content.content: Yamada-san got a good mark on the last test too, as might be expected from the fact that she studies so hard.

content: 彼女は、さすがに 10 年も組合活動をしているだけあって、なにごとも民主的に考えることのできる人だ。

content.content: As you might anticipate from her being an active union member for ten years, she is a person who can think democratically about everything.

Used to say that an outcome is as expected, based on conventional wisdom or the speaker’s knowledge of a person or thing. Although it is similar to やはり in meaning, さすがに...だけあって is used only for positive evaluation.
4. さすがに...だけのことはある［Nだけのことはある］［Na なだけのことはある］［A-いだけのことはある］［Vだけのことはある］

content: アマチュア選手が相手なら問題にしないね。さすがにプロだけのことはあるよ。

content.content: If the challengers are amateur players, he won’t care about it. They don’t call him a pro for nothing!

content: 山田さんのテニスはたいしたもんだ。さすがに熱心なだけのことはあるよ。

content.content: Yamada-san’s tennis deserves admiration. It’s just as we might expect from her dedication.

content: 山田さんはちからがあるねえ。さすがにからだがおおきいだけのことはある。

content.content: How powerful Yamada-san is! It’s just as might be expected from his large build.

content: 山田さんはこの前のテストでもいい成績だった。さすがによく勉強しているだけのことはあるね。

content.content: Yamada-san got a good grade on the last test too. It’s just as you might expect from her studying so hard.

content: 彼女はなにごとも民主的に考えることのできる人だ。さすがに20 年も組合のリーダーをやっているだけのことはある。

content.content: She is a person who can think democratically about everything. It’s just what you’d expect of someone who has been a union leader for more than twenty years.

Used to look at a certain result or situation and then find the cause or reason for it, using the speaker’s knowledge or conventional wisdom. Similar to やはり, but さすがに...だけのことはある is used only for positive evaluation. Can be combined with さすがに...だけあって to create the form さすがに...だけのことはあって.
5. さすがのNも

content: さすがの世界チャンピオンもケガには勝てなかった。

content.content: World champion though she is, she couldn’t beat an injury.

content: さすがの山田さんも、はじめてテレビに出たときは緊張したそうだ。

content.content: I heard that even Yamada-san (who is always very calm) got nervous when he appeared on television for the first time.

content: さすがの機動隊も、ひとびとのからだをはった抵抗にたいしては、それ以上まえにすすむことができなかった。

content.content: Even the riot police (who are used to dealing with situations like this) couldn’t advance any further against the resistance of people who were laying their lives on the line.

content: 私は小さいころよくいじめられるこどもだった。しかし、さすがのよわむしもおとうとやいもうとがいじめられているときだけは相手にとびかかっていったそうだ。

content.content: When I was a child, I was frequently bullied. However, people say that, wimp though I was, I would throw myself fiercely at the antagonist whenever my younger brother or sister was being bullied.

Used when someone or something that is usually evaluated in a certain way is put into a particular situation and then shows a result or behavior that diverges from that evaluation. Has basically the same function as さすがに, which is used like an adverb.

【させる】Expresses causation. When the verb in V-させる is a Group 1 verb, the vowel in the final syllable of the dictionary form changes from -u to -a and then せる is attached, as in 行く→行かせる and 飲む→飲ませる. For Group 2 verbs such as 食べる, させる is attached to the stem 食べ and the conjugation pattern is 食べる→食べさせる. The causative form of する is させる, and 来る becomes こさせる. In spoken language, the forms 行かす, 飲ます, 食べさす, and so on may also be used.

A causative sentence essentially conveys the meaning that one person orders or directs another person to do something. However, in actual usage the causative form expresses a broader range of meaning, including coercion, instruction, non-interference, permission, and so on.
（例1）〈強制〉犯人は銀行員に現金を用意させた。
〈coercion〉The criminal made the bank clerk prepare the cash.
（例2）〈指示〉社長は秘書にタイプを打たせた。
〈instruction〉The company president had the secretary do the typing.
（例3）〈放任〉疲れているようだったので、そのまま眠らせておいた。
〈non-interference〉Since she seemed to be tired, I let her sleep.
（例4）〈許可〉社長は給料を前借りさせてくれた。
〈permission〉The president let me have an advance on my salary.
（例5）〈放置〉風呂の水をあふれさせるな。
〈neglect〉Don’t let the bathwater overflow.
（例6）〈介護〉子供にミルクを飲ませる時間です。
〈care〉It’s time to give the child some milk.
（例7）〈自責〉子どもを事故で死なせてしまった。
〈self-reproach〉It’s my fault that my child died in the accident.
（例8）〈原因〉フロンガスが地球を温暖化させている。
〈cause〉Chlorofluorocarbon is causing global warming.
1. V-させるa. NがNにNを V-させる

content: 教師が学生に本を読ませた。

content.content: The teacher made the students read the book.

content: 犯人は銀行員に現金を用意させた。

content.content: The criminal made the bank clerk prepare the cash.

content: A:機械がまた故障なんですが...。

content.content: The machine is out of order again....
B:申し訳ありません。すぐに係りの者を伺わせます。
We apologize for the inconvenience. We will send the person in charge over immediately.

content: 山田はひどい奴だ。旅行中ずっと僕に運転させて、自分は寝てるんだよ。

content.content: Yamada is a horrible person. When we were traveling, he made me drive all the way while he just slept.

Expresses a variety of meanings, such as coercion, instruction, and non-interference. The causative sentence NがNにNをV-させる is derived from a sentence with a transitive verb NがNを(transitive) V. The subject Nが of the transitive sentence becomes Nに.
b. NがN　を／に　V-させる

content: 子どもを買い物に行かせた。

content.content: I had the children go shopping.

content: 社長は、まず山田をソファーにかけさせて、しばらく世間話をしてから退職の話を切りだした。

content.content: The company president first had Yamada sit on the sofa and then, after making small talk for a little while, he broached the subject of retirement.

content: 最近は小学生を塾に通わせる親が多い。

content.content: Many parents send their elementary school-aged children to juku (cram schools) these days.

content: 大きな契約だから、新入社員に行かせるのは心配だ。

content.content: Since it’s a big contract, I’m worried about letting a new employee go on her own.

Expresses a variety of meanings, such as coercion, instruction, and non-interference. The causative sentence NがNを／にV-させる is derived from a sentence with an intransitive verb Nが(intransitive) V. The subject Nが of the intransitive sentence often becomes Nを, but may sometimes become Nに.
c. NがNをV-させる〈person〉

content: 彼は、いつも冗談を言ってみんなを笑わせる。

content.content: He is always telling jokes and making everyone laugh.

content: 就職試験を受けなかったために、父をすっかり怒らせてしまった。

content.content: The fact that I didn’t take the employment test made my father very angry.

content: 私は子供の頃は乱暴で、近所の子をよく泣かせていた。

content.content: When I was a child I was wild and unruly, and often made the children in my neighborhood cry.

content: 二年も続けて落第して母をがっかりさせた。

content.content: I disappointed my mother by flunking a grade two years in a row.

content: 厳しくしつけすぎて、息子をすっかりいじけさせてしまった。

content.content: I brought my son up so strictly that he became utterly intimidated.

content: 子どもを交通事故で死なせてからというもの、毎日が失意のどん底であった。

content.content: From the time I lost my child in a traffic accident, I have been in the depths of despair every day.

Means “induce someone to do...” or “be the cause of someone doing....” In this pattern, the causative sentences use intransitive verbs that express an action that a person cannot control, such as 泣く (cry), 笑う (laugh), and 怒る (get angry). The subject Nが in Nが (intransitive) V becomes Nを in the causative sentence. Example

content: expresses a sense of self-reproach on the part of the speaker, because even though the incident in question was not intentional and s/he was not the direct cause, the child was under his/her care when the incident took place.

content.content: d. NがNを V-させる〈thing〉

content: シャーベットは、果汁を凍らせて作ります。

content.content: Sherbet is made by freezing fruit juice.

content: 打撲の傷みには、タオルを水で湿らせて冷やすとよい。

content.content: To ease the ache of a bruise, it’s good to cool it with a wet towel.

content: 貿易の不均衡が日米関係を硬化させている。

content.content: The trade imbalance is putting a strain on Japan-US relations.

content: 金融不安が、日本の経済状態を悪化させる原因となっている。

content.content: Financial instability is causing the economic situation in Japan to deteriorate.

content: 子供達は目を輝かせて話に聞き入っている。

content.content: The children are listening intently to the story, their eyes sparkling.

content: 猫は目を光らせて暗闇に潜んでいる。

content.content: The cat is lurking in the darkness, its eyes sharp.

Means “induce something to do...” or “be the cause of something doing....” In this usage, the causative form of an intransitive verb without a corresponding transitive verb, such as 凍る (freeze) or 湿る (become moist/wet), is used the same way as a transitive verb. 目を輝かせる and 目を光らせる in

content: and
are idiomatic expressions.

content.content: 2. V-させてあげる〈permission〉

content: そんなにこの仕事がやりたいのなら、やらせてあげましょう。

content.content: If you want to do this job so much, I will let you do it.

content: 従業員たちもずいぶんよく働いてくれた。2、3日休みをとらせてやってはどうだろう。

content.content: The employees have worked extremely hard. Why don’t we let them have a few days off?

content: きのうの晩、ずいぶん遅くまで勉強をしていたようだから、もう少し休ませてあげましょう。

content.content: She seems to have been up quite late studying last night, so let’s let her sleep a little while longer.
A causative expression combined with あげる, やる, etc. indicates permission or non-interference.
3. V-させておく〈non-interference〉

content: 甘えて泣いているだけだから、そのまま泣かせておきなさい。

content.content: He’s just crying like a spoilt baby, so leave him be and let him cry.

content: 注意したってどうせ人の言うことなんか聞こうとしないんだ。勝手に好きなことをさせておけばいいさ。

content.content: It doesn’t matter what advice other people give her, she won’t listen anyway. Just let her do whatever she wants.

content: 夕方になると急に冷え込みますから、あんまり遅くまで遊ばせておいてはいけませんよ。

content.content: When evening comes it gets cold all of a sudden, so you shouldn’t let them play outside too late.
A causative expression combined with おく indicates non-interference.
4. V-させてください〈request for permission〉

content: 申し訳ありませんが、今日は少し早く帰らせてください。

content.content: I’m very sorry, but please let me go home a little early today.

content: A:だれか、この仕事を引き受けてくれませんか。

content.content: Is there anyone who will take this job on?
B:ぜひ、私にやらせてください。
Please let me do it!

content: A:私が御馳走しますよ。

content.content: This will be my treat.
B:いや、いつも御馳走になってばかりですので、ここは、私に払わせてください。
Thank you, but since you always treat me, please let me pay here.

content: 少し考えさせていただけますか。

content.content: Could you give me some time to think it over?

content: 期日については、こちらで決めさせていただけるとありがたいのですが...。

content.content: We would appreciate it if you would let us decide on the deadline....
A causative expression combined with an expression of request, such as ください or いただけますか, indicates a request for permission. As in

content: , this pattern is also used to make a polite offer.

content.content: 5. V-させて　もらう／くれる〈favor〉

content: 両親が早く亡くなったので、姉が働いて私を大学に行かせてくれた。

content.content: Since both of my parents passed away when I was young, my older sister worked to put me through college.

content: 金婚式のお祝いに、子ども達にハワイに行かせてもらった。

content.content: To celebrate our golden wedding anniversary, our children gave us a trip to Hawaii.

content: 《結婚式のスピーチ》新婦の友人を代表して、一言ご挨拶させていただきます。

content.content: 《wedding speech》On behalf of the friends of the bride, I would like to say a few words.

content: 《パーティーで》では、僭越ではございますが、乾杯の音頭をとらせていただきます。

content.content: 《at a party》Now, if you will allow me, I would like to propose a toast.
A causative expression combined with もらう (receive) or くれる (give), etc. shows that the speaker views being allowed or left to do something as a kind of favor.

content: and
are idiomatic expressions used as introductory remarks in speeches, etc. They are humble expressions that imply the speaker’s gratitude or sense of honor at being asked to undertake a certain task.

content.content: 6. V-させられる〈causative passive〉［NがNにVさせられる］

content: きのうは、お母さんに3時間も勉強させられた。

content.content: Yesterday, I was forced by my mother to study for three whole hours.

content: 先輩に無理に酒を飲まされた。

content.content: I was forced to drink alcohol by a senior student.

content: この歳になって、海外に転勤させられるとは思ってもみなかった。

content.content: At my age, I certainly didn’t expect to be transferred overseas.

content: 山下さんは、毎日遅くまで残業させられているらしい。

content.content: Apparently Yamashita-san is being forced to work overtime until late every day.

content: きのうのサッカーの試合は、逆転につぐ逆転で最後までハラハラさせられた。

content.content: Yesterday’s soccer game kept me on pins and needles right up to the end, with one reversal after another.

A causative sentence with the form XがYにV-させる is rephrased from Y’s point of view to create the form YがXにV-させられる, which is a passive sentence. It means that Y is forced by X to do something against his/her will, and that Y thinks this action is bothersome or objectionable. With Group I verbs such as 行く and 読む, the causative passive form tends to become 行かされる and 読まされる (instead of 行かせられる and 読ませされる).
【さぞ...ことだろう】→
【ことだろう】
【さっぱり】
1. さっぱり...ない

content: あの人の話はいつもむずかしいことばがたくさんでてきてさっぱりわからない。

content.content: That person always uses a lot of difficult words, so I have no idea what she’s talking about.

content: 最近山田さんからさっぱり連絡がないね。

content.content: We haven’t heard from Yamada-san at all lately, have we?

content: 辞書をいくら使ってもこの本はさっぱり理解できない。

content.content: I can’t understand this book at all, even with the frequent use of a dictionary.

content: これだけ努力しているのにさっぱり上達しないのは、これは私のせいではなく、日本語そのもののせいなのではないだろうか。

content.content: I wonder if the fact that my Japanese doesn’t improve at all, in spite of all my efforts, is not my own fault but the fault of the language itself.
Used to emphasize negative expressions (mostly verbs). Often implies that things do not go as expected.
2. さっぱりだ

content: A:どう、調子は。

content.content: How is it going?
B:だめ。さっぱりだよ。
Awful. Not good at all.

content: このごろ数学の成績がさっぱりだ。

content.content: My grades in mathematics aren’t good at all these days.

content: 暖冬の影響で冬物衣料の売れ行きがさっぱりだという。

content.content: They say that due to the effect of the mild winter, sales of winter clothes are not good at all.
Means that something is not good or not going well.
【さて】
1. さて

content: さて、そろそろいこうか。

content.content: All right, shall we get going?

content: さて、つぎはどこへいこうかな。

content.content: So, I wonder where we should go next.

content: A:あの人、だれ？

content.content: That person (there), who is she?
B:さて、だれだろう。
Well, I’m not sure.

content: さて、話はかわりますが...。

content.content: Well, not to change the topic, but....
さて is a word that people use when they want to move on to the next topic or action. Used to invite someone to do something, as in

content: , to let the listener know that you are thinking, as in
and
, or to change the topic, as in
. A slightly formal expression.

content.content: 2. さてV-てみると

content: 漢字がおもしろそうだったので日本語を勉強することにしたのだが、さてはじめてみると、これがけっこうむずかしい。

content.content: I decided to study Japanese because kanji looked interesting, but after I got started, I found out that it’s pretty difficult.

content: 頂上までいけば水ぐらいあるだろうと、むりをしてのぼっていった。ところが、さてついてみると何もないのである。

content.content: I pushed myself to climb to the top of the mountain, thinking that at least there would be some water there. However, when I got to the top there was nothing.

content: 頂上までいけば水ぐらいあるだろうと、むりをしてのぼっていった。さてついてみると、あった、あった、そこには神社もあり水もあった。

content.content: I pushed myself to climb to the top of the mountain, thinking that at least there would be some water there. And when I got to the top, yes, yes, there was a shrine and also some water.

さてV-てみると is followed by an expression that indicates a result, and it means that an action based on some kind of expectation has led to a certain outcome. Tends to be used when the result is unexpected, as in

content: and
, rather than when the result was expected, as in
. A slightly formal expression.

content.content: 【さほど】［さほど Na ではない］［さほど A-くない］［さほど V-ない］

content: きょうはさほどさむくない。

content.content: It isn’t particularly cold today.

content: きのうはさほど風がなかったので、公園でバドミントンができた。

content.content: Since there wasn’t all that much wind yesterday, we were able to play badminton at the park.

content: さほど行かないうちにバス停が見えてきた。

content.content: Before we had gone very far, the bus stop came into sight.

content: その子は、熱もさほど高いわけではなかったので、朝まで待って、それから医者につれていくことにした。

content.content: Since the child didn’t have such a high fever, we decided to wait until the next morning and then take her to the doctor.
Used with a negative expression to indicate that the degree of something is not very intense. A more formal way of saying それほど...ない.
【さも】

content: かれはさもおいしそうにビールを飲みほした。

content.content: He drank up the beer with evident relish.

content: 子供はさもねむそうな様子で、大きなあくびをした。

content.content: Looking very sleepy, the child gave a big yawn.

content: 老人は、さもがっかりした様子で立ち去った。

content.content: The old man departed, looking quite disappointed.

content: その子はさもうらやましそうな声で「いいなあ」と言った。

content.content: The child said “Ii naa (How nice),” with obvious envy in his voice.

content: その植木はさも本物らしく作ってあるが、よく見るとにせ物だということがわかる。

content.content: The plant is made to look quite real, but if you look at it closely you can see that it’s a fake.
An expression that emphasizes appearance or manner. Means “seems really, extremely....” Used with そうだ (look...), らしい (seem, appear), ようすだ (have a look, manner of...), etc.
【さらに】［さらにNa／A／V］［さらに+数量詞］

content: 一日一回では効かないので、さらに薬の量を増やした。

content.content: Since one dose per day had no effect, the amount of medicine was further increased.

content: このままでも十分おいしいのだが、クリームを入れるとさらにおいしくなる。

content.content: It’s tasty enough as is, but adding cream will make it even more delicious.

content: さらに多くの方に利用していただけますように今月は入会金を半額にいたしております。またご家族でご入会いただきますと、さらにお得なファミリー割引がございます。

content.content: With the hope that even more people will use (our facilities), we have reduced membership fees by half this month. Also, if you join as a family, there is the further advantage of a family discount.

content: 途中の小屋まで5時間、それから頂上まではさらに2時間かかった。

content.content: It took five hours to get to the hut along the way, and after that an additional two hours to the top of the mountain.

content: さらに二人のメンバーが入って、団員は全部で 18 人になった。

content.content: With two more people joining, the total number of members reached eighteen.

content: 事故の全貌が明らかになるにしたがって、更に犠牲者が増える見込みである。

content.content: As the full extent of the accident becomes clear, the number of victims is expected to increase further.

Used to say that the degree of something will increase further. Has the tone of a written language expression. Also used in polite spoken language. When used with a quantity or amount, it has the meaning of “in addition, on top of.” Can be replaced by もっと, but もっと is used more in spoken language. Cannot be replaced by もっと in cases like

content: or
, when it is combined with expressions of quantity.

content.content: 【さることながら】→
【もさることながら】
【されている】→
【とされている】
【ざるをえない】［V-ざるをえない］Formed by changing the ない in V-ない to ざる. However, する becomes せざるをえない.

content: 先生に言われたことだからやらざるをえない。

content.content: Since the teacher told me to do it, I have to.

content: 先生に言われたことだからせざるをえない。

content.content: Since the teacher told me to do it, I have no choice.

content: あんな話を信じてしまうとは、我ながらうかつだったと言わざるを得ない。

content.content: I have to say it was really careless of me to believe such a story!

content: これだけ国際的な非難を浴びれば、政府も計画を白紙に戻さざるを得ないのではないか。

content.content: Having been subjected to this much international criticism, I'd say the government has no choice but to go back to the drawing board with this plan.

Means that there is no other choice but to do a certain thing. Can be replaced by V-するほかない. Often used to show that someone is taking an action against his/her will because of pressure or the urgency of a situation, as in

content: , and
. Has the tone of written language.

content.content: 1. し〈parallel〉a. ...し

content: あの店は安いし、うまい。

content.content: That restaurant is cheap, and the food is good.

content: このアパートは静かだし、日当りもいい。

content.content: This apartment is quiet and also gets a lot of sunlight.

content: 部屋にはかぎがかかっていなかったし、窓もあいていた。

content.content: The room wasn’t locked, and besides the windows were open.

content: 昨日は食欲もなかったし、少し寒気がしたのではやく寝た。

content.content: Yesterday I didn’t have much appetite and felt a slight chill, so I went to bed early.

An expression that links one clause to another, with the meaning of そして. Used to juxtapose situations that are essentially concurrent or that are related to each other in the mind of the speaker. Cannot be used to list events in chronological order.
（×）先週大阪へ行ったし、友だちに会った。
I went to Osaka last week, and besides I saw my friends.
（○）先週大阪へ行った。そして友だちに会った。
I went to Osaka last week. And then I saw my friends.
b. ...し、それに

content: 今日は雨だし、それに風もつよい。

content.content: There's rain today, along with a strong wind.

content: この会社は給料もやすいし、それに休みも少ない。

content.content: The salary at this company is low, and there are also few days off.

content: 家の修理にはお金がかかるし、それに時間もない。だから当分このままで住むつもりだ。

content.content: It'll cost money to repair the house, and I have no time. So I'm going to live as things are for the time being.
This is an expression that adds one thing to another, in the sense of “besides, on top of” or “furthermore.”
c. Nも...し、Nも

content: あの子は頭もいいし性格もいい。

content.content: That child is smart and has a pleasant personality too.

content: 新年会には山田も来たし、松本も来た。

content.content: Yamada came to the New Year’s party, and Matsumoto came too.

content: かれはタバコも吸うし、酒も飲む。

content.content: He smokes, and he drinks.

content: 小さな庭ですが、春になると花も咲きますし鳥も来ます。

content.content: The garden is small, but when spring comes the flowers bloom and the birds come, too.

content: A:すきやきの材料は全部買った？

content.content: Did you buy all the ingredients for sukiyaki?
B:ええ、ねぎも買ったし、肉も買ったし...。
Yes, I bought long green onions, and meat, and....
Used to present a list or set of similar things.
2. し〈reason〉a. ...し

content: もう遅いしこれで失礼します。

content.content: It’s already getting late and all, so I should excuse myself.

content: 暗くなってきたし、そろそろ帰りましょうか。

content.content: Since it’s gotten dark, shall we think about going home soon?

content: 今日はボーナスも出たし、久しぶりに外に食べに行こうか。

content.content: It’s my bonus day and everything, so why don’t we do something we haven’t done for a while and go out for dinner?

content: そこは電気もないし、ひどく不便なところだった。

content.content: There was no electricity there, and altogether it was an awfully inconvenient place.

content: まだ若いんだし、あきらめずにもう一度挑戦してみてください。

content.content: You’re still young and all, so don’t give up—try it one more time.
Expresses a reason. The cause-and-effect relation is weaker than ので and から, and the implication is that there are also other reasons.

content: この子はまだ 10 歳だし、体が弱いから留学は無理だ。

content.content: This child is only ten years old and her health is poor, so it is impossible for her to go abroad to study.

content: 昨日は祭日だったし、天気がよかったから、がらくた市は大勢の人でにぎわった。

content.content: Since it was a national holiday yesterday and the weather was fine, the flea market bustled with crowds of people.

content: その道は夜は暗いし危ないから一人で歩かないようにしてください。

content.content: Since the road is both dark and dangerous at night, please take care not to walk alone.

content: 風邪気味だし、それに着て行く服もないからパーティーには行かない。

content.content: Since I feel like I’m getting a cold, and I also don’t have anything to wear, I’m not going to the party.
An expression used to list two or more reasons.
c. Nは...し、Nは...しで

content: 子供は生まれるし、金はないしで大変だ。

content.content: We’ve got a new baby and there’s no money, so it’s really tough.

content: 雨は降るし、駅は遠いしで本当につかれました。

content.content: It rained, and the station was far away—I was really exhausted.

content: 遊園地では待ち時間は長いし、子供は寝てしまうしで散々でした。

content.content: The waiting times at the amusement park were long, and the children fell asleep on me—it was terrible.
This pattern is used for emphasis. Each cause is marked with は to show contrast. Followed by an expression that indicates how terrible or tiring etc. something was.
d. Nじゃあるまいし

content: 子供じゃあるまいしそんなこと一人でやりなさい。

content.content: You’re not a child, you know—things like that you should do by yourself.

content: 学生じゃあるまいし取引先にちゃんと挨拶ぐらいできなくては困る。

content.content: You’re not just a college student, so if you can’t exchange decent greetings with our clients, that puts us in a bind.

content: 泥棒じゃあるまいし、裏口からこっそり入って来ないでよ。

content.content: You’re not a thief, so don’t sneak in through the back door, all right?
Means “since...is not so.” Followed by an expression of mild reproach or reproof, such as しなさい or しては困る. For example,

content: means “if you were a child, you might have an excuse, but since you’re not....”

content.content: 【しいしい】

content: 女は遠慮しいしい部屋の片隅に座った。

content.content: The woman sat diffidently in a corner of the room.

content: 男は大きなハンカチで汗をふきふき坂を登ってきた。

content.content: The man came up the slope, wiping at the sweat on his forehead with a large handkerchief.

content: 子供たちはもらったばかりのあめをなめなめ老人についていった。

content.content: The children followed the old man as they licked away at the candy he had just given them.

A verb stem is repeated to express a repeated action, as in 食べ食べ (eat and eat) and 飲み飲み (drink and drink). For verbs such as する and みる, which have a verb stem of one syllable (i.e. し and み), い is added to create the forms しいしい and みいみい. Used when there is another concurrent action and takes the pattern しいしい...する. A somewhat old-fashioned idiomatic expression. In spoken language, ながら is used.
【しか】
1. しか...ないa. N（+助詞）しか...ない

content: 朝はコーヒーしか飲まない。

content.content: I don’t drink anything but coffee in the morning.

content: 1時間しか待てません。

content.content: I can only wait for an hour.

content: 月曜しか空いている日はないんで、打ち合せはその日にしてもらえませんか。

content.content: Since Monday is the only day I have open, could you schedule the meeting on that day?

content: こんなことは友だちにしか話せません。

content.content: I can talk about this kind of thing only to my friends.

content: この映画は 18 歳からしか見ることはできない。

content.content: This movie is restricted to persons eighteen years and over.

content: あそこの店は6時までしかやっていない。

content.content: The shop over there is only open until six o’clock.

content: かれは自然のものだけしか食べない。

content.content: He eats nothing but organic food.

content: 今月はもうこれだけしかない。

content.content: This is all we have left this month.
Used with a negative expression. Indicates focus on one thing only, at the exclusion of all else.
The meaning of しか...ない can be further intensified by combining it with だけ (only, just), as in

content: and

content.content: b. Nでしかない

content: どんなに社会的な地位のある人でも死ぬときはひとりの人間でしかない。

content.content: No matter how much social status a person has, when he dies, he’s just a single human being.

content: 彼女は学長にまでなったが、親の目から見るといつまでも子どもでしかないようだ。

content.content: She rose all the way to president of the college, but it seems that in her parents’ eyes she’ll always be nothing more than a child.

content: 会社でいばってはいるが、家では子どもに相手にされないさびしい父親でしかない。

content.content: At work he can throw his weight around, but at home he’s just a lonely father whose children ignore him.

content: 時間がなくて出来ないと言っているが、そんなのは口実でしかない。ほんとうはやりたくないのだろう。

content.content: Even though he says he can’t do it because there’s no time, that’s nothing but an excuse. The truth is he doesn’t want to do it.
Used to emphasize that something “is N,” but often conveys the meaning that N is not evaluated very highly or has limited value. Can be replaced by にすぎない (be nothing but..., be no more than...).
c. V-るしかない

content: 高すぎて買えないから、借りるしかないでしょう。

content.content: Since it’s too expensive to buy, we don’t have any other choice but to rent it, do we?

content: そんなに学校がいやならやめるしかない。

content.content: If you hate school that much, all you can do is quit.

content: 燃料がなくなったら、飛行機は落ちるしかない。

content.content: If the fuel runs out, the plane can only go down.

content: ここまで来ればもう頑張ってやるしかほかに方法はありませんね。

content.content: Since we’ve come this far, there’s nothing else to do but give it our best, is there.
Means “can only do....” Often used in contexts where there is no other available method or possibility, and thus no other choice.

content: 今はただ悪かったとしか言えない。

content.content: All I can say now is that I’m sorry.

content: 今の時点ではわからないとしか申し上げようがありません。

content.content: The only thing I can say at this point is that we don’t know.

content: 彼の立場なら知っているはずだ。隠しているとしか思えない。

content.content: Given his position, he should know. I can’t help but think that he’s hiding something.

content: 風邪で行けないというのは口実としか思えない。

content.content: It seems to me that her saying she can’t go because of a cold is only an excuse.

content: この時刻になっても連絡がないのはおかしい。どこかで事故にあったとしか考えられない。

content.content: It’s strange that we haven’t heard anything by this time. I can only think that there’s been an accident somewhere.
Used to refute other possibilities and insist strongly on just one. Used with the negative form of V-れる potential forms, such as 言えない and 思えない. The form V-ようがない, as in

content: 申し上げようがない (nothing to say) is also used.

content.content: 【しかし】

content: 手紙を出した。しかし返事は来なかった。

content.content: I sent a letter. But no reply came.

content: そのニュースを聞いて皆泣いた。しかし私は涙が出なかった。

content.content: Upon hearing the news, everyone cried. However, I didn’t shed any tears.

content: われわれ医師団は患者の命を救うために最大限の努力をいたしました。が、しかしどうしても助けることができませんでした。

content.content: Our team of doctors made the very best efforts we could to save the lives of the patients. However, there was nothing we could do to help them.

content: A:先ほどのご意見ですが、モデルが現実とかなりずれているんじゃないでしょうか。

content.content: Regarding the opinion expressed just now—isn’t the model rather out of line with reality?
B:しかしですね、個々のケースにばかりとらわれていると、全体が見えなくなってくるということもありますし。
Yes, but if we get too wound up in the individual cases, it could happen that we lose the sight of the whole picture.

content: A:社長、先方は今月末までに送金してくれと言ってますが...。

content.content: (to the company president) Shachoo, our clients are saying they want us to remit the money by the end of this month....
B:しかしだね、君、そう急に言われても困るんだよ。
But, you know, such a sudden request is a problem for us.

content: A:ずいぶん、ひどい雨ね。

content.content: It’s really a terrible downpour, isn’t it?
B:しかしそれにしても佐藤さん、遅いね。
But even so, Sato-san is really late.

Indicates that what might be expected from the previous clause will be contradicted in the clause that follows. Often used in written language. In spoken language, しかし is used in formal situations such as debates, lectures, etc. In conversation, it is also used to preface a counter-argument against the other person’s opinion or to shift the topic, as in
【しかしながら】

content: 彼の計画は思いつきとしてはすばらしいと思います。しかしながら、実現は不可能です。

content.content: I think his plan is a splendid idea. However, it’s impossible to carry out.

content: 彼女のしたことは法律の上では決して許されない。しかしながら、人道的には同情の余地が十分ある。

content.content: What she did is not permissible in terms of the law. However, there is plenty of room for sympathy from a humanitarian standpoint.
Has the same meaning as しかし, but has more of a tone of written language and is used in writing or formal conversation. Often used in writing that requires the development of a logical argument.
【しかたがない】
1. しかたがない

content: 電話の通じない所で、しかたがないから電報を打った。

content.content: Since it was a place with no telephone connections, I had no choice but to send a telegram.

content: こんなことができないなんて、しかたがない人ね。

content.content: You can’t even do something like this—you’re hopeless, aren’t you!

content: 行きたくないけど行くしか仕方がない。

content.content: I don’t want to go, but I have no other choice.

content: 会えないなら引き返すよりしかたがない。

content.content: If we can’t meet (them), we have no choice but to go back.
Means that there is no other way. Also used in the forms V-るしかしかたがない and V-るよりしかたがない, as in

content: and
respectively. Example
means the person is incompetent or troublesome. In spoken language, the form しょうがない is also used.

content.content: 2. ...てしかたがない→
【てしかたがない】
【しかも】［N／Na　でしかも］［A-くてしかも］

content: いいアパートを見つけた。部屋が広くて、南向きでしかも駅から歩いて5分だ。

content.content: I found a good apartment. The rooms are spacious, it faces south, and what’s more it’s only a five-minute walk from the station.

content: 通訳の採用枠二名に対し百人近い応募があったが、その九割が女性で、しかも半数以上は留学経験者だった。

content.content: There were nearly a hundred applicants for the two openings for interpreters, of whom ninety percent were female, and more than the half of them had studied abroad.

content: 若くて、きれいで、しかも性格がいいとなれば結婚したがる男はいくらでもいるだろう。

content.content: I would think that there are any number of men who would like to marry someone who is young and pretty and has a good personality to boot.

content: 彼女は仕事が速くて、しかも間違いが少ないので上司の信頼が厚い。

content.content: She’s a fast worker and also makes few mistakes, so her boss places a lot of trust in her.

content: A:会社の近くで安くておいしい店、知ってるんだって。

content.content: I hear you know a restaurant close to the office that's cheap and delicious.
B:うん、しかもすいてるんだよ。
Yeah, and what's more, it isn’t crowded.

content: この不況で会社は昇給なし、しかもボーナスは例年の半分になった。

content.content: Because of the recession, there have been no salary increases at the company, and on top of that, the bonus is half as much as in past years.
Used when describing something, to add another condition with a similar tendency. Means “on top of that, in addition.”
【したがって】

content: このあたりは非常に交通の便がよい。したがって地価が高い。

content.content: This area has very good access to transportation. Consequently, the price of land is high.

content: その地方は道路があまり整備されていない。したがって初心者のドライバーは避けたほうがよい。

content.content: The roads in that region are not very well-maintained. Hence, novice drivers would do well to avoid them.

content: ロケットの燃料タンクに重大な欠陥が見つかった。したがって打ち上げ計画は当分の間、延期せざるをえない。

content.content: A serious defect was found in the fuel tank of the rocket. Consequently, the launch plan must be put off for the time being.

content: 台風の接近にともなって、沖縄地方は午後から暴風雨圏にはいる。したがって本日は休校とする。

content.content: With the approach of the typhoon, the Okinawa region will be in the storm zone starting this afternoon. Consequently, school is closed today.

An expression that logically connects the reason in the first sentence (and the conclusions that can be drawn from it) to the situation in the second sentence. Means “therefore, for that reason.” A formal expression used in written language.
【しだい】
1. Nしだいだ

content: するかしないかは、あなたしだいだ。

content.content: Whether you do it or not is up to you.

content: 世の中は金しだいでどうにでもなる。

content.content: Money makes the world go round.

content: 作物の出来具合いはこの夏の天気次第です。

content.content: The quality of the crops will depend on the weather this summer.

content: 結婚した相手次第で人生が決ってしまうこともある。

content.content: Your life can be determined by the person you marry.
Means “things vary according to N or are influenced by N.” Example

content: means “it is for you to decide.”

content.content: 2. R-しだい

content: 落し物が見つかりしだい、お知らせします。

content.content: We will let you know as soon as the lost item is found.

content: 事件のくわしい経過がわかりしだい、番組のなかでお伝えします。

content.content: We will bring you further reports on this program, as the details of the incident become known.

content: 資料が手に入り次第、すぐに公表するつもりだ。

content.content: As soon as we obtain the materials, we intend to make them public.

content: 天候が回復し次第、出航します。

content.content: We will set sail as soon as the weather clears.

Means “immediately after doing....” Expresses that as soon as one action or event is realized, the next action will be carried out. The first half of the sentence often describes an event that takes place as part of a natural progression. On the other hand, the second half of the sentence indicates an intentional action on the part of the speaker. It cannot refer to a spontaneously-occurring event or action.
（×）そのニュースが伝わり次第、暴動が起こるだろう。
As soon as the news spreads, a riot will probably happen.
In addition, R-しだい cannot be used to refer to past events.
（×）休みになりしだい、旅行に行った。
As soon as the vacation starts, they went on a trip.
Often used in TV news and the like, as in
3. V-る／V-た　しだいだ

content: とりあえずお知らせした次第です。

content.content: The facts of the matter are as I have just told you.

content: 《挨拶状》今後ともよろしくご指導くださいますようお願い申し上げる次第でございます。

content.content: 《letter of greeting》Therefore I humbly request your continued guidance in the future.
Used to describe the course of events that has led to the present state of affairs, the reason(s) behind it, etc. In idiomatic expressions, adjectives are sometimes used.
（例）こんなことになってしまい、まったくお恥ずかしい次第です。
I feel thoroughly embarrassed that it should have come to this.
4. こととしだいによって

content: ことと次第によって、計画を大幅に変更しなければならなくなるかもれない。

content.content: It all depends, but we may have to make drastic changes to the plan.

content: ことと次第によっては、事件の当事者だけでなく責任者も罰することになる。

content.content: Depending on what happens, not only the person involved in the incident but also the one in charge may be penalized.
Used to preface a statement when the outcome of a course of events is uncertain or when something of importance is to be decided. An idiomatic expression.
【して】→
【しないで】→
【ないで】
【しなくて】→
【なくて】
【しはする】［R-はする］

content: 坂田さんはアルバイトに遅れはするが、ぜったいに休まない。

content.content: Though Sakata-san is sometimes late for her part-time job, she never misses work.

content: かれは人前に行きはするが、だれともしゃべらない。

content.content: Though he does go out in public, he never talks to anyone.

content: 酔ってその男をなぐりはしたが、殺してはいない。

content.content: I was drunk and I did hit him, but I didn’t kill him.

content: だれも責めはしない。悪いのは私なのだから。

content.content: I don’t blame anyone else. I’m the one who is at fault.

content: そんなことをしてもだれも喜びはしない。かえって迷惑に思うだけだ。

content.content: Even if you do something like that, no one will be happy. If anything, they'll only think it’s a bother.

Attaches to a verb stem and is used to highlight the verb’s meaning. Often used in the pattern Xしはするが、Y (...does/will do X, but Y), where the action X is first emphasized and then a contrasting aspect is presented with Y. Also used to contrast two actions with は, as in

content: . A formal expression.

content.content: 【しまつだ】［V-るしまつだ］

content: 彼女は夫の欠点を延々と並べ上げ、あげくの果てには離婚すると言って泣き出す始末だった。

content.content: She went on and on listing her husband’s shortcomings, and in the end she finally said she was going to divorce him and burst into tears.

content: 息子は大学の勉強は何の役にも立たないと言ってアルバイトに精を出し、この頃は中退して働きたいなどと言い出す始末だ。

content.content: Saying that college studies serve no purpose whatsoever, my son has put all his energy into his part-time job, and now he says he wants to drop out and get a job.

content: 一度相談にのってあげただけなのに、彼はあなただけが頼りだと言って、真夜中にでも電話をかけてくる始末だった。

content.content: I only listened to his troubles once, but now he ends up calling me in the middle of the night and telling me I’m the only one he can depend on.

Attached to the dictionary form of a verb, しまつだ expresses that a troublesome situation or annoyance has arisen due to another person’s actions. The first half of the sentence describes all the things that have led up to the situation, and the second half states the situation that has arisen as a result.
The expression この始末だ in the example below is idiomatic and implies criticism when indicating something that has occurred.
（例）山田はどうもこの頃学校に来ないと思ったらこの始末だ。バイクで人身事故を起こすような学生には、もう退学してもらうしかない。
I’ve been wondering why Yamada hasn’t come to school lately, and now this! A student like that who causes a fatal accident with his motorcycle—the only thing we can do is have him quit school.
【しゅんかん】［Nのしゅんかん］［V-たしゅんかん］

content: 立ち上がった瞬間に、家がぐらっと大きく揺れた。

content.content: The moment I stood up, the house shook violently from side to side.

content: 王子様が、眠っているお姫様にキスしたその瞬間、魔法がとけた。

content.content: The moment the prince kissed the sleeping princess, the spell was broken.

content: 試験に落ちたことがわかった瞬間、目の前が真っ暗になって血の気が引いていくのが自分でもわかった。

content.content: The moment I realized I had failed the exam, everything went dark in front of my eyes and I was aware of the color draining from my face.

content: これが誕生の瞬間だ。

content.content: This is the moment of birth.
Means “right at that time.” Seldom attaches to nouns. In spoken language, V-たとたん is used.
【しょうがない】
1. しょうがない

content: 誰もやらないならしょうがない、私一人でもやる。

content.content: If no one else will do it, then there’s no other choice.... I’ll do it myself.

content: 散歩の途中で雨が降ってきた。しょうがないから、スーパーに入って雨の止むのを待った。

content.content: It started to rain in the middle of my walk. There was nothing else I could do, so I went into a supermarket and waited for it to stop.

content: ワインがない時はしょうがないからビールにします。

content.content: When there’s no wine, I have no other option but to drink beer.

content: A:おかしもらったけど、かびがはえてて、食べられないの。

content.content: Someone gave me some snacks, but they’re moldy and inedible.
B:しょうがないな、捨ててしまおう。
Well, it can’t be helped.... let’s just throw them away.

content: しょうがない子ね、一人でトイレにも行けないの。

content.content: What a hopeless child—can’t you even go the bathroom by yourself?
Means “it cannot be helped” or “there is no other way.” Can be used to show consternation, as in

content: and
. しょうがない is the abbreviated form of しようがない (lit. there is no method/means). Informal spoken language.

content.content: 2. ...てしょうがない→
【てしょうがない】
【じつは】
1. じつは

content: 今まで黙っていたけれど、実は先月、会社を首になったんだ。

content.content: I haven’t said anything till now, but the truth is, last month I was fired from my company.

content: A:実は急に結婚することになりまして。

content.content: Actually, I know this is sudden, but I am going to get married.
B:あら、それはおめでとう。
Oh my, congratulations on that!
A:それで申し訳ないんですが今月で退職させていただきたいんですが。
So, I’m very sorry, but I would like to be allowed to resign from my job as of the end of this month.

content: 今まで知らなかったのだが、それをやったのは実は彼女だった。

content.content: I never knew until now, but she’s actually the one who did it.

content: 不況で都会からふるさとに帰って仕事をさがす人が増えているという。それを聞いて安心するという人が実は多いのではないだろうか。

content.content: They say that with this recession, there are more and more people leaving the cities and returning to their hometowns to look for work. I imagine that there are actually quite a few people who feel relieved to hear that.

content: A:井田さん、急にやせたね。どこか悪いところでもあるのかな。

content.content: Ida-san seems to have lost weight all of a sudden. I wonder if maybe there’s something wrong.
B:実は私も前からそう思っていたのよ。
To be honest, I’ve been thinking the same thing.
Means “in reality, the truth is....” Used when clarifying the facts or the truth. Example

content: is a way of broaching a topic that is unexpected to the listener. Also used to preface a request, as in
. Example
shows how じつは is used when the speaker him/herself is surprised at a newly-discovered fact. In
, it means “on the surface...is not obvious, but the fact of the matter is....” Example
shows how it is used to reveal the truth in response to something the other person has said.

content.content: 2. じつをいうと

content: A:なんだか、元気がないな。

content.content: You look a bit out of sorts.
B:うん、実を言うと金がないんだ。もう少ししたら入るはずなんだけど。
Well, to tell you the truth, I’m short on money right now. I should be getting some in a little while, though.

content: A:さっきの人、知っている人だったの。

content.content: Was that person we saw just now someone you know?
B:実を言うと別れた女房なんだ。こんなところで会うとは思わなかったよ。
To tell you the truth, she’s my former wife. I really never thought I'd meet her at this kind of place.

content: A:このごろ、お子さんの成績がひどく落ちているんですが、お母さんに、なにか心あたりはありませんか。

content.content: Recently, your child's grades have been dropping badly—as his mother, are you perhaps aware of anything that might have caused this?
B:先生、実を言いますと、この頃ほとんど家にいないんです。家に帰って来るのも何時なのか親もよく知らないような始末でして。
