To tell the truth, Sensei, he hardly spends any time at home at all these days. Things are so bad that even his father and I don’t really know what time he gets home.

Means “frankly speaking, to be candid with you.” Used in almost the same way as じつは, but is rarely used to preface a request. Often used when confiding the truth in detail after being asked the reason for something, as in
3. じつのところ

content: A:山口さん、また仕事中に寝てましたよ。

content.content: Yamaguchi-san was sleeping on the job again.
B:実のところ、僕も彼には困っているんだ、無断欠勤も多いし。
To tell you the truth, I’m having trouble with him myself. He’s often absent from work without notice.

content: A:石田選手、よくがんばりましたね。

content.content: Ishida-senshu (the athlete) really hung in there.
B:実のところかれの活躍には本当におどろいているんだ。あまり期待していなかったから、よけいそう思うのかもしれないけどね。
Actually, I’m very surprised at his performance. I wasn’t expecting too much from him, so maybe that’s why I feel all the more so.

content: A:刑事さん、犯人は正子でしょうね。

content.content: Keiji-san (Inspector), the culprit is probably Masako, don’t you think?
B:いや、実のところわからないことが多すぎるんだ。
No, to be honest with you, there are still too many things we don’t know.

Used when the speaker confides something in response to what the other person has said. Often followed by an expression of the speaker’s attitude towards what s/he has heard, an explanation of the situation, etc. Not used when confiding a simple fact, or to preface a request.
（×）実のところ結婚することになりました。
To be honest, I’m going to get married.
（○）実は結婚することになりました。
Actually, I’m going to get married.
【じゃあ】This is a casual way of sayingでは (Usage 2).
1. じゃ（あ）〈inference〉

content: A:風邪をひいて熱があるんですよ。

content.content: I’ve caught a cold and have a fever.
B:じゃあ、試合に出るのは無理ですね。
Well then, you can’t play in the game, can you?

content: A:急な用事が入っちゃって。

content.content: I have an unexpected piece of business to attend to.
B:じゃあ、パーティーに来られないの？
So, you can’t come to the party?
【では2】
2. じゃ（あ）〈expression of attitude〉

content: A:先生、終わりました。

content.content: Sensei (Professor), I’ve finished.
B:じゃあ、帰ってもいい。
Well then, you can go home.

content: A:気分が悪いんです。

content.content: I feel sick.
B:じゃあ、休みなさい。
Well then, take a rest.
【では2】
3. じゃ（あ）〈shift〉

content: じゃ、次の議題に入りましょう。

content.content: All right, let’s move on to the next item of business.

content: じゃ、始めましょう。

content.content: OK, let’s get started.

content: じゃ、今日の授業はこれで終わりにします。

content.content: All right, then, class is over for today.

content: じゃあ、またね。

content.content: OK then, see you around!
【じゃない】［N／Na　じゃない］

content: A:雨？

content.content: Rain?
B:いや、雨じゃない。
No, not rain.

content: A:雨じゃない？

content.content: Isn’t it raining?
B:ええ、雨よ。
Yes, it’s raining.

content: あら、雨じゃない。せんたく物いれなくちゃ。

content.content: Wow, look at the rain! Gotta bring in the laundry!
Casual way of saying ではない. Example

content: is a negative sentence, and the な is pronounced with a higher tone. Example
is a negative question with rising intonation. Example
is not negation but assertion, and the whole expression じゃない has falling intonation. Spoken language. Used by both men and women.

content.content: 【ではない】

【じゃないか1】［N／Na／A／V　じゃないか］This is the casual form of ではないか (Usage 1). It is used at the end of sentences in spoken language, mainly by men. Women tend to use じゃないの or じゃない more often. じゃん is an even more casual expression used by both men and women. The polite forms are じゃないですか and じゃありませんか.
【ではないか1】
1. ...じゃないか〈surprise, discovery〉

content: すごいじゃないか。大発見だね。

content.content: Isn’t that something! Quite a discovery, huh?

content: なんだ、山田君じゃないか。どうしたんだ。こんな所で。

content.content: Well now, if it isn’t Yamada-kun. What are you doing—in a place like this?
【ではないか1】
2. ...じゃないか〈criticism〉

content: どうしたんだ。遅かったじゃないか。

content.content: What happened? You’re so late.

content: 約束は守ってくれなきゃ困るじゃないか。

content.content: If you don’t keep your promise, it really puts me in a bind.
【ではないか1】
3. ...じゃないか〈confirmation〉

content: ほら、覚えていないかな。同じクラスに加藤って子がいたじゃないか。

content.content: Hey, don’t you remember? Wasn’t there a girl named Kato in the same class?

content: A:郵便局どこ？

content.content: Where’s the post office?
B:あそこに映画館があるじゃないか。あのとなりだよ。
There’s a movie theater over there, right? It’s next door to that.
【ではないか1】
4. V-ようじゃないか

content: 頑張って勝ち抜こうじゃないか。

content.content: How about giving it our best and fighting it out to the end?

content: 十分注意してやろうじゃないか。

content.content: How about doing it very carefully?
This is the casual form of V-ようではないか.
【ではないか1】4
【じゃないか2】［N／Na 　 （なん）じゃないか］［A／V　んじゃないか］

content: 隣、ひょっとして留守じゃないか。

content.content: You know our neighbor—is it possible that she might be away?

content: A:隣の家の様子、ちょっと変じゃないか。

content.content: Isn’t there something a little strange about the house next door?
B:そうね。ちょっと見て来る。
You might be right. I’ll go take a look.

content: A:この部屋、少しさむいんじゃないか。

content.content: Isn’t this room a little chilly?
B:そうね。暖房をいれましょう。
Yeah. Let’s turn on the heater.

content: ひょっとして、昼からは雨になるんじゃないか。

content.content: So is it possible that it’s going to rain after noon?
This is the casual form of ではないか (Usage 2). じゃないか has the flavor of men’s speech, while women usually use じゃないの or じゃない.

When (ん)じゃないか is pronounced with rising intonation, it is being used by the speaker to confirm an assumption with the listener and conveys the meaning “don’t you think so, too?” When the speaker uses it to talk to him/herself, it expresses an assumption that s/he is not entirely sure of. In this case, it is possible to use (ん)じゃないかな or (ん)じゃないかしら instead.
【ではないか1】4
【じゃないが】［Nじゃないが］

content: 非難するわけじゃないけど、どうしてあなたの部屋はこんなに散らかっているの。

content.content: I don’t mean to criticize, but why is your room so messy?

content: 悪口を言いたいわけじゃないけど、あの人、このごろ付き合いがわるいんだよ。

content.content: I don’t mean to speak ill of him, but that man really isn’t very sociable these days.

content: 疑うわけじゃありませんが、きのう1日どこにいたのか話してください。

content.content: It’s not that I doubt you, but please tell me where you were all day yesterday.

content: A:自慢じゃないが、息子が今年東大に入ってね。

content.content: I don’t want to brag, but my son got into Tokyo University this year.
B:あっ、それはおめでとうございます。
Oh, congratulations on that!
Means “don’t intend to..., but....” Used as an introductory remark to soften the statement or question that follows. Example

content: is an idiomatic expression.

content.content: 【じゃないだろうか】［N／Na　（なん）じゃないだろうか］［A／V　んじゃないだろうか］

content: もう帰ってしまったんじゃないだろうか。

content.content: She hasn’t already gone back home, has she?

content: あいつはやる気がないんじゃないだろうか。

content.content: It’s not that he isn’t very motivated, is it?

This is the spoken language form of ではないだろうか. The polite form is (ん)じゃないでしょうか. When the speaker uses this expression to talk to him/herself, it expresses a supposition. On the other hand, in conversation, it often means that the speaker is trying to confirm his/her supposition with the listener.
【ではないだろうか】
【じゅう】
1. Nじゅう〈space〉

content: 学校中にうわさが広まった。

content.content: The rumor spread throughout the school.

content: 国中の人がそのニュースを知っている。

content.content: People throughout the country have heard the news.

content: 家中、大掃除をした。

content.content: We cleaned the whole house, from top to bottom.

content: ふたごの転校生が教室に入ってくると、クラスじゅう、大騒ぎになった。

content.content: When he transfer students—who were twins—entered the classroom, the whole class went into an uproar.

content: サイレンの音でアパート中の住人が外にとびだした。

content.content: At the sound of the siren, all the residents of the apartment building rushed outside.

content: そこいら中で風邪がはやっている。

content.content: The flu bug is here, there, and everywhere.
Means “everything within that range” when combined with a noun that denotes a place or a bounded area. Example

content: means “here and there, all over the place.”

content.content: 2. Nじゅう〈time〉

content: 一晩中起きている。

content.content: I stay awake all through the night.

content: 一日中仕事をする。

content.content: I work all day long.

content: 家の前は年中、道路工事をしている。

content.content: The road in front of the house is under construction all year long.

content: 午後中ずっと宣伝カーの音でうるさかった。

content.content: It was noisy all afternoon from the sound of the loudspeaker vans.
Means “all throughout that period of time” when combined with a noun that denotes time or a period of time. It should be noted that 午前中 (in the morning) is pronounced ごぜんちゅう.
【じょう】［Nじょう］

content: 子供にお金を与えるのは教育上よくない。

content.content: From the point of view of education, it’s not good to give money to children.

content: サービス業という仕事上、人が休みの時は休むわけにはいかない。

content.content: A job in the service sector means that you can’t have days off when other people do.

content: 安全上、作業中はヘルメットを必ずかぶること。

content.content: For safety reasons, you are always required to wear a helmet when working.

content: 経験上、練習を三日休むと体がついていかなくなる。

content.content: From my experience, if you miss three days of training, your body can’t keep up.

content: 立場上、その質問にはお答えできません。

content.content: My position does not allow me to answer that question.

content: 図書整理の都合上、当分の間閉館します。

content.content: The library will be closed temporarily for cataloguing.
Means “from that point of view” or “regarding that point.”

content: can be replaced by 都合により (because of). A formal expression.

content.content: 【すえに】［Nのすえに］［V-たすえに］

content: 今月のすえに、首相が訪中する。

content.content: The prime minister will visit China at the end of this month.

content: 長時間の協議のすえに、やっと結論が出た。

content.content: After long hours of discussion, a conclusion was finally reached.

content: かれは三年の闘病生活の末に亡くなった。

content.content: He passed away after three years of struggle with the disease.

content: よく考えた末に決めたことです。

content.content: It is a decision that was made after careful thought.

content: 大型トラックは1キロ暴走した末に、ようやく止まった。

content.content: After driving out of control for a kilometer, the big truck finally came to a stop.
Means “at the end of a period of time.” In

content: it simply indicates the end of the time period, but it is often used with the meaning of “in the end, following a progression of events,” as shown in
and the rest of the examples. Tends to be used in written language.

content.content: 【すぎない】［N／Na／A／V　にすぎない］

content: その件は責任者にきいてください。私は事務員にすぎませんので。

content.content: Please ask the person in charge about that matter. I’m only an office worker.

content: 彼は政治家ではなく、たんなる官僚に過ぎない。

content.content: He’s not a politician, he’s merely a government official.

content: それが本当にあるかどうかは知りません。例として言っているに過ぎないんです。

content.content: I don’t know if that really exists or not. I’m just saying it as an example.

content: そんなに怒られるとは思ってもみなかった。からかったにすぎないのに。

content.content: I really didn’t think that I’d get told off like that. I was just kidding.
Means “be nothing but....” Conveys the evaluation of “not very important.”

content: means “I am not in a position of responsibility; I am just an office worker,” and
means “I am only saying this as an example.”

content.content: 【すぎる】［N／Na　すぎる］［A-すぎる］［R-すぎる］

content: この役は思春期の役だから 10 歳では子供すぎて話にならない。

content.content: This is a role for an adolescent, so someone only ten years old is too much of a child to even consider for it.

content: 下宿のおばさんは親切すぎてときどき迷惑なこともあります。

content.content: The landlady of my boardinghouse is too kind, to the degree that it’s sometimes even annoying.

content: 彼はまじめすぎて、面白味に欠ける。

content.content: He is too serious and lacking in appeal.

content: このあたりの家は高すぎて、とても買えません。

content.content: The houses in this neighborhood are too expensive—there’s no way I can buy one.

content: 銭湯の湯は私にはあつすぎます。

content.content: The hot water in the public bath is too hot for me.

content: 子供の目が悪くなったのはテレビを見すぎたせいだと思います。

content.content: I think the reason the children’s eyesight has become worse is because of watching too much TV.

content: ゆうべ飲み過ぎて頭が痛い。

content.content: Last night I drank too much, so I have a headache.
Indicates a state of excess or immoderation.
2. ...すぎ［R-すぎだ］［R-すぎのN］

content: 太郎、遊びすぎですよ。もうちょっと勉強しなさい。

content.content: Taro, you play too much. You should study a little more.

content: 働きすぎのお父さん、もっと子供と遊ぶ時間を作ってください。

content.content: Overworked fathers, please make more time to play with your children.

content: 飲み過ぎにはこの薬がいいそうだ。

content.content: This medicine is supposed to be good for when you’ve had too much to drink.

content: テレビの見すぎで成績が下がってしまった。

content.content: My school grades dropped because I watched too much TV.

content: 肥料は適度に与えてください。やりすぎはかえってよくありません。

content.content: Give it a moderate amount of fertilizer. Overdoing it will have a reverse effect.
Indicates a state of excess. Used as a noun.
3. ...ても...すぎることはない

content: 冬山登山は注意しても、し過ぎることはない。

content.content: When mountain-climbing in winter, one cannot be overly careful.

content: 手紙の返事はどんなに早くても、早すぎることはない。

content.content: It is never too soon to reply to a letter.

content: 親にはどんなに感謝してもしすぎることはないと思っています。

content.content: I think that no matter how much I thank my parents, it will never be too much.
Means “even if you do something, it can’t be said to be sufficient.”

content: means “the more careful you are, the better” and
means “the sooner the better.”

content.content: 【すくなくとも】

content: そこはちょっと遠いですよ。歩けば、すくなくとも 20 分はかかります。

content.content: That place is a little far away. On foot, it’ll take at least twenty minutes.

content: この町で部屋を借りれば、すくなくとも5万円はかかるでしょう。

content.content: If you rent a room (apartment) in this town, it’ll probably cost at least 50,000 yen.

content: すごい人出だった。少なくとも三千人はいただろう。

content.content: There was a huge turnout. At least 3,000 people were there, I guess.

content: せっかく外食するんだから、そんなものじゃなくて、少なくとも、自分では作れないなと思えるぐらいの料理を食べようよ。

content.content: Since we’re dining out, let’s not have something like that—let’s at least eat something that we don’t think we can make ourselves.
Indicates that the amount or degree of something, even at its lowest level, is “about this much.” Implies that there is quite a large amount. Often takes the form すくなくとも...は, as in

content: , and
, or すくなくとも...ぐらい(は), as in
. Also, when すくなくとも is used in combination with an expression of intention or desire, as in
, it can be replaced by せめて (at least). In spoken language, the form すくなくても is sometimes used.

content.content: 【すぐ】

content: すぐ来てください。

content.content: Please come right away.

content: 会ってすぐに結婚を申し込んだ。

content.content: I met her and proposed to her at once.

content: 空港に着いてすぐホテルに電話した。

content.content: As soon as I reached the airport, I phoned the hotel.

content: 郵便局はすぐそこです。

content.content: The post office is right over there.

content: すぐ近くまで来ている。

content.content: I am almost there.
Indicates that the time or distance is very short. In the case of time, に can be added.
【すぐにでも】

content: お急ぎならすぐにでもお届けいたします。

content.content: If you’re in a hurry, I can deliver it right away.

content: お金があればすぐにでも国に帰りたい。

content.content: If I had the money, I’d like to go back to my home country right now.

content: そんなにやめたいなら、今すぐにでも退職金を払います。

content.content: If you want to quit that much, we can pay you your retirement benefits immediately.

content: 私がてんぷらのおいしい店をみつけたと言うと、かれはすぐにでも食べに行きたそうな感じだった。

content.content: When I said that I’d found a good tempura restaurant, it seemed like he wanted to go and eat some right then.
Means “at once, immediately” or “on the spot.” Used with expressions of desire, such as 帰りたい ((I) want to go home). Also used in the form すぐに...しそうだ, as in
【すこしも...ない】

content: 強くこすっているのに、すこしもきれいにならない。

content.content: Even though I’m scrubbing hard, it doesn’t get any cleaner at all.

content: 貯金がすこしもふえない。

content.content: Our savings don’t increase in the least.
Used to intensify a negative expression.
【すなわち】

content: 彼は、1945 年、すなわち、第二次世界大戦の終わった年に生まれた。

content.content: He was born in 1945, that is, the year that World War II ended.

content: この絵は、父の母親の父、すなわち私の曾祖父が描いたものである。

content.content: This picture was drawn by the father of my father’s mother, that is, my great-grandfather.

content: 生まれによる差別、すなわち、だれの子供であるかということによる社会的差別は、どこの社会にも存在する。

content.content: Discrimination based on birth, in other words, social discrimination according to who your parents are, exists in any society.

content: 敬語とは人間と人間の関係で使い分けることばである。すなわち、話し手と聞き手、および第三者との相互関係によっていろいろに言い分ける、その言葉の使い分けである。

content.content: Honorific language involves the use of different language for different human relationships. That is, people choose the appropriate kind of language according to the interrelations among the speaker, the listener, and third parties; it’s the adjustment of language to suit the relationships at hand.

Used after a word, phrase, or sentence to signal that a paraphrase of its meaning and content will follow. The paraphrase expresses the preceding word or phrase more plainly, or conveys concrete examples, additional explanation, etc. Used in formal, written language such as academic papers, lectures, and talks. In spoken language, つまり is used more often.
【すまない】→
【ずにはすまない】
【すむ】
1. ...すむ［Nですむ］［V-てすむ］

content: もっと費用がかかると思ったが2万円ですんだ。

content.content: I thought it would cost more, but it only took 20,000 yen.

content: 用事は電話ですんだ。

content.content: I managed to take care of it over the phone.

content: 金ですむなら、いくらでも出します。

content.content: If it’s only a matter of money, I’ll pay as much as necessary.

content: ガラスを割ってしまったが、あやまっただけで済んだ。

content.content: I broke the glass, but managed to get away with only an apology.

content: あやまってすむこととすまないことがある。

content.content: There are things you can settle with an apology and things you can’t.
The original meaning of すむ is “end” or “finish,” but it is used to mean “that’s all I needed to do” or “fortunately, it wasn’t necessary to do anything more complicated.”
2. V-ないで／V-ずに　すむ

content: バスがすぐに来たので待たないですんだ。

content.content: The bus came right away, so I didn’t have to wait.

content: バスがすぐに来たので待たずにすんだ。

content.content: The bus came right away, so I didn’t have to wait.

content: 電話で話がついたので行かずにすんだ。

content.content: I managed to take care of it over the phone, so I didn’t have to go.

content: 古い自転車をもらったので、買わないで済んだ。

content.content: I was given an old bicycle, so I didn’t have to buy one.
Means “I no longer need to do what I had planned to do” or “I can avoid something I had expected.” Expresses that an undesirable situation can be avoided.
3. ...すむことではない［Nですむことではない］［V-てすむことではない］

content: 大事な書類をなくしてしまうなんて、謝ってすむことではない。

content.content: Losing an important document isn’t something you can get away with just by apologizing.

content: 少数意見だと片付けてすむことではない。

content.content: You can’t dismiss it as being a minority opinion.

content: この問題は補償金で済むことではない。心からの謝罪が必要だ。

content.content: This is not an issue that can be resolved by financial compensation. A wholehearted apology is necessary.
Means “you can’t deal with an issue by doing such-and-such; simply doing so would not be sufficient.” In

content: , it is used to mean “an apology won’t make up for it; it can’t be undone,” and in
it means “you can’t ignore it just because it’s a minority opinion.”

content.content: 【すら】Used with a noun or a noun + particle. When attached to a subject noun, it often changes to ですら. A formal expression with the feel of written language.
1. N（+助詞）すら

content: そんなことは子供ですら知っている。

content.content: Even children know such a thing.

content: むかし世話になった人の名前すら忘れてしまった。

content.content: I can’t even remember the names of the people who helped me a long time ago.

content: この寒さで、あの元気な加藤さんですら風邪を引いている。

content.content: It’s so cold that even Kato-san, who’s usually very healthy, has a cold.

content: 大企業はもちろんのこと、この辺の町工場ですら週休2日だという。

content.content: Even small-town factories in this area have two days off a week, not to mention large corporations.

content: こういった確執はどんなにうまくいっている親子の間にすら存在する。

content.content: This kind of discord can arise even between parents and children who are on good terms.
Means the same as さえ (even). Used by giving an example of something that is true even in the case of X, implying that it obviously holds true in other cases as well. Example

content: means “of course everyone knows that, even children.”

content.content: 2. N（+助詞）すら...ない

content: あまりに重すぎて、持ち上げることすらできない。

content.content: This is so heavy that I can’t even lift it.

content: そのことは親にすら言っていない。

content.content: I haven’t even told my parents about it.

content: 仕事が忙しくて日曜日すら休めない。

content.content: I’m so busy at work that I can’t rest even on Sundays.

content: 40度の熱が出ている時ですら病院に行かなかった。

content.content: I didn’t go to the hospital even when I had a forty-degree fever.

content: 入社してもう20年近くたったが、まだ課長ですらない。

content.content: It’s been twenty years since I started working at this company, but I’m not even a section chief yet.
Means “not...even.” Used by giving an extreme example to emphasize that one can’t do something. Example

content: means “of course I can’t take time off work on other days of the week, and even on Sundays when everyone else is off, I can’t have a day off.”

content.content: 【する】
1. 数量詞+する

content: バンコクまで往復でいくらぐらいしますか。

content.content: How much does a round-trip flight to Bangkok cost?

content: その旅館は一泊5万円もする。

content.content: That ryokan (Japanese inn) costs a whopping 50,000 yen a night.

content: 30分ほどして戻りますのでお待ちください。

content.content: I’ll be back in about thirty minutes, so please wait.

content: この球根は植えて半年したら芽がでます。

content.content: This bulb will sprout six months after planting it.

content: 少ししてから出かけましょう。

content.content: Let’s go out in a little while.

content: こんな建て方では10年しないうちに壊れる。

content.content: It’s built so badly that it’ll collapse within ten years.
Used with regard to the passage of time or to cost. Can be replaced by たつ in the case of time and かかる in the case of cost.
2. 副詞+する

content: 赤ちゃんの肌はすべすべしている。

content.content: Babies have smooth skin.

content: ほこりで机の上がざらざらしている。

content.content: The desk top is gritty with dust.

content: この料理は味がさっぱりしている。

content.content: The taste of this dish is light and simple.

content: 息子は体つきががっしりしている。

content.content: My son has a sturdy build.

content: 休日はみんなのんびりとしている。

content.content: We all relax on our days off.

content: なかなかしっかりしたよい青年だ。

content.content: He’s a good, dependable young man.
When adverbs are combined with ...している or ...したN, they convey the meaning that someone or something has a certain characteristic or displays a certain condition.
3. ...する［N／Na　にする］［A-くする］［V-ようにする］

content: 子供を医者にしたがる親が多い。

content.content: Many parents want their children to become doctors.

content: 部屋をきれいにしなさい。

content.content: Clean your room.

content: 冷たくするともっとおいしいですよ。

content.content: It tastes better if you chill it.

content: この食品はいそがしい人のためにすぐに食べられるようにしてあります。

content.content: This food product is made so that busy people can eat it quickly.

Means “doing something to an object to make it change.” In contrast to なる, which expresses a natural change of the object itself, する expresses an intentional change involving someone who exerts an effect on the object.
【ように3】
4. Nがする

content: 台所からいいにおいがしてきた。

content.content: A pleasant aroma came from the kitchen.

content: このサラダは変な味がする。

content.content: This salad tastes strange.

content: 古いピアノはひどい音がして、使い物にならない。

content.content: The old piano sounds so terrible that it’s useless.

content: 外に出ると冷たい風が吹いていて、寒気がした。

content.content: When I went out, a cold wind was blowing and I felt chilly.

content: その動物は小さくて柔らかく、まるでぬいぐるみのような感じがした。

content.content: The animal was small and soft, and it felt just like a stuffed toy.

content: 彼とはうまくやっていけないような気がする。

content.content: I’ve got a feeling I won’t be able to get along with him.

content: 今朝から吐き気がして何も食べられない。

content.content: I’ve been feeling queasy since this morning, and I have no appetite.

content: この肉料理にはふしぎな香りがするスパイスが使ってある。

content.content: A spice with an unusual aroma is used for this meat dish.
Attaches to nouns that refer to smell, fragrance, flavor, sound, feeling, mood, chilliness, nausea, etc. Expresses a sense or perception.

content: 来週は休講とする。

content.content: There will be no class next week.

content: 一応 60 点を合格とします。

content.content: The passing mark is set at 60% for now.
【とする2】
6. ...にする［Nにする］［Vことにする］

content: A:何になさいますか。

content.content: What would you like?
B:コーヒーにします。
I’ll have coffee.

content: 今度のキャプテンは西田さんにしよう。

content.content: Let’s make Nishida-san the next captain.

content: かぜがよくならないので旅行は止めることにします。

content.content: My cold isn’t getting any better, so I’m going to cancel the trip.

content: 事故がこわいので飛行機には乗らないことにしています。

content.content: I don’t fly because I’m scared of an accident.
Means “to decide.” Can also be used with a noun + particle, as follows.
（例）会議は5時からにします。
We’ll have the meeting start at five o’clock.
7. ...ものとする→
【ものとする】
8. Nをするa. N（を）する

content: 午後は買い物をするつもりだ。

content.content: I intend to go shopping this afternoon.

content: 日曜日には妻と散歩をしたりテニスをしたりする。

content.content: On Sundays my wife and I usually take a walk or play tennis.

content: 昔はよくダンスをしたものだ。

content.content: I used to dance a lot.

content: いたずらをすると叱られるよ。

content.content: You’ll be scolded if you make any mischief.

content: ころんで足にけがをした。

content.content: I fell down and injured my leg.

content: せきをしているので風邪をひいたのでしょう。

content.content: Since he’s coughing, he’s probably caught a cold.

（を）する is attached to nouns that express actions or effects, to create verbs. Although there are many cases in which it is attached to words of Japanese origin, it is more often used to make verbs out of words of Chinese origin and loan words.
b. Nをする〈outward appearance〉

content: きれいな色をしたネクタイをもらった。

content.content: I got a beautifully colored necktie.

content: その建物は三角形のおもしろい形をしている。

content.content: That building has an interesting triangular shape.

content: 見舞いに行ったら、かれはとても苦しそうな様子をしていたのでつらかった。

content.content: When I went to visit him he seemed to be in pain, so it was hard for me.

content: それは人間の姿をした神々の物語だ。

content.content: This is a story of gods who took on human form.

content: みすぼらしい格好をした男が訪ねてきた。

content.content: A scruffy-looking man came to visit.

content: この仏像はとてもやさしそうな顔をしている。

content.content: This Buddha has a very kind-looking face.
Takes the form Nをしている or NをしたN. Used to describe things that can be grasped visually, such as color, shape, state, form, appearance, facial expression, etc.
c. Nをする〈occupation〉

content: 彼は教師をしている。

content.content: He’s a teacher.

content: ベビー・シッターをしてくれる人を探しています。

content.content: I’m looking for someone who can work as a baby-sitter for me.

content: 社長をしているおじの紹介で就職した。

content.content: I got the job through my uncle, who is the company president.

content: 母は前は主婦だったが今は薬剤師をしている。

content.content: My mother used to be a housewife, but now she’s working as a pharmacist.
Used in the form “name of job + をしている” and means “have that occupation.”
d. Nをする〈accessories〉

content: あの赤いネクタイをした人が森さんです。

content.content: The one wearing the red necktie is Mori-san.

content: あの人はいつもイヤリングをしている。

content.content: She’s always wearing earrings.

content: 手袋をしたままで失礼します。

content.content: Excuse me for not taking off my gloves.

content: あっ、今日は時計をしてくるのを忘れた。

content.content: Oh, I forgot to wear my watch today.

content: このごろ風邪をひいてもマスクをする人はいませんね。

content.content: These days, people don’t wear face masks even if they have a cold.
Attaches to nouns that refer to things like neckties, watches, and rings, to express that they are being worn. しているis used to indicate a state, as in

content: above.

content.content: 9. NをNにする

content: 本をまくらにして昼寝した。

content.content: I took a nap, using a book as a pillow.

content: スカーフをテーブルクロスにして使っています。

content.content: I’m using a scarf as a tablecloth.

content: 客間を子どもの勉強部屋にした。

content.content: I made the guest room into a children’s study.
Means to use something for a different purpose.
0. おR-する

content: ここでお待ちします。

content.content: I’ll wait for you here.

content: お荷物お持ちしましょうか。

content.content: Would you like me to carry your luggage?
1. V-ようにする

content: 必ず連絡をとるようにする。

content.content: I’ll be sure to contact (them).

content: 朝寝坊しないようにしよう。

content.content: Let’s be sure not to oversleep.
【ように3】5

【ず】Comes from the auxiliary verb ず, which is used in literary language. Expresses negation. Can be used only in written language and idiomatic expressions. In spoken language, なくて and ないで are used. Created by changing the ない in V-ない to ず. する becomes せず.
1. V-ず

content: 途中であきらめず、最後までがんばってください。

content.content: Don’t give up in the middle—please keep going until the end.

content: 1時間待っても雨は止まず、ぬれて帰った。

content.content: The rain wouldn’t stop even after I waited for an hour, so I went home drenched.

content: 出発前日まで予約が取れず、心配させられた。

content.content: I couldn’t get a reservation until the day before my departure, so I was really worried.

content: だれにきいても住所がわからず、困った。

content.content: No matter who I asked, no one knew the address, so I was in a real fix.
Means the same as V-ないで or V-なくて.

content: is an example of simply putting two clauses side by side to mean “don’t give up.” In many cases, as in
and

, the cause-and-effect relation between the first and second clauses is clear, and V-ず is used as an expression to indicate a reason. Although V-ず is used in spoken language, it is somewhat formal and has the tone of written language.

content.content: 2. ...ず、...ず［A-からず、A-からず］［V-ず、V-ず］

content: 飲まず食わずで三日間も山中を歩きつづけた。

content.content: I continued to walk all over the mountains without eating or drinking for three whole days.

content: その時、彼はあわてず騒がず一言「失礼しました」と言って部屋を出ていった。

content.content: At the time, he didn’t get flustered or make a scene, he just left the room with a single remark: “Excuse me.”

content: 展覧会に出品されている作品はいずれも負けず劣らずすばらしい。

content.content: All the works presented at the exhibition are equally wonderful.

content: 独立した子供達とは、つかず離れずのいい関係だ。

content.content: I have a good relationship with my children, who are now on their own—not too close, but not too far.

content: 日本の5月は暑からず、寒からずちょうどいい気候です。

content.content: The climate in Japan in May is just right—not too hot but not too cold.

content: 客は多からず、少なからずほどほどだ。

content.content: The number of clients is just right—not too many and not too few.
Means “neither X nor Y.” In some cases words with similar meaning are listed, as in

content: , and
, and in other cases words with contrasting meaning are listed, as in
, and
means that after comparing several items it is found that “all of them are equally wonderful.”
means “keeping a suitable distance,” and
means “neither hot nor cold.” Idiomatic expressions. Other examples include 鳴かず飛ばず (fall into obscurity), etc.

content.content: 【ずくめ】［Nずくめ］

content: 彼女はいつも黒ずくめのかっこうをしている。

content.content: She always dresses completely in black.

content: この頃なぜかいいことずくめだ。

content.content: For some reason, one good thing after another is happening these days.

content: 今日の夕食は、新鮮なお刺身やいただきもののロブスターなど、ごちそうずくめだった。

content.content: Today’s supper was all delicacies, like fresh raw fish and some lobster we’d been given.

content: 毎日毎日残業ずくめで、このままだと自分がすり減っていきそうだ。

content.content: Every single day I have to do overtime, and I feel like I’m going to wear out if things go on like this.

Attaches to a noun and expresses the notion that one is surrounded by an abundance of something. Often used in fixed expressions, such as 黒ずくめ (entirely in black), いいことずくめ (one good thing after another), and ごちそうずくめ (nothing but delicacies). Mostly idiomatic, so expressions like 赤ずくめ (entirely in red) and 本ずくめ (nothing but books) are not used.
【ずして】［V-ずして］

content: 悪天候の中を飛行機が無事着陸すると、乗客の中から期せずして拍手がわき起こった。

content.content: When the plane landed safely in the midst of bad weather, a round of applause broke out unexpectedly among the passengers.

content: 戦わずして負ける。

content.content: You could lose the war without fighting it.

content: 労せずして手に入れる。

content.content: You can get something without making any effort.
Means “without doing....” Example

content: means “I didn’t expect it, but...,”
means “without fighting,” and
means “without hard work.” An idiomatic expression with the tone of literary language.

content.content: 【ずじまいだ】［V-ずじまいだ］

content: 出張で香港へ行ったが、いそがしくて友だちには会わずじまいだった。

content.content: I went to Hong Kong on business, but I was so busy that I came home without seeing any friends.

content: せっかく買ったブーツも今年の冬は暖かくて使わずじまいだった。

content.content: Even though I’d gone out and bought a new pair of boots, the winter was so warm this year that I never used them once.

content: 夏休みのまえにたくさん本を借りたが、結局読まずじまいで、先生にしかられた。

content.content: Although I borrowed lots of books before the summer vacation, I ended up not reading any of them and got scolded by my teacher.

content: 旅行でお世話になった人たちに、お礼の手紙を出さずじまいではずかしい。

content.content: I am ashamed of myself for not sending a letter of thanks to the people who were kind to me during the trip.
Means that something has concluded without the speaker doing a certain action. Often conveys a feeling of regret.
【ずつ】［数量詞+ずつ］

content: 一人に3つずつキャンディーをあげましょう。

content.content: I’ll give each of you three pieces of candy.

content: 5人ずつでグループを作った。

content.content: We made groups of five.

content: 雪が溶けて、少しずつ春が近づいてくる。

content.content: The snow is melting, and spring is gradually approaching.

content: いくらかずつでもお金を出し合って、焼けた寺の再建に協力しよう。

content.content: Let’s each give whatever small amount of money we can and work together to rebuild the temple that got burned down.

content: 病人はわずかずつだが食べられるようになってきた。

content.content: The patient has started to be able to eat small amounts of food.
Means “the same amount to each” or “repeat approximately the same amount.” Example

content: means “three pieces each,”
means “five people in one group,” and
means “a little each time.”

content.content: 【ずとも】［V-ずとも］

content: そんな簡単なことぐらい聞かずともわかる。

content.content: I know a simple thing like that without having to ask.

content: 《昔話》これこれそこの娘。泣かずともよい。わけを話してみなさい。

content.content: 《folktale》Come, come, my girl. You don’t have to cry. Just tell me the reason.

content: あの方は体にさわらずとも病気がわかる名医だ。

content.content: She’s such a good doctor that she knows what the illness is without having to examine the person.
Means “without doing....” Followed by expressions such as わかる (know) or いい (good/fine). A literary expression.
【ずに】［V-ずに］

content: よくかまずに食べると胃を悪くしますよ。

content.content: You’ll upset your stomach if you eat without chewing well.

content: 切手を貼らずに手紙を出してしまった。

content.content: I sent the letter without putting any stamps on it!

content: きのうはさいふを持たずに家を出て、昼ご飯も食べられなかった。

content.content: I left home without my wallet yesterday, so I couldn’t even have lunch.

content: パソコンの説明をよく読まずに使っている人は多いようだ。

content.content: Apparently there are a lot of people who use a personal computer without reading the manual carefully.

content: あきらめずに最後までがんばってください。

content.content: See it through to the end, without giving up!

content: 両親を事故で亡くしたあと、彼はだれの援助も受けずに大学を出た。

content.content: After losing his parents in an accident, he finished college without receiving support from anyone.
Followed by another verb clause (V2) and means “without doing something (V1), do something else (V2).” Written language. In spoken language, it becomes ...ないで.
【ずにいる】［V-ずにいる］

content: 禁煙を始めたが、吸わずにいるとだんだんイライラしてくる。

content.content: Though I’m trying to quit smoking, when I don’t smoke I gradually start to get irritated.

content: これでもう1ヶ月酒を飲まずにいることになる。

content.content: As of now, I’ve gone one month without drinking any alcohol.

content: 三日新聞を読まずにいると世の中のことがわからなくなる。

content.content: If you don’t read the newspaper for three days, you start to lose track of what’s happening in the world.

content: わがままな彼が、なぜあんなひどい会社をやめずにいるのか不思議だ。

content.content: It’s a mystery why a self-centered person like him doesn’t quit a horrible company like that.
Expresses the state of not doing a certain action.
【ずにおく】［V-ずにおく］

content: 父に電話がかかってきたが、疲れてよく寝ているようだったので起こさずにおいた。

content.content: There was a telephone call for my father, but since he was tired and sleeping soundly, I didn’t wake him up.

content: 彼女がショックを受けるとかわいそうだから、このことは当分言わずにおきましょう。

content.content: It would be cruel to give her such a shock, so let’s not tell her about this for the time being.

content: あとでいるかもしれないと思って、もらったお金は使わずにおいた。

content.content: I thought I might need it later, so I didn’t use the money I had received.

content: あした病院で検査を受けるなら、夕飯は食べずにおいたほうがいいんじゃないですか。

content.content: If you’re going to have tests done at the hospital tomorrow, isn’t it better not to have any dinner?
Expresses that, for some reason, a certain action is deliberately not taken.
【ずにすむ】［V-ずにすむ］

content: 漢和辞典を買おうと思っていたら、友だちが古いのをくれたので買わずにすんだ。

content.content: I was thinking about buying a Japanese kanji dictionary, but a friend gave me her old one, so I didn’t have to buy one after all.

content: いい薬ができたので手術せずにすんだ。

content.content: Since there’s good medicine available now, it turned out that I didn’t have to have surgery.

content: 一生働かずにすんだらいいんだけれど、そういうわけにはいかない。

content.content: It would be great if you could live your whole life without working, but that will never happen.

content: いまちゃんとやっておけば、あとで後悔せずにすみますよ。

content.content: If you do it properly now, you won’t have any regrets later on.

content: 安全装置が作動したので大事故にならずにすんだ。

content.content: The fail-safe device was activated, so we were able to avoid a major accident.

Means “no longer have to do something that was previously planned” or “something that was anticipated can be avoided.” Expresses that an undesirable situation has been avoided. Has the tone of written language. In spoken language, ...ないですむ is used.
【ずにはいられない】［V-ずにはいられない］

content: この本を読むと、誰でも感動せずにはいられないだろう。

content.content: Anyone who reads this book will surely be moved by it, I think.

content: 彼女の気持ちを思うと、自分のしたことを悔やまずにはいられない。

content.content: When I consider her feelings, I can’t help but feel regret for what I did.

content: 彼女の美しさには誰でも魅了されずにはいられなかった。

content.content: No one could help but be captivated by her beauty.

content: 会社でのストレスを解消するために酒を飲まずにはいられない。

content.content: To relieve the stress at my workplace, I can’t do without alcohol.

content: その冗談にはどんなまじめな人も笑わずにはいられないだろう。

content.content: I don’t think anyone, no matter how serious, could help but laugh at that joke.

Means that someone does something in spite of him/herself, or in spite of his/her determination to suppress it. Tends to be used in written language. In spoken language, it takes the form ...ないではいられない.
【ずにはおかない】［V-ずにはおかない］

content: この本は読む人を感動させずにはおかない。

content.content: This book will not fail to move anyone who reads it.

content: 彼の言動は皆を怒らせずにはおかない。

content.content: His words and actions will surely anger everyone.

content: 今のような政治情勢では国民に不信感を与えずにはおかないだろう。

content.content: Given the current political climate, this will be sure to arouse mistrust in the people of Japan.

content: 両大国の争いは世界中を巻込まずにはおかない。

content.content: A conflict between the two great powers will surely entangle the whole world.

Means that a certain kind of situation or action is bound to occur, regardless of the will of the person him/herself. Often used to refer to spontaneous actions or effects, such as a change in emotion or the outbreak of conflict.
【ずにはすまない】［V-ずにはすまない］

content: あいつはこの頃怠けてばかりだ。一言言わずにはすまない。

content.content: He’s been so lazy these days. I can’t help saying something to him.

content: 親せきみんなが出席するのなら、うちも行かずにはすまないだろう。

content.content: If all the relatives are attending, we probably have no choice but to go.

content: 意図したわけではなかったとは言え、それだけ彼女を傷つけてしまったのなら、謝らずにはすまないのではないか。

content.content: Even if you didn’t mean to, if you’ve hurt her that badly, you can’t get by without making an apology, can you?
Expresses the meaning “can’t help but do,” “unacceptable if not done.” A formal expression.
【せい】［Nのせい］［Na なせい］［A／V　せい］
1. ...せいa. ...せいで

content: わがままな母親のせいで、彼女は結婚が遅れた。

content.content: She married late because her mother was a selfish woman.

content: 3人が遅刻したせいで、みんな新幹線に乗れなかった。

content.content: Because three people were late, everyone missed the shinkansen (bullet train).

content: とうとう事業に失敗した。しかし誰のせいでもない、責任はこの私にある。

content.content: My business failed in the end. But it’s no one else’s fault; the responsibility is my own.

content: 熱帯夜が続いているせいで、電気の消費量はうなぎのぼりだという。

content.content: Due to night after night of tropical temperatures, the consumption of electricity is skyrocketing.

Expresses the locus of responsibility or the cause of something bad that has happened. Often replaced by ...ので or ...ために. The latter half of the sentence describes the unfavorable circumstances produced by such a cause. Example

content: means “because her mother was selfish,” and
means “as a result of so many consecutive hot nights.”

content.content: b. ...のは...せいだ

content: こんなに海が汚れたのはリゾート開発規制をしなかった県のせいだ。

content.content: The fact that the sea has gotten so polluted is the fault of the prefecture, which put no restrictions on resort development.

content: 目が悪くなったのはテレビを見すぎたせいだ。

content.content: My eyesight got worse as a result of watching too much TV.

content: 暮しがよくならないのは政府のせいだ。

content.content: It’s the government’s fault that our standard of living has not improved.

content: 夜眠れないのは騒音のせいだ。

content.content: I can’t sleep at night because of the noise.
States the cause of an unfavorable situation. The unfavorable situation is described first, and the cause of its occurrence then follows.
c. ...せいにする

content: A:あっ、雨。君が今日は降らないっていうから、かさ持ってこなかったのに。

content.content: Oh dear, it’s raining! You said it wouldn’t rain today, so I didn’t bring my umbrella.
B:わたしのせいにしないでよ。
Don’t blame it on me.

content: 学校は責任をとりたくないので、その事故は生徒のせいにして公表しようとしない。

content.content: The school doesn’t want to be held responsible, so it is blaming the accident on the student and not making it public.

content: 彼は仕事がうまくいった時は自分一人でしたように言い、うまくいかなかったら人のせいにするというような男だ。

content.content: He’s the kind of man who takes all the credit when work goes well, but blames it on others when it doesn’t.

content: 彼女は協調性がないのを一人っ子で育ったせいにして、自分の非を認めようとしない。

content.content: She blames her inability to work well with others on being raised as an only child, and she won’t admit to her own faults.
Indicates that responsibility for a negative outcome is being forced on someone one-sidedly. Often implies that other factors are actually to blame.

content: 歳のせいか、この頃疲れやすい。

content.content: Perhaps it’s because of my age, but these days I get tired easily.

content: 家族が見舞いに来たせいか、おじいさんは食欲がでてきた。

content.content: Grandfather regained his appetite, possibly because his family came to visit.

content: 春になったせいでしょうか、いくら寝ても眠くてたまりません。

content.content: I don’t know if it’s because spring has come, but no matter how much I sleep, I still feel drowsy.

content: 年頃になったせいか、彼女は一段ときれいになった。

content.content: Whether or not it’s because she’s of marriageable age, she’s become even prettier.

content: 彼は童顔のせいか、もう30近いのに高校生のように見える。

content.content: Maybe it’s his baby face, but he looks like a high school student even though he’s getting close to thirty.

content: 気のせいか、このごろ少し新聞の字が読みにくくなったようだ。

content.content: It might just be my imagination, but recently it seems that I’m finding it a little harder to read newspaper text.
Refers to cause or reason. Means “I can’t be certain, but because of such and such a reason....” Example

content: means “maybe because I’ve gotten older.” Used regardless of whether the result is good or bad.

content.content: 【せいぜい】

content: 結婚記念日といっても、せいぜい夕食を外に食べに行くくらいで、たいしたことはしません。

content.content: All we do for our wedding anniversary is go out for dinner—we don’t do anything fancy.

content: 忙しい会社で、年末でもせいぜい三日くらいしか休めません。

content.content: It’s a busy company, so even at the end of the year I can only take about three days off.

content: 景気が今どうなのか知りません。私にわかることといえばせいぜい貯金の金利ぐらいです。

content.content: I don’t know what the economic situation is now. All I know is the interest rates for savings accounts.

content: ふるさとと言われて思い出すことといえばせいぜい秋祭りくらいですね。

content.content: All I remember when someone asks about my hometown is the autumn festival.

content: 給料が安くて、一人で暮らすのがせいぜいだ。

content.content: My salary is so low that it’s all I can do just to support myself.

content: たいしたおもてなしも出来ませんが、せいぜい楽しんでください。

content.content: I’m not much of a host, but I hope you’ll enjoy yourself as much as you can.

content: あまり期待していないけどせいぜい頑張って来い、とコーチに言われて出た試合で勝ってしまった。

content.content: My coach had told me to do my best, even though he wasn’t expecting much, and then I won the match.
Means “do what you can, within certain limits.” Often used in the pattern せいぜい...くらい. As in

content: above, the pattern ...が、せいぜいだ may also be used. In
and
, it is used idiomatically to mean “as much as possible.”

content.content: 【せずに】→
【ずに】
【せっかく】
1. せっかく...からには

content: せっかく留学するからには、できる限り多くの知識を身につけて帰りたい。

content.content: Since I’m going abroad to study, I’d like to return having gained as much knowledge as I can.

content: せっかく代表として選ばれたからには、全力を尽くさなければならない。

content.content: I must do my very best, since I was chosen to be the representative.

content: せっかく休暇をとるからには、2日や3日でなく、10日ぐらいは休みたい。

content.content: If I’m taking a vacation, I’d like to take at least ten days or so off, not just two or three.

Used in the pattern せっかくXからにはY. X is an action that involves effort, hardship, or a rare opportunity, and Y indicates the speaker’s desire to use such an effort or opportunity effectively. Expressions of intention, hope, advice, etc. are used in Y.
2. せっかく...けれども

content: せっかくここまできたけれども、雨がひどくなってきたから引き返そう。

content.content: I know we’ve come all this way, but it’s starting to rain harder, so let’s head back.

content: せっかく皆さんに骨折っていただきましたが、実はこの計画は取りやめになりました。

content.content: Although you have all worked so hard, I’m afraid this plan has been canceled.

content: せっかく作ったのですが、喜んではもらえなかったようです。

content.content: Despite all the effort I put into making this, it doesn’t seem to have been appreciated.

Used in patterns like せっかくXけれどもY and せっかくXがY. X is an action that involves effort, hardship, or a rare opportunity. Y indicates that such an action has been wasted and expresses the speaker’s feeling of sorrow or regret for the waste.
3. せっかく...のだから

content: せっかく来たのだから夕飯を食べて行きなさい。

content.content: Since you’ve come all this way, have supper before you go.

content: せっかくここまで努力したのだから、最後までやり通しましょう。

content.content: We’ve worked so hard to get this far, so let’s see it through to the end.

content: せっかくおしゃれをしたのだから、どこかいいレストランへ行きましょうよ。

content.content: I went to the trouble of getting all dressed up, so let’s go to a nice restaurant somewhere.

When せっかく is used in the pattern せっかくX（の）だからY, X is an action that involves effort, hardship, or a rare opportunity, and Y indicates the speaker’s desire to use such an effort or opportunity effectively. Expressions of intention, hope, request, invitation, advice, etc. are used in Y.
4. せっかく...のだったら

content: せっかくピアノを習うのだったら、少しくらい高くてもいい先生についた方がいい。

content.content: If I’m going to learn to play the piano, I may as well find a good teacher, even if it costs a little more.

content: せっかく京都まで行くのなら、奈良にも行ってみたらどうですか。

content.content: If you’re going all the way to Kyoto, why not go to Nara as well?

content: せっかく音楽を楽しむのだったら、もうすこし音のいいステレオを買いたい。

content.content: If I’m going to amuse myself by listening to music, I’d like to buy a stereo with better sound quality.

Used in patterns like せっかくXのだったらY or せっかくX（の）ならY. Indicates the speaker’s expectation that, if someone gets a rare opportunity or makes an effort to do something, it would be best to make the most of that opportunity or effort. Expressions that indicate intention, hope, advice, etc. are used in Y.
5. せっかく　...のに／...ても

content: せっかく招待していただいたのに、伺えなくてすみません。

content.content: I was glad to receive your kind invitation, but I’m sorry I won’t be able to visit.

content: せっかくいい天気なのに、かぜをひいてどこにも行けない。

content.content: Despite the nice weather, I can’t go anywhere because I’ve caught a cold.

content: せっかくセーターを編んであげたのに、どうも気にいらないようだ。

content.content: Even though I went to the effort of knitting a sweater for him, he doesn’t seem to like it.

content: せっかく来ていただいても何もお話しすることはありません。

content.content: I don’t have anything to say to you, even if you make the effort to come all the way here.

content: 今回のクイズには多数のおはがきをお寄せいただきました。ただせっかくお送りいただきましても、締切日をすぎておりますものは抽選できませんのでご了承ください。

content.content: Thank you for the many postcards we’ve received for this quiz. However, please understand that those sent after the deadline cannot be used in the draw.
The patterns せっかくXのにY and せっかくXてもY have the same meaning as せっかく...けれども. ...のに shows that X refers to a situation that has been realized, and ...ても shows that X refers to a hypothetical situation.
6. せっかくのN

content: せっかくの日曜日なのに、一日中、雨が降っている。

content.content: Here it is Sunday, and wouldn’t you know it, it’s raining all day.

content: せっかくのチャンスを逃してしまった。

content.content: I let a rare opportunity slip away.

content: せっかくの努力が水の泡になってしまった。

content.content: All my efforts came to nothing.

content: せっかくのごちそうなのだから、残さないで全部食べましょう。

content.content: Since it’s such a feast, let’s eat it all up and not leave a crumb.

Used with nouns that describe an action involving a fortunate opportunity or an effort. Expresses a feeling of regret for not being able to utilize the opportunity/effort, or a feeling of hope or expectation that it should be utilized.
7. せっかく+連体修飾句+N

content: せっかく書いた原稿をなくしてしまった。

content.content: I’ve lost the draft that I worked so hard to write.

content: せっかく覚えた英語も今は使う機会がない。

content.content: Despite the effort I put into learning English, I have no opportunity to use it now.

content: せっかくきれいに咲いた花をだれかが取っていった。

content.content: Someone plucked the flower that was blooming so beautifully.

content: せっかく作った料理を誰も食べてくれない。

content.content: Despite the effort I put into cooking this meal, no one’s eating it.

Indicates an action made possible by good fortune or one’s own efforts. Expresses a feeling of regret for not being able to utilize the opportunity/effort, or a feeling of hope or expectation that it should be utilized.
8. せっかくですが

content: A:もう遅いですから、泊まっていらしたらいかがですか。

content.content: It’s already late, so why don’t you stay overnight?
B:せっかくですが、あしたは朝から用事がありますので。
Thank you, but tomorrow I have things to do starting in the morning.

content: A:今晩一緒に食事しない？

content.content: Shall we have dinner together tonight?
B:せっかくだけど、今晩はちょっと都合が悪いんだ。
Thanks, but tonight’s just not convenient.
せっかくですが and せっかくだけど are used to preface the refusal of an offer or proposal made by someone else.
9. せっかくですから

content: A:食事の準備がしてありますので、うちで召し上がってくださいよ。

content.content: Dinner is ready, so by all means, please stay and eat with us.
B:せっかくですから、お言葉に甘えて、そうさせていただきます。
That’s very kind of you. I will take you up on your generous offer.

content: せっかくだから、あなたの作ったケーキご馳走になって行くわ。

content.content: Since you went to all the trouble of baking a cake, I won’t leave without trying it.
Used to preface the acceptance of an offer or proposal made by someone else.
【せつな】［V-たせつな］

content: 目を離したせつな、子供は波にのまれていった。

content.content: The moment I glanced away, the child was swept off by a wave.

content: あたり一面火の海だった。逃げてきた道をふりかえったそのせつな、建物が轟音をたててくずれおちた。

content.content: There was a sea of fire all around me. The moment I looked back at the road I’d escaped along, the building collapsed with a thunderous roar.
Means “a short time, an instant.” Its range of use is narrower than that of 瞬間, and it has a strong literary flavor. Tends to be used in written language.
【せめて】
1. せめて

content: 夏はせめて一週間ぐらい休みがほしい。

content.content: I’d like at least one week of vacation in the summer.

content: 大学に入ったのだから、せめて教員免許ぐらい取っておこうと思う。

content.content: Now that I’m in college, I think I should at least get a teaching certificate.

content: 小さくてもいい。せめて庭のある家に住みたい。

content.content: I don’t mind if it’s tiny. I want to live in a house that at least has a garden.

content: せめてあと三日あれば、もうちょっといい作品が出せるのだが。

content.content: If only I had three more days, I’d be able to produce a slightly better-quality piece.

content: あしたが無理なら、せめてあさってぐらいまでに金を返してほしい。

content.content: If you can’t do it tomorrow, I’d like you to return the money by at least the day after.
Means “it’s not enough but at least that much.” Followed by expressions of intention or wish. Often used in the pattern せめて...ぐらいは. Example

content: means “while a long vacation isn’t possible, I would like to have at least one week.”

content.content: 2. せめて...だけでも

content: せめて一晩だけでも泊めてもらえませんか。

content.content: Couldn’t you let me stay at least one night?

content: 忙しいのはわかっているけど、せめて日曜日だけでも子供と遊んでやってよ。

content.content: I know you’re busy, but play with the kids at least on Sundays, OK?

content: うちは子供に継がせるような財産はなにもないので、せめて教育だけでもと思って無理をして大学へやっているのです。

content.content: We don’t have any assets to pass on to our children, but we thought we should at least give them an education, so even though we can’t afford it, we’re sending them to college.

content: 両親を早くなくして、苦労しました。せめて母親だけでも生きていてくれたらと思います。

content.content: Life was hard after losing my parents when I was so young. I really wish at least my mother were still alive.
Means “it’s not enough but at least that much.”

content: above means “even just one night would be all right.”

content.content: 3. せめて...なりとも

content: せめて一目なりとも子供に会いたいものだ。

content.content: I wish I could see my children, even just for a brief moment.

content: せめて一晩なりとも部屋を貸してはいただけないでしょうか。

content.content: Wouldn’t it be possible for you to let me have a room for just one night?
Means the same as せめて...だけでも. A literary expression.
4. せめてものN

content: ひどい事故だったが、死者が出なかったのがせめてもの救いだ。

content.content: It was a terrible accident, but at least we can take comfort in the fact that there were no casualties.

content: パスポートをとられなかったのが、せめてものなぐさめだ。

content.content: It’s a relief that at least my passport wasn’t stolen.

content: せめてものお礼のしるしにこれを受け取ってください。

content.content: Please take this as a small token of my appreciation.

Means that, in comparison to a potentially worse situation, it’s a good thing this is all that happened. The choice of nouns that can be used in the N slot is limited to 救い(help/salvation), なぐさめ(comfort/consolation), etc. Example

content: is an idiomatic expression that means “it’s not sufficient, but it’s a sign of my appreciation.”

content.content: 【せよ】→
【にせよ】
【せられたい】［Nせられたい］［R-られたい］

content: 上記三名の者はただちに出頭せられたい。

content.content: The three persons listed above should report at once (to this office).

content: 何等かの変更がある場合は、すぐに届出られたい。

content.content: Notify us immediately in the case of any changes.

content: 心当たりの方は係まで申し出られたい。

content.content: Persons with any information regarding this matter are asked to notify the staff in charge.
Means the same as しなさい. Used to give instructions or commands in documents issued by government offices. A formal written expression.
【せる】→
【させる】
【ぜひ】

content: ぜひ一度遊びにきてください。

content.content: Please be sure to come and visit me sometime.

content: 《引越しのあいさつ状》お近くにおいでの節は是非ともお立ち寄りください。

content.content: 《on a postcard giving notice of a change of address》Please be sure to visit us when you are in the area.

content: この大学を卒業する皆さんは、ぜひ世の中の役に立つような人間になってもらいたいものだと思います。

content.content: I sincerely hope that all of you who are graduating from this university will become useful members of society.

content: 友人から、引っ越したからぜひ遊びに来るようにという電話がかかってきた。

content.content: A friend phoned to say please visit because they’ve moved to a new house.

content: 彼女は有能だから結婚してもぜひ仕事を続けてほしい。

content.content: She’s very capable, so I really hope she keeps working even after she gets married.

Means “by all means” or “definitely.” Combines with expressions of request using てください, or expressions of hope/desire using てほしい, in order to express a strong wish. Not usually used with forms expressing a negative wish.
（×）ぜひ話さないでください。
By all means, please don’t tell anyone.
（○）ぜったいに話さないで下さい。
Don’t tell anyone, no matter what.
Also, it can only be used with respect to the activities of human beings.
（×）あしたはぜひ晴れてほしい。
I hope tomorrow will by all means be sunny.
（○）あしたは何としても晴れてほしい。
I really hope it will be sunny tomorrow.
To emphasize expressions of intention, adverbs such as かならず are used.
（×）ぜひそこに参ります。
I’ll go there by all means.
（○）かならずそこに参ります。
I’ll definitely go there.
However, ぜひ can be used to reply to a request, as for example in ぜひ行かせていただきます (I would very much like to go). This is a formal expression.
【ぜんぜん...ない】

content: テレビ、消そう。ぜんぜんおもしろくない。

content.content: Let’s turn off the TV. It’s not interesting at all.

content: なんだ、これ。ぜんぜんおいしくないぞ。塩が足りなかったかな。

content.content: What is this? It doesn’t taste very good at all. Maybe it needs more salt.

content: あの人、きょうはどうしたんだろう。全然しゃべらないね。

content.content: I wonder what’s the matter with him today. He’s not talking at all, is he.

content: A:どう、勉強進んでる？

content.content: How’s your studying going?
B:だめ、だめ、全然だめ。
It’s hopeless, just hopeless.

Usually accompanied by a negative expression to emphasize a negative meaning. Used in spoken language. More recently, in colloquial speech, it is sometimes used without a negative expression, as in ぜんぜんいい.
【そう...ない】

content: 夕食はそうおいしくなかったが全部食べた。

content.content: Dinner wasn’t particularly good but I finished it anyway.

content: 日本語はそうむずかしくないと思う。

content.content: I don’t think Japanese is that hard.

content: 松子は明るい感じの子でしたが、クラスではそう目立たない生徒でした。

content.content: Ma­tsu­ko was a cheerful girl, but she wasn’t a particularly outstanding student in the class.

content: このあたりでは雪で学校が休みになるのはそうめずらしいことではない。

content.content: It isn’t so unusual for schools in this area to close because of snow.
Means “not so much, not very....”
【そういえば】

content: A:なんだか今夜はしずかね。

content.content: It’s sort of quiet tonight, isn’t it?
B:そういえばいつものカラオケがきこえないね。
Come to think about it, we can’t hear the usual karaoke, can we.

content: A:おなかがすいてない？

content.content: Aren’t you hungry?
B:そういえば朝から何もたべてないね。
Come to think of it, I haven’t eaten anything since this morning.

content: A:山田、今日のゼミ休んでたけど風邪かな。

content.content: Yamada wasn’t at today’s seminar. I wonder if he has a cold.
B:そういえば先週から見かけないな。
Now that you mention it, I haven’t seen him since last week.

content: A:坂田さんの家に何度電話しても通じないんだけど、どうしたのかしら。

content.content: I’ve been calling Sakata-san’s house again and again but can’t get an answer. I wonder what’s the matter.
B:そういえば、火曜から旅行に行くって言ってたわよ。
Now that you mention it, she did say she was leaving to go on a trip on Tuesday.

content: きょうは4月1日か。そういえば去年のいまごろはイギリスだったなあ。

content.content: So today is April 1st. Just think, this time last year I was in England.

content: もうじき春休みか。そういえばいとこが遊びに来るって言ってたなあ。

content.content: So, pretty soon it’ll be spring break. That reminds me, my cousin said she was going to come and visit us.

Used to express that the speaker has remembered or noticed something related to the preceding conversation. Most often used in response to something another person has said, but may also follow a question or statement made by the speaker him/herself, as in examples

content: and
above. Used in spoken language.

content.content: 【そうしたら】Used to connect two sentences in chronological sequence. そしたら is a more informal equivalent.
1. そうしたら〈future〉

content: 娘は大学に入ったら下宿すると言っている。そうしたら、家の中が静かになるだろう。

content.content: My daughter says she’s going to rent a room in a boarding house when she goes to college. Then our house will be quiet, I suppose.

content: ここには木を植えて、ベンチを置こう。そうしたら、いい憩いの場所ができるだろう。

content.content: Let’s plant a tree here and put a bench by it. If we do that, it’ll make a nice place to take a rest.

content: 彼の店はもうすぐ開店するらしい。そうしたら、わたしも行ってみよう。

content.content: Apparently his shop will be opening soon. When it does, I think I’ll go and see it too.

content: 毎日30分だけ練習しなさい。そうしたら見違えるほど上達するでしょう。

content.content: Practice for just thirty minutes every day. If you do that, you’ll improve so much that people will think you’re a different person.
Follows a sentence describing some kind of plan, etc. and indicates the future result of such a plan.
2. そうしたら〈past〉

content: 暑いので窓を開けた。そうしたら大きなガが飛び込んで来た。

content.content: It was hot, so I opened the window. When I did, a big moth flew in.

content: 忘れ物をとりに夕方学校へ行った。そうしたらもう正門が閉まっていた。

content.content: I went back to the school in the evening to pick up something I’d forgotten. When I got there, the front gate was already shut.

content: ふらっとデパートに入ってみた。そうしたらちょうどバーゲンセールをしていた。

content.content: I happened to pop into a department store and found it was having a sale.

content: 前にはだぶだぶだったズボンをはいてみた。そうしたらちょうどいい大きさになっていた。

content.content: I tried on some pants that used to be very baggy and found that they were now just the right size.

content: 試験のあと、参考書を開いてみた。そうしたら、全く同じ問題がのっていた。

content.content: After the exam, I opened my reference book, just to find that it had exactly the same question in it.

Used to describe a past event that took place as the result of another event or act. Often used to describe a new discovery. Unlike そして, そうしたらlinks what happened in the previous sentence with a situation or event that is unrelated to the speaker’s own actions or intentions, or with a new occurrence, or with the discovery of a fact. そうしたら cannot be followed by expressions indicating an intentional act. Used in casual spoken language.
（×）デパートへ行った。そうしたら買物をした。
I went to the department store and found that I did some shopping.
（○）デパートへ行った。そして買物をした。
I went to the department store and did some shopping.
【そうして】
1. そうして〈list〉

content: 好きな所。雑踏の中、港、遊園地、そうして、旅立つ前の空港。

content.content: Places I like: the middle of a bustling crowd, harbors, amusement parks, and airports before starting a trip.

content: おもしろくて、そうして人の役に立つことをしたい。

content.content: I want to do something that’s interesting and at the same time useful to others.
Used to list things or add something else. Almost the same as そして, but そうして is more emphatic. In this usage, そして is generally used more often.
2. そうして〈successive events〉

content: 旅行にもって行く物を全部再点検した。そうして、やっと安心した。

content.content: I double-checked everything I’m taking on the trip. Then I finally relaxed.

content: 状況を説明する言葉をじっくり考えた。そうして、彼に電話した。

content.content: I thought carefully about the words I would use to explain the situation. Then I phoned him.

content: 次に会う時間と場所、連絡の方法などを決めた。そうして、散会した。

content.content: We decided on the next meeting time and place, method of contact, etc. Then we adjourned.

Used to express what happens next, after the thing that has just been described. Often used, when describing a sequence of events, to indicate the situation that is ultimately attained. Can usually be replaced by そして.
【そうすると】
1. そうすると〈opportunity〉

content: ビルのまわりを回ってみた。そうすると、ひとつだけ電気のついている窓があった。

content.content: I went around the building. When I did so, I found just one window with a light on.

content: 切符はまとめて20人分予約することにした。そうすると、少し割り引きがあって助かるのだ。

content.content: I decided to reserve twenty tickets all at once. You get a bit of a discount that way, which helps.

content: テニスの練習は土曜日の朝することにしよう。そうすると、土曜日の午後は、時間ができる。

content.content: I’ll practice tennis on Saturday morning. Then I’ll have some free time in the afternoon.
Means that a later event occurs or is noticed as the result of an earlier event or action. そうすると cannot be followed by expressions indicating an intentional act of the speaker.
（×）20人以上予約して下さい。そうすると割引きしましょう。
Please book for twenty people or more. Then let’s give you a discount.
In addition, the second sentence often expresses an interpretation of the event described in the first sentence.
2. そうすると〈consequence〉

content: A:ホテルを出るのが5時で、新幹線に乗るのが6時です。

content.content: We’re leaving the hotel at five o’clock, and taking the shinkansen (bullet train) at six.
B:そうすると、買い物の時間がなくなりますよ。
But then we won’t have any time for shopping!

content: A:お客の数が百から二百に増えそうなんですが。

content.content: It looks like the number of guests might increase from 100 to
B:そうすると、この会場ではできなくなりますね。
In that case, we can’t hold it in this venue, can we.

content: A:パスポートはおととし取りました。

content.content: I got a passport the year before last.
B:そうすると、来年はまだ大丈夫ですね。
So, it will still be valid next year.

Used to make a statement in response to something the previous speaker has said. そうすると is followed by an interpretation of what the other person has said, a logical conclusion, etc. Roughly equivalent to すると. Used in spoken language.
【そうだ1】［N／Na　だそうだ］［A／V　そうだ］

content: あの人は留学生ではなくて技術研修生だそうだ。

content.content: Apparently he’s not an international student, he’s a technical trainee.

content: 今年の冬は暖かいそうだ。

content.content: They say winter will be warm this year.

content: 昔はこのあたりは海だったそうだ。

content.content: I’ve heard that this area was all sea in the past.

content: そのコンサートには1万人の若者がつめかけたそうだ。

content.content: Apparently 10,000 young people thronged to the concert.

content: 米が値上がりしているそうだ。

content.content: They say the cost of rice is going up.

content: 新聞によると今年は交通事故の死者が激増しているそうだ。

content.content: According to the newspaper, deaths caused by traffic accidents are showing a sudden increase this year.

content: 担当者の話によると新製品の開発に成功したそうだ。

content.content: According to the person in charge, we have succeeded in the development of the new product.

content: うわさでは大統領が辞任するそうだ。

content.content: Rumor has it that the president is going to resign.

content: 予報では台風は今夜半に紀伊半島に上陸するそうだ。

content.content: According to the forecast, the typhoon will make landfall on the Kii Peninsula tonight at midnight.

content: パンフレットによるとこの寺は二百年前に建てられたのだそうだ。

content.content: According to the brochure, this temple was built two hundred years ago.

Follows a plain-form clause and indicates that the information in question is not the speaker’s direct knowledge, but indirect information obtained from another source (i.e. hearsay). Cannot take a negative or past-tense form.
（×）今年の冬は寒いそうではない。
They don’t say winter will be cold this year.
（○）今年の冬は寒くないそうだ。
They say winter won’t be cold this year.
（×）去年の冬は寒いそうだった。
Winter last year was apparently cold.
（○）去年の冬は寒かったそうだ。
Apparently winter last year was cold.
When the source of information, such as a newspaper or a rumor, is indicated, expressions like ...では or ...によると are used, as in

content: . See みたいだ (Usage 2) for the difference between そうだ and みたいだ／らしい.

content.content: 【そうだ2】［Na そうだ］［A-そうだ］［R-そうだ］Has the same conjugation as na-adjectives and so changes to そうにV and そうなN. When it is used in the negative form, it is possible to say Na そうではない and A-そうではない, but R-そうではない is hardly ever used. R-そうもない／そうにない／そうにもない are used instead.
1. ...そうだ〈appearance, manner〉a. ...そうだ［Na そうだ］［A-そうだ］

content: その映画はおもしろそうだ。

content.content: That movie looks interesting.

content: 彼女はいつもさびしそうだ。

content.content: She always seems lonely.

content: おいしそうなケーキが並んでいる。

content.content: Delicious-looking cakes are lined up all in a row.

content: 今日は傘を持って行った方がよさそうだ。

content.content: It would probably be better to take along an umbrella today.

content: あの人はお金がなさそうだ。

content.content: That person seems to have no money.

content: 久しぶりに彼に会ったが、あまり元気そうではなかった。

content.content: I saw him for the first time in a long while, and he didn’t look very well.

content: 子供は人形をさも大事そうに箱の中にしまった。

content.content: The child tucked the doll into the box as if it were very precious.

content: いかにも重そうな荷物を持っている。

content.content: He’s carrying a very heavy-looking piece of luggage.

content: 彼は一見まじめそうだが実は相当な遊び人だ。

content.content: On the surface he looks like a serious person, but he’s really quite a playboy.

content: このおもちゃはちょっと見たところ丈夫そうだが、使うとすぐに壊れてしまう。

content.content: At first glance this toy looks sturdy, but it breaks right away when you use it.
Expresses the speaker’s judgment regarding a state of affairs, based on something s/he has seen, heard, or done. いい becomes よさそう, as in

content: , and ない becomes なさそう, as in
. ...そうだ is sometimes accompanied by adverbs such as さも or いかにも for emphasis, as in
and
. It is usually not used to refer to attributes that can easily be identified by sight alone, such as きれいだ or 赤い.

content.content: （×）彼女はきれいそうだ。
She seems pretty.
（○）彼女はきれいに見える。
She looks pretty.
Also, when used with 一見 or ちょっと見たところ, as in

content: and
, it is often followed by a clause that indicates “but this is not actually the case.”

content.content: Seeみたいだ (Usage 2) for the difference between そうだ and みたいだ.
b. ...そうにみえる［Na そうにみえる］［A-そうにみえる］

content: 誕生パーティーで彼女はいかにもしあわせそうに見えた。

content.content: She looked very happy at the birthday party.

content: 彼は若そうに見えるが来年は60才になる。

content.content: He looks young, but next year he’ll be sixty.

content: なんだか気分が悪そうに見えますが大丈夫ですか。

content.content: You don’t look well. Are you all right?

content: その問題はむずかしそうに見えたがやってみるとそうでもなかった。

content.content: The question looked hard, but after I tried answering it, it wasn’t so bad.
Means that something looks a certain way, based on outside appearance.
c. ...そうにしている［Na そうにしている］［A-そうにしている］

content: 彼女はいつもはずかしそうにしている。

content.content: She always seems shy.

content: 先生はお元気そうにしておられたので、安心しました。

content.content: Our teacher was looking well, so I was relieved.

content: その人はコートも着ずに寒そうにしていた。

content.content: That person, not even wearing a coat, looked cold.

content: その子はいやそうにして遊び場からひとり離れて座っていた。

content.content: The child was sitting alone away from the playground, looking annoyed.

Attaches to adjectives that express a feeling or sensation and means that an action is being performed with a particular demeanor or manner. Can be replaced by そうだ, but then the meaning that some kind of action is being performed is lost.
2. R-そうだ〈possibility of occurrence 1〉a. R-そうだ

content: 星が出ているから明日は天気になりそうだ。

content.content: The stars are out, so tomorrow will probably be sunny.

content: 今年は雨が多いから、桜はすぐに散ってしまいそうだ。

content.content: It’s been raining a lot this year, so the cherry blossoms will likely fall quickly.

content: 服のボタンがとれそうだ。

content.content: A button on my (suit) is about to come off.

content: 反対運動は全国に広がりそうな気配だ。

content.content: It looks like the opposition movement will probably spread all over the country.

content: 今日中に原稿が書けそうだ。

content.content: I’ll probably be able to finish the manuscript sometime today.

content: 今夜は涼しいからぐっすり眠れそうだ。

content.content: It’s cooler tonight so I think I’ll be able to sleep really well.

content: 暑くて死にそうだ。

content.content: This heat is killing me.

content: ジェット機の音がうるさくて、気が変になりそうだ。

content.content: The noise from the jet planes is about to drive me crazy.

Used to express the judgment that there is a strong possibility an event could occur. Attaches to verbs that do not express intention, such as なる and 落ちる, as well as to V-れる verbs that express potential, such as 書ける and 眠れる. When accompanied by expressions such as もうちょっとで or 今にも, as below, it expresses the feeling that a situation is imminent or urgent.
（例）あの古い家はもうちょっとで倒れそうだ。
That old house looks like it’s about to fall down.
（例）その子は今にも泣き出しそうな顔をしていた。
The child looked like he was about to burst into tears.
Examples

content: and
are idiomatic expressions that express the degree of severity of the situation in a figurative way.

content.content: b. R-そうになる

content: 道が凍っていて、何度もころびそうになった。

content.content: The road was icy and I nearly fell down several times.

content: 車にぶつかりそうになって、あわてて道の端にとびのいた。

content.content: I was about to be hit by a car, so I frantically jumped over to the side of the road.

content: びっくりして持っていたグラスを落としそうになった。

content.content: I was surprised and nearly dropped the glass I was holding.

content: 私には子供のころ犬にかまれそうになった記憶がある。

content.content: I remember nearly being bitten by a dog when I was a child.

content: 私には、くじけそうになるといつもはげましてくれる友がいる。

content.content: I have friends who always encourage me when I am about to lose heart.
Means that a situation beyond the speaker’s control comes very close to occurring. Often used to describe past events, as in

content: above. Sometimes used with adverbs such as あやうく (barely, narrowly) and あわや (nearly, on the verge of), in which case it conveys the sense that a situation is pressing or urgent.

content.content: （例）山で遭難して、あやうく命を失いそうになった。
I had a mishap in the mountains and nearly lost my life.
In

content: and
, R-そうになる can be replaced by V-るところだ.

content.content: c. R-そうもないR-そうにない

content: この本は売れそうもない。

content.content: This book probably won’t sell.

content: 仕事は明日までには終わりそうもない。

content.content: It doesn’t look like I’ll be finished this work before tomorrow.

content: 雨は夜に入っても止みそうになかった。

content.content: Even after nightfall, the rain showed no sign of letting up.

content: 一人の力ではとうてい出来そうにもない。

content.content: This doesn’t at all seem like something one person can do alone.

content: 民家はちょっとやそっとでは壊れそうもないほど頑丈な造りだった。

content.content: Traditional Japanese-style houses were so well-built that it would take a lot to make them collapse.

content: 社長は歳をとってはいるが、元気だからなかなか辞めそうにもない。

content.content: The company president is getting older, but since he’s in good health, it doesn’t look like he’ll be quitting any time soon.
Means that a certain event is not likely to happen. Used in the forms R-そうもない, R-そうにない, and R-そうにもない.
3. R-そうだ〈possibility of occurrence 2〉

content: あの様子では二人はもうじき結婚しそうだ。

content.content: Judging from the way things are going, those two will probably get married very soon.

content: 彼はもう10日も無断で休んでいる。どうも会社を辞めそうだ。

content.content: He’s been off work without notice for ten days already. It looks as if he’s going to quit the company.

content: 彼女は熱心にパンフレットを見ていたから、誘ったら会員になりそうだ。

content.content: Since she was looking at the pamphlet so intently, she’d probably become a member if someone asked her to join.

content: あんなに叱ったら、あの子は家出しそうな気がします。

content.content: If you scold him so much, I have a feeling he’s likely to run away from home.

Attaches to verbs that express the intentional act of a third person, and expresses the judgment that there is a strong possibility such an action or event will occur. Unlike そうだ (Usage 2), this そうだ is not usually used to refer to the speaker.
（×）私は会社をやめそうだ。
It looks as if I’m going to quit the company.
4. R-てしまいそうだ

content: おいしいから全部食べてしまいそうだ。

content.content: It’s delicious, so I just might finish it all.

content: 1度やめていたタバコをまた吸ってしまいそうだ。

content.content: Even though I quit smoking, I feel like I might be about to start again.

content: 警察のきびしい尋問を受けたら、組織の秘密をしゃべってしまいそうな気がする。

content.content: If I get grilled by the police, something tells me I’ll end up giving away all the organization’s secrets.
Used with verbs that express an intentional act and expresses a feeling of fear or concern that something may happen against one’s will. Often used to describe one’s own acts/actions.
【そこで】
1. そこで〈reason〉

content: 今度の事件ではかなりの被害が出ています。そこで、ひとつ皆さんにご相談があるのですが。

content.content: There has been a lot of damage from the latest incident. So, there's something I’d like to discuss with you all.

content: 皆さんこの問題にはおおいに関心をお持ちのことと思います。そこで専門のお立場からご意見をお聞かせいただければと思うのですが、いかがでしょうか。

content.content: I think you all have a strong interest in this problem. Therefore, I would like to hear your opinion, from your perspective as specialists. What do you think?

content: 村ではだれ一人、荒れ地の開墾に賛成の者はいなかった。そこで役人はまずひとりの若者を選んでこの困難な事業に当たらせることにした。

content.content: Not a single person in the village agreed with the cultivation of the wasteland. So the officials decided first of all to choose a young man and have him take on this difficult project.

content: A:このあたりは開発が遅れてるな。

content.content: This area is lagging behind in development, isn't it.
B:そこで、相談なんだが少し金を融資してもらえないかな。
That is why I'd like to talk to you about the possibility of giving us a small loan....
Expresses a reason. Used to propose something new with respect to a previously existing state of affairs. Formal language. Can be replaced with それで.
2. そこで〈point in time〉

content: A:だんだんむずかしくなってきたし、タイ語の勉強やめようかな。

content.content: It’s getting harder and harder, so I’m thinking about quitting my Thai language study.
B:そこでやめちゃダメだよ。せっかく今までがんばってきたんだから。
Don’t stop now—not when you’ve already put so much effort into it!

content: 仕掛け花火が炸裂し、そこで祭りは終わりになった。

content.content: The exhibition fireworks went off with a bang, and with that the festival ended.
Means “at that point.” Used to describe not a place, but rather a judgment based on a certain situation.
【そこへ】

content: 友人のうわさ話をしていたら、そこへ当の本人が来てしまった。

content.content: Just as we were talking about our friend, that very person walked in.

content: 酔っぱらい客がけんかを始めた。そこへバーテンが止めに入ったが、かえって騒ぎが大きくなってしまった。

content.content: Drunken customers started a fight. Then the bartender stepped in to try to stop it, but that only made it worse.

content: 集会は整然と行われていた。ところがそこへデモ隊が入ってきて場内は騒然となった。

content.content: The meeting was proceeding smoothly. But then a group of demonstrators came in and the place was thrown into an uproar.
Means “into the scene in question.” Often followed by verbs of movement, such as 来る(to come) and 入る(to enter).
【そこへいくと】

content: A:うちの会社、残業が多くてね。先週はほとんど晩ご飯、家で食べていないんだ。

content.content: In my company, you know, there’s a lot of overtime work. Last week I hardly ate supper at home at all.
B:そりゃ、大変だな。そこへいくと僕のとこなんか楽なほうだ。
That’s tough. If you look at it that way, my company isn’t too bad.

content: お宅の坊っちゃん、よくお出来になるそうですね。そこへいくとうちの坊主なんかまったくだめですよ。

content.content: I hear your son does very well in school. My boy, in comparison, is completely hopeless.
Means “in comparison to.” Often followed by expressions of comparison. Used in spoken language.
【そしたら】

content: きのう映画を見に行ったのよ。そしたらばったり高田さんに会っちゃって。

content.content: I went to see a movie yesterday, and I bumped into Takada-san.

content: 一日に30分だけ練習しなさい。そしたら、上手になりますよ。

content.content: Practice for just thirty minutes a day. Then you’ll improve.
A more colloquial version of そうしたら. Not usually used in written language.
【そうしたら】
【そして】
1. そして〈listing〉

content: 今回の旅行ではスペイン、イタリアそしてフランスと、おもに南ヨーロッパを中心に回った。

content.content: On this trip I traveled mainly around southern Europe, to Spain, Italy, and France.

content: リーダーには指導力、判断力そして決断力が欠かせない。

content.content: For a leader, leadership ability, judgment, and decisiveness are indispensable.

content: おみやげは小さくて、そして軽いものがいい。

content.content: Souvenirs should be small and lightweight.

content: この病気には、甘いもの、あぶらっこいもの、そしてアルコールがよくない。

content.content: Sweets, greasy food, and alcohol are not good for this illness.
Used to list items or add another item to a list. Almost the same as それに, but そして tends to be used more in written language.
2. そして〈successive events〉

content: 観客は一人帰り、二人帰り、そして最後にはだれもいなくなってしまった。

content.content: One member of the audience left, and then a second one left, and in the end there was no one left at all.

content: 山間部のこの地方では、刈り入れが終わると短い秋が去り、そして厳しい冬がやってくるのだ。

content.content: In this mountainous area, once the harvesting is over, the short fall season ends and then a hard winter comes.

content: 彼はその日、部下にすべてを打ち明けた。そして今後の対応を夜遅くまで話し合った。

content.content: That day, he confided everything to his subordinate. Then they discussed what to do from now on, until late into the night.
Used to express a chronological sequence of events. Often used to indicate the last event in a series. Somewhat literary in style.
【その...その】［そのNそのN］

content: その日その日を無事に過ごせれば出世なんかしなくてもいいんです。

content.content: As long as I can get through each day without any trouble, it's all right if I don’t get promoted.

content: その人その人で考え方がちがうのは当然だ。

content.content: It’s natural that each person should have a different viewpoint.

content: 人生の大事なその時その時を写真におさめてある。

content.content: Each important moment in my life has been captured in a photograph.
The same noun is used in both N slots. Means “each, respective.”
【そのうえ】

content: あそこのレストランは高くて、そのうえまずい。

content.content: That restaurant is expensive, and what is more, the food is awful.

content: 彼の奥さんは美人だし、そのうえ料理もうまい。

content.content: His wife is a real beauty and—on top of that—is a good cook, too.

content: あの人にはすっかりお世話になった。住むところから、役所の手続きまで。そのうえアルバイトまで紹介してもらった。

content.content: I’m really indebted to that person. For everything from finding me a place to live to helping me with the procedures at government offices. And on top of that, he also found me a part-time job.

content: きのうは先生の家でごちそうになった。帰りにはおみやげまでもらい、そのうえ車で駅まで送っていただいた。

content.content: Yesterday my teacher treated me to a meal at her house. Before I went home, she even gave me a gift, and in addition to all that, she gave me a ride to the train station too.
An expression used to add something similar. Used to add information about situations or circumstances, in order to describe them in more detail. Can be replaced by それに.
【そのうち】

content: 木村さんはそのうち来ると思います。

content.content: I think Kimura-san will be here shortly.

content: そのうち雨もやむだろうから、そうしたら出かけよう。
