content.content: I think the rain will stop soon, so let’s go out when it does.

content: あんなに毎日遅くまで仕事していたら、そのうち過労で倒れるんじゃないだろうか。

content.content: If he’s working late every night like that, don’t you think he might collapse from overwork one of these days?

content: A:また一緒に食事に行こうよ。

content.content: Let’s go out for a meal together again.
B:ええ、そのうちにね。
OK, let’s do that sometime.
Means “before too much time passes.” Conversational in tone. The written language equivalent is いずれ. そのうちに may also be used.
【そのくせ】

content: 彼は味にうるさく、文句が多い。そのくせ自分ではまったく料理ができない。

content.content: He’s very particular about the taste of food and complains a lot. And yet he can’t cook at all.

content: 妻は寒いときは体があたたまるからたまご酒を飲めとかいろいろ言うが、そのくせ自分はよくかぜをひく。

content.content: My wife says all sorts of things like, “When the weather is cold, drink hot sake with a beaten egg in it to warm yourself up,” and yet she herself often catches cold.

content: この辺は雪が多いが、そのくせ時々水不足になる。

content.content: There is a lot of snow in this area, but even so there is sometimes a water shortage.
Means “nevertheless, even so.” Used when speaking critically of someone or something. An informal expression used in spoken language.
【くせ】3
【そのもの】
1. Nそのもの

content: 機械そのものには問題はないが、ソフトに問題があるようだ。

content.content: The machine itself is all right, but there seems to be a problem with the software.

content: この本がつまらないんじゃない。読書そのものが好きになれないんだ。

content.content: It isn’t that this book is boring. I just can't get into the activity of reading itself.
Means “the thing itself.”
2. Nそのものだ

content: その合唱団は天使の歌声そのものだ。

content.content: That chorus group is the very voice of angels singing.

content: あの映画は彼の人生そのものだ。

content.content: That film is just like his life.
Used to compare one thing to another and emphasize that they are just the same. May be used figuratively.
【そばから】［Vそばから］

content: 子供達は作るそばから食べてしまうので、作っても作ってもおいつかない。

content.content: My children eat everything up as fast as I make it, so even if I cook and cook, I can’t keep up with them.

content: 聞いたそばから忘れてしまう。

content.content: I forget things as soon as I hear them.

content: 読んだそばから抜けていって何もおぼえていない。

content.content: As soon as I read something I forget it, and I don’t remember anything.
Means “as soon as.” A slightly old-fashioned expression.
【そもそも】
1. そもそものN

content: 父が株に手を出したことが、わが家の苦労のそもそもの始まりだった。

content.content: When my father started dabbling in the stock market, it was the beginning of hardship for my family.

content: それはそもそも姉が持ち出した話なのに、彼女はそのことをすっかり忘れてしまっている。

content.content: Even though it was my older sister who first brought up the idea, now she’s completely forgotten about it.

content: そもそもことの起こりは、弟がうちを出て一人暮らしをすると言い出したことだった。

content.content: It all began when my younger brother started saying that he was going to leave home and live on his own.
When そもそも is combined with nouns that mean “beginning,” such as 始まり and 起こり, it means “the very beginning of a certain state of affairs.” ことの起こり in

content: indicates a problematic situation, and attaching そもそも to it shows that the trigger for the situation is being expressed.

content.content: 2. そもそも...というのは

content: そもそも人の気持ちというのは他人にコントロールできるものではないのだから、人を思い通りにしようとしても無駄だ。

content.content: You can’t control people’s feelings in the first place, so even if you try to make others be the way you want them to be, it’s impossible.

content: そもそも子供というものは型にはまらない生き方を好むものだ。規則ずくめの学校を息苦しく感じるのは当然だ。

content.content: Children by nature tend to like living without a set pattern. It’s only natural that they feel suffocated at a school with lots of rules.
Describes the essence or basic character of something. Often used to express disagreement with an action or opinion that does not take this essence into consideration.
3. そもそも

content: そもそもおまえが悪いんだよ。友達に自分の仕事をおしつけるなんて。

content.content: You’re the one who was wrong from the very beginning—trying to make your friend do your own work!

content: そもそもあんたがこっちの道を行こうって言い出したのよ。文句言わないで、さっさと歩いてよ。

content.content: You’re the one who first suggested that we should go this way. So stop complaining and start walking!
Expresses criticism of the addressee for having triggered a problematic situation.
【それから】
1. それから

content: まず玉子の黄身だけよくかき混ぜて下さい。それからサラダ油と用意しておいた調味料を加え、混ぜ合わせます。

content.content: First, take the egg yolks and beat them well. Then add the salad oil and the seasonings you’ve already prepared, and mix them all together.

content: となりの奥さんにはおとといマーケットで会いました。それから一度も見かけていません。

content.content: I met the wife from next door at the market the day before yesterday. I haven’t seen her since.

content: 彼は高校時代にある事件のためひどく傷ついた。そしてそれから人を信じなくなってしまった。

content.content: He was deeply hurt by an incident in high school. After that he stopped trusting other people.

content: きのうは夕方一度家に帰って、それから家族で食事に出かけました。

content.content: Yesterday evening I first went home, and then I went out for dinner with my family.

content: あの日のことはよく覚えています。改札口を出て、それから駅前の喫茶店に入ろうとしたときに男の人がぶつかってきたんです。

content.content: I remember that day very well. I exited the ticket gate, and then as I was about to go into a coffee shop in front of the station, a man bumped into me.
Indicates that events occur sequentially over time. Means “after that, and then.” Used in spoken language. Often used after the te-form of a verb in the pattern V-て、それから, as in

content: and

content.content: （×）昨日は風邪をひいていました。それから学校を休みました。
I had a cold yesterday. And then I didn’t go to school.
When giving a reason, use それで (so, that is why), それだから (therefore), etc.
2. NそれからN

content: 夏休みにタイ、マレーシアそれからインドネシアの3カ国を回ってきた。

content.content: During the summer vacation I traveled around three countries: Thailand, Malaysia, and Indonesia.

content: カレーとミニサラダ、あっそれからコーヒーもお願いします。

content.content: I’d like curry and a small salad, oh, and also some coffee.

content: 初級のクラスは月曜日と水曜日、それから土曜日にやっています。

content.content: We have a beginners’ class on Mondays, Wednesdays, and Saturdays.

content: 担当は山田さん、それから松本さん、この二人です。

content.content: There are two people in charge: Yamada-san and Matsumoto-san.

content: この時期の海外旅行としましては、香港それから台湾といったところが人気がありますね。

content.content: For a trip abroad at this time of year, Hong Kong and Taiwan are popular destinations.
Used when listing a series of similar matters or things. Means “and.” If nouns are being listed, a chronological sequence is not implied. Used in spoken language.
【それが】

content: 10時に会う約束だった。それが1時になっても現れないんだ。

content.content: We had an appointment to meet at ten o’clock. But he still hadn’t shown up even by one.

content: 10時に着くはずだった。それが道に迷ってひどく遅れてしまった。

content.content: I was supposed to arrive at ten o’clock. But I got lost and was really late.

content: A:お父さんはお元気でしょうね。

content.content: I suppose your father is in good health, isn’t he?
B:それが、このごろどうも調子がよくないんですよ。
You’d think so, but actually he hasn’t been feeling very well lately.

content: A:ご主人相変わらず遅いの？

content.content: Does your husband still get home late?
B:それが変なのよ、このごろ。夕食前にうちに帰ってくるの。
The funny thing is, recently he’s been coming home before supper.
Means “on the contrary, nevertheless, however.” In

content: and
it is used to introduce information that the listener doesn’t expect.

content.content: 【それこそ】

content: 野球部は練習がきびしくて、君ではそれこそ三日ともたないよ。

content.content: The baseball team’s training is really tough, so you won’t last even three days.

content: 育ち盛りの子供がたくさんいるので、毎日それこそ山のようなご飯を炊く。

content.content: I have a lot of growing children, so I have to cook a real mountain of rice every day.
This expression presents an example or analogy to emphasize that the degree of something is extreme.

content: means “the training is so hard that you won’t stay for more than three days,” and
means “they all eat so much that we need an enormous amount of rice.” Used in spoken language.

content.content: 【それだけ】

content: 1年間努力して合格したのでそれだけ喜びも大きい。

content.content: I passed after a year of hard work, so my happiness is all the greater.

content: よく働いたらそれだけおなかもすく。

content.content: The more you work, the hungrier you get.

content: あの仲の良かったふたりはとうとう別れてしまった。愛し合っていたからそれだけ憎しみも大きいようだ。

content.content: That couple who had been so close ended up splitting up. They’d really loved each other, so it seems like their hatred is that much bigger.

content: 練習を1日でもさぼるとそれだけ体が動かなくなる。

content.content: If you skip practice for even just one day, your body will move that much less.
Means “proportionate to a certain extent.”
【それで】

content: きのうの晩熱が出て、それで今日は学校を休んだ。

content.content: I had a fever last night, so I didn’t go to school today.

content: 小さい時に海でこわい思いをした。それで海が好きになれない。

content.content: When I was little, I had a scary experience at the beach. That’s why I’ve never been able to like the ocean.

content: A:来週から試験だ。

content.content: Exams start next week.
B:それで。
So?
A:しばらく遊べない。
I can’t have fun for a while.

content: A:昨日、突然いなかから親戚が出てきまして...。

content.content: Yesterday one of my relatives arrived unexpectedly from my hometown (lit. the countryside)....
B:それで。
So?
A:それで、あのう今日の残業は...。
So, um, about working overtime today....
B:かまわないよ、はやく帰りなさい。
That’s fine, just go home early.
Expresses a reason. May also be used to prompt the other person to continue speaking, as speaker B does in

content: and
. Used in spoken language. A more informal expression is で.

content.content: 【それでこそ】

content: 彼は部下の失敗の責任をとって、社長の座を降りた。それでこそ真のリーダーと言える。

content.content: He took responsibility for his subordinate’s mistake and stepped down as company president. That’s what we can call a true leader.

content: A:あの大学、卒業するのがむずかしいそうだよ。

content.content: I’ve heard that university is hard to graduate from.
B:それでこそ本当の大学だね。
That’s how a real university should be.

content: A:今度のコピー機は、まったく人手がいらないそうだ。

content.content: I hear the new photocopier doesn’t need anyone to operate it at all.
B:それでこそオフィス革命と言えるね。今までのは人を忙しくさせるだけだったから。
You can call that a real office revolution, can’t you. Up till now it had just made people even busier.

Used at the beginning of a sentence, this means “because of, for that reason.” Used to highlight a certain quality of a person or thing and express a high evaluation of that person/thing, based on the previously-stated reason. Used only for positive evaluation. An old-fashioned expression. In conversation, it is often used in semi-formulaic expressions such as それでこそ本当のNだ  (that’s a real/true N.)

【それでは】This expression is composed of では preceded by the demonstrative それ. In most cases it can be replaced by では, except in Usage 4 <negative result>, when it is always used in the form それでは. It is a rather formal expression, and in informal spoken language それじゃ（あ） and じゃ（あ） are used instead.
1. それでは〈inference〉

content: A:私は1974年の卒業です。

content.content: I graduated in
B:それでは、私は2年後輩になります。
Then I was two years behind you.

content: A:ようやく就職が内定しました。

content.content: I finally got an unofficial job offer.
B:それでは、ご両親もさぞお喜びのことでしょう。
That must mean your parents are really happy, too.
【では2】
2. それでは〈expression of attitude〉

content: A:その人にはあった事がないんです。

content.content: I’ve never met that man.
B:それでは紹介してあげますよ。
Then I’ll introduce him to you.

content: A:準備できました。

content.content: We’re ready.
B:それでは始めましょう。
Let’s get started, then.
【では2】
3. それでは〈shift〉

content: それでは、次は天気予報です。

content.content: Coming up next is the weather forecast.

content: それでは、皆さん、さようなら。

content.content: Well then, good-bye everyone.
【では2】
4. それでは〈negative result〉

content: A:入学試験、多分60パーセントもとれなかったと思います。

content.content: I don’t think I got even 60% on the entrance exam.
B:それでは合格は無理だろう。
Then you probably won’t pass.

content: A:明日までには何とか出来上がると思いますが。

content.content: I think we can manage to get it done by tomorrow.
B:それでは、間に合わないんですよ。
That’s too late!

content: こんなに大変な仕事を彼女ひとりに任せているそうだが、それでは彼女があまりにも気の毒だ。

content.content: I hear she’s been left to handle a tough job like this all on her own, but that’s not fair to her.

Used to respond to or follow up on the previous sentence or clause and means “in that case, an undesirable result will occur.” Followed by expressions with negative meaning, such as だめだ (no good/no use), 無理だ (unreasonable), or 不可能だ (impossible).
【それでも】

content: いろいろ説明してもらったが、それでもまだ納得できない。

content.content: I had it explained to me in detail, but I still can’t agree to it.

content: 試合は9時におわったが、それでもなお残ってさわいでいるファンがいた。

content.content: The game ended at nine o’clock, and yet there were still fans who were staying and making noise.

content: 葬式もすんだし、遺品の整理もついた。しかしそれでもまだ彼の死は信じられない。

content.content: The funeral is over and the estate has been sorted out. But even so, I still can’t believe that he’s dead.

content: 去年の冬に山で大けがをした。しかしそれでもまた山に登りたい。

content.content: I was badly injured in the mountains last winter. But even so, I still want to go mountain-climbing.
Means “in spite of the thing just described, still....” Often used with まだ (still/yet) or なお (still/even more).
【それとも】
1. NそれともN

content: A:コーヒー？　それとも紅茶？

content.content: Coffee? Or tea?
B:どちらでもけっこうです。
Either one is fine.

content: A:あしたのパーティーには、何を着て行くつもり？　着物、それともドレス？

content.content: What are you going to wear to the party tomorrow? A kimono, or a dress?
B:まだ、決めてないのよ。
I haven’t decided yet.

content: 進学か、それとも就職かとずいぶん悩んだ。

content.content: Going to graduate school, or finding a job—I worried a lot about which to do.
Takes the pattern XそれともY or XかそれともYか and means “either X or Y.” Used to indicate two possibilities and ask the listener which is better, as in

content: , or to ask about the listener’s intention, as in
. Cannot be used when giving instructions, as seen in the examples below.

content.content: （×）黒それとも青のインクで書いてください。
Please use a pen with black, or blue ink.
（○）黒か青のインクで書いてください。
Please use a pen with black or blue ink.
Also used when there are two possibilities and the speaker is unsure or doesn’t know which one to choose, as in

content: . In this case, それとも can be replaced by あるいは (or).

content.content: 2. ...それとも

content: 雨が降ってきましたが、どうしますか。行きますか。それとも延期しますか。

content.content: It’s started raining, so what shall we do? Shall we go? Or shall we postpone it?

content: 洋室がよろしいですか、それとも和室の方がよろしいですか。

content.content: Would you prefer a Western-style room, or would a Japanese-style room be better?

content: A:散歩にでも行く？　それとも、映画でも見ようか。

content.content: Do you want to take a walk? Or would you like to see a film?
B:そうね、久しぶりに映画もいいな。
Hmm... a movie might be nice, since we haven’t seen one in a while.

content: 就職しようか、それとも進学しようかと迷っている。

content.content: I can’t decide whether to find a job or to go on to university.

content: 彼は、初めから来るつもりがなかったのか、それとも、急に気が変わったのか、約束の時間が過ぎても現れなかった。

content.content: I don’t know if he didn’t intend to come in the first place, or if he all of a sudden changed his mind, but he never showed up, even after the appointed time.

content: この手紙を読んで、彼女は喜んでくれるだろうか。それとも、軽蔑するだろうか。

content.content: I wonder if she’ll be happy when she reads this letter. Or if she’ll despise me.
Takes the pattern XそれともY or XかそれともYか and means “either X or Y.”

content: are examples of the speaker indicating two possibilities and asking the listener which is better.
are examples in which there are two possibilities, and the speaker is either unsure which is true or doesn’t know which to choose. In
, それとも can be replaced by あるいは (or).

content.content: 【それどころか】

content: A:山の家はすずしくていいでしょうね。

content.content: The mountain lodge must be nice and cool.
B:それどころか、寒くてすっかりかぜをひいてしまいました。
Cool? It was so cold that I caught a bad cold!

content: A:彼、最近結婚したらしいね。

content.content: I hear he got married recently, didn’t he.
B:それどころか、もう赤ん坊が生まれたそうだよ。
What do you mean, “recently”? Apparently they already have a baby!
Used to convey that the degree or scope of something is far beyond what the other person had imagined.
【それなら】

content: A:どこか山登りに行こうと思うんだけど。

content.content: I’m thinking of going mountain-climbing somewhere.
B:それなら、日本アルプスがいいよ。
Then the Japanese alps would be ideal.

content: A:パーティーにはリーさんの奥さんも来るそうだ。

content.content: Apparently Lee-san wife will also attend the party.
B:それなら私も行きたいわ。
Then I’d like to go, too.

content: これ以上の援助はできないといっているが、それならこちらにも考えがある。

content.content: They’re saying they can’t offer any more assistance. Well, if that’s the case, then we have some ideas of our own about this.
Used in response to something the other person has said and means “if that is so, in that case.”
【なら1】
【それに】
1. ...それにN

content: 部屋にはさいふとかぎ、それに手帳が残されていた。

content.content: A wallet, a key, and a daily planner had been left in the room.

content: 用意するものは紙、はさみ、色えんぴつそれに輪ゴムです。

content.content: You need to prepare paper, scissors, colored pencils, and rubber bands.

content: 牛乳とそれにたまごも買ってきてね。

content.content: Please buy milk, and eggs as well.

content: A:いつがご都合がよろしいでしょうか。

content.content: When would be convenient for you?
B:そうですね、火曜と木曜それに金曜の午後もあいています。
Let’s see...I’m free on Tuesday, Thursday, and also Friday afternoon.

content: カレーにハンバーグ、それにライスもお願いします。

content.content: Curry and a hamburger, and also some rice, please.
Used to add something to a series of similar things. Cannot be replaced by そのうえ or しかも, even though these are also ways of adding something further.

content: このごろよく眠れない。それに時々めまいもする。

content.content: I haven’t been sleeping well recently. I also feel dizzy sometimes.

content: そのアルバイトは楽だし、それに時間給もいい。

content.content: That part-time job is easy, and the hourly wage is good, too.

content: 高速バスは速いし、それになんといっても安い。

content.content: The express bus is fast, and the big advantage is that it’s inexpensive.

content: 去年の夏は雨が多かった。それに気温も低くて米も不作だった。

content.content: We had a lot of rain last summer. In addition, the temperatures were low, so there was also a poor rice harvest.
Used to add something to a series of similar things. Can be replaced by そのうえ or しかも, but has a more casual, conversational tone than either of these.
【それにしては】

content: A:きのうほとんど寝てないんです。

content.content: I got almost no sleep yesterday.
B:それにしては元気がいいね。
You seem quite chipper, considering the circumstances.

content: A:これは輸入の最高級品だよ。

content.content: This is a top-of-the-line import.
B:それにしては安いのね。
So it’s not that expensive, considering.

content: かれは一流の大学をでているそうだが、それにしては仕事ができない。

content.content: Apparently he graduated from a top university, but for all that, he can’t do the job.

content: アメリカに3年いたそうだが、それにしては英語が下手だ。

content.content: I hear he was in the States for three years, but considering that, his English is pretty poor.
Means “contrary to what could be expected from the state of affairs that has just been described.”
【それにしても】

content: A:予選ではあんなに強かったのにどうして決勝で負けたんでしょうね。

content.content: He was so good in the preliminaries—I wonder why he lost in the final.
B:プレッシャーでしょう。
Probably due to pressure.
A:それにしてもひどい負け方ですね。
Even so, he really lost badly.

content: A:坂本さん、あの高校に受かったんだってね。

content.content: I hear Sakamoto-san passed the exam to get into that high school.
B:必死で勉強してたらしいよ。
Apparently she studied really hard for it.
A:それにしてもすごいね。
Even so, that’s really something!

content: A:またガソリン代、値上がりしたよ。

content.content: The cost of gasoline has gone up again.
B:それにしても政治家はなにをしてるんだろう。われわれがこんなに苦しんでいるのに。
And what are the politicians doing about it? While we’re struggling so hard.

content: A:太郎、また背がのびたようよ。

content.content: Taro seems to have grown more.
B:それにしても、あいつはよく寝るなあ。
Even so (even though children who sleep well grow well), he really does sleep a lot, doesn’t he.

content: 《A、Bが竹下さんを待っている》

content.content: 《A and B are waiting for Takeshita-san》
A:よく降りますね。
It’s really raining hard, isn’t it?
B:ええ、それにしても竹下さん遅いですね。
Yes, but even so, Takeshita-san is quite late, isn’t he?
Means “even taking that (fact) into account.” In

content: , it is used to say something that contrasts with a previous statement, while acknowledging that the previous statement is by and large true. In
and

, it is used to introduce a new topic, after expressing provisional agreement with what has been said up to that point. In the latter case, it often expresses the feelings of the speaker at that time.

content.content: 【それはそうと】

content: A:先生、レポートのしめきりはいつですか。

content.content: Sensei (Professor), when is the deadline for the report?
B:七月末だよ。それはそうと明日の演習の発表はだれだったかな。
It’s the end of July. By the way, who’s presenting at tomorrow’s seminar?

content: A:パン、買ってきたよ。

content.content: I bought some bread.
B:ありがとう。それはそうと安田さんに電話してくれた？
Thanks. By the way, did you call Yasuda-san?
Used to close the current topic of discussion and change the subject. Introduces the new topic. Often used to add something the speaker has just remembered.
【それはそれでいい】

content: 事故の責任は取ったというなら、それはそれでいい。しかし今後の補償をちゃんとしてくれなくては困る。

content.content: If you’ve taken responsibility for the accident, then that’s fine. But you’ll have to continue to pay compensation regularly, or there’ll be trouble.

content: A:部長、会議の資料そろいました。

content.content: (to the department head) Buchoo, the documents for the meeting are ready.
B:それはそれでいいけど、事前の打ち合せのほうはどうなってるのかね。
That’s fine, but what’s happening with the pre-planning session?
Means “yes, I understand that, but....” An introductory remark used to bring up a different subject, with the premise that what was previously said has been understood and accepted.
【それはそれとして】

content: 万引が問題なのはわかります。しかしそれはそれとして、もう少し広く青少年をとりまく社会環境について話し合いたいと思います。

content.content: I know shoplifting is a problem. But leaving that aside, I’d like to discuss the social environment of young people from a slightly broader perspective.

content: A:今月かなりの赤字になっているのは人件費がかかりすぎているからじゃないか。

content.content: Isn’t the reason we’re so far in the red this month that we’re spending too much on personnel?
B:まあそうだけど、それはそれとして、円高のことも考えないといけないんじゃないかな。
Well, yes, but be that as it may, I think we also have to take into consideration the rising yen.
Used to acknowledge a certain matter or situation and shift the viewpoint slightly to talk about a different matter/situation.
【それほど】

content: それほど好きならあきらめずにやりなさい。

content.content: If you like it so much, don’t give it up.

content: A:嫌いなの？

content.content: Don’t you like (that guy)?
B:いや、それほど嫌いなわけじゃないけど、あまり会いたくないんだ。
No, it’s not that I dislike him that much, but I don’t really want to see him.

content: A:テニス、ほんとにお上手ですね。

content.content: You play tennis really well, don’t you.
B:いや、それほどでもありませんよ。
No, I’m not really that good.
Means “so much; that much.” Often combined with negative expressions to express the meaning “not very; not much,” as in

content: and

content.content: 【それまでだ】

content: 人間、死んでしまえばそれまでだ。生きているうちにやりたいことをやろう。

content.content: Once we die, that’s it. Let’s do the things we want to do while we’re alive.

content: A:お土産、チョコレートにしましょうか。

content.content: Shall we take some chocolate as a gift?
B:チョコレートなんか食べてしまえばそれまでだ。なにか記念に残るものがいいよ。
With things like chocolate, once you’ve eaten it, it’s gone. It’s better to take something that will last as a keepsake.

content: 一度赤ん坊が目を覚ましたらもうそれまでだ。自分のことはなにもできない。

content.content: Once the baby wakes up, that’s it. You can’t do anything for yourself.
Means “that is the end” or “there is no more.” Used with すれば or したら, and often followed by expressions that mean “later there will be nothing left, so it is best to do something now,” as in

content: and

content.content: 【それゆえ】

content: 彼は自分の能力を過信していた。それゆえに人の忠告を聞かず失敗した。

content.content: He overestimated his own ability. That’s why he didn’t listen to others’ warnings and ended up failing.

content: 最近、腸チフスに感染して帰国する旅行者が増加している。それゆえ飲み水には十分注意されたい。

content.content: Recently the number of returning travelers who are infected with typhoid has been increasing. For that reason, please be very careful about the drinking water.

content: 我思う。ゆえに我あり。（デカルト）

content.content: I think, therefore I am. (Descartes)

content: 二つの辺が等しい。ゆえに、三角形ABCは二等辺三角形である。

content.content: Two of the sides are equal. Thus, triangle ABC is an isosceles triangle.
Links two sentences and expresses a cause-and-effect relationship. A formal literary expression, often used in academic papers in mathematics, philosophy, and so on. それゆえに and ゆえに can also be used.
【それを】

content: あれほど考え直すように言ったのに君は会社をやめた。それを今になってもう一度雇ってくれだなんて、いったい何を考えてるんだ。

content.content: I told you so many times to reconsider, but you still quit the company. And now you’re asking me to rehire you—what in the world are you thinking?

content: A:もう一度やり直そうよ。

content.content: Let’s give it another try.
B:別れようって言ったのはあなたよ。それを今さらなによ。
You’re the one who said you wanted to break up. And now you’re saying this?

content: 契約したのは1年前だ。それを今になって解約したいと言ってきても無理だ。

content.content: It was a year ago that we fixed the contract. You can’t all of a sudden say you want to cancel it now.

This expression means “despite that; and yet.” It is used to criticize another person about a current situation that involves some kind of change from a previous situation. It is often used with 今さら (now; at this late date) and 今になって (now that things have come to such a pass).
【たい】
1. R-たい

content: ああ、暑い。なにか冷たいものが飲みたい。

content.content: Wow, it’s so hot. I want to drink something cold.

content: A:子供はこんな時間までテレビを見てはいけません。

content.content: Children shouldn’t watch TV until this late.
B:ぼく、はやく大人になりたいなあ。
I really wish I could be a grown-up soon.

content: 老後は暖かい所でのんびり暮らしたい。

content.content: I want to spend my old age living a peaceful, unhurried life in a warm place.

content: その町には若い頃の苦い思い出があって、二度と行きたくない。

content.content: I have bitter memories of that town from when I was young, so I never want to go there again.

content: 大学をやめたくはなかったのだが、どうしても学資が続かなかった。

content.content: I didn’t want to drop out of university, but I just couldn’t manage to pay the expenses.

content: 今は単身赴任だが、来年3月までになんとか家族そろって住むところを見つけたい。

content.content: Now my job has me working away from my family, but by March of next year,  one way or another, I want to find a place for us all to live together.

content: A:来月も続けて受講されますか。

content.content: Will you continue taking classes next month?
B:続けたいんですが、ちょっと時間がなくて。
I’d like to continue, but I just don’t have time.

content: A:将来はどうなさるんですか。

content.content: What will you do in the future?
B:インテリア・デザインの会社で働きたいと思っていますが、まだわかりません。
I’m thinking I would like to work for an interior design company, but I’m not sure yet.

Expresses the desire or strong wish of the speaker (or the listener, in the case of an interrogative sentence) to accomplish a certain act. Conjugated in the same way as adjectives. When emphasizing the object, as in

content: , the particle を is changed to が and the form ...がR-たい is used. R-たい expressions are often softened by using the forms -たいんです or -たいと思っています, as in
and

. Also, in situations when politeness is required, it is usual to avoid direct expressions such as なにか飲みたいですか (Do you want something to drink?) and use なにか飲みますか (Will you have something to drink?) or 飲物はいかがですか (May I offer you something to drink?) instead.

content.content: ...たい（です）cannot be used to express the wish or desire of a third person. In such cases, the form ...たがる, or expressions of conjecture such as ...らしい and ...ようだ, are used instead. Quotation forms such as ...と言っていますmay also be used to report a third person’s wish.
（例）森田さんは古い車を売りたいらしい。
Apparently Morita-san wants to sell his old car.
（例）息子は友達となにかあったのか、学校に行きたくないと言っています。
I don’t know if my son had some kind of trouble with a friend or what, but he’s saying he doesn’t want to go to school.
However, R-たい can sometimes be used for a third person, when it does not come at the end of a sentence.
（例）和夫はバイクを買いたくて、夏休みはずっとガソリンスタンドで働いていた。
Kazuo wanted to buy a motorcycle, so he worked all summer at a gas station.
（例）ツアーに参加したい人は 15 日までに申し込んで下さい。
Those who want to join the tour, please apply by the 15th.
2. R-たいんですが

content: A:住民登録について聞きたいんですが、何番の窓口でしょうか。

content.content: I’d like to inquire about resident registration. Which counter would  that be?
B:3番へどうぞ。
Please go to Counter No.

content: A:フェスティバルの日程が知りたいんですが。

content.content: I’d like to know the schedule of the festival.
B:そこにパンフレットがありますから、お持ち下さい。
Please take a copy of the pamphlet over there.

content: A:すみません、ちょっとお聞きしたいんですが。

content.content: Excuse me, could I ask you something...?
B:はい、なんでしょう。
Yes, what is it?
Used to preface a polite request.
3. R-たがる

content: 自信がない人ほどいばりたがるものだ。

content.content: It’s the people who lack confidence who like to throw their weight around the most.

content: 入社後一年はやめたがる人が多いが、それを過ぎるとたいていはながく勤めるようだ。

content.content: Many employees want to quit within their first year of joining the company, but once they get past the first year, they tend to stay for a long time.
【たがる】
【たいがい】

content: あの人は、たいがい9時ごろ来ます。8時ごろの時もありますが。

content.content: That person usually arrives at around nine o’clock... but sometimes at eight or so.

content: 私は、朝食は、たいがいパンですね。

content.content: I usually have bread for breakfast.

content: そんなに遠くない所なら、たいがいは自転車を使うことにしています。

content.content: If I’m going somewhere that’s not so far away, I generally try to use my bicycle.

content: 試験の成績が悪かった人は、たいがいの場合、追試を受けることになっています。

content.content: In most cases, students who get a bad score are expected to take a make-up exam.

Used with respect to habitual activities, to express that their frequency or likelihood is high. May also be used in the forms たいがいは and たいがいの場合（は）. Cannot be used to make a conjecture about the future.
（×）今晩はたいがい7時には帰るでしょう。
He’ll usually be back at seven o’clock tonight.
（○）今晩はおそらく7時には帰るでしょう。
He’ll probably be back at seven o’clock tonight.

When used in the form たいがいのN, as in たいがいの人 (most people) or たいがいの町 (most towns), it means that the proportion of something is high, and it can be replaced by 大部分のN (the majority of N). たいてい (most) can also be used.
【たいした】
1. たいしたNだ

content: たいした人物だ。たった一人で今の事業をおこしたのだから。

content.content: He’s an amazing person. He created this business single-handedly.

content: 中国語を1年習っただけであれだけ話せるんだから、たいしたものだ。

content.content: It’s really something that she can speak Chinese so fluently after studying it for only a year.

content: あんなに大勢のお客さんに一人でフルコースの料理を作るなんて、たいした腕前だ。

content.content: For one person to be able to prepare full-course meals for so many customers is an amazing skill.

content: A:あの人、紹介状も持たずに社長に会いに行ったそうよ。

content.content: I heard he went to see the company president without even taking a letter of invitation.
B:たいした度胸ね。
That takes a lot of nerve, doesn’t it.
Means that someone’s activities or achievements are remarkable. The N slot is filled by nouns such as もの (thing), 人 (person), 人物 (person, man/woman), 腕前 (skill), 度胸 (courage, nerve), 力量 (capacity).
2. たいしたNではない

content: たいしたものではありませんが、おみやげにと思って買ってきました。

content.content: It’s nothing special, but I bought it with the idea it might do as a souvenir.

content: 私にとってボーナスが多いか少ないかはたいした問題ではない。休みが取れるかどうかが問題だ。

content.content: For me, whether or not I get a big bonus is not important. My concern is whether or not I can take time off.

content: A:朝から病院って、なにか大変なことがあったんですか。

content.content: You said you were at the hospital this morning? Was it anything serious?
B:いや、たいしたことではありません。家のねこがちょっとけがをしただけです。
No, it’s nothing serious. My cat was slightly injured, that’s all.
Means that something is not very important or serious.
3. たいしたことはない

content: A:お宅の奥さん、料理がお上手だそうですね。

content.content: I hear that your wife is a good cook.
B:いや、たいしたことはありませんよ。
No, not that good.

content: A:日本語、うまいですね。

content.content: Your Japanese is very good.
B:いや、たいしたことはありません。敬語の使い方なんか、まだまだです。
No, it’s not that good. I still struggle with using honorific language and things like that.

content: A:かぜの具合いはいかがですか。

content.content: How is your cold?
B:おかげさまで、たいしたことはありません。
Thank you for your concern. It’s not that bad.
Used to deny the extent of something, with the sense of それほど...ではない (not that much). In

content: and
, it is used as a response to a compliment and conveys a feeling of modesty.

content.content: 【たいして...ない】

content: きょうはたいして寒くないね。散歩にでも行こうか。

content.content: It’s not particularly cold today. Shall we take a walk?

content: あのすし屋は高すぎる。たいしてうまくもないのに。

content.content: That sushi restaurant is too expensive. It’s not particularly good, either.

content: あの人、うまいねえ。大して練習しているわけでもないのに。

content.content: He’s really good, isn’t he. Even though he doesn’t practice all that much.

content: 大して有能でもないのに、あの議員は勤続 25 年だそうだ。一体どんな人が投票しているんだろう。

content.content: I hear that Diet member has held his seat continuously for 25 years, despite not being especially capable. I wonder what kind of people are voting for him.
Followed by a negative form and expresses that the degree of something is not very great. Often combined with のに (despite, even though) and used to express a negative evaluation, as in

content: , and
. Can also be paraphrased using大した, as in the following paraphrases of
: 大した能力でもないのに (although he doesn’t have much capability), 能力は大したことがないのに (even though his ability is not that good).

content.content: 【たいてい】

content: あの人は、たいてい9時ごろ来ます。8時ごろの時もありますが。

content.content: That person generally arrives at around nine o’clock... but sometimes at eight or so.

content: 私は、朝食は、たいていパンですね。

content.content: I usually have bread for breakfast.

content: そんなに遠くない所なら、たいていは自転車を使うことにしています。

content.content: If I’m going somewhere that’s not very far, I usually try to use my bicycle.

content: 試験の成績が悪かった人は、たいていの場合、追試を受けることになっています。

content.content: In most cases, students who get a bad score are expected to take a make-up exam.
Used with respect to habitual activities and expresses that their frequency or probability is high. Cannot be used to make a conjecture about the future.
（×）今晩はたいてい7時には帰るでしょう。
He’ll generally be back by seven o’clock tonight.
（○）今晩はおそらく7時には帰るでしょう。
He’ll probably be back by seven o’clock tonight.

May be used in the forms たいていは and たいていの場合 (は). When used in the form たいていのN, as in たいていの人 (most people) or たいていの町 (most towns), it means that there is a high proportion of something and it can be replaced by 大部分のN (the majority of N). たいがい (most) can also be used.
【たいへん】
1. たいへん

content: 《教師が生徒に》はい、たいへんよくできました。

content.content: 《Teacher to student》Yes, very well done.

content: 先日は大変結構なものをちょうだいし、ありがとうございました。

content.content: Thank you for the lovely gift we received from you the other day.
Expresses that the degree of something is extreme. Slightly formal. In spoken Japanese, とても and すごく are more commonly used.
2. たいへんだ

content: たいへんだ。さいふがない。

content.content: Oh, no! I can’t find my wallet.

content: 日曜日も仕事ですか。大変ですねえ。

content.content: You have to work on Sunday, too? That must be tough.

content: え？　あそこのうち、子供が3人とも大学に行ってるの？　親は大変だ。

content.content: What? All three children in that family are in college? That must be hard on the parents.
Expresses surprise, sympathy, or deep emotion with respect to something unusual or unexpected.
3. たいへんなN

content: きのうはたいへんな雨でしたね。

content.content: The rain yesterday was awful, wasn’t it?

content: あのピアニストの才能は大変なものだ。

content.content: That pianist’s talent is extraordinary.

content: 家族のうち二人も入院だ。大変なことになった。

content.content: Two members of the family have been hospitalized. Things are serious.
Used to describe something unusual or unexpected. Can be used for both positive and negative evaluations.
【たかが】
1. たかがN

content: かしこいと言ってもたかが子どもだ。言うことに、いちいち腹を立ててはいけないよ。

content.content: He may be clever, but he’s only a child. You shouldn’t get annoyed by every little thing he says.

content: たかが皿1枚に 10 万円も払うのはばかげている。

content.content: It’s crazy to pay 100,000 yen for just one single plate.

content: たかが証明書一枚のために朝から2時間も待たされるなんて、ひどく能率の悪い役所だ。

content.content: I’ve had to wait two whole hours this morning to get just one certificate. What a horribly inefficient government office this is.

content: たかが1泊の旅行のためにどうしてそんな大きなカバンがいるのよ。

content.content: Why do you need such a large bag for just an overnight trip?

content: A:ぼく、この服いやだ。

content.content: I don’t like this outfit.
B:たかが服のことでなんだ。気に入らないなら家にいなさい。
They’re just clothes—why are you making such a fuss? If you don’t like them, stay at home.

Expresses a low evaluation of the noun to which it is attached, in the sense that that thing is not special or of little importance. Followed by expressions of value judgment, such as ばからしい (foolish, silly) or 気にするな (Don’t worry about it). Often used in the forms たかがNのために and たかがNのことで.
2. たかが...ぐらいで［たかが　N／A／V　ぐらいで］［たかが　N／Na 　 なぐらいで］

content: たかが風邪ぐらいで学校を休まなくてもよい。

content.content: There is no need to take a day off school simply because you have a cold.

content: たかが試験に失敗したぐらいでくよくよすることはない。

content.content: There is no need to brood just because you failed an exam.

content: たかが絵画展に入選したぐらいでこんなに祝っていただくのはなんだか恥ずかしいです。

content.content: I feel somewhat embarrassed to be given such a big celebration simply for having my painting selected for an exhibition.

content: たかが旅さきの安いおみやげぐらいで、そんなにお礼をいっていただくと困ります。

content.content: You needn’t thank me so much for just a cheap souvenir from my trip.
Means “for/because of such a small thing.” Used to say “there’s no need to do...because of X” or “there’s no need to worry about X.”
【たかだか】

content: あれはそんなに高くないと思うよ。たかだか 3000 円ぐらいのもんだろう。

content.content: I don’t think that (item) is so expensive. Probably only about 3,000 yen, at most.

content: 今度の出張はそんなに長くならないでしょう。のびたとしても、たかだか一週間程度のものだと思います。

content.content: I don’t think this business trip will be very long. Even if it’s extended, I think it’ll only be about a week at most.

content: ちょっとぐらい遅刻してもしかられないよ。あの先生なら、たかだか「これから気をつけてください」と言う程度だと思うよ。

content.content: You won’t get scolded for being a little late. I think the most that teacher will say is just “be careful from now on.”

content: 長生きしたとしてもたかだか90 年の人生だ。私は、一瞬一瞬が生の充実感で満たされているような、そんな人生を送りたいと思っている。

content.content: Even a long life is not more than ninety years. I want to live a life in which every moment is filled with a sense of accomplishment.

Used to make a conjecture that the quantity or extent of something probably won’t be very great, even based on a generous estimate. Often used with ぐらい or 程度. Cannot be used if the speaker is stating something as a fact rather than an assumption.
（×）これは安かったですよ。たかだか 2000 円でした。
This was cheap. It was at most 2,000 yen.
（○）たった 2000 円でした。
This was only 2,000 yen.
【たがる】［R-たがる］

content: 子供というものはなんでも知りたがる。

content.content: Children want to know everything.

content: 子供は歯医者に行きたがらない。

content.content: Children don’t like going to the dentist.

content: 父は海外旅行に行きたがっているが、母は行きたくないようだ。

content.content: My father wants to travel abroad, but my mother doesn’t seem to want to go.

content: 夏になると、みんな冷たくてさっぱりしたものばかり食べたがるが、それでは夏バテしてしまう。

content.content: When summer comes, all everybody wants to eat is cold, mildly-flavored food, but that leads to summer fatigue.

content: 避難している住民は一刻も早く家に帰りたがっている。

content.content: The evacuated residents want to go home as soon as possible.

content: リーさんは留学してまだ半年だが、家族のことが心配で国に帰りたがっている。

content.content: Lee-san has only been studying abroad for six months, but he wants to go home because he’s worried about his family.

content: 教授はこの実験を大学院の学生にさせたがっているが、今のような研究態勢では無理なのではないだろうか。

content.content: The professor wants to have graduate students do this experiment, but that may not be possible, given current trends in research.
Used to express the wishes or desires of a third person. Takes the form V-たがっている when a current situation is being expressed.

When たがる is not used, indirect expressions such as たいと言っている, たいらしい, and たいそうだ are used instead. たがる is not used when the speaker says something from the perspective of a third person, as in the example below.
（例）A:山本さん、どうしてパーティーに来なかったんでしょう。
I wonder why Yamamoto-san didn’t come to the party.
B:佐野に会いたくないからだよ。
Because she doesn’t want to see Sano.
On the other hand, たがる is used when the speaker is repeating what a third person thinks of him/her or has said about him/her.
（例）彼は僕が社長になりたがっていると思っているらしいが、僕はそんなつもりはまったくない。
He seems to think I want to become company president, but I have no such intention at all.
【がる】
【ただ】
1. ただ〈limit, restriction〉

content: その絵はただ古いだけであまり値打がない。

content.content: That painting is just old; it doesn’t have much value.

content: 悪いのはこちらの方だから、ただひたすら謝るほかはない。

content.content: It’s our fault, so all we can do is to keep apologizing.

content: 部下はただ命令に従うのみだ。

content.content: The only thing subordinates can do is to obey orders.

content: ただご無事をお祈りするばかりでございます。

content.content: I can only but pray that you are all right.

content: ただ一度会っただけなのにあの人が忘れられない。

content.content: I’ve only met him once, and yet I can’t forget him.

content: これまで学校をただの1日も休んだことはない。

content.content: Until now I haven’t missed even one day of school.

content: 外はただ一面の雪であった。

content.content: Outside everything was covered in a blanket of snow.
Expresses a limitation, in the sense that there is nothing except such-and-such. Often used in combination with だけ, のみ or ばかり. Means “only such-and-such.” Example

content: means “only to apologize.” When ただ expresses the scarcity of an amount, as in
and
, it can be replaced by たった or ほんの.
おもしろい計画だね。ただ金がかかりそうだ。

content.content: It’s an interesting plan. But it will probably cost a lot.

content: A:このイスはずいぶんしっかりした作りですね。

content.content: This chair is very solidly built, isn’t it?
B:ええ、ただ少し重いのでお年寄りにはちょっと不便かもしれません。
Yes, but it’s a little heavy, so it might be a bit hard for elderly people to use.

content: あいつは悪いやつだ。ただ家族にはやさしいようだが。

content.content: He’s not a good guy. But apparently he’s nice to his family.

content: A:お母さん、アメリカに留学する話。賛成してくれるでしょ？

content.content: Mom, about studying abroad in America.... You’d agree to that, wouldn’t you?
B:私はいいんだけど、ただね、お父さんがどういうかと思って…。
It’s fine with me, but you know, I wonder what your father will say....
Used to supplement a preceding statement or to describe additional conditions or exceptions. Spoken language. In written language, ただしis used.
【ただし】

content: テニスコートの使用料は1時間千円。ただし、午前中は半額となります。

content.content: The fee to use the tennis court is 1,000 yen an hour. However, in the morning it’s half-price.

content: ハイキングの参加費はバス代を含めて一人2千円です。ただし、昼食は各自ご用意ください。

content.content: The fee for taking part in the hike, including the cost of the bus, is 2,000 yen per person. However, please bring your own lunch.

content: 病人は少し落ち着いてきましたから面会はかまいません。ただし、興奮するといけませんから、あまり長く話さないようにしてください。

content.content: The patient is beginning to stabilize, so you may visit him, but he shouldn't get over-excited, so please don’t talk too long.

content: 日曜日は閉店します。ただし、祭日が日曜日と重なる場合は開店します。

content.content: We’re closed on Sundays. However, when a public holiday falls on a Sunday, then we’re open.

content: 診察時間は夜7時まで。ただし、急患はこの限りではない。

content.content: Consultation hours are until 7:00 p.m. However, this doesn’t apply to emergency cases.
Used to indicate details of special note or exceptions concerning something that was previously stated.
【ただでさえ】

content: お父さんはただでさえうるさいのだから、病気にでもなったらああしろ、こうしろと大変だろうね。

content.content: Father is demanding as it is, so if he got sick or something he’d always be saying “do this, do that” and it would be awful.

content: ただでさえ人手がたりなくて困っているのに、こんな小さな会社で一度に三人もやめられたらどうしようもない。

content.content: We have a shortage of staff as it is. If three people all quit such a small company at the same time, we wouldn’t know what to do.

Means “something is such-and-such under normal circumstances.” Used to say that since something is or has a tendency of being a certain way under normal circumstances, extraordinary circumstances would aggravate the situation.
【たっけ】

content: きのうの晩ご飯、なに食べたっけ。どうもよく覚えていないな。

content.content: What was it that I ate for supper yesterday? I really don’t remember....

content: A:試験は何課からだったっけ。

content.content: Which lessons does the exam cover again?
B:5課からだよ。
From Lesson
【っけ】
【たって】
1. ...たって［A-くたって］［V-たって］

content: 遅くなったって、必ず行きますよ。

content.content: Even if I’m late, I’ll definitely go.

content: あの人はいくら食べたって太らないんだそうだ。

content.content: I hear that man doesn’t put any weight on, no matter how much he eats.

content: いまごろ来たって遅い。食べ物は何も残っていないよ。

content.content: It’s too late to be arriving at this hour. There isn’t any food left.

content: あの人はどんなにつらくたって、決して顔に出さない人です。

content.content: No matter how hard things are for that woman, she never shows it.

content: いくら高くたって買うつもりです。めったに手に入りませんから。

content.content: No matter how expensive it is, I’m going to buy it. Because it’s almost never available.

content: 笑われたって平気だ。たとえ一人になっても最後までがんばるよ。

content.content: I don’t care if people laugh at me. Even if I’m the only one, I’ll stick it out to the end.
An informal, spoken language equivalent of ても.
【ても】
2. ...たってa. ...ったって

content: 高いったって一万円も出せば買える。

content.content: You may think it’s expensive, but you can buy it if you shell out 10,000 yen.

content: A:日曜日なんだから、どっか出かけましょうよ。

content.content: It’s Sunday, so let’s go out somewhere.
B:出かけるったって、どこも人でいっぱいだよ。
Go out? But everywhere it’s packed with people.

content: ストレス解消には、なんてったってスポーツが一番ですよ。

content.content: When all is said and done, the best thing for getting rid of stress is sports.
This is an informal equivalent of といっても and a variant of たって, pronounced with a glottal stop (っ). In addition to なんてったって, as in

content: , the expression なんたって can also be used.

content.content: 【といっても】b. V-ようったって

content: 帰ろうったって、こんな時間じゃもう電車もバスもない。

content.content: Even if I wanted to go home, there aren’t any more trains or buses at this hour.

content: こんなにへいが高くては、逃げようったって逃げられない。

content.content: With a fence this high, I couldn’t escape even if I wanted to.

content: 連絡しようったって、どこにいるかさえわからないのに無理だ。

content.content: We don’t even know where he is, so it wouldn’t be possible to contact him even if we wanted to.

content: A:ちょっと休もうよ。

content.content: Let’s stop and rest for a while.
B:休もうたってベンチもなにもないよ。
You say let’s rest, but there aren’t any benches or anything.
An informal, spoken language equivalent of V-ようといっても. Means “although one wants to do something....” Followed by expressions that mean “such a thing is difficult or impossible.”
【たて】［R-たてのN］［R-たてだ］

content: 覚えたての外国語で話してみる。

content.content: I’ll try to speak in the foreign language I’ve just learned.

content: ここのパンは焼きたてで、おいしい。

content.content: This bread is freshly baked, and it’s delicious.

content: 彼女は先生になりたてだ。

content.content: She’s just become a teacher.

content: 畑でとれたてのトマトをかじった。

content.content: I bit into a tomato that I’d just picked in the garden.

content: しぼりたてのオレンジジュースはいかがですか。

content.content: Would you like some fresh-squeezed orange juice?

content: 《貼紙》ペンキぬりたて。さわるな。

content.content: 《written notice》Wet paint. Do not touch.
Attaches to the stem of a verb and expresses the meaning “has just been V.” The range of verbs that can be used with this expression is limited.
（×）読みたての本。
A freshly read book.
（○）読んだばかりの本。
A book I’ve just read.
【たとえ】

content: たとえその事実を知っていたところで、私の気持ちは変わらなかっただろう。

content.content: Even if I’d known the truth, my feelings wouldn’t have changed.

content: たとえ子どもでもやったことの責任はとらなくてはいけない。

content.content: Even a child has to take responsibility for what he or she has done.

content: たとえどんなところに住もうとも、家族がいればいい。

content.content: It doesn’t matter where I live, as long as my family is there.

content: たとえ大金をつまれたとしてもそんな仕事はやりたくない。

content.content: I wouldn’t want to do a job like that for all the money in the world.
Means “even supposing that, even if....” たとえ is followed by expressions of concession, such as ても, とも, たところで and としても. 住もうとも in

content: is the written language equivalent of 住んだとしても.

content.content: 【たとえば】

content: 飲物でしたら、たとえばコーヒー、紅茶、ジュースなどを用意してあります。

content.content: For beverages, we have coffee, tea, soft drinks, and so on.

content: 日本語の中には、たとえばパン、ドア、ラジオなどたくさんの外来語が入っている。

content.content: In Japanese, there are many loan words, such as pan (bread), doa (door), rajio (radio), and so on.

content: ゆっくり過ごすとしたら、たとえば温泉なんかどうですか。

content.content: If you want to spend some time relaxing, how about a hot spring or something?

content: A:このごろ運動不足なんだ。だけどスポーツするひまもないし金もないし。

content.content: I haven’t been getting enough exercise lately. But I have no time to play sports, and no money either.
B:わざわざ出かけなくても、たとえばバスをやめて、駅まで歩くとかいろいろあるでしょ。
Even if you don’t make a special effort to go somewhere, you can do all sorts of things, like stop using the bus and start walking to the train station.

content: たとえばこの方程式のXを2とすると、Yは5になる。

content.content: Supposing that X in this equation is 2, then Y will be

content: たとえば今ここに1億円あるとしたら、何に使いたい？

content.content: Say that there’s a hundred million yen here, right now. What would you want to use it for?

content: たとえば地球上に飲み水がだんだんなくなっていくとしますね。そういう場合どうするか。海水の淡水化ということが当然考えられるでしょう。

content.content: Suppose that all the drinking water were gradually disappearing from the earth. What would we do in that case? Desalinating sea water would naturally be one thing to consider.
Used to give a concrete example of something introduced previously. When the example is hypothetical, as in

content: and
, たとえば is followed by an expression such as とすると or としたら.

content.content: 【たび】→
【このたび】
【たびに】［Nのたびに］［V-るたびに］

content: 健康診断のたびに、太りすぎだと言われる。

content.content: Every time I have a check-up, I’m told that I’m too fat.

content: 山に行くたびに雨に降られる。

content.content: Every time I go to the mountains, I get rained on.

content: 父は出張のたびにかならずその土地の土産を買ってくる。

content.content: My father always makes sure to buy us local souvenirs every time he goes on a business trip.

content: ふるさとは帰るたびに変わっていって、昔ののどかな風景がだんだんなくなっていく。

content.content: I see changes in my hometown every time I go back, and the tranquil scenery of the old days is gradually disappearing.

content: 彼女は会うたびにちがうメガネをかけている。

content.content: She’s wearing a different pair of glasses every time I see her.

content: この写真を見るたびにむかしを思い出す。

content.content: Every time I look at this photo, I recall the past.
Means “each time,” “every time I do...I always....”
【たぶん】

content: たぶん田中さんも来るでしょう。

content.content: I think Tanaka-san will probably come, too.

content: あしたはたぶん雨だから、今日のうちに洗濯しておこう。

content.content: It’ll probably rain tomorrow, so I’m going to get the laundry done today.

content: A:だいじょうぶでしょうか。

content.content: Is this OK?
B:たぶん。
Probably.

content: これでたぶん足りると思うけど、念のために、もう少しもっていこう。

content.content: I think this will probably be enough, but I’ll take a little more, just in case.

Expresses a supposition on the part of the speaker. Though weaker than きっと (certainly), indicates that the degree of possibility is quite high. In comparison to おそらく (perhaps, presumably), it is a more informal expression with the feel of spoken language.
【たまらない】
1. たまらない

content: A:毎日、車の音がうるさくて眠れないんです。

content.content: Every day, I can’t sleep because of the noise of the cars.
B:それはたまりませんね。
That’s terrible.

content: A:あの湖ではおもしろいほど魚がつれるんだよ。

content.content: At that lake you can really enjoy some good fishing.
B:つり好きにはたまらないね。
That’s pure delight for a keen fisherman, isn’t it.

content: A:戦争で家も家族も全部なくしたんだそうだ。

content.content: I hear he lost everything in the war, including his home and family.
B:たまらない話ね。
What a tragic story.
Originally meant “unable to endure.” Example

content: means “so awful that one can’t stand it,”
means “so good that one doesn’t know what to do,” and
means “painful to hear.”

content.content: 2. ...てたまらない

content: 和子はあしたから夏休みだと思うとうれしくてたまらなかった。

content.content: Kazuko was beside herself with joy when she realized summer vacation was starting tomorrow.

content: 最近はじめたばかりのスキューバダイビングがおもしろくてたまらない。

content.content: Scuba diving, which I’ve just started, is so much fun that I just love it.
【てたまらない】
【ため】
1. Nのため〈benefit〉

content: こんなにきついことをいうのも君のためだ。

content.content: It’s for your sake that I say such harsh things.

content: みんなのためを思ってやったことだ。

content.content: I did it with everyone’s good in mind.

content: 家族のために働いている。

content.content: I’m working for the sake of my family.

content: 子供たちのためには自然のある田舎で暮らすほうがいい。

content.content: For children, it’s better to live in the countryside surrounded by nature.

content: 過労死という言葉がありますが、会社のために死ぬなんて馬鹿げていると思います。

content.content: There is the word karooshi (death from overwork), but I think it’s ridiculous to die for the sake of your company.
Follows a noun denoting a person or a thing and indicates some kind of benefit for that person/thing. Nがため is an equivalent but old-fashioned expression.
2. ...ために〈purpose〉a. ...ために［Nのために］［V-るために］

content: 世界平和のために国際会議が開かれる。

content.content: An international conference for world peace will be held.

content: ここの小学校では異文化理解のために留学生をクラスに招待している。

content.content: At this elementary school they invite exchange students to classes for the purpose of intercultural understanding.

content: 外国語を習うためにこれまでずいぶん時間とお金を使った。

content.content: I have used quite a lot of time and money to learn foreign languages.

content: 入場券を手に入れるために朝早くから並んだ。

content.content: I queued from early morning in order to get an entrance ticket.

content: 家を買うために朝から晩まで働く。

content.content: I work from dawn to dusk in order to buy a house.

content: 疲れをいやすためにサウナへ行った。

content.content: I went to a sauna in order to get rid of my tiredness.

Expresses purpose. However, in order for ために to express purpose, the subject of both clauses in the sentence must be the same. Therefore Example 1 below has the meaning of purpose, but Example 2 only has the meaning of cause.
（例1）（私は）息子を留学させるために大金を使った。
In order to send my son to study abroad I spent a lot of money.
（例2）息子が留学するために（私は）大金を使った。
Because my son was to study abroad I spent a lot of money.
In addition, a clause that expresses something that can be done by one’s own will is preceded by ために. ように, instead of ために, is used when aiming to achieve a certain situation.
（×）聞こえるために大きい声で話した。
I spoke loudly for hearing.
（○）聞こえるように大きい声で話した。
I spoke loudly in order to be heard.
（×）よく冷えるために冷蔵庫に入れておいた。
I put it in the fridge to get cold.
（○）よく冷えるように冷蔵庫に入れておいた。
I put it into the fridge so that it would get cold.
b. V-んがため

content: 生きんがための仕事だ。

content.content: It’s work for the purpose of making a living.

content: 子供を救わんがため命を落とした。

content.content: He lost his life for the sake of a child.
Formed by replacing ない with ん in V-ない. する becomes せんがため. Means “for the purpose of....” It is a literary expression and is used as an idiomatic expression. Example

content: means “for the purpose of living,” and
means “for the purpose of saving.” There is also a similar expression V-たいがため.

content.content: 3. ...ため〈cause〉a. ...ため［Nのため］［Na なため］［A／V　ため］

content: 過労のため3日間の休養が必要だ。

content.content: Three days off are needed due to overwork.

content: 暑さのために家畜が死んだ。

content.content: The livestock died from excessive heat.

content: 事故のために現在5キロの渋滞です。

content.content: Due to an accident there is a traffic jam for the next five kilometers.

content: 台風が近づいているために波が高くなっている。

content.content: The waves are getting bigger because a typhoon is approaching.

content: 去年の夏は気温が低かったために、この地方では米は不作だった。

content.content: The temperature was low last summer, so the rice didn’t grow very well in this region.

content: 株価が急落したために市場が混乱している。

content.content: Stock prices have suddenly gone down, so the market is in trouble.

content: この辺は、5年後にオリンピックの開催が予定されているために、次々と体育施設が建設されている。

content.content: The Olympic Games are to be held in this area in five years, so sports facilities are being built one after another.
Means “because of....” Other similar expressions include せいで and おかげで.
b. ひとつには...ためである

content: 彼の性格が暗いのは、ひとつにはさびしい少年時代を送ったためである。

content.content: One reason why he has a gloomy personality is that he had a lonely youth.

content: 市民ホールが建たなかったのはひとつには予算不足のためである。

content.content: One of the reasons the public hall was not built was a lack of funds.
Used to express one of the causes of something. Often used in written language.
c. ...のは...ためだ→
【ためし】
1. ためしに...てみる

content: 先月できたレストランはおいしいという評判だ。ためしに一度行ってみよう。

content.content: The restaurant that was opened last month is said to have good food. Let’s go and try it once.

content: テレビで宣伝していたシャンプー、ためしに買ってみましょう。

content.content: Let’s try out the shampoo they were advertising on TV.

content: 新発売のインスタントラーメンためしに買ってみたがおいしくなかった。

content.content: I tried the newly marketed noodles, but they were not very good.
Means “try out; see if it is good or bad.”
2. V-たためしがない

content: 彼女は約束の時間を守ったためしがない。

content.content: She never sticks to the time she promised.

content: 彼は競馬が好きだが、彼の予想は一度も当たったためしがない。

content.content: He likes horse-racing, but his predictions have never been right.

content: 彼とはよく食事をするが、おごってくれたためしがない。

content.content: I often have a meal with him, but he never treats me.

content: 息子はあきっぽくて、何をやっても三日と続いたためしがない。

content.content: My son quickly tires of things and has never managed to continue something for more than three days.
Means “there has not been any occasion where....” Carries a feeling of blame or censure.

【たら1】［N／Na　だったら］［A-かったら］［V-たら］One of the conjugations of predicates. Expresses a condition or opportunity. Has the same meaning as と, ば and なら (and expresses a general truth or law.) Tends to be used to describe a particular isolated matter rather than a general condition. In comparison to the other three, there are fewer restrictions on clause-final forms. Often used in spoken language. Polite forms are N/Na でしたら and V-ましたら. There is no polite form for たら clauses with i-adjectives. There is also a slightly old-fashioned expression たらば,  in which ば is appended.

1. ...たら〈not-yet-realized condition〉Expresses the relation of two isolated matters, such as “if X comes about, then Y will, too” or “if X comes about, then it will make Y come about, too.” X expresses both matters that have and have not come about, while Y always expresses something that has not yet come about. Y is used in declaratory sentences stating an unrealized matter or supposition, sentences expressing intention or hope, and indicative sentences which express imperatives, prohibitions, or invitations.
a. ...たら+未実現のことがら

content: 雨だったら道が混雑するだろう。

content.content: If it rains, the road will probably get crowded with traffic.

content: もしも、あまり高かったら誰も買わないでしょう。

content.content: If it should be too expensive, probably no one will buy it.

content: 万一雨が降ったら試合は中止です。

content.content: In the event that it rains, the match will be canceled.

content: この薬を飲んだらすぐにせきはとまりますが、3時間たったら効き目がなくなります。

content.content: If you take this medicine, your cough will stop immediately, but the effect will wear off after three hours.

content: あんなに美人だったら、男性がほうっておかないだろう。

content.content: Such a beauty like that will probably not be left alone by any man.

content: ここまで来たら、一人でも帰れます。

content.content: Once I’ve come this far, I can make my way home alone.

content: そんなにたくさん食べたらおなかをこわしますよ。

content.content: You’ll upset your stomach if you eat so much.

Usage for when Y expresses a statement about matters which have not yet come about. The dictionary form of the predicate, or such a predicate combined with the supposition だろう, are used at the end of sentences.
In

content: , both X and Y are matters which have not yet come about, and when X comes about, then Y will follow. もし or 万一 are sometimes used when making suppositions about uncertain matters which have not yet come about or matters which are unlikely to come about.
is a usage which simply describes future matters that will come about in sequence, and has less of a suppositional meaning.

content.content: In

content: , X has already come about, and based on this a supposition Y is made. X often includes こ／そ／あwords (e.g. ここ, そんな) to indicate a current status.

content.content: たら tends to be used for isolated matters, and is unlikely to be used for general conditions expressing a universal truth or law. However, in spoken language, it is sometimes used for expressing repetition of one’s habit or a certain matter, as the following examples show:

content: いつも、5時になったらすぐ仕事をやめて、テニスをします。

content.content: I always stop working right away and play tennis when it is five o’clock.

content: ここは冬になったら雪が1メートルぐらいつもる。

content.content: We get about three meters of snow here when it’s winter.

content: ふだんは昼ご飯を食べたら昼寝をしますが、今日は買物に行かなければなりません。

content.content: I usually take a nap after lunch, but I have to go shopping today.

content: 古くなったらすぐに新しいのに買いかえるというような生活では、お金は貯まらない。

content.content: You can’t save money if you have the kind of lifestyle where you always buy new things when something gets old.

content: express the meaning “after X is accomplished, Y will be done.” X expresses a time frame in which Y will come about or that the action will be repeated within that time frame. In this case, たらcan be replaced byと.

content.content: b. ...たら+表出・働きかけ

content: この仕事が完成したら、長い休みをとるつもりだ。

content.content: Once this job is completed, I intend to take a long vacation.

content: もしも1千万円の宝くじに当たったら、何でも買ってあげますよ。

content.content: I’ll buy you anything you want if I win 10 million yen in the lottery.

content: 教師になったら子どもたちにものをつくる楽しさを教えたい。

content.content: If I become a teacher, I want to teach children the joy of making things.

content: お風呂に入ったらすぐ寝なさい。

content.content: Go to sleep immediately after your bath.

content: この予防注射をしたら、風呂に入ってはいけません。

content.content: You should not take a bath after you have this vaccination.

content: お酒を飲んだら絶対に運転はするな。

content.content: Never drink and drive.

content: 宿題が済んだら遊びに行ってもいいよ。

content.content: You may go play once you have finished your homework.

content: A:あちらで野田さんに会われますか。

content.content: Will you meet Noda-san there?
B:ええ、その予定ですが。
Yes, that’s the plan.
A:じゃ、お会いになったらよろしくお伝えください。
Well, in that case please give her my regards.

content: もしも遅れたら、連絡してください。

content.content: Please let me know if you’ll be late.

content: 会議が終わったら食事をしに行きましょう。

content.content: Let’s go and have dinner after the meeting is finished.

Expresses meanings such as “When X comes about, let’s do/I want to do Y” and “When X comes about, do Y/don’t do Y/I can do Y/please do Y.” Y contains “expressive” expressions which indicate the speaker’s will/hope or “indicative” expressions, such as commands, prohibitions, permissions, requests, or invitations.

Usually used to express a specific actual outcome about Y, which will come about when X has occurred. X expresses matters that precede Y, and can be replaced by expressions such as “when this happens,” “when you do...,” or “after this.” As shown below, when たら is preceded by a situational predicate such as ある, an i-adjective, or a noun, it means “if that’s the situation”; moreover, if such a situation obtains, the expression shows the will or hope of the speaker or a demand or recommendation to the listener.
When the sentence concerns the listener’s schedule or wish, it is closer to Usage 6 of たら (<introductory utterance>).

content: 暇があったら海外旅行をしたい。

content.content: I’d like to travel abroad if I have time.

content: 暑かったら、窓を開けてください。

content.content: Please open the window if you’re hot.

content: お暇でしたら、いらっしゃいませんか。

content.content: Would you like to visit me if you are free?

content: そんなに勉強が嫌だったら大学なんかやめてしまえ。

content.content: If you dislike studying that much, then quit college.

content: 熱があったら休んでもいいよ。

content.content: You may take time off if you have a fever.

When compared to たら, とand ばhave more restriction on their usage. とcannot be used with “expressive” or “indicative” expressions and when X is a verb indicating action or change, it is odd to use ば for “expressive” or “indicative” meaning.
（×）結婚すれば仕事をやめたい。
I want to quit my job if I marry.
（○）結婚したら仕事をやめたい。
I want to quit my job when I get married.
（×）お風呂に入ればすぐ寝なさい。
Go to sleep as soon as if you have a bath.
（○）お風呂に入ったらすぐ寝なさい。
Go to sleep as soon as you have taken a bath.
c. ...たら+問いかけ

content: 雨だったら試合は中止になりますか。

content.content: If it rains, will the match be canceled?

content: A:結婚したら仕事はやめるの？

content.content: You’re going to quit work when you get married?
B:ううん、しばらく続けるつもりよ。
No, I plan to continue for a while.

content: 万一雨が降ったらどうしましょうか。

content.content: What shall we do in case it rains?

content: A:もし宝くじに当たったら、何に使いますか。

content.content: If you win the lottery, what will you use it for?
B:すぐに使わないで貯金しておきます。
I won’t use it right away, I’ll save it.

content: A:大学を卒業したらどうするつもりですか。

content.content: What are you going to do after you graduate?
B:オーストラリアに留学したいと思っています。
I am thinking of studying abroad in Australia.

content: A:社長はただ今出かけておりますが。

content.content: The company president is currently out of the office.
B:何時ごろでしたらお帰りでしょうか。
What time will he be returning?

content: どのぐらい勉強したら日本語の新聞が読めるようになりますか。

content.content: How long do you have to study to be able to read a Japanese newspaper?
Used in interrogative sentences which require an answer from the listener, in the form X たら Y か.

content: and
are interrogatives, seeking “yes” or “no” answers;
are cases of interrogatives with question words such as “what” and “how”;
are cases where the Y in “is it Y, if X?” is unknown; and
are cases where X is unknown.

content.content: In interrogative sentences where the method or means X for getting a good result is asked about, as in

content: and
, たらcan be replaced byば, but in interrogatives where it is asked what action Y will take when X comes about, as in
, たら is mostly used, and the use of ば is unnatural.

content.content: （×）結婚すれば仕事をやめるつもりですか。
Do you intend to quit your job if you marry?
（○）結婚したら仕事をやめるつもりですか。
Do you intend to quit your job when you get married?
（×）大学を卒業すればどうしますか。
What are you going to do if you graduate from university?
（○）大学を卒業したらどうしますか。
What are you going to do after graduating from university?
d. 疑問詞+V-たら...のか

content: 何度言ったら分かるんだ？

content.content: How many times do I have to tell you so you understand?

content: 人間は戦争という愚行を何度繰り返したら気がすむのであろうか？

content.content: How many times do humans have to repeat the foolish action we call war before they have had enough?

content: 何年たったら一人前になれるのだろうか？

content.content: How many years will it take before I am a full-fledged member of society?

content: 何回繰り返したら覚えられるのか？

content.content: How many times do you have to repeat it before you remember it?

content: どれだけ待ったら平和な世界になるのだろうか？

content.content: How long do we have to wait to see a world at peace?

content: 一体どうしたら今の思いを伝えることができるのか？

content.content: Just how can I best convey my thoughts now?

This is an ironic expression where the たら form of the verb is attached to question words such as 何/どれだけ/どんなに. Means “no matter how ..., things won’t happen the way one wants them to,” and expresses irritation or despair regarding the situation. These sentences end with のか or のだ/のだろう（か）. V-たらcan be replaced by V-ば.
e. ...たらどんなに...か

content: 宝くじに当たったらどんなにうれしいだろう。

content.content: How happy I would be if I won the lottery!

content: 合格したら両親はどんなに喜んでくれるだろうか。

content.content: How happy my parents would be if I passed the examination!

content: 子供たちがもどってきたらどんなににぎやかになることか。

content.content: How lively it will be when the children return!

Means “how good it will be if X comes about.” Used when expressing a strong wish that X will be realized or expressing the feeling that if it comes about, then one would be really happy. だろう（か） or ことかare used at the end of the sentence.
2. ...たら〈counter-factual〉a. ...たら　...だろう／...はずだ

content: あのとき精密検査を受けていたら、手遅れにならなかっただろう。

content.content: Had there been a detailed check-up at that time, it wouldn’t have been too late.

content: 隕石が地球に衝突していなかったら恐竜は絶滅していなかったかもしれない。

content.content: Dinosaurs might not have died out had a meteorite not hit the earth.

content: ひどい話を聞かなかったら、こんなに酔うまで飲んだりしなかったにちがいない。

content.content: If I hadn’t heard the horrible story, I’m sure I wouldn’t have drunk myself to this point.

content: あの時彼と結婚していたら、私の人生はもっと幸せだったはずだ。

content.content: Had I married him at the time, my life would have been happier.

content: あの当時この「薬の害」という本を読んでいたら今ごろ苦しまなくてもよかったのに残念だ。

content.content: What a pity. Had I read the book The Harm of Medicine in those days, I might not have had to suffer as I do now.

content: A:面接試験、うまくいった？

content.content: Did the interview test go all right?
B:うまくいっていたら、こんな顔していないよ。
I wouldn’t look like this if it had gone well.

content: 点数があと 10 点高かったらこの大学に合格できるんだけど。

content.content: I would be able to pass the entrance exam to this university if only my score were ten points higher.

Used to make a supposition different from what has actually happened or the opposite of what has actually happened, and expresses what something would have been like if such were the case. In most cases, the verb is put into the stative form V-ていたら.

When making a supposition which is contrary to the facts in the past, the ta-form of predicates, such as ただろう/はずだ/のに, is used at the end of the sentence. On the other hand, when making a supposition which is contrary to the current situation, the dictionary form, such as ...するのに/のだが, is used, as in

content: and

content.content: In this usage, たら can be replaced by ば, but たら is more colloquial. Refer to ば (Usage 4) for a more detailed explanation of conditional sentence patterns expressing counter-factual matters.
b. ...たらどんなに...か

content: 背があと 10 センチ高かったらどんなによかっただろうか。

content.content: How nice it would be if only I were ten centimeters taller.

content: 10 年前に彼女に会っていたらどんなによかっただろう。

content.content: How nice it would have been had I met her ten years ago.

content.content: If my grandmother were alive, how pleased she would have been.

content: 今すぐあなたに会えたらどんなにうれしいだろうか。

content.content: How happy I would be if I could meet you right now!

Used when X is impossible or contrary to reality, and means “how good it would have been if X were the case.” Expresses the feeling that one has the strong wish that X will come about, but regrets that such a thing cannot ever happen.
When making a supposition contrary to what has already come about, ただろうか is used, as in

content.content: 3. ...たら...た〈already-realized condition〉

content: 空港に着いたら友達が迎えに来ていた。

content.content: When I arrived at the airport, my friend was waiting to meet me.

content: トンネルを出たら一面の銀世界だった。

content.content: Coming out of the tunnel brought us into a winter wonderland.

content: 変な音がするので隣の部屋に行ってみたらねずみがいた。

content.content: I went to the room next door because I heard a strange sound, and there was a mouse.

content: 山田さんは無口でおとなしい人だと思っていたが、よく話をしたらとても面白い人だということが分かった。

content.content: I thought Yamada-san was a quiet, timid person, but when I spoke to him, I realized that he was a very amusing person.

content: お風呂に入っていたら、電話がかかってきた。

content.content: The phone rang when I was in the bath.

content: デパートで買い物していたら、隣の奥さんにばったり会った。

content.content: I ran into the lady from next door when I was shopping at the supermarket.

content: 5月に入ったら急に暑くなった。

content.content: The weather suddenly turned hot right at the beginning of May.

content: 薬を飲んだら熱が下がった。

content.content: My temperature went down when I took the medicine.

content: 会社をやめたらストレスがなくなって元気になった。

content.content: After I quit the company, my stress went away and I recovered.

content: 落ちてもともとと思って試験を受けたら、思いがけず合格した。

content.content: I took the examination thinking I would fail, but I unexpectedly passed it.

content: 部屋の様子が変だと思ったら、案の定、空き巣に入られていた。

content.content: I thought something about the room seemed strange and, just as I feared, someone had broken in.

The XたらYた pattern is used to indicate that both the former and the latter have already come about. It is used when the speaker realizes Y at the point when X has already come about, or when a new situation happens as a result of it. Following Y are expressions stating that something has occurred beyond the speaker’s control, or some fact has been newly discovered or realized.

content: are usages in which the speaker discovers situation Y at the scene where action X has already been done. The discoverer, 私, is not mentioned in Y as in ...たら、私は...した, but instead the speaker uses expressions to portray the situation, such as ...たら...ということが分かった, ...たら...がいた or ...たら...があった.

content.content: （×）隣の部屋に行ったら、私はねずみを見た。
If I go to the room next door, I saw a mouse.
（○）隣の部屋に行ったら、ねずみがいた。
When I went to the room next door, there was a mouse.
Expressions of state, such as V-ていた or Nだった, are used for Y where newly-realized discoveries are expressed, as in

content: and

content.content: On the other hand, if V-たis used instead of V-ていた, the meaning changes as follows.
（例）空港に着いたら友達が迎えに来た。
After I arrived at the airport, my friend came to meet me.

In the example above, the active expression来たis used instead of 来ていた. This is used to indicate that after the speaker arrived at the airport, the friend arrived to meet him, rather than that the speaker found the friend upon arrival, as in

content: above.

content.content: As in

, when what follows the supposition in the second clause is the expected outcome, 案の定 or やっぱりare used; when the result is unexpected, then 案外、意外なことに or 思いがけず are frequently used.

content.content: たら in this usage is often replaced by と. However, if X and Y both indicate the same person’s consecutive action of which that person has control, only と can be used, and not たら.
（×）男は部屋に入ったら友達に電話した。
If the man entered the room, he phoned his friend.
（○）男は部屋に入ると友達に電話した。
The man called his friend when he entered the room.
While と is used in novels or stories, たら is used to describe things which the speaker has directly experienced.
4. ...たらさいご

content: 彼は寝たら最後、まわりでどんなに騒いでも絶対に目をさまさない。

content.content: Once he falls asleep, he won’t wake up no matter how noisy it is around him.

content: 賭事は一度手を出したら最後ずるずると抜けられなくなる人が多い。

content.content: With gambling, many people cannot break free from it once they have given it a try.

content: すっぽんは一度かみついたら最後どんなことがあっても離れない。

content.content: Once a snapping turtle bites something, it won’t let go no matter what happens.
Means that once something has happened, because of its characteristics or a strong determination, the situation will not change subsequently. Often used in the form 一度...たらさいご絶対に....
5. ...たら...で［A-かったらA-いで］［A-かったらA-かったで］［V-たらV-たで］

content: 金というのはあったらあったで使うし、なかったらないで何とかなるものだ。

content.content: Money is something that you’ll spend if you have it, and somehow get by if you don’t.

content: 自動車はあれば便利だが、なかったらなかったで何とかなるものだ。

content.content: A car is convenient if you have one, but you can manage to get by if you don’t.

content: 母は寒がりで冬が苦手だが、それでは夏が好きかというとそうではない。暑かったら暑かったで文句を言っている。

content.content: My mother hates being cold and dislikes winter, but if you think that she likes summer, that’s not the case. If it's hot, she'll complain about that, too.

content: 息子には大学に受かってほしいが、受かったら受かったでお金が要って大変だ。

content.content: I want my son to pass the university entrance examination, but if he does pass, then it’ll be hard because he’ll need money.

content: 平社員のときは給料が少なくて困ったけど、昇進したらしたでつきあいも増えるしやっぱり金はたまらない。

content.content: My low salary was a problem when I was a junior employee, but since being promoted I have more socializing and whatnot to do so I still can’t save any money after all.
Repeats the same adjectives or verbs twice, before and after. Describes a contrasting circumstance that, despite what happens, will ultimately not differ from the present one.
Some sentences express the meaning “there are problems but they are not too bad/they can be managed somehow,” as in

, while other sentences see the situation as undesirable, indicating that “either way it is troublesome/a problem,” as in

...ば...で is a synonymous expression.

6. ...たら〈introductory utterance〉Used to indicate under what condition the action in the second part of the sentence may be carried out, by restricting the scope or giving a warning or explanation in advance. It is, to a certain extent, a fixed idiomatic expression. It can be replaced by ば.
a. ...たら+依頼・勧め〈introductory utterance〉

content: もし差し支えなかったら事情を聞かせてください。

content.content: Please tell me the circumstances, if you don’t mind.

content: よろしかったら、もう一度お電話くださいませんか。

content.content: Would you call me again, if you don’t mind?

content: よかったら、週末、家にいらっしゃいませんか。

content.content: Would you like to visit our home this weekend?
Idiomatic expression used for politely asking the convenience of the other person when making a request or recommendation.
b. ...たら〈introductory utterance〉

content: 私から見たら、こんなことはたいした問題ではない。

content.content: From where I stand, it doesn’t seem like a serious problem.

content: 私に言わせたら、責任はあなたの方にあるんじゃないかと思う。

content.content: If you ask me, I’d say the responsibility lies with you.

content: 一時代前と比べたら、家事は格段に楽になったと言える。

content.content: It can be said that housework has become far easier in comparison with a generation ago.

This is one way of warning in advance from what viewpoint the utterance or judgment in the latter part of the sentence is made. It follows verbs that express a statement, an idea, or a comparison, such as 見る(see), 思う(think) and 比べる(compare), in the first part of the sentence. It is to a certain degree an idiomatic expression.
からしたら or から言ったらare synonymous expressions.
7. V-たら〈suggestion, recommendation〉

content: 立って見てないで、ちょっと手伝ってあげたら。

content.content: Why don’t you lend a hand instead of just standing and watching?

content: 危ないからやめといたら。

content.content: It’s dangerous, so don’t do it.

content: そんなに疲れているなら、すこし休んだら？

content.content: How about resting a little, if you’re so tired?

This is an expression to recommend that the listener take a certain action. The latter half of V-たらどうか is omitted. It is usually used when speaking to someone with whom the speaker is on familiar terms. When it is necessary to speak politely, たらどうですか or いかがですか are used without abbreviating the latter half.

Can be replaced by V-ば; however, たら has the nuance that the speaker is seriously recommending something, while the use of ば can contain the nuance that the speaker in fact is merely stating an option without any particular preference.
