【ったら】
【たらいい】［N／Na　 だったらいい］［A-かったらいい］［V-たらいい］
1. V-たらいい〈suggestion, recommendation〉

content: A:レポートのしめきり間に合いそうもないんだ。どうしたらいいかなあ。

content.content: I don’t think I can meet the deadline for the report. What shall I do?
B:先生に聞いてみたらどう？
How about asking the teacher?

content: A:この急ぎの仕事だれにやってもらおうか？

content.content: Whom should I ask to do this urgent job?
B:山田君に頼んだらいいよ。どんな仕事でもいやな顔しないよ。
You ought to ask Yamada-kun. He’ll cheerfully take on whatever task you give him.

content: A:もう一杯おかわりしようかな、それともやめとこうかな。

content.content: Should I have another helping or should I stop?
B:食べたいだけ食べたらいいじゃないか。そんなに太ってないんだし。
Why not eat as much as you like? You’re not that overweight.

content: ゆっくり休んだらいい。後のことは任せなさい。

content.content: It’s all right to take a long break. Leave the rest to me.

content: もう遅いから残りの仕事はあしたにしたらいい。

content.content: It’s late, so it’s all right for you to do the rest of the work tomorrow.

content: 若いうちにいろいろ苦労したらいいと思う。あとできっと役に立つはずだ。

content.content: I think it is good to have hardships when you are young. The experiences are sure to pay off later on.

Expression for offering or suggesting something to someone. Used when asking for advice about what is the best means or method to get a good result, or when giving advice. When asking for advice, it is used with a question word, such as どうしたらいいか. When advising not to do something, しなければいい can be used, but しなかったらいい would be rather unnatural.
（×）太りたくなければ食べなかったらいい。
If you don’t want to put on weight, it’s good if you don’t eat (too much).
（○）太りたくなければ食べなければいい。
If you don’t want to put on weight, don’t eat (too much).

たらいい and ばいい are synonymous and interchangeable, but たらいいis slightly less formal. When questioning what to do, どうしたら/すればいいかcan be used, but どうするといいcannot be used. However, as a response, たらいい/ばいい/といいwould all be correct.
（×）A:電車の中にかばんを忘れてしまったのですが、どうするといいですか。
I forgot my briefcase on the train. What should I do?
（◯）A:電車の中にかばんを忘れてしまったのですが、どうしたら／すればいいですか。
I forgot my briefcase on the train. What should I do?
B:遺失物係で聞いてみたら／聞いてみれば／聞いてみるといいでしょう。
You ought to ask the staff at the lost-and-found.
2. ...たらいい〈wish, desire〉

content: 生まれてくる子が男の子だったらいいのだが。

content.content: I wish the baby would be a boy.

content: 体がもっと丈夫だったらいいのに。

content.content: I wish I were physically stronger.

content: もう少し給料がよかったらいいのだが。

content.content: I wish my salary were a little higher.

content: もっと家が広かったらいいのになあ。

content.content: I wish my house were bigger.

content: 明日、晴れたらいいなあ。

content.content: How I wish it would be sunny tomorrow.

content: もう少しひまだったらなあ。

content.content: I wish I had a little more free time.

Expresses the speaker’s wish for something to happen. Often accompanied by のに／なあ／のだが at the end of the sentence. When the situation is different from what is hoped or what was hoped for cannot come true, it expresses the meaning “it’s a pity it is not so.” たらなあ is also often used in place of いい, as in
3. ...たらよかった

content: A:このあいだのパーティーおもしろかったわよ。

content.content: The party the other day was fun.
B:僕も行ったらよかった。
I wish I had gone, too.
A:そうよ。来たらよかったのに。どうして来なかったの。
Yes, you should have come. Why didn’t you?
B:アルバイトがあったんだよ。でもあの日はバイト、ひまでね。休んでもよかったんだ。
I had to do my part-time job—but work that day was so slow. You know, I really should have taken the day off.

content: きのう会社の上司とはじめて飲みに行った。彼がもうちょっと話好きだったらよかったのだが、会話が続かなくて困った。

content.content: Yesterday I went drinking with my boss for the first time. It would have been nice if he were a little more talkative, so I had trouble keeping the conversation going.
Indicates one’s regret that something didn’t happen or was not the case. Often accompanied by のに, (のに)なあ or のだが. のに is not usually used when talking about yourself.
（×）僕も行ったらよかったのに。
It would have been nice if I had gone.
（○）僕も行ったら｛よかったんだけど／よかったんだが｝。
If only I had gone it would have been nice.
【たらどうか】［V-たらどうか］

content: 別の方法で実験してみたらどうでしょうか。

content.content: How about experimenting with a different method?

content: 少しお酒でも飲んでみたらいかがですか。気分がよくなりますよ。

content.content: Why don’t you take a little something—even alcohol? You’ll feel better.

content: 遊んでばかりいないで、たまには勉強したらどう？

content.content: Instead of playing all the time, how about studying occasionally?

content: さっさと白状したらどうなんだ。

content.content: Now, come on—let's fess up!

content: アメリカに留学してみたらどうかと先生に勧められた。

content.content: I was encouraged by my teacher to consider study abroad in the U.S.

content.content: Yoshida-kun said that he won’t join the party.
B:もう一度誘ってみたら？
Why don’t you invite him again?

Idiomatic expression used in a proposal or a recommendation. Oten used in the form V-てみたらどうか. Has almost the same meaning as てはどうか, but たらどうか is more colloquial. In colloquial language, たらどうなの／どうかしら is used by women, たらどうなんだ is used by men, and たらどう is used by both men and women. However, in formal situations, たらいかがですか／いかがでしょうか is used.

content: and
are examples of when the listener simply won’t follow the speaker’s warning or recommendation; they imply the speaker’s irritation. The latter half of
is abbreviated and pronounced with a rising tone.

content.content: 【たり】［N／Na　だったり］［A-かったり］［V-たり］
1. ...たり...たりする

content: 休みの日には、ビデオを見たり音楽を聞いたりしてのんびり過ごすのが好きです。

content.content: On my day off I like to relax―watching videos or listening to music.

content: コピーをとったり、ワープロを打ったり、今日は一日中いそがしかった。

content.content: I was busy all day today with photocopying and typing.

content: 子供が大きくなって家族がそろうことはめったにないのですが、年に数回はいっしょに食事したりします。

content.content: My children have grown up so we seldom have the opportunity for the family to get together, but we do things like get together for dinner a couple times a year.

content: 給料日前には昼食を抜いたりすることもある。

content.content: I sometimes skip lunch on the day before payday.

content: アルバイトで来ている学生は曜日によって男子学生だったり女子学生だったりしますが、みなよく働いてくれます。

content.content: Depending on the day, we can have men or women students working part-time, but they all work hard for us.

content: 彼女の絵のモチーフは鳥だったり人だったりするが一貫して現代人の不安が描かれている。

content.content: Her paintings’ motifs may be persons or birds or whatever, but there’s always a common depiction of present-day anxiety.
Points out two or three representative acts among several. There are also cases where only one example is pointed out, but it implies that other examples exist too, as in

content: and
. The verb at the end of the sentence has たりするattached when the sentence ends with this pattern, as in ...たり...たりします／しました.

content.content: （×）きのうの休みにはビデオを見たり、散歩したり、手紙を書きました。
On the holiday yesterday I did things like watching videos, walking, and I wrote a letter.
（○）きのうの休みにはビデオを見たり、散歩したり、手紙を書いたりしました。
On the holiday yesterday I did things like watching videos, walking, and writing a letter.

content: 何か心配なことでもあるのか彼は腕組をして廊下を行ったり来たりしている。

content.content: I don’t know if he’s worried about something, but he’s pacing up and down the corridor with his arms folded.

content: 去年の秋は暑かったり寒かったりして秋らしい日は少なかった。

content.content: Last fall was sometimes hot and sometimes cold, without any real fall-like days.

content: 父は近頃あまり具合いがよくなく、寝たり起きたりだ。

content.content: Father has not been very well lately, lying down and getting up again and again.

content: 薬はきちんと飲まなければいけない。飲んだり飲まなかったりでは効果がない。

content.content: Medicine has to be taken properly; it has no effect if just taken sporadically.

content: くつを買おうと思うが、いいと思うと高すぎたり、サイズがあわなかったりで、なかなか気に入ったのが見つからない。

content.content: I want to buy a pair of shoes, but when I find a pair that I like they’re too expensive or the size doesn’t fit, so I just haven’t been able to get a pair that I like.

content: あすは山間部は晴れたり曇ったりの天気でしょう。

content.content: Tomorrow the mountains will be occasionally sunny and occasionally cloudy.

Expresses a situation where a state or an act alternates repeatedly or there are two contrasting situations. Other expressions frequently used for contrasting situations include あったりなかったり (sometimes exists, and sometimes does not), 上がったり下がったり (going up and down), 泣いたり笑ったり (crying and laughing), 乗ったり降りたり (getting on and off), and 出たり入ったり (coming/going in and out).

content: 英語の生活にもずいぶん慣れたが、早口で話しかけられたりしたらわからなくて困ることも多い。

content.content: I’ve gotten pretty well used to living with English, but when people speak to me very quickly, I can often have problems.

content: その人のいないところで悪口を言ったりしてはいけない。

content.content: One mustn’t say bad things about a person when he is not around.
Implies that there are other instances as well. Example

content.content: That’s strange—no one’s come yet.
B:約束、あしただったりして。
Maybe the appointment is tomorrow?

content: A:佐野さん、遅いわね。

content.content: Sano-san is late.
B:ひとりだけ先に行ってたりして。
Could she have already gone ahead by herself?

This is a way of focusing on one example. Implies that there are other possibilities, and is used when avoiding saying something directly. An indirect, bantering expression. Often used in colloquial speech by young people.
【たりとも】［...たりとも...ない］［Nたりとも...ない］［数量詞+たりとも...ない］

content: 試験まであと一カ月しかない。一日たりとも無駄にはできない。

content.content: There is only one more month before the exam. I can’t waste even one day.

content.content: The water is rapidly being used up. We can’t waste even one drop from now on.

content: 密林の中では、一瞬たりとも油断してはいけない。

content.content: One cannot relax even for a split second in a dense forest.

content: この綱領について変更は一字たりとも許されない。

content.content: Not even one letter of this manifesto may be changed.

content: だれもが敵は一人たりとも逃がさないと決意していた。

content.content: Everyone was determined not to let even one enemy escape.

Expresses the meaning that even the smallest number of people or quantity cannot be tolerated, and is used in forms such as 一人, 一滴, 一日たりとも...ない. 一 is the normal form (number) used. In more informal language, forms such as ひとりも and 一滴も are used. This is a literary expression used for very polite written language or formal spoken language (e.g. in meetings or for public speeches).

【たる】Derived from the literary expression てあり. Gives a solemn impression. Has an exaggerated tone, and is used for extremely polite written language or formal spoken language such as in public speeches.
1. NたるN

content: 国家の指導者たる者は緊急の際にすばやい判断ができなければならない。

content.content: The leader of a nation has to have the ability to make a quick decision in an emergency situation.

content: 国会議員たる者は身辺潔白でなければならないはずである。

content.content: Someone who is a member of the Diet should be completely beyond reproach (lit. squeaky clean).

content: 教師たる者は、すべてにおいて生徒の模範とならねばならないとここに書いてある。

content.content: It says here that a person who is a teacher must be a model for students in every respect.

content: 百獣の王たるライオンをカメラにおさめたいとサファリに参加した。

content.content: He participated in a safari, saying he wanted to take pictures of a lion, the so-called king of beasts.
Means “something that has the (distinguished) qualification mentioned.”
2. NたるとNたるとをとわず

content: 救出にあたっては軍人たると民間人たるとを問わず、総力を結集せよ。

content.content: In rescue work, put all your effort into saving lives, regardless of whether you’re a soldier or a civilian.

content: 医療活動は民間人たると、政府関係者たるとを問わず、全員を平等に扱う。

content.content: Medical work treats everyone equally, regardless of whether they are ordinary citizens or government officials.

content: この法律は市民たると外国人たるとを問わず等しく適用される。

content.content: This law applies equally to all, regardless of whether they are a citizen or a foreigner.
Means “regardless of whether it’s X or Y, both are....”
3. Nたるべきもの

content: それは、指導者たるべき者のとる行動ではない。

content.content: That’s not how a leader should behave.

content: 後継者たるべき者は以下の資格を備えていなければならない。

content.content: A successor should have the following qualifications.

content: 王たるべき者はそのようなことを恐れてはならない。

content.content: A king must not fear such a thing.

Means “a person who ought to have such qualification as...” or “someone who should have the position of....” The latter half of the sentence usually states “must naturally be...,” to describe the desired form of the person with the qualification or position described in the first half.
4. Nたるや

content: そのショーの意外性たるや、すべての人の注目を集めるに十分であった。

content.content: The novelty of the show was enough to get the attention of everyone.

content: その姿たるや、さながら鬼のようであった。

content.content: The figure was almost like a devil.

content: その歌声たるや、聞き入る聴衆のすべてを感動させるすばらしいものであった。

content.content: That voice was so wonderful that it impressed every audience.

content: 救出に際しての彼らの活動たるや、長く記憶にとどめるに十分値するものであった。

content.content: Their activities in doing rescue work were certainly worth keeping in memory for a long time.
Uses a noun which possesses a certain characteristic to emphasize what it expresses. Describes what property it has or what state it is in. Personal names are not used.
（×）山田先生たるや、すべての人を感動させた。
The way of Yamada-sensei impressed everyone.
（○）山田先生の話し振りたるや、すべての人を感動させた。
The way Yamada-sensei spoke impressed everyone.
This is a type of expression for emphasis when introducing the subject of the sentence. In

content: , for example, it is an exaggerated expression in comparison to only その意外性は....

content.content: 【たろう】［N／Na　だったろう］［A-かったろう］［V-たろう］

content: 母は若いころはずいぶん美人だったろう。

content.content: Mother must have been very beautiful when she was young.

content: 試験で大変だったろう。

content.content: It must have been hard with the examinations.

content: さぞや苦しかったろう。

content.content: It must have been hard.

content: A:おなかがすいたろう。

content.content: You must be hungry.
B:うん、ちょっとね。
Yeah, a little.

content: あの子はあんなに熱があるのに学校に出かけたが、今日一日だいじょうぶだったろうか。

content.content: That child went to school today even with that high a fever. I wonder if he was OK all day.

content: あわてて出かけて行ったが、無事間に合ったろうか。

content.content: He left in such a hurry. I wonder if he made it.

This is a phrase where the だ of ただろう (a combination of the ta-form of the predicate and だろう) is dropped. The meaning and use are the same. Used to express a supposition about what has already been established, and used in both written and spoken language.

content: is for spoken language and is for confirming the speaker’s supposition with the listener. In this case it is usually spoken with a rising tone. The たろうか in
and
expresses the speaker’s doubt or worry. The polite form of this is たでしょう.

content.content: 【だろう】
【だい】Used by men in casual conversation.
1. 疑問表現+だい

content: いま何時だい？

content.content: What time is it now?

content: いつだい？　花子の入学式は。

content.content: When is it? Hanako’s entrance ceremony, I mean.

content: その手紙だれからだい？

content.content: So who’s the letter from?

content: どうだい。元気かい。

content.content: So how are things? Are you doing well?

content: そんなことだれから聞いたんだい？

content.content: Who’d you hear that from?

content: 何時にどこに集ればいいんだい？

content.content: What time and where should we meet?

content: どうだい、すごいだろう。

content.content: Whaddaya think? Great, isn’t it!

content: 何だい、今頃やってきて。もう準備はぜんぶ終わったよ。

content.content: Whaddaya think you’re doing, arriving at this hour? We’re already finished getting everything ready!

Attaches to interrogative expressions, such as question words or clauses that include a question word. Expresses the feeling of asking the listener a question. Sometimes used as an exclamation that conveys the feeling of asking a question or criticizing, as in

content: and
. A slightly old-fashioned expression used in spoken language. Usually used by adult males.

content.content: 2. ...だい。［N／Na　だい］

content: そんなことうそだい。

content.content: That’s a lie!

content: いやだい。絶対教えてあげないよ。

content.content: No. I won’t tell you, ever.

content: ぼくのはこれじゃないよ。それがぼくのだい。

content.content: This one isn’t mine. That one’s mine.
Used by boys to make a strong assertion.
【だいたい】

content: 大体のことは伝えておきます。

content.content: I will convey the main points.

content: だいたいわかりました。

content.content: I understand, more or less.

content: この本をひとりで日本語に翻訳するのはだいたい無理な話だ。

content.content: It’s almost impossible for one person to translate this book into Japanese.

content: こんな時間に電話するなんてだいたい非常識な人だ。

content.content: Calling people at such an hour shows that he has practically no common sense.

content: A:あの子、いつも忘れものをするらしいの。

content.content: Apparently he always forgets to take something (to school).
B:だいたいね、注意してやらない君が悪いんだよ。
You’re the one to blame, because you never remind him.

content: だいたいぼくよりあいつの方が給料がいいなんて変だよ。

content.content: To begin with, the fact that his salary is higher than mine is just crazy.

content: A:すみません、遅れまして。

content.content: I’m sorry to be late.
B:だいたいだね、君は今まで時間通りに来たことがない。
The thing is, you’ve never arrived on time.
Means “mostly; the greater part” in examples

content: and
. Can be used to convey a sense of reproach or criticism when the speaker is stating a judgment about something that is 無理 (impossible) or 非常識 (thoughtless), as in
and
. May also be used to preface criticisms, grievances, or complaints against another person, as in
, and

content.content: 【だから】The more polite equivalent is ですから.
1. だから〈consequence〉

content: 踏切で事故があった。だから、学校に遅刻してしまった。

content.content: There was an accident at the railroad crossing. So I was late for school.

content: 部屋の電気がついている。だから、もう帰って来ているはずだ。

content.content: There’s a light on in the room. So he must be back already.

content: 時間がありません。だから、急いでください。

content.content: Time is short. So please hurry.

content: A:今夜は雨になるそうですね。

content.content: I hear it will rain this evening.
B:だから、私、傘をもって来ました。
That’s why I brought my umbrella.

Used to state a consequence derived as a result of the cause, reason, or basis described in the preceding sentence. The sentence that follows may be a factual sentence, or it may present a supposition, request, invitation, etc.

content: is an example of use in conversation, with one speaker stating the reason and the other stating the consequence.

content.content: 2. だから　...のだ／...わけだ

content: A:ジャクソンさんは、小学生の時からもう 10 年も日本語を習っているそうです。

content.content: I heard that Jackson-san has been studying Japanese for ten years already, since he was in elementary school.
B:だから、あんなに日本語が上手なんですね。
So that’s why his Japanese is so good.

content: A:今日は吉田先生、休講だそうだよ。

content.content: I heard Yoshida-sensei’s class has been canceled today.
B:ああ、そう。だからいくら待ってもだれも来ないわけか。
Oh, really? So that’s why I’ve been waiting for so long and no one has come.

content: やっぱり、不合格だったか。だから、もっと簡単な大学を受けろと言ったのだ。

content.content: So, just as I expected, you didn’t pass. That’s why I told you to try for an easier university.

Used to express a current state of affairs after discovering a certain fact; conveys the feeling that the speaker accepts the state of affairs as a natural result having arisen from that fact. In conversation, this pattern is used when the cause or reason for something has become clear from something the other person has said, and it is accompanied by sentence-final particles such as ね, indicating confirmation, or か, indicating understanding. The first syllable in だから is stressed and held slightly longer.
3. だから〈question〉

content: A:みんなお前のためにこんなに遅くまで働いているんだ。

content.content: Everyone is working this late because of you.
B:だから、どうだって言うの。
So, what are you saying?

content: A:できることは全部やったつもりです。

content.content: I’ve tried to do all that I can.
B:だから、何なんですか。
So what?

content: A:たった一度会っただけだよ。

content.content: I’ve only met her once.
B:だから？
So?

Used in conversation, with だから followed by a question. Does not express cause and effect, but is used in response to a statement made by the listener, in order to demand clarification of the intention behind that statement. Means “so what is it that you’re trying to say?” Can be replaced by それで or で. In some cases, as in

content: , it is pronounced with a rising tone and the question part is omitted. Because this usage of だから has an impolite nuance, even if the sentence ends in a polite form, it is usually not possible to say ですから.

content.content: 4. だから〈assertion〉

content: A:ちょっと、どういうことですか。

content.content: Hey, what’s going on?
B:別に特別のことはないよ。
Nothing in particular.
A:だから、どういうことって聞いているんだよ。
So I’m asking you, what’s going on?!

content: A:何で、電話してくれなかったの。

content.content: Why didn’t you call me?
B:だから、時間がなかったんだ。
I told you, I didn’t have time to.

Used in conversation. Does not express cause and effect, but is used when the speaker is trying to make the listener understand his/her intention, in situations when his/her opinion differs from the listener’s. Means “what I want to say is this.”

content: is an example of using だから to make an excuse. Because it expresses a strong assertion, it sounds forceful and often has an impolite nuance.

content.content: 【だからこそ】

content: A:どうして彼女はその不審な電話のことを社長に話さなかったんでしょうか。

content.content: I wonder why she didn’t tell the company president about that suspicious phone call.
B:彼女は社長に信頼されていたんです。だからこそまず自分で調べようとしたんだと思います。
The president trusted her. That’s precisely why she wanted to check into it by herself first, I think.

content: 私ほど彼女の幸せを願っているものはいない。だからこそ、あの時あえて身を引いたのだ。

content.content: No one cares more about her happiness than I do. That’s exactly why I stepped aside when I did.

content: A:結婚は人生の大事な節目ですから二人だけで式をあげたいんです。

content.content: Marriage is an important milestone in life, so that’s why I want to have a wedding just with the two of us.
B:確かに結婚は人生の大事な節目だ。だからこそ大勢の人に祝ってもらわなくてはいけないんだよ。
Marriage certainly is an important milestone in life. That’s exactly why you’ve got to have lots of people to celebrate it.

content: A:職場では、一人だと上司になかなか文句は言いにくいですよね。

content.content: At work, it’s pretty hard to complain to the boss all on your own, isn’t it.
B:だからこそ、皆で団結しなくてはいけないと思うんです。
That’s precisely why I think we have to unite and do it together.

content: A:最近この辺で空き巣に入られる事件が増えているらしいですね。

content.content: I hear there have been a lot of burglaries in this area lately.
B:だからこそ、このマンションに防犯ベルをつけるようお願いしているんです。
That’s precisely why I’ve been requesting a security alarm to be installed in this apartment.

content: A:高齢化社会が急速に進んでるね。

content.content: We’re rapidly becoming an aged society, aren’t we.
B:だからこそ、今すぐ老人医療の見直しをやらなければならないんだよ。
That’s exactly why we have to review the system of medical care for elderly people right now.

Combines a clause expressing a reason with the focalizer こそ. Used at the beginning of a sentence, it refers to the preceding sentence and conveys the meaning “for that reason,” with emphasis on the reason. だからon its own would be sufficient for stating an ordinary reason. だからこそ is used to strongly assert the justification for a reason. Often used in debate or argument, when one person takes the other person’s statement and uses it as a reason to assert what s/he herself/himself wants to say. のだ tends to be used at the end of the sentence.
【だからといって】

content: 毎日忙しい。しかし、だからといって、好きな陶芸をやめるつもりはない。

content.content: I’m busy every day. But that doesn’t mean I intend to quit pottery-making, which I'm so fond of.

content: わたしは彼が好きだ。しかし、だからといって、彼のすることは何でもいいと思っているわけではない。

content.content: I like him. But even so, that doesn’t mean I think everything he does is good.

content: 今この店で買うと 50 パーセント引きだそうだ。しかし、だからといって、いらないものを買う必要はない。

content.content: Apparently it’s 50% off if you buy it at this store right now. But that’s not to say you should buy something you don’t need.

content: 確かに、あの会社は待遇がいい。しかし、だからといって今の仕事をやめるのには反対だ。

content.content: It’s true that the salary and benefits at that company are good. But even so, I’m still against you quitting your current job.

Used to acknowledge the truth of something that has just been stated and to say that, in spite of such a reason, the speaker doesn’t accept the thing that is stated next. Often followed by a negative expression.
【だけ1】［N（+助詞+）だけ］［N／Na　なだけ］［A／V　だけ］Expresses limitation.
1. ...だけだa. ...だけ

content: 今度の事件に関係がないのは彼だけだ。

content.content: He’s the only one not connected with the current incident.

content: 品物なんかいりません。お気持ちだけいただきます。

content.content: I don’t need things. Your kindness alone is enough.

content: コピーをとるだけの簡単な仕事です。

content.content: It’s an easy job of just making photocopies.

content: ちょっとだけお借りします。

content.content: I’ll borrow it for just a little while.

content: あの人だけが私を理解してくれる。

content.content: Only he understands me.

content: ここは便利なだけで環境はあまりよくない。

content.content: This place is convenient, but that’s all—the surroundings are not very good.

content: たいした怪我ではありません。ちょっと指を切っただけです。

content.content: It isn’t a serious injury. I cut my finger a little, that’s all.

content: その話を聞いて泣いたのはわたしだけではない。

content.content: I wasn’t the only one who cried after hearing that story.

content: あなただけにお知らせします。

content.content: I’ll notify you, and only you.

content: あの人にだけは負けたくない。

content.content: She’s the one person I don’t want to lose to.

Expresses restriction or limitation, with the meaning “there is nothing else.” Follows a plain form when attached to a clause. When combined with が and を, it takes the forms Nだけが and Nだけを. が and を are sometimes dropped, as seen in

content: . There are two patterns of linking with particles like に and から, as in Nだけに and Nにだけ. However, in some cases these two patterns have different meanings, as in the examples below.

content.content: （例）身分は保険証でだけ証明できる。（他の手段ではできない）
You can prove your identity only with your health insurance certificate. (You can’t use any other method.)
（例）身分は保険証だけで証明できる。（保険証以外のものは要らない）
You can prove your identity with just your health insurance certificate. (You don’t need anything else but the insurance certificate.)
b. ...といってもせいぜい...だけだ

content: ボーナスといってもせいぜい一ヶ月分出るだけだ。

content.content: A bonus it may be, but it’s only about a month’s salary, at the very most.

content: 夏祭りといってもせいぜい屋台が三、四軒出るだけです。

content.content: A summer festival it may be, but there are only three or four booths at the most.

content: 旅行といってもせいぜい2泊するだけです。

content.content: I say it’s a trip, but it’s only two nights’ stay, if that.

content: はやっているといってもせいぜい週末に混むだけだ。

content.content: You may think it’s popular, but it just gets crowded on the weekends, that’s all.
Used to emphasize that there is not much of something.
c. ...たところで...だけだ

content: 急いで計算したところで間違いが多くなるだけだ。

content.content: If you calculate in a hurry, you’ll only make more mistakes.

content: 親に話したところで誤解されるだけだ。

content.content: If I tell my parents, it’ll only cause misunderstanding.

content: 早く帰ったところでねこが待っているだけだ。

content.content: If I go home early, all I have is a cat waiting for me.
Means “even if you do something, it will only result in a less-than-satisfactory outcome.”
d. ただ...だけでは

content: スポーツはただ見るだけでは面白くない。

content.content: Sports are not interesting if all you do is watch.

content: 外国へ行ってただ景色を見るだけではつまらない。そこの土地の人たちとちょっとでも触れ合う旅にしたい。

content.content: It’s boring to travel abroad and just look at the scenery. I want my trip to be one that includes at least a little contact with the local people.

content: ただ話しただけではあの人の本当のよさはわからない。

content.content: You won’t see that person’s true merits simply by talking to him.
Means “just by doing such-and-such.” Followed by expressions of negative evaluation.
e. ...だけで

content: 明日からまた仕事だと思うと、考えるだけでいやになる。

content.content: Just thinking about the fact that work starts again tomorrow makes me feel like I can’t stand it.

content: 地震は経験した人の話を聞くだけでこわい。

content.content: It’s scary just listening to the stories of people who have experienced earthquakes.

content: イルカのダンスなんて考えただけで楽しくなる。

content.content: Just thinking about dolphins dancing makes you feel happy.
Used after verbs such as 考える (think), 聞く (hear, listen to), 思う(think) or 想像する(imagine) to express that you can feel something without actually experiencing it.
2. ...だけしか...ない

content: 今月、残ったお金はこれだけしかありません。

content.content: This is all the money I have left this month.

content: 頼りになるのはもうあなただけしかいない。

content.content: The only one I have left to rely on is you.

content: こんなことは、あなたにだけしか頼めません。

content.content: You’re the only one I can ask to do this.

content: いまのところひとりだけしかレポートを出していない。

content.content: So far only one person has submitted a paper.
Used to emphasize ...だけだ (only/just...). To emphasize the small quantity of something,だけだ or (だけ)しかない is used, not だけある.
（例）A:お金がいくらありますか。
How much money do you have?
B:（×）千円だけあります。
There is only a thousand yen.
B:（○）千円だけです／千円しかありません。
Only a thousand yen./All I have is a thousand yen.
だけ cannot be used in the following cases.
（例）A:この花いくらでしたか。
How much was this flower?
B:（×）二百円だけです。
It’s only two hundred yen.
B:（○）二百円しかしませんでした／たったの二百円でした。
It only cost two hundred yen./It was just two hundred yen.
（例）A:いま何時ですか。
What time is it now?
B:（×）1時だけです。
It’s merely one o’clock.
B:（○）まだ1時です。
It’s still just one o’clock.
3. ...だけでなく...も

content: 肉だけでなく、野菜も食べなければいけない。

content.content: You have to eat not just meat but vegetables, too.

content: 英語だけでなくて、アラビア語もうまい。

content.content: She’s good at not only English but also Arabic.

content: 彼は歌が上手なだけでなく自分で曲も作る。

content.content: He’s not only good at singing, he also composes songs himself.

content: 今度の台風で、村は田畑だけでなく家屋も大きな被害を受けた。

content.content: As a result of the latest typhoon, not only the cultivated fields but also the houses in the village were badly damaged.

content: 授賞式にかれは招待を受けただけではなく、スピーチも頼まれた。

content.content: He was not only invited to the awards ceremony, he was also asked to give a speech.
Means “both; not only...but also....” In spoken language, ...だけじゃなく...もis also used.
4. ...だけのことだ

content: だれも行かないのなら私が行くだけのことだ。

content.content: If no one else is going, I’ll go by myself.

content: 入園テストといっても何もむずかしいことはないんです。先生に名前を呼ばれたら「はい」と返事をするだけのことです。

content.content: We say “kindergarten entrance test,” but it’s not hard. All they need to do is answer “yes” when the teacher calls their names.

content: いやなら無理をすることはない。断わるだけのことだ。

content.content: If you don’t want to, you don’t have to. All you need to do is say no.
Means that there is no other way, or that something is not anything special.
5. ...というだけ（の理由）で

content: その野菜はめずらしいというだけでよく売れている。

content.content: That vegetable is selling well just because it’s unusual.

content: 若いというだけで皆にもてはやされる。

content.content: Everyone makes a fuss over him just because he’s young.

content: その晩に現場近くにいたというだけで彼は逮捕された。

content.content: He was arrested only because he happened to be near the scene that night.

content: 子どもが多いというだけの理由でアパートの入居を断わられた。

content.content: I was refused an apartment, just for the reason that I have a lot of children.

content: 名前の書いてない自転車に乗っているというだけの理由で警官に職務質問を受けた。

content.content: I was questioned by the police simply because I was riding a bike with no name written on it.
Means for only one single reason.
6. V-るだけV-て

content: 彼女は文句を言うだけ言ってなにも手伝ってくれない。

content.content: All she does is complain, and she doesn’t help with anything.

content: 彼は飲むだけ飲んで会費を払わずに帰ってしまった。

content.content: He drank all he wanted to and left without paying his share.

content: 言いたいことだけ言ってさっさと出ていった。

content.content: He said what he wanted to say and left in a hurry.

content: いまどうしているか様子がわからないから、手紙を出すだけ出して返事を待とう。

content.content: I don’t know how he’s doing these days, so let’s just send a letter and wait for a reply.
In this pattern, the same verb is repeated. In some cases, as in 言いたいこと in

content: , a noun phrase that contains a verb is repeated. Means “someone is doing one thing, but not another thing that s/he should be doing.”

content.content: 【だけ2】Expresses a degree/extent.
1. V-れるだけV

content: がんばれるだけがんばってみます。

content.content: I’ll try as hard as I can.

content: そこのリンゴ、持てるだけ持って行っていいよ。

content.content: You may take as many of those apples as you can carry.

content: 彼は銀行から金を借りられるだけ借りて家を買った。

content.content: He borrowed as much money as he could from the bank and bought a house.

content: 待てるだけ待ったが、彼は待ち合わせの場所に現れなかった。

content.content: I waited for as long as I could, but he didn’t show up at the appointed place.
Verbs such as がんばる(work hard) and 持つ(hold) are repeated to express the meaning “do something as much as possible.”
2. V-たいだけV

content: ここが気に入ったのなら、いたいだけいていいですよ。

content.content: If you like it here, please feel free to stay as long as you like.

content: 遠慮しないで食べたいだけ食べなさい。

content.content: Don’t hesitate–eat as much as you like.

content: 遊びたいだけ遊んで納得した。あすからいっしょうけんめい勉強しよう。

content.content: I’m satisfied to have played as much as I wanted to. I’ll study hard starting tomorrow.

content: 彼女は泣きたいだけ泣いて気が済んだのか夕食の支度を始めた。

content.content: It might have been that she felt better after having a good cry, but then she started to prepare supper.
Repeats the verb and means “up to the point at which one’s desire is satisfied.”
3. V-るだけはV

content: やるだけはやったのだから、静かに結果を待とう。

content.content: We’ve done all we can, so let’s wait quietly for the result.

content: 息子の言い分を聞くだけは聞いてやってくれませんか。

content.content: Won’t you please at least listen to what my son has to say?

content: このことは両親にも話すだけは話しておいた方がいい。

content.content: It would be better to at least talk to your parents about this, too.
Means that someone does something to a certain extent. Followed by an expression indicating that nothing is expected or demanded beyond that extent.
4. V-る／V-た　だけのことはする

content: お金をいただいただけのことはしますが、それ以上のことは出来かねます。

content.content: I’ll do what I’m paid to do, but I can’t do anything beyond that.

content: 調査期間はわずか1ヶ月でしたが、やれるだけのことはやったつもりです。

content.content: The period of investigation was only one month, but I feel I’ve done all I can.

content: 出来るだけのことはしますが、今月中に仕上げるのはむずかしいと思います。

content.content: I’ll do my best, but I don’t think it’s possible to finish it this month.
Means “do X to a degree that complies with Y.”
5. V-るだけのN

content: どんなところでも生きていけるだけの生活力が彼にはある。

content.content: He has enough of an appetite for life that he could live anywhere.

content: その日彼の財布にはコーヒーを一杯飲むだけの金もなかった。

content.content: That day he didn’t even have enough money in his wallet to buy a cup of coffee.

content: 妻に本当のことを打ち明けるだけの勇気もなかった。

content.content: I didn’t have enough courage to confess the truth to my wife.

content: その学生には異国で暮らすだけの語学力が不足している。

content.content: That student lacks sufficient foreign language ability to live abroad.
Means “sufficient in order to....” Expresses a degree and attaches to nouns such as 生活力 (vitality, earning power), 金 (money), 勇気 (courage), 語学力 (language ability), 根性 (willpower) and やさしさ (kindness).
6. V-ば V-るだけ

content: 交渉は時間をかければかけるだけ余計にもつれていった。

content.content: The more time it took, the more complicated the negotiations became.

content: 動物は世話をすればするだけなついてきます。

content.content: The more you look after an animal, the more attached to you it gets.

content: ピアノは練習すればするだけよく指が動くようになる。

content.content: The more you practice the piano, the better your fingers move.
Means that if you do one thing, another thing will happen along with it to the same extent. Can be replaced by the pattern V-ば V-るほど, which is more commonly used.
7. これだけ...のだから

content: これだけ努力したんだからいつかは報われるだろう。

content.content: I’ve put in so much effort, so someday it is sure to pay off.

content: よくがんばったね。それだけがんばれば誰にも文句は言われないよ。

content.content: You really worked hard. If you work that hard, no one can criticize you.

content: あれだけ頼んでおいたのに彼はやってくれなかった。

content.content: In spite of all my requests, he still didn’t do it for me.

content: あれだけ練習してもうまくならないのは、彼に才能がないのだろう。

content.content: The fact that he hasn’t improved even after all that practice probably means he doesn’t have any talent.

content: どれだけ言えば、あの人にわかってもらえるのだろうか。

content.content: How much do I have to say to make that person understand?
これ, それ, あれ and どれ can all be used. （こ）れだけ is followed by ...のだから, ...ば, ...のに, or ...ても and means “this much, to this extent.”
8. ...だけましだ［Na なだけましだ］［A／V　だけましだ］

content: 風邪でのどが痛いが、熱が出ないだけましだ。

content.content: I have a sore throat due to a cold, but at least I don’t have a fever.

content: さいふをとられたが、パスポートが無事だっただけまだましだ。

content.content: I had my wallet stolen, but at least my passport was safe.

content: 私の住んでいるところは駅からも遠いし工場があってうるさい。このへんは不便だが、静かなだけましだ。

content.content: The place I live is far from the station and there’s a factory close by, so it’s noisy. Still, this area may be inconvenient, but at least it’s quiet.
Means that the current situation isn’t very good, but it’s fortunate that it isn’t any worse or that it’s only to this extent.
【だけ3】［N／A／V　だけに］［Na なだけに］Indicates a general characteristic of a person or thing, which is then used to describe what can naturally be inferred from that characteristic.
1. ...だけにa. ...だけに

content: お茶の先生だけに言葉遣いが上品だ。

content.content: Her use of language is elegant, as you’d expect from a teacher of tea ceremony.

content: 彼は現職の教師だけに受験についてはくわしい。

content.content: Being a working teacher, he knows a lot about taking examinations.

content: かれらは若いだけに徹夜をしても平気なようだ。

content.content: Because they’re young, staying up all night doesn’t seem to affect them.

content: 今回の事故は一歩まちがえば大惨事につながるだけに、原因の究明が急がれる。

content.content: Because the current accident could easily have led to a disaster, we need to determine the cause quickly.
This expression means that the latter situation arises as a natural result of the former.
b. ...だけになおさら

content: 横綱の意地があるだけになおさら大関には負けられないでしょう。

content.content: He has the pride of a yokozuna (the highest rank of sumoo), so he’s probably all the more determined not to lose against an oozeki (the second highest rank of sumoo).

content: 彼女は若かっただけになおのことその早すぎた死が惜しまれる。

content.content: Since she was so young, her premature death is even more regrettable.

content: 苦労しただけになおさら今回の優勝はうれしいでしょうね。

content.content: Especially after the hardships you’ve had, this victory must be all the more gratifying.

content: 現地は暑さに加えて、飲み水も不足しているだけになおさら救援が待たれる。

content.content: Along with the heat in the area, a lack of drinking water has made the need for aid all the more urgent.
Means “because of such-and-such, it is natural that...is all the more....” なおのことin

content: is used in the same way.

content.content: c. ...だけにかえって

content: 若くて体力があるだけにかえって無理をして体をこわしてしまった。

content.content: It was because I was young and had a lot of stamina that I ended up working too hard and ruining my health.

content: 今まで順調だっただけにかえって今度の事業の失敗は彼に致命的な打撃となった。

content.content: It was precisely because things had been going so well up till now that the failure of this enterprise dealt him a fatal blow.
Means that although something should normally have a good result, the opposite has happened.
d. NがNだけに

content: 祖父は今年 90 歳で元気だが、歳が歳だけに昼間もウトウトしていることが多くなってきた。

content.content: My grandfather is ninety this year and doing very well, but given his age, he dozes off more and more during the day.

content: この商品は今までの物よりもずっと性能がいいのですが、値段が値段だけにそうたくさんは売れないでしょう。

content.content: This product has much better performance than any in the past, but given the price, we probably won’t be able to sell very many.
2. ...だけのことはある

content: うまい魚だ。とれたてを送ってもらっただけのことはある。

content.content: This fish is delicious. There’s nothing like having freshly caught fish sent to you.

content: A:このナイフ、いつまでもよく切れるね。

content.content: This knife just keeps on cutting really well, doesn’t it?
B:買った時は高いと思ったけど、それだけのことはあるね。
I thought it was a little expensive when I bought it, but it’s been worth the price.

content: A:杉島さんの英語の発音、とってもきれいね。

content.content: Sugishima-san’s English pronunciation is really good.
B:そうね、さすがにイギリスに留学していただけのことはあるわね。
Yes, her study abroad in England has certainly paid off, hasn’t it.

content: 彼女は学校の先生をしていただけのことはあって、今も人前で話すのがうまい。

content.content: Because she was a school teacher, she’s good at public speaking even today.
Means that something is worth the effort, position, experience, etc. Expresses a positive judgment that the thing in question has a proportional result, ability, or merit.
【だけど】

content: 2時間待った。だけど、彼は現れなかった。

content.content: I waited for two hours. But he didn’t show up.

content: 朝から頭が痛かった。だけど、彼女との約束を破るのはいやだった。

content.content: I’d had a headache since the morning. But I didn’t want to break my appointment with her.

content: みきさんの言いたいことはわかる。だけど、決まったことは変えられない。

content.content: I understand what Miki-san is saying. But we can’t change what’s been decided.

content: 仕事が山ほどたまっている。だけど、なかなか働く気になれない。

content.content: I have a mountain of work to do. But it’s pretty hard to feel like working.

Signals that the thing that will be stated next is the opposite of what could be expected from the thing previously stated. Not usually used in formal writing. Also not used in the middle of a sentence.
（×）2時間待っただけど、彼は現れなかった。
I waited for two hours, and but he didn’t show up.
だけど is an informal equivalent of だけれども. In the polite style, the expression ですけれども is also used.
【だけに】→
【だけ3】
【だったら】

content: A:この仕事、私一人じゃとても無理だと思います。

content.content: I think this job is too much for me by myself.
B:だったら私が手伝いますよ。
In that case, I’ll help you.

content: A:どうしても彼には言えないよ。

content.content: I simply can’t tell him.
B:だったら私が言います。
I’ll tell him, then.

content: A:先生、入院なさったらしい。

content.content: Apparently our teacher has been hospitalized.
B:だったら、しばらくは授業はないね。
So then we won’t be having class for a while.

Means “in that case.” Used when the speaker is expressing his/her attitude or stating an inference with respect to another person’s words, a piece of new information, etc. Spoken language. Synonymous expressions include それなら and それでは.
【だって1】
1. ...だって〈inquiry〉

content: A:あっ、地震だ。

content.content: Oh! It’s an earthquake.
B:地震だって？　ちがうよ。ダンプカーが通っただけだよ。
Earthquake, you say? No, that was just a dump truck passing by.

content: A:あの人、男よ。

content.content: That person is a man.
B:男だって？　ぜったいに女だよ。
A man, you say? No, definitely a woman.

content: A:太郎、テストどうだった

content.content: How was the test, Taro?
B:おもしろかったよ。
It was fun.
A:おもしろかっただって？　むずかしかったとか、やさしかったけど問題が多かったとかほかに答えようがあるだろう。
Fun? There are other ways to answer, you know, like it was hard, or it was easy but there were lots of questions, or something like that.

content: A:福田さん、美人コンテストに出るらしいよ。

content.content: Apparently Fukuda-san is going to be in a beauty contest.
B:美人コンテストですって？　今ごろそんな時代遅れのコンテストなんかどこでやってるのよ。
A beauty contest? Where can they be having such an out-of-date contest in this day and age?

content: A:ヘリコプターがまだ到着しないんですが。

content.content: The helicopter hasn’t arrived yet.
B:なんだって？　そりゃ大変だ。
What? That’s awful.
Used to express a feeling of surprise or shock by repeating what the other person has just said. Sometimes expresses a sense of displeasure. Used with rising intonation.
An informal, spoken language expression. The polite equivalent is ...ですって, but this can only be used with a person of lower status or a person you are close to. In addition to なんだって in

content: , other expressions used to indicate strong surprise include なんですって and なんだと.

content.content: 2. ...んだって→
【って】
3. ...なんだって→
【って】5
【だって2】［Nだって］

content: それぐらいのことは子供だって知っている。

content.content: Even kids know that sort of thing.

content: 先生だって間違うことはある。

content.content: Even teachers can make mistakes.

content: 医者だって風邪ぐらいひくよ。

content.content: Even doctors can catch a cold.

content: つらいのはあなただけじゃない。浅田さんだって、坂田さんだってみんながまんしてるんです。

content.content: You’re not the only one having a hard time. Asada-san, Sakata-san—everyone is having to put up with this.

content: 好き嫌いはありません。魚だって肉だってなんだって大丈夫です。

content.content: I have no likes or dislikes concerning food. Fish or meat or anything else is all OK for me.

content: あの子はこのごろ帰りが遅い。きのうだって 11 時過ぎていた。

content.content: Recently that kid has been coming home late. Yesterday it was after eleven o’clock.

content: だれにだって一つや二つは秘密がある。

content.content: Everyone has a secret or two.
Means “even someone/something” and is similar to でも. In

content: , and
, an extreme or contrasting example X is given to express “even X....” In
and
, a number of similar examples are listed and the meaning conveyed is “not only A, but also B and C.” Informal spoken language.

content.content: 【だって3】

content: A:どうして外で遊ばないの。

content.content: Why aren’t you playing outside?
B:だって寒いんだもん。
Because it’s cold.

content: A:にんじん、残さずにちゃんと食べなさい。

content.content: Eat all your carrots and don’t leave any on your plate.
B:だってきらいだもん。
But I don’t like them!

content: A:夕刊まだかな。

content.content: I wonder if the evening paper has come yet.
B:だって、今日は日曜日でしょ、来ないわよ。
Well, today is Sunday, so we’re not going to get a paper.

content: A:きのうはどうして待ってくれなかったの。

content.content: Why didn’t you wait for me yesterday?
B:だってあそこの喫茶店、人が多くて居づらかったんだよ。
Because that café was so crowded I felt uncomfortable staying there.
Used by the speaker to reply when asked the reason for something and means “it is because....” Can be used even when the reason is not asked explicitly, as in

content: and
. Children, especially, use it in the form だって...もの/もん when they talk back. Adults sometimes use it, too. Informal spoken language.

content.content: 【だと】

content: A:今日は学校に行きたくないな。

content.content: I don’t want to go to school today.
B:なに？　行きたくないだと？　そんなことは言わせないぞ。
What? You don’t want to go? I won’t allow you to say such a thing.

content: 子:お父さんが悪いんだ。

content.content: Children: You’re the one who’s to blame, Dad.
父:何だと？　もう一度言ってみろ。
Father: What? Just try and say that one more time!

content: 大雪警報が出てるから旅行は取りやめだとさ。

content.content: A heavy snow warning has been issued, so the trip’s been canceled, I hear.
This expression is rougher than だって. Used by men.
【だって1】
【だといい】

content: A:みんな今頃安全な場所に避難していますよ。

content.content: By now, everyone should have evacuated to a safe place.
B:だといいが。心配だ。
I hope so. But I’m worried.

content: A:彼は慎重だから、危ない運転はしませんよ。

content.content: He’s cautious, so he won’t drive dangerously.
B:だといいけど。本当に大丈夫かしら。
I hope not. I wonder if he’ll really be all right.

content: A:子供達もきっとこのプレゼントに大喜びしますよ。

content.content: I’m sure the kids, too, will be very happy with this gift.
B:だといいね。
I certainly hope so.
Used at the beginning of a sentence in conversation. Means the same as そうだといい. Followed by が, けれど, or けど and expresses the meaning “I hope that is the situation.” それだといいが and そうだといいけど are also used.
【だといって】

content: A:これは全面的にあいつが悪い。

content.content: This is entirely his fault.
B:だといって、困っているのを見捨てるわけにもいかないだろう。
Even so, we can’t just abandon him in his time of trouble, can we?

content: A:こちらも人が足りないんですよ。

content.content: We don’t have enough people, either.
B:だといって、放っておけないでしょう。
But we can’t just leave things as they are, can we?
Same as そうだといって and だからといって.
【だからといって】
【だとすると】

content: A:近くに大きなホテルができるのは確実です。

content.content: It’s definite that a large hotel will be built near here.
B:だとすると、この町の雇用率が上がるかもしれませんね。
In that case, the employment rate in this town may go up.

content: A:飛行機が 10 時間も遅れてるんだそうです。

content.content: Apparently the flight has been delayed by ten hours.
B:だとすると、彼の帰りはあしたになるな。
That means he’ll be coming back tomorrow.
Essentially the same as だとすれば. そうだとすると is also used.
【だとすれば】
【だとすれば】

content: A:近くに大きなホテルができるのは確実です。

content.content: It’s definite that a large hotel will be built near here.
B:だとすれば、この町の雇用率が上がるかもしれませんね。
In that case, the employment rate in this town may go up.

content: A:この写真は、夏に京都でとったものです。

content.content: This picture was taken in Kyoto in the summer.
B:だとすれば、彼は去年の7月に日本にいたことになりますね。
So that means he was in Japan in July last year.

Used at the beginning of a sentence, when the speaker is stating a supposition or judgment based on something the other person has said. Means “judging from such a fact or state of affairs.” Similar to それなら, but だとすれば is somewhat more formal and used in written language, too. Related expressions include そうだとすれば, だとすると and そうだとすると.
【だなんて】

content: 今頃になって気が変わっただなんてよく言えますね。

content.content: You have a lot of nerve, to say at this point that you’ve changed your mind.

content: 約束したのに、できなかっただなんて、ひどい。

content.content: It’s outrageous that you couldn’t do it, even though you’d promised to.

content: 予約できるかもしれない、だなんて、無責任な言い方ですね。

content.content: Saying that you might be able to make the reservation is an irresponsible way to put it.

content: 事故で死んでしまうだなんて、あんまりだ。

content.content: It’s really too much that they were killed in an accident.

Used to criticize or complain by repeating what the other person has said. In some cases expresses a feeling of criticism or grief with respect to a circumstance that is not the speaker’s fault, as in

content: . なんて is also used by itself.

content.content: 【だにしない】［Nだにしない］

content: このような事故が起きるとは想像だにしなかった。

content.content: I never even imagined that an accident like this could occur.

content: 衛兵は直立不動のまま、微動だにしない。

content.content: The sentinel stands erect and doesn’t make the slightest movement.

content: そんな危険をおかすなんて考えるだに恐ろしい。

content.content: It is terrifying just to think about taking such a risk.

content: 一顧だにしない。

content.content: He doesn’t even give it a thought.

content: 一瞥だにしない。

content.content: He doesn’t even give it a glance.
This is a literary expression that means “doesn’t even do N,” “doesn’t do N at all.”
Sometimes it may be combined with an affirmative form and used to mean “only, just,” as in the expression 思うだに恐ろしい (terrifying just to think about...).
Examples

content: and
are idiomatic expressions. Example
means “doesn’t consider...at all,” and
means “doesn’t look at all.”

content.content: 【だの】［N／Na　だの　N／Na　だの］［A／V　だの　A／V　だの］

content: 彼女は市場に出かけると、肉だの野菜だの持ちきれないほど買ってきた。

content.content: When she went to the market, she bought such a great quantity of meat and vegetables and whatnot that she could hardly carry it all back.

content: 同窓会には中村だの池田だの20 年ぶりのなつかしい顔がそろった。

content.content: Many old familiar faces from twenty years ago, such as Nakamura and Ikeda, appeared together at the reunion.

content: チャリティーバザーには有名人の服だのサイン入りの本だのいろいろなものが集まった。

content.content: Lots of things were collected for the charity bazaar, including a celebrity’s clothing, a signed book, and so forth.

content: 彼は、やれ給料が安いだの休みが少ないだのと文句が多い。

content.content: He complains a lot about how low his salary is, how little vacation time he gets, and so on and so forth.

content: 彼はいつ会っても会社をやめて留学するだのなんだのと実現不可能なことばかり言っている。

content.content: Whenever I see him, all he talks about are things he will never accomplish, like quitting his job and going abroad to study.
Like やら and とか, this is a way of listing several items, but as seen in

content: and
, it is often used to indicate a negative evaluation of something another person has said. Means “it’s annoying because he says a lot of things like that.” The expression ...だのなんだの, as in
, is idiomatic.

content.content: 【だらけ】［Nだらけだ］

content: 間違いだらけの答案が返ってきた。

content.content: I got back an answer sheet full of mistakes.

content: 子供は泥だらけの足で部屋に上がってきた。

content.content: Children came into the room with mud all over their shoes.

content: 彼は借金だらけだ。

content.content: He’s deep in debt. / He has a lot of debt.

content: 「傷だらけの青春」という映画を見た。

content.content: I watched a film called Bruised-up Youth (original title: Split Decisions).

content: 彼女の部屋は本だらけだ。

content.content: Her room is packed with books.
Describes a situation where there is a lot of something and only that. Unlike ...でいっぱい, indicates a negative feeling of the speaker about such a situation.

content: gives the feeling that there are not just many books in the room, there are too many, and thus the room is messy.

content.content: 【だろう】［N／Na　だろう］［A／V　だろう］In written language both men and women use this expression, but in spoken language, it is generally used by men. The polite form of this is でしょう.
1. ...だろう〈supposition, conjecture〉

content: あしたもきっといい天気だろう。

content.content: The weather will probably be nice tomorrow, too.

content: この辺は木も多いし、たぶん昼間も静かだろう。

content.content: This area also has many trees and it’s probably quiet in the daytime.

content: 北海道では、今はもう寒いだろう。

content.content: Hokkaido must already be cold.

content: この程度の作文なら、だれにでも書けるだろう。

content.content: Anyone should be able to write simple sentences like this.

content: これだけ長い手紙を書けば、両親も満足するだろう。

content.content: My parents will probably be happy if I write a letter this long.

content: 彼がその試験問題を見せてくれた。ひどくむずかしい。わたしだったら、全然できなかっただろう。

content.content: He showed me the test questions. They were horribly difficult. If it were me, I probably wouldn’t have been able to answer any of them.

content: A:朝はずっと雪の中で鳥の観察をしていたんです。

content.content: I was watching birds in the snow all morning.
B:それは、寒かっただろうね。
It must have been cold.

content: A:お母さんたちは今頃どこにいるかしら。

content.content: I wonder where my mother and the others are right now.
B:もうホテルに着いているだろうよ。
They’ve got to have arrived at the hotel by now.

content: A:これでよろしいですか。

content.content: It this all right?
B:ああ、いいだろう。
Yes, I’d say so.

content: A:どれにしましょうか。

content.content: Which one shall we take?
B:これがいいだろう。
This one should be good.

Expresses the speaker’s supposition and is accompanied by falling intonation. The extent to which the speaker considers the fact to be true is higher than かもしれない, and this is often used with expressions like たぶん and きっと. Depending on the context, だろう can also be used to make the speaker’s judgment a little more vague, instead of using it for supposition.
2. ...だろう〈confirmation〉

content: A:君も行くだろう？

content.content: You’re also going, right?
B:はい、もちろん。
Yes, of course.

content: A:美術館はバスをおりてすぐみつかりました。

content.content: I got off the bus and found the art gallery right away.
B:行くの、簡単だっただろう？
It was easy to go, wasn’t it?

content: やっぱり、納得できなくてもう一度自分で交渉に行ったんだ。わかるだろう、ぼくの気持ち。

content.content: I couldn’t agree to it after all, so I went once again by myself to negotiate. You understand my feelings, don’t you?

Expresses confirmation, and is accompanied by a rising intonation. Has the connotation that the speaker expects the listener to agree with him. It is usually used by men. Women use でしょう or でしょ instead. These are used in spoken language.
3. ...だろうか

content: この計画に、母は賛成してくれるだろうか。

content.content: I don’t know if Mother will agree to this plan.

content: 今回の試合のためにはあまり練習できなかった。いい成績があげられるだろうか。

content.content: I couldn’t practice that much for this match. I wonder about my performance.

content: こんな不思議な話、だれが信じるだろうか。

content.content: Whoever would believe such a bizarre story?

content: 彼はこつこつと作品を作り続けているが、いつかその価値を認める人が出てくるだろうか。

content.content: He keeps working steadily on the piece, but will the time ever come that someone will recognize its value?

content: A:佐々木さん、こんな仕事を引き受けてくれるだろうか。

content.content: I wonder if Sasaki-san will take on a job like this?
B:だいじょうぶだよ。喜んで引き受けてくれるよ。
Don’t worry, I’m sure she’ll be glad to.

content: このコンテスト、はたしてだれが優勝するだろうか。

content.content: I wonder who will ever win this contest in the end.

content: A:山下さん、欠席ですね。

content.content: Yamashita-san is absent.
B:うん。病気だろうか。
Yes. I wonder if he’s ill.

content: この選挙は、雨が降ったからだろうか、投票率が非常に低かった。

content.content: I wonder if it was because it rained, but the voting rate was very low for this election.
Expresses the doubtful or worried feeling of the speaker about the possibility of whether a certain thing will happen.

content: is an ironic expression meaning “who would believe it, no one would.” Can also be used as in
to indirectly question the listener by getting rid of any doubts the speaker has. In addition, can also be used parenthetically to express the speaker’s doubt, as in

content.content: 4. ...ではないだろうか［N／Na　ではないだろうか］［A／V　のではないだろうか］

content: さっきすれちがった人は、高校のときの同級生ではないだろうか。

content.content: Wasn’t the person we just passed our high school classmate?

content: この統計からは彼の述べているような予測をたてるのは無理ではないだろうか。

content.content: From these statistics, isn’t it rather impossible to put forward the prediction he mentioned?

content: 選手たちの調子がとてもいいから、今回の試合ではいい成績があげられるのではないだろうか。

content.content: The players are in very good condition, so we may be able to get a good result in today’s match.

content: 一日十ページ書いていけば、来月中には完成できるのではないだろうか。

content.content: If we write ten pages a day, shouldn’t we be able to finish it sometime next month?

content: 通子はけんかして以来少しやさしくなった。いろいろと反省したのではないだろうか。

content.content: Michiko has become kinder since the argument. Maybe she’s been reflecting on all sorts of things.

content: この道の両側に桜の木を植えれば、市民のいい散歩道になるのではないだろうか。

content.content: I think it might become a nice walking path for local residents if we plant cherry trees on either side of this street.
Indicates a supposition about whether something will happen. The speaker is not as certain as when using だろう, but indicates that he feels positive about it happening. In

content: , for example, the speaker feels that he can get a good result although he is not certain. If the speaker feels that the possibility is low, then だろうか is used. In spoken language, （ん）ではないだろうか is used.

content.content: 5. Nだろうが、Nだろうが

content: 相手が重役だろうが、社長だろうが、彼は遠慮せずに言いたいことを言う。

content.content: He doesn’t hesitate to say what he wants, whether it’s to a senior manager or the president.

content: 子供だろうが、大人だろうが、法を守らなければならないのは同じだ。

content.content: Whether you’re a child or an adult, everyone has to obey the laws just the same.

content: 彼は、山田さんだろうが、加藤さんだろうが、反対する者は容赦しないと言っている。

content.content: He’s saying that whether it’s Yamada-san or Kato-san, he won’t forgive those who oppose him.

content: もし鉄道が使えなければ、ボートだろうが、ヘリコプターだろうが、とにかく使える方法でできるだけ早くそこに到着しなければならない。

content.content: If the train can’t be used, we must get there as quickly as possible by any means available, whether it’s a boat or a helicopter.
Means that “regardless of X or Y, anyone (or anything) will do.” When adjectives or verbs are used, the expression takes the form A-かろうが and V-ようが, as in 暑かろうが寒かろうが, 生きようが死のうが, and 雨が降ろうが降るまいが.
6. ...だろうにa. ...だろうに

content: その山道は、子供には厳しかっただろうに、よく歩き通した。

content.content: That mountain path must have been hard for a child. He did well to walk all the way.

content: 忙しくて大変だっただろうに、よく期日までに仕上げたものだ。

content.content: It has to have been difficult as she was so busy, but she did well in getting it done on time.

content: 共同経営者を失ったのは痛手だっただろうに、彼は一人で会社を立て直してしまった。

content.content: He rebuilt the company single-handedly, despite the hardship he must have had of losing a co-manager.

content: 冬の水は冷たくてつらいだろうに、彼らは黙々と作業を続けていく。

content.content: Water in the winter must be cold and the job hard, but he continues working in silence.

content: きちんと読めばわかっただろうに、あわてたばかりに誤解してしまった。

content.content: If I had read it carefully I should have been able to understand, but because I hurried through it, I misunderstood.
Means “one would think so, and yet....” Often implies the speaker’s sympathy or criticism.
b. ...だろうに

content: あなたの言い方がきついから、彼女はとうとう泣き出してしまった。もっとやさしい言い方もあっただろうに。

content.content: Your way of speaking was so harsh that she ended up bursting into tears. There must have been a kinder way of saying it.

content: うちでグズグズしていなかったら、今頃は旅館に到着しておいしい晩ご飯を食べていただろうに。

content.content: If we hadn’t dillydallied at home, by now we would have arrived at the inn and be eating a delicious meal.

content: もしあの大金をこの会社に投資していたら、大儲けできただろうに。

content.content: If I had invested that large sum of money in this company, I would have made a fortune.

content: 地図と磁石をもって行けば、迷ってもそんなにあわてることはなかっただろうに。

content.content: If you had taken a map and a compass, even if you had gotten lost, you wouldn’t have panicked that much.
Expresses the feeling of regret that something didn’t happen.
7. ...のだろう→
【のだろう】
【ちがいない】［N／Na　 （である）にちがいない］［A／V　にちがいない］

content: あんなすばらしい車に乗っているのだから、田村さんは金持ちにちがいない。

content.content: Tamura-san must be very rich to be driving such a splendid car.

content: あそこにかかっている絵は素晴らしい。値段も高いにちがいない。

content.content: The picture hanging there is outstanding. It must also have had a high price.

content: 学生のゆううつそうな様子からすると、試験はむずかしかったにちがいない。

content.content: Judging from the students’ depressed looks, the exam must have been difficult.

content: あの人の幸せそうな顔をごらんなさい。きっといい知らせだったにちがいありません。

content.content: Look at that guy’s happy face. It must have been good news.

content: あの人は規則をわざと破るような人ではない。きっと知らなかったにちがいない。

content.content: He’s not someone who would break rules deliberately. He must have not known.

content: A:この足跡は？

content.content: What’s this footprint?
B:あの男のものだ。犯人はあいつに違いない。
It’s that man’s. He must be the culprit.

Expresses that, based on some sort of evidence, the speaker is certain about a matter. The degree of the speaker’s certainty about or possession of an idea is higher than when using だろう. This is frequently used in written language, but it tends to sound exaggerated; thus, with the exception of circumstances like

content: , expressions such as きっと...と思います are used instead.

content.content: 【ちっとも...ない】

content: この前の旅行はちっとも楽しくなかった。

content.content: The last trip was not fun at all.

content: 日本語がちっとも上達しない。

content.content: My Japanese hasn’t improved one bit.

content: A:ごめんね。

content.content: I’m sorry.
B:いや、いや。ちっともかまわないよ。
No, no, it’s not a problem at all.

content: 妻が髪形を変えたのに、夫はちっとも気がつかなかった。

content.content: His wife changed her hairstyle, but the husband didn’t notice it at all.

content: 久しぶりに帰国した友達のためにたくさんごちそうを作ったのに、疲れていると言ってちっとも食べてくれなかった。

content.content: I cooked a lot for my friend who had come home (from abroad) after a long time, but he said he was tired and didn’t eat a bite.

content: ダイビングはこわいものと思っていたが、やってみたら、ちっともこわくなかった。

content.content: I thought scuba diving was a scary thing, but when I tried it, it wasn’t the least bit scary.
Means すこしも/ぜんぜん...ない, and is used to strengthen negativity. It is used in spoken language and is more informal than すこしも. Unlike ぜんぜん, it is not used to express frequency.
（×）ちっとも行ったことがない。
I’ve never been at all.
（○）ぜんぜん行ったことがない。
I’ve never been there.
【ちなみに】

content: この遊園地を訪れた人は、今年五十万人に上りました。これは去年の三十万人を大きく上回っています。ちなみに迷子の数も千人と去年の倍近くありました。

content.content: The number of visitors to this amusement park reached 500,000 this year, far surpassing last year’s 300,
0. Incidentally, the number of lost children was about 1,000, nearly double that of last year.

content: この人形はフランスで三百年前に作られたもので、同種のものは世界に五体しかないといいます。ちなみにお値段は一体500万円。

content.content: This doll was made in France three hundred years ago, and it’s said that there are only five in the world. For your information, the price for each doll is five million yen.

content: 山田議員の発言は政局に大きな混乱をもたらした。ちなみに山田議員は一昨年も議会で爆弾発言をしている。

content.content: Congressman Yamada’s remark has caused much confusion in the political world. For your information, Yamada also made a bombshell speech in the legislature the year before last.

Used when adding something related to the principal matter, and means “for your reference....” Used in written language or formal spoken language (e.g. news reports or meetings). This expression cannot be used for expressing an additional action.
（×）買い物に出かけた。ちなみに、友達のところに寄った。
I went shopping. For your reference, I went to my friend’s place.
（○）買い物に出かけた。ついでに、友達のところに寄った。
I went shopping. I also stopped by a friend’s house while I was out.
【ちゃんと】
1. ちゃんと

content: めがねを新しいのに変えたら、ちゃんと見えるようになった。

content.content: I changed to new glasses, and now I can see OK.

content: おじいさんは耳が遠いと言っているが本当は何でもちゃんと聞こえている。

content.content: Grandfather says he can’t hear very well, but in fact he hears everything just fine.

content: そのとき言われたことは今でもちゃんと覚えている。

content.content: Even now I remember exactly what I was told at that time.

content: 親戚の人にあったらちゃんと挨拶するように母に言われた。

content.content: I was told by my mother to greet any relative properly when meeting them.

content: あの先生はみんながちゃんと席につくまで話し始めない。

content.content: That teacher doesn’t start talking until everyone is in his seat.

content: 今朝は7時にちゃんと起きたが、雨で走りに行けなかった。

content.content: I woke up right at seven this morning, but I didn’t go running because of the rain.

content: この問題にちゃんと答えられた人は少ない。

content.content: Few people were able to answer this question correctly.

content: わたしは朝どんなに忙しくてもちゃんと食べることにしている。

content.content: No matter how busy I am in the morning, I make sure I eat right.

Means “in the way it should be.” Used in many circumstances. The concrete meaning varies depending on the context. Expresses that something follows a method which is considered to be correct or appropriate. As in

content: , may be used to express that one is behaving in line with social customs without receiving criticism, or doing something without deviating from what had been planned.

content.content: 2. ちゃんとする

content: おばあさんはきびしい人だから、おばあさんの前ではちゃんとしなさい。

content.content: Grandmother is a strict person, so behave yourself in front of her.

content: 昨日来たときは仕事場がひどくちらかっていたけれど、だれかが片付けてちゃんとしたらしい。

content.content: The workplace was very messy when I came here yesterday, but it looks like someone has cleaned and put it all in order.

content: 客に会う前にちゃんとした服に着替えた。

content.content: I put on something suitable before meeting customers.

content: ちゃんとした書類がないと、許可証はもらえない。

content.content: You can’t get a permission form without the proper documents.

content: A:これ、変な名前だね。

content.content: This is a strange name, isn’t it?
B:ええ、でもちゃんとしたレストランですよ。
Yes, but it’s a perfectly fine restaurant.

content: A:彼女のお父さんは、娘の結婚に反対しているそうですね。

content.content: I hear her father is opposed to his daughter’s marriage.
B:ええ。相手を信用していないんです。わたしは、ちゃんとした人だと思いますよ。
Yes. He doesn’t trust the man. I think he’s an all right guy, though.

Used to express the behavior of someone in a suitable way according to the circumstances, or making something in an appropriate state. ちゃんとした is used when followed by a noun, and means “socially acceptable as it is appropriate and correct.”
【ちゅう】
1. Nちゅう〈duration〉

content: 会議中だから、入ってはいけない。

content.content: The meeting is in progress, so you can’t enter now.

content: 「営業中」の札がかかっている。

content.content: There is a notice “Open” hanging on the door.

content: その件はただいま検討中です。

content.content: That matter is currently under consideration.

content: 課長の休暇中に一大事が起こった。

content.content: Something serious happened during the section chief’s absence.

content: 工事中の道路が多くて、ここまで来るのに随分時間がかかった。

content.content: It took so long to get here because many roads are under construction.

content: 勤務中は個人的な電話をかけてはいけないことになっている。

content.content: You’re not allowed to make personal phone calls during work hours.

content: 彼女はダイエット中のはずなのに、どうしてあんなにたくさん食べ物を買い込むのだろう。

content.content: She’s supposed to be on a diet. Why is she buying up so much food?

ちゅう is written with the kanji 中. Means “in the middle of doing something,” or “(a situation) is continuing.” Please note that when used in this sense, it is always read ちゅう. Nouns used with this are generally related to activities.
Examples: 電話中(in the middle of a call), 交渉中(under negotiation), 婚約中(is engaged), 執筆中(currently writing), 旅行中(currently traveling), タイプ中(typing now).
Sometimes (N-)中is read じゅう. Means “all the time during....,” as in 一日中 or 一年中.
2. Nちゅう〈period of time〉

content: 午前中は、図書館にいて、午後は実験室にいる予定だ。

content.content: I’m planning to stay in the library all morning and be in the laboratory in the afternoon.

content: 戦時中、一家はばらばらになっていた。

content.content: The family was scattered everywhere during the war.

content: 夏休み中に水泳の練習をするつもりだ。

content.content: I plan to practice swimming during summer vacation.

content: 彼は試験期間中に病気になって気の毒だった。

content.content: It’s really too bad that he got ill during the examination period.

content: この製品は、試用期間中に故障したら、ただで修理してもらえる。

content.content: This product can be repaired without charge if it breaks during the trial period.
Used with a noun to express time, in the sense of “for a certain period of time.” Note that ごぜんちゅうis used but ごごちゅうis not.
【ちょっと】
1. ちょっと〈degree〉

content: ちょっと食べてみた。

content.content: I tried eating a little.

content: 借りた本はまだちょっとだけしか読んでいない。

content.content: I’ve only read a little of the book I borrowed.

content: 目標額の10万円にはちょっと足りない。

content.content: It’s not quite enough for the target price of 100,000 yen.

content: 手紙をちょっと書き直した。

content.content: I revised the letter a little.

content: 韓国語は、ちょっとだけ話せる。

content.content: I can only speak a little Korean.

content: ちょっと左へ寄ってください。

content.content: Please move a little to the left.

content: 今日はちょっと寒い。

content.content: It’s a bit cold today.

content: 試験の問題はいつもよりちょっとむずかしかったが、なんとか解けた。

content.content: The exam questions were a bit harder than usual, but I somehow managed to solve them.
This expresses a small amount or a low degree. It is normally used in spoken language.
2. ちょっとa. ちょっと〈moderation of degree〉

content: ちょっと電話してきます。

content.content: I’ll just go and make a phone call.

content: ちょっと用がありますので、これで失礼します。

content.content: There’s something I have to do, so please excuse me.

content: ちょっとおたずねしますが、この辺に有田さんというお宅はありませんか。

content.content: Could I just ask you if there is a family named Arita-san residing near here?

content: すみません、ちょっと手伝ってください。

content.content: Excuse me, could you help me a little?

content: A:ちょっとこの辺でお茶でも飲みませんか。

content.content: Shall we have some tea somewhere near here?
B:ええ、そうですね。
Yes, let’s do that.

content: A:これで決まりですね。

content.content: All right, so it’s decided then.
B:ちょっと待ってください。わたしはまだいいとは言っていません。
Wait a minute. I haven’t said OK yet.

content: A:おでかけですか。

content.content: Are you going out?
B:ええ、ちょっとそこまで。
Yes, just around the corner.

A euphemistic expression which is used in spoken language. Does not mean a small amount, but rather hints that the degree is small. Used when the speaker is talking about his own action or when he is asking someone to do something. Adding ちょっと softens the sentence when requesting something.

content: is a set phrase used in greetings.

content.content: b. ちょっと〈softening of tone〉

content: A:この手紙の文章は、ちょっとかたすぎませんか。

content.content: The sentences in this letter are a little formal, aren’t they?
B:そうですか。じゃ、もう一度書き直してみます。
You think so? I’ll try to re-write it then.

content: A:山田さんが急病で、当分会社に出てこられないそうです。

content.content: I hear Yamada-san has suddenly taken ill and won’t be able to come to the office for some time.
B:そうか、それはちょっと大変だな。
Is that so? That’s a problem.

content: この問題は君にはちょっと難しすぎるんじゃないかな。

content.content: This question is a little too hard for you, isn’t it?

content: 一日で仕上げるのはちょっと無理だ。

content.content: It’s impossible to finish it in one day.

content: A:10時ではいかがでしょうか。

content.content: What about ten o’clock?
B:10時はちょっと都合が悪いんですけど。
I’m afraid ten o’clock is not convenient for me.
Used to soften the tone by attaching it to negative expressions such as 大変 (serious/problematic), 無理 (impossible), むずかしい (difficult).
c. ちょっと〈unfinished sentence〉

content: A:この写真ここに飾ったらどう？

content.content: How about putting this picture here?
B:そこはちょっとね...。
There? Well...

content: A:ご都合が悪いんですか。

content.content: Is that not a good time for you?
B:ええ、ちょっと月曜日は...。
Yes, I’m afraid Monday is not so good.

content: A:このコピー機空いていますか？

content.content: Is this photocopy machine free?
B:あ、すみません。まだ、ちょっと...。
Oh, sorry, not just yet I’m afraid.
Used in conversation. Only ちょっと is uttered and the rest of the sentence is omitted. Hints at negative content used for avoiding something which is difficult to say.

content: , for example, indicates that the speaker doesn’t like the place very much. Also used to soften the tone in expressions of refusal. When the latter sentence is omitted, as in
and

, it is used on its own instead of expressions of refusal, and is so understood by the listener. When using it for positive meaning such as acceptance, the latter part of the sentence is not normally omitted.

content.content: 3. ちょっと〈positive evaluation〉

content: この本、ちょっとおもしろいよ。

content.content: This book is quite interesting.

content: この先にちょっといいレストランをみつけた。

content.content: I found a pretty nice restaurant just up ahead.

content: A:彼がどんな小説を書くか、ちょっと楽しみです。

content.content: It’s going to be fun to see what kind of novel he’ll write.
B:そうですね。
Yeah, it will.

content: A:新しい職場はどう？

content.content: How is your new workplace?
B:課長さんがちょっとすてきな人なの。
The section chief is kind of attractive.

When attached to a good evaluation or an expression which indicates attribution, ちょっと indicates that the speaker judges something to be “better than usual,” rather than “a little.” A euphemistic expression. Close to かなりin meaning. すこし does not have this type of usage.
4. ちょっと...ないa. ちょっと...ない〈positive evaluation〉

content: こんなにおもしろい映画は最近ちょっとない。

content.content: You don’t often see such an interesting film nowadays.

content: この本は読み出したらちょっとやめられませんよ。

content.content: You really can’t stop once you start reading this book.

content: こんなおいしいもの、ちょっとほかでは食べられない。

content.content: You can’t easily eat something so delicious elsewhere.

content: あの人のあんな演説は、ちょっとほかの人にはまねができないだろう。

content.content: I don’t think many others can match those presentation skills of his.
Used with a negative expression for emphasis, but is in fact often used when evaluating something of higher or greater value than usual.

content: is an expression for praising a good film.

content.content: b. ちょっと...ない〈softening of tone〉

content: A:田中先生の研究室はどちらですか。

content.content: Where is Tanaka-sensei’s research laboratory?
B:すみません。ちょっとわかりません。
Sorry, I’m not sure.

content: A:あしたまでに全部現像してもらえますか。

content.content: Can I have all these photos printed by tomorrow?
B:それは、ちょっとできかねます。
That’s just not going to be possible.

content: A:今、ちょっと手が放せないので、あとでこちらからお電話します。

content.content: I just can’t drop what I’m doing now, so I’ll give you a call later.
B:そうですか。じゃあ、あとでよろしく。
I see. OK, I’ll leave it with you (please call me later).
Used with negative expressions. Softens the negative phrase. Does not mean “little.” B’s words in

content: , for example, are a euphemistic expression for saying that the speaker actually “doesn’t know at all,” not “there is just some part which he doesn’t know.”

content.content: 5. ちょっと〈appeal〉

content: ちょっと、そこのおくさん、財布落としましたよ。

content.content: Excuse me, madam, you’ve dropped your wallet.

content: ちょっと、これは何ですか。スープの中にハエが入ってるじゃないの。

content.content: Hey, what’s this! Isn’t this a fly in the soup?

content: ちょっと、だれか来て手伝って。

content.content: Hey, someone come give me a hand.

content: ちょっと、お願いだからもう少し静かにしてて。

content.content: Come on, can I ask you to be a little quieter?
Used to attract attention. Not just for calling someone, but can express feelings such as criticism, intimidation, or appeal, depending on the intonation.
6. ちょっとしたNa. ちょっとしたN〈moderation of degree〉

content: ちょっとしたアイデアだったが、大金になった。

content.content: It was just a small idea, but it led to a large profit.

content: ちょっとした風邪がもとで、亡くなった。

content.content: It was only a minor cold to start with but led to his death.

content: 酒のつまみには、何かちょっとしたものがあればそれでいい。

content.content: For snacks to go with the sake, if you have something light, that would do.
Means “something light, not especially considerable, something small.”
b. ちょっとしたN〈positive evaluation〉

content: 彼は、両親の死後、ちょっとした財産を受け継いだので、生活には困らない。

content.content: He inherited a little bit of a fortune after his parents’ death, so he has no trouble in everyday life.

content: パーティーでは奥さんの手料理が出た。素人の料理とはいえ、ちょっとしたものだった。

content.content: His wife’s homemade cooking was served at the party. Even though it was just an amateur’s cooking, it was rather good.

content: 彼の帰国は、まわりの人にとって、ちょっとした驚きだった。

content.content: His return to his home country was a bit of a surprise to people around him.
Signifies something above average and is often replaced by かなりのN. ちょっとしたN describes judgment or evaluation in a somewhat vague, moderate way.
【っきり】

content: ふたりっきりで話しあった。

content.content: We talked it over just between the two of us.

content: 一晩中つきっきりで看病した。

content.content: I never left his side all night.

content: 家を飛び出して行ったっきり戻って来ない。

content.content: He bolted out of the house and won’t come back.
Spoken version of きり.
【きり】
【っけ】［N／Na　だ（った）っけ］［A-かったっけ］［V-たっけ］［...んだ（った）っけ］

content: あの人、鈴木さんだ（った）っけ？

content.content: That was Suzuki-san, right?

content: 君、これ嫌いだ（った）っけ？

content.content: You didn’t like this, right?

content: この前の日曜日、寒かったっけ？

content.content: Was this last Sunday cold?

content: もう手紙出したっけ？

content.content: Have we posted the letter already?

content: 明日田中さんも来るんだっけ？

content.content: Tanaka-san is coming tomorrow, too?

content: しまった！今日は宿題を提出する日じゃなかったっけ。

content.content: Oh, no! Wasn’t today the day to submit homework?
Used to confirm something the speaker cannot remember clearly. Also used when talking to oneself as if to confirm something, as in

content: . Informal spoken language. Polite forms are N／Naでしたっけ, V-ましたっけ, and ...んでしたっけ, but A-かったですっけ is not used. Spoken language.

content.content: 【っこない】［R-っこない］

content: A:毎日5時間は勉強しなさい。

content.content: Study for five hours a day.
B:そんなこと、できっこないよ。
I can’t possibly do that.

content: いくら彼に聞いても、本当のことなんか言いっこないよ。

content.content: No matter how many times you ask, he’ll never tell you the truth.

content: 俳優になんかなれっこないと親にも言われたけれど、夢は捨てられなかった。

content.content: I was told by my parents that I could never become an actor, but I couldn’t give up my dream.

content: こんなひどい雨では頂上まで登れっこないから、きょうは出かけるのはやめよう。

content.content: It’s impossible to climb to the summit in this horrible rain, so let’s cancel our departure for today.

content: 山口さんなんか、頼んだってやってくれっこないよ。

content.content: There’s no way Yamaguchi-san will help, even if you ask her.

Used with a verb stem to deny categorically the possibility of something happening. Informal spoken language, similar to 絶対...しない, ...するはずがない or ...するわけがない. Often used in conversation with someone close.
【ったら】
1. Nったら

content: 太郎ったら、女の子の前で赤くなってるわ。

content.content: Look at that Taro blushing in front of the girls!

content: A:松井さん昔はほんとうに小さくてかわいかったけど、今はすっかりいいお母さんだね。

content.content: Matsui-san, you were so cute and little back in those days, and now you’re every inch a mother.
B:まあ先生ったら。小学校を卒業してからもう 20 年ですもの。
Well, Sensei (Professor), it’s already been twenty years since I graduated.

content: A:このカレンダーの赤丸なんだったかな。

content.content: What is this red circle on the calendar?
B:もうあなたったら忘れたの。私たちの結婚記念日じゃありませんか。
You’ve forgotten? It’s our wedding anniversary!

content: 多恵子ったら、どうしたのかしら。いくら呼んでも返事がないけど。

content.content: What happened to Taeko? She won’t reply no matter how many times I call her.

content: お母さんったら。ちゃんと話を聞いてよ。

content.content: Come on, Mother. Listen to me carefully!
Used in informal spoken language and means “as for....” Used when the speaker raises a topic with feelings of closeness, teasing, criticism, or worry implied. Mostly used by children and women.
2. Vったら

content: こっちへ来いったら。

content.content: I said come here.

content: やめろったらやめろよ。

content.content: (a man speaking) I said to stop, so stop it!

content: やめてったらやめてよ。

content.content: (a woman speaking) I told you to stop, so why don’t you stop?

Attached to imperative forms or te-forms to make a strong suggestion to the listener, with the feeling of “why won’t you do such-and-such, even though I’m telling you to?” The same verb is often repeated. The imperative form is used by men. Informal spoken language.

content: A:ひとりで出来るの？

content.content: Can you do it alone?
B:出来るったら。
I said I can.

content: A:飲んだらコーヒーカップちゃんと洗って。

content.content: Be sure to wash your coffee cup after you’re done.
B:うん、わかった。
OK, sure.
A:ほんとにわかったの？　コーヒーカップは？
Did you really understand? Where is your coffee cup?
B:わかったったら。同じことそう何度も言うなよ。
Hey, I said I understood. Don’t say the same thing over and over!
Expresses the feeling of refuting a doubt which the listener has expressed to the speaker. Follows a statement by the listener. Informal spoken language.
4. ったらない

content: うちのおやじ、うるさいったらない。

content.content: My old man (Dad) is a real pain.

content: あの時のあいつのあわてかたったらなかったよ。

content.content: I can’t tell you how much he panicked at that time.
Expresses that the degree is severe. Informal spoken language.
【って】
1. NってN

content: これ、キアリーって作家の書いた本です。

content.content: This is a book written by a writer named Carey.

content: A:留守の間に人が来ましたよ。

content.content: Someone visited in your absence.
B:なんて人？
What was his name?

content: 佐川さんって人に会いました。友達だそうですね。

content.content: I met someone named Sagawa-san. Apparently she’s your friend.

content: 駅前のベルって喫茶店、入ったことある？

content.content: Have you been to a cafe called Bell in front of the station?

Used in informal conversation. Contracted form of NというN. Also used in the form NっていうN, as in キアリーっていう作家 and なんていう人. Used for things that the speaker doesn’t know, or things that the listener is thought not to know. Becomes なんて, rather than って, after the interrogative 何.
（×）なんって人。
What’s he called?
（○）なんて人。
What’s he called?
2. ...って〈topic, theme〉［Nって］［Aって］［V（の）って］

content: WHOって、何のことですか。

content.content: What’s “WHO”?

content: ヒアリングって、何のことですか。

content.content: What does “hearing” mean?

content: ゲートボールって、どんなスポーツですか。

content.content: What kind of sport is gateball?

content: 赤井さんって、商社に勤めているんですよ。

content.content: That Akai-san—she works at a trading company.

content: 山田課長って、ほんとうにやさしい人ですね。

content.content: You know Yamada-kacho, the section chief—he’s really a kind person, isn’t he?
