content.content: He plans to run a coffee shop starting next year. That, however, will depend on how successful he is in obtaining the funding for it.

content: 今回の人事異動は君の将来を考えてのことだ。不満もあるだろうが辛抱してくれたまえ。

content.content: This personnel change has your future in mind. Some things may not be to your liking, but please just be patient.

The form XはYてのことだ means that X has or will become possible because condition Y has been satisfied. Emphasizes a necessary condition. Although used in conversation, it is not particularly informal in tone.

【ては】［N／Na　では］［A-くては］［V-ては］A combination of the te-form of a predicate plus は. When used with nouns or na-adjectives, it takes the te-form of だ and becomes では, but in written language であっては can also be used. In spoken language, this form is often reduced to ちゃ or じゃ.

1. ...ては〈condition〉Accompanied at the end of the sentence by an expression conveying some kind of  negative evaluation. Means that the condition indicated by ...ては will result in an undesirable outcome. Often used when recommending that such an outcome be avoided.
a. ...ては

content: この仕事に時給 500 円では人がみつかりません。

content.content: You won’t find anyone to do this job for 500 yen an hour.

content: 先方の態度がそんなにあやふやでは将来が心配だ。

content.content: That kind of shilly-shallying attitude on their part really makes me worried about the future.

content: コーチがそんなにきびしくては、だれもついてきませんよ。

content.content: If the coach is that strict, no one will go along with him.

content: そんなに大きな声を出しては魚が逃げてしまう。

content.content: That loud a voice will scare all the fish away.

content: そのことを彼女に言ってはかわいそうだ。

content.content: Telling her that would be really mean.
Generally followed by a negative comment. Indicates that a certain condition is problematic or should be avoided.
b. V-ていては

content: そんなにテレビばかり見ていては目が悪くなってしまうよ。

content.content: Watching that much TV will hurt your eyesight.

content: そんなにたばこばかり吸っていては、体に障りますよ。

content.content: That kind of constant smoking will ruin your health.

content: そんなに先生に頼っていては、進歩しませんよ。

content.content: You’ll never make any progress if you just depend on your teacher all the time.
Expresses a warning or piece of advice. Used to point out a problem someone has and to encourage a different course of action.
c. Vのでは

content: そんなに遠くから通勤していらっしゃるのでは大変ですね。

content.content: It must be hard for you to commute from so far away.

content: 年間 200 万円もかかるのではとてもその大学には行けない。

content.content: If it costs two million yen a year, you certainly can’t go to that university.

content: A:山下さん子供が5人いるんですって。

content.content: I heard Yamashita-san has five children.
B:5人もいるのでは、毎日大騒ぎだろうな。
With five children, it’s probably bedlam every day!

content: そんなふうに頭ごなしに否定されたのでは議論にならないじゃないですか。

content.content: With that kind of flat-out rejection, the discussion doesn’t go anywhere, does it.

When のでは follows a verb, the meaning is “with that sort of situation.” The last part of the sentence then states the outcome of such a situation, or the speaker’s reaction or opinion. In spoken language, Vんでは and Vんじゃ are often used.
d. V-る／V-ない　ようでは

content: 最初の日から、仕事に遅刻するようでは困る。

content.content: His coming to work late from the very first day is a real problem for us.

content: この程度の練習に参るようでは、もうやめたほうがいい。

content.content: If just this much practice is too much for you, you’d better quit.

content: そんなささいなことで傷ついて泣くようではこれから先が思いやられる。

content.content: If such a little thing hurt her and made her cry, what’s going to happen in the future?

content: こんな簡単な文書も書けないようでは、店長の仕事はつとまらない。

content.content: He’s not fit to be shop manager if he can’t write something this easy.

content: こんな短い距離も歩けないようでは夏の登山はとても無理だ。

content.content: If he can’t walk that short a distance, then the summer mountain-climbing trip is completely out of the question.

Used with expressions that convey a negative meaning, such as 困る (troublesome), いけない (wrong), and 無理だ (impossible). Means “this sort of situation is problematic.” Often used to disparage or criticize another person. In some contexts, may be used to scold or reprove someone directly.
【ようだ2】
2. V-ては〈repetition〉Attaches to a verb and expresses repetition of an action or phenomenon.
a. V-てはV

content: 家計が苦しいので、母はお金の計算をしてはため息をついている。

content.content: Funds were severely limited, and Mother let out sigh after sigh as she worked on the household budget.

content: 子供は二、三歩歩いては立ち止まって、母親の来るのを待っている。

content.content: The little child stopped every two or three steps and waited for her mother.

content: その女性は誰かを待っているらしく、1ページ読んでは顔をあげて窓の外を見ている。

content.content: The woman reading the book appears to be waiting for someone, and she lifts her head every page or so to look out the window.

content: 一行書いては考え込むので、執筆はなかなかはかどらない。

content.content: He pauses to think after every line, so his writing is making little progress.

content: 学生の頃は、小説を読んでは仲間と議論したものだ。

content.content: When I was a student, I used to read novels and then discuss them with my friends.
Expresses an action repeated after a certain time. In

content: , it is used together with たものだ and expresses the recollection of a formerly repeated action.

content.content: b. V-てはV、V-てはV

content: 書いては消し、書いては消し、やっと手紙を書き上げた。

content.content: After countless writings and erasures, he finally finished the letter.

content: 作ってはこわし、作ってはこわし、を何度もやりなおして、ようやく満足できるつぼができあがった。

content.content: Again and again he made it, only to break it and start over, and at last he completed the pot to his satisfaction.

content: 降ってはやみ、降ってはやみの天気が続いている。

content.content: The weather continues with rain off and on.

content: 食べては寝、寝ては食べるという生活をしている。

content.content: His life is nothing but eating and sleeping, sleeping and eating.
Two verbs are used twice in the same order to indicate that an action or phenomenon is repeated. As in

content: , the order may be switched to create the form V1-てはV2、V2-てはV1.

content.content: 【てはいけない】
1. V-てはいけない

content: 遊んでいたらおじいさんがきて、「芝生に入ってはいけないよ」と言った。

content.content: When we were playing, an old man came and said, “Keep off the grass.”

content: この薬は、一日に三錠以上飲んではいけないそうだ。

content.content: Apparently you’re not supposed to take more than three tablets of this medicine a day.

content: この場所に駐車してはいけないらしい。

content.content: It looks like we’re not supposed to park in this place.

content: きみ、はじめて会った人にそんな失礼なことを言っちゃいけないよ。

content.content: Listen, you can’t say such rude things to someone you’ve just met.

content: A:おかあさん、公園へ行っていい？

content.content: Mom, it is OK to go to the park?
B:宿題をすまさないうちは、遊びに行ってはいけませんよ。
You can’t go out and play when you haven’t finished your homework.

Expresses prohibition. In plain form, it is used for general statements of prohibition or by men speaking to someone of lower status. The corresponding polite form いけません is typically used by people in a supervisory position, such as parents, teachers, and superiors in the workplace, when they are speaking to someone being supervised.
2. V-なくてはいけない→
【なくてはいけない】
【てはいられない】
1. Nではいられない

content: きみは大人になりたくないと言うが、人はいつまでも子供ではいられない。

content.content: You may say that you don’t want to become an adult, but no one can stay a child forever.

content: ずっと大学にいたいが、いつまでも学生のままではいられない。

content.content: I want to stay in college longer, but I can’t be a student for the rest of my life.

content: わたしは同級生の彼と友達でいたいのに、彼はこのままではいられないと言う。

content.content: Even though I want to stay friends with that classmate, he says it isn’t possible to go on like this.

content: ずっとお世話になりっぱなしではいられないし、仕事を探すつもりです。

content.content: I really shouldn’t stay here forever taking advantage of your generosity, so I intend to look for a job.
Nでいる means that the subject will remain in the condition signified by N; use of いられない indicates that the present situation cannot continue as it is.
2. V-てはいられない

content: 時間がないから、遅れて来る人を待ってはいられない。すぐ始めよう。

content.content: There’s no time, so we can’t wait for latecomers. Let’s get started right away.

content: A:すっかりよくなるまで寝ていないと。

content.content: You should stay in bed until you’ve recovered completely.
B:こんなに忙しいときに寝てはいられないよ。
There’s no way I can stay in bed when I’m this busy.

content: あしたは試験だから、こんなところでのんびり遊んではいられない。

content.content: I can’t relax and have a good time with a big test coming up tomorrow.

content: 今晩はお客が何人か来るし、テニスなんかしてはいられない。早く買い物に行かなければならない。

content.content: I have guests coming this evening, so playing tennis is out of the question. I have to go shopping right away.

content: 今うちの商品はよく売れているが、うかうかしてはいられない。新しい製品がどんどん出てくるからだ。

content.content: Our product is selling well now, but we can’t afford to get careless. There are new products coming out one after the other, you know.

content: この事態を傍観してはいられない。

content.content: I can’t just sit back and watch this situation from the sidelines.

content: スキーのシーズンが始まると、わたしはじっとしてはいられない。

content.content: Once the skiing season starts, I can’t keep still.

content: こうしてはいられない。早く、知らせなくちゃ。

content.content: We can’t go on like this. We’ve got to hurry up and tell them what happened.

Used to indicate situations of urgency which should not continue, or for which quick action is desired. Often accompanied by adverbs such as のんびり (in a leisurely manner), うかうか (carelessly), and じっと (fixedly, steadily).
【てはだめだ】
1. V-てはだめだ〈prohibition〉

content: 駐車場で遊んではだめだ。出て行きなさい。

content.content: You can’t play in the parking lot. Please leave.

content: 「その花をとってはだめよ。」と姉が弟に言った。

content.content: “You mustn’t pick that flower,” she told her brother.

content: 文句ばかり言っていてはだめだ。自分でなんとかしろ。

content.content: Don’t just complain. Do something on your own.

content: こんなところでへばってはだめだ。あと1キロだ。しっかりしろ。

content.content: You can’t collapse at this point. There’s just one more kilometer to go. Pull yourself together!

content: 「今、あの人を叱ってはだめです。もうすこし様子を見ましょう。」と彼女は部下をかばった。

content.content: “It won’t do to reprimand him now. Let’s wait a little longer and see what happens,” she said, coming to the defense of her subordinate.

content: そんな浅いところから、飛び込んではだめだ。

content.content: You must not dive from such a shallow place.

Expresses prohibition. Often used by people in a supervisory position, such as teachers, parents, and managers, when they are speaking to someone being supervised. Often reduced from では to じゃ, or from ては to ちゃ. Same as V-てはいけない.
2. ...てはだめだ［N／Na　ではだめだ］［A-くてはだめだ］［V-ていてはだめだ］

content: 写真をとるのに、こんなに暗くてはだめだ。

content.content: It’s too dark here for taking photos.

content: 秘書になりたいそうだが、言葉がそんなにぞんざいではだめだ。

content.content: She says she wants to be a secretary, but her rough way of speaking is a real problem.

content: 富士山へ登りたいのなら、そんな靴ではだめです。登山靴をはきなさい。

content.content: If  you want to climb Fuji-san (Mt. Fuji), those shoes are no good. Wear climbing boots.

content: 今でもお母さんに洗濯してもらっているんですか。それではだめです。自立したかったら、自分でやりなさい。

content.content: Are you still having your mother do your wash? That’s no good! If you want to be independent, do it yourself.

content: 君のように遊んでばかりいてはだめだ。学生は勉強しなくてはいけない。

content.content: You can’t just fool around and have fun all the time. Students have to study!

Expresses the judgment that under a certain condition, it will be impossible to attain a certain goal. The goal is sometimes expressed in words, and sometimes only alluded to in the context. Often used in conversation. The contracted forms じゃ（あ）だめだ and ちゃ（あ）だめだ are also used.
As in

content: , this form may also be combined with verbs to create the construction V-ていてはだめだ, which is used to state that the present situation is unacceptable and to criticize or reprimand someone.

content.content: 【てはどうか】［V-てはどうか］

content: A:この辺でちょっと休憩してはどうですか。

content.content: How about taking a break here?
B:そうですね。
That sounds good.

content: 作戦を変えてみてはどうですか。

content.content: How about changing strategies?

content: この問題については、議長に一任してはどうだろうか。

content.content: What if we leave this matter up to the chairperson?

content: A:家の譲渡のことで家族の間でもめているんです。

content.content: The family is bickering about the transfer of the house.
B:弁護士に相談してみてはどうですか。
Why don’t you consult a lawyer?

content: A:この壁はちょっと暗いですね。壁紙を取りかえてみてはどうでしょうか。

content.content: Don’t you think this wall is a little dark? How about changing the wallpaper?
B:そうですね。
That could help.

content: しばらく何も言わないでそっとしておいてみては？

content.content: How about saying nothing for a while and just letting things be?

An idiomatic expression used to make suggestions or recommendations. Often used in the form V-てみては. Essentially synonymous with V-たらどうか, but V-てはどうか has the tone of written language and is commonly used when writing letters or speaking in formal situations, etc. In ordinary conversation, the V-たらどうか form is  preferred. V-ちゃどうか is used in casual conversation. In polite language, forms such as V-てはいかがですか and V-てはいかがでしょうか are used. In

content: , the latter half of the expression has been omitted.

content.content: 【てはならない】［V-てはならない］

content: 一度や二度の失敗であきらめてはならない。

content.content: It doesn’t do to give up after only one or two failures.

content: 警察が来るまで、だれもここに入ってはならないそうだ。

content.content: Apparently no one is allowed to enter until the police arrive.

content: ここで見たり聞いたりしたことは決して話してはならないと言われた。

content.content: I’ve been told that I shouldn’t under any circumstances talk about anything I’ve seen or heard here.

Expresses prohibition. Often used to state general cautions or warnings, and only in special cases is it used to address someone directly regarding a particular incident. Used mostly in written language. Both V-てはならない and its more polite form V-てはなりません are used to address someone directly in special cases only. In spoken language, forms such as V-ちゃあだめだ or V-ちゃいけない are commonly used.
【てほしい】→
【ほしい】2
【てまもなく】→
【まもなく】
【てみせる】［V-てみせる］

content: かれは柔道の型を教えるためにまずやってみせた。

content.content: To teach the juudoo form, he first showed how it’s done.

content: 歌がおじょうずだそうですね。一度歌ってみせてください。

content.content: I hear you’re good at singing. Please sing for us once.

content: ファックスの使い方がまだわからないので、一度やって見せてくれませんか。

content.content: I don’t know how to use this fax machine yet, so could you please show me once?

content: トラクターぐらいなら、一度やってみせてもらったら、後は一人で扱えると思います。

content.content: I think I could operate a tractor on my own, if someone showed me how to do it once.
Expresses the actual demonstration of an action in order to introduce or promote better understanding of something.
【てみる】
1. V-てみる

content: 一度そのめずらしい料理が食べてみたい。

content.content: I’d like to try that unusual dish just once.

content: 先日最近話題になっている店へ行ってみました。

content.content: The other day, I went to see that shop everyone’s been talking about.

content: ズボンのすそを直したので、ちょっとはいてみてください。

content.content: I’ve adjusted the hem of these pants, so please just try them on.

content: 電話番号は電話局へ問い合わせてみたのですが、わかりませんでした。

content.content: I tried contacting the telephone company to ask for the number, but they couldn’t tell me.

content: パンダはまだ見たことがない。一度見てみたいと思っている。

content.content: I’ve never seen a panda. It would be nice to see one someday.

content: 電車をやめて、自転車通勤をしてみることにした。

content.content: I decided to stop taking the train and try commuting by bicycle.

content: どの車を買うか決める前に、車に詳しい人の意見を聞いてみようと思っています。

content.content: Before I decide what kind of car to buy, I’m thinking of asking the opinion of someone who knows a lot about cars.

Indicates taking concrete action in order to find out more about a certain thing, place, etc. Not used when someone has the intention to try doing something but doesn’t actually carry out the action. For example, the sentence 会ってみたが会えなかった (I tried to meet her but couldn’t) would be a mistake. The correct statement in such a case would be 会おうとしたが会えなかった.
2. V-てみてはじめて

content: 病気になってみてはじめて健康の大切さが身にしみた。

content.content: It wasn’t until I became ill that I keenly felt the importance of good health.

content: 親に死なれてみてはじめてありがたさがわかった。

content.content: I never knew what my parents meant to me until I lost them.

content: 彼がやめてみてはじめて、この会社にとって重要な人物だったということがわかった。

content.content: It was only after he quit that we realized how important he had been to this company.
Means “for the first time after a certain situation came about.” みて in this expression does not mean “give something a try” but “a certain situation arises.”
3. V-てみると

content: 表にして比べてみると、両者は実際にはあまり違いがないということがわかる。

content.content: If you make a table and compare them, you can see that there actually isn’t much difference between the two.

content: そのルポルタージュをよく読んでみると、作者はその場所へは実際に行ったことがないとわかった。

content.content: When I read that reportage carefully, I realized that the author has never actually been to that location.

content: 今振り返ってみると、5年前の会社設立当時が自分の人生の中で最も大変だったと思う。

content.content: Now that I look back, I think the hardest time of my life was when I first established this company five years ago.

content: もう一度考えてみると、この批評はある程度当たっていないこともない。

content.content: If I think about it again, this criticism isn’t completely groundless.

content: 仕事をやめてみると、急に生活の空間が広がったような気がした。

content.content: When I quit my job, I felt as if my whole life had suddenly broadened.

content: 生のイカなんて、みかけは気持ちが悪かったが、食べてみると、意外においしかった。

content.content: You know raw squid—well, it looked revolting, but when I tried eating it, it was surprisingly good.

content: A:意地悪に見えるけど、彼は本当は好意でそう言ったんじゃないんですか。

content.content: It seems like he was being mean, but didn’t he really say that with good intentions?
B:そう言われてみると、そんな気もします。
When you put it that way, I think that might be true.

content: 一夜明けてみると、大木がなぎ倒されていた。

content.content: The next morning, the huge tree had been toppled.

Expresses the triggering of a discovery. The trigger may or may not be an intentional action. When it is intentional, the meaning is “I attempted such-and-such, and as a result, this is what I learned.” As in

content: and

, when there is no intention, the meaning is “when a certain condition arose, something was discovered.” Even if the word みる is omitted, the meaning remains essentially the same, but expressions like 読んでみると and 振り返ってみると are commonly-used idiomatic expressions.

content.content: 4. V-てみたらa. V-てみたら

content: 電話でたずねてみたら、もう切符は売り切れたと言われた。

content.content: When I called and asked, I found that the tickets had already been sold out.

content: きらいなうなぎを思い切って食べてみたらおいしいので驚いた。

content.content: When I took the plunge and tried eating eel, which I didn’t like, I was surprised at how good it was.

content: 新聞に広告を出してみたら、予想以上の反響があった。

content.content: There was a much greater response than expected when they tried advertising in the newspaper.
Expresses the triggering of a discovery.
b. V-てみたらどう

content: A:山下さんは全然わかってくれません。

content.content: Yamashita-san doesn’t understand at all.
B:もう一度会って話してみたらどうですか。
What if you try to meet with him and talk it over one more time?

content: 結果をまとめる前にもうすこしデータを増やしてみたらどうですか。

content.content: Before you summarize your results, why don’t you try to gather a little more data?

content: ひとりで考えていないで、専門家に相談してみたらどうですか。

content.content: Don’t just mull it over all by yourself—how about consulting a specialist?
Used to recommend that someone try to do something.
5. V-てもみない

content: この作品がコンクールに入選するなんて考えてもみなかった。

content.content: I never thought this piece would be selected for the contest.

content: できないと思い込んでいたので、試してもみなかった。

content.content: I was sure I couldn’t do it, so I didn’t even try.

content: はじめから断られると思っていたので、言ってもみなかった。

content.content: From the outset I thought I would get turned down, so I never said anything.

content: 彼女と結婚することになるとは思ってもみなかった。

content.content: I never imagined that I would end up marrying her.

content: あの人にもう一度会えるなんて思ってもみなかった。

content.content: I never thought I would get to see that person once more.

content: 始める前は、こんなに大変な仕事だとは思ってもみなかった。

content.content: Before I started, I never believed this would be such hard work.

Often used in the form てもみなかった to emphasize that something was not done. There is a limited set of verbs that can be used with this form. 思ってもみなかった is an idiomatic expression that is commonly used after a certain situation has actually arisen to convey the meaning “this was completely unexpected.”
6. V-てもみないで

content: 本を読んでもみないで、何が書いてあったかどうしてわかるだろう。

content.content: If you don’t even try reading the book, how can you know what it said?

content: 食べてもみないで、文句を言うのはやめてください。

content.content: Please stop complaining, when you haven’t even tried eating it.
A slightly more emphatic way to say V-ないで. Often used to express criticism.
7. Nにしてみれば→
【にしてみれば】
【ても】［N／Na　でも］［A-くても］［V-ても］A combination of the te-form of a predicate and も. For nouns and na-adjectives, it becomes でも. In informal spoken language, the forms たって and だって are also used.
1. ...ても〈converse condition〉

content: この仕事は、病気でも休めない。

content.content: I can’t take time off from this job even if I get sick.

content: その車がたとえ 10 万円でも、今の私には買えない。

content.content: Even if that car cost only 100,000 yen, I’m not in a position to buy it now.

content: 不便でも、慣れた機械の方が使いやすい。

content.content: It’s easier to use a machine that you’re used to, even if it’s a little inconvenient.

content: 風が冷たくても平気だ。

content.content: Even if the wind is cold, it doesn’t bother me.

content: ほしくなくても、食べなければいけない。

content.content: Even if you don’t want to, you have to eat something.

content: 国へ帰っても、ここの人々の親切は忘れないだろう。

content.content: Even after I return home, I don’t think I’ll ever forget the kindness of the people here.

content: 今すぐできなくても、がっかりする必要はない。

content.content: You don’t have to be discouraged if you can’t do it right away.

content: わたしは、まだ勉強不足だから、今試験を受けても受からないだろう。

content.content: I still haven’t studied enough, so if I took the test now, I doubt I’d pass.

content: たとえ両親に反対されても彼との結婚はあきらめない。

content.content: Even if my parents are against it, I’m not going to give up on marrying him.
Expresses a converse condition that negates the resultative conditional “If X happens, then Y results” (XならばY). For example, the ...ても constructions in

content: and

, respectively, negate the relationship between the conditions “If I get sick, I can take time off” and “After I return home, I’ll forget the kindness of the people here”; these express that even if condition X arises, condition Y will not result. Example
shows how the adverb たとえ is sometimes used with this construction.

content.content: 2. ...ても〈parallel condition〉Presents two or more conditions and expresses that no matter which condition is realized, the outcome will be the same.
a. ...ても

content: 2を二乗すると4になりますが、－2を二乗しても4になります。

content.content: If you square 2 you get 4, and if you square minus 2 you also get

content: 飛行機で行くと料金は片道2万円ぐらいですが、新幹線で行っても費用はだいたい同じです。

content.content: The fare for a one-way plane ticket is about 20,000 yen, but going by shinkansen (bullet train) costs about the same.

content: A:演奏会、あと 20 分で始まるんですが、タクシーで行けば間に合うでしょうか。

content.content: The concert starts in about twenty minutes—can I still make it if I take a taxi?
B:会場は駅の近くですから、歩いて行っても間に合うと思いますよ。
The hall is near the station, so I think you can make it in time even if you walk.

When two clauses expressing different conditions that yield the same outcome are presented sequentially, as in XならばZ and YならばZ, the second conditional clause is expressed with ても, in the form Y（であっ）てもZ. Since this construction conveys the meaning that either condition will yield the same result, it can be rephrased as XてもYてもZ.
（例）2を二乗しても、－2を二乗しても4になります。
Either squaring 2 or squaring minus 2 will yield
b. ...ても...ても

content: うちの子供はニンジンでもピーマンでも好き嫌いを言わないで食べます。

content.content: Our child isn’t picky—she’ll eat carrots and green peppers and everything.

content: 天気がよくても悪くても、雨が降っても風がふいても、新聞配達の仕事は休めない。

content.content: Whether the weather is good or bad, whether the rain falls or the wind blows, delivering newspapers is a job that doesn’t allow for holidays.

content: 道を歩いてもデパートへ入っても人でいっぱいだ。

content.content: Whether I walked on the streets or went into department stores, there were crowds of people everywhere.

content: 辞書で調べても先生に聞いても、まだこの文の意味が理解できない。

content.content: Even after consulting my dictionary and asking my teacher, I still don’t understand what this sentence means.

content: スポーツをしても映画を見ても気が晴れない。

content.content: Even playing sports or watching movies doesn’t lift my spirits.
The construction XてもYても (...ても) Z juxtaposes two (or more) conditions and conveys the meaning that either (or any) one of them will yield the same result.
c. V-てもV-なくても

content: 今回のレポートは出しても出さなくても、成績には全く影響ありません。

content.content: Your grade will not be affected at all, regardless of whether or not you submit this report.

content: 全員が参加してもしなくても、一応人数分の席を確保しておきます。

content.content: Whether everyone comes or not, I will at least make sure there are enough seats for all the members.

content: 1日ぐらいなら食べても食べなくても体重はたいして変化しない。

content.content: Eating or not eating for just one day won’t change your weight that much.
In forms like ...してもしなくても, this juxtaposes an affirmative condition with a negative one to express the idea that, whichever the case, the outcome will not change.
d. V-てもV-ても

content: このズボンは洗っても洗っても汚れが落ちない。

content.content: I’ve washed and washed these pants but still can’t get them clean.

content: 宿題が多すぎて、やってもやっても終わらない。

content.content: I have so much homework that even though I work and work I’m still never finished.

content: 働いても働いても、暮らしは全然楽にならない。

content.content: No matter how hard I work, it never gets easier to make a living.

The same verb is repeated in order to emphasize that, no matter how much effort one makes, the desired outcome cannot be obtained. Although the final clause is usually a negative expression, there are cases, as shown below, when an affirmative expression may follow. Even in these cases, however, the implication is that the outcome is undesirable.
（例）追い払っても追い払ってもついてくる。
No matter how often I chase it away, it keeps on following me.
（例）雑草は取っても取ってもすぐ生えてくる。
I weed and weed, but they grow back in no time at all.

3. 疑問詞...てもWhen question words such as 何, どこ, だれ, どれ, いつ, and どう are used with a ても conditional, the meaning is that, no matter what the condition is, the resulting situation is inevitable. (When a negative form follows, it means that the situation will fail to occur.)
a. いくら...ても

content: いくら華やかな職業でも、つらいことはたくさんある。

content.content: No matter how spectacular the occupation, there will be many difficult challenges.

content: いくら高い車でも、使わなかったら宝のもちぐされだ。

content.content: However expensive a car may be, if you don’t use it, it’s a waste of a valuable possession.

content: 給料がいくらよくても、休日のない職場には行きたくない。

content.content: No matter how good the salary is, I don’t want to work at a place where there are no days off.

content: いくら騒いでも、ここは森の中の一軒家だから大丈夫だ。

content.content: This is the only house in the middle of a forest, so you can make as much noise as you want.

content: いくらお金を貰っても、この絵は絶対手放せない。

content.content: No matter how much money I might get for it, I’ll never give up this picture.

content: このビデオの会話は、いくら聞いてもよく分からない。

content.content: I can’t understand the conversation on this video, no matter how many times I listen to it.
いくらXても expresses that the frequency or degree of an action or situation is very great. Used to say that, although this is a powerful condition, it has no effect on the realization of a outcome.
The outcome is usually contrary to anticipation or expectation. For example, in

content: , the expectation that “If you have a spectacular occupation, it must always be enjoyable” is contradicted by the second clause “...there will be many difficult challenges.” In
, the resulting situation is “I still don’t understand,” which runs counter to the expected outcome “If I listen to this video many times, I should be able to understand it.”

content.content: b. どんなに...ても

content: このコンピューターはどんなに複雑な問題でも解いてしまう。

content.content: This computer can solve any problem, no matter how complex.

content: どんなにつらくても頑張ろう。

content.content: I will keep on trying, no matter how hard it gets.

content: どんなに熱心に誘われても、彼女はプロの歌手にはなりたくなかった。

content.content: No matter how fervently she was scouted, she did not want to become a professional singer.

content: どんなに大きい地震がきても、この建物なら大丈夫だ。

content.content: No matter how big an earthquake may hit, this building is safe.

content: 妻はわたしがどんなに怒っても平気である。

content.content: My wife stays calm, no matter how angry I get.
Usage is the same as いくら...ても (Usage a) above. どんなに can be replaced by いくら, but the latter is more conversational.
c. 疑問詞...ても

content: だれが電話して来ても、取りつがないでください。

content.content: No matter who calls, please don’t put them through.

content: どんな仕事でも、彼は快く引き受けてくれる。

content.content: He readily agrees to do any kind of work.

content: 本は、どこで買っても同じ値段だ。

content.content: Books are the same price wherever you buy them.

content: あの人はいつ見ても美しい。

content.content: She’s beautiful no matter when you see her.

content: 何をしても、あのショックが忘れられない。

content.content: Whatever I do, I can’t forget the shock I felt.

Means どのような場合でもY (no matter what the situation is, Y holds true). No matter what element is linked to the question word, this expresses that the end result will always be situation Y (or, in the case of a negative form, that it will always fail to be Y).
d. どうV-ても

content: どう言ってみても、彼の決心を変えさせることはできなかった。

content.content: No matter how I put it, I couldn’t find a way to make him change his mind.

content: どう計算してみても、そこへ着くまで 10 時間はかかる。

content.content: No matter how you calculate, it’s going to take ten hours to get there.

content: どうがんばっても、前を走っている三人を追い抜くのは無理だと思った。

content.content: I thought that, no matter how hard I tried, it was going to be impossible for me to overtake the three runners in front.
Uses a verb of intentional action to express that, no matter what measures are taken, the outcome will not meet one’s expectations.
e. なん+助数詞+V-ても

content: 何回聞いても名前が覚えられない。

content.content: However many times I hear them, I can’t remember names.

content: この論文は何度読み返しても、理解できない。

content.content: No matter how many times I re-read this paper, I can’t make sense of it.

content: 何回話し合っても、この問題は簡単には解決できないだろう。

content.content: This is not a problem that will be easily solved, no matter how many times we talk about it.

content: あの店の料理は何度食べてもあきない。

content.content: I never get tired of the food at that restaurant, no matter how often I eat it.

content: あの映画は何回見ても面白い。

content.content: That movie is always fun to watch.

Uses an action verb to express the notion that no matter how many times the action is done, the outcome is still the same. The outcome expressed in the last part of the sentence is often contrary to expectation, as in

content: . However, it can sometimes be a desirable situation, as in
and

content.content: 4. ...ても...ただろう

content: たとえ、努力しても合格できなかっただろう。

content.content: I don’t think I could have passed even if I’d tried.

content: 彼は頭がいいので、努力しなくても合格できただろう。

content.content: He’s really smart, so he probably could have passed without much effort.

content: 人をだまして金儲けをするような商売では、たとえ成功しても両親は喜んでくれなかっただろう。

content.content: In a business where you earn money by deceiving people, I doubt that my parents would have been happy for me even if I’d succeeded.

This is a counter-factual conditional that negates the propositional relation XしていたらYしていただろう (if someone had done X, then s/he probably would have done Y). In the form XしてもYしなかっただろう (even if someone had done X, s/he probably wouldn’t have done Y), it is used to state the assumption that even if X had happened, it would have had no effect on the fact that Y did not happen.
For example,

content: denies the conditional relationship in the resultative counter-factual conditional “If he had worked hard, then he probably would have passed” (which means he didn’t work hard and thus failed).
means “He did not actually work hard, but even if he had, the result probably still would have been failure.”
negates the resultative counter-factual conditional “If he hadn’t worked hard, then he probably wouldn’t have passed” (which means he actually did work hard and thus passed).
means “He did work hard, but even if he hadn’t, the result probably still would have been success.”
雨でも運動会は行われた。

content.content: The sports meet was held even though it rained.

content: 頭が痛くても学校を休まなかった。

content.content: He didn’t miss school even when he had headaches.

content: ドアは強く押しても開かなかった。

content.content: The door wouldn’t open, even when I pushed hard on it.

content: いくら待っても彼女は現れなかった。

content.content: No matter how long we waited, she didn’t show up.

content: この本は難しすぎて、辞書を引いて読んでも、ほとんど理解できなかった。

content.content: This book was too difficult—I could hardly understand any of it, even reading it with a dictionary.
The construction XてもYた, which uses the ta-form at the end of the sentence, expresses the fact that both X and Y happened. For example,

content: means “it rained, but the sports meet was held.” While the ても form used here is similar in meaning to が, けれども, or のに, when ても is used after an action verb, it conveys the nuance that the action was repeated, or that although the action was carried out to an extreme degree, the anticipated outcome was not obtained. Thus, in sentences like
, which include いくら, it is not possible to replace ても with が, けれども, or のに.

content.content: （×）いくら待った｛が／けれど／のに｝彼女は現れなかった。
We waited how long, {but/however/even though} she didn’t show up.
6. V-てもR-きれない

content: 彼の親切に対しては、いくら感謝してもしきれない。

content.content: I cannot thank him enough for all of his kindness.

content: 学生時代になぜもっと勉強しておかなかったのかと、悔やんでも悔やみきれない。

content.content: There is no limit to the regret I feel that I didn’t study harder during my school days.

content: ここで負けたら、死んでも死にきれない。

content.content: I can’t bear to die if we lose now.
The same verb is repeated to emphasize its meaning. For example,

content: shows deep appreciation, and
emphasizes a strong sense of regret. This construction is rather idiomatic, and the range of verbs that can be used is limited. 死んでも死にきれない in
is a strong expression of being unable to give up on something or feeling deep regret.

content.content: 7. V-てもどうなるものでもない

content: いまから抗議してもどうなるものでもない。

content.content: Raising an objection now won’t accomplish anything.

content: もう一度彼に会ってもどうなるものでもないと彼女は思った。

content.content: She concluded that even if she met with him one more time, it would still be pointless.

content: 性格は直らないのだから、あの人に説教してもどうなるものでもない。

content.content: His personality can’t be mended, so even giving him a lecture will accomplish nothing.
Means that even if some action is attempted, it will not lead to a solution. Conveys a feeling of resignation.
8. V-たくてもV-れない

content: 急に仕事が入って、飲みに行きたくても行けないのだ。

content.content: Some urgent business has come up, so however much I want to go out drinking, I can’t.

content: きらいな先生の前では、泣きたくても泣けない。

content.content: I couldn’t cry in front of a teacher I hate, even if I wanted to.

An idiomatic expression that combines the ても form of V-たい with the negative form of a V-れる potential verb. Means “even if I want to, I cannot.” Used to emphasize that circumstances do not allow a certain action, or to make an excuse.

content: A:入ってもいいですか。

Please do.

content: あそこは、夕方八時から朝六時までは駐車してもいいらしい。

Could you come at about ten?

I’m sorry, but photography is not permitted here.

content.content: My mother told me that in the future I can do as I like.

content.content: If you can’t drink, then there’s no need to force yourself.

Expresses permission or approval. In conversation, it is used to give permission to or to seek permission from the other person. Also used in the form V-てもよい. Essentially synonymous with V-てもかまわない. Vていい is also used.
When setting the time for an appointment, it is not correct to say 何時に来てもいいですか (What time may I come?). 何時に来たらいいですか or 何時に来ればいいですか should be used instead (What time should I come?).
As shown in

content: and
, ...なくてもいい means ...する必要がない (it is not necessary to...).

content.content: 2. V-てもいい〈possibility〉

content: ワインのかわりに、しょうゆで味をつけてもいい。

content.content: Instead of wine, soy sauce may also be used for flavoring.

content: そのときすぐ断ってもよかったのだが、失礼だと思ったので、そうしなかったのだ。

content.content: I could have refused right then, but I thought it would be impolite, so I didn’t.

content: 滞在をもう少し延ばしてもよかったのだが、切符がとれたので、予定通り帰って来た。

content.content: We could have stayed a little longer, but since we managed to get tickets, we returned home as scheduled.

content: 就職の時、東京の会社を選んでもよかったのだが、最終的には、郷里に帰る方をとったのだ。

content.content: When I was looking for a job, I could have chosen a company in Tokyo, but ultimately I chose to return to my hometown.

content: タクシーで行ってもよかったのだが、車で送ってくれるというので、乗せてもらった。

content.content: I could have gone by taxi, but since she offered me a ride, I took her up on it.

Expresses that there are other alternatives or possibilities. With this meaning, the form ていい is seldom used. When used to refer to the past, the meaning is “there were other choices, but I did not take them.”
3. V-てもいい〈offer〉

content: A:わたしは、月曜日はちょっと家を出られないんですが。

content.content: Monday is not a good day for me to leave the house.
B:じゃあ、わたしがお宅へ伺ってもいいですよ。
OK, then I could come to your house.
A:それじゃ、そうしてください。
Then please do.

content: A:彼がいないので、この仕事が進まないんだ。

content.content: He isn’t here, so no progress is being made on this task.
B:ぼくが引き受けてもいいよ。
I could take it on.
Used by the speaker to volunteer to do a certain action. Usually used to offer to do something that will benefit the other party.
4. ...てもいい〈concession〉［N／Na　でもいい］［A-くてもいい］

content: 印かんがなければ、サインでもいいですよ。

content.content: If you don’t have your seal, then you can just sign it.

content: 給料がよければ、すこしぐらい危険な仕事でもいい。

content.content: If the pay is good, then I don’t mind a job with a little risk.

content: 試合をするのに人数が足りないので、へたでもいいですから、誰か参加者を探してください。

content.content: There aren’t enough people for the match, so please look for someone else to participate, even if he’s not very good.

content: 多少不便でもいいから、自然環境のいいところに住みたいと思う。

content.content: Even if it’s a little inconvenient, I think I want to live somewhere with a good natural environment.

content: わたしでもよければ、手伝います。

content.content: If I can be of any assistance, I’ll help.

content: この部署には若くてもいいから、しっかりした人を入れたい。

content.content: We don’t mind putting someone young in this post, provided that he or she is dependable.

content: 手紙でも、電話でもいいから、連絡してみてください。

content.content: Either a letter or a telephone call will do—just try to contact him.
This is an expression of concession, indicating that while a compromise may not be the best measure, it will still suffice. When several alternatives are listed, as in

content: , it indicates the range of possible choices. Same as ...てもかまわない.

content.content: 【てもかまわない】
1. V-てもかまわない〈permission〉

content: この集まりにはすこしぐらい遅れてもかまわない。

content.content: It doesn’t matter if you come a little late to this gathering.

content: このレポートは英語で書いても、日本語で書いてもかまいません。

content.content: This report may be written in either English or Japanese.

content: A:すみません、ここで待っていてもかまいませんか。

content.content: Excuse me, is it all right if I wait here?
B:いいですよ。どうぞ。
It’s fine. Go right ahead.

content: 今できないのなら、あとでやってもかまいません。

content.content: If you can’t do it right now, it’s no problem to do it later.

content: ここでやめてもかまわないが、そうすると、この次、また、初めからやり直さなければならないだろう。

content.content: You can quit at this point, but if you do, then next time you’ll probably have to start all over again from the beginning.

content: 飲めないのなら、無理に飲まなくてもかまいません。

content.content: If you can’t drink, then you don’t have to force yourself.

content: ここでは何もしなくてもかまわないから、ゆっくり養生して、元気をとりもどしてください。

content.content: You don’t have to do anything here, so take time to recuperate and  recover your health.

content: A:10 分待ちましたよ。

content.content: I waited for ten minutes.
B:すみません、でも先に行ってくれてもかまわなかったのに。
Sorry, but you could have gone ahead of me....
Expresses permission or approval. In conversation, it is used to give permission to or seek permission from the other party. てもいい can be used instead. As shown in

content: and
, ...なくてもかまわない means ...する必要がない (it is not necessary to...).

content.content: 2. V-てもかまわない〈possibility〉

content: タクシーで行ってもかまわなかったのだが、車で送ってくれるというので、乗せてもらった。

content.content: We could have gone by taxi, but since she said she would drive us, we rode with her.

content: お金は十分あったので、高いホテルに泊まってもかまわなかったのだが、そうはしなかった。

content.content: Since we had plenty of money, we could have stayed at an expensive hotel, but we didn’t.

Often used in the form てもかまわなかった, which indicates that it would have been possible to select a different alternative. Often suggests that such-and-such is not actually what happened. Can be replaced by ...てもよかった.
3. ...てもかまわない〈concession〉［N／Na　でもかまわない］［A-くてもかまわない］

content: 何か上着のようなものを貸してください。大きくてもかまいません。

content.content: Please lend me something like a jacket. I don’t mind if it’s too big.

content: A:このスープはまだ十分温まっていませんよ。

content.content: This soup hasn’t been heated long enough.
B:ぬるくてもかまいません。
I don’t mind if it’s lukewarm.

content: テレビは、映りさえすれば古くてもかまわない。

content.content: If the TV works, then I don’t care if it’s old.

content: 静かなアパートを捜している。静かな場所なら、多少不便でもかまわない。

content.content: We’re looking for a quiet apartment. If it’s in a quiet place, then we don’t mind if it’s not such a convenient location.

content: 意味が通じるのなら、表現は多少不自然でもかまわない。

content.content: If the meaning gets across, I don’t care if the expression is a little unnatural.

content: だれでもかまわないから、わたしの仕事を代わってほしい。

content.content: I don’t care who, but I want someone else to do my work.

content: 手紙は手書きでも、ワープロ書きでもかまわない。

content.content: The letter can be written by hand or by computer.

content: 誰か一人呼んでください。吉田さんでも、小山さんでもかまいません。

content.content: Please call someone. It can be Yoshida-san, or Koyama-san.

content: A:何時頃お電話すればいいですか。

content.content: What time shall I call?
B:朝でも晩でもかまいませんから、なるべく早く結果を知らせてください。
It doesn’t matter if it’s morning or evening, just tell me the results as soon as you can.
Expresses concession. Means that, while it is not ideal, the outcome obtained after a compromise is acceptable. When several alternatives are listed, as in

content: , it indicates the range of possibilities. てもいい can be used instead.

content.content: 【てもさしつかえない】［N／Na　でもさしつかえない］［A-くてもさしつかえない］［V-てもさしつかえない］

content: 無理をしなければ運動をしてもさしつかえありません。

content.content: If you don’t strain yourself, you may do some exercise.

content: ひとりかふたりのお客さまなら、人数を変更なさってもさしつかえありません。

content.content: There is no problem changing the number of guests, if it’s only one or two people.

content: この書類ははんこがなくてもさしつかえない。

content.content: This document doesn’t need to have your seal.

content: 最終的に決定するのに、全員の意見が聞けなくてもさしつかえはないと思う。

content.content: I think it’s still all right to make the final decision, even if we can’t listen to everyone’s opinion.

Used in the forms てもさしつかえない and なくてもさしつかえない. An expression of concession which means that the condition indicated by ても is acceptable or presents no difficulties. さしつかえはない is also used. Close in meaning to てもいい and てもかまわない, but usually used in more formal situations than these two.
【てもしかたがない】［N／Na　でもしかたがない］［A-くてもしかたがない］［V-てもしかたがない］

content: このレポートでは、やりなおしを命じられても仕方がない。

content.content: With this report, it’s no wonder I’ve been ordered to do it over again.

content: あんないいかげんな練習では、一回戦で負けてもしかたがない。

content.content: With such sloppy practice, it’s no wonder they lost the first match.

content: あんなに雪が降っては、時間通りに着けなくてもしかたがない。

content.content: With that heavy a snowfall, it can’t be helped if they don’t arrive on time.

content: これだけたくさんの人がいては、彼女がみつけられなくても仕方がない。

content.content: With this many people around, it’s no surprise we can’t find her.

content: チームの選手にけが人が多かったから、今回は最下位でもしかたがない。

content.content: There were a lot of injured players on the team, so ending up in last place this time was unavoidable.

content: 買い物にいくひまがないから、今夜のパーティーは古い服でもしかたがない。

content.content: I don’t have time to go shopping, so I’ll have to wear something old to the party tonight.

content: このところ雨ばかりだから、ビアガーデンのお客が少なくてもしかたがない。

content.content: The small number of customers at the beer gardens is to be expected, with all the rain we’ve had recently.

content: この辺は便利だから、マンションの値段が高くても仕方がない。

content.content: This is a convenient location, so it’s no wonder the condominiums are pricey.

Used in both the forms てもしかたがない and なくてもしかたがない. Means that a situation is unfortunate or unsatisfactory, but there is no other choice but to accept it. The cause or reason that brought about the situation at hand is often stated by adding ては to the end of the preceding clause.
【てもみない】→
【てみる】5
【てもよろしい】
1. V-てもよろしいa. V-てもよろしい〈permission〉

content: A:君たち、きょうは、もう帰ってもよろしい。

content.content: (the company president) Everyone, you can go home for today.
B:はい、社長。
Yes, Shachoo.

content: A:いやなら、おやめになってもよろしいですよ。

content.content: If you’d rather not, it would be all right not to go.
B:いいえ、参ります。
No, I will go.

content: A:書類はここでご覧になってもよろしいですよ。

content.content: You may look at the documents here, if you’d like.
B:ありがとうございます。
Thank you very much.
Used to grant permission. In plain form, it carries an authoritative tone. Also, the polite form よろしいです is a formal expression.
Since granting permission is something that is usually done by someone in authority, use of this form by someone of lower status to someone of higher status often sounds rude.
b. V-てもよろしいですかV-てもよろしいでしょうか

content: A:先生、お聞きしたいことがあるんですが、少しお時間をいただいてもよろしいでしょうか。

content.content: Sensei (Professor), there is something I would like to ask you. Could I possibly ask for a little of your time?
B:いいですよ。
Yes, that’s fine.

content: A:先生、これを見せていただいてもよろしいですか。

content.content: Sensei (Professor), would it be all right if I took a look at this?
B:ええ、どうぞ。
Yes, go ahead.

content: A:必要書類は明日お届けにあがってもよろしいでしょうか。

content.content: Would it be all right if I brought the necessary documents to you tomorrow?
B:結構です。よろしく。
Yes, that would be fine. Please do.

content: 社長、では10時ごろ、お迎えに参ってもよろしいでしょうか。

content.content: (to the company president) Shachoo, would it be all right then if I come to pick you up at about ten o’clock?

content: お客様、お部屋を掃除させていただいてもよろしいでしょうか。

content.content: Excuse me...would it be all right if I cleaned your room now?

A very polite way of asking for permission that is used when speaking to someone of higher status. Honorific language is used throughout the rest of the sentence too. This is a more polite form of てもいいですか. Also, でしょうか is more polite than ですか.
2. てもよろしい〈possibility〉

content: A:ネクタイピンはこちらをおつけになってもよろしいですね。

content.content: I wonder if you might prefer this tie pin.
B:そうですね。
Yes, you may be right.

content: 《料理の番組》これは、キャベツをお使いになってもよろしいと思います。

content.content: 《a cooking program》 I think that cabbage may also be used in this dish.
Indicates the possibility of choosing other alternatives. In comparison to てもいい, it is more formal.
3. ...てもよろしい〈concession〉［N／Na　でもよろしい］［A-くてもよろしい］

content: 面会はあしたでもよろしい。

content.content: The interview could also be arranged for tomorrow.

content: これ、自宅まで届けていただけますか。来週でもよろしいんですけど。

content.content: Would it be possible to have this delivered to my home? It can wait until next week, though.

content: 酒さえあれば、食べ物はなくてもよろしい。

content.content: As long as there’s sake, we don’t need anything to eat.

content: 応募したいんですが、経験が不十分でもよろしいですか。

content.content: I would like to apply, but are you sure my relative inexperience doesn’t matter?

An expression of concession. Means that, while a compromise may not be ideal, it is still acceptable. In conversation, it is used to grant or seek permission. When used in the plain form to another person, it sounds authoritative. The polite form よろしいです is a rather formal way of speaking.
【てもらう】
1. V-てもらう

content: 私はタイ人の友だちにタイ料理を教えてもらった。

content.content: I had my Thai friend teach me some Thai cooking.

content: 山本さんに香港映画のDVDを貸してもらった。

content.content: I borrowed a Hong Kong movie DVD from Yamamoto-san.

content: 今年の冬はホストファミリーにスキーに連れて行ってもらいました。

content.content: This winter my host family took me skiing.

content: みんなに 1000 円ずつ出してもらって、お祝いの花束を買った。

content.content: I had everyone contribute 1,000 yen each and bought a bouquet of flowers to say congratulations.

content: いろいろと準備してもらったのに、中止になってしまって申しわけありません。

content.content: I am very sorry it’s been cancelled, after all of your help with the preparations.

content: プリントが足りなかったら、隣の人に見せてもらってください。

content.content: If there aren’t enough handouts, please have your neighbor show you his or hers.

V-てもらう is used to express, from the speaker’s point of view, that someone has performed an action that benefits the speaker (or someone in the speaker’s in-group). When the speaker has requested the action, the form V-てもらう is often used. When the other party has performed the action of his/her own accord, it is often the case that s/he is made the subject of the sentence and the form V-てくれる is used instead.

With expressions such as 教えてもらう (be taught), 貸してもらう (be lent), and 送ってもらう (be sent), in which objects or knowledge are transferred from another party to the speaker (or his/her in-group), the form からV-てもらう may also be used, as in 友だちからタイ料理の作り方を教えてもらった (I learned Thai cooking from my friend).
2. V-てもらえるかV-てもらえないか

content: A:ちょっとドア、閉めてもらえる？

content.content: Say, can you close the door?
B:いいよ。
Sure.

content: 買い物のついでに郵便局に寄ってもらえるかな。

content.content: Can you maybe drop by the post office for me while you’re out shopping?

content: ちょっとペン貸してもらえますか。

content.content: Could you lend me your pen for a minute?

content: A:ねえ、悪いけどちょっと1000 円貸してもらえない？

content.content: Umm, sorry to ask, but could you lend me 1,000 yen?
B:いいよ。
Sure.

content: すみません、ここは子供の遊び場なんですけど、ゴルフの練習はやめてもらえませんか。

content.content: Excuse me, but this is a play area for children, so could I ask you to stop practicing golf here?

content: ここは公共の場なんですから、タバコは遠慮してもらえませんか。

content.content: Since this is a public place, could you please refrain from smoking?

The potential form of もらう is used to request the addressee to perform an action for the speaker (or the speaker’s in-group). The plain form is used when the speaker is addressing someone with lower status or with whom s/he has a close relationship. The polite form has a wide range of use, including that of cautioning another person, as in

content: and

content.content: To make a request more polite, forms such as V-てもらえないでしょうか, V-ていただけませんか, and V-ていただけないでしょうか are used.
3. V-てもらえるとありがたいV-てもらえるとうれしい

content: A:今度の日曜日、もし時間があったら、引っ越しの手伝いに来てもらえるとありがたいんですけど。

content.content: If you have time this coming Sunday, I would really be grateful if you could come and help me move.
B:あ、いいですよ。
Yes, I can do that.

content: 私が買い物から帰ってくるまでに掃除しておいてもらえるとうれしいんだけど。

content.content: I would be happy if you could finish cleaning by the time I get back from shopping.

content: 約束の時間をもう少し遅くしてもらえると、助かるんだが。

content.content: It would be a big help if you could make our appointment a little later.
V-てもらえると is followed by words such as ありがたい, うれしい, and 助かる and expresses a polite request. The sentence is often left inconclusive, ending with expressions like けど or が.
4. V-てやってもらえるかV-てやってもらえないか

content: わるいけど、ちょっと太郎の宿題を見てやってもらえる？

content.content: Sorry to ask, but can you look over Taro’s homework?

content: 彼女、人間関係でかなり落ち込んでるみたいなんだけど、それとなく一度話を聞いてみてやってもらえる？

content.content: She seems to be pretty depressed over some personal relationships, so could you find a time just to listen to her?

content: うちの娘に英語を教えてやってもらえないかしら。

content.content: I wonder if you might be able to teach our daughter English.
Used to make a request of the addressee for an action that pertains to the speaker in some way.
【てやまない】［V-てやまない］

content: 愛してやまないアルプスの山々は今日もきれいだ。

content.content: My beloved Alps are once again beautiful today.

content: 彼女は、女優をしていた間、ずっとその役にあこがれてやまなかった。

content.content: When she was an actress, she earnestly longed to play that role.

content: 今井氏は一生そのことを後悔してやまなかった。

content.content: Imai-shi never stopped regretting that all his life.

content: あの方はわたしの父が生涯尊敬してやまなかった方です。

content.content: He was a person for whom my father had a lifelong respect.

Attaches to verbs of emotion and signifies that the emotion continues to be strong. Can be used with respect to both positive and negative emotions. Often used in novels and other types of prose, but not very common in conversation.
【てやる】［V-てやる］

content: 子供に新しい自転車を買ってやったら、翌日盗まれてしまった。

content.content: The day after I bought my child a new bicycle, it was stolen.

content: 東京の弟に、今年もふるさとの名物を送ってやった。

content.content: This year again, I sent some specialties from our hometown to my younger brother in Tokyo.

content: 犬を広い公園で放してやったら、うれしそうに走り回っていた。

content.content: After letting my dog loose in the spacious park, he was running around joyfully.

content: A:荷物、重かったら持ってやるよ。

content.content: If your bag is too heavy, I’ll carry it for you.
B:あ、いい、大丈夫。
Oh, no, I’m OK.

content: こんな給料の安い会社、いつでも辞めてやる。

content.content: I’m ready to quit this low-paying company anytime.

content: A:あんたなんか死ねばいいのよ。

content.content: Why don’t you just go ahead and die?
B:そんなに言うんなら、ほんとに死んでやる。
If that’s what you want, then I’ll kill myself just to make you happy.
Expresses an action performed by the speaker (or someone in the speaker’s in-group) for someone of lower status, or for an animal. Sometimes used as an expression of anger, as in

content: and
, with the meaning that the speaker is ready to perform an action undesirable to the listener. When the addressee is the same status as the speaker, the form V-てあげる is used.

content.content: 【てん】
1. ...てん［Nのてん］［Na なてん］［A-いてん］［Vてん］

content: 兄より弟の方が行動力の点でまさっている。

content.content: The younger brother outdoes the older one when it comes to getting things done.

content: 新しい車の方が、燃費の点で安上がりだ。

content.content: A new car is more economical, if you consider fuel efficiency.

content: 値段の点では、A電気のもののほうが安いが、性能の点では、B電気のほうがよくできている。

content.content: In terms of price, the products at Electronics Store A are cheaper, but in terms of performance, the ones at Electronics Store B are better made.

content: この種類の犬は性格のやさしい点が好まれている。

content.content: This breed of dog is well-liked for its gentle disposition.

content: この小説は、現代の世相をよくとらえている点で評価が高い。

content.content: This novel is highly praised for the way it captures the essence of the present times.

content: 経験がある点で、彼のほうがこの仕事には向いている。

content.content: The fact that he has experience makes him better suited for this work (than other applicants).

content: 若い社員がたくさん活躍している点で、この会社はおもしろそうだ。

content.content: The fact that young employees are so actively involved makes this company seem interesting to me.

content: この点でみんなの意見が分かれた。

content.content: People’s opinions were divided on this point.
Used to highlight one particular characteristic of something, out of many.
2. ...というてん［Nというてん］［Na だというてん］［A-いというてん］［Vというてん］

content: 彼の設計は創造性という点で高く評価された。

content.content: His designs are praised for their originality.

content: この会社は、給料はいいが、労働条件がきびしいという点が気になる。

content.content: It’s true that this company pays well, but the harsh working conditions are a point of concern.

content: この犬は、性格がやさしいという点で、人気がある。

content.content: This dog is popular for the gentleness of its disposition.

content: この計画は人がたくさん必要だという点で問題がある。

content.content: The fact that this plan requires many people is a problem.

content: 経験があるという点で、彼のほうがこの仕事には向いている。

content.content: The fact that he has experience makes him better suited for this work (than the other applicants).

This pattern has the same meaning as Usage 1 of ...てん (above) but uses という as a connector. という can be inserted after a noun, but it is most often used to connect てん with a clause. という does not have to be used with verbs and adjectives, but it must be used when nouns and na-adjectives are followed by the predicative だ.

content: 《写真を見せながら》これが、田中先生の奥さん。で、こっちが息子さんの孝君。

content.content: 《while showing a photo》 This is Tanaka-sensei’s wife, and this is his son, Takashi-kun.

content: あしたから、試験なんだ。で、この2、3日はほとんど寝てないんだ。

content.content: I have exams starting tomorrow. So I have hardly slept these past two or three days.

content: A:私には、ちょっと無理じゃないかと思うんですが。

content.content: I think it might be just too much for me to handle...
B:で？　どうだと言うの。
So? What is it that you want to say?

content: A:今の仕事やめようと思っているんです。

content.content: I’m thinking of quitting the job I’m doing now.
B:ああ、そう。で、やめた後、どうするつもりなんだ。
Is that so? And what do you intend to do afterwards?

content: ようやく結婚式の日取りも決まりました。で、実は先生にお願いがあるのですが。

content.content: (to a teacher) The date of the wedding is finally set. And I have a favor to ask you.

Used when continuing a conversation or seeking to provide the listener with information, following an earlier statement of the speaker or the listener. Contracted form of それで, and is normally used in spoken language. In most cases, で can be replaced by それで, but when broaching a request, as in

content: , it can also be replaced by そこで.

content.content: 【それで】、
【そこで】、
【そして】、
【それから】

content: 彼女は病気で寝ています。

content.content: She’s sleeping due to illness.

content: ちょっと休んでいって下さい。

content.content: Please go have a little rest.
【ていく】
【であれ】［NであれNであれ］

content: 晴天であれ、雨天であれ、実施計画は変更しない。

content.content: If the weather is sunny or rainy, the plan to be implemented will not change.

content: 貧乏であれ、金持ちであれ、彼にたいする気持ちは変わらない。

content.content: Whether he’s rich or poor, I won’t change my feelings towards him.

content: 試験の時期が春であれ秋であれ、準備の大変さは同じだ。

content.content: Whether the examination is in the spring or the fall, the hardship of the preparation is the same.

content: アジアであれ、ヨーロッパであれ、戦争を憎む気持ちは同じはずだ。

content.content: Whether Asia or Europe, feelings of hatred toward wars are likely the same.

Means “in either case.” Usually followed by an expression to indicate that either way makes no difference to the matter. Can be replaced by ...であろうと...であろうと. Used in formal spoken language or written language. Nouns are usually used, but occasionally na-adjectives are, too. For i-adjectives, the ...かれ...かれ form, as in あつかれ、さむかれ (whether it’s hot or cold)  or よかれ、あしかれ (whether it’s good or bad), is used.
【であろうと】
1. Nであろうと、Nであろうと、

content: 雨であろうと、雪であろうと、当日は予定通り行う。

content.content: Whether it rains or snows, the day will proceed as planned.

content: トラックであろうと、軽自動車であろうと、ここを通る車はすべてチェックするようにという指令が出ている。

content.content: Whether it’s a truck or a small car, there is an order to check all the cars which pass this point.

content: 猫であろうと、虎であろうと、動物の子供がかわいいのは同じだ。

content.content: Whether it’s a cat or a tiger, all animal offspring are just as cute.

Means “either way.” Often followed by expressions that indicate that the situation hasn’t changed. Can be replaced by ...であれ...であれ. Used in formal conversation and written language. Nouns are mainly used, but occasionally na-adjectives are also used. When i-adjectives are used, they take the form ...かろうと...かろうと, as in あつかろうとさむかろうと (be it hot or cold) and よかろうとわるかろうと (be it good or bad).
2. ...であろうとなかろうと［N／Na　であろうとなかろうと］

content: 休日であろうとなかろうと、わたしの仕事には何も関係ない。

content.content: Whether it’s a holiday or not, it doesn’t have anything to do with my job.

content: 観光地であろうとなかろうと、休暇が楽しく過ごせればどこでもいい。

content.content: Whether it’s a resort or not, anywhere I can enjoy my time off would be fine.

content: 仕事であろうとなかろうと、彼は何ごとにも全力をつくさないと気がすまない。

content.content: Whether it’s his job or not, he’s not content unless he gives a hundred percent in anything he does.

content: 彼が有名であろうとなかろうと、つり仲間としてはほかの人と同じだ。

content.content: Whether he’s famous or not, among his fishing buddies he’s the same as everyone else.
Means “whether or not it is a certain way.” Followed by expressions that indicate “it is the same either way.”
【でしかない】→
【しか】
【でしょう】→
【だろう】
【でなくてなんだろう】［Nでなくてなんだろう］

content: 彼女のためなら死んでもいいとまで思う。これが愛でなくて何だろう。

content.content: I thought I was ready to die for her. If this wasn’t love, what was?

content: 出会ったときから二人の人生は破滅へ向かって進んでいった。これが宿命でなくて何だろうか。

content.content: From the moment the two met, their lives headed toward disaster.  What could this be other than fate?
Attaches to nouns such as 愛 (love), 宿命 (fate), 運命 (destiny), 真実 (truth), and so on, to emphasize that this is what something is (...である). Generally used in novels or personal essays.
【でなくては】→
【なくては】
【では1】
1. Nでは

content: 人は外見では判断できない。

content.content: You can’t judge a person by his appearance.

content: これくらいの病気ではへこたれない。

content.content: An illness of this degree is no reason to despair.

content: この仕事は1時間では終わらない。

content.content: This work can’t be finished in just an hour.

content: 日本ではタクシーに乗っても、チップを渡す必要はありません。

content.content: In Japan, there’s no need to tip when you take a taxi.

content: 私の時計では今 12 時5分です。

content.content: My watch says it’s now five minutes after twelve.

content: この地方では旧暦で正月を祝います。

content.content: In this region, the New Year is celebrated according to the old lunar calendar.
The particle で is attached to a noun and followed by は. Unlike the form of では created by attaching は to the te-form of だ, this cannot be replaced by であっては.
（×）これくらいの病気であってはへこたれない。
For being just this sick, there is no reason to despair.
（○）重い病気であっては、欠席もやむをえない。
As it’s a serious illness, he can’t avoid being absent.

では is used after a noun denoting a measure, standard, time, or location and means “with such a measure or standard; at such a time or location.” Nでは is often followed in the last part of the sentence by an expression in negative form, as in

content: and
show how this form is used to express contrast.

content.content: 2. N／Na　のでは→
【ては】、
【てはだめだ】2
【では2】Essentially a written form that is used in fairly formal situations. In casual spoken language, じゃ（あ） is used.
1. では〈inference〉

content: A:私は 1974 年の卒業です。

content.content: I graduated in
B:では、私は2年後輩になります。
Then I must be two years your junior.

content: A:この1週間毎晩帰宅は 12時過ぎだよ。

content.content: I’ve been getting home after midnight every night this week.
B:では、睡眠不足でしょう。
Then you’re probably short of sleep.

content: A:彼、日本語を 10 年も習っているんですよ。

content.content: He has been studying Japanese for some ten years.
B:では、日常の会話に困ることはないですね。
Then he probably doesn’t have any trouble with everyday conversation, does he?

content: A:緊急の会議が入ってしまいまして…

content.content: I’ve just had an urgent meeting added to my schedule...
B:では、今日のパーティにはおいでになれませんね。
Oh, then you won’t be able to attend the party today, will you.

content: 家を出たときには、あの袋はたしかに手にもっていた。では、途中のバスの中に忘れたということかな。

content.content: I know I had that bag in my hand when I left home. So, I’m guessing this means I left it on the bus.
Used at the beginning of a sentence when the speaker is making an inference, based on a newly-acquired fact or on his/her memory of something, that leads to a conclusion. In situations such as

content: , when the speaker is trying to confirm the accuracy of the inference, では functions as an expression of asking or confirmation.
is an example of an inference based on the speaker’s memory. In almost all cases, では can be replaced by それなら, そうしたら, （それ）だったら, （そう）すると, and other such expressions.

content.content: 2. では〈expression of attitude〉

content: A:すみません。教科書を忘れてしまいました。

content.content: I’m sorry, but I’ve forgotten my textbook.
B:では、となりの人に見せてもらいなさい。
Then ask the person next to you to let you look at hers.

content: A:用紙の記入、終わりましたが。

content.content: I’ve finished filling in this form.
B:じゃ、3番の窓口に出してください。
Then please submit it at Window No.

content: A:全員集合しました。

content.content: Everyone is here.
B:では、そろそろ出発しましょう。
OK, then it’s about time to get going.

content: A:実は子供が病気なんです。

content.content: Actually, I have a sick child at home.
B:では、今日は帰ってもいいです。
In that case, you may go home for today.

Appears in sentence-initial position and is used as a chance for the speaker to express an attitude arising from newly-acquired information. Followed by expressions of command, request, intention, permission, and so on. Although this では can be replaced with それなら, そしたら, and （そう）だったら, it cannot be replaced with（そう）すると.
3. では〈shift〉

content: では、次の議題に入りましょう。

content.content: Well then, let’s move on to the next item on the agenda.

content: では、始めましょう。

content.content: Well then, let’s begin.

content: では、今日の授業はこれで終わりにします。

content.content: Well then, that’s all for today’s class.

content: では、また明日。さようなら。

content.content: All right then, see you tomorrow. Goodbye.
Placed in sentence-initial position and used as a cue to shift focus to a new topic or situation. Followed by expressions that announce a topic shift or the commencement or conclusion of something.

content: is a formulaic expression used in leave-taking.

content.content: 【ではあるが】［N／Na　ではあるが］

content: この絵はきれいではあるが、感動させるものがない。

content.content: This picture may be pretty, but it has nothing that really moves me.

content: 彼は才能の豊かな人間ではあるが、努力が足りない。

content.content: He is a person of great talent, but he doesn’t make enough effort.

content: これはお金をかけた建築ではあるが、芸術性は全くない。

content.content: Though this building cost a lot of money, it has no artistry.

content: まだ 10 歳の子供ではあるが、大人びた面も持っている。

content.content: He may only be a child of ten, but there’s something of an adult about him.

content: 彼は犯罪者ではあるが、文学的な才能に恵まれていた。

content.content: It’s true he’s a criminal, but he was blessed with literary talent.

Used to state a contrasting evaluation. Before が, a certain degree of merit is acknowledged or a negative opinion is expressed, and が is then followed by a contrasting evaluation. Focus is on the latter evaluation. Often used in written language. When used with i-adjectives, this construction takes the form A-くはあるが.
【ではあるまいか】［N／Na 　（なの）ではあるまいか］［A／V　のではあるまいか］

content: この話は全くの作り話なのではあるまいか。

content.content: Isn’t this story nothing more than pure fiction?

content: この品質で、こんな値段をつけるとは、あまりにも非常識ではあるまいか。

content.content: Don’t you think it makes no sense to put such a price on something of this quality?

content: いまどき、彼のような学生はめずらしいのではあるまいか。

content.content: Wouldn’t you say that a student like him is quite remarkable nowadays?

content: 父は自分が癌だということに気づいていたのではあるまいか。

content.content: Isn’t it most likely that my father realized on his own that he had cancer?

content: 彼らは私のことを疑っているのではあるまいか。

content.content: Doesn’t it seem like they have doubts about me?
A more formal way to say ではないだろうか, with the feel of written language. Used in formal writing, such as academic papers or scholarly articles.
【ではないだろうか】
【ではない】
1. ...ではない［N／Na　ではない］

content: これは、新しい考えではない。

content.content: This is not a new idea.

content: わたしの生まれた所は、札幌だが、育ったのは、札幌ではない。

content.content: I was born in Sapporo, but I wasn’t raised in Sapporo.

content: この表現はけっして失礼ではない。

content.content: This expression is definitely not impolite.

content: 昨日行ったレストランはあまりきれいではなかった。

content.content: The restaurant we went to yesterday was not very clean.
Used to negate expressions of the form XはYだ.
2. ...ではない

content: A:すみません、日程の変更をご連絡するのを忘れていました。

content.content: I’m sorry, but I forgot to inform you about the change in schedule.
B:忘れていましたではないよ。おかげで、予定が一日狂ってしまったんだよ。
What do you mean, you forgot? Thanks to you, my entire schedule is a whole day off.

content: A:あ。そのこと、言い忘れてた。

content.content: Oh, that. I forgot to tell you about it.
B:言い忘れてたじゃないわ。おかげで大変な目にあったのよ。
It’s not enough to say that you just forgot! Do you know all the trouble you put me to?

content: A:ごめん、現像失敗しちゃった。

content.content: Sorry, your photos didn’t turn out.
B:失敗しちゃったじゃないよ。どうしてくれるんだ。
Didn’t turn out? Now what are you going to do?

content: A:あの、お借りしたビデオカメラ、こわれちゃったんです。

content.content: Um, you know that camcorder I borrowed from you? Well, it got broken.
B:こわれちゃった、じゃないよ。大事なもの、君だから貸したのに。
What do you mean, it got broken? Listen, I trusted you with something valuable.

Expresses criticism or blame by repeating the other party’s words. Used in spoken language, but only when the speaker is addressing someone with lower status or someone with whom s/he has a close relationship. As in

content: , it often takes the form じゃない.

content.content: 3. ...ではなくて→
【ではなくて】

【ではないか1】［N／Na／A／V　ではないか］Attaches to plain forms and expresses surprise on the part of the speaker, or the intention to press the addressee for acknowledgement. With nouns or the dictionary form of na-adjectives, ではないか can be attached directly without using だ. However, for non-dictionary forms, だった／ではない／ではなかった must be inserted.

This is a fixed expression consisting of the negative interrogative form of だ, and it has the tone of written language or a somewhat formal situation. Usually used by men. In casual conversation, men use the form じゃないか and women the forms じゃない or じゃないの. The form じゃん, which is even more casual, is used by both sexes. In polite language, the forms ではないですか and ではありませんか are used. Always appears in the dictionary form and cannot be used in the ta-form; this, as well as the fact that it cannot be combined with だろうか are what distinguish it from ではないか
1. ...ではないか〈surprise, discovery〉

content: やあ、大野君ではないか。

content.content: Well, if it isn’t Ono-kun!

content: これはすごい、純金ではないか。

content.content: This is really something—pure gold, right?

content: なんだ、中身、空っぽではないか。

content.content: What’s this? There’s nothing inside it, is there?

content: この店の料理、結構おいしいではありませんか。

content.content: Wouldn’t you say that this restaurant has pretty good food?

content: このレポートなかなかよくできているではありませんか。

content.content: This report really is actually rather good, isn’t it.
Expresses surprise at an unanticipated discovery. If the discovery is something desirable, then ではないか conveys a favorable impression, as in

content: and
. If the discovery is contrary to one’s expectations, then the meaning is disappointment or discouragement, as in

content.content: 2. ...ではないか〈criticism〉

content: A:悪いのは君のほうではないか。

content.content: Aren’t you the one who’s really at fault?
B:僕はそうは思いませんが。
I don’t see it that way.

content: A:病人を連れ出したりしたら、だめじゃないか。

content.content: Don’t you think it’s a bad idea to take a sick person out on a jaunt?
B:はい、これから気をつけます。
Yes, I’ll be more careful from now on.

content: A:おそかったじゃないか。

content.content: You’re late, aren’t you?
B:あの、道が混んでいたんです。
Well, the traffic was really bad.

content: A:まずいじゃありませんか、そんな発言をしては。

content.content: Isn’t there going to be trouble if you say that?
B:そうですか。
You think so?

content: A:はじめにそう言ってくれなくては困るではないか。

content.content: We could have avoided a lot of trouble if you had told us that at the beginning.
B:すみません、気がつかなくて。
I’m sorry, I wasn’t thinking.

Used to reproach or criticize an addressee of the same or lower status. The purpose is to make the addressee acknowledge properly that s/he is responsible for an undesirable state of affairs. Used with falling intonation.
3. ...ではないか〈confirmation〉

content: A:同級生に田中さんという女の子がいたじゃないか。

content.content: Wasn’t there a girl in your class named Tanaka-san?
B:ああ、髪が長くてやせた子ね。
Oh yes, a thin girl with long hair.

content: A:あそこに、郵便局が見えるじゃないですか。

content.content: You can see the post office over there, right?
B:ええ。
Yes.
A:あの手前の角を右に曲がってください。
At the corner just before it, please turn right.

content: 地下道などによくいるではありませんか。ああいう男が。

content.content: Aren’t they usually in places like underground passageways— that kind of man?

Used to remind the listener of a person or thing s/he already knows, or to bring attention to something that can be seen or heard at the present location. Since this usage is associated with a desire to confirm that the listener has understood, it is often spoken with rising intonation, and it can be substituted with other expressions of confirmation such as だろう and でしょう.
Because this usage is almost exclusively conversational, the form ではないか is actually not used very often. The forms じゃないか, じゃありませんか, and じゃないですか are used instead.
4. V-ようではないか

content: このクラスみんなでディベート大会に申し込もうではないか。

content.content: Why don’t all of us in this class apply for the debate contest?

content: とにかく、最後まで頑張ってみようではないか。

content.content: Anyway, can’t we give it our best right up to the end?

content: 遠くからはるばる来たのだから、お金の心配などしないで十分楽しもうではないか。

content.content: Since we’ve come all this way, let’s not worry about money and things, let’s just enjoy ourselves!

content: 売られた喧嘩だ。受けて立とうじゃないか。

content.content: They’re asking for a fight. What’s to stop us from taking the challenge?
Attached to the intentional form of a verb, this is used to suggest joint action or to express strongly one’s personal intention. A slightly formal expression, ordinarily used by males.

【ではないか2】［N／Na　（なの）ではないか］［A／V　のではないか］Although this form can be attached directly to nouns or to na-adjectives without inserting の, in the case of i-adjectives and verbs, の must be inserted, resulting in the form のではないか. This point distinguishes ではないか2 from ではないか
1. In casual speech, men use （ん）じゃないか and women use forms such as （ん）じゃない and んじゃないの. The polite forms are （の）ではないですか and （の）ではありませんか.
1. ...（の）ではないか

content: あそこを歩いているのは、もしかして山下さんではないか。

content.content: Might that be Yamashita-san walking over there?

content: こんな大きなアパートは一人暮らしにはちょっとぜいたくではないか。

content.content: Isn’t such a big apartment a little too luxurious for someone who lives alone?

content: もしかしたら、和子は本当は良雄が好きなのではないか。

content.content: Isn’t it possible that Kazuko is really in love with Yoshio?

content: この話は結局ハッピーエンドになるのではないか。

content.content: It looks like this story might just wind up with a happy ending.

content: ファーストフード産業が伸びれば伸びるほどごみも増えるのではないか。

content.content: As the fast food industry gets bigger and bigger, won’t that just create more trash?

content: この品質でこの値段は、ちょっと高いのではないか。

content.content: Isn’t this price a little steep for something of this quality?

content: これからますます環境問題は重要になるのではないか。

content.content: Won’t environmental problems become even more and more serious from now on?

Attached to expressions in the plain form, this expresses a conjecture on the part of the speaker, with the sense of “I can’t say for certain, but isn’t it likely that....” The speaker’s degree of conviction is lower than in the case of だろう.
2. ...（の）ではないかとおもう

content: こんなうまい話は、うそではないかと思う。

content.content: I have a hard time believing such a good deal to be true.

content: どちらかというと妹さんの方がきれいなのではないかと思う。

content.content: If I had to say, I think the younger sister is probably the prettier of the two.

content: 話がうますぎるので、山田さんは、これは詐欺ではないかと思ったんだそうです。

content.content: The deal was too good to be true, so apparently Yamada-san thought it was most likely a scam.

content: もしかすると、彼女はこの秘密を知っているのではないかと思う。

content.content: I think that there’s a good chance she might know the secret.

content: この条件はわれわれにとって不利ではないかと思われる。

content.content: This condition might possibly work to our detriment.
This construction is formed by attaching 思う to ではないか. When the dictionary form 思う is used, it always expresses the speaker’s judgment; when 思った is used, as in

content: , the judgment of a third-person subject can be expressed. The form 思われる, which is used in

, has the tone of written language. This form is often used for the purpose of softening what would otherwise sound like a strong or dogmatic opinion; it does not necessarily mean that the speaker is in doubt of something.

content.content: 【ではないだろうか】［N／Na　（なの）ではないだろうか］［A／V　のではないだろうか］

content: ひょっとして、これは悪い病気ではないだろうか。

content.content: This might perhaps be a serious illness.

content: もしかしたら、和子は本当は良雄が好きなのではないだろうか。

content.content: It might just be that Kazuko is really in love with Yoshio.

content: A:この本、子供にはまだ難しいのではないでしょうか。

content.content: Don’t you think this book might just be a little difficult for children?
B:そうでもないですよ。
I don’t think that’s the case.

content: 不況は長引くのではないだろうか。

content.content: Isn’t there a possibility that this business slump could continue to drag on?

content: 彼らはもう出発してしまったのではないだろうか。

content.content: But hasn’t he already left?

content: もしかして、私はだまされているのではないだろうか。

content.content: Maybe I’ve been fooled.

This expression is similar to ではないか2 in the sense that it presents a conjecture on the part of the speaker. However, the degree of conviction expressed here is lower, making it a rather mild statement of possibility. The polite form is ではないでしょうか. As in

content: , when it is used in conversation it means that the speaker wants to confirm his/her conjecture with the listener.

content.content: 【ではなかったか】［N／Na　（なの）ではなかったか］［A／V　のではなかったか］This is essentially a written language expression used to make conjectures about a past condition or to complain about a difference between the past and present. In spoken language, forms such as （ん）じゃなかったか (men) and （ん）じゃなかったの (women) are used.
1. ...（の）ではなかったか〈conjecture〉

content: 古代人にとってはこれも貴重な食物ではなかったか。

content.content: Was this not also an important food for ancient peoples?

content: 昔はここもずいぶん閑静だったのではなかったか。

content.content: Isn’t it true that a long time ago this place was extremely quiet?

content: 当時のわが家の暮らしは、かなり苦しかったのではなかったか。

content.content: Wasn’t it true that our family was struggling financially at that time?

content: 当時の人々は人間が空を飛ぶなどということは考えもしなかったのではなかったか。

content.content: I wouldn’t imagine that the people of that time ever thought humans would fly through the sky.

An expression used to make a conjecture about something in the past. While it is similar to ...た（だ）ろう, the form ではなかったか conveys less conviction on the part of the speaker. With the exception of cases such as the one shown in

content: , it usually follows the ta-form of a predicate and takes the form ...たのではなかったか. Essentially synonymous with ではなかっただろうか and ではなかったろうか.

content.content: 2. ...（の）ではなかったか〈contrary to expectations〉

content: 昔はとなり近所の人々は互いにもっと協力的ではなかったか。

content.content: In the past, didn’t neighbors used to be much more cooperative with each other?

content: あなたたちは規律を守ると誓ったのではなかったか。

content.content: Didn’t you pledge to obey the regulations?

content: これまでは平和に共存してきたのではなかったのか。

content.content: Haven’t they co-existed peacefully until now?

content: これからは一家が平和に暮らしていくのではなかったか。

content.content: Wasn’t it the intent of the family to live a peaceful life from now on?

Expresses to the listener a feeling of criticism, dissatisfaction, or regret regarding an undesirable state of affairs in the present that is different from the past. のではなかったか is used in written language. As in

content: , it can also take the form ではなかったのか. When used with the dictionary form of a verb, as in
, means “though something should have been done, in reality it wasn’t.”

content.content: 【ではなかろうか】［N／Na　（なの）ではなかろうか］［A／V　のではなかろうか］

content: 彼の成績では、この大学は無理ではなかろうか。

content.content: With his grades, getting into this university is hardly possible, is it?

content: 低温続きで、今年の桜はちょっと遅いのではなかろうか。

content.content: This year’s cherry blossoms are likely to be a little late, what with the continuing cool temperatures.

content: 不況は長引くのではなかろうか。

content.content: Isn’t it likely that this business slump will continue to drag on?
A somewhat old-fashioned way of saying ではないだろうか. Used in persuasive/argumentative writing. Essentially synonymous with ではあるまいか.
【ではあるまいか】
【ではなくて】［N／Na　（なの）ではなくて］［Aのではなくて］［Vのではなくて］

content: 彼がこの前一緒に歩いていた女性は、恋人ではなくて、妹なのだそうだ。

content.content: Apparently the woman he was walking with the other day wasn’t his girlfriend—it was his younger sister.

content: わたしが買ったのは、日英辞書ではなくて、英日辞書です。

content.content: I didn’t buy a Japanese-English dictionary but an English-Japanese one.

content: A:つまり、報酬が少なすぎるとおっしゃるんですね。

content.content: In other words, you’re saying that the compensation is too low.
B:いや、そうではなくて、仕事の量が問題なんです。
No, it’s not that—it’s the amount of work that’s the problem.

content: A:じゃあ、彼は会ってくれるんですね。いつ行けばいいんですか。

content.content: OK, so he’s agreed to meet us. When should we go see him?
B:いや、わたしたちが彼のところへ行くのではなくて、向こうから来るというんです。
No, no, we aren’t going to see him—he says he’s going to come to see us.
Xではなくて is used to negate X, and then the correct information is supplied in the latter half of the sentence. An expression used for correction. In conversation, it becomes ...じゃなくて.
【ではならない】→
【てはならない】
【でも1】

content: 友達はプールへ泳ぎに行った。でも、わたしはアルバイトで行けなかった。

content.content: My friends went swimming at the pool. But I couldn’t go because of my part-time job.

content: 彼は新しい、いい車をもっている。でもめったに乗らない。

content.content: He has a fine new car. But he almost never drives it.

content: 青木さんは、自分勝手な人だと言われている。でも、わたしはそうは思わない。

content.content: Many people say that Aoki-san is a self-centered person. But I don’t think so.

content: わたしの姉は貧乏な画家と結婚した。でも、とても幸せそうだ。

content.content: My older sister married a painter with no money. But she seems very happy.

Placed at the beginning of a sentence to indicate that what follows will contradict what was stated previously. Less formal than しかし and more conversational in tone. Not used in the middle of a sentence.
（×）友達はアルバイトをやめたでも、わたしはやめられなかった。
My friend quit her part-time job, and but I couldn’t quit.
