（○）友達はアルバイトをやめたが、わたしはやめられなかった。
My friend quit her part-time job, but I couldn’t quit.
【でも2】
1. Nでも

content: この機械は操作が簡単で、子供でも使えます。

content.content: This machine is easy to operate, so even a child can use it.

content: この算数の問題は大人でもむずかしい。

content.content: This arithmetic problem is difficult even for an adult.

content: この森は、夏でも涼しい。

content.content: This forest is cool even in the summer.
The pattern XでもY gives X as an extreme example that would usually not be thought of as compatible with Y, in order to express the notion that because X is Y, other things are all the more Y.
2. N（+助詞）でも

content: コーヒーでも飲みませんか。

content.content: Would you like something to drink, like coffee, or...?

content: 待っている間、この雑誌でも見ていてください。

content.content: While you’re waiting, please feel free to take a look at this magazine.

content: A:佐々木さん、いませんね。

content.content: Sasaki-san isn’t here, is he?
B:ああ、昼食にでもでかけたんでしょう。
Ah, he’s probably out to lunch or something.

content: 山下さんにでも聞いてみたらどう。

content.content: Why not ask, say, Yamashita-san about it?

content: A:先生のお宅へ行くとき、何か持って行きましょうか。

content.content: Shall we take something to our professor’s house when we visit?
B:そうですね。ワインでも買って行きましょう。
Yes, let’s buy some wine or something to take along.

content: この夏は、山にでも登ってみたい。

content.content: This summer I want to do something like mountain-climbing.

content: 病気にでもなったら困るから、日ごろ運動するようにしている。

content.content: It would be a big problem if I got sick or something, so I make it a point to exercise daily.

content: 宿題のレポートは、図書館ででも調べてみることにした。

content.content: For the report I got for homework, I decided to do some research in the library and wherever.

content: 避暑にでも行ったら元気になるかもしれない。

content.content: You might get well if you go to a summer resort or someplace to get out of the heat.

content: こんな忙しいときに客でも来たら大変なことになる。

content.content: What with being this busy, if we get an unexpected guest or something it’ll be a real problem.

content: 寒いからなべものでもしたらどうでしょうか。

content.content: Since it’s so cold, how about having nabe (hot pot) or something?
Used to give an example, with the implication that there are also other choices. Depending on the context, it is often used to indicate a specific thing in an indirect manner.
For example,

content: suggests “coffee or some other kind of drink,” but in
what is actually being referred to is the concrete action of “looking at this magazine.” In
, でも is used to give an example in a suppositional expression that means “for example, what if you (we) do such-and-such?” However, it should be noted that in usages like
, what the speaker actually wants to say is something like “Why don’t you get out of the heat?” which is an expression that doesn’t include でも. In general, でも is often used in indirect statements.

content.content: 3. R-でもしたら

content: 放っておいて、病気が悪くなりでもしたら、どうするんですか。

content.content: If you let it go and your illness gets worse, then what will you do?

content: そんな大金、落としでもしたら大変だから、銀行に入れた方がいいですよ。

content.content: With such a large sum of money, it would be terrible if you lost it or something, so you’d better put it in the bank.

content: そんなにいうならこのカメラ、貸してあげるけど、気をつけてよ、こわしでもしたら承知しないから。

content.content: If you’re going to insist, I’ll lend you this camera, but be careful— I’m not going to let you get away with it if you break it or something.

content: こどものころ、妹を泣かしでもしたら、いつも一番上の兄に怒られた。

content.content: When I was a child, if I ever did something like make my little sister cry, my oldest brother would always get mad at me.

When でもしたら is attached to the stem of a verb, it expresses the notion of a worst-case scenario. Often used to caution someone by raising the possibility of an accident, illness, or something else that would cause problems in the event of its occurrence.
4. V-てでも→
【てでも】
5. N／Na　でも→
【ても】、
【てもいい】4、
【てもかまわない】3、
【てもよろしい】
【でもあり、でもある】［N でもありN でもある］［Na でもありNa でもある］［AくもありAくもある］

content: 彼はこの会社の創始者でもあり、今の社長でもある。

content.content: He is the founder of this company and still serves as its president.

content: 娘の結婚はうれしくもあり、さみしくもある。

content.content: My daughter’s wedding makes me feel both happy and lonely.
Expresses the fact that both X and Y are realized simultaneously.
【でもあるまいし】→
【まい】3b
【でもって】
1. Nでもって

content: 行為でもって誠意を示しなさい。

content.content: Show your sincerity with your deeds.

content: 言葉は信じられない。行動でもって示してください。

content.content: I don’t put faith in words. Show me with actions.

content: お金でもって、始末しようという彼の態度が気に入らない。

content.content: I don’t like his attitude of trying to solve things with money.
Expresses measures or methods. Often used in spoken language.
2. でもって

content: 彼女は美人である。でもってスポーツ万能ときている。

content.content: She is beautiful. What’s more, she’s got all-around sports talent.

content: A:山田さんは、おこって部屋を飛び出して行ったの。みんな、びっくりよ。

content.content: Yamada-san got angry and rushed out of the room.  Everyone was shocked.
B:でもって、それから、どうなったの。
So then, what happened after that?
Used to add to a topic of conversation or it develop further. Similar to そのうえ(what’s more) and それで (and then). Used in informal conversation.
【でもない】
1. Vでもない

content: 彼は反論するでもなく、ただぼんやりたばこをすっている。

content.content: Without arguing back, he is just absent-mindedly smoking a cigarette.

content: 角のところにぼんやり人影が現れた。しかし、こちらへ歩いてくるでもない。

content.content: A faint figure appeared, close to the corner. However, it’s not walking in this direction.

content: 彼女はそんなきびしい批評をされても、しょんぼりするでもなく、いつものように淡々としていた。

content.content: Even after receiving such harsh criticism, she wasn’t despondent but remained her usually cool and unaffected self.

content: 彼はプレゼントをもらっても、喜ぶでもなく、何かほかのことを考えている様子だ。

content.content: Even after receiving a present, he doesn’t seem happy, he seems to be thinking about something else.

Expresses an attitude or situation that is not very clear. Used to indicate a situation in a given context in which a certain reaction is anticipated, but there is actually no clear indication of that reaction, and the overall state of affairs is vague and indeterminate.
2. まんざら...でもない→
【まんざら】

【と1】［N／Na　だと］［A-いと］［V-ると］Attaches to the dictionary form of a predicate. Although it is usually used with plain forms, in polite language it is also used in the form ですと or ますと. Expresses the relation that the second event is realized because of the condition created by the first event.
1. ...と〈generic condition〉

content: あまり生活が便利だと人は不精になる。

content.content: People become lazy when lifestyles are too convenient.

content: 気温が低いと桜はなかなか咲かない。

content.content: If the temperatures are low, it takes a long time for the cherry blossoms to bloom.

content: 酒を飲むと顔が赤くなる。

content.content: His face turns red if he drinks alcohol.

content: 春が来ると花が咲く。

content.content: When spring comes, flowers bloom.

content: 水は 100 度になると沸騰する。

content.content: Water boils when it reaches 100 degrees Celsius.

content: 気温が急に下がると霧が発生する。

content.content: Fog forms when the temperature drops suddenly.

content: だれでも年をとると昔がなつかしくなるものだ。

content.content: All people wax nostalgic over the past as they get older.

content: 生活が安定すると退屈になるし、不安定すぎるとストレスがたまる。

content.content: When life is stable, it gets boring, and if it’s too unstable, it causes stress.

content: 月にかさがかかると翌日は雨になる。

content.content: When the moon has a halo, it will rain the next day.

content: 来年のことを言うと鬼が笑う。

content.content: Don’t count your chickens before they’re hatched (lit. If you talk about next year, the devil will laugh).

content: 夜爪を切ると親の死に目に会えない。

content.content: If you cut your nails at night, you’ll never say your last goodbyes to your parents (lit. If you cut your nails at night, you won't be able to see your parents at the time of their death).

Expresses a conditional relationship that applies not to a specific person or thing, but to people or things in general. Means “if X happens, then Y is inevitable.” The end of the sentence is always in dictionary form, and ta-forms, conjectural forms, and so on are not possible. As in

content: , sometimes と is combined with ものだ, which signifies that a certain characteristic is intrinsic to the thing or situation at hand.

content.content: Often used to express a relationship in which the event stated in the second clause occurs automatically or spontaneously after the event in the first clause. Thus, this pattern is often used to state laws of nature. Both

content: and
are proverbial expressions.

content.content: 2. ...と〈repetition, habit〉Expresses repeated habits or actions of a particular person or thing. Often accompanied by adverbs such as 必ず(invariably), いつも(always), 毎年(every year), or よく(often). Unlike the generic condition expressed in Usage 1, this usage concerns a particular subject, and either the dictionary form or ta-form may be used at the end of the sentence.

content: おじいさんは天気がいいと裏山に散歩にでかける。

content.content: Grandfather strolls in the hills behind our house whenever the weather is fine.

content: 兄は冬になると毎年スキーに行く。

content.content: My older brother goes skiing every year when winter comes.

content: 隣の犬は私の顔を見るといつもほえる。

content.content: The dog next door barks every time she sees my face.

content: 私は面白いコマーシャルを見るとすぐその製品を買いたくなるくせがある。

content.content: Whenever I see an interesting commercial, I tend to want to buy the product right away.

content: お酒を飲むといつも頭がいたくなる。

content.content: I always get a headache when I drink alcohol.

content: キーボードを2時間たたくと肩がこる。

content.content: I get stiff shoulders whenever I type on a keyboard for two hours.

content: 彼女はストレスがたまるとむやみに食べたくなるのだそうだ。

content.content: I heard that whenever she’s under stress, she wants to eat a lot.

content: 僕がデートに遅れると彼女は必ず不機嫌になる。

content.content: My girlfriend always gets upset when I’m late for a date.

content: 彼は給料が入ると飲みに行く。

content.content: He goes out drinking whenever he gets paid.
Indicates the repetition of a present habit or action of a particular person or thing. The dictionary form of a predicate is used at the end of the sentence.
b. ...と...た（ものだ）

content: 子供のころ天気がいいと、この辺を祖母とよく散歩をしたものだ。

content.content: When I was a child, if the weather was nice, I often used to take walks with my grandmother around here.

content: 日曜日に一家で買い物に出ると、必ずデパートの食堂でお昼を食べた。

content.content: When my family went shopping together on Sundays, we always ate lunch in the department store cafeteria.

content: 祖母のところに行くと必ずおこづかいをもらったものだ。

content.content: Whenever I went to my grandmother’s, I always got some spending money.

content: 学生のころは、試験が始まると胃が痛くなったものだ。

content.content: When I was a student, as soon as exams started I would always get a stomach ache.

content: 北海道のおじさんが遊びに来ると娘たちはいつも大喜びをした。

content.content: My daughters were always overjoyed whenever their uncle from Hokkaido came to visit.

content: あのころは一日働くと、一ヶ月遊んで暮らせたものだ。

content.content: At that time, I could goof off for a month on just one day’s work.

The ta-form of a predicate is used at the end of the sentence to express the repetition of a past habit or action of a particular person or thing. Often accompanied by the phrase たものだ, which expresses reminiscence.
3. ...と〈yet-to-be-realized condition〉a. ...と+未実現のことがら

content: ここをまっすぐ行くと右手に大きな建物が見えます。

content.content: If you go straight here, you’ll see a large building on your right.

content: このボタンを押すとドアは開きます。

content.content: If you push this button, the door will open.

content: この小説を読むと世界観が変わるかもしれません。

content.content: Your view of the world may change if you read this novel.

content: 雨天だと明日の試合は中止になります。

content.content: If it rains, then tomorrow’s match will be canceled.

content: これを全部計算すると、総費用はだいたい100万円になります。

content.content: If you calculate all this, the total cost is about a million yen.

content: 動くと撃つぞ。

content.content: Move and I’ll shoot!

content: そんなに食べると太るよ。

content.content: You’ll gain weight if you eat that much.

content: 真面目に勉強しないと卒業できないよ。

content.content: If you don’t study hard, you won’t graduate, you know.

content: 生活がこんなに不安定だと落ち着いて研究ができない。

content.content: When my livelihood is this uncertain, I can’t concentrate on my research.

content: こんなにおいしいといくらでも食べてしまいそうだ。

content.content: When it’s this delicious, I could eat as much as there is.

Used to say that “if/when X occurs, then Y will occur,” with respect to a particular person or thing. The Y clause always expresses an unrealized situation, but the X clause may express either an unrealized situation or one that has already come about.

content: are cases in which X has not been realized, and
are cases in which X has already been realized.

is a threat directed at an addressee who is on the verge of moving. In this situation it would also be possible to say 動いたら撃つぞ (If you move, then I’ll shoot), but the use of と implies that both actions will occur virtually simultaneously, giving the threat more impact than when it is expressed with the たら form.
and
are ways to warn or admonish someone who is overeating and someone who is lax about studying, respectively.

content.content: The Y clause may be followed by expressions to emphasize a fact, or expressions of conjecture such as だろう or かもしれない. However, expressions meant to exert an effect on the other party, including commands, requests, and invitations, cannot be used. V-よう intentional forms cannot be used either.
（×）雨天だと明日の試合は中止しよう。
When it’s rainy, let’s cancel tomorrow’s match.
（○）雨天なら明日の試合は中止しよう。
If it rains, let’s cancel tomorrow’s match.

Since と conveys a strong implication that a condition has already been realized or is very likely to be realized in the future, there is a tendency to avoid combining it with the word もし, which signifies a hypothetical situation.
（×）もし雨天だと試合は中止になります。
Supposing when it rains, the match will be canceled.
（○）もし雨天なら試合は中止になります。
If it rains, the match will be canceled.
b. ...と+疑問詞...か

content: A:お酒を飲むとどうなりますか。

content.content: What happens if you drink alcohol?
B:顔が赤くなります。
My face turns red.

content: A:51 を3で割るといくつになりますか。

content.content: What do you get if you divide 51 by 3?
B:17 になります。
It’s

content: A:この道をまっすぐ行くと、どこに出ますか。

content.content: Where does this road lead to, if we follow it straight ahead?
B:国道1号線に出ます。
It leads to National Highway No.

This is like the form するとどうなるか (if such-and-such is done, what is the outcome?). と is followed by an interrogative clause such as どうなるか or 何があるか, which contains a question word and a verb that expresses some kind of unintentional action, such as change or existence. Expressions denoting actions that are consciously controllable, such as どうするか, cannot be used unless they indicate a habitual behavior or characteristic.
（×）水は 100 度になるとどうしますか。
What will you do when water reaches a temperature of 100 degrees Celsius?
（○）水は 100 度になるとどうなりますか。
What happens when water reaches a temperature of 100 degrees Celsius?

The particle と is similar to the pattern するとどうなるか in that the focus of the question is usually on the second half of the sentence. It is difficult to use in patterns like どうするとそうなるか, where the focus of the question is on the first half of the sentence. In these cases, it is more natural to use ば or たら rather than と.
（×）どうするとドアは開きますか。
What do you do then the door opens?
（○）どう｛すれば／したら｝ドアは開きますか。
What should be done so that the door opens?

4. ...と...た〈already-realized condition〉The situations specified before and after と are previously-realized conditions. Typically, the ta-form appears in sentence-final position, but in novels and other literary works, the dictionary form is sometimes used to express the historical present. In almost all cases, a verb is used both before and after this expression. Often used in stories and novels. In conversation, たら is more commonly used.
a. ...と...た〈trigger〉

content: 教えられた通りまっすぐ行くと、つきあたりに郵便局があった。

content.content: When I went straight down the road I had been shown, there was a post office at the end.

content: 駅に着くと、友達が迎えに来ていた。

content.content: When I arrived at the station, my friend was already there to meet me.

content: トンネルを出ると、そこは銀世界だった。

content.content: Passing through a tunnel brought us into a winter wonderland.

content: お風呂に入っていると、電話がかかってきた。

content.content: It was while I was sitting in the bath that the telephone rang.

content: 街を歩いていると、見知らぬ男が声をかけてきた。

content.content: When she was walking about the town, a strange man called to her.

content: 夜になると急に冷え込んできた。

content.content: When evening came, it suddenly turned cold.

content: 午後になるとだいぶ暖かくなった。

content.content: When afternoon came, it became much warmer.

content: ベルを鳴らすと、女の子が出て来た。

content.content: When I rang the bell, a young girl came out.

content: 仕事をやめるとたちまちお金がなくなった。

content.content: When I quit my job, my money ran out in no time.

Expresses a relationship between two situations, such as when the occurrence of the first situation makes the speaker aware of the second, or the first situation is a trigger that brings about the second.

content: , and
show that as soon as the first action is carried out, the speaker “discovers” the second situation.
and
are scenarios in which a new situation arises while the first action is taking place. In
and
, the first half of the sentence expresses a time-related condition that leads to the realization of the second situation.
and
express a relation in which the first action triggers the occurrence of the second one.

content.content: In all cases, the second situation must be part of the same overall situation as the first one, and it must also be something the speaker can observe from the outside. The following example describes an internal physical sensation of the speaker. Here the particle と is not possible, and たら must be used instead.
（×）昨夜この薬を飲むと、よく効いた。
On taking this medicine last night, it worked really well.
（○）昨夜この薬を飲んだら、よく効いた。
When I took this medicine last night, it worked really well.

In almost all cases, a verb is used in both clauses. However, when this pattern is used to express the discovery of a situation, a predicate noun or adjective may conclude the second sentence, as shown in

content: above and the example below.

content.content: （例）外に出ると、予想以上に寒かった。
On going outside, I found it much colder than I had imagined.
b. ...と...た〈successive events〉

content: 男はめざまし時計を止めると、またベッドへ戻った。

content.content: After shutting off his alarm clock, the man climbed back into bed.

content: わたしは、東京駅へ着くとその足で会社へ向かった。

content.content: After reaching Tokyo Station, I continued on to the office.

content: 母は受話機を置くと、ためいきをついた。

content.content: After putting down the receiver, Mother let out a sigh.

Expresses a situation in which the same person performs two actions in succession, the first one leading to the second. Both actions are intentional. Although the ta-form is usually used at the end of the sentence, in stage directions for things like screenplays the dictionary form may be used, as below.
（例）《シナリオ》良雄は、手をふくと、ギターを手に取る。
《script》Yoshio wipes his hands, then picks up the guitar.

The <successive events> usage of と is often found in novels or stories. With this usage, たら is unnatural, and it is almost never possible to use たら instead of と. This と can be replaced by the te-form of the verb, but it is not always possible to replace the te-form of the verb with と. For example, the te-form can be used to link three or more successive actions, but と cannot be used to do so.
（×）父は家に帰ると、ご飯を食べると、すぐ布団に入った。
When my father came home, when he ate dinner, he soon got into bed (lit. his futon).
（○）父は家に帰って、ご飯を食べて、すぐ布団に入った。
My father came home, ate dinner, and soon got into bed.

While the te-form expresses successive actions that are part of the same situation, と divides one situation into two parts. It is used to depict, from an external point of view, the change that arises as the first situation switches into the second one.

content: 彼はうちへ帰るとすぐテレビのスイッチを入れる。

content.content: As soon as he gets home, he turns on the TV.

content: 放送局は、駅を降りて右へ曲がるとすぐです。

content.content: The broadcasting station is just after you take the first right from the station.

content: うちへ帰るとすぐテレビのスイッチを入れた。

content.content: I turned on the TV as soon as I got home.

content: 彼らは土地の開発許可が降りるとすぐ工事にとりかかった。

content.content: As soon as they got the land development permit, they started construction.

content: 彼女は大学を卒業するとすぐ結婚した。

content.content: She got married right after she graduated from college.

content: スポーツをやめるとすぐ太り出した。

content.content: As soon as he stopped playing sports, he started to put on weight.
This is a combination of the conditional expression と and the adverb すぐ. It means that a first event is followed immediately by the occurrence of a second.
6. ...と〈introductory utterance〉

content: 正直に言うと、そのことについてはあまりよく分からないのです。

content.content: To be honest, I really don’t know very much about that.

content: 母に言わせると、最近の若者は行儀が悪くなっているようだ。

content.content: If you ask my mother, apparently young people these days have worse manners.

content: 本当のことを申し上げますと、手術で助かる見込みは 50 パーセント以下ではないかと思います。

content.content: If I may speak frankly, I think the chances of success for this operation may be less than fifty percent.

content: 実用的な点からみると、あまり使いやすい部屋ではない。

content.content: Looking at it from the point of view of practicality, it’s not a very easy-to-use room.

content: 今となって考えてみると、彼の言うことももっともだ。

content.content: Looking back on it now, what he said was also on the mark.

content: 昨年に比べると、今年は桜の開花がちょっと遅いようだ。

content.content: Compared with last year, this year the cherry blossoms seem to be coming into bloom a little later.

When と is used after verbs of utterance, thought, or comparison, such as 言う (say), 見る (see), 考える (think), or 比べる (compare), it functions as an introductory expression indicating the viewpoint or stance from which the thing that follows will be stated. In this usage, と can often be substituted with the forms たら, ば, and なら.
7. ...からいうと→
【からいう】
8. ...からすると→
【からする】
9. ...からみると→
【からみる】
0. ...てみると→
【てみる】
1. ...というと→
【というと】
2. ...となると→
【となると】
3. ...ともなると→
【ともなると】
4. ...によると→
【によると】
5. V-ようとV-まいと→
1. 数量詞+と〈repetition〉

content: 人々は一人、また一人とやってきた。

content.content: One person came, and then another and another.

content: 星が、一つ、また一つと消えていく。

content.content: One by one the stars disappear.

content: 白鳥が一羽、また一羽と湖に降り立った。

content.content: The swans alighted on the lake one by one.
As in 一人、また一人 (one person, then another) or 一つ、また一つ (one by one), the quantifier “one” is repeated to indicate the sporadic repetition of an event. Used in written language.
2. 数量詞+と〈cumulative increase〉

content: 人々は一人、二人と集ってきた。

content.content: The people assembled in ones and twos.

content: このコンクールも二回、三回と回を重ねるうちに、だんだんよくなってきた。

content.content: This contest has gradually improved, after being held on two or three occasions.

content: 二度三度と失敗を繰り返して、ようやく成功にこぎつけた。

content.content: After two or three repeated failures, I finally managed to achieve success.
A situation of gradually increasing amount or frequency is expressed by listing a small number with the next largest one.
3. 数量詞+とV-ない

content: 禁煙しようという彼の決心は三日と続かなかった。

content.content: His decision to quit smoking didn’t even last for three days.

content: あの人は気が短いから、5分と待っていられない。

content.content: That person has little patience, so she can’t wait even five minutes.

content: A:これだけビールを買っておけばだいじょうぶでしょう。

content.content: If we buy this much beer, it should be enough, right?
B:いや、客が多いから1時間ともちませんよ。
No, there are a lot of guests, so it won’t even last an hour.

content: あんなに宣伝したのに、参加者は二十人と集らなかった。

content.content: After all that publicity, we didn't even get twenty participants.
This pattern uses a quantifier indicating a short time or a small amount, followed by the negative form of a verb, to express the notion that this limited number was not nearly sufficient.
4. にどとV-ない→
【にどと...ない】
5. 擬態語+と

content: 彼はゆっくりと立ち上がった。

content.content: He stood up slowly.

content: 雨がザーッと降ってきた。

content.content: The rain started to fall in buckets.

content: 雨がぽつり、ぽつりと降り始めた。

content.content: It began to rain, a drop here, a drop there.

content: 列車はガタンガタンと動き始めた。

content.content: The train began to move with a bump and a jerk.

content: 傷口がずきんずきんと痛む。

content.content: The wound throbbed with pain.
と is attached to mimetic or onomatopoeic words to express the manner of an action or effect. とmay be omitted in some cases. Also, repetition of the mimetic or onomatopoeic word, as in

content: , implies that the action/effect is repeated or that the onset of the action/effect is slow and gradual.

content.content: 【とあいまって】［Nとあいまって］

content: 彼の現代的な建築は背景のすばらしい自然とあいまって、シンプルでやすらぎのある空間を生み出している。

content.content: His modern architecture blends with the splendid natural beauty of the surroundings to create a simple, relaxing space.

content: その映画は、弦楽器の音色が美しい映像と相まって、見る人を感動させずにはおかないすばらしい作品となっている。

content.content: That film is an outstanding piece of work, as the tones of the stringed instruments, coupled with the beautiful images, cannot fail to impress anyone who views it.

content: 彼の独創性が彼女の伝統美と相まって、彼らの作る家具はオリジナリティあふれたものとなっている。

content.content: His creativity works in tandem with her traditional sense of beauty, and the furniture they produce brims with originality.
Attaches to nouns to convey the meaning that “such-and-such interacts with another element” or “this characteristic works in tandem with that of another element.” Written language expression.
【とあって】
1. ...とあって［Nとあって］［Vとあって］

content: 今日は三連休とあって、全国の行楽地は家族連れの観光客で賑わいました。

content.content: Since today is part of a three-day holiday, the nation's leisure spots are bustling with family vacationers.

content: 一年に一回のお祭りとあって、村の人はみんな神社へ集まっていた。

content.content: This being the only festival of the year, the villagers all gathered at the shrine.

content: めったに聞けない彼の生演奏とあって、狭いクラブは満員になった。

content.content: As he rarely performed live, the tiny club was filled to capacity.

content: 大型の台風が接近しているとあって、どの家も対策におおわらわだ。

content.content: With the huge typhoon drawing near, every household was frantic with preparations.

content: 名画が無料で見られるとあって、席ははやばやと埋まってしまった。

content.content: Since the famous film could be seen for free, every seat was soon filled.

Means “due to such-and-such a situation.” Used to indicate special circumstances and implies that a statement of something that will naturally occur under those circumstances, or a statement of an action that should be taken, will follow. A written language expression used in news broadcasts and so on.
2. ...とあっては

content: 伊藤さんの頼みとあっては、断れない。

content.content: Since it's a request from Ito-san, I cannot refuse.

content: 彼が講演するとあっては、何とかして聞きに行かねばならない。

content.content: He’s the one giving the lecture, so I have to find some way to go hear it.

content: 高価なじゅうたんが定価の一割で買えるとあっては、店が混雑しないはずがありません。

content.content: With such an expensive carpet being sold for a tenth of its list price, I wouldn't expect the store not to be packed with people.

content: 最新のコンピューター機器がすべて展示されるとあっては、コンピューターマニアの彼が行かないわけがない。

content.content: With all the latest computer equipment on display, there's no way a computer geek like him wouldn't go.

Means “because this is the situation.” Used for special circumstances and is followed by a statement of something that will naturally occur under those circumstances, or a statement of an action that should be taken. For example,

content: would be used in a situation where a refusal is unthinkable because Ito-san is a very important person to the speaker. Although this is a somewhat formal expression, it can be used in spoken language.

content.content: 【といい】［N／Na　だといい］［A-いといい］［V-るといい］Formed by combining と1 (Usage 3) with いい. とよい is a slightly more formal form.
1. V-るといい〈suggestion, recommendation〉

content: この株は今買うといいですよ。

content.content: It's good to buy this stock now.

content: 分からないときは、この辞書を使うといい。

content.content: When you don’t understand, this dictionary is helpful.

content: 旅行には、小さいドライヤーを持っていくといい。

content.content: Taking a small blow-dryer on trips is a good idea.

content: 疲れたようだね。仕事は急がなくてもいいから、ソファで少し寝るといい。

content.content: You seem tired. Since this work is not urgent, you should lie down on the sofa for a while.

content: 私を疑いたければ存分に疑うといい。

content.content: If you want to doubt me, then go ahead and doubt!
Follows the dictionary form of a verb and expresses the notion of encouraging another person to take an action. Depending on the context, it can also be used to express a hands-off attitude, as in

content: , which has the sense of “do as you like.” Cannot be used to dissuade someone from taking an action. In such cases, the form V-ないほうがいい is used.

content.content: （×）今買わないといい。
It’s good not to buy it now.
（○）今買わないほうがいい。
You shouldn't buy it now.

Similar expressions include たらいい and ばいい, but といい implies the encouragement that “generally speaking, doing such-and-such is appropriate.” The form といい cannot be used in interrogative expressions inquiring what one ought to do. In that case, たらいい／ばいい are used instead. When answering such questions, however, it is possible to use not only たらいい／ばいい but also といい. Then たらいい／ばいい convey the meaning that “such-and-such would be sufficient” to obtain a particular result. On the other hand, といい means that “such-and-such is generally an appropriate course of action.”
（×）うまくいかない時はどうするといいですか。
What’s good to do when things don't go well?
（◯）A:うまくいかない時はどう｛したら／すれば｝いいですか。
A：When things don't go well, what should I do?
B:山本さんに｛聞いたら／聞ければ／聞くと｝いいですよ。
It would be best to ask Yamamoto-san.
2. ...といい〈wish, desire〉

content: 生まれてくる子供が、女の子だといいなあ。

content.content: It would be nice if the baby on the way is a little girl.

content: 学生がもっと積極的だといいのだが。

content.content: How I wish the students would take a little more initiative!

content: 勉強部屋がもっと広いといいのになあ。

content.content: If only this study room were a little more spacious....

content: 旅行の間、晴天が続くといい。

content.content: Let's hope that the fair weather holds during the trip.

content: 彼が時間に間に合うといいんだけど。

content.content: I hope that he makes it in time, but....

content: みんながこのことを忘れていないといいが。

content.content: You would all do well never to forget this.

content: 学生の自発的な活動が今後も継続されるといい。

content.content: It would be nice to see these voluntary activities by the students continue.

Expresses a desire for something to happen. Often used with が, けど, のに, or （のに）なあ at the end of the sentence. When accompanied by が, けど, or のに, the implication is concern that “such-and-such may not be realized,” or that the present state of affairs does not reflect what is hoped for. Has essentially the same meaning as たらいい and ばいい, and can be substituted with these in almost all cases.
3. ...とよかった（のに）

content: A:とても楽しい旅行だったわよ。あなたも来るとよかったのに。

content.content: It was a very enjoyable trip. It would have been nice if you had come along.
B:行けるとよかったんだけど、急用ができてしまってね。
It would have been great to be able to go, but something suddenly came up.

content: 本当のことを言ってくれるとよかったのに。

content.content: If only you had told me the truth.

content: この部屋、もう少し日当たりがいいとよかったんだが。

content.content: I wish this room could have had a little more sunlight.

Expresses a feeling of regret or criticism of the listener, arising from the fact that something did not actually happen or that the present reality is contrary to expectations. This usage takes the forms ばよかった or たらよかった more often than とよかった. The sentence often concludes with expressions such as のに, のだが, or のだけれど. However, のに is not usually used regarding one's own actions.
（×）僕も行けるとよかったのに。
I should have been able to go, too....
（○）僕も行けるとよかったん｛だけど／だが｝。
If only I had been able to go, too....
【といい...といい】［NといいNといい］

content: 社長といい、専務といい、この会社の幹部は古くさい頭の持ち主ばかりだ。

content.content: Whether it’s the president or the managing director, I can say that the leadership of this company are all outmoded thinkers.

content: 娘といい、息子といい、遊んでばかりで、全然勉強しようとしない。

content.content: Both my daughter and my son are only interested in having a good time, and neither of them makes any effort to study.

content: 玄関の絵といい、この部屋の絵といい、時価一千万を越えるものばかりだ。

content.content: The picture in the entrance, as well as the one in this room—everything here has a market price of well over 10 million yen.

content: これは、質といい、柄といい、申し分のない着物です。

content.content: This kimono is perfect, in terms of both its quality and design.

content: ここは、気候といい、景色といい、休暇を過ごすには、最高の場所だ。

content.content: The climate as well as the scenery make this absolutely the best place for spending a vacation.

content: あのホテルといい、このレストランといい、観光客からできるだけしぼりとろうとしているのが明白だ。

content.content: Looking at that hotel or this restaurant, it's obvious that they're all out to exploit tourists to the absolute limit.

Used to present two examples of something. Often implies that there are other similar examples as well. Used to make a criticism or evaluation, and conveys a particular feeling (such as shock, admiration, or resignation) regarding the topic at hand.
【といいますと】

content: サファリといいますと、アフリカの大自然が連想されます。

content.content: Whenever I hear “safari,” the vast natural settings of Africa come to mind.

content: 団塊の世代といいますと、1940年代の終わりごろに生まれた世代のことですね。

content.content: When you say “baby boomers,” that means the generation born at the end of the 1940s, right?

content: A:この時代は女性の時代ですね。

content.content: This era is a time for women, isn't it?
B:といいますと、どういうことでしょうか。
What do you mean by that?
This is a polite form of というと.
【というと】
【という1】

content: 道子さんはすぐにいくと言いました。

content.content: Michiko-san said she’s coming right away.

content: 卒業後は郷里へ帰って教師をしているという。

content.content: He says he’s going back to his hometown after graduation to be a teacher.

content: あの船の名前はなんといいますか。

content.content: What is that ship called?
【いう】
【という2】
1. NというN〈name〉

content: これは、プルメリアという花です。

content.content: This flower is called a frangipani.

content: 山川登美子という歌人を知っていますか。

content.content: Do you know the classical poet named Yamakawa Tomiko?

content: 中野さんという人から電話があった。

content.content: There was a phone call from someone named Nakano-san.

content: 飛行機が次に着いたのは、エベスという小さい町だった。

content.content: The next stop for the airplane was a small town called Ebesu.

content: 「天使の朝」という映画を見たが、友達はだれもその映画の名前を聞いたことがないと言った。

content.content: I saw a movie called Tenshi no Asa, but my friend said that no one had ever heard of it.
The pattern N1 という N2 is used to specify the name of N

2. Compared with simply saying これはプルメリアです (This is a frangipani), use of という implies that either the speaker or the listener, or both, are unfamiliar with the flower. In casual conversation, the form Nって is often used, as in ブルメリアって花 (a flower called frangipani) or エベスって町 (a town called Ebesu).
2. NというN〈emphasis〉

content: 道路という道路は車であふれていた。

content.content: Every road that could be called a road was overridden with traffic.

content: 家という家は飾りをいっぱいつけて、独立の喜びをあらわしていた。

content.content: Anything that could be called a house was fully decorated, showing the joy of independence.

content: ビルの窓という窓に人の顔がみえた。

content.content: Each and every window of the building had a face in it.

content: 会場をでてくる選手の顔という顔に満足感がみちあふれていた。

content.content: The face of each and every player leaving the venue was filled with satisfaction.
The same noun is repeated to express the meaning “all the N.” Used to emphasize totality. A written language expression used in literature.
3. ...というN〈content〉

content: この会社には、仕事は五時までだという規則がある。

content.content: There is a regulation at this company that quitting time is five o'clock.

content: 山田さんは自分では画家だといっているが、本当は会社経営者だといううわさが流れている。

content.content: Yamada-san says he’s an artist, but there’s a rumor going around that he’s really a company manager.

content: 弟が大学に合格したという知らせを受け取った。

content.content: My younger brother received a notice that he had passed the university entrance examinations.

content: 彼女の到着が一日遅れるという連絡が入った。

content.content: A message came that she would be arriving a day late.

content: 今度K製薬からでた新製品はよく効くし、それに使いやすいという評判である。

content.content: The word is that the new product from K Pharmaceuticals works effectively and is also easy to use.

content: たばこの煙が体によくないという事実はだれでも知っている。

content.content: Everyone knows the fact that cigarette smoke is not good for your health.

Used to state the content of N. N may be a noun of utterance such as 話 (talk), うわさ (rumor), or 評判 (report), or a noun that refers to a cohesive chunk of content such as 規則 (regulation), 記事 (article), 情報 (information), or 事件 (incident). When describing the content of an event, such as 仕事 (work) or 事件 (incident), the という may be dropped.
（例）3人の高校生が中学校に放火した（という）事件は、近所の人を不安に陥れた。
The incident (in which) three high school students set a junior high school ablaze has deeply worried the neighborhood.
【というか】
1. ...というか

content: そんなことをするなんて、ほんとに馬鹿というか、困った人だ。

content.content: That he would do something like that means he’s really a fool, or maybe I should say troublemaker.

content: この決断は、勇気があるというか、とにかく凡人にはなかなかできないことだ。

content.content: This decision is one that shows courage, or at any rate, it would be pretty hard for just an ordinary person.

content: 持っていたお金を全部あげてしまうとは、人がいいというか、びっくりさせられた。

content.content: You could say she’s a wonderful person to give all her money away, or whatever, but it certainly surprised me.

Used to make a parenthetical statement of an impression or judgment about a person, event, etc. Means something like “for example, it’s possible to say something like this.” Often followed by a statement of overall evaluation.
2. ...というか...というか

content: そんなことを言うなんて、無神経というか、馬鹿というか、あきれてものもいえない。

content.content: That he would say something like that makes him either an insensitive clod or an idiot and leaves me utterly speechless.

content: 彼女の行動は大胆というか、無邪気というか、みんなを困惑させた。

content.content: Her actions were bold or perhaps naive, but everyone was baffled by them.

content: そのときの彼の表情は、悲壮というか、雄々しいというか、言葉にはしがたいものがあった。

content.content: His expression at the time was somewhere between tragic and dauntless—a little hard to describe in words.

content: そのほめ言葉を聞いたときのわたしの気持ちは、うれしいというか、恥ずかしいというか、何とも説明しがたいものだった。

content.content: My feelings at hearing such words of praise were somewhere between happy and embarrassed—it’s really hard to explain.
Used for thinking out loud about an impression or opinion of a person or event. Often followed by a statement of overall evaluation.
【ということ】
1. ...ということ〈content〉

content: 最初のオリンピックがアテネだったということは今まで知らなかった。

content.content: I didn’t know until now that the first Olympics were in Athens.

content: 日本語のクラスで日本ではクリスマスよりお正月の方が大事だということを習った。

content.content: I learned in Japanese class that, in Japan, New Year’s is more important than Christmas.

content: この工場地帯のはしに豊かな自然が残っているということはあまり知られていない。

content.content: Not many people know that there are still some areas of rich natural beauty on the edges of this industrial zone.

content: この法律を知っている人が少ないということは、大きな問題だ。

content.content: The fact that few people know this law is a big problem.

content: 小林さんが、バンコクへ赴任するということが正式に決まった。

content.content: It has been officially decided that Kobayashi-san will be transferred to Bangkok.

content: わたしがここで言いたいのは、根本的に原因を解明しない限り、事態は改善されないということだ。

content.content: What I would like to say is, until the fundamental cause is made clear, this situation will not be resolved.

Used to specify in concrete terms the substance of a remark, a piece of knowledge, or an event. という must be used after だ. In most other cases, it is not required; however, it is usually used in long sentences in order to make it easier to understand how the parts are connected.
2. ...ということ〈meaning〉

content: 「灯台もと暗し」とは、身近なことはかえって気がつかないということである。

content.content: Toodai moto kurashi (lit. “It is darkest at the base of the lighthouse”) means that it’s actually the things closest to us that we fail to notice.

content: このことわざの意味は時間を大切にしないといけないということだ。

content.content: The meaning of this proverb is that we must make the most of the time we have.

content: A:なんであの人腕時計を指してるの？

content.content: Why is that guy pointing at his watch?
B:早くしろってことよ。
He’s saying to hurry up.

content: A:つまり、この商談は成立しないということですか。

content.content: So in other words, this business deal is not going to succeed?
B:ええ、まあそういうことです。
Umm, well, yeah, I guess that’s it.
Used to state the meaning of a word or phrase, or an interpretation of a situation.  Insertion of という is required.
3. ...ということは...（ということ）だ

content: 電車がストライキをするということは、あしたは学校が休みになるということだ。

content.content: The fact that the trains are on strike means that tomorrow the schools will be closed.

content: 一日5時間月曜から金曜まで働くということは、1週間で25 時間の労働だ。

content.content: Working five hours a day from Monday to Friday means twenty-five hours of labor a week.

content: 車が一台しかないということは、わたしたちのうち誰かバスで行かなければならないということだ。

content.content: The fact that we have only one car means that one of us will have to go by bus.

Used to state an interpretation of a situation. With the pattern XということはYだ (the fact of X means Y), the speaker first describes X, which is a situation familiar to the listener, and then indicates in Y a conjecture based on that situation, a conclusion that derives from it, and so on.
4. ...ということにする→
【ことにする】
5. ...ということだ〈hearsay〉

content: 山田さんは近く会社をやめて留学するということだ。

content.content: I hear that Yamada-san will soon quit her company and go abroad to study.

content: この店は当分休業するということで、わたしのアルバイトも今日で終わりになった。

content.content: Since this shop will be closed for a while, my part-time job also ended today.

content: 新しい冷蔵庫を買う場合は、古いのを下取りしてくれるということだから、それを確かめてから買ったほうがいい。

content.content: I hear that when you buy a new refrigerator you can also trade in the old one, so you ought to confirm this before you make your purchase.

content: 募集のしめきりは9月末（だ）ということだから、応募するのなら急いだほうがいい。

content.content: I hear that the application deadline is the end of September, so you’d better hurry if you intend to apply.

content: A:吉田さん、まだ姿が見えませんね。

content.content: I still haven’t seen anything of Yoshida-san.
B:いや、さっきまでいたんですが、もう帰りました。今夜から出張するということです。
No, he was here until just a moment ago, but then he went home. I hear he’s leaving on a business trip tonight.
Expresses information that has been acquired indirectly (i.e. hearsay). Insertion of という is required.
【というと】
1. ...というと

content: スペインというと、すぐフラメンコが心に浮かぶ。

content.content: When you say Spain, the flamenco immediately springs to mind.

content: 北海道というと、広い草原や牛の群れを思い出す。

content.content: When I hear Hokkaido, I am reminded of wide-open grasslands and herds of cattle.

content: 漱石というと、「こころ」という小説を思い出す人も多いだろう。

content.content: If you say Soseki, many people will remember the novel Kokoro.

content: モーツァルトというと没後 200年の年には随分たくさん行事がありましたね。

content.content: Speaking of Mozart, there were so many events in the year of the 200th anniversary of his death, weren’t there?

content: A:スキーというと、今年は長野オリンピックですが、Bさんスキーはなさいますか。

content.content: Speaking of skiing, the Nagano Olympics are this year—do you ski?
B:ええ、でもあまり上手じゃないんですよ。
Well, yes, but I’m not very good.
Used in response to a certain topic, to describe what it reminds the speaker of or to add some explanation about it. といえば can also be used. In spoken language, it sometimes takes the form っていうと.
2. というと...のことですか

content: 「しめなわ」というと、あの、お正月につける飾りのことですか。

content.content: When you say shimenawa (sacred straw rope), umm, is that the decoration people put up at New Year’s?

content: NGOというと、民間の援助団体のことですか。

content.content: Does NGO mean a private aid organization?

content: A:困っていたとき、ケリーが金を貸してくれまして。

content.content: When I was in trouble, Kelly lent me some money.
B:あの、ケリーというと、あの銀行家のケリーのことですか。
Umm, when you say Kelly, do you mean Kelly the banker?
A:ああ、そうです。
Yes, that’s right.

Used to confirm the meaning or definition of a word or phrase. Often used to ask a question about a word or phrase given in the preceding context. In spoken language, って may be used instead of というと. This is an expression of confirmation; a more direct question, like “When you say NGO, what is that?” (NGOというと、何のことですか), is difficult to ask.
3. というと

content: A:この企画は大筋はいいが、細かいところで少々無理があるね。

content.content: This plan is essentially sound, but there are a few problems with the details.
B:というと。
By which you mean...?
A:今から説明するよ。
I’m going to explain now.

content: A:この事件は終わったように見えて、実はまだ終わってはいないんだ。

content.content: This incident appears to be over, but in fact it is not over yet.
B:というと、まだ何か起こるんですか？
You mean to say that something may still happen?
Used in response to something another person has said, to press for further details or explanation. The polite form of this expression is といいますと.
【というところだ】

content: A:どうですか、もう仕上がりますか。

content.content: How is it going—is it finished?
B:あと2、3日というところです。
It will be in just two or three more days.

content: 先頭の選手はゴールまであと一息というところです。

content.content: The leading athlete is on the final stretch to the goal.

content: A:進度はどんなものですか。

content.content: How is everything progressing?
B:来週で入門段階が終わるというところです。
Next week I’ll be finished with the introductory level.
Used to explain the state of affairs of something at a certain stage. Can also be used in the form といったところだ.
【というのは】
1. というのは

content: 駅前の開発計画が急に取りやめになった。というのは、地域住民の強硬な反対で、マスコミまでが騒ぎだしたからだ。

content.content: The development plans for the area in front of the station were suddenly canceled. The reason for this was the stubborn opposition of local residents, which led to a furor in the mass media.

content: 申しわけありませんが、来週お休みをいただけないでしょうか。というのは、国から母が突然訪ねてくることになったんです。

content.content: I am really sorry, but could I possibly have some time off next week? I’m asking this because my mother will be making an unexpected trip here from my hometown.

content: A:あしたのご都合はいかがですか。

content.content: How is your schedule tomorrow?
B:あしたはちょっと都合が悪いんです。というのは、東京に出かけることになっているものですから。
Tomorrow is not really convenient for me. It’s because I am already scheduled to go to Tokyo.

This expression links to the preceding sentence and is used to explain the cause or reason for the situation described in that sentence, or to add a supplementary statement of the rationale for the speaker’s judgment, etc. The subsequent sentence, which starts with というのは, often ends with expressions such as からだ or のだ.

Although というのは is similar to なぜなら, なぜなら is used in cases of an obvious cause-effect relationship, while というのは does not necessarily require a clear cause-effect relationship when it is used to provide a supplementary explanation about a certain situation. Also, なぜなら is a written language expression, while というのは is most often used in spoken language.
2. ...というのは...ということだ

content: レイさんが少し遅くなるというのは一時間は遅れるということだ。

content.content: That Ray-san is going to be slightly delayed means he’ll be an hour late.

content: この地方全体で雨が一時間に10 センチ降るというのは、洪水が起こるということだ。

content.content: A rainfall of ten centimeters in just one hour over this entire region means that there will be floods.
This expression is synonymous with ということは...（ということ）だ.
【ということ】
3. ...というのはNのことだ

content: パソコンというのはパーソナルコンピューターのことだ。

content.content: Pasokon means a personal computer.

content: 十五夜というのは、満月の出る夜のことだ。

content.content: The term juugoya refers to a night with a full moon.
Used to present a definition, explanation, or interpretation of the meaning of a word, phrase, or sentence.
【というのも】
1. というのも

content: あの会社、倒産するかもしれませんよ。というのも、このところ急激に株価が下がっているんですよ。

content.content: That company might go bankrupt, you know. I say this because recently its stock prices have been falling drastically.

content: 彼は昼だけでなく、夜もアルバイトしている。というのも、親の仕送りを受けずに大学を卒業しようとしているからだ。

content.content: He works part-time, not only during the day but also at night. This is because he intends to graduate from university without any financial support from his parents.
Essentially the same as というのは.
2. というのも...からだ

content: 彼が転職したというのも、空気のきれいな田舎で病弱な子供を強くしたいと思ったからだ。

content.content: The reason he changed jobs was that he wanted to improve his sickly child’s health in the fresh air of the countryside.

content: わざわざ横浜までそのレコードを買いに行ったというのも、ただ彼女を喜ばせたかったからだ。

content.content: His reason for making a special trip all the way to Yokohama to buy that album was just so he could please his girlfriend.

content: 青木さんが怒ったというのも、部下がみんなあまりにも怠惰だったからだ。

content.content: The reason Aoki-san got angry was that all of his subordinates were so lazy.

content: 土地を売るというのも、そうしなければ相続税が払えないからだ。

content.content: They have to sell the property; otherwise, they can’t pay the inheritance tax.

Used to explain the reason for an action that someone has already performed or has decided to perform. The particle も emphasizes that this is an extraordinary action. Instead of からだ, のだ may also be used.
【というものだ】［V-るというものだ］

content: この研究は、生産量を 10 年のうちに2倍にするというものだ。

content.content: The purpose of this research is to double the volume of production within ten years.

content: 今回作られたタイムカプセルは200 年先の人々に 20 世紀からのメッセージを送るというものだ。

content.content: The time capsule we have assembled on this occasion is for giving people two hundred years in the future a message from the twentieth century.

content: 先方から提示された取引の条件は、利益の 30 パーセントを渡すというものだった。

content.content: The transaction conditions the other party wants are to hand over 30 % of the profits.
Used to explain the function or content of a certain thing.
【というものではない】

content: 食べ物などは、安ければそれでいいというものではない。

content.content: For things like food, it’s not a case of the cheaper, the better.

content: 速ければそれだけでいい車だというものでもないだろう。

content.content: You don’t really think that a car is good if it’s just fast, do you?

content: 有名な大学を卒業したからといってそれで幸せになれるというものでもない。

content.content: Just because someone graduates from a famous university doesn’t mean that she’ll be happy in life.

content: 人には自由があるからといって何をしてもよいというものではない。

content.content: The fact that someone has freedom doesn’t mean they can do whatever they want.
Means that an assertion or way of thinking does not necessarily apply in all cases. As in

content: and
, the expression というものでもない may also be used. In such cases, the effect is to refute the assertion or thinking in question in a slightly roundabout way.

content.content: 【というより】

content: 野村さんは、学校の先生というより、銀行員のようだ。

content.content: Apparently Nomura-san is more a bank clerk than a school teacher.

content: この絵本は、子供向けというより、むしろ、大人のために書かれたような作品だ。

content.content: I would say that this picture book is written not so much for children as for adults.

content: あの人は、失礼というより、無神経なのだ。

content.content: That person is more insensitive than rude.

content: 彼は、論争を静めるためというより、自分の力を見せつけるために発言したにすぎない。

content.content: He spoke up merely to show off his own power, rather than to defuse the argument.
Used to compare two ways of expressing or evaluating something. Means “it’s possible to say X, but in comparison to X, statement Y is more fitting.”
【といえど】
1. ...といえど

content: この寺院では、一国の王といえど、靴をはいたまま入ることは許されない。

content.content: At this temple, even if you’re the king of a country, you’re still not allowed to enter wearing shoes.

content: 暦の上では春といえど、この土地の人々はいまだ真冬の寒さにふるえている。

content.content: While the calendar may say it is spring, the inhabitants of this region are still shivering in midwinter cold.
Same as といえども.
2. ...といえども

content: 冬山はベテランの登山家といえども遭難する危険がある。

content.content: Even for veteran mountaineers, winter climbing still carries the danger of mishaps.

content: スポーツマンの家田さんといえども風邪には勝てなかったらしい。

content.content: Even a sportsman like Ieda-san apparently could not defeat a common cold.

content: その機密は厳重に管理されており、たとえ、部長といえども近づくことは禁じられている。

content.content: That secret information is strictly guarded, and even if you’re a department head, you’re not allowed to get close to it.

content: 弘法大師といえども字を間違えることがあるのだから、少々の失敗にくよくよすることはない。

content.content: Even the great Kobo Daishi made mistakes with his Chinese characters, so there’s no reason to fret over just a little flub.

This is an expression of concession that highlights someone’s or something’s qualifications or abilities and then presents a situation counter to the expectation that “with those qualifications/abilities, surely X should be possible.” Used in formal spoken language, as well as in novels and other types of written language. Can be substituted with でも.
【といえなくもない】

content: A:最近、彼はまじめに仕事をしていますか。

content.content: Has he been applying himself to his work recently?
B:まあ、前よりはましだといえなくもないですが。
Well, I won’t deny that his work is better, but... (I wouldn’t say that it's great).

content: A:山田君のゴルフはプロ並みだね。

content.content: Yamada-kun plays golf like a professional, doesn’t he?
B:うーん。まあ、そう言えなくもないけど...。
Mmm. Well, you might say that, but....

content: この会社に入った当初は仕事のあまりのきつさにどうなることかと思ったが、今では慣れてきたと言えなくもない。すくなくとも、前ほどは疲れなくなった。

content.content: When I first started working at this company, the intensity of the job made me wonder if I could do it or not, but now I can’t deny that I’m adjusting to it. At least I don’t get as exhausted as I used to.
A somewhat half-hearted expression of affirmation that is not as assertive as といえる. Often implies or is followed by a contradictory statement.
【といえば】
1. Nといえば

content: 川口さんといえば、どこへ行ったのか、姿が見えませんね。

content.content: Now that you mention Kawaguchi-san, where has she gone? I don’t see her here, do you?

content: 高木さんといえば切手というぐらい、彼の収集熱は有名だ。

content.content: If you say “Takagi-san,” it’s almost the same as saying “stamps”—that’s how well-known his obsession with collecting them is.

content: 森町といえば、昔から木材の産地だが、最近は温泉が吹き出して話題になっている。

content.content: Speaking of the town of Mori, it’s been a lumber production area since long ago, but recently people are talking about it because of the new hot spring that’s gushed up.
This expression is used to take a certain topic and describe what it brings to mind, add further explanation about it, etc. It is also possible to say というと.

content: おっとりしているといえば、聞こえがいいが、彼女は何をするのものろい。

content.content: If you say that she’s easygoing, it sounds good, but really she is slow at everything.

content: 緑が豊かだといえば、いい所だと思うが、実際は遠くて行くのが大変だ。

content.content: You might think it’s a wonderful place when you hear about the abundant green forests, but the fact is that it’s far away and really hard to get to.

content: 一日に一回は部下をどなりつけるといえば、こわい上司だと思われるが、実際はみんなにしたわれている。

content.content: When you hear that she yells at her subordinates at least once a day you might think she’s an intimidating boss, but the truth is that everyone adores her.

Used to state two contrasting evaluations. Means that if you consider things from the viewpoint of statement X, normally evaluation Y would result, but in fact the result is Z, a contrasting evaluation.
3. ...といえば...かもしれない

content: 彼らはビートルズの再来だといえば、ほめすぎかもしれない。

content.content: To say that they’re the next Beatles might be making too much of them.

content: この議会は今までで最低だといえば、問題があるかもしれない。

content.content: If they say this is the worst assembly ever, there might be a problem.

content: この作品が時代の流れを変えるといえば、あまりにおおげさかもしれないが、実際に見ればその素晴らしさがわかるだろう。

content.content: Saying that this work (of art) would change the course of the times might be too much of an exaggeration, but you’ll understand how splendid it is if you actually see it.

This is a roundabout way of expressing an evaluation. The second clause lessens the impact of the evaluation given in the first. The evaluation in the first clause is often what the speaker wants to claim, and a statement that affirms and further develops this evaluation often follows the second clause, as in
4. ...といえば...ぐらいのことだ

content: わたしの得意なことといえば、ビールの早飲みぐらいのことだ。

content.content: If I have to say something I’m good at, the only thing is chugging beer.

content: 町の名所といえば、小さい古墳が残っているぐらいのことだ。

content.content: The only famous site left in this town is just a small ancient burial mound.

content: うちの子供のとりえといえば、動物をかわいがるぐらいのことだ。

content.content: What are our child’s good points? I guess I could say that he’s kind to animals.
Used to say that the topic at hand (a person or thing) does not have many outstanding features. Often used to make self-effacing statements about oneself.
【といけない】［V-るといけない　から／ので］

content: 盗まれるといけないので、さいふは金庫にしまっておこう。

content.content: It would never do to have your wallet stolen, so let’s put it in the safe.

content: 雨がふるといけませんから、傘を持って行きましょう。

content.content: We don’t want to get caught in the rain, so let’s take an umbrella.

content: 忘れるといけないので、メモしておいた。

content.content: I’ve made a note, so that I won’t forget.

content: 遅れるといけないと思って、早目に家を出た。

content.content: I was worried about being late, so I left home a little earlier than usual.

Expresses a feeling of concern or apprehension with respect to an undesirable situation, in the sense that “it would be a problem if such-and-such occurred.” Usually used in the form といけないので／から／と思って and followed by an expression that signifies some sort of action taken in advance to prevent the problem from occurring. V-てはいけない has a similar meaning. However, the fact that it can be used at the end of a sentence to express prohibition differentiates it from といけない.
【といった】
1. N、NといったN

content: 黒沢、小津といった日本の有名な映画監督の作品を上映するそうだ。

content.content: It sounds like they’re going to show works by famous Japanese film directors like Kurosawa and Ozu.

content: この学校には、タイ、インドネシア、マレーシアといった東南アジアの国々からの留学生が多い。

content.content: At this school, there are a lot of foreign students from Southeast Asian countries like Thailand, Indonesia, and Malaysia.

content: この豪華な催しの行われているホールの駐車場には、ベンツ、ロールスロイスといった超高級車がずらりと止まっている。

content.content: The parking lot at the venue for this sumptuous event was filled with luxury cars such as Mercedes-Benzes and Rolls Royces.
Used for listing examples. Implies that there are others as well.
2. ...といったところだ

content: A:最近よく借りだされるビデオは何ですか。

content.content: Which videos are being rented out the most these days?
B:ダイハード、スターウォーズといったところですね。
Movies like Diehard and Star Wars.

content: A:体の調子、どうですか。

content.content: How are you feeling?
B:回復まであと一歩といったところです。
I’m quite close to full recovery.

content: A:彼の運転の腕はどうですか。

content.content: How are his driving skills?
B:まあまあといったところですね。
Well, you could say they’re not so bad.
Used to explain what the situation is at a particular stage. It is also possible to say というところだ.

といったらありはしない

content.content: 【といったらありはしない】［Nといったらありはしない］［A-いといったらありはしない］

content: この年になってから一人暮らしを始める心細さといったらありはしない。

content.content: There are no words to describe the loneliness I feel at having started to live alone at this age.

content: 彼女はこっちが立場上断れないとわかっていて、わざといやな仕事を押しつけてくるのだ。くやしいといったらありはしない。

content.content: She knows that my position makes it impossible to refuse, and so she intentionally pushes this thankless job on me! I’m incredibly peeved.
Has nearly the same meaning as といったらない, but is used only to express dissatisfaction or criticism of a situation. Has the tone of written language.

といったらありゃしない

content.content: 【といったらありゃしない】［Nといったらありゃしない］［A-いといったらありゃしない］

content: あの子は自分が周りからちやほやされているのを知った上で、それを利用しているんだよ。憎たらしいといったらありゃしない。

content.content: That girl knows she gets a lot of attention from everyone around her, and she uses it. What a horrid child she is!

content: このごろあちこちで地震があるでしょ？　おそろしいったらありゃしない。

content.content: Recently there are earthquakes all over the place, aren’t there? It’s too scary for words.
A casual form of といったらありはしない that is used in spoken language. Often reduced to ...ったらありゃしない.
【といったらない】［Nといったらない］［A-い（とい）ったらない］

content: 花嫁衣装を着た彼女の美しさといったらなかった。

content.content: Wearing her bridal costume, she was indescribably beautiful.

content: みんなが帰っていったあと、一人きりで病室に取り残されたときの寂しさといったらなかった。

content.content: Left all by myself in the hospital room after everyone had gone home, my loneliness was beyond description.

content: 彼は会議中にまじめな顔をして冗談を言うんだから、おかしいったらないよ。

content.content: The way he tells jokes with a straight face during our meetings is too funny for words.

content: 結婚以来今まで 10 年も別居せざるをえなかった妻とやっと一緒に暮らせるのだ。うれしいといったらない。

content.content: Ever since we got married ten years ago, my wife and I have had to live apart, and now we can finally be together. I can't tell you how happy I am!

Attached to nouns or i-adjectives to emphasize an extreme degree of something. Means “so...that it can’t be expressed in words” or “there is nothing else as...as.” In spoken language, the form ...ったらない may also be used. Although といったらありはしない conveys the same meaning as といったらない, the former is used only when expressing a negative evaluation of something (dissatisfaction, criticism, etc.).
【といって】
1. といって

content: お金をなくしたのは気の毒だが、といって、わたしにも貸せる程のお金はない。

content.content: It’s too bad that you lost your money, but even so, I don’t have enough to lend you any.

content: 入社以来週末も働き通しで、疲れ果ててしまった。といって、ここで仕事をやめることもできない。

content.content: I’ve worked through the weekends ever since I entered this company, and I’m completely exhausted. Still, I can’t afford to quit this job.

content: 最近の彼の働きはめざましいが、といって、すぐに昇進させるわけにはいかない。

content.content: It’s true that his work has been outstanding recently, but that doesn’t mean we should promote him right away.

content: このような対応の仕方では、解決はおぼつかないという批判が集中した。といって、これに代わる案が出て来たわけではなかった。

content.content: There were a lot of complaints that this way of dealing with the matter wouldn't lead to a clear solution. That having been said, no one came up with an alternative plan.
Follows a sentence or clause that describes a certain situation and means しかしながら (however/nonetheless). The clause that follows といって indicates that the expected outcome will not occur.
2. ...といって

content: 頭が痛いといって、彼は会社をやすんだ。

content.content: Saying that he had a headache, he stayed home from work.

content: ニュースを見るといって、娘はテレビを独占している。

content.content: My daughter took over the TV, saying she was going to watch the news.

content: 大きな事故が起こったといって、当局はトンネルを通行止めにした。

content.content: Saying there had been a big accident, the authorities closed the tunnel to traffic.

content: 石田さんは、子供の健康のためだといって、いなかに引っ越して行った。

content.content: Saying it was for the health of his child, Ishida-san moved to the countryside.

Means “stating such-and-such a reason.” Used to say that someone has given an excuse or reason for taking a certain course of action. Does not necessarily mean that what was verbalized is actually true.
3. これといって...ない

content: 現代絵画の展覧会にいったが、これといっておもしろい作品には出会わなかった。

content.content: I went to a modern art exhibition, but I didn’t come across any work that I found particularly interesting.

content: 初めて高い山に登るので少し不安だったが、これといって事故もなく無事に下山できた。

content.content: I was a little anxious about climbing a tall mountain for the first time, but there were no mishaps to speak of and I descended safely.

content: 食べ物の好き嫌いはこれといってないんですが、お酒はまったく飲めません。

content.content: There isn’t anything in particular that I don't like to eat, but I can’t touch alcohol.

content: 彼は何でもよくできて優秀なので、これといって注文はない。自由にやってくれればいい。

content.content: He is talented and excels at everything, so I don’t have any particular requests. Just let him be free to do what he wants.
Accompanied by a negation and means “there’s nothing in particular that deserves mentioning.”
【といっては】

content: あの人はなまけものだといっては言い過ぎかもしれない。

content.content: Labeling that person as lazy might be going too far.

content: 神童といってはほめすぎかもしれないが、その夜の彼の演奏は確かに見事だった。

content.content: Lauding him as a child prodigy might be somewhat extreme, but his performance that night was undeniably splendid.

content: 工業都市といってはあたらないかもしれない。ここには広大な森も広がっているからだ。

content.content: Calling this an industrial city might be missing the mark. After all, there is also extensive forestland around here.

content: 彼女をワンマンだといっては気の毒だ。ほかの人が働かないだけなのだから。

content.content: Saying that she runs a one-person operation really isn’t fair. It’s just that nobody else does any work.
Used after a judgment or evaluation of a person or event, to say that such criticism (or praise) is “an overstatement” or “off the mark.”
【といっても】
1. といっても

content: ビデオの作品を作った。といっても、せいぜい 10 分の短い作品だが。

content.content: I made a video piece. But it was a short piece, no more than ten minutes at most.

content: 新しいアルバイトが見つかった。といっても、友達の代わりに一週間働くだけだ。

content.content: I found a new part-time job. That is, I’m just filling in for a friend for a week.

content: あの人がこのクラブの会長です。といっても、大会であいさつするだけですが。

content.content: That’s the president of this club. Which is to say that she just gives the official speeches at tournaments.

content: 仕事場が変わりました。といっても、同じ階の端から端へ移っただけなんですけど。

content.content: I’m working in a new place. But I’ve really just moved from one end of the same floor to the other.
Used to revise an expectation that arises from the previous sentence by indicating that the degree or extent of something is actually not very great. Indicates a limit.
2. ...といってもa. ...といっても

content: A:休みには故郷へ帰ります。

content.content: I’m going back to my hometown for the vacation.
B:じゃあ、当分お目にかかれませんね。
Well then, we won’t be seeing you for a while, will we?
A:いや、帰るといっても、一週間程度で、すぐまた帰って来ます。
Actually, even though I’m going home, it’s only for about a week, so I'll be back soon.

content: 料理ができるといっても、卵焼きぐらいです。

content.content: I say I can cook, albeit just tamagoyaki (Japanese omelet).

content: シンガポールへ行ったといっても、実際は一日滞在しただけです。

content.content: Although I have been to Singapore, it was really just a one-day stopover.

content: A:去年は珍しく雪が降りました。

content.content: Last year we had an unusual snowfall.
B:へえ、あんな暖かい所でも降るんですか。
Really? It snows even in such a warm place?
A:いや、降ったといっても、ほんの少しで、すぐ消えてしまいました。
Well, it did snow, but only a little that melted right away.

content: 日本舞踊ができるといっても、ほんのお遊び程度です。

content.content: I can do traditional Japanese dance, but it’s just for fun, nothing more.
Used to supplement a previous statement by indicating that the degree or extent of something is actually not very great.
b. ひとくちに...といっても

content: 一口にアジアといっても、広大で、多種多様な文化があるのです。

content.content: The term “Asia” is a simple one, but it refers to a vast area with many diverse cultures.

content: 一口にバラといっても、実に豊富な種類があります。

content.content: What we call “the rose” actually includes an abundant range of varieties.

content: 一口に日本人の考え方といっても、いろいろな考え方があるので、どうとは決めにくいのです。

content.content: Even if you say “the Japanese way of thinking,” it is not easy to determine what this is, because there are many different ways of thinking.
Expresses that something summed up rather simply is actually more complex in nature.
c. ...といっても...ない

content: A:来週はテストがあるんです。

content.content: I’ve got a test next week.
B:じゃあ、このハイキングはだめですね。
Well, I guess we can’t go hiking then.
A:いえ、テストがあるといっても、そんなにたいしたものじゃありませんから、一日ぐらいはだいじょうぶです。
No, even though it’s a test, it’s not such a big deal, so taking one day off shouldn’t be a problem.

content: 山登りが趣味だと言っても、そんなに経験があるわけではありません。

content.content: I may say that mountain-climbing is one of my hobbies, but that doesn't mean I have very much experience.

content: 風邪を引いたと言っても、そんなに熱はない。

content.content: I’ve caught some kind of bug, but I don’t have any temperature to speak of.

content: アルバイトの人がやめたといっても、店のほうは別に支障はない。

content.content: It’s true that a part-time worker has quit, but that won’t cause any problems for the store.

content: 土曜日には、夫の姉が遊びに来ることになっている。しかし、お客が来るといっても、別に特に忙しいわけではない。

content.content: My husband’s sister will be coming to visit us on Saturday. But even though we’ll have a guest, I won’t be particularly busy.

Used to indicate that some kind of special situation has come about, and that although a certain consequence is expected, its degree or extent will not be very great, or no particular problem will arise.
3. ...といってもいいだろう

content: これは、この作家の最高の傑作だといってもいいだろう。

content.content: I think it could be said that this work is the author’s masterpiece.

content: 川田さんは、かれの本当の恩師だといってもいいだろう。

content.content: I suppose you could say that Kawada-san is his true mentor.

content: 事実上の決勝は、この試合だと言ってもいいだろう。

content.content: I think it’s possible to say that, for all intents and purposes, this match will be the final.
Means “such-and-such an evaluation is probably not mistaken.” Used when offering an interpretation, judgment, or critique of a situation or person. A more euphemistic expression than ...といえる.
4. ...といってもいいすぎではない

content: 環境破壊の問題は、これから世界の最も重要な課題になるといっても言い過ぎではない。

content.content: It’s not an overstatement to say that the problem of environmental destruction will be the crucial issue facing the entire world from now on.

content: 成功はすべて有田さんのおかげだといってもいいすぎではない。

content.content: It’s not too much to say that all our success is thanks to Arita-san.
Means “to say such-and-such is not an exaggeration.” Used for strong emphasis of an assertion. In formal written language, 言いすぎ can be replaced by 過言.
（例）そのニュースは国中の人々を幸福な気分にさせたといっても過言ではない。
It is not an exaggeration to say that this news made people all throughout the nation very happy.

といってもまちがいない

content.content: 【といってもまちがいない】

content: 現在、彼が日本マラソン界の第一人者といっても間違いない。

content.content: It’s safe to say that he is currently the top marathon runner in Japan.

content: この会社は祖父の力で大きくなったといってもまちがいはない。

content.content: There is no doubt that this company grew because of my grandfather’s efforts.

Used to state an interpretation, judgment, or critique of a situation or person. In comparison to といえる, this expression conveys a stronger, more confident assertion. Usually used in written language. The particle も is sometimes omitted.
【といわず...といわず】［NといわずNといわず］

content: 風の強い日だったから、口といわず、目といわず、すなぼこりが入ってきた。

content.content: It was a gusty day, so the dust blew into my mouth and eyes and everywhere.

content: 車体といわず、窓といわず、はでなペンキをぬりたくった。

content.content: They smeared gaudy paint on the body, on the windows, all over the car.

content: 入り口といわず、出口といわず、パニックになった人々が押し寄せた。

content.content: Panic-stricken people rushed for the entrances, the exits, and everywhere.
Nouns that represent parts of a certain thing are repeated. Means “the whole thing, with no distinction between individual parts.”
【とうてい...ない】

content: うちの息子の実力では、東大合格はとうてい無理だ。

content.content: With our son's academic ability, getting into Tokyo University is utterly impossible.

content: 彼女が僕を裏切るなんてとうていあり得ない。

content.content: It is simply unthinkable that she would betray me.

content: 歴史の長さにおいて、日本の大学は西洋の古い大学にはとうてい及ばない。

content.content: When it comes to the length of their histories, the universities of Japan are far behind the old established institutions of Europe.
Expresses that no matter what method is used or how a person thinks about something, that thing is unattainable, impossible, or inconceivable. Has the tone of written language.
【とうとう】
1. とうとうV-た

content: 夏休みもとうとう終わってしまった。

content.content: Summer vacation has finally come to an end.

content: 長い間入院していた祖父も、とうとう亡くなった。

content.content: After a long period of hospitalization, my grandfather finally passed away.

content: 卒業式も無事に終わって、とうとう国に帰る日になった。

content.content: His graduation successfully behind him, the day to return to his home country had come at last.

content: 20 年の歳月をかけて、研究はとうとう完成した。

content.content: After some twenty years of effort, the research was at last completed.

content: 相手があまりにしつこいので、温厚な彼もとうとう怒ってしまった。

content.content: The other person’s extreme persistence finally drove him to anger, though he was usually so easy-going.

content: 朝から曇っていたが、夕方にはとうとう雨になった。

content.content: It had been cloudy since morning, and when evening came, it finally began to rain.
Expresses that something has been realized ultimately or after spending a lot of time on it.

content: indicate that a long passage of time or a process was undergone before an anticipated final stage was reached.
indicates that persistent effort over a long period of time has led to the final result. Implies the speaker’s deep emotion regarding the events or time leading up to the outcome.

content.content: Also, as shown in

content: and
, とうとう is sometimes used when a situation that was maintained for a length of time passes a certain limit.
means “a man who usually doesn’t get angry could no longer control his ire,” and
means “it had been threatening to rain since morning, and although it held off during the daytime, in the evening it started to rain.”

content.content: Similar expressions include やっと (at long last) and ついに (finally/in the end).
For details, refer to やっと (Usage 1).
2. とうとう...V-なかった

content: 二時間も待ったが、とうとう彼は来なかった。

content.content: We waited for two hours, but in the end he never showed up.

content: 何週間も捜索が続けられたが、遺体はとうとう発見されなかった。

content.content: The search continued for several weeks, but ultimately the body was never found.

content: 全力をあげて調査が行われたが、事故の原因はとうとう分からなかった。

content.content: An all-out investigation was conducted, but the cause of the accident was never determined.
Used when an anticipated situation ultimately fails to come about. The expression ついに can be used in the same way, but やっと does not take this pattern.
【とおして】
1. Nをとおして〈intermediary〉

content: 私たちは友人を通して知り合いになった。

content.content: We got to know each other through a mutual friend.

content: 我々は体験ばかりでなく書物を通して様々な知識を得ることができる。

content.content: We can gain a range of knowledge not only from experience but also through books.

content: 実験を通して得られた結果しか信用できない。

content.content: I only trust results obtained through experiments.

content: 5年間の文通を通して二人は恋を実らせた。

content.content: Through five years of correspondence, the two grew to love each other.

content: 今日では、マスメディアを通して、その日のうちに世界の出来事を知ることができる。

content.content: Nowadays, through the mass media, we can find out about world events on the same day they happen.

Follows a noun that represents a person, thing, or action and indicates its use as an agent or means by which something is achieved. Used to say that knowledge or experience is gained through the noun in question.
2. V-ることをとおして

content: 子供は学校で他の子供と一緒に遊んだり学んだりすることを通して社会生活のルールを学んで行く。

content.content: Children learn social norms for living through playing and learning with other children at school.

content: 教師は学生に教えることを通して、逆に学生から教えられることも多い。

content.content: Through teaching, it is conversely the educators who also learn much from their students.

Follows the dictionary form of a verb and expresses the same meaning as 1 above. Typically combines with verbs of Japanese origin, such as 学ぶ (learn/study). When combined with verbs of Chinese origin, such as 学習する (study/learn) or 研究する (research), usually the pattern shown in Usage 1 is used, as in 学習をとおして (through learning) and 研究をとおして (through research).
3. Nをとおして〈during a period of time〉

content: 5日間を通しての会議で、様々な意見が交換された。

content.content: Over the five days of the conference, a wide range of opinions were exchanged.

content: この地方は1年を通して雨の降る日が少ない。

content.content: This region has few rainy days throughout the year.

content: この1週間を通して、外に出たのはたったの2度だけだ。

content.content: During this whole week, I have stepped outside only twice.
Used after expressions that indicate a period of time and means “during that period” or “within that time frame.” May express an action that continues uninterrupted throughout the time period, as in

content: , or the intermittent occurrence of an event during a set period, as in
and

content.content: 【とおす】［R-とおす］

content: やると決めたことは最後までやり通すつもりだ。

content.content: Since it’s something I decided to do, I intend to see it all the way through.

content: 途中で転んでしまったが、あきらめないでゴールまで走り通した。

content.content: I stumbled along the way, but I didn’t give up and ran all the way to the goal.

content: こんな難しい本は、私にはとても読み通せない。

content.content: It’s impossible for me to read such a difficult book all the way to the end.
When とおす is attached to verbs of intentional action, it means “do something all the way to the end.”
【とおもう】
1. ...かとおもうほど

content: 彼は、いつ寝ているのかと思うほどいそがしそうだ。

content.content: He seems so busy that it makes me wonder when he sleeps.

content: その家は、ほかに金の使い道を思いつかなかったのだろうかと思うほど、金のかかったつくりだった。

content.content: That house cost so much to build that it makes me wonder if they couldn't think of any other ways to spend their money.

content: その人のあいさつは、永遠に終わらないのではないかと思うほど長いものだった。

content.content: That person’s opening remarks were so long that we wondered if they might go on forever.

content: 死んでしまうのではないかと思うほどの厳しい修行だった。

content.content: The training was so rigorous that we wondered if it might kill us.

Means “so outrageous that it makes people wonder such-and-such.” The form Xかと思うほど（の）Y is used to emphasize the high degree of Y. Sometimes the form ...かと思うほどだ is also used, as in the following example.
（例）彼はいそがしい。いつ寝ているのかと思うほどだ。
He is busy. So much so that it makes me wonder when he sleeps.
2. ...かとおもえばa. V-るかとおもえば

content: 勉強しているかと思えば漫画を読んでいる。

content.content: There she was reading comic books, when I thought she was studying!

content: 来るかと思うと欠席だし、休むかと思うと出席している。

content.content: When I think he’ll come, he’s absent, and when I think he'll be absent, he attends.

content: 今年こそ冷夏と思えば、猛暑で毎日うだるような暑さだ。

content.content: Just when I thought we’d have a cool summer this year, there’s a heat wave and every day is a scorcher.

The forms V-るかとおもえば and V-るかとおもうと are used to express that the present situation is contrary to the speaker’s expectations. Since these express that an unexpected situation occurs repeatedly and/or that the present situation is contrary to expectation, they are typically followed by the dictionary form at the end of the sentence. This usage does not usually take the form かと思ったら.
b. V-るかとおもえば...も

content: 熱心に授業に出る学生がいるかと思えば、全然出席せずに試験だけ受けるような学生もいる。

content.content: There are students who enthusiastically come to class, and there are students who never come to class but just take the final exam.

content: 一日原稿用紙に向かっていても一枚も書けない日があるかと思うと、一気に数十枚も書ける日もある。

content.content: While there are some days when you sit staring at the manuscript paper all day long without being able to write a single page, there are also days when you can dash off dozens of pages at a stretch.

Expresses the parallel existence of conflicting or contrasting situations. Can also take the form V-るかとおもうと. Often verbs of existence like ある, いる, etc. are repeated. While the pattern V-るかとおもえば (see a, above) expresses a gap between expectation and reality, the pattern here doesn’t have such a meaning. It merely presents a comparison between two situations of a different nature.
3. ...からとおもって

content: 体にいいからと思って、緑の野菜を食べるようにしています。

content.content: I believe it's good for the health, so I make it a point to eat green vegetables.

content: せっかくパリまで来たのだからと思って、一流レストランで食事することにした。

content.content: I figured that since I’d come all the way to Paris, I should have dinner at a first-class restaurant.

content: 明日の試験に遅れては大変だからと思い、今晩は早寝することにした。

content.content: I know that it would never do to be late for tomorrow's exam, so I’m going to bed early tonight.

Follows a clause and means that an action is or will be taken on account of the reason expressed in that clause. The reason given in the first clause typically expresses something that will happen as a result of the action in the second clause (i.e. the aim of the action). In the second clause, an expression that indicates intentional action is used.
4. ...とおもったらa. V-たとおもったら→
【とおもう】9bb. 疑問詞...かとおもったら

content: 何を言うのかと思ったらそんなくだらないことか。

content.content: Who would have thought she would end up saying such a stupid thing?

content: 食事もしないで何をやってるのかと思ったら、テレビゲームか。

content.content: I was wondering what he was doing that was so important that he had to skip dinner, and it turned out to be a video game.

content: 会議中に席を立ってどこへ行くのかと思ったら、ちょっと空が見たいって言うんだよ。あいつ、最近おかしいよ。

content.content: I was wondering why he stepped out of the meeting, and he said he just wanted to take a look at the sky. That guy’s really been strange lately.

content: 2才の赤ん坊が夢中で何かやっている。何をやっているのかと思ったら、鏡にむかってにこにこ笑ったり、手をふったりしているのだ。

content.content: The two-year-old child was completely absorbed in something.  When I went to see what she was doing, I saw her looking into the mirror, grinning and waving.
Expresses that the speaker has directed his/her attention to something that s/he thinks is strange or unusual. The latter part of the sentence expresses an unexpected discovery or a surprising event.
5. ...たいとおもう→
【おもう】
6. ...とおもいきや

content: 今場所は横綱の優勝間違いなしと思いきや、3日目にケガで休場することになってしまった。

content.content: I was sure this sumoo tournament would be won by the yokozuna (grand champion), and then on the third day he withdrew because of an injury.

content: 今年の夏は猛暑が続くと思いきや、連日の雨で冷害の心配さえでてきた。

content.content: Just when I expected that the heat wave would continue this summer, we had so many days of rain that now there are even concerns about cold-weather damage to the crops.

content: これで一件落着かと思いきや、思いがけない反対意見で、この件は次回の会議に持ち越されることになった。

content.content: I thought this would settle the matter, but there was unexpected opposition, so the issue has been tabled until the next meeting.
