Follows a clause and means that, although the speaker had expected the outcome expressed in that clause, the actual outcome was, to his/her surprise, the opposite. As in

content: , sometimes the particle か appears right before と. A somewhat old-fashioned expression used in written language.

content.content: 7. ...とおもう→
【おもう】
8. ...とおもうまもなく

content: つめたい雨が降ってきたと思う間もなく、それは雪にかわった。

content.content: Just as I thought a cold rain had started to fall, it turned to snow.

content: 両目に涙があふれてきたかと思う間もなく、その子は大声で泣き出した。

content.content: The child’s eyes welled up with tears, and a loud outburst of wailing immediately followed.

content: 帰ってきたなと思う間もなく息子は「遊びに行ってくる！」と叫んで出ていった。

content.content: I had hardly welcomed my son home when he cried, "I'm going out to play!" and left.

content: 雲を突き抜けたと思う間もなく、翼の下に、街の灯が広がった。

content.content: Just as we broke through the clouds, the city lights spread out beneath the wings of the plane.

Expresses two events occurring in succession without a break in time. Sometimes the particle か appears right before と. Used in written language. In the pattern XかとおもうまもなくY (I hardly thought X had happened when Y occurred), neither the X clause nor the Y clause can express an action done by the speaker.
（×）私はうちに帰ったかと思う間もなく友達に電話した。
I hardly thought I had come home when I telephoned a friend.
（○）私は家に帰るとすぐ友達に電話した。
I telephoned a friend right after arriving home.
9. ...とおもうとa. V-るかとおもうと→
【とおもう】2ab. V-たとおもうと

content: 急に空が暗くなったかと思うと、大粒の雨がふってきた。

content.content: I had just realized how dark the sky had become when large drops of rain started to fall.

content: 山田さんたら、来たと思ったらすぐ帰っちゃった。

content.content: That Yamada-san went home right after she got here.

content: さっきまで泣いていたと思ったらもう笑っている。

content.content: Until just a moment ago he was in tears, but now there is already a smile on his face.

content: やっと暖かくなったかと思うと、今朝は突然の春の雪でびっくりした。

content.content: I thought it was finally getting warm, so I was surprised this morning at the sudden spring snowfall.

content: 夫はさっき家に戻ってきたかと思ったら、知らぬ間にまた出掛けていた。

content.content: I thought my husband had just come home, but before I knew it, he had gone out again.

content: 今までニコニコしていたかと思えば、突然泣き出したりして、本当に、よく気分の変わる人だ。

content.content: Just when you think that up till now she’s been all smiles, all of a sudden she bursts out crying and stuff; really, she’s such a temperamental person.

content: ちょっとうとうとしたかと思うと、突然大きな物音がして目が覚めた。

content.content: Just as I felt myself nodding off, suddenly there was a loud noise and I woke up.

Expresses the successive but virtually simultaneous occurrence of two contrasting situations. The forms V-たとおもったら and V-たとおもえば can also be used, and the form V-たかとおもったら is common too. In many cases, this pattern is followed by an expression that refers to the speaker's shock or surprise. Cannot be used to describe the actions of the speaker him/herself.
（×）私は、うちに帰ったと思うとまた出かけた。
I thought I had just come home when I went out again.
（○）私は、うちに帰って、またすぐに出かけた。
I came home and soon went out again.
0. ...とおもったものの  →
【ものの】
1. Nにとおもって

content: おばあちゃんへのお土産にと思って、湯飲み茶碗を買った。

content.content: I bought a Japanese teacup as a souvenir for my grandmother.

content: つまらないものですが、これ、お子さんにと思って...。

content.content: It’s just a little something I thought your child might like....

content: 健康維持にと思い、水泳を始めた。

content.content: To keep fit, I started swimming.
Used with nouns that refer to a person or a purpose/goal and means “for that person or purpose.” Followed by an expression of intentional action. Can also be used in the form ...にと思い.
2. ...ものとおもう→
【ものとおもう】
3. ...ようとおもう→
【おもう】5
【とおり】
1. 数詞／なん／いく　とおり

content: 駅からあの建物までには3通りの行き方がある。

content.content: There are three different routes from the station to that building.

content: やり方は何とおりもありますがどの方法がよろしいでしょう。

content.content: There are a number of different ways to do it, but which one do you think is best?

content: 「生」の読み方はいくとおりあるか知っていますか。

content.content: Do you know how many different readings the character 生 has?
Attaches to a number or an interrogative like 何 (nan-) or 幾 (iku-). Expresses that there are multiple methods or varieties of something.
2. ...どおり［Nどおり］［R-どおり］

content: 計画はなかなか予定どおりには進まないものだ。

content.content: Projects never seem to proceed according to plan.

content: すべて課長の指示どおり手配いたしました。

content.content: I have made all the arrangements in accordance with the section chief's instructions.

content: 自分の気持ちを思いどおりに書くことは簡単そうに見えて難しい。

content.content: It may seem easy to express just how you feel in writing, but it's actually difficult.

content: 世の中は自分の考えどおりには動いてはくれないものだ。

content.content: The world doesn’t operate the way you think it should.

Attaches to nouns that refer to a plan, project, instructions, orders, etc., or to the verb stem of verbs of thought such as 思う (think/consider) and 考える (think/deliberate). Means “in the same way as such-and-such,” “just like that,” or “just as it is.” Always takes the form ...どおり. Other examples include 命令どおり (according to orders), 型どおり (according to the prescribed form), 見本どおり (according to the sample/example), 文字どおり (literally/to the letter), and 想像どおり (as imagined).
3. V-る／V-た　とおり

content: おっしゃるとおりです。（＝あなたの意見に賛成です）

content.content: It’s just as you say. (= I agree with you.)

content: 私の言うとおりに繰り返して言ってください。

content.content: Please repeat after me, just as I say it.

content: 先生の奥さんは私が想像していたとおりの美人でした。

content.content: My teacher’s wife was as beautiful as I had imagined she would be.

content: ものごとは自分で考えているとおりにはなかなか進まない場合が多い。

content.content: There are many cases when things just don’t proceed as you think they will.
Attaches to the dictionary form or ta-form of 言う (say), 思う (think), and other verbs of utterance or thought. Means that something is similar to what was previously stated or thought.
【とか1】
1. Nとか（Nとか）

content: 病気のお見舞いには果物とかお花が好まれる。

content.content: When you visit someone in the hospital, it’s good to take something like fruit or flowers.

content: 私はケーキとか和菓子とかの甘いものはあまり好きではありません。

content.content: I don't really like sweet things, like cake or Japanese-style confectioneries.

content: 最近の大学院では、一度就職した人とか、子育てを終わった主婦とかが、再び勉強するために入学するケースが目立つようになった。

content.content: Graduate schools are recently seeing a marked increase in students who are returning to pursue further studies, including people with job experience and homemakers who have finished raising their children.

content: 日本から外国へのお土産としては、カメラとか電気製品がいいでしょう。

content.content: For gifts to take from Japan to other countries, a camera or an electric appliance of some kind might be a good idea.
Attaches to nouns referring to people or things and is used to give several similar examples. Has the tone of spoken language.
2. V-るとか（V-るとか）

content: 休日はテレビを見るとか、買い物するとかして過ごすことが多い。

content.content: I usually spend my days off doing things like watching TV or going shopping.

content: 教師の不足は、教師が教える時間数を増やすとか、一つの教室で複式の授業をするとかの方法で何とか乗り切ることにしたい。

content.content: I want to find a way to cope with the teacher shortage, such as increasing teaching hours or conducting combined classes in the same classroom.

content: 奨学金をもらっていない留学生には授業料を免除するとか、部屋代の安い宿舎を提供するとかして、経済面での援助をする必要がある。

content.content: We need to provide financial support to international students who don’t have scholarships, by waiving their tuition fees, or offering them inexpensive housing, or other things like that.
Used after action verbs to give several examples of similar actions or activities.
【とか2】

content: 山田さんとかいう人が訪ねてきていますよ。

content.content: Someone—I think it’s a Yamada-san—is here to see you.

content: 田中さんは今日は風邪で休むとか。

content.content: I hear Tanaka-san might be off because of a cold.

content: A:田中さんは？

content.content: Where’s Tanaka-san?
B:なんか今日はかぜで休むとか言っていました。
Umm, she said something like she’s caught a cold and is taking the day off.

content: 天気予報によると台風が近づいているとかいう話です。

content.content: According to the weather report, a typhoon is approaching or something.

Attaches to a noun or a quoted statement and is used by the speaker to tell someone something s/he has heard. Implies that the speaker is not completely sure of the accuracy of content. 言っている or 言った at the end of the sentence is sometimes dropped, as shown in

content: 彼女は買い物に行くとこれがいいとかあれがいいとか言って、決まるまでに本当に時間がかかる。

content.content: When she goes shopping, it takes her forever to decide whether she wants this, that, or the other thing.

content: あの二人は結婚するとかしないとか、いつまでたっても態度がはっきりしない。

content.content: Those two are never going to make up their minds about whether or not they’ll get married.

content: もう仕事はやめるとかやっぱり続けるとか、会うたびに言うことが変わる人だ。

content.content: Every time I meet him, he’s changed his mind about whether he’s going to quit his job or continue with it after all.
Used in cases of indecision, when it really isn’t clear which option will be taken. Placed after expressions that refer to opposing situations or something that changes in several ways. As in

content: , 言う is sometimes omitted.

content.content: 3. ...とかいうことだ［N／Na　だとかいうことだ］［A／V　とかいうことだ］

content: 隣の娘さんは来月結婚式を挙げるとかいうことだ。

content.content: It sounds like the girl next door is getting married next month.

content: ニュースによると大雨で新幹線がストップしているとかいうことだ。

content.content: The news is saying something about the shinkansen (bullet train) being stopped because of the heavy rain.
Used when reporting indirect information. Means “I can’t be sure, but I heard something like....”
4. ...とかで［N／Na　だとかで］［A／V　とかで］

content: 途中で事故があったとかで、彼は1時間ほど遅刻してきた。

content.content: He arrived about an hour late, apparently because there had been an accident on the way.

content: 来週引っ越すとかで、鈴木さんから二日間の休暇願いが出ています。

content.content: Suzuki-san has asked for two days off because next week she'll be moving or something.

content: 結婚式に出るとかで、彼女は着物姿で現れた。

content.content: She came dressed up in a kimono, apparently because she was on her way to a wedding.

Means “according to what I heard, the cause or reason is such-and-such.” Expresses that the cause or reason is something that was heard or learned from another person. Has the tone of spoken language.
【とかく】
1. とかく...がちだ

content: 女だというだけでとかく軽く見られがちだ。

content.content: Women tend not to get taken seriously just because of their sex.

content: 年を取ると、とかく外に出るのがおっくうになるものだ。

content.content: When you get older, going out gets to be more and more of a bother.

content: われわれはとかく学歴や身なりで人間の価値を判断してしまう傾向がある。

content.content: We are often inclined to judge a person’s worth according to his or her academic background or personal appearance.

content: とかく人の世は住みにくいものだ。

content.content: Human society is a difficult place to live in.

This expression is accompanied at the end of the sentence by expressions such as ...がちだ (prone to), やすい (easy to...), 傾向がある (there is a tendency to...), ものだ (that’s the way it is). It means “if anything, the general trend seems to be such-and-such.” Typically expresses something that is not very good or desirable. Expressions like ともすれば and ややもすると can be used instead of とかく. Generally used in written language.
2. とかく

content: 先のことを今からとかく心配してもしようがない。

content.content: Fretting now over all kinds of things in the future won't accomplish anything.

content: 他人のことをとかく言う前に自分の責任をはたすべきだ。

content.content: You ought to carry out your own responsibilities before you start saying this, that, and the other thing about other people.

content: とかくしているうちに時間ばかり過ぎていった。（書きことば的）

content.content: Meanwhile, time was wasting away. (has the feel of written language)

Expresses the way that someone thinks or talks about all kinds of things. Often implies a negative evaluation of that person’s actions or statements. Slightly literary in tone. In modern Japanese, it is more common to use とやかく.
【とかんがえられる】
1. ...とかんがえられる［N／Na　とかんがえられる］［A／V　とかんがえられる］

content: このままでは日本の映画産業は落ち込む一方だと考えられる。

content.content: At this rate, we can expect the Japanese movie industry to continue to slump.

content: ここ数年の経済動向から見ても、彼の予測の方が妥当なのではないかと考えられる。

content.content: Looking at the economic trends of the past few years, one can say that his predictions are more valid.

content: この難解な文章を 10 歳の子供が書いたとはとても考えられないですね。

content.content: It's incredible to think that such a difficult passage was written by a ten-year-old, isn't it?
Used to state one’s own ideas, with the implication that they are objective and have some kind of basis.
2. ...とかんがえられている［N／Na　とかんがえられている］［A／V　とかんがえられている］

content: 一般的に英語は世界の共通語だと考えられているが、実際には英語が通じない国はいくらもある。

content.content: Most people think that English is the world's lingua franca, but the fact is there are many countries where English isn’t spoken.

content: 火星には生物はいないと考えられていましたが、今回の探索で生命の痕跡が確認されました。

content.content: Formerly it was believed that there is no life on Mars, but the current investigation has found evidence of its existence.
Used to state a commonly held assumption. Often used to say that such an assumption is incorrect, or that it needs to be amended.
3. ...ものとかんがえられる［N　であるものとかんがえられる］［Na　であるものとかんがえられる］［A／V　ものとかんがえられる］

content: 泥棒は二階の窓から入ったものと考えられる。

content.content: It appears that the burglar entered through a window on the second floor.

content: 現在の二酸化炭素の排出量の増加傾向から、地球の温暖化はますます進むものと考えられる。

content.content: Considering the current trend of increasing carbon dioxide emissions, I believe that global warming will continue to progress exponentially.

Used to state one’s own ideas, with the implication that they are objective and logically based on various pieces of of supporting evidence. Often used in formal writing, such as scholarly papers or articles.
4. ...ものとかんがえられている［N　であるものとかんがえられている］［Na　であるものとかんがえられている］［A／V　ものとかんがえられている］

content: 今回の地震の原因は、地下断層に亀裂が生じたことによるものと考えられている。

content.content: It is thought that the cause of this earthquake was a rupture in the underground fault.

content: 携帯電話の利用者は今後急激に増加していくものと考えられている。

content.content: It is believed that the number of cell phone users will increase drastically in the future.
Used to state a widely-accepted idea that is acknowledged to be a valid judgment for a variety of reasons. Often used in formal written language.
【とき】
1. ...とき［Nのとき］［Na なとき］［A-いとき］［V-るとき］

content: 子供の時、田舎の小さな村に住んでいた。

content.content: When I was a child, I lived in a small village in the countryside.

content: 暇な時には、どんなことをして過ごしますか。

content.content: What kinds of things do you do in your free time?

content: 祖父は体の調子がいい時は、外を散歩する。

content.content: When my grandfather feels good, he goes out for a walk.

content: ひまのある時にはたいていお金がない。

content.content: When you have time to spare, you usually don't have money to spend.

content: 寝ている時に地震がありました。

content.content: When I was sleeping, an earthquake hit.
とき is placed after the dictionary form of a predicate that refers to a state and expresses that another state or event takes place concurrently.
2. ...たとき［N／Na　だったとき］［A-かったとき］［V-たとき］

content: 先代が社長だった時は、この会社の経営もうまく行っていたが、息子の代になってから、急に傾きはじめた。

content.content: When the father was president, this company did very well, but after the son took over, it suddenly started to decline.

content: 貧乏だった時は、その日の食べ物にも困ったものだ。

content.content: When I was broke, I had trouble even finding food for the day.

content: 子供がまだ小さかった時は、いろいろ苦労が多かった。

content.content: When our children were still small, we had a lot of hardships.

content: 東京にいた時は、いろいろ楽しい経験をした。

content.content: We had so many enjoyable experiences when we were in Tokyo.

content: ニューヨークで働いていた時に、彼女と知り合った。

content.content: I got to know her when I was working in New York.

とき is placed after the ta-form of a predicate that refers to a state and expresses that a past state or event takes place concurrently. The dictionary form can be used in the first clause, but it conveys a slightly different nuance.
（例）子供がまだ小さい時は、いろいろ苦労が多かった。
We had a lot of hardships when our children were still small.
The difference between the example above and

content: is that

, which uses the ta-form, implies that the speaker is thinking back on a time in the past, or that “the present situation is different from the past one.” The example above, which uses the dictionary form, does not have this implication.

content.content: 3. V-るとき

content: 電車に乗るとき、後ろから押されてころんでしまった。

content.content: As I got on the train, I was pushed from behind and fell down.

content: 関西へいらっしゃるときは、前もってお知らせください。

content.content: When you come to the Kansai District, please let us know ahead of time.

content: 東京へ行くとき夜行バスを使っていった。

content.content: I used to take the overnight bus when I went to Tokyo.

content: 父は新聞を読むときめがねをかけます。

content.content: My father wears glasses when he reads the paper.
とき is placed after the dictionary form of an action verb and expresses that another action or event occurs either before the first action has been performed, or at the same time.

content: and
are examples of the former, and
and
illustrate the latter.

content.content: 4. V-たとき

content: 家を出たときに、忘れ物に気がついた。

content.content: As I left the house, I realized I had forgotten something.

content: アメリカへ行った時に、昔の友人の家に泊めてもらった。

content.content: When I went to America, I stayed at the home of an old friend.

content: 朝、人と会ったときは「おはようございます」と言います。

content.content: When you meet people in the morning, you say ohayoo gozaimasu.

content: 火事や地震が起こったときにはエレベーターを使用しないでください。

content.content: If there is a fire or earthquake, please do not use the elevators.
とき is placed after the ta-form of an action verb and expresses that another event or state occurs after the first action.
【ときく】［N／Na　だときく］［A／V　ときく］

content: ここは昔は海だったと聞く。

content.content: I hear that, long ago, this place used to be an ocean.

content: 今の市長は、次の選挙には立候補しないと聞いている。

content.content: I've heard that the current mayor is not going to run in the next election.

content: 噂で、あの二人が婚約を破棄したと聞いた。

content.content: I heard a rumor that those two have broken off their engagement.

Can take the form ...と聞く, ...と聞いている, or ...と聞いた and expresses information that the speaker has acquired indirectly (i.e. hearsay). The form と聞く is used only in written language, and the masu-form と聞きます is not used at all.
（×）このあたりは昔海だったと聞きます。
I hear that, long ago, this area was an ocean.
（○）このあたりは昔海だったと聞いています。
I’ve heard that, long ago, this area was an ocean.
【ときたひには】This is a spoken language expression that is rather outdated. Usually ときたら is used instead.
1. Nときたひには

content: うちの女房ときたひには、暇さえあれば居眠りしている。

content.content: Take my wife—whenever she has a little free time, she dozes off!

content: うちの親父ときたひには、天気さえよければ釣りに行っている。

content.content: That father of mine—if the weather is clear, he's off fishing!
Used to introduce, as the topic of conversation, a person with extreme actions or characteristics. Expresses the feeling that the speaker is utterly astonished or dumbfounded.
2. ...ときたひには

content: 毎日残業で、しかも休日なしときたひには、病気になるのも無理はない。

content.content: What with overtime every day and, on top of that, no days off, it’s no wonder she got sick.

content: 授業には毎回遅刻で、試験も零点ときたひには、落第するのも当然だ。

content.content: He came late every time and got zero on his tests—of course he failed that class!

content: 毎日うだるような暑さが続いて、しかも水不足ときたひには愚痴もいいたくなる。

content.content: With this sweltering heat day after day, and a lack of water to boot, anyone would want to complain!

Placed after clauses or nouns that express a situation that is extreme or has an unusual degree of something. Indicates that, given such a situation, the resulting condition is to be expected. Usually conveys a negative evaluation.
【ときたら】
1. Nときたら

content: うちの亭主ときたら、週のうち3日は午前様で、日曜になるとごろごろ寝てばかりいる。

content.content: That husband of mine—he’s out till after midnight at least three times a week, and then come Sunday, he just lies around the house!

content: あそこの家の中ときたら、散らかし放題で足の踏み場もない。

content.content: You know that house over there? The inside is so cluttered that there's no place to stand!

Used by the speaker to introduce a certain person or situation as the topic of conversation and then state an evaluation of that person/situation. The topic is someone or something that is well-known to the speaker, and s/he uses ときたら to express a particularly strong emotion or evaluation that s/he has regarding it. Usually followed by expressions that indicate criticism or dissatisfaction, such as 本当にいやになる (I really hate it) or あきれてしまう (I’m shocked). Used mostly in spoken language.
2. ...ときたら

content: 毎日残業の後に飲み屋のはしごときたら、体がもつはずがない。

content.content: He works overtime every day and then goes bar-hopping, so there's no way his health could hold up.

content: 働き者で気立てがいいときたら、みんなに好かれるのも無理はない。

content.content: She’s so hard-working and good-tempered—it's no wonder everyone likes her.

content: 新鮮な刺し身ときたら、やっぱり辛口の日本酒がいいな。

content.content: If there’s fresh sashimi (raw fish), I’ll go for—what else?—a dry Japanese sake.

content: ステーキときたらやっぱり赤ワインでなくちゃ。

content.content: When you’re having steak, you’ve got to have red wine!

Used to introduce as the topic of conversation a person, thing, or situation with an extreme characteristic. Means “in this kind of case/situation, of course this is the only thing to do (or the only thing that will happen).” As shown in

content: and
, this pattern also takes the form NときたらN, in which case it conveys the meaning that “N goes best with N” or “for N, N is the best.”

content.content: 【ときているから】［N／Na／A／V　ときているから］

content: あの寿司屋は、ネタがいいうえに安いときているから、いつ行っても店の前に行列ができている。

content.content: That sushi bar not only uses good ingredients, it’s also cheap, so whenever you go, there’s always a line of people out front.

content: 秀才でしかも努力家ときているから、彼の上にでるのは簡単ではない。

content.content: As for him, he’s not only talented but also hard-working, so it isn’t easy to outdo him.

content: 収入が少なく子だくさんときているから、暮らしは楽ではない。

content.content: With such a low salary and so many children, it’s a hard life.

Used to talk about a person, thing, or situation with extreme characteristics. Expresses that the present state of affairs is a natural outcome of those characteristics. Means “since it (s/he) is so...what else can be expected?” Used mostly in spoken language.
【ときとして】
1. ときとして

content: 温暖なこの地方でも、時として雪がふることもある。

content.content: Even this region, with its mild climate, occasionally gets snow.

content: 人は時として人を裏切ることもある。

content.content: Anyone can betray someone sometime.
Used to express that “(although it is not always the case) there may be times when such-and-such can happen.” Used more in written language than in spoken.
2. ときとして...ない

content: このごろは時として心休まる日がない。

content.content: These days I have no time to relax.

content: 当時は心配事ばかり続き、時として心休まる日はなかった。

content.content: At that time I had nothing but worries and cares, with no time at all to rest and relax.
Used when there is “not even a moment” to feel at ease or at peace. This is a literary expression. In modern Japanese, it usually takes the form 一時(いっとき)として...ない.
【ときに】

content: 時に、ご家族の皆様はお元気ですか。

content.content: By the way, how is everyone in your family?

content: 時に、例の件はどうなりましたか。

content.content: Incidentally, what happened with regard to that other matter?
Used in conversation to introduce a completely new topic that is unrelated to what has been discussed up to that point. A somewhat literary expression. Usually people say ところで or さて.
【ときには】

content: 生真面目な彼だが、時には冗談をいうこともある。

content.content: Even he, dead serious as he is, can sometimes crack a joke.

content: 私だって時には人恋しくなることもある。

content.content: You know, even I get lonely once in a while.

content: いつも明るい人だが、時に機嫌の悪いこともある。

content.content: She’s always cheerful, yet there are times when she’s in a bad mood.

content: 専門家でも、時に失敗する場合もある。

content.content: Even experts can occasionally make mistakes.
Means “not always, but at times....” The particle は can be omitted, as in

content: and

content.content: 【ところ1】
1. Nのところ

content: 今のところ患者は小康状態を保っています。

content.content: At present the patient’s condition is stable.

content: 現在のところ応募者は約 100 人ほどです。

content.content: We currently have about 100 applicants.

content: このところ肌寒い日が続いている。

content.content: We’re having a spell of chilly weather these days.
Attaches to nouns denoting the present, such as 今 (now), げんざい (at present), and この... (this...). Expresses a situation as of the present moment, as in “at the present stage, at this point, recently.”
2. V-るところとなる

content: この政治的スキャンダルは遠からず世界中の人々が知るところとなるだろう。

content.content: It won’t be long before this political scandal becomes known to people all over the world.

content: 彼らの別居はたちまち周囲の人の知るところとなった。

content.content: The news of their separation immediately became common knowledge to everyone around them.
Means that a rumor or news becomes common knowledge. Usually used in the form 知るところとなる. Has the tone of written language.
3. V-るところに　よると／よれば

content: 聞くところによれば、あの二人は離婚したそうだ。

content.content: According to what I hear, apparently those two have divorced.

content: 現地記者の話すところによると、戦況は悪化する一方のようである。

content.content: The reporters on location are saying that the war situation is steadily worsening.

content: 特派員の伝えるところによると、アフリカの飢饉はさらに悪化しているらしい。

content.content: What we hear from the special correspondents is that the famine in Africa seems to be getting even worse.

Uses verbs that denote the output or transfer of information, like 聞く (hear), 話す (speak), or 伝える (tell), and is followed by a clause that specifies the information that has been relayed. The sentence often ends with expressions such as らしい (seem/appear), そうだ (they say/I hear), or とのことだ (so they say). Often used in news reports.
4. V-る／V-ている　ところのN

content: 私が知るところの限りでは、そのようなことは一切ございません。

content.content: As far as I know, that is not the case at all.

content: 彼が目指すところの理想の社会とは、身分差別のないすべての人が平等であるような社会であった。

content.content: The ideal society to which he aspired was one in which there is no discrimination according to status but equality among all people.

This expression is a rather direct translation of relative pronouns used in Western languages. In Japanese it is possible to say, for example, 彼の目指す理想の社会 (the ideal society he aspires to), so there is usually no need to use this expression; when it is used, it sounds like a translation. Used mostly in written language.
5. V-るところまでV

content: 堕ちるところまで堕ちてしまった。

content.content: She sank as low as it was possible for her to sink.

content: とにかく、行けるところまで行ってみよう。

content.content: At any rate, let’s try to go as far as we can.

content: 時間内にやれるところまでやってみてください。

content.content: Please try to do as much as you can in the allotted time.

The same verb is used at the beginning and end of this pattern to express the notion that an action or change reaches its utmost limit or an ultimate stage. When the potential form V-れる is used, as in

content: and
, the meaning is that the action is performed to the greatest extent possible.

content.content: 6. V-ているところをみると

content: 平気な顔をしているところをみると、まだ事故のことを知らせられてないのだろう。

content.content: From the calm expression on his face, I would guess that he hasn’t heard about the accident yet.

content: 大勢の人が行列しているところを見ると、安くておいしい店のようだ。

content.content: Judging from the long line of people, it looks like a good restaurant with reasonable prices.

Used when the speaker is stating a supposition based on firsthand experience.  At the end of the sentence, expressions such as らしい (seem/appear), ようだ (like/as if), or にちがいない (must be/without a doubt) are often used. The forms ...ところから and ...ところからみて may also be used.
（例）高級車に乗っているところから、相当の金持ちだと思われる。
Seeing as he drives a luxury car, we can presume he’s quite wealthy.
【ところ2】
1. V-たところ〈resultative〉

content: 先生にお願いしたところ、早速承諾のお返事をいただいた。

content.content: On making a request of my teacher, I immediately received a reply of consent.

content: 駅の遺失物係に問い合わせたところ、届いているとのことだ。

content.content: Upon contacting the lost and found office at the station, I was told that my article had been turned in.

content: ホテルに電話したところ、そのような名前の人は泊まっていないそうだ。

content.content: When I called the hotel, I was told that there was no one by that name staying there.

content: 教室に行ってみたところが、学生は一人も来ていなかった。

content.content: When I went and took a look at the classroom, there wasn't a single student there.

ところ is attached to the ta-form of an action verb to express the occurrence of a situation and the triggering of a discovery. The situations that appear before and after this expression are not in a direct cause-effect relationship; rather, their relationship is something like “when I did..., by chance/it so happened that such-and-such was the case.” The situation in the second clause is a discovery on the part of the speaker that was triggered by the action in the first clause, and this discovery is stated using language that denotes a previously-realized fact. Sometimes ところ is followed by the particle が, as in

content: , creating the form V-たところが. In this case, the second clause usually expresses a situation contrary to expectation.

content.content: 2. V-たところが〈adversative connective〉

content: 親切のつもりで言ったところがかえって恨まれてしまった。

content.content: I spoke with the intention of being kind, and instead I find myself being resented.

content: 高いお金を出して買ったところが、すぐ壊れてしまった。

content.content: I spent a lot of money to buy it, and it broke right away.

content: 仕事が終わって急いで駆けつけてみたところが、講演はもうほとんど終わってしまっていた。

content.content: After finishing work I rushed to get there as soon as I could, only to find that the performance was already almost over.

This adversative usage can be replaced by のに (even though) and expresses that an outcome is contradictory to anticipation or expectation. In contrast to the resultative usage shown above, が is usually not omitted.
【ところが】
1. ところが〈contrary to prediction〉

content: 天気予報では今日は雨になると言っていた。ところが、少し曇っただけで、結局は降らなかった。

content.content: The weather forecast was for rain today. However, it was only a little cloudy, and we never got any rain after all.

content: ダイエットを始めて3週間になる。ところが、減った体重は、わずか1キロだけだ。

content.content: It’s been three weeks since I started dieting. But I’ve only lost one measly kilogram.

content: いつもは8時半ごろ会社に着く。ところが、今日は交通事故に巻き込まれ、1時間遅れで到着した。

content.content: She always gets to work around 8:30 a.m. But today she was involved in a traffic accident and arrived an hour late.

content: 兄は大変な秀才である。ところが弟は大の勉強嫌いで、高校を無事に卒業できるかどうかも危ぶまれている。

content.content: The older brother is really brilliant. On the other hand, the younger brother absolutely hates to study, and there's concern about whether or not he'll even be able to finish high school.

content: A:春休みはゆっくりされているんでしょうね。

content.content: I guess you’re taking it easy this spring vacation, right?
B:ところが、締め切り原稿があってそうもしていられないんです。
As a matter of fact, I have an article deadline, so I really can't take it easy at all.

content: A:来週のパーティには是非いらしてくださいね。

content.content: Please tell me you’ll come to the party next week!
B:ところが、その日急に予定が入ってしまったんです。
Actually, something unexpected has come up that I have to do that day.

Used to connect two sentences when the content of the second sentence contradicts or clashes with what is naturally anticipated or expected from the first sentence. Also used when there is a relationship of contrast between two situations, as in

content: and
. In conversations like
and

, it is used to tell the addressee something like, “That’s what you may think, but the reality is different.” In other words, this usage signals a discrepancy between the other person’s expectations and reality.

content.content: In all cases, the sentence after ところが contains an expression that indicates an established fact. Non-factual expressions, including expressions of intention, desire, command, or conjecture, cannot be used. Note the examples of incorrect usage given below.
（×）合格はかなり難しそうだ。ところが、受験してみるつもりだ（意志）／挑戦してみたい（希望）／頑張れ（命令）／ひょっとしたら受かるかもしれない（推量）。

It looks like it will be difficult to pass. However, I intend to try to take the test. (intention)/...I want to take up the challenge. (desire)/...do your best! (command)/...I might just pass after all. (conjecture)
2. ところが〈discovery〉

content: 急いで家を出た。ところが、途中で財布を忘れていることに気がつき、あわてて引き返した。

content.content: I left home in a hurry. Then, on the way, I realized I had forgotten my wallet and hurried back.

content: 友人の家に電話した。ところが、1週間前から海外旅行に行って留守だという。

content.content: I called my friend’s house. But I was told that he’s not home because he’s been out of the country on a trip since a week ago.

Used when the speaker is surprised by a new turn of events, or an event that was hard to anticipate from the situation or course of events described in the previous sentence. The sentence after ところが is information newly-discovered by the speaker that contradicts what would naturally be anticipated from the situation described in the previous sentence.
This usage of ところが does not usually allow for substitution with expressions like しかし, けれども, or だが, and when substitution is possible, the meaning of the sentence changes.
【ところだ】

1. Vところだ〈phase of a situation〉ところだ attaches to verbs and is used to report the current status or progress of a situation or event. ところだった expresses that something was at a certain stage in the past. The expression ところだ itself does not usually appear in negative or interrogative forms. The preceding verb does not usually take the negative form, either.
a. V-たところだ

content: 今帰ってきたところです。

content.content: I just got home.

content: 海外勤務を終え、先月帰国したところです。

content.content: I finished my overseas assignment and returned home just last month.

content: 電話したら、あいにくちょっと前に出かけたところだった。

content.content: When I called, unfortunately she had just stepped out a little earlier.

Expresses the stage immediately after an action or change has taken place. Often used with adverbs that refer to the time immediately preceding, such as 今 (now), さっき (just a moment ago), or ちょっと前 (a little while ago).
b. V-ているところだ

content: A:もしもし、和雄君いますか。

content.content: Hello, is Kazuo-kun there?
B:今お風呂に入っているところなんです。
Right now he is taking a bath.

content: だだ今電話番号を調べているところですので、もう少々お待ちください。

content.content: I am looking up that phone number right now, so please wait a few moments.

content: ふすまを開けると、妻は着物を片付けているところだった。

content.content: When I slid the doors open, my wife was in the middle of putting her kimono away.
Expresses that an action is currently in progress.
c. V-ていたところだ

content: いい時に電話をくれました。私もちょうどあなたに電話しようと思っていたところなんです。

content.content: You’ve called at a good time. I was just thinking about giving you a call, too.

content: 思いがけなくも留学のチャンスが舞い込んできた。そのころ私は、将来の進路が決められずいろいろ思い悩んでいたところだった。

content.content: I was unexpectedly blessed with the chance to study overseas. At that time in my life, I couldn’t decide on a future direction and was worrying about all sorts of things.

Expresses that a certain condition has continued from a previous time to the point in time indicated in the sentence. Often used when explaining one’s thinking or psychological condition, to express that it has changed or a new development has come about.
d. V-るところだ

content: これから家を出るところですから、30 分ほどしたら着くと思います。

content.content: I am just about to leave home, so I should be there in about thirty minutes.

content: 飛行機は今飛び立つところだ。

content.content: The plane is just about to take off.

content: A:ご飯もう食べた？

content.content: Have you already had (breakfast/lunch/supper)?
B:ううん、これから食べるところ。
No, I’m just about to eat.

content: 家に戻って来ると、妻は買い物に出掛けるところだった。

content.content: When I returned home, my wife was just leaving to go out shopping.
Expresses the stage immediately before an action or change takes place. Sometimes used with adverbs like ちょうど (just now), 今 (now), and これから (after this/now).

2. Vところだ〈counter-factual〉Expresses a situation counter to reality. Means “if things were different, then such-and-such would be the case.” Often preceded by a conditional clause marked with たら, なら, or ば.
a. ...たらVところだ

content: 昔だったらそんな過激な発言をする人間は、処刑されているところだ。

content.content: If this were still the old days, people who make such radical statements would be executed.

content: 父がそのことを知ったら激怒するところだ。

content.content: If my father found out about that, he would be furious.

content: 先生がお元気だったら、今日のような日には一緒に中華料理でも食べているところでしょう。

content.content: If my teacher were still in good health, on a day like today we would be together eating Chinese food or something.

content: 知らせていただかなければ、とっくにあきらめていたところです。

content.content: If you hadn’t let me know, I would already have given up.

Placed after the dictionary form or ta-form of a verb and preceded by a conditional clause marked by ...ば, ...たら, etc. Expresses that, although the reality is different, the speaker can imagine a situation that would arise if a certain condition were realized.
For example,

content: means “If this were the old days, we would expect them to be executed,” but this does not happen in present-day society.

content.content: b. ...ところだった［V-るところだった］［V-ていたところだった］

content: もし気がつくのが遅かったら、大惨事になるところだった。

content.content: If we had noticed too late, it could have been a real tragedy.

content: あっ、あなたに大事な話があるのを思い出しました。うっかり忘れるところでした。

content.content: Oh, I just remembered that I have something important to discuss with you. I had almost forgotten.

content: ありがとうございます。注意していただかなければ忘れていたところでした。

content.content: Thank you so much. If you hadn’t warned me, I would have forgotten.

Means that under different circumstances a certain event would have occurred, but it was narrowly avoided, just in time. Often used with conditional clauses marked with ...ば or ...たら. To emphasize that the event was right on the verge of occurring, the expression もうすこしで...ところだった (any longer and...would have...) may be used.
c. ...なら（ば）...ところ　だが／を

content: 普通ならただではすまないところだが、今回だけは見逃してやろう。

content.content: Ordinarily I wouldn't let this pass, but I'll overlook it just this once.

content: 本来ならば直接お伺いすべきところですが、書面にて失礼致します。

content.content: I know that under normal circumstances I should come to see you in person, but I hope you don’t mind my sending you a letter instead.

content: 通常は定価どおりのところを、お得意さんに限り特別に1万円引きになっております。

content.content: Although normally we charge the list price, we are offering a special 10,000 yen discount to our best customers only.

content: いつもなら1時間で行けるところを、今日は交通事故があって3時間もかかった。

content.content: We can usually get there in an hour, but today there was a car accident, so it took us three hours.
Used with expressions such as 普通 (usually), 通常 (normally), and 本来ならば (under ordinary circumstances). Expresses that the current state of affairs is special and differs from the usual one.
【ところで】
1. ところで

content: A:お元気そうですね。

content.content: You’re looking well.
B:おかげさまで。
Thank you, I am.
A:ところで、この度は息子さんが大学に合格なさったそうで、おめでとうございます。
By the way, I heard that your son passed his university entrance exams. Congratulations!

content: A:やっと夏休みだね。ところで、今年の夏休みはどうするの。

content.content: At long last, it’s summer vacation! Say, what are your plans for this summer?
B:卒論の資料を集めるつもり。
I'm planning to collect data for my graduation thesis.

content: 今日はお疲れ様でした。ところで、駅のそばに新しい中華料理屋さんができたんですけど、今夜行ってみませんか。

content.content: Thank you for your work today. On a slightly different note... there’s a new Chinese restaurant beside the station. Would you like to go tonight?

content: 今日の授業はこれまでです。ところで、田中君を最近見かけませんが、どうしているか知っている人いますか。

content.content: This concludes today’s class. Incidentally, I haven't seen Tanaka-kun recently. Does anyone know how he’s doing?
Used to change the topic of conversation or add something pertinent to the current topic of discussion by making some kind of contrasting remark.
2. V-たところで〈point in time between two events〉

content: 論文の最後の一行を書いたところで、突然気を失った。

content.content: Just after I wrote the final line of my thesis, all of a sudden I fainted.

content: 話の区切りが付いたところで、終わることにしましょう。

content.content: When the discussion reaches a good place to leave off, let’s stop.

content: 大急ぎで走り、飛び乗ったところで電車のドアが閉まった。

content.content: I raced to the train and jumped aboard just before the doors closed.

content: ようやく事業に見通しがつくようになったところで、父は倒れてしまった。

content.content: Just as his business was finally starting to look up, my father collapsed.
Means that at the point that one action or change has come to an end and there is a natural break, a second action or change occurs (or is made to occur).
3. V-たところで〈adversative connective〉a. V-たところで...ない

content: いくら頼んだところで、あの人は引き受けてはくれないだろう。

content.content: No matter how many times you ask, I don’t think that she will agree to do it.

content: そんなに悲しんだところで、死んだ人が帰って来るわけではない。

content.content: No matter how sad you are, no one has ever come back from the dead.

content: 今頃になって急いだところで、無駄だ（＝間に合わない）。

content.content: No matter how much you hurry now, it's no use (= you won’t make it in time).

content: 到着が少しぐらい遅れたところで問題はない（＝大丈夫だ）。

content.content: It’s no big deal if you arrive a little late (= it’s all right).

content: 頑丈な作りですから倒れたところで壊れる心配はありません。

content.content: It’s sturdily made, so even if it falls over there’s no worry that it will break.

ところで attaches to the ta-form of a verb and expresses that, even if that action is taken, it will not yield the expected result. The clause describing the result contains the nai-form of a predicate or expressions that convey a negative judgment or evaluation, such as 無駄だ (it’s useless) or 無意味だ (it’s meaningless) (see

content: to
). May also be used to express a positive evaluation, with the sense “it’s all right/no problem even if you do...,” as in
and

. In this case, the relationship between the two clauses is that even if the first situation occurs, it will not affect the second. Sometimes used with adverbs like たとえ (however/even if), どんなに (no matter how), and いくら (how much), and/or “何 + counter” expressions (e.g. 何人 (how many people), 何冊 (how many copies/volumes), 何回 (how many times)).

content.content: b. V-たところで

content: うちの夫は出世したところで課長どまりだろう。

content.content: Even if my husband gets promoted, he probably won't go farther than section chief.

content: どんなに遅れたところで、せいぜい5、6分だと思います。

content.content: Even if we’re late, I'm sure it won’t be any more than five or six minutes at the most.

content: 泥棒に入られたところで、価値のあるものは本ぐらいしかない。

content.content: Even if we have a break-in, the only thing of value the robbers will find is books.
Followed by an expression that indicates a low degree of something. Means “even if such a thing should happen, the degree/quantity/number won’t be significant.”
【ところに】［V-ている／V-た  ところに］

content: 出掛けようとしたところに電話がかかってきた。

content.content: Just as we were leaving, the telephone rang.

content: ようやく実行する方向に意見がまとまったところへ思わぬ邪魔が入った。

content.content: We had finally agreed on a plan of action when there was an unexpected snag.

content: 財布をなくして困っているところに偶然知り合いが通りかかり、無事家までたどり着くことができた。

content.content: When I was in a real fix after losing my wallet, an acquaintance happened to come by and I was able to get home safely.
Takes the form ...ところに or ...ところへ and means “when I was ...ing” or  “when I did....”
Used to express the occurrence of an event that alters or changes a situation that is at a certain stage. In most cases, the event is one that impedes or blocks something’s progress, as in

content: and
. However, it can also be something that changes the current situation for the better, as in

content.content: 【ところを】
1. Vところを...V

content: お母さんは子供が遊んでいるところを家の窓から見ていた。

content.content: The mother was watching the children play, from the window of the house.

content: こっそりタバコを吸っているところを先生に見つかった。

content.content: I was sneaking a smoke when my teacher spotted me.

content: 駅前を歩いているところを警官に呼び止められた。

content.content: She was walking in front of the station when she was stopped by the police.

content: 男は金庫からお金を盗み出そうとしているところを現行犯で逮捕された。

content.content: Just as he was taking the money out of the safe, he was caught in the act and arrested.

content: 人々がぐっすり寝込んだところを突然の揺れが襲った。

content.content: The people were sleeping soundly when all of a sudden there was a jolt.

content: あやうく暴漢に襲われかけたところを見知らぬ男性に助けてもらった。

content.content: Just as I was about to be assaulted by a thug, I got help from a man I had never seen before.

This pattern contains two verbs, with the second one denoting an action that exerts a direct effect on the development of the situation expressed by the first. The second verb is a verb of sight or discovery, such as 見る (see), 見つける (find), 見つかる (be found), or 発見する (discover), or a verb that denotes cessation, capture, attack, or rescue, such as 呼び止める (call to a halt), 捕まえる (catch/capture), 捕まる (be caught/be captured), 襲う (attack), or 助ける (save/help). These all share the meaning of halting or obstructing the development of the action or event denoted by the first verb.
2. ...ところ（を）［Nのところ（を）］［Aところ（を）］［R-ちゅうのところ（を）］

content: お楽しみのところを恐縮ですが、ちょっとお時間を拝借できないでしょうか。

content.content: I am sorry to disturb you while you’re having such a pleasant time, but could I please have a few moments of your time?

content: ご多忙のところ、よくきてくださいました。

content.content: Thank you so much for taking time out of your busy schedule to be here today.

content: お忙しいところを申し訳ありませんが、ちょっとお邪魔いたします。

content.content: I am very sorry to disturb you, but I’m going to have to interrupt.

content: お取り込み中のところを失礼します。

content.content: Please excuse me for intruding when you’re in the middle of something.

content: お休み中のところをお電話してすみませんでした。

content.content: I am sorry to be calling during your vacation.

content: 難しいことは承知のうえですが、そこのところをちょっと無理して聞いていただけないでしょうか。

content.content: I am well aware of how difficult this is, but can’t I ask you to make a special effort to consider what I have to say?

content: A:最近ちょっと忙しくて...。

content.content: I am rather busy these days....
B:そこんところを何とかよろしくお願いしますよ。
I know, but I still want to ask you to find some way to help me out.

Used by the speaker to express that s/he is taking the addressee’s situation into consideration when s/he is making a difficult or unreasonable request or causing inconvenience to the other person. Often used to preface requests, apologies, or expressions of gratitude. As in

content: and
, sometimes the previously-stated circumstances are referred to with a demonstrative, resulting in forms like そこのところ (regarding that point).

content.content: 【とされている】

content: 仏教で生き物を殺すのは十悪のひとつとされている。

content.content: In Buddhism, killing a living creature is considered to be one of the ten evil deeds.

content: 地球の温暖化の一因として、大気中のオゾン層の破壊が大きくかかわっているとされている。

content.content: One of the biggest causes of global warming is believed to be the destruction of the ozone layer in the atmosphere.

content: チョムスキーの理論では、言語能力は人間が生まれつきもっている能力とされている。

content.content: In Chomsky’s theory, linguistic competence is said to be an ability that human beings are born with.

content: 歌舞伎は風俗を乱すものとされ、禁止されていた。

content.content: Kabuki was considered to have a harmful effect on public morals and so was forbidden.

Means “is thought to be...” or “is considered as....” With a nominal predicate, だ is often omitted, yielding the form Nとされている. Typically used in formal writing, such as news reports or scholarly papers.

【としたら】Formed by attaching the particle と to したら. Means something like “supposing that is true,” “supposing that such-and-such exists/occurs,” or “based on this fact/the present state of affairs.” Used to establish the conditions for the supposition “if one were to think such-and-such.” Can hardly ever be replaced by たら alone.
1. ...としたら〈not-yet-realized condition〉［N／Na　だとしたら］［A／V　としたら］

content: 家を建てるとしたら、大きい家がいい。

content.content: If you’re going to build a house, a big one is best.

content: もし1億円の宝くじがあたったとしたら、家を買おう。

content.content: If I were to win a hundred million yen in the lottery, I’d buy a house.

content: 仮にあなたが言っていることが本当だとしたら、彼は私に嘘をついていることになる。

content.content: Supposing that what you say is true, that would mean he’s lying to me.

content: いらっしゃるとしたら何時ごろになりますか。

content.content: If you were to come, what time do you think it might be?

content: 責任があるとしたら、私ではなくあなたの方です。

content.content: If someone is responsible for this, it’s not me but you.

Means “supposing we assume that such-and-such is a fact,” or “in the event that such-and-such occurs or exists.” としたら is followed by an expression of the speaker’s intention, judgment, or evaluation. Sometimes accompanied by 仮に (supposing that.../granting, for the sake of argument, that...) or もし (if/provided that...). としたら can be followed by expressions of intention or evaluation; in such cases, とすると and とすれば are not natural.
（×）宝くじがあたった｛とすると／とすれば｝家を買おう。
{When/If} I’d win the lottery, then I’ll buy a house.
2. ...としたら〈already-realized condition〉［N／Na　（なの）だとしたら］［A／V　（の）だとしたら］

content: これだけ待っても来ないのだとしたら、今日はもう来ないでしょう。

content.content: If she hasn’t come after we’ve waited this long, then she probably isn’t going to come at all today.

content: A:私はそのことを誰にも話していません。

content.content: I haven’t said anything about that to anyone.
B:あなたが話してないのだとしたら、一体誰がもらしたのだろう。
If you haven’t said anything, then who in the world let it slip?

Expresses a supposition based on the present situation or information received from another person. Means “if we consider a situation/fact like this.” Often used in the form ...のだとしたら. This usage cannot be combined with the expressions 仮に or もし (see above) .
3. （そう）だとしたら

content: A:寝台車は全て満席だって。

content.content: They say all the sleeper cars are full.
B:だとしたら、普通の座席に座って行くしかないわね。
If that’s so, then we have no other choice but to go and sit in the regular seats.

content: A:会議は1時間遅れの開始になったそうですよ。

content.content: I heard that the meeting is going to start about an hour late.
B:そうだとしたら、こんなに急いでくるんじゃなかった。
If that’s true, then we didn't have to hurry as much as we did to get here.

content: 台風の上陸と満潮の時刻が重なるらしい。だとしたら、沿岸では厳重な警戒が必要になる。

content.content: It looks like the typhoon will hit at the same time as high tide. If that's the case, coastal areas will have to be on close alert.
Refers to the preceding sentence or an utterance made by the addressee and means “if we take that fact/situation into consideration” or “if that is a fact.”
【として】
1. Nとして

content: 研究生としてこの大学で勉強している。

content.content: I am studying at this university as a research student.

content: 日本軍の行った行為は日本人として恥ずかしく思う。

content.content: As a Japanese, I am ashamed of the actions of the Japanese soldiers.

content: 子供がこんなひどい目にあわされては、親として黙っているわけにはいかない。

content.content: As a parent, I cannot sit back and say nothing while children are being treated so badly.

content: 彼は大学の教授としてより、むしろ作家としての方がよく知られている。

content.content: He is better known as a writer than as a college professor.

content: 趣味として書道を勉強している。

content.content: I am studying calligraphy as a hobby.

content: 学長の代理として会議に出席した。

content.content: I attended the meeting in place of the college president.

content: 大統領を国賓として待遇する。

content.content: We will treat the president as a state guest.

content: 軽井沢は古くから避暑地として人気があるところだ。

content.content: Karuizawa has long been popular as a resort to get away from the summer heat.

content: 文学者としては高い評価を得ている彼も、家庭人としては失格である。

content.content: While he has received great acclaim as a literary scholar, as a family man he is a failure.

content: 彼の料理の腕前はプロのコックとしても十分に通用するほどのものだ。

content.content: His cooking skills are good enough for him to make it as a professional chef.
Attaches to nouns and expresses a qualification, position, category, or title.
2. Nとしては→
【としては】
3. Nとしても

content: 私としてもこの件に関しては当惑しております。

content.content: I, too, am at a loss with respect to this matter.

content: 学長としても、教授会の意向を無視するわけにはいかないだろう。

content.content: Even as the university president, I can’t very well ignore the will of the faculty, can I?

content: 会社といたしましても、この度の不祥事は誠に遺憾に思っております。

content.content: Speaking for the company, I feel that this scandal is truly regrettable.
Attaches to nouns denoting people or organizations and means “also from such-and-such a stance or perspective.” May also be used in the polite form, as in

content: . The difference between としては and としても is that the latter implies there are also other people or members of an organization who have the same stance or perspective.

content.content: 【としても】
4. NとしてのN

content: 教師としてではなく、一人の人間としての立場から発言したいと思う。

content.content: I would like to speak not as a teacher but from the standpoint of a single human being.

content: 彼にも男としての意地があるはずです。

content.content: He too must have some male pride.

content: 日本代表としての責任を強く感じ、精一杯頑張りたいと思います。

content.content: I feel a strong sense of responsibility as a representative of Japan, and I pledge to do my utmost.
Nとして (as a/an N) is used to modify another noun.
【として...ない】［最小限の数量+として...ない］

content: 戦争が始まって以来、一日として心の休まる日はない。

content.content: Since the war began, I have not had a day’s peace.

content: 期末試験では、一人として満足のいく答案を書いた学生はなかった。

content.content: Not one single student submitted satisfactory answers to the final exam.

content: 高級品ばかりで、一つとして私が買えそうな品物は見当たらない。

content.content: There are only luxury goods; I can't find a single thing I can afford to buy.

content: だれ一人として、私の発言を支持してくれる人はいなかった。

content.content: There wasn't a single person who supported what I said.

として attaches to words that contain the element 一 (one), which indicates a minimum quantity. Followed by a predicate in the negative form and means “not any, not at all.” Examples of words to which として attaches include 一日 (one day), 一時 (いっとき) (a short time), (だれ) 一人 ((not) one person), and (何) 一つ ((not) a single thing). With question words such as なに (what) and だれ (who), として can be dropped, as below.
（例）だれ一人、私の発言を支持してくれる人はいなかった。
Not one person supported what I said.
More commonly used in written language. In spoken language, expressions like ひとつもない (not a single one) are usually used.
【としては】Formed by attaching the particle は to として. In the usage shown below, は is usually not dropped.
1. Nとしては〈position, viewpoint〉

content: 彼としては、辞職する以外に方法がなかったのでしょう。

content.content: I can imagine that, from his point of view, there was no other choice but to resign.

content: 私といたしましては、ご意見に賛成しかねます。

content.content: If I may speak for myself, I'm afraid I cannot agree with your opinion.

content: 吉田さんとしては、ああとしか答えようがなかったのでしょう。

content.content: For Yoshida-san, perhaps that was the only response it was possible to make.

content: 委員会としては、早急に委員長を選出する必要がある。

content.content: From the perspective of the committee, it is necessary to select a chairperson as soon as possible.
Used with nouns denoting people or organizations and means “speaking from/considering such-and-such a stance or perspective....” Sometimes used in polite forms, such as ...としましては or ...といたしましては.
2. Nとしては〈divergence from the average〉

content: 父は日本人としては背の高いほうです。

content.content: My father is tall for a Japanese person.

content: 100 キロの体重は普通の男性だったらずいぶん重いと思うが、相撲取りとしてはむしろ軽いほうである。

content.content: I think a body weight of 100 kilograms would be quite heavy for an ordinary man, but for a sumoo wrestler it’s actually rather light.

content: 大学院を出てすぐ大学に就職できる人は、研究者としては幸運な部類に入る。

content.content: Anyone who can find a university position right after finishing graduate school would be classed among the luckiest of researchers.

content: 学生数 2000 人というのは大学としてはかなり規模が小さい。

content.content: A student body of 2,000 is rather small for a university.

Attaches to a noun denoting a person or organization. Used to say that the person or organization in question deviates from the standard or average of the group to which it belongs, in terms of numbers or a certain characteristic. Can be replaced by ...にしては.
【としても】
1. Nとしても→
【として】
2. ...としても［N／Na　（だ）としても］［A／V　としても］

content: 彼の言っていることが真実だとしても、証拠がなければ信じるわけにはいかない。

content.content: Even if what he says is true, I can’t very well believe it without proof.

content: たとえ賛成してくれる人が一人もいないとしても、自分の意見を最後まで主張するつもりだ。

content.content: I intend to stick with my opinion to the very end, even if there isn't a single person who concurs with it.

content: 留学するとしても、来年以降です。

content.content: If I do study overseas, it will have to be next year or later.

content: 今からタクシーに乗ったとしても、時間には間に合いそうもない。

content.content: Even if we took a taxi at this point, it’s not very likely we would make it in time.

content: 渋滞でバスが遅れたとしても、電話ぐらいしてくるはずだ。

content.content: Even if the bus was delayed in traffic, I would at least expect a phone call.

content: 加藤さんの忠告がなかったとしても、やっぱり病院を変えていただろう。

content.content: Even if Kato-san hadn’t warned me, I would probably have changed hospitals anyway.

content: 同級生に駅で出会わなかったとしても、やっぱり授業をさぼって映画に行っただろう。

content.content: Even if I hadn’t run into a classmate at the station, I probably still would have cut class to go see a movie.

Takes the pattern XとしてもY (even if X, then Y). Expresses that “even if X were true/had happened, it would not have caused or hindered the occurrence of Y.” Y expresses something that contradicts or deviates from what is expected from X.
When X is a verb, the pattern V-たとしても (ta-form) is the most common, as shown in

content: . However, the pattern V-るとしても (dictionary form) is also used, as shown in

means “if something like studying abroad happens in the future,” and the time frame indicated by Y is essentially the same as that for the occurrence of X. On the other hand, V-たとしても means “even if/when situation X has arisen,” so this pattern expresses that X occurs before Y. For example,
means “even if we do take a taxi, the end result will probably still be that we won’t make it in time.”

content.content: In

content: and

, X expresses a situation that is contrary to fact, and Y expresses a result that probably would have happened anyway: “In fact, Kato-san did warn me, but even if s/he hadn’t...” and “I did actually run into a classmate, but even if I hadn’t....”

content.content: 3. ...はいいとしても

content: 彼はいいとしても、彼女が許してくれないだろう。

content.content: Even if he’s OK with it, she probably won’t allow it.

content: 計算を間違えたのはいいとしても、すぐに報告しなかったことが問題だ。

content.content: Even if we overlook the miscalculation, the fact that you didn't report it right away is a problem.

content: 時間通り来たのはいいとしても、宿題を忘れて来たのはよくない。

content.content: You may have come on time, but it's not acceptable that you forgot to bring your homework.

content: あのホテルは、部屋はいいとしても、従業員の態度がよくない。

content.content: The rooms at that hotel might be all right, but the employees don’t have a very good attitude.

Placed after nouns and clauses. Takes the pattern XはいいとしてもY (even if I accept X, still Y). Y contains an expression of negative evaluation, such as よくない (not good), and the pattern as a whole means “even if I consider X to be all right, I cannot say the same about Y.” This expression is used to contrast two situations, X and Y. It means that while X lies within the range of what is permissible, Y does not.
【とする1】

content: ぎりぎりで締め切りに間に合い、ほっとした。

content.content: I was relieved that I managed to make the deadline just in time.

content: 子供は少しの間もじっとしていない。

content.content: Kids can’t stay still even for a short while.

content: 何を言われても平然としている。

content.content: No matter what they say to her, she remains unruffled.

content: ぼんやり（と）していた記憶が時間が経つにつれてだんだんはっきり（と）してきた。

content.content: My memories, which had been blurry, gradually became sharper with time.

content: 記者の質問に対し堂々とした態度で応対した。

content.content: He handled the reporter’s questions in a dignified manner.

content: もっときちんとした格好をしなさい。

content.content: Dress a little more respectably!

content: 真夜中の電話の音にはっとして目が覚めた。

content.content: I woke with a start at the sound of the telephone in the middle of the night.

content: 何を言われても、平然としてたばこを吹かしている。

content.content: No matter what people say to her, she just keeps puffing on her cigarette with an air of unconcern.

content: 彼女はきっとして、私をにらみつけた。

content.content: She cast a sharp glance at me.

content: 昨日からの雪は、一夜明けた今も依然として降り続いている。

content.content: The snow started yesterday, continued overnight, and is still falling steadily.
This pattern combines the verb する with an adverb that has the particle と attached to it. Indicates that something has a certain appearance or condition. As shown in

content: , と is not obligatory for words like ぼんやり (vaguely) and はっきり (clearly), which can be used as adverbs without it. In

, して can be dropped. Other adverbs that combine with する include ちゃんと (properly), ゆったりと (easily/comfortably), かっかと (briskly/furiously), 悠々と (calmly/leisurely), 悠然と (with composure), and 毅然と (resolutely).

content.content: 【とする2】［N／Na　だとする］［A／V　とする］
1. ...とする〈supposition〉

content: 今仮に3億円の宝くじがあなたに当たったとします。あなたは、それで何をしますか。

content.content: Let’s say you just won 300 million yen in a lottery. What would you do with it?

content: 今、東京で関東大震災と同程度の地震が起こったとしよう。その被害は当時とは比べものにならないものになるだろう。

content.content: Imagine that an earthquake of the same intensity as the Great Kanto Earthquake has just hit Tokyo. The damage would no doubt be beyond compare with what happened then.

content: 例えば 50 人来るとして、会費は一人いくらぐらいにすればよいでしょうか。

content.content: Say, for example, that fifty people come...how much should we charge per person?

content: それはそうとして、我々はどうしたらよいでしょうか。

content.content: Be that as it may, what do you think we should do?

Means “suppose we say that....” Used to establish the conditions for a hypothetical or imaginary situation, regardless of what the actual state of affairs may be. Conveys a strong sense that the speaker is deliberately setting the conditions for a hypothetical situation.
2. ...とする〈regard as〉Used in news reports, legal texts, and other modes of formal expression.
a. ...とする［N／Na　（だ）とする］［A／V　とする］

content: 酔ったうえでの失言（だ）として、彼の責任は問われないことになった。

content.content: It was decided that he had made the inappropriate remark while intoxicated, so he was not held accountable.

content: 多額の不正融資が行われた証拠があるにもかかわらず、事実無根として片付けられた。

content.content: Despite the existence of proof that illicit loans of large sums of money had been made, the case was dismissed as groundless.

content: 裁判長は過失は被告側にあるとし、被害者に賠償金を払うよう命じた。

content.content: The presiding judge determined that the fault lay with the defendant and ordered him to pay the victim compensation.

content: 今の法律では夫婦はどちらか一方の姓を選ばなければならないとされている。

content.content: The current law stipulates that a married couple must choose the surname of either one spouse or the other.
Means ...と見なす(consider to be...) or ...と決める(decide that...). After nouns, the copula だ is often dropped.
b. ...こととするMeans “consider to be...,” “judge to be...,” or “decide that....”

content: 《規則》会議を欠席する場合は、事前に議長宛に届けを提出することとする。

content.content: 《regulation》In the event that a member is unable to attend a meeting, he or she shall submit written notice to the chair in advance.

content: この度の法律改正は喜ぶべきこととして受け止められている。

content.content: The legal revisions carried out at this time are being received as a welcome change.
Means ...と決める (decide that...) or ...と判断する (judge to be...).
c. ...ものとする

content: 意見を言わない者は賛成しているものとする。

content.content: Those who state no opinion will be considered to be in favor of this measure.

content: 1週間たってもお返事がない場合はご辞退なさったものとして扱います。

content.content: If we receive no response from you after a week has passed, we will treat you as having forfeited (your place).
Means ...と見なす (consider to be...) or ...と解釈する (interpret as...).
3. V-ようとする

content: 時計は正午を知らせようとしている。

content.content: The clock is about to strike noon.

content: お風呂に入ろうとしたところに、電話がかかってきた。

content.content: Just as I was about to get into the bathtub, there was a phone call.
【よう2】
4. NをNとする

content: 私は恩師の生き方を手本としている。

content.content: I take my mentor’s way of living as my model.

content: 祖父は散歩を日課としている。

content.content: My grandfather goes for a walk every day as part of his routine.

content: この試験では 60 点以上を合格とする。

content.content: On this exam, the passing grade is set at 60 or above.

content: 看護婦は昔は女の仕事とされていたが、この頃は男の看護士もいるそうだ。

content.content: In the past, nursing was considered to be a profession for women, but apparently these days there are male nurses too.

content: 芭蕉は人生を旅として生きた。

content.content: Matsuo Basho lived his life as a journey.

Means “consider...to be...,” “think of...as...,” or “decide that...is like....” Conveys a variety of meanings, such as using someone’s actions or way of doing things as a model, deciding to make a habit of something, or comparing one thing to something else.

content: can be replaced by Nにする, but metaphorical usages like the one shown in
do not allow this.

content.content: 【とすると】すると is attached to the particle と and refers to the preceding clause. Means “if we assume that to be a fact,” or “in the event that...occurs,” or “based on the present situation/facts.” Followed by the expression of a judgment that would hold in the event that the preceding assumption is made. This pattern is used to establish a set of hypothetical conditions and conveys the meaning “in the event that a certain assumption is made.” と by itself does not have this meaning, so とすると can hardly ever be replaced by と.
1. ...とすると〈not-yet-realized condition〉［N／Na　だとすると］［A／V　とすると］

content: 医学部に入るとすると、一体どのくらいお金が必要なのだろうか。

content.content: If I were to enter the school of medicine, I wonder just how much money I would need.

content: もし、今後も雨が降らないとすると、水不足になるのは避けられないだろう。

content.content: If the lack of rainfall continues, it probably won't be possible to avoid a water shortage.

content: 仮に被告が言っていることが事実だとすると、彼女は嘘の証言をしていることになる。

content.content: If we assume that the defendant is telling the truth, that means her testimony is a lie.

Means “if we assume that such-and-such is a fact/will occur,” even though the speaker doesn’t actually know whether or not the thing in question is a fact/will occur. Often accompanied by 仮に (supposing that) or もし (if).
2. ...とすると〈already-realized condition〉［N／Na　だとすると］［A／V　とすると］

content: 1時間待ってまだ何の連絡もないとすると、途中で事故にでもあったのかもしれない。

content.content: If there hasn’t been any word from him/her whatsoever after waiting a full hour, it could mean that there was an accident or something along the way.

content: A:図書館は明日から2週間休館になります。

content.content: The library is going to close tomorrow for two weeks.
B:2週間休館だとすると今日のうちに必要な本を借りておかなければならないな。
If it's going to be closed for two weeks, then I guess I’ll have to borrow the books I need today.
Means “taking into account the current situation/facts,” based on the actual situation or information received from another party. かりに (supposing that) and もし (if) do not combine with this usage.
3. （だ）とすると

content: A:今年の2月の平均気温は平年より数度も高いそうですよ。

content.content: They say that this year the average temperatures in February have been several degrees above normal.
B:とすると、桜の開花も早くなるでしょうね。
If that’s so, then the cherry trees will probably bloom early, won’t they?

content: 脱線事故で今日一日電車は不通の見込みだという。だとすると、道路は相当混雑するだろう。

content.content: I heard that, because of a derailment, the trains are expected to stop running all day today. If that’s the case, the roads will probably be pretty congested.
Refers to the previous sentence or a statement made by another person and means “taking into account the present situation/facts.”
【とすれば1】［Nとすれば］

content: 夫とすれば家事をおろそかにする妻には不満も多いだろうと思う。

content.content: From the point of view of the husband, there’s probably a lot of dissatisfaction with a wife who neglects the housework.

content: 当事者の彼とすれば、そう簡単に決めるわけにはいかないのです。

content.content: As someone who is involved, it isn’t so easy for him to make a decision.

content: 教師とすれば、よくできる学生に関心が行くのは自然なことだと思う。

content.content: For teachers, I think it's natural to take more interest in students who perform well.

Placed after a noun denoting a person. Means “if I look at it/think about it from that person’s perspective.” More common in written language. In spoken language, the forms にしたら and/or にしてみれば are often used.

【とすれば2】Formed by attaching すれば to the particle と. Refers to the preceding clause and means “if we assume that to be a fact,” “in the event that...occurs,” or “based on these facts/the present situation.” Used by the speaker to establish a set of hypothetical conditions and conveys the meaning “in the event that a certain assumption is made.” ば by itself does not have this meaning, so とすれば can hardly ever be replaced by ば.
1. ...とすれば〈not-yet-realized condition〉［N／Na　だとすれば］［A／V　とすれば］

content: 死ぬとすれば 10 歳年上の私の方が早いはずだ。

content.content: If one of us is going to die, then it’s bound to be me first, since I'm ten years older than you.

content: 台風は上陸するとすれば、明日の夜になるでしょう。

content.content: If the typhoon does make landfall, it'll probably be tomorrow night.

content: 仮に 20 人来るとすれば、この部屋ではちょっと狭すぎるだろう。

content.content: If we assume that twenty people will come, this room will probably be a little too small.

content: この結婚に反対する人がいるとすれば、それは一番身近な母親である可能性が高い。

content.content: If there’s going to be anyone who is against this marriage, then it’s most likely to be the person most closely related—the mother.

Expresses a hypothetical condition. Means “if we assume that such-and-such is a fact” or “in the event that such-and-such occurs/exists,” although the speaker doesn’t actually know whether or not the thing in question is a fact or will occur. Sometimes accompanied by adverbials such as かりに (supposing that) or もし (if). Often followed by expressions that indicate a judgment on the part of the speaker, such as だろう (probably/likely) or はずだ (should/must be).
2. ...とすれば〈already-realized condition〉［N／Na　だとすれば］［A／V　とすれば］

content: これだけ待っても来ないとすれば、もともと来る気がなかったんじゃないだろうか。

content.content: If she hasn't come after we’ve waited this long, I’d say she probably never intended to come in the first place.

content: 我々の計画が敵に知られていたとすれば、仲間のだれかがもらしたことになる。

content.content: If our plans were known to the enemy, that means it was one of us that leaked them.

content: A:この時間に容疑者は友人と会っていることが分かっています。

content.content: We know that the suspect was meeting with a friend at this time.
B:そうか。彼にアリバイがあるとすれば、では、犯人は一体誰なのだろう。
Is that so? Well, if he’s got an alibi, then who the heck is the culprit?

Used when the speaker comes to the realization that something is true, based on the present situation or on information received from another party. Means “taking into account the current situation/facts,” or “if I were to make a judgment based on that....” Followed by an expression that indicates a judgment on the part of the speaker. かりに (supposing that) and もし (if) are not combined with this usage.
3. （だ）とすれば

content: A:家に電話しても誰も出ないんですよ。

content.content: When I call home, nobody answers.
B:だとすれば、もうこちらに向かっているということじゃないですか。
If that’s the case, don't you think they're already on their way here?

content: あの日彼女は一日中彼と一緒だったことが証明された。とすれば、彼女にはアリバイがあるということになる。

content.content: It has been proven that, on that day, she was with him all day long. And if that is so, it means she has an alibi.

Refers to the previous sentence or a statement made by another person. Means “if that is a fact” or “if we assume that is correct.” Usage is the same as 2 above. A slightly formal expression. In ordinary conversation, expressions like だったら and そうなら are often used.
4. NをNとすればa. NがNだとすれば

content: テレビを茶の間のものとすれば、ラジオは個室のものである。

content.content: If a television is something that goes in the living room (= shared space), then a radio is something that goes in a person’s room (= private space).

content: 兄が実業家タイプだとすれば、弟は学者タイプの性格である。

content.content: If I were to say that my older brother is the entrepreneurial type, then my younger brother has the scholarly type of personality.

This is a formulaic expression that contrasts two items. It means something like “if I (we) were to say that one of them is..., then I (we) can say that the other is....” It can be replaced by NがNなら(ば), as, for example, in 兄が実業家タイプなら(ば), 弟は学者タイプだ (If my older brother is the entrepreneurial type, then my younger brother is the scholarly type). It is not entirely impossible to use とすると and としたら with this pattern, but とすれば and なら are used most often.
【とたん】
1. V-たとたん（に）

content: ドアを開けたとたん、猫が飛び込んできた。

content.content: Just as I opened the door, the cat leapt in.

content: 有名になったとたんに、彼は横柄な態度をとるようになった。

content.content: As soon as he got famous, he started to become arrogant.

content: 試験終了のベルが鳴ったとたんに教室が騒がしくなった。

content.content: As soon as the bell rang for the end of the test, the classroom got noisy.

content: 注射をしたとたん、患者のけいれんはおさまった。

content.content: The moment the injection was given, the patient's convulsions subsided.

とたん is placed after the ta-form of a verb and expresses that one action or change is followed immediately by the occurrence of another action or change. Since it is used at the time and place that the speaker notices the second action or change, it is often associated with an implication of unexpectedness. Accordingly, it cannot be used when the verb in the second clause refers to an intentional action on the part of the speaker. In such cases, expressions like とすぐに (soon after) or やいなや (no sooner than) are used instead.
（×）私は家に帰ったとたん、お風呂に入った。
Just as I got home, I took a bath.
（○）私は家に帰るとすぐにお風呂に入った。
Soon after I got home, I took a bath.
2. そのとたん（に）

content: 友だちと 30 分ほど話して、受話器を置いた。そのとたんに再び電話のベルが鳴り出した。

content.content: After talking with my friend for about thirty minutes, I put the receiver down. Just then, the phone rang again.

content: 噂の二人が部屋から姿を現した。そのとたん、外で待ち構えていた記者たちのフラッシュのシャワーが二人をおそった。

content.content: The much-talked about couple came out of the room. At that very moment, they were assailed by a shower of camera flashes from the reporters who had been lying in wait outside.
Relates to the content of the previous sentence and expresses the meaning “immediately after that,” “soon after that.”
3. とたんにV

content: 空が急に暗くなったと思ったら、途端に大粒の雨が降りだした。

content.content: Just when I was thinking that the sky had suddenly grown dark, all at once large drops of rain began to fall.

content: 日が落ちたら、途端に寒くなった。

content.content: When the sun set, all of a sudden it got cold.

content: 列車はゆっくりと動き出した。とたんに彼女の目から涙があふれ出した。

content.content: Slowly the train started to move. And all of a sudden, tears began to overflow from her eyes.
Means “suddenly,” “all at once.” With this usage, the particle に cannot be dropped.
【とちがって】［Nと（は）ちがって］［Na なのと（は）ちがって］［A／V　のと（は）ちがって］

content: 弟は大柄な兄とちがって、やせていて背も低い。

content.content: The younger brother is not like his big, strapping older brother; he’s skinny and short.

content: 人間は機械とちがって、想像力をもっている。

content.content: Humans, unlike machines, have the power of imagination.

content: 外国での生活は、自国で生活するのとちがって、思わぬ苦労をすることがある。

content.content: Life in a foreign country is not like life in your native land; sometimes there are unexpected troubles to deal with.

content: 実際に自分の目で見るのは、人から聞くのとちがって強烈な印象を受けるものだ。

content.content: Actually seeing something with your own eyes is different from hearing about it from another person; it leaves you with a stronger impression.
Means “different from....” Used when comparing one thing to another with different characteristics. Sometimes used in the form ...とちがい.
（例）評判で聞いていたのとはちがい、実際に見たら退屈な映画だった。
It was nothing like we had heard; when we actually watched it, it was quite a boring film.
【とちゅう】
1. とちゅうで

content: いつもの時間に家を出たが、途中で忘れ物に気づいて引き返した。

content.content: I left home at the usual time, but along the way I realized I had forgotten something and came back.

content: やりかけた仕事は途中で投げ出してはいけないよ。

content.content: You shouldn’t give up on a job partway through once you've started it.

content: 泥棒の足跡は途中で途切れている。

content.content: The robber’s footprints disappeared along the way.

content: この道は途中で行き止まりになっている。

content.content: This road eventually turns into a dead end.
Means “in the middle of” a place or time. Used to express that before something is finished, it is interrupted or something else occurs. With this usage, the particle で cannot be dropped.
2. ...とちゅう（で／に）［Nのとちゅう（で／に）］［V-るとちゅう（で／に）］

content: 通勤の途中、突然雨が降りだした。

content.content: On my way to work, it suddenly started to rain.

content: 買い物の途中で、急に気分が悪くなって倒れてしまった。

content.content: In the middle of shopping, I suddenly felt sick and collapsed.

content: 買い物に行く途中で、ばったり昔の友人に会った。

content.content: On my way to the store, I happened to run into an old friend.

content: 家に帰る途中、居酒屋に立ち寄った。

content.content: I stopped at a bar on my way home.

content: 駅に行く途中に郵便局があるので、そこでこの手紙を出してくれませんか。

content.content: There’s a post office on the way to the station, so could you take this letter there and mail it for me?

Follows action nouns or verbs. Indicates that another event occurs at some point before the action in question is completed, or that something exists at a place along the path one is taking. Generally, the particle で is used to indicate the point at which an event occurs, and the particle に is used to indicate a location, but these are sometimes dropped, as shown in

content: and

content.content: 3. ...とちゅう（は）

content: 会社に来る途中、ずっとこの小説を読んでいた。

content.content: On my way to the office, I was reading this novel the whole time.

content: 歩いている途中、彼に言われたことばが頭を離れなかった。

content.content: While I was walking, I couldn’t get his words to me out of my head.

content: 旅の途中は眠ってばかりいた。

content.content: All she did was sleep through the entire trip.

content: 通勤の途中は語学の勉強をすることにしている。

content.content: I make it a rule to do language study during my commute.
...とちゅう（は）is placed after a noun or verb that expresses movement from one location to another. Used to show that the second action or state continues throughout the period of motion.
【とて】
1. Nとて（も）

content: 私とて悔しい気持ちは皆と同じである。

content.content: I also have the same feelings of regret as all of you.

content: この事故に関しては、部下の彼とても責任はまぬかれない。

content.content: As a subordinate, he cannot shirk responsibility for this accident either.

content: 最近は父親とて、育児に無関心でいるわけにはいかない。

content.content: These days even fathers can’t be indifferent to child rearing.

content: これとても、特に例外的な現象というわけではない。

content.content: Even this can’t be regarded as a particularly exceptional phenomenon.

Attaches mainly to nouns that denote people or roles and means “even...” or “it’s the same with regard to that as it is to other things.” Used to make a strong assertion that, when X is compared with other things that are similar, of course the same thing can be said about X too. A somewhat old-fashioned expression. In spoken language, expressions like 私だって (I, too/even I) are used more often.
2. ...からとて［N／Na　だからとて］［A／V　からとて］

content: 病気だからとて、無断で休むのはけしからん。

content.content: Being sick is no reason to take a day off without any notice; it’s inexcusable.

content: 仕事に情熱がもてないからとて、家族を養う身としては、簡単に辞めるわけにはいかないのである。

content.content: As someone with a family to support, he can’t just quit his job because he has no passion for his work.
Means “with only that as a reason.” Used to say that it isn’t possible to make the conclusion that is stated next. A literary form of the expression からといって.
3. ...とて［Nだとて］［V-たとて］

content: いくら愚か者だとて、そのくらいのことはわきまえていてもよさそうなものだが。

content.content: No matter how foolish he is, I would have thought that he’d know at least that much.

content: たとえ病気だとて試合は休むわけにはいくまい。

content.content: Even if I’m sick, I can’t miss the match.

content: いくら頼んだとて、聞き入れてはもらえまい。

content.content: No matter how much you beg, they won’t do what you ask.

content: どんなに後悔したとて、失われたものは再び元に戻ることはないのである。

content.content: No matter how sorry you are, something that’s been lost can never be restored.

A literary form of expressions like ...でも (even if/however...), ...としても／としたって (even if), and ...たところで (no matter). Not used very often in spoken language. Often accompanied by expressions such as いくら (how much), どんなに (no matter how), たとえ (even if/supposing that).
【とても】
1. とても

content: あの映画はとても面白かった。

content.content: That movie was really interesting!

content: 今度の新入社員はとてもよく働く。

content.content: The new employee works very hard.
Expresses an extreme degree of something. Very, remarkably, extremely.
2. とても...ない

content: こんな難しい問題はとても私には解けません。

content.content: A problem this difficult is quite impossible for me to solve.

content: 一度にこんなにたくさんの単語はとても覚えられません。

content.content: There’s absolutely no way I can memorize so many words all at once.

content: あの美しさはとても言葉では表現できない。

content.content: That kind of beauty really cannot be expressed in words.

Expresses a subjective judgment by the speaker that something is futile or impossible, no matter what methods or means s/he might try to use. In written language, とても...ない can be replaced by とうてい...ない.
【とでもいう】

content: 学問の楽しみは、未知の世界を発見する喜びとでもいおうか。

content.content: The pleasure of study is the joy of discovering an unknown world, so to speak.

content: シルクの繊維としての素晴らしさは、気温や湿度の変化に対する絶妙なバランスにあるとでもいったらよいだろうか。

content.content: Is it not possible to say that the wonderful thing about silk fiber is the superb balance it maintains in the face of changes in temperature and humidity?

content: 冷房のきいた部屋から外に出た時の感じは、まるで蒸し風呂に入った感じとでもいえようか。
