content.content: The feeling when you go from an air-conditioned room to the outdoors is just like entering a steam bath, so to speak.

This expression is used to explain the characteristics or distinguishing features of one thing by comparing it to something else. Means “figuratively speaking, it might be possible to say that X is like....” Used in the forms ...とでもいおうか, ...とでもいえよう, ...とでもいってよいだろう, and so on. Has the tone of written language.
【とでもいうべき】［NとでもいうべきN］

content: そこは東洋のパリとでもいうべき優雅な雰囲気のある町である。

content.content: That city has such an atmosphere of elegance that it should be called the Paris of the East.

content: 第二のモハメッド･アリとでもいうべきボクサーが現れた。

content.content: A boxer has come along who should be called the next Muhammad Ali.

content: 彼は映画の神様とでもいうべき存在である。

content.content: Many consider him to be the god of cinema.
A roundabout metaphorical expression. A well-known name is cited, conveying the feeling that it is appropriate to make this comparison. Also used in the form ...ともいうべき.
【とともに】
1. Nとともに

content: 仲間とともに作業に励んでいる。

content.content: I’m working hard on this task with my colleagues.

content: 夫とともに幸せな人生を歩んできた。

content.content: I’ve lived a happy life with my husband.

content: 隣国とともに地域経済の発展に努めている。

content.content: Along with our neighboring countries, we are striving for regional economic development.
Placed after nouns denoting people or organizations to express doing something “together” or “jointly/cooperatively.” Tends to be used in written language.
2. ...とともに［Nとともに］［V-るとともに］

content: テレビの普及とともに、映画は衰退した。

content.content: With the spread of television, movies fell into a decline.

content: 国の経済力の発展とともに、国民の生活も豊かになった。

content.content: Along with the development of the country's economic strength, the lifestyle of the people became more affluent.

content: 地震の発生とともに津波が発生することがある。

content.content: Sometimes a tsunami occurs along with an earthquake.

content: 年をとるとともに記憶力が衰えてきた。

content.content: My memory has declined as I have grown older.

content: 《スピーチ》今後、教育内容の充実を図るとともに、地域社会に貢献する大学の建設に努力する所存でございます。

content.content: 《speech》In the future, I am committed to building a university that will contribute to the local community as I work to enrich the educational content.

Placed after a verb or noun that denotes an action or change. Expresses that another action or change will occur in response to the first, or that two things will happen at the same time. Used in written language. Means the same as ...につれて (as/with...), ...とどうじに (at the same time as...).
【となく】
1. なん+助数詞+となく

content: 原始林の中には、巨大な樹木が何本となく茂っている。

content.content: In the middle of the virgin forest grew a dense stand of huge trees.

content: 彼は世界選手権にはすでに何回となく参加した経験をもっている。

content.content: He has already participated many times in world championships.

content: 公園のベンチには若いカップルが幾組となく腰掛けて愛を語り合っている。

content.content: On the park benches were seated a lot of young couples, lost in romantic conversation.

となく is placed after the combination of a prefix that indicates an indefinite number, such as 何 (なん) or 幾 (いく), and a counter such as ...人 (...person/people) or ...回 (...time(s)). This pattern indicates that there is a rather large quantity of the thing in question. More common in written language. In spoken language, expressions like 何回も (many times) and 幾組みも (many pairs) are more commonly used.
2. ひるとなくよるとなく

content: 世界の至るところで、昼となく夜となく様々な事件が発生している。

content.content: All over the world, all sorts of incidents arise both day and night.

content: 母は昼となく夜となく病気の祖母の世話で忙しく暮らしている。

content.content: My mother has a busy life taking care of my sick grandmother day and night.
Means “day and night,” or in other words, “twenty-four hours a day.” More of a written expression.

【となったら】Follows a clause or noun and expresses either the meaning “in such a case/situation” or “should such a thing become an issue.” When the situation or issue “turns out to be the case,” the overriding meaning is that the outcome is a natural result. Stated also as となると and となれば.
1. ...となったら［N／Na　（だ）となったら］［A／V　となったら］

content: もし、一戸建の家を建てるとなったら、銀行から相当の借金をしなければならない。

content.content: If you’re going to build a single dwelling house, you’ll have to get a considerable loan from the bank.

content: 引き受ける人が誰もいないとなったら、私がやるしかない。

content.content: If there is no one else who will take on the task, then I’ll just have to do it.

content: 彼女がすでに他の人と結婚してしまったとなったら、もう諦めるしかない。

content.content: If she has already married someone else, there’s nothing to do but give up.

content: A:夫が海外勤務になったんですよ。

content.content: My husband has been assigned a position overseas.
B:そうですか。海外で生活するとなったら、お子さんの学校のことなど、いろいろ大変ですね。
Is that so? If you’re living overseas, then you’ll have all sorts of challenges, like schooling for your children and so on.

Follows a clause and means “in the case of that sort of thing/situation coming about.” Can be used either when making an assumption about a fact that has yet to be realized, or when an actual situation has been newly understood. The meaning will depend on the context. For example, in

content: , the meaning can be either “assuming such a case” or “the fact of the matter has become clear.” Hypothetical assumptions are sometimes accompanied by かりに or もし.
is a case of hearing a person’s statement and can be paraphrased with そうなったら.

content.content: 2. いざとなったら

content: いざとなったら私が責任をとります。

content.content: If the situation arises, I’ll take responsibility.

content: いざとなったら、今の仕事を辞めても自分のやりたい道に進むつもりだ。

content.content: If push comes to shove, I intend to quit my present job and proceed on the course I want to take.

Expresses what will happen in the case that some impediment arises in the implementation of some action. An expression of intent is often used in the latter clause. In that case, となったら can be restated as となれば but not となると.
3. N（のこと）となったら

content: 日本料理となったらここの板前の右に出る者はいないそうだ。

content.content: When it comes to Japanese cuisine, there’s no one better than the chef here.

content: 自分の専門のこととなったら、彼は何時間でも話し続ける。

content.content: When it comes to his field of expertise, he can continue talking for hours on end.
Used after a noun that is taken up as the point in question. Expresses the meaning “with regard to” or “when that is the topic.”
【となっては】
1. いまとなっては

content: 今となっては、名前も顔も思い出すことができない。

content.content: Now at this point, I can’t recall either his name or face.

content: 全てが終わってしまった今となっては、じたばたしてもしかたがない。

content.content: Now that everything is over and done with, there’s no sense in fretting.

content: 当時はずいぶん辛い思いをしたものだが、今となっては、それも懐かしく思い出される。

content.content: At the time it was quite painful for me, but now I can think back on it with some nostalgia.

Expresses the meaning “having proceeded through a variety of events to reach this point.” Often followed by expressions stating “that was to be expected/as one would think.” Though it is often followed by negative evaluations of “cannot be done” or “there’s no point anymore,” as in

content: and
, it can also be a neutral evaluation, as in

content.content: 2. ...となっては［N／Na　（だ）となっては］［A／V　となっては］

content: 子供達だけで海外へ行くとなっては、親としてはちょっと心配になる。

content.content: With the children going overseas all by themselves, as a parent I am a little concerned.

content: 病状がここまで進んだとなっては、もうどうすることもできない。

content.content: As the illness has progressed to this point, there’s nothing that can be done.

content: 誰も引き受けてくれないとなっては、自分でやるしかない。

content.content: As there’s no one willing to take on the task, it’s up to me to do it.

Following a clause, this expresses the meaning “in the case that such a situation arises.” Often used for conditions that have already been realized, and the latter half expresses the evaluation or judgment of the speaker regarding what s/he expects as the natural outcome of situation. In many cases, negative evaluations such as 心配だ (worrisome) or 仕方がない (can’t be helped) are expressed.
【となる】［N／Na　となる］

content: 初めて戦後生まれの人物がアメリカの大統領となった。

content.content: For the first time, a person born after the war became president of the United States.

content: 今回の協定は大筋では米国側の主張を受け入れた内容となっている。

content.content: The contents of this agreement essentially accede to the position of the American side.
【なる】5
【となると】
1. となると

content: A:先生はご病気で昨日入院されました。

content.content: The professor was hospitalized yesterday because of illness.
B:となると、しばらく授業は休講ということになりますね。
If that’s so, then our lessons will probably be canceled for a while, right?

content: 長期予報によれば今年の梅雨は空梅雨になるとのことだ。となると、野菜の値段の高騰や、水不足の心配が予想される。

content.content: The long range forecast says that this year’s rainy season will be a dry one.  In that case, steep increases in the price of vegetables and concerns about water shortages can be expected.

Used in the sentence-initial position and expresses the meaning “based on that reality.” The first clause is either something that the speaker has newly learned about or something mentioned by someone else. The second clause contains the opinion that the speaker arrives at based on that information.
2. ...となると［N／Na　（だ）となると］［A／V　となると］

content: 医学部に進むとなると相当にお金がかかるだろう。

content.content: Proceeding on to medical school will likely cost a considerable amount of money.

content: 彼は、決断するまでは時間がかかるが、やるとなると実行するのは早い。

content.content: For him, it takes a long time to make a decision, but when he does take action, he moves on it quickly.

content: いざ、海外に行くとなると、事前の準備が大変だ。

content.content: If sometime you do go overseas, the preparations beforehand are considerable.

content: 仮に、このまま水不足が続くとなると営業時間を短縮しなければならなくなる。

content.content: Should the current water shortage continue like this, we may have to shorten our hours of operation.

content: この時間になっても帰っていないとなると、何かの事件に巻き込まれている可能性がある。

content.content: When she still hasn’t come home at this late hour, there’s a possibility that she’s been involved in some incident.

content: 現場に残された指紋が彼のものと一致するとなると、彼が犯人である公算が高い。

content.content: If his fingerprints match those left at the scene, there’s a high probability that he’s the criminal.

content: これほど大企業の経営状態が悪いとなると、不況はかなり深刻ということになる。

content.content: When the operations of a large corporation are as bad as this, the recession can be said to be rather serious.

content: 社長がそう言っているとなると、変更はほとんど不可能でしょう。

content.content: If the company president said something like that, any revision is almost impossible.

Follows a clause to express the meanings “in such a case” or “when such a case arises.” Depending on the context, it can be used to talk about an actual situation or an assumed one. For a hypothetical situation, expressions such as もし／かりに are used.
3. いざとなると

content: 危険は承知の手術だが、いざとなると不安になるものだ。

content.content: There’s expected risk in any surgery, but when it actually happens, we get uneasy.

content: スピーチは原稿を何度も読んで練習してきたが、いざとなるとあがってしまい、うまくしゃべれなかった。

content.content: I reviewed the manuscript over and over and practiced the speech, but when it came time to do it, I got a bad case of nerves and couldn’t deliver it well.

An idiomatic expression with the meaning “in the case of actually implementing (something).” The second clause often continues with an expression to show that the outcome was a natural result of the situation.
4. N（のこと）となると

content: 芸能人のスキャンダルとなると、マスコミは夢中になって追跡する。

content.content: When it comes to a celebrity scandal, the mass media pursue it relentlessly.

content: 試験問題のこととなると学生は急に真剣になる。

content.content: When the lesson turns to a possible exam question, the students suddenly get serious.

Follows a noun to express the meaning “at the time that the matter becomes an issue/problem.” The latter half of the sentence continues with an expression to show that an attitude contrary to the usual one is taken when the issue arises.
5. ...かとなると

content: どうすればこの問題を解決できるかとなると、簡単には答えられない。

content.content: If I am asked what to do to solve this problem, I can’t give a simple answer.

content: 実際にだれがその危険な仕事にあたるかとなると、積極的な人は一人もいない。

content.content: If you want to know who actually is to undertake such a risky task, there’s not a single person who has come forward.
Follows a query to express the meaning “when this becomes a problem.” The latter half follows with a negative expression to show that the solution or implementation is impossible or challenging.
6. Nともなると→
【ともなると】
【となれば】
1. ...となれば［N／Na　（だ）となれば］［A／V　となれば］

content: 外国へ住むとなればやはりその国の言葉ぐらいは勉強しておいたほうがよい。

content.content: If one’s to live overseas, then it follows that it’s a good idea to study the language of that country.

content: 結婚してから両親と同居するとなれば、今の家では狭すぎるだろう。

content.content: If you’re going to live with your parents after getting married, then your present house is too small.

content: 今から急いで行ってももう間に合わないとなれば、焦ってもしかたがない。

content.content: If it’s already too late even if they rush there now, there’s no point in getting flustered.

content: 彼が言ったことが全て嘘だとなれば、我々はまんまとだまされていたことになる。

content.content: If everything he has said turns out to be a lie, it means that we have been completely deceived.

Follows a clause to convey meanings such as “in such a case that...” or “in the case of such a situation...” or “based on such a fact....” Continues with expressions that indicate either an expected judgment or the proper action to take regarding the situation. Depending on the context, the form can be used for hypothetical conditions or already-realized situations.
2. いざとなれば

content: 手持ちの現金では足りないかもしれないが、いざとなればクレジットカードを使うことができる。

content.content: You may not have enough cash on hand, but if the need arises, you can use a credit card.

content: 一人で留学するのは不安だが、いざとなれば、友達が助けてくれるから大丈夫だ。

content.content: I am worried about studying overseas by myself, but if something happens, I’ll be all right because my friends will help me.

An idiomatic expression that means “in the event that such a situation were actually to arise.” Often used to express that, even if a difficult or unmanageable situation arises, things will be all right. Also takes the forms いざとなると and いざとなったら.
3. N（のこと）となれば

content: いつもは生気のない彼の目もサッカーのこととなれば急に生き生きと輝いてくる。

content.content: His usually lifeless eyes suddenly start to sparkle animatedly when the talk turns to soccer.

content: 脳死問題となれば学者も安易な発言はできない。

content.content: When it comes to the issue of brain death, even scholars are not able to make simplistic statements.

Follows a noun and means “when that becomes the topic of conversation.” Used to introduce something as a topic. Usually followed by expressions indicating that when that becomes the topic of conversation, a person’s (or people’s) attitude or way of handling things differs from the usual.
4. ...かとなれば

content: どうすれば解決できるかとなれば、答えは簡単には出てこないものだ。

content.content: When it comes to solving problems, the answer is not always easily found.

content: 首相が発言どおり実行するかとなれば、必ずしもそうとばかりは言えない。

content.content: If you ask whether the prime minister will do exactly as he says, the answer is not necessarily yes.

となれば is placed after an interrogative expression and means “when the matter of...becomes the topic/problem at hand.” Followed by a negative expression stating, for example, that solving or implementing something is difficult or impossible. Often used to contrast one situation with another and also bring up an important problem. For example,

content: means something like, “He does state his views, but when it comes to whether or not he acts on them when the time comes....”

content.content: 5. Nともなれば→
【ともなれば】
【とにかく】Used to put aside discussion of a certain matter or action for the time being in order to focus on another matter or action. The form ともかく is also used.
1. とにかく

content: あの人はとにかく大変な秀才です。

content.content: At any rate, she’s exceptionally bright.

content: 田中さんの新しい家、とにかくすごく大きい家なんですよ。

content.content: You know Tanaka-san’s new house—whatever else you might say about it, it's incredibly huge!

content: 戦闘の後の町は、とにかくひどい状況です。

content.content: Now that the battle is over, the town is all in all in a terrible state.

Means “although many things could probably be said, this one comes first.” Followed by an expression that indicates an extraordinary degree of something, such as 非常に／大変／すごく...だ (it is extremely/very/incredibly...). Used to emphasize this meaning. Tends to be used in spoken language.
2. とにかくV

content: うまくいくか分かりませんが、とにかくやってみます。

content.content: I don’t know whether or not I'll succeed, but at any rate, I’ll try.

content: とにかく言われたことだけはやっておきました。

content.content: Anyway, I’ve done at least what I was told to do.

content: お忙しいとは存じますがとにかくおいでくださいますようお願いいたします。

content.content: We know how very busy you are, but we would be grateful if you would please just honor us with your presence.

content: まだ全員そろっていませんが、時間ですのでとにかく始めることにしましょう。

content.content: Not everyone is here yet, but since it’s time, let’s just get started.

Followed by a verb expressing an intentional action and means “giving priority to this action for now, regardless of other considerations.” Used by the speaker to assert his/her own intention, a fact, etc. or to urge the addressee to implement an action.
3. Nはとにかく（として）

content: 見かけはとにかく味はよい。

content.content: Never mind what it looks like, it tastes good.

content: 成績はとにかくとして、明るくて思いやりのあるいい子供です。

content.content: Putting aside the matter of his grades, he is a cheerful and considerate child.

content: 私はとにかく、あなたはこの仕事に満足しているんですか。

content.content: Never mind me—are you satisfied with this job?

content: あいさつはとにかくまずは中にお入りください。

content.content: The greetings can wait until later—please come inside.

content: A:先日はお世話様でした。

content.content: Thank you so much for the other day.
B:いいえ。それはとにかく、お願いした仕事の方は引き受けてくださいますか。
Not at all. Be that as it may, are you willing to take on the work I asked you about?
Placed after a noun and used to contrast that thing with something else that is more important or should be done first. In conversation, as in

content: , it can also be used at the beginning of a sentence in forms like それはとにかく（として） to refer to something the other person has said and introduce a different topic.

content.content: 【との】
1. ...とのことだ

content: みなさんによろしくとのことでした。

content.content: He said to give his regards to everyone.

content: 無事大学に合格なされたとのこと、まことにおめでとうございます。

content.content: I heard that you passed your university entrance exams—sincere congratulations on your success!

content: 社長はすこし遅れるので、会議を始めておいてくれとのことでした。

content.content: The company president will be a little late, so she said we should start the meeting without her.

content: そちらは、寒い日が続いているとのことですが、皆様お変わりありませんか。

content.content: I hear that you have been having a cold spell—how is everyone doing?

content: あの二人も、長かった婚約に終止符を打ち、6月に挙式するとのこと。

content.content: I hear that those two are bringing their long engagement to a close and getting married in June.
Means “I hear/they say that....” Used by the speaker to say something that s/he has heard or learned from another person. As in

content: and
, sometimes だ is dropped and the clause or sentence ends with こと. May take the ta-form, as in とのことだった／でした (I heard/they said that...). Cannot be used in the negative form.
恩師から結婚式には出席できないとの返事を受け取った。

content.content: I received a reply from my mentor that she won’t be able to attend the wedding.

content: 学生から留学するため一年休学させてほしいとの希望が出されている。

content.content: The student has submitted a request for a year's leave of absence in order to study abroad.

content: この件については、次回の審議に回してはどうかとの議長の提案に全員賛成した。

content.content: Everyone agreed to the proposal made by the chair for deliberation on this matter to be tabled until the next meeting.

content: 来月から一年間、札幌の支社に出向せよとの辞令を受けた。

content.content: I’ve received an official notice that I’ll be reassigned to our branch office in Sapporo for a year, starting next month.

content: 文部大臣は、学校教育を改善するためには、高等教育機関の入学試験制度の抜本的改革が必要だとの見解を述べた。

content.content: The Minister of Education has stated his view that, in order to improve formal education, a drastic overhaul of the entrance examination system for institutions of higher education is necessary.

In the pattern ...とのN, a clause that describes the content of a certain linguistic expression or thought is used to modify a noun. Used in formal style. The N slot is filled by a noun that denotes either a speech activity, such as 手紙 (letter), 返事 (reply), 依頼 (request), 提案 (proposal), 警告 (warning), or 命令 (order), or a thought activity, such as 意見 (opinion), 見解 (viewpoint), 考え (idea), or 希望 (hope). Used when talking about something that another person has said or thought. When the speaker’s own thoughts are being expressed, usually the form という is used instead of との, as below.
（例）私は夫婦別姓を合法化すべきだという意見をもっている。
I am of the opinion that the use of different surnames by married couples should be legalized.
【とは】
1. ...とは〈definition〉

content: パソコンとは、個人で使える小型のコンピューターのことだ。

content.content: A pasokon (personal computer) is a small-sized computer for individual use.

content: 蓮華とは蓮の花のことだ。

content.content: A renge (Chinese milk vetch) is a lotus flower.

content: 21世紀の日本で求められる福祉の形態とはどのようなものだろうか。

content.content: What will be the form of social welfare system required by Japanese society in the 21st century?

content: 「普遍的」とは、どんな場合にも広く一般的に当てはまるという意味だ。

content.content: “Universal” means that something applies broadly and generally, in all cases.

content: 私にとって家族とは一体何なのだろうか。

content.content: What exactly does “family” mean to me?

とは is used after a noun to describe the meaning, characteristics, or content of the noun. In the patternとは...ものだ, it is used to express the essential features of the noun, and in the patterns ...とは...のことだ／意味だ and ...とは...ということだ／意味だ, it is used to define the meaning or content of a word or phrase. Used mainly in written language. In spoken Japanese, Nというのは is more common.
2. ...とは〈quotation〉

content: A:森山さん、会社退職するそうですよ。

content.content: I’ve heard that Moriyama-san’s leaving the company, you know.
B:えっ、退職するとは、結婚するということですか。
Oh, does that mean she’s getting married?

content: 《書き置きを見て》「お世話になりました」とは、もう帰ってこないということだろうか。

content.content: 《looking at a note》“Thank you for all you’ve done for me...” I wonder if this means she won’t be coming back.

content: A:このお話、なかったことにしてください。

content.content: Let’s just say this didn’t happen.
B:「なかったことにする」とはどう言うことですか？
What do you mean, “This didn’t happen”?

content: 親に向かって「バカヤロー」とは何事だ。

content.content: What makes you think you can call your parents “stupid idiots”?

Used in response to a verbal utterance, written information, or some other linguistic input, to indicate the speaker’s evaluation of the utterance/information or to confirm its real intention. Often accompanied by feelings such as surprise, amazement, or anger. というのは is often used instead of とは. However, とは cannot be replaced by というのは in fixed expressions such as とは何事だ (see

content: above).

content.content: 3. ...とは〈surprise〉

content: 一人で5種目も優勝とはまったく驚いた。

content.content: It is absolutely amazing that you won five different events on your own.

content: 全員そろって授業をサボるとはあきれた学生達だ。

content.content: What an appalling group of students, all of them cutting class together!

content: 人を2時間も待たせておいて「すみません」の一言もないとはまったく非常識な奴だ。

content.content: Someone who keeps you waiting for two hours and then doesn’t offer a word of apology is an absolute boor.

content: タクシーの中に忘れた現金がもどってくるとは思いもよらないことでした。

content.content: I never expected that the cash I had left in the taxi would be returned to me!

とは expresses the speaker’s surprise and amazement when s/he encounters an unexpected situation. In casual speech, なんて is often used instead of とは. As shown below, the clause following とは (or なんて) may be omitted.
（例）あの人がこんな嘘をつくとは。
(What a surprise that) s/he would tell such a lie!
（例）ベテラン登山家の彼が遭難するとは。
To think that an experienced climber like him should go missing in the mountains!
（例）こともあろうに、結婚式の日がこんなひどい土砂降りになろうとは。
(I never imagined there would be) a downpour like this on my wedding day, of all days!
【とはいいながら】
1. ...とはいいながら

content: 分かっているとはいいながら、やはり別れはつらいものだ。

content.content: Although I say I understand, a separation is always painful.

content: もう過去のこととはいいながら、なかなかあきらめられない。

content.content: Even though I know that it’s over, I still can’t give up so easily.
とはいいながら is used after a clause and means “I admit this fact, but...” or “while such-and-such is true, nevertheless....”
2. とはいいながら

content: 過ぎたことは悔やんでも仕方がない。とはいいながら、思い出すとつい涙が出てしまう。

content.content: There’s no point in regretting the past. Still, I can’t help shedding a tear every time I remember it.

content: 結婚相手を決める場合は何よりもお互いの相性が大事である。とはいいながら、いざとなると相手の家柄や経済力、容姿などのことが問題になる。

content.content: When you choose a marriage partner, mutual compatibility is the most important factor. Having said that, when it comes down to it, things like his or her family’s social standing, as well as earning power and appearance, become big issues.
とはいいながら is used at the beginning of a sentence. It refers to the preceding sentence and means “I admit this fact, but....”
【とはいうものの】

content: フランス語は大学時代に習ったとはいうものの、もうすっかり忘れてしまった。

content.content: It’s true I learned French when I was at university, but I’ve completely forgotten it.

content: 大学時代は英文学専攻だった。とはいうものの、英語はほとんどしゃべれない。

content.content: I was an English literature major in college. However, I can hardly speak English at all.
【ものの】2、
【ものの】3

【とはいえ】とはいえ follows a clause or a sentence and means “that is true, but....” Used when the actual result contradicts what is expected from the previous clause/sentence. A formal expression used mainly in written Japanese. とはいいながら, とはいうものの and と(は)いっても may be used instead of とはいえ.
1. ...とはいえ［N／Na　（だ）とはいえ］［A／V　とはいえ］

content: 男女平等の世の中とはいえ、職場での地位や仕事の内容などの点でまだ差別が残っている。

content.content: Despite the so-called equality of the sexes in today’s world, there is still discrimination in the workplace with respect to things like status and job content.

content: 国際化が進んだとはいえ、やはり日本社会には外国人を特別視するという態度が残っている。

content.content: Although internationalization has progressed, when all is said and done, Japanese society retains an attitude of looking at foreigners in a special way.

Used after a clause, とはいえ means “that is true, but....” Used when the actual result contradicts what is expected from the preceding clause. A formal, mainly written expression. とはいいながら, とはいうものの, and と(は)いっても may be used instead.
2. とはいえ

content: 病状は危険な状態を脱して、回復に向かっている。とはいえ、まだ完全に安心するわけにはいかない。

content.content: She is out of critical condition and on her way to recovery. Having said that, we cannot let our guard down completely yet.

content: 生徒の非行には家庭環境が強く影響する。とはいえ、学校教育のあり方に責任の一端もある。

content.content: The home environment strongly affect pupils’ delinquency. That said, the current system of school education is also partly responsible for it.

Used at the beginning of a sentence, とはいえ refers to the previous sentence and means “that is true, but....” Used when the actual result contradicts what is expected from the previous sentence. A written expression. とはいいながら, とはいうものの, and と(は)いっても may be used instead.
【とはいっても】

content: 初めて小説を書いた。とはいっても、ごく短いものだけれど。

content.content: I wrote a novel for the first time. But I should tell you it’s really short.

content: 病気でねこんだとはいっても、風邪をひいただけですよ。

content.content: Although I said I was sick in bed, I just had a cold, you know.
Meaning and usage are the same asといっても.
【といっても】1、
【といっても】2
【とはうってかわって】［Nとはうってかわって］

content: 父は若い時とはうってかわって、とても優しくなった。

content.content: My father has become very kind and gentle, a complete change from how he was when he was young.

content: 村は昔の姿とはうってかわり、近代的なビルが立ち並んでいる。

content.content: The village looks completely different from how it used to look, with the streets now lined with modern buildings.

content: 社長はこれまでとはうってかわったように、強硬な態度に出てきた。

content.content: The company president has taken a firm stance, a complete turnabout from his previous attitude.

Used in the forms とはうってかわって, とはうってかわり, and とはうってかわったように, this expression conveys the meaning of transformation to a new state that is completely different from the previous one. As shown in the following example, it can also be used adverbially, without Nとは.
（例）教室はうってかわったように静まり返っていた。
The classroom was completely quiet, as if nothing had happened.
【とはかぎらない】［N／Na／A／V　とはかぎらない］

content: 日本語を教えているのは日本人とはかぎらない。

content.content: Not all Japanese language teachers are Japanese.

content: 有名な作家の小説ならどれでもおもしろいとはかぎらない。

content.content: It doesn’t always follow that every novel written by a famous author is  interesting.

content: スーパーマンだからって、何でもできるとはかぎらないよ。

content.content: Just because he’s Superman doesn’t mean he can do anything.

content: ここのお料理もいつもおいしいとはかぎらないんですよ。

content.content: There’s no guarantee that the food here is always good, either.

content: 完治したからといって再発しないとはかぎらないのだから、気を付けるにこしたことはない。

content.content: Even though you’ve made a complete recovery, there’s no guarantee that your illness won’t flare up again, so you can’t be too careful.
Means “it is not always the case that....” Implies that there is an exception to a situation or state of affairs generally considered to be true.
【とはちがって】→
【とちがって】
【とばかり】
1. ...とばかり

content: 今がチャンスとばかり、チャンピオンは猛烈な攻撃を開始した。

content.content: The champion launched a fierce attack, as if to say that this was a chance not to be missed.

content: 横綱はいつでもかかってこいとばかりに身構えた。

content.content: The yokozuna (a sumoo wrestler of the highest rank) stood poised to attack, as if to say, “Come and get me!”

content: もう二度と来るなとばかりに私の目の前でピシャッと戸を閉めた。

content.content: She slammed the door in my very face, as much as to say, “Never come back!”

content: 「どうだ、すごいだろう」とばかりに、新しい車を見せびらかしている。

content.content: He’s showing off his brand-new car to us, as much as to say, “Look! Isn’t this great?”

Used after a clause, とばかりexpresses the meaning “as if to say....” It is used to convey the speaker’s sense that another person actually wants to say something like what is expressed in the とばかり clause. とばかりis followed by words/phrases that indicate a strong degree of vigor or force. It is a formal, mainly written expression and is often used in idiomatic expressions, such as この時とばかりに攻め込む／攻めかかる “now is the time to strike/attack” and えいっとばかりに切りつける／切りかかる “slash at/strike at (someone) with all one’s might” (lit. “with a shout of exertion; with a battle cry”).
2. ...といわんばかり

content: お前は黙っていろと言わんばかりに兄は私をにらみつけた。

content.content: My older brother glared at me, as if to say, “Keep your mouth shut!”

content: 警察は「お前がやったんだろう」と言わんばかりの態度で男を尋問した。

content.content: The attitude of the police officer as he interrogated the man was, “Come on, you know you did it!”
Used after a clause, といわんばかり means “look/act as if s/he is about to say....” Used in essentially the same way as 1 above.
【とみえて】［N／Na　（だ）とみえて］［A／V　とみえて］
1. ...とみえて

content: 最近忙しいとみえて、いつ電話しても留守だ。

content.content: He must be very busy recently, because he is not in whenever I call.

content: 夜中に雨が降ったとみえて、水たまりができている。

content.content: It seems to have rained during the night, because there are puddles outside.

content: 何かいいことがあったとみえて、朝からずっとにこにこしている。

content.content: Something nice must have happened to him, because he’s been grinning since morning.

content: 隣の家は留守とみえて、ドアの前に数日分の新聞がたまっている。

content.content: It looks like our next-door neighbor is away, because there are newspapers from the past several days piled up in front of the door.
States a conjecture based on a current state of affairs. The first clause contains the speaker’s conjecture, and the second presents the reason or basis for this conjecture. For instance, in

content: above, the speaker states the conjecture 夜中に雨が降ったようだ (it looks like it rained during the night) in the first clause, and this conjecture is based on the state of affairs 水たまりができている (there are puddles) given in the second clause. The second clause describes a fact that the speaker has actually observed.

content.content: 2. ...とみえる

content: 今日の田中君はやけに気前がいい。何かいいことがあったとみえる。

content.content: Today Tanaka-kun is being unusually generous with his money. Something good must have happened.

content: 合格発表を見に行った妹は、帰ってくるなり部屋に閉じ込もってしまった。どうも不合格だったとみえる。

content.content: As soon as my sister, who went to find out her results for the entrance exam, got back, she locked herself in her room. It looks like she failed.

content: 学生にパソコンの使い方を説明したが、ほかの人に聞いているところを見ると、一度聞いただけではよくわからなかったとみえる。

content.content: Although I explained to the student how to use a computer, it seems that hearing it just once was not enough for him to understand, because I saw him asking someone else.

content: 花子は先生にほめられた絵を会う人ごとに見せている。ほめられたことがよほどうれしかったとみえる。

content.content: Hanako shows the drawing her teacher praised her for to everyone she sees. She must have been so happy that she was praised.
とみえる is used to state, as if the speaker were talking to him/herself, a conjecture based on what s/he has observed. Young Japanese speakers do not use this expression very often.
【とも】とも attaches to inflected words and has the same meaning as ても. However, since it is a literary usage, it sounds old-fashioned in comparison to ても.
1. ...とも［A-くとも］［A-かろうと（も）］

content: 田中さんの送別会には、少なくとも 30 人は集まるだろう。

content.content: At least thirty people will come to the farewell party for Tanaka-san.

content: どんなに苦しくとも、最後まで諦めないで頑張るつもりだ。

content.content: I’ll make every effort to see this through to the end without giving up, no matter how hard it may be.

content: どんなに辛かろうと、苦しかろうと必ずやり遂げてみせます。

content.content: No matter how painful and difficult it may be, I will accomplish this without fail.
とも attaches to the -く and/or -かろう forms of i-adjectives. In spoken language, -くても is commonly used instead of -くとも. In

content: , とも is followed by an estimate of quantity and means “even if I were to estimate in such-and-such a way...” (in this case, “even if I were to make a low estimate...”). Similar usage is found in expressions such as 多くとも10人 (no more than ten people), 長くとも30分 (no longer than thirty minutes), 遅くとも5時までに (by no later than five o’clock), and so on. The も in とも is often omitted when ‑かろうと is repeated, as in

content.content: 2. V-ようと（も）

content: たとえ両親に反対されようと（も）、彼女と結婚するつもりだ。

content.content: Even if our parents are opposed to it, I’m going to marry her.

content: たとえ失敗しようと（も）、やると決めたことは実行する。

content.content: Even if it ends in failure, I will do what I’ve decided to do.

content: どんな苦労があろうと（も）、二人で助け合って幸せな人生を歩んでゆきたい。

content.content: No matter what difficulties we face, we want to help each other live a happy life together.

content: 雨が降ろうと風が吹こうと、練習は決して休まない。

content.content: Whether the rain falls or the wind blows (= no matter what happens), I never miss practice.
【よう2】6d
3. ...であろうと（も）［N／Na　であろうと（も）］

content: 病人であろうと年寄りであろうと何の配慮もなしに敵は攻撃を仕掛けて来る。

content.content: No matter whether the target is the sick or the old, the enemy launches its attacks with no mercy.

content: たとえ健康であろうと中年を過ぎたら、定期検診を受けたほうがいい。

content.content: Even if you’re in good health, after you’ve reached middle age you should have regular check-ups.

content: 高名な僧侶であろうとも、迷いを断てないこともある。

content.content: Even high-ranking priests are sometimes unable to dismiss doubts.
A somewhat old-fashioned expression that means the same as N/Naであっても.
【であろうと】1
【ともあろうものが】［Nともあろうものが］

content: 大蔵官僚ともあろうものが、賄賂を受け取るとは驚いた。

content.content: It is shocking to know that even an official of the Ministry of Finance took a bribe.

content: 警察官ともあろうものが、強盗をはたらくとは何ということだろう。

content.content: It is astounding that a police officer, of all people, committed burglary.

content: 母親ともあろうものが、生まれた自分の子供をゴミ箱に捨てるとは、まったく恐ろしい話だ。

content.content: It is absolutely terrifying that a mother would dump her own new-born in a garbage can.

Means “such a (competent, honorable, etc.) person (does something unexpectedly).” Placed after a noun indicating social status, role or occupation, it is used to describe an action that, according to conventional wisdom, a person in such a role should not have performed. ともあろうものが is followed by an expression that conveys surprise, anger, or suspicion. もの can be replaced by other words that refer to people, such as 人 (person) or 人物 (person/figure).
（例）国会議員ともあろう人物がこのような巨額の脱税を平気で行うのだから、議員のモラルも低下したものである。
The professional morals of politicians have really deteriorated when a member of the Diet, of all people, thinks nothing of evading such an enormous amount of tax.
【ともいうべき】→
【とでもいうべき】
【ともかぎらない】［N／Na　ともかぎらない］［Aともかぎらない］［V-ないともかぎらない］

content: A:司会者を探してるんだけど、山下さん結婚式の司会なんか、引き受けてくれないよね？

content.content: I’m looking for an emcee, but Yamashita-san probably isn’t up for emceeing a wedding reception, is she?
B:一度聞いてみたら？　引き受けてくれないとも限らないよ。
Why don’t you ask her? She might agree to do it.

content: 山田は来ないと言っていたが、気まぐれな彼のことだから、ふらりと現れないともかぎらない。

content.content: Yamada said he wouldn’t come, but he’s such an impulsive person, there’s always a chance that he might just show up.

content: 病院は慎重に選んだ方がいい。へたな医者にかかっては、命を落とさないともかぎらない。

content.content: You should choose a hospital carefully. There’s no guarantee that you won’t lose your life if you get treated by a bad doctor.

content: 教師の言うことが正しいとは限らないし、本に書いてあることが、正しいとも限らない。

content.content: What a teacher says is not necessarily always correct, nor is what is written in books.

Means “X is not definite, and there is a possibility of the opposite.” It is often used in the pattern V-ないともかぎらない, in which case it means there is still a slight possibility that something might happen under circumstances in which it is regarded as less than probable. A similar expression is とはかぎらない.
【ともかく】
1. Nはともかく（として）

content: 見かけはともかく味はよい。

content.content: This may not look good, but it tastes delicious.

content: 学歴はともかく人柄にやや難点がある。

content.content: His educational background is fine, but there is a little problem with his personality.

content: 奥さんはともかくとしてご主人はとてもいい人だ。

content.content: I can’t say much about the wife, but the husband is a very nice person.

content: 細かい点はともかく全体的に見れば、うまく行ったと言えるのではなかろうか。

content.content: Putting aside the details, can we not conclude that on the whole it went very well?

content: 勝敗はともかくとして、一生懸命頑張ろう。

content.content: Whether we win or lose, let’s make every effort to do our best.
Nはともかく means “putting aside N (for the moment).” It is used to say that the matter described after ともかく is more important and should be given priority. Nはとにかく(として) can also be used.
2. ともかくV

content: 雨で中止になるかもしれないが、ともかく行ってみよう。

content.content: It may get rained out, but let’s go anyway.

content: ともかく、言われたことだけはやっておきました。

content.content: Anyway, I did what I was told.

content: ともかく使ってみないことにはいい製品かどうかは分からない。

content.content: I can’t tell whether this is a good product or not until I actually use it.

content: ともかくお医者さんに見てもらった方がよい。

content.content: You should go and see a doctor anyway.
Used with verbs that express an intentional act, ともかく means to go ahead and take action, rather than spending time debating the pros and cons of that action. ともかく can be replaced by とにかく.
【ともすると】

content: ベテラン教師でもともするといい子ばかりに目がいってしまう。

content.content: Even experienced teachers tend to pay attention only to the good pupils.

content: この学生は時間にルーズで、ともすると授業に1時間も平気で遅れて来る。

content.content: This student is careless about time, so she is apt to turn up for class as much as an hour late without thinking anything of it.

content: 夏はともすると睡眠不足になりがちである。

content.content: We tend to suffer from a lack of sleep in the summer.

content: 核兵器はともすると人類の破滅を引き起こしかねない危険性をはらんでいる。

content.content: Nuclear weapons are likely to harbor the danger of bringing about the destruction of mankind.

Expresses that a certain event is likely to happen as a result of some kind of triggering condition. Used most often with respect to the occurrence of undesirable situations and often appears with expressions such as ...がちだ (tend to...) and ...かねない (could...). ともすれば can be used instead of ともすると.
【ともなう】→
【にともなって】
【ともなく】
1. 疑問詞（+助詞）+ともなく

content: どこからともなく、沈丁花のいい香りが漂ってくる。

content.content: The pleasant fragrance of daphne wafted in from somewhere.

content: 明くる朝、旅人はどこへともなく立ち去って行った。

content.content: The next morning, the traveler left to go nowhere in particular.

content: 誰からともなく拍手が起こり、やがて会場は拍手喝采の渦に包まれた。

content.content: Someone started clapping, and soon the hall was filled with gales of thunderous applause.

content: 生徒達は夜遅くまで騒いでいたが、いつともなくそれぞれの部屋に戻っていった。

content.content: The students were making noise until late at night, but at some point they all went back to their rooms.

content: 二人はどちらからともなく走り寄り固く抱きあった。

content.content: The two of them—I don’t know who went first—ran up to each other and locked each other in a tight embrace.

When used with a question word such as どこ (where), いつ (when), だれ (who) or どちら (which), ともなく means “but it is not possible to specify the exact place, time, person, or thing.” When a particle is used, it is placed immediately after the question word.
2. V-るともなく

content: どこを眺めるともなく、ぼんやり遠くを見つめている。

content.content: He is gazing absently into the distance, at nothing in particular.

content: 老人は誰に言うともなく「もう秋か」とつぶやいた。

content.content: “It’s already fall,” the old man murmured to no one in particular.

content: 何を考えるともなく、一日中物思いにふけっていた。

content.content: I was lost in thought all day about nothing in particular.

When used with a verb expressing an intentional human act, such as 見る (look at), 話す (speak), 言う (say), or 考える (think), ともなく indicates that the action is being carried out without any clear intention or aim. It is often preceded by a question word such as 何 (what) or どこ (where).
【ともなって】→
【にともない】、
【にともなって】
【ともなると】［N／V　ともなると］

content: いつもは早起きの息子だが、日曜日ともなると昼頃まで寝ている。

content.content: If it’s a Sunday, my son, who usually gets up early, sleeps till around noon.

content: 主婦ともなると独身時代のような自由な時間はなくなる。

content.content: Once you become a homemaker, you’ll have no time for yourself like you did when you were single.

content: 子供を留学させるともなると、相当の出費を覚悟しなければならない。

content.content: When you consider letting your child study abroad, you should be prepared for some heavy expenditures.
【ともなれば】
【ともなれば】［Nともなれば］［Vともなれば］

content: 9月ともなれば、真夏の暑さはなくなり過ごしやすくなる。

content.content: Once September comes, the summer heat is over and the weather is more comfortable.

content: 子供も 10 歳ともなればもう少し物分かりがよくてもいいはずだ。

content.content: Once a child is ten, she should be a little more perceptive.

content: 結婚式ともなればジーパンではまずいだろう。

content.content: When it comes to a wedding ceremony, it’s not appropriate to wear jeans.

content: 主婦ともなれば朝寝坊してはいられない。

content.content: If you’re a homemaker, you can’t sleep in in the morning.

content: 学長に就任するともなれば、今までのようにのんびり研究に打ち込んではいられなくなる。

content.content: Once you assume the presidency of the university, you won’t be able to focus freely and easily on your research, as you have until now.

Used with a noun or a verb referring to time, age, a role or an event, ともなれば means “if/when such a thing or event is realized.” It is followed by an expression indicating the speaker’s judgment that if such a change in situation takes place, a certain consequence will naturally follow. ともなると can also be used instead of ともなれば.
【ともに】→
【とともに】
【ともよい】→
【なくともよい】
【とやら】
1. Nとやら

content: 例の啓子さんとやらとはうまくいっていますか。

content.content: Are you getting along well with that Keiko-san, or whatever her name is?

content: 娘が「ムサカ」とやらいうギリシャ料理を作ってくれました。

content.content: My daughter cooked me a Greek dish called something like moussaka.
Means “called something like...” and is used after a name that the speaker does not remember precisely. In

content: , とやら is attached directly to a particle, but this can be considered to be an abbreviation of the phrase とやらいう人 (a person called something like...), with いう人 (a person called) omitted.
私の答案を見て、先生がびっくりした顔をしていたとやら。

content.content: I heard that when the teacher saw my answers she looked astonished, or something.

content: 結局あの二人は結婚して、田舎で仲良く暮らしているとやら。

content.content: I heard that those two ended up getting married and are living happily together in the countryside, or something.

とやら follows information that the speaker has heard from someone else and means, “it may not be completely accurate, but I heard something like this.” Although the meaning of とやら is similar to that of とか聞いている, とのことだ and そうだ, とやら conveys a strong sense that the information quoted is not very precise because the speaker’s recollection is vague. とやら is rarely used in everyday spoken language.
【とりわけ】

content: 兄弟は3人とも頭がよいが、次男はとりわけ優秀だ。

content.content: The three brothers are all bright, but the second one is especially brilliant.

content: 暖冬の影響か、今年の春はとりわけ桜の開花が早い。

content.content: I don’t know whether it’s an effect of the mild winter, but the cherry blossoms have started to bloom particularly early this spring.

content: 今回の不況はこれまでの中でもとりわけ深刻だ。

content.content: This recession is particularly severe compared with those in the past.

content: どの学科もあまり成績がよくないが、とりわけ国語がひどい。

content.content: I don’t get very good marks in any subject, and Japanese is particularly bad.

とりわけ is used to place focus on the one thing in particular that stands out in comparison with others, in situations where none of the things is ordinary. It can be used for either positive or negative evaluation. とりわけ can be replaced by expressions such as 特に (especially/particularly), ことに (particularly/above all), and ことのほか (exceedingly/exceptionally).
【とわず】→
【をとわず】
【とんだ】［とんだN］

content: あなたが邪魔したなどと、とんだ思い違いをしていました。

content.content: Saying that you had disturbed me was a complete misunderstanding on my part.

content: A:通勤の途中で、事故に遭ってしまったんですよ。

content.content: I had an accident on my way to work, you know.
B:それはとんだ災難でしたね。
What a terrible thing to have happened!

content: 親にかくれてたばこを吸うとは、とんだ不良娘だ。

content.content: What a terrible daughter, to smoke behind her parents’ backs.

content: もし1分でも気が付くのが遅れていたら、とんだ大事故になっていたかもしれない。

content.content: If I had noticed even just one minute later, it might have turned into a disastrous accident.

content: とんだ野郎に見込まれてしまったものだ。

content.content: Some guy like that is counting on me.

content: 委員会の議長に選ばれるとは、とんだことになってしまった。

content.content: Being elected to chair the committee was totally unexpected.

とんだ precedes a noun referring to a person or situation and means that the person or situation is contrary to one’s expectations. It usually conveys a negative evaluation, with the meaning of “awful,” “stunning; shocking,” “troublesome,” or “terrible,” and is used to describe an unexpected result or a person who doesn’t conform to commonly-accepted standards of behavior. However, in cases such as

content: above, とんだ can also convey a positive evaluation that implies warmth and familiarity, with the meaning of “(a) unique and uncommon (individual).”

content.content: 【とんでもない】
1. とんでもないN

content: 子供は時々とんでもない質問をして親を困らせることがある。

content.content: Children sometimes ask outlandish questions that perplex their parents.

content: 明け方の4時などという、とんでもない時間に電話がかかってきてびっくりした。

content.content: I was surprised to receive a phone call at the ungodly hour of four o’clock in the morning.

content: 海中に都市を作るとは、とんでもない計画だ。

content.content: Building a city under the sea is an outrageous plan.
Means “totally unforeseen,” “unexpected,” or “beyond the boundaries of conventional thinking.” Its evaluative meaning is not as strongly negative as that of とんだ.
2. とんでもない

content: A:ずいぶん景気がよさそうですね。

content.content: Your business seems to be going really well, doesn’t it?
B:とんでもない。借金だらけで首が回りませんよ。
Are you kidding? I’m up to my neck in debt.

content: 先生: そのかばん、持ってあげましょう。

content.content: Teacher: Shall I carry that bag?
学生: 先生に荷物を持っていただくなんてとんでもないです。
Student: I wouldn’t dream of letting my teacher carry my bag for me!

content: A:この度は本当にお世話になりました。

content.content: Thank you very much for your help.
B:とんでもございません。こちらこそいろいろご迷惑をおかけいたしまして...。
Not at all. I should thank you for all your trouble.
Means “no, that isn’t so” and is used in conversation to contradict strongly an interlocutor’s utterance. When used to decline a generous offer or refuse words of gratitude from another person, as in

content: and
above, it becomes an expression of polite reserve. とんでもありません／ございません are polite forms of とんでもない.

content.content: 【どうしても】
1. どうしてもR-たい

content: 次の休みにはどうしても北海道へ行きたい。

content.content: I am set on going to Hokkaido for my next vacation.

content: 競争率の高いのは知っているけれど、どうしてもあの大学へ入りたいのです。

content.content: I realize that there is stiff competition, but I am determined to get into that university.

content: どうしても今年中に運転免許をとらなければならないし、とりたいと思う。

content.content: One way or another, I have to get my driver’s license this year, and I want to.

content: 両親が反対したが、わたしはどうしても演劇の道に進みたいと思っていた。

content.content: My parents were against it, but I knew I wanted to go into the world of acting at any cost.

Combines with an expression of want or desire to express the notion that, although the desired result is considered difficult to achieve, the speaker has the will to overcome any obstacle in order to accomplish it. Indicates strong desire.
2. どうしても...ない

content: 仕事がひどく忙しいので、今月末まではどうしてもあなたのところへは行けません。

content.content: I am swamped with work, so there is no way I can come to see you before the end of the month.

content: 何度もやってみたが、この問題だけはどうしても解けなかった。

content.content: I tried over and over again, but I could not for the life of me solve this problem.

content: 努力はしているが、あの課長はどうしてもすきになれない。

content.content: I'm trying my best, but I don’t think I'll ever like that section chief.

content: あしたまでに車の修理をしてほしいと頼んだが、人手が足りないのでどうしても無理だと言われた。

content.content: I asked them to fix my car by tomorrow, but they told me it’s impossible because they’re short-staffed.

content: もしどうしても都合が悪いなら、別の人を推薦してくださっても結構です。

content.content: If for some reason it doesn’t work for you, you can go ahead and recommend someone else.

This pattern combines the negative form of the potential V-れる with expressions of denial such as 無理だ (it’s impossible), だめだ (it’s no use), or 都合が悪い (it is not convenient). Indicates that something cannot be achieved in spite of one’s best efforts.
【どうじに】
1. ...とどうじに［Nとどうじに］［V-る／V-た　（の）とどうじに］

content: スタートの合図と同時に選手達はいっせいに走り出した。

content.content: When the starting signal was given, the athletes all took off running at once.

content: 私が乗り込むと同時に電車のドアは閉まった。

content.content: The train door closed just as I got on.

content: 私が部屋に入ったのとほとんど同時に電話が鳴りだした。

content.content: The telephone began ringing almost the instant I entered the room.
Expresses the occurrence of one thing right after another. The particle の can be placed between a verb and the particle と, as in
2. ...とどうじに［N／Na　であるとどうじに］［A／V　とどうじに］

content: この手術はかなりの危険を伴うと同時に費用もかかる。

content.content: This operation entails considerable risk, as well as expense.

content: 社会に巣立つ若い男女の意欲に対して、期待するところが大きいと同時にいささかの懸念も残る。

content.content: The drive of young men and women taking their place as members of society engenders great expectations, but also a little concern.

content: 当選できて大変うれしく思いますと同時に、議員としての責任に身の引き締まる思いです。

content.content: While I am very happy to have been elected, at the same time I feel the tension of my responsibilities as a member of the assembly.
Expresses that two situations come about at the same time. Depending on the context, the relation expressed between the clauses may be one of cumulation, as in

content: , or contrast, as in
and
. Usually preceded by a plain form. However, in formal speeches and so on it may be preceded by a polite form, as in

content.content: 3. どうじに

content: 医者という職業は体力を必要とする。同時に、人間の繊細な心理に対する深い理解も要求される。

content.content: The medical profession requires physical strength. At the same time, it also demands a deep understanding of the subtle details of human psychology.

content: 過疎地の開発も大切である。が、同時に自然の保護には十分な注意が必要である。

content.content: The development of underpopulated areas is important. Still, at the same time, it is necessary to pay sufficient attention to protection of the environment.

content: 医学の進歩は人類に大きな恩恵をもたらした。しかし、同時に人間の生命に対してどこまで手を加えられるのかという倫理上の問題を新たに生じさせている。

content.content: Progress in medical science has bestowed great benefits on humankind. However, at the same time, it has also created new ethical problems regarding the extent to which persons should be able to modify human life.

Used between two sentences to express that two situations have arisen concurrently. The meaning of the second clause usually contrasts that of the first, and 同時に is often preceded by が or しかし, as shown in

content: and
. Often used in written language.

content.content: 【どうせ】
1. どうせ

content: どうせ私は馬鹿ですよ。

content.content: After all, I'm a fool.

content: 三日坊主の彼のことだから、どうせ長続きはしないだろう。

content.content: He can never stick to anything, so I don't expect this to last anyway.

Expresses an attitude of resignation or carelessness on the part of the speaker, in the sense that regardless of what s/he does, the conclusion or outcome is foregone and cannot be changed by the will or effort of an individual. Often followed by the description of an undesirable situation.
2. どうせ...（の）なら

content: どうせやるならもっと大きいことをやれ。

content.content: If you’re going to do it, then do something bigger.

content: どうせ参加しないのなら、早めに知らせておいたほうがいい。

content.content: If you’re not going to attend anyway, you ought to tell them early.

content: どうせ2か月余りの命なら、本人のやりたいことをやらせたい。

content.content: If she only has about two months left to live, I want to let her do anything she wants.

content: 急いでもどうせ間に合わないのだったら、ゆっくり行こう。

content.content: If we can’t get there on time even if we hurry, let’s take our time.

Means “if such-and-such an outcome will follow in any case” and is used to state an attitude or action that should be taken under such circumstances. The phrase ...のだったら may also be used. Followed by an expression that indicates the speaker’s effort to influence the addressee through his/her will, hope, obligation, command, or invitation.
3. どうせV-るいじょう（は）どうせV-るからには

content: やる以上は必ず成功して戻ってこい。

content.content: If you’re going to do it, then make sure you succeed before you return.

content: どうせ試合に出るからには、必ず優勝してみせる。

content.content: Since I’m going to compete in the match, I’ll show you a victory.

content: どうせ留学するからには、博士号まで取って帰ってきたい。

content.content: As long as I’m going to study abroad, I'd like to go all the way and bring home a doctorate.
Means “such-and-such an action has been predetermined, so....” Followed by an expression of the speaker's will, hope, obligation, command, or invitation with respect to the addressee.
4. どうせ...のだから

content: どうせ間に合わないのだから、いまさらあわてても仕方がない。

content.content: Since we aren’t going to make it in time anyway, there’s no point in scrambling now.

content: どうせ合格するはずがないのだから、気楽にいこう。

content.content: Since there isn’t any chance that I’ll pass the exam anyway, I’m just going to take it easy.

content: どうせやらなければならないのだから、早めにやってしまいましょう。

content.content: Since we have to do it anyway, let’s get it out of the way early.

Used to express the speaker’s intention or judgment regarding a situation with a foregone conclusion or outcome. Often followed by an expression that indicates the speaker’s attitude of resignation or carelessness regarding the situation.
5. どうせ（のこと）だから

content: どうせのことだから、飛び切り高級なホテルに泊まろう。

content.content: Since we have to stay somewhere, let’s stay at a really posh hotel.

content: どうせのことだから、駅までお送りします。

content.content: Since I’m going that way anyway, I’ll drive you to the station.

content: 当分バスも来ないみたいだし、どうせだからお茶でも飲まない？

content.content: It looks like there won’t be a bus for awhile, so as long as we’re here, would you like to get something to drink?

An idiomatic expression that means “in any case, doing...is a foregone conclusion, so....” Often followed by expressions of intention or invitation, such as 思い切って...しよう (I’m going to/let’s take the plunge and do such-and-such) or ついでに...しよう (I’m going to/let’s do such-and-such along with something else). In spoken language, the form どうせだから is often used.
【どうぜん】
1. Nどうぜん

content: 実の娘同然に大切に育ててくれた。

content.content: She lovingly raised me as her own daughter.

content: このみじめなくらしは奴隷同然だ。

content.content: This miserable life is tantamount to a slave's.

content: ボロ同然に捨てられて、彼は会社に復讐を誓った。

content.content: He was cast off like a beggar, and vowed to take revenge on the company.
Means “the same as, identical to....” Although it is close in meaning to ...のようだ (like...), 同然 is more emotional and often conveys a tone of derision or dissatisfaction.
2. ...もどうぜん［Nもどうぜん］［V-たもどうぜん］

content: この子は本当は姪ですが、小さいころから一緒に暮らしているので娘も同然です。

content.content: This child is really my niece, but she's lived with us since she was small, so she's like a daughter to us.

content: あの人はアルバイト社員だが、仕事の内容からみると正社員も同然だ。

content.content: That person is a part-time employee, but looking at the work she does, she's virtually the same as a full-time employee.

content: 別れた恋人はわたしにとっては死んだも同然の人だ。

content.content: To me, my ex-boyfriend is someone who is as good as dead.

content: 10000 票の差が開いたから、これでもう勝ったも同然だ。

content.content: A margin of 10,000 votes has opened up, which means the victory is already as good as ours.

Means that a certain situation, while not actually true, is very close to being true. Means “(almost) the same as...,” but in many cases 同然 also conveys an emotional evaluation and implies a pre-conceived opinion.
【どうにか】
1. どうにか

content: おかげさまでどうにかやっておりますのでご安心ください。

content.content: I’m happy to say that, thanks to all of you, we are managing somehow, so please put your mind at ease.

content: 急いで行ったらどうにか間に合った。

content.content: We hurried to get there, and somehow made it on time.

content: どうにか希望の大学に合格できましたので、ご安心ください。

content.content: I managed to pass the entrance examination for the college of my choice, so there is no need to worry any more.

Expresses that, as a result of hardships or effort, a desired situation has been more or less realized, though not sufficiently. For further emphasis, the form どうにかこうにか is sometimes used. See やっと (Usage 2) regarding the difference between どうにか and なんとか／やっと.
2. どうにかする

content: 早くどうにかしないと手遅れになってしまうよ。

content.content: If you don’t do something soon, it will be too late.

content: そちらの手違いで予約もれになってしまったのだから、どうにかしてもらいたい。

content.content: It’s your mistake that our reservation wasn’t recorded, so you’ve got to do something about it.

content: この水不足をどうにかしないと大変だ。

content.content: Something has got to be done about this water shortage, or we'll really be in trouble.
Means “take some kind of measure” in order to solve a problem that has arisen. It is also possible to say 何とかする.
3. どうにかなる

content: そんなに心配しなくてもどうにかなるよ。

content.content: Don’t be so worried; it’ll all be OK, you’ll see.

content: A:レポート遅れそうなんだよ。

content.content: It looks like my report is going to be late.
B:大丈夫、先生に頼めばどうにかなるよ。
No worries; if you ask the teacher, something can be worked out.

content: この猛暑、どうにかならないかな。

content.content: Isn’t there anything that can be done about this terrible heat wave?
Means that a problem will solve itself, or that there is some way to work out a solution. It is also possible to say 何とかなる.
【どうにも】
1. どうにも...ない

content: こうむし暑くてはどうにもやりきれない。

content.content: I just can’t take this high humidity.

content: 彼の怠惰な性格はどうにも直しようがない。

content.content: There’s nothing we can do to change his lazy streak.

どうにも is followed by negative expressions such as できない or V-ようがない and means that, no matter what measures are taken, something is impossible. Pronounced with the accent on どうにも. For further emphasis, the form どうにもこうにも is sometimes used.
2. どうにも　ならない／できない

content: 過ぎたことはいまさらくやんでもどうにもならない。

content.content: There’s no point in moping about something that’s over and done with.

content: ここまで病状が悪化してしまっては、もうどうにもできない。

content.content: If the symptoms have worsened to this point, there's really nothing more that can be done.
Expresses that no matter what is done, a situation cannot be changed. Used when a bad situation cannot be improved. The accent is usually どうにも.
【どうも】
1. どうも〈uncertain〉

content: 母のことがどうも気になってならない。

content.content: Somehow I can’t help thinking about my mother.

content: 最近、彼はどうも様子がおかしい。

content.content: There’s been something strange about him recently.

content: あの人の考えていることはどうもよく分からない。

content.content: I just don’t understand what makes that person tick.

content: 努力はしているのだが、どうもうまくいかない。

content.content: We’re doing our best, but it’s just not going well.

content: 今日は朝からどうも気分がふさぐ。

content.content: For some reason I’ve been feeling down since this morning.

content: A:奥さんの具合はいかがですか。

content.content: How is your wife doing?
B:それがどうもね...。
Well, you know, it’s hard to say....

Expresses the speaker’s uncertainty or doubt regarding a current situation or his/her own senses or emotions. Means something like, “I don’t really know why that is so/why I feel this way.” The predicate is the negative form of a verb/adjective or an expression that conveys a negative evaluation, such as 変だ (it’s strange), おかしい (odd), or 気分がふさぐ (feel down).

content: is a circumlocution that does not verbalize the intended あまりよくない (not very good). どうも can often be substituted with なんだか or 何となく.

content.content: 2. どうも　...そうだ／...ようだ／...らしい

content: この空模様ではどうも雨になりそうだ。

content.content: This sky looks like we’re going to get some rain.

content: 彼の言ったことはどうも全部うそのようだ。

content.content: It seems as if everything he said was a lie.

content: おじの病気はどうもガンらしい。

content.content: Our uncle's illness looks like it might be cancer.
When accompanied by expressions such as そうだ (look/seem), ようだ (looks like), or らしい (appear/seem), どうも expresses a conjecture on the part of the speaker based on some piece of evidence.
3. どうも〈dismay〉

content: ちっとも勉強しないで遊んでばかりで、どうも困った息子です。

content.content: My son gives me no end of headaches, since he never studies and only wants to have a good time.

content: A:先輩、一曲歌ってくださいよ。

content.content: (to a senior student/colleague) Senpai, sing a song for us, please.
B:これは、どうもまいったな。
Oh boy, now what do I do?
Used along with expressions like 困った (troublesome/distressing) and まいった (Oh, no!), this emphasizes a feeling of dismay or slight surprise.
4. どうも〈salutation〉

content: お手紙どうもありがとうございます。

content.content: Thank you very much for your letter.

content: お待たせしてどうもすいません。

content.content: I am so sorry to have kept you waiting.

content: 先日はどうも。

content.content: Thank you for the other day.
Used in greetings and salutations to emphasize a feeling of appreciation or apology. As in

content: , the latter part of the sentence is sometimes omitted. Actually often used in expressions like どうも、どうも, which is merely a conventionalized greeting that conveys no particular feeling.

content.content: 【どうもない】

content: 彼は酒を1升ぐらい飲んでもどうもない。

content.content: It’s no problem for him to down a whole bottle (1 shoo=1.8 liters) of sake.

content: A:この牛乳、ちょっと変な味しない？

content.content: Doesn’t this milk taste a little strange?
B:（飲んでみて）どうもないよ。
(after drinking some) It seems all right to me.
This is a spoken language expression that means 平気だ (it’s fine), 大丈夫だ (it’s all right), 問題がない (no problem).
【どうやら】
1. どうやら...そうだ

content: この分でいくと、どうやら桜の開花は早まりそうだ。

content.content: If it (the weather) continues like this, the cherry blossoms may well bloom early.

content: むこうから歩いて来るのはどうやら田中さんのようだ。

content.content: That looks like Tanaka-san walking toward us from over there.

content: 部屋から次々と人が出て来るところをみると、どうやら会議は終わったらしい。

content.content: Seeing people come out of the room one after the other, it looks like the meeting is over.

Followed by expressions of conjecture such as そうだ, ようだ, or らしい. Indicates uncertainty on the part of the speaker, in the sense that although s/he isn’t absolutely sure, s/he thinks that such an inference is possible.
2. どうやら（こうやら）

content: 急いだのでどうやら間に合った。

content.content: We hurried, so somehow or other, we made it on time.

content: どうやら論文も完成に近づいた。

content.content: I’ve somehow managed to come close to finishing my thesis.

content: どうやらこうやら卒業することができました。

content.content: By hook or by crook, I was able to graduate.
Expresses that, although the outcome is in some way insufficient, a situation or stage of completion that was set as a goal has finally been achieved, as a result of one’s efforts.
【どうり】
1. ...どうりがない

content: こんなに難しい本が子供に読める道理がない。

content.content: It’s absurd to think that a child should be able to read such a difficult book.

content: 上司なら部下にどんな命令をしてもよいなどという道理はない。

content.content: It’s not acceptable to think that if you’re the boss you can order your subordinates around any way you like.

content: そんな道理はない。

content.content: That makes no sense.
Means that no matter how one thinks about something, there is no reason or basis to accept it as correct. The particle が sometimes changes to は, as in

content: and

content.content: 2. どうりで

content: A:彼女 13 歳までアメリカで育ったんだって。

content.content: I heard that she grew up in the U.S. until she was thirteen.
B:へえ。どうりで英語の発音がいいわけだね。
Really? It’s no wonder her English pronunciation is so good.

content: A:彼女の両親は学者だよ。

content.content: Both of her parents are scholars.
B:道理で彼女も頭がいいはずだ。
So that explains why she's so smart too!
Used when someone learns the most reasonable explanation for a state of affairs and accepts it, with the sense of “of course, that makes sense/that must be why.”
【どおし】［R-どおし］

content: 1週間働き通しだ。

content.content: I’ve worked through the whole week.

content: 一日中立ち通しで働いている。

content.content: She works standing up all day long.

content: 一日中歩き通しで、足が痛くなった。

content.content: I walked the whole day, so my feet hurt.

content: 朝から晩まで座り通しの仕事は、かえって疲れるものだ。

content.content: It’s actually more tiring to work sitting down from morning to night.
Expresses the continuation of an action or state over a period of time. どおし is usually attached to the stem of a verb, but the expression 夜通し (all night long) is an example of use with a noun.
【どき】［Nどき］［R-どき］

content: 昼飯どきは、この辺りはサラリーマンで一杯になる。

content.content: This area is filled with company employees at lunchtime.

content: 木の芽時は、どうも体調がよくない。

content.content: I just don’t feel very good when the trees start budding in early spring.

content: 梅雨時はじめじめして、カビが生えやすい。

content.content: The rainy season is damp and mold grows easily.

content: 株でもうけるには、買い時と売り時のタイミングに対するセンスが必要だ。

content.content: To make money in the stock market you need a good sense of timing for when to buy and when to sell.

content: 会社の引け時には、ビルのエレベーターは帰宅を急ぐ人で満員になる。

content.content: At quitting time, the building’s elevators are packed with workers rushing home.

content: お中元の季節と歳末は、デパートの書き入れ時だ。

content.content: Department stores make the most money during the summer and year-end gift-giving seasons.
Expresses when something usually occurs or is carried out, when something is at its peak, or the most appropriate time to do something.
【どこか】
1. どこか〈indefinite〉

content: このテレビ、どこかがこわれているんじゃないかな。

content.content: I wonder if this television has some part that’s not working.

content: 今頃はどこかをさまよっているかもしれない。

content.content: He might be wandering around somewhere right now.

content: どこかでお茶でも飲みませんか。

content.content: Would you like to go and have a cup of tea somewhere?

content: 春休みにはどこかへ出かける予定がありますか。

content.content: Do you have any plans to go somewhere during spring vacation?

content: どこかから赤ん坊の泣いている声が聞こえてくる。

content.content: From somewhere I could hear the sound of a baby crying.

content: 顏色が悪いが、どこか悪いところでもあるのではないか。

content.content: Your color isn’t good—are you sure there’s nothing wrong with you?

Expresses an unspecified location. Followed by particles such as が, を, から, で, に, and へ, but が is often dropped. In spoken language, it often takes the form どっか. In addition, when it is used to modify nouns (as below), it takes the pattern どこか + adnominal modifier clause + ところ.
（○）どこか静かなところで話しましょう。
Let’s talk somewhere quiet.
（×）静かなどこかで話しましょう。
Let’s talk in a quiet somewhere.
2. どこか〈uncertain〉

content: あの人はどこかかわいいところがある。

content.content: There’s something charming about that person.

content: 彼女にはどこか私の母に似たところがある。

content.content: There’s something about her that reminds me of my mother.

content: このあたりの風景にはどこか懐かしい記憶を呼び起こすものがある。

content.content: There’s something in the landscape around here that brings back fond memories.
Means that, although the speaker cannot quite put his/her finger on which part of something is X, s/he senses that there is a part that is X.
【どことなく】

content: 彼女はどことなく色気がある。

content.content: There’s something alluring about her.

content: あの先生はどことなく人をひきつける魅力をもっている。

content.content: There’s something about that teacher that draws people to him.
Expresses that, although it is impossible to specify exactly where it comes from, a certain impression or feeling is imparted. It is also possible to say どこかしら and どこか.
【どころ】
1. ...どころか［N／Na（な）　どころか］［A-いどころか］［V-るどころか］

content: 病気どころか、ぴんぴんしている。

content.content: We thought she was sick, but there she was in the pink of health!

content: A:あの人、まだ独身でしょう。

content.content: That person is still single, right?
B:独身どころか、子供が3人もいますよ。
Far from it! He has three children, you know!

content: 彼女は静かなどころか、すごいおしゃべりだ。

content.content: She’s hardly the quiet type—she talks nonstop!

content: A:そちらは涼しくなりましたか。

content.content: Has it cooled off where you are?
B:涼しいどころか、連日 30 度を越える暑さが続いていますよ。
Just the opposite! It isn't cool at all—the heat continues day after day, with temperatures over thirty degrees!

content: 風雨は弱まるどころか、ますます激しくなる一方だった。

content.content: The wind and rain did not abate but, on the contrary, continued to increase in intensity.

content: この夏休みはゆっくり休むどころか、仕事に追われどおしだった。

content.content: This summer vacation has been anything but relaxing—I’ve been swamped with work the whole time!
Attaches to nouns, adjectives, etc. When used with na-adjectives, as in

content: , the na is sometimes inserted, but it can also be omitted. The fact stated after どころか is the exact opposite of what was stated before it. Used to state a fact that completely overturns the anticipations or expectations of the speaker or listener.

content.content: In

content: , for example, Speaker B doesn’t just say “No, s/he isn’t” in response to Speaker A’s assumption that the person in question “is single”; instead, Speaker B tells Speaker A that the person actually “has three children,” with the effect of thoroughly refuting Speaker A’s original assumption.

content.content: 2. ...どころか...ない［...どころか...さえ（も）...ない］［...どころか...も...ない］［...どころか...だって...ない］

content: 最近の大学生の中には、英語どころか日本語の文章さえもうまく書けない者がいる。

content.content: These days there are some college students who can’t even write well in Japanese, let alone English!

content: 旅行先で熱を出してしまい、見物どころか、温泉にも入れなかった。

content.content: I came down with a fever on the trip, so I never even got to bathe in the hot spring, let alone go sightseeing!

content: 彼女の家まで行ったが、話をするどころか姿も見せてくれなかった。

content.content: I went all the way to her house, but she wouldn’t even come to the door, let alone speak to me.

content: A:今夜お暇ですか。

content.content: Do you have some free time this evening?
B:暇などころか、食事をする暇さえありませんよ。
Free time? I don’t even have time to eat supper!

content: お前のような奴には、1万円どころか1円だって貸してやる気はない。

content.content: I wouldn’t lend one yen to someone like you, let alone 10,000 yen!

The meaning and conjunctive use of this expression correspond to those of 1 (see above). どころか is followed by expressions of negation such as さえ(も)...ない, も...ない, and だって...ない to express not only that the average standard or expectation will not be met, but also that one far easier or far lower will not be met, either.

content: , for instance, means that although it is generally expected that Japanese university students should have the ability to use English as a foreign language, some students have such a severe lack of writing ability that they cannot even write properly in Japanese, which should be easier for them than English.

content.content: 3. ...どころではない［Nどころではない］［V-ているどころではない］

content: この1か月は来客が続き、勉強どころではなかった。

content.content: I’ve had a string of visitors this past month, so I haven’t done much studying.

content: こう天気が悪くては海水浴どころではない。

content.content: This kind of bad weather puts a stop to any swimming in the sea.

content: 仕事が残っていて、酒を飲んでいるどころではないんです。

content.content: I still have work to do, so this is hardly the time to go drinking.

content: A:今晩一杯いかがですか。

content.content: How about getting together for a drink tonight?
B:仕事がたまっていて、それどころではないんです。
I have a pile of work to do, so that’s out of the question.
Attaches to verbs and action nouns to convey the meaning that “this is not a situation or case in which such-and-such can be done.” As in

content: , sometimes a demonstrative like それ (that) is used to refer to the previous utterance. Example
could be paraphrased as 酒を飲んでいるどころではない, which means “This is not a time to go drinking.”

content.content: 4. NどころのはなしではないNどころのさわぎではない

content: 受験生の息子を二人もかかえ海外旅行どころの話ではありません。

content.content: With two sons studying for entrance exams, the last thing we should be talking about is an overseas trip.

content: こう忙しくてはのんびり釣りどころの話ではない。

content.content: As busy as I am right now, this is no time to talk about taking it easy and going fishing!

content: 原子力発電所の事故発生でバカンスどころのさわぎではなくなった。

content.content: The accident at the nuclear power plant put an end to any talk of a vacation.
Used with nouns or action nouns and has essentially the same meaning as Usage 3 above. Implies that “this is no time to be making irresponsible comments like that!”
【どちらかというと】

content: 私はどちらかというと、人前で発言するのが苦手である。

content.content: Given the choice, I’d rather not speak up in front of other people.

content: この店はどちらかというと若者向けで、年配の客はあまり見当たらない。

content.content: This store is more for young people, so you won't see many elderly shoppers.

content: あの教授はどちらかといえば学者というよりビジネスマンタイプである。

content.content: That professor is more the businessman type than a scholar.

content: 大阪も悪くないが、どちらかというと私は京都の方が好きだ。

content.content: Osaka isn’t bad, but on the whole I prefer Kyoto.

content: 最近の大学生は、どちらかといえば男子より女子のほうがよく勉強して成績もよい傾向がある。

content.content: The recent trend for college students is that, generally speaking, the women study harder and get better grades than the men.

Means “on the whole” or “in general.” Used when making an evaluation of the character or special features of people or things. Means that, by and large, a certain characteristic or tendency can be acknowledged. Essentially synonymous with どちらかといえば.
【どちらかといえば】→
【どちらかというと】
【ども1】［Nども］

content: 申し訳ありません。私どもの責任です。

content.content: I am very sorry. This is our fault.

content: 手前どもの店では、この品物は扱っておりません。

content.content: I’m afraid that we don’t carry this product.

content: 《けんかのことば》野郎ども、みんなそろってかかって来い。

content.content: 《fighting words》Hey, you bunch of jerks, bring it on!

content: 政界は偽善者どもの集まりだ。

content.content: Political circles are gatherings of hypocrites.

Indicates a plural number and attaches mainly to nouns that refer to people. Similar to たち. However, when it attaches to a first-person pronoun, it is more polite than 私たち because it conveys a humble attitude. Another difference is that 私たち may or may not include the listener, but 私ども always excludes the listener. As shown in

content: and
, when ども is used with a second- or third-person pronoun, it usually conveys a sense of contempt towards that person. Other examples include 女ども (the women), 者ども (all of you), and so on.

content.content: 【ども2】［V-ども］

content: 行けども行けども、原野は続く。

content.content: No matter how far I go, there is nothing but endless plains.

content: 声はすれども、姿は見えず。

content.content: I can hear a voice, but I can’t see anyone.

content: 振り向いて見れど、そこにはだれもいなかった。

content.content: Though I looked back, no one was there.
V-ども attaches to the stem of the ba-form of verbs and has the same meaning as V-ても and Vけれども. For example, the ども clause in

content: means 行っても行っても (no matter how far I go), and the one in
means 声はするけれども (I can hear a voice, but...).
and
are idiomatic expressions, and
is a literary expression. Except for these special usages, and also the form といえども (even though/just because), V-どもis not used very often.

content.content: 【どんな】［どんなN+助詞+も］

content: 母はどんなことでもやさしく聞いてくれる。

content.content: My mother kindly listens to whatever I have to say.

content: どんな状況においても対応できる準備ができている。

content.content: I am ready to cope with any situation.

content: どんな人間にも幸福に生きて行く権利がある。

content.content: Every human being has the right to lead a happy life.

content: 彼女はどんな人からも好かれる女性です。

content.content: She is a woman who is liked by everyone.

content: 教師はどんな学生に対してもわけへだてなく付き合う必要がある。

content.content: Teachers need to be able to deal impartially with any kind of student.

content: 彼はどんなことにも興味をもつ人間だ。

content.content: He is a person who is interested in anything and everything.

The pattern どんなN+助詞+も expresses that the situation or state of affairs described after this clause holds true in all cases, regardless of the particular characteristics of the thing or person referred to by N.
【どんなに】
1. どんなに...だろう（か）

content: 希望校に合格できたらどんなにいいだろうか。

content.content: How great it would be if I could pass the entrance exam for the school of my choice.

content: 息子の戦死を知ったら両親はどんなに悲しむことでしょう。

content.content: How sad his parents would be if they knew that their son had died in the war.

content: 父が生きていたらどんなに喜んでくれたことだろうか。

content.content: How pleased my father would have been for me if he were alive!

content: 子供が無事だと分かった時、私はどんなにうれしかっただろう。

content.content: How delighted I was when I found out that my child was safe.

content: 私はこの日がくることをどんなに望んだことだろう。

content.content: How eagerly I had waited for this day!
The pattern どんなに...だろう(か) combines with expressions of joy, sorrow, hope, and so on to create exclamatory statements indicating that the degree of emotion is far greater than what is usual. In

content: , this pattern is used to make a conjecture about something that hasn’t actually happened and conveys the meaning of “if X were so, then surely (I) would be/would have been extremely Y.” On the other hand, in
and
it expresses that someone actually was very happy or did eagerly look forward to something.

content.content: 2. どんなに...ても

content: どんなに金持ちでも愛情に恵まれなければ幸福とは言えない。

content.content: No matter how rich you are, you cannot claim to be happy without being loved.

content: たとえどんなに苦しくても最後まで頑張ります。

content.content: No matter how hard it will be, I’ll make every effort to see this through to the end.

content: どんなに働いても暮らしはちっとも楽にならない。

content.content: No matter how hard I work, it doesn’t get any easier to make ends meet.

Means that, regardless of the degree or level of the condition indicated by this clause, what is stated in the subsequent clause is always true (or, in the case of a negative form, not true). どんなに...ても can be immediately preceded by たとえ (if; even if) and replaced by いかに／いくら...ても (however/no matter how (much)).
【ないか】...ないか is used mainly by male speakers. However, ...ない？, which is an abbreviated form of polite expressions such as ...ませんか and か, is used by both male and female speakers.
1. V-ない（か）〈invitation〉

content: ちょっと、食べてみない？

content.content: Want to try some of this?

content: 今度、いっしょにスキーに行かないか。

content.content: Why don’t we go skiing sometime?

content: そろそろお茶にしませんか。

content.content: How about taking a break for tea pretty soon?

content: ちょっと寄っていきません？

content.content: Would you like to drop by there?

When combined with verbs expressing a volitional action, the pattern V-ない(か) is used to suggest that an interlocutor take some action or to invite him/her to do something together. The polite form of V-ない(か) is V-ませんか. V-ない(か) forms are usually pronounced with rising intonation, and か can be omitted.
2. V-てくれない（か）〈request〉

content: お塩、とってくれない？

content.content: Can you pass me the salt?

content: ちょっと手伝ってくれませんか。

content.content: Would you help me for a moment?

content: この本、2、3日貸してもらえない？

content.content: Can I borrow this book for a few days?

content: 5時までにおいでくださいませんか。

content.content: Would it be possible for you to be here by five o’clock?

content: 明日もう一度ご来店いただけないでしょうか。

content.content: Could you come to our shop again tomorrow?

This pattern, used in the forms V-てくれないか and V-てもらえないか, expresses a request from a speaker to an interlocutor. It is more polite when used in forms such as V-てくださいませんか／いただけませんか／いただけませんでしょうか or お／ご...くださいませんか, as in

content: , and お／ご...いただけないでしょうか, as in

content.content: Note that when this pattern is used with もらう and いただく, the potential forms もらえる and いただける should be negated to create the forms V-てもらえないか／いただけないか.
