content.content: You don’t have to give them such meticulous guidance, you know. They’ve already had sufficient training.

content: 何も試合直前になって延期したいと言ってくることはないだろうに。

content.content: I can’t see any reason for them to ask us to postpone the game just before it starts.

When なにも is followed by expressions such as (そこまで)...しなくてもいい and (そう)...する必要がない, it conveys the feeling “even though there is no particular need to do X.” This pattern is often used to chide or criticize the addressee when s/he is overdoing something or taking it too far.
c. なにも...わけではない

content: 私はなにも、あなたがやっていることを非難しているわけではないんです。ただちょっと注意したほうがいいと思って忠告しているんじゃないですか。

content.content: I don’t mean at all to criticize what you’re doing. I’m just giving you a piece of advice because I think you should be a little more careful.

content: 私は何もこの仕事がやりたくないわけではないのです。今は他の仕事があるので、少し時間がほしいとお願いしているだけなのです。

content.content: It’s not that I don’t want to do this job. I’m just asking you to give me a little more time, because right now I have other work to do.

content: あなたは私が邪魔をしていると思っているようですが、何も私は邪魔をしているわけではないのです。手順を踏んで慎重に話を進めようとしているだけなんです。

content.content: You seem to think that I’m trying to stand in your way, but that is not my intention at all. I just want to move the discussion forward carefully, one step at a time.

content: A:お母さんは私のことが嫌いなんでしょう。

content.content: I know you don’t like me, Mom.
B:何を言ってるの。私は何もあなたが嫌いで反対しているわけではないのよ。あなたのことを気にかけているから、反対しているんじゃないの。
What are you talking about? It’s not because I don’t like you that I’m against what you’re doing. Don’t you know I’m against it because I’m concerned about you?
The speaker uses なにも...わけではない to refute the addressee’s perception of the speaker’s behavior. In some cases, the speaker responds to something the addressee has just said, as in

content: . However, in most cases the speaker uses なにも...わけではない to refute an inference s/he has made about what the addressee is thinking.

content.content: 2. ...もなにもa. Nもなにも

content: 戦争で、家もなにも全てを失ってしまった。

content.content: I lost my house and everything else in the war.

content: 事故のショックで、自分の名前も何も、すっかり忘れてしまいました。

content.content: In the shock of the accident, I forgot everything, even my own name.

content: ペンも何も持っていなかったので、メモが取れませんでした。

content.content: Since I didn’t have a pen or anything else to write with, I couldn’t take notes.

content: 住所も何も書いていないのでどこに連絡すればいいのか分からない。

content.content: I have no idea who to contact, because there’s no address or any other written information.

...もなにも attaches to nouns and means “the thing that is specified, as well as all other similar things.” It is followed by expressions of loss or negation, such as 失う (lose), 忘れる (forget), or 分からない (not know).
b. ...もなにも［A／V　もなにも］

content: A:高田さん、あなた必ずやるって約束してくれたじゃないですか。

content.content: Takada-san, didn’t you promise that you would be sure to do this?
B:約束するもなにも、私はそんなことを言った覚えもないですよ。
Promise? I don’t remember saying anything of the kind.

content: A:怪我をしたときは痛かったでしょう。

content.content: I suppose it was painful when you got injured.
B:痛いもなにも、一瞬死ぬんじゃないかと思ったくらいだ。
It wasn’t just painful—it was so bad that for a moment I thought I was going to die.

content: A:彼に会ってずいぶん驚いていましたね。

content.content: You were really surprised to see him, weren’t you.
B:驚いたもなにも、彼のことは死んだと思っていたんですから。
I was more than surprised, because I thought he had died.

The speaker uses ...もなにも in response to something the addressee has just said, to deny it strongly or to emphasize that it involves a greater degree of something than the addressee thinks it does. Usually used in spoken Japanese.
3. なにもかも

content: 嫌なことは何もかも忘れて楽しみましょう。

content.content: Let’s forget about all the bad things and enjoy ourselves.

content: 何もかも、あなたの言うとおりにします。

content.content: I’ll do whatever you say, about everything.

content: あの人なら何もかも任せておいて大丈夫です。

content.content: It’s fine to leave everything to her.

content: 戦争で何もかもすっかり失ってしまった。

content.content: I lost absolutely everything in the war.

なにもかも is used to talk about things or events and means that something applies to everything, without limitation. Similar to 全部 (all/the whole) and すべて (everything)．For people, the expression だれもかれも (everyone) is used, and for places, it becomes どこもかも／どこもかしこも (everywhere).
【なにやら】
1. なにやら

content: なにやら変な臭いがする。

content.content: Something smells strange.

content: みんなで集まってなにやら相談をしているらしい。

content.content: It seems that they’re all getting together and discussing something.

content: なにやら雨が降りそうな天気ですね。

content.content: It looks kind of like it’s going to rain, doesn’t it.

content: この曲を聞いていたらなにやら悲しい気分になってしまった。

content.content: When I listened to this music, I somehow felt sad.

content: あの一家はなにやら伊豆の方へ引越しをするそうです。

content.content: I heard that, for some reason, that family is moving to the Izu area.
Indicates that something cannot be clearly defined. Means “I don’t know what it is, but...,” “I don’t know for sure, but...,” or “I don’t know the exact reason, but....”
2. ...やらなにやら［Nやらなにやら］［A-い／V-る　やらなにやら］

content: お菓子やらなにやらを持ち寄ってパーティーを開いた。

content.content: We all brought cookies and things and had a party.

content: 子供の病気やらなにやらで、落ち着いて考える暇もなかった。

content.content: What with my child’s illness and everything, I didn’t even have time to sit down and think.

content: 酔っぱらって、泣き叫ぶやら何やらの大騒ぎを演じたあげく、大いびきをかいて寝込んでしまった。

content.content: After getting drunk, screaming and whatnot, and overall making a big fuss, he fell fast asleep, snoring loudly.
Indicates that there are many other things similar to the thing that is specifically mentioned. Often implies that many different things or events are jumbled together in a disorderly fashion.
【なにより】
1. なにより

content: 料理を作るのがなにより得意です。

content.content: I’m better at cooking than I am at anything else.

content: 息子が無事でいるかどうかがなにより気がかりだ。

content.content: I’m most worried about whether or not my son is safe.

content: なにより嬉しかったのは、友達に会えたことです。

content.content: What pleased me most is that I could see my friend.

content: あなたから励ましの言葉をいただいたことになにより感激いたしました。

content.content: Your words of encouragement touched me more deeply than anything else.
なにより means “the best of all” or “more than anything else.”
2. なによりだ

content: お元気そうでなによりです。

content.content: It’s good to see you looking so well.

content: 就職先が決まったそうで何よりです。

content.content: I’m happy to hear that you’ve found a job.

content: 温泉に入るのがなによりの楽しみだ。

content.content: Nothing gives me more pleasure than taking a hot spring bath.
Means “something is the best of all comparable things.” When used to modify a noun, this expression takes the form なによりのN, as shown in

content: . The form なによりだ is usually used when the speaker is making a positive evaluation of a situation or event concerning the addressee. It is not used for events concerning the speaker him/herself.

content.content: （×）私が東大に入学できて何よりです。
I’m so glad I got into Tokyo University.
The form なによりの..., however, can be used not only with regard to the addressee or a third party but also with regard to the speaker him/herself.
【なまじ】

content: なまじ急いでタクシーに乗ったために、渋滞に巻き込まれてかえって遅刻してしまった。

content.content: Because I was in a rush and jumped into a taxi, I ended up getting caught in a traffic jam and arriving late.

content: 今の段階でなまじ私が発言すれば、かえって事態を混乱させることになりかねない。

content.content: If I were to make an incomplete comment at this stage, it would only confuse the situation.

content: なまじ自信があったのがわざわいして、重大なミスを犯してしまった。

content.content: Overconfidence in my own ability led me to make to a serious mistake.

content: なまじ彼女の状況が理解できるだけに、こんな仕事はとても頼みづらい。

content.content: It’s because I understand her current situation that it’s hard to ask her to take this job on.

content: なまじの知識は役に立たないどころか邪魔になることもある。

content.content: A little knowledge is not just useless; it can even be a hindrance.

content: 彼女の前ではなまじなことは言わない方がいい。彼女はこの問題を徹底的に調べているらしいから、我々もそのつもりで準備しなければ負けてしまう。

content.content: We shouldn’t say anything half-baked in front of her. It sounds like she’s been investigating this problem thoroughly, so if we don’t prepare with that in mind, we’ll be outplayed.

Expresses a situation in which something positive ends inconclusively or only halfway, without displaying its full value. Used to say that something with an intrinsically positive value actually results in a negative outcome.
When なまじ modifies a noun, it is used in the patterns なまじのN and なまじなN, as in

content: and
. In these cases, なまじ can be replaced by 中途半端な (halfway, unfinished). For instance,
means that knowledge, which is usually a good thing to have, instead becomes a hindrance because it is superficial.

content.content: 【なら1】 When なら is attached directly to a noun, it expresses the topic of a sentence. The form ならば may also be used.
1. Nなら

content: A:めがねはどこかな。

content.content: I wonder where my glasses are.
B:めがねならタンスの上に置いてありましたよ。
Your glasses? They were on top of the dresser.

content: A:アルバイトを雇うには金がかかりますよ。

content.content: Hiring a part-time worker will be expensive.
B:お金のことなら心配しなくていいですよ。何とかなりますから。
If it’s a matter of money, you don’t have to worry. We can manage.

content: A:佐藤さん見ませんでしたか。

content.content: Have you seen Sato-san?
B:佐藤さんなら、図書館にいましたよ。
Sato-san? He was in the library.

content: 時間ならば十分ありますから、ご心配なく。

content.content: As for time, we have plenty of it, so don’t worry.

content: 例のことならもう社長に伝えてあります。

content.content: If you mean that thing we talked about, I’ve already informed the company president.

なら is used when the speaker takes something that the addressee has said, something mentioned during discussion of the previous topic, or something that can be predicted from the current situation, makes it a new topic, and then continues talking about it. Often used when the speaker adopts as a topic something that was previously brought up by the addressee.

なら can often be replaced by the topic marker は. However, なら essentially has the hypothetical meaning “if N were the topic,” while は does not have such meaning. Therefore, when なら is replaced by は, the meaning of the sentence changes slightly. なら is synonymous with Nだったら, and these two expressions are interchangeable.
2. NならNだ

content: 山ならやっぱり富士山だ。

content.content: When it comes to mountains, naturally it has to be Fuji-san (Mt. Fuji).

content: ストレス解消法ならゴルフに限る。

content.content: If you’re looking for a way to get rid of stress, nothing beats golf.

content: 酒ならなんといってもここの地酒が一番だ。

content.content: When it comes to sake, the locally brewed sake here is unquestionably the best.

content: カキ料理なら広島が本場だ。

content.content: If you want good oyster cuisine, Hiroshima is the place to go.

Nなら can be followed by Nだ, or by expressions such as Nに限る (there’s nothing better than N), Nが一番だ (N is the best), and Nがいい (N is good). Nなら is used to define the range of the topic and then describe the most highly evaluated item within that range. In this usage, Nなら can be replaced by Nは without any great change in meaning.

content: あの人となら結婚してもいい。

content.content: I wouldn’t mind getting married, if it were to him.

content: フランス語はだめですが、英語でなら会話ができます。

content.content: I’m no good at French, but in English, I can carry on a conversation.

content: あと一人だけなら入場できます。

content.content: Only one more person can get in.

content: A:足の具合はいかがですか。

content.content: How is your leg?
B:ゆっくりとなら歩けるようになりました。
If I go slowly, I can walk now.

content: 仕事の後なら時間があります。

content.content: If it’s after work, I’ll have time.

When なら follows a noun, adverb, or noun/particle combination, it expresses the meaning that “Y doesn’t hold in other cases, but in the case of X, Y can be realized.” The Y clause that follows なら usually represents something desirable, and this pattern is used when the speaker actively selects an X that makes Y possible. This usage of なら is similar to the contrastive use of は. However, なら can be combined with interrogative words, while は cannot.
（○）何時なら都合がいいですか。
What time would be convenient for you?
（○）誰となら結婚してもいいですか。
Who would it have to be, in order for you to consider getting married?
（×）何時は都合がいいですか。
What is the time convenient for you?
（×）誰とは結婚してもいいですか。
I wouldn’t mind marrying who.

【なら2】［N／Na　なら］［N／Na　だった（の）なら］［A-い／A-かった　（の）なら］［V-る／V-た　（の）なら］When combined with the dictionary form or the ta-form of a predicate, なら expresses the meaning “if the actual situation or circumstances were like that.” The forms のならば, のなら, and ならば are also used. In spoken Japanese, の often becomes ん.

Although there is often no clear difference in meaning related to the presence or absence of の, のなら tends to be used in response to a statement on the part of the addressee, or a concrete situation, and conveys the meaning “if you say so,” “if that is true,” or “if that is the actual situation.” On the other hand, when の is not used, なら tends to convey the meaning of “generally, in such cases” or “if/when someone does so.” When (の)なら is combined with a noun or a na-adjective, の is often omitted. When (の)なら is combined with a verb or an i-adjective, it is synonymous with のだったら, and these two are interchangeable. However, の in のだったら cannot be omitted.
（×）知っているだったら教えてほしい。
If you happen know, I want you to tell me.
（○）知っている（の）なら教えてほしい。
If you happen to know, I want you to tell me.
知っているのだったら教えてほしい。
If you happen to know, I want you to tell me.
1. ...（の）なら〈hypothetical condition〉

B:風邪なら早く帰って休んだほうがいいよ。
If you’ve got a cold, you should go home early and rest.

content: 彼女のことがそんなに嫌いなら別れたらいい。

content.content: If you dislike her so much, you should break up with her.

content.content: I have a splitting headache.
B:そんなに痛い（の）なら早く帰ったほうがいいですよ。
If it hurts that much, you should go home early.

content: 行きたくない（の）ならやめておいたらどうですか。

content.content: If you don’t want to go, why don’t you just say no?

content: 真相を知っている（の）なら私に教えてほしい。

content.content: If you know the truth, I’d like you to tell me.

content: 郵便局に行く（の）なら、この手紙を出してきてくれますか。

content.content: If you’re going to the post office, could you mail this letter for me?

content: あなたがそんなに反対する（の）ならあきらめます。

content.content: If you’re so against it, I’ll give up on it.

content: A:ちょっと買い物に行ってくる。

content.content: I’m off to do a little shopping.
B:買い物に行く（の）ならついでにおしょうゆを買ってきてちょうだい。
If you’re going shopping, please pick up some soy sauce while you’re out.

content: A:沖縄ではもう梅雨に入ったそうですよ。

content.content: I hear the rainy season in Okinawa has already started.
B:沖縄で梅雨に入ったのなら、九州の梅雨入りも間近ですね。
If the rainy season has started in Okinawa, it’ll start soon in Kyushu, too.

content: 二人が昼からこの店で会っていたのなら、二人には午前中のアリバイはないことになる。

content.content: If the two of them were with each other for (part of) the afternoon in this shop, that means they don’t have an alibi for the morning.

When combined with the dictionary form or the ta-form of a predicate, (の)なら expresses a hypothetical condition and means “if that is the actual situation” or “if that is true.” A speaker uses (の)なら to state his/her own opinion or view, to make a request, or to give advice to the addressee, in light of something the addressee has just said or the situation at hand.

なら cannot be used to refer to things that occur as a matter of course or events that arise naturally with the passage of time. In such cases, expressions like たら, ば, and/or と must be used instead. Also, expressions that merely state a fact cannot be used at the end of a sentence with なら. Expressions indicating a judgment, intention, command, request/demand, suggestion, evaluation, or some other subjective attitude on the part of the speaker must be used.
（×）春が来るなら花が咲きます。
If spring comes, flowers bloom.
（×）雨が降るなら道がぬかります。
If rain falls, the road gets muddy.
（○）春が｛来たら／来れば／来ると｝花が咲きます。
When spring comes, flowers bloom.
（○）雨が｛降ったら／降ると／降れば｝道がぬかります。
When it rains, the road gets muddy.
（○）《午後から雨が降ると聞いて》雨が降る（の）なら、傘を持って行こう。（意志）
《having heard that it will rain in the afternoon》If it’s going to rain, I’ll take an umbrella. (intention)

たら, ば and と are used when the condition expressed in the first clause happens prior to the second clause and the situation or event in the second clause is realized as a result. On the other hand, なら can be used even when the situation in the second clause is realized first and the situation in the conditional clause follows.
（例）イタリアに行ったらイタリア語を習いなさい。（イタリアに行ってからイタリアで習う）
When you go to Italy, study Italian. (= study the language in Italy, after arriving there)
（例）イタリアに行くならイタリア語を習いなさい。（イタリアへ行く前に自分の国で習う）
If you’re going to Italy, study Italian. (= study the language in your own country, before going to Italy)
2. ...（の）なら〈counter-factual〉

content: 電話をくれるのなら、もう少し早い時間に電話してほしかった。

content.content: If you were going to call me, I wish you had called a little earlier.

content: 神戸に来ていたのなら、電話してくれればよかったのに。

content.content: If you were in Kobe, you should have phoned me.

content: あいつが来るのならこのパーティには来なかったんだが。

content.content: If I’d known he was coming, I wouldn’t have come to this party.

content: 結婚式に出席する（の）なら黒いスーツを買うのだが。

content.content: If I were going to a wedding, I would buy myself a black suit.

When (の)なら is used in the pattern X(の)ならY, either Y alone or both X and Y may contradict the given facts. In the first case, (の)なら is used when the speaker learns a new fact, X, and the pattern means “if I had known X (= factual), I could have done Y (= counter-factual), but since I didn’t know X, I didn’t do Y.” In the second case, (の)なら means “if X is done (= counter-factual), Y should be done (= counter-factual), but since X is actually not done, Y is not done either.”

, in which both X and Y are counter-factual, means “if I were going to attend a wedding, I would buy a black suit, but since I’m not actually going to a wedding, I’m not going to buy one.”

only Y is counter-factual, and although both X and Y are counter-factual in

content.content: （例）先週、神戸に来ていたのなら案内してあげたのに。

If you were in Kobe last week, I could have shown you around. (Means “I didn’t know you were in Kobe last week, so I couldn’t show you around.” X (you were in Kobe last week) is factual, while Y (I could have shown you around) is counter-factual.)
（例）先週、神戸に来て｛いれば／いたら｝案内してあげたのに。
If you had come to Kobe last week, I would have shown you around. (Means “you didn’t come to Kobe last week, so I couldn’t show you around.” Both X and Y are counter-factual.)
（例）結婚式に出るなら黒いスーツを買ったのだけど。

If I were going to a wedding, I would have bought a black suit. (Means “I’m not planning to attend a wedding, so I didn’t buy a black suit.” Both X and Y are counter-factual, and if both were realized, X would follow Y.)
（例）黒いスーツを買って｛いれば／いたら｝結婚式に出たのだが。

If I had bought a black suit, I would have attended the wedding. (Means “I hadn’t bought a black suit, so I didn’t attend the wedding.” Both X and Y are counter-factual, and if both were realized, Y would follow X.)
3. V-る（の）なら...がいい

content: 靴を買うならイタリア製がいい。

content.content: If you’re buying shoes, Italian-made ones are the best.

content: 食事をするなら、このレストランがいいよ。

content.content: If you’re going to eat out, I’d recommend this restaurant.

content: 英語を習うならアメリカかカナダに留学することをすすめたい。

content.content: If you want to learn English, I’d suggest studying in the United States or Canada.

content: A:大学を卒業したら留学したいと思っているんだ。

content.content: I’m thinking of going abroad to study after I graduate from college.
B:留学するのならオーストラリアがいいよ。
If you’re going to study abroad, I’d recommend Australia.

When (の)なら is followed by expressions such as がいい and をすすめる, its function is to recommend the best way or method of doing something. This pattern is often used in advertising slogans and/or commercials.

When talking about an action in general, rather than a particular person’s action, の is usually omitted. The meaning of V-るなら...がいい is similar to the meaning of expressions in which なら and は are used as topic markers, such as Nなら...がいい and Nは...がいい.
（例）靴を買うならイタリア製がいい。
If you’re buying shoes, Italian-made ones are the best.
（例）靴ならイタリア製がいい。
When it comes to shoes, Italian-made ones are the best.
（例）靴はイタリア製がいい。
As for shoes, Italian-made ones are the best.
4. V-る（の）なら　...しろ／...するな

content: 何事もやるなら最後まで徹底的にやれ。

content.content: Whatever you do, follow it through to the very end.

content: 女性と付き合うなら真剣に付き合いなさい。

content: 留学するならいい加減な気持ちではするな。

content.content: If you’re going to study abroad, don’t do it halfway.

content: 私のことを笑うなら勝手に笑えばいい。

content.content: If you want to laugh at me, feel free to do so.

content: 泣きたいのなら好きなだけ泣けばいい。

content.content: If you feel like crying, go ahead and cry your heart out.

When (の)なら is preceded and followed by the same verb, its function is to give instructions about how something should be done. (の)なら may be followed by expressions of command or prohibition, as well as expressions of suggestion or recommendation such as すればいい.

convey the meaning “if you want to do so, go ahead and do as you please.”

However, when it is used in response to an utterance or intention of a particular person, with the meaning “if you have such an intention” or “if you want to do so,” it may take the form のなら, as shown in
5. ...（の）なら...で［Na ならNa で］［A（の）ならAで］［V（の）ならVで］

When the same word is repeated before and after (の)なら, the speaker is acknowledging a certain situation to be as it is. S/he then states what kind of action should be taken under such circumstances, or expresses criticism or regret that such an action has not been taken.
6. ...（の）なら...と［NならN（だ）と］［Na ならNa（だ）と］［A（の）ならAと］［V（の）ならVと］

content: 欠席なら欠席と前もって知らせておいてください。

content: そうならそうと言ってほしかった。

content: 行く（の）なら行く、行かない（の）なら行かないとちゃんと言ってくれなければ困るじゃないですか。

The same word is repeated before and after (の)なら, and ...とis followed by expressions of utterance such as 言う and 連絡する. This pattern expresses the speaker’s attitude that the listener or a third person should clearly indicate his/her intentions regarding his/her own actions.

This pattern is usually used to criticize someone else for not expressing his/her intentions clearly, or to advise him/her that s/he should have indicated them clearly. However, it can also be used by the speaker to express his/her regret that s/he didn’t make his/her own intentions clear, as shown in
7. ...（の）ならべつだが［N／Na　ならべつだが］［A／V　（の）ならべつだが］

content: 自分のことなら話は別だが、人のことにそんなに気を揉んでも仕方がないだろう。

content.content: If it were your own problem, it’d be a different matter, but there’s no use worrying so much about other people.

content.content: If you really can’t stand it, that’d be different, but one idea to consider is hanging in there and staying with the company.

(の)ならべつだが assumes two distinct situations. It is used to introduce one situation as being inapplicable and to state the speaker’s opinion concerning the other possible situation. It is often followed by expressions intended to influence the listener, such as criticism, warning, or advice. As shown in

, (の)ならべつだが may also take the form ...なら話は別だが．

B:来たくないと言うのなら来てもらわなくてもいい。
If you’re saying you don’t want to come, that’s fine with me.

content: 責任をもつと言うのなら、信頼して任せてみてはどうですか。

content.content: If she says she’ll take responsibility, why don’t you trust her and let her handle it?

content: 子供が大事だと言うのなら、もっと家庭を大切にしなくてはだめだ。

content.content: If you say your child is important, then you have to take better care of your family.

content.content: If it’s true that their business is at a standstill, then they shouldn’t be able to put on such a flashy sales campaign.

というのなら is used to indicate a judgment on the part of the speaker regarding the content of the preceding conversation. It is followed by an expression of permission, advice, or suggestion directed toward the listener, or an inference made by the speaker. ということなら can also be used.
9. ...ということなら

content: 癌だということなら退院させてくれるはずがない。

content.content: If it really is cancer, there’s no way that they’ll release you from the hospital.

content: 自分たちでやるということなら、やらせてみてはどうか。

content: 期限内にできないということなら、ほかの業者に頼むことにしよう。

content.content: If he says they can’t finish it by the deadline, then we’ll ask another dealer.

Expresses the speaker’s response to something a third party has said. Used in more or less the same way as というのなら. However, というのなら can be used to respond to something said by either a direct addressee or a third person who is not present, in which cases it means “if you say so” or “if s/he says so,” respectively. ということなら usually means the latter only.

【なら3】［N／Na　（だった）なら］［A-い／A-かった　なら］［V-る／V-た　なら］In contrast with Usage 2 of なら, Usage 3 does not take the pattern のなら. Usage 3 is used in the form なら or ならば and is equivalent to the ba-form of N/Naだ. However, it can also be used after the dictionary form or the ta-form of a verb or i-adjective. When Usage 3 of なら is preceded by a verb or an i-adjective, it can be replaced by ば or たら with very little change in meaning. たなら is an emphatic form of たら and sounds a little old-fashioned.
1. N／Na　なら（ば）

content: 10 人一緒なら団体の割り引き料金になる。

content.content: Groups of ten get a reduced rate.

content: まわりがもう少し静かならば落ち着いて勉強できるのですが。

content.content: If it were a little quieter around here, I could settle down and study.

content: 東京ならこんなに安い家賃で家は借りられません。

content.content: If this were Tokyo, you would never be able to rent a house for such a low price.

content: その話が本当なら大変なことになりますよ。

content.content: If that story is true, you’re going to be in big trouble.

content: 私があなたならそんなふうには考えなかったと思う。

content.content: If I were you, I wouldn’t have thought like that.

content: 日曜日、お天気ならハイキングに行きましょう。

content.content: If the weather’s nice on Sunday, let’s go hiking.

N/Naなら(ば) is the ba-form of N/Naだ. It expresses a hypothetical condition, such as “if such-and-such was the case” or “supposing that...,” or a counter-factual condition, such as “if the circumstances were the other way around.” In formal written Japanese, であれば, which is the ba-form of である, can also be used. N/Naなら(ば) can be replaced by だったら.

The difference between Usage 3 of なら and Usage 1 is that Usage 1 attaches to nouns only and means “if N were the topic,” while Usage 3 expresses a supposition (if it were the case that...) regarding something that is either not known to be true, or is contrary to fact. However, in many cases it is difficult to decide which usage of なら actually applies.
2. NがNならNはNだ

content: 銀座が東京の中心なら心斎橋は大阪の中心だ。

content.content: If Ginza is the center of Tokyo, Shinsaibashi is the center of Osaka.

content: パリが芸術の都なら、ロンドンは金融の都だ。

content.content: If Paris is the city of art, London is the city of finance.

content: 兄が努力型の秀才なら弟は天才型の秀才だ。

content.content: If the older brother is the hard-working prodigy type, the younger brother is the genius type.

NがNならNはNだ is used to compare people or things that have contrasting characteristics. Each person or thing is likened to something different (using different terms), and the pattern itself means “if ...can be expressed as ..., then ...can be expressed as ....”
3. NがNならNもNだ

content: 親が親なら子も子だ。

content.content: What can you expect from a child with parents like that? (lit. Like parent, like child.)

content: 先生が先生なら学生も学生だ。

content.content: What can you expect from students with a teacher like that?

content: 亭主が亭主なら女房も女房だ。

content.content: Both the husband and wife are hopeless.

content: アメリカもアメリカなら日本も日本だ。

content.content: Both America and Japan are equally to blame.

The N slots in the pattern NがNならNもNだ are filled by pairs of nouns that represent people in a relationship, such as “husband” and “wife,” or institutions, organizations, etc. This pattern expresses a negative evaluation of the behavior or attitude of the people or organizations in question and means “both of them are equally terrible” or “they’re a totally outrageous bunch of people.” It is used to describe two parties with undesirable characteristics or attitudes, such as being thoughtless, lazy, impertinent, or rude. This pattern also takes the form N1もN1ならN2もN2だ, as in
4. ...なら（ば）［A／V　なら（ば）］

Used with the dictionary form or the ta-form of an i-adjective or verb, なら(ば) means “in the event that such a situation is realized.” It is a hypothetical conditional used to state an assumption about a situation that may be realized in the future, as well as a prediction about something that will happen if that situation is realized. なら(ば) is similar in meaning to するなら and したなら. It is a literary expression that often appears in editorial or academic texts. It can be replaced by ば and たら, and in spoken Japanese the latter are more commonly used.

5. ...たなら［N／Na　だったなら］［A-かったなら］［V-たなら］

content: 私が全能の神様だったなら、あなたを助けてあげられるのに。

content.content: If I were the Almighty God, I could help you.

content: もう少し発見が早かったなら助かったのに。

content.content: If only she had been found a little earlier, she would have been saved.

content: 困ることがあったならいつでも相談に来い。

content.content: Come and talk to me anytime you have a problem.

content: もしも私に翼があったなら大空を自由にかけまわりたい。

content.content: If I had wings, I would like to fly freely all over the open sky.

content: 《歌詞》あの坂を越えたなら幸せが待っている。

content.content: 《song》Happiness awaits over that hill.

...たなら, an emphatic form of たら that sounds a little old-fashioned, is used to express hypothetical or counter-factual conditions. It is often used in the lyrics of popular songs, but in daily conversation たら is more common.
6. V-るなら〈viewpoint〉

content: 事情を知らない人の目から見るなら、少しおおげさな感じがするかもしれない。

content.content: In the eyes of someone who doesn’t know the actual situation, it may seem a bit blown out of proportion.

content: 私に言わせるなら、この作品はあまり面白いとは思えない。

content.content: If you ask me, I don’t think this piece is all that interesting.

content: 戦前と比べるなら生活レベルはずいぶん向上したといえるだろう。

content.content: We can say that the standard of living has improved considerably, compared with before the war.

content: 一部を除くなら、彼の意見は正しいと思う。

content.content: Except for some parts, I think his opinion is correct.

When the dictionary form of verbs such as 見る, 言う, and 比べる is followed by なら, the result is an idiomatic expression that indicates the viewpoint from which a judgment or opinion (given in the subsequent clause) is stated. This pattern tends to be used in written Japanese. たら／と／ば can also be used with these verbs, and the resulting forms are, for the most part, interchangeable with V-るなら. Similar expressions include ...によるなら and ...を別にするなら.
【ならいい】［N／Na　ならいい］［A／V　（の）ならいい］

content: お母さんが病気ならいいよ。早く家に帰ってあげなさい。

content.content: If your mother is unwell, don’t worry (about this). Go home and take care of her.

content: 勉強がそんなに嫌いならいいよ。大学など行かないで就職したらいい。

content.content: If you hate studying that much, I won’t force you. You should get a job rather than something like going to a university.

content: A:悪いけど、その仕事はあまり得意じゃないんだ。

content.content: I’m sorry, but I’m not very good at that kind of job.
B:やりたくない（の）ならいいよ。他の人に頼むから。
If you don’t want to do it, that’s all right. I’ll ask somebody else.

content: それほど熱心に言う（の）ならいいじゃありませんか。やりたいことをやらせてあげなさいよ。

content.content: Isn’t it all right if she says she’s that enthusiastic? Go ahead and let her do what she wants.

On the basis of the previous utterance or situation, ならいい expresses the speaker’s attitudes such as allowance or non-intervention and means “considering the previous utterance or situation, it’s okay to do something/you can do it/you don’t have to do it.” For instance, the sentence in

content: means “if you don’t want to do that, you don’t have to do it.”

content.content: 【ならでは】［Nならでは］

content: 親友ならではの細かい心遣いが嬉しかった。

content.content: I was so happy to receive such careful attention that only such a close friend could give.

content: 二枚目俳優ならではの端正な顔立ちをしていた。

content.content: He had the fine features you’d expect of a nimaime (matinee idol).

content: 当店ならではのすばらしい料理をお楽しみください。

content.content: Please enjoy our house specialties.

content: あの役者ならでは演じられないすばらしい演技だった。

content.content: It was just like that actor to give such a brilliant performance.

With a noun showing a person or an organization, ならでは expresses the meaning of “just because it is N (a person, a thing), it is that wonderful,” “only N can do that,” or “N is the only one which makes that possible.” Often appears in the pattern NならではのN, but also appears in Nならでは...ない. ならでは expresses a high opinion of N and is used in catch phrases for a shop or company advertisement.
【ならない】
1. V-てならない→
【てならない】
2. V-てはならない→
【てはならない】
3. V-なくてはならない→
【なければ】
4. V-なければならない→
【なければ】2
【ならびに】［NならびにN］

content: 各国の首相ならびに外相が式典に参列した。

content.content: Premiers and foreign ministers from every country attended the ceremony.

content: この美術館は主に東欧の絵画並びに工芸品を所蔵している。

content.content: This museum has a collection of mainly paintings and handicrafts from Eastern Europe.

content: 本日ご出席の卒業生の諸君ならびに御家族の皆さま方に心からお祝い申し上げます。

content.content: I offer my sincere congratulations to both the graduates and their families who  are attending this ceremony today.

content: 優勝者には賞状ならびに記念品が手渡されることになっている。

content.content: The champion will be handed both a certificate and a trophy.

content: 用紙に住所、氏名ならびに生年月日を記入して下さい。

content.content: Please fill in your address, name, and date of birth on the form.
Used to add a new N (thing/person) similar to the preceding N. Formal expression mainly used in written language. Also used in formal speech such as an address at a ceremony.
【なり1】
1. V-るなり

content: 家に帰るなり自分の部屋に閉じ込もって出てこない。

content.content: As soon as he came home, he locked himself up in his room.

content: 立ち上がるなり目まいがして倒れそうになった。

content.content: When I stood up, I suddenly felt dizzy and was about to collapse.

content: 会うなり金を貸してくれなどと言うので驚いた。

content.content: I was very surprised because as soon as she saw me, she asked me to lend her money and more.

With an action verb, V-るなり expresses the meaning of “right after that action.” This expression is similar to ...したとたんに or ...するやいなや. V-るなり is used when something unexpected happens right after the action.
2. V-たなりa. V-たなり（で）

content: 座ったなり動こうともしない。

content.content: Since he sat down, he has not moved at all.

content: うつむいたなり黙りこんでいる。

content.content: She has been silent since she bowed her head.

content: 立ったなりでじっとこちらの様子を伺っている。

content.content: He’s been standing there and watching our every action.
Expresses a state which continues as it is and does not get anything/circumstances moving. Can be rephrased as ...したまま. V-たなり sounds a little archaic.
b. V-たなり

content: 家を出たなり一カ月も帰ってこなかった。

content.content: Since he left home, a month has passed.

content: お辞儀をしたなり何も言わずに部屋を出て行った。

content.content: As soon as she bowed, she left the room without saying a word.

content: 住民の反対にあって、工事は中断されたなり解決のめどもついていない。

content.content: Because of the objection of the residents, the construction was interrupted and there is no sign of any solution when the problem will be solved.

Expresses a state which continues to be as it is without changing even though it is normally expected to trigger the following state after something happens. Can be rephrased as ...したまま. Sounds a little archaic.
【なり2】
1. ...なり［Nなり］［V-るなり］

content: 何かお飲物なりお持ちしましょうか。

content.content: Shall I bring you a drink or something?

content: そんなに忙しいんだったら友達になり手伝ってもらったらいいのに。

content.content: If you are so busy, you should ask a friend or somebody to help you.

content: そんなに心配なら先生に相談するなりしてみてはどうですか。

content.content: If you are worrying that much, why don’t you do something like consult your teacher?

content: 壁に絵を飾るなりしたらもっと落ちつくと思いますよ。

content.content: I think doing something like putting pictures on the wall would calm the mood more.
Attaches to a variety of elements such as nouns and verbs and is used to refer to one possibility among several others as an example.
2. V-るなりV-ないなり

content: 行くなり行かないなりはっきり決めてほしい。

content.content: I want you to decide whether you are going to go or not.

content: やるなりやらないなり、はっきりした態度をとらなければならない。

content.content: Whether you do it or not, you must make up your mind.

content: 来るなり来ないなりをきちんと連絡してもらわなければ困ります。

content.content: If you won’t give me a definite answer as to whether or not you’re coming, I’ll have trouble.

With an affirmative form of a verb followed by a negative form of the same verb, expresses the meaning of choosing one over the other. Followed by expressions indicating that choosing one over the other is required, desired, or suggested. Since V-るなりV-ないなり involves the speaker’s feeling to force the other party to choose one over the other, this expression could be considered rude if used inappropriately.
（×）参加なさるなりなさらないなりをお知らせください。
Please let me know whether you will attend or not.
（○）参加なさるかどうかをお知らせください。
Kindly let me know whether you will be attending or not.
3. ...なり...なり［NなりNなり］［V-るなりV-るなり］

content: 彼の父親なり母親なりに相談しなければならないだろう。

content.content: I should probably consult an appropriate person like his father or mother, for instance.

content: 東京なり大阪なり、好きなところで生活すればいい。

content.content: I don’t care whether it will be in Tokyo or in Osaka or wherever—live someplace you like.

content: 叱るなり誉めるなり、はっきりとした態度をとらなければだめだ。

content.content: Whether you scold or praise him, you need to have a clear idea of your own stance.
NなりNなり and V-るなりV-るなり express the meaning of choosing between two things in the same group. It implies that there are some other possibilities in addition to the two.
4. ...なりなんなり［N／V　なりなんなり］

content: チューリップなりなんなり、少し目立つ花を買ってきて下さい。

content.content: Please go buy some flowers—like tulips—that are a little showy.

content: ここは私が支払いますからコーヒーなりなんなり好きなものを注文して下さい。

content.content: I’ll pay for you here, so please order coffee or anything you like.

content: 転地療養するなり何なりして少し体を休めたほうがいい。

content.content: You should go somewhere for a change or do something to take at least a little rest.

content: この部屋は寒そうだから、カーペットを入れるなり何なりしなければいけないね。

content.content: We need to carpet this room or do something because it seems cold.
N/Vなりなんなり expresses the meaning that anything would be fine if it is similar to what the speaker mentions. When it refers to a place, ...なりどこなり is used.
（例）外国なりどこなり、好きなところへ行ってしまえ。
Whether it’s a foreign country or somewhere else, go anywhere you like.
【なり3】
1. ...なりa. ...なり［Nなり］［A-いなり］

content: 私なりに努力はしてみましたが、力が及びませんでした。

content.content: I tried my best, but it was beyond my ability.

content: この事態は役人だけに任せておくのではなく、私たち住人なりの対応策を考えなければならない。

content.content: We shouldn’t leave this matter to the officials, but as residents we should consider our own countermeasures.

content: 彼らは経験が浅いなりによく頑張ってやってくれる。

content.content: For all their lack of experience, they are still doing what they can.

content: 母親が留守の間は、子供たちなりに一生懸命考えて、食事を作っていたようです。

content.content: While their mother was away, it seems the children planned as best they could and did the cooking.

content: この結論は私なりに悩んだ末のものです。

content.content: This is my conclusion I arrived at after much worrying.

Expresses the meaning that a certain thing/state/event is in accordance with what is anticipated in normal circumstances. Used when the speaker evaluates something positively even though s/he recognizes its limit or defect.
b. ...なり［Nなり］［V-るなり］

content: 彼は妻の言うなりになっている。

content.content: He does everything his wife says.

content: その店なら、道なりにまっすぐ行くと右側にあります。

content.content: If that’s the shop, just follow this street straight on and it’ll be on the right.
Expresses the meaning that something/someone follows another without going against it/the person. Used only in fixed phrases such as 言うなり and 道なり. 言うなり can be rephrased as 言いなり.
2. ...なら...なり［NならNなり］［Na ならNa なり］［A-いならA-いなり］［V-るならV-るなり］

content: 嫌なら嫌なりの理由があるはずだ。

content.content: There has to be a reason why she so dislikes it.

content: 若いなら若いなりにやってみればいい。

content.content: Young people should make their own way.

content: 貧乏なら貧乏なりに楽しく生きられる方法がある。

content.content: Even poor people can find their own way to live happy lives.

content: 我々の要求を受け入れられないなら、受け入れられないなりにもっと誠意を持って対応すべきだ。

content.content: If you cannot meet our demand(s), you should at least show that you take your responsibilities seriously for what you have done to us.

content: 金があるならあるなりに心配ごともつきまとう。

content.content: More money is accompanied by more worries.

content: 新しいビジネスを始めるなら始めるなりの準備というものが必要だ。

content.content: If you are to start a new business, you need to prepare for that.

Repeating the same word, expresses the meaning that something is in accordance with the thing mentioned or something is suitable to the thing mentioned. Implies that there is typically a limit, defect, or strength of its own, and means that even such a limit, defect, or strength is in accordance with the thing mentioned. ...なら...なり clauses are often followed by expressions such as そうするはずだ ((I am) certain that (they) will do so), そうしなければならない (must do so), or そうしてほしい ((I hope they) will do so). This expression can be rephrased as ...ば...なり.
（例）金があればあるなりに気を使わなければならない。
The more money you have, the more care you have to take.
3. には...なり［NにはNなり］［V-るにはV-るなり］

content: 若い人には若い人なりの考えがあるだろう。

content.content: Young people probably have their own way of thinking.

content: 学生には学生なりの努力が求められている。

content.content: Students are expected to make efforts on their own.

content: 金持ちには金持ちなりの心配事がある。

content.content: Even the rich have their own concerns.

content: この商売にはこの商売なりに、いろいろな苦労や面白さがある。

content.content: This business has its own problems and interesting parts in various respects.

content: 断わるには断わるなりの手順というものがある。

content.content: There is a certain procedure to follow when you decline an offer.

The same noun or verb is used in the expression ...には...なり. Implies that there is typically a limit, defect, or strength of its own, and expresses the meaning that even with such a characteristic, this is in accordance with something or this is suitable to something.
4. NはNなり

content: 彼らは彼らなりにいろいろ努力しているのだから、それは認めてやってほしい。

content.content: They are trying their best in various ways, so I would like you to acknowledge that.

content: 私は私なりのやりかたでやってみたい。

content.content: I’d like to try my own way.

content: 私は私なりに考えて子供をしつけてきたつもりです。

content.content: I believe that I have done what I felt best in bringing up my children.

content: 古い機械は古い機械なりに、年代を経た趣と手慣れた使いやすさがある。

content.content: Old machines have their own merits, as they have the true character of past times and are easy to handle.

Repeating the same noun, implies that a person or a thing has his/her/its own limit or defect. It means that even with such a characteristic, this is in accordance with something or this is suitable for something.
5. それなり

content: 小さな会社だがそれなりの利益は上げている。

content.content: This is a small company, but as such, they are making a profit.

content: 嫌だというならそれなりの理由があるのだろう。

content.content: If he says he doesn’t like it, there should be a reason as such.

content: 子供たちもそれなりに力を合わせて頑張っている。

content.content: Children are working together and trying their best.

content: 努力をすればそれなりの成果はあがるはずだ。

content.content: If you work hard, you can expect that much more.
Implies that there is a limit or defect and means that even with such a characteristic, this is in accordance with something.
【なりと】
1. Nなりと（も）

content: よろしかったら私の話なりとも聞いて下さい。

content.content: If you would, please spare me a few moments and listen to my story.

content: ここにおかけになってお茶なりと召し上がっていらして下さい。

content.content: Please have a seat here and have some tea or something.
Mainly follows a noun and is used to show one of several examples.
2. 疑問詞（+格助詞）+なりと

content: お前みたいな勝手なやつはどこへなりと行ってしまえばいい。

content.content: Someone as self-centered as you should just get lost!

content: だれとなりと、好きな男と一緒になるがいい。

content.content: You can marry any kind of man, whomever you like.

content: なんなりとお好みのものをお持ちしますのでおっしゃって下さい。

content.content: I’ll bring you anything you like, so please let me know your desire.

content: ご希望がありましたら、どうぞ遠慮せずに何なりとお申しつけ下さい。

content.content: If you have any particular preference, please don’t hesitate to tell us.
Question word + なりと appears in fixed, idiomatic expressions such as どこへなりと(wherever to), だれとなりと (whoever with) and なんなりと (whatever). Means that someone can choose whatever s/he likes.
【なる】
1. ...なる［N／Na　になる］［A-くなる］［V-ようになる］

content: 木が切り倒されて山が裸になってしまった。

content.content: The trees were cut down and the mountain is now bare.

content: 彼女は働きすぎて病気になった。

content.content: Because she worked too much, she became ill.

content: このあたりは、昔は静かなところだったのですが、ずいぶんにぎやかになったものですね。

content.content: This used to be a very quiet place in the past, but it’s gotten pretty bustling now, hasn’t it?

content: 酒を飲んで顔が赤くなりました。

content.content: I drank and my face got red.

content: 道路が拡張されたために車が増えて、段々住みにくくなっています。

content.content: Since the road was extended, the number of cars has increased and it’s gradually gotten less pleasant to live here.

content: 練習の成果があって、ようやく平仮名が全部読めるようになりました。

content.content: My practice paid off and I finally came to be able to read all the hiragana syllabary.

content: 以前は無口だったが、最近はよくしゃべるようになりました。

content.content: I used to be a man of few words, but recently I’ve come to talk quite a lot.

content: 彼と一緒に仕事をするようになって、ずいぶんいろいろなことを学びました。

content.content: Since I started working together with him, I have learned so many things.
Expresses that things are changing. するindicates some changes which someone intentionally causes to happen, whereas なる shows automatic/natural changes of the things by themselves.
【ように3】
2. Nからなる

content: この本は4つの章からなっている。

content.content: This book consists of four chapters.

content: この委員会は委員長以下5人の委員からなっている。

content.content: This committee consists of five members in addition to a chairperson.

content: 日本の議会は参議院と衆議院とからなる。

content.content: The House of Councilors and the House of Representatives comprise the Diet in Japan.

content: 3つの主要な論点からなる議題を提案した。

content.content: I proposed the agenda on three main points of discussion.
With a noun, Nからなる means that something is composed of N. Can appear in patterns such as XとYとからなる, as shown in

content: . When used at the end of the sentence, Nからなる often becomes ...からなっている, but ...からなる may be used in formal, written Japanese. To modify a noun, the form ...からなるN is used.

content.content: 3. ...ことになる

content: この大会も今年で4回目ということになりますね。

content.content: This competition is the fourth one this year, isn’t it?

content: 私とあの人はいとこどうしということになる。

content.content: This means that person and I are cousins.
【ことになる】
4. R-そうになる

content: 叱られて泣きそうになった。

content.content: I was close to tears when I was scolded.

content: この臭いをかぐとくしゃみが出そうになる。

content.content: When I smell this odor, it makes me feel like sneezing.
【そうだ2】2b
5. ...となる［N／Na　となる］

content: 彼はまだ 20 歳なのに、もうすぐ1児の父となります。

content.content: Even though he is only twenty, he’ll become the father of a child soon.

content: 人々は次々に島を出て行き、ついにそこは無人島となった。

content.content: People left the island one after another, and eventually it turned into a desert island.

content: その法案には様々な問題があることが明らかとなった。

content.content: It became clear that the bill had various problems.

content: この戦争は最終的には悲劇的な結末となった。

content.content: This war ultimately came to a tragic end.

content: 結局は、両国の話し合いは物別れとなった。

content.content: In the end, the negotiations between the two countries broke down.

With a noun or a na-adjective, …となる means that a certain thing/state/event expressed in this phrase changes. Since it implies that the thing/state/event reaches an ultimate stage, expressions which cannot refer to such an ultimate stage, such as にぎやか, 病気, and 元気, are unlikely to be used with ...となる. ...となる is always rephrased as ...になる, but ...になる cannot always be ...となる.
（×）にぎやかとなった。
It turned out to be lively.
（○）にぎやかになった。
It turned out to be lively.
6. ...となると→
【となると】
7. Nともなると

content: 3月ともなるとだいぶ暖かく感じられるようになります。

content.content: If it is in March, it will likely feel quite warm.

content: 大学生ともなると、ある程度は自分でお小遣いをかせがなければならない。

content.content: Once you become a college student, you have to earn some of your own pocket money
【ともなると】
8. ...になる［Nになる］［V-ることになる］

content: 来年から5月4日は休校日になります。

content.content: From next year, May 4th will be a school holiday.

content: 今年の秋に結婚することになりました。

content.content: We have decided to get married this fall.

Expresses the meaning that some decision or agreement is made for a future event or some result happens. Implies that without questioning who made a decision, this result has occurred in the ordinary course of things/events or by some other force. N + particle + になる may be used, as shown in the following examples.
（例）会議は5時からになりました。
The meeting is now to start at five.
【ことになる】
9. Nになると

content: 国語なら教えられるが、数学になると全く手がでない。

content.content: I can teach language arts, but as for mathematics, I can’t teach it at all.

content: 練習ではうまくいったのに、いざ本番になると上がってしまいました。

content.content: I did very well at the rehearsal, but when it came to the actual performance, I got nervous.
Means “when it reaches a certain level or stage.” Can be rephrased as Nとなると.
0. おR-になる

content: 先生はお帰りになりました。

content.content: The teacher has gone home.

content: おかけになってお待ち下さい。

content.content: Please have a seat and wait for a moment.
【お...になる】
【なるたけ】

content: この仕事はなるたけ早く仕上げて下さい。

content.content: Please finish this work as soon as possible.

content: 壊れやすい品物だから、なるたけ気を付けて運んでね。

content.content: Because this is a fragile item, carry it as carefully as possible.
なるたけis a casual way of saying できるだけ and なるべく.
【なるべく】
1. なるべく

content: 今晩はなるべく早めに帰ってきて下さいね。

content.content: If it’s at all possible, come back a little earlier tonight.

content: 明日は試合だから、今日は無理をしないでなるべく体を休めておくようにしよう。

content.content: Since we’ll have a match tomorrow, let’s give ourselves as much of a rest as we can today.

content: この活動には、なるべく多くの人に参加してもらいたい。

content.content: I would like as many people as possible to participate in this activity.

content: この品物は壊れやすいから、なるべく注意して取り扱って下さいね。

content.content: This item is fragile, so please handle it as carefully as possible.

content: かなり長い距離を歩くと聞きましたので、荷物はなるべく少なくするようにしました。

content.content: Since I’d heard that we would walk a fairly long way, I tried to lighten my load as much as I could.
Means “as much as possible” or “as much as one can.” Often followed by an expression indicating the speaker’s intention, desire, or request.
2. なるべくなら

content: なるべくなら、今晩は早く帰って休みたい。

content.content: If possible, I would like to go back home early tonight and have a rest.

content: なるべくなら、だれにも会わずに帰ろうと思っていたのですが、知り合いに見つかって声をかけられてしまいました。

content.content: If at all possible, I wanted to go home without meeting anyone, but I was called after by an acquaintance who spied me.

content: この話はなるべくなら人に知られたくないので、黙っていて下さいね。

content.content: If it’s possible, keep mum on this matter, because I don’t want anyone to know about it.

content: なるべくなら武力を使わずに話し合いで解決したいものだ。

content.content: If possible, it is more desirable to talk with each other to solve a problem, without resorting to violence.
Expresses the meaning of “if possible” or “if one can.” Often followed by some phrases expressing the speaker’s desire or intention.
【なるほど】

content: いい店だとは聞いていたが、なるほどサービスもいいし料理もうまい。

content.content: I’ve heard that this is a good restaurant. Indeed, the service is excellent and the food is really good.

content: あなたの言うことはなるほどもっともだが、私の立場も考えてほしい。

content.content: It is true that what you are saying is reasonable, but I would like you to consider my position.

content: なるほど、富士山というのは美しい山だ。

content.content: Indeed, Fuji-san (Mount Fuji) is a beautiful mountain.

content: なるほど、噂には聞いていましたが、実際に使ってみると本当に便利なものなのですね。

content.content: I had heard talk about it and—as they said—it really was convenient when I used it.

content: A:きのうは久しぶりに大学時代の友達に会ってきたよ。

content.content: Yesterday I saw my friends from my university days after a long while.
B:なるほど。だからあんなに嬉しそうにしていたんですね。
Oh, so that’s why you looked so happy.

content: A:このコピー機は、濃度調整が自動でできるようになっております。

content.content: This copier is able to control the boldness of fonts automatically.
B:なるほど。
I see.
A:それから、用紙の選択も自動になっております。
Furthermore, it can also automatically select the paper size.
B:なるほど。
I got it.

Expresses the speaker’s understanding with satisfaction that the speaker agrees with knowledge s/he obtained from others or accepts what the listener is contending. Also used when the speaker reconfirms his/her own information, or when the speaker is convinced by an answer to his/her question. なるほど sounds casual and less formal than 納得, as in

content: . There is a use in which the speaker shows the listener that s/he agrees with the listener or s/he is making brief responses while listening to the listener. However, なるほど is not used towards superiors because this use may sound arrogant.

content.content: 【なれた】［R-なれたN］

content: 使いなれた道具を使う。

content.content: I use the tools which I’ve gotten used to.

content: 老後も住み慣れた土地で暮らしたい。

content.content: When I’m old, too, I want to reside in a locale where I am used to living.

content: そのベテランの工員は、扱い慣れた自信に満ちた態度で機械を操作していた。

content.content: That veteran worker was skillfully operating the machine with the confidence of long experience.

content: 彼は人前で話し慣れているから、上がらない。

content.content: Since he is accustomed to speaking in public, he doesn’t get nervous.

With a verb stem, なれた expresses the meaning that one did the same action many times so s/he is well-experienced or has gotten accustomed to it. Often appears in the form ...なれた, which modifies a noun. Occasionally takes the form ...なれている／なれていない as a sentence-final predicate, as in
【なれば】
1. ...となれば→
【となれば】
2. ...ともなれば→
【ともなれば】
【なんか】
1. なんか〈things〉A casual way of saying なにか. Used in spoken Japanese.
【なにか】a. なんか

content: A:なんかたべるものない？

content.content: Is there anything to eat?
B:冷蔵庫見てみたら？　なんか入っていると思うけど。
Why don’t you look inside the fridge? I think there should be something.

content: 誕生日にはなんか買ってやろうと思っています。

content.content: I’m thinking of buying something for his birthday.

content: 今日手伝えなかったことは、きっと何かで償うよ。

content.content: I’ll surely make up for what I couldn’t do for you today.

content: 何か変な音が聞こえませんでしたか。

content.content: Didn’t you just hear some strange noise?

content: この部屋、何か臭わない？

content.content: Don’t you think this room smells like something?
Expresses something or some state which one cannot clearly refer to.
b. なんか〈appearance〉

content: 彼女と話していると、なんかほっとした気持ちになる。

content.content: When I talk to her, I just feel relieved for some reason.

content: あの人の言っていること、なんか変だと思いませんか。

content.content: Don’t you think what she is saying is somewhat strange?

content: 今日は子供たちがなんか妙に静かですね。なにかいたずらをしているんじゃありませんか。

content.content: The children are unusually quiet today. I wonder if they are up to something naughty.

content: なんか不思議だなあ、この町は。前に来たことがあるような気がしてならない。

content.content: I don’t know why, but I feel strange about this town. I can’t help thinking that I’ve been here before.
Expresses the meaning of “I don’t know why it’s so” or “for some reason.”
c. ...かなんか［N／A／V　かなんか］

content: 今度の休みは映画かなんか行かない？

content.content: Shall we go to a movie or something on the next day off?

content: この傷は石かなんかがぶつかってできたものでしょう。

content.content: I guess that a stone or something hit it to create this scrape.

content: お見舞いには果物かなんかを持って行くことにしよう。

content.content: I’ll take fruit or something when I pay a visit at the hospital.

content: 田中君は試験が近いかなんかでとても忙しそうです。

content.content: Tanaka-kun seems to be very busy because his exams are approaching or something.

content: A:田中君はどうしたの？

content.content: What happened to Tanaka-kun?
B:忘れものをしたかなんかで、取りに戻っています。
He went back because he forgot something, I guess.
Expresses something that one cannot refer to clearly but is similar to the thing mentioned.
d. Nやなんか

content: スポーツは好きですが、野球やなんかの球技はあまり得意ではないんですよ。

content.content: I like sports, but I’m not good at ball games like baseball.

content: 出張やなんかで旅行をするときはいつもこの鞄を持っていきます。

content.content: I always bring this bag when I do things like make a business trip.

content: この話は友達やなんかには言わないで下さいね。

content.content: Please don’t tell this story to your friends or anybody else, OK?

content: 山で遭難したときは、持っていたチョコレートやなんかを食べて救助を待ちました。

content.content: When I got lost in the mountains, while I was waiting to be saved I ate things like the chocolate that I had brought with me.
Used to express the thing mentioned, N, and some other similar things.
2. なんかa. Nなんか

content: お酒はワインなんか好きで、よく飲んでいます。

content.content: As for alcohol, I like things like wine and drink it quite often.

content: 食料品なんかは近くの店で買うことができます。

content.content: You can buy groceries and other things at the shop nearby.

content: 山本さんや鈴木さんなんかはこの案に反対のようです。

content.content: People like Yamamoto-san and Suzuki-san seem to be against this idea.

content: 部品やなんかは揃っているんですが、技術者がいないので直せないんです。

content.content: We have all the parts and things, but we can’t fix it because we don’t have a technician.
Exemplifies the main one(s) among various other items. Implies that there are other similar sorts of things. This expression is used in the form など in casual speech.
b. V-たりなんかして

content: 休みの日は本を読んだりなんかして過ごします。

content.content: I spend my days off doing things like reading books.

content: どうしたの？　ひとりで笑ったりなんかして。

content.content: What’s the deal? How come you’re snickering by yourself and all?

content: お父さんたら急に怒り出したりなんかして。この頃少し疲れてるのかな。

content.content: What’s with Father that he does things like suddenly get angry? I wonder if he hasn’t been a little tired out these days.
Exemplifies main one(s) among various other actions. Implies that there are other similar sorts of actions. A colloquial equivalent of など that is used in casual speech.
c. なんか...ない

content: お金がないから、旅行なんか滅多にできない。

content.content: I don’t have any money at all, so I can hardly do things like take a trip.

content: あんな男となんか口もききたくない。

content.content: I don’t even want to speak to such a guy.

content: そんなばかげたことなんか考えたこともありません。

content.content: I’ve never thought about such a stupid thing.

content: こんな汚い部屋になんか一日だって泊まりたくない。

content.content: I don’t want to stay in such a filthy room even for one night.

content: こんな天気の良い日に家の中で本を読んでなんかいないで、外を散歩しましょうよ。

content.content: Don’t do things like reading a book inside on such a nice day as this. Let’s  take a walk outside.

content: あんな映画ちっともおもしろくなんかないよ。

content.content: That movie is not at all interesting.

With a variety of elements such as a noun, a verb, or a noun + verb, this なんか is followed by some negative expression. Although なんか...ない expresses negation towards a thing/state/event mentioned in the sentence, it also implies at the same time the speaker’s derogatory, humble, or unexpected feeling toward the thing/state/event expressed in the phrase with なんか. なんか...ない is rephrased as など...ない in casual speech.
【なんか...ものか】［...なんかV-るものか］

content: 家になんか帰ってやるものか。

content.content: I never, ever go back home.

content: 誰がそんな話なんか信じるものか。

content.content: Who the hell believes such a story?

content: あんな男となんか二度と口を利いてやるものか。

content.content: I won’t talk to such a guy ever again.

content: あんなひとに教えてなんかやるものか。

content.content: It’ll be a long time before I ever teach someone like that.

content: 一人でも寂しくなんかあるものか。

content.content: I’m not in the least lonely.

content: A:講演会いかがでしたか。おもしろい話が聞けたでしょう。

content.content: How was the lecture? You must have heard an interesting talk.
B:おもしろくなんかあるものですか。すごくくだらない話でしたよ。
It wasn’t in the least bit interesting. It was a really worthless lecture.

With a variety of elements such as a noun, a verb, an adjective, or a noun + verb, なんか...ない negates the following statement. At the same time, it expresses the speaker’s derogatory feeling towards a thing/state/event mentioned in the phrase with なんか, and means “this is stupid, insignificant, outrageous.” なんか...ない is a casual way of saying など...ものか.
【なんだか】

content: このあたりはなんだか気味が悪いね。

content.content: It’s scary around here for some reason.

content: あなたと話していたら、なんだか少し気分が楽になってきた。

content.content: After talking to you, I somehow feel a little relieved.

content: 彼は最近なんだか私のことを避けているような気がする。

content.content: I have a feeling that he’s trying to avoid me lately, for some reason.
Expresses the meaning “I don’t know what the cause or reason is” or “for some reason.” This is a casual way of saying なぜか.
【なんだろう】→
【でなくてなんだろう】
【なんて1】
1. なんてa. なんてV

content: よく聞こえないのですが、あの人はなんて言っているのですか。

content.content: I can’t hear him very well—what is that person saying?

content: この字は何て書いてあるのか分からない。

content.content: I don’t know what this character means.

content: このことを知ったら、お母さん何て思うかしら。

content.content: If she gets to know about it, how would my mother feel?
Followed by a verb such as 言う(say) or 書く(write) and means that the content expressed by such a verb is unclear. A casual way of saying なんと.
b. なんて（いう）N

content: さっき来た人はなんていう人ですか。

content.content: What is the name of the person who came here just now?

content: 後藤さんは何ていう会社にお勤めですか。

content.content: What is the name of the company where Goto-san works?

content: あの人、なんて名前だったかしら。

content.content: I wonder what the name of that person was.

content: 彼、なんて町に住んでいるんだっけ。

content.content: What is the name of the town he lives in again?
Used to ask for a name of a person or a place. A casual way of saying なんというN.
c. なんて（いう）Nだ

content: あなたって人は、なんていう人なの。

content.content: What kind of person are you?

content: あれだけの仕事を1日で片づけてしまうなんて、何ていう早業だろう。

content.content: To finish that whole job in just one day—what a quick worker!

content: 事故で子供を失ってしまうなんて、なんて事だ。

content.content: I can’t imagine what it’s like to lose a child in an accident.

content: 友人を見殺しにするなんて、あなたってなんて人なの。

content.content: What kind of person are you just to stand by and not help a friend?
A casual way of saying なんというNだ. Expresses the speaker’s extreme surprise or amazement.
d. なんてことない

content: これくらいのけが、なんて事ないさ。

content.content: Such an injury is nothing to me.

content: この程度の仕事は何て事ない。1日で片付くさ。

content.content: It’s no problem to do such a job. I can finish it in a day.

content: 一見何て事ない仕事のようだけれど、やってみると非常に手がかかる。

content.content: This work looks easy at first, but when you actually do it, it’s really time-consuming.
Means that something is not so considerable. This is a casual way of saying なんということはない.
2. なんて...んだろう［なんて...Nなんだろう］［なんてNa なんだろう］［なんてA-いんだろう］

content: ここはなんて寂しいところなんでしょう。

content.content: What a god-forsaken place this is!

content: 彼の演奏はなんてすばらしいんだろう。

content.content: How excellent his performance is!

content: この子は何てかわいげのない子供なんだろう。

content.content: What a charmless, unendearing child!

content: 家の中に木を植えるとは、何て大胆な発想なんだろう。

content.content: What a bold idea, to plant a tree inside the house!
なんて...んだろう is used to express the speaker’s surprise or amazement with admiration or explanation. It can be rephrased as なんてまあ. なんて...んだろう is a casual way of saying なんと...のだろう.
【なんて2】
1. Nなんて

content: あなたなんて大嫌い。

content.content: I hate you!

content: そんな馬鹿げた話なんて、だれも信じませんよ。

content.content: Nobody believes such a ridiculous story.

content: あの人の言うことなんて、嘘に決まっています。

content.content: Everything that person says has got to be a lie!
Topicalizes something that the speaker thinks ridiculous or stupid. A colloquial expression.

content: みんなには時間を守れなんて言ったけど、そう言った本人が遅刻してしまった。

content.content: She had told us all to be on time, but the very person who had said it arrived late.

content: 息子が大学進学は嫌だなんて言い出して困っている。

content.content: I’ve been really troubled since my son said he didn’t like the idea of continuing on to a university.

content: 私が彼をだましたなんて言っているらしいけど、彼のほうこそ嘘を付いているんです。

content.content: He seems to be saying that I deceived him, but he’s the one who was lying.

content: あやまれば許してもらえるなんて甘い考えは捨てなさい。

content.content: Forget about your wishful thinking that if you apologize, you are forgiven.

content: まさか、親に頼めば借金を払ってもらえるなんて思っているんじゃないでしょうね。

content.content: Surely you’re not thinking that if you ask your parents, they’ll pay your debt.

Followed by a verb such as 言う (say), 思う (think), 考える (think about) or a noun corresponding to one of these verbs. Expresses the speaker’s unexpected or scornful feeling towards what is said in the preceding clause along with the content of the speaker’s utterance and thought. This is a casual way of saying などと．
3. ...なんて［N／Na　（だ）なんて］［A／V　なんて］

content: 一家そろって海外旅行だなんて、うらやましいですね。

content.content: I envy you for being able to travel abroad with all your family.

content: あなたにそんなことを言うなんて、実にひどい男だ。

content.content: What a truly horrible man he is to say such a thing to you!

content: こんなところであなたに会うなんて、びっくりしましたよ。

content.content: It’s surprising to see you here.

content: こんな安い給料でまじめに働くなんて馬鹿らしい。

content.content: It’s ridiculous to work hard for this low pay.

content: あんな怠け者が一生懸命働きたいなんて、嘘にきまっているでしょう。

content.content: There’s no way such a lazy person like that would want to work hard!

content: この吹雪の中を出て行くなんて、命を捨てに行くようなものだ。

content.content: Venturing out in this blizzard is like throwing your life away.

Followed by an expression to show the speaker’s evaluation, such as うらやましい (envious) or ひどい (terrible), and indicates the thing/state/event to be evaluated. Often accompanies the speaker’s surprise, unexpectedness, or scornful feeling to consider a thing/person stupid or ridiculous. Used in casual speech.
【なんでも】
1. なんでも

content: ほしいものは何でも手に入る。

content.content: I can get anything I want.

content: 何でも好きなものを注文して下さい。

content.content: Please order anything you like.

content: あの人は植物の事なら何でも知っている。

content.content: That person knows everything about plants.
Expresses the meaning of “whatever,” “all kinds of things,” or “everything.”
2. なんでも...らしい／...そうだ

content: 何でも彼女はもうすぐ仕事をやめるそうですよ。

content.content: I hear she’s quitting her job soon.

content: うわさによると、何でも彼らは浜松に引っ越したという話だ。

content.content: There is a rumor that they’ve moved to Hamamatsu.

content: 何でもこの窪地は、隕石が落下したあとだということです。

content.content: I hear this hollow was created by a meteor.

content: 何でもこのあたりには幽霊が出るっていう話ですよ。

content.content: There’s talk that ghosts appear around here.
Followed by a hearsay expression such as らしい／そうだ／という話だ／ということだ, なんでも is used to convey something the speaker has heard but is unsure about.
3. なんでもないa. なんでもない

content: あの頃の苦労に比べればこんな苦労は何でもない。

content.content: This trouble is nothing compared with what I had at that time.

content: 何でもないことにそんなに大騒ぎするな。

content.content: Don’t make such a fuss about nothing.

content: この程度の仕事は彼女にとっては何でもないことです。

content.content: It is no trouble for her to do such work like this.

content: A:顔色が悪いけど気分でも悪いんじゃないですか。

content.content: You look pale—do you feel sick?
B:いいえ、何でもありません。大丈夫です。
No, it’s nothing.
Expresses the meaning “this is nothing that we should concern ourselves about” or “this is nothing serious.”
b. Nでもなんでもない

content: 病気でも何でもない。ただ怠けたくて休んでいただけだ。

content.content: I’m not sick or anything like that. I just feel lazy and like taking a rest.

content: こんなものは芸術でも何でもありません。だれだって少し練習すれば作れます。

content.content: This is not art at all. Anyone can create it with a little bit of practice.

content: お前とはもう友達でもなんでもない。二度と僕の前に顔を出さないでくれ。

content.content: I’m not a friend of yours any more. Never show yourself to me again.

content: 彼は政治家でもなんでもない。ただのペテン師だ。

content.content: He’s not a politician or anything like that. He’s just a fraud.

With a noun, emphasizes the meaning “that’s not what it is.” In many instances, there is positive value for the correct choice in the sentence, and by refuting that, でもなんでもない states the speaker’s negative evaluation more strongly.
4. なにがなんでも→
【なにがなんでも】
【なんと】
1. なんと

content: ご両親はなんとおっしゃっていましたか。

content.content: What did your parents say?

content: なんと言ってなぐさめてよいか分かりません。

content.content: I don’t know what to say to comfort you.

content: 報告書には何と書いてありましたか。

content.content: What did the report say?

content: 彼らには何と伝えればいいんでしょうか。

content.content: Whatever should I tell them?
Has the meaning of “by what means” or “how.” Followed by a verb such as 言う(say) or 書く(write) and means that the content expressed by such a verb is unclear.
2. なんと...のだろう［なんと...Nなのだろう］［なんとNa なのだろう］［なんとA-いのだろう］

content: なんと美しい人なのでしょう。

content.content: What a beautiful person she is!

content: 彼女の気持ちが理解できなかったなんて、俺はなんと馬鹿だったのだろう。

content.content: How stupid I was because I couldn’t understand her feelings!

content: 軽装で雪山に登るとは、何と無謀な若者たちなのだろう。

content.content: How reckless those young people were to climb a snow-covered mountain in light clothing!

Used to express the speaker’s exclamation towards what s/he thinks surprising, amazing, or marvelous. May be rephrased as なんてまあ. A somewhat formal expression. More typically, なんて...んだろう is used in spoken Japanese.
【なんという】
1. なんというN

content: あの人は何という名前ですか。

content.content: What is the name of that person?

content: その赤いのは何という花ですか。

content.content: What is the name of that red flower?
Used to ask for a name of a thing/person. In casual speech, it can be なんていうN.
2. なんという+連体修飾句+N

content: なんという馬鹿なやつだ。

content.content: What a fool he is!

content: 若いのになんという冷静沈着な人物なのだろう。

content.content: What a cool-headed person for her age!

content: 練習がつらいならやめてしまえだなんて、なんという思いやりのないことを言ってしまったのだろう。

content.content: How thoughtless of me to say to just quit if the practice was too hard.

content: 子供たちまで皆殺しにするなんて何という残虐な奴らだろう。

content.content: How cruel they are to kill everyone including children!

Followed by a noun which is modified by a clause or phrase, なんというN is used to express the speaker’s exclamation towards a thing/person/state with which s/he is surprised or amazed, or a thing/person/state which s/he admires. なんという often appears in the expression なんという...のだろう.
3. なんというNだ

content: こんな大きな石を一人で持ち上げられるなんて、何という男だ。

content.content: What a man he is to be able to lift a big rock like this!

content: 一瞬のうちにして、家族全部を失ってしまうなんて、なんということだ。

content.content: What a tragedy it is to lose all her family members in a matter of seconds!

content: 何ということだろう。月が真っ赤に染まっている。

content.content: How amazing! The moon has turned red.

content: 外国で同じバスに乗りあわせるなんて、何という偶然だろう。

content.content: What a coincidence to be seated on the same bus as you in a foreign country!
Used to express the speaker’s exclamation about something s/he is surprised with, amazed with, or in admiration of.
4. なんということもない

content: 何ということもなく、毎日が穏やかに過ぎて行く。

content.content: Every day passes peacefully with nothing out of the ordinary.

content: 特に何ということもない平凡な人間だ。

content.content: I am an ordinary person with no special ability.
Expresses the meaning that there is nothing remarkable to speak of.
【なんとか】
1. なんとか〈volitional〉

content: なんとかして山田さんを助け出そう。

content.content: Let’s save Yamada-san somehow.

content: このゴミの山を早くなんとかしないといけない。

content.content: We must somehow get rid of this pile of garbage soon.

content: 早くなんとか手を打たないと、大変なことになりますよ。

content.content: If we don’t do something immediately, the situation will get out of hand.

content: お忙しいことは承知していますが、何とか明日までに仕上げていただけないでしょうか。

content.content: Although I understand that you are busy, could you possibly manage to finish this by tomorrow?

content: A:あしたまでに仕上げるのはちょっと無理ですね。

content.content: It’s impossible for me to get it done by tomorrow.
B:そこを何とかできないでしょうか。何とかお願いしますよ。
Couldn’t you manage to do that somehow? I’d really appreciate it.
Followed by a verb with the meaning of trying all possible means to do something, such as なんとかする or なんとか手を打つ, expresses the meaning of “taking a certain action for something.”
In the expression なんとかして...する／しよう, as in

content: , expresses the meaning of finding a way out of some difficult situation by taking an action. When followed by some expression of request, as shown in
and
, implies the speaker’s request to be asking too much of the listener although the speaker understands the listener’s difficult situation.

content.content: 2. なんとか〈barely manage (to do something)〉

content: 安月給だがなんとか食べていくことはできる。

content.content: Despite my low salary, I can just eke out a living.

content: みなさんのご支援でなんとかここまで頑張ってやって来れました。

content.content: Thanks to all your support, I have managed to make it to this point.

content: 銀行が金を貸してくれると言うから、何とか倒産だけはまぬがれることができそうだ。

content.content: Since the bank told me that they would lend me money, it seems that I will somehow manage to at least avoid bankruptcy.

Followed by an expression with some potential form, expresses the meaning that one can somehow manage to do something despite a difficulty or insufficiency. See やっと (Usage 2) for differences between なんとか, どうにか, and やっと.
3. なんとかなる

content: そんなに心配しなくてもなんとかなりますよ。

content.content: Don’t worry, it will all work out somehow.

content: 二階の雨漏り、何とかならないかしら。

content.content: Can’t we do anything about the leaky roof on the second floor?

content: これだけ蓄えがあれば何とかなるだろう。

content.content: I guess we can get by on this much savings.
Expresses the meaning that one can change an unfavorable situation to a favorable one, or one can manage to make do although something is insufficient.
【なんとかいう】
1. なんとかいうa. なんとかいう

content: 私の言うことは聞こうとしないから、あなたから何とか言ってやって下さい。

content.content: Because she has no intention to listen to what I’m saying, please try to talk to her.

content: 黙っていないで何とか言ったらどうなんだ。

content.content: Don’t just sit there in silence—how about saying something?
なんとかいう is used when the speaker commands or ask to do something. It expresses the meaning of strongly asking the listener to speak out and at least say something. なんとかいう appears in spoken Japanese.
b. なんとかいうN

content: 大阪の何とかいう人から電話がありましたよ。

content.content: Mr. What’s-his-name from Osaka called you.

content: 以前佐藤さんが何とかいう学校に通っていただろう。あれはなんていう名前だったかな。

content.content: You know, Sato-san went to so-and-so school before. Do you remember the name of the school?
Used to refer to something or someone whose name is unknown by the speaker. Spoken Japanese.
2. ...とかなんとかいうa. NとかなんとかいうN

content: ポエムとか何とかという喫茶店で会うと言っていました。

content.content: He told me that he would meet her at a coffee shop called “Poem” or something.

content: 田中とか何とかいう男の人がたずねてきましたよ。

content.content: Mr. Tanaka, or someone called something like that, came to see you.
Expresses the meaning that the speaker has some idea about a name or a word but is unsure about it.
b. ...とかなんとかいう

content: あの男は給料が安いとかなんとか言って辞めたそうだ。

content.content: That man quit his job because the salary was low, or for some other reason.

content: 彼女は自信を失ったとか何とか言っていたようです。

content.content: I heard that she said she lost her confidence or something like that.

content: やりたくないとか何とか言っているようだが、本当はやってみたくてしかたがないんだ。

content.content: She says things like she doesn’t want to do it, but the truth is she can’t wait to try it.

Used when the speaker is uncertain about whether the content of the sentence is true or not. Expresses the meaning that one cannot solely specify something/someone because there are some others mentioned in previous utterances.
【なんとしても】

content: なんとしても彼には負けたくない。

content.content: I want to beat him no matter what it takes.

content: なんとしても彼に追いつくことができなかった。

content.content: Whatever I did, I couldn’t catch up with him.

content: なんとしても戦争の再発だけは防がなければならない。

content.content: We must prevent another war at all costs.
Expresses the meaning “even though one leaves no stone unturned” or “no matter how hard one works.” A formal, written way of saying どうしても.
【なんとなく】

content: なんとなく旅に出てみたくなりました。

content.content: I feel like taking a trip for some reason.

content: 彼と話していると、なんとなく気分が休まるんです。

content.content: I don’t know why, but it calms me down when I talk to him.

content: 何となく町をぶらついていて彼女に出会ったのです。

content.content: I met her when I was out just strolling around town.
Expresses the meaning “without any specific reason or purpose.”
【なんとはなしに】

content: なんとはなしに昔の友達に会って見たくなりました。

content.content: I feel like meeting my old friend for some reason.

content: 何とはなしに嫌な予感がするので、早く家に帰りました。

content.content: Because I had a kind of feeling that something bad would happen, I went home early.

content: 何とはなしに町を歩いていたら後ろから呼びとめられた。

content.content: When I was just wandering around town, a voice from behind told me to stop.
Same as なんとなく.
【なんとなく】
【なんとも】
1. なんとも

content: なんとも申し訳ないことをしてしまいました。

content.content: I did something very regrettable to you.

content: 何とも困ったことをしてくれたものだ。

content.content: You caused me so much trouble.

content: あいつの生意気な態度には、何とも腹がたって仕方がない。

content.content: That’s guy’s conceited attitude just burns me up!

content: 人が突然消えてしまうなんて、何とも不思議な話ですね。

content.content: What a strange story to hear about someone suddenly disappearing.
なんとも expresses the meaning that concerning some unfavorable situation, the speaker feels that the situation is extreme so that s/he does not know how to describe it.
2. なんとも...ないa. なんともV-ない

content: 結果がどうなるかはまだなんとも言えませんね。

content.content: There’s no telling yet what the result will be.

content: みんなは納得したかも知れないが、私は何とも釈然としない気持ちだ。

content.content: Although everyone might have been convinced, I’m still not totally satisfied.

content: 彼女の言っていることは何とも分かりかねる。

content.content: I can’t fully understand what she’s saying.

content: あんなことをする人たちの気持ちは何とも理解できない。

content.content: I just can’t understand how those people feel when they do such a thing.
With an expression such as 言えない or 分からない, expresses the speaker’s feeling that s/he does not know what to say, cannot understand some situation, or is not totally satisfied.
b. なんともV-ようがない

content: こんな事になって、なんともお詫びのしようがありません。

content.content: I cannot apologize to you enough for such a terrible incident.

content: 非常に複雑な状況なので、なんとも説明のしようがありません。

content.content: Because the situation is very complicated, there’s no way to explain it.

content: 成功するかどうか、今の段階では何とも言いようがない。

content.content: You never know at this point whether it will succeed or not.

content: 資料がこんなに少ないのでは、何とも判断のしようがありません。

content.content: There’s no way to make a judgment based on such limited data.
With an expression such as 言いようがない or 説明のしようがない, expresses the speaker’s feeling that s/he does not know what to say, cannot clearly understand some situation, or is not totally satisfied.

content: is idiomatic and expresses the speaker’s apologetic feeling. Expressions such as なんとお礼を言ってよいのか分かりません are more commonly used instead of なんとも to indicate the speaker’s gratitude.

content.content: c. なんともないなんともおもわない

content: A:気分が悪いんじゃありませんか。

content.content: Don’t you feel sick?
B:いいえ、なんともありません。ちょっと疲れただけです。
No, I’m fine. I’m just a little tired.

content: 軽い打ち身だけで、頭のけがは何ともありませんでした。

content.content: The injury on my head is not serious at all; it’s just a bruise.

content: A:あの映画、こわかったでしょう。

content.content: You must have been scared by that movie.
B:ううん。何ともなかったよ。
No, not at all.

content: 私がこんなに心配しているのに、彼の方は何とも思っていない様子でした。

content.content: Even though I’m worrying this much, he doesn’t seem to care at all.

content: こんなに馬鹿にされているのに、あなたは何とも感じないのですか。

content.content: Don’t you feel anything even though you’re made a fool of like this?

content: A:さっきはあんなこと言ってごめんなさい。

content.content: I’m sorry I said that a short while ago.
B:いや、別に何とも思ってないよ。
That’s OK, it doesn’t matter.

Means “it is nothing” or “there is not any particular problem.” Often used in relation to a health condition or emotional state. なんともない, when it appears in phrases such as 何とも思わない and 何とも感じない, means that the speaker does not think or feel that something is serious.
d. A-くもなんともない

content: そんな話は恐くも何ともないさ。

content.content: I’m not in the least terrified of such a story.

content: 彼の冗談はおもしろくも何ともない。

content.content: His joke isn’t funny at all.

content: 一人でいたって寂しくも何ともない。

content.content: Even if I’m alone, I never feel lonely.

content: 人の日記なんか読みたくも何ともないよ。

content.content: I don’t have the slightest interest to read someone’s diary.

content: そんなくだらないもの、ほしくも何ともない。

content.content: I never want that kind of trashy thing.

With an expression of feeling such as 恐い or おもしろい, or with an expression of desire such as したい or ほしい, A-くもなんともない expresses the speaker’s feeling of “that is not true” to negate something strongly. This is rephrased as まったく...ない or 全然...ない.
【なんにしても】

content: なんにしても健康が一番です。

content.content: Health is the most important after all.

content: なんにしてもこの場は引き上げたほうがいい。

content.content: Whatever the case, we’d better leave this place.

content: なんにしても年内に立ち退いてもらいます。

content.content: No matter what, I’d like you to move out by the end of this year.
Expresses the meaning “in any case, although there other possible scenarios.”
【なんにしろ】［Nはなんにしろ］

content: 事情は何にしろ、早く故障した部品を取りかえなければならない。

content.content: Whatever the circumstances are, we must replace the broken part as soon as possible.

content: 理由は何にしろ、あなたのやったことは間違っている。

content.content: Whatever the reason may be, what you did was wrong.

content: 理由は何にしろ、約束が果たせなかったことについては責任をとってもらいます。

content.content: Whatever the reason may be, I want you to take responsibility for breaking your promise.

Expresses the meaning “although there are various circumstances or reasons.” Used when the speaker warns, advises, or demands even though s/he recognizes there may be some extenuating circumstances or reasons.
【なんら...ない】
1. なんらV-ない
