content: 彼らがどう言おうと、私にはなんらかかわりのないことだ。

content.content: Whatever they say, this has nothing to do with me.

content: 彼の話からは何ら得るところがなかった。

content.content: There is nothing I could get out of his talk.

content: 我々がこれほど努力しているのに、状況は何ら変わらない。

content.content: Even though we are making efforts like this, the situation hasn’t changed at all.

なんらV-ない, appearing in contexts such as まったく...ない and 少しも...ない, expresses the speaker’s feeling to negate something strongly. Used in formal expressions. In spoken Japanese, なにも...ない is used more often.
2. なんらのNもV-ない

content: 彼らの対応にはなんらの誠意も感じられない。

content.content: I can’t see any sincerity at all in their dealings.

content: 住民の生活に対しては何らの配慮もなされていない。

content.content: There is no consideration taken for the life of the residents.

content: 彼らからは何らの回答も得られなかった。

content.content: I couldn’t get any answer at all from them.
Expresses the speaker’s feeling to negate something strongly. Used for formal expressions. In spoken Japanese, なんのNもV-ない is used more often.
1. R-にV

content: 待ちに待った帰国の日がついにやってきた。

content.content: The long-awaited day to return to my country has finally come.

content: 電車は遅れに遅れて、東京駅に着いたときは夜中を過ぎていた。

content.content: The train had a very long delay, so when we got to Tokyo Station, it was already past midnight.

content: 彼の死を悼んで、人々は泣きに泣いた。

content.content: People lamented his death, so they just cried and cried.
By repeating the same verb, emphasizes that a degree of an action or influence mentioned in the sentence is extreme. Often used in past contexts.
2. V-るにV-れない

content: 人手が足りないのでやめるにやめられない。

content.content: Because they are short of hands, I can’t quit my job now.

content: ものすごくおかしな話だったけど、みんながまじめな顔をして聞いているので、笑うに笑えなかった。

content.content: Although that was a very funny story, I couldn’t laugh because everyone was listening to it with such serious faces.

content: 戦時中は言うに言えない苦労をしてきた。

content.content: I was subjected to unspeakable hardships during the war.

content: 事業は失敗するし、妻には逃げられるし、全く泣くに泣けない気持ちだ。

content.content: Since my business failed and my wife left me, I’m too sad even to cry.

content: ここまで深入りしてしまっては、いまさら引くに引けない。

content.content: Because I am so involved in this, there’s no way I can pull back now.
By repeating the same verb, expresses the meaning “even though one wants to do it, it cannot be done” or “one cannot possibly do something.” V-るにV-れない in

content: are examples of idiomatic expressions, and those in
and
mean that the situation is too hard for a certain action to be taken, although the speaker wants to do it. V-るにV-れない in
expresses the situation where the speaker cannot stop doing it.

content.content: 【にあたって】［Nにあたって］［V-るにあたって］

content: 開会にあたってひとことご挨拶を申し上げます。

content.content: On the occasion of opening this meeting, I would like to give a few words of greeting.

content: 年頭にあたって集会を持ち、住民達の結束が揺るぎないものであることを確認しあった。

content.content: On the occasion of the New Year, we had a meeting to confirm that our solidarity as fellow residents was unshakable.

content: 試合に臨むにあたって、相手の弱点を徹底的に研究した。

content.content: Prior to the match, I thoroughly investigated my opponent’s weakness.

content: お嬢さんを嫁に出すにあたってのお気持ちはいかがでしたか。

content.content: How did you feel when you gave away your daughter in marriage?

content: 新しい生活を始めるにあたっての資金は、親の援助で何とか調達できた。

content.content: As for the expenses necessary to start my new life, I could manage to arrange for them with my parent’s support.

With a noun or the dictionary form of a verb, expresses the meaning of “facing an important time which can be considered a turning point of something, someone, or some state/event.” Similar to this expression is ...にさいして. にあたって is often used as a formal expression for a speech at a ceremony or in letters of thanks. A more formal expression which can be used in place of にあたって is ...にあたり(まして). When modifying a noun, にあたって changes its form to ...にあたってのN, as shown in

content: and

content.content: 【にあたらない】→
【にはあたらない】
【にあたり】［Nにあたり］［V-るにあたり］

content: 代表団の選出にあたり、被選挙人名簿を作成した。

content.content: On the occasion of selecting members of the delegation, I compiled a list of eligible people.

content: 今回の企画を実現するにあたりまして、皆様から多大のご支援を賜りましたことを感謝致します。

content.content: Upon the completion of this plan, I would like to thank you all for your tremendous support.
にあたり is a more formal way of saying にあたって.
【にあたって】
【にあって】
1. Nにあって

content: 異国の地にあって、仕事を探すこともままならない。

content.content: Being in a foreign country, it isn’t easy looking for a job.

content: 住民代表という立場にあって、寝る時間も惜しんでその問題に取り組んでいる。

content.content: As a representative of the residents, I am tackling the problem sparing little time for sleep.

content: 大臣という職にあって、不正を働いていたとは許せない。

content.content: For someone in the position of a minister, committing an injustice is inexcusable.

content: 母は病床にあって、なおも子供達のことを気にかけている。

content.content: Even from her sickbed, my mother is caring for her children.

With a noun, expresses the meaning of “under the circumstance mentioned in the noun.” The relationship between the circumstance and the thing/state/event stated in the following is not always fixed. Depending on the contexts before and after the expression, it can be adversative or sequential. The sentences in

content: and
are adversative examples, whereas those in
and
are sequential examples. にあって in
and
means “even in the circumstance/although under the circumstance.”

content.content: 2. Nにあっても

content: 彼は苦境にあっても、めげずに頑張っている。

content.content: Even with hardships, he’s doing his best without giving up.

content: 暖かい家庭の中にあっても、彼女の心は満たされなかった。

content.content: Even with her warmhearted family, she felt dissatisfied.

content: 母は死の間際にあっても、子供達の幸福を願い続けた。

content.content: Even on her deathbed, the mother kept wishing for her children’s happiness.

With a noun, expresses the meaning of “even under the circumstances stated in the noun.” Followed by some state/event which contradicts what can normally be expected under such circumstances. A formal, written expression.
3. Nにあっては〈circumstances〉

content: こんな厳寒の地にあっては、新鮮な野菜が食卓に上るなど、滅多にないことだ。

content.content: In such a bitterly cold place, it’s rare for fresh vegetables to make it to the table.

content: いつ戦争が起こるか知れない状況にあっては、明るい未来を思い描くことなどできない。

content.content: In a situation where one never knows when a war might break out, it’s difficult to imagine a bright future.

content: 夫が病床にあっては、子供達に十分な教育を受けさせることもできなかった。

content.content: Since my husband was ill in bed, I couldn’t have my children receive an adequate education.

content: わが社にあっては、若者が自由に発言できる雰囲気を大切にしている。

content.content: In our company, we value an atmosphere in which young employees can speak out freely.

content: 「鉄の女」といわれた彼女も家庭にあっては良き母であった。

content.content: Even the woman called “the Iron Lady” was a good mother at home.

With a noun expressing a place or circumstances, expresses the meaning of “under the circumstances stated in the sentence.” This is similar to ...において. When an expression which shows some difficult situation, such as 厳寒の地 (bitterly cold place) or 病床(sickbed) is used with にあっては, expressions of some unfavorable circumstances follow. If this is not the case, にあっては simply expresses the meaning of “at, in, as for” as shown in

content: and
. This is a formal, written expression.

content.content: 4. Nにあっては〈person〉

content: 高橋さんにあっては、どんな強敵でも勝てそうにありませんね。

content.content: When it comes to Takahashi-san, she can’t lose no matter how strong her opponent is.

content: あの男にあっては、嘘もまことと言いくるめられる。油断は禁物だ。

content.content: Talking about that man, he can wheedle you into believing his lies. You don’t dare let down your guard.

content: あなたにあってはかなわないな。しょうがない。お望み通りに致しましょう。

content.content: No one can get the better of you. OK, OK. I’ll do what you want.
With a noun expressing a person, used to assess the person who cannot be beaten by anybody else. The sentence in

content: is uttered when the speaker cannot decline the listener’s adroit invitation or assertive demand, and may contain a slight shade of meaning that the speaker is teasing the hearer. にあっては can be rephrased with ...にかかっては.

content.content: 【にいたる】にいたる is a formal, written expression.
1. ...にいたる［N／V　にいたる］

content: この川は大草原を横切って流れ、やがては海に至る。

content.content: This river runs across a vast grassland and eventually flows into the ocean.

content: 彼はトントン拍子で出世を続け、やがて大蔵大臣になるに至る。

content.content: His career advanced rapidly and he ultimately became the Minister of Finance.

content: 仕事を辞めて留学するに至った動機は、人生の目標というものを見つめなおしてみたいと思ったことであった。

content.content: The motivation behind why I quit the job and went abroad to study was that I wanted to reconsider my goals in life again.

content: さんざん悩んだ結果、仕事を辞めて田舎で自給自足の生活をするという結論に至った。

content.content: The end result of all my worrying was a decision to quit my job and lead a self-sufficient life in the country.
Expresses the meaning “to reach, to lead to.” Can be a spatial meaning such as reaching a certain place, as shown in

content: , or can be an abstract meaning such as reaching some stage or conclusion as a result of some change of thing/state/even or thought. にいたる is a formal, written expression.

content.content: 2. Nにいたるまで

content: 旅行中に買ったものからハンドバッグの中身に至るまで、厳しく調べられた。

content.content: Everything―from what I had bought during the trip to the contents of my handbag―was intently examined.

content: 部長クラスから新入社員に至るまで、すべての社員に特別手当が支給された。

content.content: A special remuneration was paid to all—from the department heads on down to the new employees.

content: テレビの普及によって、東京などの大都市から地方の村々に至るまで、ほぼ同じような情報が行き渡るようになった。

content.content: With the spread of television, essentially the same information has come to be sent everywhere, from large cities like Tokyo to rural villages.
Expresses almost the same meaning as Nまで. However, Nにいたるまで is used to mention things/states/events in great detail. This expression is often used with ...から．
3. ...にいたって［N／V　にいたって］

content: 編集段階に至って、初めて撮影したビデオの映像が使いものにならないことがわかったが、すでに遅かった。

content.content: Not until we got to the editing stage did we first realize that the video we’d shot was useless, but then it was already too late.

content: 上司にはっきり注意されるに至って、ようやく自分の言葉遣いに問題があることに気づいた。

content.content: It was not until my boss warned me explicitly that I realized that I had a problem with my way of speaking.

content: 卒業するに至って、やっと大学に入った目的が少し見えてきたような気がする。

content.content: When I was about to graduate, I felt I finally could see something of the goals I had in entering a university.
N/Vにいたって expresses the meaning “only when it comes to some extreme stage indicated by N/V.” This expression is often followed by words such as ようやく, やっと and 初めて.
4. Nにいたっては

content: 父も母も私の転職に大反対し、姉にいたっては、そんなことより早く結婚しろと言い出す始末だった。

content.content: Both my father and mother are totally against my changing jobs, and what’s more, my elder sister finally ended up saying that it was more important for me to get married quickly.

content: 首相が代わってからというもの、住宅問題も教育問題も手付かずで、軍事面にいたっては予算が増加する一方である。

content.content: After the prime minister was replaced, housing and educational problems have not been touched on, and to boot, the budget for military affairs keeps increasing.

content: 不登校の生徒に対して、どの教師も何の対応もしようとせず、教頭にいたってはどこかよその学校に転校してもらえたらなどと言う始末である。

content.content: No teachers try to deal with truants at all, and even worse is the vice-principal, who ends up saying that she hopes they will transfer to another school somewhere else.

content: ことここにいたっては、家庭裁判所に仲裁を頼むしかないのではないだろうか。

content.content: Since the problem has come to this stage, there isn’t anything else to do but ask a family court to mediate, right?
Used to mention the most extreme case among some negative things/states/events. ことここにいたっては as in

content: is an idiomatic expression that means “when the problem becomes as serious as this.”

content.content: 5. ...にいたっても［N／V　にいたっても］

content: 投票率が史上最低という事態に至っても、なお自分たちが国民から信頼されていると信じて疑わない政治家も少なくない。

content.content: Quite a few politicians are convinced that people still trust them, even if the voting percentages for them are the lowest in history.

content: 大学を卒業するに至っても、まだ自分の将来の目的があやふやな若者が大勢いる。

content.content: Even when they are about to graduate from university, there are many young people whose future goals are still hazy.

content: 高校での成績が下から10番以内にまで下がるに至っても、両親は僕に東京大学を受験させたがった。

content.content: Even when my grades in high school dropped to among the worst ten, my parents wanted me to take the entrance exam for Tokyo University.
Expresses the meaning “even when it reaches some extreme stage.” Often followed by words like まだ, なお or いまだに.
【にいわせれば】［Nにいわせれば］

content: あの人に言わせれば、こんな辞書はまったく使いものにならないということらしい。

content.content: According to him, this dictionary seems to be totally useless.

content: 映画好きのいとこに言わせれば、この映画は映像と音楽が見事に調和した、素晴らしい作品だという話だ。

content.content: According to my cousin, who likes movies, this movie was an excellent piece of work in which the picture and music harmonize very well with each other.

content: あなたは気に入っているかもしれないが、私に言わせればそんな作品は素人のお遊びみたいなものだ。

content.content: You may like it, but if I may say so, this work is that of an amateur at play.

content: 彼に言わせると、今度見つかった恐竜の化石は、進化の歴史を変えるかもしれないような重要なものなんだそうだ。

content.content: According to him, the dinosaur fossil which has recently been found is so important that it may change evolutionary history.
With a noun expressing a person, means “according to the person.” Used to state that the view is supported by the speaker’s firm confidence.
【において】
1. Nにおいて〈circumstances〉

content: 卒業式は大講堂において行われた。

content.content: The graduation ceremony took place in the auditorium.

content: その時代において、女性が学問を志すのは珍しいことであった。

content.content: It was very rare for women to receive an education in those days.

content: 調査の過程において様々なことが明らかになった。

content.content: In the process of the survey, various things were revealed.

content: 日本の物理学会において、彼の右に出る者（＝彼より優れている者）はいない。

content.content: In the Japan Society of Physics, no one can match him (= (there is no one) who is superior to him).

content: 当時の状況において戦争反対を訴えるのは限りなく勇気のいることだった。

content.content: Under the circumstances in those days, it was extremely daring to take a stand opposing the war.

With a noun expressing a place, time, or circumstances, describes some background of an event or a state which occurs. Can often be rephrased as で as exemplified in 大講堂で (in the auditorium). However, において gives the impression that this is more formal than で. When において modifies the following noun, it becomes NにおけるN, as in 大講堂における式典 (ceremony in the auditorium) .
2. Nにおいて〈domain〉

content: 絵付けの技術において彼にかなうものはいない。

content.content: With regard to painting on china, there is no comparison with his skills.

content: 大筋においてその意見は正しい。

content.content: Basically, that view is correct.

content: 造形の美しさにおいてはこの作品が優れている。

content.content: As for beauty in form, this work is superior to all others.

content: 資金援助をするという点においては賛成だが、自衛隊を派遣するという点においては強く反対する。

content.content: I agree with the idea of financial support, but I strongly disagree with the idea to dispatch the Self-Defense Forces there.
Expresses the meaning of “as for N” or “in N’s respect.” Often followed by an expression to evaluate the thing/state/event in N or to compare it with another.
【におうじた】→
【におうじて】
【におうじて】［Nにおうじて］

content: 物価の変動に応じて給料を上げる。

content.content: We raise wages in proportion to any fluctuation in prices.

content: 売行きに応じて生産量を加減する。

content.content: We adjust the amount of production in proportion to our sales.

content: 状況に応じて戦法を変える。

content.content: We change our tactics depending on the situation.

content: 状況に応じた戦法をとる。

content.content: We choose a tactic according to the situation.

content: 功績に応じた報酬を与える。

content.content: We remunerate them in proportion to their accomplishments.

Expresses the meaning of “corresponding to a change in state or variability.” Followed by expressions meaning “a certain change happens in accordance with N,” such as 加減する(adjust) or 戦法を変える(change tactics) . When it modifies a noun, Nにおうじて becomes NにおうじたN, as exemplified in

content: and

content.content: 【におかれましては】［Nにおかれましては］

content: 先生におかれましては、お元気そうでなによりです。

content.content: I am most pleased to hear that you are well.

content: 先生におかれましては、ますます御壮健の由、私ども一同喜んでおります。

content.content: We are all pleased to hear that you are more and more in good health.
With a noun expressing someone superior, used to ask or tell him/her about his/her health or recent conditions. This is a very formal idiomatic expression used in letters.
【における】［NにおけるN］

content: 過去における過ちを謝罪する。

content.content: I apologize for my grave mistake in the past.

content: 在職中における功労が認められた。

content.content: My contribution at work was recognized.

content: 学校における母語の使用が禁止された。

content.content: The use of native languages has been prohibited at school.
Used to modify the following noun and expresses a place, time or a situation which contextualizes a certain state. In a context like

content: , における can be rephrased as での when it expresses some background of an event, but it should be noted that における sounds more formal than での. Becomes において when modifying a verb, as in 過去において過ちを犯した (made a grave mistake in the past).

content.content: 【にかかったら】→
【にかかっては】
【にかかっては】［Nにかかっては］

content: 彼の毒舌にかかっては社長も太刀打ちできない。

content.content: Even the company president can’t match his sharp tongue.

content: あなたにかかっては私も嫌とは言えなくなる。

content.content: To hear you tell it, I can’t say no.

content: 彼女にかかってはいつもしらないうちにイエスと言わされてしまう。

content.content: She always makes me say yes without my noticing it.

With a noun expressing a person or behavior, にかかっては indicates the person or the behavior, followed by an expression to mean that no one can match him/her or his/her behavior including what s/he said. にかかっては can be rephrased as にあっては. However, にかかっては is different from にあっては in that the former is used to imply a viewpoint of someone who perceives no comparison with the person or the behavior expressed in にかかっては.
（○）私にかかっては社長も太刀打ちできないさ。
I tell you even the company president can’t match me.
（×）私にあっては社長も太刀打ちできないさ。
I tell you even the company president can’t match me.
にかかっては can change to にかかったら or にかかると.
【にかかると】→
【にかかっては】
【にかかわらず】
1. Nにかかわらず

content: 試合は晴雨にかかわらず決行する。

content.content: The match will be played whether it rains or not.

content: 性別にかかわらず優れた人材を確保したい。

content.content: We want to secure talented people, regardless of sex.

content: このクラブは年齢や社会的地位にかかわらず、どなたでも参加できます。

content.content: Regardless of age or social status, anybody can join this club.
With a noun which implies a certain range of differences such as weather, sex, or age, expresses the meaning of “regardless of such differences” or “without considering such differences.”
2. ...にかかわらず［V-る V-ないにかかわらず］［A-い A-くないにかかわらず］

content: 経験のあるなしにかかわらず、だれでも参加することができる。

content.content: Whether someone has experience or not, he or she can participate.

content: 結果の善し悪しにかかわらず彼の努力は評価されるだろう。

content.content: Whether the result is good or bad, his effort will be appreciated.

content: 成功するしないにかかわらず、努力することに意義があると思う。

content.content: Whether you succeed or not, I think it’s worthwhile working hard.

content: 父が賛成するかしないかにかかわらず、私はこの仕事に就こうと思う。

content.content: Whether my dad is in favor of it or not, I plan to take this job.

With an expression to indicate two opposing things/states/events, expresses the meaning of “regardless of these two” or “without considering these two as a problem.” When used as an idiomatic expression such as 経験のあるなし(having experience or not) or 結果の善し悪し(outcome being good or bad), the subject of the clause is marked by の. Otherwise, it is normally marked by が. As shown in

content: , にかかわらず can appear in phrases such as ...か...ないか.

content.content: 【にかかわる】［Nにかかわる］

content: 人の命にかかわる仕事をするにはそれなりの覚悟がいる。

content.content: When you have a job that affects whether people live or die, you need to be ready for anything.

content: こんなひどい商品を売ったら店の評判にかかわる。

content.content: Selling such poor products affects our shop’s reputation.

content: 例の議員が武器の密輸に関係していたかどうかはっきりさせなければならない。これは政党の名誉にかかわる重大な問題だ。

content.content: We should make it clear whether the councilor in question was involved in smuggling arms. This is an important matter which affects the party’s honor.

content: たとえ噂でも倒産しそうだなどという話が広まると、会社の存続にかかわる。

content.content: If a rumor goes around that the company is about to go bankrupt, it affects the continuing existence of the company.

content: あんな人にいつまでもかかわっていたら、あなたまで評判を落としてしまいますよ。

content.content: If you continue to be mixed up with such a person, you will hurt your reputation, too.

content: この裁判にかかわって以来、子どもの人権について深く考えるようになった。

content.content: Since I began to be involved in this trial, I have been thinking deeply about children’s human rights.

content: 事件が起きてから十年たった。いつまでもこの事件にかかわっているわけにはいかないが、いまだに犯人はつかまっていない。

content.content: It is ten years since this incident happened. I can’t be involved in it forever, but the culprit has not been arrested yet.
Expresses the meaning of “to affect” or “to be involved.” にかかわる in

content: means “to affect,” and the noun is chosen to express something influential such as 名誉 (honor), 評判 (reputation), 生死 (life and death) or 合否 (pass or failure). In contrast, にかかわる in
means “to be involved” or “to be linked,” and the noun is used to express a person, profession, or an incident.

にかぎったことではない

content.content: 【にかぎったことではない】→
【かぎる】2
【にかけたら】［Nにかけたら］

content: スピードにかけたら、その投手の右に出る者はいない。

content.content: That pitcher is second to none in speed.

content: 記憶力にかけたら、彼女は学校中の学生の中で5本の指に入るだろう。

content.content: As for good memory, she is probably among the top five students in the whole school.
Expresses the meaning of “concerning something.” Can be rephrased as Nにかけては.
【にかけて】2
【にかけて】
1. NからNにかけて

content: 台風は今晩から明日の朝にかけて上陸するもようです。

content.content: The typhoon will probably hit land some time between tonight and tomorrow morning.

content: 今月から来月にかけて休暇をとるつもりだ。

content.content: I intend to take a holiday from this month to next month.

content: 北陸から東北にかけての一帯が大雪の被害に見舞われた。

content.content: They were hard hit by a heavy snow throughout the Hokuriku and Tohoku districts.

With a noun expressing a place or time, means “between/over the two places or times.” When it indicates time, there are two cases. One is that にかけて refers to a particular moment between the two, as shown in

content: , and the other is that it refers to the time over the two, as shown in

. にかけて has uses similar to those for ...から...まで(に). However, にかけて is used when the speaker is not overly concerned with the time or space between or over the two mentioned in the sentence or about clearly-defined boundaries.

content.content: 2. Nにかけて

content: 話術にかけては彼の右にでるものはいない。

content.content: No one can match him in story-telling.

content: 忍耐力にかけては人より優れているという自信がある。

content.content: I have confidence that I surpass all others in patience.

content: 彼は誠実な男だが、商売にかけての才能はあまり期待できない。

content.content: He is a man of sincerity, but when it comes to his business ability, he doesn’t meet our expectations.
Expresses the meaning of “concerning something.” Often followed by an expression to state some evaluation for a skill or ability. Becomes NにかけてのN, as shown in

content: , when modifying a noun.

content.content: 3. Nにかけて（も）

content: 命にかけてもこの秘密は守り通す。

content.content: I pledge my life to keep this secret.

content: 私の命にかけて、彼らを助け出してみせます。

content.content: I pledge my life to save them.

content: 面子にかけても約束は守る。

content.content: On my honor, I will keep my promise.

An idiomatic expression. With a noun expressing something which assures someone’s existence or value socially, such as 命 (life), 名誉 (honor), 信用 (trust) or 面子 (face), used to express the speaker’s firm determination and means “even if it is risked” or “at all costs.” Followed by an expression showing the speaker’s determination or promise.
【にかこつけて】［Nにかこつけて］

content: 仕事にかこつけてヨーロッパ旅行を楽しんできた。

content.content: I enjoyed traveling Europe under the pretext of being on a business trip.

content: 病気にかこつけて仕事もせずにぶらぶらしている。

content.content: She is lazing around without working under the pretext of being sick.

content: 接待にかこつけて上等な酒を思いっきり飲んできた。

content.content: I drank all the quality liquor I wanted under the pretext of entertaining a business acquaintance.
With a noun expressing a thing/state/event, expresses the meaning of “under the pretext of doing something even though it is not a direct reason or cause.”
【にかたくない】［Nにかたくない］

content: このままインフレが続くと社会不安が増大し、政権の基盤が危うくなることは想像にかたくない。

content.content: It is not difficult to imagine that social unrest will increase and political foundations will be shaken if inflation continues like this.

content: 親からも教師からも見放された太郎が、非行グループの誘いに救いを求めそうになっただろうことは想像に難くない。

content.content: It is not difficult to imagine that Taro, whom his parents and teacher gave up on, was probably about to jump at the tempting offer from the juvenile gang.

content: なぜ彼があのような行動に走ったのか、事件の前後の事情をよく聞いてみれば理解にかたくない。

content.content: If you listen carefully to the situations before and after the incident, it is easy to understand why he took such an action.
Usually used in phrases such as 想像／理解にかたくない (not difficult to imagine/understand) idiomatically. It means that one can imagine easily or it is obvious for everyone. A formal, written expression.
【にかまけて】［Nにかまけて］

content: 仕事にかまけてちっとも子供の相手をしてやらない。

content.content: She is too busy at her work to take care of her child.

content: 遊びにかまけて勉強しようともしない。

content.content: He is too busy playing to try to study.

content: 資料の整理にばかりかまけていては、仕事は前へ進まない。

content.content: I am very busy just sorting the materials, so my work doesn’t progress.

With a noun expressing a thing/state/event, expresses the meaning that someone devotes his/her energies to something without looking at other things. Often followed by some negative expression meaning that the other things are disregarded and neglected.
【にかわって】［Nにかわって］

content: 母にかわって、私があいさつします。

content.content: I’ll make a greeting on behalf of my mother.

content: 急病の母にかわって、父が出席した。

content.content: My father went in place of my mother, who was stricken with a sudden sickness.

content: 本日ご出席いただけなかった山田さんに代わって、ご家族の方に賞状と副賞を受け取っていただきます。

content.content: On behalf of Yamada-san, who could not be here today, I would like a member of her family to receive a certificate of accomplishment and a supplementary prize.

content: 21世紀には、これまでの先進諸国に代わって、アジア諸国が世界をリードするようになるのではないだろうか。

content.content: Isn’t it the case that in the 21st century, Asian countries will take the lead in the world instead of those advanced countries that have led until now?

content: 山田さんが立候補を辞退するとなると、彼女に代わる実力者を立てなければならない。

content.content: If Yamada-san withdraws as a candidate, we have to recommend another capable person in her place.
Expresses the meaning that someone takes action on behalf of the person who was to have done so. When it modifies a noun, becomes NにかわるN. Can be rephrased as ...のかわりに．
【にかわり】［Nにかわり］

content: 急病の母にかわり、父が出席いたします。

content.content: My father will be present on behalf of my mother, who was stricken with a sudden sickness.

content: 21世紀には、これまでの先進諸国に代わり、アジア諸国が世界をリードする立場に立つという予測があるが、まだ未知数の部分が多いと言わざるを得ない。

content.content: It is predicted that in the 21st century, Asian countries will take the lead in the world instead of the other advanced countries; however, we must say that the outlook for such an outcome is still uncertain.
にかわり is a formal, written expression of ...にかわって.
【にかわって】
【にかわる】→
【にかわって】
【にかんして】［Nにかんして］

content: その事件に関して学校から報告があった。

content.content: We received a report on the incident from school.

content: 地震災害に関しては、我が国は多くの経験と知識をもっている。

content.content: With regard to the disaster caused by earthquakes, our country has considerable experience and knowledge.

content: その問題に関して質問したいことがある。

content.content: I have a question to ask concerning this matter.

content: 地質学に関しての本を読んでいる。

content.content: I’m reading a book on geology.

content: その事件に関しての報告はまだ受けていない。

content.content: I haven’t received any report of the incident yet.

content: コンピュータに関する彼の知識は相当なものだ。

content.content: His knowledge concerning computers is considerable.

content: 地質調査に関する報告をするように求められた。

content.content: I was asked to report on the geological survey.
Expresses the meaning of “concerning something” or “as to something.” Becomes Nに関してのN or NにかんするN, as shown in

content: , when it modifies a noun. A little more formal than について.

content.content: 【にかんする】→
【にかんして】
【にきまっている】［N／A／V　にきまっている］

content: こんないたずらをするのはあいつにきまっている。

content.content: I’m sure he’s the guy who would pull such a stunt.

content: きっと彼も参加したがるに決まっている。

content.content: I bet that he wants to join in.

content: そんなことを言ったら彼女が気を悪くするに決まっているじゃないか。

content.content: If you say such a thing, isn’t it likely she’ll get really upset?

content: A:田辺さん、ちゃんと時間にまにあったかしら。

content.content: I wonder if Tanabe-san arrived in time.
B:30分も遅く出ていったのだから、遅刻したに決まっているじゃないの。
She left thirty minutes late, so she must have arrived late.

Expresses the speaker’s conviction that something must be the case. When the speaker asserts his/her conviction contradicting the listener’s, にきまっている becomes に決まっているじゃない（か／の）. An expression in spoken Japanese.
【にくい】［R-にくい］

content: あの人の話は発音が不明瞭で分かりにくい。

content.content: It’s hard to understand what he says because his pronunciation isn’t clear.

content: 砂利道はハイヒールでは歩きにくい。

content.content: It’s hard to walk on a gravel path wearing high heels.

content: 人前ではちょっと話しにくい内容なのです。

content.content: This matter is a little bit difficult to talk about in public.

content: あんなえらい先生のところにはなかなか相談に行きにくい。

content.content: It’s fairly difficult to go consult with such a high-ranking professor.

Conjugates in the same way as i-adjectives. With the stem of a verb, expresses the meaning that something is hard to do or not easily done. Used when something is physically hard to achieve, as shown in

content: and
, or when it is psychologically hard to accomplish, as shown in
and
. Except for examples such as 分かりにくい(difficult to understand), にくい is preceded by a verb of volitional action such as 歩く(walk) or 話す(talk).

content.content: （×）あの人は喜びにくい人です。
That person is difficult to please.
（○）あの人を喜ばせるのはむずかしい。
It is difficult to please that person.
There is also an expression which shows the opposite meaning: R-やすい.
【にくらべて】［Nにくらべて］［Vのにくらべて］

content: 例年に比べて今年は野菜の出来がいい。

content.content: The vegetables this year are better compared with those in years past.

content: 男性に比べて女性の方が柔軟性があると言われる。

content.content: It is said that women have more flexibility than men.

content: パソコンを使うと、手で書くのに比べて字もきれいだし早い。

content.content: When you use a personal computer, the print is neater and more quickly written compared with that written by hand.

content: 大都市間を移動するのに比べて、田舎の町へ行くのは何倍も時間がかかる。

content.content: Traveling to a town in the countryside takes us several times longer than traveling between big cities.

content: 東京に比べると大阪の方が物価が安い。

content.content: Compared with Tokyo, the cost of living in Osaka is less expensive.

content: ジョギングに比べると、水泳は全身運動で身体にもいいということだ。

content.content: I hear that compared with jogging, swimming makes you use the entire body and is good for your health.
Used in the pattern of XにくらべてY or XにくらべるとY to discuss Y in comparison with X. May be rephrased as XよりY.
【にくらべると】→
【にくらべて】
【にくわえ】［Nにくわえ］

content: 激しい風にくわえ、大雨に見舞われて、被害が拡大した。

content.content: In addition to the strong winds, heavy rain caused further damage.

content: 学生たちは日々の課題にくわえ、毎週週明けにはレポート提出を義務付けられていた。

content.content: In addition to their daily assignments, the students were required to submit a paper every Monday.
A formal, written expression equivalent to ...にくわえて.
【にくわえて】
【にくわえて】［Nにくわえて］

content: 激しい風にくわえて、雨もひどくなってきた。

content.content: In addition to strong winds, it started to rain more heavily.

content: 学生たちは毎日の宿題にくわえて毎週レポートを出さなければならなかった。

content.content: In addition to their daily assignments, the students had to submit a paper every week.

content: ふたりは、子供の誕生に加えて、仕事も順調に進み、幸せで一杯の毎日を送っている。

content.content: In addition to the birth of a baby, their jobs are going smoothly, so the couple’s days are filled with happiness.

content: その地場産業は、国内需要の低迷に加えて安価な外国製品の流入に押されて、苦しい状態が続いている。

content.content: Besides suffering from the decreased domestic demand, the local industry has been faced with difficulties because of the inflow of inexpensive foreign products.
Expresses the meaning that some thing/state/event is not completed by itself but is complemented by another thing/state/event. A slightly formal, written expression.
【にこしたことはない】［Nであるにこしたことはない］［Na （である）にこしたことはない］［A-いにこしたことはない］［V-るにこしたことはない］

content: 体はじょうぶにこしたことはない。

content.content: Keeping your health is always better.

content: 金はあるにこしたことはない。

content.content: Money is never unnecessary.

content: そうじのことを考えないかぎり、家は広いにこしたことはない。

content.content: As long as you don’t think about cleaning, spacious houses are always better.

content: なにごとも慎重にやるにこしたことはないといつも私に言っている父が、きのう階段から落ちて足を折った。

content.content: My father, who had kept saying to me that things should always be done carefully, fell down the stairs and broke his leg.
Expresses the meaning of “...is better.” This expression is often used to indicate something naturally considered as common knowledge.
【にこたえ】［Nにこたえ］

content: その青年は人々の期待にこたえ、大きな熊を撃ち取った。

content.content: In line with people’s expectations, the young man shot a big bear.

content: 消費者の声に応え、従来より操作が簡単な製品を開発する方針だ。

content.content: To satisfy the demand of customers, we plan to develop a product which they can operate more easily previous ones.
A formal, written expression of ...にこたえて.
【にこたえて】
【にこたえて】［Nにこたえて］

content: その選手は両親の期待にこたえてみごとに完走した。

content.content: The athlete met the expectations of her parents and reached her goal splendidly.

content: 多数の学生の要望に応えまして、日曜日も図書館を開館することにしました。

content.content: In order to fulfill the demand of many students, we have decided to open the library on Sundays, too.

content: 多くの消費者の皆様のご意見にお応えして、この程、より使いやすい製品を発売いたしました。

content.content: To satisfy the needs of many customers, we recently launched a new product which is even more user-friendly.

content: 国連からの要請に応えて、政府は救援チームを派遣することにした。

content.content: To comply with a request from the United Nations, the government has decided to dispatch a rescue corps there.

content: 多くのファンの声援に応える完璧なプレーをなしとげた。

content.content: He finally demonstrated a perfect shot in answer to the cheers of his many fans.
With a noun expressing “expectation” or “request,” にこたえて expresses the meaning of “to realize something.” Becomes NにこたえるN when modifying a noun. A rather formal, written expression.
【にさいし】［Nにさいし］［V-るにさいし］

content: 今回の合併に際し、大規模な合理化が行われた。

content.content: On the occasion of this merger, an extensive streamlining took place.

content: 会長選出に際し不正が行われたとの噂がある。

content.content: There is a rumor that some irregularities occurred in the election for the chairperson.
A formal, written expression of ...にさいして.
【にさいして】
【にさいして】［Nにさいして］［V-るにさいして］

content: お別れに際して一言ご挨拶を申し上げます。

content.content: Upon the occasion of parting, I would like to say a few words.

content: 今回の初来日に際して、大統領は通商代表団を伴ってきた。

content.content: On this first visit to Japan, the President has come with a team of business representatives.

content: この度の大規模なアジア現代美術展を開催するに際して、各国の多数のアーティストの協力と参加を得られたことには大きな意義がある。

content.content: On the opening of this large-scale exhibition of modern Asian art, it is of great significance that we have been supported by the cooperation and participation of many artists from various countries.

content: 長年の懸案であった平和条約を締結するに際して、両国はお互いの歴史認識を深め合う意義を改めて認識すべきである。

content.content: At the conclusion of this peace treaty which has been pending for many years, both countries should recognize the significance of the deepening of our understanding of each other’s history.

content: 今回の会議参加に際しての最大の懸案事項はやはり安全保証問題であろう。

content.content: The problem of the security pact is the most important item at this meeting in which we are participating.
Expresses the meaning of “on some occasion.” Becomes N/V-るにさいしてのN when modifying a noun. A formal, written expression.
【にさきだち】［Nにさきだち］［V-るにさきだち］

content: 実験にさきだち、入念なチェックを行った。

content.content: Before the experiment, I checked everything thoroughly.

content: 出陣に先立ち神に祈りをささげた。

content.content: Prior to my departure for the front, I offered a prayer to God.
A formal, written expression of さきだって.
【にさきだって】
【にさきだって】［Nにさきだって］［V-るにさきだって］

content: 試験開始にさきだって、注意事項を説明する。

content.content: Before starting the exam, I will explain some points of caution.

content: 首相来日に先だって、事務次官レベルの事前協議が始まった。

content.content: Prior to the prime minister’s visit to Japan, advance deliberations among administrative vice-ministers had started.

content: 開会を宣言するに先だって、今回の災害の犠牲者に黙祷を捧げたいと思います。

content.content: Before I begin my address to mark the opening of this conference, I would like to offer a silent prayer for the victims of this disaster.

content: 交渉を始めるに先だって、お互いの内政問題を議題にしないという暗黙の合意が両国の間にできたようだ。

content.content: Before entering into negotiations, they seem to have agreed tacitly that they would not list the internal affairs of each other’s country on the agenda.

Expresses the meaning of “before starting something.” Used to state some action which should be performed prior to something. When it modifies a noun, にさきだって becomes NにさきだつN. However, there is no pattern such as V-るにさきだつN．
（○）首相来日に先立つ事前協議が始まった。
Advance deliberations prior to the prime minister’s visit to Japan have started.
（×）首相が来日するに先立つ事前協議が始まった。
Advance deliberations prior to the prime minister’s visit to Japan have started.
【にしたがい】［Nにしたがい］［V-るにしたがい］

content: 引率者の指示に従い行動すること。

content.content: All actions are to follow the leader’s instructions.

content: 上昇するに従い気温が上がる。

content.content: The temperature rises as you go up.
A formal, written expression of にしたがって.
【にしたがって】
【にしたがって】
1. Nにしたがって

content: 引率者の指示にしたがって行動して下さい。

content.content: Please act according to the leader’s instructions.

content: しきたりに従って式をとり行った。

content.content: We performed the ceremony following the convention.

content: 上司の命令に従って不正を働いた。

content.content: I obeyed my boss’s orders to commit the injustice.

content: 矢印に従って進んで下さい。

content.content: Please follow the arrows.
With a noun expressing a person, an order, or an instruction, expresses the meaning of “being submissive without resisting someone/something” or “acting according to someone’s instructions.”
2. V-るにしたがって

content: 上昇するにしたがって気圧が下がる。

content.content: The air pressure goes down as you go up.

content: 進むにしたがって道は険しくなる。

content.content: As you proceed, the road becomes steeper.

content: この材質は年月を重ねるに従って美しいつやがでて来る。

content.content: With age, this type of material develops a beautiful sheen.

Expresses the meaning of “as some action or function advances.” Followed by a thing/state/event indicating some change as the action or function of a previously mentioned progress, such as 気圧が下がる(the air pressure goes down) or 険しくなる(become steep).
【にしたって】A casual way of saying にしろ or にしても in spoken Japanese.
1. Nにしたって

content: 社長にしたって成功の見通しがあって言っていることではない。

content.content: Even the president, for example, is not saying this because she expects a successful outcome.

content: 彼にしたって、今ごろは自分の行いを恥じているはずだ。

content.content: Even he must be ashamed by now of what he has done.

content: 結婚式にしたってあんなに派手にやる必要はなかったんだ。

content.content: Even for a wedding ceremony, you know, it didn’t have to be so luxurious.

content: 住むところにしたって、探すのには一苦労だ。

content.content: As for a place to live, it’s hard to find one, too.

content: 食事の支度ひとつにしたってあの歳では重荷になっているはずだ。

content.content: Everything, including preparing for meals, is a burden to her at her age.

With a noun expressing a person or a thing/state/event, expresses the meaning of “in case of such a person, thing or event.” Used to state something among many other similar things as an example. Implies that there are other things which can be said in the same way.
2. V-るにしたって

content: 人に注意を与えるにしたって、もう少し言葉遣いには気を付けるべきだ。

content.content: Even when you’re giving a warning, you should be a little more careful about your language.

content: 休暇を増やすにしたって、仕事量が変わらなければ休むこともできない。

content.content: Even though I want to take more vacation time, I can’t take more days off unless the amount of work decreases.

content: 休暇をとるにしたって、旅行などとても無理だ。

content.content: Even if I can take time off, it’s impossible for me to travel.

Expresses the meaning of “even in such a case.” Implies “the speaker acknowledges what was mentioned before to some extent, but...,” and is followed by some event/state which cannot be expected normally.
3. 疑問詞+にしたって

content: どちらにしたって勝てる見込みはほとんどない。

content.content: In any case, it’s not likely he’ll win.

content: なにをやるにしたって金がかかる。

content.content: Whatever you do, you need money.

content: だれにしたってこんな問題にはかかわりあいたくない。

content.content: No one wants to be involved in such a problem.

content: なんにしたってこの種の問題を解決するには時間がかかる。

content.content: In any case, it takes time to solve this kind of problem.
With an interrogative such as いずれ, どちら, なに, or だれ, expresses the meaning of “whatever the case” or “whoever it is.” Can be preceded by a clause with an interrogative, as shown in

content: . A casual way of saying ...にしても in spoken Japanese.

content.content: 【にしたら】［Nにしたら］

content: せっかくの申し出を断ってしまったのだから、彼にしたら、自分の親切が踏みにじられたと感じていることだろう。

content.content: Since we declined his generous offer, I think he feels that we have trampled on his kindness.

content: 母親は子供のためを思って厳しくしつけようとしたのでしょうが、子供にしたら自分が嫌われていると思いこんでしまったのです。

content.content: I think the mother tried to strictly discipline her child for his sake, but from the child’s point of view, he assumed that his mother disliked him.

content: 学生の語学力を高めるには必要な訓練なのだが、学生にしたら退屈きわまりない授業だと思うにちがいない。

content.content: This is necessary training to develop the students’ language ability, but for the students themselves, I’m sure they think this is an extremely boring lecture.

content: 私にしたら親切のつもりだったのですが、言い方がきつかったのか彼はすっかり怒ってしまいました。

content.content: From my side it was meant to be kind, but I phrased it harshly and he went into a rage.

With a noun expressing a person, expresses the meaning of “from the viewpoint of this person.” Used to mean that the speaker speculates on someone’s thought from his/her point of view. Cannot be used to refer to the speaker’s viewpoint.
（×）私にしたらたいへん嬉しく思います。
From my point of view, I’m very pleased.
（○）私としてはたいへん嬉しく思います。
As for me, I am very pleased.
【にして】
1. Nにして〈stage〉

content: この歳にして初めて人生のなんたるかが分かった。

content.content: I learned how life should be only after I became this age.

content: 40にしてようやく子宝に恵まれた（＝子供が生まれた）。

content.content: At long last, at the age of forty, I was blessed with a bundle from heaven (=my child was born).

content: 長年苦労を共にした妻にして初めて理解できることである。

content.content: This is what my wife could understand only after we shared our struggles for many long years.
Means “to come to such a level.” Used to express that some event happens only after it comes to a certain stage. Often used in a phrase such as Nにしてようやく or Nにして初めて.
2. Nにして〈juxtaposition〉

content: 教師にして学問のなんであるかを知らない。

content.content: Even though she is a teacher, she doesn’t know what learning means.

content: 彼は科学者にして優秀な政治家でもある。

content.content: He is not only a scientist but also an outstanding politician.
Means “not only N but also....” There are two uses in this expression. One is to mean “even though it is N” contradictory as shown in

content: , and the other is to simply juxtapose two items as shown in
. A formal, written expression.
幸いにして大事にいたらずにすんだ。

content.content: Luckily, it didn’t lead to anything enormous.

content: 不幸にして、重い病にかかってしまった。

content.content: Unfortunately, I caught a serious disease.

content: その事故で一瞬にして家族全員を失った。

content.content: In an instant, I lost all the members of my family in the accident.

content: 生まれながらにして体の弱い子供だった。

content.content: I was a weak child by birth.

content: その小舟は、たちまちにして波に飲まれて沈んでいった。

content.content: The small boat was swallowed up by the waves and sank in a second.

With a particular type of a noun or an adverb, used to state some situation. There are two uses in this expression: one is to state the speaker’s evaluation of whether the following state/event is fortunate or not, as shown in

content: and
, and the other is to state what some state is like or how some event happens, as shown in

content.content: 【にしてからが】［Nにしてからが］

content: リーダーにしてからがやる気がないのだから、ほかの人たちがやるはずがない。

content.content: Because even the leader doesn’t have any motivation, we can’t expect anyone else to do it.

content: 課長にしてからが事態を把握していないのだから、ヒラの社員によくわからないのも無理はない。

content.content: Because even the section chief doesn’t grasp the situation, it’s hardly impossible that his subordinates don’t know about it either.

content: 夫にしてからが、自分の事を全然分かってくれようともしない。

content.content: Even my husband doesn’t try to understand me.

By indicating the most extreme case, used to state the speaker’s feeling of “because even this is so, it goes without saying that others are the same.” Mostly expresses the speaker’s negative evaluation. Can be rephrased as からして.
【にしては】［N／Na／V　にしては］

content: 子供にしてはむずかしい言葉をよく知っている。

content.content: For her age, the child really knows a lot of difficult words.

content: このアパートは都心にしては家賃が安い。

content.content: The rent for this apartment is quite inexpensive for the center of the city.

content: 貧乏人にしてはずいぶん立派なところに住んでいる。

content.content: For a poor person, he lives in a relatively nice place.

content: 始めたばかりにしてはずいぶん上達したものだ。

content.content: Considering you’ve just started, you’ve improved a lot.

content: 近々結婚するにしてはあまり楽しそうな様子ではない。

content.content: Even though he will get married soon, he doesn’t look very happy.

content: 下調べをしたにしては不十分な内容であった。

content.content: Even though she had done her research, the content was insufficient.

Expresses the meaning of “it is rather; considering that.” Followed by a thing/event/state which is contradictory to what is normally expected. Can often be rephrased as X（な）のに. However, although のに implies that X is already confirmed, Xにしては does not contain such implications.
【にしてみたら】→
【にしてみれば】
【にしてみれば】［Nにしてみれば］

content: 今何の歌がはやっているかなんて、私にしてみればどうでもいいことだ。それよりもっと大切なことが山ほどある。

content.content: To know what song is popular now makes no difference to me at all. There are much more important things.

content: 長い間使っていなかった古いコンピュータをあげたのだが、彼女にしてみればとてもありがたかったらしく、何度も何度もお礼を言われた。

content.content: I gave her an old computer which I hadn’t used for a long time. For her, it seemed to be something very valuable and she thanked me again and again.

content: 私は軽い気持ちで話していたのだが、あの人にしてみれば大きな問題だったのだろう。彼は落ち込んで誰とも口をきかなくなってしまった。

content.content: I just mentioned it casually, but for him it was probably a major problem. He got depressed and stopped talking to anyone.

content: 母にしてみれば、大切に育ててきた息子が突然家を出ていったのだから、たいそうショックだろうが、私は親離れしようとしている弟に声援を送りたい気持ちだった。

content.content: For my mother, it was probably a shock to have the son she had so lovingly raised suddenly leave home, but my feeling was to support my younger brother as he tried to gain his independence from his parents.
With a noun expressing a person, expresses the meaning “for that person.” Used to state that the person has a different view from others. Can be rephrased as ...にしてみたら.
【にしても】Becomes ...にしたって in casual speech, and...にせよ or ...にしろ in formal speech.
1. Nにしても

content: 彼にしても、こんな騒ぎになるとは思ってもいなかったでしょう。

content.content: For him as well, he never thought it would become such a big deal.

content: 母にしても初めから賛成していたわけではありません。

content.content: For my mother, too, it’s not that she agreed from the beginning.

content: かなりハードな仕事だし、給料にしても決していいというわけでもない。

content.content: This is such hard work, and in addition, the salary is not very good either.

content: 歩き方ひとつにしてもきちんと作法に則っている。

content.content: Considering just how to walk, for instance, she is following the manners properly.

content: 身につけているものひとつにしても育ちのよさが感じられた。

content.content: Looking just at what he wears, I could see he has been brought up well.

With a noun expressing a person or a thing, used to talk about the person or thing while implying that there is something else similar to the person or thing. When emphasizing the implication that one thing or person is chosen among various things/persons and other things/persons don’t need to be mentioned, にしても becomes ...ひとつにしても as shown in

content: and

content.content: 2. ...にしても［N（である）にしても］［A／V　にしても］

content: 子供のいたずらにしても笑って済ませられる問題ではない。

content.content: Even if this is just children’s mischief, it’s no laughing matter.

content: たとえ失敗作であるにしても十分に人を引き付ける魅力がある。

content.content: Even if this work is a failure, it has enough appeal to attract people.

content: 忙しいにしても連絡ぐらいは入れられただろうに。

content.content: Even though she was busy, she could just have made contact with me.

content: 私を嫌っているにしても、こんな仕打ちはあんまりだ。

content.content: Even if he dislikes me, it’s too much of him to behave like that.

content: いくら貧しいにしても人から施しは受けたくない。

content.content: No matter how poor I am, I don’t want to receive alms.

Expresses the meaning of “even if I admit the situation mentioned in....” Followed by some state or event contradictory to what is normally expected. Often used with an interrogative, such as いくら or どんなに, as shown in
3. ...にしても...にしても［NにしてもNにしても］［VにしてもVにしても］

content: 山田にしても佐藤にしても、この仕事に向いているとはいえない。

content.content: Speaking of Yamada or Sato, I can’t say this job is suitable for either.

content: 犬にしても猫にしてもこのマンションではペットを飼ってはいけないことになっている。

content.content: Putting aside whether it is a dog or a cat, this apartment does not allow pets.

content: 当選にしても落選にしても、今回の選挙に立候補したことは大いに意味があった。

content.content: Whether she was elected or not, it was significant to run in this election.

content: 行くにしても行かないにしても、一応準備だけはしておきなさい。

content.content: Whether you go or not, you’d better be prepared in any case.

content: 勝つにしても負けるにしても、正々堂々と戦いたい。

content.content: Whether I win or lose, I’d like to play fair.

content: 勝ったにしても負けたにしても、よく頑張ったとほめてやりたい。

content.content: Whether she wins or not, I’d like to praise her for her great effort.
Taking two items in the same genre or two opposing items, expresses the meaning of “either way.”
4. 疑問詞+にしても

content: いずれにしても結論は次回に持ち越されることになった。

content.content: At any rate, it was decided that the decision would be postponed.

content: だれにしてもそんなことはやりたくない。

content.content: No one wants to do such a thing.

content: なんにしても年内に立ち退いてもらいます。

content.content: I will have you moved out before the end of the year, no matter what.

content: だれがやったにしても、我々全員で責任をとらなければならない。

content.content: Whoever did it, we all have to take responsibility.

content: 何をするにしても、よく考えてから行動しなさい。

content.content: Whatever you do, think carefully before taking action.

With an interrogative such as いずれ, だれ or なに, means something like “in any case” or “whoever it is.” There are also some cases in which にしても is preceded by a clause containing an interrogative, as shown in

content: and

content.content: 5. それにしても→
【それにしても】
【にしろ】

content: 役人がわいろを受け取ったかどうか問題になっているが、かりに金銭の授受はなかったにしろ、なんらかの報酬をもらったことは間違いない。

content.content: Whether the officer took a bribe or not is at issue, but even if there was no money given or received, there is no doubt that he received some sort of remuneration.

content: 妻にしろ子供達にしろ、彼の気持ちを理解しようとするものはいなかった。

content.content: Neither his wife nor his children—no one tried to understand his feelings.

content: どちらの案を採用するにしろ、メンバーには十分な説明をする必要がある。

content.content: Whichever proposal you adopt, you need to explain it sufficiently to the members.
A formal, written expression of ...にしても. Can be rephrased as ...にせよ．
【にしても】
【にすぎない】→
【すぎない】
【にする】→
【する】
【にせよ】

content: 直接の責任は部下にあるにせよ、彼の監督不行届きも糾弾されるだろう。

content.content: Even though his subordinate was directly responsible, his lack of supervision will probably be criticized.

content: 来るにせよ来ないにせよ、連絡ぐらいはしてほしい。

content.content: Whether you come or not, I want you to at least contact me.

content: いずれにせよもう一度検査をしなければならない。

content.content: At any rate, we have to do another inspection.
A formal, written expression of にせよ. Can be rephrased as ...にしろ.
【にしても】
【にそういない】［N／V　にそういない］

content: 犯人はあの男に相違ない。

content.content: The criminal must be that man.

content: 彼女は3日前に家を出たまま帰ってこない。きっとなにか事件に巻き込まれたに相違ない。

content.content: She left home three days ago and hasn’t come back yet. She must have been involved in some incident.

content: これを知ったら、彼はきっと烈火のごとく怒り出すに相違ない。

content.content: If he gets to know this, I’m sure he will fly into a rage.
Expresses the speaker’s firm conviction and means “it must be so” or “I’m sure ....” Used in formal, written Japanese, and can be rephrased as ...にちがいない.
【にそくして】［Nにそくして］

content: 事実にそくして想像をまじえないで事件について話してください。

content.content: Based on the facts and without embellishing, please tell me about the incident.

content: 経験にそくしていうと、ぼくの人生にとって若いときの異文化体験の意味はとても大きい。

content.content: Based on past experiences, my encountering different cultures in my youth has had a great significance in my life.

content: ゼロ才児保育につきましてはそれぞれの家庭で事情が異なると思いますから、実情に即して対処いたします。

content.content: I think the care of babies under the age of one differs from family to family, so I will deal with this to meet the needs of the actual circumstances.

content: この問題は私的な感情ではなく、法にそくして解釈しなければならない。

content.content: This problem must be solved in accordance with the law and not personal feelings.

content: 法律に則して言うと、今回の事件は刑事事件として取り扱うべき性格のものだ。

content.content: Based on the law, this incident is characteristic of a criminal case and should be treated accordingly.

With a noun expressing a fact, experience, or a norm, にそくして expresses the meaning of “along something,” “following something” or “based on something.” When にそくして is preceded by a noun expressing a fact or experience, 即して is used as shown in

content: , whereas when it is preceded by a noun expressing a law or a norm, 則して is used as shown in
and

content.content: 【にそった】→
【にそって】
【にそって】［Nにそって］

content: この道に沿ってずっと行くと、右手に大きい公園が見えてきます。

content.content: If you go straight along this street, you’ll find a big park on your right.

content: 川岸に沿って、桜並木が続いていた。

content.content: There was a line of cherry trees along the river bank.

content: この塀に沿って植えてある花は、日陰でもよく育つ。

content.content: The flowers that were planted along this fence grow well even in the shade.

content: 書いてある手順に沿ってやってください。

content.content: Please do it following the written procedures.

content: マニュアルに沿った手紙の書き方しか知らないのでは、いざというとき困る。

content.content: If you only know how to write a letter based on what the manual says, you’ll have problems in an emergency.

content: 妻は夫に添って病室に入っていった。

content.content: The wife entered the hospital room alongside her husband.

With a noun expressing something that leads to somewhere such as a river or a street, or something that shows some sequence such as procedures or manuals, expresses the meaning of “as something follows, along the edge of something, following something.” Written as 沿う. There is another use in にそって, which means that something is accompanied by a thing or a person without parting as shown in

content: . Written as 添う in this case. When modifying a noun, にそって becomes NにそったN, as shown in

content.content: 【にたいして】
1. ...にたいして［Nにたいして］［Naなのにたいして］［A-いのにたいして］［Vのにたいして］

content: 私の発言に対して彼は猛烈に攻撃を加えてきた。

content.content: He criticized me aggressively about my remarks.

content: 私の質問に対して何も答えてくれなかった。

content.content: I didn’t get any answer to my questions.

content: 彼は女性に対しては親切に指導してくれる。

content.content: With women, he offers kind guidance.

content: 現在容疑者に対しての取り調べが行われているところです。

content.content: The interrogation of the suspect is underway at the moment.

content: 私が手を振って合図したのに対して、彼女は大きく腕を振って応えてくれた。

content.content: When I waved my hand to her to give a sign, she responded to me by giving me a big wave.

Expresses the meaning of “toward a thing/state/event, responding to a thing/state/event,” and is followed by some expression indicating some kind of motion such as an action or attitude toward the thing/state/event. When modifying a noun, becomes ...にたいしてのN or ...にたいするN.
2. N+数量詞+にたいして

content: 研究員1人に対して年間 40万円の補助金が与えられる。

content.content: 400,000 yen is allocated to each researcher as an annual subsidy.

content: 学生 20 人に対して教員一人が配置されている。

content.content: For every twenty students, one teacher is assigned.

content: 砂3に対して1の割合で土を混ぜます。

content.content: Sand is mixed with soil in a ratio of three to one.

content: 学生1人に対して 20 平米のスペースが確保されている。

content.content: A space of twenty square meters is reserved for each student.
With a numbered unit expressed in quantity or size, expresses the meaning of “according to some unit.” Can be rephrased as ...について or ...につき.
3. ...のにたいして

content: 彼が自民党を支持しているのに対して、彼女は共産党を支援している。

content.content: He supports the Liberal Democratic Party, whereas she supports the Communist Party.

content: 兄が背が高いのに対して、弟の方はクラスで一番低い。

content.content: Although the elder brother is tall, the younger brother is the shortest in his class.
Used to juxtapose two items in contrast.
【にたいする】
1. NにたいするN

content: 私の疑問に対する答えはなかなか得られない。

content.content: It’s pretty hard to receive an answer to my question.

content: 子供に対する親の愛情ははかり知れない。

content.content: Parents’ love for their child is immeasurable.

content: 親に対する反抗心をむき出しにしてくってかかった。

content.content: Exposing her rebellion against her parents, she lashed out at them.

content: 書画に対する造詣が深い。

content.content: His expertise with documents is considerable.
Expresses the meaning of “toward something” or “regarding something” and modifies the following noun. Can be rephrased as NにたいしてのN, as in その問に対しての解答 (an answer to that question).
2. N+数量詞+にたいするN

content: 研究員1人に対する年間の補助は40万円である。

content.content: 400,000 yen is allocated to each researcher as an annual subsidy.

content: 教員1人に対する学生数は20人という計算になる。

content.content: The figure would be one teacher for every twenty students.
With some numbered unit expressing a quantity or size, expresses the meaning of “according to some unit” and is used to modify the following noun.
【にたえない】
1. V-るにたえない

content: 幼い子供が朝から晩まで通りで物乞いをしている姿は見るにたえない。

content.content: It is unbearable to see young children begging on the street all day long.

content: 近ごろの週刊誌は暴露記事が多く、読むにたえない。

content.content: I can’t stand reading recent weekly magazines because they have a lot of exposés.

content: 地震のあと、町はパニック状態となった。暴徒が次々に商店をおそい、正視するにたえない光景が繰り広げられた。

content.content: After the earthquake, the whole town panicked. Mobs attacked shops one after another and an unbearable sight unfolded before our eyes.
Expresses the meaning that it is hard to see or hear something because its state is dreadful. Can be used with a few specific types of verbs, such as 見る, 読む, and正視する.
2. Nにたえない

content: このようなお言葉をいただき、感謝の念にたえません。

content.content: I cannot be grateful enough to you for giving me such a compliment.

content: 晩年近くなってボランティア活動を通じて若い人々とこのようなすばらしい出会いがあろうとは考えてもみないことであった。感激にたえない。

content.content: I had never thought about such wonderful encounters with young people through volunteer work in my later years. It’s absolutely wonderful.
With some limited types of nouns, such as 感謝 (gratitude) and 感激 ((the feeling of being) deeply moved), Nにたえない is used to emphasize the meaning of the noun. Usually used in formal speech.
【にたえる】
1. Nにたえる

content: この木はきびしい冬の寒さにたえて、春になると美しい花を咲かせます。

content.content: This tree manages to survive hard winters and produces beautiful flowers when spring comes.

content: 重圧に耐えられなくなって、彼は社長の座を降りた。

content.content: The strain came to be too much for him, so he stepped down as company president.
Expresses the meaning that someone does not give in but perseveres. As an expression to negate にたえる, たえられない(cannot endure/persevere) is often used.
2. ...にたえる［Nにたえる］［V-るにたえる］

content: アマチュアの展覧会ではあるが鑑賞にたえる作品が並んでいる。

content.content: Although this is an amateur exhibition, there are works worth looking at.

content: きびしい読者の批評にたえる紙面作りを目指したい。

content.content: We’re aiming to produce newspaper articles that can stand up to strong reader criticism.

content: 読むに耐える記事が書けるようになるまでには相当の訓練が要る。

content.content: You need considerable training before you will be able to write an article worth reading.

With a specific type of noun or verb such as 鑑賞(appreciation), 批判(criticism), 読む(read) or 見る(look), expresses the meaning that it is worth doing such a thing. When it is negated, にたえる usually becomes たえない, and たえられない is not used.
【にたえない】
【にたりない】［V-るにたりない］

content: とるに足りない（＝つまらない）ことをそんなに気にするな。

content.content: Don’t worry so much about little things.

content: あんなものは恐れるに足りない。

content.content: That isn’t scary enough.

content: 彼は信頼するに足りない人物だ。

content.content: He is not a person you can trust.
Expresses the meaning of “it is not so much” or “it is not worth doing something.”
【にたる】［V-るにたるN］

content: 昨今の政治家は私利私欲に走り、尊敬するにたる人物はいなくなってしまった。

content.content: Nowadays politicians seek their own interests, and so there is no one worth respecting.

content: 学校で子供たちが信頼するにたる教師に出会えるかどうかが問題だ。

content.content: Whether children can meet a trustworthy teacher at school is the problem.

content: 一生のうちに語るに足る冒険などそうあるものではない。

content.content: In our life there are not many adventures worth talking about.

content: 会議では皆それぞれ勝手なことをいうばかりで、耳を傾けるに足る意見は出なかった。

content.content: In the meeting everybody just made self-centered remarks, and no one made a point worth listening to.

content: すべてが眠ったような平和な島では、報道するに足るニュースなどなにもなかった。

content.content: On the peaceful island where everything seems to be asleep, there was no news worth reporting.
With a specific type of verb such as 尊敬する(respect) or 信頼する(trust), expresses the meaning of “it deserves enough to do something” or “it is suitable to do something.” A formal, written expression.
【にちがいない】→
【ちがいない】
【について】
1. Nについて

content: 農村の生活様式について調べている。

content.content: I am investigating the styles of living in farming villages.

content: その点については全面的に賛成はできない。

content.content: I cannot entirely agree with that point.

content: 彼女は自分自身について何も語ろうとしない。

content.content: She doesn’t try to talk about herself at all.

content: 事故の原因について究明する。

content.content: I will investigate the cause of the accident.

content: 経営方針についての説明を受けた。

content.content: I heard the explanation regarding the management policy.

content: 将来についての夢を語った。

content.content: I talked about my dreams for the future.

content: ことの善悪についての判断ができなくなっている。

content.content: I cannot judge whether things are right and wrong now.
Expresses the meaning of “regarding something.” When modifying a noun, becomes NについてのN, as shown in

content: . In polite speech, つきまして is used in stead of について.

content.content: （例）その件につきましては後でお返事さしあげます。
With regard to that matter, I will give you a reply later.
2. N+数量詞+について

content: 車1台について5千円の使用料をちょうだいします。

content.content: To rent a car, the fee is 5,000 yen.

content: 乗客1人について3つまでの手荷物を持ち込むことができます。

content.content: Each passenger is allowed to take three pieces of carry-on luggage.

content: 作業員5人について1部屋しか割り当てられなかった。

content.content: Only one room was allocated for five workers.
With a numbered unit expressed in quantity or size, expresses the meaning of “according to some unit.” Can be rephrased as ...にたいして.
【につき】
1. Nにつき〈about, regarding〉

content: 本部の移転問題につき審議が行われた。

content.content: There was a debate over the issue of relocating the head office.

content: 領土の分割案につき関係各国の代表から厳しい批判が浴びせられた。

content.content: The proposal of territorial division was harshly condemned by representatives of all countries concerned.
A formal expression of Nについて.
【について】
2. Nにつき〈reason〉

content: 改装中につきしばらくお休みさせていただきます。

content.content: The restaurant is closed temporarily for renovation.

content: 父は高齢につき参加をとりやめさせていただきます。

content.content: I’m afraid that my father will have to forego attending on account of his advanced age.
With a noun, expresses the meaning of “for reasons of N (something).” について is used in a formal letter.
3. N+数量詞+につき

content: 参加者 200 人につき、5人の随行員がついた。

content.content: Five attendants are allocated to 200 participants.

content: テニスコートの使用料は1時間につき千円ちょうだいします。

content.content: The fee for one hour of court time (for tennis) is 1,000 yen.

content: 食費は1人1日につき2千円かかる。

content.content: It costs each person 2,000 yen for meals per day.
A formal expression of N + numeral + について.
【について】2
【につけ】
1. Nにつけ

content: 何事につけ我慢が肝心だ。

content.content: Patience is the most important on all occasions.

content: 彼は何かにつけ私のことを目のかたきにする。

content.content: Whenever we meet he is always very hostile to me.

content: 山田さんご夫妻には何かにつけ親切にしていただいています。

content.content: In so many ways, Mr. and Mrs. Yamada are always kind to me.
Used in idiomatic expressions such as 何事につけ or 何かにつけ. 何事につけ and 何かにつけ express the meaning “on all occasions” and “whenever there is a chance,” respectively.
2. V-るにつけ

content: 彼女の姿を見るにつけ、その時のことが思い出される。

content.content: Whenever I see her, I am reminded of the incident.

content: そのことを考えるにつけ後悔の念にさいなまれる。

content.content: Whenever I think about it, I am always full of remorse.

content: その曲を聞くにつけ、苦しかったあの時代のことが思い出される。

content.content: Whenever I listen to the music, it reminds me of those hard times.

An idiomatic expression. With a verb such as 見る(see/look), 思う(think) or 考える(think about), expresses the meaning of “whenever someone sees or thinks about a thing, regarding the thing....” Followed by a clause containing a phrase expressing some feeling or thought, such as 思い出(memories) or 後悔(regrets).
3. ...につけ...につけ［AにつけAにつけ］［VにつけVにつけ］

content: いいにつけ悪いにつけ、あの人達の協力を仰ぐしかない。

content.content: Whether good or bad, we have no choice but to ask those people for advice.

content: 話しがまとまるにつけ、まとまらないにつけ、仲介の労を取ってくれた方にはお礼をしなければなりません。

content.content: Whether we come to an agreement or not, we have to give the person who mediated for us some token of gratitude for her trouble.
An idiomatic expression to list two contrasting items. Expresses the meaning of “either way.”
【につれて】［Nにつれて］［V-るにつれて］

content: 町の発展につれて、前になかった新しい問題が生まれて来た。

content.content: With the development of the town, new problems we had never encountered have emerged.

content: 時間がたつにつれて、悲しみは薄らいできた。

content.content: As time passed, my sadness has faded.

content: 設備が古くなるにつれて、故障の箇所が増えて来た。

content.content: As the facilities got older, more things have broken down.

content: 試合が進むにつれて、観衆も興奮してきて大騒ぎとなった。

content.content: As the match went on, the gallery got excited and burst into cheers.

content: 成長するにつれて、娘は無口になってきた。

content.content: As she grew up, my daughter turned quiet.
Expresses an approximate proportionate relation in which as a matter or situation develops, another also develops. Can be につれ in formal, written Japanese.
【にて】［Nにて］

content: 校門前にて写真撮影を行います。

content.content: We will take photographs in front of the school gate.

content: では、これにて失礼致します。

content.content: Well, may I be excused now?

content: 会場係は当方にて手配いたします。

content.content: As for staff in charge of the venue, we will arrange for them.
Expresses the place of an event, or is used for idiomatic expressions such as これにて(now) or 当方にて(ourselves). Used in written Japanese, such as in a formal letter. Can be rephrased as で.
【にとって】［Nにとって］

content: 彼にとってこんな修理は何でもないことです。

content.content: For him, such repairs are nothing.

content: 年金生活者にとってはインフレが深刻な問題である。

content.content: For pensioners, inflation is a serious problem.

content: 度重なる自然災害が国家の再建にとって大きな痛手となった。

content.content: The succession of natural disasters became a huge obstacle to reconstructing the country.

content: 病床の私にとっては、友人の励ましがなによりも有り難いものだった。

content.content: When I was sick in bed, I appreciated the encouragement of my friends more than anything.

With a noun mostly expressing a person or an organization, expresses the meaning of “from the point of view.” May express the meaning of “considering that aspect” when it is preceded by a noun expressing a thing, state or an event, as shown in

content: . Followed by some expression to show (in)ability or the speaker’s evaluation, such as むずかしい(difficult), 有り難い(grateful), or 深刻だ(serious). Cannot be followed by an expression to show the speaker’s attitude, such as 賛成, 反対 or 感謝する.

content.content: （×）その案は私にとって反対です。
For me, I disagree with the plan.
（○）私はその案に反対です。
I disagree with the plan.
【にとどまらず】［Nにとどまらず］

content: その流行は大都市にとどまらず地方にも広がっていった。

content.content: The fad didn’t stop within the big cities but spread to the countryside, too.

content: 干ばつはその年だけにとどまらず、その後3年間も続いた。

content.content: The drought hit us not only that year but also the following three years.

content: 大気汚染による被害は、老人や幼い子供達にとどまらず、若者達にまで広がった。

content.content: The damage caused by air pollution affected not only the elderly and little children but also young people.
With a noun expressing a region or time, expresses the meaning of “without staying in” or “not only something, but also....”
【にともない】［Nにともない］［Vのにともない］

content: 高齢化にともない、老人医療の問題も深刻になりつつある。

content.content: With the aging population, the problem of health care for the elderly is getting more serious.

content: 地球の温暖化にともない、海面も急速に上昇している。

content.content: In step with global warming, the sea level has risen rapidly.

content: 政界再編の動きに伴いまして、このたび新しく党を結成するはこびとなりました。

content.content: Following the trend of political realignment, it has been decided that we will form a new political party.
A more formal expression of にともなって.
【にともなって】
【にともなって】［Nにともなって］［Vのにともなって］

content: 気温の上昇にともなって湿度も上がり蒸し暑くなってきた。

content.content: With the rise in temperature, the humidity has gone up and it has become muggy.

content: 学生数が増えるのにともなって、学生の質も多様化してきた。

content.content: With the increased number of students, their character has diversified.

content: 父親の転勤に伴って、一家の生活拠点は仙台からニューヨークへと移ることになった。

content.content: Because of the father’s transfer, the family’s base has moved from Sendai to New York.

With an expression showing some change either before or after, expresses the meaning that the change expressed before accompanies the change expressed after にともなって. Used to state some change on a large scale but not really some change for personal matters. A formal, written style of expression.
【にどと...ない】［にどとV-ない］

content: こんな恐ろしい思いは二度としたくない。

content.content: I never want to have such a horrible experience.

content: 同じ間違いは二度と犯さないようにしましょう。

content.content: Let’s not make the same mistake again.

content: こんなチャンスは二度と訪れないだろう。

content.content: This will be the chance of a lifetime.

content: あんなサービスの悪いレストランには二度と行きたくない。

content.content: I never ever want to go back to that restaurant with such poor service.

content: 今、別れたら、あの人にはもう二度と会えないかもしれない。

content.content: If I leave him now, I may not be able to see him any more.
Used to negate something firmly, such as 絶対に...ない(never do...) and 決して繰り返さない(never to repeat).
【になく】［Nになく］

content: 店の中はいつになく静かだった。

content.content: It was unusually quiet in the shop.

content: 例年になく、今年の夏は涼しい日が多い。

content.content: We have more cool days this summer than normal.

content: 彼女は歌がうまいと言われて、柄にもなく顔を赤らめていた。

content.content: It was unlike her to blush when she was told that she was good at singing.
An idiomatic expression that expresses the meaning “something unusually differs.” Can be rephrased as ...にもなく.
【になると】→
【なる】9
【ににあわず】［Nににあわず］

content: いつもの佐藤さんに似合わず口数が少なかった。

content.content: It was unlike Sato-san to have spoken so little.

content: 彼は大きな体に似合わず気の小さいところがある。

content.content: Contrary to his appearance, he is sometimes timid.
Expresses the meaning “does not correspond to the nature of something/someone.”
【には】
1. NにはNには is a form in which は is attached to a noun with the particle に, to emphasize the phrase.
a. Nには〈time, place, direction, other person, etc.〉

content: 春には桜が咲きます。

content.content: In spring, the cherry trees bloom.

content: 10 時には帰ってくると思います。

content.content: By ten o’clock, she should come back.

content: この町には大学が三つもあります。

content.content: In this town, there are three universities.

content: 結局国には帰りませんでした。

content.content: In the end, I didn’t go back to my country.

content: 山田さんにはきのう会いました。

content.content: As for Yamada-san, I saw him yesterday.

content: みなさんには申し訳ありませんが、今日の集まりは中止になりました。

content.content: I’m sorry to tell everyone this, but the meeting has been canceled today.

Contains a phrase with the particle に to which は expressing some topic or contrasting N with something else is attached, and emphasizes phrases with various meanings. When either meaning of は is not necessarily expressed, only Nに is used.
b. Nには〈standard of evaluation〉

content: このセーターは私には大きすぎる。

content.content: This sweater is too big for me.

content: この問題はむずかしすぎて私には分かりません。

content.content: This question is so difficult that I can’t understand it.

content: この仕事は経験のない人には無理でしょう。

content.content: This job is not possible for inexperienced people to do.

With a noun expressing a person, expresses the meaning of “for that person.” Shows for whom the speaker’s evaluation, such as 大きい(big), むずかしい(difficult), できる(able to do), or できない(not able to do), is intended. Has the contrastive implication of “setting other people aside.” Nには but not really Nに is used in this usage.
c. Nには〈target of respect〉

content: 皆様にはお変わりなくお過ごしのことと存じます。

content.content: I trust that you are all continuing to do well.

content: 先生にはお変わりなくお過ごしのこととお喜び申し上げます。

content.content: I trust that you, my teacher, are also keeping well.

With a noun addressing someone in a superior position, used to express the speaker’s respect toward that person. Used only in a formal letter or some similar occasion. To be more formal, ...におかれましては is used.
2. V-るには

content: そこに行くには険しい山を超えなければならない。

content.content: To reach there, we have to go over a steep mountain.

content: その電車に乗るには予約をとる必要があります。

content.content: To take the train, it is necessary to make a reservation.

content: 健康を維持するには早寝早起きが一番だ。

content.content: To keep your health, it’s best to go to bed early and get up early.
Expresses the meaning of “in order to do something” or “if you think you want to do something.”
3. V-るにはVが

content: 行くには行くが、彼に会えるかどうかは分からない。

content.content: I’ll go anyway, but I don’t know if I can see him.

content: A:あしたまでに完成させると約束したんですって？

content.content: I heard you promised you would finish by tomorrow. Is that right?
B:うん。約束するにはしたけれど、できるかどうか自信がないんだ。
Yeah, you’re right that I promised, but I’m not sure whether I can.

content: いちおう説明するにはしたのですが、まだみんな、十分に理解できていないようでした。

content.content: I did explain it once to them, but it didn’t seem that everyone fully understood.
With the same verb repeated, expresses the meaning of “someone will do/did anyway, but it is not clear if the result will be satisfactory.”
【にはあたらない】［V-るにはあたらない］

content: 中学校で教師をしている友人の話によると、学校でのいじめが深刻だという。しかし驚くにはあたらない。大人の社会も同じなのだから。

content.content: According to my friend who is teaching in junior high school, the problem of bullying at school is serious. But there’s nothing surprising about that. The same problem can be seen in adult society.

content: 彼ひとりだけ仲間を置いて下山したからといって、非難するには当たらない。あのような天候のもとではそれ以外の方法はなかっただろう。

content.content: You can’t put the blame on him just because he left friends and went down the mountain. I think there was no other thing for him to do under such weather conditions.

content: 子どもがちっとも親のいうことをきかないからといって、嘆くには当たらない。きっといつか親の心がわかる日がくる。

content.content: It’s nothing to be surprised at just because a child doesn’t listen to his parents. One day, he will understand how parents feel toward their children.

content: 彼が会議でひとことも発言しなかったからといって責めるには当たらない。あのワンマン社長の前ではだれでもそうなのだ。

content.content: There’s no need to criticize him just because he didn’t speak a word at the meeting. In front of that dictatorial president, everybody behaves like that.

With a verb such as 驚く(be surprised) or 非難する(reprove), expresses the meaning of “it is not appropriate, it is off the point.” Often used with an expression showing some reason, such as ...からといって, and means “it is off the point to be surprised at or blame someone because of such a reason.”
【にはおよばない】
1. ...にはおよばない［Nにはおよばない］［V-るにはおよばない］

content: 検査では何も異常は見つかりませんでした。すっかり元気になりましたから、ご心配には及びません。

content.content: Nothing abnormal was found in the examination. I’m completely recovered, so you don’t need to worry.

content: 分かりきったことだから、わざわざ説明するには及ばない。

content.content: This is an obvious matter, so you don’t need to explain.

content: こんな遠くまで、はるばるお越しいただくには及びません。

content.content: Please do not bother to come all the way to such a distant place.
Expresses the meaning of “it is not necessary to do something” or “there is no need to do something.” Can be rephrased as ...にはあたらない.
2. それにはおよばない

content: A:車で家までお送りしましょう。

content.content: Let me drive you home.
B:いいえ、それには及びません。歩いても5分ほどの所ですから、どうぞご心配なく。
No, please don’t bother. It takes me only five minutes or so on foot, so don’t worry.

content: A:空港までお迎えにあがりますよ。

content.content: I’ll pick you up at the airport.
B:大丈夫です。よく知っている所ですから、それには及びませんよ。
I’ll be fine. I know the place well, so please don’t bother.

Used to decline an offer made by the listener and means “you don’t need to go to such an extent.” Implies the speaker’s acknowledgement of the listener’s consideration, and sounds more formal than その必要はありません.
【にはんし】［Nにはんし］

content: 大方の予想に反して、我らのチームが圧勝した。

content.content: Contrary to general expectations, our team swept the match.

content: 人々の期待に反し、景気は依然低迷を続けている。

content.content: Against all expectations, the economy has remained sluggish.
A formal, written expression of ...にはんして.
【にはんして】
【にはんして】［Nにはんして］

content: 予想にはんして、今年の試験はそれほど難しくはなかったそうだ。

content.content: Contrary to expectations, I heard the exam this year was not so difficult.

content: 周囲の期待に反して、彼らは結局結婚しなかった。

content.content: Against all expectations, they didn’t get married after all.

content: 年初の予測に反して、今年は天候不順の年となった。

content.content: Contrary to predictions at the beginning of the year, the weather has been changeable this year.

content: 今回の交渉では、大方の見方に反して、相手側がかなり思い切った譲歩案を提示した模様だ。

content.content: Against the widely-held view, it seems that the opponent proposed a drastic compromise at negotiations.

With a noun showing some prediction about some time in future such as 予想(prediction) or 期待(expectation), expresses that the result is not the same as predicted. Can be rephrased as ...とは違って(differently to) or ...とは反対に(in contrast to) and is rather a formal, written expression. When it modifies a noun, にはんして becomes Nにはんする／にはんしたN.
（例）先週の試合は、大方の予想に反する結果となった。
The match last week turned out contrary to most people’s expectations.
【にひきかえ】［Nにひきかえ］

content: 兄にひきかえ弟はだれにでも好かれる好青年だ。

content.content: In contrast to his elder brother, he is a pleasant young man that everybody likes.

content: 努力家の姉に引きかえ、弟は怠け者だ。

content.content: In contrast to his hardworking elder sister, he is a lazy oaf.

content: このごろは子供っぽい男子学生にひきかえ女子学生のほうが社会性があってしっかりしているようだ。

content.content: Recently, the female students are more sociable and stable than the childish male students.

content: 市当局の柔軟な姿勢にひきかえ、窓口の高圧的な対応は市民の反発を招いている。

content.content: In contrast to the flexible attitude of the city authorities, the oppressive way they are treated at the window meets with strong opposition from citizens.
Comparing two contrastive items, expresses the meaning of “in contrast to the one, the other is/does....” In spoken Japanese, Nにくらべて is used instead.
【にほかならない】
1. Nにほかならない

content: この会を成功のうちに終わらせることが出来ましたのは、皆様がたのご協力のたまものに他なりません。

content.content: It was entirely your cooperation that has resulted in a successful conclusion to the meeting.

content: 年を取るというのは、すなわち経験を積むということに他ならない。

content.content: Aging is nothing other than collecting more experiences.
Used to assert something and expresses the meaning of “there is nothing more than something” or “it is the very something.”
2. ...にほかならない［...から／...ため　にほかならない］

content: 父が肺ガンになったのは、あの工場で長年働いたために他ならない。

content.content: My father’s lung cancer is entirely due to the fact that he worked at that factory for many years.

content: 彼が私を憎むのは、私の業績をねたんでいるからに他ならない。

content.content: The reason he hates me is entirely because he is jealous of my accomplishments.

content: この仕事にこんなにも打ち込むことができたのは、家族が支えていてくれたからに他ならない。

content.content: I could throw myself into my work only because I was supported by my family.
Used to assert that the reason or cause of some event is nothing more than that, or that is the very reason.
【にむかって】
1. Nにむかって〈direction〉

content: この飛行機は現在ボストンに向かっています。

content.content: This plane is now heading to Boston.

content: 病人はだんだん快方に向かっています。

content.content: The patient is gradually recovering.

content: 両国の関係は最悪の事態に向かって一気に進んでいった。

content.content: The relationship between the two countries has escalated to the worst possible scenario.

content: 春に向かってだんだん暖かくなってきた。

content.content: It has gotten warmer on its way to spring.
