content: このトンネルは出口に向かって下り坂になっている。

content.content: This tunnel slopes down toward the exit.
Expresses a direction of something moved, or a resultant state after some time or some situation has changed. にむかって in

content: indicates a destination of “this plane,” “the patient,” or “the relationship between the two countries,” respectively, and can be used as a sentential predicate, as shown in
and
. にむかって in
and
is followed by a clause expressing some change and expresses the meaning of “some change of state occurs as it is approaching somewhere.” For instance, にむかって in
expresses that as spring is coming, some change of state, namely, a rise in temperature, is caused.

content.content: 2. Nにむかって〈face something〉

content: 机に向かって本を読む。

content.content: She sits at the desk to read a book.

content: 黒板に向かって座る。

content.content: He sits in front of the blackboard.

content: マリア像に向かって祈りを捧げる。

content.content: She prays to the statue of the Virgin Mary.

content: 私の部屋は正面に向かって左側にあります。

content.content: My room is on the left side of the house as you face it.
With a noun expressing a person or a thing, means to be in a position directly facing some person or thing.
3. Nにむかって〈other person〉

content: 親に向かって乱暴な口をきくな。

content.content: Don’t speak so roughly to your parents!

content: 敵に向かって発砲する。

content.content: He fires at the enemy.

content: 上司に向かって反抗的な態度を示す。

content.content: She shows a defiant attitude toward her boss.
With a noun expressing a person, indicates the person towards whom someone takes some attitude or action. Can be rephrased as ...にたいして.
【にむけて】
1. Nにむけて〈direction〉

content: 入口に背を向けて座っている。

content.content: She is sitting with her back to the entrance.

content: 飛行機は機首を北に向けて進んでいた。

content.content: The airplane was flying with its nose pointing north.

content: 飛行機は機首を北に向けた。

content.content: The airplane has turned north.
With a noun expressing a place or direction, expresses some destination of a thing moving or some attitude/position of a person. Can be used as a sentential predicate, as shown in
2. Nにむけて〈destination〉

content: 飛行機はヨーロッパに向けて飛び立った。

content.content: The airplane took off for Europe.

content: 彼らは任地に向けて出発した。

content.content: They left for their place of work.
With a noun expressing a place, expresses a goal of a thing moving. Followed by some expression showing some move.
3. Nにむけて〈other person〉

content: 人々に向けて戦争の終結を訴えた。

content.content: She appealed to the public for an end to the war.

content: アメリカに向けて、強い態度を取り続けた。

content.content: They keep taking an aggressive attitude toward the United States.

content: 彼は戦争の当事者たちに向けて根気強く停戦協定の締結を訴え続けた。

content.content: He has patiently been appealing to those concerned with the war for the conclusion of a truce.
With a noun expressing a person or an organization, expresses the meaning of “toward.”
4. Nにむけて〈goal〉

content: スポーツ大会に向けて厳しい練習が続けられた。

content.content: They continued practicing very hard for the sports competition.

content: 国際会議の開催に向けてメンバー全員の協力が求められた。

content.content: For the opening of the international conference, the cooperation of all members was requested.

content: 平和的な問題解決に向けて人々は努力を惜しまなかった。

content.content: People spared no efforts in resolving the issue peacefully.
With a noun expressing an event, expresses the meaning of “to aim toward realizing some event.” Followed by a clause expressing some action.
【にめんした】→
【にめんして】
【にめんして】
1. Nにめんして〈face something〉

content: 美しい庭に面して、バルコニーが広がっている。

content.content: The balcony, facing the beautiful garden, stretches before me.

content: この家は広い道路に面している。

content.content: This house faces a wide road.

content: リゾート地のホテルで、海に面した部屋を予約した。

content.content: At the resort, I reserved a hotel room facing the sea.
With a noun expressing a place with a certain expanse such as a road, a garden, or the sea, expresses that some space faces the front of the place. As shown in

content: , にめんして can appear as にめんしている at the end of the sentence. When it modifies a noun, にめんしてbecomes NにめんしたN.

content.content: 2. Nにめんして〈confrontation〉

content: 彼女は非常事態に面しても適切な行動の取れる強い精神力の持ち主なのだ。

content.content: She is a person of great mental vigor who can take appropriate action even in an emergency.

content: 彼は危機的状況に面しても冷静に対処できる人だ。

content.content: He is a man who can calmly cope even when confronting a crisis.
Expresses the meaning of “facing a difficult situation, such as some trouble or crisis.”
【にも】
1. NにもIn this pattern, the particle も is added to the combination of a noun with the particle に attached, in order to emphasize the noun.
a. Nにも〈time, place, direction, other person, etc.〉

content: あそこにも人がいます。

content.content: There are people over there too.

content: 田中さんにも教えてあげよう。

content.content: I’ll tell Tanaka-san, too.

content: 箱根にも日光にも行きました。

content.content: I went not only to Hakone but also to Nikko.

も is used to emphasize phrases with the particle に that express various meanings, adding the meaning that “the same can be said not only about that, but also about something else, too.” When it is not necessary to add the meaning of “also, too,” Nに is used by itself.
b. Nにも〈target of respect〉

content: ご家族のみなさまがたにもおすこやかにお過ごしのことと拝察申し上げます。

content.content: I trust that your family is also doing well. (formal conventional greeting)

content: 皆々様にもご健勝にお過ごしの由、お喜び申し上げます。

content.content: I am pleased to know that you are all fine. (formal conventional greeting)

にも is placed after a noun that indicates someone of higher status, and it is used to express the speaker’s respect for that person. Used only in idiomatic expressions, such as greetings in a very formal letter. ...におかれましては is an even more formal expression that may be used instead.
2. V-ようにもa. V-ようにも...ない

content: 助けを呼ぼうにも声が出ない。

content.content: Even though I tried to cry out for help, I had no voice.

content: 機械を止めようにも、方法が分からなかったのです。

content.content: Even though I wanted to stop the machine, I didn’t know how.

content: 先に進もうにも足が疲れて一歩も踏み出せなかった。

content.content: Although I tried to move forward, my legs were too tired to take a step.

content: 手術をしたときはすでに手遅れで、助けようにも助けようがなかったのです。

content.content: When she had the operation, it was already too late, so there was no way to help her.
Placed after the intentional form of a verb, such as 呼ぼう (will call out) or 止めよう (will stop), and followed by a negative expression. Means “even though I want to do something, I cannot do it.”
b. V-ようにもV-れない

content: 少し休みたいけれど、忙しくて休もうにも休めない。

content.content: I’d like to rest a little, but I’m too busy to take time off.

content: こんなに遠くまで来てしまっては、帰ろうにも帰れない。

content.content: Having come such a long way, I couldn’t go home even if I tried.

content: こんな恐ろしい事件は、忘れようにも忘れられない。

content.content: No matter how hard I try, I can’t forget a horrible incident like this.

content: 土砂崩れで道がふさがれており、それ以上進もうにも進めない状態だった。

content.content: The road was blocked by a landslide, so the situation was that no one could proceed beyond that point, try as they may.

にも is placed after the intentional form of a verb, such as 帰ろう (will go home) or 忘れよう (try to forget), and followed by the negative potential form of the same verb. Means “even though I want to do something, I cannot do it” or “I cannot do...no matter how hard I try.”
【にもかかわらず】［N／A／V　にもかかわらず］［Na であるにもかかわらず］

content: 悪条件にもかかわらず、無事登頂に成功した。

content.content: Despite the unfavorable conditions, she safely made a successful ascent of the mountain.

content: 母が止めたにもかかわらず、息子は出かけていった。

content.content: Although his mother tried to stop him, the son went out.

content: あれだけ努力したにもかかわらず、すべて失敗に終わってしまった。

content.content: Even though I tried so hard, it all ended in failure.

content: 規則で禁止されているにもかかわらず、彼はバイクで通学した。

content.content: Despite the fact that it is against the rules, he went to school by motorbike.

Means “in spite of such-and-such a situation.” Followed by a clause that expresses a situation quite different from what would normally be expected to occur from the situation described in the preceding clause. Can also be used at the beginning of a sentence, as below.
（例）危険な場所だと十分注意されていた。にもかかわらず、軽装で出かけて遭難するはめになった。
I was amply warned that it was a dangerous place. Nevertheless, I went out in light clothing and ended up getting lost.
【にもとづいた】→
【にもとづいて】
【にもとづいて】［Nにもとづいて］

content: 実際にあった話に基づいて小説を書いた。

content.content: I wrote a novel based on a true story.

content: 計画表に基づいて行動する。

content.content: She proceeds according to the schedule.

content: 過去の経験に基づいて判断を下す。

content.content: He makes judgments based on past experience.

content: この小説は実際にあったことに基づいている。

content.content: This novel is based on something that actually happened.

content: 長年の経験に基づいた判断だから、信頼できる。

content.content: Because her judgment is based on many years of experience, I can rely on it.
Means “founded on something” or “on the basis of something.” Can be used as a predicate, as shown in

content: . When it modifies a noun, it takes the form ...にもとづいたN, as shown in
. The form ...にもとづいてのN may also be used.

content.content: 【にもなく】［Nにもなく］

content: 今日はがらにもなく背広なんかを着ている。

content.content: How unlike him to wear a suit today.

content: その光景を見て、我にもなく動揺してしまった。

content.content: Seeing that sight, I was uncharacteristically shaken.
An idiomatic expression that means “different from the usual appearance or nature of someone or something.”
【にもならない】
1. Nにもならない

content: あまりにばかばかしい話で、冗談にもならない。

content.content: This is such a silly story that I can’t accept it even as a joke.

content: こんなに細い木では焚きつけにもならない。

content.content: A piece of wood this thin can’t even be used as kindling.
Follows a noun that denotes something of limited usefulness, such as 冗談 (joke) or 焚きつけ (kindling), and means that the thing in question does not have even that much value.
2. V-るきにもならない

content: あまりにばかばかしくて笑う気にもならない。

content.content: It’s too ridiculous even to make me feel like laughing.

content: 彼の考え方があまりに子供っぽいので、腹を立てる気にもならなかった。

content.content: His way of thinking was so childish that I couldn’t even get angry.

Means “I’m not getting the feeling that I want to do such-and-such.” In many cases, implies a negative evaluation on the part of the speaker, in the sense that the thing referred to in the first clause has such little value that it doesn’t make him/her feel like doing the action in question.
【によったら】→
【によると】1b
【によって】
1. Nによって〈cause〉

content: 私の不注意な発言によって、彼を傷つけてしまった。

content.content: I hurt him with my thoughtless comment.

content: 踏切事故によって、電車は3時間も遅れました。

content.content: An accident at the railroad crossing delayed the train for three whole hours.

content: ほとんどの会社は不況によって経営が悪化した。

content.content: The business activity of almost all companies has deteriorated because of the recession.
Placed after a noun and means “that (= the noun) is the cause of something.” Followed by an expression that indicates a result.
2. Nによって〈agent in a passive sentence〉

content: この建物は有名な建築家によって設計された。

content.content: This building was designed by a famous architect.

content: その村の家の多くは洪水によって押し流された。

content.content: Many of the houses in the village were washed away by the flood.

content: 敵の反撃によって苦しめられた。

content.content: We were tormented by the enemy’s counterattack.

content: これらの聖典はヨーロッパからの宣教師たちによってもたらされた。

content.content: These sacred books were brought by missionaries from Europe.

content: 3年生の児童たちによって校庭に立派な人文字が描かれた。

content.content: A splendid living Chinese character was formed by the third-grade students in the schoolyard.

content: この奇抜なファッションは新しいものを好む若者たちによってただちに受け入れられた。

content.content: This bizarre fashion was instantly accepted by young people who like something new.

Expresses the agent in a passive sentence. Nによって is the same as Xに in the pattern XにYされる. However, when the verb Y expresses the production of something, like 設計する (design), 作る (make) or 書く (write), によって must be used instead of に. Also, when the preceding noun is a thing that is understood to be a cause, like 洪水 (flood) and 敵の反撃 (the enemy’s counterattack) in

content: and
, によって can be replaced by で.

content.content: （例）洪水で押し流された。
They were washed away by the flood.
3. Nによって〈means〉

content: この資料によって多くの事実が明らかになった。

content.content: Many facts have been revealed by this data.

content: 給料をカットすることによって、不況を乗り切ろうとしている。

content.content: They are trying to pull through the recession by reducing wages.

content: 交通網の整備によって、遠距離通勤が可能になった。

content.content: Long-distance commuting has been made possible by improvement of the transportation network.

content: コンピュータによって大量の文書管理が可能になった。

content.content: Computers have made it possible to manage large quantities of documents.

content: インターネットによって世界中の情報がいとも簡単に手に入るようになった。

content.content: The internet has made it possible to obtain information from all over the world with no trouble at all.
Means “by means of something” or “by using some method.”
4. Nによって〈basis〉

content: この資料によっていままで不明だった多くの点が明らかになった。

content.content: Based on this data, many things that were previously unknown have been brought to light.

content: 行くか行かないかは、あしたの天気によって決めよう。

content.content: Let’s decide whether or not to go based on the weather tomorrow.

content: 先生の御指導によってこの作品を完成させることができました。

content.content: Thanks to the teacher’s supervision, I was able to complete this work.

content: 試験の成績よりも通常の授業でどれだけ活躍したかによって成績をつけようと思う。

content.content: I’m planning to grade you based on your classroom performance rather than your exam marks.

content: 恒例によって会議の後に夕食会を設けることにした。

content.content: As is customary, we’ve decided to have a dinner party after the meeting.

content: 例によって彼らは夜遅くまで議論を続けた。

content.content: As usual, they went on with their discussion until late at night.
Attaches to a noun or an interrogative expression followed by か and means “on the grounds of something,” “on the basis of something.” Examples

content: and
are idiomatic expressions that mean “as usual, as always.”

content.content: 5. Nによって〈individual case〉

content: 人によって考え方が違う。

content.content: Ways of thinking differ from person to person.

content: 明日は所によって雨が降るそうだ。

content.content: I hear it’s going to rain in some areas tomorrow.

content: 時と場合によって、考え方を変えなければならないこともある。

content.content: Sometimes we have to change our way of thinking, depending on the time and situation.

content: 場合によってはこの契約を破棄しなければならないかもしれない。

content.content: Depending on the circumstances, I may have to cancel this agreement.

content: 事と次第によっては、裁判に訴えなければならない。

content.content: Depending on what happens, I may have to take the matter to court.
Means “according to various cases of the thing in question.”

content: is an idiomatic expression that means the same as 場合によって (depending on the circumstances/situation)．

content.content: 【によらず】［Nによらず］

content: この会社では、性別や年齢によらず、能力のあるなしによって評価される。

content.content: This company evaluates workers according to their ability, irrespective of sex or age.

content: 古いしきたりによらず、新しい簡素なやりかたで式を行いたい。

content.content: I would like to do the ceremony in a simple new way, rather than following tradition.

content: 彼は見かけによらず頑固な男だ。

content.content: Although he doesn’t look it, he’s a stubborn man.

content: 何事によらず、注意を怠らないことが肝心だ。

content.content: In all things, it is crucial not to stop paying attention.
Means “irrespective of something,” “without corresponding to something.”

content: and
are idiomatic expressions that mean “despite outward appearances” and “in all cases,” respectively.

content.content: 【により】

content: 水質汚染がかなり広がっていることが、環境庁の調査により明らかになった。

content.content: A survey by the Environment Agency has revealed that water pollution has spread considerably.

content: 関東地方はところにより雨。

content.content: It will rain in some parts of the Kanto District.
This is another way of saying によって that is often used in written language.
【によって】
【による】［Nによる］

content: 学長による祝辞に引き続いて、卒業生代表によるスピーチが行われた。

content.content: Following the college president’s congratulatory address, a speech was given by the representative of the graduates.

content: 計画の大幅な変更は、山田の強い主張によるものである。

content.content: The drastic change in the plan is due to Yamada’s strong insistence.

content: 地震による津波の心配はないということである。

content.content: They say there is no danger of a tsunami being caused by the earthquake.

content: 晩御飯を食べて帰るかどうかは、会議の終わる時間による。

content.content: Whether or not I eat dinner before I go home will depend on what time the meeting ends.

content: 車で行くかどうかは場合による。晴れていたら自転車の方が気持ちがいいが、もし雨が降ったら車で行くしかない。

content.content: Whether I go by car or not will depend. If it’s sunny, it would be more pleasant to ride my bicycle, but if it rains, I won’t have any choice but to go by car.
Used to indicate “agent,” “cause,” “basis,” etc. In

content: , the noun in Nによる denotes an agent or cause, while in
and

it expresses a condition for deciding something. When the noun expresses an agent or a cause, this pattern is used in formal, written Japanese. When the noun expresses a condition, this pattern can be used in everyday spoken Japanese, too.

content.content: 【によると】
1. Nによるとa. Nによると

content: 天気予報によると、明日は晴れるそうです。

content.content: According to the weather forecast, it will be sunny tomorrow.

content: 彼の説明によると、この機械は廃棄物を処理するためのものだということです。

content.content: According to his explanation, this machine is for the disposal of waste.

content: あの雲の様子によると、明日は多分晴れるだろう。

content.content: Judging from those clouds, I think it will probably be sunny tomorrow.

Indicates a source from which the speaker has heard something, or a basis from which the speaker infers something. Followed by an expression of hearsay such as ...そうだ (I hear/they say) or ...ということだ (they say), or a suppositional expression such as ...だろう (probably), ...らしい (apparently), etc. In

content: and
, it would also be possible to use ...によれば.

content.content: b. ことによると／ばあいによると

content: ことによると今回の旅行はキャンセルしなければならないかもしれない。

content.content: It may turn out that I’ll have to cancel the upcoming trip.

content: 場合によると彼らも応援に来てくれるかもしれない。

content.content: Depending on the situation, they might come to help us.
Fixed, idiomatic expressions with the meaning of “maybe, perhaps” or “under certain conditions.” Followed by a suppositional expression. Also used in the forms ことによったら and 場合によったら.
2. Vところによると

content: 聞いたところによると、最近は飛行機でいく方が電車より安い場合もあるそうですね。

content.content: From what I’ve heard, you know, these days flying can sometimes be cheaper than going by train.

content: 彼の主張するところによると、彼は事件とは関係ないということだ。

content.content: Based on what he claims, he has nothing to do with the incident.

content: 祖父の語ったところによると、このあたりには昔古い農家があったということだ。

content.content: According to what my grandfather told me, there used to be old farmhouses around here a long time ago.

Indicates a source from which the speaker has heard something, or the basis for a judgment. Followed by an expression of hearsay, such as ...そうだ (I hear/they say) or ...ということだ (they say), or an expression of judgment, such as a supposition or assertion. Also used in the form ...ところによれば.
【によれば】

content: この記録によれば、その城が完成したのは11世紀末のことだ。

content.content: According to this record, the castle was completed at the end of the eleventh century.

content: 彼の話によれば、この茶碗は骨董品として価値の高いものだそうだ。

content.content: According to what he says, apparently this bowl has great value as an antique.
Same as ...によると.
【によると】1a、
【によると】2
【にわたって】［Nにわたって］

content: この研究グループは水質汚染の調査を 10 年にわたって続けてきた。

content.content: This research group has been surveying water pollution over a span of ten years.

content: 彼はこの町を数回にわたって訪れ、ダム建設についての住民との話し合いをおこなっている。

content.content: He has visited this town several times and discussed the construction of a dam with the residents.

content: 首相はヨーロッパからアメリカ大陸まで8カ国にわたって訪れ、経済問題についての理解を求めた。

content.content: The prime minister has visited eight countries from Europe to the United States, seeking an understanding of economic problems.

content: 外国人労働者に関する意識調査の質問項目は多岐に渡っており、とても一言で説明することはできない。

content.content: The questions on the opinion poll regarding foreign workers cover a range of topics, so I really can’t explain them in just a few words.

Attaches to a word or phrase that denotes a period of time, number of times, range of places, etc. Expresses that the period/number/range is large. Often followed by verbs like 行う (perform/carry out), 続ける (continue), or 訪れる (visit). Used in written language and/or formal style.
【にわたり】［Nにわたり］

content: 話し合いは数回にわたり、最終的には和解した。

content.content: There were a number of meetings, and eventually they settled their differences.

content: 彼の研究は多岐にわたり、その成果は世界中の学者に強い影響を与えた。

content.content: His research was extensive and the results had a strong influence on scholars all over the world.

content: 彼女が訪れた国は実に 23 カ国に渡り、その旅を記録した写真集は普通の人々の生活を生き生きと写し取っていることで評判になっている。

content.content: She actually visited a total of 23 countries, and the collection of photographs she took to record her travels has been well-received for its vivid portrayal of the lives of ordinary people.
Has the same meaning as にわたって. While にわたって often modifies a verb that comes right after it, にわたり is usually used at the end of a clause. Used in written language and/or formal style.

【ぬ】An auxiliary verb that expresses negation in classical Japanese. In modern Japanese, traces of ぬ remain in the ん found in expressions like ...ません (do not...), 知らん (don’t know), and 好かん (don’t like). Also used in a number of idiomatic fixed expressions.
1. V-ぬ

content: 知らぬ存ぜぬで（＝知らないと主張し続けて）押し通す。

content.content: She persists in denying that she knows anything at all.

content: 知らぬが仏（＝相手が知らないうちに何か相手にとって都合の悪いことをする場合に用いる）。

content.content: Ignorance is bliss. (= an expression used when someone does something disadvantageous to the other person without that person noticing)

content: 予期せぬ（＝予期しない）事件が起こった。

content.content: An unexpected incident has occurred.

content: 急いで対策を考えなければならぬ。

content.content: We must quickly consider countermeasures.
Used in fixed expressions that are idioms. Means ...ない (not...).

content: is the literary form of the expression ...なければならない.

content.content: 2. V-ぬうちに

content: 誰にも気付かれぬうちにここを抜け出そう。

content.content: Let’s get out of here before anyone finds us.

content: 暗くならぬうちに家にたどり着けるといいのだが。

content.content: I hope I can get home before it gets dark....
Literary form of the expression ...ないうちに.
【うち】2c
3. V-ぬばかり

content: おまえは馬鹿だと言わぬばかりの顔をした。

content.content: The look on his face was almost as if he were saying, “You’re stupid.”

content: 泣かぬばかりに懇願した。

content.content: On the verge of tears, she implored me.
Used in fixed, idiom-like expressions and means “it looks as if someone is about to do something.” Literary form of the expression V-んばかり.
【ばかり】
4. V-ぬまでも

content: この崖から落ちたら、死に至らぬまでも重傷はまぬがれないだろう。

content.content: If you fall off this cliff, you probably can’t escape serious injury, even if you don’t die.

content: 実刑は受けぬまでも罰金は払わせられるだろう。

content.content: Even if he’s not sentenced to imprisonment, he’ll probably be made to pay a fine.
Literary form of the expression ...ないまでも.
【ないまでも】
5. V-ぬまに

content: 鬼のいぬ間に洗濯（＝邪魔になる人がいない間にしたいことをする）。

content.content: When the cat’s away, the mice will play. (= do whatever you want while a person who will stop you is away)

content: 知らぬ間にこんなに遠くまで来てしまった。

content.content: I have come this far without realizing it.
Used in idiomatic fixed expressions. Means “while not doing....”
【ぬき】
1. Nぬきで

content: この集まりでは、形式張ったこと抜きで気楽にやりましょう。

content.content: At this gathering, let’s relax and have fun, without standing on ceremony.

content: この後は偉い人抜きで、若手だけで飲みに行きましょう。

content.content: After this, let’s leave all the bigwigs behind and go have a drink with just the younger members.

content: 前置きは抜きで、さっそく本論に入りましょう。

content.content: Let’s skip the preliminaries and go straight to the main subject.
Means “excluding/without....” Can also be used in the form Nはぬきで, as shown in
2. Nぬきに... V-れない

content: この企画は、彼の協力抜きには考えられない。

content.content: I cannot imagine carrying out this plan without his cooperation.

content: 資金援助抜きに研究を続けることは不可能だ。

content.content: It’s impossible to continue my research without financial support.

content: 今回の企画の成功は山田君の活躍抜きに語れない。

content.content: We cannot talk about the success of this project without mentioning Yamada-kun’s efforts.

Placed after a noun and followed at the end of the sentence by an expression such as ...できない (cannot do...), V-れない (cannot do...), or 不可能だ (it’s impossible). Means “cannot do...without such-and-such.”
3. Nはぬきにして

content: この際、仕事の話は抜きにして、大いに楽しみましょう。

content.content: Let’s take this opportunity to put shop talk aside and really enjoy ourselves.

content: 冗談は抜きにして、内容の討議に入りましょう。

content.content: All joking aside, let’s start discussing the matter at hand.
Means “excluding...” or “stopping/quitting....”
【ぬく】［R-ぬく］

content: 苦しかったが最後まで走りぬいた。

content.content: It was very hard, but I ran all the way to the end.

content: 一度始めたからには、あきらめずに最後までやりぬこう。

content.content: Now that we’ve started, let’s see it through to the end, without giving up.

content: 考え抜いた結果の決心だからもう変わることはない。

content.content: I reached this decision after thinking long and hard about it, so I’m not going to change my mind.

content: この長い漂流を耐え抜くことができたのは、「ここで死にたくない」という強い気持ちがあったからだと思います。

content.content: I think the reason I was able to survive being adrift at sea for so long is that I had a strong feeling that “I don’t want to die here.”
Means finishing all of the necessary actions or processes, right up to the end. Conveys a strong implication that suffering has been endured in order to accomplish something.
【ぬまでも】［V-ぬまでも］

content: 邸宅とは言わぬまでも、せめて小さな一戸建ぐらいは建てたいものだ。

content.content: I’m not asking for a mansion, but I’d at least like to build a small house of my own.

content: この崖から落ちたら、死に至らぬまでも、重傷はまぬがれないだろう。

content.content: If you fall off this cliff, you probably can’t avoid serious injury, even if you don’t die.
Literary form of the expression ...ないまでも.
【ないまでも】
【ねばならない】［V-ねばならない］

content: 平和の実現のために努力せねばならない。

content.content: We must strive to achieve peace.

content: 一致協力して問題解決に当たらねばならない。

content.content: We have to join forces to solve the problem.
This is a form of ...なければならない that is used in written language.
【なければ】2
【ねばならぬ】［V-ねばならぬ］

content: 暴力には力を合わせて立ち向かわなければならぬ。

content.content: We must work together to fight against violence.

content: 自然破壊は防がねばならぬ。

content.content: We must protect the environment from destruction.
An even more literary expression than ...ねばならない.
【なければ】2
1. NのNa. NのN〈affiliation〉

content: これはあなたの財布じゃないですか。

content.content: Isn’t this your wallet?

content: こちらは東京電気の田中さんです。

content.content: This is Tanaka-san, from the Tokyo Electric Company.

content: 東京のアパートはとても高い。

content.content: Apartments in Tokyo are very expensive.
The first noun modifies the noun that comes after it and expresses the owner, affiliation, location, etc. of the thing indicated by the second noun.
b. NのN〈characteristic〉

content: 病気の人を見舞う。

content.content: (I) visit the patient.

content: バラの花を贈る。

content.content: (I) give roses.

content: 3時の電車に乗る。

content.content: (I) take the three o’clock train.

content: カップ1杯の水を加える。

content.content: (I) add a cup of water.
The first noun modifies the noun that comes after it and expresses a variety of meanings, such as a characteristic, the state, the kind, or the quantity of the noun.
c. NのN〈apposition〉

content: 友人の和男に相談した。

content.content: I consulted my friend, Kazuo.

content: 社長の木村さんをご紹介しましょう。

content.content: Let me introduce you to Kimura-san, the company president.

content: これは次女の安子でございます。

content.content: This is my second daughter, Yasuko.
Expresses that the N preceding の and the N following it are the same person/thing. The second noun slot is often filled by a proper noun, such as the name of someone or something.
d. N（+助詞）のN

content: 子供の成長は早い。

content.content: Children grow up fast.

content: 自転車の修理を頼んだ。

content.content: (I) requested bicycle repairs.

content: アメリカからの観光客を案内する。

content.content: (I) guide tourists from the United States.

content: 京都までのバスに乗った。

content.content: (I) took the bus that goes to Kyoto.

content: 田中さんとの旅行は楽しかった。

content.content: The trip with Tanaka-san was fun.

content: 京都での宿泊はホテルより旅館のほうがいい。

content.content: If you stay in Kyoto, you should try a Japanese-style inn rather than a hotel.

Expresses the relationship between two nouns: 子供 and 成長 in 子供が成長する (children grow up), 自転車 and 修理 in 自転車を修理する (repair the bicycle), アメリカ and 観光客 in アメリカから観光客が来る (tourists come from the United States). The first noun modifies the second. When the particles が and を are used in the kernel (basic) clauses, as in 子供が成長する and 自転車を修理する, these particles do not appear in the NのN phrases, which in this case are 子供の成長 (children’s growth) and 自転車の修理 (bicycle repairs). Other types of particles, however, must be retained, as in アメリカからの観光客 (tourists from the United States) and 田中さんとの旅行 (the trip with Tanaka-san). The particle に does not appear in this pattern at all. へ is used instead of に, as in the example below.
（×）母にの手紙
a letter to for my mother
（○）母への手紙
a letter to my mother
e. Nの...N

content: 彼の書いた絵はすばらしい。

content.content: The picture he drew is marvelous.

content: 学生たちの歌う声が聞こえる。

content.content: I can hear the students singing.

content: タイプの上手な人を探している。

content.content: I am looking for a person who is good at typing.

content: 花の咲く頃にまた来てください。

content.content: Please come to visit us again when flowers are in bloom.

In this pattern, の is used instead of が in a clause that modifies a noun. For example, the clauses 彼が書いた絵 (the picture he drew) and タイプが上手な人 (a person who is good at typing), which modify the nouns 絵 (picture) and 人 (person), respectively, become 彼の書いた絵 and タイプの上手な人.
2. ...のa. Nの

content: これは私のです。

content.content: This is mine.

content: 電気製品はこの会社のが使いやすい。

content.content: Regarding electric products, the ones from this company are easy to use.

content: この電話は壊れてますので、隣の部屋のをお使い下さい。

content.content: This phone is out of order, so please use the one in the next room.

content: ラーメンなら、駅前のそば屋のが安くておいしいよ。

content.content: When it comes to Chinese noodles, those in the noodle shop by the station are delicious and inexpensive.

content: 柄物のハンカチしか置いてないけど、無地のはありませんか。

content.content: I can find only handkerchiefs with a pattern...do you have any plain ones?
Means “something from/in (that belongs to/that has) N.”
b. ...の［Na なの］［A／V　の］

content: これはちょっと小さすぎます。もう少し大きいのはないですか。

content.content: This is a little too small. Do you have one that’s a little larger?

content: みんなで料理を持ちよってパーティーをしたんだけど、私が作ったのが一番評判よかったんだ。

content.content: We had a potluck party where everyone brought a dish, and the one I made was the most popular.

content: これは大きすぎて使いにくい。もっと小さくて便利なのを探さなくてはならない。

content.content: This one is hard to use because it’s too big. I have to look for something smaller and handier.

content: その牛乳は古いから、さっき買ってきたのを使って下さい。

content.content: That milk is old, so please use the one that I’ve just bought.
Placed after a verb or an adjective and means “something large,” “something I made,” etc.
c. Nの...の［Nの Na なの］［Nの　A／V　の］

content: 戸棚のなるべく頑丈なのを探してきてほしい。

content.content: I want you to go out and find a cabinet that’s as sturdy as possible.

content: ビールの冷えたのはないですか。

content.content: Is there any beer that’s been chilled?

content: 袋の中にリンゴの腐ったのが入っていた。

content.content: There was a rotten apple in the bag.
Used to talk about the thing denoted by N, referring in particular to a restricted class of things that are in the state expressed by the modifying clause. For instance,

content: literally means “with regard to beer, the ones (bottles/cans) that have been chilled.”

content.content: 1. ...の〈question〉［N／Na　なの］［A／V　の］

content: A:遊んでばかりいて。試験、本当に大丈夫なの？

content.content: All you do is fool around. Are you really sure you can pass the exam?
B:心配するなよ。大丈夫だってば。
Don’t worry about me. I’ll be all right.

content: A:明子ちゃんは、なにをして遊びたいの？

content.content: Akiko-chan, what do you want to play?
B:バトミントン。
Badminton.

content: A:スポーツは何が得意なの？

content.content: What sport are you good at?
B:テニスです。
Tennis.

content: 元気ないね。どうしたの？

content.content: You seem a little out of spirits. What’s the matter?
Used with rising intonation to express a question. Used in spoken Japanese, when the speaker is talking to a child or someone s/he knows well.
2. ...の〈mild assertion〉［N／Na　なの］［A／V　の］

content: お母さん、あの子がいじわるするの。

content.content: Mom, that kid is mean to me.

content: A:あした映画に行きませんか。

content.content: Would you like to go to see a movie tomorrow?
B:残念だけど、明日はほかに用事があるの。
I’m afraid I have something else to do tomorrow.

content: 彼は私に腹を立てているみたいなの。

content.content: He seems to be angry with me.

content: A:元気ないですね。

content.content: You don’t look very peppy.
B:ええ、ちょっと気分が悪いの。
No, I don’t feel so well.

content: A:もう少し早く歩けない？

content.content: Can’t you walk a little faster?
B:ごめんね。ちょっと足が痛いの。
Sorry. My foot hurts.
Used with falling intonation to make a mild assertion. Usually used by women or children.
3. ...の〈confirmation〉

content: 和夫: やあ、明子さん。今日は。

content.content: Kazuo: Hi, Akiko-san. How are you?
明子: あら和夫さん。来てたの。
Akiko: Oh, Kazuo-san. So you’re here.

content: 春子: 正子さん、朝日高校出身なんですって？　私もよ。

content.content: Haruko: Masako-san, did I hear that you went to Asahi High School? Me, too.
正子: へえ、春子さんも朝日高校出身なの。
Masako: Really? You went to Asahi High School too?

content: A:君の発表すごくおもしろかったよ。

content.content: Your presentation was really interesting.
B:あれ、君も聞いてくれていたの。
Oh, were you listening too?
Used with either rising or falling intonation to ask the listener to confirm something.
4. ...の〈mild imperative〉［V-る／V-ない　の］

content: 病気なんだから、大人しく寝ているの。

content.content: You’re sick, so you need to be quiet and stay in bed.

content: そんなわがままは言わないの。

content.content: Don’t be so selfish.

content: 明日は早いんだから、今晩は早く寝るの。

content.content: You’ll be leaving early tomorrow, so go to bed early tonight.

content: 男の子はこんなことで泣かないの。

content.content: Boys shouldn’t cry over something like this.
Used with level or falling intonation when a woman gives a mild order or prohibition to someone of lower status.
1. ...の...のと［NだのNだのと］［Na だのNa だのと］［AのAのと］［VのVのと］

content: 量が多すぎるの少なすぎるのと文句ばかり言っている。

content.content: She’s always complaining that there’s too much or too little.

content: 頭が痛いの気が進まないのと言っては、誘いを断っている。

content.content: He always declines invitations, saying he has a headache or doesn’t feel like going.

content: 形が気にいらないの色が嫌いだのと、気むずかしいことばかり言っている。

content.content: She’s always fussy about things, saying she doesn’t like the shape or hates the color.

content: 私の父は、行儀が悪いの言葉づかいが悪いのと、口うるさい。

content.content: My father is always lecturing me, saying that my manners are bad and I use bad  language.
...の...のと lists two things that are similar and expresses that someone is fussy about a lot of things. There are also idiomatic expressions that use this pattern, as below.
（例）なんのか（ん）のと（＝ああだこうだと、いろいろ）文句ばかり言っている。
She is always complaining about one thing or another (= various things).
（例）四の五の言わずに（＝あれこれ言わずに）ついてこい。
Just shut up (= without grumbling about this and that) and follow me.
2. ...の...ないのa. ...の...ないのと［A-いのA-くないのと］［V-るのV-ないのと］

content: 行くの行かないのと言い争っている。

content.content: They’re arguing about whether to go or not.

content: 結婚したいのしたくないのとわがままを言う。

content.content: He’s being selfish about whether he wants to get married or not.

content: 会社を辞めるの辞めないのと悩んでいた。

content.content: She was worried about whether she should leave the company or not.

content: A:あの二人、離婚するんですって？

content.content: Is it true that those two are getting a divorce?
B:ううん。離婚するのしないのと大騒ぎしたけど、結局はうまくおさまったみたいよ。
No. They made a big fuss about whether or not to get a divorce, but apparently they were eventually able to work things out.
Lists two things that contrast and expresses that someone is making a fuss about a lot of things.
b. ...の...ないのって［A-いのA-くないのって］［V-るのV-ないのって］

content: A:北海道、寒かったでしょ。

content.content: It was cold in Hokkaido, wasn’t it?
B:寒いの寒くないのって。耳が凍るんじゃないかと思ったよ。
It wasn’t just cold. I thought my ears would freeze!

content: A:あの治療は痛かったでしょうね。

content.content: That treatment must have been very painful.
B:痛いの痛くないのって。思わず大声で叫んじゃったよ。
Did it ever hurt! I couldn’t help screaming.

Expresses an extremely intense degree of something. Means “an extremely...state or condition.” Often followed by the description of a situation that arose as a result of the extreme condition. Also used in the form ...のなんのって. Used in casual spoken Japanese.
3. ...のなんのa. ...のなんのと［A／V　のなんのと］

content: 高すぎるのなんのと、文句ばかり言っている。

content.content: She’s always complaining, saying it’s too expensive and so on.

content: やりたくないのなんのとわがままを言い始めた。

content.content: He has started getting selfish, saying he doesn’t want to do this or that.

content: 頭が痛いのなんのと理由をつけては学校を休んでいる。

content.content: She’s been making excuses for not coming to school, saying she has a headache or whatever.
Expresses the way that someone is making a fuss about something unfavorable or unpleasant.
b. ...のなんのって［A／V　のなんのって］

content: A:彼女に会って驚いたんじゃない？

content.content: Weren’t you surprised to see her?
B:驚いたのなんのって。すっかり変わっちゃってるんだもの。初めは全然違う人かと思ったよ。
Was I ever! She has completely changed. At first I thought she was somebody else.

content: A:あのホテルは車の音がうるさくありませんでしたか。

content.content: Didn’t the noise of the traffic bother you at that hotel?
B:いやあ、うるさいのなんのって、結局一晩中寝られなかった。
Did it ever! I ended up not being able to sleep all night.

content: 喜んだのなんのって、あんなに嬉しそうな顔は見たことがない。

content.content: How delighted she was! I’ve never seen such a happy face.
Has the same meaning as ...の...ないのって in 2b.
【のいたり】→
【いたり】
【のか】［N／Na　なのか］［A／V　のか］
1. ...のか〈realization〉

content: なんだ、猫だったのか。誰か人がいるのかと思った。

content.content: Oh, so it’s just a cat? I thought there was somebody there.

content: 彼は知っていると思っていたのに。全然知らなかったのか。

content.content: I thought he knew. So he actually had no idea, huh.

content: なんだ。まだだれも来ていないのか。ぼくが一番遅いと思ってたのに。

content.content: You mean nobody is here yet? I thought I would be the last one to arrive.
Used with falling intonation. Expresses mild surprise on the part of the speaker when s/he finds out that something is not what s/he expected.
2. ...のか〈question〉

content: 朝の5時？　そんなに早く起きるのか？

content.content: Five in the morning? You get up that early?

content: 君は娘に恋人がいたことも知らなかったのか？

content.content: Didn’t you know that your daughter had a steady boyfriend?

content: A:もう帰るのか？

content.content: Are you going home already?
B:うん。今日は疲れたから。
Yeah, I’m tired today.
Used with rising intonation to ask someone a question or confirm something.
3. ...のか〈indirect question〉

content: 何時までに行けばいいのか聞いてみよう。

content.content: Let’s ask her what time we should be there.

content: 彼はいつも無表情で、何を考えているのかさっぱり分からない。

content.content: He’s always expressionless, so I never have the slightest idea what he’s thinking.

content: この書類、どこに送ったらいいのか教えて下さい。

content.content: Can you tell me where I should send this document?

content: 行くのか行かないのかはっきりして下さい。

content.content: Please make up your mind whether or not you’re going to go.

content: あの人はやる気があるのかないのか、さっぱり分からない。

content.content: I have no idea whether s/he intends to do it or not.
Used to turn questions like 何時までに行けばいいのですか (by what time should I be there?) or 行くのですか、行かないのですか (are you going or not?) into indirect questions that are incorporated into another sentence.
【のきわみ】→
【きわみ】

【のだ】［N／Na　なのだ］［A／V　のだ］Usually used in written Japanese. In spoken Japanese, it often becomes んだ. The polite form of this expression is のです, which is also used in spoken Japanese. In casual spoken Japanese, だ may be dropped so the sentence ends with の (e.g. どうしたの？). In formal written Japanese, のである may be used.
1. ...のだ〈explanation〉

content: 道路が渋滞している。きっとこの先で工事をしているのだ。

content.content: The road is jammed with traffic. There must be some construction going on ahead.

content: 彼をすっかり怒らせてしまった。よほど私の言ったことが気にさわったのだろう。

content.content: I made him totally angry. What I said must have really offended him.

content: 泰子は私のことが嫌いなのだ。だって、このところ私を避けようとしているもの。

content.content: I’m sure Yasuko doesn’t like me, because she’s trying to avoid me these days.
Used to explain the cause or reason for what was stated in the preceding sentence, for the speaker’s immediate circumstances, etc.
2. ...のだ〈claim〉

content: やっぱりこれでよかったのだ。

content.content: This was the right decision after all.

content: 誰がなんと言おうと私の意見は間違っていないのだ。

content.content: Whatever anyone else may say, my opinion is ultimately right.

content: 誰が反対しても僕はやるのだ。

content.content: I’m going to do it, no matter who is against it.
Used by the speaker to make a strong assertion to convince him/herself of something or to show his/her own determination.
3. 疑問詞...のだ

content: 彼は私を避けようとしている。いったい私の何が気に入らないのだ。

content.content: He’s trying to avoid me. What in heaven’s name is it about me that he doesn’t like?

content: こんな馬鹿げたことを言い出したのはだれなのだ。

content.content: Whoever started saying such a stupid thing?
Placed after a clause containing a question word and used by the speaker to ask him/herself or the addressee for some kind of explanation.
4. つまり...のだ

content: 防災設備さえ完備していればこのようなことにならなかった。つまりこの災害は天災ではなく人災だったのだ。

content.content: If only disaster prevention equipment had been fully supplied, this wouldn’t have happened. In other words, this was not a natural disaster but a man-made one.

content: 私が言いたいのは、緊急に対策を打たなければならないということなのだ。

content.content: What I want to say is that we must take emergency measures to deal with this.

content: 会社の経営は最悪の事態を迎えている。要するに、人員削減はもはや避けられないことなのだ。

content.content: Company operations are facing the worst situation possible. In short, personnel cuts are now virtually unavoidable.
Used after expressions like つまり (in other words), 私が言いたいのは (what I want to say is), and 要するに (in short). Used to paraphrase what was stated previously.
5. だから...のだ

content: コンセントが抜けている。だからスイッチを入れてもつかなかったのだ。

content.content: It wasn’t plugged in. That’s why it didn’t start when we switched it on.

content: エンジンオイルが漏れている。だから変な臭いがしたのだ。

content.content: The engine oil is leaking. That’s why we smelled something strange.

content: 産業廃棄物の不法投棄が後を立たない。そのために我々の生活が脅かされているのだ。

content.content: There is no end to the illegal dumping of industrial waste. That is why our lives are threatened.
Used after expressions such as だから (that’s why) and そのために (for that reason). Means that what is stated in the sentence with のだ is a consequence of what was stated in the preceding sentence.
6. ...のだから［N／Na　なのだから］［A／V　のだから］

content: まだ子供なのだから、わからなくても仕方がないでしょう。

content.content: Because he’s still a child, it can’t be helped if he doesn’t understand.

content: 私でもできたのだから、あなたにできないはずがない。

content.content: Since even I was able to do it, there’s no reason you shouldn’t be able to.

content: あした出発するのだから、今日中に準備をしておいた方がいい。

content.content: Since we’re leaving tomorrow, we should get ready today.

content: 冬の山は危険なのだから、くれぐれも慎重に行動してくださいね。

content.content: Mountains in the winter are dangerous, so please proceed with the greatest caution.

Placed after a clause. Indicates that the speaker acknowledges whatever is stated in that clause to be a fact, as well as that this fact is the cause or reason that leads to the judgment etc. stated in clause that follows. For instance, in

content: , after the speaker acknowledges that “he is still a child,” s/he makes the judgment, based on this fact, that he (the child) should not be expected to understand. In contrast, in the sentenceまだ子供だからわからないのだろう, which means “the reason he doesn’t understand is probably that he is a child,” the speaker is guessing the reason. In spoken Japanese, のだから often becomes ...んだから.

content.content: 【のだった】
1. V-るのだった〈regret〉

content: あと 10 分あれば間に合ったのに。もう少し早く準備しておくのだった。

content.content: If I’d just had ten more minutes, I could have made it. I should have gotten ready a little earlier.

content: こんなにつまらない仕事なら、断わるのだった。

content.content: If I’d known this was going to be such a boring job, I would have turned it down.

content: 試験は悲惨な結果だった。こんなことなら、もっとしっかり勉強しておくのだったと後悔しています。

content.content: My results on the exam were horrible. Now I’m sorry, because I would have studied harder if I’d known it would be like this.
Expresses the speaker’s feeling of regret when s/he realizes that s/he should have carried out an action that s/he did not actually do. In casual spoken Japanese, the form ...んだった is usually used.
2. ...のだった〈strong feeling〉［N／Na　なのだった］［A／V　のだった］

content: 田辺はそれが贈賄であると知りながら、金を渡したのだった。

content.content: Even though he knew it was a bribe, Tanabe handed over the money.

content: この小さな事故が後の大惨事のきっかけとなるのだったが、その時はことの重大さにだれも気付いていなかった。

content.content: This slight mishap would trigger the disaster that came later, but at the time nobody realized its importance.
This use of のだった is comparable to Usage 1 of のだ. However, のだった is used when describing a past event with some kind of emotion. Often seen in written Japanese, such as novels and essays.
【のだったら】［N／Na　なのだったら］［A／V　のだったら］

content: 風邪なんだったら、そんな薄着はだめだよ。

content.content: If you have a cold, you shouldn’t wear such light clothing.

content: そんなに嫌いなんだったら、むりに食べなくてもいいよ。

content.content: If you dislike it that much, you don’t have to eat it.

content: こんなに寒いんだったら、もう1枚着て来るんだった。

content.content: If I’d known it was going to be this cold, I would have come wearing another layer.

content: A:そのパーティ、私も行きたいな。

content.content: I want to go to that party, too.
B:あなたが行くんだったら私も行こうかな。
If you’re going, then maybe I’ll go, too.
Refers to something the speaker has just heard, a current state of affairs, etc. Means “if so” or “under those circumstances.” In spoken Japanese, the form んだったら is often used.
【のだろう】［N／Na　なのだろう］［A／V　のだろう］This expression is a combination of のだ and だろう. In spoken Japanese, the form んだろう is often used.
1. ...のだろう〈supposition, conjecture〉...んだろう

content: 大川さんはうれしそうだ。何かいいことがあったのだろう。

content.content: Okawa-san looks happy. I guess something good must have happened to him.

content: 子供はよく眠っている。今日一日よく遊んだのだろう。

content.content: The child is sleeping soundly. I guess she played hard all day today.

content: 大きなスーパーマーケットができて一年もしないうちに、前の八百屋は営業をやめてしまった。きっと、お客をみんなとられたのだろう。

content.content: In less than a year after the big supermarket was built, the fruit and vegetable store out front closed down. I’m sure all their customers were taken away by the supermarket.

content: 実験に失敗したのにこのような興味深い結果が得られたのには、何か別の要因があるのだろう。

content.content: There must be some other factor that explains why we were able to obtain interesting results like this, even though the experiment failed.

content: この製品は特別に売れ行きがいい。きっと宣伝が上手なんだろう。

content.content: This product sells particularly well. The ad campaign must be pretty good.

Used with falling intonation to express a conjecture. When の is inserted right before だろう, it implies a judgment on the part of the speaker with respect to a certain event, such as a supposition about the reason or cause for it.
2. ...のだろう〈confirmation〉...んだろう

content: A:10 年ぶりの同窓会だね。君も行くんだろう？

content.content: It’s the first class reunion in ten years. You’re going too, right?
B:うん、行くつもりだ。
Yes, I’m planning to.

content: A:来月ディズニーランドに行くの。

content.content: I’m going to Disneyland next month.
B:え、また？　もう何回も行ったんだろう？
What, again? Haven’t you already been there lots of times?
A:うん。でもおもしろいんだもん。
Yeah, but it’s fun!

content: A:来週は試験だから、週末は忙しいんだろう？

content.content: You have exams next week, so you’re probably busy over the weekend, aren’t you?
B:うん。まあね。
Yeah. Sort of.

content: A:新しいコンピュータ買ったんだって？　新型は便利なんだろう？

content.content: I heard you bought a new computer. The new models are really handy, aren’t they?
B:ええ。本当に便利ですよ。
Yes, it’s really handy.

Used with rising intonation to seek confirmation. When の／ん is placed right before だろう, it implies that the speaker is trying to confirm something on the basis of information or a supposition derived from the preceding context or situation. Usually used in spoken Japanese by males. Often used in the form んだろう.
3. ...のだろうか...んだろうか

content: 子どもたちが公園にたくさんいる。今日は学校が休みなのだろうか。

content.content: There are lots of children in the park. I wonder if today is a school holiday.

content: A:山口さんこの頃元気がないね。

content.content: Yamaguchi-san doesn’t look good these days.
B:うん。顔色も悪いし、体の具合でも悪いのだろうか。
Yeah. She looks pale, so I wonder if maybe she’s sick or something.

content: A:来年は入試だというのに、太郎ったら、全然勉強しようとしないんですよ。

content.content: That Taro—even though he has entrance exams next year, he doesn’t want to study at all.
B:うん。あれでどこかの高校に入れるんだろうか。心配だなあ。
I know. If he keeps this up, I wonder whether he’ll be able to get into a high school. I’m worried about him.

content: A:山下さん、うれしそうね。

content.content: Yamashita-san looks happy, doesn’t she?
B:ほんとだね。何かいいことでもあったんだろうか。
She really does. I wonder if something good happened to her.
Expresses a feeling of suspicion or worry on the part of the speaker. Used when the speaker is making a conjecture about something, based on contextual information or the situation at hand.
【ので】［N／Na　なので］［A／V　ので］

content: 雨が降りそうなので試合は中止します。

content.content: Because it looks like rain, we’re canceling the game.

content: もう遅いのでこれで失礼いたします。

content.content: It’s late, so I need to get going.

content: 風邪をひいたので会社を休みました。

content.content: I caught a cold, so I took some time off work.

content: 入学式は 10 時からですので、9時頃家を出れば間に合うと思います。

content.content: The entrance ceremony starts at ten o’clock, so I think I’ll make it in time if I leave home around nine.

content: A:これからお茶でもどうですか。

content.content: Shall we have a cup of tea now?
B:すみません、ちょっと用事がありますので。
I’m sorry, but I have something to do.

Used to express that the situation described in the clause that follows ので occurs because of the cause or reason stated in the clause before it. Used when the causal relation between the situations in the first and second clauses can be recognized objectively. Thus, the situation in the second clause is usually something that has already occurred or is sure to occur. Expressions based on a judgment made by the speaker, such as commands, tend not to be used in this clause.
（×）時間がないので急げ。
Because there’s no time, get moving.
（○）時間がないから急げ。
We don’t have time, so get moving.
Often used to convey the reason for a refusal or to give an excuse, as shown in

content: . In casual spoken Japanese, it takes the form んで.

content.content: 【のであった】［N／Na　なのであった］［A／V　のであった］

content: 彼は大学を辞めて故郷に帰った。ようやく父のあとを受けて家業を継ぐ決心がついたのであった。

content.content: He dropped out of college and went back to his hometown. This was because he had finally decided to take over the family business from his father.

content: ついに両国に平和が訪れたのであった。

content.content: At last, peace came to the two nations.
のであった is a formal way of saying のだった. Used when the speaker looks back at the past with some kind of emotion.
【のだった】2
【のである】［N／Na　なのである］［A／V　のである］

content: 解決には時間がかかりそうだ。問題は簡単ではないのである。

content.content: It looks like it will take some time to reach a solution. That is because the problem is not simple.

content: 結局のところ、政局に大きな変化は期待できないのである。

content.content: After all, we cannot expect a radical change in the political situation.
のである is a formal way of saying のだ.
【のだ】
【のです】［N／Na　なのです］［A／V　のです］This is the polite form of のだ. In spoken Japanese, のです is used in polite conversations. However, usually んです is used more often.
1. ...のです〈explanation〉

content: 遅くなってすみません。途中で渋滞に巻き込まれてしまったのです。

content.content: I’m sorry to be late. I got stuck in traffic on the way.

content: 電話を使わせていただきたいのですが、よろしいでしょうか。

content.content: I’d like to make a call, so would it be all right if I used your phone?

content: ハヤブサは突然急降下を始めました。獲物を見つけたのです。

content.content: The falcon suddenly began to swoop down. It had spotted prey.
【のだ】
2. ...のです〈claim〉

content: これからはあなたたちがこの店をまもり発展させて行くのです。

content.content: From now on it will be all of you who maintain and build up this store.

content: やはり私の考えは間違っていなかったのです。

content.content: As I’d expected, my thinking was not wrong.

content: あなたはことの本質を理解していないのです。

content.content: You don’t understand the true nature of the matter.

content: だれがなんと言おうと、私は仕事を辞めるのです。

content.content: Whatever anyone else may say, I’m going to quit my job.
【のだ】
3. ...のです〈topic cue〉

content: 先週京都へ行ってきたのですが、そこで偶然高橋さんに会いましてね。相変わらず仕事に励んでいるようでした。

content.content: I went to Kyoto last week, and I ran into Takahashi-san there. It looks like she’s still plugging away at work, as usual.

content: 実は近々結婚するのです。それでご挨拶にうかがいたいのですが、ご都合はいかがでしょうか。

content.content: As a matter of fact, I will be getting married quite soon, so I would like to pay you a visit. Could you tell me when it would be convenient for you?
Used to create the opportunity to introduce a new topic by reporting a background situation or state of affairs.
4. ...のですか

content: どうして彼が犯人だとわかったのですか。

content.content: How did you know he was guilty?

content: 田中さんはタフですね。なにかスポーツでもしているのですか。

content.content: You’re really tough, Tanaka-san. Do you play any sports?

content: A:もうお帰りになるのですか。

content.content: Are you going home now?
B:ええ。ほかに用事もありますので。
Yes. I have some other things to do.
Used when the speaker asks the addressee for some kind of explanation regarding a situation at the time of speaking or the topic at hand.
5. つまり...のです

content: 締切は今月末、つまりあと5日しかないのです。

content.content: The deadline is the end of this month. This means we have only five days left.

content: 私が言いたいのは、緊急に対策を打たなければならないと言うことなのです。

content.content: What I want to say is that we need to take countermeasures immediately.
【のだ】
6. だから...のだ

content: ずいぶん熱が高いですよ。だから頭がいたかったのですね。

content.content: You have quite a high temperature. That’s why you had a headache, isn’t it.

content: 社長は私を信頼していない。だからこの仕事を任せてもらえなかったのだ。

content.content: The company president doesn’t trust me. That’s why he didn’t give me this job.

content: ここにすきまがあるようですね。そのために風が吹き込んでくるのですよ。

content.content: It looks like there is a crack here. That’s why the wind is blowing in.
【のだ】
7. ...のですから

content: 時間はあるのですから、ゆっくりやって下さい。

content.content: You have plenty of time, so please do it slowly.

content: ここまで来たのだから、あともう一息です。

content.content: We’ve come this far, so one more push and we’ll be there.
【のだ】6
【のでは】［N／Na　なのでは］［A／V　のでは］

content: そんなに臆病なのでは、どこにも行けませんよ。

content.content: If you’re that timid, you won’t be able to go anywhere.

content: 雨なのではしかたがない。あしたにしよう。

content.content: There’s nothing we can do about the rain. Let’s make it tomorrow.

content: こんなに暑いのでは、きょうの遠足はたいへんだろうね。

content.content: With this heat, today’s school outing will probably be quite gruelling.

content: こんなにたくさんの人に見られているのでは緊張してしまうでしょう。

content.content: With so many people looking at him/her, who wouldn’t get nervous?

Means “if so” or “under those circumstances,” with respect to something the speaker has just heard, the situation at the time of speaking, etc. Followed by expressions that indicate a negative attitude on the part of the speaker, such as こまる (be in a fix) or たいへんだ (it’s hard/terrible). In spoken Japanese, the forms なんじゃ or んじゃ are often used.
【のではあるまいか】→
【ではあるまいか】
【のではないか】→
【ではないか2】
【のではないだろうか】→
【ではないだろうか】
【のではなかったか】［N／Na　なのではなかったか］［A／V　のではなかったか］
1. ...のではなかったか〈doubt, question〉

content: 当時の人々は人間が空を飛ぶなどということは考えもしなかったのではなかったか。

content.content: Isn’t it true that people those days never even imagined that human beings could fly through the sky?

content: 古代人にとってはこれも貴重な食物なのではなかったか。

content.content: Wasn’t this also a valuable food for ancient people?
【ではなかったか】
2. ...のではなかったか〈criticism〉

content: あなたたちは規律を守ると誓ったのではなかったか。

content.content: Didn’t you promise that you would obey the rules?

content: これまでは平和に共存してきたのではなかったか。

content.content: Haven’t we co-existed peacefully up till now?
Used to express the speaker’s criticism of the addressee or his/her feeling of regret because the present situation has turned out to be contradictory to the one described in the preceding clause.
【のではなかろうか】→
【ではなかろうか】
【のに1】［N／Na　なのに］［A-い／A-かった　のに］［V-る／V-た　のに］

1. ...のに〈mid-sentence〉Placed after a clause and used in the pattern XのにY. Expresses that the result Y is not what X would naturally lead one to expect, but something contradictory. Both X and Y express an established fact. This means that expressions indicating a situation that is not established as a fact, such as questions, commands, requests, invitations, intentions, desires, or suppositions, cannot usually appear in Y.
（×）雨が降っているのに出かけなさい。
Even though it’s raining, go out.
（×）雨が降っているのに出かけたい。
Even though it’s raining, I want to go out.
（×）雨が降っているのに出かけるだろう。
Even though it’s raining, I’ll probably go out.
a. ...のに〈converse cause〉

content: 5月なのに真夏のように暑い。

content.content: Although it’s May, it’s as hot as the middle of summer.

content: 家が近いのによく遅刻する。

content.content: Even though she lives close by, she’s often late.

content: 雨が降っているのに出かけていった。

content.content: Despite the rain, I went out.

content: 真夜中過ぎたのにまだ帰ってこない。

content.content: It’s already past midnight, but he hasn’t come back yet.

content: 今日は日曜日なのに会社に行くんですか。

content.content: Even though today is Sunday, you’re going to work?

content: 5月なのに何でこんなに暑いんだろう。

content.content: Why is it so hot, even though it’s still May?
In this use of the pattern XのにY, there is a causal relation between X and Y, but this causal relation is not realized.
For example, のに in

content: expresses that the usual causal relation, which is “because it was raining, I didn’t go out,” is not established; rather, two incompatible conditions are realized at the same time. This usage is often accompanied by the speaker’s surprise or doubt regarding an unexpected result or discrepancy.

content.content: In

content: , のに is used to ask the reason for the current situation, which is unexpected. It expresses the speaker’s sense of surprise and misgiving.

is an interrogative sentence, but のに can be used in this case. The reason is that the situation of the addressee going to work (= Y) is an established fact. The speaker is astonished that “even though it’s Sunday, you’re going to work,” and this interrogative sentence uses the form のですか to ask a question about this fact.

content.content: In contrast, an interrogative sentence without のだ that asks if the addressee is going to work would be unnatural, as below.
（×）今日は日曜日なのに会社に行きますか。
Even though today is Sunday, are you going to work?
b. ...のに〈contrast〉

content: 昨日はいい天気だったのに今日は雨だ。

content.content: It was nice yesterday, but today it’s raining.

content: あの中国人は日本語はあまり上手でないのに、英語はうまい。

content.content: Even though that Chinese person isn’t very good at Japanese, his English is good.

content: お兄さんはよく勉強するのに弟は授業をよくサボる。

content.content: The older brother studies hard, while the younger one often skips class.
In this usage, XのにY expresses a contrast between X and Y, not a causal relation.
For example, in

content: there is a contrastive relation between X, which is 日本語が上手でない (s/he is not good at Japanese), and Y, which is 英語がうまい (s/he is good at English), and のに links X and Y. The relation between X and Y is not a causal relation, like “because that Chinese person is not good at Japanese, s/he is good at English.”

content.content: のに in

content: can be paraphrased as けれども or が (see below). However, while けれども and が express a simple contrastive relation between the first and second clauses, のに implies that the relation between X and Y deviates from the one usually expected and that the speaker feels it is “unusual” or “strange.”

content.content: （例）あの中国人は日本語はあまり上手でない｛けれども／が｝、英語はうまい。
That Chinese person isn’t very good at Japanese, but his/her English is good.
c. ...のに〈unexpected〉

content: 合格すると思っていたのに、不合格だった。

content.content: I thought I would pass the exam, but I failed.

content: 今晩中に電話するつもりだったのに、うっかり忘れてしまった。

content.content: I intended to make a phone call tonight, but it slipped my mind.

content: 和子さんには来てほしかったのに、来てくれなかった。

content.content: I especially wanted Kazuko-san to come, but she didn’t.

content: せっかくおいでくださったのに、申し訳ございませんでした。

content.content: After you took the trouble to come all the way here...I really must apologize.
Expresses that an outcome is different from what was expected or predicted.
In examples

content: , X (in the pattern XのにY) is an expression of expectation, intention, or desire, such as ...と思っていた (I thought...), つもりだった (I intended), or 来てほしかった (I wanted (her) to come). Y describes an outcome that is contrary to X.

means せっかくお出でくださったのに、(留守にしていて)申し訳ございません (you took the trouble to come all the way here, so I really must apologize (for being out)). However, the outcome 留守にしていて (for being out) is not actually verbalized, and のに is followed immediately by the speaker’s expression of apology for the unexpected outcome.

content.content: 2. ...のに〈sentence-final〉

content: スピードを出すから事故を起こしたんだ。ゆっくり走れと言っておいたのに。

content.content: You had an accident because you drive too fast. I told you before you went out that you should drive slowly!

content: 絶対来るとあんなに固く約束したのに。

content.content: After he’d promised so firmly that he would definitely come!

content: もっと早く出発すればよかったのに。

content.content: We should have left earlier.

content: あなたも来ればいいのに。

content.content: You really should come, too!

content: あと5秒早ければ始発電車に間に合ったのに。

content.content: If I’d arrived five seconds earlier, I would have made the first train.

Used at the end of a sentence to express a feeling of regret regarding a result that differs from what was expected. Often used when the speaker is criticizing or complaining about someone else’s actions, or at the end of a counter-factual conditional sentence, as in
3. せっかく...のに→
【せっかく】
4. Nでも...のに

content: 電気屋でも直せないのに、あなたに直せるはずがないじゃないの。

content.content: Even an electrician can’t fix it, so how should you be able to fix it?

content: 九州でもこんなに寒いのに、まして北海道はどんなに寒いだろう。

content.content: If it’s this cold even in Kyushu, how cold must it be in Hokkaido?

content: こんな簡単な問題、小学生でも解けるのに、どうして間違えたりしたの？

content.content: Even an elementary school student could solve such an easy problem, so why did you get it wrong?

Expresses the development of a logical argument, as in “if N, then something is supposed to be such-and-such, but that was not the result (e.g. I thought an electrician would be able to fix it, but s/he couldn’t)” and “even N is such-and-such, so someone/something with less potential than N is all the more such-and-such (e.g. it is even more difficult for you, as a non-professional, to fix it).”
【のに2】［V-るのに］

content: この道具はパイプを切るのに使います。

content.content: This tool is used for cutting pipe.

content: 暖房は冬を快適に過ごすのに不可欠です。

content.content: It is essential to have heating in order to pass the winter comfortably.

content: 彼を説得するのには時間が必要です。

content.content: It will take time to convince him.

のに is placed after the dictionary form of a verb and expresses a purpose. Can be paraphrased as ...するために. However, the range of expressions that come after ...るのに is restricted to words/phrases like 使う (use), 必要だ (it’s necessary), and 不可欠だ (it’s indispensable), so this pattern is used less freely than ...するために．
（×）留学するのに英語を習っている。
I’m learning English for to study abroad.
（○）留学するために英語を習っている。
I’m learning English in order to study abroad.
The form Nに (without の) is used with nouns to express the meaning of purpose, as below.
（例）辞書は語学の勉強に必要だ。
Dictionaries are necessary for language learning.
【のは...だ】［N／Na　なのは...だ］［A／V　のは...だ］Used in the pattern XのはYだ. X states something that the listener already knows or can expect, and Y expresses something new and previously unknown to the listener.
1. ...のは　Nだ／N+助詞+だ

content: このことを私に教えてくれたのは山田さんです。

content.content: The person who told me this is Yamada-san.

content: 彼の言うことを信じているのはあなただけだ。

content.content: You’re the only one who believes what he says.

content: ここに通うようになったのは去年の3月からです。

content.content: It was March of last year when I started to come here.

Used to describe a certain situation and then indicate a person, thing, etc. relevant to the realization of that situation. だ／です is preceded by either a noun or a noun/particle combination. However, the particles が and を cannot be used.
（×）このことを私に教えてくれたのは山田さんがです。
The person who told me this is Yamada-san.
2. のは...からだ

content: 彼女が試験に失敗したのは、体の調子が悪かったからだ。

content.content: The reason she failed the exam was that she didn’t feel well.

content: 大阪に行ったのは事故の原因をたしかめたかったからです。

content.content: The reason I went to Osaka was that I wanted to determine the cause of the accident.
Used to express a certain situation or event and then state the cause or reason for it.
3. のは...ためだ

content: 電車が遅れたのは、踏切事故があったためだ。

content.content: The reason the train was late was that there was an accident at a railroad crossing.

content: 彼らが国に帰ったのは、子供たちに会うためだ。

content.content: The reason they went back to their country was so they could see their children.
Used to express a certain situation or event and then state the cause or reason for it.
4. のは...おかげだ

content: 子供が助かったのはあなたのおかげです。

content.content: It is thanks to you that my child was saved.

content: この事業が成功したのは、みんなが力を合わせて頑張ったおかげだ。

content.content: We owe the success of this project to your teamwork and effort.
Used to express a favorable situation or event and then state what caused it.
5. のは...せいだ

content: 雪崩に巻き込まれたのは、無謀な計画のせいだ。

content.content: The reason we got caught in an avalanche was that our plan was reckless.

content: 試合に負けたのは私がミスをしたせいだ。

content.content: We lost the game because I made an error.
Used to express an unfavorable situation or event and then state what caused it.
【のみ】
1. Nのみ

content: 経験のみに頼っていては成功しない。

content.content: You’ll never succeed if you depend only on experience.

content: 金持ちのみが得をする世の中だ。

content.content: Only the rich gain advantages in this world.

content: 洪水の後に残されたのは、石の土台のみだった。

content.content: It was only the stone foundation that was left after the flood.
Means to restrict something to just one thing. Used in formal language with the tone of written Japanese. In spoken Japanese, だけ and ばかり are used.
2. V-るのみだ

content: 準備は整った。あとはスイッチをいれるのみだ。

content.content: Everything is ready. All that’s left is to switch it on.

content: 早くしなければと焦るのみで、いっこうに仕事がはかどらない。

content.content: All I do is rush to get things done quickly, and I don’t make any progress with my work at all.
Means “only that.” Can indicate being in a state right before a certain action is carried out, as in

content: , or that a certain action is performed exclusively and repeatedly, as in
. Can be paraphrased as ...するばかりだ．

content.content: 3. Nあるのみだ

content: こうなったからは前進あるのみだ。

content.content: Since things have ended up like this, there’s nothing we can do but move forward.

content: 成功するためには、ひたすら努力あるのみです。

content.content: In order to succeed, all you have to do is devote yourself to hard work.
Placed after nouns like 前進 (progress/advance), 努力 (effort), and 忍耐 (patience) and means “that is the only thing one should do.”
【のみならず】
1. ...のみならず...も［NのみならずNも］［Na であるのみならずNa でも］［A-いのみならずA-くも］［VのみならずNもV］

content: 若い人のみならず老人や子供達にも人気がある。

content.content: This is popular with young people, as well as with old people and children.

content: 戦火で家を焼かれたのみならず、家族も失った。

content.content: I not only had my house destroyed by the flames of war but also lost my family.

content: 彼女は聡明であるのみならず容姿端麗でもある。

content.content: Besides being intelligent, she is also good-looking.
Used to add one thing to another. Means “not only this, but also....” Means the same as だけでなく...も, but is more formal and has the tone of written language．
2. のみならず

content: 彼はその作品によって国内で絶大な人気を得た。のみならず、海外でも広く名前を知られることとなった。

content.content: Because of that (literary) work, he gained great popularity in this country. In addition, his name became well-known abroad.

content: 彼女はありあまる才能に恵まれていた。のみならず彼女は努力家でもあった。

content.content: She was endowed with more than enough talent. What is more, she was also a hard worker.
Refers to what was said in the preceding context and means “not only that (but also...).” Implies that there is another thing that is similar. A formal expression with the tone of written language.
【は...で】［NはNで］

content: 彼の言うことなど気にせず、君は君で自分が正しいと思ったことをやればいいのだ。

content.content: Don’t pay attention to anything he says; you should do whatever you yourself think is right.

content: 姉はオリンピックで金メダルを取り、妹は妹で、初めて書いた小説が芥川賞を受賞した。

content.content: The older sister got a gold medal at the Olympic Games, and the younger sister, on the other hand, was awarded the Akutagawa Prize for her very first novel.

content: タヌキは若い女に化け、キツネはキツネで立派な侍に変わった。

content.content: The raccoon dog transformed itself into a young woman, and the fox turned into a great samurai.
The pattern XはXで, created by repeating the same noun, is used to say something about X while comparing it with something else.

【はい】Used to express an affirmative answer, a back-channel response (see below), and so on. うん and ええ are similar to はい. However, うん is used only in informal situations with family members, friends, or other people who have a close relationship to the speaker, or towards people of lower status than the speaker. In formal situations, はい or ええ is used. To express a negative answer, いいえ, ううん, and いや are used.
1. はい〈affirmation〉

content: A:これはあなたの本ですか。

content.content: Is this your book?
B:はい、そうです。
Yes, it is.

content: A:明日、学校へいきますか。

content.content: Are you going to school tomorrow?
B:はい、行きます。
Yes, I am.

content: A:おいしいですか。

content.content: Is it good?
B:はい、とてもおいしいです。
Yes, it’s really delicious.

content: A:便利ですか。

content.content: Is it convenient?
B:はい、便利です。
Yes, it is convenient.

content: A:国へ帰るんですか。

content.content: So, are you going back to your country?
B:はい、そうです。
Yes, I am.

Used in reply to a question the speaker has asked to confirm whether or not a judgment s/he has made is correct. Means that the speaker’s judgment is, in fact, correct. In this case, はい、そうです can be used only in response to a question about a noun, as exemplified in
When responding to a question with a verb or an adjective, the same verb or adjective must be repeated, as shown in

content: and
. However, if the question form is のですか or んですか, as in
, then はい、そうです can be used.

content.content: （例）A:これは、あなたの車ではありませんね。
This isn’t your car, is it?
B1: はい、ちがいます。
That’s right, it isn’t.
B2: いいえ、わたしのです。
Actually (= that’s wrong), it is mine.

With a negative question like the one in the example above, はい is used when the speaker’s judgment is correct, and いいえ is used when his/her judgment is incorrect. Thus, if the judgment “this is not your car” is correct, the response should be はい, as in B1’s response はい、違います (That’s right, it isn’t) or はい、私の車ではありません (That’s right, it’s not my car).

As can be seen in the examples above, the answer to a negative question is はい when the expectation or judgment of the person asking the question is correct, and いいえ when it is not. In other words, the answer is not determined by whether the judgment itself is affirmative or negative. In actual conversation, answering a negative question without はい or いいえ is also common.
2. はい〈consent〉

content: A:行ってくれますね。

content.content: You’ll go for me, won’t you?
B:はい。
Yes.

content: A:いっしょにやりましょう。

content.content: Let’s do it together.
B:はい。
Yes, let’s.

content: A:これをあっちに持って行ってください。

content.content: Please take this over there.
B:はい、わかりました。
All right, I will.

content: A:いっしょに食事をしませんか。

content.content: Shall we have dinner together?
B1: はい、行きましょう。
B1: Yes, let’s go.
B2: いや、今日はちょっと。
B2: Actually, today’s not so good for me....

content: 母:早くおふろに入りなさい。

content.content: Mother: Hurry up and get into the bath.
子:はいはい。
Child: Yes, yes!
母:「はい」は、一回！
Mother: You only need to say “yes” once!
Used to consent to a request, demand, invitation, etc.

content: is in the form of a question, but since it is a request, not an inquiry to confirm whether or not something is correct, consent is indicated by the use of はい. When declining a request, speakers tend not to use いいえ, since it may sound like a rather strong refusal. As shown in
, repetition of はい in response to a request or demand sounds rather rude, because it gives the impression that the speaker is responding reluctantly.

content.content: 3. はい〈response〉

content: A:山田君。

content.content: Yamada-kun?
B:はい。
Yes.

content: A:ちょっとおたずねしますが...。

content.content: Could I ask you something...?
B:はい。
Yes.

content: A:あのう。

content.content: Excuse me....
B:はい。
Yes?

content: A:おーい。ちょっと。

content.content: Hey, you there.
B:はい。
Yes?

Used by an addressee to respond when someone calls out to him/her, when attendance is being taken, and so on. In this case, ええ cannot be used. In casual situations, the addressee may also respond with はあい, なに, なあに, etc.
4. はい〈back-channel response〉

content: 《電話で》

content.content: 《on the phone》
A:来週の旅行のことですが...。
About the trip next week....
B:はい。
Yes.
A:他の方は皆さんいらっしゃることになったんですが...。
All the others have decided to go, but....
B:あ、はい。
Oh, really.
A:ええ、それで、Bさんのご都合はどうかと思いまして...。
Yes, so I’m wondering whether or not you can go too....
B:すみません。それがですねえ。急に用事ができてしまいまして、申し訳ないんですが...。
I’m sorry. About that, you know...something has come up all of a sudden. I’m very sorry, but....
A:だめですか...。
So you can’t come....

はい, ええ and うん are often used as “back-channel” responses. These are brief responses that show only that the addressee understands or is listening to what the speaker is saying. They do not mean that the addressee agrees with the speaker.
5. はい〈getting someone’s attention〉

content: はい、みなさんこっちを向いて。

content.content: Okay, everyone, look over here.

content: はい、みなさん出発しますよ。

content.content: All right, everyone, we’re leaving now.

content: はいどうぞ。

content.content: Here you are.

content: はい、お茶。

content.content: Here is your tea.

content: はい、これでございます。

content.content: Here you are, this is it.
Used to attract the addressee’s attention. In this case, うん and ええ cannot be used.
6. はい〈confirmation〉

content: A:おじいさんは、こちらには長くお住まいですか。

content.content: Has this been your home for a long time, Grandfather?
B:私ですか。私は、戦前からずっとここに住んでおります。はい。
Me? I’ve been living here since before the war. Yes.

content: 客:どっちが似合うかしら。

content.content: Customer: I wonder which one looks best on me.
店員: そりゃもう、どちらもお似合いでございます。はい。
Salesperson: Well, I would say that both of them suit you. Yes, indeed.
When a speaker adds はい to the end of one of his/her own statements or remarks, it sounds like s/he is confirming what s/he has just said. Sounds old-fashioned or humble.
【はいざしらず】→
【いざしらず】
【はおろか】［Nはおろか］

content: 私は、海外旅行はおろか国内旅行さえ、ほとんど行ったことがない。

content.content: I’ve hardly ever traveled in this country, much less abroad.

content: 吉井さんはアレルギーがひどくて、卵はおろかパンも食べられないそうだ。

content.content: Since Yoshii-san has terrible allergies, she can’t even eat bread, let alone eggs.

content: この学生には単位は出せません。今学期はレポートはおろか出席さえしていないんです。

content.content: I can’t give this student credit for this course. Not only has he never turned in a paper, he’s never even been to class.

content: 発見されたとき、その男の人は住所はおろか名前すら記憶していなかったという。

content.content: I heard that when that man was found, he couldn’t even remember his name, let alone his address.

content: もし歩いていてピストルを突きつけられたら絶対に逆らわないでお金を渡しなさい。さもないと金はおろか命までなくすことになるよ。

content.content: If someone points a gun at you on the street, you must give up your money without resisting. Otherwise, you will lose not only your money but also your life.

content: 戦争も末期になると、青年はおろか妻子ある中年の男まで戦場に送り込まれた。

content.content: Towards the end of the war, not only young men but also middle-aged men with wives and children were sent to the front.

Often used with a negative expression, in the pattern XはおろかYさえ／も／すら...ない. Means that something is a matter of course or goes without saying. Used to emphasize Y by first presenting X, which has a lower degree of something. Used in formal, old-fashioned styles. In spoken Japanese, ...どころか is used instead.
【はじめ】
1. Nをはじめ（として）...など

content: 日本の伝統芸能としては、歌舞伎をはじめ、能、茶の湯、生け花などが挙げられる。

content.content: The traditional performing arts in Japan include Kabuki, as well as Noh, tea ceremony, flower arrangement, and so on.

content: 日本語には外来語が多い。英語をはじめフランス語、ドイツ語、ポルトガル語、オランダ語などさまざまな外国語起源の外来語が使われている。

content.content: Japanese has many loan words. It uses loan words originating from a variety of foreign languages, starting with English and including French, German, Portuguese, and Dutch as well.
Used to give a representative example first, and then list in succession a number of similar examples.
2. Nをはじめ（として）...まで

content: その会議には、歴史学者をはじめ、町の研究家から一般市民にいたるまで、さまざまな人々が参加した。

content.content: Many different people, from historians to researchers in the town and down to the general public, participated in the conference.

content: 彼の葬儀には、友人知人を始め、面識のない人までが参列した。

content.content: A variety of people, from his friends and acquaintances all the way to people who had never met him in person, attended his funeral.
Used to indicate that something encompasses a wide range of things, from a prime example to more peripheral ones.
【はじめて】［V-て（みて）はじめて］

content: 病気になってはじめて健康のありがたさがわかる。

content.content: People don’t know the value of good health until they become ill.

content: 外国に行って初めて自分の国について何も知らないことに気がついた。

content.content: I first realized that I knew nothing about my own country only when I went abroad.

content: 言われてみて初めて、自分がいかに狭量であったかに気がついた。

content.content: I didn’t realize how narrow-minded I was until someone told me so.

Means “realize for the first time only after something happens.” Used to express that, as the result of a certain experience, a person has realized something that s/he didn’t previously know, or something that s/he did know but had never thought about very seriously.
【はず】［Nのはず］［Na なはず］［A／V　はず］
1. ...はずだ〈speaker’s judgment〉

content: A:山田さんも明日の会議には出席するんですか。

content.content: Will Yamada-san attend the meeting tomorrow, too?
B:いや、今週は東京に行くと言っていたから、明日の会議には来ないはずだよ。
No, she said she was going to be in Tokyo this week, so she won’t be at the meeting tomorrow.

content: あれから4年たったのだから、今年はあの子も卒業のはずだ。

content.content: It’s been four years since then, so he must be graduating this year too.

content: 今はにぎやかなこの辺りも、昔は静かだったはずだ。

content.content: It must have been quiet around here a long time ago, even though it’s bustling these days.

content: A:本当にこのボタンを押せばいいのかい？　押しても動かないよ。

content.content: Are you sure we’re supposed to push this button? I did, but nothing happened.
B:説明書によるとそれでいいはずなんだけど。変だなあ。
According to the instructions, that’s how it should work. How strange!

content: A:あそこにいるの、下田さんじゃありませんか。

content.content: Isn’t that Shimoda-san over there?
B:おかしいな。下田さんは昨日ニューヨークに発ったはずだよ。
That’s funny. Shimoda-san was supposed to have left for New York yesterday.

content: A:会議は一時からですか。

content.content: Does the meeting start at one o’clock?
B:ええ、そのはずです。
Yes, it’s supposed to.

Used to state something that the speaker thinks is a natural or logical judgment, based on some kind of evidence. This judgment must be based on a logical train of thought. Thus, はず cannot be used in cases such as the one below.
（×）めがねが見つからない。またどこかに置き忘れたはずだ。
I can’t find my glasses. I should have left them somewhere again.
（○）めがねが見つからない。またどこかに置き忘れたんだ。
I can’t find my glasses. I’ve left them somewhere again.
As shown in

content: and
, when reality does not conform to the speaker’s judgment, はず expresses a sense of surprise or suspicion.

content.content: はず can be used with respect to a third party’s plans, as in 彼は来年帰国するはずです (he should be returning to his country next year). However, it cannot be used with respect to the speaker’s own actions. In that case, つもり (intend to), V-ようと思う (be going to do...), or ...予定だ (plan to...) are used instead.
（×）私は来年帰国するはずです。
I should be returning to my country next year.
（○）私は来年帰国する予定です。
I plan to return to my country next year.
However, はず can be used with respect to the speaker’s own actions when an outcome can’t be determined according to his/her own will or when it differs from his/her intended actions, as shown below.
（○）マニュアルを何回も読んだからできるはずなんだけど、どうしてもコンピューターが起動しない。
I’ve read the manual over and over again, so I should be able to do this, but the computer won’t boot up no matter what.
（○）その旅行には、私も行くはずでしたが、結局行けませんでした。
I was supposed to go along on the trip, but in the end I couldn’t.
2. ...はずだ〈understanding〉［Na なはずだ］［A／V　はずだ］

content: この部屋、寒いねえ。（窓が開いているのを見つけて）寒いはずだ。窓が開いているよ。

content.content: This room is cold, isn’t it? (realizing that the window is open) No wonder it’s cold. The window is open!

content: 《作品を見ながら》彼が自慢するはずだ。本当にすばらしいできだ。

content.content: 《looking at a work of art》No wonder he was boasting about this. It really is a magnificent piece.

content: さっきから道が妙にすいていると思っていたが、すいているはずだ。今日は日曜日だ。

content.content: I was just thinking how strange it is that the roads are so empty, but they ought to be. Today is Sunday.
