Expresses the speaker’s feeling of being convinced, after discovering a fact that adequately explains something s/he was previously suspicious of or didn’t fully understand.
3. V-たはず

content: おかしなことに、閉めたはずの金庫のカギが開いていた。

content.content: Strangely, the safe—which I thought I had locked—was open.

content: A:書類、間違っていたよ。

content.content: There was a mistake on the document.
B:えっ、よく確かめたはずなんですけど。すみません。
Really? I thought I had checked it carefully. I’m sorry.

content: ちゃんとかばんに入れたはずなのに、家に帰ってみると財布がない。

content.content: I thought I had put my wallet in my bag, but when I returned home I couldn’t find it.
Used when there is a discrepancy between what the speaker expected to be true and the actual situation. Expresses a feeling of regret or suspicion on the part of the speaker.
4. ...はずがない〈negation of possibility〉

content: あの温厚な人がそんなひどいことをするはずがない。

content.content: A good-natured person like him can’t have done such a terrible thing.

content: かぎがない？　そんなはずはない。さっき机の上に置いたんだから。

content.content: You can’t find the key? That’s impossible. I just left it on the desk a minute ago.

content: これは君の部屋にあったんだよ。君が知らないはずはない。

content.content: We found this in your room. So you can’t say you don’t know anything about it.
Used in the form はずがない or はずはない. Means “inconceivable,” “impossible,” or “strange.” Expresses strong doubt on the part of the speaker.
For instance,

content: means “It doesn’t make sense that you don’t know. Surely you must know.”

content.content: The expression ...ないはずだ, which is an instance of Usage 1 (above), is used when the speaker thinks that something is “probably not” the case. For example, if

content: were rephrased as そんなひどいことはしないはずだ, it would mean “he isn’t likely to have done such a terrible thing,” which is a weaker assertion than the one expressed by ...はずがない.

content.content: 5. ...はずだった

content: 彼も来るはずだったが、急用ができて来られないそうだ。

content.content: He was supposed to come too, but I heard that he can’t because something urgent came up.

content: 理論上はうまくいくはずだったが、実際にやってみると、うまくいかなかった。

content.content: In theory it should have worked fine, but in practice it didn’t.

content: 初めの計画では、道路はもっと北側を通るはずだったのに、いつの間にか変更されてしまった。

content.content: According to the original plan, the road was supposed to be constructed farther north, but that changed without any notice.

Means that the speaker “had thought that naturally something would happen.” Used to express that the actual result is different from the one the speaker expected. Often implies the speaker’s surprise, disappointment, or regret. Also, often used in adversative constructions such as はずだったが／のに／けれど (should have...but.../although...was supposed to...).
6. ...はずではなかった

content: こんなはずではなかった。もっとうまくいくと思っていたのに。

content.content: This is not what was supposed to happen. I thought it would work out much better.

content: こんなはずじゃなかったのに。

content.content: It really wasn’t meant to turn out like this.

content: 彼が来るはずではなかったのに。

content.content: He wasn’t supposed to come.

Often used in the expression こんなはずではなかった (see above). Indicates the speaker’s disappointment or regret with respect to the actual situation, which differs from what s/he had expected. Often used in the pattern ...はずではなかったのに.
【はずみ】［Nのはずみ　で／に］［V-たはずみ　で／に］

content: ころんだはずみに足首を捻挫してしまった。

content.content: I sprained my ankle when I happened to fall down.

content: 衝突のはずみで、乗客は車外に放り出された。

content.content: The passengers were thrown out of the car on impact.

content: このあいだは、もののはずみで「二度とくるな」などと言ってしまったが、本当にそう思っているわけではない。

content.content: The other day, I said “Don’t ever come again!” in the heat of the moment, but I didn’t really mean it.
Means “by the impetus of a certain action.” Used to express the occurrence of something unexpected or unintended. もののはずみで in

content: is an idiomatic expression that means “on the spur of the moment, in the heat of the moment.” はずみで can often be replaced by V-た拍子に (at the moment of.../in the act of doing...).

content.content: 【はたして】
1. はたして...か

content: 説明書の通りに組み立ててみたが、はたしてこれでうまく動くものかどうか自信がない。

content.content: I tried to assemble it according to the instructions, but I’m not confident that it will actually work properly.

content: この程度の補償金で、はたして被害者は納得するだろうか。

content.content: Will this amount of compensation really satisfy the victims?

content: この程度の金額で、はたして彼が承知するだろうか。

content.content: Do you think he’ll really agree to such a small amount of money?

content: はたして、どのチームが優勝するだろうか。

content.content: I wonder which team will actually win the championship.

content: 機械には特に悪いところがないとすると、はたして何が故障の原因だったのだろうか。

content.content: If there wasn’t anything wrong with the machine, then what on earth caused the breakdown?

content: はたして誰の言っていることが真実なのだろうか。

content.content: Who is actually telling the truth?
Means “is/will it really...?” Appears in patterns like はたして...か, はたして...だろうか, and はたして...かどうか. Used when the speaker suspects that something may not go as well as expected. As shown in

content: , this pattern is used in interrogative sentences that include a question word such as いつ, どこ, だれ, なに, or どう. In this case, it means “in the end, actually.” Has the tone of written language.

content.content: 2. はたして...した

content: 彼もやって来るのではないかと思っていたところ、はたして現れた。

content.content: Just as I was thinking he would come too, sure enough, he showed up.

content: はたして彼女は合格した。

content.content: She passed the exam, just as I had expected.
Means “did..., as I had expected” or “sure enough, did....” Used when something that the speaker was expecting actually happens. Has the tone of written language.
3. はたして...としても

content: はたして彼の言うことが事実であったとしても、彼に責任がないということにはならない。

content.content: Even if what he says is true, it doesn’t mean that he has no responsibility.
Means “even if...is true,” “if...is actually true,” or “supposing that...is true.” Emphasizes that the statement is hypothetical. A literary expression that is not used in everyday spoken language.
【はとわず】→
【をとわず】
【はやいか】［V-るがはやいか］

content: 小学校5年の息子は、ただいまと言うが早いか、もう遊びに行ってしまった。

content.content: No sooner did my fifth-grade son say “I’m home” than he left to go play outside.

content: 彼は、そばにあった棒をつかむがはやいか、どろぼうになぐりかかった。

content.content: He had scarcely grabbed a stick that was nearby when he starting hitting the robber.
Expresses a situation in which one action is performed immediately after another. Means “almost at the same time as doing...” or “as soon as....”

content: means “he left so soon that I don’t know which came first, his saying ‘I’m home’ or his leaving to go out and play,” or in other words, “he left to go out and play almost at the same time as he said ‘I’m home.’” Has the tone of written language.

content.content: 【はんいで】［Nのはんいで］［NからNのはんいで］［Vはんいで］

content: 私にわかる範囲でよければお答えしましょう。

content.content: If the best of my knowledge is sufficient for you, I will answer.

content: 差しつかえない範囲でお答え下さい。

content.content: Please answer to whatever extent suits you.

content: 駅から歩いて 10 分ぐらいの範囲で、いいアパートはありませんか。

content.content: Are there any nice apartments within a ten-minute walking distance of the station?

content: 今日の午後、花火工場で爆発事故がありました。半径5キロから 10 キロの範囲で、被害があったもようです。

content.content: There was an explosion at the fireworks factory this afternoon. Apparently there was damage within a five- to ten-kilometer radius of the site.
Expresses a certain limited extent.
【はんたいに】
1. はんたいに

content: あの子は、靴を反対にはいている。

content.content: That child is wearing his shoes on the wrong feet.

content: 父は酒が一滴も飲めない。反対に母はとても酒に強い。

content.content: My father can’t drink at all. In contrast, my mother holds her liquor very well.

content: 彼はどろぼうに飛びかかったが、反対にやられてしまった。

content.content: He lunged at the robber but got pinned down instead.

content: 今学期は、いっしょうけんめい勉強したが、成績は反対にさがってしまった。

content.content: I studied really hard this term, but my grades went down instead of up.
Means “conversely.” As shown in

content: , it is sometimes used with respect to two elements that have been reversed, such as “left and right” or “up and down.” It can also be used to express contrasting situations, as in
, or a result that is the opposite of what is normally expected, as in
and

content.content: 2. ...と（は）はんたいに

content: 姉は友だちと騒ぐのが好きだが、私は姉と反対に静かに音楽でも聞いている方が好きだ。

content.content: My older sister likes to party with friends, but I’m the opposite and like to do things like listening quietly to music.

content: 私の部屋は南むきで陽あたりがいいが、うるさい。それとは反対に妹の部屋は、陽あたりは悪いが静かだ。

content.content: My room faces south and gets a lot of sunshine, but it’s noisy. In contrast, my little sister’s room doesn’t get a lot of sunshine, but it’s quiet.

content: 山田さんが晩年いい作品を残したのと反対に、若くして賞をとった石田さんはその後ぱっとしなかった。

content.content: Yamada-san left behind some fine works in his later years, but Ishida-san, who had received an award at a young age, was not very impressive after that.

content: 弟が有名になっていくのとは反対に、兄の人気は衰えてきた。

content.content: The younger brother is becoming famous and, conversely, the older brother is losing popularity.
Means “on the contrary.” Can be used to compare two contrasting things, as shown in

content: , and
, or to describe two situations that are changing in inverse proportion to each other, as shown in

content.content: 【はんめん】
1. ...はんめん［Nであるはんめん］［Na　な／である　はんめん］［A-いはんめん］［V-るはんめん］

content: この薬はよく効く反面、副作用も強い。

content.content: This medicine works very well, but on the other hand, it has strong side effects.

content: 化学繊維は丈夫である反面、火に弱いという欠点がある。

content.content: While synthetic fiber is strong, the drawback is that it’s not fire-resistant.

content: 自動車は便利な反面、交通事故や大気汚染というマイナスの側面も持っている。

content.content: Cars are convenient, but at the same time they have negative aspects such as being associated with traffic accidents and air pollution.

content: 彼は目上に対しては腰が低い反面、目下に対してはいばっている。

content.content: Although he is courteous to people with higher status, he looks down his nose at those with lower status.

content: おじはがんこ者である反面、涙もろい性格だ。

content.content: My uncle is a stubborn mule, but at the same time he is quite sentimental.
Means “but on the contrary....” Expresses the co-existence of two contrasting aspects within a single thing or situation.
2. そのはんめん（では）

content: 田中先生はたいへんきびしい方だが、その反面、とてもやさしいところもある。

content.content: Tanaka-sensei is very strict, but on the other hand, he has a streak of real kindness.

content: 加藤さんは仕事が速いので有名だ。しかし、その反面、ミスも多い。

content.content: Kato-san is well-known as a quick worker. However, at the same time, she makes a lot of mistakes.

content: 急激な近代化とそれに伴う経済成長のおかげで、我々の生活は確かに向上した。だが、その反面では、伝統的な固有の文化が失われるという結果をもたらした。

content.content: Thanks to rapid modernization and the economic growth that came with it, the quality of our lifestyle has definitely improved. Still, the downside is that this has resulted in the loss of our unique traditional culture.
Means the same as Usage
1. Used in the pattern ...が／けれど、その反面... (...but, on the other hand...), as shown in

content.content: 【ば】［N／Na　なら（ば）］［A-ければ］［V-ば］ば is a conjugation form for predicates and indicates a condition. It is the most typical marker for conditional clauses in Japanese, and its usage overlaps partially with that of たら, と, and なら.

When this conditional follows a noun or a na-adjective, ば is often dropped and the form N/Naなら is used. N/Naであれば is a formal, written expression for N/Naなら. The negative form N/Naでなければ is used in both written and spoken Japanese. The i-adjective いい always takes the form よければ, not いければ.

ば is usually used the same way as たら. However, ば tends to be used more in written Japanese, while たら is used more in spoken Japanese. In casual spoken language, sometimes the combination of “consonant + eba” at the end of a word changes to “consonant + ya” (e.g. あれば→ありゃ, 行けば→行きゃ, 飲めば→飲みゃ, なければ→なけりゃ), and the combination A-ければ may change to A-きゃ (e.g. なければ→なきゃ).

Used to state a conditional relation regarding a general state of affairs, not a specific person or thing. Means “when X happens, Y also happens, without exception.” Expresses logical or rule-based relations or cause-and-effect relations that are not situated at a particular point in time but always hold true. The dictionary form is always used at the end of the sentence. Not used to talk about a personal experience or one particular event. Used to say that “when X is realized, Y is the natural consequence,” “such-and-such generally happens,” or “something is intrinsically such-and-such.”

When this expression is used, the subject is often omitted. When the subject appears, it is one that refers to some kind of group as a whole, such as 人はだれでも (everyone/all people) or Nというものは (N in general). This use of the ba-form is often followed at the end of the sentence by ものだ, which indicates that the thing in question intrinsically has a certain nature, as exemplified in

content.content: 2. ...ば〈repetition, habit〉Used with respect to a particular person or thing and expresses a habit or an action that is repeated. Means “every time X happens, Y happens too,” “whenever X is done, Y is invariably done as well.” The difference between this usage and the generic conditional described in 1 is that the generic conditional, which describes a situation that has an indefinite subject and transcends time, is always used with the dictionary form of a predicate at the end of the sentence, whereas the repetitive/habitual conditional can be used with not only the dictionary form but also the ta-form. This conditional is used to describe a habit or a repeated action of a definite subject.

content.content: Like ば, たら can also be used to state a past fact. However, while ば expresses an action that was repeated in the past or a situation that was always realized under certain conditions, たら usually expresses a past event that took place one time only.
（例1）ビールを2本飲めば酔っぱらいました。

content.content: 3. ...ば〈not-yet-realized condition〉Expresses the relation “if X happens, Y will happen,” with respect to a particular thing or person. X can be something that either has or has not been realized, but Y is always something that has not yet been realized.

The generic conditional ば described in Usage 1 is used to talk about things or events in general and is always accompanied by the dictionary form of a predicate at the end of the sentence. On the other hand, the hypothetical conditional ば is used to apply a general condition to a particular situation and state a prediction. It can be combined with expressions such as だろう and かもしれない at the end of the sentence.
（例）〈一般条件〉食事を減らせば誰でもやせる。
〈generic condition〉If you reduce your food intake at meals, anyone can lose weight.
（例）〈仮定条件〉食事を減らせばあなたもやせるだろう。
〈not-yet-realized condition〉If you reduce your food intake at meals, you too will lose weight.

The slot for Y in this pattern may be filled by a statement describing an unrealized situation, an expression of intention or command, or some other expression that reveals the speaker’s thoughts/feelings or his/her desire to exert an influence on someone.

It means “no matter how much I do..., things don’t go the way I want them to,” and it expresses the speaker’s sense of exasperation or desperation regarding a certain situation. Expressions like のか, のだ, and のだろう(か) are used at the end of the sentence. V-ば can be replaced by V-たら.

4. ...ば〈counter-factual〉A statement of something contrary to fact comes before ば, and after ば comes a description of something that should (have) happen(ed) if the situation were the opposite. Used to talk about an undesirable situation that has already been realized, or about a situation that is obviously impossible to realize.

When this pattern is used to say that a desired situation has not been realized, it conveys a feeling of regret or disappointment. On the other hand, when it is used to say that an undesirable situation has been avoided, it implies the speaker’s feeling of relief, as in “it’s a good thing such-and-such didn’t happen.”

In many cases, it is impossible to distinguish a counter-factual use from a factual one on the basis of form alone. However, the patterns below are often used in counter-factual conditional sentences. Also, this usage of ば can always be substituted with たら.

content.content: 忘れていたところだった in

content: can be rephrased as 忘れているところだった. However, the former expresses a past situation, with the sense of “I managed not to forget,” while the latter expresses a present situation, with the sense of “I’ve managed to remember.”

content.content: 【ところだ】2d. ...ば　V-た／V-ていた

content: 安ければ買った。

content.content: If it had been inexpensive, I would have bought it.

content: もっと早く来れば間に合った。

content.content: If I had come earlier, I would have been in time.

content: 手当てが早ければ、彼は助かっていた。

content.content: If he had been treated sooner, he would have been saved.

content: きちんとした説明があれば、私も反対しなかった。

content.content: If a proper explanation had been given, I wouldn’t have objected either.

In this pattern, ば takes the ta-form of a verb at the end of the sentence and expresses a counter-factual situation or event. Used with respect to a past situation, to hypothesize an action that was not actually performed or a state that differs from reality, and to express a situation or event that would have occurred under the hypothetical circumstances.

content: , for instance, means “if I had come earlier, I would have been in time; however, since I actually came late, I was not in time.”

content.content: In general, counter-factual conditional sentences often end with expressions like のに／のだが／のだけれど, or だろう／かもしれない／はずだ／にちがいない／と思う, or ところだ(った), as shown in patterns (a)-(c) above. However, there are cases in which no such expression is used, as shown in this pattern (d). Note that when the ta-form is used in sentence-final position, in particular, conditional sentences with ば and たら may express different meanings.
（例1）ボタンを押したら爆発した。
When I pressed the button, it exploded.
（例2）ボタンを押せば爆発した。
If I had pressed the button, it would have exploded.

Example 1, which means “I pressed the button. Then it exploded,” expresses an event that actually took place. On the other hand, example 2 is a counter-factual conditional sentence that means “If I had pressed the button, it would have exploded, but I didn’t actually press the button, so it didn’t explode.”
5. ...ば〈already-realized condition〉

content: 彼は変わり者だという評判だったが、会ってみれば、うわさほどのことはなかった。

content.content: He had the reputation of being quite a strange character, but when I met him, he was not half as strange as was rumored.

content: 言われてみればそれももっともな気がする。

content.content: Now that you say so, I think that’s a good point too.

content: 始める前は心配だったが、すべてが終わってみれば、それほど大したことではなかったと思う。

content.content: I was worried before I started, but now that it’s all over, I don’t think it was such a big deal.

The pattern XばY is used to express that the speaker realized Y at the time X occurred. For this usage, たら and と are more usual, and the use of ば is restricted to somewhat old-fashioned literary expressions such as those found in poetry and novels. When this pattern is used in spoken Japanese, it usually takes the form V-てみれば and expresses the speaker’s understanding or acceptance after learning the truth about something, with the sense of “that is quite right” or “of course, it stands to reason.”
In

content: , ば can be replaced by たら, but when たら is used, it means “as a result of taking such-and-such an action, I realized something.” For example, when ば in

is replaced by たら to say 会ってみたら、うわさほどのことはなかったよ, the たら sentence means “as a result of meeting him, I found out that he was not as (strange) as was rumored.” Thus, when a speaker is describing a new realization just the way it happened, s/he usually uses たら or と; if ば is used, it often sounds unnatural.

content.content: （×）昨日、台所で変な音がするので泥棒かと思って行ってみれば、弟がラーメンを作っていた。
Yesterday I heard a strange noise in the kitchen so I thought it might be a thief, but if I went to see, my brother was making raamen noodle soup.
（○）昨日、台所で変な音がするので泥棒かと思って｛行ってみたら／行ってみると｝、弟がラーメンを作っていた。
Yesterday I heard a strange noise in the kitchen so I thought it might be a thief, but when I went to see, my brother was making raamen noodle soup.
（×）朝起きれば、雨が降っていた。
If I got up in the morning, it was raining.
（○）朝｛起きたら／起きると｝、雨が降っていた。
When I got up in the morning, it was raining.
When talking about one person who performs two actions in succession, one time only, と should be used, not ば or たら. See the example below.
（×）次郎は家に｛帰れば／帰ったら｝、テレビを見た。
If Jiro came home, he watched TV.
（○）次郎は家に帰ると、テレビを見た。
When Jiro came home, he watched TV.
6. ...ば...で［A-ければ A-いで］［V-ば V-たで］

content: 自動車がないとさぞ不便だろうと思っていたが、なければないでやっていけるものだ。

content.content: I thought it would be very inconvenient to live without a car, but I can actually manage without one.

content: 父は暑さに弱い。それでは冬が好きかというとそうではない。寒ければ寒いで文句ばかり言っている。

content.content: My father can’t take the heat. But that doesn’t mean he likes winter. Once it gets cold, he does nothing but complain about it.

content: 金などというものは、無ければ困るが、あればあったでやっかいなものだ。

content.content: Money is something that is trouble if you don’t have any, but a nuisance if you do have some.

content: 子供が小さい間は、病気をしないだろうかちゃんと育つだろうかと心配ばかりしていたが、大きくなれば大きくなったで、受験やら就職やら心配の種はなくならない。

content.content: When my children were little, I fretted over whether they would get sick or grow up the right way. Now that they’re getting older, there is no end to worries about entrance exams and job-hunting and so forth.
The same verb or adjective is repeated in this pattern, which is used to say that situations that should contrast with each other are essentially the same. For instance,

content: means “if I had a car, it would be convenient, but even without a car, I don’t have as much trouble as I’d expected,”
means “My father complains, regardless of whether it is hot or cold,”
means “Money is always troublesome, whether you have it or not,” and
means “Children make us worry while they’re small and also after they’ve grown up.” In
, it is possible to omit the second use of 大きく and say 大きくなればなったで instead. ...たら...で is a synonymous expression.

content.content: 7. ...ば〈introductory utterance〉This pattern is used to indicate in advance the conditions under which the following statement will be made, or to give advance warning or explanation of something. It includes idiomatic expressions that are rather fixed. In most cases, ば can be replaced by たら.
a. ...ば+request, recommendation

content: もし、お差し支えなければ、ご住所とお名前をお聞かせください。

content.content: If you wouldn’t mind, please tell me your name and address.

content: A:今日の説明会はもう終わったんでしょうか。

content.content: Has today’s briefing already finished?
B:はい、3時に終了いたしました。よろしければ、来週の火曜にも説明会がございますが。
Yes, it was over at three. If it’s convenient for you, there will be another briefing next Tuesday.

content: よろしければ、もう一杯いかがですか。

content.content: If it suits you, would you care for another glass?

The expressions above in ba-form are idiomatic expressions used to make requests, recommendations, or suggestions. They show the speaker’s consideration for the listener’s situation or feelings. They mean “as long as it is not contrary to your convenience or intentions.” These are polite expressions that convey the speaker’s reservation—that is, the attitude that it is not necessary for the listener to act on the request, suggestion, etc., if it is inconvenient for him/her or if s/he does not want to do it.
b. ...ば〈viewpoint〉

content: A:本当に行くのかい。

content.content: Are you really going?
B:うん。でも正直言えば、本当は行きたくないんだ。
Yeah. But to be honest, I really don’t want to.

content: 50 年前と比べれば、日本人もずいぶん背が高くなったと言える。

content.content: Compared with fifty years ago, we can say that Japanese people too have gotten quite a bit taller.

content: 今は円高なので、国内旅行よりも海外旅行の方が安くつくらしい。考えてみればおかしな話だ。

content.content: I’ve heard that because the yen is strong now, traveling abroad is less expensive than traveling in Japan. If you think about it, that’s really strange.

content: 思えば、事業が成功するまでのこの 10 年は長い年月だった。

content.content: Looking back, these past ten years—until the project succeeded—were really long ones.

Verbs of utterance, thought, or comparison, such as 言う (say/speak), 思う (think), and 比べる (compare), are used in the ba-form to give advance warning or explanation of the perspective or standpoint from which the statement or judgment that follows will be made.
The ba-form expressions in

content: and
can be rephrased as 正直言って／言うと／言ったら and 比べて／比べると／比べたら, respectively.
can be rephrased as 考えてみると／みたら. The expression 思えば in
, which means “when I think about it once again,” is used to take an emotional look back at the past. It cannot be rephrased with the te-form, たら, or と.

content.content: As noted above, this usage of the ba-form consists mostly of idiomatic expressions that are rather fixed. Additional examples include はっきり言えば (frankly speaking/to put it bluntly), 極端に言えば (to put it in extreme terms), からみれば (from the viewpoint of), からすれば (from the standpoint of), and so on.
8. V-ば〈suggestion, recommendation〉

content: 《服売り場で》

content.content: 《at a clothing store》
A:これなんかどうかなあ。
What about this one?
B:着てみれば。
Why don’t you try it on?

content: A:ゆうべから、すごく頭が痛いんだ。

content.content: I’ve had a terrible headache since yesterday evening.
B:そんなに痛いの？　会社休めば。
That bad, huh? Why don’t you take a day off?

content: A:あ、これ間違ってる。

content.content: Oh, this is wrong.
B:教えてあげれば。
Why don’t you tell him?

V-ば is pronounced with rising intonation and used to suggest that the listener take a particular action. When the speaker ends a sentence with V-ば, it often sounds like s/he is unconcerned or has only passing interest in the matter at hand. Can be substituted with V-たらor V-たらどう. Used in casual spoken Japanese.

content: 彼は心臓が悪いくせに酒も飲めばたばこも吸う。

content.content: Even though he has a bad heart, he not only drinks but also smokes.

content: 彼は器用な男で料理もできれば裁縫もできる。

content.content: He is good with his hands, and he not only cooks but also sews.

content: 勲章なんかもらっても、うれしくもなければ、名誉だとも思わない。

content.content: Even if I were given a medal, I wouldn’t feel pleased or honored.

content: 動物が好きな人もいれば、嫌いな人もいる。

content.content: Some people like animals, but some don’t.

content: 人の一生にはいい時もあれば悪い時もある。

content.content: We have both good and bad times in our lives.
This pattern is used to list similar items for emphasis, as shown in

content: , or to list contrasting items in order to express that there is a variety of cases, as shown in
and

. These examples can be paraphrased using ...し, as in 酒も飲むしたばこも吸う (he drinks and moreover he smokes). Also, the first instance of も can be changed to が, as in 動物の好きな人がいれば嫌いな人もいる (some people like animals, but others don’t).

content.content: Oh Dad, hurry up and come!

content: 絶対に私が正しいんだってば。

content.content: I’m telling you, I’m definitely right!

content: 考えれば考えるほど分からなくなる。

content.content: The more I think, the more confused I get.

content: 食べれば食べるほど太る。

content.content: The more I eat, the more I gain weight.
【ほど】4b

content: その部品なら 1000 円も出せば買えるよ。

content.content: You can buy this part for only 1,000 yen.

content: こんな作業は5分もあれば終わる。

content.content: It would take only five minutes to finish a job like this.
【も】4d
【ばあい】［Nのばあい］［Na なばあい］［A／V　ばあい］

content: 雨天の場合は順延します。

content.content: In the case of rain, we will postpone it.

content: 火事、地震など、非常の場合には、エレベーターを使用せずに階段をご利用下さい。

content.content: In case of an emergency, such as a fire or earthquake, please use the stairs, not the elevator.

content: あの場合にはやむを得なかった。

content.content: In that case, it was unavoidable.

content: 陸からの救助が困難な場合には、ヘリコプターを利用することになるだろう。

content.content: If it is difficult to conduct a rescue operation from the ground, we’ll have to use a helicopter.

content: この契約が成立した場合には謝礼をさしあげます。

content.content: If you succeed in closing this contract, I will give you a bonus.

content: 万一8時になっても私が戻らない場合には警察に連絡して下さい。

content.content: If for some reason I’m not back by eight o’clock, please contact the police.
Used to focus on one situation out of many that could potentially happen.
In

content: , ...時は can be used instead of 場合. However, 場合 cannot be used to express concrete temporal relations in the speaker’s personal experience, as shown below.

content.content: （○）私が行った時には会議は始まっていた。
When I arrived, the meeting had already started.
（×）私が行った場合には会議は始まっていた。
In the case that I arrived, the meeting had already started.
2. ...ばあいもある

content: 患者の様態によっては手術できない場合もある。

content.content: Depending on the patient’s condition, there are cases in which an operation cannot be performed.

content: 商品はたくさん用意しておりますが、品切れになる場合もございます。

content.content: We carry a full line of products; however, there may be times that we run out of stock.

content: 優秀な学生であっても、希望した学校に入学できない場合もあるし、逆の場合もありうる。

content.content: Even for an outstanding student, there may be cases in which  can’t get into the school of hisher choice, and the opposite is also possible.
Used to state that a certain situation may arise. As shown in

content: and
, this expression is often used to say something like “this is usually no problem, but there are exceptional cases in which it isn’t possible, so I am notifying you in advance.”

content.content: In

content: , examples of contrasting cases are presented in order to show that there are many possibilities.

content.content: 3. ...ばあいをのぞいて

content: 緊急の場合を除いて、非常階段を使用しないで下さい。

content.content: Please do not use the fire escape, except in the case of an emergency.

content: 非常時の場合を除いてこの門が閉鎖されることはない。

content.content: This gate is never closed, except in an emergency.

content: 病気やけがなど特別な場合を除いて、再試験は行わない。

content.content: Unless there are special circumstances such as illness or injury, a make-up exam will not be offered.
Used to state an exceptional rule or regulation that applies under special circumstances. Often followed by an expression such as ...ないでください or ...しない.

content: means “use the fire escape only in emergencies” and
means “a make-up exam will be provided only under special circumstances such as illness or an injury.” 場合以外は may be used instead.

content.content: 4. V-ているばあいではない

content: 今は泣いている場合じゃないよ。

content.content: This is no time for tears.

content: もう議論している場合ではない、行動あるのみだ。

content.content: There is no time for further discussion; we should just take action.

content: A:入学試験に落ちたら、学校に行かなくてもすむな。

content.content: If I fail the entrance exam, I won’t have to go to school.
B:冗談を言っている場合じゃないだろう。少しは勉強したらどうだ。
This is no time for joking around. How about studying a little?
Used to say that the present situation or the listener’s actions are inappropriate, and to caution the listener that the present situation is very serious in nature.
5. ばあいによっては→
【によって】5
【ばいい】［N／Na　なら（ば）いい］［A-ければいい］［V-ばいい］An idiomatic expression that consists of the ba-form of a conjugated predicate combined with いい. ばよい and ばよろしい are slightly more formal expressions.
【たらいい】、
【といい】
1. V-ばいい〈suggestion, recommendation〉

content: 休みたければ休めばいい。

content.content: If you want to take a rest, then you should take a rest.

content: お金がないのなら、お父さんに借りればいいじゃない。

content.content: If you don’t have any money, why not borrow some from your father?

content: A:どうすればやせられるでしょうか。

content.content: What can I do to lose weight?
B:食べる量を減らして、たくさん運動すればいいんじゃないですか。
You could reduce the amount of food you eat and do a lot of exercise, couldn’t you?

content: A:何時ごろ行きましょうか。

content.content: Around what time should I come?
B:10 時までに来てくれればいい。
It would be good if you could be here by ten.

An expression used to recommend or suggest that the addressee take a certain action. Used to give or seek advice regarding what kind of measures or means should be taken in order to achieve a particular desired result. Synonymous with たらいい and can usually be rephrased as such. However, ばいい conveys a strong sense that “doing this alone is necessary and sufficient.” Depending on the context, ばいい may sometimes express a lack of interest on the part of the speaker or show that s/he is pointedly wondering why the addressee does not understand even such a simple matter. When ばいい is used to seek advice, it may be used in the form of a question that specifies a purpose, as shown in (3A) どうすればやせられるか (what can I do to lose weight?), or it may just be used in the interrogative form どうすればいいか (what can I do?).
2. ...ばいい〈wish, desire〉

content: この子が男の子ならいいのに。

content.content: If only she were a boy.

content: もうすこし暇ならいいのに。

content.content: I wish I had a little more free time.

content: もう少し給料が高ければいいのだが。

content.content: I wish my salary were a bit higher.

content: もっと家が広ければいいのになあ。

content.content: How I wish my house were more spacious!

content: 明日、雨が晴れればいいなあ。

content.content: I really hope it’ll clear up tomorrow.

content: 父が生きていればなあ。

content.content: If only my father were still alive.

content: 順子さんもパーティに出席してくれればいいなあ。

content.content: I hope Junko-san will come to the party too.

Expresses the speaker’s hope or desire that something will happen. Often followed by an expression like のだが, のに, or (のに)なあ at the end of the sentence. When the current situation differs from the one that is desired, or when the desired situation is impossible, ばいい expresses a feeling of regret, like “I’m sorry that it isn’t so.” As shown in

content: , the form ...ばなあ, which leaves out いい, is also used often. In almost all cases, ばいい can be replaced by たらいい.

content.content: 3. ...ばよかった

content: 親がもっと金持ちならばよかったのに。

content.content: I wish my parents had been richer.

content: 体がもっと丈夫ならばよかったのに。

content.content: If only I were healthier and stronger.

content: もう 10 センチ背が高ければよかったのに。

content.content: I wish I could have been ten centimeters taller.

content: あんな映画、見に行かなければよかった。

content.content: I shouldn’t have gone to see a movie like that.

content: A:スキー旅行楽しかったよ。君も来ればよかった。

content.content: The ski trip was fun. You should have come too.
B:僕も行ければよかったと思うよ。残念だった。
I wish I could have gone along too. It was too bad.

Expresses criticism of the addressee or a sense of regret when something did not actually happen or the current situation is contrary to what the speaker had hoped for. When the negative form なければよかった is used, as in

content: , it means that the speaker regrets something that s/he actually did. ばよかった may be followed at the end of the sentence by のに, のだが, or のだけれど. たらよかった is a synonymous expression. With this usage, it is not impossible to say とよかった. However, たらよかった and ばよかった are more common. のに is not usually used when the speaker is talking about his/her own actions.

content.content: （×）僕も行ければよかったのに。
I wish I could have gone too.
（○）僕も行ければよかったんだが。
I wish I could have gone too.
【ばかり】
1. 数量詞+ばかり

content: 一時間ばかり待ってください。

content.content: Please wait for an hour or so.

content: 三日ばかり会社を休んだ。

content.content: I took about three days off work.

content: りんごを三つばかりください。

content.content: Please give me three or so apples.

content: 1000 円ばかり貸してくれませんか。

content.content: Could you lend me a thousand yen or so?

content: この道を 100 メートルばかり行くと大きな道路に出ます。

content.content: If you continue on this road a hundred meters or so, you’ll get to a main road.

content: 来るのが少しばかり遅すぎたようだ。

content.content: It seems I’ve come a little too late.

content: ちょっとばかり頭がいいからといってあんなにいばることはないじゃないか。

content.content: There’s no reason for him to be acting so high and mighty just because he’s a little clever.
Attaches to an expression of amount or quantity and expresses an approximate amount. In

content: , ばかり can be replaced by ほど. In daily conversation, ほど is used more often.

content.content: In modern Japanese, ばかり can be used to express a length or span of time, as shown in

content: and
. However, it cannot be used for a specific time of day or date. In such cases, ぐらい or ごろ should be used instead.

content.content: （×）3時ばかりに来てください。
Please come at three o’clock or so.
（○）3時｛ぐらい／ごろ｝に来てください。
Please come at three o’clock or so.
（×）10 月3日ばかりに来てください。
Please come around the 3rd of October.
（○）10 月3日｛ぐらい／ごろ｝に来てください。
Please come around the 3rd of October.

content: and

mean the same as “please give me three apples” and “please lend me a thousand yen,” but adding ばかり makes the quantity a little less definite and softens the expression. ばかり can also be combined with すこし (a little), わずか (slightly), or 少々 (a bit), as in
and

content.content: 2. ...ばかり〈limit, restriction〉In spoken Japanese, ばっかり may also be used.
a. N（+助詞+）ばかり

content: このごろ、夜遅くへんな電話ばかりかかってくる。

content.content: Recently I’ve been getting nothing but strange phone calls late at night.

content: うちの子はまんがばかり読んでいる。

content.content: My child reads nothing but comics.

content: 彼はいつも文句ばかり言っている。

content.content: He does nothing but complain all the time.

content: 今日は朝から失敗ばかりしている。

content.content: All I’ve done since morning today is make mistakes.

content: 6月に入ってから、毎日雨ばかりだ。

content.content: Since the beginning of June, it’s been raining all day every day.

content: 子供とばかり遊んでいる。

content.content: She’s always playing just with the children.

content: 父は末っ子にばかり甘い。

content.content: My father indulges only the youngest of his children.

content: この店の材料は厳選されたものばかりで、いずれも最高級品だ。

content.content: The ingredients used in this store are all strictly selected, so everything is the highest grade.
Means “only this and nothing else.” Used to say that there are many things of the same kind, or repeated occurrences of the same action or event.
As shown in

content: and

, ばかり is often placed immediately after a noun. When it is used before が or を, it may keep the form ばかりが or ばかりを, but が and を are often dropped. With other particles, ばかり attaches to the combination of “noun + particle” and takes the forms Nとばかり and Nにばかり, as shown in
and

. ばかり is never used right after まで or より, or after から when it expresses a reason. ばかり is similar to だけ and のみ. However, when it implies “repeating over and over,” “always,” or “all,” だけ and のみ cannot be used instead.

content.content: （○）うちの子はいい子ばかりだ。
My children are all good kids.
（×）うちの子はいい子｛だけ／のみ｝だ。
My children are only good kids.
（○）母は朝から晩まで小言ばかり言っている。
My mother does nothing but pick on us from morning till night.
（×）母は朝から晩まで小言｛だけ／のみ｝言っている。
My mother only picks on us from morning till night.
b. V-てばかりいる

content: 彼は寝てばかりいる。

content.content: He does nothing but sleep.

content: 遊んでばかりいないで、勉強しなさい。

content.content: Don’t just play all the time, study.

content: 食べてばかりいると太りますよ。

content.content: If you’re always eating, you’ll get fat, you know.

content: 母は朝から怒ってばかりいる。

content.content: My mother has been angry since this morning.

Used to say that a certain action has been repeated many times or that someone/something always remains in the same state. Conveys a critical attitude on the part of the speaker. In this usage, ばかり cannot be replaced by だけ or のみ.
c. ...ばかりで［Na ばかりで］［A-いばかりで］［V-るばかりで］

content: 彼は言うばかりで自分では何もしない。

content.content: He is always complaining but does nothing on his own.

content: サウナなんか熱いばかりで、ちっともいいと思わないね。

content.content: A sauna is just hot, and that’s all. I don’t find it the least bit appealing.

content: このごろの野菜はきれいなばかりで味はもうひとつだ。

content.content: Vegetables these days just look nice on the outside and don’t taste very good.

content: 忙しいばかりで、ちっとももうからない。

content.content: I’m just busy all the time, and I don’t make any money at all.

Means that the only thing that exists or happens is what is emphasized by ばかり, and nothing more. Conveys a negative evaluation on the part of the speaker. Followed by a negative expression in the last part of the sentence.
d. Nばかりは

content: そればかりはお許し下さい。

content.content: Please forgive me. I’ll do anything but that.

content: 命ばかりはお助け下さい。

content.content: I’ll give you anything, but please spare my life.

content: 今度ばかりは許せない。

content.content: I can’t tolerate it this time.

content: 他のことは譲歩してもいいが、この条件ばかりはゆずれない。

content.content: I can compromise on other things, but with respect to this condition I cannot give in.

content: いつもは厳格な父も、この時ばかりは叱らなかった。

content.content: Even my father, who was always strict, didn’t scold us that time.

When ばかりは is attached to a noun or a demonstrative such as これ, それ, or あれ, it emphasizes “that alone and nothing else,” or “on that occasion, if no other.” A formal expression used in written language. If used in everyday spoken Japanese, it sounds pompous and old-fashioned.
3. V-たばかりだ

content: さっき着いたばかりです。

content.content: I just arrived a few moments ago.

content: このあいだ買ったばかりなのに、テレビが壊れてしまった。

content.content: Here I just bought a new TV the other day, and already it’s broken.

content: まだ3時になったばかりなのに、表はうす暗くなってきた。

content.content: Even though it’s only three o’clock, it’s starting to get dark outside.

content: 日本に来たばかりのころは、日本語もよく判らなくて本当に困った。

content.content: When I first came to Japan, I had a lot of trouble because I couldn’t understand Japanese very well.

content: 山田さんは一昨年結婚したばかりなのに、もう離婚を考えているらしい。

content.content: Even though Yamada-san just got married two years ago, apparently she’s already thinking about a divorce.
Means that not much time has passed since a certain action was completed. As shown in

content: , it can also be used when the speaker feels that not much time has elapsed, even if the action did not occur immediately before the time of speech.

content.content: 4. V-るばかりだ〈unidirectional change〉

content: 手術が終わってからも、父の病気は悪くなるばかりでした。

content.content: Even after the operation, my father’s illness kept on getting worse.

content: コンピュータが導入されてからも、仕事は増えるばかりでちっとも楽にならない。

content.content: Even since we started to use computers, the amount of work just keeps on increasing and it doesn’t get any easier at all.

content: 英語も数学も学校を出てからは、忘れていくばかりだ。

content.content: Since I left school, English and math just keep on slipping from my mind.
Expresses a one-way change for the worse. Can be rephrased as ...する一方だ.
5. V-るばかりだ〈completion of preparation〉

content: 荷物もみんな用意して、すぐにも出かけるばかりにしてあった。

content.content: I got all my baggage ready and was all set to leave immediately.

content: 部品も全部そろって後は組み立てるばかりという時になって、説明書がないことに気がついた。

content.content: I had all the parts ready and the only thing left to do was assemble them, when I noticed there was no instruction manual.

content: 料理もできた。ビールも冷えている。後は、お客の到着を待つばかりだ。

content.content: The food is ready. The beer is chilled. Now all that’s left is to wait for our guests to arrive.

content: 今はただ祈るばかりだ。

content.content: All I can do now is pray.
Often used in the forms V-るばかりにしてある and V-るばかりになっている. As shown in

content: , it is used to say that preparations are complete and the next action can be taken at any time. Can also be used to say “I’ve done everything, so the only thing left that I can do is...,” as shown in

content.content: 6. ...ばかり〈figure of speech〉a. ...ばかりのN［A-いばかりのN］［V-るばかりのN］

content: 頂上からの景色は輝くばかりの美しさだった。

content.content: The view from the top of the mountain was dazzlingly beautiful.

content: 船はまばゆいばかりの陽の光を浴びながら進んでいった。

content.content: The ship was moving forward in a radiant glow of sunshine.

content: 透き通るばかりの肌の白さに目をうばわれた。

content.content: My eyes were captivated by the clarity of her fair skin.

content: 用意された品々は目を見張るばかりの素晴らしさである。

content.content: The goods they’ve prepared are truly a wonderful sight to behold.

content: 雲つくばかりの大男が現れた。

content.content: A towering giant appeared (= a huge man whose head almost reached the clouds).

Used to state metaphorically that the degree of something is enormous or intense. Many expressions with ばかりのN are idiomatic, and this pattern tends to be used in written language. It is often used in stories and tales.
b. V-んばかり

content: デパートはあふれんばかりの買物客でごったがえしていた。

content.content: The department store was all but overflowing with throngs of customers.

content: 彼のスピーチが終わると、われんばかりの拍手がわきおこった。

content.content: When his speech ended, thunderous applause broke out.

content: 山々は赤に黄色に燃えんばかりに輝いている。

content.content: The mountains are glowing as if they are burning red and yellow.

content: お姫様の美しさは輝かんばかりでした。

content.content: The beauty of the princess was dazzling.

content: 泣かんばかりに頼むので、しかたなく引き受けた。

content.content: She implored me, almost in tears, so I had no choice but to accept the task.

content: ひさびさの再会を喜んだ祖母は手をひかんばかりにして我々を招きいれた。

content.content: Overjoyed at seeing us after such a long time, my grandmother half pulled us into her house.

content: 彼女は意外だと言わんばかりに不満気な顔をしていた。

content.content: She had an expression of dissatisfaction, as if to say that this was all so unexpected.

content: 彼はまるで馬鹿だと言わんばかりの目付きで私の方を見た。

content.content: The look in his eyes was as much as to say that I was a complete fool.

content: 彼はほとんど返事もせずに、早く帰れと言わんばかりだった。

content.content: Hardly replying at all, he looked as if he wanted me to leave instantly.
This pattern uses the negative form of a verb (V-ない), but ない is replaced with ん.
Used metaphorically to express an enormous or excessive degree of something.

content: mean “N which seems almost about to...,” and
means “she was so beautiful that it looked as if she was shining.”
and
mean “it almost seems as if she is about to....” and “it could be said that she was actually doing...,” respectively. In
, the form ...と言わんばかり is used, which means that although something was not actually said, the speaker gets a certain feeling from another person’s appearance or behavior.

content.content: Often used with words such as 様子 (appearance), 態度 (attitude), 目付き (expression), or 口調 (tone).
7. ...ばかりにa. ...ばかりに［Aばかりに］［V-たばかりに］

content: 働きがないばかりに、妻に馬鹿にされている。

content.content: Because he is shiftless, his wife treats him like a fool.

content: 二人は好き合っているのだが、親同士の仲が悪いばかりに、いまだに結婚できずにいる。

content.content: The two of them like each other, but because their parents don’t get along, they still haven’t been able to get married.

content: 彼の言葉を信じたばかりにひどいめにあった。

content.content: All because I believed what he said, I got into big trouble.

content: コンピュータを持っていると言ったばかりに、よけいな仕事まで押しつけられる羽目になってしまった。

content.content: All because I said I had a computer, I ended up being forced to do a lot of extra work.
Means “precisely because of a certain thing.” Followed by a clause describing an unfavorable situation that persists or an unfavorable event that arose as a result of that thing.
b. R-たいばかりにほしいばかりに

content: 彼に会いたいばかりに、こんなに遠くまでやって来た。

content.content: I came here from so far away just because I wanted to see him.

content: 嫌われたくないばかりに、心にもないお世辞を言ってしまった。

content.content: Just because I didn’t want to be disliked, I paid him a lot of compliments that I didn’t really mean.

content: わずかな金がほしいばかりに、人を殺すなんて、なんて馬鹿げたことだろう。

content.content: How ridiculous to kill someone just because you want a little money.

Means “I want (to do) it, no matter what” or “I don’t want (to do) it at all.” Followed by a clause indicating that the speaker doesn’t mind suffering or is ready to do something s/he really doesn’t want to do, in order to get what s/he wants.
8. V-てばかりもいられない

content: 父が亡くなって一か月が過ぎた。これからの生活を考えると泣いてばかりもいられない。

content.content: It has been a month since my father passed away. Thinking about my life from now on, I can’t just sit here and cry.

content: このごろ体の調子がどうも良くない。かといって、休んでばかりもいられない。

content.content: I haven’t been feeling very well recently. But having said that, I can’t afford to just keep on resting.

content: ひとごとだと思って、笑ってばかりもいられない。

content.content: I shouldn’t feel as if it has nothing to do with me and just keep laughing at it.

content: よその国のことだと傍観してばかりもいられない。

content.content: We shouldn’t just stand by as if it were of no concern to our country.

Can also be used in the form V-てばかりはいられない. Means “can’t just do such-and-such and nothing else” and is used to say, with respect to a current state of affairs, that the speaker feels that s/he or someone else “shouldn’t be complacent” or “had better stay on guard.” Often used with words that express some kind of feeling or behavior, like 笑う (laugh), 泣く (cry), 喜ぶ (be glad), 傍観する (sit back and watch), or 安心する (feel relieved).
9. ...とばかりはいえない

content: 一概にマンガが悪いとばかりは言えない。中にはすばらしいものもある。

content.content: We cannot necessarily say that comics are all bad. There are some that are terrific.

content: 一流大学を出て、一流企業に勤めているからといって、人間としてりっぱだとばかりはいえない。

content.content: We can’t say that she’s a wonderful human being just because she graduated from a top-ranked university and works at a leading company.
Means “we cannot make a sweeping assumption, because there are cases where this doesn’t hold true,” or “we cannot say such-and-such in general.”
0. ...とばかりおもっていた［N／Na　だとばかりおもっていた］［A／V　とばかりおもっていた］

content: 河田さんは独身だとばかり思っていたが、もうお子さんが二人もあるそうだ。

content.content: I’ve always thought that Kawada-san is single, but now I hear that he already has two children.

content: 試験は来週だとばかり思っていたら、今週の金曜日だった。

content.content: I was thinking all along that the exam was going to be next week, but I’ve just found out that it’s this Friday.

content: A:昨日はどうしてパーティーに来なかったんですか。

content.content: Why didn’t you come to the party yesterday?
B:えっ、昨日だったんですか。明日だとばかり思っていました。
What? Was it yesterday? I was sure it was going to be tomorrow.
Means “I was mistakenly under the impression that....” Used when something has prompted the speaker to realize that s/he was wrong. When the context is clear, a follow-up explanation can be omitted.
1. ...とばかり（に）

content: 相手チームの調子が崩れた。彼らはこのときとばかりに攻め込んだ。

content.content: The opposing team lost its stride. This was the moment for them to launch an attack.

content: 「えいっ」とばかり切りつけた。

content.content: She slashed at him fiercely.

content: 今がチャンスとばかりに攻めかかった。

content.content: As if this was his last chance, he threw himself into an attack.
【とばかり】
【ばかりか】A formal expression with the tone of written language.
1. ...ばかりか　...も／...まで［Nばかりか　...も／...まで］［Na なばかりか　...も／...まで］［A／V　ばかりか　...も／...まで］

content: 彼女は、現代語ばかりか古典も読める。

content.content: She can read not only modern works but also the classics.

content: 会社の同僚ばかりか家族までが私を馬鹿にしている。

content.content: Not only my colleagues at work but also my family treat me like a fool.

content: そのニュースが放送されると、日本国内ばかりか遠く海外からも激励の手紙がよせられた。

content.content: When the news was broadcast, letters of encouragement were sent to them not only from within Japan but also from abroad.

content: 手術をしても歩けるようにはならないかもしれないと言われていたが、手術後の回復はめざましく、歩けるようになったばかりか軽い運動もこなせるようになった。

content.content: Although he was told that he might not be able to walk even after surgery, his recovery has been remarkable; not only has he started to be able to walk, he can even do some light exercise.

content: 最近では、東京や大阪のような大都市ばかりか、中小都市でも道路の渋滞がひどくなってきているらしい。

content.content: Recently, traffic congestion seems to be getting much worse, not only in big cities such as Tokyo and Osaka, but even in small and medium-sized cities.
Means “not only...but also....” Used to make a statement about something of a lesser degree and then indicate that this also extends to something else at a higher degree.
For example,

content: means “she can read not only modern works but also the classics, which are much more difficult.”
means “not only my colleagues, but even my family (who should have the most faith in me) are treating me like a fool.”

content.content: When this expression is used in the form V-ないばかりか, it tends to be used to refer to something unfavorable.
（例）彼は自分の失敗を認めないばかりか、相手が悪いなどと言い出す始末だ。
He not only ignores his own mistakes, he tops things off by saying that the other party is to blame.
（例）親切に忠告してやったのに、彼は、まじめに聞かないばかりかしまいには怒りだした。
Even though I gave him a piece of advice out of kindness, he not only refused to listen seriously, he also ended up getting angry.
（例）薬を飲んだが、全然きかないばかりか、かえって気分が悪くなってきた。
Although I took some medicine, it didn’t work for me at all; instead, it made me feel sick.
2. そればかりか

content: 上田さんは英語が話せる。そればかりか韓国語もインドネシア語も話せる。

content.content: Ueda-san can speak English. In addition, he can also speak Korean and Indonesian.

content: 彼はその男に着る物を与えた。そればかりか、いくらかの金まで持たせてやった。

content.content: He gave some clothes to the man. What is more, he also let him have some money.

content: 日本の私立高校には、たいてい制服がある。そればかりか靴やカバンまで決まっているという学校が多い。

content.content: Students at private high schools in Japan usually wear a school uniform. Moreover, many schools even have designated shoes and school bags.
Used the same way as Usage 1 (above). The first sentence describes something of a relatively lower degree, and the second one indicates that this extends to another thing at a higher degree.
【ばかりでなく...も】

content: 山田さんは英語ばかりでなく中国語も話せる。

content.content: Yamada-san can speak not only English but also Chinese.

content: 漢字が書けないばかりではなく、ひらがなも書けない。

content.content: She can write neither kanji nor hiragana.

content: 佐藤さんがイギリスに行くことは、友人ばかりではなく家族でさえも知らなかった。

content.content: Not only his friends but even his family had no idea that Sato-san would go to England.

content: このアパートは、暑いばかりではなく音もうるさい。

content.content: This apartment is not only hot, it’s also noisy.
Used in the pattern XばかりでなくYも, which means “of course X, and also Y.” も can be replaced by まで (even) or さえ (even). In spoken Japanese, だけじゃなくて is used more often than ばかりでなく.
【ばこそ】［N／Na　であればこそ］［A-ければこそ］［V-ばこそ］

content: すぐれた教師であればこそ、学生からあれほど慕われるのです。

content.content: It is because she is such an excellent teacher that she is so adored by her students.

content: 体が健康であればこそ、つらい仕事もやれるのだ。

content.content: It is only because you are healthy that you can do the hard work, too.

content: 問題に対する関心が深ければこそ、こんなに長く研究を続けてこられたのだ。

content.content: It is because you are deeply interested in this problem that you have been able to continue your research for such a long time.

content: あなたを信頼していればこそ、お願いするのですよ。

content.content: It is because I trust you that I am asking you.

content: 家族を愛すればこそ、自分が犠牲になることなどはおそれない。

content.content: It’s precisely because I love my family that I’m not afraid of sacrificing myself.

Formed by attaching こそ to ば. A slightly old-fashioned expression used to emphasize the reason for something. Means “for this very reason.” Often followed by のだ at the end of the sentence. In most cases, から (because) can be used instead. However, with から the emphasis on the reason is lost.
（例）すぐれた教師だから、学生からあれほど慕われるのです。
She is an excellent teacher, so she is really adored by her students.
からこそ is similar to ばこそ. However, からこそ can be used with a cause or reason that has either positive or negative meaning, whereas ばこそ is unlikely to be used in the case of a negative cause/reason.
（×）体が弱ければこそ嫌いなものも無理して食べなければならない。
It is because you are weak that you should force yourself to eat things you don’t like.
（○）体が弱いからこそ嫌いなものも無理して食べなければならない。
It is because you are weak that you should force yourself to eat things you don’t like.
Has the tone of written language. Used in written texts and formal spoken language.
【からこそ】
【ぱなし】［R-っぱなし］Attaches to the stem of a verb. Can also be used in the form R-はなし.
1. R-っぱなし〈non-interference〉

content: ドアを開けっ放しにしないでください。

content.content: Please don’t leave the door open.

content: しまった。ストーブをつけっぱなしで出てきてしまった。

content.content: Oh, no! I left home without switching the heater off.

content: うちの子ときたら、食べたら食べっぱなし、服は脱いだら脱ぎっぱなしで、家の中がちっとも片づかない。

content.content: Our child leaves dirty dishes lying around after she eats and clothes lying around after she changes, so the house is never tidy.

Means that someone doesn’t do what s/he should do but “leaves something as it is,” or something “stays as it is” even though it shouldn’t. Unlike V-たまま, っぱなし often implies a negative evaluation of the action or event in question.
2. R-っぱなし〈duration〉

content: 新幹線はとても混んでいて、東京から大阪まで立ちっぱなしだった。

content.content: Because the shinkansen (bullet train) was very crowded, I had to stand all the way from Tokyo to Osaka.

content: うちのチームはここの所ずっと負けっぱなしだ。

content.content: These days our team keeps on losing one game after another.

content: 今日は失敗ばかりで、一日中文句の言われっぱなしだった。

content.content: Today I did nothing but make mistakes, so I got told off all day long.
Means that the same state of affairs or the same situation continues for a long time.
【ひいては】

content: 今回の事件は、一社員の不祥事であるばかりでなく、ひいては会社全体の信用をも失墜させる大きな問題であると言うことができる。

content.content: This incident is not only an indiscretion for one employee but could be said to be a huge problem that will discredit the company as a whole.

content: 無謀な森林の伐採は森に住む小動物の命を奪うだけでなく、ひいては地球的規模の自然破壊につながるものである。

content.content: The reckless destruction of forests will not only kill small forest animals but could also lead to the destruction of the natural environment on a global scale.
Means “as a consequence of,” or “furthermore” to what has been expressed in the previous phrase.

content: is used in the context where “what has the appearance of being a local issue may in fact have wider significance,” and
is used where “a relatively small issue develops into a larger issue.”

content.content: 【ひかえて】
1. NをNにひかえて〈time〉

content: 試合を 10 日後に控えて選手たちは練習に余念がない。

content.content: Players are practicing hard for the match in ten days’ time.

content: 結婚を間近に控えた娘が他の男と遊び回るなんてとんでもない。

content.content: It is inconceivable that a young woman who is to be married shortly should be fooling around with other men.

content: 入学試験を目前に控えてあわただしい毎日だ。

content.content: With the entrance examination almost here, I’m in a rush every day.

Indicates that an event X is approaching in Y amount of time, taking the form of XをYにひかえて. For Y, phrases that refer to time such as “shortly, in ten days’ time, in a few months’ time” are often used. Sometimes Y にis omitted. As in the case of

content: , ひかえたN is used to modify a noun.

content.content: 2. NをNにひかえて〈place〉

content: 神戸は背後に六甲山をひかえて東西に広がっている。

content.content: With Mt. Rokko as a backdrop, Kobe spreads from east to west.

content: 彼の別荘は後ろに山をひかえた景色のよい場所にある。

content.content: His holiday home is located in a scenic place with a mountain as a backdrop.
Used to describe a location that has large-scale scenic elements such as a mountain, lake,  sea, or bay set right behind it. As seen in

content: , ひかえたN is used to modify a noun.

content.content: 【ひさしぶり】→
【ぶり】2
【ひじょうに】

content: きょうはひじょうに寒い。

content.content: It is extremely cold today.

content: 非常に結構なお味でした。

content.content: The taste was excellent.

content: その御提案は非常にありがたいのですが、家族ともよく相談しませんと。

content.content: I am very grateful for what you are proposing but I need to discuss it further with my family.
States that the degree of something is remarkable. A formal expression. In colloquial language, とても and すごく are often used.
【ひではない】［Nのひではない］

content: アラビア語の難しさは英語などの比ではない。

content.content: The difficulty of Arabic is unmatched by English and other such languages.

content: 彼は専門的な教育を受けたことはないが、その博識は並の学者の比ではない。

content.content: Though he has never received any special training, the depth of his knowledge cannot be matched by any ordinary scholar.

content: 現在でも医学部に入学することは難しい。しかし、当時女性が医者になることの困難さは現代の比ではなかった。

content.content: Even now it is not easy to enter medical school.  However, the difficulties a woman faces in order to become a doctor nowadays can’t begin to compare with  the difficulties in those times.
Means “incomparable, to the extent that there is no comparison.”
【ひとつ】
1. ひとつ...ないEmphasizes the absence of something.  Similar expressions such as ...も...ない, ...として...ない are also used. To express frequency, 一度も／一回も／一ぺんも ...ない are used.
a. Nひとつ...ない［Nひとつない］［NひとつV-ない］

content: 雲一つない青空。

content.content: Cloudless blue sky.

content: しみひとつない美しい肌。

content.content: Beautiful skin without a single blemish.

content: 街は清潔で、ちりひとつ落ちていない。

content.content: The town is so clean that not a piece of rubbish is to be found.

content: 夜の公園には、猫の仔一匹いなかった。

content.content: There wasn’t a single cat in the park at night.

content: あたりはしーんとして、物音ひとつしない。

content.content: The area was perfectly still and not a sound was heard.

content: 彼の意見に誰一人反対しなかった。

content.content: Not one person objected to his opinion.

content: 昨日から何ひとつ食べていない。

content.content: I haven’t eaten a thing since yesterday.
Means “there is absolutely no ....” As in the case of

content: and
, by stating that there are no clouds/blemishes, the blueness of the sky and the beauty of the skin are emphasized. In the cases of
, when using a verb, the expression becomes a negative of the verb, “not at all V.”  As a counter, apart from ひとつ, “one + counter” (such as 一匹、一人、一枚) is often used.  Also, as in the cases of
and
, 誰ひとり...ない and 何ひとつ...ない emphasize the meaning of “nobody” and “nothing.”

content.content: b. ...ひとつも...ない［ひとつもない］［ひとつも　A-くない］［ひとつも　V-ない］

content: 知った顔はひとつもない。

content.content: There is no one I recognize.

content: この料理はひとつもうまくない。

content.content: There’s nothing tasty with this food.

content: 彼の作文には、まちがいはひとつもなかった。

content.content: His essay didn’t have a single mistake.

content: このごろのファッションなんか、ひとつもいいと思わない。

content.content: I don’t think fashions these days have anything good about them.

content: あいつは、君の忠告なんかひとつも覚えてやしないよ。

content.content: He won’t remember anything you warned him about.
Emphasizes that “there is no N” or “it is not A/not V.”
2. もうひとつ／いまひとつ　...ない

content: 給料はいいが、仕事の内容がもうひとつ気に入らない。

content.content: The pay is good but the contents of the job are not quite satisfying.

content: 風邪がもうひとつよくならない。

content.content: I just can’t shake off this cold.

content: 今年のみかんは、甘味がもうひとつ足りない。

content.content: This year’s oranges are not quite sweet enough.

content: 今年のみかんは、甘味がもうひとつだ。

content.content: This year’s oranges don’t have the sweetness I want.

Used in the patterns もうひとつ...ない or 今ひとつ...ない and indicates that something has not reached the level the speaker had expected. The situation is not bad, but at the same time the level achieved is not sufficient or satisfactory.

content: means that the speaker does not like the contents of the job very much.
means that the speaker’s cold isn’t completely better.
and
mean that the oranges are slightly lacking in sweetness.

content.content: 3. Nひとつ...できない

content: 近ごろの子供はぞうきんひとつ満足にしぼれない。

content.content: Children nowadays can’t even wring a cloth properly.

content: 女優のくせに、歌ひとつ歌えない。

content.content: Even though she’s an actress, she can’t even sing anything.

content: このごろの若いやつは、挨拶ひとつ満足にできない。

content.content: Young people these days can’t even greet others properly.

content: 留学してから、もう半年にもなるのに、息子ははがきひとつよこさない。

content.content: My son has been abroad studying for six months already but has yet to send even a postcard.

content: ビール一杯飲めないようでは、社会にでてから困るだろう。

content.content: You will have problems when you go out into the world if you can’t drink even a glass of beer.

content: 当時はたいへん貧しく、子供達に着物一枚新しく買ってやれなかった。

content.content: In those days we were so poor that we couldn’t even buy any new clothes for our children.

Used to emphasize the fact that a simple thing cannot be achieved or accomplished on this occasion, even though it would have been possible in any other situation. Often used to express the speaker’s disapproval or criticism by implying that any more than what has been stated is not achievable.
4. ひとつ

content: ひとつよろしくお願いしますよ。

content.content: Could you please do me a favor?

content: ひとつ頼まれてほしいことがあるんだが。

content.content: There is something I would like you to help me with.

content: ひとつ頼まれてくれないか。

content.content: Will you do something for me?

content: ここはひとつやってみるか。

content.content: Shall we have a go at this?

content: ひとつ話にのってみようか。

content.content: Shall I take up the suggestion?

content: おひとつどうぞ。

content.content: Please have one (food or drink).

content: ひとついかがですか。

content.content: Would you like to try one/some?
Used idiomatically in conversation. Means “try, have a go.” Used in requests as in the cases of examples

content: , or in describing trying something as in the case of examples
and
.  Also used when offering food or drink as shown in examples
and

content.content: 【ひとつまちがえば】

content: 出産というのは大変な仕事で、医学の進んだ現在でもひとつまちがえば命にかかわる。

content.content: Giving birth is a huge undertaking, and even with the high standard of modern medicine, one slightest mistake can make a difference of life or death.

content: 政治家の不用意な発言が続いている。ひとつ間違えば外交問題にも発展しかねない。

content.content: Politicians have been making a series of verbal blunders. One careless utterance could escalate into a diplomatic incident.

content: カーレースは、ひとつまちがえば、大事故につながることもある危険な競技である。

content.content: Car racing is a dangerous pursuit in which a small error can lead to a major accident.

content: ひとつ間違えば大惨事になるところだった。

content.content: At that point, one mistake could have turned it into a disaster.

content: 乗る予定だった飛行機が墜落した。ひとつ間違えば、私もあの事故で死んでいたと思うとぞっとする。

content.content: The airplane I was supposed to catch crashed. It chills me to think that I came so close to dying in that accident.
Means “by a very small margin.”

Shows that there is a high probability of something disastrous happening, and whether this materializes or not is determined by something very small and marginal. Often used in the form of ひとつまちがえば...こともある／かねない (if it went the wrong way...it could result in ...).
In the cases of

content: and
, disastrous situations have been narrowly avoided. In particular, ひとつ間違えば...ところだった indicates that “although it didn’t happen, it was very close.”

content.content: 【ひととおり】
1. ひととおり

content: 教科書は一通り読んだが、まだ問題集には手を付けていない。

content.content: I have read through the textbook, but I have not yet started on the workbook.

content: テニスを始めようと思って、道具は一通り揃えたのだが、忙しくて暇がない。

content.content: Thinking I would take up tennis, I bought all the equipment, but I have been too busy to find time for it.

content: そんなに上手なわけではないが、お茶もお花も一通りは習った。

content.content: Though I am not particularly good, I have completed both tea ceremony and flower arranging lessons.
Means “scanned through the whole thing” or “more or less satisfactorily.”
2. ひととおりのN

content: 一通りのことはできるようになった。

content.content: I am now able to do what is necessary.

content: この問題は難しくて一通りの説明ではわからない。

content.content: This problem is so difficult that it can’t be understood with just a general explanation.

content: 私が合格した時、母は一通りの喜びようではなかった。

content.content: When I passed the examination, my mother was absolutely over the moon (lit. beyond the ordinary level of joy).

content: みんなが頑張っているのだから、成功しようとすれば、一通りの努力ではだめだ。

content.content: As everyone is doing his or her best, so to succeed, just a passing amount of effort is not enough.

Means “the usual N” or “average N.” Often used in the forms ひととおりのNではない, ひととおりのNでは、...ない, it expresses the meaning that “it cannot be at just an average degree” or “it’s not possible at just the usual degree.”
3. ひととおりではない

content: 成功するまでの彼の努力は、一通りではなかった。

content.content: The amount of effort he had spent to succeed was extraordinary.

content: 愛用していたパソコンが壊れたので、あわてて友だちから借りてきたが、慣れない機械というのは、使いにくいこと一通りではない。

content.content: The personal computer I normally used broke and I had to borrow one from a friend in a hurry, but the difficulty in trying to use an unfamiliar model was  extraordinary.
Means “over and above the normal amount.”

content: means that one put in an extraordinary amount of effort.
means that it is extremely hard to use.

content.content: 【ひとり...だけでなく】［ひとりNだけでなく］

content: 子供のいじめは、ひとり日本だけでなく世界諸国の問題でもある。

content.content: Bullying among children is a problem that is not unique to Japan but is found in all countries of the world.

content: この活動は、ひとり本校だけでなく、広く地域に呼びかけて進めたい。

content.content: We would like to promote this activity not only within one school but also make a wider appeal to the community.
Means “not simply this only.” Used in written language and particularly for formal or serious topics.
The more classical and literary version of the above is  ひとり...のみならず.
【ひとり...のみならず】［ひとりNのみならず］

content: 環境汚染の問題は、ひとり我が国のみならず全世界の問題でもある。

content.content: The problem of environmental pollution concerns not only our nation but also the entire world.

content: このNGOの組織には、ひとりイギリスのみならず、多くの国の人々が参加している。

content.content: Not only British, but also people from many other countries belong to this NGO.
The more formal and literary expression of  ひとり...だけでなく.
【ひとり...だけでなく】
【ふう】
1. Nふう

content: あの寺は中国風だ。

content.content: That temple is Chinese in style.

content: 音楽家だというので、ちょっと変わった人間を想像していたが、やってきたのはサラリーマン風のごく普通の男だった。

content.content: As I had heard that he was a musician, I had imagined him to be an unusual person. But the man who showed up was a very ordinary, businessman-type person.

content: 美智子さんは、今風のしゃれた装いでパーティーに現れた。

content.content: Michiko-san turned up at a party in a trendy, fashionable outfit.
Means “in a certain style or fashion” or the appearance of something/someone is “like” something. Takes the form  NふうのN when modifiying a noun.
2. ...ふう〈appearance〉［Na なふう］［A-いふう］［V-ている／V-た　ふう］

content: そんなに嫌がっているふうでもなかった。

content.content: He didn’t look as though he was objecting to it so much.

content: 男は何気ないふうを装って近づいて来た。

content.content: The man came near us with an unassuming air.

content: 久しぶりに会った松井さんは、ずいぶんやつれて、生活にも困っているふうだった。

content.content: When I met Matsui-san after a long time, she looked exhausted and as if she was having difficulty in making ends meet.

content: なんにも知らないくせに知ったふうなことを言うな。

content.content: Don’t talk as though you understand when you don’t know anything!
Indicates the way or state in which someone appears to others.
3. ...ふう〈way, manner〉a. こういうふう

content: こういうふうにやってごらん。

content.content: Try doing it like this.

content: あの人も、ああいうふうに遊んでばっかりいると、ろくなことにはならないよ。

content.content: That guy, too, won’t amount to anything if he just keeps spending his time idly like that.

content: どういうふうに説明していいのかわからない。

content.content: I don’t know how to explain this.

content: A:きみ、最近太りすぎじゃない？

content.content: Haven’t you been putting on too much weight these days?
B:失礼な奴だな。そういうふうに、人の嫌がることをはっきり言うもんじゃないよ。
How rude of you! You shouldn’t go around like that pointing out things that offend people!

content: そういうふうな言い方は失礼だよ。

content.content: It sounds rude to say things in such a manner.
Similarly, そういう, ああいう, どういう may also be used to indicate specific ways or methods. Conjugate in the same way as na-adjectives.  The variations are こんなふう, そんなふう, あんなふう, どんなふう.
b. ...というふうに

content: 好きな時間に会社へ行き、好きな時間に帰るというふうにはいかないものだろうか。

content.content: I guess I can’t do things like choose when to go to work and when to return home.

content: ひとり帰り、またひとり帰りというふうにして、だんだん客が少なくなってきた。

content.content: Leaving one by one, the audience gradually grew smaller.

content: 今月は京都、来月は奈良というふうに、毎月どこか近くに旅行することにした。

content.content: We have decided to take a trip to a nearby place each month, such as Kyoto this month and Nara the next.
Used to describe how to do something, or the method or the state of something, by giving examples.
【ふしがある】

content: 彼はどうも行くのをいやがっているふしがある。

content.content: It seems as though he’s got something that makes him reluctant to go.

content: 犯人は、その日被害者が家にいることを知っていたと思われるふしがある。

content.content: It would seem that the culprit knew the victim would be at home that day.

content: その男の言動には、どことなくあやしいふしがある。

content.content: There’s something suspicious about that man’s words and actions.
Means “it would seem to be....” Used when it is presumed to be the case judging from someone’s words or actions, as in

content: and
. Can also be used when “there are reasons to be suspicious,” as in the case of

content.content: 【ふそくはない】

content: 相手にとって不足はない。

content.content: He is a worthy opponent.

content: 給料には不足はないが、仕事の内容がもうひとつ気に入らない。

content.content: I have no complaints about the pay but I am not happy with the job content.

content: 彼は大統領として不足のない人物だ。

content.content: He has all the qualities required of a president.
Means that everything meets the expectations of the speaker and there are no complaints.
【ふと】
1. ふと

content: 彼は映画の広告を見つけて、ふと立ち止まった。

content.content: When he noticed the poster for the film, he suddenly stopped walking.

content: ふと思いついて近所の本屋に寄ってみることにした。

content.content: On a whim, she decided to pop into a bookshop nearby.

content: 人は死んでしまうとどうなるのだろうなどと妙なことをふと考えた。

content.content: I suddenly had strange thoughts about what happens to people when they die.

content: 普段は何とも思わないのだが、何かの拍子に、忙しいだけのこんな生活がふとむなしくなるときがある。

content.content: I usually don’t think anything about it, but in an unexpected moment, there are times when a life that is only busy with so many things becomes pointless.
Means “at an unexpected moment” or “unexpectedly.” As seen in

content: , it means taking actions without any particular reason or purpose, on a whim or by accident. As in the cases of
, and

, combined with verbs such as考える, 思う, 思い出す (think, wonder, remember) or むなしくなる, さびしくなる (feel empty, sad) that indicate mood changes, it means recalling something or noticing something at an unexpected moment without knowing why.

content.content: 2. ふとV-ると

content: ふと見上げると、空にはぽっかり白い雲が浮かんでいた。

content.content: When I looked up, I noticed a soft, white cloud floating in the sky.

content: ふと見回すと、まわりには誰もいなくなっていた。

content.content: When I suddenly looked around, there was nobody left.

content: 仕事をしていて、ふと気がつくと外はもう暗くなっていた。

content.content: I had been working for some time before I realized it was already dark outside.
Means “doing something without any particular thought.” Begins a phrase at the end of a sentence telling what the speaker has realized.
3. ふとしたN

content: 長い一生の間には、ふとしたことで、人生が嫌になることがあるものだ。

content.content: During this long life, there are times when just a little thing can make it unpleasant.

content: ふとしたきっかけで、彼とつきあうようになった。

content.content: It was by chance that I started going out with him.

content: 小さいころ、祖母にはずいぶん可愛がってもらった。今でも、ふとしたひょうしに祖母のことを思い出すことがある。

content.content: When I was little, my grandmother doted on me. Even now, sometimes something unexpected makes me remember her.

content: 赤ん坊は、ふとした病気がもとで死んでしまった。

content.content: The baby died from an illness that had seemed insignificant at the time.
Means “unremarkable causes, reasons, triggers.”

content: means that the baby “died from an illness that was not considered to be serious.”

content.content: 【ぶり】
1. ...ぶり［Nぶり］［R-ぶり］

content: 最近の彼女の活躍ぶりは、みんなが知っている。

content.content: Everyone knows how brilliantly she has been performing recently.

content: 東京の電車の混雑ぶりは異常だ。

content.content: Trains in Tokyo are unbelievably crowded.

content: 間違いを指摘された時の、彼のあわてぶりといったらなかった。

content.content: He looked really flustered when his error was pointed out to him.

content: 彼は飲みっぷりがいいね。

content.content: He has a splendid way of drinking!

content: 佐藤さんの話しぶりからすると、交渉はあまりうまくいっていないようだ。

content.content: Judging from the way Sato-san is talking, the negotiations do not seem to be going well.
Means the way things are or their state when comes after action nouns or verb stems such as 活躍ぶり, 混雑ぶり, 勉強ぶり. 食べる becomes 食べっぷり and 飲む becomes 飲みっぷり. Example

content: means that the person drinks in such a hearty manner that it is a joy to watch.
10 数年ぶりに国に帰った。

content.content: I went home for the first time in more than ten years.

content: 国に帰るのは5年ぶりだ。

content.content: It has been five years since I last went to my hometown.

content: 父の半年ぶりの帰国に、家族みんなが大喜びした。

content.content: All the family rejoiced at the homecoming of  their father after half a year.

content: 三日ぶりにふろに入った。

content.content: I took a bath for the first time in three days.

content: 遭難者は 18 時間ぶりに救出された。

content.content: The victim was rescued after eighteen hours.

content: 最近、ずっと忙しかったが、今日は久しぶりにゆっくりすごした。

content.content: I have been very busy lately, but today I took it easy for the first time in a long while.

content: A:下田さん、お元気ですか。御無沙汰してます。

content.content: Shimoda-san, how are you? It has been a long time since I last saw you.
B:やあ、田中さん。久しぶりですね。
Ah, Tanaka-san! Long time no see!
Attaches to expressions of time.  Often used in the form of ...ぶりに...した to indicate that an action has taken place after a long space of time. As in the case of

content: , it is also possible to use a phrase indicating a relatively short time, but this is only possible in specific contexts. For example, in the case of

, the situation might be “normally I take a bath every day, but because I had a cold I hadn’t been able to take a bath for three days,” and therefore for the speaker, the time (three days) appears very long. The phrases ひさしぶりですね and おひさしぶりです are greetings used when meeting someone after a long interval.

content.content: 【ぶる】［N／Na　ぶる］

content: 彼は、通ぶってフランスの上等なワインしか飲まない。

content.content: He pretends to be a connoisseur by drinking only expensive French wine.

content: 父は学者ぶって解説を始めた。

content.content: My father started explaining as though he were an expert.

content: あの人は上品ぶってはいるが、たいした家柄の出ではない。

content.content: She tries to look posh, but in fact she isn’t from a family of any consequence.

content: 彼はもったいぶってなかなか教えてくれない。

content.content: He is so pompous that he wouldn’t part with the information readily.

content: 三年生になった長女は、先輩ぶって一年生の妹にいろいろ教えたりしている。

content.content: The eldest daughter is now in the third grade and helps her little first grade sister like a true upperclassman.

Means that someone behaves in a manner that is typical of the role the person is emulating.  Often used in the context of いかにもたいした...である (behaving as if the person is a “real someone/something”). As in the cases of

content: , it often shows the speaker’s negative evaluation of someone who “behaves as though he is X” or who is pretentious and makes a fuss over something minor. In
, もったいぶって is an idiomatic phrase that means “affected, putting on airs” and is used in conjunction with phrases such as なかなか教えない／言わない. It has limited usage.

content.content: 【ぶん】
1. ...ぶん［Nのぶん］［Vぶん］［期間を表す名詞+ぶん］

content: 甘いものが大好きな弟は、私のぶんのケーキまで食べてしまった。

content.content: My brother, who has a sweet tooth, has eaten my share of the cake.

content: 心配しなくていいよ。君のぶんはちゃんと残しておいたから。

content.content: You don’t need to worry. I have put aside your share.

content: 子供に食べさせる分まで奪われてしまった。

content.content: Even the portion kept for the children has been taken.

content: 来月分の食費まで先に使ってしまった。

content.content: I have spent next month’s food allowance already.

content: 部屋を借りるためには、はじめに家賃三ヶ月分のお金が必要です。

content.content: In order to rent an apartment, three months’ rent as a down payment is required up front.
Means a portion, allocation, or something for a specific purpose.

content: means that “the money put aside for next month’s food has been spent already,” and
means “the amount of money equivalent to three months’ rent.”

content.content: 2. ...ぶん（だけ）［Nのぶん］［Naなぶん］［A／V　ぶん］

content: 1年間の休職の分だけ、仕事がたまっていた。

content.content: A year’s worth of work piled up during my 12-month absence.

content: 外で元気な分、彼は家ではおとなしい。

content.content: He is as quiet at home as he is outgoing in public.

content: 食べれば食べたぶん（だけ）太る。

content.content: I put on as much weight as I eat.

content: 早く始めれば、その分（だけ）仕事が早く終わる。

content.content: If we start early, we can finish the work that much quicker.

content: 彼を信頼していたぶん（だけ）裏切られたときのショックも大きかった。

content.content: My disappointment matched the trust I had placed in him.
Means that the level matches the thing that it is being compared to.
As in the cases of

content: and
, it is often used in the pattern ...V-ばV-たぶんだけ or ...V-ば、そのぶんだけ.  It indicates “that much” or “the equivalent amount.”
means that one puts on as much weight as one eats.
means that the work gets done that much quicker if it is started earlier.
means that the high level of trust placed in him is proportionate to the degree of shock felt. だけ may be abbreviated.

content.content: 3. このぶんでいくとこのぶんでは

content: 一年かかって、まだ半分も終わっていない。このぶんでいくと完成するには三年ぐらいかかりそうだ。

content.content: It has taken a year and we haven’t done even half of what we need to do. At this rate, it will take three years or so before we complete it.

content: このぶんでは徹夜になりそうだ。

content.content: The way things are going, we will be working through the night.

content: このぶんでいくと、仕事は予定より早く終わりそうだ。

content.content: If everything goes on like this, the work will finish sooner than planned.
Means “if it goes on like this” or “if it continues at this pace.”
4. ...ぶんには［Naなぶんには］［A／V　ぶんには］

content: はたで見ているぶんには楽そうだが、自分でやってみるとどんなに大変かがわかる。

content.content: It looks like fun if you are an onlooker, but if you try it yourself, you will know how hard it is.

content: 私はいかなる宗教も信じない。しかし、他人が信じるぶんには一向にかまわない。

content.content: I do not believe in any religion.  However, I do not object in any way to other people’s beliefs.

content: A:申し訳ありません。会議の始まる時間がいつもより少し遅くなりそうなんですが。

content.content: I am sorry to inform you that the meeting is likely to start a little later than usual.
B:遅くなるぶんには、かまわないよ。
I wouldn’t mind the meeting starting a little later (rather than starting earlier).
Means “as long as.”
