content: means “as long as one does not participate but only observes, it looks like fun.”
means, “I don’t believe in any religion, but I do not mind if other people choose to believe in one.”
means, “starting the meeting later is acceptable,  but starting it sooner is not.”

content.content: 【へた】na-adjective. In modifying a noun, it takes the form of へたなN.
1. へたa. へた

content: 字がへたなので、もっぱらコンピュータを愛用している。

content.content: As my handwriting is not very good, I use a computer all the time.

content: A:日本語がへたで、すみません。

content.content: I am sorry, my Japanese is very poor.
B:へただなんてとんでもない。とてもおじょうずですよ。
What nonsense (that you are not good at Japanese)! Your Japanese is good!

content: 父は、へたなくせにゴルフが好きだ。

content.content: Despite being not very good at it, my father still likes golf.

content: へたな言いわけはやめなさい。

content.content: Stop making lame excuses.

content: 社長は気むずかしい人だから、へたなことを言って、怒らせないように気をつけたほうがいい。

content.content: The company president is hard to please. You had better be careful not to annoy her by saying something out of line.
Indicates that one is not good at or poor at something.

content: show that something is not done well or the technique is not good. In the case of
, it is used to mean a careless action or speech.

content.content: b. Nは...がへただ［NはNがへただ］［NはV-るのがへただ］

content: 私は計算がへただ。

content.content: I am poor at mental math.

content: 私は歌を歌うのが下手だ。

content.content: I am not good at singing.

content: 山下さんはピアノはうまいが、歌は下手だ。

content.content: Yamashita-san is good at playing the piano but poor at singing.

content: 英語は読む方はなんとかなるが、話すのは下手だ。

content.content: I can manage reading but I am not good at speaking in English.

content: A:テニスはやるんだろう？

content.content: You play tennis, don’t you?
B:うん、へただけどね。
Yes. Not so well, though.

Means that one cannot do something well, or one is not good at something. Another expression, ...が苦手だ, is similar. However, while 苦手だ includes the meaning of not liking something/someone very much, へただ does not.
2. へたに

content: このごろの機械は複雑だから、故障しても素人がへたにいじらない方がいい。

content.content: Machines these days are so complex that an amateur should not tamper with them when one breaks down.

content: へたに動かすと爆発するかもしれないので、うかつに手がだせない。

content.content: It might explode if it’s handled clumsily, so we can’t do anything careless with it.

content: A:うちの娘が反抗期でね。家族と口もきかないんだ。注意した方がいいのかなあ。

content.content: Our daughter is going through a rebellious stage. She won’t talk to her own family. I wonder if I should have a word with her.
B:でも、へたに注意するとよけいに反抗するかもしれないよ。
Well, if you give her advice in a clumsy way, she may rebel even more.
Means doing something without due care or consideration. Similar to うかつに (thoughtlessly, carelessly). As in

content: , it can be used to mean that there is a high probability of something not going well and therefore, it is best not to attempt anything. Or as in the cases of
and
, it can be used to mean that one ought to proceed very carefully as something untoward can happen if one is not well prepared.

content.content: 3. へたをすると

content: A:試験はどうだった？

content.content: How was the exam?
B:それが、あまり良くなかったんだ。へたをすると、卒業できないかもしれないなあ。
Well, I didn’t do too well. In the worst case scenario, I may not be able to graduate.

content: 風邪のようなありふれた病気でもへたをすると命とりになることがある。

content.content: Even a minor illness like the common cold can be fatal if care is not taken.

content: 不景気で中小企業の倒産があいついでいる。へたをすると、うちの会社も倒産するかもしれない。

content.content: Because of the recession, many small- to medium-scale companies have been going bankrupt. If things get worse, my company may go bust, too.

content: 道を歩いていたら、上から植木鉢が落ちてきた。へたをすると大怪我をするところだった。

content.content: When I was walking in the street, a flowerpot fell from directly above me. I very narrowly escaped a serious injury.
Means “if things go wrong” or “it might have been.” As in the cases of

content: , it is used when a bad consequence is anticipated. It is often used to express the speaker’s fear or anxiety.
, which has the pattern へたをすると...V-るところだった, indicates that things nearly went very badly but did not.

content.content: 【べからざる】［V-るべからざる］

content: 川端康成は日本の文学史上、欠くべからざる作家だ。

content.content: Kawabata Yasunari is a writer who could not be omitted in any history of Japanese literature.

content: 大臣の地位を利用して、企業から多額の金を受け取るなどは、政治家として許すべからざる犯罪行為である。

content.content: It is an unforgivable criminal act for a politician to use his or her position as a government minister to receive large sums of money from companies.

content: いかなる理由があったにせよ、警官が一般市民に暴行を加えるなど、あり得べからざる異常事態だ。

content.content: Whatever the reason, it is beyond belief that a policeman should use physical violence on an ordinary citizen.

Used in the form of べからざるN. It is the classical written language version of べきでないN. It indicates that the action or the state is not right or undesirable and means ...ことができないN or ...てはいけないN (N that cannot do something or N that should not do something).

content: means that the person cannot be omitted or must not be forgotten.
means that the criminal act is so terrible that it should be stopped.
refers to an incident that would not/should not take place.

content.content: A limited number of verbs can take this form. As in the cases of

content: , it is often used in idiomatic phrases such as 欠くべからざる人物, 許すべからざる行為, あり得べからざる事態. Note that in the case of 得る in
, べからざる is attached to 得, forming 得べからざる. It is a formal written language style. Also note that the pronunciation of 得 in 得べからざる is u rather than e.

content.content: 【べからず】［V-るべからず］

content: 落書きするべからず。

content.content: No graffiti.

content: 芝生に入るべからず。

content.content: Keep off the grass.

content: 犬に小便させるべからず。

content.content: Do not use this area as a toilet for your dogs.

Indicates the prohibition of a certain action. It is a classical written language form of べきでない. It means that the action is not proper, desirable, or good and has the same meaning as the form V-てはいけない.
It is a forceful prohibition often used on signs or notice boards. In recent years, softer expressions such as 芝生に入ってはいけません or 芝生育成中 are more common.

Other phrases commonly used on signs or notice boards in order to stop people from taking certain actions include ...禁止 and V-ることを禁ず. All indicate strong prohibition and are very formal. They are not used in spoken language.
【べき】［N／Na　であるべき］［A-くあるべき］［V-るべき］This is a conjugation of the literary auxiliary verb べし. It attaches to the dictionary form of verbs in modern usage. する becomes either するべき or すべき in form.

content: 学生は勉強す（る）べきだ。

content.content: Students ought to study.

content: 他人の私生活に干渉す（る）べきではない。

content.content: You should not interfere with someone else’s private life.

content: 近頃は小学生まで塾に通っているそうだが、子供はもっと自由に遊ばせるべきだ。

content.content: I hear nowadays even primary school children attend cram schools, but I think children should have greater freedom just to play.

content: 女性は常に化粧をして美しくあるべきだなどという考えには賛成できない。

content.content: I cannot agree with the idea that women should always be made up and look pretty.

content: 地球的規模で自然破壊が進んでいる。人間は自然に対してもっと謙虚であるべきだ。

content.content: Ecological destruction is progressing on a global scale. People ought to be more thoughtful about nature.

content: 教師: 君、成績が良くないね。もっと勉強するべきだね。

content.content: Teacher:  Your academic record is not good. You ought to study harder.
学生: すみません。
Student:  Sorry.

content: A:海外研修に行くかどうか迷っているんだ。

content.content: I am debating whether I should go on an overseas study tour.
B:そりゃ、行くべきだよ。いいチャンスじゃないか。
You should go! It is a good opportunity, isn’t it?

content: この仕事はきみがやるべきだ。

content.content: You should do this job.

content: 会社の電話で私用の電話をするべきじゃないね。

content.content: You shouldn’t be making personal calls on the company telephone, you know.
Means that “it should be done,” “it is proper to do ...,” or “... must be done.” The negative form is べきではない meaning “it is not good to do ...” or “doing ... is not appropriate” or “must not do ....”
In

content: , the speaker is expressing his view on general matters. If used in relation to the actions of another, it becomes advice for or against doing something, prohibition, or an order. This expression is used in both spoken and written language.

content.content: 2. ...べき　だった／ではなかった［V-る／V-ておく　べきだった］

content: あの時買っておくべきだった。

content.content: I should have bought it then.

content: あんなひどいことを言うべきではなかった。

content.content: I shouldn’t have said such a nasty thing!

content: 君はやっぱりあのときに留学しておくべきだったんだよ。

content.content: In hindsight, you should have gone abroad to study then.
Indicates one’s regrets over an action one took or didn’t take and means “I wish I had done ...” or “I wish I hadn’t done ....”

content: means that the speaker wished he had bought it then but he did not.
means that the speaker wished he had not said something unkind but in reality, he did. In

, the speaker is saying to his friend that he should have gone abroad to study. When the speaker talks about himself, it shows his regrets or remorse. This expression is often used in both everyday written and spoken language.
外交政策について、議論すべきことは多い。

content.content: With regard to the diplomatic policies, there are many issues that need to be discussed.

content: エジプトのピラミッドは、永遠に残すべき人類の遺産である。

content.content: The pyramids of Egypt are a world legacy that should be protected for future generations forever.

content: エイズは恐るべき速さで世界中に広がっている。

content.content: AIDS is spreading around the world at a fearful speed.

content: 人は皆死すべき運命を背負っている。

content.content: Everyone is fated to die.
Means “something that has to be done” or “the inevitable consequence.”

content: indicates what has to be discussed as an important issue.
means that a world heritage should be maintained as a matter of course and should be passed on to the future generations.
and
are idiomatic phrases each meaning “incredible speed” and “unavoidable eventual death” respectively.

content.content: A formal expression that is often used in written language.
【べく】［V-るべく］The verb stem of an auxiliary verb べし that is used in classical written language. It is used in modern Japanese as an expression that is formal and is in the style of written language.
1. ...べくV-た

content: 大学に進むべく上京した。

content.content: They went to Tokyo in order to go to university.

content: 速やかに解決すべく努力致します。

content.content: We will do our best to resolve the issue promptly.

content: しかるべく処置されたい。

content.content: Please deal with the matter appropriately.
Means “in order to do ...” or “so that ... can be done.”

content: is asking for an appropriate action to be taken. Used in formal expressions in the style of written language.

content.content: 2. V...べくしてV-た

content: この機械の危険性は以前から何度も指摘されていた。この事故は起こるべくして起こったといえる。

content.content: The danger of this machinery has been pointed out on numerous occasions. It could be said that this accident was waiting to happen.

content: 彼が勝ったのは偶然ではない。練習につぐ練習を重ねて、彼は勝つべくして勝ったのだ。

content.content: His victory was not coincidental. Practice after practice brought about his well-deserved victory.
Means something has happened as it has been anticipated as a matter of course when the verb is repeated.

content: means that people had been worried that an accident might take place and indeed, an accident did happen.
means that it is no wonder he won because he had worked for it so hard, and it is not because of luck or coincidence.

content.content: A formal expression in the style of written language.
3. ...べくもない

content: 多勢に無勢では勝つべくもない。

content.content: Being so outnumbered by our opponents, we have no chance of winning.

content: 優勝は望むべくもない。

content.content: There is no hope of coming in first.

content: 突然の母の死を、遠く海外にいた彼は知るべくもなかった。

content.content: Being so far away overseas, there was no way for him to learn of his mother’s sudden death.
Means that something is not achievable, cannot be done, or something cannot happen. It is a formal expression in the style of written language, and it is not used very often in modern Japanese.
【べし】［V-るべし］

content: 学生はすべからく勉強に励むべし。

content.content: Students should apply themselves to their studies.

content: 後生おそるべし。

content.content: The next generation carries our hopes.

content: 今度の試験は、よほど難しかったらしく、クラスで一番良くできる生徒でも 60 点しかとれなかった。後は推して知るべしだ。

content.content: The recent examination must have been very difficult because even the brightest student in the class got only sixty points. You can imagine how the rest of the class did.

An expression used in the classical written language, rarely used in modern language except in idioms. Expresses a command with the meaning of “ought to do ... as a matter of course” or “it is appropriate to do ....”

content: takes the form of すべからく...べし and in this context it means, “It’s a matter of course that students must study, so study!”
is an idiom meaning, “Young people have great potential and therefore they should be nurtured.”

is an idiomatic phrase meaning, “if one thinks about it, it will become apparent.” In the context of this example, it means that it goes without saying that all the rest of the students got poorer marks.

content.content: 【べつだん】
1. べつだん...ない

content: べつだん変わったことはない。

content.content: Nothing has really changed.

content: 彼はいつもより口数が少ないようだったが、私はべつだん気にもしなかった。

content.content: He seemed less talkative than usual, but I did not pay any attention to it.
Means “not especially” or “nothing particularly.” It is a slightly formal expression with the tone of written language.
2. べつだんのN

content: 別段のご配慮をいただきたく存じます。

content.content: We would be grateful for your special attention to this matter.

content: 来賓として招かれて、別段の扱いを受けた。

content.content: Being invited as a guest, I was treated exceptionally well.
Means “special” or “extraordinary.”

content: is a very formal expression.

content.content: 【べつとして】
1. Nはべつとして

content: 中国語は別として、そのほかのアジアの言語となると学習する人が極端に少なくなる。

content.content: Besides Chinese, very few people are now studying any other Asian languages.

content: 京都や奈良といった観光地は別として、小さい寺や神社には観光収入はないのが普通だ。

content.content: Apart from tourist sites such as Kyoto and Nara, small temples and shrines tend not to get any revenue from tourism.

content: 中国での生活が長かった西田さんは別として、うちの会社には他に中国語のできる人はいない。

content.content: Apart from Nishida-san who lived in China for a long time, there is no one else in my company who can speak Chinese.
Means “except something” or “something is special.” Alternatively, べつにして (putting ... aside) is used.
2. ...はべつとして［...かどうかはべつとして］［疑問詞+かはべつとして］

content: 将来役に立つかどうかは別として、学生時代にいろいろな分野の勉強をしておくことは、けっして無駄ではない。

content.content: Regardless of whether or not they will become useful in the future, it is not a waste of time to study in a variety of fields while one is a student.

content: 実現可能かどうかは別として、この計画は一度検討してみる価値はあると思う。

content.content: Putting aside whether it is realizable or not, this plan is worth evaluating.

content: だれが言ったかは別として、今回のような発言がでてくる背景には根深い偏見が存在すると思われる。

content.content: No matter who may have said it, the fact that such an opinion is expressed indicates that there are deep-rooted prejudices amongst us.
Means that something is put aside for the time being. Alternatively, べつにして may be used.
【べつに】
1. べつに...ない

content: 別に変わったことは何もない。

content.content: Nothing has really changed.

content: 会社の宴会など別に行きたくはないが、断わる適当な理由も見つからないので、しかたなく行くことにした。

content.content: Though I really didn’t want to attend the company party, since I could not find any appropriate reason to refuse, I decided to go as a duty.

content: 今どき洋酒なんか、別に珍しくはないが、海外旅行のおみやげにとわざわざ持ってきてくれた彼の気持ちがうれしい。

content.content: Although these days western liquors aren’t particularly unusual, I appreciate his kindness to make a special effort to bring some back as a present from his recent trip abroad.

content: あなたなんかいなくても、別に困らないわ。

content.content: I wouldn’t miss you at all if you weren’t around!

content: A:どうかしたの。

content.content: Is anything the matter?
B:いや、べつに。
No, nothing in particular.
Means “not especially” or “not particularly ....”  As in the case of

content: , ...ない may be omitted.

content.content: 2. （...とは）べつに［Nとはべつに］［Vのとはべつに］

content: 料金とは別に 600 円の送料が必要です。

content.content: It requires 600 yen as postage, in addition to the charge.

content: サービス料は別にいただきます。

content.content: A service charge will be added to the bill.

content: みんなに配ったのとは別に、君には特別なプレゼントを用意しておいた。

content.content: Apart from what was distributed to everybody, I have prepared a special present for you.

content: 昨日来たのとは別に、もうひとつ小包が来ています。

content.content: In addition to the one that arrived yesterday, another parcel has come.

content: 映画館はすごく込んでいたので、友だちとは別に座ることにした。

content.content: As the cinema was very crowded, I decided to sit separately from my friends.

content: 彼女は旅館に泊まった私達とは別にとなりの町のホテルに泊まった。

content.content: She stayed in a different hotel in the next town while we stayed in an inn.

content: show “apart from ...” or “except ....”
and
mean “away from ...” or “different from ....”

content.content: 3. Nべつに

content: クラス別に写真を撮った。

content.content: We took photos of each class separately.

content: 小学校や中学校では男女別に名簿をつくるのをやめようという動きがある。

content.content: There is a movement among elementary and junior high schools for not producing separate student rosters according to sex.

content: アンケートの結果を、年齢別に集計した。

content.content: The results of the questionnaire have been tabulated according to age.

content: 調査の結果を国別に見ていくと、中国をはじめとしたアジアの国々の経済成長が著しいことがわかる。

content.content: When we examine the results of the survey by country, it becomes apparent that the economic development in China and other Asian countries is remarkable.
Means “by N” or “N as a standard.”
【べつにして】→
【べつとして】
【ほう】
1. ...ほう〈direction〉［Nのほう］［Vほう］

content: 京都の北のほうは冬には雪がずいぶん積もる。

content.content: The northern parts of Kyoto get rather deep snowfalls.

content: あっちの方へ行ってみましょう。

content.content: Let’s try going in that direction.

content: A:どこに座ろうか。

content.content: Where shall we sit?
B:前の方にしようよ。
Let’s go towards the front.

content: まっすぐ私の方を見てください。

content.content: Please look straight towards me.

content: 太陽が沈むほうに向かって鳥が飛んで行った。

content.content: Birds flew away in the direction of the sunset.

content: A:それで、山下さんはまっすぐ家に帰ると言ったんですね？

content.content: And then, Yamashita-san said she would be going straight home, right?
B:ええ、そう言いました。でも、山下さんが歩いて行った方には駅もバス停もないんで、おかしいなと思ったんです。
Yes, so she said. But I thought it was strange as there were no stations or bus stops in the direction she was heading.
Indicates a general direction. It is often used in conjunction with directional nouns such as 東／西／南／北, あっち／こっち／どっち, こちら／そちら／どちら, 前／後, 左／右, 上／下.
2. ...ほう〈one of two〉［Nのほう］［Na なほう］［A／V　ほう］

content: A:どちらになさいますか。

content.content: Which one would you like?
B:じゃ、大きいほうをください。
Well, please give me the larger one.

content: A:いくらですか。

content.content: How much is it?
B:こちらの赤い方が1万円、あちらの方が1万3千円となっております。
This red one is 10,000 yen and that one over there is 13,000 yen.

content: どちらでもあなたのお好きな方で結構です。

content.content: Whichever you like is fine by me.

content: A:連絡は御自宅と会社とどちらにさしあげましょうか。

content.content: Should we contact you at home or at the office?
B:自宅の方にお願いします。
Please contact me at home.

content: 私の方からお電話します。

content.content: I will call you.

content: A:たいへん申し訳ございませんでした。

content.content: I am so sorry.
B:いや、悪いのはこちらの方です。
No, it was I who was at fault.

content: 妻:悟は学校で問題なくやっているのかしら。

content.content: Wife: I wonder if Satoru is doing all right at school.
夫:放っておけばいいさ。何かあれば、学校の方から何か言ってくるだろう。
Husband: Leave him alone. If there is anything, there’ll be some contact from the school.

content: A:パチンコで5千円も負けちゃったよ。

content.content: I have lost 5,000 yen in Pachinko.
B:君なんか、まだましな方だよ。僕なんか一万円以上負けてるよ。
You’re hardly the worst case. I have lost over 10,000 yen!

content: 自分で言うのもなんだが、子供のころ僕は成績のよい方だった。

content.content: Though I say so myself, I was one of the more academic children.

content: A:御専門は物理学でしたね。

content.content: I believe you specialize in physics.
B:ええ、原子力の方をやっております。
Yes, I am working in the field of atomic energy.

content: 二つの作品のうち先生が手伝った方はさすがに完成度が高い。

content.content: Between the two works, the one the teacher had helped with was not surprisingly of high quality.
Points at one of two things.

content: and
contrast the speaker and the listener by placing the speaker as “my side/this side” and the listener as “your side/that side.” In
, 学校の方から and 学校から mean the same thing. Here, “the school side” and “our side” are contrasted. As in the cases of
and
, it is sometimes used to indicate a certain area/field or direction.
means that the person was good at school work.
does not contrast two things but indicates the particular field of atomic energy within the field of physics.

content.content: 3. ...ほう〈comparison〉［Nのほう］［Na なほう］［A／V　ほう］a. ...ほうが...より（も）

content: 飛行機のほうが新幹線より速い。

content.content: An airplane is faster than shinkansen (bullet train).

content: 高いより安い方がいいに決まっている。

content.content: There is no question that cheaper is better.

content: 新幹線で行く方が飛行機で行くより便利だ。

content.content: It is more convenient to go by shinkansen (bullet train) than by airplane.

content: イタリアへ行くなら、ローマやベニスみたいな観光地より田舎の方がおもしろいよ。

content.content: If you are going to Italy, the countryside is more interesting than tourist spots like Rome and Venice.

content: スポーツは見るより自分でやる方が好きだ。

content.content: I like participating in sports more than watching them.

content: 漢字は読むことより書くことの方が難しい。

content.content: It is more difficult to write than to read kanji.

content: 加藤さんよりも佐藤さんの方が、親切に相談にのってくれる。

content.content: Sato-san is kinder than Kato-san when it comes to listening to my concerns.

content: 彼のけがよりも精神的なショックの方が心配だ。

content.content: I am more worried about his psychological shock than the injury.

In comparing two things, the one that is indicated by ...ほうが is superior to the other. It can be used in conjunction with ...より（も） forming ...より（も）...のほうが but either one of the two tends to be dropped when it is clear which one is upheld within the context.
b. どちらのほう

content: A:田中さんと井上さんとでは、どちらのほうが背が高いですか。

content.content: Between Tanaka-san and Inoue-san, which one is taller?
B:田中さんの方が背が高いです。
Tanaka-san is taller.

content: A:コーヒーと紅茶と、どちらのほうがよろしいですか。

content.content: Which would you prefer, coffee or tea?
B:どちらでも結構です。
Either one will be fine by me.
Used to compare two things and explain the result. It is possible to omit のほう and use just どちら.
4. Vほうがいい〈advice〉

content: 僕が話すより、君が直接話す方がいいと思う。

content.content: I think it would be better if you spoke directly to them rather than have me say something.

content: そんなに頭が痛いんだったら医者に行ったほうがいいよ。

content.content: If your headache is so bad, you had better go and see the doctor.

content: あいつとつきあうのはやめたほうがいい。

content.content: It would be better if you stopped being friends with him.

content: A:ときどき胃が痛むんだ。

content.content: I get a stomachache sometimes.
B:たいしたことはないと思っても、一度医者に行っておく方がいいよ。
Even if you think it is nothing, it is better to see a doctor just in case.

content: 退院したばかりなんだから、あまり無理をしない方がいいと思うよ。

content.content: You shouldn’t overdo it since you have only just been discharged from the hospital.

content: あの人おしゃべりだから、話さない方がいいんじゃない。

content.content: She is such a gossip, so isn’t it better not to tell her?
Used in giving advice to the listener by presenting what the speaker thinks good or right. It attaches to the dictionary form, ta-form or nai-form of a verb.

There is not a big difference between using the dictionary form or ta-form.  However, if the speaker wishes to give his advice strongly, the ta-form is more common.  For example, if the speaker is facing a person who is suffering from a cold, V-たほうがいい is used more commonly. The nai-form is always used as ...ない and never becomes ...なかったほうがいい.
（○）あの人には話さないほうがいいよ。
It is better not to tell him.
（×）あの人に話さなかったほうがいいよ。
It is better not to tell him.
5. ...ほうがましだ〈choice〉［Nのほうがましだ］［Na なほうがましだ］［A-いほうがましだ］［Vほうがましだ］

content: A:テストとレポートとどっちがいい？

content.content: Between tests and reports, which one do you prefer?
B:レポートの方がましかな。
I’d have to say a report.

content: どうせやらなくちゃいけないなら、日曜日に働くよりは、金曜日に残業して片づけてしまう方がまだましだ。

content.content: If I must do the job anyway, it is better to work late on Friday and get it done than to work on Sunday.

content: あんな男と結婚するくらいなら死んだほうがましだ。

content.content: I would rather die than marry that man.

content: 途中でやめるぐらいなら始めからやらないほうがましだ。

content.content: It is better not to start at all than to quit in the middle.
Indicates the lesser of the two evils in the comparison for the speaker. It means that, if one has to choose between the two unfavorable things, this one is more acceptable than the other is.

Sometimes the item of comparison is shown by using ...くらいなら. The phrase ...くらいなら is similar to ...より in meaning except in the case of the former, the speaker’s negative feeling towards the choice is present.
6. ...ほうがよかった〈regret〉［Nのほうがよかった］［Na なほうがよかった］［A／V　ほうがよかった］

content: 人に頼まないで自分でやった方がよかった。

content.content: It would have been better if I’d done it myself rather than asking someone else to do it.

content: A:髪を切ったんだけど、似合う？

content.content: I got a haircut. Do you think it suits me?
B:えっ、切ったの。長い方がよかったのに。
Oh, you got it cut? It was better longer....

content: せっかくの連休だからと思って、ドライブに出たが、車が渋滞していてまったく動かない。こんなことなら、来ない方がよかった。

content.content: We came out for a ride because we wanted to take advantage of the long weekend (lit. consecutive holidays), but the roads are so jammed that traffic isn’t moving. We would have been better off not coming out if we were going to end up like this.

content: 少し有名になると仕事がどんどん入ってくるようになったが、苦労のわりには収入は増えない。いっそ、無名のままの方がよかった。

content.content: I have more and more work coming in since I’ve become somewhat well-known, but for all my hard work my income hasn’t increased. It would have been better if I had stayed a nobody.

Shows the speaker’s regrets by presenting to the listener that what happened in reality was less favorable or appropriate than the alternative. If it refers to the speaker’s own action, it indicates the speaker’s regret, and if it refers to other people’s actions, it can express the speaker’s regret, disappointment, or sympathy.
【ほうだい】
1. R-（たい）ほうだい

content: 近所の子供たちは、後片付けもせずに、家の中を散らかし放題に散らかして帰っていった。

content.content: The neighborhood children went home without tidying up, leaving my home strewn with things hither and yon.

content: 誰も叱らないものだから、子供達はやりたいほうだい部屋の中を散らかしている。

content.content: Because nobody scolds them, the children make as much of a mess as they like in the room.

content: 口の悪い姉は相手の気持ちも考えずいつも言いたい放題だ。

content.content: My sharp-tongued sister always speaks her mind without caring how the other person may feel.

By attaching to stems of the verbs such as やる, する, and 言う, it indicates someone’s action that is taken without caring about others around him/her. The speaker’s negative assessment of the situation is inferred. There is an idiomatic expression 勝手放題にする (doing as one likes).
2. R-ほうだい

content: バイキング料理というのは、同じ料金で食べほうだいの料理のことだ。

content.content: “Viking cuisine” means that one can eat as much as one likes for a set price.

content: 《ビアホールの広告》2000 円で飲み放題。

content.content: 《Beer Hall advertisement》Drink as much as you like for 2,000 yen.

content: 病気をしてからは、あんなに好きだった庭いじりもできず、庭も荒れ放題だ。

content.content: Since he became ill, he hasn’t been able to enjoy working in the garden like he used to, and the garden has gone wild.
Indicates that something can be done with no restriction, or freely. It is often used in conjunction with verbs such as 食べる and 飲む. As in the case of

content: , it can mean “without taking any particular action, leave things as they are.”

content.content: 【ほか】
1. ...ほかa. ...ほか［Nのほか］［Na なほか］［A／V　ほか］

content: 今日のパーティーには、学生のほかに先生方もお呼びしてある。

content.content: We have invited not only students but also teachers to the party today.

content: うちの会社には、田中さんのほかにはロシア語のできる人はいない。

content.content: Besides Tanaka-san, there is no one who can speak Russian at our office.

content: 今回の会議には、学識経験者のほか、銀行、電気メーカーといった企業の人事部長が参加した。

content.content: In addition to those with academic experience, personnel managers from banks, from electronic manufacturers, and from other industries attended the meeting this time.

content: お支払いは、銀行、郵便局のほか、お近くのコンビニエンスストアなどでも扱っております。

content.content: In addition to banks and post offices, payments can be made at nearby convenience stores.

content: 今度引っ越したアパートは、ちょっと駅から遠い他はだいたい希望通りだ。

content.content: The apartment I have just moved into meets most of my wishes except that it is a little far from the station.

content: きょうは授業にでる他には特に何も予定はない。

content.content: Apart from going to class, I have no other plans for today.
Means “apart from ....” It can take different forms such as ほか, ほかに, ほかは.
b. Nほか

content: 田中他三名が出席します。

content.content: Tanaka and three others will attend.

content: 出演山田太郎他。

content.content: Performed by Yamada Taro and others.

Used to indicate that there are other people or things apart from the main person or the main thing represented by N. This is a formal expression with the tone of written language, often used in introducing panel speakers or members of the casts of plays.
2. ほかに（は）

content: A:留守番ありがとう。何か変わったことはありませんでしたか。

content.content: Thank you for house-sitting for me. Did anything happen while I was away?
B:まちがい電話が一本かかってきただけで、ほかには何も変わったことはありませんでした。
Someone called with a wrong number, but otherwise, there is nothing else to mention.

content: 《税関で》

content.content: 《at customs》
A:何か申告するものはありますか。
Do you have anything to declare?
B:ウイスキーが5本です。
I have five bottles of whiskey.
A:他には？
Anything else?
B:他にはべつに。
Nothing else.

content: ボーイ: コーヒーでございます。他に御用はございませんか。

content.content: Waiter: Here is your coffee. Will there be anything else, sir?
客:今のところ、特にありません。
Guest: Nothing at the moment.
ほかに（は） indicates “Apart from ....”
3. ほかのN

content: 石田さんに頼もうと思ったが、忙しそうなので、他の人に頼んだ。

content.content: I was going to ask Ishida-san to do it, but since he seems to be busy, I have asked someone else.

content: ここがよく分かりません。ほかのところはやさしかったんですが。

content.content: I don’t understand this part (of the question, etc.). Other parts were easy, though.

content: A:この店は高すぎるね。

content.content: This shop (or restaurant) is too expensive.
B:そうね。ほか（の店）へ行きましょう。
Yes. Let’s go to another shop.

content: これはちょっと高すぎますから、他のを見せてくれませんか。

content.content: This is a little too expensive. Would you show me a different one?
Means “a different one from what is being discussed currently.” As in the case of

content: , N can be omitted from ほかの物 and the abbreviated form ほかの may be used.

content.content: 4. ...ほかはない［V-るほかはない］a. ...ほかはない

content: 気は進まないが、上司の命令であるので従うほかはない。

content.content: Though I am not keen on the idea, since it is an order from my superior, I don’t have any choice but to obey.

content: だれも代わりに行ってくれる人がいないので、自分で行く他はない。

content.content: Since no one else would take my place, I have to go myself.

content: 体力も気力も限界だ。この勝負はあきらめる他はない。

content.content: I am at my limit physically and mentally. There is nothing I can do but to give up on this competition.

Means “there is no other option but to do ..., even though it is not a desirable one.” It is in the style of written language, and there are similar expressions such as ...ほかすべがない and ...しか手がない. In spoken language, similar expressions include ...しかない and ...ほかしかたがない.
b. ...というほかはない

content: 十分な装備を持たずに冬山に登るなど、無謀と言うほかはない。

content.content: It is nothing but reckless to go climbing in the mountains during winter without adequate equipment and provisions.

content: あんな高いところから落ちたのにこの程度のけがですんだのは、幸運だったと言う他はない。

content.content: It is nothing short of a miracle that they escaped from more serious injury after falling from such a height.

content: 世界には前世の記憶をもった人がいるという。それが事実だとしたら、ただ不思議と言うほかはない。

content.content: They say that there are people in the world who have memories of their previous lives. If that is true, it is truly amazing.
This expression means “there are no other words to describe (something) but ...” or “it is really ....” Formal expression with the feel of written language.
5. ...よりほかに...ない...よりほかは...ない

content: 田中さんよりほかに頼れる人はいない。

content.content: Apart from Tanaka-san there is nobody else whom I can depend on.

content: 入学試験も目前にせまった。ここまでくれば、がんばるより他はない。

content.content: The entrance examination is almost here. At this stage, there is nothing I can do but try my best.
【より】3b、
【より】3c
6. ほかならないa. Nにほかならない

content: 今回の優勝は彼の努力のたまものにほかならない。

content.content: The victory in the recent championship is completely a fruit of his own effort.

content: 日本における投票率の低さは、政治に対する失望感の現れにほかならない。

content.content: The low turnout rate in Japan is an indication of the level of disillusionment people feel toward politics.

content: このような事故が起きた原因は、利益優先で安全性を軽視してきた結果にほかならない。

content.content: The only reason for this accident is the emphasis that has been put on making profits at the expense of safety.
Means X is nothing other than Y when presented as XはYにほかならない. It is a formal expression used in written language, not in spoken language.
b. ほかならないN／ほかならぬN

content: ほかならない彼の頼みなので、引き受けることにしました。

content.content: Since no one else besides him has asked me a favor, I have decided to help.

content: 他ならない鈴木さんからの御依頼ですから、喜んでお引受けいたしましょう。

content.content: Since it is Suzuki-san who is asking me a favor, I would be glad to help.

content: ほかならぬ彼の頼みなので、断わるわけにはいかなかった。

content.content: Since the request came from him, and not from anyone else, I could not refuse to help.

content: うわさ話をしていたところにやって来たのは、ほかならぬ当人だった。

content.content: The person who showed up was the very person we had been talking about.

content: 現在の繁栄をもたらしたのも、自然破壊をもたらしたのも、他ならぬ人間である。

content.content: Both the current prosperity and the destruction of nature were brought about by human beings and nothing else.
Means “none other than N.” In the cases of examples

content: to

, there is an assumption that, if it were a different person who was asking for a favor, the speaker would not have been as accommodating. It is often used in the context that the person is important to the speaker and therefore it is not possible to reject the request. In examples
and
, an emphasis is placed on the topic in the format of “it is indeed N” or “none other than N.” ほかならぬ is used more often than ほかならない.

content.content: 【ほしい】As an adjective, 欲しい can be used. In the form of V-てほしい, however, ほしい is often written in hiragana.
1. Nがほしい

content: もっと広い家が欲しい。

content.content: I would like a more spacious house.

content: A:誕生日のプレゼントは何が欲しい？

content.content: What do you want for a birthday present?
B:そうね。新しい服が欲しいな。
Well, I guess I want some new clothes.

content: 子供の頃、僕は野球のユニホームが欲しかった。

content.content: When I was a child, I wanted to have a baseball uniform.

content: 今は何も欲しくない。

content.content: I don’t want anything at the moment.

content: 《小説》彼はどうしても金がほしい。そのことを考えると夜もねむれないぐらいだ。

content.content: 《novel》 He wants the money in the worst way. He wants it so badly that he can’t get to sleep at night thinking about it.
Expresses the speaker’s desire to obtain or to have as his own. Being an adjective of emotion, ほしい in the declarative form can be used either in indicating the speaker’s desire as shown in example

content: or asking the listener what s/he desires as in the case of

. The declarative form ほしい at the end of a sentence cannot be used to indicate the wishes/desires of a third-person sentence’s subject. The third person’s wishes and desires must be expressed in the form ...は...をほしがっている or ...がほしいようだ.

content.content: （○）妹は人形を欲しがっている。
My sister wants a doll.
（×）妹は人形がほしいです。
My sister wants a doll.
When the perspective can shift freely, for example, in narrative fiction as shown in

content: , it is possible to use a declarative form at the end of a sentence. Also, it must be noted that, as in the case of

, a direct inquiry about the listener’s desire or wish can only be made when the speaker and the listener are in a close relationship. In a polite situation, it is better to avoid using ほしい (e.g. 砂糖がほしいですか) and use indirect expressions such as 砂糖はいかがですか.

content.content: 2. V-てほしいa. NにV-てほしい

content: この展覧会には、たくさんの人に来てほしい。

content.content: I would like lots of people to come to this exhibition.

content: あまり仕事が多いので、だれかに手伝ってほしいと思っている。

content.content: There is so much work that I would like someone to help me.

content: 母には、いつまでも元気で長生きしてほしい。

content.content: I want my mother to keep well and live for a long time.

content: 妻にはいつまでもきれいでいてほしい。

content.content: I want my wife to stay beautiful forever.

content: 僕を置いて外国へなんか行かないでほしい。

content.content: I don’t want you to go abroad and leave me behind.

content: 子供たちには自分の利益ばかり考えるような人間にだけはなってほしくない。

content.content: Above all, I don’t want my children to become selfish people thinking only of their own interests.

content: A:A：うちの会社にも落度があったかもしれません。

content.content: It may be that our company was also to blame.
B:君にまで、そんなことを言って欲しくないね。
I wouldn’t like to hear that sort of thing from you, of all people.
Indicates the speaker’s wish or request for someone else to do something. Means “I would like the other person to do V,” as in examples

content: and
, or “I want things to remain the way they are,” as in examples
and

content.content: There are two negative forms of V-てほしい: V-ないでほしい and V-てほしくない. As in the case of example

content: , V-ないでほしい is often used in place of V-ないでください, when asking the other person not to do V. V-てほしくない can be used in two situations: when the speaker states his wish that does not affect the listener as in the case of example
, or when the speaker is criticizing the listener’s action as in the case of

content.content: b. ...がV-てほしい

content: 寒い冬にはもうあきあきしてきた。早く春がきてほしい。

content.content: I have had enough of this cold winter. I wish spring would come soon.

content: 早く夏休みが始まってほしい。

content.content: I am longing for the summer vacation to start.

content: これだけ晴天が続くと、農家ならずとも雨が降ってほしいと思わない人はいないだろう。

content.content: After such a long period of dry weather, I don’t think there’s anyone—not just farmers—who doesn’t wish for rain.

content: 彼の愛が永遠に変わらないでほしいと思うのはぜいたくでしょうか。

content.content: Is it asking too much to think I want his love for me to last forever?

Indicates that the speaker is wishing for a certain event to take place. When the object in question is a person, it takes the form Nに as seen in 2a. If what is wished for is an event, as in the cases of examples

content: , Nが is used.

content.content: 3. ほしい（んだけれど）Nがほしい or V-てほしい, which indicates the speaker’s desire or wish, can be used as an indirect request. When expressed with a degree of hesitation such as ほしいんですが... and ほしいんだけど..., the request sounds politer and softer.
a. Nがほしいんですが

content: 客:すみません。これがほしいんですが。

content.content: Customer: Excuse me. I would like this one, please.
店員: こちらでございますか。ありがとうございます。
Assistant: This one, madam?  Thank you very much.

content: 店員: これなどいかがですか。

content.content: Assistant: How about something like this?
客:そうねえ、もうちょっと明るい色のがほしいんだけど。
Customer: Ah, yes, but I want something in a little brighter color.

content: 《友だちの家で》

content.content: 《at a friend’s house》
A:水が一杯ほしいんだけど。
Can I have a glass of water?
B:いいよ。ちょっと待って。
Sure. Wait a minute.

content: 《おもちゃ屋で》

content.content: 《at a toy shop》
子供: お母さん、これほしい。
Child: Mom, I want this.
母親: ダメ。今日は何も買いません。
Mother: No. I’m not buying you anything today.
Indicates what the speaker wants to obtain and is used by the speaker as an indirect request. It is often used as a set phrase すみません。Nがほしいんですが／ですけど as shown in examples

content: and

content.content: b. V-てほしい（んだけれど）

content: 客:プレゼントなので、リボンをかけてほしいんですが。

content.content: Customer: Since it’s a present, I’d like you to put a ribbon on it.
店員: はい、少々お待ちください。
Assistant: Certainly. One moment, please.

content: A:今日は早く帰ってきてほしいんだけど。

content.content: I would like you to come home early today, if you can.
B:うん、わかった。
OK, I will.

content: A:田中さんに来週の予定を教えてあげてほしいんですが。

content.content: I wonder if you would let Tanaka-san know next week’s schedule.
B:ああ、いいですよ。
All right.

content: あしたは出かけないでほしいんだけど。

content.content: I would appreciate it if you didn’t go out tomorrow.

content: 君にこの仕事をやってほしいんだが。

content.content: I would like you to do this job.

content: 君には東京に行ってほしい。

content.content: I want you to go to Tokyo.

V-てほしい（んだけれど） is used as an indirect request, asking the listener to perform a certain action indicated by the verb V. When the speaker asks the listener not to take a certain action, V-ないでほしい is used. Examples

content: and
are normally used by men, and suggest that they are putting pressure on the listener.

content.content: 4. V-させてほしい（んだけれど）

content: A:来週休ませてほしいんですけど。

content.content: Would it be possible for me to take time off next week?
B:ああ、いいよ。
Yes, you can.

content: この件はぼくに任せてほしいんだけど。

content.content: I would very much like you to let me handle this.

content: 私に行かせてほしいんですが。

content.content: Would you please allow me to go?
Taking the form（私に）Vさせてほしいんですが／けれど, this is used when the speaker asks for permission to proceed with an action.
【ほしがる】［Nをほしがる］

content: 山下さんは新しい車を欲しがっている。

content.content: Yamashita-san wants a new car.

content: 桃子が欲しがっているのは女の子の人形ではなくて、熊のぬいぐるみだ。

content.content: What Momoko wants is not a girl’s doll but a teddy bear.

content: 人の物を欲しがってはいけない。

content.content: You mustn’t covet other people’s possessions.

content: 当時まだ一年生だった僕は、母の注意をひきたいばかりに、わざと妹のおもちゃをほしがってみせた。

content.content: When I was in first grade, in order to get my mother’s attention, I intentionally made a point of coveting my younger sister’s toys.
Used to convey that the speaker wants something, which s/he is making apparent by actions or words.
Is normally used to express the wish of a person other than the speaker, whereas for the speaker’s own wishes, ...がほしい is used. However, as in the case of example

content: , when the speaker is pretending to want something, it is possible to use ほしがる.

content.content: 【ほとんど】
1. ほとんど

content: この小説はほとんど読んでしまった。

content.content: I have almost finished reading this novel.

content: 京都の有名な寺にはほとんどいったことがある。

content.content: I have visited almost all the famous temples in Kyoto.

content: 新しいビルは、ほとんど完成している。

content.content: The new building is almost completed.

content: 彼ほどの成績なら、合格はほとんど確実だ。

content.content: Judging by his academic record, it is almost certain that he will pass the examination.

content: 地域のスポーツクラブに行ってみたら、ほとんどが年輩の人だったのには驚いた。

content.content: I was surprised to find that there were mainly elderly people at the local sports club.

content: このクラスのほとんどが、アジアからの留学生だ。

content.content: Most students in this class are from Asian countries.
Means “almost” or “the majority.” Being used to modify the predicate of the sentence as in the cases of examples

content: , it can mean “not entirely, but almost all” or “almost 100%” as in the case of
. It can also be used in the form of （Nの）ほとんどが indicating “most of N” as in the cases of
and

content.content: 2. ほとんど...ない

content: 給料日前でほとんど金がない。

content.content: Since it is a few days before I get paid, I have very little money at the moment.

content: 彼は酒はほとんど飲まない。

content.content: He hardly drinks any alcohol.

content: 英語はほとんど読めない。

content.content: I can hardly read any English.

content: この仕事を三日で仕上げるのは、ほとんど不可能に近い。

content.content: It would be almost impossible to complete this task within three days.

content: このごろは忙しくて、あれほど好きだったテニスにも、ほとんど行っていない。

content.content: I have been so busy lately that I’ve hardly had time to play tennis, which I used to enjoy so much.

content: 今でこそ有名だが、10 年ほど前には、彼の名前を知っている人は、ほとんどいなかった。

content.content: He is now very famous, but ten or so years ago, there was hardly anyone who knew his name.

content: ほとんど飲まず食わずで、一日中働き続けた。

content.content: I continued to work all day, almost without eating or drinking.

content: 遭難して三日めには、食糧もほとんどなくなった。

content.content: By the third day after we’d lost our way, the food was almost gone.
Means that the amount is very little, or the frequency is low.
3. ほとんど...た［ほとんどV-るところだった］［ほとんどR-かけた］

content: 子供の頃、チフスでほとんど死にかけたことがある。

content.content: I nearly died from typhoid fever when I was a child.

content: 横道から飛び出してきた自転車とほとんどぶつかるところだった。

content.content: I nearly collided with a bicycle that came speeding out of a side road.

content: 事業は、ほとんどうまくいきかけたのだが、運悪く得意先が倒産してしまい、それからは悪いこと続きだった。

content.content: We nearly made a success of the business, but unfortunately one of the customers went bankrupt, and after that there was nothing but trouble.
Means that something looked very likely to happen but in reality it did not. Often used in the sense of a narrow escape, as in the cases of examples

content: and

content.content: 【ほど】
1. 数量詞+ほど〈approximation〉

content: 水を 10 CCほど入れてください。

content.content: Please add about 10 ml of water.

content: 修理には一週間ほどかかります。

content.content: It will take a week or so to repair.

content: 完成するまでに3時間ほどかかります。

content.content: It will take approximately three hours to complete.

content: 仕事はまだ半分ほど残っている。

content.content: There is still about half the work yet to be done.

content: A:りんごください。

content.content: I would like some apples, please.
B:いくつですか。
How many would you like?
A:五つほど。
Five or so.

Indicates an approximate quantity when attached to a quantifier. Can be used with lengths of time, such as hours or days. However, it cannot be used with expressions that have no length such as the time of the day or date, where ごろ is used instead.
（×）3時ほど来て下さい。
Please come at about 3:00 p.m.
（○）3時ごろ来て下さい。
Please come around 3:00 p.m.
The meaning of 五つほど in example

content: is the same as五つください but it sounds politer to give the listener the option to choose “around five” apples.

content.content: ほど, when used with a numerical value to mean “approximately,” can be replaced by くらい or ぐらい.
2. ...ほど...ない〈comparison〉［Nほど...ない］［Vほど...ない］a. ...ほど...ない

content: 今年の夏は去年ほど暑くない。

content.content: This summer hasn’t been as hot as last summer.

content: 試験は思っていたほど難しくなかった。

content.content: The exam wasn’t as difficult as I’d thought it was going to be.

content: 教師の仕事はそばでみているほど楽ではない。

content.content: The job of a teacher isn’t as easy as it may seem to a bystander.

content: 佐藤は今井ほど勤勉な学生ではない。

content.content: Sato isn’t as conscientious a student as Imai.

content: この地域は大都市近郊ほどは、宅地開発が進んでいない。

content.content: Housing in this area has not been developed as much as in the suburbs of a big city.
Taking the form XはYほど...ない, it means X is less than Y. For example, in the expression XはYほど大きくない, X is smaller than Y.

While XはYより... indicates a simple comparison of X and Y, in the case of XはYほど...ない, there can be an additional meaning of “X and Y are both ..., but when comparing the two, ....” For example, in the case of

content: , it is understood that this summer is hot, but not as hot as last year.

content.content: b. ...ほど...Nはない

content: 試験ほどいやなものはない。

content.content: There is nothing as unpleasant as exams.

content: いろんな方が親切にして下さいましたが、あなたほど親身になって下さった方は他にありません。

content.content: Many different people have been kind to me, but no one has been as sincere as you.

content: 東京ほど家賃の高いところはない。

content.content: There is no other place where the rent is as expensive as in Tokyo.

content: これほどすばらしい作品は他にありません。

content.content: There is no other work (of art) that is as splendid as this one.

content: 川口さんほどよく勉強する学生はいない。

content.content: There is no other student who studies as hard as Kawaguchi-san.

content: 子供に先立たれることほどつらいことはない。

content.content: There is nothing so heartbreaking as having your own child die before you do.
By stating that there is no comparison, N in Nほど has the highest degree within the comparison. Example

content: means that an examination is the most hateful thing of all. Example
means “You were the kindest.”

content.content: 3. ...ほど〈degree〉a. ...ほど［Nほど］［A-いほど］［V-るほど］

content: この商品はおもしろいほどよく売れる。

content.content: It’s almost funny how well this product is selling!

content: 顔も見たくないほどきらいだ。

content.content: I hate her so much that I can’t even stand to look at her face.

content: 今日は死ぬほど疲れた。

content.content: I was tired to death today!

content: そのニュースをきいて、彼は飛び上がるほど驚いた。

content.content: When he heard the news, he could have jumped up in astonishment.

content: 東京中を足が棒になるほど歩き回ったが、探していた本は見つからなかった。

content.content: I walked around Tokyo until my legs were about to give out, but I didn’t find the book I was looking for.

content: 医者の話では、胃に親指の先ほどの腫瘍があるという。

content.content: According to the doctor, I have a tumor the size of the tip of my thumb in my stomach.

content: それほど言うなら、好きなようにすればいい。

content.content: If you’re going to make such a fuss, do it your own way.

content: なんの連絡もしてこないから、どれほど心配したかわからない。

content.content: You can’t begin to imagine how much I worried about you when there was no contact whatsoever!
Used to explain the degree of the action or state by comparing it to an example N. When N is an indicative これ, それ, あれ or どれ, the meaning is the equivalent of こんなに, そんなに, あんなに or どんなに, respectively.
b. ...ほどだ［Na なほどだ］［A／V　ほどだ］

content: ずいぶん元気になって、昨日なんか外に散歩にでかけたほどです。

content.content: She’s feeling so much better that she even went out for a walk yesterday.

content: 彼は犬がたいへん嫌いだ。道に犬がいれば、わざわざ遠回りするほどだ。

content.content: He cannot stand dogs. If there’s a dog on the street, he’ll take a detour to avoid it.

content: コンサートはたいへんな人気で、立ち見がでるほどだった。

content.content: The concert was so popular that it was finally a case of standing room only.

content: このシャツは着やすいし値段も安いので、とても気に入っている。色違いで3枚も持っているほどだ。

content.content: I really like this shirt because it is so comfortable and the price is right. So much so that I have it in three different colors!

content: 事故後の彼の回復ぶりは、奇跡とも言えるほどだ。

content.content: The recovery he has made after the accident might well be called a miracle.
Used to describe the degree of the thing mentioned by giving concrete examples for comparison.
c. ...ほどの...ではない［...ほどのNではない］［...ほどの　こと／もの　ではない］

content: 医者に行くほどのけがではない。

content.content: It is not an injury that requires medical attention.

content: そんなに深刻に悩むほどの問題ではない。

content.content: It is not such an issue that you should be so agonized over it.

content: そんなに怒るほどのことではない。

content.content: It is not something that’s worth getting so angry about.

content: 確かに便利そうな機械だが、20 万円も出すほどのものではない。

content.content: This machine does seem to be useful, but it is not worth spending 200,000 yen on it.
Indicates that something is “less of a degree... than ....” Implies that this is not something serious or important.
d. ...というほどではない［N／Na　というほどではない］［A／V　というほどではない］

content: 酒は好きだが、毎日飲まないではいられないというほどじゃない。

content.content: I like alcohol, but not to the extent that I need to drink every day.

content: 英語は少し勉強しましたが、通訳ができるというほどではありません。

content.content: I have studied English a little, but I am not good enough to become an interpreter.

content: 数年前から胃を悪くしているが、手術をしなければいけないというほどではない。

content.content: I have been suffering from stomach problems for the past few years, but it is not bad enough to require an operation.

content: A:高級車買ったんだって？

content.content: Did I hear you have bought a deluxe car?
B:いや、高級車というほどじゃないけれど。わりといい車なんだ。
I wouldn’t call it deluxe, but it’s a fairly good car.
Means that the degree of something is not close to what is described by N/Na/A/V. In this expression, a commonly-known example is used as a reference point. For example, as in the case of

content: , being able to interpret requires a high standard of English, so the speaker’s English is not as proficient as that of an interpreter. Similarly, in the case of
, having to have an operation is generally regarded as serious, but the speaker’s condition is not as serious as this.

content.content: 4. ...ほど〈proportional change〉a. ...ほど［N／Na　ほど］［A-いほど］［V-るほど］

content: 年をとるほど体が弱くなる。

content.content: The older one gets the weaker one’s body becomes.

content: 上等のワインは、古くなるほどうまくなる。

content.content: Good wine becomes even better the older it gets.

content: 駅に近いほど家賃は高くなる。

content.content: The closer the property is to the station, the higher the rent.

content: 北へ行くほど寒くなる。

content.content: It gets colder the farther north you go.

content: まじめな人ほどストレスがたまる。

content.content: The more conscientious a person is, the more he or she suffers from stress.

content: 健康に自信がある人ほど、病気になかなか気づかないことが多い。

content.content: People who believe in their own good health often fail to notice that they are ill.

content: 酔うほどに、宴はにぎやかになっていった。

content.content: The drunker people became, the livelier the party got.
As the level of something indicated by V in Vほど increases, something else related to the original V changes proportionately. For example, in the case of

content: , as someone grows older, his body gets weaker. In the case of
, wine that is kept longer improves.

content.content: The structure of ...ほど... Naに／A-く／V-ようになる is often used in stating general knowledge or observation, as in the cases of

content: . Example
uses ...ほどに that is formal and usually used in written language. There are similar expressions such as ...につれて and ...ば...ほど.

content.content: b. ...ば...ほど［N／Na　であればあるほど］［A-ければA-いほど］［V-ばV-るほど］

content: 食べれば食べるほど太る。

content.content: The more you eat the fatter you get.

content: A:どれぐらいのご予算ですか。

content.content: How much is the budget?
B:（安ければ）安いほどいいんですが。
The cheaper the better.

content: 活発で優秀な学生であればあるほど、知識を一方的に与えるような授業はつまらなく感じるのだろう。

content.content: The more active and brighter the student is, the more bored he or she is likely to feel in a class where the teacher simply teaches facts (without soliciting any response).

content: 電気製品というのは、高くなればなるほど、使いにくくなる。

content.content: For electronic goods, the more expensive they are, the more difficult they are to use.

content: どうしたらいいのか、考えれば考えるほどわからなくなってしまった。

content.content: The more I thought about what I should do, the more confused I became.

content: 眠ろうとすればするほど眼が冴えてくる。

content.content: The harder I try to get to sleep the wider awake I become.

content: この説明書は、読めば読むほどわからなくなる。

content.content: The more I read this instruction manual, the more confused I get.
Repeating the same word X (N, A or V), XばXほどY means “the more X, the more Y.” As state X changes over time, state Y changes proportionately to X. As in the cases of examples

content: , the changes in X and Y may be inversely proportionate.

content.content: 【ほどなく】［V-てほどなく］［V-るとほどなく］

content: 祖父が亡くなってほどなく祖母も亡くなった。

content.content: Soon after my grandfather died, my grandmother died, too.

content: 広島と長崎に原爆が落とされてほどなく、第二次世界大戦は終結した。

content.content: Shortly after the atomic bombs were dropped on Hiroshima and Nagasaki, World War II concluded.

content: 新しい社長が就任すると、ほどなく社内で経営側への非難が始まった。

content.content: Shortly after the new company president assumed her position, criticism of the management started in the office.

content: Z社がパソコンを大幅値下げすると、ほどなく他社もそれに追随して値下げを始めた。

content.content: When Company Z dramatically cut the price of their PCs, other companies immediately began to follow suit.
Means “shortly afterwards, soon, before too long.” It is used to describe a past event. It is a formal expression often used in written language. ほどなくして may be used in the place of ほどなく.
【ぽい】

content: 気が短くて怒りっぽい。

content.content: She is short-tempered and gets angry easily.

content: 将来の計画について熱っぽく語っていた。

content.content: He was talking about the plan for the future enthusiastically.
【っぽい】

【まい】Structurally, まい is placed after a Group 1 verb in dictionary form, or a Group 2 verb in either verb stem or dictionary form. As for the Group 3 verbs 来る and する, there are two possibilities each of くるまい／こまい and するまい／すまい, respectively. Of the two, くるまい and するまい are more common in both verbs.
When used with non-verbs, ない becomes あるまい, Nではない becomes Nではあるまい, Naではない  becomes Na ではあるまい, and A-くない becomes A-くあるまい.
Can also be attached to ます to form ますまい.
1. ...まいa. V-まい〈volition〉

content: 酒はもう二度と飲むまい。

content.content: I shall not drink sake ever again.

content: あいつにはもう二度と会うまい。

content.content: I shall not see her ever again.

content: A:佐々木とけんかしたんだって？

content.content: Is it true that you quarreled with Sasaki?
B:そうなんだよ。人が親切で言ってるのに聞こうともしないんだ。あいつにはもう何も言うまいと思っているんだ。
Yes. He wouldn’t listen to me when I was advising him out of kindness. I have made up my mind that I won’t say anything to him anymore.

content: 二日酔いの間はもう二度と飲みすぎるまいと思うが、ついまた飲み過ぎてしまう。

content.content: When I have a hangover I always think that I won’t drink too much ever again, but then I can’t help indulging myself in drinking again.

content: その時、広子は、二度と田中には会うまいと固く決心した。

content.content: Just then, Hiroko firmly made up her mind that she would not see Tanaka ever again.

content: 母を悲しませまいと思ってそのことは知らせずにおいた。

content.content: I kept it secret from my mother so as not to upset her.
Expresses the speaker’s intention of not doing something. In spoken language, V-ないようにしよう and V-ないつもりだ are commonly used. To express someone else’s intention, as in the case of example

content: , ...まいと決心する／思う／考える are used. Example
is in a formal style often found in written language, and it means that the speaker does not want to make his mother upset.

content.content: b. V-まいとする

content: 銃を奪われまいとして争いになった。

content.content: It developed into a fight as both sides tried to keep the gun from being taken by the other.

content: 夏子は泣くまいとして歯を食いしばった。

content.content: Natsuko clenched her teeth to keep herself from crying.

content: 家族の者を心配させまいとする気持ちから、会社をやめたことは言わずにおいた。

content.content: From my desire not to worry my family, I said nothing about the fact that I had left my company.
Means “trying not to do something.” A formal expression often found in writing. When it is used in the form of ...まいとして, して is sometimes omitted.
（例）銃を奪われまいと争いになった。
It developed into a fight as both sides tried to keep the gun from being taken by the other.
2. ...まい〈supposition, conjecture〉

content: このうれしさは他人にはわかるまい。

content.content: I don’t suppose anyone else could understand how happy I feel now.

content: 税金を減らすのに反対する人はまずあるまい。

content.content: I don’t suppose there is anyone who opposes a decrease in taxation.

content: 山田氏の当選はまず間違いあるまい。

content.content: There’s no mistaking that Yamada-shi (Mr. Yamada) will win the election.

content: 年老いた両親も亡くなって、ふるさとにはもうだれもいなくなってしまった。もう二度と訪れることもあるまい。

content.content: Now that both my elderly parents have died, there is nobody waiting for me in my hometown. I don’t think I will be visiting it again.

content: こんな話をしてもだれも信じてはくれまいと思って、今まで黙っていたのです。

content.content: Because I thought no one would believe me even if I tried to explain, I haven’t told anyone about this until now.

content: 顔を見るだけで他人の過去を当てるなんて妙な話だが、これだけ証人がいるのならまんざら嘘でもあるまい。

content.content: Though it is very strange that anyone can tell someone else’s past by just looking at his or her face, with so many attesting to this fact, there could be some truth to it.

content: 他ならぬ松下さんの御依頼ですから、父もまさかいやとは言いますまい。

content.content: Since it is a request from none other than Matsushita-san, I would never have thought that my father would refuse it.

content: 子供が初めて下宿した時には、かぜをひいてはいまいか、一人でさびしがっていはしまいかと心配でならなかった。

content.content: When my child first started living in a boarding house, I was so worried over whether she might catch a cold or feel lonely.
Means that someone will likely not do something. Expresses the speaker’s conjecture. Rarely used in spoken language, as in the case of example

content: . 言わないだろう or 言わないでしょう is more common. However, it may be used in spoken language when it is used in quotations accompanying と思って or と考えて, as in example

content.content: 3. ...でもあるまいa. Nでもあるまい

content: 仕事を紹介して下さる人もあるが、私ももう 70 だ。この歳になって、いまさら会社勤めでもあるまい。

content.content: Some people want to find work for me, but I am already seventy.  At this age, I can’t see starting to work for a company.

content: 自分から家を出ておきながら、今ごろになって、同居でもあるまい。

content.content: He left home on his own a long time ago, so at this point we can hardly expect him to live with his family again.

Indicates that something or an action is not appropriate or befitting the situation. Often used in the form of いまさら／いまごろ、...でもあるまい, indicating that time has passed and it is no longer appropriate for a certain event to take place or to take a certain action.
b. Nでもあるまいし

content: 子供でもあるまいし、自分のことは自分でしなさい。

content.content: You are no longer a child, so take charge of your own things yourself.

content: 学生でもあるまいし、アルバイトはやめて、きちんと勤めなさい。

content.content: You are not a student, so stop working part-time and get a real job.

content: 17 や 18 の小娘でもあるまいし、男に振られたぐらいで、いつまでもくよくよするのはやめなさい。

content.content: You are no longer a girl of seventeen or eighteen, so stop moping on and on just for being dumped by a guy.

Means “because something/someone is not N” or “because something/someone is not supposed to be N.” Often used in conjunction with a prohibitive or imperative form and is often used in scolding or criticizing someone. The form では／じゃあるまいし is also found.
c. V-ることもあるまい

content: あんなにひどい言い方をすることもあるまいに。

content.content: There wasn’t any need for saying it so harshly, was there?

content: あの程度のことで、大の大人が泣くこともあるまい。

content.content: There is no need for a fully grown adult to cry over something so trivial as that.

content: 電話か手紙で用は足りるのだから、わざわざ行くほどのこともあるまい。

content.content: Since the matter can be dealt with by telephone or letter, there is hardly any need for anyone to go there in person.
Used in order to convey the opinion that a certain action is inappropriate or unnecessary. A formal expression often used in written language. In spoken language, V-ることもないだろう is used more often.
4. まいかa. ...ではあるまいか［N／Na　（なの）ではあるまいか］［A／V　のではあるまいか］

content: 彼は若くみえるが、本当はかなりの年輩なのではあるまいか。

content.content: Though he looks young, I wonder if he is in fact quite old.

content: 佐藤さんは知らないふりをしているが、全部わかっているのではあるまいか。

content.content: Though Sato-san is pretending not to know anything, she may in fact know everything.

content: 児童の自殺があいついだのには、現在の教育制度に、何か問題があるのではあるまいか。

content.content: I wonder if there aren’t some problems in the current system of education that have caused this outbreak of children’s suicides.

content: 他人への無関心が、このような事件を引き起こす一因となったのではあるまいか。

content.content: Indifference towards other people may have been one of the factors that caused this incident.

content: 知識のみを偏重してきたことは、現在の入試制度の大きな欠陥ではあるまいか。

content.content: Putting too much emphasis on book-learning alone may be considered as a major defect in the current entrance examination system.

content: 会社や組織のためにのみ働き続ける生活は、誰よりも本人が一番苦しいのではあるまいか。

content.content: For a life that is spent working continuously for a company or organization, it is the person him/herself who probably suffers more than anyone else.
Indicates the speaker’s conjecture ...ではないだろうか (I wonder if it isn’t a case of ...).
When used in conjunction with a noun or na-adjective, takes either of the two forms: N/Naではあるまいか or N/Naなのではあるまいか.
As in the cases

content: through
, often used in introducing the discussion point or in presenting the speaker’s assertion by taking the form of a question to the listener. A formal expression used mainly in written language.

content.content: b. V-てくれまいかV-てもらえまいか

content: 忙しいからと一度は断わったのだが、なんとかやってもらえまいかと何度も頼まれてしかたなく引き受けた。

content.content: I had refused to do it once by saying that I was too busy, but then I gave in and agreed to do it since I was begged so many times.

content: A:例のニューヨーク支店の件だが、支店長として、まず君に行ってもらえまいか。

content.content: About the New York store... I wonder if you would go there first of all as the store manager.
B:かしこまりました。
Yes, I will.
Indicates a request. A masculine, formal expression. In spoken language, either V-てくれ or V-てもらえないだろうか is more common. As in

content: , often used for quoting another person with the forms ...と頼まれた／言われた.

content.content: 5. V-ようがV-まいが→
【よう2】4c
6. V-ようとV-まいと→
【よう2】6c
【まえ】
1. Nのまえに

content: 駅の前に大きなマンションが建った。

content.content: A big apartment building has been built in front of the station.

content: 僕の前に田中が座っていた。

content.content: Tanaka was sitting in front of me.

content: 食事の前に手を洗いましょう。

content.content: Let’s wash our hands before our meal.

content: 授業の前に先生のところへ行くように言われた。

content.content: I was told to go and see the teacher before the class.
Represents a spatial or a chronological relationship. Examples

content: and
show the spatial relationship where N is positioned right in front or ahead of something/someone. In the cases of
and
, it indicates that something takes place before the event N.

content.content: 2. V-るまえに

content: 食事をする前に手を洗いましょう。

content.content: Let’s wash our hands before we eat.

content: 私は、夜寝る前に軽く一杯酒を飲むことにしている。

content.content: I always have a little nightcap before I go to bed.

content: 大学を卒業する前に、一度ゆっくり仲間と旅行でもしてみたい。

content.content: I would love to take a leisurely trip with my friends before I graduate from college.

content: 結婚する前には、大阪の会社に勤めていました。

content.content: Before I got married, I was working for a company in Osaka.

Taking the form of XまえにY, it indicates that the event Y takes place before the event X. Regardless of the tense of the sentence, the verb immediately preceding ...まえに always takes the dictionary form.
（○）食事をする前に手を洗った。
Before eating, we washed our hands.
（×）食事をした前に手を洗った。
Before we ate, we washed our hands.
3. Nをまえに（して）

content: 国会議員のA氏は記者団を前に終始上機嫌だった。

content.content: Congressman A stayed in an upbeat mood in front of the pool of reporters.

content: テーブルの上の書類の山を前に、どうしたらいいのか、途方にくれてしまった。

content.content: Facing the mountain of paperwork on the table, I had absolutely no idea what I should do.

content: 試験を前にして、学生たちは緊張していた。

content.content: As the examination was approaching, students were getting nervous.

content: 首相は出発を前に、記者会見を行う予定。

content.content: Before his departure, the Prime Minister plans to hold a press conference.
Represents a spatial or chronological relationship. Examples

content: and
indicate that something/someone is facing something/someone. In the cases of
and
, an event is just about to take place. For the chronological relationship, it is possible to replace it with ...をひかえて.

content.content: 【まさか】
1. まさか...ないだろう

content: 彼には何度も念を押しておいたから、まさか遅れることはないだろう。

content.content: Since I reminded him so many times, I don’t think he would dare to be late.

content: いくら強いといっても、相手はまだ小学生だ。まさか大の大人が負けるようなことはないだろう。

content.content: However strong his opponent may be, it’s still just an elementary school child. There’s no way a grown adult could lose to him.

content: まさかそんなことはないと思うが念のためにもう一度調べてみよう。

content.content: I don’t think it is possible, but to be sure, I will check it again.

content: あんなに何度も練習したのだから、まさか失敗することはあるまい。

content.content: Since she practiced so many times, a failure is simply unthinkable.

content: A:お金が足りませんが...

content.content: I’m afraid there isn’t enough money....
B:まさかそんなはずはない。
That’s impossible!

content: A:だれが秘密をもらしたんだろう。

content.content: I wonder who leaked the secret.
B:君、まさか僕を疑っているんじゃないだろうね。
Surely you’re not suspecting that it was me!

content: まさか、あなた、あの人と結婚する気じゃないでしょうね。

content.content: Come now, you’re not intending to marry that person, are you?

Negative expressions such as ないだろう, まい, はずはない and わけがない at the ends of sentences express the speaker’s negative thoughts that “something like that cannot happen” or “it cannot be true.” Also, as in the cases of

content: and
, they can express the speaker’s strong doubt when used in the structure まさか...じゃないだろう／でしょうね.

content.content: 2. まさか...とはおもわなかった［まさか N だとはおもわなかった］［まさか Na だとはおもわなかった］［まさか A とはおもわなかった］［まさか V とはおもわなかった］

content: 山田さんが病気で入院しているとは聞いていたが、まさかこんなに悪いとは思わなかった。

content.content: I had heard that Yamada-san was in the hospital, but I had no idea it was this serious.

content: まさか私が優勝できるとは思いませんでした。

content.content: I never thought for a moment that I might win first place.

content: まさか彼があんな冗談を本気にするとは思わなかった。

content.content: I didn’t think he would take such a joke seriously.

content: まさか彼がこんなに早く亡くなるなんて誰も想像していなかった。

content.content: Nobody imagined that he might die so soon.

content: まさかこんな大惨事になるとは誰も予想していなかった。

content.content: No one foresaw a disaster of this magnitude.

content: A:犯人は彼だったよ。

content.content: He was the culprit.
B:まさか。
Impossible!
Accompanying phrases such as とは思わなかった, とは知らなかった express how surprised the speaker is by an unforeseen turn of an event. In spoken language, まさか may be used on its own, as in the case of
3. まさか+否定表現

content: A:あんな失敗をするなんて、あいつは馬鹿じゃないか。もっときつく言ったほうがいいんじゃないですか。

content.content: He must be an idiot to make such a mistake. Shouldn’t you talk to him more strongly ?
B:まさか本人に面と向かって「ばか」とも言えないじゃないか。
I can’t very well tell him to his face that he is an idiot, can I?

content: いくら助けてやりたくても、まさかテストの答えを教えるわけにもいかないし、自力で頑張ってもらうしかない。

content.content: However much I would like to help her, I certainly cannot tell her the answers to the test, so all I can do is leave her to do his best.

By giving an extreme example of an action that the speaker cannot or will not take using the negative potential form V-れる, or other negative expressions such as ともいえない or わけにもいかない, it is used to indicate the speaker’s emotions such as annoyance, irritation, displeasure, frustration, or even despair about the present situation to the extent of contemplating taking such an action.
4. まさかのN

content: 健康には自信があるが、家族のことを考えてまさかの時のために保険に入っている。

content.content: I have no worries about my health, but I do have a life insurance policy in consideration of my family in a worst-case scenario.

content: まさかの場合は、ここに電話してください。

content.content: In case anything unforeseen should happen, please call this number.
Means “in case of emergency, should an unlikely event take place.”
【まさに】This is a formal expression often used in written language. Thus, when used in spoken language, it seems exaggerated or bombastic.
1. まさに

content: 警察に届けられていたのは、まさに私がなくした書類だった。

content.content: The document that had been turned in to the police was the very document that I had lost.

content: その絵は実際の幽霊を描いたものとして有名で、その姿にはまさに鬼気迫るものがある。

content.content: The painting is famous for depicting real ghosts, and the figures in it are truly eerie.

content: 《領収書》金十万円正に受領致しました。

content.content: 《receipt》Receipt of the sum of 100,000 yen is acknowledged.

content: A:日本政府のはっきりしない態度が、アジア諸国との関係を悪化させているのではないか。

content.content: I wonder if the ambiguous stance of the Japanese government isn’t harming its relationships with other Asian countries.
B:まさにそのとおりだ。
I am sure that is the case.

content: この夏、「世界リゾート博」を訪れた人は 113 万人を超えた。同博宣伝部長のS氏は「晴天続きのまさにリゾート日和でした。」とほくほく顔だった。

content.content: This summer, the number of people who went to the World Resort Expo surpassed 1,130,
0. The Expo marketing manager, S-shi (Mr. S) congratulated himself by saying, “The stretch of fine weather was perfect for a resort lifestyle.”
Means “certainly” or “truly.”
2. まさに...V-ようとしている（ところだ）

content: 私が到着した時、会議はまさに始まろうとしているところだった。

content.content: When I arrived, the meeting was just about to start.

content: 《テレビ中継放送》今まさに世紀の祭典オリンピックが始まろうとしております。

content.content: 《TV remote broadcasting》The ceremony of the century, the Olympic Games, is about to start now.

content: ハイジャックの犯人をのせた飛行機は警察が包囲する中、今まさに飛び立とうとしている。

content.content: The airplane with the hijackers aboard is attempting to take off with the police surrounding it.

content: 彼らが駅に到着した時、列車はまさに動きださんとしているところだった。

content.content: When they arrived at the station, the train was just about to leave.
Means “(something) is going to take place any time now” or “(something) is about to start now.” When a more formal expression is required, it may be used together with “V-んとしている,” as shown in example
【まして】
1. まして（や）

content: 日本語の勉強を始めて3年になるが、まだ新聞を読むのも難しい。まして古典などはとても読めない。

content.content: It has been three years since I started learning Japanese, but it is hard enough reading newspapers, let alone the classics.

content: この辺りは昼でも人通りが少ない。まして夜ともなると、怖くて一人では歩けない。

content.content: There are very few people who pass through this area even during the day. It goes without saying that at night I would be too scared to walk about on my own.

content: 僕にでもできた仕事だ。まして君のような優秀な人間にできないはずはない。

content.content: Even I could have done this job. There is no reason why such an able person as you can’t do it.

content: 家族の死は常に悲しい。まして、子供の死ともなれば、残された者の嘆きは、いかばかりであろうか。

content.content: A death in the family is always sad. And when it is the death of a child, how absolutely devastating it must be for the surviving family.

Often used in the patterns Xは...ましてYは... or Xでも...ましてYは.... Comparing X with Y, which possesses the quality used to describe X to an even greater extent, it means “as even X is (descriptive expression), Y is of course even more so.” ましてや is a rather formal expression that has the tone of written language.
2. Nにもまして

content: 日本の夏は暑い。しかし、暑さにもまして耐えがたいのは、湿度の高さだ。

content.content: Japanese summers are hot. However, what’s even harder to bear than the heat is the high level of humidity.

content: 本当にいい映画だった。映像の美しさはもちろんだが、それにもまして音楽がすばらしかった。

content.content: It really was a good movie. The images were beautiful, of course, but the music was even more wonderful.

content: 彼はもともとまじめでよく働く人間だが、子どもが生まれてからというもの、以前にもましてよく働くようになった。

content.content: By nature he’s a hardworking person, but since his children were born, he works even harder than before.

content: 何にもましてうれしかったのは、友人の加藤君と 10 年ぶりに再会できたことだった。

content.content: What made me happier than anything else was meeting my friend Kato-kun again for the first time in ten years.

Used in the patterns Xにもまして...なのはYだ, XにもましてYが... etc., means “X is of course (descriptive expression) but Y is more so.” By comparing Y to X, the expression emphasizes the high degree to which Y possesses the quality discussed. As in the case of

content: , when used in the form 前にもまして or 以前にもまして it means “still (even) more than before.” As in the case of
, 何にもまして means “more than anything,” “the most.”

content.content: 【まじき】→
【あるまじき...だ】
【まず】
1. まず

content: まずはじめに、本日の予定をお知らせいたします。

content.content: First, please let me inform you of today’s schedule.

content: 《司会者の発言》次にみなさんのご意見をお伺いしたいと思います。では、まず川口さんからお願いします。

content.content: 《Chairperson’s speech》Next I propose to hear everyone’s opinion. So then, I shall ask Kawaguchi-san to speak first.

content: 今年の夏は暑いらしいから、ボーナスが入ったら、まずクーラーを買おうと思っている。

content.content: Since they say this summer will be hot, when I get my bonus, I’m thinking the first thing I’ll do is buy an air conditioner.

content: 日本の年中行事として、まず盆と正月が挙げられる。

content.content: As for Japan’s annual events, the Bon Festival and the New Year are the first to mention.

content: その国の文化を知るには、まず言葉からだ。

content.content: To understand that country’s culture, you have to start with learning the language.
Expresses the meaning “at the beginning” or “to begin with.” Examples

content: and
mean “setting other things aside” or “before everything else.”

content.content: 2. まずは

content: まずは一安心した。

content.content: My first reaction was one of relief.

content: 《手紙》まずはご報告まで。

content.content: 《in a letter》This first is just for your information.

content: 《手紙》取り急ぎ、まずはお礼まで。

content.content: 《in a letter》I wanted to express my thanks as soon as possible.

content: 《手紙》まずは用件のみにて、失礼いたします。

content.content: 《in a letter》Please accept my apologies for the business-like nature of this letter.

Means “not completely, but largely” or “not enough (sufficiently) but for the time being (all that is possible).” Phrases such as まずはほっとした (feel relieved for now) and まずはよかった (good outcome for now), similar to that used in

content: , can also be expressed using set phrases such as なにはともあれ and とにかく.
are idiomatic expressions used to conclude letters.

content.content: 3. まず　...だろう／...まい

content: 患者: もう、普通の生活に戻っても大丈夫でしょうか。

content.content: Patient:Will it be all right if I return to my daily routine now?
医者: そうですね。無理さえしなければ、まず大丈夫でしょう。
Doctor:Yes. So long as you don’t overdo things, I should say you will be fine.

content: 予算は十分にあるから、足りなくなることはまずないだろう。

content.content: As we have an ample budget, I doubt we will run out.

content: 山田氏の当選はまず間違いあるまい。

content.content: I have no doubts that Yamada-shi (Ms. Yamada) will win the election.

content: この怪我ではまず助かるまい。

content.content: I doubt she can survive this injury.

content: この案に反対する人はまずいない。

content.content: I am sure there is no one who would oppose this plan.

content: 彼が一度「だめだ」と言ったら、もう可能性はないと思ってまず間違いない。

content.content: Once he has said “no,” I am certain that there is no possibility.

Used together with phrases such as だろう and まい, expresses the relative certainty of the speaker’s conjecture. まず...まい is a formal, written expression, meaning “I doubt that...” or “I think it unlikely that....” Examples which do not use だろう, such as

content: and
, demonstrate the even stronger conviction of the speaker.

content.content: 【また】
1. またa. また〈repetition〉

content: また、飛行機が落ちたらしい。

content.content: It seems that another plane has crashed.

content: 同じ問題をまた間違えた。

content.content: I got the same question wrong again.

content: A:すみません。来週の金曜日、休ませていただきたいのですが。

content.content: Excuse me. If possible I’d take like to take a day off next Friday.
B:またですか。先週も休んだでしょう。
Again? You took it off last week, too, didn’t you?

content: A:さようなら、また来てくださいね。

content.content: Goodbye. Please come again, OK?
B:有難うございます。また、おじゃまします。
Thank you very much. I would love to come again.

content: 《授業の終わりに》では、また来週。

content.content: 《at the end of a class》Well, see you again next week.

content: A:じゃ、また。

content.content: Okay, see you again.
B:じゃあね。
See you!
Demonstrates the repeated occurrence of the same thing. As in

content: , it is also used as a parting salutation.

content.content: b. また〈adjunction〉

content: 教科書は、大学生協で購入できる。また、大きな書店でも販売している。

content.content: You can purchase the textbook at the university cooperative. It is also sold at large bookstores.

content: 10 月から大手私鉄の運賃が平均 20 ％値上げされる。また、地下鉄、市バスも来年4月に値上げを予定している。

content.content: Beginning in October, the major private railway companies will raise their fares by an average of 20%. Moreover, there are also plans to raise subway and city bus fares starting in April of next year.

content: 《テレビのニュースで》現在、新幹線は京都神戸間が不通になっております。また、在来線は大阪神戸間が不通となっております。

content.content: 《television news》The shinkansen (bullet train) service between Kyoto and Kobe is currently suspended. Additionally, service on all other railway lines between Osaka and Kobe has also been suspended.

content: 《テレビのニュースで》天皇皇后両陛下の韓国御訪問は、10 月と決まりました。また、首席随行員は渡辺外相が務めます。

content.content: 《television news》The visit of Their Majesties, the Emperor and Empress, to Korea has been arranged for October. Furthermore, Foreign Minister Watanabe will serve as their chief attendant.
Used to give further explanation or to add new information in connection to a matter already related.
c. また〈list〉

content: 彼は良き父であり、また良き夫でもある。

content.content: He is a good father and also a good husband.

content: この本はおもしろく、またためになる。

content.content: This book is interesting and also educational.

content: 喫煙は健康に悪いし、また、周囲の迷惑にもなる。

content.content: Smoking is bad for your health and also a nuisance to those around you.
Means “in addition...” or “moreover....” Used to list similar matters or information. Often used in the form また...も.
d. また〈choice〉

content: 参加してもよい。また、参加しなくてもよい。

content.content: It’s okay if you participate. It’s also okay if you don’t.

content: 黒か青のインクで書くこと。また、パソコンの使用も可。

content.content: Write in black or blue ink. Alternatively, it is also acceptable to use a personal computer.
Means “one of two (options).” Often used in the form また...も.
2. ...もまた［Nもまた］［Na なのもまた］［A／V　のもまた］

content: 山でのキャンプ生活は電気もガスもないが、不便なのもまた楽しい。

content.content: When camping in the mountains there is no electricity or gas, but there’s also something fun about the inconvenience.

content: 暑いのも困るが寒いのもまたたいへんだ。

content.content: The heat is troublesome but the cold is just as much a problem.

content: 晴れた日の散歩は楽しい。しかし、雨にぬれながら歩くのもまた風情があっていいものだ。

content.content: A walk on a clear day is enjoyable. However, walking while getting wet in the rain also has its attractions.

content: 天才といえども、彼もまた人の子だ。うれしいときもあれば悲しいときもある。

content.content: A genius though he is, he is also human. He has both happy times and sad times.
Means “in the same way,” or “just as.” As in

content: , it introduces a thing which is similar to that previously related. In the case of
it means “even a genius like him is the same as normal people.”
いったいまたどうしてそんなことを。

content.content: Why (on earth) would you do that kind of thing?

content: どうしてまた、こんなことになったのだろうか。

content.content: Why (on earth) has this kind of thing happened?

content: しかしよくまた、こんなことができたものだ。
