content.content: It is amazing how anyone could have done such a thing!

content: これはまたきれいな絵ですね。

content.content: This is such a beautiful picture, isn’t it?
When used together with phrases such as いったい, どうして, and これは, shows the speaker’s feeling of surprise or wonder.
4. またのN

content: またのお越しをお待ちしております。

content.content: We look forward to serving you again.

content: きょうは忙しいので、この話はまたの機会にお願いします。

content.content: Since today is very busy, I would like to discuss this matter at some other opportunity.

content: 彼は医者だが、またの名を北山淳といって有名な小説家でもある。

content.content: He is a doctor but he is also a famous novelist by the name of Kitayama Jun.
Means “the next” or “another” (occasion). Examples

content: and
are common set phrases limited to use with nouns such as “another opportunity/chance/time/day/name.” またの名を...という in
means “(his) other name is.../also known as....”

content.content: 5. NまたN

content: 一行は、山また山の奥地に進んで行った。

content.content: The party proceeded into the mountainous interior.

content: 残業また残業で休む暇もない。

content.content: I have no time to rest because I am constantly working overtime.

content: 人また人で歩くこともできない。

content.content: With people on top of people, it’s impossible to walk.
By repeating the same noun, demonstrates a situation in which the same things form a series/chain or a situation in which the same thing continues.
【またしても】

content: またしても空の事故が起こった。

content.content: There has been another air traffic accident.

content: またしてもあいつにしてやられた。

content.content: Once again, I’ve been outmaneuvered by him.

content: 《高校野球の実況中継で》平安高校、またしてもホームランを打ちました！

content.content: 《in a high school baseball live broadcast》Heian High School has hit a home run once again!
Used in cases where the speaker expresses his surprise that the same thing continues to happen or is repeated. As in examples

content: and

, it is often used in reference to a negative occurrence. The expression emphasizes the また but, as its tone is quite serious, it is often used in writing, on television or radio news or commentaries. In everyday conversation また is more commonly used.

content.content: 【または】［NまたはN］

content: 黒か青のペンまたはえんぴつで書いてください。

content.content: Please write with either a black or a blue pen or, alternatively, in pencil.

content: 13 日までに到着するように郵送するか、または、持参してください。

content.content: Please mail it so that it arrives by the 13th or, alternatively, bring it with you.

content: 400 字詰め原稿用紙に手書き、またはA4の用紙にタイプすること。

content.content: Either handwrite it on 400-character manuscript paper or, alternatively, type it on A4 paper.
Demonstrates that either of two options is acceptable. In example

content: , it doesn’t matter whether a pen or a pencil is used, while in
it is acceptable to either mail or bring the object. This is a written expression and is often used when giving instructions.

content.content: 【またもや】

content: またもや、彼が登場した。

content.content: He appeared (on stage) once again.

content: またもや人為的なミスによる飛行機事故が起きたことは、看過できない問題である。

content.content: That an air traffic accident has been caused by human error once again is a problem which cannot be ignored.

content: またもや、汚職事件が発覚した。

content.content: Once again, a corruption scandal has come to light.
Means また、またしても. Indicates that the same thing has continued to occur.  Its tone is a little outdated and so また and またしても are more commonly used. またも can also be used.  It is mainly used in writing.
【まだ】
1. まだ...ない

content: A:昼ご飯は、もう食べましたか。

content.content: Have you already eaten lunch?
B:いいえ、まだ食べていません。
No, I haven’t eaten yet.

content: A:この本は、もう読みましたか。

content.content: Have you read this book already?
B:いいえ、まだです。
No, not yet.

content: 事故の原因は、まだわかっていない。

content.content: The cause of the accident is still unknown.

content: 子:お母さん、ご飯まだ？

content.content: Child:Mom, is dinner ready yet?
母:もうちょっと待ってね。
Mother: Wait a little while longer.

content: 風邪はまだよくならない。

content.content: My cold is still not better.

content: その時はまだ何が起こったのかわからなかった。

content.content: At that time I still did not know what had happened.

content: 外国には、まだ一度も行ったことがない。

content.content: I have not yet been abroad even once.
Shows that something that had been planned or was expected to happen has not happened as yet, or is not completed.

The phrase いいえ、まだ...ていません (no, not yet done) is often used as the negative response to もう...ましたか (done yet?) questions. いいえ、まだです (not yet done) can also be used.  If いいえ、まだ...ません (no, not yet V) is used, it may be interpreted that the speaker has no intention of doing so and therefore there are situations in which this is inappropriate.
（×）A:昼ごはんはもう食べましたか。
Have you had your lunch yet?
B:いいえ、まだ食べません。
No, I’m not going to yet.
2. まだ〈continuation from the past〉

content: A:敏子は何をしているの？

content.content: What is Toshiko doing?
B:おねえちゃんは、まだ電話をしているよ。
My sister’s still on the telephone.

content: もう一週間になるのに、父と母はまだけんかをしている。

content.content: Even though it’s been a week, Dad and Mom are still fighting.

content: 子どもの時に大きな地震があった。あの時のことは、今でもまだはっきりと覚えている。

content.content: When I was a child there was a big earthquake. Even now, I remember that day clearly.

content: 今年になっても、日本の経済はまだ低迷を続けている。

content.content: Even this year, the Japanese economy is still sluggish.

content: A:昔、みんなで温泉に行ったことがあったね。

content.content: A long time ago we all went to a hot spring together, didn’t we?
B:ああ、まだおじいさんが生きていたころだね。
Ah, that was when Grandfather was still alive.

content: 昔と違って、 60 代といってもまだ若い。

content.content: Unlike in the past, people in their sixties are still young.

content: 9月なのにまだ暑い。

content.content: Even though it’s September, it’s still hot.

content: さなえちゃんは偉そうなことを言ってても、まだ子供だねえ。

content.content: Sanae-chan may talk big, but she is still a child.

content: まだ未成年なのに酒を飲んではいけない。

content.content: As you are still a minor, you must not drink alcohol.
Often used in the form まだV-ている, demonstrates a continuous condition or situation. When used in the form まだV-ていた, as in example

content: , demonstrates a point in the past at which a certain condition or situation continued and which differs from the present. Therefore,
means “He is not alive now, but he was still living then.” In examples
the same condition as in the past continues in the present and a lack of progression to the expected natural next stage or condition is emphasized. In
, although summer has passed and it should be a pleasantly cooler time, it is not. Example
means that she has not become an adult. Example
means that you have not yet reached the age at which it is permissible to drink alcohol.

content.content: 3. まだ〈continuation into the future〉

content: これから、まだもっと寒くなる。

content.content: From now on it will become even colder.

content: 雨は、まだ二、三日続くだろう。

content.content: This rain will probably continue for another two or three days yet.

content: 景気はまだ当分よくならないと思われる。

content.content: It is thought that business is unlikely to improve for the time being.

content: まだこの株は値上がりする。

content.content: This stock will continue to increase in value.

content: まだまだこれからが大変ですよ。

content.content: From now on it will become even more serious.

Demonstrates that the present condition or situation will continue into the future also. When まだまだ is used it means “even more” or “yet more” and shows that a condition or situation continues to a higher level or for a longer period of time. まだまだ cannot be used when, as in example

content: , a specified time period such as “two or three days” or “three days” is given.

content.content: 4. まだ...ある

content: 開演までには、まだ時間がある。

content.content: There is still some time until the start (of a play or concert).

content: 目的地まで、まだ 20 キロはある。

content.content: There are still twenty kilometers to our destination.

content: 食糧はまだ三日分ほど残っている。

content.content: We still have about three days’ worth of food left.

content: まだ他にも話したいことがある。

content.content: There are still other things I would like to discuss.
Expresses that a thing or time is left or remaining.
5. まだ〈time lapse〉

content: まだ一時間しかたっていない。

content.content: Still only one hour has passed.

content: 日本にきて、まだ半年だ。

content.content: It has only been half a year since I came to Japan.

content: まだ 10 分ほどしか勉強していないのに、もう眠くなってきた。

content.content: Even though I have been studying for only about ten minutes, I have already become sleepy.

content: 震災からまだ一年にしかならないのに、街の復興はめざましい。

content.content: Even though it is only one year since the earthquake, the town’s reconstruction is remarkable.

content: もう夕方かとおもったが、まだ3時だ。

content.content: I thought it was already evening but it is still only three o’clock.
In conjunction with time expressions, used to emphasize that only a little time has passed since a particular occurrence or event.
6. まだ〈comparison〉

content: 何日もかかって、長いレポートを書かされるよりは、一日ですむ試験の方がまだいい。

content.content: An exam that can be finished in one day is still better than being made to write a long report that takes days.

content: 家事はみんな嫌いだが、掃除よりも洗濯の方が、まだましだ。

content.content: Everyone hates housework, but doing the laundry is at least not as bad as cleaning.

content: A:ああ、いやだ。試験が5つもある。

content.content: Oh, it’s terrible. I have five exams!
B:君なんか、まだましな方だよ。僕なんか、11もあるよ。
You are luckier than some. I have eleven!

content: 今度の地震で家も財産もなくしたが、命があっただけ、まだ救われる。

content.content: I lost both my home and my fortune in this earthquake, but I’m just glad to be alive.
When used in forms such as まだいい and まだましだ this expresses that neither of two things is good but that one is a little preferable to the other.
【まったく】
1. まったく...ない

content: きのうのクラスはまったくおもしろくなかった。

content.content: Yesterday’s class was not at all interesting.

content: 彼は家ではまったく勉強をしない。

content.content: He does not study at all at home.

content: この一週間全く雨が降っていない。

content.content: It hasn’t rained at all this week.

content: その選手のフォームは全く文句のつけようのない美しさだ。

content.content: The beauty of that player’s form cannot be criticized.

content: そのバイオリニストのアルバムは、デビューアルバムとしては全く申し分のない出来である。

content.content: One cannot say anything bad about that violinist’s album as a debut album.

Used to emphasize the negative meaning. It is more formal than ぜんぜん, すこしも and ちっとも, etc. In order to intensify phrases such as 文句のつけようがない, 申し分のない, and 非の打ち所がない, etc., it is difficult to use any expression other than まったく.
2. まったく

content: これとこれはまったく同じものです。

content.content: This and this are entirely the same.

content: それとこれとはまったくちがう話だ。

content.content: That and this are completely different conversations.

content: まったくいやな雨だなあ。

content.content: This rain is so unpleasant.

content: またお金わすれたの？　まったくこまった人ね。

content.content: You forgot your money again?  You really are impossible.

content: A:うっとうしい天気だね。

content.content: What miserable weather!
B:まったくだ。
You said it!

content: きのうの演奏は全くすばらしいものだった。

content.content: Yesterday’s performance was absolutely wonderful.
Used to emphasize the extent of something. In example

content: it is used to give strong affirmation in response to what the other person has said.

content.content: 【まで】
1. NからNまで

content: シンポジウムは1時から3時まで第3会場で行います。

content.content: The symposium will be held from one o’clock until three o’clock in venue number three.

content: A:大阪から東京までどのぐらいかかりますか。

content.content: Approximately how long does it take from Osaka to Tokyo?
B:新幹線なら3時間ぐらいでしょう。
If you take the shinkansen (bullet train) it will take about three hours.

content: 《ホテルで》

content.content: 《at a hotel》
A:シングルでいくらですか。
How much is a single?
B:シングルのお部屋は、7500 円から 12000 円までとなっております。
A single room costs from 7,500 yen up to 12,000 yen.

content: 教科書の 25 頁から 35 頁まで読んでおいてください。

content.content: Please read from page 25 to page 35 of the textbook in advance.

content: この映画は、子供からお年寄りまでご家族みんなで楽しんで頂けます。

content.content: This film can be enjoyed by all the family together, from children to the elderly.

content: A:昼休みは何時までですか。

content.content: Until what time is lunch break?
B:1時までです。
Until one o’clock.
Used with nouns of time, place, or quantity to indicate a range or span. When it is not necessary to state the starting point, Nまで can be used by itself.
2. Nまで〈destination〉

content: バスに乗らずに駅まで歩いて行くことにした。

content.content: I decided to walk to the station without taking the bus.

content: 公園まで走りましょう。

content.content: Let’s run to the park.

content: 毎日学校まで歩きます。

content.content: I walk to school every day.

content: 川幅が広くて向こう岸まで泳げそうもない。

content.content: The river is so wide it’s probably impossible to swim to the other side.

content: 先週の日曜日は、散歩がてら隣の町まで行ってみた。

content.content: Last Sunday I went out for a walk to the neighboring town.

content: A:京都にはどうやって行ったらいいですか。

content.content: What would be a good way to get to Kyoto?
B:そうですねえ。山手線で東京駅まで行って、新幹線に乗るのが一番早いと思いますよ。
Hmm.  I think the quickest way is to go to Tokyo Station on the Yamanote Line and then take the shinkansen (bullet train).

content: わからないことがありましたら、係までおたずね下さい。

content.content: If there is something you don’t understand, please ask the person on duty.

Used with verbs such as 行く, 来る, 歩く, 走る, 泳ぐ and so on, expresses where the movement ends. Verbs such as 歩く, 走る, 泳ぐ and the like cannot be directly attached to に and へ, but they can be used together with まで.
（○）公園まで走りましょう。
Let’s run to the park.
（×）公園｛に／へ｝走りましょう。
Let’s run to the park.
（○）毎日学校まで歩きます。
I walk to school every day.
（×）毎日学校｛に／へ｝歩きます。
I walk to school every day.
（○）向こう岸まで泳いだ。
I swam to the other side.
（×）向こう岸｛に／へ｝泳いだ。
I swam to the other side.
Also, as can be understood from the next examples, as まで demonstrates the place at which continuing movement ends, it cannot be used when referring to two places at the same time.
（○）イタリアではローマとミラノ｛に／へ｝行った。
In Italy, I went to Rome and Milan.
（×）イタリアではローマとミラノまで行った。
In Italy, I went to Rome and Milan.
係まで in

content: has the same meaning as 係に, but its tone is more formal.

content.content: 3. ...まで〈time〉a. Nまで

content: 3時まで勉強します。

content.content: I will study until three o’clock.

content: きのうは結局朝方まで飲んでいた。

content.content: Yesterday I ended up drinking till the wee hours.

content: 私はなまけもので、日曜日はもちろん普通の日でも、たいてい11 時頃まで寝ている。

content.content: I am a lazy person, so not only on Sundays but also on ordinary days I usually sleep until about eleven o’clock.

content: ついこのあいだまでセーターを着ていたのに、この二三日急に暖かくなった。

content.content: Even though I was wearing a sweater until just the other day, these last two or three days it has suddenly become warm.

content: 祖父は死ぬ直前まで意識がはっきりしていた。

content.content: My grandfather was conscious until just before he died.

Attached to a time noun, this indicates that an action or occurrence continued up until the point in time denoted by まで. After it, expressions which demonstrate the continuation of an action or situation are used. It cannot be used with expressions which demonstrate the occurrence of an event.
（×）5時まで到着します。
We will arrive by five o’clock.
（○）5時までに到着します。
We will arrive by five o’clock.
Please see the entry for までに regarding the difference between まで and までに.
b. V-るまで

content: あなたが帰ってくるまで、いつまでも待っています。

content.content: I will wait forever until you return.

content: 私がいいと言うまで目をつぶっていてください。

content.content: Please keep your eyes closed until I say it’s OK.

content: 辻さんは結婚して退職するまで、貿易会社に勤めていたそうだ。

content.content: I heard that Tsuji-san had been working at a trading company until she got married and resigned.

content: 《医者が患者に》もう少し暖かくなるまで外出はしないほうがいいでしょう。

content.content: 《a doctor to a patient》It is best that you don’t go out until it has gotten a little warmer.

content: 佐藤さんが会社を辞めるなんて、昨日山田さんに聞くまで知りませんでした。

content.content: I didn’t know that Sato-san would be leaving the company until I heard it from Yamada-san yesterday.

content: 肉がやわらかくなるまで、中火で煮ます。

content.content: Cook the meat over medium heat until it becomes tender.
Attached to a clause which includes an event, signifies the continuation of an action or situation until that event occurs. As in example

content: , it is often used when explaining a procedure or process and here instructs one to stop boiling the meat at the stage where it has become tender after being cooked over medium heat.

content.content: 4. ...まで〈degree〉a. Nまで

content: 近頃は子供ばかりか、いい年をしたおとなまでマンガを読んでいる。

content.content: These days, not only children but even fully grown-up adults read manga.

content: きみまでそんなことを言うのか。

content.content: Even you say such a thing?

content: 一番信頼していた部下までが、彼を裏切った。

content.content: Even his most trusted subordinate betrayed him.

content: 子供にまでばかにされている。

content.content: Even children make fun of me.

content: そんなつまらないものまで買うんですか。

content.content: Are you going to buy even such a worthless thing?

content: 落ちぶれた身には、風までが冷たい。

content.content: To a man who has fallen so low, even the wind seems cold and unfeeling.

content: だんだん暗くなって来るのにさがしている家は見つからない。その上、雨まで降ってきた。

content.content: It is getting dark and we still can’t find the house we are looking for. On top of that, it has even started to rain.

content: 今年はいいことばかりだ。新しい家に引っ越したし、子供も生まれた。その上、宝くじまで当たった。

content.content: This year has brought only good things. We moved to a new house and had a baby. On top of that, we even won the lottery.

content: 私にも悪い点はあるが、そこまで言われたら、黙ってはいられない。

content.content: I admit that I have my own bad points, but if you are going to say that much, I can’t keep quiet any more.

content: 生活に困って盗みまでするようになった。

content.content: I was so hard up that it led me to stealing.
Used to convey the speaker’s surprise when describing a situation in which something beyond the usual in addition to the usual things has happened. Example

content: , for example, means “Usually manga are read by children. However, these days, not only children but also adults are reading them.” Example
means “It was bad enough that it was getting dark, but the fact that it started raining made the situation even worse.” Example
expresses, conversely, that on top of a good thing, an even better thing has happened. As in 子供にまで in example
, this expression can take the pattern N + particle + まで.

content.content: b. V-るまでになる

content: 苦労の甲斐あって、やっと日本語で論文が書けるまでになった。

content.content: His efforts have paid off and he has progressed to where he can finally write an essay in Japanese.

content: 人工飼育されていたひなは、ひとりで餌がとれるまでに成長した。

content.content: The hand-reared chick has grown enough to be able to get food by itself.

content: リハビリの結果、ひじを曲げられるまでになった。

content.content: As a result of rehabilitation, I have improved to where I can now bend my elbow.

In addition to なる, can be used together with verbs that show change such as  成長する, 育つ, 回復する, and 進歩する. Expresses how the current effect or situation has been reached after a long period of time or through effort. It is often used to express the outcome of striving to achieve something.
c. V-るまで（のこと）もない

content: この程度の風邪なら、医者に行くまでのこともない。うまいものを食べて、一日ぐっすり眠れば治る。

content.content: If your cold is no worse than this, there is no need to go to the doctor. You will recover if you eat tasty things and sleep soundly for one day.

content: その程度の用事ならわざわざ出向くまでもない。電話でじゅうぶんだ。

content.content: You don’t need to make a point of going out to do that kind of errand. It’s enough to do it by telephone.

content: 皆さんよく御存知のことですから、わざわざ説明するまでもないでしょう。

content.content: It’s something you all know well, so I don’t think there’s a need for me to give any particular explanation.

content: 改めてご紹介するまでもありませんが、山本先生は世界的に有名な建築家でいらっしゃいます。

content.content: There’s no need for me to introduce him again, but Yamamoto-sensei is an internationally famous architect.

content: 田中先生は、御専門の物理学は言うまでもなく、平和運動の推進者としてたいへん有名であります。

content.content: I don’t need to tell you that Tanaka-sensei’s specialty is physics, and he is very famous as a promoter of the peace movement.

content: 子供の頃、兄が大事にしていた万年筆を持ちだしてなくしてしまったことがある。後でひどく怒られたことは言うまでもない。

content.content: When I was a child I took a fountain pen that was very important to my older brother and lost it. It goes without saying that he was very angry with me afterwards.
Means “it is not necessary to do....” Can be used in cases where, as in examples

content: and
, “as the degree to which something is the case is so slight, it is unnecessary to do... / it is okay not to do....” Can also be used, as in examples
to
, in cases where “as something is a matter of course, it is unnecessary to do....” In example
, it means “of course, afterwards he was angry with me.”

content.content: d. ...までして［Nまでして］［V-てまで］

content: 色々ほしいものはあるが、借金までして買いたいとは思わない。

content.content: There are many things I want but not to the extent that I would take out a loan to buy them.

content: 徹夜までしてがんばったのに、テストでいい点が取れなかった。

content.content: Even though I made the effort to study all night, I still didn’t get a good score on the test.

content: 彼が自殺までして守りたかった秘密というのは何だろう。

content.content: I wonder what secret he wanted to hide so much that he chose to commit suicide for it.

content: 彼は、友だちを騙してまで、出世したいのだろうか。

content.content: I wonder if he wants to succeed even to the extent that he would cheat his friends.

content: 自然を破壊してまで、山の中に新しい道路をつくる必要はない。

content.content: It is not necessary to go so far as to destroy nature just to build new roads in the mountains.
Used with phrases that express extremities, this means “to do such a thing as....”  As in examples

content: and

, it is used to express criticism of methods of which the speaker does not approve used to achieve an aim. It is often used in such contexts as “It is not good to take such steps in order to...” or “(I) wouldn’t want to do such a thing in order to....” It can also be used, as in examples
and
, to mean, “to have made greater efforts than usual” or “to have made tremendous sacrifices to reach a goal.”

content.content: 5. ...までだa. V-るまで（のこと）だ

content: 父があくまで反対するなら、家を出るまでのことだ。

content.content: If my father opposes it to the end, it is something I will leave home for.

content: もし入学試験に失敗しても、私はあきらめない。もう一年がんばるまでのことだ。

content.content: Even if I fail the entrance exam, I won’t give up. It is something I’ll work hard for another year for.
Shows the speaker’s determination “not to be discouraged, even if the current method is no good, and to try another way.”
b. V-たまで（のこと）だ

content: そんなに怒ることはない。本当のことを言ったまでだ。

content.content: You don’t have to be so angry. I only spoke the truth.

content: 妻:どうして子供たちに結婚する前の話なんかしたんですか。

content.content: Wife: Why did you talk about us before we were married in front of the children?
夫:聞かれたから答えたまでで、別に深い意味はないよ。
Husband: I only told them because they asked. There wasn’t any particular reason.
Expresses that the speaker has carried out a certain action without an ulterior motive or agenda and simply for the reason given.
c. これ／それ　までだ

content: いくらお金を貯めても、死んでしまえばそれまでだから、生きているうちに楽しんだ方がいい。

content.content: However much money you save, you can’t take it with you when you die, so it’s better to enjoy it while you’re alive.

content: 運がよかったと言ってしまえばそれまでだが、彼があの若さで成功したのにはそれなりの理由がある。

content.content: You could just say he was lucky, but there must be a reason why he was successful at such a young age.

content: もはや、これまでだ。

content.content: No more—I’ve had it.
Used in the form V-ば、それまでだ, means “that is the end.” Also, as in example

content: , it is used idiomatically at times when the speaker has found him/herself in a desperate situation or facing a dilemma.

content.content: 6. V-ないまでも

content: 喜びはしないまでも、いやがりはしないだろう。

content.content: I wouldn’t go so far as to say she would delight in it, but she wouldn’t hate it, either.

content: 優勝とは言わないまでも、ベスト4ぐらいはねらいたい。

content.content: I wouldn’t go so far as to say I want to win, but I’m aiming at being somewhere around the top four.
【ないまでも】
【までに】［Nまでに］［V-るまでに］

content: レポートは来週の木曜日までに提出して下さい。

content.content: Please submit your report by Thursday of next week.

content: 何時までに伺えばよろしいですか。

content.content: What time should I be there by?

content: 明日までにこの仕事を済ませてしまいたい。

content.content: I want to get this job finished by tomorrow.

content: 夏休みが終わるまでにこの本を読んでしまいたい。

content.content: I want to finish reading this book by the end of summer vacation.

Attached to nouns of time or clauses which show events, expresses the time frame or deadline of an action. When an expression which shows an action or function comes after this phrase, it shows that the action or function will take place at a point in time before the given time period or deadline.

...まで...する shows that an action or situation continues until a certain point in time, but ...までに...する does not denote continuity and demonstrates the occurrence of a certain event. Therefore, phrases expressing continuity cannot be used after ...までに.
（×）5時までにここで待っています。
I will be waiting here until five o’clock.
（○）5時までここで待っています。
I will be waiting here until five o’clock.
Apart from demonstrating time frames, there is an idiom 参考までに that is used in letters, etc. Here it means “for reference” or “for your information.”
（例）ご参考までに資料をお送りします。
I will send the documents for your reference.
【まま】In speech, まんま is also used.
1. ...ままだ［Nのままだ］［Na なままだ］［A-いままだ］［V-たままだ］

content: 10 年ぶりに会ったが、彼は昔のままだった。

content.content: I met him for the first time in ten years, but he was the same as ever.

content: テーブルの上は、朝出かけた時のままだった。

content.content: The table was as they had left it when they went out in the morning.

content: このあたりは開発もされず、昔と変わらず、不便なままだ。

content.content: There’s been no development in this area, so nothing’s changed from before—it’s as inconvenient as ever.

content: 小学生の息子に辞書を買ってやったが、あまり使わないのか、いつまでも新しいままだ。

content.content: I bought my son in elementary school a dictionary, but I’m guessing he hasn’t used it much because it still looks brand new.

content: 彼には、去年一万円借りたままだ。

content.content: I still owe him the 10,000 yen I borrowed from him last year.

content: 彼は、先週からずっと会社を休んだままだ。

content.content: He’s been away from work since last week.

content: 母は一時ごろに買物に出かけたままだ。

content.content: Mother has been out shopping since about one o’clock.

content: 桜の木は台風で倒れたままだ。

content.content: The cherry blossom tree is still lying where it fell during the typhoon.

content: 新幹線は込んでいて、大阪から東京までずっと立ったままだった。

content.content: The shinkansen (bullet train) was crowded and I had to stand all the way from Osaka to Tokyo.

content: 彼はずっとうつ向いたままだった。

content.content: He remained looking down all the time.
Demonstrates that the same situation continues without change. As in examples

content: , when attached to a noun, a na-adjective or an i-adjective, it shows that a situation from a point in the past continues into the present without change. Also, as in
, when attached to a verb in the ta-form, it shows that, once the action denoted by the verb is complete, the same situation continues.

content.content: Often used in cases where the thing which is expected to happen next has still not taken place. For example,

content: expresses that what has been borrowed has still not been returned, while
expresses that the person being talked about has still not come in to the company.

content.content: 2. ...まま（で）［Nのまま（で）］［Na なまま（で）］［A-いまま（で）］［V-たまま（で）］

content: 日本のトマトは、煮たりしないで生のまま食べた方がうまい。

content.content: Japanese tomatoes are best eaten raw, without stewing them.

content: 店員: 袋にお入れしましょうか。

content.content: Shop assistant: Shall I put them in the bag?
客:いや、そのままでけっこうです。
Customer:  No, they’re fine as they are.

content: 年をとっても、きれいなままでいたい。

content.content: Even when I get old, I want to stay pretty.

content: 日本酒はあたためて飲む人が多いが、私は冷たいままで飲むのが好きだ。

content.content: There are many people who heat sake to drink it, but I like to have it cold.

content: 靴をはいたまま部屋に入らないで下さい。

content.content: Please don’t enter the room with your shoes still on.

content: クーラーをつけたまま寝ると風邪をひきますよ。

content.content: You’ll catch a cold if you sleep with the air-conditioner left on.

content: ストーブを消さないまま学校に来てしまった。

content.content: I came to school without turning off the heater.

content: 三日前に家をでたまま行方がわからない。

content.content: He left the house three days ago and I still don’t know where he is.

content: 急いでいたので、さよならも言わないまま、帰ってきてしまった。

content.content: Because I was in a hurry, I came back without even saying goodbye.

content: 戦後の混乱で父とはずっと連絡がとれなかった。結局父は、私が結婚したことも知らないまま亡くなった。

content.content: Because of the chaos after the war, I lost contact with my father. In the end, he died still not even knowing I had gotten married.
Means that the same situation continues without change. In examples

content: , the present situation is not changed, or does not change. In examples
, attached to verbs in the ta-form, or in negative forms, it means “in that situation, (I) do....”

content.content: This phrase is used in cases where verbs which denote a momentary action are used and the result or effect of that action continues and a subsequent action or situation occurs. The subjects of the verbs must be the same.
（×）電車はこんでいて、山田さんは立ったまま、私はすわっていた。
The train was crowded; Yamada-san stayed standing, and I was sitting down.
（○）電車はこんでいて、山田さんは立ったままだったが、私はすわっていた。
As the train was crowded, Yamada-san remained standing but I was sitting down.
（×）彼が待っているまま、私は他の人と話していた。
He continued waiting; I was talking to someone else.
（○）彼を待たせたまま、私は他の人と話していた。
I kept him waiting while I was talking to someone else.
3. ...まま（に）a. V-るまま（に）

content: 足の向くまま、気の向くまま、ふらりと旅に出た。

content.content: I simply set out on a journey to go wherever my feet and mood took me.

content: 気の向くままに、絵筆をはしらせた。

content.content: I moved the paintbrush as my mood dictated.

content: あなたの思うまま、自由に計画を立ててください。

content.content: Please feel free to make a plan as you see fit.
Means “to let things take their own course” or “to do (something) as it pleases (one).” Can be used with a limited range of verbs, such as 足の向くまま and 気の向くまま.
b. V-られるまま（に）

content: 春の風に誘われるままに、公園を散歩した。

content.content: Lured on by the spring breeze, I walked in the park.

content: 彼は、上司に命令されるままに行動していただけだ。

content.content: He was only acting according to the commands of his superiors.

content: 被害者は犯人に要求されるままに金を渡していたようだ。

content.content: The victim seems to have handed over the money as the criminal demanded.
Shows the way a person is complying with the will or demand of another, doing exactly as s/he was told. The form V-られるがままに can also be used.
c. ...ままに  なる／する［V-たままに  なる／する］

content: 暑いのでドアはあけたままにしておいてください。

content.content: Because it is hot, please leave the door open.

content: 病気はだんだん悪くなってきている。このままにしておいてはいけない。

content.content: His illness is getting worse. We cannot leave it as it is.

content: 家族を失って、彼女は悲しみにうちひしがれている。今は、そっとこのままにしておいた方がいい。

content.content: She is heartbroken at the loss of her family. For now, it’s better just to let her be.

content: 電気がついたままになっていた。

content.content: The light had been left on.

content: あの事件以来、ドアはこわれたままになっている。

content.content: The door has been left broken since that incident.
Means “the same situation continues/is continued without change.” In examples

content: , V-たままにしておく and このままにしておく mean that, for some reason, the speaker intentionally leaves the situation unchanged. In examples
and
,  V- たままになっている means “(a thing) is left as it is.”

content.content: 4. V-たままを

content: 見たままを話してください。

content.content: Please tell it like you saw it.

content: 遠慮なく、思ったままを言ってください。

content.content: Without reservation, please say what you think.

content: 田中さんに聞いたままを伝えただけです。

content.content: I’m just saying what I heard from Tanaka-san.
Means “without modification” or “in (that) way.”  感じたまま、見たまま、聞いたまま, and so on can be used.
5. ...がまま［V-る／V-られる　がまま］

content: 言われるがままに、はんこを押してしまった。

content.content: I did what I was told and stamped my seal on it.

content: なぐられても、けられても、彼はされるがままになっていた。

content.content: Even when he was beaten and kicked, he let them do with him as they pleased.

content: あるがままの姿を見てもらいたい。

content.content: I would like you to see it (or someone) as the way it (or someone) is.
A fixed idiomatic expression expressing that the condition of something is without modification or alteration. Both

content: and
have the same meaning as V-られるまま（に）. Example
means “as (one) was told to do” and
means “to accept what was done, without resistance.” Example
means “to (see) the thing/someone, as it/someone is, without adornment or decoration.”

content.content: 【まみれ】［Nまみれ］

content: 子供たちは汗まみれになっても気にせずに遊んでいる。

content.content: The children keep on playing without even caring that they are dripping with sweat.

content: あの仏像は何年も放っておかれたので、ほこりまみれだ。

content.content: Because that Buddhist statue was neglected for years, it is covered in dust.

content: 犯行現場には血まみれのナイフが残されていた。

content.content: A knife covered in blood was left at the scene of the crime.

Shows the condition that something dirty covers the whole surface of a thing. It can be used in the forms Nまみれになる, Nまみれだ and Nまみれの and can only be used with a limited range of nouns such as sweat, dust, blood, mud, etc.
【まもなく】
1. まもなく

content: 《駅のアナウンス》まもなく急行がまいります。

content.content: 《a station announcement》The express train will be arriving shortly.

content: 《劇場のアナウンス》まもなく開演です。席のほうにお戻りください。

content.content: 《a theater announcement》The performance will be starting shortly. Please return to your seats.

content: 一学期も終わりに近づき、まもなく楽しい夏休みがやって来る。

content.content: The first term is finishing soon and soon the enjoyable summer vacation will be here.
Shows that there is only a little time before the next thing occurs. This expression is a little more formal than すぐに.
2. V-ると／V-て　まもなく

content: 彼女は結婚してまもなく、夫の海外赴任についてアメリカへ行ってしまった。

content.content: Soon after getting married, she accompanied her husband to America on his overseas assignment.

content: 病院に運ばれてまもなく、みちこは女のあかちゃんを出産した。

content.content: Shortly after being taken to the hospital, Michiko gave birth to a baby girl.

content: 会社をやめてまもなく、青木さんは喫茶店を開業した。

content.content: Soon after quitting the company, Aoki-san opened a coffee shop.

content: 夜があけるとまもなく小鳥たちが鳴き始める。

content.content: Shortly after dawn breaks, small birds begin to sing.
Used to show temporal context; to express the fact that shortly after one thing occurs, another connected event also occurs.

The expression V-てすぐ is very similar. V-てすぐ is used when two events occur in quick succession but V-るとまもなく／V-てまもなく is used with less urgency, in cases where a little time passes between the two events.
【まるで】
1. まるで

content: 今日は風が強くて、まるで台風みたいだ。

content.content: Today the wind is strong. It seems just like a typhoon.

content: あんなつまらないことで怒りだすなんて、まるで子供みたいだ。

content.content: When you lose your temper over a little thing like that you seem just like a child.

content: 彼は、入学試験を受ける友人のことを、まるで自分のことのように心配している。

content.content: He worries about his friend taking the entrance examination as if it were he himself taking it.

content: きのうあんなに大きな事件があったのに、街はまるで何事もなかったかのように平静を取り戻していた。

content.content: Despite that big incident yesterday, the town has regained its calm again just as if nothing had happened.

content: 大事件にもかかわらず、人々はまるで何事もなかったかのごとく振舞っている。

content.content: In spite of the major incident, people are behaving as if nothing has happened.

Used in the forms まるで...ようだ／みたいだ and まるで...かのように／かのごとく. Figuratively compares another example with an existing condition or state and demonstrates that although in reality the two are different, they are very close. It cannot be used together with らしい.
（×）あの人は、まるで女らしい人です。
That person is just as if she were very ladylike.
（○）あの人は｛たいへん／とても｝女らしい人です。
That person is (very) ladylike.
2. まるで...ない

content: 私は外国語はまるでだめなんです。

content.content: I am absolutely hopeless at foreign languages.

content: うちの兄弟はまるで似ていない。

content.content: My siblings look completely different.

content: いくら仕事ができても、自分の身の回りのことがまるでできないようでは、一人前のおとなとは言えない。

content.content: However professional you may be, you can’t say you are properly an adult if you can’t take care of your own personal needs.

content: あいつのやり方はまるでなってない。

content.content: That guy’s way of doing things just doesn’t work.

content: みんなの話では、ずいぶん嫌な男のように思えたが、実際に会ってみると、聞いていたのとはまるで違っていた。

content.content: According to what everyone said, I’d had the impression he was a truly horrible man, but when I actually met him he was completely different from what I had heard.
When accompanied by a negative form or an expression with negative meaning, this conveys the meaning “completely not” or “absolutely not.” In example

content: the meaning is “completely hopeless,” “no good at all.”

content.content: 【まわる】［R-まわる］

content: この寒いのに子供達は外を走り回っている。

content.content: Even though it is this cold, the children are running around outside.

content: 病人がスイカが食べたいというので、スイカを求めて 12 月の街を駈けずり回った。

content.content: Because the sick person says that he wants to eat watermelon, I have been dashing around the December streets searching for watermelon.

content: 売れっ子ジャーナリストの彼は世界中を飛び回っている。

content.content: He is a popular journalist who flies all over the world.

content: 子供は小犬に追いかけられて、部屋中を逃げまわった。

content.content: Chased by the puppy, the child ran all around the room to get away.

Used together with verbs which express movement like 動く (move), 走る (run), 飛ぶ (fly), 泳ぐ (swim), and verbs which express activity such as 暴れる (rage), 遊ぶ (play), and 跳ねる (jump), this means “to do ... here and there” or “to do ... in that area.”
【まんざら】
1. まんざら...でもないまんざら...ではない

content: 彼のことはまんざら知らないわけでもない。

content.content: I wouldn’t say he is a complete stranger to me (in fact, quite the opposite).

content: 祖母は、一時期教師をしていたことがあるから、人前でしゃべるのはまんざら素人でもない。

content.content: My grandmother was a teacher for a time, so she isn’t exactly a novice when it comes to speaking in public.

content: 大勢の人の前で歌うのは、まんざら嫌いでもない。

content.content: I don’t completely hate singing in front of a crowd of people.

content: 彼女の様子では、まんざら彼が嫌いでもないようだ。

content.content: Judging from her expression, I wouldn’t say she dislikes him (perhaps the opposite is true).

content: おれもまんざら捨てたものではない。

content.content: I’m not exactly useless, either.
Expresses the meaning “not necessarily X” or “not absolutely X.” A negative form or expression is directed towards X. Examples

content: and
mean “it is not that disagreeable; in fact, I like it,” while
is a common expression meaning “I have some pretty good points.”

content.content: 2. まんざらでもない

content: 子供のことをほめられて彼はまんざらでもないようすだった。

content.content: He looked rather smug when his child was praised.

content: まんざらでもない顔をしていた。

content.content: He was looking rather smug.

content: お世辞だとわかっていても、自分が描いた絵をほめられるのはまんざらでもない。

content.content: Even though he knows it is flattery, he is not displeased to have the pictures he has painted praised.

content: 今でこそみんな忘れてしまったが、学生のころの英語の成績はまんざらでもなかった。

content.content: Even though everyone has forgotten by now, when she was a student her English grades weren’t all that bad.
Means “not a negative but, rather, a positive feeling.” It is often used in such forms as まんざらでもない様子／ふう／みたい／ようだ and まんざらでもない（という）顔をしている. Also, as in

content: , it means “not bad; rather, it’s quite good.”

content.content: 【まんまと】

content: やつにまんまと騙された。

content.content: I was completely deceived by that guy.

content: まんまと、してやられた。

content.content: I was thoroughly hoodwinked.

content: まんまと一杯くわされた。

content.content: I was completely taken in.

content: 犯人は、金をだまし取ることにまんまと成功した。

content.content: The criminal completely succeeded in taking the money by deception.

Means “extremely skillfully” or “splendidly.” After まんまと, certain customary, fixed phrases are often used, such as 騙す(deceive), してやる (outsmart), 一杯くわせる(play a trick), and 忍び込む (steal into). It can be used in cases where success has been achieved by outwitting or deceiving someone, or in cases where unpraiseworthy measures have been used in order to achieve something.
As in examples

content: , when used in the form まんまとV-された, this expresses the speaker’s feeling of mortification or surprise at the magnificence of the deception of which he or she has been the victim.

content.content: 【みえる】
1. ...がみえる［Nがみえる］［Nが V-るのがみえる］［Nが V-ているのがみえる］［Nが V-るところがみえる］［Nが V-ているところがみえる］

content: 晴れた日には、ここから富士山がよく見える。

content.content: On a clear day, you can see Fuji-san (Mt. Fuji) very well from here.

content: 田舎は空気がきれいなので星がよく見える。

content.content: As the air is clean in the countryside, you can see the stars well.

content: この部屋の窓から、電車が通るのがよく見える。

content.content: From the window in this room, you can clearly see the trains passing by.

content: この部屋の窓から、子供達が公園で遊んでいるのが見える。

content.content: From the window in this room, you can see the children playing in the park.

content: ちょうどそのとき、裏口からだれかが出てくるところが見えました。

content.content: Just at that moment, I saw someone coming out of the back entrance.

content: 子供の頃、私の部屋から、庭の桜の木が見えた。

content.content: When I was a child, from my room, I could see the cherry trees in the garden.

content: 彼は生まれつき目が見えない。

content.content: He has been blind from birth.

content: 目が悪いので、めがねがないと遠くの文字は見えない。

content.content: My eyes are bad, so without glasses, I cannot see letters at a distance.

content: 黒板の字が小さくて見えません。

content.content: The writing on the blackboard is too small to see.

Expresses the sense that something is not seen through conscious intention but rather that it has naturally entered the line of sight or can be seen. 見えない expresses that something cannot be seen due to a problem with eyesight, for example, or because there is an obstacle in the way, or because the object is too far away.

みられる can also be used to express 見ることができる, but this means “to be allowed to see” or “to have the chance to see” something and not simply that it can visually be seen. Therefore, as in the following example, in cases where there is a question of having the opportunity to see something or not, みえる cannot be used.
（◯）A:歌舞伎を見たいんですが、どこへ行けば見られますか。
I want to see Kabuki. Where can I go to see it?
B:そりゃ、歌舞伎座でしょうね。
That would be the Kabuki-za.
（×）歌舞伎を見たいんですが、どこへ行けば見えますか。
I would like to see Kabuki.  Where can I go and see it?
（○）大都会では、蝶やとんぼが身近に見られなくなった。
In the big cities, you can’t see butterflies around anymore.
（×）大都会では、蝶やとんぼが身近に見えなくなった。
In the big cities, you can’t see butterflies around anymore.
2. みえるa. Nがみえる

content: 今学期の彼の成績には、努力の跡が見える。

content.content: You can see the evidence of his efforts in his grades this term.

content: 彼女にはまったく反省の色が見えない。

content.content: She shows no sign of remorse.

content: 当時の日記には、当時彼が苦悩していた様子があちこちに見える。

content.content: In his diaries of that time, evidence of his suffering can be seen here and there.

content: 彼が父親を嫌っていることは、言葉の端々に見える。

content.content: You can see in every word that he hates his father.
Expresses the meaning “can recognize,” “can understand,” or “can feel” a particular thing.
b. ...が...みえる［...が　N／Na　にみえる］［...が　A-くみえる］［...が　V-てみえる］

content: 壁のしみが人の形に見える。

content.content: The stain on the wall looks like the shape of a person.

content: あの子は背が高くて、とても小学生には見えない。

content.content: That child is tall, so she doesn’t look at all like an elementary school student.

content: 父は最近体の調子がいいらしく、前よりずっと元気に見える。

content.content: Recently my father’s health seems good and he looks much better than he did before.

content: あの人は、実際の年よりずっと若く見える。

content.content: That person looks much younger than he really is.

content: みんなに祝福されて、彼の顔はいっそう輝いて見えた。

content.content: When everyone wished him well, his face appeared to shine all the more.
Expresses the meaning that, judging from what the speaker has seen, something is thought or felt to be so. It can also be used in the forms ...そうにみえる and ...ようにみえる, as in patterns c and d below.
c. ...そうにみえる［Na そうにみえる］［A-そうにみえる］［R-そうにみえる］

content: 料理にパセリかなにか緑色のものを添えるとおいしそうに見える。

content.content: A meal looks delicious when you garnish it with parsley or some other greens.

content: この人形は今にも動きだしそうに見える。

content.content: This doll looks as if it might come alive at any moment.

content: その日の山本さんは、なんだか寂しそうに見えた。

content.content: On that day, Yamamoto-san looked somewhat lonely.

content: この仕事ははじめ楽しそうに見えたが、やってみるとなかなかたいへんだ。

content.content: This work looked fun to begin with, but when you try it, it’s pretty difficult.

content: あいつは一見やさしそうに見えるが冷たいところのある男だ。

content.content: At first glance he seems kind, but he’s a man with a coldness to him.

content: このごろの電気製品は、いろいろな機能がついていて一見便利そうに見えるが、実際にはいらないものばかりだ。

content.content: Nowadays, electrical goods have lots of functions that look useful at first glance but in reality are all completely unnecessary.
Means that, judging from what the speaker has seen, something is thought or felt to be so. It is also frequently used, as in examples

content: , to mean “from its external appearance, this seems to be ..., but the truth is not known” or “the reality is different.”

content.content: d. ...ようにみえる［Nのようにみえる］［Na なようにみえる］［A-ようにみえる］［Vようにみえる］

content: この宝石は猫の目のように見えるところから、キャッツアイという名前がついている。

content.content: Because this jewel looks like the eye of a cat, it is called “the cat’s eye.”

content: 夏休みの間に、子供たちは急に成長したように見える。

content.content: The children appear to have suddenly grown a lot during the summer vacation.

content: 便利なように見えたので買ってみたが、使ってみるとたいしたことはなかった。

content.content: As it looked convenient I bought it, but when I tried using it, it wasn’t anything special.

content: 彼は賛成しているように見えるが、本当のところはわからない。

content.content: He seems to approve, but I don’t know if he really does.

content: 男は何も知らないといったが、何かを隠しているように見えた。

content.content: The man said he knew nothing, but he looked like he was hiding something.
Expresses the meaning that, judging from what the speaker has seen, something is thought or felt to be so. Example

content: means “because it looks like a cat’s eye....” As in examples
, it is also often used to express “from the external appearance, this seems to be (so), but the truth is not known” or “the reality is different.”

content.content: e. ...とみえる

content: すぐに返事をしないところをみると、佐藤さんはあまり気が進まないとみえる。

content.content: From the fact that she hasn’t replied immediately, it appears that Sato-san is reluctant.

content: その子はおもちゃを買ってもらったのがよほどうれしかったとみえて、寝ている間も離さなかった。

content.content: That child seemed very happy to have been bought a toy and wouldn’t let go of it even while sleeping.

content: 母はたいへん驚いたとみえて、しばらく口をきかなかった。

content.content: Mother looked so surprised—for a while she couldn’t say a word.

content: 山田は、まだ飲み足りないとみえて、しきりにもう一軒行こうと誘う。

content.content: Yamada seems as though he hasn’t had enough to drink and keeps on asking to go to another bar.

Means that, judging from what the speaker has seen, something is thought or felt to be so. It can also be used in spoken language, but would generally be seen as written language. In speech, みたいだ and らしい are more commonly used.
f. ...かにみえる...かのようにみえる

content: 彼は他人の非難などまったく意に介していないかにみえる。

content.content: He seems completely indifferent to the criticisms of others.

content: きのうあんな事件があったのに、街は静かで何ごともなかったかにみえる。

content.content: Even though such an incident occurred yesterday, the town is quiet and appears as though nothing had happened.

content: 景気の悪化は一応おさまったかにみえるが、まだまだ安心はできない。

content.content: It appears that, for the time being, the worsening of business conditions has abated, but we still can’t feel complacent.

content: その法案は、そのまますんなりと参議院を通過するかにみえたが、僅差で否決されるという意外な結末を迎えた。

content.content: It seemed that that bill would easily pass through the House of Councilors as it was, but it came to an unexpected end of being rejected by a narrow margin.

Means “on the surface (it) can be felt, or thought, to be so.”  It can be used to convey that “the truth is not known but on the surface (it) appears to be (that way) / the possibility exists that, in reality, (it) is not (that way).”  When used in the form かにみえたが, as in example

content: , it means “(it) was thought to be (so) but, in reality, something different occurred.”  It is a formal, written expression. In speech ようにみえる and みたいにみえる are used.

content.content: 3. Nがみえる

content: あなた、山下さんが見えましたよ。

content.content: Darling, Yamashita-san has just come.

content: 先週、斎藤さんが挨拶に見えた。

content.content: Last week, Saito-san made a formal visit.

content: 明日のパーティーには、田中さんも見えるはずだ。

content.content: Tanaka-san should also be coming to the party tomorrow.

content: A:留守中だれか来ましたか。

content.content: Did anyone come while I was out?
B:今日はどなたも見えませんでした。
Nobody came to visit today.
This is honorific language for 来る. It is the same as いらっしゃる and おいでになる. Furthermore, there is also the polite expression ...がお見えになる.
【みこみ】
1. ...みこみがある［Nのみこみがある］［V-るみこみがある］

content: A:先生、この足はもう治らないんでしょうか。

content.content: Doctor, will this leg never get better?
B:残念ですが、回復の見込みはほとんどありません。
Unfortunately, the prospects of recovery are almost nil.

content: もう二十日も晴天が続いている。水不足が心配されているが、近いうちに雨が降る見込みはまったくない。

content.content: The fine weather has already continued for no less than twenty days.  There is concern about a water shortage as there is no hope of rain falling soon.

content: A:このあたりに地下鉄の駅ができるというのは、どの程度見込みのある話なんですか。

content.content: How much truth is there to the talk of a subway station being built in this area?
B:さあ、どうなんでしょうね。
Yeah, I wonder.

content: 川口はいつも文句ばかり言っている。あんなやつは、見込みがない。

content.content: Kawaguchi always does nothing but complain. That guy has no prospects.
Expresses the meaning that “there is that possibility, expectation, or plan.” Used in the form ...見込みのあるN when modifying a noun. As in example

content: , where it is clear from the context what is meant, only 見込みがある is used and the first half is omitted. As in
, when a person is described as either 見込みがある or 見込みがない, the meaning is that they have or do not have any future prospects or promise.

content.content: 2. ...みこみだ［Nのみこみだ］［V-るみこみだ］

content: 《ニュース》JR東海道線は、明朝6時には回復する見込みです。

content.content: 《on the news》It is expected that the service on the Tokaido Line will resume by 6 a.m. tomorrow.

content: 《新聞記事》JR東海道線は、明朝6時には回復の見込み。

content.content: 《newspaper headline》Tokaido Line to resume by 6 a.m. tomorrow.

content: 台風の影響で新幹線のダイヤはたいへん乱れております。復旧は夜遅くになる見込みです。

content.content: Because of the typhoon, the shinkansen (bullet train) schedule has become very disrupted. It should be back to normal late tonight.

content: 《履歴書》〇〇年3月 31 日高校卒業見込み。

content.content: 《resume》To graduate from high school on March 31, 20--. (planned)
Means “plan” or “forecast.” In example

content: it is a set phrase used to express on a resume something which is expected to happen in the future and means the same as 卒業予定. It is a formal, written expression. Apart from written passages, it is often used in announcements and on the news.

content.content: 3. みこみがたつ

content: やっと、借金の返済の見込みが立った。

content.content: I finally have hope of paying off my debt.

content: 《アナウンス》先ほど、JR東海道線で脱線事故があったもようです。今のところ、復旧の見込みは立っておりません。

content.content: 《announcement》Just a moment ago, there was a derailment on the  Tokaido Line. At present the schedule for resumption of service has not been announced.
Means “anticipate or expect.” Example

content: means that it is not yet known when services will be restored.

content.content: 4. みこみちがいだ／みこみはずれだ

content: 彼には大いに期待していたが、まったくの見込み違いだった。

content.content: I had high hopes for him, but my expectations were completely off mark.

content: 今年は冷夏で、クーラーなどの電気製品はさっぱり売れなかった。猛暑を期待していたのに、見込みはずれだった。

content.content: Because this year’s summer has been cool, electronic goods such as air conditioners haven’t sold at all. We were anticipating a heat wave but our projections were wrong.
Often used in the ta-form, as in みこみちがいだった or みこみはずれだった, meaning “different than expected” or “what was anticipated/hoped for did not happen.” みこみがはずれた is also used.
【みこんで】［...をみこんで］［Nをみこんで］［V-るのをみこんで］

content: 君を見込んで頼むのだが、ぜひ今度の仕事に参加してほしい。

content.content: I make this request with full confidence in you and certainly hope that you will participate in future projects.

content: 君を男と見込んで頼みたいことがある。

content.content: I have something I want to ask you as a man of the world.

content: 完成までに時間がかかる地下鉄工事などは、物価の上昇を見込んで、余裕のある予算を組んでおいた方がよい。

content.content: In anticipation of rising commodity prices, it is better if projects which take time to complete, such as subway construction, have some surplus in the budget.

content: 商品には、はじめから売れ残るのを見込んだ値段がつけてある。

content.content: From the start, the price of commodities includes anticipated surplus stocks.
Means “anticipating...” or “expecting....” As in examples

content: and
, it demonstrates that, a person’s knowledge being valued highly, there is the expectation that s/he will do an excellent job. Also, as in
and
, it expresses “(something) being accounted for from the beginning,” and “expectations being formed in advance.”

content.content: 【みせる】
1. ...をみせる［NがNに...をみせる］

content: 私は友だちにアルバムをみせた。

content.content: I showed my friend the album.

content: 来月工場に行って、実際に製品を作っているところを見せてもらうことになった。

content.content: It has been decided that, next month, we will go to a factory and be shown how the products are actually made.

content: その子はうまく字が書けるようになったのを母親に見せたくてしかたがないようだった。

content.content: That child just had to show his mother how good he had gotten at writing characters.

content: 家族と離れて元気がなかった彼も、最近やっと笑顔を見せるようになった。

content.content: Separated from his family and depressed, he has at last recently come to show us some smiles.

content: 9月に入って、さすがの猛暑も衰えをみせるようになった。

content.content: The coming of September showed a decline in the usual summer heat.

content: 微熱が続いたのであちこちの医者に見せたが、結局原因はわからなかった。

content.content: Because my slight fever continued, I saw several doctors, but in the end the cause remained unknown.
Means to “enable a person to see (something)” in examples

content: . Means to show an internal or emotional state through attitude or facial expressions in
. 医者にみせる in
means to receive a medical examination from a doctor.

content.content: 2. かおをみせるすがたをみせる

content: このごろ彼はちっとも学校に顔を見せない。

content.content: Recently, he hasn’t put in a single appearance at school.

content: 久しぶりだね。たまには顔を見せてくれよ。

content.content: Long time no see. You should put in an appearance once in a while.

content: 8時ごろになって、やっと月が雲の晴れ間から顔を見せた。

content.content: When it got to around eight o’clock, the moon finally appeared through a break in the clouds.

content: 8時ごろになって、やっと星が姿を見せた。

content.content: At around eight o’clock we finally got a glimpse of the stars.
Means that “a person arrives” or that “a thing which could not previously be seen becomes visible.”
3. Nが...を...みせる［Nが...をNa にみせる］［Nが...をA-くみせる］［Nが...をV-ようにみせる］

content: 華やかな衣装が彼女を実際より若く見せている。

content.content: Showy clothing makes her look younger than she really is.

content: 明るいライトが商品をいっそうきれいに見せている。

content.content: Bright lighting makes goods look all the more beautiful.

content: ショートカットの髪がいっそう彼女を活発に見せている。

content.content: Her short haircut makes her look all the perkier.

content: 明るい照明が商品を新鮮にみせている。

content.content: Bright lighting makes the stock look fresh.
Attached to a noun, this expresses the meaning that the thing denoted by the noun as the cause leads the observer to a certain feeling about it.
4. ...ようにみせる［Nのようにみせる］［Na なようにみせる］［A-いようにみせる］［Vようにみせる］

content: 犯人は、わざとドアを壊して外部から侵入したように見せている。

content.content: The culprit intentionally damaged the door to make it look like he had entered from the outside.

content: 出かけたように見せて、実は家の中に隠れていた。

content.content: Making it look as if she had gone out, in reality she was hiding inside the house.

content: 彼は娘の家出をあまり気にしていないように見せてはいるが、本当は心配でたまらないのだ。

content.content: He makes it seem as though he isn’t bothered by his daughter running  away from home, but really he is beside himself with worry.
Expresses the meaning that, although something looks or is made to look a certain way, in reality it is different.
5. V-てみせる→
【てみせる】
【みたいだ】［N／Na／A／V　みたいだ］A casual expression mainly used in speaking. In formal sentences or situations ようだ is used more commonly. It is unusual to replace ようだ in idiomatic expressions with みたいだ.

1. ...みたい〈simile〉Used to show a condition, nature, form, or behavior of things by giving something similar as an example. It is the same as よう. まるで／ちょうど...みたい can be used to emphasize extreme similarity. As あたかも, いかにも, and さながら are formal written expressions, they cannot be used with みたい.
a. NみたいなN

content: この薬は、チョコレートみたいな味がする。

content.content: This medicine tastes like chocolate.

content: 竹下さんって、あの学生みたいな人でしょ？

content.content: Takeshita-san is that guy who looks like a student, right?

content: いい年をして、子供みたいな服を着ないでほしいな。

content.content: At your age, I wish you wouldn’t wear such childish clothes.

content: 飛行機みたいな形の雲が浮かんでいる。

content.content: There’s a cloud there that looks like an airplane.
When used in the form N1みたいなN2, N2 is described by giving an example of something (N1) to which it bears some resemblance.
Can be rephrased using N1のようなN
2. Not to be confused with NらしいN, where N1=N
2. N1みたいなN2 only gives something which resembles N2 as an example and so N2 is not actually the thing denoted by N

1. For example, 男みたいな人 means that the person appears like a man but, in reality, is not a man. In contrast to this, 男らしい人 means that the person is very manly, or that masculine characteristics are prominent in that person, and it is used in reference to males.
b. ...みたいだ［N／V　みたいだ］

content: すごい風だ。まるで台風みたいだ。

content.content: What a wind! It’s just like a typhoon.

content: 君ってまるで子供みたいだね。

content.content: You’re just like a child.

content: その地方の方言に慣れるまでは、まるで外国語を聞いているみたいだった。

content.content: Until I got used to the dialect of that area, it was just like listening to a foreign language.

content: 私が合格するなんてうそみたい。

content.content: That I have passed (the exam) seems unbelievable.

What the speaker felt about the condition, nature, form, or behavior of things is expressed by giving an easy-to-comprehend example of something which bears some resemblance to them. It can be replaced with ...ようだ. Many women omit the sentence-final だ in everyday conversation, as in example

content: . うそみたいだ means “(it’s) unbelievable” or “(I’m) very surprised.”

content.content: c. ...みたいに［N／A／V　みたいに］

content: もう9月も半ばなのに、真夏みたいに暑い。

content.content: Even though it’s the middle of September, it’s hot like midsummer.

content: この服は、買って何年にもなるが、新品みたいにきれいだ。

content.content: It’s many years since I bought these clothes, but they look as good as new.

content: 子供みたいにすねるのはやめろよ。

content.content: Stop sulking like a child.

content: こんなにうまいコーヒーが、一杯 100 円だなんて、ただみたいに安いね。

content.content: Having coffee this good for only 100 yen a cup—it’s so cheap it seems free.

content: 私ばかりが悪いみたいに言わないでよ。あなただって悪いんだから。

content.content: Don’t speak as if only I was bad! You were bad, too!

content: A:学校ではあまり会わないね。

content.content: We don’t see you much at school.
B:おいおい、そんな言い方をしたら、僕が授業をさぼってばかりいるみたいに聞こえるじゃないか。
Hey, when you talk like that, it sounds like I’m always skipping classes.
Used to show the condition, nature, form, or behavior of things by giving something similar as an example. Examples

content: and
imply “even though (that) is not the case....”

content.content: d. ...みたいなものだ［Nみたいなものだ］［V-たみたいなものだ］

content: 僕の給料なんか、会社の儲けに比べたら、ただみたいなものさ。

content.content: When it comes to my salary, compared to the company’s profits, it’s like I’m working for free.

content: 《野球をみながら》こんなに点差があけば、もう勝ったみたいなものだ。

content.content: 《while watching baseball》With this kind of point spread, it’s like they’ve already won.

content: A:中田さん、店、売ったんだって？

content.content: Is it true that Nakata-san sold his shop?
B:売ったというか、まあ、取られたみたいなものだ。借金の抵当にはいってたんだそうだよ。
Sold? Well, more like it was taken. Apparently it was used as collateral against a loan.
Means “(it) has still not actually happened but (it) is almost sure to” or “the situation is almost the same as....” In speech, もんだ is often used in place of ものだ.
2. ...みたいだ〈supposition, conjecture〉

content: 誰も彼女の本名を知らないみたいだ。

content.content: It seems that nobody knows her real name.

content: 田中さんは甘いものが嫌いみたいだ。

content.content: It seems that Tanaka-san dislikes sweet things.

content: どうもかぜをひいたみたいだ。

content.content: I might have caught a cold.

content: 今度発売された辞書は、すごくいいみたいだよ。

content.content: The dictionary being launched now seems really good.

content: 何か焦げているみたいだ。へんな匂いがする。

content.content: Something seems to be burning. There is a strange smell.

content: A:あの人誰？

content.content: Who is that?
B:誰だろう。近所の人じゃないみたいだね。
Hmm, I wonder. He doesn’t look like someone from around here.

content: A:試験はいつあるんだい。

content.content: When’s your exam?
B:来週みたいだよ。
It looks like next week.

content: A:あの人会社をやめたの？

content.content: Has that person quit the company?
B:みたいだね。
It would seem so.

content: A:小林さんはもうアメリカに行ったのかな？

content.content: Kobayashi-san has already gone to America, hasn’t she?
B:ええ、きのう出発したみたいですよ。
Yeah, it seems she left yesterday.

content: A:山本さん怒っていたでしょう？

content.content: Yamamoto-san was angry, wasn’t he?
B:うん、すごく怒ってるみたいだった。
Yeah, he seemed very angry.

content: そのときの佐々木さんはなんだか怖くて、いつもの彼ではないみたいだった。

content.content: Sasaki-san was kind of scary at that time. He didn’t seem like his usual self.

Shows the speaker’s supposition. Means “(I) can’t be certain but (I) think it is so.”  Expresses the speaker’s inference based on what they themselves have experienced, something they have seen, heard, or sensed.

In contrast to this, when expressing a supposition based on information gained indirectly, such as something heard from another person, らしい is used. When reporting something as it was heard from another, そうだ is used.
（例）山下さんは今日は来ないみたいですね（もう、時間も遅いし）。
It looks like Yamashita-san is not coming today (because the time is already late).
（例）山下さんは今日は来ないらしいですよ（直接きいたわけではないが、他の人がそう言っていた）。
It looks like Yamashita-san is not coming today (I haven’t heard this directly but somebody else was saying so).
（例）山下さんは今日は来ないそうです（山下さんから「行かない」という伝言があった）。
It looks like Yamashita-san is not coming today (I had a message from Yamashita-san saying she is not coming).

...みたいだ and ...みたいだった are both often used, but their meanings are different. As in the next example, V-たみたいだ concerns a thing which occurred in the past and shows the inferred outcome at the time of speaking.
（例）A:田中さんはいつ来たのかな？
I wonder when Tanaka-san arrived.
B:午前中は見かけなかったから、昼から来たみたいですよ。
I didn’t see him this morning and so he must have come after noon.
V-たみたいだった shows that the speaker thought something to be the case at a certain point in the past.
（例）昨日の夜は妙だった。誰か来たみたいだったから、ドアをあけてみたが、だれもいなかった。そんなことが何度もあった。
Last night was strange. Because I thought someone had come, I opened the door, but there was nobody there. That kind of thing has happened many times.
Also, when describing a situation as it is seen, for example, when there is a cake before your eyes, このケーキはおいしいみたいだ is not used. In such a case このケーキはおいしそうだ is used.
（例）A:これ、新しく買ったスマートフォンです。
This is my new smartphone.
（○）B：便利そうですね。
B：It looks handy.
（×）B：便利みたいですね。
B：It looks handy.

The そう that is used in such cases is different from the そう used to express hearsay and so care must be taken. When expressing hearsay we use おいしいそうだ(they say it is tasty) and 便利だそうだ (they say it is handy/convenient).
3. ...みたい〈example〉［NみたいなN］［Nみたいに］

content: 東京や大阪みたいな大都会には住みたくない。

content.content: I don’t want to live in a big city like Tokyo or Osaka.

content: A:三分間写真の機械って、どんなところにある？

content.content: What kind of place will have an instant photo booth?
B:さあ、デパートみたいなところにはあるんじゃないかな。
Well, won’t they have them in places like department stores?

content: 何か細くて長い棒みたいな物はありませんか。

content.content: Do you have something long and thin like a pole?

content: 佐藤さんみたいに英語が上手になりたい。

content.content: I want to become good at English like Sato-san.

content: 今年みたいに暑いと、働くのが本当にいやになる。

content.content: When it’s as hot as this year, work really becomes a pain.

content: 君みたいなあわて者、見たことがないよ。

content.content: I’ve never seen anyone as discombobulated as you.

content: 彼みたいに勝手なことばかりしていると、そのうち誰も相手にしなくなる。

content.content: If he keeps on doing selfish things like he is now, eventually nobody will want to have anything to do with him.
Used to give examples. Example

content: means “big cities such as Tokyo and Osaka, for example,” while
means “large shops like department stores, for example.”

content.content: Examples

content: , and

take the form of exemplifications but, in reality, they can be thought to mean the same as “because this summer was really hot, I didn’t like to work,” “you really are disorganized,” and “because he always does selfish things, eventually nobody will want anything to do with him.” In polite speech ...のような／ように is used.

content.content: 【みだりに】

content: みだりに動物にえさを与えないでください。

content.content: Please do not feed the animals (without permission).

content: みだりに他人の部屋に立ち入るべきではない。

content.content: You should not enter another person’s room without permission.

content: 新聞と言えども、個人のプライバシーをみだりに公表することはゆるされない。

content.content: Although it’s a newspaper, it doesn’t have the right to infringe upon people’s privacy.

Means “without necessity,” “without permission,” or “capriciously.” Expressions forbidding certain actions or behavior, such as みだりに...するな／してはいけない, come after this. In everyday conversation 勝手に...しないでください is often used. It is a formal written expression.
【みる】
1. ...をみる［Nをみる］［Vのをみる］

content: テレビを見るのが好きだ。

content.content: I like to watch television.

content: 窓からぼんやりと雲が流れて行くのを見ていた。

content.content: I was absentmindedly watching the clouds drift by from the window.

content: このごろは忙しくて新聞を見るひまもない。

content.content: Recently, I’ve been so busy I haven’t even had the chance to read the paper.

content: 料理の味を見てください。

content.content: Please taste the food.

content: 風呂の湯かげんをみる。

content.content: (I’ll) check the bathwater.

content: しばらく反響を見てみよう。

content.content: Let’s check the reaction for a little while.

content: 機械の調子をみる。

content.content: (I’ll) check the condition of the machine.

content: 近所のおばさんに子供の面倒をみてもらっている。

content.content: I’m having a lady in our neighborhood look after my kids.

content: もしよかったら、うちの子の勉強を見てもらえませんか。

content.content: I wonder if you would tutor our child?

content: あの人の言うことを全部本気にしていると馬鹿をみるよ。

content.content: If you take everything she says seriously, you’ll make a fool of yourself.

content: あの人は子供の時からずっと辛い目をみてきたのだから、今度こそ幸せになって欲しい。

content.content: That person has had a hard life since childhood, so I hope he will be happy from now on.

content: 作品は 20 年後に完成をみた。

content.content: The work was completed after twenty years.
Aside from its basic meaning of “to see with the eye,” this can also mean “to sense with the tongue, hands, etc.” or to “take care of.” Examples

content: and
are idiomatic expressions meaning to have that kind of experience. Example
is a formal written expression which means that “after a long time, (something is) finally complete or successful.” When we say 医者が患者をみる, the Chinese character 診る is used.

content.content: 2. Nを...みる［Nを A-くみる］［Nが V-るとみる］

content: 試験を甘くみていると失敗しますよ。

content.content: If you think the test is going to be a breeze, you’ll fail.

content: 政府は今回の事件を重くみて、対策委員会を設置することを決定しました。

content.content: The government is looking at this incident very seriously and has decided to establish a task force to deal with it.

content: 警察は、A容疑者にはまだ余罪があるとみて、厳しく追求する構えです。

content.content: The police believe that suspect A has committed further crimes and are pursuing him relentlessly.
Means “thinks...” or “surmises....” It is a formal, written expression.
3. にみる

content: 最近の新聞の論調にみる経済偏重の傾向は目にあまるものがある。

content.content: Looking at the recent tone of the press, the trend towards making too much of the economy is unacceptable.

content: 今回の地震は、近年まれにみる大災害となった。

content.content: In recent years, we have seen few disasters as terrible as this earthquake.

content: 《新聞や雑誌などの見出し》アンケート調査にみる大学生の生活実態と金銭感覚

content.content: 《a newspaper or magazine headline》Survey shows the actual lifestyles and financial stances of university students.
Means “can be seen from....” It is used in writing and is a formal expression.
4. ...ところをみると

content: うれしそうな顔をしているところをみると、試験はうまくいったようだ。

content.content: Judging from her happy face, it seems the exam went well.

content: いまだに返事がないところを見ると、交渉はうまく行っていないようだ。

content.content: Judging from the fact that they still have not received a response, the negotiations don’t seem to be going well.

content: 平気な顔をしているところをみると、まだ事故のことを知らされていないのだろう。

content.content: Looking at his calm expression, I suspect he hasn’t been told of the accident yet.
Expresses the speaker’s conjecture based on their direct experience. Often used with the sentence endings らしい／ようだ／にちがいない. The form ...ところからみて is also used.
（例）高級車に乗っているところからみて、相当の金持ちらしい。
As she’s riding in a luxury car, she must be quite well off.
5. V-てみる→
【てみる】
6. ...からみると→
【からみる】1
【みるからに】

content: 部屋に入ってきたのは、見るからに品の良い中年の女性だった。

content.content: Entering the room was an elegant-looking middle-aged lady.

content: このコートは見るからに安物だ。

content.content: This coat looks cheap.

content: あの人はいつも見るからに上等そうなものを着ている。

content.content: That person always looks like she’s wearing high-quality things.

content: 店の奥から、見るからにやさしそうなおばあさんが出てきました。

content.content: A kind-looking old lady came out from inside the store.

content: 通夜、葬式と続いて、ふだんは元気な彼も見るからに疲れたようすで座っていた。

content.content: What with the wake and the subsequent funeral, even the man you know as usually so full of pep sat down looking quite tired.
Means to such an extent that it “can be ascertained easily from the external appearance of...” or “can be comprehended just by looking at....”
【むき】
1. Nむき〈direction〉

content: 南向きの部屋は明るくて暖かい。

content.content: Rooms facing south are bright and warm.

content: 右向きに置いてください。

content.content: Please leave it facing the right.

content: 横向きに寝てください。

content.content: Please lie down on your side.

content: 前向きに検討したいと考えております。

content.content: I intend to consider this positively.

Attached to nouns which denote bearings and directions such as “north,” “east,” “south,” “west,” “forwards,” “backwards,” “left,” “right,” “up,” and “down,” this means facing that direction. The 前向きに of example

content: is a idiomatic expression meaning “if possible, to endeavor to realize....”

content.content: 2. Nむき〈suitability〉

content: 女性向きのスポーツにはどんなものがありますか。

content.content: Which sports are considered suitable for women?

content: この映画は子供向きだ。

content.content: This film is suitable for children.

content: この家は部屋数も多く台所も広い。どちらかというと大家族向きだ。

content.content: This house has many rooms and a large kitchen. If I had to choose, I’d say it’s suitable for a large family.

content: この機械はたいへん性能がよいが、値段も高く大型で一般家庭向きではない。

content.content: This appliance is very efficient but, as the cost is high and it is large-sized, it is not for the average household.

content: セールスの仕事には向き不向きがある。

content.content: Some can and some can’t work in sales.

content: この機械は大きすぎて家庭で使うのには不向きだ。

content.content: As this appliance is too large, it is unsuitable for use in the home.
Means “perfect for N/suited to N.” Rather than saying Nむきでない we can say Nに不向きだ. The 向き不向きがある of

content: is a customary expression meaning “to have or not have aptitude.” For the difference between this and むけ, please refer to the entry for むけ.

content.content: 3. Vむきもある

content: 君の活躍を快く思わないむきもあるようだから、はでな言動は慎んだ方がいい。

content.content: As there are some who are not exactly delighted with all your endeavors, you’d better use discretion in your language and behavior.

content: 今回の計画については実現を危ぶむむきもある。

content.content: Some have misgivings about the current plan’s implementation.
Means “there are such people.” Example

content: means “there are people who do not take... kindly” and example
means “there are people who think the implementation will be difficult.” It is a formal, written expression.

content.content: 4. むきになる

content: むきになって言い張った。

content.content: She got uptight and insisted on it.

content: そんなにむきにならなくてもいいじゃないか。

content.content: You don’t need to get so upset.

content: 彼はいい男だが、仕事の話となるとすぐむきになるので困る。

content.content: He’s a good man but the problem is that, when the conversation turns to work, he quickly gets all upset.
Expresses the meaning “to become serious and angry or to insist emphatically, even though it’s not a big deal.” Example

content: means “You had better settle down a little.”

content.content: 【むく】

content: 彼は学者としてはすぐれているが、教師にはむかない。

content.content: He excels as a scholar but is not suited to being a teacher.

content: 私は人と接する仕事にむいていると思う。

content.content: I think I would be suited to a job working with people.

content: 私は知らない人に会うのが嫌いなので、セールスの仕事にはむいていません。

content.content: I don’t like meeting new people and so I’m not suited to working in sales.

content: この仕事は美智子さんみたいにおしゃれな人に向いていると思うんだけど。

content.content: I think this job would suit someone stylish like Michiko-san.

content: 私に向いた仕事はないでしょうか。

content.content: Isn’t there any job suited to me?
Means “has an aptitude.” It can be used in the forms （人）が（仕事）にむく and  （仕事）が（人）にむく. The form むいている is also used. Also, the form NにむいたN when modifying a noun is often used.
【むけ】
1. NむけのN

content: この会社では、子供向けのテレビ番組を作っている。

content.content: This company makes children’s television programs.

content: 小学生向けの辞書は字が大きくて読みやすい。

content.content: Dictionaries aimed at elementary school children have large characters and so are easy to read.

content: 輸出むけの製品はサイズが少し大きくなっている。

content.content: Goods for export are made slightly larger.
Used in the form N1むけのN2 , this means N2 is made with N1 as its target. In the case of

content: it means “a program made for children.”

content.content: ...むきの... and ...ようの... are similar phrases. ...むき means “suitable for.” ...ようの... means “for the use of...” or “for use when....” 来客用のスリッパ (guest slippers) and パーティー用バッグ (party purse) are examples of the way in which it can be used.
2. Nむけに

content: 当社では、輸出向けに左ハンドルの自動車を早くから生産している。

content.content: From early on, this company has been manufacturing left-hand drive cars for export.

content: 最近、中高年むけにスポーツクラブや文化教室を開いている地方自治体が増えている。

content.content: Recently the number of local governments opening sports clubs and culture classes aimed at the middle-aged and elderly has been increasing.

content: Y社では、若い女性むけにアルコール分が少なくカラフルな、缶入りカクテルを開発中である。

content.content: Company Y is developing low-alcohol, colorful, canned cocktails targeted at young women.
Means “targeting.../with... as its target.”
【むけて】［Nにむけて］

content: 全日空 103 便は8月 10 日午前8時に、成田からロンドンに向けて出発した。

content.content: All Nippon Airways Flight 103 departed from Narita for London at 8 a.m. on the 10th of August.

content: 来たるべきオリンピックに向けて準備が着々と進められている。

content.content: Preparations for the forthcoming Olympics are steadily progressing.

content: 新空港建設については、事前に住民に向けての十分な説明が為されなければならない。

content.content: Sufficient explanation must be given to residents beforehand regarding the construction of a new airport.
Demonstrates a destination or aimed-for direction as in example

content: , and the aimed-for future target as in example
. Demonstrates the target at which an action is aimed, as in the case of example

content.content: 【むしろ】
1. むしろ

content: じゃましようと思っているわけではない。むしろ君たちに協力したいと思っているのだ。

content.content: I wasn’t thinking of getting in the way. Rather, I wanted to work with you guys.

content: A:総選挙からこっち、景気はよくなりましたか。

content.content: Have business conditions improved since the general election?
B:そうですね。むしろ前より悪くなったんじゃないですか。
Hmm. I should say they have actually worsened.

content: 景気はよくなるどころか、むしろ悪くなってきている。

content.content: Far from improving, business conditions are actually deteriorating.
Expresses the meaning that, when comparing two things, if pushed to say, one is more X than the other.
2. ...より（も）むしろ［Nより（も）むしろ］［V-る／V-ている　より（も）むしろ］

content: お盆のこむ時期には、旅行なんかするよりも、むしろ家でゆっくりしたい。

content.content: During the Obon holidays when everything’s so crowded, rather than taking a trip or something, I’d like to relax at home.

content: 大都会よりもむしろ地方の中・小都市で働きたいと考える人が増えてきている。

content.content: The number of people who want to work in a small- or medium-sized town rather than in a big city is increasing.

content: 円高のせいで、国内旅行よりもむしろ海外へ行く方が安くつくという逆転現象が起こっている。

content.content: Because of the strong yen, foreign travel has become, conversely,  cheaper than domestic tourism.

content: この点については教師よりもむしろ学生の方がよく知っている。

content.content: On this point, the students—rather than the teachers—know better.
Used in the form XよりもむしろY, this demonstrates the meaning that, if pushed to say, Y is more (something) than X.
As in examples

content: and

, rather than a simple comparison, this is often used to express the speaker’s value judgment that “if choosing one of two things, when pushed to say, the latter is better.” Expressions which demonstrate the speaker’s taste or inclination, such as ...するほうがよい, ...したい, or Nがいい／よい often come afterwards.

content.content: In examples

content: and
, the implication is “running contrary to general thought” or “running contrary to expectations.” It can be rephrased using かえって, 逆に, 反対に and so on.

content.content: 3. V-るぐらいならむしろ

content: 行きたくない大学に無理をして行くぐらいなら、むしろ働きたいと思っている。

content.content: If it’s a case of pushing myself to go to a university I don’t want to enter, I’d sooner get a job.

content: こんなに金利の安い時に貯金なんかするぐらいなら、むしろ海外旅行にでも行った方がいい。

content.content: When interest rates are this low, it would be better to go on a trip abroad or something than to save money.

content: あんな奴に援助を受けるぐらいなら、むしろ死を選ぶ。

content.content: I’d rather die than accept assistance from that sort of guy.
Used in the form XぐらいならY, this means that, for the speaker, Y is preferable to X, or that, as X is undesirable, s/he chooses Y. XくらいならY is also used.
4. ...というよりむしろ...だ

content: あの人は天才というより、むしろ努力の人です。

content.content: That person is not so much a genius as a hard worker.

content: 今回の出来事は、事故というよりむしろ人災だ。

content.content: This incident is not so much an accident as a man-made calamity.

content: 彼女は美人と言うよりむしろ可愛いという感じだ。

content.content: She is not so much beautiful as she is cute.
Used as a comparative expression or judgment of a thing. It means “you could say X/see (the thing) in X way but, to say Y/to see (the thing) in Y way is more appropriate.”
【むやみに】

content: 人の物にむやみにさわらないほうがいい。

content.content: You shouldn’t handle other people’s things so freely.

content: 山で道に迷ったときはむやみに歩き回らないほうがいい。

content.content: When you lose the path in the mountains, it is better not to wander around aimlessly.

content: たとえ小さな虫でも、むやみに殺してはいけない。

content.content: Even if it’s a small insect, it is wrong to kill it recklessly.

content: 最近、父は年のせいか、むやみに怒る。

content.content: Recently, probably because of his age, my father gets angry for no reason.
Shows the condition of doing something without thinking of the consequences or results.  Prohibitive phrases such as するな, してはいけない and しない方がよい or するのはよくない are often used after this. Also,

content: demonstrates the passing of time. むやみやたらに is a more emphatic way of expressing this. The form むやみと can also be used.

content.content: 【むり】
1. むり

content: 無理を言わないでよ。

content.content: Don’t be unreasonable.

content: 無理なことをお願いしてすみません。

content.content: I’m sorry for making such an unreasonable request.

content: 若い時とは違って無理がきかない。

content.content: I can’t overdo it like I could when I was young.
Means “an unreasonable thing” or “a thing which goes too far.” Example

content: is a set phrase meaning “unable to bear an excessively heavy burden.”

content.content: 2. ...はむりだ

content: 一日に新しい漢字を 50 も覚えるのは無理だ。

content.content: Remembering fifty new Chinese characters a day is impossible.

content: その仕事は子供には無理ですよ。

content.content: That work is impossible for a child.

content: A:これ、明日までに修理してもらえますか。

content.content: Can you fix this by tomorrow?
B:明日ですか、ちょっと無理ですね。
Tomorrow? No, that’s impossible.
Means something will be difficult, extremely troublesome, or impossible.
3. ...にはむりがある

content: 今度の計画には無理がある。

content.content: This plan isn’t feasible.

content: この工事を3か月で完成させるというのには無理がある。

content.content: It is not possible to complete this construction work within three months.

content: 君の考え方には無理があるよ。

content.content: There are flaws in your way of thinking.
Expresses the meaning that there are points which cannot be actualized, or that there are points which are unreasonable.
4. むりに

content: A:かばんが壊れちゃった。

content.content: My bag broke.
B:そんな小さなかばんに無理に詰め込むからだよ。
It’s because you overstuffed such a small bag.

content: このスーツケースは、鍵を壊して無理に開けようとするとブザーがなるようになっています。

content.content: If this suitcase has its lock broken and is forced open, a buzzer sounds.

content: いやがる友人を無理につれて行った。

content.content: She forced her friend, who was protesting, to go with her.

content: 行きたくなければ、無理に行くことはない。

content.content: If you don’t want to, you don’t have to go.

content: 彼がいやがっても、無理にでも連れて行くつもりだ。

content.content: Even if he doesn’t want to come with me, I am going to bring him along no matter what.
