Expresses a situation in which someone is forced to do something they cannot or do not want to do.
5. むりをする

content: 無理をすると体をこわしますよ。

content.content: If you overdo it, your health will suffer.

content: 夜遅くまで勉強するのもいいが、試験も近いのに、今無理をして病気にでもなったら大変だよ。

content.content: All very well to study late into the night, but as the exam is close, it would be terrible if you got sick now from pushing yourself too far.

content: あの会社は不動産取引でかなり無理をしていたようです。

content.content: That company seems to have considerably overextended itself in its real estate transactions.
Expresses the meaning that (someone) is forced to do something difficult or which (they) cannot do.
6. ...のもむりもない...のもむり（は）ない

content: あんなひどいことを言われては、彼が怒るのも無理はない。

content.content: He cannot help but get angry to have such hurtful things said about him.

content: うちの子は遊んでばかりいる。あんなに遊んでばかりいては成績が悪いのも無理はない。

content.content: My child does nothing but play. No wonder his grades are poor.

content: A:仕事をする気になれないなあ。

content.content: I just can’t get in the mood to work.
B:こんなに暑くちゃ、無理ないよ。
When it’s this hot, it’s no wonder.
Connected to a phrase detailing a circumstance, this expresses the feeling that the circumstance is natural. The reason why it is thought to be natural is often given at the same time. As in example

content: , ...のも can be omitted.

content.content: 【めく】［Nめく］

content: 少しずつ春めいてきた。

content.content: Little by little it became spring-like.

content: どことなく謎めいた女性がホールの入り口に立っていた。

content.content: A woman with something of a mysterious air was standing in the entrance of the hall.

content: 彼は、皮肉めいた言い方をした。

content.content: He spoke cynically.

content: 彼の作り物めいた笑いが、気になった。

content.content: I was worried by his forced smile.
Attached to a noun, this expresses that “(something) has that element to (it).” For example, in

content: it is used around the end of winter to express that the weather is gradually becoming more like spring. The nouns which can be used with this are restricted. When it is used to modify a noun it is used in the form NめいたN, as in examples
and

content.content: 【めぐって】［Nをめぐって］

content: 憲法の改正をめぐって国会で激しい論議が闘わされている。

content.content: Fierce debates are being fought in the Diet surrounding the revision of the constitution.

content: 彼の自殺をめぐって様々なうわさや憶測が乱れとんだ。

content.content: There are various rumors and speculation surrounding his suicide.

content: 人事をめぐって、社内は険悪な雰囲気となった。

content.content: An ugly atmosphere has developed within the company concerning personnel.
Means “relating to...” or “concerning....” Used to include the peripheral circumstances of a thing and to take them as the subject. Unlike ...について, there are many verbs with which it cannot be used.
（×）日本の経済をめぐって研究しています。
I am researching the Japanese economy.
（○）日本の経済について研究しています。
I am researching the Japanese economy.

Only verbs such as 議論する (to argue), 議論を闘わす (to have a heated debate), うわさが流れる (to be rumored) and 紛糾する (to become complicated) can be used with めぐる, and the nouns must be something that various people can argue about or discuss. をめぐり is often used in writing. When it is used to modify a noun, the form becomes NをめぐるN or NをめぐってのN.
（例）政治献金をめぐる疑惑がマスコミに大きくとりあげられている。
Suspicions surrounding political donations have been widely reported by the mass media.
（例）父親の遺産をめぐっての争いは、日増しにひどくなっていった。
The quarrels over their father’s inheritance were getting worse by the day.
【めったに】
1. めったに...ない

content: 私は酒はめったに飲まない。

content.content: I seldom drink alcohol.

content: うちの子は丈夫でめったに病気もしない。

content.content: Our child is in good health and rarely gets sick.

content: 人混みは好きではないので、東京や大阪などの大都市にはめったに行かない。

content.content: I don’t like crowds of people and so I rarely go to big cities like Tokyo or Osaka.

content: この頃の機械は優秀で故障はめったにない。

content.content: Appliances these days are well-made and so rarely break down.

content: わが家はずいぶん田舎にあるので、お客がやって来ることはめったにない。

content.content: Our house is in a pretty rural area, so we rarely have guests dropping by.

content: 学生時代の友人とも遠く離れてしまって、めったに会うこともない。

content.content: I rarely meet friends from my university days because we live so far apart.

content: 近頃は町中で野生の小動物を見かけるようなこともめったになくなった。

content.content: Nowadays you rarely catch sight of small wild animals in town anymore.
Expresses that the frequency with which something is done is extremely low. Often used in the form めったにV-ない, as in examples

content: , or in the form ...はめったにない, as in examples
and

content.content: たまに also expresses low frequency, but the point of emphasis is different. For example, both

content: and
below mean “alcohol is consumed very infrequently” but the めったに...ない in example
emphasizes the low frequency. In contrast, たまに in example
expresses that, although the frequency is low, it does take place.

content.content: （例1）私は酒はめったに飲みません。
I rarely drink alcohol.
（例2）私は酒は嫌いですが、友だちに誘われたときなど、たまには飲むこともあります。
I don’t like alcohol but, when I am invited by a friend, for example, I occasionally do drink it.
For these phrases, frequency decreases in this order: あまり...ない > ほとんど／めったに...ない > ぜんぜん／まったく...ない.
2. めったな

content: めったなことで驚かない私も、そのときばかりはさすがにうろたえてしまった。

content.content: I am usually not surprised by things, but even so, I lost my cool just at that moment.

content: A:山下さんが盗ったんじゃない？

content.content: Didn’t Yamashita-san steal it?
B:しっ。証拠もないのに、めったなことを言うもんじゃないよ。
Shh! There’s no evidence of that, so don’t say such things.

content: この機械は丈夫ですから、めったなことでは故障しません。

content.content: This appliance is so durable it hardly ever breaks down.

content: このことは、めったな人に話してはいけない。

content.content: You shouldn’t talk of this to just anyone.
An idiomatic expression. Used in the form of めったなことで（は）...ない, it expresses that “unless there is a set of extreme circumstance/conditions, the event/action in question does not take place.” Example

content: means “generally not surprised, can take most things calmly” and
means “it is wrong to say irresponsible/imprudent things.”

content.content: Use of the form めったなN, as in example

content: , is becoming rare. Means “it is wrong to talk (of this) to people other than a select (few/group).”

content.content: 1. Nも〈cumulative increase〉a. Nも

content: A:なんだか、すごく疲れました。

content.content: Phew, I’m really tired.
B:ええ、私もです。
Yeah, me, too.

content: 東京へ行くので、帰りに静岡にも寄って来る。

content.content: As I’m going to Tokyo, I’ll also stop off in Shizuoka on the way home.

content: 今日も雨だ。

content.content: Today’s another rainy day.

content: 私のアパートは日当りが悪い。そのうえ、風通しも良くない。

content.content: My apartment doesn’t get much sun. On top of that, the ventilation is also poor.

content: 今日は風が強いし、雨も降りだしそうだ。

content.content: Today it is windy, and it also looks like rain.
Used to add something to another thing of the same type. There are also cases such as example

content: where an assumption of similarity is made but its existence is only hinted at. It is not always attached directly to a noun, but as in
, it can also be attached to a noun plus a particle.

content.content: b. NもNも

content: セルソさんもイサベラさんもペルーの人です。

content.content: Both Celso-san and Isabella-san are from Peru.

content: 山下さんも田中さんも、英語はあまり得意じゃないでしょう。

content.content: Neither Yamashita-san nor Tanaka-san seems to be very good at English.

content: 空港までは電車でもバスでも行ける。

content.content: You can get to the airport by both train and bus.

content: 田中さんにも山下さんにも連絡しておきました。

content.content: I have contacted both Tanaka-san and Yamashita-san.

content: A:田中さんか森本さんを呼んできてくれない？

content.content: Will you call Tanaka-san or Morimoto-san?
B:田中さんも森本さんもまだ出社していないんですけれど。
I’m afraid neither Tanaka-san nor Morimoto-san has arrived at work yet.

content: 雨も降ってきたし、風も強くなってきました。

content.content: Rain started to fall and the wind grew strong, too.

content: 金もないし、暇もない。

content.content: I have neither money nor time.

content: 猫が好きな人もいるし、嫌いな人もいる。

content.content: There are people who love cats as well as people who hate them.
Used to enumerate and pick out two things of the same kind. It is not always attached directly to a noun but, as in examples

content: and
, can also be attached to a noun plus a particle.

content.content: 2. ...も...も〈antithetical phrases〉a. ...も...も...ない［NもNも...ない］［Na もNa もない］［A-くもA-くもない］［R-もR-もしない］

content: 寒くも暑くもなく、ちょうどいい気候だ。

content.content: It isn’t cold and it isn’t hot—the climate is just right.

content: 成績は上がりも下がりもしない。現状維持だ。

content.content: Results aren’t going up or down. The status quo is being maintained.

content: 趣味で音楽をやるのに上手も下手もない。

content.content: My hobby is music, but I’m not particularly good or bad at it.

content: 今はな、長男も次男もない時代だな。

content.content: Now is an age where there’s no difference between a first and second son.

content: 最近は男も女もない時代だ。

content.content: Nowadays, we live in an age where it doesn’t matter if you’re a man or a woman.

content: あまりの強さに手も足もでない（＝どうしようもない）。

content.content: Because (the opponent) is so strong there is nothing I can do (to counteract that).

content: 根も葉もない（＝根拠のない）噂をたてられる。

content.content: A groundless rumor was started.

content: 私は逃げも隠れもしない。文句があったら、いつでも来なさい。

content.content: I’ll neither run nor hide. If you’ve got a complaint, come to me anytime.
Picks out pairs such as “cold/hot” and “hands/legs” and means “neither (of them).” It is often used in idiomatic or set phrases such as にっちもさっちもいかない (a situation about which nothing can be done).
（例）今回の事件はにっちもさっちもいかない状態だ。
Nothing can be done about this incident.
b. V-るもV-ないもない

content: A:すみません。十日までにはできそうもありません。

content.content: I’m sorry. There’s no possibility that it can be done by the 10th.
B:何を言ってるんだ。いまさら、できるもできないもないだろう。やってもらわないと困るよ。
What are you saying?! By now it’s not a case of can or cannot. If you don’t get it done, it will be a big problem!

content: A:すみませんでした。許してください。

content.content: I’m sorry, please forgive me.
B:許すも許さないもない。君の責任じゃないんだから。
It’s not a question of forgiveness. It’s not your fault in the first place.

content: A:ご主人、単身赴任なさるんですって？ 賛成なさったんですか。

content.content: Your husband is going to be transferred by himself? Have you agreed to this?
B:賛成するもしないもないんですよ。全部一人で決めてしまってから、言うんですから。
I can’t agree or disagree. He told me after he’d already decided everything by himself.

content: A:反対なさるんじゃないかと心配しているんですが。

content.content: I’m worried that you may oppose it.
B:反対するもしないもない。喜んで応援するよ。
It’s not a question of opposing (it) or not. I’ll happily back you up.

Using repetition of the same verb, this means “it’s not a question of (doing) or (not doing).” Repeating part of the other person’s words, it is used to strongly repudiate them or to strongly rebuke the person for saying such things.
c. ...もなにもない

content: 愛もなにもない乾いた心に潤いが戻ってきた。

content.content: Emotion returned to what had been a loveless, empty heart.

content: 政治倫理も何もない政界には、何を言っても無駄だ。

content.content: In a political world with no ethics or anything, whatever you say is pointless.

content: 母:テレビを消して、手伝ってちょうだい。

content.content: Mother: Turn off the television and help me.
子供: だってぇ、今いいところなんだもん。
Child: But, this is a good part right now.
母:だってもなにもありません。すぐ来なさい。
Mother: No buts. Come here now.

content: A:被害状況をよく調べましてから、救助隊を派遣するかどうか決定したいと考えております。

content.content: I want to determine whether or not to dispatch a rescue team after inspecting the damage carefully.
B:何を言っているんだ。調べるも何もないだろう。これだけけが人が出ているんだから。
What are you saying?! There’s no point in an inspection. There are so many injured persons.

content: A:反対なさるんじゃないかと心配しているんですが。

content.content: I am worried that you might oppose it...
B:反対するもなにもない。喜んで応援するよ。
Opposed? That’s nonsense! Of course, I will gladly support you.
Used to strengthen a negation. In examples

content: and
, when attached to a noun, it demonstrates the meaning that “not only one thing but another thing also is lacking” and, therefore, emphasizes that lack. In examples
to
, repeating part of the other person’s words, it is used to strongly repudiate them or to strongly rebuke the person for saying such things. The same usage rules apply as to V-るもV-ないもない.

content.content: d. ...も...も［V-るも　V-る／V-ない　も］

content: 行くも止まるも君の心一つです。

content.content: Whether you go or stay is entirely up to you.

content: 行くも行かないもあなたしだいです。

content.content: Whether you go or not, it’s up to you.

content: 成功するもしないも努力しだいだ。

content.content: Whether you succeed or not, it depends on your effort.

content: 勝つも負けるも時の運だ。

content.content: Winning or losing is all down to the luck of the moment.

Used with pairs of opposites, like 行く・行かない (to go/not to go) and 勝つ・負ける (to win/to lose), and followed by expressions like Xしだいだ and Xにかかっている. Means “which one you choose depends on X” or “whatever comes to pass, X will decide it.”
3. 極端な事例+も［N（+助詞）も］［V-るのも］

content: 日本語をはじめて1年になりますが、まだひらがなも書けません。

content.content: It’s been a year since I started Japanese, but I still can’t even write hiragana.

content: スミスさんは、かなり難しい漢字も読めます。

content.content: Smith-san can read some pretty difficult Chinese characters.

content: こんな簡単な仕事は子供にもできる。

content.content: Even a child can do such an easy job.

content: 恐ろしくて、声もでませんでした。

content.content: I was terrified and couldn’t make even a sound.

content: 立っていることもできないほど疲れました。

content.content: I was so tired I couldn’t even remain standing.

content: あんな奴は顔を見るのも嫌だ。

content.content: I hate that guy so much that I can’t even look at his face!

content: 最悪の場合も考えておいたほうがよい。

content.content: You’d better prepare yourself for the worst, just in case.

content: 頭が痛いときには、小さな音でさえもがまんできない。

content.content: When my head hurts I can’t stand even a small noise.

content: 人類は月にまでも行くことができるようになった。

content.content: Mankind has even made it to the moon.
By putting forward an extreme example, this suggests that naturally a thing which is (something) to a lesser degree than that is also the case. For example, in example

content: as they can’t write the easiest script, hiragana, the implication is that of course they cannot write the more difficult katakana and Chinese characters. Also, as in examples
and
, the meaning is strengthened by using it together with さえ and まで.

content.content: 4. 数量詞+もa. 数量詞+も

content: 雨はもう三日も降っています。

content.content: It’s already been raining for three days.

content: 大根一本が 300 円もするなんて...。

content.content: 300 yen for just one daikon (Japanese white radish) !

content: 反戦デモには十万人もの人が参加した。

content.content: As many as 100,000 people took part in the anti-war demonstration.

content: いっぺんにビールを 20 本も飲むなんて、あいつはどうかしているよ。

content.content: That guy must be crazy, drinking twenty beers in one sitting.

content: ほしいけれど、10 万円もするなら、買えない。

content.content: I want it, but if it costs 100,000 yen, I can’t buy it.

content: 新しい車を買おうと思って貯金を始めたが、目標までまだ50 万円も足りない。

content.content: I was thinking of buying a new car and so I started saving, but I’m still 500,000 yen short.
Used to emphasize the largeness of a quantity or the extent or degree of something.
b. 数量詞+も...ない

content: 泳ぐのは苦手で、ほんの5mも泳げない。

content.content: I’m bad at swimming and can’t swim even just five meters.

content: ここからあそこまで10 mもないだろう。

content.content: I don’t think it’s even ten meters from here to there.

content: 財布の中には、500 円も残っていない。

content.content: I don’t even have 500 yen left in my wallet.

content: ベッドに入って 10 分もたたないうちに寝てしまった。

content.content: I went to bed and fell asleep before even ten minutes had passed.

Used to emphasize the sense of the smallness of a quantity or the lowness of a degree. Care must be taken not to confuse the rules of usage for this with those for Usage 4a of も, which emphasizes a high level of degree.
（例）こんな豪勢な暮らしをしていて、わずか 10 万円も支払えないのか。（程度小）
Living in this kind of luxury, can’t you even pay 100,000 yen? (a small amount for a rich person)
（例）学生の身分で月々 10 万円も支払えるはずがない。（程度大）
You can’t spend 100,000 yen a month when you’re (just) a student. (a large amount for a student)
c. 最小限の数量+も...ない

content: 客はひとりも来なかった。

content.content: Not even one guest came.

content: 彼女のことは一日も忘れたことはない。

content.content: Not a day goes by when I don’t think of her.

content: 外国へは一回も行ったことがない。

content.content: I haven’t been abroad even once.

content: 失敗は彼が原因だったが、彼を責めようとする人はひとりもいなかった。

content.content: It was his fault that they failed, but not one person blamed him for it.

content: この料理は少しもおいしくない。

content.content: This food is not even a little tasty.
Attached to “one (person/thing/time)” or used together with phrases which deny that there is even a little of something, this means “absolutely not.../ not at all....”
d. 数量詞+も　...ば／...たら

content: この仕事なら、三日もあれば充分だ。

content.content: Three days should be enough for this job.

content: A:ICレコーダーって、いくらぐらいするものですか。

content.content: About how much is a digital voice recorder?
B:そうですねえ、安いものなら、五千円もあれば買えますよ。
Hmm, if you want a cheap one, you can buy one for just 5,000 yen.

content: もうしばらく待ってください。 10分もしたら、先生は戻っていらっしゃると思います。

content.content: Please wait a little longer. I think the doctor will return in about ten minutes.

content: 雨はだんだん小降りになってきた。あと 10 分もすればきれいに晴れ上がるだろう。

content.content: The rain is letting up. I bet it will clear up beautifully in another ten minutes.

content: このあたりは、自然が豊かだが、もう 10 年もたてば、開発されてしまうだろう。

content.content: This area has rich natural beauty, but in another ten years it will probably end up being developed.

This shows that there is a sufficient quantity or degree of something for a certain thing to take place. たら and と can also be used in place of ば. Furthermore, sentence endings such asだろう, でしょう and と思う, which express the speaker’s conjecture, are often used with this expression.
e. 数量詞+も...か

content: 事故にあってから、救出されるまで1時間もあったでしょうか、夢中だったのでよくわかりません。

content.content: After the accident, I think I waited about an hour to be rescued, but as I was dazed I can’t be sure.

content: A:その魚はどれくらいの大きさでしたか。

content.content: How big was the fish?
B:そうですねえ。50 cmもあったかなあ。
Hmm, I guess it was about fifty centimeters.

content: 昔、家の庭に大きな木があった。高さは4、5mもあっただろうか。杉か何かだったと思う。

content.content: A long time ago there was a large tree in my family’s yard. It must have been about four or five meters tall. I think it was a cedar or something.

content: 直径3センチもあろうかという氷の固まりが降ってきた。

content.content: Chunks of ice with a diameter of as much as three centimeters fell.
Often used with phrases such as あったでしょうか and あろうか. Expresses the speaker’s subjective judgment about a quantity.
5. 疑問詞+もa. 疑問詞（+助詞）+も

content: 山田さんはいつも本を読んでいる。

content.content: Yamada-san is always reading books.

content: だれもが知っている。

content.content: Everyone knows.

content: どれもみんなすばらしい。

content.content: They’re all wonderful.

content: どちらも正しい。

content.content: Either is correct.

content: 誰も知らない。

content.content: Nobody knows.

content: このことは誰にも話さないでください。

content.content: Please don’t speak to anyone about this.

content: 何も買えない。

content.content: I can’t buy anything.

content: この辞書はどれも役にたたない。

content.content: None of these dictionaries is any good.

content: どちらも正しくない。

content.content: Neither is correct.
Used with terms such as だれ (who), なに (what), どれ (which), どこ (where), and いつ (when), this expresses that, whatever the case may be, the statement applies. As in examples

content: , in an affirmative sentence, the whole is affirmative, and in negative sentences, like
, the whole is negative. However, いくらもある, which comes next, expresses that there are a lot, while いくらもない expresses that there is almost none.

content.content: （例）そんな話はいくらもある。
There are many such stories.
（例）財布の中には、いくらも入っていない。
There is almost nothing in my purse.
b. なん+助数詞+も

content: タイには何人も友だちがいる。

content.content: I have lots of friends in Thailand.

content: 何回も海外旅行をしたことがある。

content.content: I have been abroad many times.

content: 何度もノックしたが、返事がない。

content.content: I knocked many times but there was no answer.

content: 雨は何日も降り続いた。

content.content: The rain continued for many days.

content: 何か月も留守にしたので、庭は荒れ放題だ。

content.content: Because I’ve been away for many months, the garden has gone to seed.
Expresses that there is a large quantity or high frequency of something.
c. なん+助数詞+も...ない

content: この問題が解ける人は何人もいないでしょう。

content.content: There are few people who can solve this problem.

content: 私の国では、雨が降る日は一年に何日もない。

content.content: In my country, there are few days in a year when it rains.

content: すぐに終わります。何分もかかりません。

content.content: I will finish soon. It should take no more than a few minutes.

content: こんなチャンスは、人生に何度もない。

content.content: This is a once in a lifetime kind of chance.
Expresses that there is a small quantity or low frequency of something. Care must be taken, as in certain cases this may be used to express a large quantity, as seen in example 2 below.
（例1）試験まで後何日もない。（＝短い間）
The test isn’t many days off. (short duration)
（例2）彼は何ヵ月も姿を見せなかった。（＝長い間）
I haven’t seen him around for months. (long duration)
6. Nも〈topic〉

content: 秋も深まって、紅葉が美しい。

content.content: Fall has deepened, and the foliage is beautiful.

content: 夜もふけた。

content.content: It is (now) late in the evening.

content: 長かった夏休みも終わって、あしたからまた学校が始まります。

content.content: The long summer holiday is finishing and from tomorrow school will start again.

content: 彼にも困ったものだ。

content.content: He is troublesome.

content: さっきまであんなに泣いていた赤ん坊もようやく寝ました。

content.content: The baby that was crying so much until a moment ago has finally fallen asleep.

content: 彼のきげんも直って、平和な空気が戻った。

content.content: His mood improved and a peaceful atmosphere returned.
As in examples

content: , this expresses the speaker’s deep emotion regarding a change which occurs together with the passing of time, the beginning or ending of something, or the changing of the seasons. As in
, where there is a hint of another similar thing, this is used to soften the presentation of something.

content.content: 7. NもN〈emphasis〉

content: あいつは、うそつきもうそつき、大うそつきだ。

content.content: That guy’s the king of liars, nothing but a big liar!

content: 彼の両親の家は、山奥も山奥、一番近い駅から車で3時間もかかるところにある。

content.content: His parents’ house is way in the mountains. And I mean really far—from the nearest station it takes three hours by car.

content: A:佐藤さん、酒飲みなんですって？

content.content: Sato-san is a heavy drinker, you say?
B:酒飲みも酒飲み、ものすごい酒飲みだ。
A drinker among drinkers—he really puts it away!
Repeats the same noun so as to emphasize that the degree being talked about is not usual.
8. NもNならNもNだが

content: 親も親なら子も子だね。

content.content: With parents like that, no wonder the kids are the way they are!

content: 兄さんも兄さんだが、姉さんだってひどいよ。

content.content: The older brother is as he is, but his sister is horrible!

content: わいろをもらう政治家も政治家だが、それを贈る企業も企業だ。

content.content: Politicians will accept bribes and corporations will give them.
Used in the form XもXならYもYだ, this expresses critically that both X and Y have problems.
9. ...もあり...もある［NでもありNでもある］［Na でもありNa でもある］［A-くもありA-くもある］

content: 彼はこの会社の創始者でもあり、今の社長でもある。

content.content: He is not only the founder of this company, but also the present company president.

content: 藤田さんは私の義兄でもあり師でもある。

content.content: Fujita-san is both my brother-in-law and my teacher.

content: 彼の言ったことは、心外でもあり不愉快でもある。

content.content: What he said was both regrettable and unpleasant.

content: 娘の結婚は、嬉しくもありさみしくもある。

content.content: There is both happiness and sadness at the wedding of a daughter.
In the form XもありYもある, this means that someone or something is X as well as Y.
0. ...もあれば...もある［NもあればNもある］［VこともあればVこともある］

content: 起きる時間は決まっていない。早く起きることもあれば遅く起きることもある。

content.content: I don’t have a set time to get up. There are times when I get up early and times when I get up late.

content: 人生、楽もあれば苦もある。

content.content: Life has both easy times and hard times.

content: 株価の変動は誰にも分からない。上がることもあれば、下がることもある。

content.content: Nobody can foresee the fluctuations in stock prices. They go up and they go down.

content: 車に乗っていると、便利な時もあれば、不便な時もある。

content.content: Traveling by car is sometimes convenient and sometimes inconvenient.

content: 温泉といってもいろいろだ。硫黄が含まれているものもあれば、炭酸が含まれているものもある。

content.content: There are various kinds of hot springs. There are those which are sulfurous and those which have carbonic acid in them.
Shows the variation in something and expresses that there are different cases. It is often used to enumerate contrasting things.
1. ...もV-ない［NもV-ない］［R-もしない］

content: あいつは本当に失礼な奴だ。道であっても、挨拶もしない。

content.content: He really is rude, that guy. He doesn’t even greet me if we meet on the street.

content: 息子は体のぐあいでも悪いのか、夕食に手もつけない。

content.content: Our son must be sick or something. He won’t even touch his dinner.

content: あの子は、ほんとうに強情だ。あんなにひどく叱られても、泣きもしない。

content.content: That child is really stubborn. He doesn’t even cry after being scolded like that.

content: 前から気がついていたのか、母は父が会社をやめたと聞いても驚きもしなかった。

content.content: Mother must have realized beforehand, because she wasn’t even surprised when she heard that Father had left the company.

content: うちの猫は魚がきらいで、さしみをやっても見向きもしない。

content.content: My cat doesn’t like fish and even turns her nose up at sashimi(raw fish).

content: さわりもしないのに、ガラスのコップが割れてしまった。

content.content: I didn’t even touch it, but the glass cup broke.

content: 夕方になっても、電気もつけないで、本に熱中していた。

content.content: Although evening came, I was so absorbed in my book that I didn’t even turn the light on.

content: 山田さんは怒ったのか、さよならも言わないで帰ってしまった。

content.content: Yamada-san must be angry. He went home without even saying goodbye.

content: この寒いのに、子供たちは、上着も着ないで、走り回っている。

content.content: It’s this cold, and yet the children are running around without even their coats on.
Used to emphasize a negative. Often used to express the speaker’s surprise or shock that what would usually be expected is not done or does not happen.
2. ...もV-ずに

content: わたしは深く考えもせず、失礼なことを言ってしまった。

content.content: Without thinking very much, I said something rude.

content: 彼女は食事もとらずに、けが人の看病をしている。

content.content: She continues nursing the injured without taking any food.

content: 彼女は、若い女性が興味を持ちそうなことにはいっさい目もくれず、研究に没頭していた。

content.content: Without taking any interest in the things that interest young women, she immersed herself in research.
A way of saying ...もしないで (without doing...) that has the tone of written language.
3. ...もの／...こと　もV-ない［V-る　もの／こと　もV-ない］

content: 寝坊したので、食べるものも食べないであわてて会社へ行った。

content.content: Because I had overslept, I rushed to the office without eating anything.

content: 急に雨が降り出したので、買うものも買わないで帰ってきてしまった。

content.content: Because it suddenly started to rain, I came home without buying the things I meant to buy.

content: 時間が足りなかったので、言いたいことも十分には言えなかった。

content.content: Because there wasn’t enough time, I couldn’t say everything I had wanted to.

content: こんな無能な医者では助かる命も助からない。

content.content: This kind of incompetent doctor couldn’t save a life.
Repeating the same verb, this means “cannot do (something) that would usually be possible.” There is also the following idiomatic expression.
（例）叔父が急に亡くなったというので、取るものも取りあえず（＝大急ぎで）駆けつけた。
My uncle died suddenly and so, without a moment’s delay (in a big hurry), we rushed to be there.
【もう1】
1. もう+数量詞

content: すみません、もう5分ここにいてください。

content.content: Excuse me, please wait here another five minutes.

content: もう一時間待って、彼が来なかったら先に行く。

content.content: I’ll wait another hour and then, if he doesn’t come, I’ll go on ahead.

content: もう一人紹介したい人がいる。

content.content: There’s one more person I’d like to introduce.

content: もう百円あれば、切符が買える。

content.content: If you had 100 yen more, you could buy a ticket.

content: もう 10 ページ読めば、この本は読み終えられる。

content.content: If you read another ten pages, you can finish this book.

content: もう一回だけテストしてみよう。

content.content: Let’s try the test just once more.

content: もう一度だけ会ってください。

content.content: Please meet him just one more time.

content: みんなが来てから、もう一回先生に電話してみた。

content.content: After everyone had arrived, I tried to call the teacher one more time.
This is used to add further quantities to something. For example,

content: means “You have some money but if you could add 100 yen to it, you would be able to buy a ticket.”

content.content: Often used as another way of saying あと, as in あと5分. However, あと also includes the meaning “This is the last of what remains,” but もう does not particularly carry that meaning. In situations where it is difficult to say this is the last (time), もう is used rather than あと. For example,みんなが来てからあと一回先生に電話してみた is somewhat unnatural.
2. もうすこしa. もうすこし／もうちょっと〈quantity〉

content: もう少し、ミルクをください。

content.content: Could I have a little more milk, please.

content: もう少しここで過ごしたい。

content.content: I want to stay here a little longer.

content: もう少し待てば、順番が回ってくる。

content.content: If you wait a little longer, your turn will come.

content: ゴールまで、もうちょっとだ。

content.content: It’s just a little bit more to the goal.

Expresses a small fluctuation or change in the current situation. あとすこし is also used. Moreover, asもうちょっと is less formal than もうすこし, it is more commonly used in daily conversation. This cannot be used in cases where the quantity is large.
（×）もうたくさんほしい。
I want more.
（○）もっとたくさんほしい。
I want more.
b. もうすこし／もうちょっと〈degree〉

content: もう少しいい車を買いたい。

content.content: I want to buy a slightly better car.

content: 温度はもう少し低くした方がいい。

content.content: You’d better bring the temperature down a little.

content: もう少し大きな声で話したほうがいい。

content.content: You ought to speak a little more loudly.

content: かれなら、もう少しむずかしい問題もできるだろう。

content.content: As for him, I think he could handle slightly more difficult problems.

content: もうちょっと安いものはありませんか。

content.content: Don’t you have anything a little cheaper?
Used with expressions which show an attribute or condition, this demonstrates a slightly higher degree than the present condition.
c. もうすこしでV-そうだった

content: もう少しでうまくいきそうだったのに、邪魔が入ってしまった。

content.content: Everything was just about to work out well when a wrench was thrown into the works.

content: もう少しで会社に遅れそうになったが、ぎりぎりで間にあった。

content.content: It seemed I was going to be late for work, but I made it just in time.

content: もう少しで本当のことを言いそうになったが、何とか我慢した。

content.content: I was so close to telling the true story, but somehow managed to keep my self-control.

content: 二人はもう少しでけんかしそうになったが、わたしが何とか止めた。

content.content: The two of them seemed close to getting into a fight, but somehow I stopped them.
Means “a certain situation is on the verge of occurring.” もう少しで...ところだ is often used instead. In casual conversation もうちょっとで is also used.
d. もうすこしでV-るところだった

content: もう少しでけがするところだった。

content.content: I was almost injured.

content: ぼんやり歩いていて、もう少しで車にひかれるところだった。

content.content: I was walking along absentmindedly and almost got hit by a car.

content: 赤ちゃんはもう少しで寝るところだったのに、電話の音で目をさましてしまった。

content.content: The baby was just about to fall asleep, but the phone rang and she opened her eyes.

content: 実験はまた失敗したが、本当はもう少しで成功するところだったのだ。

content.content: The experiment failed again, but the truth is that we were close to succeeding.
This is a way of intensifying V-るところだった.
【ところだ】2b
【もう2】
1. もう〈completion〉

content: 今日の仕事はもう全部終わった。

content.content: Today’s work is all done.

content: A:今評判になっているあの映画、もう見ましたか。

content.content: Have you seen that film that everyone’s talking about now?
B:ええ、この前の日曜日に見ました。
Yes, I watched it last Sunday.

content: 食事はもうできている。

content.content: Dinner is ready.

content: その問題なら、もう解決している。

content.content: That problem? It’s been resolved already.

content: 彼の娘はもう大学を卒業したそうだ。

content.content: I heard that his daughter has already graduated from college.

content: 駅についたときにもう特急は出てしまっていた。

content.content: When I got to the station, the limited express had already left.

content: 手紙はもう投函したので、取り返せないんです。

content.content: I have already mailed the letter, so I can’t get it back.

content: A:すみません、今日はもう閉店ですか。

content.content: Excuse me, are you already closed for today?
B:いいえ、まだ開いています。
No, we’re still open.

content: A:この本はもう出ましたか。

content.content: Is this book out yet?
B:いいえ、まだ出ていません。予定は来週です。
No, not yet. It is scheduled (to be out) next week.

When used with a verb phrase, this indicates the completion of a deed or event by a certain point in time. It is also used in interrogative sentences asking whether or not something has been completed. When the point of completion has not yet been reached, まだ...ない is used in both declarative and interrogative sentences.
2. もう　+時間／+年齢

content: おしゃべりに夢中になっていたら、もう5時だ。

content.content: We got lost in conversation and it’s already five o’clock.

content: 気がついたらもう朝だった。

content.content: Before we knew it, it was already morning.

content: この子はもう 10 才だから、十分事故の証人になれる。

content.content: This child is already ten years old, so she can serve as a witness to an accident.

content: こよみの上ではもう春なのに、まだ雪が降っている。

content.content: Although the calendar says it is spring, it is still snowing.

content: もう夜が明けるのに彼らはまだ話し続けている。

content.content: They kept on talking even though dawn was breaking.

content: もう8時ですよ。起きなさい、学校に遅れますよ。

content.content: It’s already eight o’clock. Get up, or you’ll be late for school.
Used with expressions which show time or age, it shows that a point which is rather late has been reached. As in examples

content: and
, it includes the feeling that a certain point in time has been reached sooner than was thought.

content.content: 3. もうNa だ／もういい

content: もうおなかが一杯だ。

content.content: I’m already full.

content: 今日はもう十分に楽しんだ。

content.content: I’ve already had a lot of fun today.

content: A:お湯はわいていますか。

content.content: Is the water boiling yet?
B:ええ、もういいですよ。
Yes, it’s ready.

content: A:機械、直ったんですか。

content.content: Is the machine fixed?
B:ええ、これでもういいはずです。
Yes, it should be fine now.

content: A:ちょっと目を閉じて。1、2、3。

content.content: Just shut your eyes. One, two, three.
B:もういい？
Okay now?
A:いいよ。はい、目を開けて。
Okay, open your eyes.

Used with phrases such as 一杯だ and 十分だ, this means “(it) ought to be enough/satisfactory.” もういい, basically meaning “a satisfactory situation or state has been reached,” is used in various circumstances. Depending on the context, it can mean “to have done enough,” or “to have resolved (it).” For the negative usage rules for もういい, please see Usage 5b of もう.
4. もう...ない

content: 山田さんはもうここにはいません。

content.content: Yamada-san is no longer here.

content: この喫茶店はもう営業していない。

content.content: This coffee shop is no longer in business.

content: 疲れて、もう何も考えられなくなった。

content.content: I was so tired I couldn’t think anymore.

content: 交渉のあと、だれももう文句を言わなかった。

content.content: After the negotiations, nobody had any more complaints.

content: かれとは、もうこれ以上話したくない。

content.content: I don’t want to say anything more to him.

content: わたしは、18 才、もう子供ではない。

content.content: I’m eighteen. I’m not a child anymore.

content: もう二度とあの人には会わないだろう。

content.content: I don’t suppose I’ll ever meet her again.

content: もう誰も信じられないと言って、彼女は泣いていた。

content.content: She was crying and said, “I can’t trust anyone anymore.”

content: こんな待遇の悪い職場にはもうがまんができない。

content.content: I can’t take it anymore in a workplace like this with such terrible conditions.

content: さいふの中にはもう 100 円しか残っていなかったので、家へ帰るのにバスにも乗れなかった。

content.content: Since I only had 100 yen left in my wallet, I couldn’t even catch the bus home.

content: 10 万円の値段がついたので、もうこれ以上は上がらないだろうと思った。

content.content: Because it was already priced at 100,000 yen, I didn’t think the price could go any higher.
This means, with something like a certain point in time as the limit, there is nothing further or nothing after that.
5. もう〈negative attitude〉a. もう+否定的表現

content: こんな退屈な仕事はもうやめたい。

content.content: I want to quit this kind of boring work.

content: もうあの人の愚痴を聞くのはいやだ。

content.content: I’m sick of hearing that person’s complaints.

content: これ以上歩き続けるのは体力的にもう無理です。

content.content: It’s physically impossible for me to walk any further.

content: あの人をかばい続けられるのももう限界だ。

content.content: I can’t carry on sticking up for that man.

content: 戦争をするのは、もうたくさんだ。

content.content: I’ve had it with the war.

content: こんなまずいものを食べるのはもうたくさんだ。

content.content: I can’t eat any more of such disgusting stuff.

content: もういいかげんに妹をいじめるのはやめなさい。

content.content: Stop picking on your younger sister.

Using predicates with a negative meaning such as 無理だ and いやだ, this means the situation cannot be tolerated any further. Meaning “the limit has been reached and so I can’t take anymore,” もうたくさんだ is often used when the speaker is feeling quite emotional. It can also be used in cases, such as example

content: , which prohibit further such behavior.

content.content: b. もういい

content: A:ほかに出す書類がありますか。

content.content: Do you have any other documents to hand in?
B:これでもういいです。
That’s all.

content: A:チョコレート買いましょうか。

content.content: Shall we buy some chocolate?
B:いや、これだけ食料があれば、もういいです。
No, this should be enough food.

content: A:もう一杯いかがですか。

content.content: How about one more (glass/cup)?
B:いや、もういいです。
No, I’ve had enough.

content: A:急なアルバイトさえなかったら、来られたんだけど。

content.content: If I just hadn’t had that sudden part-time work, I could have come.
B:言い訳はもういいよ。
That’s enough of your excuses.

content: A:お母さんの気持ちも考えてみなさい。

content.content: Try to think about your mother’s feelings, too.
B:もういいよ。お説教は聞き飽きたよ。
Enough! I’m tired of your preaching!

content: A:頑張っていたのに、うまく行かなくて残念だったね。

content.content: It’s such a shame that it didn’t go well even though you did your best.
B:もういいんです。何か、ほかの事を考えます。
Oh, it’s okay. I will think of something else.

content: A:もう一回探しなおせば、みつかるかもしれません。

content.content: If we have another look, we may be able to find it.
B:もういいよ。あきらめよう。
I’ve had enough! Let’s give it up.
Fundamentally this means “because this is enough, more than this is not necessary.” It is used in various circumstances. In example

content: it is used to decline something. Also, in
and
, meaning “this is the limit, I can’t accept more than this,” it conveys the speaker’s attitude of refusal. It is often used in cases in which something has become disagreeable or tedious. As in
and

, it is also used as an expression which conveys the feeling of being sick of or giving up on something which had been adhered to until that point. For the affirmative usage rules of もういい, see Usage 3 of もう.

content.content: 6. もう〈criticism〉

content: お母さんたら、もう。わたしの友達の悪口を言うのはやめてよ。

content.content: Mom, enough! Stop badmouthing my friends.

content: もう、あなたったら、こんなやさしい計算もできないの。

content.content: Oh, come on, dear. Can’t you even do a simple calculation like this?

content: 山田さんたら、もう、また「お茶入れて」ですって。自分でやればいいのに。

content.content: That Yamada-san telling me again, “Make some tea.” He should make it himself.

content: A:あ、また、汚した。

content.content: Oh, it’s dirty again.
B:もう。
Already again!

At the start or in the middle of a sentence, this expresses a feeling of criticism towards the other person. Only used in casual conversation and is often used by women. Frequently used with the highly critical (っ)たら.
【もうすぐ】

content: 田中さんはもうすぐ来ます。

content.content: Tanaka-san will arrive soon.

content: もうすぐ夏休みですね。

content.content: It’s almost summer vacation!

content: クリスマスまで、もうすぐだ。

content.content: It’s not long until Christmas.

content: 桜の花ももうすぐ咲きそうだ。

content.content: The cherry blossoms also will soon be blooming.

content: もうすぐここに30階建てのマンションが建つそうだ。

content.content: I hear that a thirty-story apartment building will soon be built here.
Expresses that there is not much time from the present until a certain thing occurs. Refers to a longer period of time than that referred to by すぐ. Often used in spoken language.
【もかまわず】［N（に）もかまわず］［Vの（に）もかまわず］

content: 喜びのあまり、人目もかまわず抱きついた。

content.content: Overwhelmed by happiness, they embraced without caring who was watching.

content: 役員たちから慎重な対応を求める声が上がっているのもかまわず、社長は新分野への参入を決断した。

content.content: Paying no heed to the cautionary voices of his staff, the company president decided to enter the new field.

content: 世論から厳しい批判を浴びせられているのにも構わず、その議員は再び立候補した。

content.content: With no regard for the harsh criticism being heaped upon her by the public, that member of the Diet announced her candidacy again.
Means “to take no notice of....” Often used in the idiomatic phrase 人目もかまわず.
【もくされている】［Nともくされている］

content: 今度の競馬では、マックイーンが一番人気と目されている。

content.content: McQueen is considered the favorite in this horse race.

content: 彼がその事件の最重要参考人と目されている。

content.content: He is considered the most important witness to that incident.

content: 事業の後継者と目されているのは、重役の市川氏だ。

content.content: Director Ichikawa-shi (Mr. Ichikawa) is recognized as the successor to the business.

content: 知事選挙で最有力候補と目されているのは、早田氏です。

content.content: Hayata-shi (Mr. Hayata) is regarded as the front-runner in the gubernatorial election.
Means “to be regarded as...,” “to have such a reputation.” However, 目されている is used in cases where the truth or what will happen is still unknown.
【もさることながら】［Nもさることながら］

content: 彼は、大学の成績もさることながら、スポーツ万能で親孝行という申し分のない息子だ。

content.content: What with his good college grades and, what’s more, his outstanding sports ability, we can’t complain at all about how good a son he is to us.

content: このドレスは、デザインもさることながら、色使いがすばらしい。

content.content: The color scheme for this dress is truly outstanding, not to mention its design.

content: あのレストランは、料理もさることながら、眺めの良さが最も印象的だった。

content.content: The food at that restaurant was impressive, but the great view was even more so.
Used in the form XもさることながらY and means “X is... but Y is even more so” or “there is X but, moreover, there is Y.” Usually used in reference to something which is thought to be positive.

【もし】With a conditional phrase following it, this expression conveys the speaker’s attitude in establishing his/her assumptions about a thing. It is often used at the beginning of a sentence. Synonyms are かりに and もしも. For the differences between this and もしも, see the entry for もしも.
1. もし...たら

content: もし雨が降ってきたら、洗濯物を取り込んでおいてね。

content.content: If it starts to rain, bring the washing in, will you?

content: もしよろしければ、週末、家にいらっしゃいませんか。

content.content: If it’s all right with you, would you come to my home this weekend?

content: もしお暇なら、いっしょにドライブに行きませんか。

content.content: If you have time, will you come for a drive with me?

content: もし気が付くのが1秒でも遅かったら大惨事になっていただろう。

content.content: If you had noticed just one second later, it would have been a huge disaster.
Phrases such as ...は／...なら can be used in place of たら. Accompanying a hypothetical situation where what follows is a result of that situation, means “supposing... then....” As in examples

content: to
, it is used to predict or imagine an event, the truth of which is pending or not yet known, and, as in
, it is used to anticipate or imagine an event which is inconsistent with reality.

content.content: This is similar to かりに, but かりに is used to suppose something which does not actually exist, while もし can be used whether or not something actually exists, but the speaker desires to make a supposition. For this reason, it can be used both in

content: , where something is likely to happen, and in
, which is contrary to the truth.

content.content: （×）かりに雨が降ってきたら、洗濯物を取り込んでおいてね。
Supposing that it should start to rain, bring the washing in, will you?
2. もし　...ても／...としても

content: 天気予報では曇りですが、もし雨でも遠足は決行します。

content.content: The weather forecast says it will be cloudy, but even if it rains, we’ll go on the field trip.

content: 薬で治りそうですが、もし手術をすることになっても、簡単に済みます。

content.content: It seems that it will get better with medicine, but, even if surgery is necessary, it’s a simple procedure.

content: もし泥棒に入られたとしたって、たいして金目になるものはない。

content.content: Even if a burglar breaks in, there is nothing of monetary value.

content: もし入社試験に合格しても、本人に入社の意志がないのなら辞退すべきだ。

content.content: Even if one passes the company entrance test, if the person has no intention of joining the company, he or she ought to turn the offer down.

Used with conditional clauses such as ても, としても, and としたって, expresses the meaning “even if such a situation should come into being.” Often carries the implication that “there is little possibility, but....” Generally かりに can be used in its place.
【もしかしたら】
1. もしかしたら...かもしれない

content: 仕事の量が減ったから、もしかしたらわたしも日曜日に出かけられるかもしれない。

content.content: My workload has lessened and so perhaps I might be able to go out on Sunday.

content: 今はいい天気だが、すこし雲が出て来たから、もしかしたら雨が降るかもしれない。

content.content: It is nice weather now, but clouds are gathering and it might rain.

content: この名刺があれば、もしかしたら、彼に面会できるかもしれない。

content.content: If I have this business card, perhaps I might be able to meet with him.

content: 彼はここ2、3日大学に出て来ない。もしかしたら彼は病気かもしれない。

content.content: He hasn’t been to college classes for two or three days. Perhaps he’s sick.

content: もしかしたら、中田さんが知っているかもしれないが、はっきりしたことはまだわからない。

content.content: Perhaps Nakata-san knows, but I’m still really not sure.

content: もしかしたら、山川さんがその本をもっているのではないだろうか。

content.content: Could Yamakawa-san maybe have that book?

When accompanied by conjectural phrases such as ...かもしれない and ...のではないだろうか, expresses the supposition that “that too might be possible.” Indicates the speaker’s lack of confidence in his/her own judgment. もしかすると, もしかして, and ひょっとすると are also used.
2. もしかしたら...か

content: A:あの人、もしかしたら、山本さんじゃないですか。

content.content: That person, might it possibly be Yamamoto-san?
B:ええ。そうですよ。ご存じですか。
Yes, it is. Do you know her?

content: もしかしたら事故にでもあったんじゃない？

content.content: Has there been an accident or something?

content: もしかしたら今日は雨になるのではないだろうか。

content.content: Don’t you think it might turn to rain today?
Used with phrases which express a question, such as ...か and じゃない？, demonstrates the speaker’s lack of confidence in his/her own judgment. もしかすると, もしかして, and ひょっとして are also used.
【もしくは】A written expression. Used in the form XもしくはY. A formal expression, often used in official documents, this is not used in everyday conversation. In daily conversation, XかY is often used.
1. NもしくはN

content: 黒もしくは青のインクを使用すること。

content.content: Black or blue ink is to be used.

content: お問い合わせは、電話もしくは往復葉書でお願いします。

content.content: For inquiries we request that either the telephone or a stamped, self-addressed postcard be used.

content: この施設は、会員もしくはその家族に限り使用できる。

content.content: Use of this establishment is restricted to members and their families.

content: 《法令》第 84 条第2項の規定による命令に違反した者は、これを6ヶ月以下の懲役もしくは禁固または一万円以下の罰金に処する。

content.content: 《laws and ordinances》Those persons in violation of Article 84, Clause 2, are punishable by a period of hard labor not exceeding six months, imprisonment, or a fine not exceeding 10,000 yen.
Means “one of the two.” Shows that, of X and Y, one must be chosen, or that, if the conditions of X or Y are met, either is fine. In

content: , its special use in legal terminology, the X of XまたはY can further be divided into two, as in XaもしくはXb. The connection then becomes XaもしくはXb、またはY.

content.content: 2. V-るか、もしくは

content: 応募書類は、5月10日までに郵送するか、もしくは持参すること。

content.content: Application documents must be either posted by the 10th of May or submitted in person.

content: パンフレットを御希望の方は、葉書で申し込むか、もしくはFAXをご利用下さい。

content.content: For a copy of the brochure, please send a request by postcard or by fax.

content: 受講申し込みは、京都市内にお住まい、もしくは京都市内に通勤なさっている方に限ります。

content.content: Applications to attend the lectures are limited to those who either live or work within the Kyoto city limits.
Means “one of two.” Examples

content: and
mean that “one of X and Y must be chosen.” Example
shows two conditions and means that it is all right if the conditions of either X or Y are met. In this case it doesn’t matter if both conditions are met. As in
, in cases where a noun which expresses movement is taken, the form NもしくはNする is used.

content.content: 【もしも】Used to further express the word もし, this means “supposing such were the case.”
1. もしも...たら

content: もしも家が買えるなら、海辺の洋館がいい。

content.content: If I could buy a house, a western-style one near the beach would be nice.

content: もしも僕が君の立場だったら、違う行動をとると思う。

content.content: If I were in your situation, I think I would behave differently.

content: もしも私が君ぐらい若ければ世界中を飛びまわっているだろう。

content.content: If I were as young as you, I think I would be travelling extensively around the world.

content: もしも地震が起こるのがあと30 分遅ければ、被害は甚大なものになっていただろう。

content.content: If the earthquake had happened thirty minutes later, the damage would probably have been enormous.

Used with conditional expressions such as たら／ば／なら, this expresses the assumption that “if such were the case,” in reference to things which may or may not become reality or which are inconsistent with the facts.
2. もしものN

content: 父にもしものことがあったらどうしよう。

content.content: If something happened to Father, what would we do?

content: もしもの場合にはすぐ連絡してください。

content.content: If something should happen, please contact me right away.

content: 大地震はそんなにちょくちょく起こるわけではないが、もしもの時のために準備をしておいた方がよい。

content.content: It’s not that major earthquakes happen so frequently, but it’s better to be prepared for such a time.

Nouns such as 時, 場合, こと come after もしも and express the meaning that “if by some chance, such a situation should be the case....” This is used in reference to such things as death, critical conditions, major disasters, and undesirable serious situations. Example

content: is a euphemistic way of talking about death. 万一 carries roughly the same meaning and can be used in this way also. もし cannot be used in this way.

content.content: 【もちまして】→
【もって2】
【もちろん】
1. もちろん

content: A:一緒に行きますか。

content.content: Shall we go together?
B:もちろん。
Of course.

content: A:そこへ行ったら、彼女に会えますか。

content.content: If I go there, can I meet her?
B:もちろんですよ。
Of course.

content: この仕事は、残業が多くなるかもしれません。もちろん、その分の給料はちゃんと支払われます。

content.content: In this job, there is likely to be a lot of overtime. Of course, you will be duly paid for that.

content: A:あの、休日は、きちんと取れるのでしょうか。

content.content: Um, is it clearly possible to take days off?
B:それは、もちろんですよ。
Yes, of course it is.

Shows that something is accepted as natural. Emphasizes that a situation will be just as expected. Also, as in the example below, used in cases where some reservation is expressed in relation to something which has just been mentioned.
（例）わたしはこの計画に賛成です。もちろん、実行できるかどうかは社長の決定を待たなければなりませんが。
I approve of this plan. Of course, we must wait for the company president’s decision on whether or not we can implement it.
（例）娘は、土曜日の午後はアルバイトをして、友達と喫茶店でおしゃべりをして帰って来ます。もちろん、いつもそうだというわけではありませんが、だいたいそういう習慣になっていたようです。

My daughter works at a part-time job on Saturday afternoons, and afterwards she chats with her friends in a coffee shop before coming home. Of course, this is not always the case, but it seems to have become her usual habit.
2. Nはもちろん

content: 彼は、英語はもちろん、ドイツ語も中国語もできる。

content.content: He of course knows English, but also can speak German and Chinese.

content: 彼は、スポーツ万能で、テニスはもちろん、ゴルフもサッカーもうまい。

content.content: He’s an excellent athlete, and so of course he’s good at tennis, but also golf and football.

content: 委員長の高田さんはもちろん、委員会の全メンバーが参加します。

content.content: Of course the committee chairman, Takada-san, will participate as will all the committee members.

content: 来週のパーティーは、いろいろな国の料理はもちろん、カラオケもダンスもある。

content.content: At next week’s party there will of course be food from various countries, but there will also be Karaoke and a dance.

content: この本は、勉強にはもちろん役に立つし、見るだけでも楽しい。

content.content: This book is of course useful for studying but it’s also fun just to look at it.

content: 彼は子供の送り迎えはもちろん、料理もせんたくも家事は何でもやる。

content.content: Of course he drops off and picks up the children, but he also cooks, does the laundry, and does all kinds of housework.
Used to point out/emphasize a noun which is representative and which is felt to be naturally included before also enumerating other things of the same type. There is also the expression もちろんのこと.
【もって1】［Nをもって］

content: 自信をもってがんばってね。

content.content: Have confidence and do your best!

content: A:しめきりが明日というレポートがみっつもあるんだ。

content.content: I have three reports with a deadline of tomorrow.
B:余裕をもってやらないからこういうことになるのよ。
This happened because you didn’t give yourself enough time.

content: わたしは、そのとき確信をもって、こう言ったんです。

content.content: At that time, I said this with conviction.

content: これは、自信をもっておすすめできる商品です。

content.content: This is a product that I can recommend with confidence.
Uses the same verb 持つ, as is used in “to hold (a thing)” and “to have/take a thing (in one’s hand)” but when used with abstract nouns such as “confidence” and “belief,” it means “with (that).”
【もって2】
1. Nをもって

content: このレポートをもって、結果報告とする。

content.content: With this report, we announce the results.

content: この書類をもって、証明書とみなす。

content.content: With this document, this is an official certificate.

content: これをもって、挨拶とさせていただきます。

content.content: (at the end of a speech) With this, I shall now conclude my remarks.
Means ...によって. Spoken language used in official meetings and conferences. Is also a formal expression used in writing in documents. Often used in sentences meaning とみなす.
2. Nをもちまして

content: 本日をもちまして当劇場は閉館いたします。

content.content: This theater will close as of today.

content: 当店は7時をもちまして閉店させていただきます。

content.content: This store will be closing as of seven o’clock.

content: これをもちまして閉会（と）させていただきます。

content.content: With these, we declare the ceremony closed.

content: 只今をもちまして受付は締め切らせていただきます。

content.content: As of now, reception is closed.
Used to inform a gathering that a period of time or a situation is to be ended. Its use is limited to formal speeches and it cannot be used in casual conversation. More polite than をもって.
【もっと】

content: もっと大きい声で話してくれませんか。

content.content: Could you speak more loudly?

content: もっと時間をかければもっといいものができると思います。

content.content: If I could take more time, I think I could do something better.

content: 地下鉄が開通すればこのあたりはもっと便利になる。

content.content: If they opened a subway, this area would become more accessible.

content: A:痛むのはこの辺ですか。

content.content: Is the pain in this area?
B:いや、もっと右です。
No, it’s more to the right.

content: A:そのラケット、よく売れてますよ。

content.content: That racket is selling very well.
B:これよりもっと軽いのはありませんか。
Do you have anything lighter than this one?
A:あちらの黒いののほうがもっと軽いんですが、あまり軽すぎるのも使いにくいんじゃないでしょうか。
That black one is lighter, but won’t one that is too light also be difficult to use?

content: もっと（はっきり）言うと、あの子はやる気がまったくない。

content.content: To speak more plainly, that child hasn't got the slightest intent to do this.

content: もっと驚いたことには会社でそのことを知らなかったのは私だけだった。

content.content: What is even more surprising is that I was the only one in the company who didn’t know.
Shows that the respective degree of something is higher than at present. As in

content: , it can be used with nouns where the degree or level of something is being determined (front, back, high, low). Spoken language.

content.content: 【もっとも】
1. もっとも

content: レポートは来週提出して下さい。もっとも、はやくできた人は今日出してもかまいません。

content.content: Please hand in the report by next week. Of course, those who have completed it early may hand it in today.

content: この事故では、橋本さんに責任がある。もっとも、相手の村田さんにも落度があったことは否定できない。

content.content: Hashimoto-san is responsible for this accident. Still, it can’t be denied that the other party, Murata-san, also made a mistake.

content: 彼は強かったなあ。もっとも、毎日あれだけ練習しているのだから当然か。

content.content: He was so strong. That’s to be expected considering how much he practices every day.
Used to partially revise the contents of the preceding statement.
2. もっとも　...が／...けど

content: あしたから旅行に行きます。もっとも二、三日の旅行ですが。

content.content: I am going on a trip from tomorrow. But it’s only for two or three days.

content: あのホテルにした方がいいんじゃない。もっとも、私も行ったことがないから、本当にいいかどうかわからないけど。

content.content: Wouldn’t it be good to choose that hotel? Although, as I haven’t been there myself, I don’t know for sure if it’s any good.

content: 彼女がそう言っていました。もっともうそか本当かは分からないけど。

content.content: She said so. But whether it’s true or not, I have no idea.

content: わたしは来年東大へ行きます。もっとも試験に受かればの話ですが。

content.content: Next year I am going to Tokyo University. I mean, that’s if I pass the exam.

content: スポーツをするなら、サッカーが一番面白い。もっとも疲れることは疲れるけど。

content.content: When it comes to playing sports, football is the most interesting. That isn’t to say that it’s not an exhausting sport.

In addition to partially revising the content of the text which has gone before, this is also used to deny assumptions that the listener may have made on the basis of that content. ...けど is used in speech.
【もっぱら】
1. もっぱら

content: 世間ではもっぱら消費税のことでもちきりだ。

content.content: The consumption tax is the talk of the town.

content: いろいろな酒類があったが、彼はもっぱら日本酒ばかり飲んでいた。

content.content: There were various kinds of alcohol available, but he was only drinking sake.

content: A:愛読書は何ですか。

content.content: What is your favorite book?
B:私はもっぱら推理小説です。
I am really into detective novels.

content: 日曜はもっぱらテレビにゴロ寝です。

content.content: Sunday is all about lying around in front of the television.
Means “just about only that” or “by and large.”
2. もっぱらのN

content: K監督の新作が面白いともっぱらの評判だ。

content.content: People are saying that the latest movie from (Director) K is interesting.

content: 王子の花嫁候補の第一位はあの令嬢だと、もっぱらのうわさだ。

content.content: Rumor has it that that young lady is the top contender to become the prince’s bride.

content: もうすぐ大きな異動があると、社内ではもっぱらのうわさになっている。

content.content: The rumor within the company is that there will be a big relocation soon.
Used in conjunction with 評判 or うわさ, this expresses the meaning that “everyone is saying (something).”
【もと】
1. Nのもと（で）

content: 子供は太陽のもとで思いきりはねまわるのが一番だ。

content.content: The best thing for children is to frolic to their heart’s content in the sunshine.

content: 彼はすぐれた先生のもとでみっちり基礎を学んだ。

content.content: He diligently learned the fundamentals under the tutelage of an outstanding teacher.

content: 先生のあたたかい指導のもとで、生徒たちは伸び伸びと自分らしい作品を作り出していった。

content.content: Under the teacher’s friendly guidance, the students produced works which reflected who they really were.

content: 各国の選挙監視団の監視のもとで、建国以来初の民主的な選挙が行われた。

content.content: Under the observation of a multinational election observation committee, the first democratic election since the founding of the country was held.
Means “under...” or “within scope of the influence of....” When used to modify a noun, the form used is NのもとでのN.
（例）選挙監視団の監視のもとでの選挙が行われた。
The election was held under the eye of an electoral observation committee.
This is a written expression. In addition, Nのもと is also used.
（例）各国の選挙監視団の監視のもと、建国以来初の民主的な選挙が行われた。
The first democratic election since the founding of the country was held under the observation of a multinational election observation committee.
2. Nのもとに

content: 両親の了解のもとに3年間の留学が可能になった。

content.content: With parental consent, three years of study abroad became possible.

content: 弁護士立ち会いのもとに当事者間の協議が行われた。

content.content: Negotiations between the interested parties concerned were held in the presence of lawyers.

content: 他分野での対立点は棚上げにするという暗黙の合意のもとに、両者の連携は成り立っている。

content.content: With the tacit agreement that points of contention in other areas had been shelved, a league was established between the parties.
Means “with... as a condition,” or “under... these circumstances.” Written expression.
【もともと】
1. もともと

content: その本はもともと彼のものだったんだ。だから、彼に返すのは当然のことだ。

content.content: That’s his book to begin with, so of course you’ll return it him.

content: 彼は結局裁判で負けたが、もともと彼の主張は根拠が薄いものだった。

content.content: In the end he lost the trial but, from the start, his whole arguments had a flimsy basis.

content: 彼はもともと保守系だ。あんな発言をしてもおかしくない。

content.content: He is conservative to the core. It’s no surprise that he would make that kind of statement.

content: もともと彼は九州の出身だから、大学を出た後九州の会社に就職してもおかしくない。

content.content: He’s originally from Kyushu, so it’s not strange that he should look for a job with a Kyushu-based company after graduating from college.

content: もともと（は）別々の国だったが、統一されてひとつの国になった。

content.content: Originally they were separate countries but they unified and became a single nation.

content: あのマンションの敷地はもともと（は）工場だった。

content.content: The site of that apartment block was originally a factory.

content: あの歌手はもともと（は）サラリーマンだった。

content.content: That singer was originally a businessman.
Means “originally.” Used to discuss the origins of something. Often used when considering a comparison between a certain situation and that which preceded it. もともとは is also used.
2. ...てもともとだ

content: 初めからあまり可能性はなかったから、失敗してももともとだ。

content.content: As there was not much possibility from the start, it made no difference if we failed.

content: 勉強不足だとは思うが、とにかく、試験を受けてみよう。落ちてもともとだ。

content.content: I don’t think I’ve studied enough but, at any rate, I’ll try to take the test. It makes no difference if I fail.

content: 断られてもともとだと思って、思い切って彼女にプロポーズしてみた。

content.content: Thinking he had nothing to lose if she said no, he boldly proposed to her.

content: A:先生にいい点をくれるよう頼んでみたけど、できないと言われたよ。

content.content: I asked the teacher to give me good grades but she said she couldn’t do it.
B:まあ、だめでもともとだね。
Not that you had high hopes in the first place, did you?

Used with phrases which express meanings such as “no good” and “fail.” Means “it’s the same as if nothing were done.” Used in cases where there is only a slim possibility of something occurring, or in cases where a challenge failed. ...てももともとだ is also used.
【もとより】
1. もとより

content: そのことはもとより承知しています。

content.content: I accepted that from the start.

content: 反対に会うのは、もとよりわかっていたことです。

content.content: I knew from the start that I would meet opposition.
Means “from the beginning.” It is often used with sentence endings such as わかっていた and そう思っていた. A slightly formal expression.
2. ...はもとより

content: タブレットはもとより、パソコンすら使ったことがない。いつも手書きだ。

content.content: I have never even used a personal computer, much less a tablet. I always write by hand.

content: すしはもとより、すきやきも彼は食べられない。とにかく日本料理はいっさいだめだ。

content.content: He can’t even eat sukiyaki, never mind sushi. He just can’t stand Japanese food.

content: 胃はもとより肺もやられているのが検査でわかった。

content.content: From the examination we learned that, besides the stomach, the lungs had also been damaged.

content: 結果はもとより、その過程も大切だ。

content.content: Of course the result is important, but so is the process.

content: 迎えに行くのはもとより、彼の滞在中一切の世話をしなければならない。

content.content: Of course you’ll go and meet him, but you must also take care of him in every way during his stay.
Points out something that is thought to be a matter of course from the start and means “not only that, but also this is more essential/more trivial.”
【もどうぜん】→
【どうぜん】2
【もの】The Chinese character 物 is used in cases which show a concrete object which can be grasped in the hand. In other cases, it is usual to use もの.
1. もの〈thing〉

content: この部屋にはいろいろな物がある。

content.content: There are various things in this room.

content: 何かすぐ食べられる物があれば、それでいい。

content.content: If there is something I can eat quickly, that would be fine.

content: どうぞ、すきなものをとってください。

content.content: Please, take anything you like.

content: 赤ちゃんは、動かないものには興味を示さない。

content.content: Babies show no interest in things that do not move.

content: 買いたいものがあるので、帰りにデパートに寄る。

content.content: There’s something I want to buy, so I’ll drop by a department store on my way home.

content: この料理の本の中には、わたしにできるものはひとつもない。

content.content: There isn’t a single thing I can make in this cookbook.

content: 古い蔵書の中でおもしろいものをみつけた。

content.content: I found something interesting in the collection of old books.

content: この写真は彼女のものだ。

content.content: This photograph is hers.

content: 不思議なものを見たような気がする。

content.content: I feel like I have seen something mysterious.

content: 山のすそに、けむりのようなものが見えた。

content.content: I could see something like smoke at the base of the mountain.
Commonly used to describe any object, or some incident happening in a process, that exists without special connection to the speaker.

There are many difficult aspects in distinguishing between usage of もの and こと. However, a fundamental difference is whether it shows something that takes place within the process of a time period. In cases which relate to an action or event, こと rather than もの is used. For example, we don’t say 話したいものがある but rather 話したいことがある. Similarly, たいへんなことが起こった is correct, not たいへんなものが起こった.
2. もの〈words, knowledge, works, etc.〉

content: 子供がものを言うようになった。

content.content: The child is now able to say things.

content: あの人はあまりものを知らない。

content.content: That person doesn’t know much about things.

content: 学生のころから、ものを書くのがすきだった。

content.content: I have enjoyed writing things since I was a student.

content: かれとわたしとは、ものの考え方が違う。

content.content: My way and his way of thinking about things are different.

content: 市役所に苦情を持ち込んだら、たまたまもののわかる人がいて、すぐ解決してくれた。

content.content: When I lodged my complaint with the city hall, by chance there was someone there who understood and quickly resolved it for me.

Used together with such verbs as 言う, 見る, 知る. Depending on the verb this can mean such things as “words,” “knowledge,” or “works.” The phrase ものを言う, apart from meaning “to speak,” can also be used to mean “demonstrate ability.”
（例）彼の肩書きがものを言う。
His title speaks volumes.
ものがわかる in example

content: means “has the ability to understand.”

content.content: 3. Nというものa. Nというもの

content: 彼女は愛国心というものをもっていないのだろうか。

content.content: Doesn’t she have any patriotism?

content: わたしは一度も愛情などというものを感じたことがない。

content.content: I have never once felt anything like what is called love.

content: 今まで彼は恐れというものを知らなかった。

content.content: Up until now, he had never known the thing called fear.
Used to emphasize nouns that express abstract concepts such as “love.”
b. Nというものは...だ

content: 人間というものは不可解だ。

content.content: People are inscrutable things.

content: 男にとって、女というものはいつまでたっても謎だ。

content.content: For a man, a woman will always remain an enigma.

content: 金というものは、なくても困るし、あり過ぎても困る。

content.content: Money is a thing that is troubling when there is none, and troubling when there is too much.

content: 幸福というものは、あまり続き過ぎると、感じられなくなる。

content.content: Happiness is a thing which, when it goes on for too long, you become unable to feel.

content: 時間というものは、だれに対しても平等だ。

content.content: Time is something that is the same for everyone.

Attached to nouns such as “human beings” and “happiness,” this is used to express a generalization regarding the attributes or nature of that thing. The expression ...というのは is also used. As in examples

content: and
, it is also used in verb phrases. It expresses a variety of strong sentiments depending on the context. In noun phrases, ...とは...だ can be used in its place.

content.content: 4. V-れないものはV-れない

content: A:これだけお願いしてもだめですか。

content.content: Will you still refuse me if I only ask for this?
B:いくら頼まれても、できないものはできないんだ。
No matter how many times you ask, something that can’t be done simply can’t be done.

content: A:まだわかりませんか。

content.content: Do you still not understand?
B:いくら言われても、わからないものはわからないんだ。
No matter how many times I’m told, I can’t understand something that I can’t.

content: A:本当にあしたまでに仕上がらないんですか。

content.content: Will you really not be finished by tomorrow?
B:急がされても、書けないものは書けないんです。
Even if I’m hurried, I can’t write what I can’t write.
Uses the form V-れる, which shows possibility, or verbs like 分かる which contain a notion of possibility. An expression which emphasizes that something cannot be done. Often used with ...ても.

content: 借りたお金は返しておきました。もらいっぱなしではいやだもの。

content.content: I have paid back the money that I borrowed. I hate to be just on the receiving end.

content: A:展覧会に出品する話は断ったんですか。

content.content: Did you turn down the offer to place something in the exhibition?
B:ええ。しめきりが早くて。わたし、そんなに速くかけないもの。
Yes. The deadline was so soon. I’m not someone who can draw that fast.

content: わたし、姉ですもの。弟の心配をするのは当たり前でしょう。

content.content: I am an older sister. It’s natural that I should worry about my younger brother, right?

content: A:寝坊したから、会社は休んだの。

content.content: I overslept so I took the day off work.
B:これだもん。いやになるよな。
That’s it! You really annoy me.

content: 雪が降ったんだもの。行けるわけないでしょう。

content.content: It has snowed. There is no way we can go.

content: A:もうすこしいたら。

content.content: Why don’t you stay a while longer?
B:いっぱいやることがあるんだもの。帰らなくちゃ。
I’ve got a lot of things to do so I’ve got to go home.

content: A:また、出かけるの。

content.content: Are you going out again?
B:うん。だって、吉田さんも行くんだもの。
After all, Yoshida-san’s going, too.

content: A:どうして抗議しないんだ。

content.content: Why don’t you object?
B:だって仕方がないもの。
Because there’s no way around it.

content: A:冷蔵庫を空にしたの、よっちゃんでしょ。

content.content: I bet it was you that emptied the refrigerator, Yotchan.
B:うん、だってお腹すいちゃったんだもん。
Yeah, but I was starving!
Used as an ending for a sentence in casual conversation, this demonstrates a reason. Often used to insist upon the legitimacy (of what one is saying).
Often used by young women or children. Its more casual form is もん and is often used by both men and women in the younger age range. Can also be used with だって, as in examples

content: . Used with だって, it shows a reason given in a spoiled manner. It is mainly used by children and young women.

content.content: 【ものか】［Na なものか］［A-いものか］［V-るものか］
1. ...ものか／...もんか

content: A:はさみも持って行く？

content.content: Are you taking scissors?
B:そんなもの必要なもんか。
Why would that be necessary?

content: A:藤井さんが一番になったそうね。

content.content: They say Fujii-san has become number one.
B:そんなことがあるもんか。何かの間違いだろう。
That can’t be! There must be some kind of mistake.

content: こんな複雑な文章、訳せるものですか。

content.content: There is no way such a complicated sentence can be translated.

content: 誘われたって、だれが行くものか。

content.content: Even if they invited me, there’s no way I would go.

content: あんな人に、頼むもんか。

content.content: There is no way I would ask such a person a favor.

content: 誰が人に手渡したりするものですか。

content.content: There is no way I would hand this over to someone else.
With a falling intonation, expresses a feeling of strong denial. Examples

content: express the speaker’s strong intention that something will not be done. Used in casual conversation.

content.content: Usually, ものか is used by men and the polite ものですか is used by women.
2. V-ないものだろうか

content: もう少し涼しくならないものかなあ。

content.content: I wish it would get a little cooler.

content: もう少し分かりやすく書けなかったものか。

content.content: Couldn’t you have written it (in a way that would have been) a little easier to understand?

content: 何とかして晩までに青森まで行けないものか考えてみよう。

content.content: Let’s think if there is a way for us to get to Aomori by evening.

content: だれかに協力してもらえないものだろうか。

content.content: Can’t I get some cooperation from somebody on this?

content: 2時間の通勤時間を何とか利用できないものかと考えた。

content.content: I thought about whether there was some way I could take advantage of my two-hour commute.

content: A:彼と話しができないものでしょうか。

content.content: I wonder if we could talk to him.
B:何とか方法を考えましょう。
Let me think of some way to do that.
Shows that the speaker wishes for a certain event to take place. The ...なかったものか in example

content: contains a feeling of bewilderment that something has not taken place. Also, when used with the sentence ending (と)考える, means that whether or not the realization of an event or occurrence is possible is being considered. Can also be used, as in
, to make a tentative request.

content.content: 3. どうしたもの（だろう）か

content: 反対派への説明はどうしたものかね。

content.content: How are we supposed to explain this to the opposition?

content: 彼らに対する報酬はどうしたものだろうか。

content.content: What should I do to remunerate them?

content: 今後の資金繰りはどうしたものか、少し考えさせてくれ。

content.content: Let me think a little about what we should do for funding from now on.
Expresses a feeling of confusion over what the best course of action is. Can also be used as a question of someone present.
【ものがある】［Na なものがある］［A-いものがある］［V-るものがある］

content: この作品は発想に斬新なものがある。

content.content: There is an originality of conception to this work.

content: 彼の潜在能力にはすばらしいものがある。

content.content: He has wonderful potential.

content: この文章はまだまだ未熟だが、しかし随所にキラリと光るものがある。

content.content: This composition is still not polished, but there are flashes of brilliance everywhere.

content: 彼女の企画書は結局通らなかったが、いくつかの点で見るべきものがある。

content.content: In the end, her (business) proposal was not accepted, but there were some points that were commendable.
Means that certain characteristics are evident. The 見るべきもの in example

content: means “excellent points that are notable.” In place of ある, forms such as 見られる and 認められる can also be used.

content.content: （例）この文章はまだまだ未熟だが、しかし随所にキラリと光るものが見られる。
This composition is still not polished, but you can see flashes of brilliance everywhere.
Has the tone of written language.
【ものだ】［Na なものだ］［A-いものだ］［Vものだ］
1. ...ものだ〈true nature〉

content: 人の心は、なかなかわからないものだ。

content.content: The human heart is not easily understood.

content: 人間は本来自分勝手なものです。

content.content: People are essentially selfish.

content: 赤ん坊は泣くものだ。

content.content: Babies are meant to cry.

content: 金というのはすぐなくなるものだ。

content.content: Money is a thing which soon disappears.

content: 水は本来低きに流れるものです。

content.content: Water naturally flows downhill.

content: 世間とは冷たいものだ。一時は騒いでもすぐに忘れる。

content.content: It’s a cold world. Even big disturbances are soon forgotten.

content: 人生なんて、はかないものだ。

content.content: Life is a transient thing.

content: A:すみません、レポートを書くのを忘れました。

content.content: I’m sorry, I forgot to write the report.
B:学生というのは本来勤勉なものだ。アルバイトばかりしていてはいけないよ。
A student should essentially be diligent. Just doing your part-time job is not enough!

Used to express the truth/generally accepted thinking/essential qualities of a thing, with strong emotion. It is often used with the phrase 本来. As well as expressing the general nature of a thing, it can also be used as an admonition. For example,

content: states the attitude a student should have.

content.content: 2. ...ものだ〈strong feeling〉a. ...ものだ

content: 「スマホがないと生活できない」とは、今の学生はぜいたくなことを言うものだ。

content.content: Today’s students say extravagant things like “I cannot live without a mobile phone.”

content: この校舎も古くなったものだ。

content.content: This school building has gotten old now.

content: この町も、昔と違ってきれいになったものだ。

content.content: This town has gotten cleaner than in days gone by.

content: 昔のことを思うと、いい世の中になったものだと思う。

content.content: Looking back at the past, I think that times have gotten better.

content: あたりを見回して、かれはつくづく遠くへ来たものだと思った。

content.content: Looking around the area, he thought about what a very long way he had come.
This expresses strong feelings or admiration.
b. よく（も）...ものだ

content: あんなに負債の大きかった会社の再建がよくできたものだ。

content.content: Restructuring a company that had such large debts was a thing well done.

content: こんなむずかしい問題が、よく解けたものだ。

content.content: Solving such a difficult problem is really something.

content: 昔世話になっていた人に、よくもあんな失礼なことができたものだ。

content.content: How dare you do such a rude thing to someone to whom you are indebted!

content: 完成した作品を見ると、みんなよく頑張ったものだと思う。

content.content: Looking at the completed work, I think everyone tried really hard.

content: こんな小さい記事がよく見つけられたものだ。

content.content: You did well to find such a small article.

content: あんなに不況のときによく就職できたものだと思う。

content.content: I think you did really well to find a job in such a time of recession.
Expresses a feeling of admiration or amazement at a certain event or action. Often appears unnatural if used without よく(も).
3. V-たいものだ

content: そのお話はぜひうかがいたいものです。

content.content: I would very much like to hear that story.

content: それはぜひ見たいものだ。

content.content: Of course I would want to see that.

content: 海外へ行かれるときには、わたしも一度、ご一緒したいものです。

content.content: How wonderful it would be if I could have an opportunity to come along with you when you go on a trip abroad.

content: 私も彼の好運にあやかりたいものだ。

content.content: I wish I could share in his good fortune.

content: 今のわたしを、死んだ両親にみてもらいたいものだ。

content.content: I wish my late parents could see me now.

content: このまま平和な生活が続いてほしいものだ。

content.content: I want this peaceful life to continue as it is.
Used with expressions of desire such as たい and ほしい, emphasizes the feeling or emotion of the expression.
4. V-たものだ

content: 学生のころはよく貧乏旅行をしたものでした。

content.content: I traveled around a lot on a shoestring budget when I was a student.

content: 彼は、若い頃は周りの人とよくけんかをしたものだが、今はすっかりおだやかになった。

content.content: When he was young he often quarreled with the people around him, but now he has completely mellowed.

content: 小さい頃はよくみんなで近くの森へ遊びに行ったものでした。

content.content: When we were small, we would often all go to play in the nearby forest.

content: そのころは週末になると映画館にいりびたったものでした。

content.content: At that time, when the weekend came around, we would often hang out at the movie theater.

content: 小学校時代、彼のいたずらには、先生たちが手を焼いたものでした。

content.content: When he was in elementary school, the teachers had difficulty dealing with his pranks.
Used to reflect with strong emotion on things which occurred on a habitual basis in the past.
【ものだから】［N／Na　なものだから］［Aものだから］［Vものだから］
1. ...ものだから

content: 私の前を走っている人が転んだものだから、それにつまづいて私もころんでしまった。

content.content: The person running in front of me fell down and so I tripped (on him/her) and fell, too.

content: 「父危篤すぐ帰れ」という電報が来たものだから、あわてて新幹線に飛び乗って帰って来た。

content.content: I got a telegram saying, “Father critically ill. Return immediately,” and so I jumped on a shinkansen (bullet train) and came back.

content: 彼がこの本をあまりに薦めるものだから、つい借りてしまった。

content.content: He recommended this book so much that (against my better judgment) I borrowed it.

content: 駅まであまりに遠かったものだから、タクシーに乗ってしまった。

content.content: It was too far to the station, so I took a taxi.

content: A:昨日は練習に来なかったね。

content.content: You didn’t come to the practice yesterday, eh?
B:ええ、妹が熱を出したものですから。
That’s right, because my little sister had a temperature.

content: 英語が苦手なものですから外国旅行は尻ごみしてしまいます。

content.content: Because I’m bad at English, I’m hesitant to take trips abroad.
Shows cause or reason. It can be rephrased as から, but volitional and imperative expressions cannot follow.
（×）近いものだから、歩こう。
Because it’s close, let’s walk.
（○）近いから歩こう。
Because it’s close, let’s walk.
Often used to express that the situation is intense or serious and, because of that, something is done. Usually used in speech and becomes もんだから in casual speech.
2. ...おもったものだから

content: 彼はもう知っていると思ったものだから、伝えませんでした。

content.content: Because I thought he already knew, I didn’t tell him.

content: 彼女はたぶんいないと思ったものですから、電話しませんでした。

content.content: I thought she would probably not be there, and so I didn’t telephone her.

content: 子供の様子がいつもとは違うと思ったものですから、すぐ病院へ連れて行きました。

content.content: I thought the child’s appearance was different than normal, so I immediately took her to the hospital.

content: 雨が降るといけないと思ったものですから、洗濯ものを取り込んでおきました。

content.content: Thinking it would not be good if it rained, I brought the laundry in.

content: 手紙では間に合わないと思ったものだから、ファックスにしました。

content.content: I didn’t think a letter would make it on time, so I sent a fax.
This is almost the same as 思ったから but has more of a sense of giving an excuse.
【ものではない】
1. V-るものではない

content: 人の悪口を言うものではない。

content.content: You shouldn’t badmouth people.

content: 男は人前で泣くものではありません。

content.content: Men shouldn’t cry in public.

content: 動物をいじめるものではない。

content.content: You shouldn’t be unkind to the animals.
Taking a verb that expresses people’s actions, means “ought/should not....” Used in cases where advice or a warning is being given.
2. V-たものではない

content: こんなすっぱいみかん、食べられたもんじゃない。

content.content: Such a sour mandarin orange is inedible.

content: こんな下手な写真など、人に見せられたものではない。

content.content: I couldn’t possibly show such an awful photograph to people.

content: あいつにまかせたら何をしでかすか分かったものではない。

content.content: If you leave it to him, you never know what blunders he will make!

Taking a verb which shows possibility such as できる(can do) and わかる(can understand), used to emphasize the feeling that something is not a possibility. Usually used in speech. Becomes もんじゃないin casual speech. Used in giving a negative assessment of a thing.
【ものでもない】
1. V-たものでもない

content: しろうとばかりの劇だが、すぐれたところもあり、そう馬鹿にしたものでもない。

content.content: It was an all-amateur play but there were some excellent parts, so it isn’t to be belittled.

content: みんな、主任になったばかりの佐々木さんを若すぎて頼りないと言うが、彼の行動力はそう見くびったものでもない。

content.content: Everyone is saying that Sasaki-san, who has just taken charge, is too young and lacking in leadership qualities, but her dynamism is not to be underrated.

content: 年をとったといっても、わたしのテニスの腕はまだまだ捨てたものではない。

content.content: You could say I’ve gotten old, but my tennis skills are not to be underestimated.
With expressions containing the meaning “to slight,” expresses the meaning that something is “not that bad.”
2. V-ないものでもない

content: この程度の料理なら、私にも作れないものでもない。

content.content: If it’s only that level of cooking, (perhaps) even I could make it.

content: 道は険しいが、気をつけて歩いて行けば行けないものでもない。
