content.content: The route is steep, but if we walk carefully, we should be able to get there.

content: 理由次第では、手を貸さないものでもない。

content.content: Depending on your reasons, I might consider helping you.

content: このルートで休みなしに走れば、間に合わぬものでもない。

content.content: If we run this route without taking a break, we might possibly make it on time.
Conservatively expresses that something “can” be done. A formal, somewhat old-fashioned phrase. Fundamentally the same as V-なくもない.
【ものとおもう】
1. ...ものとおもう

content: そういうことはないものと思うが、一応確かめてみよう。

content.content: I don’t think that is so, but let’s check just in case.

content: 母は、子供たちも一緒に行くものと思っている。

content.content: Mother believes the children will come along, too.
Used in the form ものとおもう, shows the speaker’s conviction.ものとおもっているexpresses the conviction of the person who is the subject. In the case of example

content: , the subject of ものと思っているis the mother.

content.content: 2. ...ものとおもっていた

content: スキーはむずかしいものと思っていたが、やってみたら、簡単だった。

content.content: I used to think that skiing was a difficult thing, but when I tried it, I found it was easy.

content: 間違いはもう全部直したものと思っていたら、まだ少しあると言われた。

content.content: I thought I had corrected all of the mistakes but was told there were still a few.

content: あしたはストで休みになるものと思っていたから、授業の準備は全然しなかった。

content.content: I thought that tomorrow’s strike would mean classes would be cancelled, so I didn’t prepare for them.

content: 古典なんて退屈なものと思っていたが、読んでみたら、意外におもしろかった。

content.content: I thought that the classics would be boring, but, upon reading them, I found them surprisingly interesting.

content: 吉田さんは来ないものと思って、5人分の食事しか作らなかった。

content.content: Thinking that Yoshida-san was not coming, I only made enough food for five people.
Expresses an impression that the speaker or the subject has. Usually used in cases where what was believed to be true turns out, in reality, not to be the case.
3. ...ものとおもわれる

content: 選挙の結果については明日の夕方には大勢がわかるものと思われる。

content.content: There is reason to believe that we will know how the election is likely to turn out by tomorrow evening.

content: この調子の悪さでは、あまりいい結果は期待できないものと思われる。

content.content: With the condition this horrible, the thinking is that no good result can be expected.

content: 犯人は東京方面へ逃げたものと思われる。

content.content: It is thought that the suspect fled in the direction of Tokyo.
Means the same as と思われる and used to express a conjecture. もの before と思われる is usually used in somewhat formal conversations and compositions.
【ものとする】

content: このことは共通の理解を得たものとする。

content.content: This is (to be considered) the reaching of mutual understanding.

content: これで契約が成立したものとする。

content.content: With this the contract is (considered to be) in effect.
This means “to consider as...” or “to interpret as....”
【ものともせずに】→
【をものともせずに】
【ものなら】
1. ...ものなら

content: できるものなら世界中を旅行してみたい。

content.content: If I could do it, I’d like to travel all over the world.

content: もし願いがかなうものなら、この美術館にある絵が全部ほしい。

content.content: If wishes came true, I would want all the pictures in this gallery.

content: もし希望通りのことができるものなら、今すぐ引退して、趣味の花作りに打ち込みたい。

content.content: If I could just do as I wished, I would retire at once and devote myself to my hobby of growing flowers.

content: こんな職場などやめられるものならやめてしまいたいが、家族がいるから、そうはいかない。

content.content: If I could I would quit this kind of workplace, but as I have a family, I can’t.

content: A:今年はスキーに行かないんですか。

content.content: Aren’t you going skiing this year?
B:行けるもんならもう行っているわよ。忙しくてどうしても休みがもらえないの。
If I could I would already have gone. (However,) I’m busy and can’t get time off no matter what.

content: やれるものならやってみろ。

content.content: Do your best!

Used to hypothesize “if... could be realized/implemented...,” in relation to things which have little possibility of being realized/implemented. It often uses verbs of potential. Also, when the same verb is repeated, emphasizes the fact that something cannot be done in reality. Example

content: is a set phrase which is used to challenge/defy the other party.

content.content: 2. V-ようものなら

content: そんなことを彼女に言おうものなら、軽蔑されるだろう。

content.content: If you said that kind of thing to her, you would be looked down on.

content: そんな言葉を使おうものなら何と下品な女かと思われるだろう。

content.content: If you used that kind of language, you would probably be thought of as a low class girl.

content: 最後の試験に遅刻でもしようものなら、僕の一生は狂ってしまうだろう。

content.content: If I were late or something for my final exam, my whole life would be turned upside down.

content: 彼女は気が短くて、僕がデートにすこしでも遅れでもしようものなら、怒って帰ってしまう。

content.content: She has a short temper, and even if I’m just a little late for a date she goes home angry.

content: となりの子供はわがままで、ちょっと注意でもしようものなら、大声で泣き叫ぶ。

content.content: The child next door is so self-centered, and if you scold him even a little, he screams loudly.

A way of expressing a somewhat exaggerated condition and means “if by any chance such a thing should happen.” Following that it is usual to continue with content which details that “a terrible situation will arise.”
【ものの】

content: 輸入果物は、高いもののめずらしいらしく、人気があってよく売れている。

content.content: Imported fruit is expensive, but perhaps because people seem to find it unusual, it is popular and sells well.

content: 新しい登山靴を買ったものの、忙しくてまだ一度も山へ行っていない。

content.content: I bought new hiking boots, but I’ve been busy and have yet to go to the mountains even once.

content: 今日中にこの仕事をやりますと言ったものの、とてもできそうにない。

content.content: I said I would finish this work by the end of today, but it doesn’t look at all possible.

content: 自然の多い郊外に家を買ったものの、休みの日は寝てばかりだ。

content.content: I bought a house in the suburbs with lots of undisturbed nature (close by), but on my days off I just sleep.

content: 次の企画を始めるお金はあるものの、アイデアがなくて困っている。

content.content: I have the money to start the next project, but I just can’t come up with any ideas for it.

content: 招待状は出したものの、まだほかの準備は全くできていない。

content.content: I have sent out the written invitations, but I still haven’t been able to do any other preparations at all.

content: 先月仕事で久しぶりに東京へ行った。大学時代の友人に電話でもかけてみようとは思ったものの、忙しさにまぎれて、つい、そのままにしてしまった。

content.content: Last month I went to Tokyo for the first time in a long time on business. I wanted to give one of my college friends a call or something, but I ended up being so busy that it ultimately never happened.

Mentioning a past event or a current situation, used to continue the sentence and means “but/however....” Afterwards, the sentence usually continues with a statement that what was expected to occur did not or does not look likely to occur.
Example

content: means “they are expensive and, therefore, not likely to sell well and yet they do.” With phrases such as やるといったのにむずかしい in example

, phrases which express that “(the speaker) has no confidence in the situation that is to follow” or “it is difficult” often continue the sentence and relate to a thing they have said, or done, or to a particular circumstance.

content.content: 2. ...とはいうものの

content: 四月とはいうものの風がつめたく、桜もまだだ。

content.content: Although it is April, the wind is cold and the cherry blossoms are late.

content: 相手は子供とはいうものの、なかなか手ごわい。

content.content: Although just a child, the opponent is pretty tough.

content: 「石の上にも三年」とは言うものの、こんなに訓練がきびしくてはやめたくなる。

content.content: They say “perseverance prevails” (lit. three years on a (cold) stone (will make the stone warm)), but training like this is hard and makes me think about quitting.

content: 人間は平等だとはいうものの、この世は不平等なことばかりだ。

content.content: All people are equal, but this world is full of inequalities.
This means that something which is generally thought does not apply. Example

content: means that “usually in April it is warm and cherry blossoms bloom, but this year that is not the case.” As in example
, it is often used in proverbs or maxims.

content.content: 3. とはいうものの

content: 大学時代は英文学専攻だった。とはいうものの、英語はほとんどしゃべれない。

content.content: I majored in English literature in college. Having said that, I can barely speak English.

content: 車庫付きの家も買ったし、すっかり結婚の準備は整っている。とはいうものの、肝心の結婚相手がまだ見つかっていないのが悩みだ。

content.content: I have bought a house with a garage and all the preparations for marriage are in order. Be that as it may, the crux of the problem is that I still haven’t found someone to marry.
Expresses that the situation is different than what would be expected as a result of the previous statement. Means “that may be so but” or “however.”
【ものを】

content: 黙っていればわからないものを、彼はつい白状してしまった。

content.content: If he’d kept quiet they wouldn’t have known, but against his better judgment, he confessed.

content: 本来ならば長兄が会社を継ぐはずのものを、その事故のせいで次兄が継ぐことになってしまった。

content.content: By all rights, the eldest brother should have taken over the company, but because of that accident, the second eldest did.

content: 知らせてくれたら、すぐ手伝いに行ったものを、何も言わないとはみずくさい人だ。

content.content: If I had only been told, I would have gone to help, but her not saying anything shows how standoffish she is.

content: 場所が場所なら大事故となるものを、この程度のけがですんでよかったと思いなさい。

content.content: Consider yourself lucky to have escaped with such (minor) injuries since it could have been a serious accident had it taken place elsewhere.
Means broadly the same as のに, but is often used to express dissatisfaction in relation to a disappointing result having arisen, as in examples
2. ...すればいいものを

content: すぐに医者に行けばいいものを、がまんしていたから、ひどくなってしまったのだ。

content.content: I should have gone straight to the doctor’s, but I put up with it and it got really bad.

content: そこで引き返せばいいものを、まっすぐ行ったものだから、山に迷い込んでしまった。

content.content: I should have retraced my steps at that point, but I went straight on and ended up lost in the mountains.

content: そのまま逃げだせばいいものを、うろうろしていたので彼は結局警官に捕まってしまった。

content.content: He should have run away, but he wandered around and in the end was caught by the police.

content: 部屋が火につつまれたときすぐ逃げればよかったものを、ペットを助けに行ったばかりに逃げ遅れて死んでしまった。

content.content: When the room was engulfed by flames he should have quickly escaped, but he went back in to save his pet, couldn’t get out, and died in the fire.

content: わたしに話してくれればいいものを、どうして、ひとこと言ってくれなかったんですか。

content.content: You should have spoken to me, so why didn’t you say a single word about it?
Means “if (you) had done... probably nothing bad would have resulted from it but, because (you) didn’t, the result was not good.” It is often used to express feelings of regret or of blame.
【もはや】This is an adverb and is more formal than もう.
1. もはや...だ

content: 少し前までは車を持つことが庶民の夢だったが、もはや一家に車二台の時代だ。

content.content: Until not so long ago it was the dream of the masses to own a car, but now we live in the age of the two-car family.

content: 資金繰りに走り回ったがついに不渡り手形を出してしまった。もはや会社もこれまでだ。

content.content: I ran around trying to raise funds, but in the end I sent out a bad check. That was it for the company.

content: 地球の自然環境の悪化はもはや無視できないところまで来ている。

content.content: We have already come to the point at which we cannot ignore the deterioration in the earth’s natural environment.

content: 保守か革新かという論点はもはや時代遅れだ。

content.content: The question of conservative versus reformist is already out of date.
Expresses a juncture in progress made so far, that the current situation has already reached a certain point or is becoming a certain way.
2. もはや...ない

content: この理論が時代遅れになった今、彼から得るものはもはや何もない。

content.content: Now that this theory has become out of date, there’s nothing that we can get from him.

content: 終戦から半世紀もたっている。もはや戦後ではないという人もいる。

content.content: Half a century has passed since the end of the war. There are people who say it is no longer the post-war period.

content: 彼のスキャンダルがあちこちでうわさになりはじめた。こうなってはもはや手の打ちようがない。

content.content: Rumors of his scandal have started to pop up here and there. It’s already too late to do anything about it.

content: 長年彼のうそにだまされてきて、もはやだれ一人として彼を信じる者はなかった。

content.content: After many years of being tricked by his lies, there was no one who would believe him.
Expresses that a situation which has been continuing until now will no longer continue. Example

content: means “if the rumor has already spread in this way, there is nothing that can be done to stop it.”

content.content: 【もらう】→
【てもらう】
1. NやN

content: 机の上には皿や紙コップなどが置いてあった。

content.content: Things like plates and paper cups had been placed on the table.

content: バスは中学生や高校生ですぐにいっぱいになった。

content.content: The bus was soon full of junior and senior high school students as well as others.

content: その村には米や野菜はあるが、肉はなかなか手に入らない。

content.content: In that village they have food such as rice and vegetables, but it is not easy to lay your hands on meat.
Used to list things. In cases where XとY is used, there are only X and Y. In cases where XやY is used, it implies that there are also things other than those two.
2. 数量詞+や+数量詞

content: うちの息子は一度外国に出かけると1ヶ月や2ヶ月はなんの連絡もありません。

content.content: Once our son has gone abroad we hear nothing from him for a month or two.

content: 善人だと言われている人でも、悪いことの一つや二つはしているだろう。

content.content: Even those who are said to be good people probably do one or two bad things.

content: 彼女ももうすぐ二十歳なんだから、ボーイフレンドが一人や二人いてもおかしくない。

content.content: She will soon be twenty and so it isn’t unusual for her to have a boyfriend or two.

content: 彼は気前がいいから、5万や10 万なら理由を聞かずに貸してくれる。

content.content: He is generous and so he will lend me 50,000 or 100,000 yen without asking the reason.

content: 狭い部屋ですが、一晩や二晩ならがまんできるでしょう。

content.content: It’s a small room, but I hope you can put up with it for a night or two.

content: 給料は安いが、子供の一人や二人は育てられる。

content.content: My salary is low but we can raise a child or two on it.

content: 国際化の時代なのに外国語の一つや二つできないようでは困ります。

content.content: It’s the age of internationalization, so not being able to speak a foreign language or two is a problem.

Gives an approximate amount and expresses that it is not a considerable amount. Used with expressions such as 大丈夫だ, かまわない, and たいしたことはない. It is often used to say “one or two” (e.g. one or two people).
1. V-るや

content: 「どうして俺なんか生んだんだ」という兄のことばを聞くや、母は顔を真っ赤にしておこりだした。

content.content: Hearing my older brother ask why he had been born, my mother’s face turned bright red and she flew into a rage.

content: 「父死す」の電報を受け取るや、すぐさま彼は汽車に飛び乗った。

content.content: When he received the telegram saying “Father has passed away” he immediately jumped on a train for home.
Means “at the same time as...” or “immediately on ...ing.” An old, written expression.
2. V-るやいなや

content: 彼はそれを聞くやいなや、ものも言わずに立ち去った。

content.content: As soon as he heard that, he took his leave without saying a word.

content: その薬を飲むやいなや、急に眠気がおそってきた。

content.content: As soon as I took that medicine, I was overcome with drowsiness.

content: 開店のドアが開くや否や、客はなだれのように押しよせた。

content.content: No sooner had the store’s doors opened than an avalanche of customers pushed their way in.
Expresses a state in which, as a result of one action, the next thing occurs immediately. Means “in the split second when something is or is not done” or “immediately after....” Written language.
【やがて】

content: 秋が終わり、やがてきびしい冬がやってきた。

content.content: Fall ended and before long a severe winter had come.

content: 小さな誤解が、やがて取り返しのつかない国際問題に発展することもある。

content.content: It may be a small misunderstanding, but before long, it could develop into an unsolvable international problem.

content: あの子は心をとざして、だれに対しても反抗的だが、やがてわかる時がくる。今はそっとしておいてやろう。

content.content: That child has closed his heart and rebels against everyone, but eventually he will come to understand. Let’s be gentle with him now.

content: この小川がやがて大きな河になりそして海にそそぎこむ。

content.content: This stream soon becomes a large river that pours into the sea.
Means “before long” or “soon.” Can be used with expressions that mean “to become such a way through natural change” such as ...になる and ...にいたる.
【やすい】［R-やすい］

content: このペンはとても書きやすい。

content.content: This pen is easy to write with.

content: 先生は気さくで話しやすいが、奥さんはこわそうなので家に遊びに行きにくい。

content.content: Our teacher is good-humored and easy to talk to but his wife seems scary, so going to their house is difficult.

content: その町は物価も安く、人も親切で住みやすいところです。

content.content: In that town the cost of living is cheap and the people are kind; it is an easy place to live.

content: かたかなの「ツ」と「シ」は間違えやすいので気をつけてください。

content.content: Katakana ‘tsu’ and ‘shi’ are easily confused, so please be careful.

content: 彼はふとりやすい体質なので、食べすぎないようにしているそうだ。

content.content: He is prone to putting on weight, so he tries not to overeat, I hear.

content: そのおもちゃは壊れやすくてあぶない。

content.content: That toy will break easily and is dangerous.

Conjugates in the same way as i-adjectives. Attaches to the verb stem and expresses that that action can be done easily or is possible. When referring to a predisposition, expressions in the form of すぐに...する are more commonly used. For example, すぐに人を好きになる is used instead of 恋をしやすい. Phrases such as すぐにおこる, おこりっぽい, and すぐに泣く are more common than おこりやすい and 泣きやすい. The phrase ...にくい carries the opposite meaning.
【やたらに】

content: 今日はやたらに忙しい一日だった。

content.content: Today was an extremely busy day.

content: 最近やたらにのどがかわく。なにか病気かもしれない。

content.content: Recently, I have been excessively thirsty. Perhaps I have some illness.

content: 今年の夏はやたらに雨が多い。

content.content: This summer there has been an extremely large amount of rain.

content: 彼は、女子学生とみると、やたらに話しかけては嫌われているようだ。

content.content: It seems that he has been making himself unpopular by speaking to every female student when he happens to see one.

content: この学校はやたらに規則を変更するので困る。

content.content: It is a nuisance that this school changes the rules without considering the repercussions.
Expresses that the extent of something is extreme or that the situation is irregular. やたらと is also used. There are also the expressions むやみやたらに and めったやったらに.
【やっと】
1. やっと〈realization of expectations〉

content: 三回試験を受けて、やっと合格した。

content.content: On my third attempt, I finally passed the exam.

content: テストもやっと終わった。

content.content: The tests are also finally over.

content: 何日も練習してやっとできるようになった。

content.content: I practiced for days and finally became able to do it.

content: やっと、退院できるところまで快復した。

content.content: At last I recovered enough to leave the hospital.

content: 1995 年にトンネルはやっと完成した。

content.content: The tunnel was finally completed in

content: きびしく注意したので、孫もやっといたずらをしなくなった。

content.content: Because he was harshly scolded, my grandchild finally stopped making mischief.

content: 明日でやっと試験も終わる。

content.content: Tomorrow I will finally finish the exams.

content: 貯金もかなりできた。これでやっと独立できる。

content.content: I have some savings. With them I will finally stand on my own two feet.

content: 娘も来年はやっと卒業だ。

content.content: My daughter will also finally graduate next year.

Expresses a situation in which, after hard work or after a difficult time, the thing the speaker had been hoping for has been realized. Often used in the form やっとV-た. It shows the speaker’s feelings of relief or pleasure and that something took time or was difficult.

ようやく, とうとう, and ついに are similar expressions. とうとう and ついに can be used in relation to things the speaker either desires or does not desire. However, やっと can only be used in relation to something the speaker has been hoping for.
（例）長い間入院していた祖父が｛とうとう／ついに｝亡くなった。
After being in the hospital for a long time, my grandfather finally passed away.

In the above example, if やっと is used it means that the speaker has been waiting a long time for their grandfather to die. If とうとう or ついに is used, it bears no relation to whether the speaker wished for it or not but rather is a neutral expression meaning that, after a long time or journey, the final stage has been reached.

Furthermore, as they are used in cases in which the thing the speaker had been anticipating has materialized, やっと and ようやく cannot be used when something the speaker had hoped for has not materialized in the end.
（×）彼は、｛やっと／ようやく｝来なかった。
In the end he didn’t come.
（○）彼は、｛とうとう／ついに｝来なかった。
In the end he didn’t come.

2. やっと〈barely manage (to do something)〉Can be used in both speaking and writing. どうにか, なんとか, かろうじて, and からくも are similar expressions. どうにか and なんとか are spoken expressions and かろうじて is a somewhat formal written expression. からくも is a formal written expression. For details of how this differs from かろうじて, refer to かろうじて (Usage 1).
a. やっとV-た

content: タクシーをとばして、やっと約束の時間に間に合った。

content.content: Having raced there in a taxi, I just made my appointment on time.

content: 試合は延長戦にもつれこんだが、全力を振り絞ってやっと勝った。

content.content: The game went into extra innings, but mustering all their strength, they finally won.

content: うちの子は先月やっと二才になったばかりだ。

content.content: My child just turned two last month.

content: 彼が出発してから、まだやっと三日しかたっていない。

content.content: Still only three days have passed since he left.
As in examples

content: and
, used in cases where something was difficult, but through the application of effort or through the endurance of hardship, things came out well in the end. As in
and
, when used with expressions of quantity, demonstrates that that quantity is the utmost, that there is no more than that, and that the quantity is small. Here,
means “to just reach the age of two (very young)” and
means “merely three days.”

content.content: b. やっとV-ている

content: 退職してからは、国から支払われる年金で、やっと生活している。

content.content: I can just get by on the pension I get from the state after retiring.

content: 私は太りやすい体質で、ダイエットをしてやっと現在の体重を維持している。

content.content: I put on weight easily and have to diet just to maintain my current weight.

content: 人工呼吸器を使って、やっと生きている状態だ。

content.content: The use of an artificial respirator is only just keeping him/her alive.

content: 一面焼け野原で、焼け残った家も、燃え残った柱のおかげで、やっと立っているというありさまだった。

content.content: In the burned-out ruins, the shell of the house was barely standing owing to the burnt remains of the pillars.
As in examples

content: and
, can be used in cases where “(it) is not enough but, through hardship, the current situation can be maintained.” As in
and
, also used in cases where the worst situation (death or ruin) is one step away but, somehow, the current situation is maintained.

content.content: c. やっとV-るN

content: 私の家は、家族5人がやっと暮らせる広さしかない。

content.content: In my house there is just barely the room for the five members of my family to manage to live.

content: 柿の実は、大人が背伸びをしてやっと届くところにあった。

content.content: The persimmons were on high branches that an adult on tiptoe could just reach.

content: 何年も英語を勉強しているが、やさしい本がやっと読める程度で、新聞なんかとても読めない。

content.content: I’ve been studying English for many years and can just manage to read a simple book, but there is no way I could read something like a newspaper.
Indicates “N that is achievable to the degree of やっと／なんとか／どうにか...できる.” Shows that “(something) is difficult but can somehow just be done.” Used with expressions of possibility.
d. やっとNだ

content: 宿題はなかなか終わらない。まだやっと半分だ。

content.content: It is taking a long time to finish my homework. I’ve still got half of it to do.

content: この本はすごく難しくて、なかなか進まない。三時間かかって、やっと5ページだ。

content.content: This book is really difficult and I’m not making much progress with it. It’s taken me three hours to read just five pages.

content: 私の収入は、何もかも全部含めても、やっと 10 万円だ。

content.content: If I put all my income together, it just comes to 100,000 yen.

content: 娘は、まだやっと 18 才だ。結婚なんかとんでもない。

content.content: My daughter is still just eighteen years old. Things like marriage are unthinkable.

content: うちの子は、まだやっと幼稚園だ。

content.content: My child is still only in kindergarten.
As in examples

content: , used with expressions of quantity, shows that that quantity has been reached after tremendous efforts. Used in cases where the speaker thinks that the quantity is not proportionate to the effort put in. Also, used with expressions of age or school year as in
and
, means “no more than...” or “very young/immature.”

content.content: e. やっとのN

content: 戦争中は毎日食べていくのがやっとの生活だった。

content.content: During the war, it was all one could do to eat every day.

content: 日常会話がやっとの語学力では、大学の授業を受けるのは難しいだろう。

content.content: If everyday conversation is the limit of your language ability, it will probably be difficult for you to take university classes.

content: やっとの思いで、彼女に秘密を打ち明けた。

content.content: After agonizing over it, he told her his secret at last.

content: やっとのことで、一戸建ての家を手にいれた。

content.content: At long last I got my own house.
Used in the forms ...するのがやっとのN and NがやっとのN, means “doing something with all one’s might, there is no scope beyond that effort.” Also, the やっとの思いで and やっとのことで of

content: and
are idiomatic expressions meaning “after going to great trouble/putting in great effort.”

content.content: f. Nが／...のが　やっとだ

content: 家の前の道は、車一台が通るのがやっとだ。

content.content: Just a single car can pass along the road in front of my house (as the road is narrow).

content: 私の給料では、食べていくのがやっとだ。

content.content: On my wages, all I can afford is to put food on the table every day.

content: 子供の頃は体力がなくて、毎日学校に通うのがやっとだった。

content.content: In my childhood I was physically weak and it was all I could do to get to school and back.

content: この本はすごく難しくて、なかなか進まない。一日に5ページがやっとだ。

content.content: This book is very difficult and I’m making little progress. I can only read five pages a day.
Means “to do (something) with all one’s might with no scope beyond that.”
【やなんぞ】［Nやなんぞ］

content: 大学の名前やなんぞでぼくを評価してほしくない。

content.content: I don’t want to be judged on things like the name of my university.

content: 不況やなんぞには負けていられない。皆で会社のためにがんばろう。

content.content: We cannot be defeated by things like a recession. Let’s all do our best for the company.

content: 塾やなんぞに行っても、やる気がなくちゃだめだ。

content.content: Even if you go to cram school or whatever, it’s no good if you have no motivation.

content: たった一度の受賞やなんぞで得意になってはいけないよ。

content.content: You really shouldn’t let getting an award once go to your head.
Means ...やなにか but is used negatively. やなんか can also be used. A somewhat old-fashioned expression.
【やむ】［R-やむ］

content: 夜中の三時ごろになってやっと赤ん坊は泣きやんだ。

content.content: At around three in the morning the baby at last stopped crying.

content: となりの部屋の電話のベルが鳴りやんだ。

content.content: The telephone in the next room stopped ringing.

content: 一ヶ月降り続いた雨が降りやんだ後は一面の洪水だった。

content.content: After the rain which had been falling for one month stopped, the whole area was flooded.

Means “a phenomenon, which had been continuing, stops.” Used together with limited intransitive verbs such as 泣く(cry), 鳴る(sound) and 降る(raining/snowing). 降りやむ(stop raining/snowing) is usually abbreviated to やむ.
【やら】

content: 来月はレポートやら試験やらでひどく忙しくなりそうだ。

content.content: It looks like I will be awfully busy next month, what with reports and exams.

content: スケート場は子供やらつきそいの母親やらでごったがえしていた。

content.content: The skating rink was chaotic with children and their mothers chaperoning them.

content: 日が沈んで、山道は寒いやらこわいやらで小さい子は泣きだしてしまった。

content.content: The sun set, and the mountain road was cold and scary so the small child began to cry.

content: 皆さんにこんなに祝ってもらえるとは恥ずかしいやら、嬉しいやら、なんともお礼の言いようがありません。

content.content: To receive such congratulations from everyone makes me feel both embarrassed and happy and there is nothing I can say to thank you enough.

content: きのうは電車で財布をすられるやら傘を忘れるやらでさんざんだった。

content.content: Yesterday my wallet was pickpocketed on the train and I forgot my umbrella. It was terrible!
Like ...や...などいろいろ and ...たり...たりして, used to pick out examples from many. Often used to mean “various things happened, it was terrible.”
2. ...のやら...のやら

content: 行きたいのやら行きたくないのやら、あの人の気持ちはどうもよくわからない。

content.content: Does she or doesn’t she want to go; I just can’t figure out her intentions.

content: 息子に結婚する気があるのやらないのやら私にはわかりません。

content.content: I don’t know whether my son wants to get married or not.

content: うちの子はいつも部屋にいるけど、勉強しているのやらしていないのやら、まったくわからない。

content.content: My child is always in his room, but whether he is studying or not, I have absolutely no idea.

content: こんなに辛くては、味がいいのやら悪いのやらさっぱりわからない。

content.content: I can’t tell at all whether something this spicy tastes good or bad.

content: 本人に直接、病名を言っていい（の）やら悪い（の）やら判断がつかない。

content.content: I can’t decide whether it would be good or bad to tell the person herself the name of the disease directly.

content: 毎日カバンを持って家を出るけど、どこで何をしているのやら。

content.content: He leaves the house with his briefcase every day, but I have no idea where he goes or what he even does.

Means “(I) don’t know which of the two is the case.” Often used in cases where the speaker is having difficulty making a decision or where the attitude of the subject of the conversation is not known. In spoken language, often abbreviated as in example

content: , with the latter part していないのやらわからない being omitted.

content.content: 3. 疑問詞...のやら

content: きのうの昼に何を食べたのやらまったく思い出せない。

content.content: I really can’t remember what I ate for lunch yesterday.

content: お祝いに何をあげていいのやらわからない。

content.content: I don’t know what to give them as a congratulations.

content: どこにしまったのやらいくらさがしても見つからない。

content.content: I haven’t found it no matter how much I search; I have no idea where I put it.

content: 彼に会ったのがいつのことやらはっきり覚えていない。

content.content: I don’t remember clearly when I met him.

content: 40 年も会っていないのではじめは誰が誰やらさっぱりわからなかった。

content.content: Having not met them for forty years, at first I had no idea who was who.
Means “(I) don’t understand what, when, where, who, how....” の is often omitted. だれがだれやら of example

content: is an idiomatic phrase used to emphasize that the speaker does not know/recognize someone. なにがなにやら, どれがどれやら, どこがどこやら and いつのことやら are also used. A somewhat old-fashioned expression.

content.content: 4. 疑問詞+やら

content: なにやら騒がしいと思ったら、近所が火事だった。

content.content: I thought that it was noisy for some reason, and then I realized that the neighborhood was on fire.

content: 妻の誕生日がいつやらはっきりおぼえていない。

content.content: I don’t remember exactly when my wife’s birthday is.

content: 会議のあとでどこやら高そうなバーに連れて行かれた。

content.content: After the meeting I was taken to some expensive-looking bar somewhere.

content: どうやらやっと事件の解決の糸口が見えてきた。

content.content: Somehow, we could at last see the beginnings of a resolution to the affair.
Attached to interrogative words such as なに and どこ, shows that something is indicated only vaguely. Example

content: can be rephrased as なにか, なんだか,
as いつか,
as どこか and
as どうにか.

content.content: 【やる】→
【てやる】
【ゆえ】An old-fashioned, written expression.
1. ゆえ

content: ゆえあって故郷を捨て、この極寒の地に参りました。

content.content: Circumstances led me to abandon my hometown and come to this frozen place.

content: 彼はゆえなく職務を解かれ、失意のうちに亡くなった。

content.content: He was relieved of his duties without reason and died of despair.

content: 若い女が故ありげな様子で門のそばにたたずんでいた。

content.content: The young woman was standing by the gate looking as though there was a reason why she had to be there.
Means “cause” or “reason.” Example

content: is in the style of literary narration. Example
means “to be dismissed from work for no reason.” Example
means “as if with some reason.” ゆえあって, ゆえなく, and ゆえありげ are all idiomatic expressions.

content.content: 2. Nのゆえに

content: 貧困のゆえに高等教育を受けられない子供たちがいる。

content.content: There are children who cannot undertake higher education due to poverty.

content: 政府の無策の故に国内は内乱状態に陥った。

content.content: Due to the government’s lack of measures, the country descended into civil war.
This means “with... as the cause/with... as the reason,” “on account of.”

content: 女性であるが故に差別されることがある。

content.content: Sometimes I am discriminated against because I am a woman.

content: 事が重大であるが故に、報告の遅れが悔やまれる。

content.content: As the matter is very serious, the delay in reporting it is particularly regrettable.

content: 親が放任していたが故に非行に走る若者もいる。

content.content: There are young people who turn towards delinquency because their parents have let them do what they want.

content: 容易に会えぬが故に会いたさがつのる。

content.content: The fact that it is not easy for us to meet makes us want to see each other even more.

content: 若さ（が）故の過ちもあるのだ。

content.content: They are the foibles of youth.
Taking the clause in plain form, means “that is the cause/reason for.” As in

content: , can be used with a noun.

content.content: 4. ...のはNゆえである

content: 息子は窃盗、万引で何度つかまったことか。それでも見捨てないのは子供可愛さゆえである。

content.content: My son has been caught stealing and shoplifting so many times. Even so, I don’t abandon him because I love him as he is my own flesh and blood.

content: 冬山登山は確かに死と隣り合わせだ。だがそれでも行くのは冬山の魅力ゆえである。

content.content: Winter mountain-climbing and death certainly can go together. However, be that as it may, the reason I go is the fascination of the winter mountains.
Means “the reason (I)... is that....” It is used to elaborate the reason something is done in cases where the situation is one of difficulty.
【よう1】
1. R-ようがない

content: こんなにひどく壊れていては、直しようがない。

content.content: As it is this badly broken, you cannot mend it.

content: あの二人の関係はもう修復しようがない。

content.content: Their relationship has gone beyond repair.

content: ここまで来てしまったからにはもう戻りようがない。

content.content: As you’ve come this far, there is no option of going back.

content: そんなにひどいことをしたのなら、言い訳のしようがないと思う。

content.content: In my opinion, there’s no room for excuses when you’ve done something so bad.

Means “whatever means you use, it is impossible.” Used in cases where there are no other possible steps. With verbs such as 修復する(restore) and 改善する(improve), also takes the form ...のしようがない other than ...しようがない.
（例）あの二人の関係はもう修復のしようがない。
Their relationship cannot be mended.
2. R-ようで（は）

content: 気の持ちようで何とでもなることだ。

content.content: By changing your outlook, it could work out.

content: 考えようではサラリーマン生活も悪くはない。

content.content: Depending on how you think, the life of a salaryman is not bad.

content: あなたの気持ちの持ちようひとつできまるんだから。

content.content: It all depends on how you feel.

content: 物は言いようで角が立つ。

content.content: The way you say things can offend.

content: 仕事はやりようでいくらでも時間を節約できる。

content.content: Depending on how you work, you can save as much time as you like.

content: 馬鹿とはさみは使いよう。

content.content: Even fools and (blunt) scissors can be useful (depending on how they are used).
Means “depending on one’s way of thinking/way of doing.” The form R-ようひとつで, as in example

content: , means the thing which comes after will be decided by that alone. Phrases such as どのようにもできる／どうにでもなる (can do/can be done in whatever ways) or 異なる／いろいろだ(different/varied) come afterwards. The latter half of
, 使いようでどうにもなる is omitted, and in its entirety it is a proverb meaning “anything can be put to good use; it depends on how you use it.”

content.content: 3. R-ようによっては

content: 考えようによっては、彼らの人生も幸せだったと言えるのかもしれない。

content.content: Depending on your way of thinking, you could say that their life was happy too.

content: その仕事はやりようによってはとても素晴らしいものになるだろう。

content.content: Depending on how you do that job, it could be something really wonderful.

content: あの山は、見ようによっては仏像が寝ているように見える。

content.content: Depending on how you cast your eyes, that mountain can look like a statue of a sleeping Buddha.
Means “depending on one’s way of thinking/way of doing.” Used to say that the result differs depending on one’s method or viewpoint.

【よう2】［V-よう］One of the Japanese verb conjugation forms. Expresses the speaker’s will or conjecture. -よう attaches to the continuative form of Group 2 verbs, for example: 見よう((will) see) , 食べよう((will) eat). 来る(come) and する(do) become こよう((will) come) and しよう((will) do). In the case of Group 1 verbs, -う is added to the o-row, for example: 行こう((will) go), 読もう((will) read), 話そう((will) speak). In polite Japanese, the form is R-ましょう, as in 食べましょう, 行きましょう.

1. V-よう〈intention〉Using verbs which demonstrate intentional acts, expresses the intent behind the speaker’s action. The rules of usage differ depending on the situation in which it is used, for example in a report, an invitation, or an indirect demand.
In polite Japanese, expressions such as ...しましょう／いたしましょう are used.
a. V-よう〈volition〉

content: 夏休みには海に行こう。

content.content: Let’s go to the sea during summer vacation.

content: 来年こそはよい成績がとれるように頑張ろう。

content.content: Let’s do our best to get good grades next year for sure.

content: 何にもすることないから、テレビでも見ようっと。

content.content: As there is nothing to do, I’ll watch television or something.

content: はっきり申しましょう。あなたにはこの仕事は無理です。

content.content: Let me be frank with you. For you, this job is impossible.

content: A:今夜一杯いかがですか。

content.content: How about a drink this evening?
B:そうですねえ。今日は遠慮しておきましょう。
Hmm. I’m going to take it easy today.
Using verbs which demonstrate intentional acts expresses the speaker’s intention and assumption that the action will take place. Example

content: is an expression typical of someone speaking to themselves. Can also be pronounced in the shorter form V-よっと.

content.content: b. V-よう〈offer〉

content: 足が痛いのか。おぶってやろう。

content.content: Do your legs hurt? I’ll carry you.

content: 忙しいのなら、手伝ってあげよう。

content.content: If you’re busy, I’ll help you.

content: その荷物、お持ちしましょう。

content.content: Let me carry that luggage (for you).

content: 切符は私が手配いたしましょう。

content.content: I’ll arrange the tickets.

content: 駅までお送りしましょう。

content.content: I’ll take you to the station.
Used by the speaker to offer something they can do for another person. It is an action the speaker intends to do for the benefit of another. In humble speech, as in examples

content: , it becomes ...いたしましょう or お...しましょう／いたしましょう.

content.content: c. V-よう〈invitation〉

content: 君もいっしょに行こうよ。

content.content: Why don’t you come with us?

content: 一度ゆっくり話し合おう。

content.content: Let’s discuss it at our leisure some time.

content: 今夜は飲み明かそうよ。

content.content: Let’s drink the night away tonight.

content: お待たせしました。では出かけましょう。

content.content: Thank you for waiting. Right, let’s be going.

Used to invite the listener to act together with the speaker. In contrast to the meaning〈offer〉in b, where only the speaker is to undertake the action,〈invitation〉is used to invite the listener also to act together with the speaker.
d. V-よう〈appeal〉

content: 横断する時は左右の車に注意しよう。

content.content: Watch out for cars from the left and right when crossing.

content: 飲酒運転は絶対に避けよう。

content.content: Let us make sure we will never drink and drive.

content: 食事の前には手を洗いましょう。

content.content: Please wash your hands before eating.

content: 動物にいたずらしないようにしましょう。

content.content: Please don’t disturb the animals.

Used to appeal to a mass of people either to carry out or to refrain from carrying out a certain action. An expression often used on posters or bunting which is to be seen by many people and appeals to people to follow its instructions/advice.
e. もらおう／V-てもらおう

content: ビールをもう一本もらおう。

content.content: Get me another beer.

content: あんたには死んでもらおう。

content.content: You must die!

content: ちょっと警察署まで来ていただきましょう。

content.content: We’d like you to come to the police station.

In the form (V-て)もらおう／いただこう, used to make an indirect demand of the listener. Similar to expressions used to make requests such as ビールをください(please give (me) beer), 死んでくれ(die!), and 来てください(please come) but (V-て)もらおう has the stronger nuance that the speaker is making a unilateral demand. From a social perspective, it is difficult to use this if one is not a person of higher social rank or in a position of higher authority in the workplace.

2. V-よう〈supposition, conjecture〉Like だろう, this expresses the speaker’s conjecture but is somewhat more old-fashioned. Has the tone of written language. i-adjectives also have the same rules of usage as this (A-かろう) , as inよかろう／寒かろう.
a. V-よう

content: 場合によっては延期されることもあろう。

content.content: Depending on the situation, it may be postponed.

content: この点については次のようなことが言えよう。

content.content: Regarding this point, perhaps we can say the following.

content: 午後からは全国的に晴れましょう。

content.content: It is likely to be sunny across the country from the afternoon.

content: 山沿いでは雪になりましょう。

content.content: There is likely to be snow in the mountains.
This shows the speaker’s conjecture. It is often used with phrases which express possibility but not will, such as ある and なる or 言える, できる, 考えられる and あり得る. The negative form is V-まい.
An old-fashioned, written expression. In speech, だろう is used. V-ましょうis the polite form of V-ようand was often used on weather forecasts in the past but nowadays でしょう is used.
b. V-ようか

content: 結論としては、次のようなことが言えようか。

content.content: I wonder if we might conclude the following.

content: こんなひどいことをする人間がこの世にあろうか。

content.content: Are there really people in this world who would do such a horrible thing?

content: こんなに貧しい人達をどうして放っておけようか。

content.content: How can we ignore such needy people?

content: そんな馬鹿げたことがありえましょうか。

content.content: Is such stupidity possible?
A way of saying だろうか in writing. Shows doubt or rhetorical negation. The irony in examples

content: can be interpreted as meaning “I wonder/no, that’s not the case.” Many use it in the direct style.

content.content: 3. V-ようか〈intention〉Makes a question of the volitional form of a verb and is used in cases where the speaker is expressing some doubt as to their own intentions or ideas and asks for the listener’s intent. The basic rules of usage are the same as V-よう but, through the addition of the か, the meaning changes to expressing uncertainty or asking a question.
a. V-ようか〈volition〉

content: どうしようか。

content.content: What should we do?

content: 昼ご飯は何にしようかな。

content.content: What should we have for lunch?

content: 行こうか、それともやめておこうか。

content.content: Should I go or should I give it a miss?

content: 私の考えていること、白状しちゃおうか。

content.content: Should I confess what I’m thinking?

content: こんな仕事やめてしまおうかしら。

content.content: Perhaps I ought to quit this kind of work?

content: これからどうして暮らしていこうか。

content.content: How am I going to live now?

Expresses that the speaker is in two minds over whether to conduct the act or not and has not decided. Apart from か, かな and かしら can also be attached. As かな and かしら are more in the style of someone speaking to themselves, it is difficult to use them with polite Japanese and ましょうかな／ましょうかしら and so on are not usually used.
b. V-ようか〈offer〉

content: 君の代わりに僕がやろうか。

content.content: Shall I do it instead of you?

content: 荷物、僕が持とうか。

content.content: Shall I carry your luggage?

content: 何かお手伝いしましょうか。

content.content: Can I help you with something?

content: いいこと教えてあげましょうか。

content.content: Shall I tell you something good?
Used with both rising and falling intonation but, when used with a rising intonation, the sense that a question is being asked is stronger.
c. V-ようか〈invitation〉

content: 結婚しようか。

content.content: Shall we get married?

content: 何時に待ち合わせしようか。

content.content: What time shall we meet?

content: どこかで食事しましょうか。

content.content: Shall we get a meal somewhere?

content: いっしょに海外旅行しましょうか。

content.content: Shall we take a trip abroad together?

Used to invite the listener to undertake an action together with the speaker. Often used with falling intonation but, when rising intonation is used, the sense that a question is being asked is stronger.
d. もらおうか／V-てもらおうか

content: お茶を一杯もらおうか。

content.content: Could I have a cup of tea?

content: これ、コピーしてもらおうか。

content.content: Copy this for me.

content: 君には、しばらく席をはずしていだだきましょうか。

content.content: Would you leave us for a moment?

content: A:もうすぐ、帰ると思います。

content.content: I think she’ll return soon.
B:じゃ、ここで待たせてもらいましょうか。
In that case, I will wait here.

Used to indirectly make a demand of the listener. The attachment of the か adds the sense that the speaker has only just arrived at that thought or that there is a feeling of hesitation and so this makes the request slightly softer than without it. From a social perspective, it is usually used by people of superior rank speaking to their subordinates.

4. V-ようがA written version of V-ても and means “whatever kind of action is taken/whatever kind of situation occurs.” Phrases such as 自由だ／勝手だ(be free (to do)/be up to (someone)), which express that an event, a decision, or a demand will come to take place regardless of that action/situation come afterwards. There are many instances in which it can be rephrased as V-ようと but there are also cases in which it cannot be rephrased.
a. V-ようが

content: どこで何をしようが私の勝手でしょう。

content.content: What I do and where is up to me.

content: 人になんと言われようが、自分の決めたことは実行する。

content.content: Whatever people say to you, do what you have decided to do.

content: 彼がどうなろうが、私の知ったことではない。

content.content: Whatever happens to him is nothing to do with me.

Shows that the latter thing occurs without being restricted by the former. The latter part uses expressions such as 自由だ(be free(to do))／勝手だ(be up to (the person)) which demonstrate intention or determination.
b. V-ようがV-ようが

content: 出掛けようが家にいようが、あなたの自由です。

content.content: Go out, stay in, it’s up to you.

content: 雨が降ろうがやりが降ろうが、試合は決行します。

content.content: Whether drops or spears fall from the sky, the match shall take place.

content: みんなに笑われようがバカにされようが、気にしない。

content.content: I don’t care whether I’m laughed at or made fun of by everyone.
Used to list things which are opposite or which are similar, this means “whatever happens/whatever (one) does.” The rules of usage are the same as for Usage 4a above.
c. V-ようがV-まいが

content: あなたが出席しようがしまいが、私は出席します。

content.content: Whether you attend or not, I will.

content: 勉強をやろうがやるまいが私の勝手でしょう。

content.content: It’s up to me whether I study or not.

content: パーティは参加しようがしまいが、皆さんの自由です。

content.content: Whether they attend the party or not is up to everyone individually.
Using both the positive and the negative volitional form of the same verb, this means “whichever action (one) takes.” A formal way of saying ...してもしなくても.
5. V-ようじゃないか

content: 一緒に飲もうじゃないか。

content.content: We should go drinking together.

content: みんなでがんばろうじゃないか。

content.content: Let’s do our best together.

content: よし、そんなにおれと喧嘩したいのなら、受けて立とうじゃないか。

content.content: Right, if you want to fight with me so much, I’ll take you on.

content: 今夜は、語り明かそうではありませんか。

content.content: Let’s talk all night tonight.

Attached to verbs which express intention, this is a strong declaration of one’s intentions and is used to invite the listener to act together with the speaker. Mainly used by men and has a stronger sense of influence over the other person than V-ようか. Women usually use ...ましょう. The polite form is ...ようではありませんか／ないですか.

6. V-ようとA written version of V-ても and means “whatever kind of action is taken/whatever kind of situation occurs.” Phrases such as 自由だ／勝手だ(be free (to do)/be up to (someone)), which express that a thing will come to take place regardless of that action/situation come afterwards. There are many instances in which it can be rephrased as V-ようが but there are also cases in which it cannot be rephrased as ても.
a. V-ようと

content: なにをしようと私の自由でしょう。

content.content: What I do is up to me.

content: どこへ行こうとあなたの勝手です。

content.content: Where you go is up to you.

content: どんなに馬鹿にされようと、腹をたてるでもなく彼はひたすら働いている。

content.content: However much people make fun of him, he just carries on working without getting angry.
Expresses that the latter thing occurs without being restricted by the former. Phrases such as 勝手だ(up to (someone))／自由だ(free (to do)／関係ない(nothing to do with) come afterwards.
b. V-ようとV-ようと

content: 努力しようと怠けようと結果がすべてだ。

content.content: Whether you work hard or are lazy, it’s the result that counts.

content: あなたが泣こうとわめこうと、僕には関係ない。

content.content: Whether you cry or shout, it’s nothing to do with me.

content: 行こうとやめようと私の勝手だ。

content.content: Whether I go or not is up to me.

content: 遊ぼうと勉強しようとお好きなようにしてください。

content.content: Whether you play or study, please do as you wish.

content: 煮て食おうと焼いて食おうとご自由に。

content.content: Eat boiled or baked as you wish.

content: 駆け落ちしようと心中しようと勝手にしろ。

content.content: Elope or commit double (lovers’) suicide as you wish.

Used to list things which are opposite or which are similar, this means “it doesn’t matter what (you) do/it’s up to you” and that, whatever action one takes, regardless of that the latter thing will occur.
c. V-ようとV-まいと

content: 行こうと行くまいとあなたの自由だ。

content.content: Whether you stay or go is up to you.

content: たくさん食べようと食べまいと料金は同じだ。

content.content: Whether you eat a lot or not, the cost is the same.

content: 君が彼女に会おうと会うまいと僕には関係のないことだ。

content.content: Whether you meet her or not is nothing to do with me.
Means “whether one does... or not.”
d. V-ようとも

content: 皆にどんなに反対されようとも決めたことは実行する。

content.content: However much people oppose me, I’ll do what I’ve decided.

content: たとえどんなことが起ころうとも、彼からは一生離れない。

content.content: Whatever happens, I’ll never leave him.

content: どんなに脅かされようとも、彼は毅然とした態度をくずさなかった。

content.content: However much he was threatened, they didn’t break his resolve.

content: いかに富に恵まれようとも、精神が貧しくては幸せとは言えない。

content.content: However much wealth you are blessed with, if you have no heart it cannot be called happiness.

Adding も to V-ようと, this is a written expression for V-ても. The meaning and rules of usage are the same as for instances without も but this carries a slightly more old-fashioned nuance. Often used with phrases such as (たとえ)どんなに／いかに.
7. V-ようとおもう

content: お正月には温泉に行こうと思う。

content.content: I think I’ll go to a hot spring at New Year’s.

content: 来年はもっと頑張ろうと思う。

content.content: I think I’ll try harder next year.

content: 今夜は早く寝ようと思っている。

content.content: I’m thinking of going to bed early this evening.

content: 今の仕事を辞めようかと思っている。

content.content: I’m wondering whether I should quit my job.

content: 外国に住もうとは思わない。

content.content: I have no intention of living abroad.

content: あなたは一生この仕事を続けようと思いますか。

content.content: Do you think you’ll do this job for life?
Taking verbs which demonstrate intention, this is used to express the speaker’s plans or intentions. In interrogative sentences it is used to ask the listener’s intentions. Also, the かと思う of example

content: demonstrates that the speaker’s indecisiveness or hesitancy. V-ようと(は)思わない means that the speaker has no such intention.

content.content: Similar to つもりだ but differs in that つもりだ can be used to express the will of a third person.
（○）山田さんは留学するつもりだ。
Yamada-san intends to study abroad.
（×）山田さんは留学しようと思う。
Yamada-san intends to study abroad.
Moreover, V-ると思う is used to express the speaker’s conjecture rather than will and cannot be used in cases where one wishes to express intention. In such cases V-ようと思う must be used.
（×）私は東京へ行くと思う。（意志の表現としては誤り）
I think I will go to Tokyo. (Incorrect as an expression of intention.)
（○）私は東京へ行こうと思う。
I think I will go to Tokyo.
8. V-ようとするa. V-ようとする〈immediately before〉

content: 時計は正午を知らせようとしている。

content.content: The clock is about to strike midday.

content: 長かった夏休みもじきに終わろうとしている。

content.content: The long summer holiday is coming to an end.

content: 日は地平線の彼方に沈もうとしている。

content.content: The sun is setting over there on the horizon.

content: 上り坂にさしかかろうとする所で車がエンストを起こしてしまった。

content.content: I stalled the car’s engine as I approached the ascent.

content: お風呂に入ろうとしていたところに、電話がかかってきた。

content.content: Just as I was about to get in the bath, the phone rang.

Means “just before/on the verge of” an action or change taking place. Typically used with non-volitional verbs such as 始まる(begin) and 終わる(end) but, when used in the form V-ようとするところ, it can also be used with volitional verbs. In instances in which non-volitional verbs are used, it is often a literary or poetic expression.
b. V-ようとする〈attempt〉

content: 息子は東大に入ろうとしている。

content.content: My son is trying to get into Tokyo University.

content: 彼女は 25 歳になる前に何とか結婚しようとしている。

content.content: She is trying to get married somehow before she turns

content: いくら思い出そうとしても、名前が思い出せない。

content.content: However hard I try, I cannot remember his name.

content: 棚の上の花びんをとろうとして、足を踏みはずしてしまった。

content.content: I lost my footing trying to get the vase from the shelf.

content: 本人にやろうとする意欲がなければ、いくら言っても無駄です。

content.content: If the person him/herself has no motivation, whatever you say is futile.

content: 寝ようとすればするほど、目がさえてきてしまった。

content.content: The more I tried to sleep, the more wide-awake I became.
Taking verbs which demonstrate intentional action, this expresses that attempts or efforts are made to realize that action.
c. V-ようと（も／は）しない

content: うちの息子はいくら言っても勉強をしようとしない。

content.content: Whatever I say, my son has no intention of studying.

content: 隣の奥さんは私に会っても挨拶ひとつしようとしない。

content.content: Even when she sees me, the lady next door never greets me.

content: その患者は食べ物を一切うけつけようとしない。

content.content: That patient won’t have any food.

content: 声をかけても振り向こうともしない。

content.content: Even when I call out, he will not even turn to face me.

content: 彼女はこの見合い話をおそらく承諾しようとはしないだろう。

content.content: I don’t think she’ll consent to this arranged marriage.

Taking verbs which express intentional action, this expresses a lack of intention to carry out that action or deed. When も is inserted, as in V-ようともしない, it emphasizes a denial and means “have no intention even of ...ing.” As in example

content: , は is also sometimes inserted.

content.content: 9. V-ようとはおもわなかった

content: こんなことになろうとは思わなかった。

content.content: I had no idea this kind of thing would happen.

content: 被害がこれほどまで広がろうとは、専門家も予想しなかった。

content.content: Even the experts didn’t predict that the damage would be so widespread.

content: 息子が、たった一度の受験で司法試験に合格しようとは夢にも思わなかった。

content.content: I didn’t even dream that my son would pass the bar exam at just the first attempt.

content: たったの五日で論文が完成しようとは誰一人想像しなかった。

content.content: No one imagined that I would finish my thesis in just five days.
Taking non-volitional verbs such as なる, means “that such a thing would happen was not predicted.”合格しよう(will pass) and 完成しよう(will do) of examples

content: and

express that the thing happened naturally or spontaneously and, as such, like 合格／完成できる and 合格／完成することになる, they do not express the speaker’s intention. Apart from 思う, verbs which follow are those such as 予想／想像する(predict/imagine) and always take the form -なかった. It is a written expression.

content.content: 0. V-ようにもV-られない

content: 頭が痛くて、起きようにも起きられない。

content.content: My head hurts and I couldn’t get up even if I wanted to.

content: まわりがうるさくて、落ち着いて考えようにも考えられない。

content.content: It’s noisy around me and, even though I want to calm down and think, I can’t.

content: 風が強すぎて走ろうにも走れない。

content.content: The wind is so strong and I can’t run however much I try.

content: 雨が降っているので、外で遊ぼうにも遊べない。

content.content: Because it’s raining, even though you want to play outside you can’t.

Attached to verbs which demonstrate intentional actions, means “even though one intends to... one can’t.” The same verb is repeated before and after. It is often used in cases where something cannot be done regardless of a strong wish to do it.
【ようするに】

content: 要するに、日本は官僚型政治だ。

content.content: In a word, Japan has a bureaucratic government.

content: いろいろ理由はあるが、要するに君の考えは甘い。

content.content: There are various reasons but, in short, your thinking is naive.

content: 要するに看護婦さんが足りないのだ。

content.content: The point is that there are not enough nurses.

content: 《前にいろいろ説明したあとで》要するに、私が言いたいことはこれに尽きる。

content.content: 《after explaining many things》In short, that’s all I want to say.

content: 《相手の話をさえぎって》要するに、君の考えはお決まりのものだね。

content.content: 《interrupting another speaking》In short, you think the same as everyone else.

content: 要するに、君は何が言いたいのだ。

content.content: In a word, what’s your point?

Used in to summarize what has gone before, to express one’s own conclusion and to question or confirm another’s conclusions. Not suitable for use in sentences which do not express a personal opinion but which state a natural outcome. In such cases, phrases such as 結局(in the end) should be used. It is a written expression.
（×）健闘したが、要するに日本チームは負けてしまった。
It was a good effort but, in the end, the Japanese team lost.
（○）健闘したが、結局日本チームは負けてしまった。
It was a good effort but in the end the Japanese team lost.
【ようだ1】［Nのようだ］［A／V　ようだ］Conjugating na-adjectives, this becomes ように and ような in the continuative and attributive forms.
1. ...ようだ〈simile〉a. ...ようだ

content: この雪はまるで綿のようです。

content.content: This snow is just like cotton wool.

content: 彼女の心は氷のように冷たい。

content.content: Her heart is as cold as ice.

content: 男は狂ったように走り続けた。

content.content: He kept running like mad.

content: 赤ん坊は火がついたように泣き出した。

content.content: The baby burst out crying as if she were on fire.

content: あたりは、水を打ったように静まりかえっている。

content.content: The area suddenly became completely silent.

content: 新製品は面白いようによく売れた。

content.content: The new product sold like hot cakes.

content: 6月が来たばかりなのに真夏のような暑さだ。

content.content: Although June has just begun, it is hot like midsummer.

content: 会場は割れるような拍手の渦につつまれた。

content.content: The venue was engulfed by the tumultuous applause.

content: 身を切るような寒さが続いている。

content.content: The biting coldness continues.

Used to liken a situation, quality, form, or action to something which is essentially different. Not only used to liken a thing to something with similar properties but also to entirely distinct, fanciful, things. Often attached to nouns and verbs but, occasionally, as in example

content: , also attached to i-adjectives. However, cannot be attached to na-adjectives. Also, sometimes used with accompanying adverbs which are used to express similes, such as あたかも, いかにも, さながら, まるで and ちょうど.

content.content: （例）町はすっかりさびれてしまって、まるで火が消えたようだ。
The town is in complete decline, just like a fire has gone out.
（例）家族が一堂に揃い、あたかも盆と正月がいっしょに来たようだ。
To have the family all together in one room is just like the Bon Festival and the New Year’s holiday have come at the same time. (= a very busy and happy time)

Often appears in customary, fixed expressions. Idiomatic expressions other than those which appear here are: 雲をつかむような話／竹を割ったような性格／血のにじむような努力／手が切れるような新札／飛ぶように売れる／目を皿のようにして探す (a vague story/a straightforward character/to sweat blood/a crisp new note/to sell like hot cakes/to search with wide eyes) .
In speech, みたいだ is often used. Furthermore, in writing ごとし can also be used.
b. V-る／V-た　かのようだ

content: 彼はなにも知らなかったかのように振る舞っていた。

content.content: He was acting as though he didn't know anything.

content: 父はあらかじめ知っていたかのように、平然としていた。

content.content: My father was calm, as though he already knew.

content: 本当は見たこともないのに、いかにも自分の目で見てきたかのように話す。

content.content: You haven’t even seen (it) but you talk as though you have.

content: 極楽にでもいるかのような幸せな気分だ。

content.content: I’m so happy I feel like I’m in paradise.

content: 犯人は事件のことを初めて聞いたかのような態度をとった。

content.content: The criminal acted as though he was hearing about the incident for the first time.

content: あたり一面霧に包まれ、まるで別世界にいるかのようだ。

content.content: The whole area is enveloped in mist; it is like I am in another world.

Taking the dictionary or ta-form of a verb, expresses that, although in reality (it) is not the case, one’s conduct or feeling is that it is. It is often used in cases which pick out things as examples which are inconsistent with reality or are imaginary.
2. ...ような／...ようにa. ...ように〈example〉

content: あの人のように英語がペラペラ話せたらいいのに。

content.content: I wish I could speak English as fluently as that person.

content: ニューヨークのように世界中の人々が住む都市では、各国の本格的な料理を味わうことができる。

content.content: In cities like New York, where people from all around the world live, you can taste authentic food from many countries.

content: 母親が美人だったように、娘たちもみな美人ぞろいだ。

content.content: The daughters are all beauties like their mother was.

content: 私が発音するようにあとについて言ってください。

content.content: Please pronounce it as I do, after me.

content: 先生がおっしゃったようにお伝えしておきました。

content.content: I told it as my teacher told it to me.
Taking the form XようにY, used to give a specific person or thing as an example of conformity/consistency in quality, content or method with Y. Example

content: means “to imitate an action” and
can be rephrased as とおりに.

content.content: In contrast to Usage 1 inようだ〈simile〉, an expression which compares an essentially different and distinct thing to X in the phrase まるでXのように, with this usage X is given as an example of a specific thing which shares a property or content with Y. However, it is not always possible to distinguish between these two usages.
b. ...ようなN〈example〉

content: 風邪をひいたときは、みかんのようなビタミンCを多く含む果物を食べるといい。

content.content: When you catch a cold, it’s good to eat a lot of fruit like oranges which contain a lot of vitamin C.

content: あなたのようなご親切な方にはなかなか出会えません。

content.content: It’s not very often we meet people as kind as you.

content: これはどこにでもあるようなものではない。

content.content: This is not the kind of thing you find everywhere.

content: 彼はあなたが思っているような人ではない。

content.content: He is not the kind of person you think he is.

content: このまま放っておくと、取り返しがつかないようなことになりかねない。

content.content: If you leave it as it is, it’s quite possible that you won’t be able to sort it out.

content: これを食べても死ぬようなことはありません。安心してください。

content.content: You won’t die if you eat this. Please rest assured.

content: 薬を飲んでもよくならないような場合は医者に相談してください。

content.content: In cases where you do not recover after taking medicine, please consult your doctor.

Used to give a concrete example of the noun which follows it. For example, in みかんのような果物(a fruit like an orange), the latter noun represents a higher concept than the former. When continued after a clause, the sentence can be valid without ような but there will be some difference in the meaning if it is included or not. For example, if ような is removed from

content: as 薬を飲んでもよくならない場合 it refers to a specific situation where “the condition does not improve after taking the medicine,” but in case of 薬を飲んでもよくならないような場合 then it means “cases like when you take the medicine but the condition does not improve” indicating that there are many other similar situations.

content.content: c. ...ように〈introductory utterance〉

content: ご存じのように、日本は人口密度の高い国です。

content.content: As you know, Japan is a country with a high density of population.

content: あなたがおっしゃっていたように、彼は本当に素敵な方ですね。

content.content: As you were saying, he’s a really lovely man.

content: すでに述べたようにアフリカの食糧不足は深刻な状況にある。

content.content: As has already been mentioned, Africa’s food shortage is serious.

content: ことわざにもあるように、外国に行ったらその国の習慣に従って暮らすのが一番である。

content.content: As the maxim says, when you go abroad, it’s best to live by the customs of that country.

content: あのにこにこした表情が表しているように、彼はとても明るい性格の人です。

content.content: As his smiling expression shows, he has a very cheerful character.

Shows that what is about to be said is consistent with what has been stated previously or is a well-known fact. Used to give notice that further explanation is about to be given. Can be replaced with とおり.
d. つぎのように／いかのように

content: 結果は次のようにまとめることができる。

content.content: The results can be summarized in the following manner.

content: 中には以下のような意見もあった。

content.content: Among them there were the following kinds of opinion.

content: 本稿の結論をまとめれば、次のようになる。

content.content: We can summarize the article’s conclusions as follows.

content: 以下で示すように、我が国の出生率は下がる一方である。

content.content: As seen below, the birthrate of our country is declining.
Used to announce that concrete detail is to follow. In vertical text compositions, 右のように and 左のように are also used.
【ようだ2】［Nのようだ］［Na なようだ］［A／V　ようだ］As well as the form Nの／Naなようだ, nouns and na-adjctives can also take the forms N／Naだったようだ and N／Naじゃないようだ.
1. ...ようだ〈supposition, conjecture〉

content: あの人はこの大学の学生ではないようだ。

content.content: That person doesn't seem like a student of this university.

content: どうやら君の負けのようだね。

content.content: It seems that you lose.

content: 先生はお酒がお好きなようだ。

content.content: It seems that the teacher likes sake.

content: こちらの方がちょっとおいしいようだ。

content.content: This one seems to be more delicious.

content: どうも風邪を引いてしまったようだ。

content.content: I somehow seem to have caught a cold.

content: あの声は、誰かが外で喧嘩しているようだ。

content.content: Judging from that voice, someone appears to be fighting outside.

content: ざっと見たところ、最低 500 人は集まっているようだ。

content.content: To roughly judge by looking, I would say there are at least 500 people gathered here.

Shows the speaker’s impression or conjectural judgement about things. Used in cases where the speaker synthesizes their observations regarding the outward appearance of a thing or their own sensations. This is done through the expression of the speaker’s physical sensations, the senses of sight, hearing, taste and so on, by the speaker saying such things as “for some reason there is such a feeling/(it) looks such a way” and results in the passing of a conjectural judgement.
そのようだ and そんなようだ can be used in cases where something already detailed is accepted in the following manner.
（例）A:雨が降ってきましたね。
It started to rain.
B:ええ、そのようですね。
Yes, it seems like it.

As this is a roundabout way of saying this, そうですね is an example of how this can be said without using ようだ. In this way, ようだ is used to avoid or moderate conclusive expressions which contrast with those of the other party and is often used with adverbs such as どうやら, どうも, 何となく and 何だか.
2. ...ようなきがする...ようなかんじがする

content: ちょっと期待を裏切られたような気がする。

content.content: I feel a little disappointed.

content: もう他に方法はないような気がする。

content.content: It seems that there is no other way.

content: あまりほめられると、ちょっとくすぐったいような感じがする。

content.content: It’s a bit embarrassing to be praised too much.

content: 何となく不吉なことが起こるような予感がした。

content.content: For some reason, I had a premonition that something sinister would occur.

content: 運動したら、何だか体が軽くなったような感じだ。

content.content: When I exercised, I felt as though my body had become a little more relaxed.
When nouns such as 気, 感じ and 予感 are attached to ような the meaning is roughly the same as in cases which end with ようだ.
3. ...ように　おもう／かんじる

content: こちらのほうがお似合いになるように思います。

content.content: I think this one might suit you better.

content: 心なしか彼の表情が陰ったように思われた。

content.content: His expression appeared to darken somewhat.

content: あの二人はとても仲がいいように見える。

content.content: Those two seem to be very close.

content: その日の彼は様子がいつもと違うように感じた。

content.content: On that day he seemed different to normal.

content: 今年の冬は去年より、少し暖かいように感じられる。

content.content: This winter seems a little warmer than last year’s.

Taking a verb which expresses a thought or sensation such as おもう(think), おもわれる(appear), みえる(appear) or 感じる(feel) after ように, this is used to state one’s sensations, impressions, or opinions, in a roundabout way.
4. ...ようでは

content: こんな問題が解けないようではそれこそ困る。

content.content: If you can’t solve such a problem, I’ll be worried.

content: きみが行かないようでは誰も行くわけがない。

content.content: If you won’t go, then there is no way anyone else will go.

content: こんなことができないようでは、話にならない。

content.content: If you can’t do something as easy as this, it is a complete non-starter.

content: こんな質問をするようでは、まだまだ勉強がたりない。

content.content: If you have to ask such questions, you still haven’t studied enough.
Means “in such a situation.” Expressions which give a negative judgement such as 困る／だめだ and things which are contrary to expectations come afterwards.
5. ...ようで（いて）

content: 一見やさしいようで、実際やってみると案外むずかしい。

content.content: It looks easy but, in reality, when you try it, it’s unexpectedly difficult.

content: ふだんはおとなしいようでいて、いざとなるとなかなか決断力に富んだ女性です。

content.content: She seems quite quiet and gentle usually but when it comes to it, she can turn into a remarkably decisive lady.

content: 一見、内気で温厚なようだが、実は短気で、喧嘩っぱやい性格の男だ。

content.content: At first glance he seems shy and gentle but, in truth, he has a short temper and gets into fights easily.
Means “from appearances, gives this kind of impression but....” Often takes the form 一見／見かけは...ようで、実際は... and shows that a thing’s real nature differs. ...ようだが can also be used.
6. ...ようでもあり...ようでもあるし

content: 僕の言ったことが彼には分かったようでもあり、全く理解していないようでもある。

content.content: He seemed to have understood what I said, but at the same time, he didn’t seem to have understood at all.

content: この会社での 30 年間は、長かったようでもあり、あっと言う間だったような感じもします。

content.content: My thirty years at this company seem to have been long but seem to have gone by in an instant.

content: 彼は本当は結婚したい気持ちがあるようでもあるし、まったくその気がないようでもある。

content.content: He seems to really want to get married but then, doesn’t seem to  want to at all.
Expressing opposing details or contradictory things, shows that significantly contrasting or inconsistent sensations and impressions co-exist within the speaker. ...ようでもあるし is a written expression.
7. ...ような...ような

content: そのようなことがあったようななかったような...

content.content: Such a thing seems to have been and to not have been....

content: 分かったような分からないような中途半端な感じだ。

content.content: I feel like I understand and yet don't understand; I’m halfway there.

content: 悲しいような懐かしいような複雑な気持ちである。

content.content: It’s a complex feeling of sadness and nostalgia.
This is used in a similar way to Usage 6 above but is more often used as a spoken expression than Usage 6 above.
8. ...ようなら／...ようだったら

content: この薬を飲んでも熱が下がらないようなら、医者と相談した方がよいでしょう。

content.content: If, even when you take this medicine, your fever does not reduce, you had better consult your doctor.

content: 遅れるようだったら、お電話ください。

content.content: If you are going to be late, please call.

content: 明日お天気がよいようでしたら、ハイキングに行きませんか。

content.content: If the weather is going to be good tomorrow, shall we go hiking?
Where ようだ demonstrates a condition, means “in case.” ...ようであれば is also used in writing.
【ような1】

content: 6月が来たばかりなのに真夏のような暑さだ。

content.content: Although June has only just begun, it is hot like midsummer.

content: 会場は割れるような拍手の渦につつまれた。

content.content: The grounds were engulfed by tumultuous applause.
【ようだ1】
【ような2】

content: ちょっと期待を裏切られたような気がする。

content.content: I feel as though my expectations haven’t been met.

content: あそこに置いたような置かなかったような、記憶がはっきりしない。

content.content: I can’t recall well whether I left it there or I didn’t.
【ようだ2】
【ように1】

content: あの人のように英語がペラペラしゃべれるようになりたい。

content.content: I want to be able to speak English as fluently as that person.

content: 私が発音するようにあとについて言って下さい。

content.content: Please pronounce it as I do, after me.
【ようだ1】
【ように2】

content: こちらのほうがお似合いになるように思われます。

content.content: I think this one would suit you better.

content: 心なしか彼の表情が陰ったように思われた。

content.content: His expression seemed to darken somewhat.
【ようだ2】
【ように3】
1. V-る／V-ない　よう（に）〈purpose〉

content: 後ろの席の人にも聞こえるように大きな声で話した。

content.content: I said it in a loud enough voice so that even the people in the seats behind could hear it.

content: 子供にも読めるよう名前にふりがなをつけた。

content.content: I put my name in furigana so that even children would be able to read it.

content: 赤ん坊を起こさないようにそっと布団を出た。

content.content: I got out of the futon softly, so as not to wake the baby.

content: 忘れないようにノートにメモしておこう。

content.content: I will make a note of this so I won’t forget.

Using a verb before and after, this means “do... so as to make such a circumstance or situation occur/do... so as not to....”に is sometimes omitted. Before ように, verbs which show non-volitional actions, such as なる and できる, or verbs which show possibility in the form V-れる are often used, as are the negative forms of verbs and expressions which show the state or condition of a thing. The clause which follows ように is a verb which demonstrates the speaker’s intentional act. The subject may differ before and after, as in examples

content: , or it may be the same, as in

content.content: Furthermore, in cases where the subject is the same before and after, and where the first verb demonstrates an intentional action, it is usual to use ために.
（×）息子が家で仕事ができるために父親は家を改築した。（異主語･非意志的）
So that his son could work from home, the father renovated the house. (different subject, non-volitional)
（○）息子が家で仕事ができるように父親は家を改築した。（異主語･非意志的）
So that his son could work from home, the father renovated the house. (different subject, non-volitional)
（○）家で仕事をするために家を改築した。（同一主語・意志的）
He renovated the house so he could work from home. (same subject, volitional)
2. V-る／V-ない　よう（に）〈admonition〉

content: 忘れ物をしないようにしてください。

content.content: Don’t leave anything behind.

content: 時間内に終了するようお願いします。

content.content: Please finish within the time (allowed).

content: 風邪をひかないようご注意ください。

content.content: Please take care not to catch a cold.

content: 私語は慎むようにしなさい。

content.content: Please refrain from whispering amongst yourselves.

content: 集合時間は守るように。

content.content: Keep to the appointed time.

content: 授業中はおしゃべりしないように。

content.content: No chatting during class.

Used to give advice to or to remonstrate with the listener. Verbs such as しなさい／してください and お願いします are used in the latter half but are sometimes omitted, in which case the expression ends with ように. Also, it is possible to omit the に from ように but, where the sentence ends with ように, it is usual not to do so, as in examples

content: and
. Used in the form V-ないように, this often expresses negative advice or recommendations.

content.content: 3. V-る／V-ない　よう（に）〈prayer〉

content: 息子が大学に合格できるよう神に祈った。

content.content: I prayed to God that my son would pass the university entrance exam.

content: 現状がさらに改善されるよう期待している。

content.content: I hope that the present situation will improve again.

content: 《年賀状》新しい年が幸い多き年でありますよう祈っております。

content.content: 《New Year’s card》Wishing you a joyful new year.

content: 《病気見舞の手紙》早く全快なさいますよう、祈念いたしております。

content.content: 《get-well card》I am praying for your swift and complete recovery.

content: どうか合格できますように。

content.content: Wishing you success in the (e.g. entrance) exams.

content: すべてがうまくいきますよう。

content.content: Hoping all goes well.

content: あしたは雨が降りませんように。

content.content: Praying that it does not rain tomorrow.

Expresses one’s or another’s hopes, prayers and wishes. Verbs such as 祈る(pray), 祈念する(say a prayer), 念じる(pray silently), 望む(desire), 願う(wish), 希望する(hope) and 期待する(expect) are used after ように. As in examples

content: and
, the expression can end with ように. In such cases the polite form is usually used before ように. It is often used to bring a speech or letter to a close.

content.content: 4. V-る／V-ない　よう（に）いう

content: すぐ家に帰るように言われました。

content.content: I was told to go home at once.

content: これからは遅刻しないように注意しておきました。

content.content: I warned them not to be late from now on.

content: 戻りましたら、家に電話するようお伝えください。

content.content: Please tell him to call me at home when he comes back (to the office).

content: 隣の人に、ステレオの音量を下げてもらうように頼んだ。

content.content: I asked my neighbor to turn the volume of her stereo down.

Using verbs of communication, such as 言う(say) and 伝える(convey) in the latter half, this is used to indirectly quote a request. Direct quotations take the following form: command/request+と+verb of communication.
（例）「すぐ帰れ」と言った。
She said, “Go home at once.”
（例）「ステレオの音量を下げてください」と頼んだ。
I asked, “Please would you turn down the volume of your stereo?”
5. V-る／V-ない　ようにする

content: 私は肉を小さく切って、こどもにも食べられるようにした。

content.content: I cut the meat into small pieces so that even children could eat it.

content: 大きな活字を使い、老人にも読みやすいようにする。

content.content: We use large print so that it’s easy for the elderly to read.

content: できるだけ英会話のテレビを見るようにしている。

content.content: I’m watching as much English conversation program on TV as I possibly can.

content: 彼女の機嫌を損ねることは言わないようにした。

content.content: I tried not to say things that would hurt her feelings.

content: 試験日には、目覚まし時計を2台セットして寝坊しないようにしよう。

content.content: On exams days I set two alarm clocks so that I don’t overlay.

content: 油ものは食べないようにしている。

content.content: I try not to eat fried foods.
Means to make efforts with the aim of/to aim to/to see to it that an action or situation occurs. As in examples

content: , when the negative form is used, it means to aim for the action or situation not to occur....ようにしている of
and
means to do that thing customarily. A verb usually comes before ように but, as in example
, V-やすい is also used. In this case 読みやすくする could also be used.

content.content: 6. V-る／V-ない　ようになる

content: 日本語が話せるようになりました。

content.content: I have become able to speak Japanese.

content: 眼鏡をかければ、黒板の字が見えるようになります。

content.content: I can see the letters on the blackboard if I wear my glasses.

content: 赤ちゃんはずいぶん活発に動くようになりました。

content.content: The baby has started moving very vigorously.

content: 隣の子供は最近きちんとあいさつするようになった。

content.content: The neighbor’s child has recently begun to make the proper greetings.

content: 注意したら文句を言わないようになった。

content.content: After I had a word, he stopped complaining.

Taking the dictionary form of verbs, expresses a change from a situation in which something is not possible to one in which it is, or, from one in which a thing cannot be realized to one in which it can. It is often used to express possibility in the form V-れる, as in example

content: . In cases where the negative form is used, as in
, it expresses a change to a situation in which a thing is not done. In this case 言わなくなった could also be said.

content.content: 【ようやく】
1. ようやく［ようやく　V-た／V-る］［ようやくNだ］

content: 冬の長い夜も終わりに近づき、ようやく東の空が白み始めた。

content.content: The long winter night drew to a close and little by little the eastern sky began to grow light.

content: 降り続いた雨もようやく上がって、陽が差し始めた。

content.content: When the rain finally stopped after a long time, the sun started to shine.

content: 冬の朝は遅い。7時頃になってようやく陽が昇る。

content.content: Winter mornings are late. Around seven o’clock, the sun gradually rises.

content: 子供たちも、ようやく一人前になって、それぞれ独立していった。

content.content: The children are finally adults and have each gained their independence.

content: 会議も終わる頃になって、彼はようやく現れた。

content.content: He finally appeared around the time the meeting was coming to an end.

content: 水道とガスは、震災から3ヶ月たって、ようやく復旧した。

content.content: The water and gas supplies were finally restored three months after the earthquake.

content: 何度も計画を変更して、ようやく社長の了解を得ることができた。

content.content: After changing the plan many times, we finally got the company president’s consent.

content: 来年は娘もようやく卒業だ。

content.content: My daughter will finally graduate next year.
As in examples

content: , this is used to express a gradual change in a natural phenomenon. Also, as in
, it is used to express the speaker’s expectation or hope that something will change which has taken a long time or after many things have happened along the way.

content.content: Often used when a situation that is desirable to the speaker occurs but its use is not limited to instances where the speaker has especially been waiting and hoping for something. In cases where the speaker wishes to express their happiness or relief that something they have especially been waiting and hoping for is realized, やっと is often used.

2. ようやくThis shows that something is realized after taking much time or effort. Similar expressions are: どうにか, なんとか, やっと, かろうじて and からくも. For the differences in their usage, please refer to Usage 1 in やっと
a. ようやくV-た

content: タクシーを飛ばして、ようやく時間に間に合った。

content.content: Driving fast in a taxi, I just made it on time.

content: 試合は延長戦にもつれこんだが、一点差でようやく勝つことができた。

content.content: The match proceeded to a deadlock in the extra innings but we just managed to win with a one-point difference.

content: 何時間にもわたる手術の結果、ようやく命をとりとめた。

content.content: After many hours of surgery, she just pulled through.
Means “that was perilous but (I)....” It is used to express that a good result has been achieved. Where a difficult situation has been avoided, かろうじて...なかった is used.
（○）｛ようやく／やっと／かろうじて｝約束の時間に間に合った。
I just made the appointment on time.
（×）危ないところだったが、｛ようやく／やっと｝大事故にはならなかった。
That was dangerous but a major accident was just avoided.
（○）危ないところだったが、かろうじて大事故にはならなかった。
That was dangerous but a major accident was just avoided.
b. ようやくV-ている

content: 世界は、微妙なかけひきで、ようやく軍事的な均衡を保っている。

content.content: By subtle tactics, a military equilibrium is just barely sustained in the world.

content: 両親から援助を受けて、ようやく生計を立てている。

content.content: With my parents’ assistance, I can just about eke out a living.

content: 病人は、人工呼吸器を使って、ようやく息をしているという状態だ。

content.content: The patient can just (barely) breathe using an artificial respirator.
Means “it’s terrible but, somehow (I am)...ing.” It does not express the same urgency as cases which use やっと.
c. ようやくV-るN

content: 家と家のすき間は、人一人がようやく通れる広さしかない。

content.content: The space between the houses is just wide enough for one person to pass through.

content: 人に支えてもらって、ようやく歩ける状態だ。

content.content: I can just (barely) walk with someone’s support.

content: 本人は気にしているが、「ここにある」と言われて、ようやく気が付く程度の傷で、たいしたことはない。

content.content: Though he is worried about it, the scar is so insignificant that one only notices it when someone points it out.

content: 鍵は、大人が背伸びをして、ようやく手が届く高さに隠してあって、子供にはとることができない。
